verses.text: At the first God made the heaven and the earth.
And the earth as aste and ithout form; and it as dark on the face of the deep: and the Spirit of God as moving on the face of the aters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there as light.
And God, looking on the light, sa that it as good: and God made a division beteen the light and the dark,
Naming the light, Day, and the dark, Night. And there as evening and there as morning, the first day.
And God said, Let there be a solid arch stretching over the aters, parting the aters from the aters.
And God made the arch for a division beteen the aters hich ere under the arch and those hich ere over it: and it as so.
And God gave the arch the name of Heaven. And there as evening and there as morning, the second day.
And God said, Let the aters under the heaven come together in one place, and let the dry land be seen: and it as so.
And God gave the dry land the name of Earth; and the aters together in their place ere named Seas: and God sa that it as good.
And God said, Let grass come up on the earth, and plants producing seed, and fruit-trees giving fruit, in hich is their seed, after their sort: and it as so.
And grass came up on the earth, and every plant producing seed of its sort, and every tree producing fruit, in hich is its seed, of its sort: and God sa that it as good.
And there as evening and there as morning, the third day.
And God said, Let there be lights in the arch of heaven, for a division beteen the day and the night, and let them be for signs, and for marking the changes of the year, and for days and for years:
And let them be for lights in the arch of heaven to give light on the earth: and it as so.
And God made the to great lights: the greater light to be the ruler of the day, and the smaller light to be the ruler of the night: and he made the stars.
And God put them in the arch of heaven, to give light on the earth;
To have rule over the day and the night, and for a division beteen the light and the dark: and God sa that it as good.
And there as evening and there as morning, the fourth day.
And God said, Let the aters be full of living things, and let birds be in flight over the earth under the arch of heaven.
And God made great sea-beasts, and every sort of living and moving thing ith hich the aters ere full, and every sort of inged bird: and God sa that it as good.
And God gave them his blessing, saying, Be fertile and have increase, making all the aters of the seas full, and let the birds be increased in the earth.
And there as evening and there as morning, the fifth day.
And God said, Let the earth give birth to all sorts of living things, cattle and all things moving on the earth, and beasts of the earth after their sort: and it as so.
And God made the beast of the earth after its sort, and the cattle after their sort, and everything moving on the face of the earth after its sort: and God sa that it as good.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, like us: and let him have rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the air and over the cattle and over all the earth and over every living thing hich goes flat on the earth.
And God made man in his image, in the image of God he made him: male and female he made them.

And God gave them his blessing and said to them, Be fertile and have increase, and make the earth full and be masters of it; be rulers over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the air and over every living thing moving on the earth.
And God said, See, I have given you every plant producing seed, on the face of all the earth, and every tree hich has fruit producing seed: they ill be for your food:
And to every beast of the earth and to every bird of the air and every living thing moving on the face of the earth I have given every green plant for food: and it as so.
And God sa everything hich he had made and it as very good. And there as evening and there as morning, the sixth day.
And the heaven and the earth and all things in them ere complete.
And on the seventh day God came to the end of all his ork; and on the seventh day he took his rest from all the ork hich he had done.
And God gave his blessing to the seventh day and made it holy: because on that day he took his rest from all the ork hich he had made and done.
These are the generations of the heaven and the earth hen they ere made.

In the day hen the Lord God made earth and heaven there ere no plants of the field on the earth, and no grass had come up: for the Lord God had not sent rain on the earth and there as no man to do ork on the land.
But a mist ent up from the earth, atering all the face of the land.
And the Lord God made man from the dust of the earth, breathing into him the breath of life: and man became a living soul.
And the Lord God made a garden in the east, in Eden; and there he put the man hom he had made.
And out of the earth the Lord made every tree to come, delighting the eye and good for food; and in the middle of the garden, the tree of life and the tree of the knoledge of good and evil.
And a river ent out of Eden giving ater to the garden; and from there it as parted and became four streams.
The name of the first is Pishon, hich goes round about all the land of Havilah here there is gold.
And the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.
And the name of the second river is Gihon: this river goes round all the land of Cush.
And the name of the third river is Tigris, hich goes to the east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.
And the Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to do ork in it and take care of it.
And the Lord God gave the man orders, saying, You may freely take of the fruit of every tree of the garden:
But of the fruit of the tree of the knoledge of good and evil you may not take; for on the day hen you take of it, death ill certainly come to you.
And the Lord God said, It is not good for the man to be by himself: I ill make one like himself as a help to him

And from the earth the Lord God made every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and took them to the man to see hat names he ould give them: and hatever name he gave to any living thing, that as its name.
And the man gave names to all cattle and to the birds of the air and to every beast of the field; but Adam had no one like himself as a help.
And the Lord God sent a deep sleep on the man, and took one of the bones from his side hile he as sleeping, joining up the flesh again in its place:
And the bone hich the Lord God had taken from the man he made into a oman, and took her to the man.
And the man said, This is no bone of my bone and flesh of my flesh: let her name be Woman because she as taken out of Man.
For this cause ill a man go aay from his father and his mother and be joined to his ife; and they ill be one flesh.
And the man and his ife ere ithout clothing, and they had no sense of shame.
No the snake as iser than any beast of the field hich the Lord God had made. And he said to the oman, Has God truly said that you may not take of the fruit of any tree in the garden?
And the oman said, We may take of the fruit of the trees in the garden:
But of the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, If you take of it or put your hands on it, death ill come to you.
And the snake said, Death ill not certainly come to you:
For God sees that on the day hen you take of its fruit, your eyes ill be open, and you ill be as gods, having knoledge of good and evil.
And hen the oman sa that the tree as good for food, and a delight to the eyes, and to be desired to make one ise, she took of its fruit, and gave it to her husband.
And their eyes ere open and they ere conscious that they had no clothing and they made themselves coats of leaves stitched together.

And there came to them the sound of the Lord God alking in the garden in the evening ind: and the man and his ife ent to a secret place among the trees of the garden, aay from the eyes of the Lord God.
And the voice of the Lord God came to the man, saying, Where are you?
And he said, Hearing your voice in the garden I as full of fear, because I as ithout clothing: and I kept myself from your eyes.
And he said, Who gave you the knoledge that you ere ithout clothing? Have you taken of the fruit of the tree hich I said you ere not to take?
And the man said, The oman hom you gave to be ith me, she gave me the fruit of the tree and I took it.
And the Lord God said to the oman, What have you done? And the oman said, I as tricked by the deceit of the snake and I took it.

And the Lord God said to the snake, Because you have done this you are cursed more than all cattle and every beast of the field; you ill go flat on the earth, and dust ill be your food all the days of your life:
And there ill be ar beteen you and the oman and beteen your seed and her seed: by him ill your head be crushed and by you his foot ill be ounded.
To the oman he said, Great ill be your pain in childbirth; in sorro ill your children come to birth; still your desire ill be for your husband, but he ill be your master.

And to Adam he said, Because you gave ear to the voice of your ife and took of the fruit of the tree hich I said you ere not to take, the earth is cursed on your account; in pain you ill get your food from it all your life.
Thorns and aste plants ill come up, and the plants of the field ill be your food;
With the hard ork of your hands you ill get your bread till you go back to the earth from hich you ere taken: for dust you are and to the dust you ill go back.
And the man gave his ife the name of Eve because she as the mother of all ho have life.
And the Lord God made for Adam and for his ife coats of skins for their clothing.
And the Lord God said, No the man has become like one of us, having knoledge of good and evil; and no if he puts out his hand and takes of the fruit of the tree of life, he ill go on living for ever.
So the Lord God sent him out of the garden of Eden to be a orker on the earth from hich he as taken.
So he sent the man out; and at the east of the garden of Eden he put inged ones and a flaming sord turning every ay to keep the ay to the tree of life.
And the man had connection ith Eve his ife, and she became ith child and gave birth to Cain, and said, I have got a man from the Lord.
Then again she became ith child and gave birth to Abel, his brother. And Abel as a keeper of sheep, but Cain as a farmer.
And after a time, Cain gave to the Lord an offering of the fruits of the earth.
And Abel gave an offering of the young lambs of his flock and of their fat. And the Lord as pleased ith Abel’s offering;
But in Cain and his offering he had no pleasure. And Cain as angry and his face became sad.
And the Lord said to Cain, Why are you angry? and hy is your face sad?
If you do ell, ill you not have honour? and if you do rong, sin is aiting at the door, desiring to have you, but do not let it be your master.
And Cain said to his brother, Let us go into the field: and hen they ere in the field, Cain made an attack on his brother Abel and put him to death.
And the Lord said to Cain, Where is your brother Abel? And he said, I have no idea: am I my brother’s keeper?
And he said, What have you done? the voice of your brother’s blood is crying to me from the earth.
And no you are cursed from the earth, hose mouth is open to take your brother’s blood from your hand;
No longer ill the earth give you her fruit as the reard of your ork; you ill be a anderer in flight over the earth.
And Cain said, My punishment is greater than my strength.
You have sent me out this day from the face of the earth and from before your face; I ill be a anderer in flight over the earth, and hoever sees me ill put me to death.
And the Lord said, Truly, if Cain is put to death, seven lives ill be taken for his. And the Lord put a mark on Cain so that no one might put him to death.
And Cain ent aay from before the face of the Lord, and made his living-place in the land of Nod on the east of Eden.
And Cain had connection ith his ife and she became ith child and gave birth to Enoch: and he made a ton, and gave the ton the name of Enoch after his son.
And Enoch had a son Irad: and Irad became the father of Mehujael: and Mehujael became the father of Methushael: and Methushael became the father of Lamech.
And Lamech had to ives; the name of the one as Adah, and the name of the other Zillah.
And Adah gave birth to Jabal: he as the father of such as are living in tents and keep cattle.
And his brother’s name as Jubal: he as the father of all players on instruments of music.
And Zillah gave birth to Tubal-cain, ho is the father of every maker of cutting instruments of brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal-cain as Naamah.
And Lamech said to his ives, Adah and Zillah, give ear to my voice; you ives of Lamech, give attention to my ords, for I ould put a man to death for a ound, and a young man for a blo;
If seven lives are to be taken as punishment for Cain’s death, seventy-seven ill be taken for Lamech’s.
And Adam had connection ith his ife again, and she gave birth to a son to hom she gave the name of Seth: for she said, God has given me another seed in place of Abel, hom Cain put to death.
And Seth had a son, and he gave him the name of Enosh: at this time men first made use of the name of the Lord in orship.
This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day hen God made man, he made him in the image of God;
Male and female he made them, naming them Man, and giving them his blessing on the day hen they ere made.
Adam had been living for a hundred and thirty years hen he had a son like himself, after his image, and gave him the name of Seth:
And after the birth of Seth, Adam ent on living for eight hundred years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Adam’s life ere nine hundred and thirty: and he came to his end.
And Seth as a hundred and five years old hen he became the father of Enosh:
And he ent on living after the birth of Enosh for eight hundred and seven years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Seth’s life ere nine hundred and telve: and he came to his end.
And Enosh as ninety years old hen he became the father of Kenan:
And after the birth of Kenan, Enosh ent on living for eight hundred and fifteen years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Enosh ere nine hundred and five: and he came to his end.
And Kenan as seventy years old hen he became the father of Mahalalel:
And after the birth of Mahalalel, Kenan ent on living for eight hundred and forty years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Kenan’s life ere nine hundred and ten; and he came to his end.
And Mahalalel as sixty-five years old hen he became the father of Jared:
And after the birth of Jared, Mahalalel ent on living for eight hundred and thirty years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Mahalalel’s life ere eight hundred and ninety-five: and he came to his end.
And Jared as a hundred and sixty-to years old hen he became the father of Enoch:
And Jared ent on living after the birth of Enoch for eight hundred years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Jared’s life ere nine hundred and sixty-to: and he came to his end.
And Enoch as sixty-five years old hen he became the father of Methuselah:
And after the birth of Methuselah, Enoch ent on in God’s ays for three hundred years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Enoch’s life ere three hundred and sixty-five:
And Enoch ent on in God’s ays: and he as not seen again, for God took him.
And Methuselah as a hundred and eighty-seven years old hen he became the father of Lamech:
And after the birth of Lamech, Methuselah ent on living for seven hundred and eighty-to years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Methuselah’s life ere nine hundred and sixty-nine: and he came to his end.
And Lamech as a hundred and eighty-to years old hen he had a son:
And he gave him the name of Noah, saying, Truly, he ill give us rest from our trouble and the hard ork of our hands, because of the earth hich as cursed by God.
And after the birth of Noah, Lamech ent on living for five hundred and ninety-five years, and had sons and daughters:
And all the years of Lamech’s life ere seven hundred and seventy-seven: and he came to his end.
And hen Noah as five hundred years old, he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And after a time, hen men ere increasing on the earth, and had daughters,
The sons of God sa that the daughters of men ere fair; and they took ives for themselves from those ho ere pleasing to them.
And the Lord said, My spirit ill not be in man for ever, for he is only flesh; so the days of his life ill be a hundred and tenty years.

There ere men of great strength and size on the earth in those days; and after that, hen the sons of God had connection ith the daughters of men, they gave birth to children: these ere the great men of old days, the men of great name.
And the Lord sa that the sin of man as great on the earth, and that all the thoughts of his heart ere evil.
And the Lord had sorro because he had made man on the earth, and grief as in his heart.

And the Lord said, I ill take aay man, hom I have made, from the face of the earth, even man and beast and that hich goes on the earth and every bird of the air; for I have sorro for having made them.
But Noah had grace in the eyes of God.
These are the generations of Noah. Noah as an upright man and ithout sin in his generation: he ent in the ays of God.
And Noah had three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
And the earth as evil in God’s eyes and full of violent ays.
And God, looking on the earth, sa that it as evil: for the ay of all flesh had become evil on the earth.
And God said to Noah, The end of all flesh has come; the earth is full of their violent doings, and no I ill put an end to them ith the earth.
Make for yourself an ark of gopher ood ith rooms in it, and make it safe from the ater inside and out.
And this is the ay you are to make it: it is to be three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits ide, and thirty cubits high.
You are to put a indo in the ark, a cubit from the roof, and a door in the side of it, and you are to make it ith a loer and second and third floors.
For truly, I ill send a great flo of aters over the earth, for the destruction from under the heaven of all flesh in hich is the breath of life; everything on the earth ill come to an end.
But ith you I ill make an agreement; and you ill come into the ark, you and your sons and your ife and your sons’ ives ith you.
And you ill take ith you into the ark to of every sort of living thing, and keep them safe ith you; they ill be male and female.
To of every sort of bird and cattle and of every sort of living thing hich goes on the earth ill you take ith you to keep them from destruction.
And make a store of every sort of food for yourself and them.
And all these things Noah did; as God said, so he did.
And the Lord said to Noah, Take all your family and go into the ark, for you only in this generation have I seen to be upright.
Of every clean beast you ill take seven males and seven females, and of the beasts hich are not clean, to, the male and his female;
And of the birds of the air, seven males and seven females, so that their seed may still be living on the face of the earth.
For after seven days I ill send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, for the destruction of every living thing hich I have made on the face of the earth.
And Noah did everything hich the Lord said he as to do.
And Noah as six hundred years old hen the aters came floing over all the earth.
And Noah, ith his sons and his ife and his sons’ ives, ent into the ark because of the floing of the aters.
Of clean beasts, and of beasts hich are not clean, and of birds, and of everything hich goes on the earth,
In tos, male and female, they ent into the ark ith Noah, as God had said.
And after the seven days, the aters came over all the earth.
In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, all the fountains of the great deep came bursting through, and the indos of heaven ere open;
And rain came don on the earth for forty days and forty nights.
On the same day Noah, ith Shem, Ham, and Japheth, his sons, and his ife and his sons’ ives, ent into the ark;
And ith them, every sort of beast and cattle, and every sort of thing hich goes on the earth, and every sort of bird.
They ent ith Noah into the ark, to and to of all flesh in hich is the breath of life.
Male and female of all flesh ent in, as God had said, and the ark as shut by the Lord.
And for forty days the aters ere over all the earth; and the aters ere increased so that the ark as lifted up high over the earth.
And the aters overcame everything and ere increased greatly on the earth, and the ark as resting on the face of the aters.
And the aters overcame everything on the earth; and all the mountains under heaven ere covered.
The aters ent fifteen cubits higher, till all the mountains ere covered.
And destruction came on every living thing moving on the earth, birds and cattle and beasts and everything hich ent on the earth, and every man.
Everything on the dry land, in hich as the breath of life, came to its end.

Every living thing on the face of all the earth, man and cattle and things moving on the face of the earth, and birds of the air, came to destruction: only Noah and those ho ere ith him in the ark, ere kept from death.
And the aters ere over the earth a hundred and fifty days.
And God kept Noah in mind, and all the living things and the cattle hich ere ith him in the ark: and God sent a ind over the earth, and the aters ent don.
And the fountains of the deep and the indos of heaven ere shut, and the rain from heaven as stopped.
And the aters ent sloly back from the earth, and at the end of a hundred and fifty days the aters ere loer.
And on the seventeenth day of the seventh month the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
And still the aters ent on falling, till on the first day of the tenth month the tops of the mountains ere seen.
Then, after forty days, through the open indo of the ark hich he had made,
Noah sent out a raven, hich ent this ay and that till the aters ere gone from the earth.
And he sent out a dove, to see if the aters had gone from the face of the earth;
But the dove sa no resting-place for her foot, and came back to the ark, for the aters ere still over all the earth; and he put out his hand, and took her into the ark.
And after aiting another seven days, he sent the dove out again;
And the dove came back at evening, and in her mouth as an olive-leaf broken off: so Noah as certain that the aters had gone don on the earth.
And after seven days more, he sent the dove out again, but she did not come back to him.
And in the six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the aters ere dry on the earth: and Noah took the cover off the ark and sa that the face of the earth as dry.
And on the tenty-seventh day of the second month the earth as dry.
And God said to Noah,
Go out of the ark, you and your ife and your sons and your sons’ ives.
Take out ith you every living thing hich is ith you, birds and cattle and everything hich goes on the earth, so that they may have offspring and be fertile and be increased on the earth.
And Noah ent out ith his sons and his ife and his sons’ ives;
And every beast and bird and every living thing of every sort hich goes on the earth, ent out of the ark.
And Noah made an altar to the Lord, and from every clean beast and bird he made burned offerings on the altar.

And hen the seet smell came up to the Lord, he said in his heart, I ill not again put a curse on the earth because of man, for the thoughts of man’s heart are evil from his earliest days; never again ill I send destruction on all living things as I have done.
While the earth goes on, seed time and the getting in of the grain, cold and heat, summer and inter, day and night, ill not come to an end.
And God gave his blessing to Noah and his sons, and said, Be fertile, and have increase, and make the earth full.
And the fear of you ill be strong in every beast of the earth and every bird of the air; everything hich goes on the land, and all the fishes of the sea, are given into your hands.
Every living and moving thing ill be food for you; I give them all to you as before I gave you all green things.
But flesh ith the life-blood in it you may not take for food.
And for your blood, hich is your life, ill I take payment; from every beast I ill take it, and from every man ill I take payment for the blood of his brother-man.
Whoever takes a man’s life, by man ill his life be taken; because God made man in his image.
And no, be fertile and have increase; have offspring on the earth and become great in number.
And God said to Noah and to his sons,
Truly, I ill make my agreement ith you and ith your seed after you,
And ith every living thing ith you, all birds and cattle and every beast of the earth hich comes out of the ark ith you.
And I ill make my agreement ith you; never again ill all flesh be cut off by the aters; never again ill the aters come over all the earth for its destruction.
And God said, This is the sign of the agreement hich I make beteen me and you and every living thing ith you, for all future generations:
I ill put my bo in the cloud and it ill be for a sign of the agreement beteen me and the earth.
And henever I make a cloud come over the earth, the bo ill be seen in the cloud,
And I ill keep in mind the agreement beteen me and you and every living thing; and never again ill there be a great flo of aters causing destruction to all flesh.
And the bo ill be in the cloud, and looking on it, I ill keep in mind the eternal agreement beteen God and every living thing on the earth.
And God said to Noah, This is the sign of the agreement hich I have made beteen me and all flesh on the earth.
And the sons of Noah ho ent out of the ark ere Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and Ham is the father of Canaan.
These three ere the sons of Noah and from them all the earth as peopled.
In those days Noah became a farmer, and he made a vine-garden.
And he took of the ine of it and as overcome by drink; and he as uncovered in his tent.
And Ham, the father of Canaan, sa his father unclothed, and gave nes of it to his to brothers outside.
And Shem and Japheth took a robe, and putting it on their backs ent in ith their faces turned aay, and put it over their father so that they might not see him unclothed.
And, aaking from his ine, Noah sa hat his youngest son had done to him, and he said,
Cursed be Canaan; let him be a servant of servants to his brothers.
And he said, Praise to the Lord, the God of Shem; let Canaan be his servant.
May God make Japheth great, and let his living-place be in the tents of Shem, and let Canaan be his servant.
And Noah ent on living three hundred and fifty years after the great flo of aters;
all the years of his life ere nine hundred and fifty: and he came to his end.
No these are the generations of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth: these are the sons hich they had after the great flo of aters
The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog and Madai and Javan and Tubal and Meshech and Tiras.
And the sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz and Riphath and Togarmah.
And the sons of Javan: Elishah and Tarshish, the Kittim and the Dodanim.
From these came the nations of the sea-lands, ith their different families and languages.
And the sons of Ham: Cush and Mizraim and Put and Canaan.
And the sons of Cush: Seba and Havilah and Sabtah and Raamah and Sabteca; and the sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
And Cush as the father of Nimrod, ho as the first of the great men of the earth.
He as a very great boman, so that there is a saying, Like Nimrod, a very great boman.
And at the first, his kingdom as Babel and Erech and Accad and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
From that land he ent out into Assyria, building Nineveh ith its ide streets and Calah,
And Resen beteen Nineveh and Calah, hich is a very great ton.
And Mizraim as the father of the Ludim and Anamim and Lehabim and Naphtuhim;
And Pathrusim and Casluhim and Caphtorim, from hom came the Philistines.
And Canaan as the father of Zidon, ho as his oldest son, and Heth,
And the Jebusite and the Amorite and the Girgashite,
And the Hivite and the Arkite and the Sinite,
And the Arvadite and the Zemarite and the Hamathite; after that the families of the Canaanites ent far and ide in all directions;
Their country stretching from Zidon to Gaza, in the direction of Gerar; and to Lasha, in the direction of Sodom and Gomorrah and Admah and Zeboiim.
All these, ith their different families, languages, lands, and nations, are the offspring of Ham.
And Shem, the older brother of Japheth, the father of the children of Eber, had other sons in addition.
These are the sons of Shem: Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad and Lud and Aram.
And the sons of Aram: Uz and Hul and Gether and Mash.
And Arpachshad became the father of Shelah; and Shelah became the father of Eber.
And Eber had to sons: the name of the one as Peleg, because in his time the peoples of the earth became separate; and his brother’s name as Joktan.
And Joktan as the father of Almodad and Sheleph and Hazarmaveth and Jerah
And Hadoram and Uzal and Diklah
And Obal and Abimael and Sheba
And Ophir and Havilah and Jobab; all these ere the sons of Joktan.

Did he not say to me himself, She is my sister? and she herself said, He is my brother: ith an upright heart and clean hands have I done this.
And God said to him in the dream, I see that you have done this ith an upright heart, and I have kept you from sinning against me: for this reason I did not let you come near her.

So no, give the man back his ife, for he is a prophet, and let him say a prayer for you, so your life may be safe: but if you do not give her back, be certain that death ill come to you and all your house.
So Abimelech got up early in the morning and sent for all his servants and gave them ord of these things, and they ere full of fear.

Then Abimelech sent for Abraham, and said, What have you done to us? hat rong have I done you that you have put on me and on my kingdom so great a sin? You have done to me things hich are not to be done.
And Abimelech said to Abraham, Why did you do this thing?
And Abraham said, Because it seemed to me that there as no fear of God in this place, and that they might put me to death because of my ife.
And, in fact, she is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my ife:
And hen God sent me andering from my father’s house, I said to her, Let this be the sign of your love for me; herever e go, say of me, He is my brother.
Then Abimelech gave to Abraham sheep and oxen and men-servants and omen-servants, and gave him back his ife Sarah.
And Abimelech said, See, all my land is before you; take hatever place seems good to you.
And he said to Sarah, See, I have given to your brother a thousand bits of silver so that your rong may be put right; no your honour is clear in the eyes of all.
Then Abraham made prayer to God, and God made Abimelech ell again, and his ife and his omen-servants, so that they had children.
For the Lord had kept all the omen of the house of Abimelech from having children, because of Sarah, Abraham’s ife.
And the Lord came to Sarah as he had said and did to her as he had undertaken.
And Sarah became ith child, and gave Abraham a son hen he as old, at the time named by God.
And Abraham gave to his son, to hom Sarah had given birth, the name Isaac.
And hen his son Isaac as eight days old, Abraham made him undergo circumcision, as God had said to him.
No Abraham as a hundred years old hen the birth of Isaac took place.
And Sarah said, God has given me cause for laughing, and everyone ho has nes of it ill be laughing ith me.
And she said, Who ould have said to Abraham that Sarah ould have a child at her breast? for see, I have given him a son no hen he is old.
And hen the child as old enough to be taken from the breast, Abraham made a great feast.
And Sarah sa the son of Hagar the Egyptian playing ith Isaac.
So she said to Abraham, Send aay that oman and her son: for the son of that oman is not to have a part in the heritage ith my son Isaac.
And this as a great grief to Abraham because of his son.
But God said, Let it not be a grief to you because of the boy and Hagar his mother; give ear to hatever Sarah says to you, because it is from Isaac that your seed ill take its name.
And I ill make a nation of the son of your servant-oman, because he is your seed.
And early in the morning Abraham got up, and gave Hagar some bread and a ater-skin, and put the boy on her back, and sent her aay: and she ent, andering in the aste land of Beer-sheba.
And hen all the ater in the skin as used up, she put the child don under a tree.
And she ent some distance aay, about an arro flight, and seating herself on the earth, she gave ay to bitter eeping, saying, Let me not see the death of my child.
And the boy’s cry came to the ears of God; and the angel of God said to Hagar from heaven, Hagar, hy are you eeping? have no fear, for the child’s cry has come to the ears of God.
Come, take your child in your arms, for I ill make of him a great nation.
Then God made her eyes open, and she sa a ater-spring, and she got ater in the skin and gave the boy a drink.
And God as ith the boy, and he became tall and strong, and he became a boman, living in the aste land.
And hile he as in the aste land of Paran, his mother got him a ife from the land of Egypt.
No at that time, Abimelech and Phicol, the captain of his army, said to Abraham, I see that God is ith you in all you do.

No, then, give me your oath, in the name of God, that you ill not be false to me or to my sons after me, but that as I have been good to you, so you ill be to me and to this land here you have been living.
And Abraham said, I ill give you my oath.
But Abraham made a protest to Abimelech because of a ater-hole hich Abimelech’s servants had taken by force.
But Abimelech said, I have no idea ho has done this thing; you never gave me ord of it, and I had no knoledge of it till this day.
And Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the to of them made an agreement together.
And Abraham put seven young lambs of the flock on one side by themselves.
Then Abimelech said, What are these seven lambs hich you have put on one side?
And he said, Take these seven lambs from me as a itness that I have made this ater-hole.
So he gave that place the name Beer-sheba, because there the to of them had given their oaths.
So they made an agreement at Beer-sheba, and Abimelech and Phicol, the captain of his army, ent back to the land of the Philistines.
And Abraham, after planting a holy tree in Beer-sheba, gave orship to the name of the Lord, the Eternal God.
And Abraham ent on living in the land of the Philistines as in a strange country.
No after these things, God put Abraham to the test, and said to him, Abraham; and he said, Here am I.
And he said to him, Take your son, your dearly loved only son Isaac, and go to the land of Moriah and give him as a burned offering on one of the mountains of hich I ill give you knoledge.

And Abraham got up early in the morning, and made ready his ass, and took ith him to of his young men and Isaac, his son, and after the ood for the burned offering had been cut, he ent on his ay to the place of hich God had given him ord.
And on the third day, Abraham, lifting up his eyes, sa the place a long ay off.
Then he said to his young men, Keep here ith the ass; and I and the boy ill go on and give orship and come back again to you.
And Abraham put the ood for the burned offering on his son’s back, and he himself took the fire and the knife in his hand, and the to of them ent on together.
Then Isaac said to Abraham, My father; and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, We have ood and fire here, but here is the lamb for the burned offering?
And Abraham said, God himself ill give the lamb for the burned offering: so they ent on together.

And they came to the place of hich God had given him knoledge; and there Abraham made the altar and put the ood in place on it, and having made tight the bands round Isaac his son, he put him on the ood on the altar.
And stretching out his hand, Abraham took the knife to put his son to death.
But the voice of the angel of the Lord came from heaven, saying, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I.

And he said, Let not your hand be stretched out against the boy to do anything to him; for no I am certain that the fear of God is in your heart, because you have not kept back your son, your only son, from me.
And lifting up his eyes, Abraham sa a sheep fixed by its horns in the brushood: and Abraham took the sheep and made a burned offering of it in place of his son.
And Abraham gave that place the name Yaheh-yireh: as it is said to this day, In the mountain the Lord is seen.
And the voice of the angel of the Lord came to Abraham a second time from heaven,
Saying, I have taken an oath by my name, says the Lord, because you have done this and have not kept back from me your dearly loved only son,
That I ill certainly give you my blessing, and your seed ill be increased like the stars of heaven and the sand by the seaside; your seed ill take the land of those ho are against them;
And your seed ill be a blessing to all the nations of the earth, because you have done hat I gave you orders to do.
Then Abraham ent back to his young men and they ent together to Beer-sheba, the place here Abraham as living.
After these things, Abraham had nes that Milcah, the ife of his brother Nahor, had given birth to children;
Uz the oldest, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel, the father of Aram,
And Chesed and Hazo and Pildash and Jidlaph and Bethuel.
Bethuel as the father of Rebekah: these eight ere the children of Milcah and Nahor, Abraham’s brother.
And his servant Reumah gave birth to Tebah and Gaham and Tahash and Maacah.
No the years of Sarah’s life ere a hundred and tenty-seven.
And Sarah’s death took place in Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan: and Abraham ent into his house, eeping and sorroing for Sarah.
And Abraham came from his dead and said to the children of Heth,
I am living among you as one from a strange country: give me some land here as my property, so that I may put my dead to rest.
And in anser the children of Heth said to Abraham,
My lord, truly you are a great chief among us; take the best of our resting-places for your dead; not one of us ill keep back from you a place here you may put your dead to rest.
And Abraham got up and gave honour to the children of Heth, the people of that land.
And he said to them, If you ill let me put my dead to rest here, make a request for me to Ephron, the son of Zohar,
That he ill give me the hollo in the rock named Machpelah, hich is his property at the end of his field; let him give it to me for its full price as a resting-place for my dead among you.
No Ephron as seated among the children of Heth: and Ephron the Hittite gave Abraham his anser in the hearing of the children of Heth, and of all those ho came into his ton, saying,
No, my lord, I ill give you the field ith the hollo in the rock; before all the children of my people ill I give it to you for a resting-place for your dead.
And Abraham ent don on his face before the people of the land.
And Abraham said to Ephron, in the hearing of the people of the land, If only you ill give ear to me, I ill give you the price of the field; take it, and let me put my dead to rest there.
So Ephron said to Abraham,
My lord, give ear to me: the value of the land is four hundred shekels; hat is that beteen me and you? so put your dead to rest there.
And Abraham took note of the price fixed by Ephron in the hearing of the children of Heth, and gave him four hundred shekels in current money.
So Ephron’s field at Machpelah near Mamre, ith the hollo in the rock and all the trees in the field and round it,
Became the property of Abraham before the eyes of the children of Heth and of all ho came into the ton.
Then Abraham put Sarah his ife to rest in the hollo rock in the field of Machpelah near Mamre, that is, Hebron in the land of Canaan.
And the field and the hollo rock ere handed over to Abraham as his property by the children of Heth.
No Abraham as old and far on in years: and the Lord had given him everything in full measure.
And Abraham said to his chief servant, the manager of all his property, Come no, put your hand under my leg:
And take an oath by the Lord, the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you ill not get a ife for my son Isaac from the daughters of the Canaanites among hom I am living;
But that you ill go into my country and to my relations and get a ife there for my son Isaac.
And the servant said, If by chance the oman ill not come ith me into this land, am I to take your son back again to the land from hich you came?
And Abraham said, Take care that you do not let my son go back to that land.

The Lord God of heaven, ho took me from my father’s house and from the land of my birth, and made an oath to me, saying, To your seed I ill give this land: he ill send his angel before you and give you a ife for my son in that land.
And if the oman ill not come ith you, then you are free from this oath; only do not take my son back there.
And the servant put his hand under Abraham’s leg, and gave him his oath about this thing.
And the servant took ten of his master’s camels, and all sorts of good things of his master’s, and ent to Mesopotamia, to the ton of Nahor.
And he made the camels take their rest outside the ton by the ater-spring in the evening, at the time hen the omen came to get ater.
And he said, O Lord, the God of my master Abraham, let me do ell in hat I have undertaken this day, and give your mercy to my master Abraham.
See, I am aiting here by the ater-spring; and the daughters of the ton are coming out to get ater:

No, may the girl to hom I say, Let don your vessel and give me a drink, and ho says in anser, Here is a drink for you and let me give ater to your camels: may she be the one marked out by you for your servant Isaac: so may I be certain that you have been good to my master Abraham.
And even before his ords ere ended, Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, ho as the ife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, came out ith her ater-vessel on her arm.
She as a very beautiful girl, a virgin, ho had never been touched by a man: and she ent don to the spring to get ater in her vessel.
And the servant came running to her and said, Give me a little ater from your vessel.
And she said, Take a drink, my lord: and quickly letting don her vessel onto her hand, she gave him a drink.
And having done so, she said, I ill get ater for your camels till they have had enough.
And after putting the ater from her vessel into the animals’ drinking-place, she ent quickly back to the spring and got ater for all the camels.
And the man, looking at her, said nothing, aiting to see if the Lord had given his journey a good outcome.
And hen the camels had had enough, the man took a gold nose-ring, half a shekel in eight, and to ornaments for her arms of ten shekels eight of gold;
And said to her, Whose daughter are you? is there room in your father’s house for us?
And she said to him, I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah, Nahor’s ife.
And she said, We have a great store of dry grass and cattle-food, and there is room for you.
And ith bent head the man gave orship to the Lord;
And said, Praise be to the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, ho has given a sign that he is good and true to my master, by guiding me straight to the house of my master’s family.
So the girl ent running and took the nes of these things to her mother’s house
No Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he came out quickly to the man at the ater-spring.

And hen he sa the nose-ring and the ornaments on his sister’s hands, and hen she gave him ord of hat the man had said to her, then he ent out to the man ho as aiting ith the camels by the ater-spring.
And he said to him, Come in, you on hom is the blessing of the Lord; hy are you aiting outside? for I have made the house ready for you, and a place for the camels.
Then the man came into the house, and Laban took their cords off the camels and gave them dry grass and food, and he gave to him and the men ho ere ith him ater for ashing their feet.
And meat as put before him, but he said, I ill not take food till I have made my business clear to you. And they said, Do so.
And he said, I am Abraham’s servant.
The Lord has given my master every blessing, and he has become great: he has given him flocks and herds and silver and gold, and men-servants and omen-servants and camels and asses.
And hen Sarah, my master’s ife, as old, she gave birth to a son, to hom he has given all he has.
And my master made me take an oath, saying, Do not get a ife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites among hom I am living;
But go to my father’s house and to my relations for a ife for my son.
And I said to my master, What if the oman ill not come ith me?
And he said, The Lord, hom I have ever kept before me, ill send his angel ith you, ho ill make it possible for you to get a ife for my son from my relations and my father’s house;
And you ill be free from your oath to me hen you come to my people; and if they ill not give her to you, you ill be free from your oath.
And I came today to the ater-spring, and I said, O Lord, the God of my master Abraham, if it is your purpose to give a good outcome to my journey,
Let it come about that, hile I am aiting here by the ater-spring, if a girl comes to get ater and I say to her, Give me a little ater from your vessel, and she says,
Take a drink, and I ill get ater for your camels; let her be the oman marked out by the Lord for my master’s son.
And even hile I as saying this to myself, Rebekah came out ith her vessel on her arm; and she ent don to the spring to get ater; and I said to her, Give me a drink.
And straight aay she took don her vessel from her arm, and said, Take a drink, and I ill get ater for your camels.
And questioning her, I said, Whose daughter are you? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor, and Milcah his ife. Then I put the ring on her nose and the ornaments on her hands.
And ith bent head I gave orship and praise to the Lord, the God of my master Abraham, by hom I had been guided in the right ay, to get the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.
And no, say if you ill do hat is good and right for my master or not, in order that it may be clear to me hat I have to do.
Then Laban and Bethuel said in anser, This is the Lord’s doing: it is not for us to say Yes or No to you.
See, here is Rebekah: take her and go, and let her be your master’s son’s ife, as the Lord has said.
And at these ords, Abraham’s servant ent don on his face and gave praise to the Lord.
Then he took jeels of silver and jeels of gold and fair robes and gave them to Rebekah: and he gave things of value to her mother and her brother.
Then he and the men ho ere ith him had food and drink, and took their rest there that night; and in the morning he got up, and said, Let me no go back to my master.
But her brother and her mother said, Let the girl be ith us a eek or ten days, and then she may go.
And he said, Do not keep me; the Lord has given a good outcome to my journey; let me no go back to my master.
And they said, We ill send for the girl, and let her make the decision.
And they sent for Rebekah and said to her, Are you ready to go ith this man? And she said, I am ready.
So they sent their sister Rebekah and her servant ith Abraham’s servant and his men.
And they gave Rebekah their blessing, saying, O sister, may you be the mother of thousands and ten thousands; and may your seed overcome all those ho make ar against them.
So Rebekah and her servant-omen ent ith the man, seated on the camels; and so the servant took Rebekah and ent on his ay.
No Isaac had come through the aste land to Beer-lahai-roi; for he as living in the South.
And hen the evening as near, he ent andering out into the fields, and lifting up his eyes he sa camels coming.
And hen Rebekah, looking up, sa Isaac, she got don from her camel,
And said to the servant, Who is that man coming to us through the field? And the servant said, It is my master: then she took her veil, covering her face ith it.
Then the servant gave Isaac the story of all he had done.
And Isaac took Rebekah into his tent and she became his ife; and in his love for her, Isaac as comforted after his father’s death.
And Abraham took another ife named Keturah.
She became the mother of Zimran and Jokshan and Medan and Midian and Ishbak and Shuah.
And Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan. And from Dedan came the Asshurim and Letushim and Leummim.
And from Midian came Ephah and Epher and Hanoch and Abida and Eldaah. All these ere the offspring of Keturah.
No Abraham gave all his property to Isaac;
But to the sons of his other omen he gave offerings, and sent them aay, hile he as still living, into the east country.
No the years of Abraham’s life ere a hundred and seventy-five.
And Abraham came to his death, an old man, full of years; and he as put to rest ith his people.
And Isaac and Ishmael, his sons, put him to rest in the hollo rock of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron, the son of Zohar the Hittite, near Mamre;
The same field hich Abraham got from the children of Heth: there Abraham as put to rest ith Sarah, his ife.
No after the death of Abraham, the blessing of God as ith Isaac, his son.
No these are the generations of Ishmael, the son of Abraham, hose mother as Hagar the Egyptian, the servant of Sarah:
These are the names of the sons of Ishmael by their generations: Ishmael’s first son as Nebaioth; then Kedar and Adbeel and Mibsam
And Mishma and Dumah and Massa,
Hadad and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names in their tons and their tent-circles; telve chiefs ith their peoples.
And the years of Ishmael’s life ere a hundred and thirty-seven: and he came to his end, and as put to rest ith his people.
And their country as from Havilah to Shur hich is east of Egypt: they took their place to the east of all their brothers.
No these are the generations of Abraham’s son Isaac:
Isaac as forty years old hen he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramaean of Paddan-aram, and the sister of Laban the Aramaean, to be his ife.
Isaac made prayer to the Lord for his ife because she had no children; and the Lord gave ear to his prayer, and Rebekah became ith child.
And the children ere fighting together inside her, and she said, If it is to be so, hy am I like this? So she ent to put her question to the Lord.
And the Lord said to her, To nations are in your body, and to peoples ill come to birth from you: the one ill be stronger than the other, and the older ill be the servant of the younger.
And hen the time came for her to give birth, there ere to children in her body.
And the first came out red from head to foot like a robe of hair, and they gave him the name of Esau.
And after him, his brother came out, gripping Esau’s foot; and he as named Jacob: Isaac as sixty years old hen she gave birth to them.
And the boys came to full groth; and Esau became a man of the open country, an expert boman; but Jacob as a quiet man, living in tents.
No Isaac’s love as for Esau, because Esau’s meat as greatly to his taste: but Rebekah had more love for Jacob.
And one day Jacob as cooking some soup hen Esau came in from the fields in great need of food;
And Esau said to Jacob, Give me a full meal of that red soup, for I am overcome ith need for food: for this reason he as named Edom.
And Jacob said, First of all give me your birthright.
And Esau said, Truly, I am at the point of death: hat profit is the birthright to me?
And Jacob said, First of all give me your oath; and he gave him his oath, handing over his birthright to Jacob.
Then Jacob gave him bread and soup; and he took food and drink and ent aay, caring little for his birthright.
Then came a time of great need in the land, like that hich had been before in the days of Abraham. And Isaac ent to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, at Gerar.
And the Lord came to him in a vision and said, Do not go don to Egypt; keep in the land of hich I ill give you knoledge:
Keep in this land, and I ill be ith you and give you my blessing; for to you and to your seed ill I give all these lands, giving effect to the oath hich I made to your father Abraham;
I ill make your seed like the stars of heaven in number, and ill give them all these lands, and your seed ill be a blessing to all the nations of the earth;
Because Abraham gave ear to my voice and kept my ords, my rules, my orders, and my las.
So Isaac ent on living in Gerar;

And hen he as questioned by the men of the place about his ife, he said, She is my sister; fearing to say, She is my ife; for, he said, the men of the place may put me to death on account of Rebekah; because she is very beautiful.
And hen he had been there for some time, Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looking through a indo, sa Isaac playing ith Rebekah his ife.
And he said to Isaac, It is clear that she is your ife: hy then did you say, She is my sister? And Isaac said, For fear that I might be put to death because of her.
Then Abimelech said, What have you done to us? one of the people might ell have had connection ith your ife, and the sin ould have been ours.
And Abimelech gave orders to his people that anyone touching Isaac or his ife as to be put to death.
No Isaac, planting seed in that land, got in the same year fruit a hundred times as much, for the blessing of the Lord as on him.
And his ealth became very great, increasing more and more;
For he had great ealth of flocks and herds and great numbers of servants; so that the Philistines ere full of envy.
No all the ater-holes, hich his father’s servants had made in the days of Abraham, had been stopped up ith earth by the Philistines.
And Abimelech said to Isaac, Go aay from us, for you are stronger than e are.
So Isaac ent aay from there, and put up his tents in the valley of Gerar, making his living-place there.
And he made again the ater-holes hich had been made in the days of Abraham his father, and hich had been stopped up by the Philistines; and he gave them the names hich his father had given them.
No Isaac’s servants made holes in the valley, and came to a spring of floing ater.
But the herdmen of Gerar had a fight ith Isaac’s herdmen, for they said, The spring is ours: so he gave the spring the name of Esek, because there as a fight about it.
Then they made another ater-hole, and there as a fight about that, so he gave it the name of Sitnah.

Then he ent aay from there, and made another ater-hole, about hich there as no fighting: so he gave it the name of Rehoboth, for he said, No the Lord has made room for us, and e ill have fruit in this land.
And from there he ent on to Beer-sheba.
That night the Lord came to him in a vision, and said, I am the God of your father Abraham: have no fear for I am ith you, blessing you, and your seed ill be increased because of my servant Abraham.
Then he made an altar there, and gave orship to the name of the Lord, and he put up his tents there, and there his servants made a ater-hole.
And Abimelech had come to him from Gerar, ith Ahuzzath his friend and Phicol, the captain of his army.
And Isaac said to them, Why have you come to me, seeing that in your hate for me you sent me aay from you?
And they said, We sa clearly that the Lord as ith you: so e said, Let there be an oath beteen us and you, and let us make an agreement ith you;
That you ill do us no damage, even as e put no hand on you, and did you nothing but good, and sent you aay in peace: and no the blessing of the Lord is on you.
Then he made a feast for them, and they all had food and drink.
And early in the morning they took an oath one to the other: then Isaac sent them aay and they ent on their ay in peace.
And that day Isaac’s servants came to him and gave him ord of the ater-hole hich they had made, and said to him, We have come to ater.
And he gave it the name of Shibah: so the name of that ton is Beer-sheba to this day.
And hen Esau as forty years old, he took as his ives Judith, the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
And Isaac and Rebekah had grief of mind because of them.
No hen Isaac as old and his eyes had become clouded so that he as not able to see, he sent for Esau, his first son, and said to him, My son: and he said, Here am I.
And he said, See no, I am old, and my death may take place at any time:
So take your arros and your bo and go out to the field and get meat for me;
And make me food, good to the taste, such as is pleasing to me, and put it before me, so that I may have a meal and give you my blessing before death comes to me.
No Isaac’s ords to his son ere said in Rebekah’s hearing. Then Esau ent out to get the meat.
And Rebekah said to Jacob, her son, Your father said to your brother Esau in my hearing,
Go and get some roe’s meat and make me a good meal, so that I may be full, and give you my blessing before the Lord before my death.
No, my son, do hat I say.
Go to the flock and get me to fat young goats; and I ill make of them a meal to your father’s taste:
And you ill take it to him, so that he may have a good meal and give you his blessing before his death.
And Jacob said to Rebekah, his mother, But Esau my brother is covered ith hair, hile I am smooth:
If by chance my father puts his hand on me, it ill seem to him that I am tricking him, and he ill put a curse on me in place of a blessing.
And his mother said, Let the curse be on me, my son: only do as I say, and go and get them for me.
So he ent and got them and took them to his mother: and she made a meal to his father’s taste.
And Rebekah took the fair robes of her oldest son, hich ere ith her in the house, and put them on Jacob, her younger son:
And she put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck:
And she gave into the hand of Jacob, her son, the meat and the bread hich she had made ready.
And he came to his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I: ho are you, my son?
And Jacob said, I am Esau, your oldest son; I have done as you said: come no, be seated and take of my meat, so that you may give me a blessing.
And Isaac said, Ho is it that you have got it so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the Lord your God made it come my ay.
And Isaac said, Come near so that I may put my hand on you, my son, and see if you are truly my son Esau or not.
And Jacob ent near his father Isaac: and he put his hands on him; and he said, The voice is Jacob’s voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau.
And he did not make out ho he as, because his hands ere covered ith hair like his brother Esau’s hands: so he gave him a blessing.
And he said, Are you truly my son Esau? And he said, I am.
And he said, Put it before me and I ill take of my son’s meat, so that I may give you a blessing. And he put it before him and he took it; and he gave him ine, and he had a drink.
And his father Isaac said to him, Come near no, my son, and give me a kiss.

And he came near and gave him a kiss; and smelling the smell of his clothing, he gave him a blessing, and said, See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field on hich the blessing of the Lord has come:
May God give you the de of heaven, and the good things of the earth, and grain and ine in full measure:

Let peoples be your servants, and nations go don before you: be lord over your brothers, and let your mother’s sons go don before you: a curse be on everyone by hom you are cursed, and a blessing on those ho give you a blessing.
And hen Isaac had come to the end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob had not long gone aay from Isaac his father, Esau came in from the field.
And he made ready a meal, good to the taste, and took it to his father, and said to him, Let my father get up and take of his son’s meat, so that you may give me a blessing.
And Isaac his father said to him, Who are you? And he said, I am your oldest son, Esau.
And in great fear Isaac said, Who then is he ho got meat and put it before me, and I took it all before you came, and gave him a blessing, and his it ill be?
And hearing the ords of his father, Esau gave a great and bitter cry, and said to his father, Give a blessing to me, even to me, O my father!
And he said, Your brother came ith deceit, and took aay your blessing.
And he said, Is it because he is named Jacob that he has tice taken my place? for he took aay my birthright, and no he has taken aay my blessing. And he said, Have you not kept a blessing for me?
And Isaac ansering said, But I have made him your master, and have given him all his brothers for servants; I have made him strong ith grain and ine: hat then am I to do for you, my son?
And Esau said to his father, Is that the only blessing you have, my father? give a blessing to me, even me! And Esau as overcome ith eeping.
Then Isaac his father made anser and said to him, Far from the fertile places of the earth, and far from the de of heaven on high ill your living-place be:
By your sord ill you get your living and you ill be your brother’s servant; but hen your poer is increased his yoke ill be broken from off your neck.
So Esau as full of hate for Jacob because of his father’s blessing; and he said in his heart, The days of eeping for my father are near; then I ill put my brother Jacob to death.
Then Rebekah, hearing hat Esau had said, sent for Jacob, her younger son, and said to him, It seems that your brother Esau is purposing to put you to death.
So no, my son, do hat I say: go quickly to Haran, to my brother Laban;
And be there ith him for a little time, till your brother’s rath is turned aay;
Till the memory of hat you have done to him is past and he is no longer angry: then I ill send ord for you to come back; are the to of you to be taken from me in one day?

Then Rebekah said to Isaac, My life is a eariness to me because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob takes a ife from among the daughters of Heth, such as these, the omen of this land, of hat use ill my life be to me?
Then Isaac sent for Jacob, and blessing him, said, Do not take a ife from among the omen of Canaan;
But go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel, your mother’s father, and there get yourself a ife from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.
And may God, the Ruler of all, give you his blessing, giving you fruit and increase, so that you may become an army of peoples.
And may God give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your seed, so that the land of your anderings, hich God gave to Abraham, may be your heritage.
So Isaac sent Jacob aay: and he ent to Paddan-aram, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Aramaean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

So hen Esau sa that Isaac had given Jacob his blessing, and sent him aay to Paddan-aram to get a ife for himself there, blessing him and saying to him, Do not take a ife from among the omen of Canaan;
And that Jacob had done as his father and mother said and had gone to Paddan-aram;
It as clear to Esau that his father had no love for the omen of Canaan,
So Esau ent to Ishmael and took Mahalath, the daughter of Abraham’s son Ishmael, the sister of Nebaioth, to be his ife in addition to the ives he had.
So Jacob ent out from Beer-sheba to go to Haran.

And coming to a certain place, he made it his resting-place for the night, for the sun had gone don; and he took one of the stones hich ere there, and putting it under his head he ent to sleep in that place.
And he had a dream, and in his dream he sa steps stretching from earth to heaven, and the angels of God ere going up and don on them.
And he sa the Lord by his side, saying, I am the Lord, the God of Abraham your father, and the God of Isaac: I ill give to you and to your seed this land on hich you are sleeping.

Your seed ill be like the dust of the earth, covering all the land to the est and to the east, to the north and to the south: you and your seed ill be a name of blessing to all the families of the earth.
And truly, I ill be ith you, and ill keep you herever you go, guiding you back again to this land; and I ill not give you up till I have done hat I have said to you.
And Jacob, aaking from his sleep, said, Truly, the Lord is in this place and I as not conscious of it.
And fear came on him, and he said, This is a holy place; this is nothing less than the house of God and the dooray of heaven.
And early in the morning Jacob took the stone hich had been under his head, and put it up as a pillar and put oil on it.
And he gave that place the name of Beth-el, but before that time the ton as named Luz.
Then Jacob took an oath, and said, If God ill be ith me, and keep me safe on my journey, and give me food and clothing to put on,
So that I come again to my father’s house in peace, then I ill take the Lord to be my God,
And this stone hich I have put up for a pillar ill be God’s house: and of all you give me, I ill give a tenth part to you.
Then Jacob ent on his journey till he came to the land of the children of the East.
And there he sa a ater-hole in a field, and by the side of it three flocks of sheep, for there they got ater for the sheep: and on the mouth of the ater-hole there as a great stone.
And all the flocks ould come together there, and hen the stone had been rolled aay, they ould give the sheep ater, and put the stone back again in its place on the mouth of the ater-hole.
Then Jacob said to the herdmen, My brothers, here do you come from? And they said, From Haran.
And he said to them, Have you any knoledge of Laban, the son of Nahor? And they said, We have.
And he said to them, Is he ell? And they said, He is ell, and here is Rachel his daughter coming ith the sheep.
Then Jacob said, The sun is still high and it is not time to get the cattle together: get ater for the sheep and go and give them their food.
And they said, We are not able to do so till all the flocks have come together and the stone has been rolled aay from the mouth of the ater-hole; then e ill get ater for the sheep.
While he as still talking ith them, Rachel came ith her father’s sheep, for she took care of them.
Then hen Jacob sa Rachel, the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, coming ith Laban’s sheep, he came near, and rolling the stone aay from the mouth of the hole, he got ater for Laban’s flock.
And eeping for joy, Jacob gave Rachel a kiss.
And Rachel, hearing from Jacob that he as her father’s relation and that he as the son of Rebekah, ent running to give her father nes of it.
And Laban, hearing nes of Jacob, his sister’s son, came running, and took Jacob in his arms, and kissing him, made him come into his house. And Jacob gave him nes of everything.
And Laban said to him, Truly, you are my bone and my flesh. And he kept Jacob ith him for the space of a month.
Then Laban said to Jacob, Because you are my brother are you to be my servant for nothing? say no, hat is your payment to be?
No Laban had to daughters: the name of the older as Leah, and the name of the younger as Rachel.
And Leah’s eyes ere clouded, but Rachel as fair in face and form.
And Jacob as in love ith Rachel; and he said, I ill be your servant seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.
And Laban said, It is better for you to have her than another man: go on living here ith me.
And Jacob did seven years’ ork for Rachel; and because of his love for her it seemed to him only a very little time.
Then Jacob said to Laban, Give me my ife so that I may have her, for the days are ended.
And Laban got together all the men of the place and gave a feast.
And in the evening he took Leah, his daughter, and gave her to him, and he ent in to her.
And Laban gave Zilpah, his servant-girl, to Leah, to be her aiting-oman.
And in the morning Jacob sa that it as Leah: and he said to Laban, What have you done to me? as I not orking for you so that I might have Rachel? hy have you been false to me?
And Laban said, In our country e do not let the younger daughter be married before the older.
Let the eek of the bride-feast come to its end and then e ill give you the other in addition, if you ill be my servant for another seven years.
And Jacob did so; and hen the eek as ended, Laban gave him his daughter Rachel for his ife.
And Laban gave Rachel his servant-girl Bilhah to be her aiting-oman.
Then Jacob took Rachel as his ife, and his love for her as greater than his love for Leah; and he ent on orking for Laban for another seven years.
No the Lord, seeing that Leah as not loved, gave her a child; hile Rachel had no children.
And Leah as ith child, and gave birth to a son to hom she gave the name Reuben: for she said, The Lord has seen my sorro; no my husband ill have love for me.
Then she became ith child again, and gave birth to a son; and said, Because it has come to the Lord’s ears that I am not loved, he has given me this son in addition: and she gave him the name Simeon.
And she as ith child again, and gave birth to a son; and said, No at last my husband ill be united to me, because I have given him three sons: so he as named Levi.
And she as ith child again, and gave birth to a son: and she said, This time I ill give praise to the Lord: so he as named Judah; after this she had no more children for a time.
No Rachel, because she had no children, as full of envy of her sister; and she said to Jacob, If you do not give me children I ill not go on living.
But Jacob as angry ith Rachel, and said, Am I in the place of God, ho has kept your body from having fruit?
Then she said, Here is my servant Bilhah, go in to her, so that she may have a child on my knees, and I may have a family by her.
So she gave him her servant Bilhah as a ife, and Jacob ent in to her.
And Bilhah became ith child, and gave birth to a son.
Then Rachel said, God has been my judge, and has given ear to my voice, and has given me a son; so he as named Dan.
And again Bilhah, Rachel’s servant, as ith child, and gave birth to a second son.
And Rachel said, I have had a great fight ith my sister, and I have overcome her: and she gave the child the name Naphtali.
When it as clear to Leah that she ould have no more children for a time, she gave Zilpah, her servant, to Jacob as a ife.
And Zilpah, Leah’s servant, gave birth to a son.
And Leah said, It has gone ell for me: and she gave him the name Gad.
And Zilpah, Leah’s servant, gave birth to a second son.
And Leah said, Happy am I! and all omen ill give itness to my joy: and she gave him the name Asher.
No at the time of the grain-cutting, Reuben sa some love-fruits in the field, and took them to his mother Leah. And Rachel said to her, Let me have some of your son’s love-fruits.

But Leah said to her, Is it a small thing that you have taken my husband from me? and no ould you take my son’s love-fruits? Then Rachel said, You may have him tonight in exchange for your son’s love-fruits.

In the evening, hen Jacob came in from the field, Leah ent out to him and said, Tonight you are to come to me, for I have given my son’s love-fruits as a price for you. And he ent in to her that night.
And God gave ear to her and she became ith child, and gave Jacob a fifth son.
Then Leah said, God has made payment to me for giving my servant-girl to my husband: so she gave her son the name Issachar.
And again Leah became ith child, and she gave Jacob a sixth son.
And she said, God has given me a good bride-price; no at last ill I have my husband living ith me, for I have given him six sons: and she gave him the name Zebulun.
After that she had a daughter, to hom she gave the name Dinah.
Then God gave thought to Rachel, and hearing her prayer he made her fertile.
And she as ith child, and gave birth to a son: and she said, God has taken aay my shame.
And she gave him the name Joseph, saying, May the Lord give me another son.
No after the birth of Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, Let me go aay to my place and my country.
Give me my ives and my children, for hom I have been your servant, and let me go: for you have knoledge of all the ork I have done for you.
And Laban said, If you ill let me say so, do not go aay; for I have seen by the signs that the Lord has been good to me because of you.
Say then hat your payment is to be and I ill give it.
Then Jacob said, You have seen hat I have done for you, and ho your cattle have done ell under my care.
For before I came you had little, and it has been greatly increased; and the Lord has given you a blessing in everything I have done; but hen am I to do something for my family?
And Laban said, What am I to give you? And Jacob said, Do not give me anything; but I ill again take up the care of your flock if you ill only do this for me:
Let me go through all your flock today, taking out from among them all the sheep hich are marked or coloured or black, and all the marked or coloured goats: these ill be my payment.
And so you ill be able to put my honour to the test in time to come; if you see among my flocks any goats hich are not marked or coloured, or any sheep hich is not black, you may take me for a thief.
And Laban said, Let it be as you say.

So that day he took all the he-goats hich ere banded or coloured, and all the she-goats hich ere marked or coloured or had hite marks, and all the black sheep, and gave them into the care of his sons;
And sent them three days’ journey aay: and Jacob took care of the rest of Laban’s flock.
Then Jacob took young branches of trees, cutting off the skin so that the hite ood as seen in bands.
And he put the banded sticks in the drinking-places here the flock came to get ater; and they became ith young hen they came to the ater.
And because of this, the flock gave birth to young hich ere marked ith bands of colour.
These lambs Jacob kept separate; and he put his flock in a place by themselves and not ith Laban’s flock.
And henever the stronger ones of the flock became ith young, Jacob put the sticks in front of them in the drinking-places, so that they might become ith young hen they sa the sticks.
But hen the flocks ere feeble, he did not put the sticks before them; so that the feebler flocks ere Laban’s and the stronger ere Jacob’s.
So Jacob’s ealth as greatly increased; he had great flocks and omen-servants and men-servants and camels and asses.
No it came to the ears of Jacob that Laban’s sons ere saying, Jacob has taken aay all our father’s property, and in this ay he has got all this ealth.
And Jacob sa that Laban’s feeling for him as no longer hat it had been before.
Then the Lord said to Jacob, Go back to the land of your fathers, and to your relations, and I ill be ith you.
And Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to come to him in the field among his flock.
And he said to them, It is clear to me that your father’s feeling is no longer hat it as to me; but the God of my father has been ith me
And you have seen ho I have done all in my poer for your father,
But your father has not kept faith ith me, and ten times he has made changes in my payment; but God has kept him from doing me damage.

If he said, All those in the flock hich have marks are to be yours, then all the flock gave birth to marked young; and if he said, All the banded ones are to be yours, then all the flock had banded young.
So God has taken aay your father’s cattle and has given them to me.
And at the time hen the flock ere ith young, I sa in a dream that all the he-goats hich ere joined ith the she-goats ere banded and marked and coloured.
And in my dream the angel of the Lord said to me, Jacob: and I said, Here am I.
And he said, See ho all the he-goats are banded and marked and coloured: for I have seen hat Laban has done to you.
I am the God of Beth-el, here you put oil on the pillar and took an oath to me: no then, come out of this land and go back to the country of your birth.
Then Rachel and Leah said to him in anser, What part or heritage is there for us in our father’s house?
Are e not as people from a strange country to him? for he took a price for us and no it is all used up.
For the ealth hich God has taken from him is ours and our children’s; so no, hatever God has said to you, do.
Then Jacob put his ives and his sons on camels;
And sending on before him all his cattle and his property hich he had got together in Paddan-aram, he made ready to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.
No Laban had gone to see to the cutting of the ool of his sheep; so Rachel secretly took the images of the gods of her father’s house.
And Jacob ent aay secretly, ithout giving nes of his flight to Laban the Aramaean.
So he ent aay ith all he had, and ent across the River in the direction of the hill-country of Gilead.
And on the third day Laban had nes of Jacob’s flight.
And taking the men of his family ith him, he ent after him for seven days and overtook him in the hill-country of Gilead.
Then God came to Laban in a dream by night, and said to him, Take care that you say nothing good or bad to Jacob.
No hen Laban overtook him, Jacob had put up his tent in the hill-country; and Laban and his brothers put up their tents in the hill-country of Gilead.
And Laban said to Jacob, Why did you go aay secretly, taking my daughters aay like prisoners of ar?
Why did you make a secret of your flight, not giving me ord of it, so that I might have sent you aay ith joy and songs, ith melody and music?
You did not even let me give a kiss to my sons and my daughters. This as a foolish thing to do.
It is in my poer to do you damage: but the God of your father came to me this night, saying, Take care that you say nothing good or bad to Jacob.
And no, it seems, you are going because your heart’s desire is for your father’s house; but hy have you taken my gods?
And Jacob, in anser, said to Laban, My fear as that you might take your daughters from me by force.
As for your gods, if anyone of us has them, let him be put to death: make search before us all for hat is yours, and take it. For Jacob had no knoledge that Rachel had taken them.
So Laban ent into Jacob’s tent and into Leah’s tent, and into the tents of the to servant-omen, but they ere not there; and he came out of Leah’s tent and ent into Rachel’s.
No Rachel had taken the images, and had put them in the camels’ basket, and as seated on them. And Laban, searching through all the tent, did not come across them.
And she said to her father, Let not my lord be angry because I do not get up before you, for I am in the common condition of omen. And ith all his searching, he did not come across the images.
Then Jacob as angry ith Laban, and said, What crime or sin have I done that you have come after me ith such passion?
No that you have made search through all my goods, hat have you seen hich is yours? Make it clear no before my people and your people, so that they may be judges beteen us.
These tenty years I have been ith you; your sheep and your goats have had young ithout loss, not one of your he-goats have I taken for food.
Anything hich as ounded by beasts I did not take to you, but myself made up for the loss of it; you made me responsible for hatever as taken by thieves, by day or by night.
This as my condition, asted by heat in the day and by the bitter cold at night; and sleep ent from my eyes.
