These tenty years I have been in your house; I as your servant for fourteen years because of your daughters, and for six years I kept your flock, and ten times as my payment changed.

If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been ith me, you ould have sent me aay ith nothing in my hands. But God has seen my troubles and the ork of my hands, and this night he kept you back.
Then Laban, ansering, said, These omen are my daughters and these children my children, the flocks and all you see are mine: hat no may I do for my daughters and for their children?
Come, let us make an agreement, you and I; and let it be for a itness beteen us.
Then Jacob took a stone and put it up as a pillar.
And Jacob said to his people, Get stones together; and they did so; and they had a meal there by the stones.
And the name Laban gave it as Jegar-sahadutha: but Jacob gave it the name of Galeed.
And Laban said, These stones are a itness beteen you and me today. For this reason its name as Galeed,
And Mizpah, for he said, May the Lord keep atch on us hen e are unable to see one another’s doings.
If you are cruel to my daughters, or if you take other ives in addition to my daughters, then though no man is there to see, God ill be the itness beteen us.
And Laban said, See these stones and this pillar hich I have put beteen you and me;
They ill be itness that I ill not go over these stones to you, and you ill not go over these stones or this pillar to me, for any evil purpose.
May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, be our judge. Then Jacob took an oath by the Fear of his father Isaac.
And Jacob made an offering on the mountain, and gave orders to his people to take food: so they had a meal and took their rest that night on the mountain.
And early in the morning Laban, after kissing and blessing his daughters, ent on his ay back to his country.
And on his ay Jacob came face to face ith the angels of God.
And hen he sa them he said, This is the army of God: so he gave that place the name of Mahanaim.
No Jacob sent servants before him to Esau, his brother, in the land of Seir, the country of Edom;
And he gave them orders to say these ords to Esau: Your servant Jacob says, Till no I have been living ith Laban:
And I have oxen and asses and flocks and men-servants and omen-servants: and I have sent to give my lord nes of these things so that I may have grace in his eyes.
When the servants came back they said, We have seen your brother Esau and he is coming out to you, and four hundred men ith him.
Then Jacob as in great fear and trouble of mind: and he put all the people and the flocks and the herds and the camels into to groups;
And said, If Esau, meeting one group, makes an attack on them, the others ill get aay safely.
Then Jacob said, O God of my father Abraham, the God of my father Isaac, the Lord ho said to me, Go back to your country and your family and I ill be good to you:
I am less than nothing in comparison ith all your mercies and your faith to me your servant; for ith only my stick in my hand I ent across Jordan, and no I have become to armies.
Be my saviour from the hand of Esau, my brother: for my fear is that he ill make an attack on me, putting to death mother and child.
And you said, Truly, I ill be good to you, and make your seed like the sand of the sea hich may not be numbered.
Then he put up his tent there for the night; and from among his goods he took, as an offering for his brother Esau,
To hundred she-goats and tenty he-goats, to hundred females and tenty males from the sheep,
Thirty camels ith their young ones, forty cos, ten oxen, tenty asses, and ten young asses.
These he gave to his servants, every herd by itself, and he said to his servants, Go on before me, and let there be a space beteen one herd and another.
And he gave orders to the first, saying, When my brother Esau comes to you and says, Whose servant are you, and here are you going, and hose are these herds?
Then say to him, These are your servant Jacob’s; they are an offering for my lord, for Esau; and he himself is coming after us.
And he gave the same orders to the second and the third and to all those ho ere ith the herds, saying, This is hat you are to say to Esau hen you see him;

And you are to say further, Jacob, your servant, is coming after us. For he said to himself, I ill take aay his rath by the offering hich I have sent on, and then I ill come before him: it may be that I ill have grace in his eyes.
So the servants ith the offerings ent on in front, and he himself took his rest that night in the tents ith his people.
And in the night he got up, and taking ith him his to ives and the to servant-omen and his eleven children, he ent over the river Jabbok.
He took them and sent them over the stream ith all he had.
Then Jacob as by himself; and a man as fighting ith him till dan.
But hen the man sa that he as not able to overcome Jacob, he gave him a blo in the hollo part of his leg, so that his leg as damaged.
And he said to him, Let me go no, for the dan is near. But Jacob said, I ill not let you go till you have given me your blessing.
Then he said, What is your name? And he said, Jacob.
And he said, Your name ill no longer be Jacob, but Israel: for in your fight ith God and ith men you have overcome.
Then Jacob said, What is your name? And he said, What is my name to you? Then he gave him a blessing.
And Jacob gave that place the name of Peniel, saying, I have seen God face to face, and still I am living.
And hile he as going past Peniel, the sun came up. And he ent ith unequal steps because of his damaged leg.
For this reason the children of Israel, even today, never take that muscle in the hollo of the leg as food, because the hollo of Jacob’s leg as touched.
Then Jacob, lifting up his eyes, sa Esau coming ith his four hundred men. So he made a division of the children beteen Leah and Rachel and the to omen-servants.
He put the servants and their children in front, Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Joseph at the back.
And he himself, going before them, ent don on his face to the earth seven times till he came near his brother.
Then Esau came running up to him, and folding him in his arms, gave him a kiss: and the to of them ere overcome ith eeping.
Then Esau, lifting up his eyes, sa the omen and the children, and said, Who are these ith you? And he said, The children hom God in his mercy has given to your servant.
Then the servants and their children came near, and ent don on their faces.
And Leah came near ith her children, and then Joseph and Rachel, and they did the same.
And he said, What ere all those herds hich I sa on the ay? And Jacob said, They ere an offering so that I might have grace in my lord’s eyes.
But Esau said, I have enough; keep hat is yours, my brother, for yourself.
And Jacob said, Not so; but if I have grace in your eyes, take them as a sign of my love, for I have seen your face as one may see the face of God, and you have been pleased ith me.
Take my offering then, ith my blessing; for God has been very good to me and I have enough: so at his strong request, he took it.
And he said, Let us go on our journey together, and I ill go in front.
But Jacob said, My lord may see that the children are only small, and there are young ones in my flocks and herds: one day’s over-driving ill be the destruction of all the flock.
Do you, my lord, go on before your servant; I ill come on sloly, at the rate at hich the cattle and the children are able to go, till I come to my lord at Seir.
And Esau said, Then keep some of my men ith you. And he said, What need is there for that, if my lord is pleased ith me?
So Esau, turning back that day, ent on his ay to Seir.
And Jacob ent on to Succoth, here he made a house for himself and put up tents for his cattle: for this reason the place as named Succoth.
So Jacob came safely from Paddan-aram to the ton of Shechem in the land of Canaan, and put up his tents near the ton.
And for a hundred bits of money he got from the children of Hamor, the builder of Shechem, the field in hich he had put up his tents.
And there he put up an altar, naming it El, the God of Israel.
No Dinah, the daughter hom Leah had by Jacob, ent out to see the omen of that country.
And hen Shechem, the son of Hamor the Hivite ho as the chief of that land, sa her, he took her by force and had connection ith her.
Then his heart ent out in love to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he said comforting ords to her.
And Shechem said to Hamor, his father, Get me this girl for my ife.
No Jacob had ord of hat Shechem had done to his daughter; but his sons ere in the fields ith the cattle, and Jacob said nothing till they came.
Then Hamor, the father of Shechem, came out to have a talk ith Jacob.

No the sons of Jacob came in from the fields hen they had nes of it, and they ere ounded and very angry because of the shame he had done in Israel by having connection ith Jacob’s daughter; and they said, Such a thing is not to be done.
But Hamor said to them, Shechem, my son, is full of desire for your daughter: ill you then give her to him for a ife?
And let our to peoples be joined together; give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.
Go on living ith us, and the country ill be open to you; do trade and get property there.
And Shechem said to her father and her brothers, If you ill give ear to my request, hatever you say I ill give to you.
Hoever great you make the bride-price and payment, I ill give it; only let me have the girl for my ife.
But the sons of Jacob gave a false anser to Shechem and Hamor his father, because of hat had been done to Dinah their sister.
And they said, It is not possible for us to give our sister to one ho is ithout circumcision, for that ould be a cause of shame to us:
But on this condition only ill e come to an agreement ith you: if every male among you becomes like us and undergoes circumcision;
Then e ill give our daughters to you and take your daughters to us and go on living ith you as one people.
But if you ill not undergo circumcision as e say, then e ill take our daughter and go.
And their ords ere pleasing to Hamor and his son Shechem.
And ithout loss of time the young man did as they said, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he as the noblest of his father’s house.
Then Hamor and Shechem, his son, ent to the meeting-place of their ton, and said to the men of the ton,

It is the desire of these men to be at peace ith us; let them then go on living in this country and doing trade here, for the country is ide open before them; let us take their daughters as ives and let us give them our daughters.
But these men ill make an agreement ith us to go on living ith us and to become one people, only on the condition that every male among us undergoes circumcision as they have done.
Then ill not their cattle and their goods and all their beasts be ours? so let us come to an agreement ith them so that they may go on living ith us.
Then all the men of the ton gave ear to the ords of Hamor and Shechem his son; and every male in the ton underent circumcision.
But on the third day after, before the ounds ere ell, to of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, took their sords and came into the ton by surprise and put all the males to death.
And Hamor and his son they put to death ith the sord, and they took Dinah from Shechem’s house and ent aay.
And the sons of Jacob came on them hen they ere ounded and made aste the ton because of hat had been done to their sister;
They took their flocks and their herds and their asses and everything in their ton and in their fields,
And all their ealth and all their little ones and their ives; everything in their houses they took and made them aste.

And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, You have made trouble for me and given me a bad name among the people of this country, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and because e are small in number they ill come together against me and make ar on me; and it ill be the end of me and all my people.
But they said, Were e to let him make use of our sister as a loose oman?
And God said to Jacob, Go up no to Beth-el and make your living-place there: and put up an altar there to the God ho came to you hen you ere in flight from your brother Esau.
Then Jacob said to all his people, Put aay the strange gods hich are among you, and make yourselves clean, and put on a change of clothing:
And let us go up to Beth-el: and there I ill make an altar to God, ho gave me an anser in the day of my trouble, and as ith me herever I ent.
Then they gave to Jacob all the strange gods hich they had, and the rings hich ere in their ears; and Jacob put them aay under the holy tree at Shechem.
So they ent on their journey: and the fear of God as on the tons round about, so that they made no attack on the sons of Jacob.
And Jacob came to Luz in the land of Canaan ( hich is the same as Beth-el), he and all his people.
And there he made an altar, naming the place El-beth-el: because it as there he had the vision of God hen he as in flight from his brother.
And Deborah, the servant ho had taken care of Rebekah from her birth, came to her end, and as put to rest near Beth-el, under the holy tree: and they gave it the name of Allon-bacuth.
No hen Jacob as on his ay from Paddan-aram, God came to him again and, blessing him, said,
Jacob is your name, but it ill be so no longer; from no your name ill be Israel; so he as named Israel.
And God said to him, I am God, the Ruler of all: be fertile, and have increase; a nation, truly a group of nations, ill come from you, and kings ill be your offspring;
And the land hich I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I ill give to you; and to your seed after you I ill give the land.
Then God ent up from him in the place here he had been talking ith him.
And Jacob put up a pillar in the place here he had been talking ith God, and put a drink offering on it, and oil.
And he gave to the place here God had been talking ith him, the name of Beth-el.
So they ent on from Beth-el; and hile they ere still some distance from Ephrath, the pains of birth came on Rachel and she had a hard time.
And hen her pain as very great, the oman ho as helping her said, Have no fear; for no you ill have another son.
And in the hour hen her life ent from her ( for death came to her), she gave the child the name Ben-oni: but his father gave him the name of Benjamin.
So Rachel came to her end and as put to rest on the road to Ephrath ( hich is Beth-lehem).
And Jacob put up a pillar on her resting-place; hich is named, The Pillar of the resting-place of Rachel, to this day.
And Israel ent journeying on and put up his tents on the other side of the toer of the flock.
No hile they ere living in that country, Reuben had connection ith Bilhah, his father’s servant-oman: and Israel had nes of it.
No Jacob had telve sons: the sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob’s first son, and Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Zebulun;
The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin;
The sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s servant: Dan and Naphtali;
The sons of Zilpah, Leah’s servant: Gad and Asher; these are the sons hom Jacob had in Paddan-aram.
And Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre, at Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, here Abraham and Isaac had been living.
And Isaac as a hundred and eighty years old.
Then Isaac came to his end and as put to rest ith his father’s people, an old man after a long life: and Jacob and Esau, his sons, put him in his last resting-place.
No these are the generations of Esau, that is to say, Edom.
Esau’s ives ere omen of Canaan: Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon the Hivite,
And Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, the sister of Nebaioth.
Adah had a son Eliphaz; and Basemath as the mother of Reuel;
Oholibamah as the mother of Jeush, Jalam, and Korah; these are the sons of Esau, hose birth took place in the land of Canaan.

Esau took his ives and his sons and his daughters, and all the people of his house, and his beasts and his cattle and all his goods hich he had got together in the land of Canaan, and ent into the land of Seir, aay from his brother Jacob.
For their ealth as so great that the land as not ide enough for the to of them and all their cattle.
So Esau made his living-place in the hill-country of Seir ( Esau is Edom).
And these are the generations of Esau, the father of the Edomites in the hill-country of Seir:
These are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, the son of Esau’s ife Adah, and Reuel, the son of Esau’s ife Basemath.
The sons of Eliphaz ere Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.
And Eliphaz, the son of Esau, had connection ith a oman named Timna, ho gave birth to Amalek: all these ere the children of Esau’s ife Adah.
And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah: they ere the children of Esau’s ife Basemath.
And these are the sons of Esau’s ife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon: she as the mother of Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
These ere the chiefs among the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz, Esau’s first son: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
Korah, Gatam, Amalek: all these ere chiefs in the land of Edom, the offspring of Eliphaz, the seed of Adah.
And these are the sons of Esau’s son Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, Mizzah: these ere the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom, the children of Esau’s ife Basemath.
And these are the sons of Esau’s ife Oholibamah: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah: these ere the chiefs ho came from Esau’s ife Oholibamah, daughter of Anah.
These ere the sons of Esau ( that is, Edom), and these ere their chiefs.
These are the sons of Seir the Horite ho ere living in that country; Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan: these are the chiefs of the Horites, offspring of Seir in the land of Edom.
The children of Lotan ere Hori and Hemam; Lotan’s sister as Timna.
And these are the children of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
And these are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah; that same Anah ho made the discovery of the ater-springs in the aste land, hen he as looking after the asses of his father Zibeon.
And these are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah his daughter.
These are the children of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Keran.
These are the children of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
These are the children of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These ere the Horite chiefs: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. Such ere the Horite chiefs in their order in the land of Seir.
And these are the kings ho ere ruling in the land of Edom before there as any king over the children of Israel.
Bela, son of Beor, as king in Edom, and the name of his chief ton as Dinhabah.
At his death, Jobab, son of Zerah of Bozrah, became king in his place.
And at the death of Jobab, Husham, from the country of the Temanites, became king in his place.
And at the death of Husham, Hadad, son of Bedad, ho overcame the Midianites in the field of Moab, became king; his chief ton as named Avith.
And at the death of Hadad, Samlah of Masrekah became king.
And at the death of Samlah, Shaul of Rehoboth by the River became king in his place.
And at the death of Shaul, Baal-hanan, son of Achbor, became king.
And at the death of Baal-hanan, Hadar became king in his place; his chief ton as named Pau, and his ife’s name as Mehetabel; she as the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Me-zahab.
These are the names of the chiefs of Esau in the order of their families and their places: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
Magdiel, Iram; these are the Edomite chiefs, in their places in their heritage; this is Esau, the father of the Edomites.
No Jacob as living in the land here his father had made a place for himself, in the land of Canaan.

These are the generations of Jacob: Joseph, a boy seventeen years old, as looking after the flock, together ith his brothers, the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s ives; and Joseph gave their father a bad account of them.
No the love hich Israel had for Joseph as greater than his love for all his other children, because he got him hen he as an old man: and he had a long coat made for him.
And because his brothers sa that Joseph as dearer to his father than all the others, they ere full of hate for him, and ould not say a kind ord to him.
No Joseph had a dream, and he gave his brothers an account of it, hich made their hate greater than ever.
And he said to them, Let me give you the story of my dream.
We ere in the field, getting the grain stems together, and my grain kept upright, and yours came round and ent don on the earth before mine.
And his brothers said to him, Are you to be our king? ill you have authority over us? And because of his dream and his ords, their hate for him became greater than ever.
Then he had another dream, and gave his brothers an account of it, saying, I have had another dream: the sun and the moon and eleven stars gave honour to me.

And he gave ord of it to his father and his brothers; but his father protesting said, What sort of a dream is this? am I and your mother and your brothers to go don on our faces to the earth before you?
And his brothers ere full of envy; but his father kept his ords in mind.
No his brothers ent to keep atch over their father’s flock in Shechem.
And Israel said to Joseph, Are not your brothers ith the flock in Shechem? come, I ill send you to them. And he said to him, Here am I.
And he said to him, Go no, and see if your brothers are ell and ho the flock is; then come back and give me ord. So he sent him out of the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.
And a man sa him andering in the country, and said to him, What are you looking for?
And he said, I am looking for my brothers; please give me ord of here they are keeping their flock.
And the man said, They have gone aay from here, for they said in my hearing, Let us go to Dothan. So Joseph ent after them and came up ith them at Dothan.
But they sa him hen he as a long ay off, and before he came near them they made a secret design against him to put him to death;
Saying to one another, See, here comes this dreamer.
Let us no put him to death and put his body into one of these holes, and e ill say, An evil beast has put him to death: then e ill see hat becomes of his dreams.
But Reuben, hearing these ords, got him out of their hands, saying, Let us not take his life.
Do not put him to a violent death, but let him be placed in one of the holes; this he said to keep him safe from their hands, ith the purpose of taking him back to his father again.
So hen Joseph came to his brothers, they took off his long coat hich he had on;
And they took him and put him in the hole: no the hole had no ater in it.
Then seating themselves, they took their meal: and looking up, they sa a travelling band of Ishmaelites, coming from Gilead on their ay to Egypt, ith spices and perfumes on their camels.
And Judah said to his brothers, What profit is there in putting our brother to death and covering up his blood?
Let us give him to these Ishmaelites for a price, and let us not put violent hands on him, for he is our brother, our flesh. And his brothers gave ear to him.
And some traders from Midian ent by; so pulling Joseph up out of the hole, they gave him to the Ishmaelites for tenty bits of silver, and they took him to Egypt.
No hen Reuben came back to the hole, Joseph as not there; and giving signs of grief,
He ent back to his brothers, and said, The child is gone; hat am I to do?
Then they took Joseph’s coat, and put on it some of the blood from a young goat hich they had put to death,
And they took the coat to their father, and said, We came across this; is it your son’s coat or not?
And he sa that it as, and said, It is my son’s coat; an evil beast has put him to death; ithout doubt Joseph has come to a cruel end.
Then Jacob, giving signs of grief, put on haircloth, and ent on eeping for his son day after day.
And all his sons and all his daughters came to give him comfort, but he ould not be comforted, saying ith eeping, I ill go don to the underorld to my son. So great as his father’s sorro for him.
And in Egypt the men of Midian gave him for a price to Potiphar, a captain of high position in Pharaoh’s house.
No at that time, Judah ent aay from his brothers and became the friend of a man of Adullam named Hirah.
And there he sa the daughter of a certain man of Canaan named Shua, and took her as his ife.
And she gave birth to a son, and he gave him the name Er.
And again she gave birth to a son, and he gave him the name Onan.
Then she had another son, to hom she gave the name Shelah; she as at Chezib hen the birth took place.
And Judah took a ife for his first son Er, and her name as Tamar.
No Er, Judah’s first son, did evil in the eyes of the Lord, so that he put him to death.
Then Judah said to Onan, Go in to your brother’s ife and do hat it is right for a husband’s brother to do; make her your ife and get offspring for your brother.
But Onan, seeing that the offspring ould not be his, ent in to his brother’s ife, but let his seed go on to the earth, so that he might not get offspring for his brother.
And hat he did as evil in the eyes of the Lord, so that he put him to death, like his brother.

Then Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-la, Go back to your father’s house and keep yourself as a ido till my son Shelah becomes a man: for he had in his mind the thought that death might come to him as it had come to his brothers. So Tamar ent back to her father’s house.

And after a time, Bath-shua, Judah’s ife, came to her end; and after Judah as comforted for her loss, he ent to Timnah, here they ere cutting the ool of his sheep, and his friend Hirah of Adullam ent ith him.
And hen Tamar had nes that her father-in-la as going up to Timnah to the ool-cutting,
She took off her ido’s clothing, and covering herself ith her veil, she took her seat near Enaim on the road to Timnah; for she sa that Shelah as no a man, but she had not been made his ife.
When Judah sa her he took her to be a loose oman of the ton, because her face as covered.
And turning to her by the roadside, he said to her, Let me come in to you; for he had no idea that she as his daughter-in-la. And she said, What ill you give me as my price?
And he said, I ill give you a young goat from the flock. And she said, What ill you give me as a sign till you send it?
And he said, What ould you have? And she said, Your ring and its cord and the stick in your hand. So he gave them to her and ent in to her, and she became ith child by him.
Then she got up and ent aay and took off her veil and put on her ido’s clothing.
Then Judah sent his friend Hirah ith the young goat, to get back the things hich he had given as a sign to the oman: but she as not there.
And he put questions to the men of the place, saying, Where is the loose oman ho as in Enaim by the ayside? And they said, There as no such oman there.
So he ent back to Judah, and said, I have not seen her, and the men of the place say that there is no such oman there.
And Judah said, Let her keep the things, so that e may not be shamed; I sent the young goat, but you did not see the oman.
No about three months after this, ord came to Judah that Tamar, his daughter-in-la, had been acting like a loose oman and as ith child. And Judah said, Take her out and let her be burned.

And hile she as being taken out, she sent ord to her father-in-la, saying, The man hose property these things are, is the father of my child: say then, hose are this ring and this cord and this stick?
Then Judah said openly that they ere his, and said, She is more upright than I am, for I did not give her to Shelah my son. And he had no more connection ith her.
And hen the time came for her to give birth, it as clear that there ere to children in her body.
And hile she as in the act of giving birth, one of them put out his hand; and the oman ho as ith her put a red thread round his hand, saying, This one came out first.
But then he took his hand back again, and his brother came first to birth: and the oman said, What an opening you have made for yourself! So he as named Perez.
And then his brother came out, ith the red thread round his hand, and he as named Zerah.
No Joseph as taken don to Egypt; and Potiphar the Egyptian, a captain of high position in Pharaoh’s house, got him for a price from the Ishmaelites ho had taken him there.
And the Lord as ith Joseph, and he did ell; and he as living in the house of his master the Egyptian.
And his master sa that the Lord as ith him, making everything he did go ell.
And having a high opinion of Joseph as his servant, he made him the overseer of his house and gave him control over all he had.

And from the time hen he made him overseer and gave him control of all his property, the blessing of the Lord as ith the Egyptian, because of Joseph; the blessing of the Lord as on all he had, in the house and in the field.
And he gave Joseph control of all his property, keeping no account of anything, but only the food hich as put before him. No Joseph as very beautiful in form and face.
And after a time, his master’s ife, looking on Joseph ith desire, said to him, Be my lover.
But he ould not, and said to her, You see that my master keeps no account of hat I do in his house, and has put all his property in my control;
So that no one has more authority in this house than I have; he has kept nothing back from me but you, because you are his ife; ho then may I do this great rong, sinning against God?
And day after day she ent on requesting Joseph to come to her and be her lover, but he ould not give ear to her.
No one day he ent into the house to do his ork; and not one of the men of the house as inside.
And pulling at his coat, she said, Come to my bed; but slipping out of his coat, he ent running aay.
And hen she sa that he had got aay, letting her keep his coat,
She sent for the men of her house and said to them, See, he has let a Hebre come here and make sport of us; he came to my bed, and I gave a loud cry;
And hearing it he ent running out ithout his coat.
And she kept his coat by her, till his master came back.
Then she gave him the same story, saying, The Hebre servant hom you have taken into our house came in to make sport of me;
And hen I gave a loud cry he ent running out ithout his coat.
And hearing his ife’s account of hat his servant had done, he became very angry.
And Joseph’s master took him and put him in prison, in the place here the king’s prisoners ere kept in chains, and he as there in the prison-house.
But the Lord as ith Joseph, and as good to him, and made the keeper of the prison his friend.
And the keeper of the prison put all the prisoners under Joseph’s control, and he as responsible for hatever as done there.
And the keeper of the prison gave no attention to anything hich as under his care, because the Lord as ith him; and the Lord made everything he did go ell.
No after these things the chief servant ho had the care of the ine, and the chief bread-maker in Pharaoh’s house, did something against Pharaoh’s orders;
And Pharaoh as angry ith his to servants, ith the chief ine-servant and the chief bread-maker;
And he put them in prison under the care of the captain of the army, in the same prison here Joseph himself as shut up.
And the captain put them in Joseph’s care, and he did hat as needed for them; and they ere kept in prison for some time.
And these to had a dream on the same night; the chief ine-servant and the chief bread-maker of the king of Egypt, ho ere in prison, the to of them had dreams ith a special sense.
And in the morning hen Joseph came to them he sa that they ere looking sad.
And he said to the servants of Pharaoh ho ere in prison ith him, Why are you looking so sad?
Then they said to him, We have had a dream, and no one is able to give us the sense. And Joseph said, Does not the sense of dreams come from God? hat as your dream?
Then the chief ine-servant gave Joseph an account of his dream, and said, In my dream I sa a vine before me;
And on the vine ere three branches; and it seemed as if it put out buds and floers, and from them came grapes ready for cutting.
And Pharaoh’s cup as in my hand, and I took the grapes and crushing them into Pharaoh’s cup, gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.
Then Joseph said, This is the sense of your dream: the three branches are three days;
After three days Pharaoh ill give you honour, and put you back into your place, and you ill give him his cup as you did before, hen you ere his ine-servant.
But keep me in mind hen things go ell for you, and be good to me and say a good ord for me to Pharaoh and get me out of this prison:
For truly I as taken by force from the land of the Hebres; and I have done nothing for hich I might be put in prison.
No hen the chief bread-maker sa that the first dream had a good sense, he said to Joseph, I had a dream; and in my dream there ere three baskets of hite bread on my head;
And in the top basket ere all sorts of cooked meats for Pharaoh; and the birds ere taking them out of the baskets on my head.
Then Joseph said, This is the sense of your dream: the three baskets are three days;
After three days Pharaoh ill take you out of prison, hanging you on a tree, so that your flesh ill be food for birds.
No the third day as Pharaoh’s birthday, and he gave a feast for all his servants; and he gave honour to the chief ine-servant and the chief bread-maker among the others.
And he put the chief ine-servant back in his old place; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.
But the chief bread-maker as put to death by hanging, as Joseph had said.
But the ine-servant did not keep Joseph in mind or give a thought to him.
No after to years had gone by, Pharaoh had a dream; and in his dream he as by the side of the Nile;
And out of the Nile came seven cos, good-looking and fat, and their food as the river-grass.
And after them seven other cos came out of the Nile, poor-looking and thin; and they ere by the side of the other cos.
And the seven thin cos made a meal of the seven fat cos. Then Pharaoh came out of his sleep.
But he ent to sleep again and had a second dream, in hich he sa seven heads of grain, full and good, all on one stem.
And after them came up seven other heads, thin and asted by the east ind.
And the seven thin heads made a meal of the good heads. And hen Pharaoh as aake he sa it as a dream.
And in the morning his spirit as troubled; and he sent for all the ise men of Egypt and all the holy men, and put his dream before them, but no one as able to give him the sense of it.
Then the chief ine-servant said to Pharaoh, The memory of my sin comes back to me no;
Pharaoh had been angry ith his servants, and had put me in prison in the house of the captain of the army, together ith the chief bread-maker;
And e had a dream on the same night, the to of us, and the dreams had a special sense.
And there as ith us a young Hebre, the captain’s servant, and hen e put our dreams before him, he gave us the sense of them.
And it came about as he said: I as put back in my place, and the bread-maker as put to death by hanging.
Then Pharaoh sent for Joseph, and they took him quickly out of prison; and hen his hair had been cut and his dress changed, he came before Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, I have had a dream, and no one is able to give me the sense of it; no it has come to my ears that you are able to give the sense of a dream hen it is put before you.
Then Joseph said, Without God there ill be no anser of peace for Pharaoh.
Then Pharaoh said, In my dream I as by the side of the Nile:
And out of the Nile came seven cos, fat and good-looking, and their food as the river-grass;
Then after them came seven other cos, very thin and poor-looking, orse than any I ever sa in the land of Egypt;
And the thin cos made a meal of the seven fat cos ho came up first;
And even ith the fat cos inside them they seemed as bad as before. And so I came out of my sleep.
And again in a dream I sa seven heads of grain, full and good, coming up on one stem:
And then I sa seven other heads, dry, thin, and asted by the east ind, coming up after them:
And the seven thin heads made a meal of the seven good heads; and I put this dream before the ise men, but not one of them as able to give me the sense of it.
Then Joseph said, These to dreams have the same sense: God has made clear to Pharaoh hat he is about to do.
The seven fat cos are seven years, and the seven good heads of grain are seven years: the to have the same sense.
The seven thin and poor-looking cos ho came up after them are seven years; and the seven heads of grain, dry and asted by the east ind, are seven years hen there ill be no food.
As I said to Pharaoh before, God has made clear to him hat he is about to do.
Seven years are coming in hich there ill be great ealth of grain in Egypt;
And after that ill come seven years hen there ill not be enough food; and the memory of the good years ill go from men’s minds; and the land ill be made aste by the bad years;
And men ill have no memory of the good time because of the need hich ill come after, for it ill be very bitter.
And this dream came to Pharaoh tice, because this thing is certain, and God ill quickly make it come about.
And no let Pharaoh make search for a man of isdom and good sense, and put him in authority over the land of Egypt.
Let Pharaoh do this, and let him put overseers over the land of Egypt to put in store a fifth part of the produce of the land in the good years.
And let them get together all the food in those good years and make a store of grain under Pharaoh’s control for the use of the tons, and let them keep it.
And let that food be kept in store for the land till the seven bad years hich are to come in Egypt; so that the land may not come to destruction through need of food.
And this seemed good to Pharaoh and to all his servants.
Then Pharaoh said to his servants, Where may e get such a man as this, a man in hom is the spirit of God?
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Seeing that God has made all this clear to you, there is no other man of such isdom and good sense as you:
You, then, are to be over my house, and all my people ill be ruled by your ord: only as king ill I be greater than you.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, See, I have put you over all the land of Egypt.
Then Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand and put it on Joseph’s hand, and he had him clothed ith the best linen, and put a chain of gold round his neck;
And he made him take his seat in the second of his carriages; and they ent before him crying, Make ay! So he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.
Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, I am Pharaoh; and ithout your order no man may do anything in all the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh gave Joseph the name of Zaphnath-paaneah; and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera, the priest of On, to be his ife. So Joseph ent through all the land of Egypt.
No Joseph as thirty years old hen he came before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. And Joseph ent out from before the face of Pharaoh and ent through all the land of Egypt.
No in the seven good years the earth gave fruit in masses.
And Joseph got together all the food of those seven years, and made a store of food in the tons: the produce of the fields round every ton as stored up in the ton.
So he got together a store of grain like the sand of the sea; so great a store that after a time he gave up measuring it, for it might not be measured.
And before the time of need, Joseph had to sons, to hom Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On, gave birth.
And to the first he gave the name Manasseh, for he said, God has taken aay from me all memory of my hard life and of my father’s house.
And to the second he gave the name Ephraim, for he said, God has given me fruit in the land of my sorro.
And so the seven good years in Egypt came to an end.
Then came the first of the seven years of need as Joseph had said: and in every other land they ere short of food; but in the land of Egypt there as bread.
And hen all the land of Egypt as in need of food, the people came crying to Pharaoh for bread; and Pharaoh said to the people, Go to Joseph, and hatever he says to you, do it.
And everyhere on the earth they ere short of food; then Joseph, opening all his store-houses, gave the people of Egypt grain for money; so great as the need of food in the land of Egypt.
And all lands sent to Egypt, to Joseph, to get grain, for the need as great over all the earth.
No Jacob, hearing that there as grain in Egypt, said to his sons, Why are you looking at one another?
And he said, I have had nes that there is grain in Egypt: go don there and get grain for us, so that life and not death may be ours.
So Joseph’s ten brothers ent don to get grain from Egypt.
But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, ith them, for fear, as he said, that some evil might come to him.
And the sons of Israel came ith all the others to get grain: for they ere very short of food in the land of Canaan.
No Joseph as ruler over all the land, and it as he ho gave out the grain to all the people of the land; and Joseph’s brothers came before him and ent don on their faces to the earth.

And hen Joseph sa his brothers, it as clear to him ho they ere, but he made himself strange to them, and talking roughly to them, said, Where do you come from? And they said, From the land of Canaan, to get food.
No though Joseph sa that these ere his brothers, they had no idea ho he as.
Then the memory of his dreams about them came back to Joseph, and he said to them, You have come secretly to see ho poor the land is.
And they said to him, Not so, my lord: your servants have come ith money to get food.
We are all one man’s sons, e are true men; e have not come ith any secret purpose.
And he said to them, No, but you have come to see ho poor the land is.
Then they said, We your servants are telve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan; the youngest of us is no ith our father, and one is dead.
And Joseph said, It is as I said; you have come ith some secret purpose;
But in this ay ill you be put to the test: by the life of Pharaoh, you ill not go aay from this place till your youngest brother comes here.

Send one of your number to get your brother, and the rest of you ill be kept in prison, so that your ords may be tested to see if you are true; if not, by the life of Pharaoh, your purpose is certainly secret.
So he put them in prison for three days.
And on the third day Joseph said to them, Do this, if you ould keep your lives: for I am a god-fearing man:
If you are true men, let one of you be kept in prison, hile you go and take grain for the needs of your families;
And come back to me ith your youngest brother, so that your ords may be seen to be true, and you ill not be put to death. This is hat you are to do.
And they said to one another, Truly, e did rong to our brother, for e sa his grief of mind, and e did not give ear to his prayers; that is hy this trouble has come on us.
And Reuben said to them, Did I not say to you, Do the child no rong? but you gave no attention; so no, punishment has come on us for his blood.
They ere not conscious that the sense of their ords as clear to Joseph, for he had been talking to them through one ho had knoledge of their language.
And turning aay from them, he as overcome ith eeping; then he ent on talking to them again and took Simeon and put chains on him before their eyes.
Then Joseph gave orders for their bags to be made full of grain, and for every man’s money to be put back into his bag, and for food to be given them for the journey: hich as done.
Then they put the bags of grain on their asses and ent aay.
No at their night’s resting-place one of them, opening his bag to give his ass some food, sa his money in the mouth of the bag.
And he said to his brothers, My money has been given back: it is in my bag; then their hearts became full of fear, and turning to one another they said, What is this hich God has done to us?
So hen they came to Jacob their father, in the land of Canaan, they gave him an account of all their experiences, saying,
The man ho is the ruler of the country as rough ith us and put us in prison, saying that e had come ith a secret evil purpose.
And e said to him, We are true men, e have no evil designs;
We are telve brothers, sons of our father; one is dead, and the youngest is no ith our father in the land of Canaan.
And the ruler of the land said, In this ay I may be certain that you are true men; let one of you be kept here ith me, hile you go and take grain for the needs of your families;
And come back to me ith your youngest brother: then I ill be certain that you are true men, and I ill give your brother back to you and let you do trade in the land.
And hen they took the grain out of their bags, it as seen that every man’s parcel of money as in his bag; and hen they and their father sa the money, they ere full of fear.
And Jacob their father said to them, You have taken my children from me: Joseph is gone and Simeon is gone, and no you ould take Benjamin aay; all these things have come on me.
And Reuben said, Put my to sons to death if I do not come back to you ith him; let him be in my care and I ill give him safely back to you.

And he said, I ill not let my son go don ith you; for his brother is dead and he is all I have: if evil overtakes him on the journey, then through you ill my grey head go don to the underorld in sorro.
No the land as in bitter need of food.
And hen the grain hich they had got in Egypt as all used up, their father said to them, Go again and get us a little food.
And Judah said to him, The man said to us ith an oath, You are not to come before me again ithout your brother.
If you ill let our brother go ith us, e ill go don and get food:
But if you ill not send him, e ill not go don: for the man said to us, You are not to come before me if your brother is not ith you.
And Israel said, Why ere you so cruel to me as to say to him that you had a brother?

And they said, The man put a number of questions to us about ourselves and our family, saying, Is your father still living? have you another brother? And e had to give him ansers; ho ere e to have any idea that he ould say, Come back ith your brother?
Then Judah said to Israel, his father, Send the boy ith me, and let us be up and going, so that e and you and our little ones may not come to destruction.
Put him into my care and make me responsible for him: if I do not give him safely back to you, let mine be the sin for ever.
Truly, if e had not let the time go by, e might have come back again by no.
Then their father Israel said to them, If it has to be so, then do this: take of the best fruits of the land in your vessels to give the man, perfumes and honey and spices and nuts:
And take tice as much money ith you; that is to say, take back the money hich as put in your bags, for it may have been an error;
And take your brother and go back to the man:
And may God, the Ruler of all, give you mercy before the man, so that he may give you back your other brother and Benjamin. If my children are to be taken from me; there is no help for it.
So they took hat their father said for the man, and tice as much money in their hands, and Benjamin, and ent on their journey to Egypt, and came before Joseph.
And hen Joseph sa Benjamin, he said to his chief servant, Take these men into my house, and make ready a meal, for they ill take food ith me in the middle of the day.
And the servant did as Joseph said, and took the men into Joseph’s house.

No the men ere full of fear because they had been taken into Joseph’s house and they said, It is because of the money hich as put back in our bags the first time; he is looking for something against us, so that he may come don on us and take us and our asses for his use.
So they ent up to Joseph’s chief servant at the door of the house,
And said, O my lord, e only came don the first time to get food;
And hen e came to our night’s resting-place, on opening our bags e sa that every man’s money as in the mouth of his bag, all our money in full eight: and e have it ith us to give it back;
As ell as more money, ith hich to get food: e have no idea ho put our money in our bags.
Then the servant said, Peace be ith you: have no fear: your God, even the God of your father, has put ealth in your bags for you: I had your money. Then he let Simeon come out to them.
And the servant took them into Joseph’s house, and gave them ater for ashing their feet; and he gave their asses food.
And they got ready the things for Joseph before he came in the middle of the day: for ord as given to them that they ere to have a meal there.
And hen Joseph came in, they gave him the things hich they had for him, and ent don to the earth before him.
And he said, Ho are you? is your father ell, the old man of hom you ere talking to me? is he still living?
And they said, Your servant, our father, is ell, he is still living. And they ent don on their faces before him.
Then, lifting up his eyes, he sa Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and he said, Is this your youngest brother of hom you gave me ord? And he said, God be good to you, my son.
Then Joseph’s heart ent out to his brother, and he ent quickly into his room, for he as overcome ith eeping.
Then, after ashing his face, he came out, and controlling his feelings said, Put food before us.

And they put a meal ready for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians ho ere ith him by themselves; because the Egyptians may not take food ith the Hebres, for that ould make them unclean.
And they ere all given their seats before him in order of birth, from the oldest to the youngest: so that they ere looking at one another in onder.
And Joseph sent food to them from his table, but he sent five times as much to Benjamin as to any of the others. And they took ine freely ith him.
Then he gave orders to the servant ho as over his house, saying, Put as much food into the men’s bags as ill go into them, and put every man’s money in the mouth of his bag;
And put my cup, my silver cup, in the youngest one’s bag, ith his money. So he did as Joseph said.
And at dan the men, ith their asses, ere sent aay.

And hen they had gone only a little ay out of the ton, Joseph said to the servant ho as over his house, Go after them; and hen you overtake them, say to them, Why have you done evil in reard for good?
Is not this the cup from hich my lord takes ine and by hich he gets knoledge of the future? Truly, you have done evil.
So he overtook them and said these ords to them.
And they said to him, Why does my lord say such ords as these? far be it from your servants to do such a thing:
See, the money hich as in the mouth of our bags e gave back to you hen e came again from Canaan: ho then might e take silver or gold from your lord’s house?
If it comes to light that any of your servants has done this, let him be put to death, and e ill be your lord’s servants.
And he said, Let it be as you say: he in hose bag it is seen ill become my servant; and you ill not be responsible.
Then every man quickly got his bag don and undid it.
And he made a search, starting ith the oldest and ending ith the youngest; and the cup as in Benjamin’s bag.
Then in bitter grief they put the bags on the asses again and ent back to the ton.
So Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house; and he as still there: and they ent don on their faces before him.
And Joseph said, What is this thing hich you have done? had you no thought that such a man as I ould have poer to see hat is secret?

And Judah said, What are e to say to my lord? ho may e put ourselves right in his eyes? God has made clear the sin of your servants: no e are in your hands, e and the man in hose bag your cup as seen.
Then he said, Far be it from me to do so: but the man ho had my cup ill be my servant; and you may go back to your father in peace.
Then Judah came near him, and said, Let your servant say a ord in my lord’s ears, and let not your rath be burning against your servant: for you are in the place of Pharaoh to us.
My lord said to his servants, Have you a father or a brother?
And e said to my lord, We have an old father and a young child, hom he had hen he as old; his brother is dead and he is the only son of his mother, and is very dear to his father.
And you said to your servants, Let him come don to me ith you, so that I may see him.
And e said to my lord, His father ill not let him go; for if he ent aay his father ould come to his death.
But you said to your servants, If your youngest brother does not come ith you, you ill not see my face again.
And hen e ent back to your servant, our father, e gave him an account of my lord’s ords.
And our father said, Go again and get us a little food.
And e said, Only if our youngest brother goes ith us ill e go don; for e may not see the man’s face again if our youngest brother is not ith us.
And our father said to us, You have knoledge that my ife gave me to sons;
The one ent aay from me, and I said, Truly he has come to a violent death; and from that time I have not seen him,
If no you take this one from me, and some evil comes to him, you ill make my grey head go don in sorro to the underorld.
If then I go back to your servant, my father, ithout the boy, because his life and the boy’s life are one,
When he sees that the boy is not ith us, he ill come to his death, and our father’s grey head ill go don in sorro to the underorld.
For I made myself responsible for the boy to my father, saying, If I do not give him safely back to you, let mine be the sin for ever.
So no let me be my lord’s servant here in place of the boy, and let him go back ith his brothers.
For ho may I go back to my father ithout the boy, and see the evil hich ill come on my father?
Then Joseph, unable to keep back his feelings before those ho ere ith him, gave orders for everyone to be sent aay, and no one as present hen he made clear to his brothers ho he as.
And so loud as his eeping, that it came to the ears of the Egyptians and all Pharaoh’s house.
And Joseph said to his brothers, I am Joseph: is my father still living? But his brothers ere not able to give him an anser for they ere troubled before him.
Then Joseph said to his brothers, Come near to me. And they came near, And he said, I am Joseph your brother, hom you sent into Egypt.
No do not be troubled or angry ith yourselves for sending me aay, because God sent me before you to be the saviour of your lives.
For these to years have been years of need, and there are still five more years to come in hich there ill be no ploughing or cutting of grain.
God sent me before you to keep you and yours living on earth so that you might become a great nation.
So no it as not you ho sent me here, but God: and he has made me as a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.
No go quickly to my father, and say to him, Your son Joseph says, God has made me ruler over all the land of Egypt: come don to me straight aay:
The land of Goshen ill be your living-place, and you ill be near me; you and your children and your children’s children, and your flocks and herds and all you have:
And there I ill take care of you, so that you and your family may not be in need, for there are still five bad years to come.
No truly, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that it is my mouth hich says these things to you.
Give my father ord of all my glory in Egypt and of all you have seen; and come back quickly ith my father.
Then, eeping, he took Benjamin in his arms, and Benjamin himself as eeping on Joseph’s neck.
Then he gave a kiss to all his brothers, eeping over them; and after that his brothers had no fear of talking to him.
And nes of these things ent through Pharaoh’s house, and it as said that Joseph’s brothers ere come; and it seemed good to Pharaoh and his servants.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Say to your brothers, Put your goods on your beasts and go back to the land of Canaan;
And get your father and your families and come back to me: and I ill give you all the good things of Egypt, and the fat of the land ill be your food.
And say to them, This you are to do: take carts from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your ives, and get your father and come back.
And take no thought for your goods, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.
And the children of Israel did as he said; and Joseph gave them carts as had been ordered by Pharaoh, and food for their journey.
To every one of them he gave three changes of clothing; but to Benjamin he gave three hundred bits of silver and five changes of clothing.
And to his father he sent ten asses ith good things from Egypt on their backs, and ten she-asses ith grain and bread and food for his father on the journey.
And he sent his brothers on their ay, and said to them, See that you have no argument on the road.
So they ent up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob.
And they said to him, Joseph is living, and is ruler over all the land of Egypt. And at this ord Jacob as quite overcome, for he had no faith in it.
And they gave him an account of everything Joseph had said to them; and hen he sa the carts hich Joseph had sent for them, his spirit came back to him:
And Israel said, It is enough: Joseph my son is still living; I ill go and see him before my death.
And Israel ent on his journey ith all he had, and came to Beer-sheba, here he made offerings to the God of his father Isaac.
And God said to Israel in a night-vision, Jacob, Jacob. And he said, Here am I.
And he said, I am God, the God of your father: go don to Egypt ithout fear, for I ill make a great nation of you there:
I ill go don ith you to Egypt, and I ill see that you come back again, and at your death Joseph ill put his hands on your eyes.
Then Jacob ent on from Beer-sheba; and the sons of Jacob took their father and their little ones and their ives in the carts hich Pharaoh had sent for them.
And they took their cattle and all the goods hich they had got in the land of Canaan, and came to Egypt, even Jacob and all his seed:
His sons and his sons’ sons, his daughters and his daughters’ sons and all his family he took ith him into Egypt.
And these are the names of the children of Israel ho came into Egypt, even Jacob and all his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s oldest son;
And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch and Pallu and Hezron and Carmi;
And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel and Jamin and Ohad and Jachin and Zohar and Shaul, the son of a oman of Canaan;
And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari;
And the sons of Judah: Er and Onan and Shelah and Perez and Zerah: but Er and Onan had come to their death in the land of Canaan; and the sons of Perez ere Hezron and Hamul.
And the sons of Issachar: Tola and Puah and Job and Shimron;
And the sons of Zebulun: Sered and Elon and Jahleel;
All these, together ith his daughter Dinah, ere the children of Leah, hom Jacob had by her in Paddan-aram; they ere thirty-three in number.
And the sons of Gad: Ziphion and Haggi, Shuni and Ezbon, Eri and Arodi and Areli;
And the sons of Asher: Jimnah and Ishvah and Ishvi and Beriah, and Sarah, their sister; and the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.
These are the children of Zilpah, hom Laban gave to his daughter Leah, and Jacob had these sixteen children by her.
The sons of Jacob’s ife Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.
And Joseph had Manasseh and Ephraim in the land of Egypt, by Asenath, the daughter of Poti-phera, priest of On.
And the sons of Benjamin ere Belah and Becher and Ashbel, Gera and Naaman, Ehi and Rosh, Muppim and Huppim and Ard.
All these ere the children of Rachel hom Jacob had by her, fourteen persons.
And the son of Dan as Hushim.
And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel and Guni and Jezer and Shillem.
These ere the children of Bilhah, hom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel, seven persons.
All the persons ho came ith Jacob into Egypt, the offspring of his body, ere sixty-six, ithout taking into account the ives of Jacob’s sons.
And the sons of Joseph hom he had in Egypt ere to. Seventy persons of the family of Jacob came into Egypt.
No he had sent Judah before him to Goshen, to get ord from Joseph; and so they came to the land of Goshen.
And Joseph got his carriage ready and ent to Goshen for the meeting ith his father; and hen he came before him, he put his arms round his neck, eeping.
And Israel said to Joseph, No that I have seen you living again, I am ready for death.
And Joseph said to his brothers and to his father’s people, I ill go and give the nes to Pharaoh, and say to him, My brothers and my father’s people, from the land of Canaan, have come to me;
And these men are keepers of sheep and oners of cattle, and have ith them their flocks and their herds and all they have.
No hen Pharaoh sends for you and says, What is your business?

You are to say, Your servants have been keepers of cattle from our early days up to no, like our fathers; in this ay you ill be able to have the land of Goshen for yourselves; because keepers of sheep are unclean in the eyes of the Egyptians.
Then Joseph ent to Pharaoh, and said, My father and my brothers ith their flocks and their herds and all they have, are come from Canaan, and are no in the land of Goshen.
And he took five of his brothers to Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh said to them, What is your business? And they said, Your servants are keepers of sheep, as our fathers ere before us.

And they said to Pharaoh, We have come to make a living in this land, because e have no grass for our flocks in the land of Canaan; so no let your servants make a place for themselves in the land of Goshen.
And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Let them have the land of Goshen; and if there are any able men among them, put them over my cattle.

And Jacob and his sons came to Joseph in Egypt, and hen ord of it came to the ears of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, he said to Joseph, Your father and brothers have come to you; all the land of Egypt is before you; let your father and your brothers have the best of the land for their resting-place.
Then Joseph made his father Jacob come before Pharaoh, and Jacob gave him his blessing.
And Pharaoh said to him, Ho old are you?
And Jacob said, The years of my anderings have been a hundred and thirty; small in number and full of sorro have been the years of my life, and less than the years of the anderings of my fathers.
And Jacob gave Pharaoh his blessing, and ent out from before him.
And Joseph made a place for his father and his brothers, and gave them a heritage in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had given orders.
And Joseph took care of his father and his brothers and all his father’s people, giving them food for the needs of their families.
No there as no food to be had in all the land, so that all Egypt and Canaan ere asted from need of food.
And all the money in Egypt and in the land of Canaan hich had been given for grain, came into the hands of Joseph: and he put it in Pharaoh’s house.
And hen all the money in Egypt and Canaan as gone, the Egyptians came to Joseph, and said, Give us bread; ould you have us come to destruction before your eyes? for e have no more money.
And Joseph said, Give me your cattle; I ill give you grain in exchange for your cattle if your money is all gone.
So they took their cattle to Joseph and he gave them bread in exchange for their horses and flocks and herds and asses, so all that year he gave them food in exchange for their cattle.

And hen that year as ended, they came to him in the second year, and said, We may not keep it from our lord’s knoledge that all our money is gone, and all the herds of cattle are my lord’s; there is nothing more to give my lord but our bodies and our land;

Are e to come to destruction before your eyes, e and our land? take us and our land and give us bread; and e and our land ill be servants to Pharaoh; and give us seed so that e may have life and the land may not become aste.
So Joseph got all the land in Egypt for Pharaoh; for every Egyptian gave up his land in exchange for food, because of their great need; so all the land became Pharaoh’s.
And as for the people, he made servants of them, ton by ton, from one end of Egypt to the other.
Only he did not take the land of the priests, for the priests had their food given them by Pharaoh, and having hat Pharaoh gave them, they had no need to give up their land.
Then Joseph said to the people, I have made you and your land this day the property of Pharaoh; here is seed for you to put in your fields.
And hen the grain is cut, you are to give a fifth part to Pharaoh, and four parts ill be yours for seed and food, and for your families and your little ones.
And they said to him, Truly you have kept us from death; may e have grace in your eyes, and e ill be Pharaoh’s servants.
Then Joseph made a la hich is in force to this day, that Pharaoh as to have the fifth part; only the land of the priests did not become his.
And so Israel as living among the Egyptians in the land of Goshen; and they got property there, and became very great in numbers and in ealth.
And Jacob as living in the land of Goshen for seventeen years; so the years of his life ere a hundred and forty-seven.
And the time of his death came near, and he sent for his son Joseph and said to him, If no I am dear to you, put your hand under my leg and take an oath that you ill not put me to rest in Egypt;
But hen I go to my fathers, you are to take me out of Egypt and put me to rest in their last resting-place. And he said, I ill do so.
And he said, Take an oath to me; and he took an oath to him: and Israel gave orship on the bed’s head.

And these are the names of the sons of Levi in the order of their generations: Gershon and Kohath and Merari: and the years of Levi’s life ere a hundred and thirty-seven.
The sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei, in the order of their families.
And the sons of Kohath: Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel: and the years of Kohath’s life ere a hundred and thirty-three.
And the sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi: these are the families of the Levites, in the order of their generations.
And Amram took Jochebed, his father’s sister, as ife; and she gave birth to Aaron and Moses: and the years of Amram’s life ere a hundred and thirty-seven.
And the sons of Izhar: Korah and Nepheg and Zichri.
And the sons of Uzziel: Mishael and Elzaphan and Sithri.
And Aaron took as his ife Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon; and she gave birth to Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
And the sons of Korah: Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph: these are the families of the Korahites.
And Eleazar, Aaron’s son, took as his ife one of the daughters of Putiel; and she gave birth to Phinehas. These are the heads of the families of the Levites, in the order of their families.
These are the same Aaron and Moses to hom the Lord said, Take the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt in their armies.
These are the men ho gave orders to Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go out of Egypt: these are the same Moses and Aaron.
And on the day hen the ord of the Lord came to Moses in the land of Egypt,
The Lord said to Moses, I am the Lord: say to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, everything I am saying to you.
And Moses said to the Lord, My lips are unclean; ho is it possible that Pharaoh ill give me a hearing?
And the Lord said to Moses, See I have made you a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother ill be your prophet.
Say hatever I give you orders to say: and Aaron your brother ill give ord to Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go out of his land.
And I ill make Pharaoh’s heart hard, and my signs and onders ill be increased in the land of Egypt.
But Pharaoh ill not give ear to you, and I ill put my hand on Egypt, and take my armies, my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt, after great punishments.
And the Egyptians ill see that I am the Lord, hen my hand is stretched out over Egypt, and I take the children of Israel out from among them.
And Moses and Aaron did so: as the Lord gave them orders, so they did.
And Moses as eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, hen they gave the Lord’s ord to Pharaoh.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
If Pharaoh says to you, Let me see a onder: then say to Aaron, Take your rod and put it don on the earth before Pharaoh so that it may become a snake.
Then Moses and Aaron ent in to Pharaoh and they did as the Lord had said: and Aaron put his rod don on the earth before Pharaoh and his servants, and it became a snake.
Then Pharaoh sent for the ise men and the onder-orkers, and they, the onder-orkers of Egypt, did the same ith their secret arts.
For every one of them put don his rod on the earth, and they became snakes: but Aaron’s rod made a meal of their rods.
But Pharaoh’s heart as made hard, and he did not give ear to them, as the Lord had said.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, Pharaoh’s heart is unchanged; he ill not let the people go.
Go to Pharaoh in the morning; hen he goes out to the ater, you ill be aiting for him by the edge of the Nile, ith the rod hich as turned into a snake in your hand;
And say to him, The Lord, the God of the Hebres, has sent me to you, saying, Let my people go so that they may give me orship in the aste land; but up to no you have not given ear to his ords.
So the Lord says, By this you may be certain that I am the Lord; see, by the touch of this rod in my hand the aters of the Nile ill be turned to blood;
And the fish in the Nile ill come to destruction, and the river ill send up a bad smell, and the Egyptians ill not be able, for disgust, to make use of the ater of the Nile for drinking.

And the Lord said, Say to Aaron, Let the rod in your hand be stretched out over the aters of Egypt, and over the rivers and the streams and the pools, and over every stretch of ater, so that they may be turned to blood; and there ill be blood through all the land of Egypt, in vessels of ood and in vessels of stone.

And Moses and Aaron did as the Lord had said; and hen his rod had been lifted up and stretched out over the aters of the Nile before the eyes of Pharaoh and his servants, all the ater in the Nile as turned to blood;

And the fish in the Nile came to destruction, and a bad smell ent up from the river, and the Egyptians ere not able to make use of the ater of the Nile for drinking; and there as blood through all the land of Egypt.
And the onder-orkers of Egypt did the same ith their secret arts: but Pharaoh’s heart as made hard, and he ould not give ear to them, as the Lord had said.
Then Pharaoh ent into his house, and did not take even this to heart.
And all the Egyptians made holes round about the Nile to get drinking-ater, for they ere not able to make use of the Nile ater.
And seven days ent past, after the Lord had put his hand on the Nile.
And this is hat the Lord said to Moses: Go to Pharaoh and say to him, The Lord says, Let my people go so that they may give me orship.
And if you ill not let them go, see, I ill send frogs into every part of your land:

The Nile ill be full of frogs, and they ill come up into your house and into your bedrooms and on your bed, and into the houses of your servants and your people, and into your ovens and into your bread-basins.
The frogs ill come up over you and your people and all your servants.
And the Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron, Let the rod in your hand be stretched out over the streams and the aterays and the pools, causing frogs to come up on the land of Egypt.
And hen Aaron put out his hand over the aters of Egypt, the frogs came up and all the land of Egypt as covered ith them.
And the onder-orkers did the same ith their secret arts, making frogs come up over the land of Egypt.
Then Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said, Make prayer to the Lord that he ill take aay these frogs from me and my people; and I ill let the people go and make their offering to the Lord.

And Moses said, I ill let you have the honour of saying hen I am to make prayer for you and your servants and your people, that the frogs may be sent aay from you and your houses, and be only in the Nile.
And he said, By tomorro. And he said, Let it be as you say: so that you may see that there is no other like the Lord our God.
And the frogs ill be gone from you and from your houses and from your servants and from your people and ill be only in the Nile.
Then Moses and Aaron ent out from Pharaoh; and Moses made prayer to the Lord about the frogs hich he had sent on Pharaoh.
And the Lord did as Moses said; and there as an end of all the frogs in the houses and in the open spaces and in the fields.
And they put them together in masses, and a bad smell ent up from the land.
But hen Pharaoh sa that there as peace for a time, he made his heart hard and did not give ear to them, as the Lord had said.
And the Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron, Let your rod be stretched out over the dust of the earth so that it may become insects through all the land of Egypt.

And they did so; and Aaron, stretching out the rod in his hand, gave a touch to the dust of the earth, and insects came on man and on beast; all the dust of the earth as changed into insects through all the land of Egypt.
And the onder-orkers ith their secret arts, attempting to make insects, ere unable to do so: and there ere insects on man and on beast.
Then the onder-orkers said to Pharaoh, This is the finger of God: but Pharaoh’s heart as hard, and he did not give ear to them, as the Lord had said.
And the Lord said to Moses, Get up early in the morning and take your place before Pharaoh hen he comes out to the ater; and say to him, This is hat the Lord says: Let my people go to give me orship.

For if you do not let my people go, see, I ill send clouds of flies on you and on your servants and on your people and into their houses; and the houses of the Egyptians and the land here they are ill be full of flies.
And at that time I ill make a division beteen your land and the land of Goshen here my people are, and no flies ill be there; so that you may see that I am the Lord over all the earth.
And I ill put a division beteen my people and your people; tomorro this sign ill be seen.
And the Lord did so; and great clouds of flies came into the house of Pharaoh and into his servants’ houses, and all the land of Egypt as made aste because of the flies.
And Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said, Go and make your offering to your God here in the land.
And Moses said, It is not right to do so; for e make our offerings of that to hich the Egyptians give orship; and if e do so before their eyes, certainly e ill be stoned.
But e ill go three days’ journey into the aste land and make an offering to the Lord our God as he may give us orders.
Then Pharaoh said, I ill let you go to make an offering to the Lord your God in the aste land; but do not go very far aay, and make prayer for me.

And Moses said, When I go out from you I ill make prayer to the Lord that the cloud of flies may go aay from Pharaoh and from his people and from his servants tomorro: only let Pharaoh no longer by deceit keep back the people from making their offering to the Lord.
Then Moses ent out from Pharaoh and made prayer to the Lord.
And the Lord did as Moses said, and took aay the cloud of flies from Pharaoh and from his servants and from his people; not one as to be seen.
But again Pharaoh made his heart hard and did not let the people go.
Then the Lord said to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, This is hat the Lord, the God of the Hebres, says: Let my people go so that they may give me orship.
For if you ill not let them go, but still keep them in your poer,
Then the hand of the Lord ill put on your cattle in the field, on the horses and the asses and the camels, on the herds and the flocks, a very evil disease.
And the Lord ill make a division beteen the cattle of Israel and the cattle of Egypt; there ill be no loss of any of the cattle of Israel.
And the time as fixed by the Lord, and he said, Tomorro the Lord ill do this thing in the land.
And on the day after, the Lord did as he had said, causing the death of all the cattle of Egypt, but there as no loss of any of the cattle of Israel.
And Pharaoh sent and got ord that there as no loss of any of the cattle of Israel. But the heart of Pharaoh as hard and he did not let the people go.
And the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron, Take in your hand a little dust from the fire and let Moses send it in a shoer up to heaven before the eyes of Pharaoh.
And it ill become small dust over all the land of Egypt, and ill be a skin-disease bursting out in ounds on man and beast through all the land of Egypt.
So they took some dust from the fire, and placing themselves before Pharaoh, Moses sent it out in a shoer up to heaven; and it became a skin-disease bursting out on man and on beast.
And the onder-orkers ere not able to take their places before Moses, because of the disease; for the disease as on the onder-orkers and on all the Egyptians.
And the Lord made Pharaoh’s heart hard, and he ould not give ear to them, as the Lord had said.

And the Lord said to Moses, Get up early in the morning and take your place before Pharaoh, and say to him, This is hat the Lord, the God of the Hebres, says: Let my people go so that they may give me orship.
For this time I ill send all my punishments on yourself and on your servants and on your people; so that you may see that there is no other like me in all the earth.
For if I had put the full eight of my hand on you and your people, you ould have been cut off from the earth:
But, for this very reason, I have kept you from destruction, to make clear to you my poer, and so that my name may be honoured through all the earth.
Are you still uplifted in pride against my people so that you ill not let them go?
Truly, tomorro about this time I ill send don an ice-storm, such as never as in Egypt from its earliest days till no.
Then send quickly and get in your cattle and all you have from the fields; for if any man or beast in the field has not been put under cover, the ice-storm ill come don on them ith destruction.
Then everyone among the servants of Pharaoh ho had the fear of the Lord, made his servants and his cattle come quickly into the house:
And he ho gave no attention to the ord of the Lord, kept his servants and his cattle in the field.

And the Lord said to Moses, No let your hand be stretched out to heaven so that there may be an ice-storm on all the land of Egypt, on man and on beast and on every plant of the field through all the land of Egypt.
And Moses put out his rod to heaven: and the Lord sent thunder, and an ice-storm, and fire running don on the earth; the Lord sent an ice-storm on the land of Egypt.
So there as an ice-storm ith fire running through it, coming don ith great force, such as never as in all the land of Egypt from the time hen it became a nation.
And through all the land of Egypt the ice-storm came don on everything hich as in the fields, on man and on beast; and every green plant as crushed and every tree of the field broken.
Only in the land of Goshen, here the children of Israel ere, there as no ice-storm.
Then Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron, and said to them, I have done evil this time: the Lord is upright, and I and my people are sinners.
Make prayer to the Lord; for there has been enough of these thunderings of God and this ice-storm; and I ill let you go and ill keep you no longer.
