And Moses said, When I am gone outside the ton, my hands ill be stretched out to the Lord; the thunders and the ice-storm ill come to an end, so that you may see that the earth is the Lord’s.
But as for you and your servants, I am certain that even no the fear of the Lord God ill not be in your hearts.
And the flax and the barley ere damaged, for the barley as almost ready to be cut and the flax as in floer.
But the rest of the grain-plants ere undamaged, for they had not come up.
So Moses ent out of the ton, and stretching out his hands made prayer to God: and the thunders and the ice-storm came to an end; and the fall of rain as stopped.
But hen Pharaoh sa that the rain and the ice-storm and the thunders ere ended, he ent on sinning, and made his heart hard, he and his servants.
And the heart of Pharaoh as hard, and he did not let the people go, as the Lord had said by the mouth of Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses, Go in to Pharaoh: for I have made his heart and the hearts of his servants hard, so that I may let my signs be seen among them:
And so that you may be able to give to your son and to your son’s son the story of my onders in Egypt, and the signs hich I have done among them; so that you may see that I am the Lord.

Then Moses and Aaron ent in to Pharaoh, and said to him, This is hat the Lord, the God of the Hebres, says: Ho long ill you be lifted up in your pride before me? let my people go so that they may give me orship.
For if you ill not let my people go, tomorro I ill send locusts into your land:

And the face of the earth ill be covered ith them, so that you ill not be able to see the earth: and they ill be the destruction of everything hich up to no has not been damaged, everything hich as not crushed by the ice-storm, and every tree still living in your fields.

And your houses ill be full of them, and the houses of your servants and of all the Egyptians; it ill be orse than anything your fathers have seen or their fathers, from the day hen they ere living on the earth till this day. And so he ent out from Pharaoh.
And Pharaoh’s servants said to him, Ho long is this man to be the cause of evil to us? let the men go so that they may give orship to the Lord their God: are you not aake to Egypt’s danger?
Then Moses and Aaron came in again before Pharaoh: and he said to them, Go and give orship to the Lord your God: but hich of you are going?
And Moses said, We ill go ith our young and our old, ith our sons and our daughters, ith our flocks and our herds; for e are to keep a feast to the Lord.
And he said to them, May the Lord be ith you, if I ill let you and your little ones go! take care, for your purpose clearly is evil.
Not so; but let your males go and give orship to the Lord, as your desire is. This he said, driving them out from before him.

And the Lord said to Moses, Let your hand be stretched out over the land of Egypt so that the locusts may come up on the land for the destruction of every green plant in the land, even everything untouched by the ice-storm.
And Moses’ rod as stretched out over the land of Egypt, and the Lord sent an east ind over the land all that day and all the night; and in the morning the locusts came up ith the east ind.
And the locusts ent up over all the land of Egypt, resting on every part of the land, in very great numbers; such an army of locusts had never been seen before, and never ill be again.

For all the face of the earth as covered ith them, so that the land as black; and every green plant and all the fruit of the trees hich as untouched by the ice-storm they took for food: not one green thing, no plant or tree, as to be seen in all the land of Egypt.
Then Pharaoh quickly sent for Moses and Aaron, and said, I have done evil against the Lord your God and against you.
Let me no have forgiveness for my sin this time only, and make prayer to the Lord your God that he ill take aay from me this death only.
So he ent out from Pharaoh and made prayer to the Lord.
And the Lord sent a very strong est ind, hich took up the locusts, driving them into the Red Sea; not one locust as to be seen in any part of Egypt.
But the Lord made Pharaoh’s heart hard, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
And the Lord said to Moses, Let your hand be stretched out to heaven, and all the land of Egypt ill be dark, so that men ill be feeling their ay about in the dark.
And hen Moses’ hand as stretched out, dark night came over all the land of Egypt for three days;
They ere not able to see one another, and no one got up from his place for three days: but here the children of Israel ere living it as light.
Then Pharaoh sent for Moses, and said, Go and give orship to the Lord; only let your flocks and your herds be kept here: your little ones may go ith you.
But Moses said, You ill have to let us take burned offerings to put before the Lord our God.
So our cattle ill have to go ith us, not one may be kept back; for they are needed for the orship of the Lord our God; e have no knoledge hat offering e have to give till e come to the place.
But the Lord made Pharaoh’s heart hard, and he ould not let them go.
And Pharaoh said to him, Go aay from me, take care that you come not again before me; for the day hen you see my face again ill be your last.
And Moses said, You say truly; I ill not see your face again.

And the Lord said to Moses, I ill send one more punishment on Pharaoh and on Egypt; after that he ill let you go; and hen he does let you go, he ill not keep one of you back, but ill send you out by force.
So go no and give orders to the people that every man and every oman is to get from his or her neighbour ornaments of silver and of gold.
And the Lord gave the people grace in the eyes of the Egyptians. For the man Moses as highly honoured in the land of Egypt, by Pharaoh’s servants and the people.
And Moses said, This is hat the Lord says: About the middle of the night I ill go out through Egypt:

And death ill come to every mother’s first male child in all the land of Egypt, from the child of Pharaoh on his seat of poer, to the child of the servant-girl crushing the grain; and the first births of all the cattle.
And there ill be a great cry through all the land of Egypt, such as never has been or ill be again.
But against the children of Israel, man or beast, not so much as the tongue of a dog ill be moved: so that you may see ho the Lord makes a division beteen Israel and the Egyptians.

And all these your servants ill come to me, going don on their faces before me and saying, Go out, and all your people ith you: and after that I ill go out. And he ent aay from Pharaoh burning ith rath.
And the Lord said to Moses, Pharaoh ill not give ear to you, so that my onders may be increased in the land of Egypt.
All these onders Moses and Aaron did before Pharaoh: but the Lord made Pharaoh’s heart hard, and he did not let the children of Israel go out of his land.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,
Let this month be to you the first of months, the first month of the year.
Say to all the children of Israel hen they are come together, In the tenth day of this month every man is to take a lamb, by the number of their fathers’ families, a lamb for every family:

And if the lamb is more than enough for the family, let that family and its nearest neighbour have a lamb beteen them, taking into account the number of persons and ho much food is needed for every man.
Let your lamb be ithout a mark, a male in its first year: you may take it from among the sheep or the goats:
Keep it till the fourteenth day of the same month, hen everyone ho is of the children of Israel is to put it to death beteen sundon and dark.
Then take some of the blood and put it on the to sides of the door and over the door of the house here the meal is to be taken.
And let your food that night be the flesh of the lamb, cooked ith fire in the oven, together ith unleavened bread and bitter-tasting plants.
Do not take it uncooked or cooked ith boiling ater, but let it be cooked in the oven; its head ith its legs and its inside parts.
Do not keep any of it till the morning; anything hich is not used is to be burned ith fire.
And take your meal dressed as if for a journey, ith your shoes on your feet and your sticks in your hands: take it quickly: it is the Lord’s Passover.
For on that night I ill go through the land of Egypt, sending death on every first male child, of man and of beast, and judging all the gods of Egypt: I am the Lord.
And the blood ill be a sign on the houses here you are: hen I see the blood I ill go over you, and no evil ill come on you for your destruction, hen my hand is on the land of Egypt.
And this day is to be kept in your memories: you are to keep it as a feast to the Lord through all your generations, as an order for ever.

For seven days let your food be unleavened bread; from the first day no leaven is to be seen in your houses: hoever takes bread ith leaven in it, from the first till the seventh day, ill be cut off from Israel.
And on the first day there is to be a holy meeting and on the seventh day a holy meeting; no sort of ork may be done on those days but only to make ready hat is necessary for everyone’s food.
So keep the feast of unleavened bread; for on this very day I have taken your armies out of the land of Egypt: this day, then, is to be kept through all your generations by an order for ever.
In the first month, from the evening of the fourteenth day, let your food be unleavened bread till the evening of the tenty-first day of the month.

For seven days no leaven is to be seen in your houses: for hoever takes bread hich is leavened ill be cut off from the people of Israel, if he is from another country or if he is an Israelite by birth.
Take nothing hich has leaven in it; herever you are living let your food be unleavened cakes.
Then Moses sent for the chiefs of Israel, and said to them, See that lambs are marked out for yourselves and your families, and let the Passover lamb be put to death.
And take some hyssop and put it in the blood in the basin, touching the to sides and the top of the dooray ith the blood from the basin; and let not one of you go out of his house till the morning.

For the Lord ill go through the land, sending death on the Egyptians; and hen he sees the blood on the to sides and the top of the door, the Lord ill go over your door and ill not let death come in for your destruction.
And you are to keep this as an order to you and to your sons for ever.
And hen you come into the land hich the Lord ill make yours, as he gave his ord, you are to keep this act of orship.
And hen your children say to you, What is the reason of this act of orship?

Then you ill say, This is the offering of the Lord’s Passover; for he ent over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, hen he sent death on the Egyptians, and kept our families safe. And the people gave orship ith bent heads.
And the children of Israel ent and did so; as the Lord had given orders to Moses and Aaron, so they did.

And in the middle of the night the Lord sent death on every first male child in the land of Egypt, from the child of Pharaoh on his seat of poer to the child of the prisoner in the prison; and the first births of all the cattle.
Then Pharaoh got up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians; and a great cry ent up from Egypt; for there as not a house here someone as not dead.
And he sent for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, Get up and go out from among my people, you and the children of Israel; go and give orship to the Lord as you have said.
And take your flocks and your herds as you have said, and be gone; and give me your blessing.
And the Egyptians ere forcing the people on, to get them out of the land quickly; for they said, We are all dead men.
And the people took their bread-paste before it as leavened, putting their basins in their clothing on their backs.
And the children of Israel had done as Moses had said; and they got from the Egyptians ornaments of silver and of gold, and clothing:
And the Lord had given the people grace in the eyes of the Egyptians so that they gave them hatever as requested. So they took aay all their goods from the Egyptians.
And the children of Israel made the journey from Rameses to Succoth; there ere about six hundred thousand men on foot, as ell as children.
And a mixed band of people ent ith them; and flocks and herds in great numbers.
And they made unleavened cakes from the paste hich they had taken out of Egypt; it as not leavened, for they had been sent out of Egypt so quickly, that they had no time to make any food ready.
No the children of Israel had been living in Egypt for four hundred and thirty years.
And at the end of four hundred and thirty years, to the very day, all the armies of the Lord ent out of the land of Egypt.
It is a atch-night before the Lord ho took them out of the land of Egypt: this same night is a atch-night to the Lord for all the children of Israel, through all their generations.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, This is the la of the Passover: no man ho is not an Israelite is to take of it:
But every man’s servant, hom he has got for money, may take of it, hen he has had circumcision.
A man from a strange country living among you, and a servant orking for payment, may not take part in it.
It is to be taken in one house; not a bit of the flesh is to be taken out of the house, and no bone of it may be broken.
All Israel is to keep the feast.

And if a man from another country is living ith you, and has a desire to keep the Passover to the Lord, let all the males of his family undergo circumcision, and then let him come near and keep it; for he ill then be as one of your people; but no one ithout circumcision may keep it.
The la is the same for him ho is an Israelite by birth and for the man from a strange country ho is living ith you.
So the children of Israel did as the Lord gave orders to Moses and Aaron.
And on that very day the Lord took the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Let the first male child of every mother among the children of Israel be kept holy for me, even the first male birth among man or beast; for it is mine.

And Moses said to the people, Let this day, on hich you came out of Egypt, out of your prison-house, be kept for ever in memory; for by the strength of his hand the Lord has taken you out from this place; let no leavened bread be used.
On this day, in the month Abib, you are going out.

And it ill be that, hen the Lord takes you into the land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, the land hich he made an oath to your fathers that he ould give you, a land floing ith milk and honey, you ill do this act of orship in this month.
For seven days let your food be unleavened cakes; and on the seventh day there is to be a feast to the Lord.
Unleavened cakes are to be your food through all the seven days; let no leavened bread be seen among you, or any leaven, in any part of your land.
And you ill say to your son in that day, It is because of hat the Lord did for me hen I came out of Egypt.
And this ill be for a sign to you on your hand and for a mark on your bro, so that the la of the Lord may be in your mouth: for ith a strong hand the Lord took you out of Egypt.
So let this order be kept, at the right time, from year to year.
And hen the Lord takes you into the land of Canaan, as he made his oath to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,
You are to put on one side for the Lord every mother’s first male child, the first-fruit of her body, and the first young one of every beast; every male is holy to the Lord.
And for the young of an ass you may give a lamb in payment, or if you ill not make payment for it, its neck is to be broken; but for all the first sons among your children, let payment be made.
And hen your son says to you in time to come, What is the reason for this? say to him, By the strength of his hand the Lord took us out of Egypt, out of the prison-house:

And hen Pharaoh made his heart hard and ould not let us go, the Lord sent death on all the first sons in Egypt, of man and of beast: and so every first male ho comes to birth is offered to the Lord; but for all the first of my sons I give a price.
And this ill be for a sign on your hand and for a mark on your bro: for by the strength of his hand the Lord took us out of Egypt.

No after Pharaoh had let the people go, God did not take them through the land of the Philistines, though that as near: for God said, If the people see ar, they may have a change of heart and go back to Egypt.
But God took the people round by the aste land near the Red Sea: and the children of Israel ent up in fighting order out of the land of Egypt.
And Moses took the bones of Joseph ith him, for Joseph had made the children of Israel take an oath, saying, God ill certainly keep you in mind; and you are to take my bones aay ith you.
Then they ent on their journey from Succoth, and put up their tents in Etham at the edge of the aste land.
And the Lord ent before them by day in a pillar of cloud, guiding them on their ay; and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light: so that they ere able to go on day and night:
The pillar of cloud ent ever before them by day, and the pillar of fire by night.
And the Lord said to Moses,

Give orders to the children of Israel to go back and put up their tents before Pi-hahiroth, beteen Migdol and the sea, in front of Baal-zephon, opposite to hich you are to put up your tents by the sea.
And Pharaoh ill say of the children of Israel, They are andering ithout direction, they are shut in by the aste land.
And I ill make Pharaoh’s heart hard, and he ill come after them and I ill be honoured over Pharaoh and all his army, so that the Egyptians may see that I am the Lord. And they did so.

And ord came to Pharaoh of the flight of the people: and the feeling of Pharaoh and of his servants about the people as changed, and they said, Why have e let Israel go, so that they ill do no more ork for us?
So he had his ar-carriage made ready and took his people ith him:
And he took six hundred carriages, all the carriages of Egypt, and captains over all of them.
And the Lord made the heart of Pharaoh hard, and he ent after the children of Israel: for the children of Israel had gone out ithout fear.
But the Egyptians ent after them, all the horses and carriages of Pharaoh, and his horsemen, and his army, and overtook them in their tents by the sea, by Pihahiroth, before Baal-zephon.
And hen Pharaoh came near, the children of Israel, lifting up their eyes, sa the Egyptians coming after them, and ere full of fear; and their cry ent up to God.
And they said to Moses, Was there no resting-place for the dead in Egypt, that you have taken us aay to come to our death in the aste land? hy have you taken us out of Egypt?
Did e not say to you in Egypt, Let us be as e are, orking for the Egyptians? for it is better to be the servants of the Egyptians than to come to our death in the aste land.
But Moses said, Keep here you are and have no fear; no you ill see the salvation of the Lord hich he ill give you today; for the Egyptians hom you see today you ill never see again.
The Lord ill make ar for you, you have only to keep quiet.
And the Lord said to Moses, Why are you crying out to me? give the children of Israel the order to go forard.
And let your rod be lifted up and your hand stretched out over the sea, and it ill be parted in to; and the children of Israel ill go through on dry land.
And I ill make the heart of the Egyptians hard, and they ill go in after them: and I ill be honoured over Pharaoh and over his army, his ar-carriages, and his horsemen.
And the Egyptians ill see that I am the Lord, hen I get honour over Pharaoh and his ar-carriages and his horsemen.
Then the angel of God, ho had been before the tents of Israel, took his place at their back; and the pillar of cloud, moving from before them, came to rest at their back:
And it came beteen the army of Egypt and the army of Israel; and there as a dark cloud beteen them, and they ent on through the night; but the one army came no nearer to the other all the night.
And hen Moses’ hand as stretched out over the sea, the Lord ith a strong east ind made the sea go back all night, and the aters ere parted in to and the sea became dry land.
And the children of Israel ent through the sea on dry land: and the aters ere a all on their right side and on their left.
Then the Egyptians ent after them into the middle of the sea, all Pharaoh’s horses and his ar-carriages and his horsemen.
And in the morning atch, the Lord, looking out on the armies of the Egyptians from the pillar of fire and cloud, sent trouble on the army of the Egyptians;

And made the heels of their ar-carriages stiff, so that they had hard ork driving them: so the Egyptians said, Let us go in flight from before the face of Israel, for the Lord is fighting for them against the Egyptians.
And the Lord said to Moses, Let your hand be stretched out over the sea, and the aters ill come back again on the Egyptians, and on their ar-carriages and on their horsemen.
And hen Moses’ hand as stretched out over the sea, at dan the sea came floing back, meeting the Egyptians in their flight, and the Lord sent destruction on the Egyptians in the middle of the sea.
And the aters came back, covering the ar-carriages and the horsemen and all the army of Pharaoh hich ent after them into the middle of the sea; not one of them as to be seen.
But the children of Israel ent through the sea alking on dry land, and the aters ere a all on their right side and on their left.
So that day the Lord gave Israel salvation from the hands of the Egyptians; and Israel sa the Egyptians dead on the sea’s edge.
And Israel sa the great ork hich the Lord had done against the Egyptians, and the fear of the Lord came on the people and they had faith in the Lord and in his servant Moses.
Then Moses and the children of Israel made this song to the Lord, and said, I ill make a song to the Lord, for he is lifted up in glory: the horse and the horseman he has sent don into the sea.
The Lord is my strength and my strong helper, he has become my salvation: he is my God and I ill give him praise; my father’s God and I ill give him glory.
The Lord is a man of ar: the Lord is his name.
Pharaoh’s ar-carriages and his army he has sent don into the sea: the best of his captains have gone don into the Red Sea.
They ere covered by the deep aters: like a stone they ent don under the aves.
Full of glory, O Lord, is the poer of your right hand; by your right hand those ho came against you are broken.
When you are lifted up in poer, all those ho come against you are crushed: hen you send out your rath, they are burned up like dry grass.
By your breath the aves ere massed together, the floing aters ere lifted up like a pillar; the deep aters became solid in the heart of the sea.
Egypt said, I ill go after them, I ill overtake, I ill make division of their goods: my desire ill have its ay ith them; my sord ill be uncovered, my hand ill send destruction on them.
You sent your ind and the sea came over them: they ent don like lead into the great aters.
Who is like you, O Lord, among the gods? ho is like you, in holy glory, to be praised ith fear, doing onders?
When your right hand as stretched out, the mouth of the earth as open for them.
In your mercy you ent before the people hom you have made yours; guiding them in your strength to your holy place.
Hearing of you the peoples ere shaking in fear: the people of Philistia ere gripped ith pain.
The chiefs of Edom ere troubled in heart; the strong men of Moab ere in the grip of fear: all the people of Canaan became like ater.
Fear and grief came on them; by the strength of your arm they ere turned to stone; till your people ent over, O Lord, till the people ent over hom you have made yours.
You ill take them in, planting them in the mountain of your heritage, the place, O Lord, here you have made your house, the holy place, O Lord, the building of your hands.
The Lord is King for ever and ever.
For the horses of Pharaoh, ith his ar-carriages and his horsemen, ent into the sea, and the Lord sent the aters of the sea back over them; but the children of Israel ent through the sea on dry land.
And Miriam, the oman prophet, the sister of Aaron, took an instrument of music in her hand; and all the omen ent after her ith music and dances.
And Miriam, ansering, said, Make a song to the Lord, for he is lifted up in glory; the horse and the horseman he has sent into the sea.
Then Moses took Israel forard from the Red Sea, and they ent out into the aste land of Shur; and for three days they ere in the aste land here there as no ater.
And hen they came to Marah, the ater as no good for drinking, for the aters of Marah ere bitter, hich is hy it as named Marah.
And the people, crying out against Moses, said, What are e to have for drink?
And in anser to his prayer, the Lord made him see a tree, and hen he put it into the ater, the ater as made seet. There he gave them a la and an order, testing them;

And he said, If ith all your heart you ill give attention to the voice of the Lord your God, and do hat is right in his eyes, giving ear to his orders and keeping his las, I ill not put on you any of the diseases hich I put on the Egyptians: for I am the Lord your life-giver.
And they came to Elim here there ere telve ater-springs and seventy palm-trees: and they put up their tents there by the aters.

And they ent on their ay from Elim, and all the children of Israel came into the aste land of Sin, hich is beteen Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they ent out of the land of Egypt.
And all the children of Israel ere crying out against Moses and Aaron in the aste land:

And the children of Israel said to them, It ould have been better for the Lord to have put us to death in the land of Egypt, here e ere seated by the flesh-pots and had bread enough for our needs; for you have taken us out to this aste of sand, to put all this people to death through need of food.

Then the Lord said to Moses, See, I ill send don bread from heaven for you; and the people ill go out every day and get enough for the day’s needs; so that I may put them to the test to see if they ill keep my las or not.
And on the sixth day they are to make ready hat they get in, and it ill be tice as much as they get on the other days.
And Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel, This evening it ill be clear to you that it is the Lord ho has taken you out of the land of Egypt:
And in the morning you ill see the glory of the Lord; for your angry ords against the Lord have come to his ears: and hat are e that you are crying out against us?

And Moses said, The Lord ill give you meat for your food at evening, and in the morning bread in full measure; for your outcry against the Lord has come to his ears: for hat are e? your outcry is not against us but against the Lord.
And Moses said to Aaron, Say to all the people of Israel, Come near before the Lord for he has given ear to your outcry.
And hile Aaron as talking to the children of Israel, their eyes ere turned in the direction of the aste land, and they sa the glory of the Lord shining in the cloud.
And the Lord said to Moses,

The outcry of the children of Israel has come to my ears: say to them no, At nightfall you ill have meat for your food, and in the morning bread in full measure; and you ill see that I am the Lord your God.
And it came about that in the evening little birds came up and the place as covered ith them: and in the morning there as de all round about the tents.
And hen the de as gone, on the face of the earth as a small round thing, like small drops of ice on the earth.
And hen the children of Israel sa it, they said to one another, What is it? for they had no idea hat it as. And Moses said to them, It is the bread hich the Lord has given you for your food.
This is hat the Lord has said, Let every man take up as much as he has need of; at the rate of one omer for every person, let every man take as much as is needed for his family.
And the children of Israel did so, and some took more and some less.
And hen it as measured, he ho had taken up much had nothing over, and he ho had little had enough; every man had taken hat he as able to make use of.
And Moses said to them, Let nothing be kept till the morning.
But they gave no attention to Moses, and some of them kept it till the morning and there ere orms in it and it had an evil smell: and Moses as angry ith them.
And they took it up morning by morning, every man as he had need: and hen the sun as high it as gone.
And on the sixth day they took up tice as much of the bread, to omers for every person: and all the rulers of the people gave Moses ord of it.
And he said, This is hat the Lord has said, Tomorro is a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the Lord: hat has to be cooked may be cooked; and hat is over, put on one side to be kept till the morning.
And they kept it till the morning as Moses had said: and no smell came from it, and it had no orms.
And Moses said, Make your meal today of hat you have, for this day is a Sabbath to the Lord: today you ill not get any in the fields.
For six days you ill get it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there ill not be any.
But still on the seventh day some of the people ent out to get it, and there as not any.
And the Lord said to Moses, Ho long ill you go against my orders and my las?
See, because the Lord has given you the Sabbath, he gives you on the sixth day bread enough for to days; let every man keep here he is; let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
So the people took their rest on the seventh day.
And this bread as named manna by Israel: it as hite, like a grain seed, and its taste as like cakes made ith honey.

And Moses said, This is the order hich the Lord has given: Let one omer of it be kept for future generations, so that they may see the bread hich I gave you for your food in the aste land, hen I took you out from the land of Egypt.
And Moses said to Aaron, Take a pot and put one omer of manna in it, and put it aay before the Lord, to be kept for future generations.
So Aaron put it aay in front of the holy chest to be kept, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And the children of Israel had manna for their food for forty years, till they came to a land ith people in it, till they came to the edge of the land of Canaan.
No an omer is the tenth part of an ephah.
And the children of Israel ent on from the aste land of Sin, by stages as the Lord gave them orders, and put up their tents in Rephidim: and there as no drinking-ater for the people.
So the people ere angry ith Moses, and said, Give us ater for drinking. And Moses said, Why are you angry ith me? and hy do you put God to the test?
And the people ere in great need of ater; and they made an outcry against Moses, and said, Why have you taken us out of Egypt to send death on us and our children and our cattle through need of ater?
And Moses, crying out to the Lord, said, What am I to do to this people? they are almost ready to put me to death by stoning.
And the Lord said to Moses, Go on before the people, and take some of the chiefs of Israel ith you, and take in your hand the rod hich as stretched out over the Nile, and go.

See, I ill take my place before you on the rock in Horeb; and hen you give the rock a blo, ater ill come out of it, and the people ill have drink. And Moses did so before the eyes of the chiefs of Israel.
And he gave that place the name Massah and Meribah, because the children of Israel ere angry, and because they put the Lord to the test, saying, Is the Lord ith us or not?
Then Amalek came and made ar on Israel in Rephidim.
And Moses said to Joshua, Get together a band of men for us and go out, make ar on Amalek: tomorro I ill take my place on the top of the hill ith the rod of God in my hand.
So Joshua did as Moses said to him, and ent to ar ith Amalek: and Moses, Aaron, and Hur ent up to the top of the hill.
No hile Moses’ hand as lifted up, Israel as the stronger: but hen he let his hand go don, Amalek became the stronger.

But Moses’ hands became tired; so they put a stone under him and he took his seat on it, Aaron and Hur supporting his hands, one on one side and one on the other; so his hands ere kept up ithout falling till the sun ent don.
And Joshua overcame Amalek and his people ith the sord.

And the Lord said to Moses, Make a record of this in a book, so that it may be kept in memory, and say it again in the ears of Joshua: that all memory of Amalek is to be completely uprooted from the earth.
Then Moses put up an altar and gave it the name of Yaheh-nissi:
For he said, The Lord has taken his oath that there ill be ar ith Amalek from generation to generation.
No nes came to Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-la, of all God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, and ho the Lord had taken Israel out of Egypt.
And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-la, took Zipporah, Moses’ ife, after he had sent her aay,
And her to sons, one of hom as named Gershom, for he said, I have been living in a strange land:
And the name of the other as Eliezer, for he said, The God of my father as my help, and kept me safe from the sord of Pharaoh:
And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-la, came ith his sons and his ife to here Moses had put up his tent in the aste land, by the mountain of God.
And he said to Moses, I, your father-in-la, have come to you, ith your ife and your to sons.
And Moses ent out to his father-in-la, and ent don on his face before him and gave him a kiss; and they said to one another, Are you ell? and they came into the tent.

And Moses gave his father-in-la an account of all the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians because of Israel, and of all the troubles hich had come on them by the ay, and ho the Lord had given them salvation.
And Jethro as glad because the Lord had been good to Israel, freeing them from the poer of the Egyptians.
And Jethro said, Praise be to the Lord, ho has taken you out of the hand of Pharaoh and out of the hand of the Egyptians; freeing the people from the yoke of the Egyptians.
No I am certain that the Lord is greater than all gods, for he has overcome them in their pride.
Then Jethro, Moses’ father-in-la, made a burned offering to God: and Aaron came, ith the chiefs of Israel, and had a meal ith Moses’ father-in-la, before God.
No on the day after, Moses took his seat to give decisions for the people: and the people ere aiting before Moses from morning till evening.
And hen Moses’ father-in-la sa all he as doing, he said, What is this you are doing for the people? hy are you seated here by yourself, ith all the people aiting before you from morning till evening?
And Moses said to his father-in-la, Because the people come to me to get directions from God:
And if they have any question beteen themselves, they come to me, and I am judge beteen a man and his neighbour, and I give them the orders and las of God.
And Moses’ father-in-la said to him, What you are doing is not good.
Your strength and that of the people ill be completely used up: this ork is more than you are able to do by yourself.
Give ear no to my suggestion, and may God be ith you: you are to be the people’s representative before God, taking their causes to him:
Teaching them his rules and his las, guiding them in the ay they have to go, and making clear to them the ork they have to do.

But for the rest, take from among the people able men, such as have the fear of God, true men hating profits rongly made; and put such men over them, to be captains of thousands, captains of hundreds and of fifties and of tens;

And let them be judges in the causes of the people at all times: and let them put before you all important questions, but in small things let them give decisions themselves: in this ay, it ill be less hard for you, and they ill take the eight off you.
If you do this, and God gives approval, then you ill be able to go on ithout eariness, and all this people ill go to their tents in peace.
So Moses took note of the ords of his father-in-la, and did as he had said.
And he made selection of able men out of all Israel, and made them heads over the people, captains of thousands, captains of hundreds and of fifties and of tens.
And they ere judges in the causes of the people at all times: the hard questions they put before Moses; but on every small point they gave decisions themselves.
And Moses let his father-in-la go aay, and he ent back to his land.
In the third month after the children of Israel ent out from Egypt, on the same day, they came into the aste land of Sinai.
And hen they had gone aay from Rephidim and had come into the aste land of Sinai, they put up their tents in the aste land before the mountain: there Israel put up its tents.
And Moses ent up to God, and the voice of the Lord came to him from the mountain, saying, Say to the family of Jacob, and give ord to the children of Israel:
You have seen hat I did to the Egyptians, and ho I took you, as on eagles’ ings, guiding you to myself.
If no you ill truly give ear to my voice and keep my agreement, you ill be my special property out of all the peoples: for all the earth is mine:
And you ill be a kingdom of priests to me, and a holy nation. These are the ords hich you are to say to the children of Israel.
And Moses came and sent for the chiefs of the people and put before them all these ords hich the Lord had given him orders to say.
And all the people, ansering together, said, Whatever the Lord has said e ill do. And Moses took back to the Lord the ords of the people.

And the Lord said to Moses, See, I ill come to you in a thick cloud, so that hat I say to you may come to the ears of the people and they may have belief in you for ever. And Moses gave the Lord ord of hat the people had said.
And the Lord said to Moses, Go to the people and make them holy today and tomorro, and let their clothing be ashed.
And by the third day let them be ready: for on the third day the Lord ill come don on Mount Sinai, before the eyes of all the people.

And let limits be marked out for the people round the mountain, and say to them, Take care not to go up the mountain or near the sides of it: hoever puts his foot on the mountain ill certainly come to his death:
He is not to be touched by a hand, but is to be stoned or have an arro put through him; man or beast, he is to be put to death: at the long sounding of a horn they may come up to the mountain.
Then Moses ent don from the mountain to the people, and made the people holy; and their clothing as ashed.
And he said to the people, Be ready by the third day: do not come near a oman.
And hen morning came on the third day, there ere thunders and flames and a thick cloud on the mountain, and a horn sounding very loud; and all the people in the tents ere shaking ith fear.
And Moses made the people come out of their tents and take their places before God; and they came to the foot of the mountain,
And all the mountain of Sinai as smoking, for the Lord had come don on it in fire: and the smoke of it ent up like the smoke of a great burning; and all the mountain as shaking.
And hen the sound of the horn became louder and louder, Moses’ ords ere ansered by the voice of God.
Then the Lord came don on to Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain, and the Lord sent for Moses to come up to the top of the mountain, and Moses ent up.
And the Lord said to Moses, Go don and give the people orders to keep back, for fear that a great number of them, forcing their ay through to see the Lord, may come to destruction.
And let the priests ho come near to the Lord make themselves holy, for fear that the Lord may come on them suddenly.
And Moses said to the Lord, The people ill not be able to come up the mountain, for you gave us orders to put limits round the mountain, marking it out and making it holy.
And the Lord said to him, Go don, and you and Aaron may come up; but let not the priests and the people make their ay through to the Lord, or he ill come on them suddenly.
So Moses ent don to the people and said this to them.
And God said all these ords:
I am the Lord your God ho took you out of the land of Egypt, out of the prison-house.
You are to have no other gods but me.
You are not to make an image or picture of anything in heaven or on the earth or in the aters under the earth:

You may not go don on your faces before them or give them orship: for I, the Lord your God, am a God ho ill not give his honour to another; and I ill send punishment on the children for the rongdoing of their fathers, to the third and fourth generation of my haters;
And I ill have mercy through a thousand generations on those ho have love for me and keep my las.
You are not to make use of the name of the Lord your God for an evil purpose; hoever takes the Lord’s name on his lips for an evil purpose ill be judged a sinner by the Lord
Keep in memory the Sabbath and let it be a holy day.
On six days do all your ork:

But the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God; on that day you are to do no ork, you or your son or your daughter, your man-servant or your oman-servant, your cattle or the man from a strange country ho is living among you:

For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and the sea, and everything in them, and he took his rest on the seventh day: for this reason the Lord has given his blessing to the seventh day and made it holy.
Give honour to your father and to your mother, so that your life may be long in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you.
Do not put anyone to death ithout cause.
Do not be false to the married relation.
Do not take the property of another.
Do not give false itness against your neighbour.
Let not your desire be turned to your neighbour’s house, or his ife or his man-servant or his oman-servant or his ox or his ass or anything hich is his.
And all the people ere atching the thunderings and the flames and the sound of the horn and the mountain smoking; and hen they sa it, they kept far off, shaking ith fear.
And they said to Moses, To your ords e ill give ear, but let not the voice of God come to our ears, for fear death may come on us.
And Moses said to the people, Have no fear: for God has come to put you to the test, so that fearing him you may be kept from sin.
And the people kept their places far off, but Moses ent near to the dark cloud here God as.
And the Lord said to Moses, Say to the children of Israel, You yourselves have seen that my voice has come to you from heaven
Gods of silver and gods of gold you are not to make for yourselves.

Make for me an altar of earth, offering on it your burned offerings and your peace-offerings, your sheep and your oxen: in every place here I have put the memory of my name, I ill come to you and give you my blessing.
And if you make me an altar of stone do not make it of cut stones: for the touch of an instrument ill make it unclean.
And do not go up by steps to my altar, for fear that your bodies may be seen uncovered.
No these are the las hich you are to put before them.
If you get a Hebre servant for money, he is to be your servant for six years, and in the seventh year you are to let him go free ithout payment.
If he comes to you by himself, let him go aay by himself: if he is married, let his ife go aay ith him.
If his master gives him a ife, and he gets sons or daughters by her, the ife and her children ill be the property of the master, and the servant is to go aay by himself.
But if the servant says clearly, My master and my ife and children are dear to me; I have no desire to be free:
Then his master is to take him to the gods of the house, and at the door, or at its frameork, he is to make a hole in his ear ith a sharp-pointed instrument; and he ill be his servant for ever.
And if a man gives his daughter for a price to be a servant, she is not to go aay free as the men-servants do.

If she is not pleasing to her master ho has taken her for himself, let a payment be made for her so that she may go free; her master has no poer to get a price for her and send her to a strange land, because he has been false to her.
And if he gives her to his son, he is to do everything for her as if she as his daughter.
And if he takes another oman, her food and clothing and her married rights are not to be less.
And if he does not do these three things for her, she has the right to go free ithout payment.
He ho gives a man a death-blo is himself to be put to death.
But if he had no evil purpose against him, and God gave him into his hand, I ill give you a place to hich he may go in flight.
But if a man makes an attack on his neighbour on purpose, to put him to death by deceit, you are to take him from my altar and put him to death.
Any man ho gives a blo to his father or his mother is certainly to be put to death.
Any man ho gets another into his poer in order to get a price for him is to be put to death, if you take him in the act.
Any man cursing his father or his mother is to be put to death.
If, in a fight, one man gives another a blo ith a stone, or ith the shut hand, not causing his death, but making him keep in bed;
If he is able to get up again and go about ith a stick, the other ill be let off; only he ill have to give him payment for the loss of his time, and see that he is cared for till he is ell.
If a man gives his man-servant or his oman-servant blos ith a rod, causing death, he is certainly to undergo punishment.
But, at the same time, if the servant goes on living for a day or to, the master is not to get punishment, for the servant is his property.

If men, hile fighting, do damage to a oman ith child, causing the loss of the child, but no other evil comes to her, the man ill have to make payment up to the amount fixed by her husband, in agreement ith the decision of the judges.
But if damage comes to her, let life be given in payment for life,
Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
Burning for burning, ound for ound, blo for blo.
If a man gives his man-servant or his oman-servant a blo in the eye, causing its destruction, he is to let him go free on account of the damage to his eye.
Or if the loss of a tooth is caused by his blo, he ill let him go free on account of his tooth.
If an ox comes to be the cause of death to a man or a oman, the ox is to be stoned, and its flesh may not be used for food; but the oner ill not be judged responsible.

But if the ox has frequently done such damage in the past, and the oner has had ord of it and has not kept it under control, so that it has been the cause of the death of a man or oman, not only is the ox to be stoned, but its oner is to be put to death.
If a price is put on his life, let him make payment of hatever price is fixed.
If the death of a son or of a daughter has been caused, the punishment is to be in agreement ith this rule.
If the death of a man-servant or of a oman-servant is caused by the ox, the oner is to give their master thirty shekels of silver, and the ox is to be stoned.
If a man makes a hole in the earth ithout covering it up, and an ox or an ass dropping into it comes to its death;
The oner of the hole is responsible; he ill have to make payment to their oner, but the dead beast ill be his.
And if one man’s ox does damage to another man’s ox, causing its death, then the living ox is to be exchanged for money, and division made of the price of it, and of the price of the dead one.
But if it is common knoledge that the ox has frequently done such damage in the past, and its oner has not kept it under control, he ill have to give ox for ox; and the dead beast ill be his.

If a man takes ithout right another man’s ox or his sheep, and puts it to death or gets a price for it, he is to give five oxen for an ox, or four sheep for a sheep, in payment: the thief ill have to make payment for hat he has taken; if he has no money, he himself ill have to be exchanged for money, so that payment may be made.
If a thief is taken in the act of forcing his ay into a house, and his death is caused by a blo, the oner of the house is not responsible for his blood.
But if it is after dan, he ill be responsible.
If he still has hat he had taken, hatever it is, ox or ass or sheep, he is to give tice its value.
If a man makes a fire in a field or a vine-garden, and lets the fire do damage to another man’s field, he is to give of the best produce of his field or his vine-garden to make up for it.

If there is a fire and the flames get to the thorns at the edge of the field, causing destruction of the cut grain or of the living grain, or of the field, he ho made the fire ill have to make up for the damage.
If a man puts money or goods in the care of his neighbour to keep for him, and it is taken from the man’s house, if they get the thief, he ill have to make payment of tice the value.
If they do not get the thief, let the master of the house come before the judges and take an oath that he has not put his hand on his neighbour’s goods.

In any question about an ox or an ass or a sheep or clothing, or about the loss of any property hich anyone says is his, let the to sides put their cause before God; and he ho is judged to be in the rong is to make payment to his neighbour of tice the value.
If a man puts an ass or an ox or a sheep or any beast into the keeping of his neighbour, and it comes to death or is damaged or is taken aay, ithout any person seeing it:
If he takes his oath before the Lord that he has not put his hand to his neighbour’s goods, the oner is to take his ord for it and he ill not have to make payment for it.
But if it is taken from him by a thief, he is to make up for the loss of it to its oner.
But if it has been damaged by a beast, and he is able to make this clear, he ill not have to make payment for hat as damaged.
If a man gets from his neighbour the use of one of his beasts, and it is damaged or put to death hen the oner is not ith it, he ill certainly have to make payment for the loss.
If the oner is ith it, he ill not have to make payment: if he gave money for the use of it, the loss is covered by the payment.
If a man takes a virgin, ho has not given her ord to another man, and has connection ith her, he ill have to give a bride-price for her to be his ife.
If her father ill not give her to him on any account, he ill have to give the regular payment for virgins.
Any oman using unnatural poers or secret arts is to be put to death.
Any man ho has sex connection ith a beast is to be put to death.
Complete destruction ill come on any man ho makes offerings to any other god but the Lord.
Do no rong to a man from a strange country, and do not be hard on him; for you yourselves ere living in a strange country, in the land of Egypt.
Do no rong to a ido, or to a child hose father is dead.
If you are cruel to them in any ay, and their cry comes up to me, I ill certainly give ear;
And in the heat of my rath I ill put you to death ith the sord, so that your ives ill be idos and your children ithout fathers.
If you let any of the poor among my people have the use of your money, do not be a hard creditor to him, and do not take interest.
If ever you take your neighbour’s clothing in exchange for the use of your money, let him have it back before the sun goes don:
For it is the only thing he has for covering his skin; hat is he to go to sleep in? and hen his cry comes up to me, I ill give ear, for my mercy is great.
You may not say evil of the judges, or put a curse on the ruler of your people.
Do not keep back your offerings from the ealth of your grain and your vines. The first of your sons you are to give to me.
In the same ay ith your oxen and your sheep: for seven days let the young one be ith its mother; on the eighth day give it to me.
You are to be holy men to me: the flesh of no animal hose death has been caused by the beasts of the field may be used for your food; it is to be given to the dogs.
Do not let a false statement go further; do not make an agreement ith evil-doers to be a false itness.
Do not be moved to do rong by the general opinion, or give the support of your ords to a rong decision:
But, on the other hand, do not be turned from hat is right in order to give support to a poor man’s cause.
If you come across the ox or the ass of one ho is no friend to you andering from its ay, you are to take it back to him.
If you see the ass of one ho has no love for you bent don to the earth under the eight hich is put on it, you are to come to its help, even against your desire.
Let no rong decisions be given in the poor man’s cause.
Keep yourselves far from any false business; never let the upright or him ho has done no rong be put to death: for I ill make the evil-doer responsible for his sin.
Take no reards in a cause: for reards make blind those ho have eyes to see, and make the decisions of the upright false.

Do not be hard on the man from a strange country ho is living among you; for you have had experience of the feelings of one ho is far from the land of his birth, because you yourselves ere living in Egypt, in a strange land.
For six years put seed into your fields and get in the increase;

But in the seventh year let the land have a rest and be unplanted; so that the poor may have food from it: and let the beasts of the field take the rest. Do the same ith your vine-gardens and your olive-trees.
For six days do your ork, and on the seventh day keep the Sabbath; so that your ox and your ass may have rest, together ith the son of your servant and the man from a strange land living among you.
Take note of all these things hich I have said to you, and let not the names of other gods come into your minds or from your lips.
Three times in the year you are to keep a feast to me.

You are to keep the feast of unleavened bread; for seven days let your bread be ithout leaven, as I gave you orders, at the regular time in the month Abib ( for in it you came out of Egypt); and let no one come before me ithout an offering:
And the feast of the grain-cutting, the first-fruits of your planted fields: and the feast at the start of the year, hen you have got in all the fruit from your fields.
Three times in the year let all your males come before the Lord God.
Do not give the blood of my offering ith leavened bread; and do not let the fat of my feast be kept all night till the morning.
The best of the first-fruits of your land are to be taken into the house of the Lord your God. The young goat is not to be cooked in its mother’s milk.
See, I am sending an angel before you, to keep you on your ay and to be your guide into the place hich I have made ready for you.
Give attention to him and give ear to his voice; do not go against him; for your rongdoing ill not be overlooked by him, because my name is in him.
But if you truly give ear to his voice, and do hatever I say, then I ill be against those ho are against you, fighting those ho are fighting you.
And my angel ill go before you, guiding you into the land of the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Canaanite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, and they ill be cut off by my hand.
Do not go don on your faces and give orship to their gods, or do as they do; but overcome them completely, and let their pillars be broken don.
And give orship to the Lord your God, ho ill send his blessing on your bread and on your ater; and I ill take all disease aay from among you.
All your animals ill give birth ithout loss, not one ill be ithout young in all your land; I ill give you a full measure of life.
I ill send my fear before you, putting to flight all the people to hom you come; all those ho are against you ill go in flight, turning their backs before you.
I ill send hornets before you, driving out the Hivite and the Canaanite and the Hittite before your face.
I ill not send them all out in one year, for fear that their land may become aste, and the beasts of the field be increased overmuch against you.
Little by little I ill send them aay before you, till your numbers are increased and you take up your heritage in the land.

I ill let the limits of your land be from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the aste land to the river Euphrates: for I ill give the people of those lands into your poer; and you ill send them out before you.
Make no agreement ith them or ith their gods.
Let them not go on living in your land, or they ill make you do evil against me: for if you give orship to their gods, it ill certainly be a cause of sin to you.
And he said to Moses, Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, and Nadab and Abihu and seventy of the chiefs of Israel; and give me orship from a distance.
And Moses only may come near to the Lord; but the others are not to come near, and the people may not come up ith them.
Then Moses came and put before the people all the ords of the Lord and his las: and all the people, ansering ith one voice, said, Whatever the Lord has said e ill do.
Then Moses put don in riting all the ords of the Lord, and he got up early in the morning and made an altar at the foot of the mountain, ith telve pillars for the telve tribes of Israel.
And he sent some of the young men of the children of Israel to make burned offerings and peace-offerings of oxen to the Lord.
And Moses took half the blood and put it in basins; draining out half of the blood over the altar.
And he took the book of the agreement, reading it in the hearing of the people: and they said, Everything hich the Lord has said e ill do, and e ill keep his las.
Then Moses took the blood and let it come on the people, and said, This blood is the sign of the agreement hich the Lord has made ith you in these ords.
Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the chiefs of Israel ent up:
And they sa the God of Israel; and under his feet there as, as it seemed, a jeelled floor, clear as the heavens.
And he put not his hand on the chiefs of the children of Israel: they sa God, and took food and drink.

And the Lord said to Moses, Come up to me on the mountain, and take your place there: and I ill give you the stones on hich I have put in riting the la and the orders, so that you may give the people knoledge of them.
Then Moses and Joshua his servant got up; and Moses ent up into the mountain of God.
And he said to the chiefs, Keep your places here till e come back to you: Aaron and Hur are ith you; if anyone has any cause let him go to them.
And Moses ent up into the mountain, and it as covered by the cloud.
And the glory of the Lord as resting on Mount Sinai, and the cloud as over it for six days; and on the seventh day he said Moses’ name out of the cloud.
And the glory of the Lord as like a flame on the top of the mountain before the eyes of the children of Israel.
And Moses ent up the mountain, into the cloud, and as there for forty days and forty nights.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel that they are to make me an offering; from every man ho has the impulse in his heart take an offering for me.
And this is the offering you are to take from them: gold and silver and brass;
And blue and purple and red, and the best linen, and goats’ hair;
And sheepskins coloured red, and leather, and hard ood;
Oil for the light, spices for the seet-smelling oil, seet perfumes for burning;
Beryls and stones of value to be put on the ephod and on the priest’s bag.
And let them make me a holy place, so that I may be ever present among them.
Make the House and everything in it from the designs hich I ill give you.
And they are to make an ark of hard ood; to and a half cubits long, and a cubit and a half ide and high.
It is to be plated inside and out ith the best gold, ith an edge of gold all round it
And make four rings of gold for it, to be fixed on its four feet, to rings on one side of it and to on the other.
And make rods of the same ood, plating them ith gold.
And put the rods through the rings at the sides of the ark, for lifting it.
The rods are to be kept in the rings, and never taken out.
Inside the ark you are to put the record hich I ill give you.
And you are to make a cover of the best gold, to and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half ide.
And at the to ends of the cover you are to make to inged ones of hammered gold,
One at one end and one at the other; the inged ones are to be part of the cover.
And their ings are to be outstretched over the cover, and the inged ones are to be opposite one another, facing the cover.
And put the cover over the ark, and in the ark the record hich I ill give you.
And there, beteen the to inged ones on the cover of the ark, I ill come to you, face to face, and make clear to you all the orders I have to give you for the children of Israel.
And you are to make a table of the same ood, to cubits long, a cubit ide and a cubit and a half high,
Plated ith the best gold, ith a gold edge all round it;
And make a frame all round it, as ide as a man’s hand, ith a gold edge to the frame.
And make four gold rings and put them at the four angles, on the four feet of the table;
The rings are to be fixed under the frame to take the rods ith hich the table is to be lifted.
Make rods of the same ood, plated ith gold, for lifting the table.
And make the table-vessels, the spoons and the cups and the basins for liquids, all of the best gold.
And on the table at all times you are to keep my holy bread.
And you are to make a support for lights, of the best gold; its base and its pillar are to be of hammered gold; its cups, its buds, and its floers are to be made of the same metal.
It is to have six branches coming out from its sides; three branches from one side and three from the other.
Every branch having three cups made like almond floers, every cup ith a bud and a floer, on all the branches.
And on the pillar, four cups like almond floers, every one ith its bud and its floer:
And under every to branches a bud, made ith the branch, for all the six branches of it.
The buds and the branches are to be made of the same metal; all together one complete ork of hammered gold.
Then you are to make its seven vessels for the lights, putting them in their place so that they give light in front of it.
And the instruments and trays for use ith it are all to be of the best gold.
A talent of gold ill be needed for it, ith all these vessels.
And see that you make them from the design hich you sa on the mountain.
And you are to make a House for me, ith ten curtains of the best linen, blue and purple and red, orked ith designs of inged ones by a good orkman.
Every curtain is to be tenty-eight cubits long and four cubits ide, all of the same measure.
Five curtains are to be joined together, and the other five are to be joined together.
And you are to put tists of blue cord on the edge of the outside curtain of the first group of five, and on the edge of the outside curtain of the second group of five;
Fifty tists on one curtain and fifty on the other, the tists to be opposite one another.
Then make fifty gold hooks, joining the curtains together by the hooks, and in this ay the House ill be made.
And you are to make curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the House, eleven curtains.
Every curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits ide, all of the same measure.
Five of these curtains are to be joined together, and the other six are to be joined together, the sixth being folded over to make a hanging in front of the tent.
And you are to put fifty tists of cord on the edge of the outside curtain of one group, and fifty tists on the edge of the outside curtain of the other group.
Then make fifty brass hooks and put the hooks into the tists, joining the tent together to make it one.
And the folded part hich is over of the curtains of the tent, the half-curtain hich is folded back, ill be hanging don over the back of the House.
And the cubit hich is over of the ten curtains at the sides ill be hanging over the to sides of the House as a cover.
And then you are to make a cover for the tent, of sheepskins coloured red, and a cover of leather over that.
And you are to make upright boards of hard ood for the House.
Every board is to be ten cubits high and a cubit and a half ide.
Every board is to be joined to the one nearest to it by to tongues, and so for every board in the House.
These are the boards needed for the house; tenty boards for the south side,
With forty silver bases under the tenty boards, to bases under every board to take its tongues.
And tenty boards for the second side of the house on the north,
With their forty silver bases, to under every board.
And six boards for the back of the House on the est,
With to boards for the angles of the House at the back.
The to are to be joined together at the base and at the top to one ring, forming the to angles.
So there are to be eight boards, ith their sixteen silver bases, to bases under every board.
And make rods of the same ood, five for the boards on the one side,
And five for the boards on the other side of the House, and five for the est side of the House at the back.
And the middle rod is to go through the rings of all the boards from end to end.
And the boards are to be plated ith gold, having gold rings for the rods to go through: and the rods are to be plated ith gold.
And you are to make the House from the design hich you sa on the mountain.
And you are to make a veil of the best linen, blue and purple and red, orked ith designs of inged ones by a good orkman:
Hanging it by gold hooks from four pillars of ood, plated ith gold and fixed in silver bases.
And you are to put up the veil under the hooks, and put inside it the ark of the la: the veil is to be a division beteen the holy place and the most holy.
You are to put the cover on the ark of the la, inside the most holy place.
And outside the veil you are to put the table, and the support for the lights opposite the table on the south side of the House; and the table is to be on the north side.
And you are to make a curtain for the dooray of the Tent, of the best linen ith needleork of blue and purple and red.
And make five pillars for the curtain, of hard ood plated ith gold; their hooks are to be of gold and their bases of brass.
And make an altar of hard ood, a square altar, five cubits long, five cubits ide and three cubits high.
Put horns at the four angles of it, made of the same, plating it all ith brass.
And make all its vessels, the baskets for taking aay the dust of the fire, the spades and basins and meat-hooks and fire-trays, of brass.
And make a netork of brass, ith four brass rings at its four angles.
And put the netork under the shelf round the altar so that the net comes half-ay up the altar.
And make rods for the altar, of hard ood, plated ith brass.
And put the rods through the rings at the to opposite sides of the altar, for lifting it.
The altar is to be hollo, boarded in ith ood; make it from the design hich you sa on the mountain.
And let there be an open space round the House, ith hangings for its south side of the best linen, a hundred cubits long.
Their tenty pillars and their tenty bases are to be of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their bands are to be of silver.
And on the north side in the same ay, hangings a hundred cubits long, ith tenty pillars of brass on bases of brass; their hooks and their bands are to be of silver.
And for the open space on the est side, the hangings are to be fifty cubits ide, ith ten pillars and ten bases;
And on the east side the space is to be fifty cubits ide.
On the one side of the dooray ill be hangings fifteen cubits long, ith three pillars and three bases;
And on the other side, hangings fifteen cubits long, ith three pillars and three bases.
And across the dooray, a veil of tenty cubits of the best linen, made of needleork of blue and purple and red, ith four pillars and four bases.
All the pillars round the open space are to have silver bands, ith hooks of silver and bases of brass.
The open space is to be a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits ide, ith sides five cubits high, curtained ith the best linen, ith bases of brass.
All the instruments for the ork of the House, and all its nails, and the nails of the open space are to be of brass.
Give orders to the children of Israel to give you clear olive oil for the lights, so that a light may be burning there at all times.

Let Aaron and his sons put this in order, evening and morning, before the Lord, inside the Tent of meeting, outside the veil hich is before the ark; this is to be an order for ever, from generation to generation, to be kept by the children of Israel.
No let Aaron your brother, and his sons ith him, come near from among the children of Israel, so that they may be my priests, even Aaron, and Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar, his sons.
And make holy robes for Aaron your brother, so that he may be clothed ith glory and honour.
Give orders to all the ise-hearted orkmen, hom I have made full of the spirit of isdom, to make robes for Aaron, so that he may be made holy as my priest.

This is hat they are to make: a priest’s bag, an ephod, and a robe, and a coat of coloured needleork, a head-dress, and a linen band; they are to make holy robes for Aaron your brother and for his sons, so that they may do the ork of priests for me.
They are to take the gold and blue and purple and red and the best linen,
And make the ephod of gold and blue and purple and red and the best linen, the ork of a designer.
It is to have to bands stitched to it at the top of the arms, joining it together.
And the beautifully orked band, hich goes on it, is to be of the same ork and the same material, of gold and blue and purple and red and tisted linen-ork.
You are to take to beryl stones, on hich the names of the children of Israel are to be cut:
Six names on the one stone and six on the other, in the order of their birth.
With the ork of a jeeller, like the cutting of a stamp, the names of the children of Israel are to be cut on them, and they are to be fixed in tisted frames of gold.

And the to stones are to be placed on the ephod, over the arm-holes, to be stones of memory for the children of Israel: Aaron ill have their names on his arms hen he goes in before the Lord, to keep the Lord in mind of them.
And you are to make tisted frames of gold;
And to chains of the best gold, tisted like cords; and have the chains fixed on to the frames.
And make a priest’s bag for giving decisions, designed like the ephod, made of gold and blue and purple and red and the best linen.
It is to be square, folded in to, a hand-stretch long and a hand-stretch ide.
And on it you are to put four lines of jeels; the first line is to be a cornelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald;
The second, a ruby, a sapphire, and an onyx;
The third, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
The fourth, a topaz, a beryl, and a jasper; they are to be fixed in tisted frames of gold.
The jeels are to be telve in number, for the names of the children of Israel; every jeel having the name of one of the telve tribes cut on it as on a stamp.
And you are to make to chains of gold, tisted like cords, to be fixed to the priest’s bag.
And put to gold rings on the to ends of the bag.
Put the to gold chains on the to rings at the ends of the bag;
Joining the other ends of the chains to the gold frames and putting them on the front of the ephod, at the top of the arms.
Then make to gold rings and put them on the loer ends of the bag, at the edge of it on the inner side nearest to the ephod.
And make to more gold rings and put them on the front of the ephod at the top of the arms, at the join, over the orked band:
So that the rings on the bag may be fixed to the rings of the ephod by a blue cord and on to the band of the ephod, so that the bag may not come loose from the ephod.
And so Aaron ill have the names of the children of Israel on the priest’s bag over his heart henever he goes into the holy place, to keep the memory of them before the Lord.

And in the bag you are to put the Urim and Thummim, so that they may be on Aaron’s heart henever he goes in before the Lord; and Aaron may have the poer of making decisions for the children of Israel before the Lord at all times.
The robe hich goes ith the ephod is to be made all of blue;
With a hole at the top, in the middle of it; the hole is to be edged ith a band to make it strong like the hole in the coat of a fighting-man, so that it may not be broken open.
And round the skirts of it put fruits in blue and purple and red, ith bells of gold beteen;
A gold bell and a fruit in turn all round the skirts of the robe.
Aaron is to put it on for his holy ork; and the sound of it ill be clear, hen he goes into the holy place before the Lord, and hen he comes out, keeping him safe from death.
You are to make a plate of the best gold, cutting on it, as on a stamp, these ords: HOLY TO THE LORD.
Put a blue cord on it and put it on the front of the tisted head-dress:

And it ill be over Aaron’s bro, so that Aaron ill be responsible for any error in all the holy offerings made by the children of Israel; it ill be on his bro at all times, so that their offerings may be pleasing to the Lord.
The coat is to be made of the best linen, orked in squares; and you are to make a head-dress of linen, and a linen band orked in needleork.
And for Aaron’s sons you are to make coats, and bands, and head-dresses, so that they may be clothed ith glory and honour.
These you are to put on Aaron, your brother, and on his sons, putting oil on them, separating them and making them holy, to do the ork of priests to me.
And you are to make them linen trousers, covering their bodies from the middle to the knee;

Aaron and his sons are to put these on henever they go into the Tent of meeting or come near the altar, hen they are doing the ork of the holy place, so that they may be free from any sin causing death: this is to be an order for him and his seed after him for ever.
This is hat you are to do to make them holy, to do the ork of priests to me: Take one young ox and to male sheep, ithout any mark on them,
And unleavened bread, and unleavened cakes mixed ith oil, and thin unleavened cakes on hich oil has been put, made of the best bread-meal;
Put these in a basket and take them, ith the ox and the to sheep.
And let Aaron and his sons come to the door of the Tent of meeting, and there let them be ashed ith ater.
Take the robes, and put the coat and the dress and the ephod and the priest’s bag on Aaron; put the band of needleork round him,
And let the head-dress be placed on his head and the holy cron on the head-dress.
Then take the oil and put it on his head.
And take his sons and put their robes on them;
And put the linen bands round Aaron and his sons, and the head-dresses on them, to make them priests by my order for ever: so you are to make Aaron and his sons holy to me.
Then let the ox be taken in front of the Tent of meeting: and let Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.
And you are to put the ox to death before the Lord at the door of the Tent of meeting.
Then take some of the blood of the ox, and put it on the horns of the altar ith your finger, draining out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.
And take all the fat covering the inside of the ox, and the fat joining the liver and the to kidneys ith the fat round them, and let them be burned on the altar;
But the flesh of the ox and its skin and its aste parts are to be burned outside the circle of the tents, for it is a sin-offering.
Then take one of the sheep, and let Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head.
Then let it be put to death, so that the sides of the altar are marked ith its blood.
Then the sheep is to be cut up into its parts, and after ashing its legs and its inside parts, you are to put them ith the parts and the head,
And let them all be burned on the altar as a burned offering to the Lord: a seet smell, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
Then take the other sheep; and after Aaron and his sons have put their hands on its head,

You are to put the sheep to death, and take some of its blood and put it on the point of Aaron’s right ear, and of the right ears of his sons, and on the thumbs of their right hands and the great toes of their right feet, dropping the rest of the blood on the sides of the altar.
Then take some of the blood on the altar, and the oil, and put it on Aaron and his robes and on his sons and on their robes, so that he and his robes and his sons and their robes may be made holy.

Then take the fat of the sheep, the fat tail, the fat covering the insides, and the fat joining the liver and the to kidneys ith the fat round them, and the right leg; for by the offering of this sheep they are to be marked out as priests:
And take one bit of bread and one cake of oiled bread and one thin cake out of the basket of unleavened bread hich is before the Lord:
And put them all on the hands of Aaron and of his sons, to be aved for a ave offering before the Lord.
Then take them from their hands, and let them be burned on the burned offering on the altar, a seet smell before the Lord, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
Then take the breast of Aaron’s sheep, aving it before the Lord; and it is to be your part of the offering.
So you are to make holy the breast of the sheep hich is aved and the leg hich is lifted up on high, that is, of the sheep hich is offered for Aaron and his sons;

And it ill be their part as a right for ever from the children of Israel, it is a special offering from the children of Israel, made from their peace-offerings, a special offering lifted up to the Lord.
And Aaron’s holy robes ill be used by his sons after him; they ill put them on hen they are made priests.
For seven days the son ho becomes priest in his place ill put them on hen he comes into the Tent of meeting to do the ork of the holy place.
Then take the sheep of the ave offering and let its flesh be cooked in ater in a holy place.
And let Aaron and his sons make a meal of it, ith the bread in the basket, at the door of the Tent of meeting.
All those things hich ere used as offerings to take aay sin, and to make them holy to be priests, they may have for food: but no one ho is not a priest may have them, for they are holy food.
And if any of the flesh of the offering or of the bread is over till the morning, let it be burned ith fire; it is not to be used for food, for it is holy.
All these things you are to do to Aaron and his sons as I have given you orders: for seven days the ork of making them priests is to go on.
Every day an ox is to be offered as a sin-offering, to take aay sins: and by this offering on it, you ill make the altar clean from sin; and you are to put oil on it and make it holy.
For seven days you are to make offerings for the altar and make it holy, so that it may become completely holy, and anything touching it ill become holy.
No this is the offering hich you are to make on the altar: to lambs in their first year, every day regularly.
One lamb is to be offered in the morning and the other in the evening:
And ith the one lamb, a tenth part of an ephah of the best meal, mixed ith a fourth part of a hin of clear oil; and the fourth part of a hin of ine for a drink offering.
And the other lamb is to be offered in the evening, and ith it the same meal offering and drink offering, for a seet smell, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
