This is to be a regular burned offering made from generation to generation, at the door of the Tent of meeting before the Lord, here I ill come face to face ith you and have talk ith you.
There I ill come face to face ith the children of Israel, and the Tent ill be made holy by my glory
I ill make holy the Tent of meeting and the altar: and Aaron and his sons I ill make holy, to be my priests
Among the children of Israel I ill make my living-place, and I ill be their God.
And they ill see that I am the Lord their God, ho took them out of the land of Egypt, so that I might be ever ith them: I am the Lord their God.
And you are to make an altar for the burning of perfume; of hard ood let it be made.
The altar is to be square, a cubit long and a cubit ide, and to cubits high, and its horns are to be made of the same.
It is to be plated ith the best gold, the top of it and the sides and the horns, ith an edging of gold all round it.
Under the edge on the to opposite sides, you are to make to gold rings, to take the rods for lifting it.
And make these rods of the same ood, plating them ith gold.
And let it be placed in front of the veil before the ark of the la, before the cover hich is over the la, here I ill come face to face ith you.
And on this altar seet spices are to be burned by Aaron every morning hen he sees to the lights.
And every evening, hen he puts the lights up in their places, the spices are to be burned, a seet-smelling smoke going up before the Lord from generation to generation for ever.
No strange perfume, no burned offering or meal offering, and no drink offering is to be offered on it.
And once every year Aaron is to make its horns clean: ith the blood of the sin-offering he is to make it clean once every year from generation to generation: it is most holy to the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,
When you are taking the number of the children of Israel, let every man ho is numbered give to the Lord a price for his life, so that no disease may come on them hen they are numbered.
And this is hat they are to give; let every man ho is numbered give half a shekel, by the scale of the holy place: ( the shekel being valued at tenty gerahs:) this money is an offering to the Lord.
Everyone ho is numbered, from tenty years old and over, is to give an offering to the Lord.
The man of ealth is to give no more and the poor man no less than the half-shekel of silver, hen the offering is made to the Lord as the price for your lives.

And you are to take this money from the children of Israel to be used for the ork of the Tent of meeting, to keep the memory of the children of Israel before the Lord and to be the price of your lives.
And the Lord said to Moses,
You are to make a brass ashing-vessel, ith a brass base; and put it beteen the Tent of meeting and the altar, ith ater in it;
That it may be used by Aaron and his sons for ashing their hands and feet;
Whenever they go into the Tent of meeting they are to be ashed ith ater, to keep them from death; and henever they come near to do the ork of the altar, or to make an offering by fire to the Lord,
Their hands and feet are to be ashed. so that they may be safe from death: this is an order to them for ever; to him and his seed from generation to generation.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Take the best spices, five hundred shekels’ eight of liquid myrrh, and of seet cinnamon half as much, that is, to hundred and fifty shekels, and to hundred and fifty shekels of seet calamus,
And of cassia, five hundred shekels’ eight measured by the scale of the holy place, and of olive oil a hin:
And make these into a holy oil, a perfume made by the art of the perfume-maker; it is to be a holy oil.
This oil is to be put on the Tent of meeting, and on the ark of the la,
And on the table and all its vessels, and on the support for the lights, ith its vessels, and on the altar for burning spices,
And on the altar of burned offerings ith its vessels, and on the ashing-vessel and its base.
And you are to make them most holy; anything touching them ill become holy.
And put the oil on Aaron and his sons, making them holy to do the ork of priests to me.
And say to the children of Israel, This is to be the Lord’s holy oil, from generation to generation.
It is not to be used for man’s flesh, and no other is to be made like it: holy it is, and you are to keep it holy.
Whoever makes any like it, or puts it on one ho is not a priest, ill be cut off from his people.
And the Lord said to Moses, Take seet spices, stacte and onycha and galbanum, ith the best frankincense, in equal eights;
And make from them a perfume, such as is made by the art of the perfume-maker, mixed ith salt, and clean and holy.
And put some of it, crushed very small, in front of the ark in the Tent of meeting, here I ill come face to face ith you; it is to be most holy.
You are not to make any perfume like it for yourselves: it is to be kept holy to the Lord.
Whoever makes any like it, for its seet smell, ill be cut off from his people.
And the Lord said to Moses,
I have made selection of Bezalel, the son of Uri, by name, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah:
And I have given him the spirit of God and made him ise and full of knoledge and expert in every sort of handork,
To do all sorts of delicate ork in gold and silver and brass;
In cutting stones for framing, and to do every form of oodork.

And I have made selection of Oholiab ith him, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and in the hearts of all ho are ise I have put the knoledge to make hatever I have given you orders to have made;
The Tent of meeting, and the ark of the la, and the cover hich is on it, and all the things for the tent,
And the table ith its vessels, and the holy light-support ith all its vessels, and the altar for the burning of spices,
And the altar of burned offerings ith all its vessels, and the ashing-vessel ith its base,
And the robes of needleork, the holy robes for Aaron and for his sons, for their use hen acting as priests,
And the holy oil, and the perfume of seet spices for the holy place; they ill do hatever I have given you orders to have done.
And the Lord said to Moses,

Say to the children of Israel that they are to keep my Sabbaths; for the Sabbath day is a sign beteen me and you through all your generations; so that you may see that I am the Lord ho makes you holy.
So you are to keep the Sabbath as a holy day; and anyone not honouring it ill certainly be put to death: hoever does any ork on that day ill be cut off from his people.
Six days may ork be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the Lord; hoever does any ork on the Sabbath day is to be put to death.
And the children of Israel are to keep the Sabbath holy, from generation to generation, by an eternal agreement.
It is a sign beteen me and the children of Israel for ever; because in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he took his rest and had pleasure in it.
And hen his talk ith Moses on Mount Sinai as ended, he gave him the to stones of the la, to stones on hich as the riting made by the finger of God.

And hen the people sa that Moses as a long time coming don from the mountain, they all came to Aaron and said to him, Come, make us a god to go before us: as for this Moses, ho took us up out of the land of Egypt, e have no idea hat has become of him.
Then Aaron said to them, Take off the gold rings hich are in the ears of your ives and your sons and your daughters, and give them to me.
And all the people took the gold rings from their ears and gave them to Aaron.
And he took the gold from them and, hammering it ith an instrument, he made it into the metal image of a young ox: and they said, This is your god, O Israel, ho took you out of the land of Egypt.
And hen Aaron sa this, he made an altar before it, and made a public statement, saying, Tomorro there ill be a feast to the Lord.
So early on the day after they got up and made burned offerings and peace-offerings; and took their seats at the feast, and then gave themselves to pleasure.
And the Lord said to Moses, Go don quickly; for your people, hom you took out of the land of Egypt, are turned to evil ays;

Even no they are turned aay from the rule I gave them, and have made themselves a metal ox and given orship to it and offerings, saying, This is your god, O Israel, ho took you up out of the land of Egypt.
And the Lord said to Moses, I have been atching this people, and I see that they are a stiff-necked people.
No do not get in my ay, for my rath is burning against them; I ill send destruction on them, but of you I ill make a great nation.
But Moses made prayer to God, saying, Lord, hy is your rath burning against your people hom you took out of the land of Egypt, ith great poer and ith the strength of your hand?

Why let the Egyptians say, He took them out to an evil fate, to put them to death on the mountains, cutting them off from the earth? Let your rath be turned aay from them, and send not this evil on your people.

Have in mind Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, to hom you gave your oath, saying, I ill make your seed like the stars of heaven in number, and all this land ill I give to your seed, as I said, to be their heritage for ever.
So the Lord let himself be turned from his purpose of sending punishment on his people.
Then Moses came don the mountain ith the to stones of the la in his hand; the stones had riting on their to sides, on the front and on the back.
The stones ere the ork of God, and the riting as the riting of God, cut on the stones.
No hen the noise and the voices of the people came to the ears of Joshua, he said to Moses, There is a noise of ar in the tents.
And Moses said, It is not the voice of men ho are overcoming in the fight, or the cry of those ho have been overcome; it is the sound of songs hich comes to my ear.
And hen he came near the tents he sa the image of the ox, and the people dancing; and in his rath Moses let the stones go from his hands, and they ere broken at the foot of the mountain.
And he took the ox hich they had made, burning it in the fire and crushing it to poder, and he put it in the ater and made the children of Israel take a drink of it.
And Moses said to Aaron, What did the people do to you that you let this great sin come on them?
And Aaron said, Let not my lord be angry; you have seen ho the purposes of this people are evil.
For they said to me, Make us a god to go before us: as for this Moses, ho took us up out of the land of Egypt, e have no idea hat has come to him.
Then I said to them, Whoever has any gold, let him take it off; so they gave it to me, and I put it in the fire, and this image of an ox came out.
And Moses sa that the people ere out of control, for Aaron had let them loose to their shame before their haters:
Then Moses took his place at the ay into the tents, and said, Whoever is on the Lord’s side, let him come to me. And all the sons of Levi came together to him.

And he said to them, This is the ord of the Lord, the God of Israel: Let every man take his sord at his side, and go from one end of the tents to the other, putting to death his brother and his friend and his neighbour.
And the sons of Levi did as Moses said; and about three thousand of the people ere put to death that day.
And Moses said, You have made yourselves priests to the Lord this day; for every one of you has made the offering of his son and his brother; the blessing of the Lord is on you this day.
And on the day after, Moses said to the people, Great has been your sin: but I ill go up to the Lord, and see if I may get forgiveness for your sin.
Then Moses ent back to the Lord and said, This people has done a great sin, making themselves a god of gold;
But no, if you ill give them forgiveness — but if not, let my name be taken out of your book.
And the Lord said to Moses, Whoever has done evil against me ill be taken out of my book.
But no, go, take the people into that place of hich I have given you ord; see, my angel ill go before you: but hen the time of my judging has come, I ill send punishment on them for their sin.
And the Lord sent punishment on the people because they gave orship to the ox hich Aaron made.

And the Lord said to Moses, Go forard from this place, you and the people hom you have taken up out of the land of Egypt, to that land about hich I made an oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, To your seed ill I give it.
And I ill send an angel before you, driving out the Canaanite and the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite:
Go up to that land floing ith milk and honey; but I ill not go up among you, for you are a stiff-necked people, for fear that I send destruction on you hile you are on the ay.
Hearing this bad nes the people ere full of grief, and no one put on his ornaments.

And the Lord said to Moses, Say to the children of Israel, You are a stiff-necked people: if I come among you, even for a minute, I ill send destruction on you; so take off all your ornaments, so that I may see hat to do ith you.
So the children of Israel took off their ornaments at Mount Horeb, and did not put them on again.

No it as Moses’ ay to put up the Tent of meeting outside the tent-circle, at some distance aay; giving it the name of The Tent of meeting. And everyone desiring to make his prayer to the Lord ent to the Tent of meeting outside the tent-circle.
And henever Moses ent out to the Tent of meeting, all the people got up and everyone ent to the door of his tent, looking after Moses till he ent inside the Tent.
And henever Moses ent into the Tent, the pillar of cloud came don, and took its place by the door of the Tent, as long as the Lord as talking ith Moses.
And all the people sa the cloud at the door of the Tent, and they ent don on their faces, everyone at the door of his tent.

And the Lord had talk ith Moses face to face, as a man may have talk ith his friend. And hen Moses came back to the tents, his servant, the young man Joshua, the son of Nun, did not come aay from the Tent.

And Moses said to the Lord, See, you say to me, Be this people’s guide on their journey, but you have not made clear to me hom you ill send ith me. But you have said, I have knoledge of you by name, and you have grace in my eyes.
If then I have grace in your eyes, let me see your ays, so that I may have knoledge of you and be certain of your grace; and my prayer is that you ill keep in mind that this nation is your people.
And he said, I myself ill go ith you and give you rest.
And Moses said, If you yourself are not going ith us, do not send us on from here.
For is not the fact of your going ith us the sign that I and this people have grace in your eyes, so that e, that is, I and your people, are separate from all other people on the face of the earth?
And the Lord said to Moses, I ill do as you say: for you have grace in my eyes, and I have knoledge of you by your name.
And Moses said, O Lord, let me see your glory.
And he said, I ill make all the light of my being come before you, and ill make clear to you hat I am; I ill be kind to those to hom I ill be kind, and have mercy on those on hom I ill have mercy.
But it is not possible for you to see my face, for no man may see me and still go on living.
And the Lord said, See, there is a place near me, and you may take your place on the rock:
And hen my glory goes by, I ill put you in a hole in the rock, covering you ith my hand till I have gone past:
Then I ill take aay my hand, and you ill see my back: but my face is not to be seen.
And the Lord said to Moses, Make to other stones like the first to; and I ill put on them the ords hich ere on the first stones, hich ere broken by you.
And be ready by the morning, and come up on Mount Sinai, and come before me there in the morning, on the top of the mountain.
No one is to come up ith you, and let no man be seen anyhere on the mountain; let no flocks or herds come near to get their food at its foot.
So Moses got to stones cut like the first; and early in the morning he ent up Mount Sinai, as the Lord had said, ith the to stones in his hand.
And the Lord came don in the cloud and took his place by the side of Moses, and Moses gave orship to the name of the Lord.
And the Lord ent past before his eyes, saying, The Lord, the Lord, a God full of pity and grace, slo to rath and great in mercy and faith;

Having mercy on thousands, overlooking evil and rongdoing and sin; he ill not let rongdoers go free, but ill send punishment on children for the sins of their fathers, and on their children’s children to the third and fourth generation.
Then Moses quickly ent don on his face in orship.
And he said, If no I have grace in your eyes, let the Lord go among us, for this is a stiff-necked people, and give us forgiveness for our rongdoing and our sin, and take us for your heritage.

And the Lord said, See, this is hat I ill undertake: before the eyes of your people I ill do onders, such as have not been done in all the earth or in any nation: and all your people ill see the ork of the Lord, for hat I am about to do for you is greatly to be feared.
Take care to do the orders hich I give you today; I ill send out from before you the Amorite and the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.
But take care, and do not make any agreement ith the people of the land here you are going, for it ill be a cause of sin to you.
But their altars are to be overturned and their pillars broken and their images cut don:
For you are to be orshippers of no other god: for the Lord is a God ho ill not give his honour to another.
So see that you make no agreement ith the people of the land, and do not go after their gods, or take part in their offerings, or be guests at their feasts,
Or take their daughters for your sons; for hen their daughters give orship before their gods, they ill make your sons take part ith them.
Make for yourselves no gods of metal.
Keep the feast of unleavened bread; for seven days your food is to be bread ithout leaven, as I gave you orders, at the regular time in the month Abib; for in that month you came out of Egypt.
Every first male child is mine; the first male birth of your cattle, the first male of every ox and sheep.

A lamb may be given in payment for the young of an ass, but if you ill not make payment for it, its neck ill have to be broken. For all the first of your sons you are to make payment. No one is to come before me ithout an offering.
Six days let ork be done, but on the seventh day take your rest: at ploughing time and at the grain-cutting you are to have a day for rest.
And you are to keep the feast of eeks hen you get in the first-fruits of the grain, and the feast at the turn of the year hen you take in the produce of your fields.
Three times in the year let all your males come before the Lord, the God of Israel.
For I ill send out the nations before you and make ide the limits of your land; and no man ill make an attempt to take your land hile you go up to give orship to the Lord, three times in the year.
No leaven is to be offered ith the blood of my offering, and the offering of the Passover feast may not be kept till the morning.
Take the first-fruits of your land as an offering to the house of the Lord your God. Let not the young goat be cooked in its mother’s milk
And the Lord said to Moses, Put all these ords in riting; for on them is based the agreement hich I ill make ith you.
And for forty days and forty nights Moses as there ith the Lord, and in that time he had no food or drink. And he put in riting on the stones the ords of the agreement, the ten rules of the la.
No hen Moses came don from Mount Sinai, ith the to stones in his hand, he as not conscious that his face as shining because of his talk ith God.
But hen Aaron and all the children of Israel sa Moses, and the shining of his face, they ould not come near him for fear.
Then Moses sent for them; and Aaron, ith the chiefs of the people, came to him; and Moses had talk ith them.
And later, all the children of Israel came near, and he gave them all the orders hich the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
And at the end of his talk ith them, Moses put a veil over his face.
But henever Moses ent in before the Lord to have talk ith him, he took off the veil till he came out. And henever he came out he said to the children of Israel hat he had been ordered to say;
And the children of Israel sa that the face of Moses as shining: so Moses put the veil over his face again till he ent to the Lord.
And Moses sent for all the children of Israel to come together, and said to them, This is hat the Lord has said and these are his orders.
Six days let ork be done, but the seventh day is to be a holy day to you, a Sabbath of rest to the Lord; hoever does any ork on that day is to be put to death.
No fire is to be lighted in any of your houses on the Sabbath day.
And Moses said to all the meeting of the children of Israel, This is the order hich the Lord has given:
Take from among you an offering to the Lord; everyone ho has the impulse in his heart, let him give his offering to the Lord; gold and silver and brass;
And blue and purple and red and the best linen and goats’ hair,
And sheepskins coloured red, and leather, and hard ood,
And oil for the lights, and spices for the holy oil and for the seet perfumes for burning.
And beryls and jeels to be cut for the ephod and for the priest’s bag.
And let every ise-hearted man among you come and make hatever has been ordered by the Lord;
The House and its tent and its cover, its hooks and its boards, its rods and its pillars and its bases;
The ark ith its cover and its rods and the veil hanging before it;
The table and its rods and all its vessels, and the holy bread;
And the support for the lights, ith its vessels and its lights and the oil for the light;
And the altar for burning spices, ith its rods, and the holy oil and the seet perfume, and the curtain for the door, at the door of the House;
The altar of burned offerings, ith its netork of brass, its rods, and all its vessels, the ashing-vessel and its base;
The hangings for the open space, its pillars and their bases, and the curtain for the dooray;
The nails for the House, and the nails for the open space and their cords;
The robes of needleork for the ork of the holy place, the holy robes for Aaron the priest, and the robes for his sons hen acting as priests.
And all the children of Israel ent aay from Moses.

And everyone hose heart as moved, everyone ho as guided by the impulse of his spirit, came ith his offering for the Lord, for hatever as needed for the Tent of meeting and its ork and for the holy robes.
They came, men and omen, all ho ere ready to give, and gave pins and nose-rings and finger-rings and neck-ornaments, all of gold; everyone gave an offering of gold to the Lord.
And everyone ho had blue and purple and red and the best linen and goats’ hair and sheepskins coloured red and leather, gave them.
Everyone ho had silver and brass gave an offering of them to the Lord; and everyone ho had hard ood, such as as needed for the ork, gave it.
And all the omen ho ere expert ith their hands, made cloth, and gave the ork of their hands, blue and purple and red and the best linen.
And those omen ho had the knoledge, made the goats’ hair into cloth.
And the rulers gave the beryls and the cut jeels for the ephod and the priest’s bag;
And the spice and the oil for the light, and the holy oil and the seet perfumes.
The children of Israel, every man and oman, from the impulse of their hearts, gave their offerings freely to the Lord for the ork hich the Lord had given Moses orders to have done.
And Moses said to the children of Israel, See, the Lord has made selection of Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;
And he has made him full of the spirit of God, in all isdom and knoledge and art of every sort;
As an expert designer of beautiful things, orking in gold and silver and brass;
Trained in the cutting of stones and the ornamenting of ood and in every sort of handork.
And he has given to him, and to Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, the poer of training others.

To them he has given knoledge of all the arts of the handorker, of the designer, and the expert orkman; of the maker of needleork in blue and purple and red and the best linen, and of the maker of cloth; in all the arts of the designer and the trained orkman they are expert.

So let Bezalel and Oholiab get to ork, ith every ise-hearted man to hom the Lord has given isdom and knoledge, to do hatever is necessary for the ordering of the holy place, as the Lord has given orders.
Then Moses sent for Bezalel and Oholiab, and for all the ise-hearted men to hom the Lord had given isdom, even everyone ho as moved by the impulse of his heart to come and take part in the ork:
And they took from Moses all the offerings hich the children of Israel had given for the building of the holy place. And still they ent on giving him more free offerings every morning.
Then the ise men, ho ere doing all the ork of the holy place, came from their ork;
And said to Moses, The people are giving much more than is needed for the ork hich the Lord has given us orders to do.
So Moses made an order and had it given out through all the tents, saying, Let no man or oman make any more offerings for the holy place. So the people ere kept from giving more.
For the material they had as enough and more than enough for all the ork hich had to be done.
Then all the expert orkmen among them made the House ith its ten curtains; of the best linen, blue and purple and red, they made them, ith inged ones orked by expert designers.
Every curtain as tenty-eight cubits long and four cubits ide, all of the same measure.
And five curtains ere joined together, and the other five curtains ere joined together.
And they put tists of blue cord on the edge of the outside curtain of the first group, and in the same ay on the outside curtain of the second group.
Fifty tists on the one curtain and fifty on the edge of the curtain of the other group; the tists being opposite to one another.
And they made fifty hooks of gold, joining the curtains one to another ith the hooks; and so the House as made.
And they made curtains of goats’ hair for the tent; eleven curtains ere made.
Every curtain as thirty cubits long and four cubits ide, all of the same measure.
Five curtains ere joined together to make one group, and six curtains ere joined together to make the other group.
And they put fifty tists of cord on the edge of the outside curtain of the first group, and fifty tists on the edge of the outside curtain of the second group,
And fifty hooks of brass for joining them together to make the tent.
And they made a cover of sheepskins coloured red, to go over the tent, and a cover of leather over that.
And for the uprights of the House they made boards of hard ood.
The boards ere ten cubits long and one cubit and a half ide.
Every board had to tongues fixed into it; all the boards ere made in this ay.
They made tenty boards for the south side of the House:
And for these tenty boards, forty silver bases, to bases under every board, to take its tongues.
And for the second side of the House, on the north, they made tenty boards,
With their forty silver bases, to bases for every board.
And for the est side of the House, at the back, they made six boards,
And to boards for the angles at the back.
These ere joined together at the base and at the top to one ring, so forming the to angles.
So there ere eight boards ith sixteen bases of silver, to bases under every board.
And they made rods of hard ood; five for the boards on one side of the House,
And five for the boards on the other side of the House, and five for the boards at the back, on the est.
The middle rod as made to go right through the rings of all the boards from one end to the other.
All the boards ere plated ith gold, and the rings through hich the rods ent ere of gold, and the rods ere plated ith gold.
And he made the veil of the best linen, blue and purple and red, orked ith inged ones designed by expert orkmen.
And they made four pillars for it of hard ood plated ith gold: they had hooks of gold and four silver bases.
And they made a curtain for the door of the tent, of the best linen ith needleork of blue and purple and red;
And five pillars for the curtain, ith their hooks; the heads of the pillars ere of gold and they ere circled ith bands of gold; and their five bases ere of brass.
And Bezalel made the ark of hard ood, to and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half ide and a cubit and a half high;
Plating it inside and out ith the best gold, and putting an edge of gold all round it.
And he made four gold rings for its four angles, to on one side and to on the other,
And rods of the same ood plated ith gold.
These rods he put in the rings at the sides of the ark, for lifting it.
And he made the cover all of gold, to and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half ide.
And he made to inged ones, hammered out of one bit of gold, for the to ends of the cover;
Placing one at one end and one at the other; the inged ones ere part of the cover.
And their ings ere stretched out over the cover; the faces of the inged ones ere opposite one another and facing the cover.
And he made the table of hard ood, to cubits long, a cubit ide and a cubit and a half high;
Plating it ith the best gold and putting a gold edge all round it.
And he made a frame all round it about as ide as a man’s hand, edged ith gold all round.
And he made four gold rings, and put the rings at the angles of its four feet.
The rings ere fixed under the frame to take the rods ith hich the table as to be lifted.
The rods for lifting the table he made of hard ood plated ith gold.
And all the table-vessels, the plates and spoons and basins and the cups for liquids, he made of the best gold.
Then he made the support for the lights, all of the best gold; its base and its pillar ere of hammered gold; its cups and buds and floers ere all made out of the same metal:
It had six branches coming out from its sides, three from one side and three from the other;
Every branch having three cups made like almond floers, every cup ith a bud and a floer on all the branches;
And on its pillar, four cups like almond floers, every one ith its bud and its floer;
And under every to branches a bud, made ith the branch, for all six branches of it.
The buds and the branches ere made of the same metal, all together one complete ork of the best hammered gold.
And he made the seven vessels for the lights, and all the necessary instruments for it, of gold.
A talent of the best gold as used for the making of it and its vessels.
And he made the altar for the burning of spices, using the same hard ood; it as square, a cubit long and a cubit ide and to cubits high; the horns made of the same.
The top and the sides and the horns ere all plated ith the best gold; and he put an edge of gold all round it.
And he made to gold rings, placing them on the to opposite sides under the edge, to take the rods for lifting it.
The rods he made of the same hard ood, plating them ith gold.
And he made the holy oil and the perfume of seet spices for burning, after the art of the perfume-maker.
The altar of burned offerings he made of hard ood; a square altar, five cubits long, five cubits ide and three cubits high,
And he put horns at its four angles made of the same, plating it all ith brass;
And brass as used for all the vessels of the altar, the baskets and the spades, the basins and the meat-hooks and the fire-trays; all the vessels he made of brass
And he made a netork of brass for the altar, under the frame round it, stretching half-ay up;
And four rings for the four angles of this netork, to take the rods.
The rods he made of hard ood plated ith brass.
He put the rods through the rings at the opposite sides of the altar for lifting it; he made the altar hollo, boarded in ith ood.
And he made the ashing-vessel of brass on a brass base, using the polished brass looking-glasses given by the omen ho did ork at the doors of the Tent of meeting.
To make the open space, he put hangings on the south side, of the best linen, a hundred cubits long:
Their tenty pillars and their tenty bases ere brass; and the hooks of the pillars and their bands ere of silver.
And for the north side. hangings a hundred cubits long, on tenty brass pillars in brass bases, ith silver hooks and bands.
And on the est side, hangings fifty cubits long, on ten pillars in ten bases, ith silver bands.
And on the east side, the open space as fifty cubits long.
The hangings on one side of the dooray ere fifteen cubits long, on three pillars ith their three bases;
And the same on the other side of the dooray; on this side and on that the hangings ere fifteen cubits long, on three pillars ith their three bases.
All the hangings ere of the best linen.
And the bases of the pillars ere of brass; their hooks and the bands round the tops of them ere of silver; all the pillars ere ringed ith silver.

And the curtain for the dooray of the open space as of the best linen, ith designs of blue and purple and red in needleork; it as tenty cubits long and five cubits high, to go ith the hangings round the sides.
There ere four pillars ith their bases, all of brass, the hooks being of silver, and their tops and their bands being covered ith silver.
All the nails used for the House and the open space round it ere of brass.
This is the price of the making of the House, even the House of itness, as it as valued by the ord of Moses, for the ork of the Levites under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything as the Lord had given orders to Moses.
And ith him as Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; a designer and a trained orkman, expert in needleork of blue and purple and red and the best linen.
The gold used for all the different ork done for the holy place, the gold hich as given, as tenty-nine talents, and seven hundred and thirty shekels in eight, by the scale of the holy place.
And the silver given by those ho ere numbered of the people as a hundred talents, and a thousand, seven hundred and seventy-five shekels in eight, by the scale of the holy place.
A beka, that is, half a shekel by the holy scale, for everyone ho as numbered; there ere six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty men of tenty years old and over.
Of this silver, a hundred talents as used for making the bases of the pillars of the holy place and of the veil; a talent for every base.
And a thousand, seven hundred and seventy-five shekels of silver as used to make the hooks for the pillars, and for plating the tops of the pillars and for making their bands.
The brass hich as given as seventy talents, to thousand four hundred shekels;
From it he made the bases of the dooray of the Tent of meeting and the brass altar and the netork for it and all the vessels for the altar,
And the bases for the open space all round and for its dooray, and all the nails for the House and for the open space.
And from the needleork of blue and purple and red they made the robes used for the ork of the holy place, and the holy robes for Aaron, as the Lord had given orders to Moses.
The ephod he made of gold and blue and purple and red and the best linen;
Hammering the gold into thin plates and cutting it into ires to be orked into the blue and the purple and the red and the linen by the designer.
And they made to bands for joining its edges together at the top of the arms.
And the beautifully orked band hich ent on it as of the same design and the same material, orked in gold and blue and purple and red and tisted linen-ork, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
Then they made the beryl stones, fixed in tisted frames of gold and cut like the cutting of a stamp, ith the names of the children of Israel.
These he put on the ephod, over the arm-holes, to be stones of memory for the children of Israel, as the Lord had said to Moses.
The priest’s bag as designed like the ephod, of the best linen orked ith gold and blue and purple and red.
It as square and folded in to, as long and as ide as the stretch of a man’s hand;
And on it they put four lines of stones: in the first line as a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald;
In the second, a ruby, a sapphire, and an onyx;
In the third, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
In the fourth, a topaz, a beryl, and a jasper; they ere fixed in tisted frames of gold.
There ere telve stones for the telve tribes of Israel; on every one the name of one of the tribes of Israel as cut, like the cutting of a stamp.
And on the bag they put gold chains, tisted like cords.
And they made to gold frames and to gold rings, the rings being fixed to the ends of the priest’s bag;
And they put the to tisted chains on the to rings at the ends of the priest’s bag;
And the other to ends of the chains ere joined to the to frames and fixed to the front of the ephod over the arm-holes.
And they made to rings of gold and put them on the to loer ends of the bag, on the inner side nearest to the ephod.
And to other gold rings ere put on the front of the ephod, over the arm-holes, at the join, and over the orked band.
And the rings on the bag ere fixed to the rings of the ephod by a blue cord, keeping it in place over the band, so that the bag might not get loose, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
The robe hich ent ith the ephod as made all of blue;
With a hole at the top in the middle, like the hole in the coat of a fighting-man, edged ith a band to make it strong.
The skirts of the robe ere orked all round ith fruits in blue and purple and red made of tisted linen.
And beteen the fruits all round the skirt they put gold bells, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
All round the skirt of the robe ere bells and fruits in turn.
The coats for Aaron and his sons they made of the best linen;
And the tisted head-dress for Aaron, and beautiful head-dresses of linen, and linen trousers,
And a linen band orked ith a design of blue and purple and red, as the Lord had said to Moses.
The plate for the holy cron as made of the best gold, and on it ere cut these ords, HOLY TO THE LORD.
It as fixed to the head-dress by a blue cord, as the Lord had given orders to Moses.
So all the ork on the House of the Tent of meeting as done; as the Lord had given orders to Moses, so the children of Israel did it.
Then they took the House to Moses, the tent ith all the things for it; its hooks, its boards, its rods, its pillars, and its bases;
The outer cover of sheepskins coloured red, and the cover of leather, and the veil for the dooray;
The ark of the la, ith its rods and its cover;
The table, ith all its vessels and the holy bread;
The support for the lights, ith the vessels for the lights to be put in their places on it, and all its vessels, and the oil for the lights;
And the gold altar, and the holy oil, and the seet perfume for burning, and the curtain for the dooray of the tent;
And the brass altar, ith its netork of brass, and its rods and all its vessels, and the ashing-vessel and its base;

The hangings for the open space, ith the pillars and their bases, and the curtain for the dooray, and the cords and nails, and all the instruments necessary for the ork of the House of the Tent of meeting;
The robes for use in the holy place, and the holy robes for Aaron and his sons hen acting as priests.
The children of Israel did everything as the Lord had given orders to Moses.
Then Moses, hen he sa all their ork and sa that they had done everything as the Lord had said, gave them his blessing.
And the Lord said to Moses,
On the first day of the first month you are to put up the House of the Tent of meeting.
And inside it put the ark of the la, hanging the veil before it.
And put the table inside, placing all the things on it in order; and put in the support for the lights, and let its lights be burning.
And put the gold altar for burning perfumes in front of the ark of the la, hanging the curtain over the dooray of the House.
And put the altar of burned offerings before the dooray of the House of the Tent of meeting.
And let the ashing-vessel, ith ater in it, be put beteen the Tent of meeting and the altar.
And put up the hangings forming the open space all round it, ith the curtain over its dooray.
And take the holy oil and put it on the House and everything in it, and make it and everything in it holy:
And put oil on the altar of burned offering, and make it and all its vessels holy; this altar is to be most holy.
And put oil on the ashing-vessel and its base, and make them holy.
Then let Aaron and his sons come to the door of the Tent of meeting; and after ashing them ith ater,
You are to put on Aaron the holy robes; and you are to put oil on him, and make him holy, so that he may be my priest.
And take his sons ith him and put coats on them;
And put oil on them as you did on their father, so that they may be my priests: the putting on of oil ill make them priests for ever, from generation to generation.
And Moses did this; as the Lord gave him orders, so he did.
So on the first day of the first month in the second year the House as put up.
Moses put up the House; placing its bases in position and lifting up its uprights, putting in the rods and planting the pillars in their places;
Stretching the outer tent over it, and covering it, as the Lord had given him orders.
And he took the la and put it inside the ark, and put the rods at its side and the cover over it;
And he took the ark into the House, hanging up the veil before it as the Lord had given him orders.
And he put the table in the Tent of meeting, on the north side outside the veil.
And he put the bread on it in order before the Lord, as the Lord had said.
The support for the lights he put in the Tent of meeting, opposite the table, on the south side:
Lighting the lights before the Lord, as the Lord had given him orders.
And he put the gold altar in the Tent of meeting, in front of the veil:
Burning seet perfumes on it, as the Lord had given him orders.
And he put up the curtain at the dooray of the House.
And at the door of the House of the Tent of meeting, he put the altar of burned offerings, offering on it the burned offering and the meal offering, as the Lord had given him orders.
And beteen the altar and the Tent of meeting he put the vessel ith ater in it for ashing.
In it the hands and feet of Moses and Aaron and his sons ere ashed,
Whenever they ent into the Tent of meeting, and hen they came near the altar, as the Lord had given orders to Moses.
And he put up the hangings forming the open space round the House and the altar, and put the curtain over the dooray. So Moses made the ork complete.
Then the cloud came don covering the Tent of meeting, and the House as full of the glory of the Lord;
So that Moses as not able to go into the Tent of meeting, because the cloud as resting on it, and the House as full of the glory of the Lord.
And henever the cloud as taken up from the House, the children of Israel ent forard on their journey:
But hile the cloud as there, they made no move till it as taken up.
For the cloud of the Lord as resting on the House by day, and at night there as fire in the cloud, before the eyes of all the people of Israel, and so it as through all their journeys.
And the voice of the Lord came to Moses out of the Tent of meeting, saying,
Give these orders to the children of Israel: When anyone of you makes an offering to the Lord, you are to take it from the cattle, from the herd or from the flock.
If the offering is a burned offering of the herd, let him give a male ithout a mark: he is to give it at the door of the Tent of meeting so that he may be pleasing to the Lord.
And he is to put his hand on the head of the burned offering and it ill be taken for him, to take aay his sin.
And the ox is to be put to death before the Lord: then Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to take the blood and put some of it on and round the altar hich is at the door of the Tent of meeting.
And the burned offering is to be skinned and cut up into its parts.
And Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to put fire on the altar and put the ood in order on the fire:
And Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to put the parts, the head and the fat, in order on the ood hich is on the fire on the altar:
But its inside parts and its legs are to be ashed ith ater, and it ill all be burned on the altar by the priest for a burned offering, an offering made by fire, for a seet smell to the Lord.
And if his offering is of the flock, a burned offering of sheep or goats, let him give a male ithout a mark.
And he is to put it to death on the north side of the altar before the Lord: and Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to put some of the blood on and round the altar.
And the offering is to be cut into its parts, ith its head and its fat; and the priest is to put them in order on the ood hich is on the fire on the altar:

But the inside parts and the legs are to be ashed ith ater; and the priest ill make an offering of all of it, burning it on the altar: it is a burned offering, an offering made by fire, for a seet smell to the Lord.
And if his offering to the Lord is a burned offering of birds, then he is to make his offering of doves or of young pigeons.
And the priest is to take it to the altar, and after its head has been tisted off, it is to be burned on the altar, and its blood drained out on the side of the altar:
And he is to take aay its stomach, ith its feathers, and put it don by the east side of the altar, here the burned aste is put:

And let it be broken open at the ings, but not cut in to; and let it be burned on the altar by the priest on the ood hich is on the fire; it is a burned offering; an offering made by fire for a seet smell to the Lord.
And hen anyone makes a meal offering to the Lord, let his offering be of the best meal, ith oil on it and perfume:

And let him take it to Aaron’s sons, the priests; and having taken in his hand some of the meal and of the oil, ith all the perfume, let him give it to the priest to be burned on the altar, as a sign, an offering made by fire, for a seet smell to the Lord.
And the rest of the meal offering ill be for Aaron and his sons; it is most holy among the Lord’s fire offerings.
And hen you give a meal offering cooked in the oven, let it be of unleavened cakes of the best meal mixed ith oil, or thin unleavened cakes covered ith oil.
And if you give a meal offering cooked on a flat plate, let it be of the best meal, unleavened and mixed ith oil.
Let it be broken into bits, and put oil on it; it is a meal offering.
And if your offering is of meal cooked in fat over the fire, let it be made of the best meal mixed ith oil.
And you are to give the meal offering made of these things to the Lord, and let the priest take it to the altar.
And he is to take from the meal offering a part, for a sign, burning it on the altar; an offering made by fire for a seet smell to the Lord.
And the rest of the meal offering ill be for Aaron and his sons; it is most holy among the Lord’s fire offerings.
No meal offering hich you give to the Lord is to be made ith leaven; no leaven or honey is to be burned as an offering made by fire to the Lord.
You may give them as an offering of first-fruits to the Lord, but they are not to go up as a seet smell on the altar.
And every meal offering is to be salted ith salt; your meal offering is not to be ithout the salt of the agreement of your God: ith all your offerings give salt.
And if you give a meal offering of first-fruits to the Lord, give, as your offering of first-fruits, ne grain, made dry ith fire, crushed ne grain.
And put oil on it and perfume: it is a meal offering.
And part of the meal of the offering and part of the oil and all the perfume is to be burned for a sign by the priest: it is an offering made by fire to the Lord.
And if his offering is given for a peace-offering; if he gives of the herd, male or female, let him give it ithout any mark on it, before the Lord.
And he is to put his hand on the head of his offering and put it to death at the door of the Tent of meeting; and Aaron’s sons, the priests, are to put some of the blood on and round the altar.
And he is to give of the peace-offering, as an offering made by fire to the Lord; the fat covering the inside parts and all the fat on the inside parts,
And the to kidneys, and the fat on them, hich is by the top part of the legs, and the fat joining the liver and the kidneys, he is to take aay;
That it may be burned by Aaron’s sons on the altar, on the burned offering hich is on the ood on the fire: it is an offering made by fire of a seet smell to the Lord.
And if hat he gives for a peace-offering to the Lord is of the flock, let him give a male or female, ithout any mark on it.
If his offering is a lamb, then let it be placed before the Lord:
And he is to put his hand on the head of his offering and put it to death before the Tent of meeting; and Aaron’s sons are to put some of its blood on and round the altar.

And of the peace-offering, let him give an offering made by fire to the Lord; the fat of it, all the fat tail, he is to take aay near the backbone; and the fat covering the inside parts and all the fat on the inside parts,
And the to kidneys, ith the fat on them, hich is by the top part of the legs, and the fat joining the liver and the kidneys, he is to take aay;
That it may be burned by the priest on the altar; it is the food of the offering made by fire to the Lord.
And if his offering is a goat, then let it be placed before the Lord,
And let him put his hand on the head of it and put it to death before the Tent of meeting; and the sons of Aaron are to put some of its blood on and round the altar.
And of it let him make his offering, an offering made by fire to the Lord; the fat covering the inside parts and all the fat on the inside parts,
And the to kidneys, ith the fat on them, hich is by the top part of the legs, and the fat joining the liver and the kidneys, let him take aay;
That it may be burned by the priest on the altar; it is the food of the offering made by fire for a seet smell: all the fat is the Lord’s.
Let it be an order for ever, through all your generations, in all your houses, that you are not to take fat or blood for food.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel: These are the offerings of anyone ho does rong through error, doing any of the things hich by the Lord’s order are not to be done:
If the chief priest by doing rong becomes a cause of sin to the people, then let him give to the Lord for the sin hich he has done, an ox, ithout any mark, for a sin-offering.
And he is to take the ox to the door of the Tent of meeting before the Lord; and put his hand on its head and put it to death before the Lord.
And the chief priest is to take some of its blood and take it to the Tent of meeting;
And the priest is to put his finger in the blood, shaking drops of it before the Lord seven times, in front of the veil of the holy place.

And the priest is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar on hich perfume is burned before the Lord in the Tent of meeting, draining out all the rest of the blood of the ox at the base of the altar of burned offering hich is at the door of the Tent of meeting.
And he is to take aay all the fat of the ox of the sin-offering; the fat covering the inside parts and all the fat of the inside parts,
And the to kidneys, ith the fat on them, hich is by the top part of the legs, and the fat joining the liver and the kidneys, he is to take aay,
As it is taken from the ox of the peace-offering; and it is to be burned by the priest on the altar of burned offerings.
And the skin of the ox and all its flesh, ith its head and its legs and its inside parts and its aste,
All the ox, he is to take aay outside the circle of the tents into a clean place here the burned aste is put, and there it is to be burned on ood ith fire.
And if all the people of Israel do rong, ithout anyone’s knoledge; if they have done any of the things hich by the Lord’s order are not to be done, causing sin to come on them;
When the sin hich they have done comes to light, then let all the people give an ox for a sin-offering, and take it before the Tent of meeting.
And let the chiefs of the people put their hands on its head before the Lord, and put the ox to death before the Lord.
And the priest is to take some of its blood to the Tent of meeting;
And put his finger in the blood, shaking drops of the blood seven times before the Lord in front of the veil.

And he is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar hich is before the Lord in the Tent of meeting; and all the rest of the blood is to be drained out at the base of the altar of burned offering at the door of the Tent of meeting.
And he is to take off all its fat, burning it on the altar.
Let him do ith the ox as he did ith the ox of the sin-offering; and the priest ill take aay their sin and they ill have forgiveness.
Then let the ox be taken aay outside the tent-circle, that it may be burned as the other ox as burned; it is the sin-offering for all the people.
If a ruler does rong, and in error does any of the things hich, by the order of the Lord his God, are not to be done, causing sin to come on him;
When the sin hich he has done is made clear to him, let him give for his offering a goat, a male ithout any mark.
And he is to put his hand on the head of the goat and put it to death in the place here they put to death the burned offering before the Lord: it is a sin-offering.

And the priest is to take some of the blood of the offering ith his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burned offering, draining out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burned offering.
And all the fat of it is to be burned on the altar like the fat of the peace-offering; and the priest ill take aay his sin and he ill have forgiveness.
And if any one of the common people does rong in error, doing any of the things hich the Lord has given orders are not to be done, causing sin to come on him;
When the sin hich he has done is made clear to him, then he is to give for his offering a goat, a female ithout any mark, for the sin hich he has done.
And he is to put his hand on the head of the sin-offering and put it to death in the place here they put to death the burned offering.
And the priest is to take some of the blood ith his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burned offering, and all the rest of its blood is to be drained out at the base of the altar.

And let all its fat be taken aay, as the fat is taken aay from the peace-offerings, and let it be burned on the altar by the priest for a seet smell to the Lord; and the priest ill take aay his sin and he ill have forgiveness.
And if he gives a lamb as his sin-offering, let it be a female ithout any mark;
And he is to put his hand on the head of the offering and put it to death for a sin-offering in the place here they put to death the burned offering.

And the priest is to take some of the blood of the offering ith his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burned offering, and all the rest of the blood is to be drained out at the base of the altar;

And let him take aay all its fat, as the fat is taken aay from the lamb of the peace-offerings; and let it be burned by the priest on the altar among the offerings made by fire to the Lord: and the priest ill take aay his sin and he ill have forgiveness.
And if anyone does rong by saying nothing hen he is put under oath as a itness of something he has seen or had knoledge of, then he ill be responsible:

If anyone becomes unclean through touching unconsciously some unclean thing, such as the dead body of an unclean beast or of unclean cattle or of any unclean animal hich goes flat on the earth, he ill be responsible:
Or if he becomes unclean through touching unconsciously any unclean thing of man, hatever it may be, hen it is made clear to him he ill be responsible:

Or if anyone, ithout thought, takes an oath to do evil or to do good, hatever he says ithout thought, ith an oath, having no knoledge of hat he is doing; hen it becomes clear to him, he ill be responsible for any of these things.
And hoever is responsible for any such sin, let him make a statement openly of his rongdoing;
And take to the Lord the offering for the rong hich he has done, a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin-offering, and the priest ill take aay his sin.
And if he has not money enough for a lamb, then let him give, for his offering to the Lord, to doves or to young pigeons; one for a sin-offering and one for a burned offering.
And let him take them to the priest, ho ill first give the sin-offering, tisting off its head from its neck, but not cutting it in to;
And he is to put drops of the blood of the offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood is to be drained out at the base of the altar; it is a sin-offering.
And the second is for a burned offering, in agreement ith the la; and the priest ill take aay his sin and he ill have forgiveness.

But if he has not enough money for to doves or to young pigeons, then let him give, for the sin he has done, the tenth part of an ephah of the best meal, for a sin-offering; let him put no oil on it, and no perfume, for it is a sin-offering.
And let him come to the priest ith it, and the priest ill take some of it in his hand, to be burned on the altar as a sign, among the offerings of the Lord made by fire: it is a sin-offering.
And the priest ill take aay his sin and he ill have forgiveness: and the rest of the offering ill be the priest’s, in the same ay as the meal offering.
And the Lord said to Moses,

If anyone is untrue, sinning in error in connection ith the holy things of the Lord, let him take his offering to the Lord, a male sheep from the flock, ithout any mark, of the value fixed by you in silver by shekels, by the scale of the holy place.

And he is to make payment to the priest for hat he has done rong in relation to the holy thing, together ith a fifth part of its value in addition; and the priest ill take aay his sin by the sheep of his offering, and he ill have forgiveness.
And if anyone does rong, and does any of the things hich the Lord has given orders are not to be done, though he has no knoledge of it, still he is in the rong and he is responsible.

Let him come to the priest ith a sheep, a male ithout any mark out of the flock, of the value fixed by you, as an offering for his error; and the priest ill take aay the sin hich he did in error, and he ill have forgiveness.
It is an offering for his error: he is certainly responsible before the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,

If anyone does rong, and is untrue to the Lord, acting falsely to his neighbour in connection ith something put in his care, or something given for a debt, or has taken aay anything by force, or has been cruel to his neighbour,
Or has taken a false oath about the loss of something hich he has come across by chance; if a man has done any of these evil things,
Causing sin to come on him, then he ill have to give back the thing he took by force or got by cruel acts, or the goods hich ere put in his care or the thing he came on by chance,
Or anything about hich he took a false oath; he ill have to give it all back, ith the addition of a fifth of its value, to him hose property it is, hen he has been judged to be in the rong.
Then let him take to the Lord the offering for his rongdoing; giving to the priest for his offering, a male sheep from the flock, ithout any mark, of the value fixed by you:
And the priest ill take aay his sin from before the Lord, and he ill have forgiveness for hatever crime he has done
And the Lord said to Moses,

Give orders to Aaron and to his sons, saying, This is the la for the burned offering: the offering is to be on the fire-ood on the altar all night till the morning; and the fire of the altar is to be kept burning.
And the priest is to put on his linen robes and his linen trousers, and take up hat is over of the offering after it has been burned on the altar, and put it by the side of the altar.
Then having taken off his linen robes and put on other clothing, he is to take it aay into a clean place, outside the tent-circle.

The fire on the altar is to be kept burning; it is never to go out; every morning the priest is to put ood on it, placing the burned offering in order on it, and there the fat of the peace-offering is to be burned.
Let the fire be kept burning on the altar at all times; it is never to go out.
And this is the la for the meal offering: it is to be offered to the Lord before the altar by the sons of Aaron.
The priest is to take in his hand some of the meal of the meal offering and of the oil of it, and all the perfume on it, burning it on the altar as a sign, for a seet smell to the Lord.
And hatever is over Aaron and his sons may have for their food, taking it ithout leaven in a holy place; in the open space of the Tent of meeting they may take a meal of it.
It is not to be cooked ith leaven. I have given it to them as their part of the offerings made by fire to me; it is most holy, as are the sin-offerings and the offerings for error.
Every male among the children of Aaron may have it for food; it is their right for ever through all your generations, from the offerings made by fire to the Lord: anyone touching them ill be holy.
And the Lord said to Moses,

This is the offering hich Aaron and his sons are to make to the Lord on the day hen he is made a priest: the tenth part of an ephah of the best meal for a meal offering for ever; half of it in the morning and half in the evening.
Let it be made ith oil on a flat plate; hen it is ell mixed and cooked, let it be broken and taken in as a meal offering, for a seet smell to the Lord.
And the same offering is to be given by that one of his sons ho takes his place as priest; by an order for ever, all of it is to be burned before the Lord.
Every meal offering offered for the priest is to be completely burned: nothing of it is to be taken for food.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to Aaron and his sons, This is the la for the sin-offering: the sin-offering is to be put to death before the Lord in the same place as the burned offering; it is most holy.
The priest by hom it is offered for sin, is to take it for his food in a holy place, in the open space of the Tent of meeting.
Anyone touching the flesh of it ill be holy: and if any of the blood is dropped on any clothing, the thing on hich the blood has been dropped is to be ashed in a holy place.
But the vessel of earth in hich the flesh as cooked is to be broken; or if a brass vessel as used, it is to be rubbed clean and ashed out ith ater.
Every male among the priests may take it for his food: it is most holy.
No sin-offering, the blood of hich is taken into the Tent of meeting, to take aay sin in the holy place, may be used for food: it is to be burned ith fire.
And this is the la of the offering for rongdoing: it is most holy.
They are to put to death the offering for rongdoing in the same place as the burned offering; and the priest is to put the blood on and round the altar.
And all the fat of it, the fat tail and the fat covering the inside parts, is to be given as an offering.
And the to kidneys, and the fat on them, hich is by the top of the legs, and the fat joining the liver and the kidneys, he is to take aay:
They are to be burned by the priest on the altar for an offering made by fire to the Lord: it is an offering for rongdoing.
Every male among the priests may have it as food in a holy place: it is most holy.
As is the sin-offering, so is the offering for rongdoing; there is one la for them: the priest ho makes the offering to take aay sin, he is to have it.
And the priest offering any man’s burned offering for him, may have the skin of the burned offering hich is offered by him.
And every meal offering hich is cooked in the oven and everything made in a cooking pot or on a flat plate, is for the priest by hom it is offered.
And every meal offering, mixed ith oil or dry, is for all the sons of Aaron in equal measure.
And this is the la for the peace-offerings offered to the Lord.

If any man gives his offering as a praise-offering, then let him give ith the offering, unleavened cakes mixed ith oil and thin unleavened cakes covered ith oil and cakes of the best meal ell mixed ith oil.
With his peace-offering let him give cakes of leavened bread, as a praise-offering.
And let him give one out of every offering to be lifted up before the Lord; that it may be for the priest ho puts the blood of the peace-offering on the altar.
And the flesh of the praise-offering is to be taken as food on the day hen it is offered; no part of it may be kept till the morning.
But if his offering is made because of an oath or given freely, it may be taken as food on the day hen it is offered; and the rest may be used up on the day after:
But if any of the flesh of the offering is still unused on the third day, it is to be burned ith fire.

And if any of the flesh of the peace-offering is taken as food on the third day, it ill not be pleasing to God and ill not be put to the account of him ho gives it; it ill be unclean and a cause of sin to him ho takes it as food.
And flesh touched by any unclean thing may not be taken for food: it is to be burned ith fire; and as for the flesh of the peace-offerings, everyone ho is clean may take it as food:
But he ho is unclean hen he takes as food the flesh of the peace-offerings, hich are the Lord’s, ill be cut off from his people.

And anyone ho, after touching any unclean thing of man or an unclean beast or any unclean and disgusting thing, takes as food the flesh of the peace-offerings, hich are the Lord’s, ill be cut off from his people.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel: You are not to take any fat, of ox or sheep or goat, for food.
And the fat of that hich comes to a natural death, and the fat of that hich is attacked by beasts, may be used for other purposes, but not in any ay for food.
For anyone ho takes as food the fat of any beast of hich men make an offering by fire to the Lord, ill be cut off from his people.
And you are not to take for food any blood, of bird or of beast, in any of your houses.
Whoever takes any blood for food ill be cut off from his people.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel: He ho makes a peace-offering to the Lord, is to give an offering to the Lord out of his peace-offering:
He himself is to take to the Lord the offering made by fire, even the fat ith the breast, so that the breast may be aved for a ave offering before the Lord.
And the fat is to be burned by the priest on the altar, but the breast is for Aaron and his sons.
And the right leg you are to give to the priest for an offering to be lifted up out of hat is given for your peace-offerings.
That man, among the sons of Aaron, by hom the blood of the peace-offering and the fat are offered, is to have the right leg for his part.

For the breast hich is aved and the right leg hich is lifted up on high I have taken from the children of Israel, from their peace-offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as their right for ever from the children of Israel.
This is the holy part given to Aaron and to his sons, out of the offerings made to the Lord by fire, on the day hen they ere made priests before the Lord;
Which the Lord said the children of Israel ere to give them, on the day hen he made them his priests. It is their right for ever from generation to generation.
These are the las for the burned offering, the meal offering, and the offering for rongdoing; and for the making of priests, and for the giving of peace-offerings;
As they ere given by the Lord to Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day hen the Lord gave orders to the children of Israel to make their offerings to the Lord, in the aste land of Sinai.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Take Aaron, and his sons ith him, and the robes and the holy oil and the ox of the sin-offering and the to male sheep and the basket of unleavened bread;
And let all the people come together at the door of the Tent of meeting.
And Moses did as the Lord said, and all the people came together at the door of the Tent of meeting.
And Moses said to the people, This is hat the Lord has given orders to be done.
Then Moses took Aaron and his sons; and after ashing them ith ater,
He put the coat on him, making it tight ith its band, and then the robe, and over it the ephod, ith its band of needleork to keep it in place.
And he put the priest’s bag on him, and in the bag he put the Urim and Thummim.
And on his head he put the head-dress, and in front of the head-dress the plate of gold, the holy cron, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And Moses took the holy oil and put it on the House and on all the things in it, to make them holy.
Seven times he put oil on the altar and on all its vessels, and on the ashing-basin and its base, to make them holy.
And some of the oil he put on Aaron’s head, to make him holy.
Then he took Aaron’s sons, clothing them ith the coats, and putting the bands round them, and the head-dresses on their heads, as the Lord had given him orders.
And he took the ox of the sin-offering: and Aaron and his sons put their hands on the head of the ox,

And he put it to death; and Moses took the blood and put it on the horns of the altar and round it ith his finger, and made the altar clean, draining out the blood at the base of the altar; so he made it holy, taking aay hat as unclean.
And he took all the fat on the inside parts, and the fat on the liver, and the to kidneys ith their fat, to be burned on the altar;
But the ox, ith its skin and its flesh and its aste, as burned ith fire outside the tent-circle, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And he put the male sheep of the burned offering before the Lord, and Aaron and his sons put their hands on its head,
And he put it to death; and Moses put some of the blood on and round the altar.
And hen the sheep had been cut into parts, the head and the parts and the fat ere burned by Moses.

And the inside parts and the legs ere ashed ith ater and all the sheep as burned by Moses on the altar; it as a burned offering for a seet smell: it as an offering made by fire to the Lord, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And he put the other sheep before the Lord, the sheep ith hich they ere made priests; and Aaron and his sons put their hands on the head of the sheep,
And he put it to death; and Moses took some of the blood and put it on the point of Aaron’s right ear and on the thumb of his right hand and on the great toe of his right foot.

Then he took Aaron’s sons, and Moses put some of the blood on the point of their right ears and on the thumbs of their right hands and on the great toes of their right feet: and Moses put the blood on and round the altar.
And he took the fat, and the fat tail, and the fat on the inside parts, and the fat on the liver, and the to kidneys ith their fat, and the right leg;
And out of the basket of unleavened bread hich as before the Lord he took one unleavened cake, and one cake of bread ith oil on it, and one thin cake, and put them on the fat and on the right leg:
And he put them all on the hands of Aaron and on the hands of his sons, aving them for a ave offering before the Lord.
And Moses took them from their hands, and they ere burned on the altar on the burned offering, as a priest’s offering for a seet smell, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
And Moses took the breast, aving it for a ave offering before the Lord; it as Moses’ part of the sheep of the priest’s offering, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.

And Moses took some of the holy oil and of the blood hich as on the altar and put it on Aaron and on his robes, and on his sons and on his sons’ robes; and made Aaron holy, and his robes and his sons and his sons’ robes ith him.

And Moses said to Aaron and to his sons, The flesh is to be cooked in ater at the door of the Tent of meeting, and there you are to take it as food, together ith the bread in the basket, as I have given orders, saying, It is the food of Aaron and his sons.
And that hich is over of the flesh and of the bread is to be burned ith fire.
And you are not to go out from the door of the Tent of meeting for seven days, till the days for making you priest are ended; for this ill be the ork of seven days.
What has been done this day, has been ordered by the Lord to take aay your sin.
And you are to keep atch for the Lord at the door of the Tent of meeting day and night for seven days, so that death may not come to you: for so he has given me orders.
And Aaron and his sons did all the things about hich the Lord had given orders through Moses.
And on the eighth day Moses sent for Aaron and his sons and the responsible men of Israel;
And he said to Aaron, Take a young ox for a sin-offering and a male sheep for a burned offering, ithout a mark, and make an offering of them before the Lord.
And say to the children of Israel: Take a he-goat for a sin-offering, and a young ox and a lamb, in their first year, ithout any mark on them, for a burned offering;
And an ox and a male sheep for peace-offerings, to be put to death before the Lord; and a meal offering mixed ith oil: for this day you are to see the Lord.
And they took the things ordered by Moses, before the Tent of meeting, and all the people came near, aiting before the Lord.
And Moses said, This is hat the Lord has said you are to do; and you ill see the glory of the Lord.

And Moses said to Aaron, Come near to the altar and make your sin-offering and your burned offering to take aay your sin and the sin of the people, and make the people’s offering to take aay their sin; as the Lord has given orders.
So Aaron came near to the altar and put to death the ox for the sin-offering for himself;
And the sons of Aaron gave him the blood and he put his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, draining out the blood at the base of the altar;
But the fat and the kidneys and the fat on the liver of the sin-offering ere burned by him on the altar as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And the flesh and the skin ere burned ith fire outside the tent-circle;
And he put to death the burned offering; and Aaron’s sons gave him the blood and he put some of it on and round the altar;
And they gave him the parts of the burned offering, in their order, and the head, to be burned on the altar.
And the inside parts and the legs, hen they had been ashed ith ater, ere burned on the burned offering on the altar.
And he made an offering for the people and took the goat of the sin-offering for the people and put it to death, offering it for sin, in the same ay as the first.
And he took the burned offering, offering it in the ordered ay;
And he put the meal offering before the Lord, and taking some of it in his hand he had it burned on the altar, separately from the burned offering of the morning.
And he put to death the ox and the sheep, hich ere the peace-offerings for the people; and Aaron’s sons gave him the blood and he put some of it on and round the altar;
And as for the fat of the ox and the fat tail of the sheep and the fat covering the inside parts and the kidneys and the fat on the liver;
They put the fat on the breasts, and the fat as burned on the altar.
And Aaron took the breasts and the right leg, aving them for a ave offering before the Lord, as Moses gave orders.
And Aaron, lifting up his hands to the people, gave them a blessing; and he came don from offering the sin-offering, and the burned offering, and the peace-offerings.
And Moses and Aaron ent into the Tent of meeting, and came out and gave the people a blessing, and the glory of the Lord as seen by all the people.
And fire came out from before the Lord, burning up the offering on the altar and the fat: and hen all the people sa it, they gave a loud cry, falling don on their faces.
And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took their vessels and put fire in them and perfume, burning strange fire before the Lord, hich he had not given them orders to do.
And fire came out from before the Lord, burning them up and causing their destruction before the Lord.
Then Moses said to Aaron, This is hat the Lord said, I ill be holy in the eyes of all those ho come near to me, and I ill be honoured before all the people. And Aaron said nothing.
And Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, the brother of Aaron’s father, and said to them, Come near and take your brothers aay from before the holy place, outside the tent-circle.
So they came and took them, in their coats, outside the tent-circle, as Moses had said.

And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons, Do not let your hair be loose, and give no signs of grief; so that death may not overtake you, and his rath come on all the people; but let there be eeping among your brothers and all the house of Israel for this burning of the Lord’s fire.
And do not go out from the door of the Tent of meeting, or death ill come to you; for the holy oil of the Lord is on you. And they did as Moses said.
And the Lord said to Aaron:
Take no ine, or strong drink, you or your sons ith you, hen you go into the Tent of meeting, that it may not be the cause of death to you; this is an order for ever through all your generations.
And make a division beteen the holy and the common, and beteen the unclean and the clean;
Teaching the children of Israel all the las hich the Lord has given them by the hand of Moses.

And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons ho ere still living, Take the rest of the meal offering from the offerings of the Lord made by fire, and take it for your food, ithout leaven, at the side of the altar, for it is most holy.
It is to be for your food in a holy place, because it is your right and your sons’ right, from the offerings of the Lord made by fire: for so am I ordered.

And the breast hich is aved and the leg hich is lifted up on high, you are to take as your food in a clean place; you and your sons and your daughters ith you: for they are given to you as your right and your sons’ right, from the peace-offerings of the children of Israel.

Let them take the breast hich is aved and the leg hich is lifted up on high, ith the fat of the burned offering, to be aved for a ave offering before the Lord; and this ill be for you and for your sons ith you, for a right for ever, as the Lord has given orders.
And Moses as looking for the goat of the sin-offering, but it as burned; and he as angry ith Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron, ho ere still living, saying,

Why did you not make a meal of the sin-offering in the holy place? For it is most holy and he has given it to you, so that the sin of the people may be put on it, to take aay their sin before the Lord.
See, its blood as not taken into the holy place: certainly it as right for you to have taken it as food in the holy place, as I gave orders.

And Aaron said to Moses, You have seen that today they have made their sin-offering and their burned offering before the Lord, and such things as these have come on me. If I had taken the sin-offering as food today, ould it have been pleasing to the Lord?
And after hearing this, Moses as no longer angry.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
