Say to the children of Israel: These are the living things hich you may have for food among all the beasts on the earth.
You may have as food any beast hich has a division in the horn of its foot, and hose food comes back into its mouth to be crushed again.
But, at the same time, of those beasts, you may not take for food the camel, because its food comes back but the horn of its foot is not parted in to; it is unclean to you.
And the rock-badger, for the same reason, is unclean to you.
And the hare, because the horn of its foot is not parted in to, is unclean to you.
And the pig is unclean to you, because though the horn of its foot is parted, its food does not come back.
Their flesh may not be used for food, and their dead bodies may not even be touched; they are unclean to you.

These you may have for food of all things living in the ater: anything living in the ater, in the seas or rivers, hich has special parts for simming and skin formed of thin plates, may be used for food.
All other things living and moving in the ater, in the sea or in the rivers, are a disgusting thing to you;
They may not be used for food, and their dead bodies are disgusting to you.
Anything in the ater hich has no special parts for simming and no thin plates on its skin is disgusting to you.
And among birds these are to be disgusting to you, and not to be used for food: the eagle and the gier-eagle and the ospray;
And the kite and the falcon, and birds of that sort;
Every raven, and birds of that sort;
And the ostrich and the night-hak and the sea-hak, and birds of that sort;
And the little ol and the cormorant and the great ol;
And the ater-hen and the pelican and the vulture;
The stork and the heron, and birds of that sort, and the hoopoe and the bat.
Every inged four-footed thing hich goes on the earth is disgusting to you;
But of the inged four-footed things, those hich have long legs for jumping on the earth you may have for food;
Such as all the different sorts of locust.
But all other inged four-footed things hich go on the earth are disgusting to you.
By these you ill be made unclean; anyone touching their dead bodies ill be unclean till evening:
Whoever takes aay the dead body of one of them is to have his clothing ashed, and ill be unclean till evening.
Every beast, in the horn of hose foot there is not a complete division, and hose food does not come back, is unclean to you: anyone touching one of these ill be unclean.
Any four-footed beast hich goes on the ball of its foot, is unclean to you: anyone touching the dead body of one of these ill be unclean till evening.
Anyone ho takes aay the dead body of one of these is to have his clothing ashed and be unclean till evening.
And these are unclean to you among things hich go lo don on the earth; the easel and the mouse and the great lizard, and animals of that sort;
And the ferret and the land crocodile and the lizard and the sand-lizard and the chameleon.
All these are unclean to you: anyone touching them hen they are dead ill be unclean till evening.

The dead body of any of these, falling on anything, ill make that thing unclean; if it is any vessel of ood, or clothing, or skin, or bag, hatever it is, if it is used for any purpose, it ill have to be put into ater, and ill be unclean till evening; after that it ill be clean.
And if one of them gets into any vessel of earth, hatever is in the vessel ill be unclean and the vessel ill have to be broken.
Any food in it, and anything on hich ater from it comes, ill be unclean: any drink taken from such a vessel ill be unclean.
Any part of the dead body of one of these, falling on anything, ill make it unclean; if it is an oven or a cooking-pot it ill have to be broken: they are unclean and ill be unclean to you.
But at the same time a fountain or a place here ater is stored for use ill be clean; but anyone touching their dead bodies ill be unclean.
If any part of the dead body of one of these gets on to any seed for planting, it is clean;
But if ater is put on the seed, and any part of the dead body gets on to it, it ill be unclean to you.
And if any beast hich may be used for food comes to a natural death, anyone touching its dead body ill be unclean till evening.

And he ho makes use of any part of its body for food is to have his clothing ashed and be unclean till evening; and anyone taking aay its body is to have his clothing ashed and be unclean till evening.
Everything hich goes flat on its body on the earth is disgusting, and is not to be used for food.
Whatever goes on its stomach or on four feet or has a great number of feet, even all those going flat on the earth, may not be used for food, for they are disgusting.
You are not to make yourselves disgusting ith anything hich goes about flat on the earth; you may not make yourselves unclean ith them, in such a ay that you are not holy to me.
For I am the Lord your God: for this reason, make and keep yourselves holy, for I am holy; you are not to make yourselves unclean ith any sort of thing hich goes about flat on the earth.
For I am the Lord, ho took you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God; so be you holy, for I am holy.
This is the la about beasts and birds and every living thing moving in the aters, and every living thing hich goes flat on the earth:
Marking out the unclean from the clean, and the living thing hich may be used for food from that hich may not.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, If a oman is ith child and gives birth to a male child, she ill be unclean for seven days, as hen she is unell.
And on the eighth day let him be given circumcision.

And she ill be unclean for thirty-three days till the flo of her blood is stopped; no holy thing may be touched by her, and she may not come into the holy place, till the days for making her clean are ended.
But if she gives birth to a female child, then she ill be unclean for to eeks, as hen she is unell; and she ill not be completely clean for sixty-six days.

And hen the days are ended for making her clean for a son or a daughter, let her take to the priest at the door of the Tent of meeting, a lamb of the first year for a burned offering and a young pigeon or a dove for a sin-offering:
And the priest is to make an offering of it before the Lord and take aay her sin, and she ill be made clean from the flo of her blood. This is the la for a oman ho gives birth to a male or a female.

And if she has not money enough for a lamb, then let her take to doves or to young pigeons, one for a burned offering and the other for a sin-offering, and the priest ill take aay her sin and she ill be clean,
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
If a man has on his skin a groth or a mark or a hite place, and it becomes the disease of a leper, let him be taken to Aaron the priest, or to one of the priests, his sons;

And if, hen the priest sees the mark on his skin, the hair on the place is turned hite and the mark seems to go deeper than the skin, it is the mark of a leper: and the priest, after looking at him, ill say that he is unclean.
But if the mark on his skin is hite, and does not seem to go deeper than the skin, and the hair on it is not turned hite, then the priest ill keep him shut up for seven days;

And the priest is to see him on the seventh day; and if, in his opinion, the place on his skin has not become orse and is not increased in size, then the priest ill keep him shut up for seven days more:

And the priest is to see him again on the seventh day; and if the mark is less bright and is not increased on his skin, then let the priest say that he is clean: it is only a skin-mark, and after his clothing has been ashed he ill be clean.
But if the size of the mark on his skin is increased after he has been seen by the priest, let him go to the priest again:
And if, after looking at him, he sees that the mark is increased in his skin, let the priest say that he is unclean; he is a leper.
When the disease of a leper is seen on a man, let him be taken to the priest;
And if the priest sees that there is a hite groth on the skin, and the hair is turned hite, and there is diseased flesh in the groth,
It is an old disease in the skin of his flesh, and the priest ill say that he is unclean; he ill not have to be shut up, for he is clearly unclean.
And if the disease comes out all over his skin, from his head to his feet, as far as the priest is able to see,
And if the priest sees that all his flesh is covered ith the leper’s disease, the priest ill say that he is clean: it is all turned hite, he is clean.
But henever diseased flesh is seen on him, he ill be unclean.
And hen the priest sees the diseased flesh he ill say that he is unclean; the diseased flesh is unclean, he is a leper.
Or if the diseased flesh is turned again and changed to hite then he is to come to the priest,
And the priest ill see him: and if the place is turned hite, then the priest ill say that he is free from the disease.
And if a bad place has come out on the skin and is ell again,
And on the same place there is a hite groth of a bright mark, red and hite, then let the priest see it;

And after looking at it, if it seems to go deeper than the skin, and the hair on it is turned hite, then the priest ill say that the man is unclean: it is the leper’s disease, it has come out in the bad place.
But if, after looking at it, he sees that there are no hite hairs on it, and it is not deeper than the skin, and it is not very bright, then let the priest keep him shut up for seven days:
And if it is increasing on the skin, the priest ill say that he is unclean: it is a disease.
But if the bright mark keeps in the same place and gets no greater, it is the mark of the old ound, and the priest ill say that he is clean.
Or if there is a burn on the skin of the flesh, and if the diseased flesh in the burn becomes a bright place, red and hite or hite,

The priest is to see it: and if the hair on the bright place is turned hite and it seems to go deeper than the skin, he is a leper: it has come out in the burn, and the priest ill say that he is unclean: it is the leper’s disease.

But if, after looking at it, the priest sees that there is no hite hair on the bright place, and it is not deeper than the skin, and is not very bright, then let the priest keep him shut up for seven days:
And the priest is to see him again on the seventh day; if it is increased in the skin, then the priest ill say that he is unclean: it is the leper’s disease.
And if the bright place keeps the same size and gets no greater on the skin, but is less bright, it is the effect of the burn, and the priest ill say that he is clean: it is the mark of the burn.
And hen a man or a oman has a disease on the head, or in the hair of the chin,

Then the priest is to see the diseased place: and if it seems to go deeper than the skin, and if there is thin yello hair in it, then the priest ill say that he is unclean: he has the mark of the leper’s disease on his head or in the hair of his chin.
And after looking at the diseased place, if it does not seem to go deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, then the priest ill have him shut up for seven days:
And on the seventh day the priest ill see the place: and if it is not increased, and there is no yello hair in it, and it does not seem to go deeper than the skin,
Then his hair is to be cut off, but not on the diseased place, and he is to be shut up for seven days more:

And on the seventh day the priest ill see the place: and if it is not increased, and does not seem to go deeper than the skin, the priest ill say that he is clean: and after his clothing has been ashed he ill be clean.
But if the disease in his skin becomes orse after he has been made clean,
Then the priest is to see him: and if the mark is increased, the priest, ithout looking for the yello hair, ill say that he is unclean.
But if, in his opinion, the groth is stopped, and black hair has come up on it, the disease has gone; he is clean and the priest ill say that he is clean.
And if a man or a oman has bright marks on the skin of their flesh, that is, bright hite marks,
Then the priest is to see them: and if the hite marks on their skin are not very bright, it is a skin disease hich has come out on the skin; he is clean.
And if a man’s hair has come out and he has no hair, still he is clean.
And if the hair has gone from the front part of his head, so that he has no hair there, still he is clean.
But if, on his head or on his bro, here he has no hair, there is a red and hite place, it is the disease of the leper coming out on his head or on his bro.
Then if the priest sees that the groth of the disease has become red and hite on his head or on his bro here there is no hair, like the mark in the skin of a leper;
He is a leper and unclean; the priest is to say that he is most certainly unclean: the disease is in his head.
And the leper ho has the disease on him is to go about ith signs of grief, ith his hair loose and his mouth covered, crying, Unclean, unclean.
While the disease is on him, he ill be unclean. He is unclean: let him keep by himself, living outside the tent-circle.
And any clothing of ool or of linen in hich is the mark of the disease;
If it is in the threads of the linen or of the ool, or in leather, or in anything made of skin;
If there are red or green marks on the clothing, or on the leather, or in the threads of the cloth, or in anything made of skin, it is the leper’s disease: let the priest see it.
And after it has been seen by the priest, the thing hich is so marked is to be shut up for seven days:

And he is to see the mark on the seventh day; if the mark is increased in the clothing, or in the threads of the material, or in the leather, hatever the leather is used for, it is the disease biting into it: it is unclean.
And the clothing, or the ool or linen material, or anything of leather in hich is the disease, is to be burned: for the disease is biting into it; let it be burned in the fire.
And if the priest sees that the mark is not increased in the clothing or in any part of the material or in the leather,
Then the priest ill give orders for the thing on hich the mark is, to be ashed, and to be shut up for seven days more:

And if, after the mark has been ashed, the priest sees that the colour of it is not changed and it is not increased, it is to be burned in the fire: the disease is orking in it, though the damage may be inside or outside.
And if the priest sees that the mark is less bright after the ashing, then let him have it cut out of the clothing or the leather or from the threads of the material:
And if the mark is still seen in the clothing or in the threads of the material or in the leather, it is the disease coming out: the thing in hich the disease is ill have to be burned ith fire.
And the material of the clothing, or anything of skin, hich has been ashed, if the mark has gone out of it, let it be ashed a second time and it ill be clean.
This is the la about the leper’s disease in the thread of ool or linen material, in clothing or in anything of skin, saying ho it is to be judged clean or unclean.
And the Lord said to Moses,
This is the la of the leper on the day hen he is made clean: he is to be taken to the priest;
And the priest is to go outside the tent-circle; and if, after looking, the priest sees that the mark of the disease has gone from him,
Then the priest is to give orders to take, for him ho is to be made clean, to living clean birds and some cedar ood and red thread and hyssop.
And the priest ill give orders for one of the birds to be put to death in a vessel made of earth, over floing ater.
And he ill take the living bird and the ood and the red thread and the hyssop and put them in the blood of the bird hich as put to death over floing ater.
And shaking it seven times over the man ho is to be made clean, he ill say that he is clean and ill let the living bird go free into the open country.

And he ho is to be made clean ill have his clothing ashed and his hair cut and have a bath, and he ill be clean. And after that he ill come back to the tent-circle; but he is to keep outside his tent for seven days.

And on the seventh day he is to have all the hair cut off his head and his chin and over his eyes — all his hair is to be cut off — and he ill have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and he ill be clean.

And on the eighth day let him take to male lambs, ithout any marks on them, and one female lamb of the first year, ithout a mark, and three tenth parts of an ephah of the best meal, mixed ith oil, and one log of oil.
And the priest ho is making him clean ill put the man ho is being made clean, together ith these things, before the door of the Tent of meeting.
And the priest is to take one of the male lambs and give it as an offering for rongdoing, and the log of oil, aving them for a ave offering before the Lord;

And he is to put the male lamb to death in the place here they put to death the sin-offering and the burned offering, in the holy place; for as the sin-offering is the property of the priest, so is the offering for rongdoing: it is most holy.

And let the priest take some of the blood of the offering for rongdoing and put it on the point of the right ear of him ho is to be made clean, and on the thumb of his right hand and on the great toe of his right foot;
And take some of the oil and put it in the hollo of his left hand;
And let the priest put his right finger in the oil hich is in his left hand, shaking it out ith his finger seven times before the Lord;

And of the rest of the oil hich is in his hand, the priest ill put some on the point of the right ear of the man ho is to be made clean, and on the thumb of his right hand and on the great toe of his right foot, over the blood of the offering for rongdoing;
And the rest of the oil in the priest’s hand he ill put on the head of him ho is to be made clean; and so the priest ill make him free from sin before the Lord.
And the priest ill give the sin-offering, and take aay the sin of him ho is to be made clean from his unclean condition; and after that he ill put the burned offering to death.
And the priest is to have the burned offering and the meal offering burned on the altar; and the priest ill take aay his sin and he ill be clean.

And if he is poor and not able to get so much, then he may take one male lamb as an offering for rongdoing, to be aved to take aay his sin, and one tenth part of an ephah of the best meal mixed ith oil for a meal offering, and a log of oil;
And to doves or to young pigeons, such as he is able to get; and one ill be for a sin-offering and the other for a burned offering.
And on the eighth day he ill take them to the priest, to the door of the Tent of meeting before the Lord, so that he may be made clean.
And the priest ill take the lamb of the offering for rongdoing and the oil, aving them for a ave offering before the Lord;

And he ill put to death the lamb of the offering for rongdoing and the priest ill take some of the blood of the offering for rongdoing and put it on the point of the right ear of him ho is to be made clean, and on the thumb of his right hand and on the great toe of his right foot;
And the priest ill put out some of the oil in the hollo of his left hand,
Shaking out drops of oil ith his right finger before the Lord seven times:

And the priest ill put some of the oil hich is in his hand on the point of the ear of the man ho is to be made clean and on the thumb of his right hand and on the great toe of his right foot, on the place here the blood of the offering for rongdoing as put;
And the rest of the oil hich is in the priest’s hand he ill put on the head of him ho is to be made clean, to take aay his sin before the Lord.
And he ill make an offering of one of the doves or the young pigeons, such as he is able to get;
And of these, he ill give one for a sin-offering and one for a burned offering, ith the meal offering; and the priest ill take aay the sin of him ho is to be made clean before the Lord.
This is the la for the man ho has the disease of the leper on him, and ho is not able to get that hich is necessary for making himself clean.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
When you have come into the land of Canaan hich I ill give you for your heritage, if I put the leper’s disease on a house in the land of your heritage,
Then let the oner of the house come and say to the priest, It seems to me that there is a sort of leper’s disease in the house.

And the priest ill give orders for everything to be taken out of the house, before he goes in to see the disease, so that the things in the house may not become unclean; and then the priest is to go in to see the house;
And if he sees that the alls of the house are marked ith hollos of green and red, and if it seems to go deeper than the face of the all;
Then the priest ill go out of the door of the house, and keep the house shut up for seven days:
And the priest is to come again on the seventh day and have a look and see if the marks on the alls of the house are increased in size;
Then the priest ill give orders to them to take out the stones in hich the disease is seen, and put them out into an unclean place outside the ton:
And he ill have the house rubbed all over inside, and the paste hich is rubbed off ill be put out into an unclean place outside the ton:
And they ill take other stones and put them in place of those stones, and he ill take other paste and put it on the alls of the house.
And if the disease comes out again in the house after he has taken out the stones and after the alls have been rubbed and the ne paste put on,
Then the priest ill come and see it; and if the disease in the house is increased in size, it is the leper’s disease orking out in the house: it is unclean.
And the house ill have to be pulled don, the stones of it and the ood and the paste; and everything is to be taken out to an unclean place outside the ton.
And, in addition, anyone ho goes into the house at any time, hile it is shut up, ill be unclean till evening.
And anyone ho has been sleeping in the house ill have to have his clothing ashed; and anyone ho takes food in that house ill have to have his clothing ashed.
And if the priest comes in, and sees that the disease is not increased after the ne paste has been put on the house, then the priest ill say that the house is clean, because the disease is gone.
And in order to make the house clean, let him take to birds and cedar-ood and red thread and hyssop;
And put one of the birds to death in a vessel of earth over floing ater;
And take the cedar-ood and the hyssop and the red thread and the living bird and put them in the blood of the dead bird and in the floing ater, shaking it over the house seven times.
And he ill make the house clean ith the blood of the bird and the floing ater and ith the living bird and ith the cedar-ood and the hyssop and the red thread.
But he ill let the living bird go out of the ton into the open country; so he ill take aay sin from the house and it ill be clean.
This is the la for all signs of the leper’s disease and for skin diseases;
And for signs of disease in clothing, or in a house;
And for a groth or a bad place or a bright mark on the skin;
To make clear hen it is unclean and hen it is clean: this is the la about the disease of the leper.
And the Lord said to Moses and to Aaron,
Say to the children of Israel: If a man has an unclean flo from his flesh, it ill make him unclean.
If the flo goes on or if the part is stopped up, to keep back the flo, he is still unclean.
Every bed on hich he has been resting ill be unclean, and everything on hich he has been seated ill be unclean.
And anyone touching his bed is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.
And he ho has been seated on anything on hich the unclean man has been seated is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.
And anyone touching the flesh of the unclean man is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.
And if liquid from the mouth of the unclean man comes on to him ho is clean, then he is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.
And any leather seat on a horse on hich the unclean man has been seated ill be unclean.

And anyone touching anything hich as under him ill be unclean till the evening; anyone taking up any of these things is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.
And anyone on hom the unclean man puts his hands, ithout ashing them in ater, is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.
And any vessel of earth hich has been touched by the unclean man ill have to be broken and any vessel of ood ashed.
And hen a man ho has a flo from his body is made clean from it, he is to take seven days to make himself clean, ashing his clothing and bathing his body in floing ater, and then he ill be clean.
And on the eighth day he is to take to doves or to young pigeons and come before the Lord to the door of the Tent of meeting and give them to the priest:
And they are to be offered by the priest, one for a sin-offering and one for a burned offering, and the priest ill take aay his sin before the Lord on account of his flo.
And if a man’s seed goes out from him, then all his body ill have to be bathed in ater and he ill be unclean till evening.
And any clothing or skin on hich the seed comes is to be ashed ith ater and be unclean till evening.
And if a man has sex relations ith a oman and his seed goes out from him, the to of them ill have to be bathed in ater and ill be unclean till evening.
And if a oman has a flo of blood from her body, she ill have to be kept separate for seven days, and anyone touching her ill be unclean till evening.
And everything on hich she has been resting, hile she is kept separate, ill be unclean, and everything on hich she has been seated ill be unclean.
And anyone touching her bed ill have to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.
And anyone touching anything on hich she has been seated ill have to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.
Anyone touching anything on the bed or on the thing on hich she has been seated, ill be unclean till evening.
And if any man has sex relations ith her so that her blood comes on him, he ill be unclean for seven days and every bed on hich he has been resting ill be unclean.

And if a oman has a flo of blood for a long time, not at the time hen she generally has it, or if the flo goes on longer than the normal time, she ill be unclean hile the flo of blood goes on, as she is at other normal times.
Every bed on hich she has been resting ill be unclean, as at the times hen she normally has a flo of blood, and everything on hich she has been seated ill be unclean, in the same ay.
And anyone touching these things ill be unclean, and his clothing ill have to be ashed and his body bathed in ater and he ill be unclean till evening.
But hen her flo of blood is stopped, after seven days she ill be clean.
And on the eighth day let her get to doves or to young pigeons and take them to the priest to the door of the Tent of meeting,
To be offered by the priest, one for a sin-offering and one for a burned offering; and the priest ill take aay her sin before the Lord on account of her unclean condition.

In this ay may the children of Israel be made free from all sorts of unclean conditions, so that death may not overtake them hen they are unclean and hen they make unclean my holy place hich is among them.
This is the la for the man ho has a flo from his body, or hose seed goes from him so that he is unclean;
And for her ho has a flo of blood, and for any man or oman ho has an unclean flo, and for him ho has sex relations ith a oman hen she is unclean.
And the Lord said to Moses, after the death of the to sons of Aaron hen they took in strange fire before the Lord and death overtook them;

The Lord said to Moses, Say to Aaron, your brother, that he may not come at all times into the holy place inside the veil, before the cover hich is on the ark, for fear that death may overtake him; for I ill be seen in the cloud on the cover of the ark.
Let Aaron come into the holy place in this ay: ith an ox for a sin-offering and a male sheep for a burned offering.

Let him put on the holy linen coat, and the linen trousers on his body, and the linen band round him, and the linen head-dress on his head; for this is holy clothing, and before he puts them on his body is to be ashed ith ater.
And let him take from the children of Israel to he-goats for a sin-offering and one male sheep for a burned offering.
And Aaron is to give the ox of the sin-offering for himself, to make himself and his house free from sin.
And he is to take the to goats and put them before the Lord at the door of the Tent of meeting.
And Aaron ill make selection from the to goats by the decision of the Lord, one goat for the Lord and one for Azazel.
And the goat hich is marked out for the Lord, let Aaron give for a sin-offering.
But the goat for Azazel is to be placed living before the Lord, for the taking aay of sin, that it may be sent aay for Azazel into the aste land.
And Aaron is to give the ox of the sin-offering for himself and take aay sin from himself and his house, and put to death the ox of the sin-offering hich is for himself.
And he is to take a vessel full of burning coal from the altar before the Lord and in his hand some seet perfume crushed small, and take it inside the veil;
And let him put the perfume on the fire before the Lord so that the ark may be covered ith a cloud of the smoke of the perfume, in order that death may not overtake him.
And let him take some of the blood of the ox, shaking drops of it from his finger on the cover of the ark on the east side, and before it, seven times.

Then let him put to death the goat of the sin-offering for the people, and take its blood inside the veil and do ith it as he did ith the blood of the ox, shaking drops of it on and before the cover of the ark.

And let him make the holy place free from hatever is unclean among the children of Israel and from their rongdoing in all their sins; and let him do the same for the Tent of meeting, hich has its place among an unclean people.

And no man may be in the Tent of meeting from the time hen Aaron goes in to take aay sin in the holy place till he comes out, having made himself and his house and all the people of Israel free from sin.

And he is to go out to the altar hich is before the Lord and make it free from sin; and he is to take some of the blood of the ox and the blood of the goat and put it on the horns of the altar and round it;
Shaking drops of the blood from his finger on it seven times to make it holy and clean from hatever is unclean among the children of Israel.
And hen he has done hatever is necessary to make the holy place and the Tent of meeting and the altar free from sin, let him put the living goat before the Lord;

And Aaron, placing his to hands on the head of the living goat, ill make a public statement over him of all the evil doings of the children of Israel and all their rongdoing, in all their sins; and he ill put them on the head of the goat and send him aay, in the care of a man ho ill be aiting there, into the aste land.
And the goat ill take all their sins into a land cut off from men, and he ill send the goat aay into the aste land.
Then let Aaron come into the Tent of meeting and take off the linen clothing hich he put on hen he ent into the holy place, and put them don there;

And after bathing his body in ater in a holy place, he is to put on his clothing and come out and give his burned offering and the burned offering of the people, to take aay his sin and the sin of the people.
And the fat of the sin-offering is to be burned by him on the altar.
And the man ho takes aay the goat for Azazel is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and then he may come back to the tent-circle.

And the ox of the sin-offering and the goat of the sin-offering, hose blood as taken in to make the holy place free from sin, are to be taken aay outside the tent-circle and their skins and their flesh and their aste are to be burned ith fire.
And the man by hom they are burned is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater, and then he may come back to the tent-circle.

And let this be an order to you for ever: in the seventh month, on the tenth day, you are to keep yourselves from pleasure and do no sort of ork, those ho are Israelites by birth and those from other lands ho are living among you:
For on this day your sin ill be taken aay and you ill be clean: you ill be made free from all your sins before the Lord.
It is a special Sabbath for you, and you are to keep yourselves from pleasure; it is an order for ever.

And the man on hose head the holy oil has been put, and ho has been marked out to be a priest in his father’s place, ill do hat is necessary to take aay sin, and ill put on the linen clothing, even the holy robes:
And he ill make the holy place and the Tent of meeting and the altar free from sin; he ill take aay sin from the priests and from all the people.
And let this be an order for ever for you, so that the sin of the children of Israel may be taken aay once every year. And he did as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to Aaron and to his sons and to all the children of Israel: This is the order hich the Lord has given.
If any man of Israel puts to death an ox or a lamb or a goat, in or outside the tent-circle;

And has not taken it to the door of the Tent of meeting, to make an offering to the Lord, before the Lord’s House, its blood ill be on him, for he has taken life, and he ill be cut off from among his people:

So that the children of Israel may take to the Lord, to the door of the Tent of meeting and to the priest, the offerings hich they have put to death in the open country, and that they may make their peace-offerings to the Lord.
And the priest ill put blood on the altar of the Lord at the door of the Tent of meeting, burning the fat for a seet smell to the Lord.
And let them make no more offerings to evil spirits, after hich they have gone, turning aay from the Lord. Let this be a la to them for ever, through all their generations.
And say to them, If any man of Israel, or any other living among them, makes a burned offering or other offering,
And does not take it to the door of the Tent of meeting to make an offering to the Lord, that man ill be cut off from among his people.
And if any man of Israel, or any other living among them, takes any sort of blood for food, my rath ill be turned against that man and he ill be cut off from among his people.
For the life of the flesh is in its blood; and I have given it to you on the altar to take aay your sin: for it is the blood hich makes free from sin because of the life in it.
For this reason I have said to the children of Israel, No man among you, or any others living ith you, may take blood as food.
And any man of Israel, or any other living among them, ho gets ith his bo any beast or bird used for food, is to see that its blood is covered ith earth.
For the blood is the life of all flesh: and so I have said to the children of Israel, You may not take any sort of blood as food, and any man ho does so ill be cut of.

And anyone ho takes as food anything hich has come to a natural end, or anything hich has been put to death by beasts, if he is one of you by birth, or of another nation, ill have to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening, and then he ill be clean.
But if his clothing is not ashed and his body bathed, his sin ill be on him.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, I am the Lord your God.

You may not do those things hich ere done in the land of Egypt here you ere living; and you may not do those things hich are done in the land of Canaan here I am taking you, or be guided in your behaviour by their rules.
But you are to be guided by my decisions and keep my rules, and be guided by them: I am the Lord your God.
So keep my rules and my decisions, hich, if a man does them, ill be life to him: I am the Lord.
You may not have sex connection ith anyone ho is a near relation: I am the Lord.
You may not have sex relations ith your father or your mother: she is your mother, you may not take her.
And you may not have sex relations ith your father’s ife: she is your father’s.
You may not take your sister, the daughter of your father or of your mother, herever her birth took place, among you or in another country.
You may not have sex relations ith your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter, for they are part of yourself;
Or your father’s ife’s daughter, the child of your father, for she is your sister.
You may not have sex connection ith your father’s sister, for she is your father’s near relation.
You may not have sex connection ith your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s near relation.
You may not have sex relations ith the ife of your father’s brother, for she is of your family;
Or ith your daughter-in-la, for she is your son’s ife, and you may not take her.
You may not have sex relations ith your brother’s ife, for she is your brother’s.
You may not take as ife a oman and her daughter, or her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter, for they are of one family: it is an act of shame.
And you may not take as ife a oman and at the same time her sister, to be in competition ith her in her life-time.
And you may not go near a oman or have sex relations ith her hen she is unclean, at her regular time.
And you may not have sex relations ith your neighbour’s ife, making yourself unclean ith her.
And you may not make any of your children go through the fire as an offering to Molech, and you may not put shame on the name of your God: I am the Lord.
You may not have sex relations ith men, as you do ith omen: it is a disgusting thing.
And you may not have sex relations ith a beast, making yourself unclean ith it; and a oman may not give herself to a beast: it is an unnatural act.
Do not make yourself unclean in any of these ays; for so have those nations hom I am driving out from before you made themselves unclean:
And the land itself has become unclean; so that I have sent on it the reard of its rongdoing, and the land itself puts out those ho are living in it.
So then keep my rules and my decisions, and do not do any of these disgusting things, those of you ho are Israelites by birth, or any others ho are living ith you:
( For all these disgusting things ere done by the men of this country ho ere there before you, and the land has been made unclean by them;)
So that the land may not put you out from it, hen you make it unclean, as it put out the nations hich ere there before you.
For all those ho do any of these disgusting things ill be cut off from among their people.
So then, keep my orders, so that you may not do any of these disgusting things hich ere done before you, or make yourselves unclean through them: I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to all the people of Israel, You are to be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy.
Let every man give honour to his mother and to his father and keep my Sabbaths: I am the Lord your God.
Do not go after false gods, and do not make metal images of gods for yourselves: I am the Lord your God.
And hen you give a peace offering to the Lord, do it in the ay hich is pleasing to the Lord.
Let it be used for food on the same day on hich it is offered, or on the day after; and hatever is over on the third day is to be burned ith fire.
If any of it is used for food on the third day, it is a disgusting thing and ill not be pleasing to the Lord.
And as for anyone ho takes it for food, his sin ill be on him, for he has put shame on the holy thing of the Lord: he ill be cut off from his people.
And hen you get in the grain from your land, do not let all the grain be cut from the edges of the field, or take up hat has been dropped on the earth after the getting in of the grain.
And do not take all the grapes from your vine-garden, or the fruit dropped on the earth; let the poor man, and the man from another country, have these: I am the Lord your God.
Do not take anyone’s property or be false in act or ord to another.
And do not take an oath in my name falsely, putting shame on the name of your God: I am the Lord.
Do not be cruel to your neighbour or take hat is his; do not keep back a servant’s payment from him all night till the morning.
Do not put a curse on those ho have no hearing, or put a cause of falling in the ay of the blind, but keep the fear of your God before you: I am the Lord.
Do no rong in your judging: do not give thought to the position of the poor, or honour to the position of the great; but be a judge to your neighbour in righteousness.
Do not go about saying untrue things among your people, or take aay the life of your neighbour by false itness: I am the Lord.
Let there be no hate in your heart for your brother; but you may make a protest to your neighbour, so that he may be stopped from doing evil.
Do not make attempts to get equal ith one ho has done you rong, or keep hard feelings against the children of your people, but have love for your neighbour as for yourself: I am the Lord.
Keep my las. Do not let your cattle have offspring by those of a different sort; do not put mixed seed into your field; do not put on a robe made of to sorts of cloth.

If any man has sex relations ith a servant-oman ho has given her ord to be married to a man, and has not been made free for a price or in any other ay, the thing ill be looked into; but they ill not be put to death because she as not a free oman.
Let him take his offering for rongdoing to the Lord, to the door of the Tent of meeting; let him give a male sheep as an offering for rongdoing.
And the priest ill take aay his sin before the Lord ith the sheep hich is offered for his rongdoing, and he ill have forgiveness for the sin hich he has done.
And hen you have come into the land, and have put in all sorts of fruit-trees, their fruit ill be as if they had not had circumcision, and for three years their fruit may not be used for food.
And in the fourth year all the fruit ill be holy as a praise-offering to the Lord.
But in the fifth year you may take the fruit and the increase of it for your food: I am the Lord your God.
Nothing may be used for food ith its blood in it; you may not make use of strange arts, or go in search of signs and onders.
The ends of the hair round your face and on your chin may not be cut off.
You may not make cuts in your flesh in respect for the dead, or have marks printed on your bodies: I am the Lord.
Do not make your daughter common by letting her become a loose oman, for fear that the land may become full of shame.
Keep my Sabbaths and have respect for my holy place: I am the Lord.
Do not go after those ho make use of spirits, or onder-orkers; do not go in their ays or become unclean through them: I am the Lord your God.
Get up from your seats before the hite-haired, and give honour to the old, and let the fear of your God be before you: I am the Lord.
And if a man from another country is living in your land ith you, do not make life hard for him;
Let him be to you as one of your countrymen and have love for him as for yourself; for you ere living in a strange land, in the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.
Do not make false decisions in questions of yard-sticks and eights and measures.
Have true scales, true eights and measures for all things: I am the Lord your God, ho took you out of the land of Egypt;
You are to keep all my rules and my decisions and do them: I am the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,

Again, say to the children of Israel, If any man of the children of Israel, or any other man living in Israel, gives his offspring to Molech, he is certainly to be put to death: he is to be stoned by the people of the land;
And my face ill be turned against that man, and he ill be cut off from his people; because he has given his offspring to Molech, making my holy place unclean, and making my holy name common.
And if the people of the land do not take note of that man hen he gives his offspring to Molech, and do not put him to death,
Then my face ill be turned against him and his family, and he and all those ho do evil ith him ill be cut off from among their people.
And hoever goes after those ho make use of spirits and onder-orkers, doing evil ith them, against him ill my face be turned, and he ill be cut off from among his people.
So make and keep yourselves holy, for I am the Lord your God.
And keep my rules and do them: I am the Lord, ho make you holy.
Every man cursing his father or his mother is certainly to be put to death; because of his curse on his father or his mother, his blood ill be on him.
And if a man has sex relations ith another man’s ife, even the ife of his neighbour, he and she are certainly to be put to death.
And the man ho has sex relations ith his father’s ife has put shame on his father: the to of them are to be put to death; their blood ill be on them.
And if a man has sex relations ith his son’s ife, the to of them are to be put to death: it is unnatural; their blood ill be on them.
And if a man has sex relations ith a man, the to of them have done a disgusting thing: let them be put to death; their blood ill be on them.
And if a man takes as ife a oman and her mother, it is an act of shame; let them be burned ith fire, all three of them, so that there may be no shame among you.
And if a man has sex relations ith a beast, let him be put to death, and let the beast be put to destruction.
And if a oman goes near a beast and has sex relations ith it, you ill put an end to the oman and the beast: their blood ill be on them.

And if a man takes his sister, daughter of his father or his mother, and has sex relations ith her and she ith him, it is an act of shame: they are to be cut off before the children of their people; he has had sex relations ith his sister, and his sin ill be on him.

And if a man has sex relations ith a oman at the time hen she is unell, he has seen her fountain and she has let the fountain of her blood be uncovered, and the to of them are to be cut off from among their people.
And you may not have sex connection ith your mother’s sister or your father’s sister, for they are his near relations: their sin ill be on them.
And if a man has sex relations ith the ife of his father’s brother, he has put shame on his father’s brother: their sin ill be on them; till the day of their death they ill have no children.
And if a man takes his brother’s ife, it is an unclean act; he has put shame on his brother; they ill have no children.
So then, keep my rules and my decisions and do them, so that the land hich I am giving you as your resting-place may not violently send you out again.
And do not keep the rules of the nations hich I am driving out before you; for they did all these things, and for that reason my soul as turned against them.
But I have said to you, You ill take their land and I ill give it to you for your heritage, a land floing ith milk and honey: I am the Lord your God ho have made you separate from all other peoples.

So then, make division beteen the clean beast and the unclean, and beteen the clean bird and the unclean: do not make yourselves disgusting by any beast or bird or anything hich goes flat on the earth, hich has been marked by me as unclean for you.
And you are to be holy to me; for I the Lord am holy and have made you separate from the nations, so that you may be my people.
Any man or oman ho makes use of spirits, or ho is a onder-orker, is to be put to death: they are to be stoned ith stones: their blood ill be on them.
And the Lord said to Moses, Say to the priests, the sons of Aaron, Let no man make himself unclean for the dead among his people;
But only for his near relations, for his mother or his father, his son or his daughter, and his brother;
And for his sister, a virgin, for she is his near relation and has had no husband, he may make himself unclean.
But let him, being a chief among his people, not make himself unclean in such a ay as to put shame on himself.
They are not to have their hair cut off for the dead, or the hair on their chins cut short, or make cuts in their flesh.
Let them be holy to their God and not make the name of their God common; for the fire offerings of the Lord and the bread of their God are offered by them, and they are to be holy.
They may not take as ife a loose or common oman, or one ho has been put aay by her husband: for the priest is holy to his God.
And he is to be holy in your eyes, for by him the bread of your God is offered; he is to be holy in your eyes, for I the Lord, ho make you holy, am holy.
And if the daughter of a priest makes herself common and by her loose behaviour puts shame on her father, let her be burned ith fire.

And he ho is the chief priest among his brothers, on hose head the holy oil has been put, ho is marked out to put on the holy robes, may not let his hair go loose or have his clothing out of order as a sign of sorro.
He may not go near any dead body or make himself unclean for his father or his mother;
He may not go out of the holy place or make the holy place of his God common; for the cron of the holy oil of his God is on him: I am the Lord.
And let him take as his ife one ho has not had relations ith a man.
A ido, or one hose husband has put her aay, or a common oman of loose behaviour, may not be the ife of a priest; but let him take a virgin from among his people.
And he may not make his seed unclean among his people, for I the Lord have made him holy.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to Aaron, If a man of your family, in any generation, is damaged in body, let him not come near to make the offering of the bread of his God.
For any man hose body is damaged may not come near: one ho is blind, or has not the use of his legs, or one ho has a broken nose or any unnatural groth,
Or a man ith broken feet or hands,
Or one hose back is bent, or one ho is unnaturally small, or one ho has a damaged eye, or hose skin is diseased, or hose sex parts are damaged;
No man of the offspring of Aaron hose body is damaged in any ay may come near to give the fire offerings of the Lord: he is damaged, he may not come near to make the offerings.
He may take of the bread of God, the holy and the most holy;
But he may not go inside the veil or come near the altar, because he is damaged; and he may not make my holy places common; for I the Lord have made them holy.
These are the ords hich Moses said to Aaron and to his sons and to all the children of Israel.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Give orders to Aaron and to his sons to keep themselves separate from the holy things of the children of Israel hich they give to me, and not to make my holy name common: I am the Lord,

Say to them, If any man of all your seed through all your generations, being unclean, comes near the holy things hich the children of Israel make holy to the Lord, he ill be cut off from before me: I am the Lord.

No man of the seed of Aaron ho is a leper, or ho has a flo from his body, may take of the holy food till he is clean. And any man touching anything hich is unclean because of the dead, or any man hose seed goes from him;
Or anyone touching any unclean thing hich goes flat on the earth, or someone by hom he may be made unclean in any ay hatever;
Any person touching any such unclean thing ill be unclean till evening, and may not take of the holy food till his flesh has been bathed in ater;
And hen the sun has gone don he ill be clean; and after that he may take part in the holy food, because it is his bread.
That hich comes to a natural death, or is attacked by beasts, he may not take as food, for it ill make him unclean: I am the Lord.
So then, let them keep hat I have put into their care, for fear that sin may come on them because of it, so causing their death because they have made it common: I am the Lord, ho make them holy.
No outside person may take of the holy food, or one living as a guest in the priest’s house, or a servant orking for payment.
But any person for hom the priest has given money, to make him his, may take of it ith him; and those ho come to birth in his house may take of his bread.
And if the daughter of a priest is married to an outside person she may not take of the holy things hich are lifted up as offerings.

But if a priest’s daughter is a ido, or parted from her husband, and has no child, and has come back to her father’s house as hen she as a girl, she may take of her father’s bread; but no outside person may do so.
And if a man takes the holy food in error, he ill have to give the holy thing back to the priest, ith the addition of a fifth part.
And they may not make common the holy things hich the children of Israel give to the Lord,
So causing sin to come on them hen they take their holy things for food: I am the Lord ho make them holy.
And the Lord said to Moses,

Say to Aaron and to his sons and to all the children of Israel, If any man of the children of Israel, or of another nation living in Israel, makes an offering, given because of an oath or freely given to the Lord for a burned offering;
So that it may be pleasing to the Lord, let him give a male, ithout any mark, from among the oxen or the sheep or the goats.
But anything hich has a mark you may not give; it ill not make you pleasing to the Lord.
And hoever makes a peace-offering to the Lord, in payment of an oath or as a free offering, from the herd or the flock, if it is to be pleasing to the Lord, let it be free from any mark or damage.
Anything blind or broken or damaged or having any disease or any mark on it may not be offered to the Lord; you may not make an offering of it by fire on the altar to the Lord.
An ox or a lamb hich has more or less than its natural parts, may be given as a free offering; but it ill not be taken in payment of an oath.
An animal hich has its sex parts damaged or crushed or broken or cut, may not be offered to the Lord; such a thing may not be done anyhere in your land.
And from one ho is not an Israelite you may not take any of these for an offering to the Lord; for they are unclean, there is a mark on them, and the Lord ill not be pleased ith them.
And the Lord said to Moses,
When an ox or a sheep or a goat is given birth, let it be ith its mother for seven days; and after the eighth day it may be taken as an offering made by fire to the Lord.
A co or a sheep may not be put to death ith its young on the same day.
And hen you make an offering of praise to the Lord, make it in a ay hich is pleasing to him.
Let it be used for food on the same day; do not keep any part of it till the morning: I am the Lord.
So then, keep my orders and do them: I am the Lord.
And do not make my holy name common; so that it may be kept holy by the children of Israel: I am the Lord ho make you holy,
Who took you out of the land of Egypt that I might be your God: I am the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, These are the fixed feasts of the Lord, hich you ill keep for holy meetings: these are my feasts.
On six days ork may be done; but the seventh day is a special day of rest, a time for orship; you may do no sort of ork: it is a Sabbath to the Lord herever you may be living.
These are the fixed feasts of the Lord, the holy days of orship hich you ill keep at their regular times.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at nightfall, is the Lord’s Passover;
And on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread; for seven days let your food be unleavened bread.
On the first day you ill have a holy meeting; you may do no sort of field-ork.
And every day for seven days you ill give a burned offering to the Lord; and on the seventh day there ill be a holy meeting; you may do no field-ork.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, When you have come to the land hich I ill give you, and have got in the grain from its fields, take some of the first-fruits of the grain to the priest;
And let the grain be aved before the Lord, so that you may be pleasing to him; on the day after the Sabbath let it be aved by the priest.
And on the day of the aving of the grain, you are to give a male lamb of the first year, ithout any mark, for a burned offering to the Lord.

And let the meal offering ith it be to tenth parts of an ephah of the best meal mixed ith oil, an offering made by fire to the Lord for a seet smell; and the drink offering ith it is to be of ine, the fourth part of a hin.

And you may take no bread or dry grain or ne grain for food till the very day on hich you have given the offering for your God: this is a rule for ever through all your generations herever you are living.
And let seven full eeks be numbered from the day after the Sabbath, the day hen you give the grain for the ave offering;
Let fifty days be numbered, to the day after the seventh Sabbath; then you are to give a ne meal offering to the Lord.
Take from your houses to cakes of bread, made of a fifth part of an ephah of the best meal, cooked ith leaven, to be aved for first-fruits to the Lord.

And ith the bread, take seven lambs of the first year, ithout any marks, and one ox and to male sheep, to be a burned offering to the Lord, ith their meal offering and their drink offerings, an offering of a seet smell made by fire to the Lord.
And you are to give one male goat for a sin-offering and to male lambs of the first year for peace-offerings.
And these ill be aved by the priest, ith the bread of the first-fruits, for a ave offering to the Lord, ith the to lambs: they ill be holy to the Lord for the priest.
And on the same day, let it be given out that there ill be a holy meeting for you: you may do no field-ork on that day: it is a rule for ever through all your generations herever you are living.

And hen you get in the grain from your land, do not let all the grain at the edges of the field be cut, and do not take up the grain hich has been dropped in the field; let that be for the poor, and for the man from another country: I am the Lord your God.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, let there be a special day of rest for you, a day of memory, marked by the bloing of horns, a meeting for orship.
Do no field-ork and give to the Lord an offering made by fire.
And the Lord said to Moses,
The tenth day of this seventh month is the day for the taking aay of sin; let it be a holy day of orship; you are to keep from pleasure, and give to the Lord an offering made by fire.
And on that day you may do no sort of ork, for it is a day of taking aay sin, to make you clean before the Lord your God.
For any person, hoever he may be, ho takes his pleasure on that day ill be cut off from his people.
And if any person, hoever he may be, on that day does any sort of ork, I ill send destruction on him from among his people.
You may not do any sort of ork: this is an order for ever through all your generations herever you may be living.
Let this be a Sabbath of special rest to you, and keep yourselves from all pleasure; on the ninth day of the month at nightfall from evening to evening, let this Sabbath be kept.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, On the fifteenth day of this seventh month let the feast of tents be kept to the Lord for seven days.
On the first day there ill be a holy meeting: do no field-ork.

Every day for seven days give an offering made by fire to the Lord; and on the eighth day there is to be a holy meeting, hen you are to give an offering made by fire to the Lord; this is a special holy day: you may do no field-ork on that day.

These are the fixed feasts of the Lord, to be kept by you as holy days of orship, for making an offering by fire to the Lord; a burned offering, a meal offering, an offering of beasts, and drink offerings; every one on its special day;
In addition to the Sabbaths of the Lord, and in addition to the things you give and the oaths you make and the free offerings to the Lord.

But on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, hen you have got in all the fruits of the land, you ill keep the feast of the Lord for seven days: the first day ill be a Sabbath, and the eighth day the same.
On the first day, take the fruit of fair trees, branches of palm-trees, and branches of thick trees and trees from the riverside, and be glad before the Lord for seven days.
And let this feast be kept before the Lord for seven days in the year: it is a rule for ever from generation to generation; in the seventh month let it be kept.
For seven days you ill be living in tents; all those ho are Israelites by birth are to make tents their living-places:
So that future generations may keep in mind ho I gave the children of Israel tents as their living-places hen I took them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.
And Moses made clear to the children of Israel the orders about the fixed feasts of the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Give orders to the children of Israel to give you clean olive oil for the light, so that a light may be burning at all times,
Outside the veil of the ark in the Tent of meeting; let Aaron see that it is burning from evening till morning at all times before the Lord: it is a rule for ever through all your generations.
Let Aaron put the lights in order on the support before the Lord at all times.
And take the best meal and make telve cakes of it, a fifth part of an ephah in every cake.
And put them in to lines, six in a line, on the holy table before the Lord.
And on the lines of cakes put clean seet-smelling spices, for a sign on the bread, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
Every Sabbath day regularly, the priest is to put it in order before the Lord: it is offered for the children of Israel, an agreement made for ever.
And it ill be for Aaron and his sons; they are to take it for food in a holy place: it is the most holy of all the offerings made by fire to the Lord, a rule for ever.
And a son of an Israelite oman, hose father as an Egyptian, ent out among the children of Israel and had a fight ith a man of Israel by the tents;
And the son of the Israelite oman said evil against the holy Name, ith curses; and they took him to Moses. His mother’s name as Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
And they kept him shut up, till a decision might be given by the mouth of the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Take the curser outside the tent-circle; and let all in hose hearing the ords ere said put their hands on his head, and let him be stoned by all the people.
And say to the children of Israel, As for any man cursing God, his sin ill be on his head.

And he ho says evil against the name of the Lord ill certainly be put to death; he ill be stoned by all the people; the man ho is not of your nation and one ho is an Israelite by birth, hoever says evil against the holy Name is to be put to death.
And anyone ho takes another’s life is certainly to be put to death.
And anyone ounding a beast and causing its death, ill have to make payment for it: a life for a life.
And if a man does damage to his neighbour, as he has done, so let it be done to him;
Wound for ound, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; hatever damage he has done, so let it be done to him.
He ho puts a beast to death ill have to make payment for it; he ho puts a man to death ill himself be put to death.
You are to have the same la for a man of another nation living among you as for an Israelite; for I am the Lord your God.
And Moses said these ords to the children of Israel, and they took the man ho had been cursing outside the tent-circle and had him stoned. The children of Israel did as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses on Mount Sinai,
Say to the children of Israel, When you come into the land hich I ill give you, let the land keep a Sabbath to the Lord.
For six years put seed into your land, and for six years give care to your vines and get in the produce of them;
But let the seventh year be a Sabbath of rest for the land, a Sabbath to the Lord; do not put seed into your land or have your vines cut.
That hich comes to groth of itself may not be cut, and the grapes of your uncared-for vines may not be taken off; let it be a year of rest for the land.
And the Sabbath of the land ill give food for you and your man-servant and your oman-servant and those orking for payment, and for those of another country ho are living among you;
And for your cattle and the beasts on the land; all the natural increase of the land ill be for food.
And let seven Sabbaths of years be numbered to you, seven times seven years; even the days of seven Sabbaths of years, that is forty-nine years;
Then let the loud horn be sounded far and ide on the tenth day of the seventh month; on the day of taking aay sin let the horn be sounded through all your land.
And let this fiftieth year be kept holy, and say publicly that everyone in the land is free from debt: it is the Jubilee, and every man may go back to his heritage and to his family.
Let this fiftieth year be the Jubilee: no seed may be planted, and that hich comes to groth of itself may not be cut, and the grapes may not be taken from the uncared-for vines.
For it is the Jubilee, and it is holy to you; your food ill be the natural increase of the field.
In this year of Jubilee, let every man go back to his heritage.
And in the business of trading goods for money, do no rong to one another.
Let your exchange of goods ith your neighbours have relation to the number of years after the year of Jubilee, and the number of times the earth has given her produce.
If the number of years is great, the price ill be increased, and if the number of years is small, the price ill be less, for it is the produce of a certain number of years hich the man is giving you.
And do no rong, one to another, but let the fear of your God be before you; for I am the Lord your God.
So keep my rules and my decisions and do them, and you ill be safe in your land.
And the land ill give her fruit, and you ill have food in full measure and be safe in the land.
And if you say, Where ill our food come from in the seventh year, hen e may not put in seed, or get in the increase
Then I ill send my blessing on you in the sixth year, and the land ill give fruit enough for three years.
And in the eighth year you ill put in your seed, and get your food from the old stores, till the fruit of the ninth year is ready.
No exchange of land may be for ever, for the land is mine, and you are as my guests, living ith me for a time.
Wherever there is property in land, the oner is to have the right of getting it back.
If your brother becomes poor, and has to give up some of his land for money, his nearest relation may come and get back that hich his brother has given up.
And if he has no one to get it back for him, and later he himself gets ealth and has enough money to get it back;
Then let him take into account the years from the time hen he gave it up, and make up the loss for the rest of the years to him ho took it, and so get back his property.

But if he is not able to get it back for himself, then it ill be kept by him ho gave a price for it, till the year of Jubilee; and in that year it ill go back to its first oner and he ill have his property again.
And if a man gives his house in a alled ton for money, he has the right to get it back for the space of a full year after he has given it up.

And if he does not get it back by the end of the year, then the house in the ton ill become the property of him ho gave the money for it, and of his children for ever; it ill not go from him in the year of Jubilee.
But houses in small unalled tons ill be the same as property in the country; they may be got back, and they ill go back to their oners in the year of Jubilee.
But the houses in the tons of the Levites may be got back by the Levites at any time.

And if a Levite does not give money to get back his property, his house in the ton hich as exchanged for money ill come back to him in the year of Jubilee. For the houses of the tons of the Levites are their property among the children of Israel.
But the land on the outskirts of their tons may not be exchanged for money, for it is their property for ever.
And if your brother becomes poor and is not able to make a living, then you are to keep him ith you, helping him as you ould a man from another country ho is living among you.
Take no interest from him, in money or in goods, but have the fear of your God before you, and let your brother make a living among you.
Do not take interest on the money hich you let him have or on the food hich you give him.
I am the Lord your God, ho took you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan, that I might be your God.
And if your brother becomes poor and gives himself to you for money, do not make use of him like a servant ho is your property;
But let him be ith you as a servant orking for payment, till the year of Jubilee;
Then he ill go out from you, he and his children ith him, and go back to his family and to the property of his fathers.
For they are my servants hom I took out from the land of Egypt; they may not become the property of another.
Do not be a hard master to him, but have the fear of God before you.
But you may get servants as property from among the nations round about; from them you may take men-servants and omen-servants.

And in addition, you may get, for money, servants from among the children of other nations ho are living ith you, and from their families hich have come to birth in your land; and these ill be your property.
And they ill be your children’s heritage after you, to keep as their property; they ill be your servants for ever; but you may not be hard masters to your countrymen, the children of Israel.
And if one from another nation living among you gets ealth, and your countryman, at his side, becomes poor and gives himself for money to the man from another nation or to one of his family;
After he has given himself he has the right to be made free, for a price, by one of his brothers,
Or his father’s brother, or the son of his father’s brother, or any near relation; or if he gets money, he may make himself free.

And let the years be numbered from the time hen he gave himself to his oner till the year of Jubilee, and the price given for him ill be in relation to the number of years, on the scale of the payment of a servant.
If there is still a long time, he ill give back, on account of it, a part of the price hich as given for him.
And if there is only a short time, he ill take account of it ith his master, and in relation to the number of years he ill give back the price of making him free.
And he ill be ith him as a servant orking for payment year by year; his master is not to be cruel to him before your eyes.
And if he is not made free in this ay, he ill go out in the year of Jubilee, he and his children ith him.
For the children of Israel are servants to me; they are my servants hom I took out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.
Do not make images of false gods, or put up an image cut in stone or a pillar or any pictured stone in your land, to give orship to it; for I am the Lord your God.
Keep my Sabbaths and give honour to my holy place: I am the Lord.
If you are guided by my rules, and keep my las and do them,
Then I ill give you rain at the right time, and the land ill give her increase and the trees of the field ill give their fruit;

And the crushing of the grain ill overtake the cutting of the grapes, and the cutting of the grapes ill overtake the planting of the seed, and there ill be bread in full measure, and you ill be living in your land safely.

And I ill give you peace in the land, and you ill take your rest and no one ill give you cause for fear; and I ill put an end to all evil beasts in the land, and no sord of ar ill go through your land.
And you ill put to flight those ho are against you, and they ill be put to death by your sords.
Then five of you ill put to flight a hundred, and a hundred of you ill put to flight ten thousand, and all ho are against you ill be put to death by your sords.
And I ill have pleasure in you and make you fertile and greater in number; and I ill keep my agreement ith you.
And old stores long kept ill be your food, and you ill take out the old because of the ne;
And I ill put my holy House among you, and my soul ill not be turned aay from you in disgust.
And I ill be present among you and ill be your God and you ill be my people.
I am the Lord your God, ho took you out of the land of Egypt so that you might not be servants to them; by me the cords of your yoke ere broken and I made you go upright.
But if you do not give ear to me, and do not keep all these my las;
And if you go against my rules and if you have hate in your souls for my decisions and you do not do all my orders, but go against my agreement;

This ill I do to you: I ill put fear in your hearts, even asting disease and burning pain, drying up the eyes and making the soul feeble, and you ill get no profit from your seed, for your haters ill take it for food.
And my face ill be turned from you, and you ill be broken before those ho are against you, and your haters ill become your rulers, and you ill go in flight hen no man comes after you.
And if, even after these things, you ill not give ear to me, then I ill send you punishment seven times more for your sins.
And the pride of your strength ill be broken, and I ill make your heaven as iron and your earth as brass;
And your strength ill be used up ithout profit; for your land ill not give her increase and the trees of the field ill not give their fruit.
And if you still go against me and ill not give ear to me, I ill put seven times more punishments on you because of your sins.
I ill let loose the beasts of the field among you, and they ill take aay your children and send destruction on your cattle, so that your numbers ill become small and your roads become aste.
And if by these things you ill not be turned to me, but still go against me;
Then I ill go against you, and I ill give you punishment, I myself, seven times for all your sins.

And I ill send a sord on you to give effect to the punishment of my agreement; and hen you come together into your tons I ill send disease among you and you ill be given up into the hands of your haters.
When I take aay your bread of life, ten omen ill be cooking bread in one oven, and your bread ill be measured out by eight; you ill have food but never enough.
And if, after all this, you do not give ear to me, but go against me still,
Then my rath ill be burning against you, and I ill give you punishment, I myself, seven times for your sins.
Then you ill take the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters for food;
And I ill send destruction on your high places, overturning your perfume altars, and ill put your dead bodies on your broken images, and my soul ill be turned from you in disgust.
And I ill make your tons aste and send destruction on your holy places; I ill take no pleasure in the smell of your seet perfumes;
And I ill make your land a aste, a onder to your haters living in it.
And I ill send you out in all directions among the nations, and my sord ill be uncovered against you, and your land ill be ithout any living thing, and your tons ill be made aste.
Then ill the land take pleasure in its Sabbaths hile it is aste and you are living in the land of your haters; then ill the land have rest.
All the days hile it is aste ill the land have rest, such rest as it never had in your Sabbaths, hen you ere living in it.

And as for the rest of you, I ill make their hearts feeble in the land of their haters, and the sound of a leaf moved by the ind ill send them in flight, and they ill go in flight as from the sord, falling don hen no one comes after them;
Falling on one another, as before the sord, hen no one comes after them; you ill give ay before your haters.
And death ill overtake you among strange nations, and the land of your haters ill be your destruction.
And those of you ho are still living ill be asting aay in their sins in the land of your haters; in the sins of their fathers they ill be asting aay.
And they ill have grief for their sins and for the sins of their fathers, hen their hearts ere untrue to me, and they ent against me;
So that I ent against them and sent them aay into the land of their haters: if then the pride of their hearts is broken and they take the punishment of their sins,
Then I ill keep in mind the agreement hich I made ith Jacob and ith Isaac and ith Abraham, and I ill keep in mind the land.
And the land, hile she is ithout them, ill keep her Sabbaths; and they ill undergo the punishment of their sins, because they ere turned aay from my decisions and in their souls as hate for my las.

But for all that, hen they are in the land of their haters I ill not let them go, or be turned aay from them, or give them up completely; my agreement ith them ill not be broken, for I am the Lord their God.
And because of them I ill keep in mind the agreement hich I made ith their fathers, hom I took out of the land of Egypt before the eyes of the nations, to be their God: I am the Lord.
These are the rules, decisions, and las, hich the Lord made beteen himself and the children of Israel in Mount Sinai, by the hand of Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, If a man makes a special oath, you ill give your decision as to the value of the persons for the Lord.
And you ill put the value of a male from tenty years to sixty years old at fifty shekels of silver, by the scale of the holy place.
And if it is a female, the value ill be thirty shekels.
And if the person is from five to tenty years old, the value ill be tenty shekels for a male, and ten for a female.
And if the person is from one month to five years old, then the value for a male ill be five shekels of silver, and for a female three shekels.
And for sixty years old and over, for a male the value ill be fifteen shekels, and for a female, ten.
But if he is poorer than the value hich you have put on him, then let him be taken to the priest, and the priest ill put a value on him, such as it is possible for him to give.
And if it is a beast of hich men make offerings to the Lord, hatever any man gives of such to the Lord ill be holy.
It may not be changed in any ay, a good given for a bad, or a bad for a good; if one beast is changed for another, the to ill be holy.
And if it is any unclean beast, of hich offerings are not made to the Lord, then let him take the beast before the priest;
And let the priest put a value on it, if it is good or bad; hatever value the priest puts on it, so ill it be.
But if he has a desire to get it back for himself, let him give a fifth more than your value.
And if a man has given his house as holy to the Lord, then the priest ill put a value on it, if it is good or bad; as the priest gives decision so ill the value be fixed.
And if the oner has a desire to get back his house, let him give a fifth more than your value, and it ill be his.
