And if a man gives to the Lord part of the field hich is his property, then let your value be in relation to the seed hich is planted in it; a measure of barley grain ill be valued at fifty shekels of silver.
If he gives his field from the year of Jubilee, the value ill be fixed by your decision.

But if he gives his field after the year of Jubilee, the amount of the money ill be orked out by the priest in relation to the number of years till the coming year of Jubilee, and the necessary amount ill be taken off your value.
And if the man ho has given the field has a desire to get it back, let him give a fifth more than the price at hich it as valued and it ill be his.
But if he has no desire to get it back, or if he has given it for a price to another man, it may not be got back again.
But the field, hen it becomes free at the year of Jubilee, ill be holy to the Lord, as a field given under oath: it ill be the property of the priest.
And if a man gives to the Lord a field hich he has got for money from another, hich is not part of his heritage;
Then the value fixed by you up to the year of Jubilee ill be orked out for him by the priest, and in that day he ill give the amount of your value as holy to the Lord.
In the year of Jubilee the field ill go back to him from hom he got it, that is, to him hose heritage it as.
And let all your values be based on the shekel of the holy place, that is, tenty gerahs to the shekel.
But a man may not give by oath to the Lord the first-fruits of cattle hich are offered to the Lord: if it is an ox or a sheep it is the Lord’s.

And if it is an unclean beast, then the oner of it may give money to get it back, in agreement ith the value fixed by you, by giving a fifth more; or if it is not taken back, let it be given for money in agreement ith your valuing.

But nothing hich a man has given completely to the Lord, out of all his property, of man or beast, or of the land hich is his heritage, may be given aay or got back in exchange for money; anything completely given is most holy to the Lord.
Any man given completely to the Lord may not be got back: he is certainly to be put to death.
And every tenth part of the land, of the seed planted, or of the fruit of trees, is holy to the Lord.
And if a man has a desire to get back any of the tenth part hich he has given, let him give a fifth more.
And a tenth part of the herd and of the flock, hatever goes under the rod of the valuer, ill be holy to the Lord.
He may not make search to see if it is good or bad, or make any changes in it; and if he makes exchange of it for another, the to ill be holy; he ill not get them back again.
These are the orders hich the Lord gave to Moses for the children of Israel in Mount Sinai.
And the Lord said to Moses in the aste land of Sinai, in the Tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt,
Take the full number of the children of Israel, by their families, and by their fathers’ houses, every male by name;
All those of tenty years old and over, ho are able to go to ar in Israel, are to be numbered by you and Aaron.
And to give you help, take one man from every tribe, the head of his father’s house.
These are the names of those ho are to be your helpers: from Reuben, Elizur, the son of Shedeur;
From Simeon, Shelumiel, the son of Zurishaddai;
From Judah, Nahshon, the son of Amminadab;
From Issachar, Nethanel, the son of Zuar;
From Zebulun, Eliab, the son of Helon;
Of the children of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama, the son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel, the son of Pedahzur,
From Benjamin, Abidan, the son of Gideoni;
From Dan, Ahiezer, the son of Ammi-shaddai;
From Asher, Pagiel, the son of Ochran;
From Gad, Eliasaph, the son of Reuel;
From Naphtali, Ahira, the son of Enan.
These are the men named out of all the people, chiefs of their fathers’ houses, heads of the tribes of Israel.
And Moses and Aaron took these men, marked out by name;
And they got together all the people on the first day of the second month; and everyone made clear his family and his father’s house, by the number of the names, from tenty years old and over.
As the Lord had given orders to Moses, so they ere numbered by him in the aste place of Sinai.
The generations of the sons of Reuben, the oldest son of Israel, ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over, ho as able to go to ar;
Forty-six thousand, five hundred of the tribe of Reuben ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Simeon ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over, ho as able to go to ar;
Fifty-nine thousand, three hundred of the tribe of Simeon ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Gad ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Forty-five thousand, six hundred and fifty of the tribe of Gad ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Judah ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Seventy-four thousand, six hundred of the tribe of Judah ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Issachar ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Fifty-four thousand, four hundred of the tribe of Issachar ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Zebulun ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Fifty-seven thousand, four hundred of the tribe of Zebulun ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Joseph ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Forty thousand, five hundred of the tribe of Ephraim ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Manasseh ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Thirty-to thousand, to hundred of the tribe of Manasseh ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Benjamin ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Thirty-five thousand, four hundred of the tribe of Benjamin ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Dan ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years and over ho as able to go to ar;
Sixty-to thousand, seven hundred of the tribe of Dan ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Asher ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Forty-one thousand, five hundred of the tribe of Asher ere numbered.
The generations of the sons of Naphtali ere numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses, every male of tenty years old and over ho as able to go to ar;
Fifty-three thousand, four hundred of the tribe of Naphtali ere numbered.
These are they ho ere numbered by Moses and Aaron and by the telve chiefs of Israel, one from every tribe.
So all those ho ere numbered of the children of Israel, by their families, all those of tenty years old and over ho ere able to go to ar,
Were six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty.
But the Levites, of the tribe of their fathers, ere not numbered among them.
For the Lord said to Moses,
Only the tribe of Levi is not to be numbered among the children of Israel,

But to them you are to give the care of the Tent of meeting ith its vessels and everything in it: they are to take up the Tent, and be responsible for everything to do ith it, and put up their tents round it.
And hen the Tent of meeting goes forard, the Levites are to take it don; and hen it is to be put up, they are to do it: any strange person ho comes near it is to be put to death.
The children of Israel are to put up their tents, every man in his tent-circle round his flag.
But the tents of the Levites are to be round the Tent of meeting, so that rath may not come on the children of Israel: the Tent of meeting is to be in the care of the Levites.
So the children of Israel did as the Lord had given orders to Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
The children of Israel are to put up their tents in the order of their families, by the flags of their fathers’ houses, facing the Tent of meeting on every side.
Those hose tents are on the east side, looking to the dan, ill be round the flag of the children of Judah, ith Nahshon, the son of Amminadab, as their chief.
The number of his army as seventy-four thousand, six hundred.
And nearest to him ill be the tribe of Issachar, ith Nethanel, the son of Zuar, as their chief.
The number of his army as fifty-four thousand, four hundred.
After him, the tribe of Zebulun, ith Eliab, the son of Helon, as their chief.
The number of his army as fifty-seven thousand, four hundred.
The number of all the armies of Judah as a hundred and eighty-six thousand, four hundred. They go forard first.
On the south side is the flag of the children of Reuben, in the order of their armies, ith Elizur, the son of Shedeur, as their chief.
The number of his army as forty-six thousand, five hundred.
And nearest to him, the tribe of Simeon, ith Shelumiel, the son of Zurishaddai, as their chief.
The number of his army as fifty-nine thousand, three hundred.
Then the tribe of Gad, ith Eliasaph, son of Reuel, as their chief.
The number of his army as forty-five thousand, six hundred and fifty.
The number of all the armies of Reuben together came to a hundred and fifty-one thousand, four hundred and fifty. They go forard second.
Then the Tent of meeting is to go forard, ith the tents of the Levites, in the middle of the armies; in the same order as their tents are placed, they are to go forard, every man under his flag.
On the est side ill be the flag of the children of Ephraim, ith Elishama, the son of Ammihud, as their chief.
The number of his army as forty thousand, five hundred.
And by him the tribe of Manasseh ith Gamaliel, the son of Pedahzur, as their chief.
The number of his army as thirty-to thousand, to hundred.
Then the tribe of Benjamin, ith Abidan, the son of Gideoni, as their chief.
The number of his army as thirty-five thousand, four hundred.
The number of all the armies of Ephraim as a hundred and eight thousand, one hundred. They go forard third.
On the north side ill be the flag of the children of Dan, ith Ahiezer, the son of Ammishaddai, as their chief.
The number of his army as sixty-to thousand, seven hundred.
Nearest to him ill be the tribe of Asher, ith Pagiel, the son of Ochran, as their chief.
The number of his army as forty-one thousand, five hundred;
Then the tribe of Naphtali, ith Ahira, the son of Enan, as their chief.
The number of his army as fifty-three thousand, four hundred.
The number of all the armies in the tents of Dan as a hundred and fifty-seven thousand, six hundred. They ill go forard last, by their flags.

These are all ho ere numbered of the children of Israel, in the order of their fathers’ families: all the armies in their tents together came to six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty.
But the Levites ere not numbered among the children of Israel, as the Lord said to Moses.
So the children of Israel did as the Lord said to Moses, so they put up their tents by their flags, and they ent forard in the same order, by their families, and by their fathers’ houses.
No these are the generations of Aaron and Moses, in the day hen the ord of the Lord came to Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the oldest, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the priests, on hom the holy oil as put, ho ere marked out as priests.

And Nadab and Abihu ere put to death before the Lord hen they made an offering of strange fire before the Lord, in the aste land of Sinai, and they had no children: and Eleazar and Ithamar did the ork of priests before Aaron their father.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Make the tribe of Levi come near, and put them before Aaron the priest, to be his helpers,
In order that they may be responsible to him and to all Israel for the care of the Tent of meeting, and to do the ork of the House;
And they ill have the care of all the vessels of the Tent of meeting, and ill do for the children of Israel all the necessary ork of the House.
Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; so that they may be his ithout question from among the children of Israel.
And give orders that Aaron and his sons are to keep their place as priests; any strange person ho comes near is to be put to death.
And the Lord said to Moses,
See, I have taken the Levites out of the children of Israel to be mine in place of the first sons of the children of Israel;
For all the first sons are mine; on the day hen I put to death all the first sons in the land of Egypt, I took for myself every first male birth of man and beast. They are mine; I am the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses in the aste land of Sinai,
Let all the children of Levi be numbered by their families and their fathers’ houses; let every male of a month old and over be numbered.
So Moses did as the Lord said, numbering them as he had been ordered.
These ere the sons of Levi by name: Gershon and Kohath and Merari.
And these are the names of the sons of Gershon, by their families: Libni and Shimei.
And the sons of Kohath, by their families: Amram and Izhar and Hebron and Uzziel.
And the sons of Merari by their families: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites in the order of their fathers’ houses.
From Gershon come the Libnites and the Shimeites; these are the families of the Gershonites.
Those ho ere numbered of them, the males from one month old and over, ere seven thousand, five hundred.
The tents of the Gershonites are to be placed at the back of the House, to the est.
The chief of the Gershonites is Eliasaph, the son of Lael.
In the Tent of meeting, the Gershonites are to have the care of the House, and the Tent ith its cover, and the veil for the door of the Tent of meeting,
And the hangings for the open space round the House and the altar, and the curtain for its dooray, and all the cords needed for its use.
From Kohath come the Amramites and the Izharites and the Hebronites and the Uzzielites; these are the families of the Kohathites.
Those ho ere numbered of them, the males from one month old and over, ere eight thousand, six hundred, ho ere responsible for the care of the holy place.
The tents of the Kohathites are to be placed on the south side of the House.
Their chief is Elizaphan, the son of Uzziel.
In their care are the ark, and the table, and the lights, and the altars, and all the vessels used in the holy place, and the veil, and all they are used for.
Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, ill be head over all the Levites and overseer of those responsible for the care of the holy place.
From Merari come the Mahlites and the Mushites; these are the families of Merari.
Those ho ere numbered of them, the males of a month old and over, ere six thousand, to hundred.
The chief of the families of Merari as Zuriel, the son of Abihail: their tents are to be placed on the north side of the House.
And in their care are to be all the boards of the Tent, ith their rods and pillars and bases, and all the instruments, and all they are used for,
And the pillars of the open space round it, ith their bases and nails and cords.

And those hose tents are to be placed on the east side of the House in front of the Tent of meeting, looking to the dan, are Moses and Aaron and his sons, ho ill do the ork of the holy place for the children of Israel; and any strange person ho comes near ill be put to death.
All the Levites numbered by Moses and Aaron at the order of the Lord, all the males of one month old and over numbered in the order of their families, ere tenty-to thousand.
And the Lord said to Moses, Let all the first male children be numbered, and take the number of their names.

And give to me the Levites ( I am the Lord) in place of the first sons of the children of Israel; and the cattle of the Levites in place of the first births among the cattle of the children of Israel.
So Moses had all the first sons among the children of Israel numbered, as the Lord said to him.
Every first son from a month old and over as numbered by name, and the number came to tenty-to thousand, to hundred and seventy-three.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Take the Levites in place of all the first sons of the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites in place of their cattle; the Levites are to be mine; I am the Lord.
And the price you have to give for the to hundred and seventy-three first sons of the children of Israel hich are in addition to the number of the Levites,
Will be five shekels for every one, by the scale of the holy place ( the shekel is tenty gerahs);
And this money, the price of those over the number of the Levites, is to be given to Aaron and his sons.
So Moses took the money, the price of those hose place had not been taken by the Levites;
From the first sons of Israel he took it, a thousand, three hundred and sixty-five shekels, by the scale of the holy place;
And he gave the money to Aaron and his sons, as the Lord had said.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
Let the sons of Kohath, from among the sons of Levi, be numbered by their families, in the order of their fathers’ houses;
All those from thirty to fifty years old ho are able to do the ork of the Tent of meeting.
And this is to be the ork of the sons of Kohath in connection ith the most holy things.
When all the people go forard, Aaron is to go in ith his sons, and take don the veil of the curtain, covering the ark of itness ith it;
And putting over it the leather cover and over that a blue cloth; and putting its rods in place.
And on the table of the holy bread they are to put a blue cloth, and on it all the vessels, the spoons and the basins and the cups; and the holy bread ith them;
And over them they are to put a red cloth, covering it ith a leather cover, and putting its rods in their places.
And they are to take a blue cloth, covering ith it the light-support ith its lights and its instruments and its trays and all the oil vessels hich are used for it:
All these they are to put in a leather cover, and put it on the frame.
On the gold altar they are to put a blue cloth, covering it ith a leather cover; and they are to put its rods in their places.
All the vessels hich are used in the holy place they are to put in a blue cloth, covering them ith a leather cover, and put them on the frame.
And they are to take aay the burned aste from the altar, and put a purple cloth on it;

Placing on the cloth all its vessels, the fire-baskets, the meat-hooks, the spades, and the basins; all the vessels of the altar; they are to put a leather cover over all these, and put its rods in their places.

And after the holy place and all its vessels have been covered up by Aaron and his sons, hen the tents of the people go forard, the sons of Kohath are to come and take it up; but the holy things may not be touched by them for fear of death.

And Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, is to be responsible for the oil for the light, and the seet perfumes for burning, and the regular meal offering, and the holy oil; the House and the holy place and everything in it ill be in his care.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
Do not let the family of the Kohathites be cut off from among the Levites;
But do this to them, so that life and not death may be theirs hen they come near the most holy things; let Aaron and his sons go in and give to every one his ork and that hich he is to take up;
But they themselves are not to go in to see the holy place, even for a minute, for fear of death.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Let the sons of Gershon be numbered by families, in the order of their fathers’ houses;
All those from thirty to fifty years old ho are able to do the ork of the Tent of meeting.
This is to be the ork of the Gershonites, the things they are to do and take up.
They are to take up the curtains of the House, and the Tent of meeting ith its cover and the leather cover over it, and the hangings for the door of the Tent of meeting;
And the hangings for the open space round the House and the altar, and the curtain for its dooray, ith the cords and all the things used for them; hatever is necessary for these, they are to do.
From the mouth of Aaron and his sons the Gershonites ill have ord about all the things they are to do and take up; you are to give them their orders.
This is the ork of the family of the Gershonites in the Tent of meeting, and they ill be under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
The sons of Merari are to be numbered by families, in the order of their fathers’ houses;
Every one from thirty to fifty years old ho is able to do the ork of the Tent of meeting.
And this is their part in the ork of the Tent of meeting: the transport of the boards and the rods of the Tent, ith the pillars and their bases;

And the pillars of the open space outside it, ith their bases and their nails and cords and all the instruments used, and everything hich has to be done there; all the instruments for hich they are responsible are to be numbered by name.
This is the ork hich the sons of Merari are to do in connection ith the Tent of meeting, under the direction of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
So Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of the people took in hand the numbering of the sons of the Kohathites, by families, in the order of their fathers’ houses;
Numbering all those from thirty to fifty years old ho ere able to do the ork in the Tent of meeting;
And the number of all these as to thousand, seven hundred and fifty.
This is the number of those of the Kohathites ho did the ork in the Tent of meeting, as they ere numbered by Moses and Aaron at the order of the Lord.
And those of the sons of Gershon ho ere numbered by families,
All those from thirty to fifty years old ho ere able to do the ork in the Tent of meeting,
Who ere numbered by families in the order of their fathers’ houses, ere to thousand, six hundred and thirty.
This is the number of the sons of Gershon ho did the ork in the Tent of meeting, as they ere numbered by Moses and Aaron at the order of the Lord.
And those of the sons of Merari ho ere numbered by families, in the order of their fathers’ houses,
All those from thirty to fifty years old ho did the ork in the Tent of meeting,
Who ere numbered by families, ere three thousand, to hundred.
This is the number of the sons of Merari, numbered by Moses and Aaron at the order of the Lord.
And all the Levites ho ere numbered by Moses and Aaron and the chiefs of the people, by families, in the order of their fathers’ houses,
Those from thirty to fifty years old ho ere able to do the ork of the Tent of meeting and of its transport,
Came to eight thousand, five hundred and eighty.
At the order of the Lord they ere numbered by Moses, every one in relation to his ork and to his part in the transport; so they ere numbered by Moses at the order of the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Give orders to the children of Israel to put outside the tent-circle every leper, and anyone ho has any sort of flo from his body, and anyone ho is unclean from the touch of the dead;
Male or female they are to be put outside the tent-circle, so that they may not make unclean my resting-place among them.
So the children of Israel did as the Lord had said to Moses, and put them outside the tent-circle.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, If a man or a oman does any of the sins of men, going against the ord of the Lord, and is in the rong;
Let them say openly hat they have done; and make payment for the rong done, ith the addition of a fifth part, and give it to him to hom the rong as done.
But if the man has no relation to hom the payment may be made, then the payment for sin made to the Lord ill be the priest’s, in addition to the sheep offered to take aay his sin.
And every offering lifted up of all the holy things hich the children of Israel give to the priest, ill be his.
And every man’s holy things ill be his: hatever a man gives to the priest ill be his.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, If any man’s ife does rong, sinning against him
By taking as her lover another man, and keeps it secret so that her husband has no knoledge of it, and there is no itness against her, and she is not taken in the act;
If the spirit of doubt comes into her husband’s heart, and he has doubts of his ife, ith good cause; or if he has doubts of her ithout cause:

Then let him take her to the priest, offering for her the tenth part of an ephah of barley meal, ithout oil or perfume; for it is a meal offering of a bitter spirit, a meal offering keeping rongdoing in mind.
And the priest ill make her come near and put her before the Lord;
And the priest ill take holy ater in a pot and put in it dust from the floor of the House;

And he ill make the oman come before the Lord ith her hair loose, and ill put the meal offering, the offering of a bitter spirit, in her hands; and the priest ill take in his hand the bitter ater causing the curse;
And he ill make her take an oath, and say to her, If no man has been your lover and you have not been ith another in place of your husband, you are free from this bitter ater causing the curse;
But if you have been ith another in place of your husband and have made yourself unclean ith a lover:
Then the priest ill put the oath of the curse on the oman, and say to her, May the Lord make you a curse and an oath among your people, sending on you asting of the legs and disease of the stomach;
And this ater of the curse ill go into your body, causing disease of your stomach and asting of your legs: and the oman ill say, So be it.
And the priest ill put these curses in a book, ashing out the riting ith the bitter ater;
And he ill give to the oman the bitter ater for drink; and the bitter ater causing the curse ill go into her.
And the priest ill take from her hand the meal offering of doubt, aving it before the Lord, and ill take it to the altar;
And he ill take some of it in his hand, burning it on the altar as a sign, and then he ill give the oman the bitter ater.

And it ill be that if the oman has become unclean, sinning against her husband, hen she has taken the bitter ater it ill go into her body, causing disease of the stomach and asting of the legs, and she ill be a curse among her people.
But if she is clean she ill be free and ill have offspring.
This is the la for testing a ife ho goes ith another in place of her husband and becomes unclean;
Or for a husband ho, in a bitter spirit, has doubts in his heart about his ife; let him take her to the priest, ho ill put in force this la.
Then the man ill be free from all rong, and the oman’s sin ill be on her.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, If a man or a oman takes an oath to keep himself separate and give himself to the Lord;
He is to keep himself from ine and strong drink, and take no mixed ine or strong drink or any drink made from grapes, or any grapes, green or dry.
All the time he is separate he may take nothing made from the grape-vine, from its seeds to its skin.
All the time he is under his oath let no blade come near his head; till the days hile he is separate are ended he is holy and his hair may not be cut.
All the time he is separate he may not come near any dead body.
He may not make himself unclean for his father or his mother, his sister or his brother, if death comes to them; because he is under an oath to keep himself separate for God.
All the time he is separate he is holy to the Lord.
If death comes suddenly to a man at his side, so that he becomes unclean, let his hair be cut off on the day hen he is made clean, on the seventh day.
And on the eighth day let him take to the priest, at the door of the Tent of meeting, to doves or to young pigeons;
And the priest ill give one for a sin-offering and the other for a burned offering to take aay the sin hich came on him on account of the dead, and he ill make his head holy that same day.
And he ill give to the Lord his days of being separate, offering a he-lamb of the first year as an offering for error: but the earlier days ill be a loss, because he became unclean.
And this is the la for him ho is separate, hen the necessary days are ended: he is to come to the door of the Tent of meeting,

And make his offering to the Lord; one he-lamb of the first year, ithout a mark, for a burned offering, and one female lamb of the first year, ithout a mark, for a sin-offering, and one male sheep, ithout a mark, for peace-offerings,
And a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of the best meal mixed ith oil, and thin unleavened cakes covered ith oil, ith their meal offering and drink offerings.
And the priest ill take them before the Lord, and make his sin-offering and his burned offering;
Giving the sheep of the peace-offerings, ith the basket of unleavened bread; and at the same time, the priest ill make his meal offering and his drink offering.
Then let his long hair, the sign of his oath, be cut off at the door of the Tent of meeting, and let him put it on the fire on hich the peace-offerings are burning.
And the priest ill take the cooked leg of the sheep and one unleavened cake and one thin cake out of the basket, and put them on the hands of the separate one after his hair has been cut,
Waving them for a ave offering before the Lord; this is holy for the priest, together ith the aved breast and the leg hich is lifted up; after that, the man may take ine.

And the Lord said to Moses,

And hen Moses ent into the Tent of meeting to have talk ith him, then the Voice came to his ears from over the cover hich as on the ark of itness, from beteen the to inged ones. And he had talk ith him.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to Aaron, When you put the lights in their places, the seven lights ill give light in front of the support.
And Aaron did so; he put the lights in their places so that they gave light in front of the support, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
The support for the lights as of hammered gold ork, from its base to its floers it as of hammered ork; from the design hich the Lord had given to Moses, he made the support for the lights.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Take the Levites out from among the children of Israel and make them clean.

And this is ho you are to make them clean: let the holy ater hich takes aay sin be put on them, and let the hair all over their bodies be cut off ith a sharp blade, and let their clothing be ashed and their bodies made clean.
Then let them take a young ox and its meal offering, crushed grain mixed ith oil, and take another ox for a sin-offering.
And make the Levites come forard in front of the Tent of meeting, and let all the children of Israel come together:
And you are to take the Levites before the Lord: and the children of Israel are to put their hands on them:
And Aaron is to give the Levites to the Lord as a ave offering from the children of Israel, so that they may do the Lord’s ork.

And the Levites are to put their hands on the heads of the oxen, and one of the oxen is to be offered for a sin-offering and the other for a burned offering to the Lord to take aay the sin of the Levites.
Then the Levites are to be put before Aaron and his sons, to be offered as a ave offering to the Lord.
So you are to make the Levites separate from the children of Israel, and the Levites ill be mine.
After that, the Levites ill go in to do hatever has to be done in the Tent of meeting; you are to make them clean and give them as a ave offering.
For they have been given to me from among the children of Israel; in place of every mother’s first son, the first to come to birth in Israel, I have taken them for myself.
For every mother’s first son among the children of Israel is mine, the first male birth of man or beast: on the day hen I sent death on all the first sons in the land of Egypt, I made them mine.
And in place of the first sons among the children of Israel, I have taken the Levites.

And I have given them to Aaron and to his sons, from among the children of Israel, to undertake for them all the ork of the Tent of meeting, and to take aay sin from the children of Israel so that no evil may come on them hen they come near the holy place.
All these things Moses and Aaron and the children of Israel did to the Levites; as the Lord gave orders to Moses about the Levites, so the children of Israel did.
And the Levites ere made clean from sin, and their clothing as ashed, and Aaron gave them for a ave offering before the Lord; and Aaron took aay their sin and made them clean.
And then the Levites ent in to do their ork in the Tent of meeting before Aaron and his sons: all the orders hich the Lord had given Moses about the Levites ere put into effect.
And the Lord said to Moses,
This is the rule for the Levites: those of tenty-five years old and over are to go in and do the ork of the Tent of meeting;
But after they are fifty years old, they are to give up their ork and do no more;
But be ith their brothers in the Tent of meeting, taking care of it but doing no ork. This is hat you are to do in connection ith the Levites and their ork.
And the Lord said to Moses, in the aste land of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt,
Let the children of Israel keep the Passover at its regular time.
In the fourteenth day of this month, at evening, you are to keep it at the regular time, and in the ay ordered in the la.
And Moses gave orders to the children of Israel to keep the Passover.
So they kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at evening, in the aste land of Sinai: as the Lord gave orders to Moses, so the children of Israel did.
And there ere certain men ho ere unclean because of a dead body, so that they ere not able to keep the Passover on that day; and they came before Moses and before Aaron on that day:
And these men said to him, We have been made unclean by the dead body of a man; hy may e not make the offering of the Lord at the regular time among the children of Israel?
And Moses said to them, Do nothing till the Lord gives me directions about you.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, If any one of you or of your families is unclean because of a dead body, or is on a journey far aay, still he is to keep the Passover to the Lord:
In the second month, on the fourteenth day, in the evening, they are to keep it, taking it ith unleavened bread and bitter-tasting plants;
Nothing of it is to be kept till the morning, and no bone of it is to be broken: they are to keep it by the rules of the Passover.

But the man ho, not being unclean or on a journey, does not keep the Passover, ill be cut off from his people: because he did not make the offering of the Lord at the regular time, his sin ill be on him.

And if a man from another country is among you and has a desire to keep the Passover to the Lord, let him do as is ordered in the la of the Passover: there is to be the same rule for the man from another nation and for him ho had his birth in the land.
And on the day hen the House as put up, the cloud came don on it, on the Tent of itness; and in the evening there as a light like fire over the House till the morning.
And so it as at all times: it as covered by the cloud, and by a light as of fire by night.
And henever the cloud as taken up from over the House, then the children of Israel ent journeying on; and in the place here the cloud came to rest, there the children of Israel put up their tents.
At the order of the Lord the children of Israel ent forard, and at the order of the Lord they put up their tents: as long as the cloud as resting on the House, they did not go aay from that place.
When the cloud as resting on the House for a long time the children of Israel, aiting for the order of the Lord, did not go on.
Sometimes the cloud as resting on the House for to or three days; then, by the order of the Lord, they kept their tents in that place, and hen the Lord gave the order they ent on.

And sometimes the cloud as there only from evening to morning; and hen the cloud as taken up in the morning they ent on their journey again: or if it as resting there by day and by night, henever the cloud as taken up they ent forard.

Or if the cloud came to rest on the House for to days or a month or a year ithout moving, the children of Israel ent on aiting there and did not go on; but henever it as taken up they ent forard on their journey.
At the ord of the Lord they put up their tents, and at the ord of the Lord they ent forard on their journey: they kept the orders of the Lord as he gave them by Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Make to silver horns of hammered ork, to be used for getting the people together and to give the sign for the moving of the tents.
When they are sounded, all the people are to come together to you at the door of the Tent of meeting.
If only one of them is sounded, then the chiefs, the heads of the thousands of Israel, are to come to you.
When a loud note is sounded, the tents placed on the east side are to go forard.
At the sound of a second loud note, the tents on the south side are to go forard: the loud note ill be the sign to go forard.
But hen all the people are to come together, the horn is to be sounded but not loudly.
The horns are to be sounded by the sons of Aaron, the priests; this is to be a la for you for ever, from generation to generation.

And if you go to ar in your land against any ho do you rong, then let the loud note of the horn be sounded; and the Lord your God ill keep you in mind and give you salvation from those ho are against you.

And on days of joy and on your regular feasts and on the first day of every month, let the horns be sounded over your burned offerings and your peace-offerings; and they ill put the Lord in mind of you: I am the Lord your God.
No in the second year, on the tentieth day of the second month, the cloud as taken up from over the Tent of itness.
And the children of Israel ent on their journey out of the aste land of Sinai; and the cloud came to rest in the aste land of Paran.
They ent forard for the first time on their journey as the Lord had given orders by the hand of Moses.
First the flag of the children of Judah ent forard ith their armies: and at the head of his army as Nahshon, the son of Amminadab.
And at the head of the army of the children of Issachar as Nethanel, the son of Zuar.
And at the head of the army of the children of Zebulun as Eliab, the son of Helon.
Then the House as taken don; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, ho ere responsible for moving the House, ent forard.
Then the flag of the children of Reuben ent forard ith their armies: and at the head of his army as Elizur, the son of Shedeur.
And at the head of the army of the children of Simeon as Shelumiel, the son of Zurishaddai.
At the head of the army of the children of Gad as Eliasaph, the son of Reuel.
Then the Kohathites ent forard ith the holy place; the others put up the House ready for their coming.
Then the flag of the children of Ephraim ent forard ith their armies: and at the head of his army as Elishama, the son of Ammihud.
At the head of the army of the children of Manasseh as Gamaliel, the son of Pedahzur.
At the head of the army of the children of Benjamin as Abidan, the son of Gideoni.
And the flag of the children of Dan, hose tents ere moved last of all, ent forard ith their armies: and at the head of his army as Ahiezer, the son of Ammishaddai.
At the head of the army of the children of Asher as Pagiel, the son of Ochran.
And at the head of the army of the children of Naphtali as Ahira, the son of Enan.
This as the order in hich the children of Israel ere journeying by armies; so they ent forard.

Then Moses said to Hobab, the son of his father-in-la Reuel the Midianite, We are journeying to that place of hich the Lord has said, I ill give it to you: so come ith us, and it ill be for your profit: for the Lord has good things in store for Israel.
But he said, I ill not go ith you, I ill go back to the land of my birth and to my relations.
And he said, Do not go from us; for you ill be eyes for us, guiding us to the right places in the aste land to put up our tents.
And if you come ith us, e ill give you a part in hatever good the Lord does for us.
So they ent forard three days’ journey from the mountain of the Lord; and the ark of the Lord’s agreement ent three days’ journey before them, looking for a resting-place for them;
And by day the cloud of the Lord ent over them, hen they ent forard from the place here they had put up their tents.
And hen the ark ent forard Moses said, Come up, O Lord, and let the armies of those ho are against you be broken, and let your haters go in flight before you.
And hen it came to rest, he said, Take rest, O Lord, and give a blessing to the families of Israel.
No the people ere saying evil against the Lord; and the Lord, hearing it, as angry and sent fire on them, burning the outer parts of the tent-circle.
And the people made an outcry to Moses, and Moses made prayer to the Lord, and the fire as stopped.
So that place as named Taberah, because of the fire of the Lord hich had been burning among them.
And the mixed band of people ho ent ith them ere overcome by desire: and the children of Israel, eeping again, said, Who ill give us flesh for our food?
Seet is the memory of the fish e had in Egypt for nothing, and the fruit and green plants of every sort, sharp and pleasing to the taste:
But no our soul is asted aay; there is nothing at all: e have nothing but this manna before our eyes.
No the manna as like a seed of grain, like small clear drops.

The people ent about taking it up from the earth, crushing it beteen stones or hammering it to poder, and boiling it in pots, and they made cakes of it: its taste as like the taste of cakes cooked ith oil.
When the de came don on the tents at night, the manna came don ith it.
And at the sound of the people eeping, every man at his tent-door, the rath of the Lord as great, and Moses as very angry.
And Moses said to the Lord, Why have you done me this evil? and hy have I not grace in your eyes, that you have put on me the care of all this people?
Am I the father of all this people? have I given them birth, that you say to me, Take them in your arms, like a child at the breast, to the land hich you gave by an oath to their fathers?
Where am I to get flesh to give to all this people? For they are eeping to me and saying, Give us flesh for our food.
I am not able by myself to take the eight of all this people, for it is more than my strength.
If this is to be my fate, put me to death no in anser to my prayer, if I have grace in your eyes; and let me not see my shame.

And the Lord said to Moses, Send for seventy of the responsible men of Israel, ho are in your opinion men of eight and authority over the people; make them come to the Tent of meeting and be there ith you.

And I ill come don and have talk ith you there: and I ill take some of the spirit hich is on you and put it on them, and they ill take part of the eight of the people off you, so that you do not have to take it by yourself.

And say to the people, Make yourselves clean before tomorro and you ill have flesh for your food: for in the ears of the Lord you have been eeping and saying, Who ill give us flesh for food? for e ere ell off in Egypt: and so the Lord ill give you flesh, and it ill be your food;
Not for one day only, or even for five or ten or tenty days;

But every day for a month, till you are tired of it, turning from it in disgust: because you have gone against the Lord ho is ith you, and have been eeping before him saying, Why did e come out of Egypt?
Then Moses said, The people, among hom I am, are six hundred thousand men on foot; and you have said, I ill give them flesh to be their food for a month.
Are flocks and herds to be put to death for them? or are all the fish in the sea to be got together so that they may be full?
And the Lord said to Moses, Has the Lord’s hand become short? No you ill see if my ord comes true for you or not.
And Moses ent out and gave the people the ords of the Lord: and he took seventy of the responsible men of the people, placing them round the Tent.

Then the Lord came don in the cloud and had talk ith him, and put on the seventy men some of the spirit hich as on him: no hen the spirit came to rest on them, they ere like prophets, but only at that time.

But to men ere still in the tent-circle one of them named Eldad and the other Medad: and the spirit came to rest on them; they ere among those ho had been sent for, but they had not gone out to the Tent: and the prophet’s poer came on them in the tent-circle.
And a young man ent running to Moses and said, Eldad and Medad are acting as prophets in the tent-circle.
Then Joshua, the son of Nun, ho had been Moses’ servant from the time hen he as a child, said, My lord Moses, let them be stopped.
And Moses said to him, Are you moved by envy on my account? If only all the Lord’s people ere prophets, and the Lord might put his spirit on them!
Then Moses, ith the responsible men of Israel, ent back to the tent-circle.

Then the Lord sent a ind, driving little birds from the sea, so that they came don on the tents, and all round the tent-circle, about a day’s journey on this side and on that, in masses about to cubits high over the face of the earth.
And all that day and all night and the day after, the people ere taking up the birds; the smallest amount hich anyone got as ten homers: and they put them out all round the tents.
But hile the meat as still beteen their teeth, before it as tasted, the rath of the Lord as moved against the people and he sent a great outburst of disease on them.
So that place as named Kibroth-hattaavah; because there they put in the earth the bodies of the people ho had given ay to their desires.
From Kibroth-hattaavah the people ent on to Hazeroth; and there they put up their tents.
No Miriam and Aaron said evil against Moses, because of the Cushite oman to hom he as married, for he had taken a Cushite oman as his ife.
And they said, Have the ords of the Lord been given to Moses only? have they not come to us? And the Lord took note of it.
No the man Moses as more gentle than any other man on earth.
And suddenly the Lord said to Moses and Aaron and Miriam, Come out, you three, to the Tent of meeting. And the three of them ent out.
And the Lord came don in a pillar of cloud, taking his place at the door of the Tent, and made Aaron and Miriam come before him.
And he said, No give ear to my ords: if there is a prophet among you I ill give him knoledge of myself in a vision and ill let my ords come to him in a dream.
My servant Moses is not so; he is true to me in all my house:
With him I ill have talk mouth to mouth, openly and not in dark sayings; and ith his eyes he ill see the form of the Lord: hy then had you no fear of saying evil against my servant Moses?
And burning ith rath against them, the Lord ent aay.
And the cloud as moved from over the Tent; and straight aay Miriam became a leper, as hite as sno: and Aaron, looking at Miriam, sa that she as a leper.
Then Aaron said to Moses, O my lord, let not our sin be on our heads, for e have done foolishly and are sinners.
Let her not be as one dead, hose flesh is half asted hen he comes out from the body of his mother.
And Moses, crying to the Lord, said, Let my prayer come before you, O God, and make her ell.

And the Lord said to Moses, If her father had put a mark of shame on her, ould she not be shamed for seven days? Let her be shut up outside the tent-circle for seven days, and after that she may come in again.
So Miriam as shut up outside the tent-circle for seven days: and the people did not go forard on their journey till Miriam had come in again.
After that, the people ent on from Hazeroth and put up their tents in the aste land of Paran.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Send men to get knoledge about the land of Canaan, hich I am giving to the children of Israel; from every tribe of their fathers you are to send a man, every one a chief among them.
And Moses sent them from the aste land of Paran as the Lord gave orders, all of them men ho ere heads of the children of Israel.
And these ere their names: of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua, the son of Zaccur.
Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat, the son of Hori.
Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb, the son of Jephunneh.
Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal, the son of Joseph.
Of the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea, the son of Nun.
Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti, the son of Raphu.
Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel, the son of Sodi.
Of the tribe of Joseph, that is of the family of Manasseh, Gaddi, the son of Susi.
Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel, the son of Gemalli.
Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur, the son of Michael
Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi, the son of Vophsi.
Of the tribe of Gad, Gevel, the son of Machi.
These are the names of the men hom Moses sent to get knoledge about the land. And Moses gave to Hoshea, the son of Nun, the name of Joshua.
So Moses sent them to have a look at the land of Canaan, and said to them, Go up into the South and into the hill-country;
And see hat the land is like; and if the people living in it are strong or feeble, small or great in number;
And hat sort of land they are living in, if it is good or bad; and hat their living-places are, tent-circles or alled tons;
And if the land is fertile or poor, and if there is ood in it or not. And be of good heart, and come back ith some of the produce of the land. No it as the time hen the first grapes ere ready.
So they ent up and got a vie of the land, from the aste land of Zin to Rehob, on the ay to Hamath.

They ent up into the South and came to Hebron; and Ahiman and Sheshai and Talmai, the children of Anak, ere living there. ( No the building of Hebron took place seven years before that of Zoan in Egypt.)
And they came to the valley of Eshcol, and cutting don a vine-branch ith its grapes, to of them took it on a rod beteen them; and they took some pomegranates and figs.
That place as named the valley of Eshcol because of the grapes hich the children of Israel took from there.
At the end of forty days they came back from vieing the land.
And they came back to Moses and Aaron and all the children of Israel, to Kadesh in the aste land of Paran; and gave an account to them and to all the people and let them see the produce of the land.
And they said, We came to the land here you sent us, and truly it is floing ith milk and honey: and here is some of the produce of it.
But the people living in the land are strong, and the tons are alled and very great; further, e sa the children of Anak there.
And the Amalekites are in the South; and the Hittites and the Jebusites and the Amorites are living in the hill-country; and the Canaanites by the sea and by the side of Jordan.
Then Caleb made signs to the people to keep quiet, and said to Moses, Let us go up straight aay and take this land; for e are ell able to overcome it.
But the men ho had gone up ith him said, We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than e.

And they gave the children of Israel a bad account of the land they had been to see, saying, This land through hich e ent is a land causing destruction to those living in it; and all the people e sa there are men of more than common size.
There e sa those great men, the sons of Anak, offspring of the Nephilim: and e seemed to ourselves no more than insects, and so e seemed to them.
Then all the people gave load cries of grief, and all that night they gave themselves up to eeping.
And all the children of Israel, crying out against Moses and Aaron, said, If only e had come to our death in the land of Egypt, or even in this aste land!
Why is the Lord taking us into this land to come to our death by the sord? Our ives and our little ones ill get into strange hands: ould it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?
And they said to one another, Let us make a captain over us, and go back to Egypt.
Then Moses and Aaron ent don on their faces before the meeting of the people.
And Joshua, the son of Nun, and Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, to of those ho had been to see the land, giving signs of grief,
Said to all the children of Israel, This land hich e ent through to see is a very good land.
And if the Lord has delight in us, he ill take us into this land and give it to us, a land floing ith milk and honey.
Only, do not go against the Lord or go in fear of the people of the land, for they ill be our food; their strength has been taken from them and the Lord is ith us: have no fear of them.
But all the people said they ere to be stoned. Then the glory of the Lord as seen in the Tent of meeting, before the eyes of all the children of Israel.
And the Lord said to Moses, Ho long ill this people have no respect for me? ho long ill they be ithout faith, in the face of all the signs I have done among them?
I ill send disease on them for their destruction, and take aay their heritage, and I ill make of you a nation greater and stronger than they.
And Moses said to the Lord, Then it ill come to the ears of the Egyptians; for by your poer you took this people out from among them;

And they ill give the nes to the people of this land: they have had ord that you, Lord, are present ith this people, letting yourself be seen face to face, and that your cloud is resting over them, and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
No if you put to death all this people as one man, then the nations ho have had ord of your glory ill say,
Because the Lord as not able to take this people into the land hich he made an oath to give them, he sent destruction on them in the aste land.
So no, may my prayer come before you, and let the poer of the Lord be great, as you said:

The Lord is slo to rath and great in mercy, overlooking rongdoing and evil, and ill not let rongdoers go free; sending punishment on children for the sins of their fathers, to the third and fourth generation.
May the sin of this people have forgiveness, in the measure of your great mercy, as you have had mercy on them from Egypt up till no.
And the Lord said, I have had mercy, as you say:
But truly, as I am living, and as all the earth ill be full of the glory of the Lord;
Because all these men, having seen my glory and the signs hich I have done in Egypt and in the aste land, still have put me to the test ten times, and have not given ear to my voice;
They ill not see the land about hich I made an oath to their fathers; not one of these by hom I have not been honoured ill see it.
But my servant Caleb, because he had a different spirit in him, and has been true to me ith all his heart, him I ill take into that land into hich he ent, and his seed ill have it for their heritage.
No the Amalekites and the Canaanites are in the valley; tomorro, turning round, go into the aste land by the ay to the Red Sea.
Then the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
Ho long am I to put up ith this evil people and their outcries against me? The ords hich they say against me have come to my ears.
Say to them, By my life, says the Lord, as certainly as your ords have come to my ears, so certainly ill I do this to you:
Your dead bodies ill be stretched out in this aste land; and of all your number, all those of tenty years old and over ho have been crying out against me,
Not one ill come into the land hich I gave my ord you ould have for your resting-place, but only Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua, the son of Nun.
And your little ones, hom you said ould come into strange hands, I ill take in, and they ill see the land hich you ould not have.
But as for you, your dead bodies ill be stretched in this aste land.
And your children ill be anderers in the aste land for forty years, undergoing punishment for your false ays, till your bodies become dust in the aste land.
And as you ent through the land vieing it for forty days, so for forty years, a year for every day, you ill undergo punishment for your rongdoing, and you ill see that I am against you.
I the Lord have said it, and this I ill certainly do to all this evil people ho have come together against me: in this aste land destruction ill come on them, and death ill be their fate.
And the men hom Moses sent to see the land, and ho, by the bad account they gave of the land, ere the cause of the outcry the people made against Moses,
Those same men ho said evil of the land, came to their death by disease before the Lord.
But Joshua, the son of Nun, and Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, of those ho ent to see the land, ere not touched by disease.
And hen Moses put these ords before the children of Israel, the people ere full of grief.
And early in the morning they got up and ent to the top of the mountain, saying, We are here and e ill go up to the place hich the Lord said he ould give us: for e have done rong.
And Moses said, Why are you no acting against the Lord’s order, seeing that no good ill come of it?
Go not up, for the Lord is not ith you, and you ill be overcome by those ho are fighting against you.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you ill be put to death by their sords: because you have gone back from the ay of the Lord, the Lord ill not be ith you.
But they gave no attention to his ords and ent to the top of the mountain, though Moses and the ark of the Lord’s agreement did not go out of the tent-circle.
Then the Amalekites came don, and the Canaanites ho ere living in the hill-country, and overcame them completely, driving them back as far as Hormah.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, When you have come into the land hich I am giving to you for your resting-place,

And are going to make an offering by fire to the Lord, a burned offering or an offering in connection ith an oath, or an offering freely given, or at your regular feasts, an offering for a seet smell to the Lord, from the herd or the flock:
Then let him ho is making his offering, give to the Lord a meal offering of a tenth part of a measure of the best meal mixed ith a fourth part of a hin of oil:
And for the drink offering, you are to give ith the burned offering or other offering, the fourth part of a hin of ine for every lamb.
Or for a male sheep, give as a meal offering to tenth parts of a measure of the best meal mixed ith a third part of a hin of oil:
And for the drink offering give a third part of a hin of ine, for a seet smell to the Lord.
And hen you make ready a young ox for a burned or other offering, or for the effecting of an oath, or for peace-offerings to the Lord:
Then ith the ox give a meal offering of three tenth parts of a measure of the best meal mixed ith half a hin of oil.
And for the drink offering: give half a hin of ine, for an offering made by fire for a seet smell to the Lord.
This is to be done for every young ox and for every male sheep or he-lamb or young goat.
Whatever number you make ready, so you are to do for every one.
All those ho are Israelites by birth are to do these things in this ay, hen giving an offering made by fire of a seet smell to the Lord.

And if a man from another country or any other person living among you, through all your generations, has the desire to give an offering made by fire of a seet smell to the Lord, let him do as you do.
There is to be one la for you and for the man of another country living ith you, one la for ever from generation to generation; as you are, so is he to be before the Lord.
The la and the rule are to be the same for you and for those from other lands living ith you.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel, When you come into the land here I am guiding you,
Then, hen you take for your food the produce of the land, you are to give an offering lifted up before the Lord.
Of the first of your rough meal you are to give a cake for a lifted offering, lifting it up before the Lord as the offering of the grain-floor is lifted up.
From generation to generation you are to give to the Lord a lifted offering from the first of your rough meal.
And if in error you go against any of these las hich the Lord has given to Moses,
All the las hich the Lord has given you by the hand of Moses, from the day hen the Lord gave them, and ever after from generation to generation;

Then, if the rong is done in error, ithout the knoledge of the meeting of the people, let all the meeting give a young ox as a burned offering, a seet smell to the Lord, ith its meal offering and its drink offering, as is ordered in the la, together ith a he-goat for a sin-offering.

So the priest ill make the people free from sin, and they ill have forgiveness; for it as an error, and they have given their offering made by fire to the Lord, and their sin-offering before the Lord, on account of their error:
And all the meeting of the children of Israel, as ell as those from other lands living among them, ill have forgiveness; for it as an error on the part of the people.
And if one person does rong, ithout being conscious of it, then let him give a she-goat of the first year for a sin-offering.
And the priest ill take aay the sin of the person ho has done rong, if the rong as done unconsciously, and he ill have forgiveness.
The la in connection ith rong done unconsciously is to be the same for him ho is an Israelite by birth and for the man from another country ho is living among them.
But the person ho does rong in the pride of his heart, if he is one of you or of another nation by birth, is acting ithout respect for the Lord, and ill be cut off from his people.
Because he had no respect for the ord of the Lord, and did not keep his la, that man ill be cut off ithout mercy and his sin ill be on him.
No hile the children of Israel ere in the aste land, they sa a man ho as getting sticks on the Sabbath day.
And those ho sa him getting sticks took him before Moses and Aaron and all the people.
And they had him shut up, because they had no directions about hat as to be done ith him.
Then the Lord said to Moses, Certainly the man is to be put to death: let him be stoned by all the people outside the tent-circle.
So all the people took him outside the tent-circle and he as stoned to death there, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel that through all their generations they are to put on the edges of their robes an ornament of tisted threads, and in every ornament a blue cord;
So that, looking on these ornaments, you may keep in mind the orders of the Lord and do them; and not be guided by the desires of your hearts and eyes, through hich you have been untrue to me:
And that you may keep in mind all my orders and do them and be holy to your God.
I am the Lord your God, ho took you out of the land of Egypt, so that I might be your God: I am the Lord your God.
No Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, ith Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Pallu, the son of Reuben, made themselves ready,
And came before Moses, ith certain of the children of Israel, to hundred and fifty chiefs of the people, men of good name ho had a place in the meeting of the people.

They came together against Moses and against Aaron, and said to them, You take overmuch on yourselves, seeing that all the people are holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them; hy then have you put yourselves in authority over the people of the Lord?
And Moses, hearing this, ent don on his face;
And he said to Korah and his band, In the morning the Lord ill make clear ho are his, and ho is holy, and ho may come near him: the man of his selection ill be caused to come near him.
So do this: let Korah and all his band take vessels for burning perfumes;
And put spices on the fire in them before the Lord tomorro; then the man marked out by the Lord ill be holy: you take overmuch on yourselves, you sons of Levi.
And Moses said to Korah, Give ear no, you sons of Levi:

Does it seem only a small thing to you that the God of Israel has made you separate from the rest of Israel, letting you come near himself to do the ork of the House of the Lord, and to take your place before the people to do hat has to be done for them;
Letting you, and all your brothers the sons of Levi, come near to him? and ould you no be priests?
So you and all your band have come together against the Lord; and Aaron, ho is he, that you are crying out against him?
Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab: and they said, We ill not come up:
Is it not enough that you have taken us from a land floing ith milk and honey, to put us to death in the aste land, but no you are desiring to make yourself a chief over us?
And more than this, you have not taken us into a land floing ith milk and honey, or given us a heritage of fields and vine-gardens: ill you put out the eyes of these men? We ill not come up.
Then Moses as very angry, and said to the Lord, Give no attention to their offering: not one of their asses have I taken, or done rong to any of them.
And Moses said to Korah, You and all your band are to come before the Lord tomorro, you and they and Aaron:

And let every man take a vessel for burning perfumes, and put seet spices in them; let every man take his vessel before the Lord, to hundred and fifty vessels; you and Aaron and everyone ith his vessel.
So every man took his vessel and they put fire in them, ith spices, and came to the door of the Tent of meeting ith Moses and Aaron.
And Korah made all the people come together against them to the door of the Tent of meeting: and the glory of the Lord as seen by all the people.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
Come out from among this people, so that I may send sudden destruction on them.
Then falling don on their faces they said, O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, because of one man’s sin ill your rath be moved against all the people?
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the people, Come aay from the tent of Korah Dathan, and Abiram.
So Moses got up and ent to Dathan and Abiram, and the responsible men of Israel ent ith him.
And he said to the people, Come aay no from the tents of these evil men, ithout touching anything of theirs, or you may be taken in the punishment of their sins.
So on every side they ent aay from the tent of Korah Dathan, and Abiram: and Dathan and Abiram came out to the door of their tents, ith their ives and their sons and their little ones.
And Moses said, No you ill see that the Lord has sent me to do all these orks, and I have not done them of myself.
If these men have the common death of men, or if the natural fate of all men overtakes them, then the Lord has not sent me.

But if the Lord does something ne, opening the earth to take them in, ith everything hich is theirs, and they go don living into the underorld, then it ill be clear to you that the Lord has not been honoured by these men.
And hile these ords ere on his lips, the earth under them as parted in to;
And the earth, opening her mouth, took them in, ith their families, and all the men ho ere joined to Korah, and their goods.
So they and all theirs ent don living into the underorld, and the earth as shut over them, and they ere cut off from among the meeting of the people.
And all Israel round about them ent in flight at their cry, For fear, said they, that e go don into the heart of the earth.
Then fire came out from the Lord, burning up the to hundred and fifty men ho ere offering the perfume.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, that he is to take out of the flames the vessels ith the perfumes in them, turning the fire out of them, for they are holy;

And let the vessels of those men, ho ith their lives have made payment for their sin, be hammered out into plates as a cover for the altar; for they have been offered before the Lord and are holy; so that they may be a sign to the children of Israel.
So Eleazar the priest took the brass vessels hich had been offered by those ho ere burned up, and they ere hammered out to make a cover for the altar:

To be a sign, kept in memory for ever by the children of Israel, that no man ho is not of the seed of Aaron has the right of burning spices before the Lord, so that he may not be like Korah and his band: as the Lord said to him by the mouth of Moses.
But on the day after, all the children of Israel made an outcry against Moses and against Aaron, saying, You have put to death the Lord’s people.
No hen the people had come together against Moses and Aaron, looking in the direction of the Tent of meeting, they sa the cloud covering it, and the glory of the Lord came before their eyes.
Then Moses and Aaron came to the front of the Tent of meeting.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Come out from among this people, so that I may send sudden destruction on them. And they ent don on their faces.

And Moses said to Aaron, Take your vessel and put in it fire from the altar, and seet spices, and take it quickly into the meeting of the people, and make them free from sin: for rath has gone out from the Lord, and the disease is starting.

And at the ords of Moses, Aaron took his vessel, and ent running among the people; and even then the disease had made a start among them; and he put spices in his vessel to take aay the sin of the people.
And he took his place beteen the dead and the living: and the disease as stopped.
No fourteen thousand, seven hundred deaths ere caused by that disease, in addition to those ho came to their end because of hat Korah had done.
Then Aaron ent back to Moses to the door of the Tent of meeting: and the disease came to a stop.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Say to the children of Israel that they are to give you rods, one for every family, for every chief, the head of his father’s house, making telve rods; let every man’s name be placed on his rod.
And let Aaron’s name be placed on the rod of Levi: for there is to be one rod for the head of every family.
And let them be stored up in the Tent of meeting, in front of the ark of itness here I come to you.
And the rod of that man ho is marked out by me for myself ill have buds on it; so I ill put a stop to the outcries hich the children of Israel make to me against you.
So Moses gave these orders to the children of Israel, and all their chiefs gave him rods, one for the head of every family, making telve rods: and Aaron’s rod as among them.
And Moses put the rods before the Lord in the Tent of itness.
No on the day after, Moses ent into the Tent of itness; and he sa that Aaron’s rod, the rod of the house of Levi, had put out buds, and as covered ith buds and floers and fruit.
Then Moses took out all the rods from before the Lord, and gave them back to the children of Israel: and they sa them, and every man took his rod.

And the Lord said to Moses, Put Aaron’s rod back in front of the ark of itness, to be kept for a sign against this false-hearted people, so that you may put a stop to their outcries against me, and death may not overtake them.
This Moses did: as the Lord gave orders, so he did.
And the children of Israel said to Moses, Truly, destruction has come on us; an evil fate has overtaken us all.
Death ill overtake everyone ho comes near, ho comes near the House of the Lord: are e all to come to destruction?

And the Lord said to Aaron, You and your sons and your father’s family are to be responsible for all rongdoing in relation to the holy place: and you and your sons are to be responsible for the errors hich come about in your ork as priests.
Let your brothers, the family of Levi, come near ith you, so that they may be joined ith you and be your servants: but you and your sons ith you are to go in before the ark of itness.
They are to do your orders and be responsible for the ork of the Tent; but they may not come near the vessels of the holy place or the altar, so that death may not overtake them or you.
They are to be joined ith you in the care of the Tent of meeting, doing hatever is needed for the Tent: and no one of any other family may come near you.
You are to be responsible for the holy place and the altar, so that rath may never again come on the children of Israel.
No, see, I have taken your brothers the Levites from among the children of Israel: they are given to you and to the Lord, to do the ork of the Tent of meeting.

And you and your sons ith you are to be responsible as priests for the altar and everything on it, and everything inside the veil; you are to do the ork of priests; I have given you your position as priests; and any other man ho comes near ill be put to death.

And the Lord said to Aaron, See, I have given into your care my lifted offerings; even all the holy things of the children of Israel I have given to you and to your sons as your right for ever, because you have been marked ith the holy oil.

This is to be yours of the most holy things, out of the fire offerings; every offering of theirs, every meal offering and sin-offering, and every offering hich they make on account of error, is to be most holy for you and your sons.
As most holy things they are to be your food: let every male have them for food; it is to be holy to you.

And this is yours: the lifted offering hich they give and all the ave offerings of the children of Israel I have given to you and to your sons and to your daughters as your right for ever: everyone in your house ho is clean may have them for food.
All the best of the oil and the ine and the grain, the first-fruits of them hich they give to the Lord, to you have I given them.
The earliest produce from their land hich they take to the Lord is to be yours; everyone in your house ho is clean may have it for his food.
Everything given by oath to the Lord in Israel is to be yours.
The first birth of every living thing hich is offered to the Lord, of man or beast, is to be yours; but for the first sons of man payment is to be made, and for the first young of unclean beasts.
Payment is to be made for these hen they are a month old, at the value fixed by you, a price of five shekels by the scale of the holy place, that is, tenty gerahs to the shekel.

But no such payment may be made for the first birth of an ox or a sheep or a goat; these are holy: their blood is to be dropped on the altar, and their fat burned for an offering made by fire, a seet smell to the Lord.
Their flesh is to be yours; like the breast of the ave offering and the right leg, it is to be yours.

All the lifted offerings of the holy things hich the children of Israel give to the Lord, I have given to you and to your sons and to your daughters as a right for ever. This is an agreement made ith salt before the Lord, to you and to your seed for ever.
And the Lord said to Aaron, You ill have no heritage in their land, or any part among them; I am your part and your heritage among the children of Israel.
And to the children of Levi I have given as their heritage all the tenths offered in Israel, as payment for the ork they do, the ork of the Tent of meeting.
In future the children of Israel are not to come near the Tent of meeting, so that death may not come to them because of sin.

But the Levites are to do the ork of the Tent of meeting, and be responsible for errors in connection ith it: this is a la for ever through all your generations; and among the children of Israel they ill have no heritage.

For the tenths hich the children of Israel give as a lifted offering to the Lord I have given to the Levites as their heritage. and so I have said to them, Among the children of Israel they ill have no heritage.
And the Lord said to Moses,

Say to the Levites, When you take from the children of Israel the tenth hich I have given to you from them as your heritage, a tenth part of that tenth is to be offered as an offering lifted up before the Lord.
And this lifted offering is to be put to your credit as if it as grain from the grain-floor and ine from the vines.
So you are to make an offering lifted up to the Lord from all the tenths hich you get from the children of Israel, giving out of it the Lord’s lifted offering to Aaron the priest.
From everything given to you, let the best of it, the holy part of it, be offered as a lifted offering to the Lord.
Say to them, then, When the best of it is lifted up on high, it is to be put to the account of the Levites as the increase of the grain-floor and of the place here the grapes are crushed.
It is to be your food, for you and your families in every place: it is your reard for your ork in the Tent of meeting.

And no sin ill be yours on account of it, hen the best of it has been lifted up on high; you are not to make a rong use of the holy things of the children of Israel, so that death may not overtake you.
And the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
This is the rule of the la hich the Lord has made, saying, Give orders to the children of Israel to give you a red co ithout any mark on her, and on hich the yoke has never been put:
Give her to Eleazar the priest and let him take her outside the tent-circle and have her put to death before him.
Then let Eleazar the priest take some of her blood on his finger, shaking the blood seven times in the direction of the front of the Tent of meeting:
And the co is to be burned before him, her skin and her flesh and her blood and her aste are to be burned:
Then let the priest take cedar-ood and hyssop and red thread, and put them into the fire here the co is burning.
And the priest, after ashing his clothing and bathing his body in ater, may come back to the tent-circle, and ill be unclean till evening.
And he ho does the burning is to have his clothing ashed and his body bathed in ater and be unclean till evening.

Then let a man ho is clean take the dust of the burned co and put it outside the tent-circle in a clean place, here it is to be kept for the children of Israel and used in making the ater hich takes aay hat is unclean: it is a sin-offering.

And he ho takes up the dust of the burned co is to have his clothing ashed ith ater and be unclean till evening: this is to be a la for ever, for the children of Israel as ell as for the man from another country ho is living among them.
Anyone touching a dead body ill be unclean for seven days:
On the third day and on the seventh day he is to make himself clean ith the ater, and so he ill be clean: but if he does not do this on the third day and on the seventh day, he ill not be clean.

Anyone touching the body of a dead man ithout making himself clean in this ay, makes the House of the Lord unclean; and that man ill be cut off from Israel: because the ater as not put on him, he ill be unclean; his unclean condition is unchanged.
This is the la hen death comes to a man in his tent: everyone ho comes into the tent, and everyone ho is in the tent, ill be unclean for seven days.
And every open vessel ithout a cover fixed on it ill be unclean.

And anyone touching one ho has been put to death ith the sord in the open country, or the body of one ho has come to his end by a natural death, or a man’s bone, or the resting-place of a dead body, ill be unclean for seven days.
And for the unclean, they are to take the dust of the burning of the sin-offering, and put floing ater on it in a vessel:
