And a clean person is to take hyssop and put it in the ater, shaking it over the tent, and all the vessels, and the people ho ere there, and over him by hom the bone, or the body of one ho has been put to death ith the sord, or the body of one ho has come to his end by a natural death, or the resting-place as touched.

Let the clean person do this to the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day: and on the seventh day he is to make him clean; and after ashing his clothing and bathing himself in ater, he ill be clean in the evening.

But the man ho, being unclean, does not make himself clean in this ay, ill be cut off from the meeting of the people, because he has made the holy place of the Lord unclean: the ater has not been put on him, he is unclean.
This is to be a la for them for ever: he ho puts the ater on the unclean person is to have his clothing ashed; and anyone touching the ater ill be unclean till evening.
Anything touched by the unclean person ill be unclean; and any person touching it ill be unclean till evening.
In the first month all the children of Israel came into the aste land of Zin, and put up their tents in Kadesh; there death came to Miriam, and they put her body to rest in the earth.
And there as no ater for the people: and they came together against Moses and against Aaron.
And the people ere angry ith Moses and said, If only death had overtaken us hen our brothers came to their death before the Lord!
Why have you taken the Lord’s people into this aste, for death to come to us and to our cattle there?
Why have you made us come out of Egypt into this evil place? This is no place of seed or figs or vines or other fruits, and there is no ater for drinking.
Then Moses and Aaron ent aay from the people to the door of the Tent of meeting; and, falling on their faces there, they sa the glory of the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,

Take the rod, you and Aaron, your brother, and make all the people come together, and before their eyes give orders to the rock to give out its ater; and so make ater come out of the rock for them, and give the people and their cattle drink.
And Moses took the rod from before the Lord as he gave him orders.
Then Moses and Aaron made the people come together in front of the rock, and he said to them, Give ear no, you people hose hearts are turned from the Lord; are e to get ater for you out of the rock?
And lifting up his hand, Moses gave the rock to blos ith his rod: and ater came streaming out, and the people and their cattle had drink enough.
Then the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, Because you had not enough faith in me to keep my name holy before the children of Israel, you ill not take this people into the land hich I have given them.
These are the aters of Meribah; because the children of Israel ent against the Lord, and they sa that he as holy among them.
Then Moses sent men from Kadesh to the king of Edom to say to him, Your brother Israel says, You have knoledge of all the things e have been through;
Ho our fathers ent don into Egypt, and e ere living in Egypt for a long time; and the Egyptians ere cruel to us and to our fathers:
And the Lord gave ear to the voice of our cry, and sent an angel and took us out of Egypt: and no e are in Kadesh, a ton on the edge of your land;

Let us no go through your land: e ill not go into field or vine-garden, or take the ater of the springs; e ill go by the highay, not turning to the right or to the left, till e have gone past the limits of your land.
And Edom said, You are not to go through my land, for if you do I ill come out against you ith the sord.
And the children of Israel said to him, We ill go up by the highay: and if e or our cattle take of your ater, e ill give you a price for it: only let us go through on our feet, nothing more.
But he said, You are not to go through. And Edom came out against them in his strength, ith a great army.
So Edom ould not let Israel go through his land; and Israel ent in another direction.
And they ent on from Kadesh, and came, ith all their people, to Mount Hor.
And at Mount Hor, at the edge of the land of Edom, the Lord said to Moses and Aaron,
Aaron ill be put to rest ith his people; he ill not go into the land hich I have given to the children of Israel, because you ent against my ord at the aters of Meribah.
So take Aaron and Eleazar, his son, up into Mount Hor;
And take Aaron’s robes off him and put them on Eleazar, his son: and death ill come to Aaron there, and he ill be put to rest ith his people.
So Moses did as the Lord had said, and before the eyes of all the people they ent up Mount Hor.
And Moses took off Aaron’s robes, and put them on Eleazar, his son; and there on the top of the mountain death came to Aaron: then Moses and Eleazar came don from the mountain.
And hen the people sa that Aaron as dead, all the children of Israel gave themselves up to eeping for him for thirty days.
And it came to the ears of the Canaanite, the king of Arad, living in the South, that Israel as coming by the ay of Atharim, and he came out against them and took some of them prisoners.
Then Israel made an oath to the Lord, and said, If you ill give up this people into my hands, then I ill send complete destruction on all their tons.
And the Lord, in anser to the voice of Israel, gave the Canaanites up to them; and they put them and their tons completely to destruction: and that place as named Hormah.
Then they ent on from Mount Hor by the ay to the Red Sea, going round the land of Edom: and the spirit of the people as overcome ith eariness on the ay.

And crying out against God and against Moses, they said, Why have you taken us out of Egypt to come to our death in the aste land? For there is no bread and no ater, and this poor bread is disgusting to us.
Then the Lord sent poison-snakes among the people; and their bites ere a cause of death to numbers of the people of Israel.
Then the people came to Moses and said, We have done rong in crying out against the Lord and against you: make prayer to the Lord to take aay the snakes from us. So Moses made prayer for the people.
And the Lord said to Moses, Make an image of a snake and put it on a rod, and anyone ho has been ounded by the snakes, looking on it ill be made ell.
So Moses made a snake of brass and put it on a rod; and anyone ho had a snakebite, after looking on the snake of brass, as made ell.
Then the children of Israel ent on and put up their tents in Oboth.
And journeying on again from Oboth, they put up their tents in Iye-abarim, in the aste land before Moab looking east.
And moving on from there, they put up their tents in the valley of Zered.

From there they ent on and put up their tents on the other side of the Arnon, hich is on the aste land at the edge of the land of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the line of division beteen Moab and the Amorites:
As it says in the book of the Wars of the Lord, Vaheb in Suphah, and the valley of the Amon;
The slope of the valleys going don to the tents of Ar and touching the edge of Moab.
From there they ent on to Beer, the ater-spring of hich the Lord said to Moses, Make the people come together and I ill give them ater.
Then Israel gave voice to this song: Come up, O ater-spring, let us make a song to it:
The fountain made by the chiefs, made deep by the great ones of the people, ith the la-givers’ rod, and ith their sticks. Then from the aste land they ent on to Mattanah:
And from Mattanah to Nahaliel: and from Nahaliel to Bamoth:
And from Bamoth to the valley in the open country of Moab, and to the top of Pisgah looking over Jeshimon.
And Israel sent men to Sihon, king of the Amorites, saying,
Let me go through your land: e ill not go into field or vine-garden, or take the ater of the springs; e ill go by the highay till e have gone past the limits of your land.
And Sihon ould not let Israel go through his land; but got all his people together and ent out against Israel into the aste land, as far as Jahaz, to make ar on Israel.
But Israel overcame him, and took all his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the country of the children of Ammon, for the country of the children of Ammon as strongly armed.
And Israel took all their tons, living in Heshbon and all the tons and small places of the Amorites.
For Heshbon as the ton of Sihon, king of the Amorites, ho had made ar against an earlier king of Moab and taken from him all his land as far as the Arnon.
So the makers of ise sayings say, Come to Heshbon, building up the ton of Sihon and making it strong:
For a fire has gone out of Heshbon, a flame from the ton of Sihon: for the destruction of Ar in Moab, and the lords of the high places of the Arnon.
Sorro is yours, O Moab! Destruction is your fate, O people of Chemosh: his sons have gone in flight, and his daughters are prisoners, in the hands of Sihon, king of the Amorites.
They are ounded ith our arros; destruction has come on Heshbon, even to Dibon; and e have made the land aste as far as Nophah, stretching out to Medeba.
So Israel put up their tents in the land of the Amorites.
And Moses sent men secretly to Jazer, and they took its tons, driving out the Amorites ho ere living there.
Then turning they ent up by the ay of Bashan; and Og, king of Bashan, ent out against them ith all his people, to the fight at Edrei.
And the Lord said to Moses, Have no fear of him: for I have given him up into your hands, ith all his people and his land; do to him as you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, at Heshbon.
So they overcame him and his sons and his people, driving them all out: and they took his land for their heritage.
Then the children of Israel, journeying on, put up their tents in the lolands of Moab, on the other side of Jordan at Jericho.
No Balak, the son of Zippor, sa hat Israel had done to the Amorites.
And in Moab there as great fear of the people, because their numbers ere so great: and the feeling of Moab as bitter against the children of Israel.

Then Moab said to the responsible men of Midian, It is clear that this great people ill be the destruction of everything round us, making a meal of us as the ox does of the grass of the field. At that time Balak, the son of Zippor, as king of Moab.

So he sent men to Balaam, son of Beor, at Pethor by the River in the land of the children of his people, saying to him, See, a people has come out of Egypt, covering all the face of the earth, and they have put up their tents opposite to me:

Come no, in anser to my prayer, and put a curse on this people, for they are greater than I: and then I may be strong enough to overcome them and send them out of the land: for it is clear that good comes to him ho has your blessing, but he on hom you put your curse is cursed.
So the responsible men of Moab and Midian ent aay, taking in their hands reards for the prophet; and they came to Balaam and said to him hat Balak had given them orders to say.
And he said to them, Take your rest here tonight, and I ill give you an anser after hearing hat the Lord says; so the chiefs of Moab kept there ith Balaam that night.
And God came to Balaam and said, Who are these men ith you?
And Balaam said to God, Balak, the son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent them to me, saying,
See, the people ho have come out of Egypt are covering all the earth: no, put a curse on this people for me, so that I may be able to make ar on them, driving them out of the land.
And God said to Balaam, You are not to go ith them, or put a curse on this people, for they have my blessing.
In the morning Balaam got up and said to the chiefs of Balak, Go back to your land, for the Lord ill not let me go ith you.
So the chiefs of Moab ent back to Balak and said, Balaam ill not come ith us.
So Balak sent more chiefs, greater in number and of higher position than the others.
And they came to Balaam and said, Balak, son of Zippor, says, Let nothing keep you from coming to me:
For I ill give you a place of very great honour, and hatever you say to me I ill do; so come, in anser to my prayer, and put a curse on this people.

But Balaam, in anser; said to the servants of Balak, Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, it ould not be possible for me to do anything more or less than the orders of the Lord my God.
So take your rest here this night, till I have knoledge hat more the Lord has to say to me.
And that night God came to Balaam and said to him, If these men have come for you, go ith them: but do only hat I say to you.
So in the morning Balaam got up and, making his ass ready, ent ith the chiefs of Moab.
But God as moved to rath because he ent: and the angel of the Lord took up a position in the road to keep him from his purpose. No he as seated on his ass, and his to servants ere ith him.
And the ass sa the angel of the Lord aiting in the road ith his sord in his hand; and turning from the road, the ass ent into the field; and Balaam gave the ass blos, to get her back on to the road.
Then the angel of the Lord took up his position in a narro road through the vine-gardens, ith a all on this side and on that.
And the ass sa the angel of the Lord, and ent near the all, crushing Balaam’s foot against the all; and he gave her more blos.
Then the angel of the Lord ent further, stopping in a narro place here there as no room for turning to the right or to the left.
And the ass sa the angel of the Lord and ent don on the earth under Balaam; and full of rath, Balaam gave her hard blos ith his stick.
Then the Lord gave the ass the poer of talking, and opening her mouth she said to Balaam, What have I done to you that you have given me blos these three times?
And Balaam said to the ass, You have made me seem foolish: if only I had a sord in my hand I ould put you to death.
And the ass said to Balaam, Am I not your ass upon hich you have gone all your life till this day? and have I ever done this to you before? And he said, No.
Then the Lord made Balaam’s eyes open, and he sa the angel of the Lord in the ay ith his sord in his hand: and he ent don on his face to the earth.
And the angel of the Lord said to him, Why have you given your ass blos these three times? See, I have come out against you to keep you back, because your purpose is not pleasing to me.
And the ass sa me, turning to one side from me three times: if she had not gone to one side, I ould certainly have put you to death and kept her safe.
And Balaam said to the angel of the Lord, I have done rong, for I did not see that you ere in the ay against me: but no, if it is evil in your eyes, I ill go back again.
And the angel of the Lord said to Balaam, Go ith the men; but say only hat I give you to say. Then Balaam ent on ith the chiefs of Balak.
No Balak, hearing that Balaam had come, ent to the chief ton of Moab, on the edge of the Arnon, in the farthest part of the land, for the purpose of meeting him.
And Balak said to Balaam, Did I not send to you, requesting you ith all my heart to come to me? hy did you not come? am I not able to give you a place of honour?
Then Balaam said to Balak, No I have come to you; but have I poer to say anything? Only hat God puts into my mouth may I say.
And Balaam ent ith Balak to Kiriath-huzoth.
And Balak made offerings of oxen and sheep, and sent to Balaam and the chiefs ho ere ith him.
And in the morning Balak took Balaam up to the high places of Baal, and from there he as able to see the outer limits of the people.
And Balaam said to Balak, Make me here seven altars and get ready seven oxen and seven male sheep.
And Balak did as Balaam had said; and Balak and Balaam made an offering on every altar of an ox and a male sheep.

Then Balaam said to Balak, Take your place by your burned offering, and I ill go and see if the Lord comes to me: and I ill give you ord of hatever he says to me. And he ent to an open place on a hill.
And God came to Balaam, and Balaam said to him, I have made ready seven altars, offering an ox and a male sheep on every altar.
And the Lord put ords in Balaam’s mouth, and said, Go back to Balak, and this is hat you are to say.
So he ent back to him here he as aiting by his burned offering ith all the chiefs of Moab.
And in the ords hich the Lord had given him he said, From Aram Balak has sent for me, the king of Moab from the mountains of the East: come, put curses on Jacob for me and be angry ith Israel.
Ho may I put curses on him ho is not cursed by God? ho may I be angry ith him ith hom the Lord is not angry?
From the top of the rocks I see him, looking don on him from the hills: it is a people made separate, not to be numbered among the nations.
Who is able to take the measure of the dust of Jacob or the number of the thousands of Israel? May my death be the death of the upright and my last end like his!
Then Balak said to Balaam, What have you done to me? I sent for you so that my haters might be cursed, and see, you have given them a blessing.
And in anser he said, Am I not ordered to say only hat the Lord puts into my mouth?
And Balak said to him, Come ith me no into another place from hich you ill not be able to see them all, but only the outskirts of them; and you ill send curses on them from there.
So he took him into the country of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and there they made seven altars, offering an ox and a male sheep on every altar.
Then he said to Balak, Take your place here by your burned offering, hile I go over there to the Lord.
And the Lord came to Balaam, and put ords in his mouth, and said, Go back to Balak, and this is hat you are to say.
So he came to him here he as aiting by his burned offering ith the chiefs of Moab by his side. And Balak said to him, What has the Lord said?
And in the ords hich the Lord had given him he said, Up! Balak, and give ear; give attention to me, O son of Zippor:
God is not a man, to say hat is false; or the son of man, that his purpose may be changed: hat he has said, ill he not do? and ill he not give effect to the ords of his mouth?
See, I have had orders to give blessing: and he has given a blessing hich I have no poer to take aay.
He has seen no evil in Jacob or rongdoing in Israel: the Lord his God is ith him, and the glad cry of a king is among them.
It is God ho has taken them out of Egypt; his horns are like those of the mountain ox.
No evil poer has effect against Jacob, no secret arts against Israel; at the right time it ill be said of Jacob and of Israel, See hat God has done!
See, Israel comes up like a she-lion, lifting himself up like a lion: he ill take no rest till he has made a meal of those he has overcome, drinking the blood of those he has put to death.
Then Balak said to Balaam, If you ill not put a curse on them, at all events do not give them a blessing.
But Balaam in anser said to Balak, Did I not say to you, I may only do hat the Lord says?
Then Balak said to Balaam, Come no, I ill take you to another place; it may be that God ill let you put a curse on them from there.
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, looking don over the aste land.
And Balaam said to Balak, Make me seven altars here and get seven oxen and seven male sheep ready for me.
And Balak did as Balaam said, offering an ox and a male sheep on every altar.
No hen Balaam sa that it as the Lord’s pleasure to give his blessing to Israel, he did not, as at other times, make use of secret arts, but turning his face to the aste land,
And lifting up his eyes, he sa Israel there, ith their tents in the order of their tribes: and the spirit of God came on him.
And moved by the spirit, he said, These are the ords of Balaam, son of Beor, the ords of the man hose eyes are open:
He says, hose ears are open to the ords of God, ho has seen the vision of the Ruler of all, falling don, but having his eyes open:
Ho fair are your tents, O Jacob, your houses, O Israel!
They are stretched out like valleys, like gardens by the riverside, like floering trees planted by the Lord, like cedar-trees by the aters.
Peoples ill be in fear before his strength, his arm ill be on great nations: his king ill be higher than Agag, and his kingdom made great in honour.
It is God ho has taken him out of Egypt; his horns are like those of the mountain ox; the nations arring against him ill be his food, their bones ill be broken, they ill be ounded ith his arros.
He took his sleep stretched out like a lion, and like a she-lion: by hom ill his rest be broken? May a blessing be on everyone ho gives you blessing, and a curse on everyone by hom you are cursed.

Then Balak as full of rath against Balaam, and angrily aving his hands he said to Balaam, I sent for you so that those ho are against me might be cursed, but no, see, three times you have given them a blessing.
Go back quickly to the place you came from: it as my purpose to give you a place of honour, but no the Lord has kept you back from honour.
Then Balaam said to Balak, Did I not say to the men you sent to me,

Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, it ould not be possible for me to go outside the orders of the Lord, doing good or evil at the impulse of my mind; hatever the Lord says I ill say?
So no I ill go back to my people: but first let me make clear to you hat this people ill do to your people in days to come.
Then he ent on ith his story and said, These are the ords of Balaam, the son of Beor, the ords of him hose eyes are open:
He says, hose ear is open to the ords of God, ho has knoledge of the Most High, ho has seen the vision of the Ruler of all, falling don and having his eyes open:

I see him, but not no: looking on him, but not near: a star ill come out of Jacob, and a rod of authority out of Israel, sending destruction to the farthest limits of Moab and on the head of all the sons of Sheth.
Edom ill be his heritage, and he ill put an end to the last of the people of Seir.
And Israel ill go on in strength, and Jacob ill have rule over his haters.
Then, turning his eyes to Amalek, he ent on ith his story and said, Amalek as the first of the nations, but his part ill be destruction for ever.
And looking on the Kenites he ent on ith his story and said, Strong is your living-place, and your secret place is safe in the rock.
But still the Kenites ill be asted, till Asshur takes you aay prisoner.
Then he ent on ith his story and said, But ho may keep his life hen God does this?
But ships ill come from the direction of Kittim, troubling Asshur and troubling Eber, and like the others their fate ill be destruction.
Then Balaam got up and ent back to his place: and Balak ent aay.
No hen Israel as living in Shittim the people became false to the Lord, doing evil ith the daughters of Moab:
For they sent for the people to be present at the offerings made to their gods; and the people took part in their feasts and gave honour to their gods.
So Israel had relations ith the omen of Moab in honour of the Baal of Peor: and the Lord as moved to rath against Israel.
Then the Lord said to Moses, Take all the chiefs of the people, hanging them up in the sun before the Lord, so that the rath of the Lord may be turned from Israel.
So Moses said to the judges of Israel, Let everyone put to death those of his men ho have had relations ith the omen of Moab in honour of the Baal of Peor.

Then one of the children of Israel came to his brothers, taking ith him a oman of Midian, before the eyes of Moses and all the meeting of the people, hile they ere eeping at the door of the Tent of meeting.
And Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, seeing it, got up from among the people and took a spear in his hand,

And ent after the man of Israel into the tent, driving the spear through the to of them, through the man of Israel and through the stomach of the oman. So the disease as stopped among the children of Israel.
But tenty-four thousand of them had come to their death by the disease.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Through Phinehas, and because of his passion for my honour, my rath has been turned aay from the children of Israel, so that I have not sent destruction on them all in my rath.
So say to them that I ill make ith him an agreement of peace:
And by this agreement, he and his sons after him have the right to be priests for ever; because, by his care for the honour of his God, he took aay the sin of the children of Israel.
No the man of Israel ho as put to death ith the oman of Midian as Zimri, the son of Salu, a chief of one of the families of the Simeonites.
And the oman of Midian ho as put to death as Cozbi, the daughter of Zur; he as the head of a family in Midian.
Then the Lord said to Moses,
Take up arms against the Midianites and overcome them;

For they are a danger to you ith their false ays, causing sin to come on you in the question of Peor, and because of Cozbi, their sister, the daughter of the chief of Midian, ho as put to death at the time of the disease hich came on you because of Peor.
No after the disease as over, the Lord said to Moses and Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest,
Let all the children of Israel be numbered, by the names of their fathers’ families, all those of tenty years old and over ho are able to go to ar in Israel.
So Moses and Eleazar the priest gave them the order in the lolands of Moab by Jordan at Jericho, saying,
Let all the people of tenty years old and over be numbered, as the Lord has given orders to Moses and the children of Israel ho have come out of Egypt.
Reuben, the first son of Israel: the sons of Reuben by their families: of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites: of Pallu, the family of the Palluites:
Of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites: of Carmi, the family of the Carmites.
These are the families of the Reubenites: their number as forty-three thousand, seven hundred and thirty.
And the sons of Pallu, Eliab

And the sons of Eliab: Nemuel and Dathan and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram ho had a place in the meeting of the people, ho together ith Korah made an outcry against Moses and Aaron and against the Lord:

And they ent don into the open mouth of the earth, together ith Korah, hen death overtook him and all his band; at the time hen to hundred and fifty men ere burned in the fire, and they became a sign.
But death did not overtake the sons of Korah.
The sons of Simeon by their families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites: of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites: of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites:
Of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites: of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
These are the families of the Simeonites, tenty-to thousand, to hundred.
The sons of Gad by their families: of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites: of Haggi, the family of the Haggites: of Shuni, the family of the Shunites:
Of Ozni, the family of the Oznites: of Eri, the family of the Erites:
Of Arod, the family of the Arodites: of Areli, the family of the Arelites.
These are the families of the sons of Gad as they ere numbered, forty thousand, five hundred.
The sons of Judah, Er and Onan: and Er and Onan had come to their death in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Judah by their families ere: of Shelah, the family of the Shelahites: of Perez, the family of the Perezites: of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites.
And the sons of Perez ere: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites: of Hamul, the family of the Hamulites.
These are the families of Judah as they ere numbered, seventy-six thousand, five hundred.
The sons of Issachar by their families: of Tola, the family of the Tolaites: of Puvah, the family of the Punites:
Of Jashub, the family of the Jashubites: of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
These are the families of Issachar, as they ere numbered, sixty-four thousand, three hundred.
The sons of Zebulun by their families: of Sered, the family of the Seredites: of Elon, the family of the Elonites: of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites.
These are the families of the Zebulunites as they ere numbered, sixty thousand, five hundred.
The sons of Joseph by their families: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the family of the Machirites: and Machir as the father of Gilead: of Gilead, the family of the Gileadites.
These are the sons of Gilead: of Iezer, the family of the Iezerites: of Helek, the family of the Helekites:
And of Asriel, the family of the Asrielites: and of Shechem, the family of the Shechemites:
And of Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites: and of Hepher, the family of the Hepherites.
And Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, had no sons, but only daughters, and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad ere Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the families of Manasseh; and those ho ere numbered of them ere fifty-to thousand, seven hundred.
These are the sons of Ephraim by their families: of Shuthelah, the family of the Shuthelahites: of Becher, the family of the Becherites: of Tahan, the family of the Tahanites.
And these are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the family of the Eranites:
These are the families of Ephraim as they ere numbered, thirty-to thousand, five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph by their families.
The sons of Benjamin by their families: of Bela, the family of the Belaites: of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites: of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites:
Of Shephupham, the family of the Shuphamites: and of Hupham, the family of the Huphamites.
And the sons of Bela ere Ard and Naaman: of Ard, the family of the Ardites: of Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
These are the sons of Benjamin by their families: and those ho ere numbered of them ere forty-five thousand, six hundred.
These are the sons of Dan by their families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan by their families.
All the families of the Shuhamites, as they ere numbered, ere sixty-four thousand, four hundred.
The sons of Asher by their families: of Imnah, the family of the Imnites: of Ishvi, the family of the Ishvites: of Beriah, the family of the Beriites.
Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the family of the Heberites: of Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites:
And the name of the daughter of Asher as Serah.
These are the families of the sons of Asher as they ere numbered, fifty-three thousand, four hundred.
The sons of Naphtali by their families: of Jahzeel, the family of the Jahzeelites: of Guni, the family of the Gunites:
Of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites: of Shillem, the family of the Shillemites.
These are the families of Naphtali by their families: and those ho ere numbered of them ere forty-five thousand, four hundred.
Those ho ere numbered of the children of Israel ere six hundred and one thousand, seven hundred and thirty.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Let there be a division of the land among these, for their heritage, in relation to the number of names.
To those families ho are more in number, give a greater heritage; to those ho are less in number, a smaller part: to every one let the heritage be given in relation to the number in his family.
But let the distribution of the land be made by the decision of the Lord: by the names of the tribes of their fathers let their heritage be given them.
As it is ordered by the decision of the Lord, let distribution be made beteen those ho are more in number and those ho are less.
These ere those of the Levites ho ere numbered by their families: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites: of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites: of Merari, the family of the Merarites.

These are the families of Levi: the family of the Libnites, the family of the Hebronites, the family of the Mahlites, the family of the Mushites, the family of the Korahites. And Kohath as the father of Amram.
Amram’s ife as Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, hom he had in Egypt: by Amram she had Moses and Aaron and their sister Miriam.
Aaron’s sons ere Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Death overtook Nadab and Abihu hen they made an offering of strange fire before the Lord.
Of these, tenty-three thousand males, from one month old and over, ere numbered: they ere not numbered ith the rest of the children of Israel, for they had no heritage among the children of Israel.
All these ere numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest hen the children of Israel ere numbered in the lolands of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
But among all these as not one of those numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest hen the children of Israel ere numbered in the aste land of Sinai.
For the Lord had said of them, Death ill certainly overtake them in the aste land. And of them all, only Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua, the son of Nun, ere still living.

Then the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh, the son of Joseph, came forard: their names are Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah.
They came before Moses and Eleazar the priest and the chiefs and all the people at the door of the Tent of meeting, and said,
Death overtook our father in the aste land; he as not among those ho ere banded together ith Korah against the Lord; but death came to him in his sin; and he had no sons.
Why is the name of our father to be taken aay from among his family, because he had no son? Give us a heritage among our father’s brothers.
So Moses put their cause before the Lord.
And the Lord said to Moses,
What the daughters of Zelophehad say is right: certainly you are to give them a heritage among their father’s brothers: and let the property hich ould have been their father’s go to them.
And say to the children of Israel, If a man has no son at the time of his death, let his heritage go to his daughter.
And if he has no daughter, then give his heritage to his brothers.
And if he has no brothers, then give his heritage to his father’s brothers.

And if his father has no brothers, then give it to his nearest relation in the family, as his heritage: this is to be a decision made by la for the children of Israel, as the Lord gave orders to Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses, Go up into this mountain of Abarim so that you may see the land hich I have given to the children of Israel.
And hen you have seen it, you ill be put to rest ith your people, as your brother Aaron as:

Because in the aste land of Zin, hen the people ere angry, you and he ent against my ord and did not keep my name holy before their eyes, at the aters. ( These are the aters of Meribah in Kadesh in the aste land of Zin.)
Then Moses said to the Lord,
Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, put a man at the head of this people,
To go out and come in before them and be their guide; so that the people of the Lord may not be like sheep ithout a keeper.
And the Lord said to Moses, Take Joshua, the son of Nun, a man in hom is the spirit, and put your hand on him;
And take him before Eleazar the priest and all the meeting of the people, and give him his orders before their eyes.
And put your honour on him, so that all the children of Israel may be under his authority.

He ill take his place before Eleazar the priest, so that he may get directions from the Lord for him, ith the Urim: at his ord they ill go out, and at his ord they ill come in, he and all the children of Israel.
So Moses did as the Lord said: he took Joshua and put him before Eleazar the priest and the meeting of the people:
And he put his hands on him and gave him his orders, as the Lord had said by Moses.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Give orders to the children of Israel and say to them, Let it be your care to give me my offerings at their regular times, the food of the offerings made by fire to me for a seet smell.
Say to them, This is the offering made by fire hich you are to give to the Lord; he-lambs of the first year ithout any mark, to every day as a regular burned offering.
Let one be offered in the morning, and the other at evening;
And the tenth part of an ephah of the best meal for a meal offering mixed ith the fourth part of a hin of clear oil.
It is a regular burned offering, as it as ordered in Mount Sinai, for a seet smell, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
And for its drink offering take the fourth part of a hin for one lamb: in the holy place let the ine be drained out for a drink offering for the Lord.
Let the other lamb be offered at evening; like the meal offering of the morning and its drink offering, let it be offered as an offering made by fire for a seet smell to the Lord.
And on the Sabbath day, to he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark, and to tenth parts of the best meal for a meal offering mixed ith oil, and its drink offering:
This is the burned offering for every Sabbath day, in addition to the regular burned offering, and its drink offering.
And on the first day of every month you are to give a burned offering to the Lord; to oxen, one male sheep, and seven he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark;
And three tenth parts of the best meal for a meal offering mixed ith oil, for every ox; and to tenth parts of the best meal for a meal offering mixed ith oil, for the one sheep;
And a separate tenth part of the best meal mixed ith oil for a meal offering for every lamb; for a burned offering of a seet smell, an offering made by fire to the Lord.

And their drink offerings are to be half a hin of ine for an ox, and the third part of a hin for a male sheep, and the fourth part of a hin for a lamb: this is the burned offering for every month through all the months of the year.
And one he-goat for a sin-offering to the Lord; it is to be offered in addition to the regular burned offering and its drink offering.
And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Lord’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this month there is to be a feast; for seven days let your food be unleavened cakes.
On the first day there is to be a holy meeting: you may do no sort of field-ork:
And you are to give an offering made by fire, a burned offering to the Lord; to oxen, one male sheep, and seven he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark:
And their meal offering, the best meal mixed ith oil: let three tenth parts of an ephah be offered for an ox and to tenth parts for a male sheep;
And a separate tenth part for every one of the seven lambs;
And one he-goat for a sin-offering to take aay your sin.
These are to be offered in addition to the morning burned offering, hich is a regular burned offering at all times.
In this ay, every day for seven days, give the food of the offering made by fire, a seet smell to the Lord: it is to be offered in addition to the regular burned offering, and its drink offering.
Then on the seventh day there ill be a holy meeting; you may do no field-ork.
And at the time of the first-fruits, hen you give an offering of ne meal to the Lord at your feast of eeks, there is to be a holy meeting: you may do no field-ork:
And give a burned offering for a seet smell to the Lord; to oxen, one male sheep, and seven he-lambs of the first year;
And their meal offering, the best meal mixed ith oil, three tenth parts for an ox, to tenth parts for a male sheep,
And a separate tenth part for every one of the seven lambs;
And one he-goat to take aay your sin.
These are in addition to the regular burned offering and its meal offering; take care that they are ithout any mark, and let them be offered ith their drink offerings.
In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, let there be a holy meeting; on it you may do no field-ork; let the day be marked by the bloing of horns;
And give to the Lord a burned offering for a seet smell; one ox, one male sheep, seven he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark on them:
And their meal offering, the best meal mixed ith oil, three tenth parts for an ox, to tenth parts for a male sheep,
And a separate tenth part for every one of the seven lambs;
And one he-goat for a sin-offering, to take aay your sin:

In addition to the burned offering of the ne moon, and its meal offering, and the regular burned offering and its meal offering, and their drink offerings, as they are ordered, for a seet smell, an offering made by fire to the Lord.
And on the tenth day of this seventh month there ill be a holy meeting; keep yourselves from pleasure, and do no sort of ork;
And give to the Lord a burned offering for a seet smell; one ox, one male sheep, seven he-lambs of the first year: only those ithout any mark on them may be used:
And their meal offering, the best meal mixed ith oil, three tenth parts for an ox, to tenth parts for a male sheep,
A separate tenth part for every one of the seven lambs;
One he-goat for a sin-offering; in addition to the offering for taking aay your sin, and the regular burned offering and its meal offering, and their drink offerings.
And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month let there be a holy meeting; do no field-ork, and keep a feast to the Lord for seven days;
And give a burned offering, an offering made by fire of a seet smell to the Lord, thirteen oxen, to male sheep, fourteen he-lambs of the first year, all ithout any mark on them;
And their meal offering, the best meal mixed ith oil, three tenth parts for every one of the thirteen oxen, to tenth parts for every male sheep,
And a separate tenth part for every one of the fourteen lambs;
And one he-goat for a sin-offering; in addition to the regular burned offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.
On the second day of the feast give an offering of telve oxen, to male sheep, fourteen he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark on them;
And their meal offering and their drink offerings for the oxen and the sheep and the lambs, in relation to their number, as it is ordered:
And one he-goat for a sin-offering in addition to the regular burned offering, and its meal offering, and their drink offerings.
And on the third day eleven oxen, to male sheep, fourteen he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark;
And their meal offering and drink offerings for the oxen, for the male sheep, and for the lambs, in relation to their number, as it is ordered:
And one he-goat for a sin-offering; in addition to the regular burned offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.
And on the fourth day ten oxen, to male sheep, fourteen he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark:
And their meal offering and their drink offerings for the oxen, for the male sheep, and for the lambs, in relation to their number, as it is ordered.
And one he-goat for a sin-offering; in addition to the regular burned offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.
And on the fifth day nine oxen, to male sheep, fourteen he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark:
And their meal offering and their drink offerings for the oxen, for the male sheep, and for the lambs, in relation to their number, as it is ordered:
And one he-goat for a sin-offering; in addition to the regular burned offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.
And on the sixth day eight oxen, to male sheep, fourteen he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark:
And their meal offering and their drink offerings for the oxen, for the male sheep, and for the lambs, in relation to their number, as it is ordered:
And one he-goat for a sin-offering; in addition to the regular burned offering, its meal offering, and its drink offerings.
And on the seventh day seven oxen, to male sheep, fourteen he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark:
And their meal offering and their drink offerings for the oxen, for the male sheep, and for the lambs, in relation to their number, as it is ordered:
And one he-goat for a sin-offering; in addition to the regular burned offering, its meal offering, and its drink offering.
On the eighth day let there be a holy meeting: you may do no field-ork;
And give a burned offering, an offering made by fire of a seet smell to the Lord: one ox, one male sheep, seven he-lambs of the first year, ithout any mark:
With the meal offering and the drink offerings for the ox, the male sheep, and the lambs, in relation to their number, as it is ordered:
And one he-goat for a sin-offering; in addition to the regular burned offering, and its meal offering, and its drink offering.

These are the offerings hich you are to give to the Lord at your regular feasts, in addition to the offerings for an oath, and the free offerings you give, for your burned offerings and your drink offerings and your peace-offerings.
So Moses gave the children of Israel all these directions as the Lord had given him orders.
And Moses said to the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, This is the order of the Lord.
When a man takes an oath to the Lord, or gives an undertaking having the force of an oath, let him not go back from his ord, but let him do hatever he has said he ill do.
If a oman, being young and under the authority of her father, takes an oath to the Lord or gives an undertaking;
If her father, hearing of her oath or the undertaking she has given, says nothing to her, then all her oaths and every undertaking she has given ill have force.

But if her father, hearing of it, makes her take back her ord, then the oaths or the undertakings she has given ill have no force; and she ill have forgiveness from the Lord, because her oath as broken by her father.
And if she is married to a husband at the time hen she is under an oath or an undertaking given ithout thought;
If her husband, hearing of it, says nothing to her at the time, then the oaths she made and the undertakings she gave ill have force.
But if her husband, hearing of it, makes her take it back, then the oath she made and the undertaking she gave ithout thought ill have no force or effect, and she ill have the Lord’s forgiveness.
But an oath made by a ido or one ho is no longer married to her husband, and every undertaking she has given, ill have force.
If she made an oath hile she as under the authority of her husband,
And her husband, hearing of it, said nothing to her and did not put a stop to it, then all her oaths and every undertaking she gave ill have force.

But if her husband, on hearing of it, made them ithout force or effect, then hatever she has said about her oaths or her undertaking has no force: her husband has made them ithout effect, and she ill have the Lord’s forgiveness.
Every oath, and every undertaking hich she gives, to keep herself from pleasure, may be supported or broken by her husband.

But if the days go on, and her husband says nothing hatever to her, then he is giving the support of his authority to her oaths and undertakings, because at the time of hearing them he said nothing to her.
But if at some time after hearing of them, he makes them ithout force, then he is responsible for her rongdoing.
These are the las hich the Lord gave Moses in relation to a man and his ife, or a father and a young daughter ho is under his authority.
Then the Lord said to Moses,
Give the Midianites punishment for the rong they did to the children of Israel: and after that you ill go to rest ith your people.
So Moses said to the people, Let men from among you be armed for ar to put into effect against Midian the Lord’s punishment on them.
From every tribe of Israel send a thousand to the ar.
So from the thousands of Israel a thousand ere taken from every tribe, telve thousand men armed for ar.

And Moses sent them out to ar, a thousand from every tribe, and ith them Phinehas, the son of Eleazar the priest, taking in his hands the vessels of the holy place and the horns for sounding the note of ar.
And they made ar on Midian, as the Lord gave orders to Moses; and they put to death every male.
They put the kings of Midian to death ith the rest, Evi and Reken and Zur and Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian: and Balaam, the son of Beor, they put to death ith the sord.
The omen of Midian ith their little ones the children of Israel took prisoner; and all their cattle and flocks and all their goods they took for themselves;
And after burning all their tons and all their tent-circles,
They ent aay ith the goods they had taken, man and beast.
And the prisoners and the goods and everything they had taken, they took to Moses and Eleazar the priest and the people of Israel, to the tent-circle in the lolands of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
Then Moses and Eleazar the priest and the chiefs of the people ent out to them before they had come into the tent-circle.
And Moses as angry ith the chiefs of the army, the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds ho had come back from the ar.
And Moses said to them, Why have you kept all the omen safe?
It as these ho, moved by Balaam, ere the cause of Israel’s sin against the Lord in the question of Peor, because of hich disease came on the people of the Lord.
So no put every male child to death, and every oman ho has had sex relations ith a man.
But all the female children ho have had no sex relations ith men, you may keep for yourselves.

You yourselves ill have to keep outside the tent-circle for seven days, anyone of you ho has put any person to death or come near a dead body; and on the third day and on the seventh day make yourselves and your prisoners clean.
And every bit of clothing, and anything made of leather or goats’ hair or ood, you are to make clean.
Then Eleazar the priest said to the men of ar ho had been to the fight, This is the rule of the la hich the Lord has given to Moses:
But gold and silver and brass and iron and tin and lead,

And anything hich may be heated, is to go through the fire and be made clean; but in addition it is to be put in the ater of cleaning: and anything hich may not go through the fire is to be put in the ater.
And on the seventh day, after ashing your clothing, you ill be clean, and then you may come into the tent-circle.
And the Lord said to Moses,
Get an account of everything hich as taken in the ar, of man and of beast, you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of families of the people:
And let division be made of it into to parts, one for the men of ar ho ent out to the fight, and one for all the people:
And from the men of ar ho ent out let there be offered to the Lord one out of every five hundred, from the persons, and from the oxen and asses and sheep:
Take this from their part and give it to Eleazar the priest as an offering to be lifted up to the Lord.

And you came back, eeping before the Lord; but the Lord gave no attention to your cries and did not give ear to you.
So you ere kept aiting in Kadesh for a long time.
Then e ent back, journeying into the aste land by the ay to the Red Sea, as the Lord had said to me: and e ere a long time going round Mount Seir.
And the Lord said to me,
You have been journeying round this mountain long enough: no go to the north;
And give the people orders, saying, You are about to go through the land of your brothers, the children of Esau, ho are living in Seir; and they ill have fear of you; so take care hat you do:
Make no attack on them, for I ill not give you any of their land, not even space enough for a man’s foot: because I have given Mount Seir to Esau for his heritage.
You may get food for your needs from them for a price, and ater for drinking.

For the blessing of the Lord your God has been on you in all the ork of your hands: he has knoledge of your anderings through this great aste: these forty years the Lord your God has been ith you, and you have been short of nothing.
So e ent on past our brothers, the children of Esau, living in Seir, by the road through the Arabah, from Elath and Ezion-geber. And turning, e ent by the road through the aste land of Moab.
And the Lord said to me, Make no attack on Moab and do not go to ar ith them, for I ill not give you any of his land: because I have given Ar to the children of Lot for their heritage.
( In the past the Emim ere living there; a great people, equal in numbers to the Anakim and as tall;
They are numbered among the Rephaim, like the Anakim; but are named Emim by the Moabites.

And the Horites in earlier times ere living in Seir, but the children of Esau took their place; they sent destruction on them and took their land for themselves, as Israel did to the land of his heritage hich the Lord gave them.)
Get up no, and go over the stream Zered. So e ent over the stream Zered.

Thirty-eight years had gone by from the time hen e came aay from Kadesh-barnea till e ent over the stream Zered; by that time all the generation of the men of ar among us ere dead, as the Lord had said.
For the hand of the Lord as against them, orking their destruction, till all ere dead.
So hen death had overtaken all the men of ar among the people,
The ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
You are about to go by Ar, the limit of the country of Moab;

And hen you come near the land of the children of Ammon, give them no cause of trouble and do not make ar on them, for I ill not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon for your heritage: because I have given it to the children of Lot.
( That land is said to have been a land of the Rephaim, for Rephaim had been living there in earlier times, but they ere named Zamzummim by the Ammonites;
They ere a great people, tall as the Anakim, and equal to them in number; but the Lord sent destruction on them and the children of Ammon took their place, living in their land;
As he did for the children of Esau living in Seir, hen he sent destruction on the Horites before them, and they took their land here they are living to this day:
And the Avvim, living in the small tons as far as Gaza, came to destruction by the hands of the Caphtorim ho came out from Caphtor and took their land.)

Get up no, and go on your journey, crossing over the valley of the Arnon: see, I have given into your hands Sihon, the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and all his land: go forard to make it yours, and make ar on him,
From no on I ill put the fear of you in all peoples under heaven, ho, hearing of you, ill be shaking ith fear and grief of heart because of you.
Then from the aste land of Kedemoth I sent representatives to Sihon, king of Heshbon, ith ords of peace, saying,
Let me go through your land: I ill keep to the highay, not turning to the right or to the left;
Let me have food, at a price, for my needs, and ater for drinking: only let me go through on foot;
As the children of Esau did for me in Seir and the Moabites in Ar; till I have gone over Jordan into the land hich the Lord our God is giving us.
But Sihon, king of Heshbon, ould not let us go through; for the Lord your God made his spirit hard and his heart strong, so that he might give him up into your hands as at this day.
And the Lord said to me, See, from no on I have given Sihon and his land into your hands: go forard no to take his land and make it yours.
Then Sihon came out against us ith all his people, to make an attack on us at Jahaz.
And the Lord our God gave him into our hands; and e overcame him and his sons and all his people.
At that time e took all his tons, and gave them over to complete destruction, together ith men, omen, and children; e had no mercy on any:
Only the cattle e took for ourselves, ith the goods from the tons e had taken.
From Aroer on the edge of the valley of the Arnon and from the ton in the valley as far as Gilead, no ton as strong enough to keep us out; the Lord our God gave them all into our hands:
But you did not go near the land of the children of Ammon, that is, all the side of the river Jabbok or the tons of the hill-country, herever the Lord our God had said e ere not to go.
Then turning e took the road to Bashan: and Og, king of Bashan, came out against us ith all his people, and made an attack on us at Edrei.
And the Lord said to me, Have no fear of him: for I have given him and all his people and his land into your hands; do to him as you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, ho as ruling in Heshbon.
So the Lord our God gave up Og, king of Bashan, and all his people into our hands; and e overcame him so completely that all his people came to their end in the fight.
At that time e took all his tons; there as not one ton of the sixty tons, all the country of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan, hich e did not take.
All these tons had high alls round them ith doors and locks; and in addition e took a great number of unalled tons.
And e put them to the curse, every ton together ith men, omen, and children.
But e took for ourselves all the cattle and the stored ealth of the tons.
At that time e took their land from the to kings of the Amorites on the far side of Jordan, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon;
( By the Sidonians, Hermon is named Sirion, and by the Amorites Shenir;)
All the tons of the table-land and all Gilead and Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, tons of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

( For Og, king of Bashan, as the last of all the Rephaim; his bed as made of iron; is it not in Rabbah, in the land of the children of Ammon? It as nine cubits long and four cubits ide, measured by the common cubit.)
And this land hich e took at that time, from Aroer by the valley of the Arnon, and half the hill-country of Gilead ith its tons, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
The rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, all the land of Argob, together ith Bashan, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. ( This land is named the land of the Rephaim.
Jair, the son of Manasseh, took all the land of Argob, as far as the country of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, naming it, Bashan, Havvoth-Jair after himself, as it is to this day.)
And Gilead I gave to Machir.

And the land from Gilead to the valley of the Arnon, ith the middle of the valley as a limit, as far as the river Jabbok hich is the limit of the country of the children of Ammon, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites;
As ell as the Arabah, ith the river Jordan as their limit, from Chinnereth to the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah to the east.
At that time I gave you orders, saying, The Lord has given you this land for your heritage: all the men of ar are to go over armed before your brothers the children of Israel.
But your ives and your little ones and your cattle ( for it is clear that you have much cattle) may go on living in the tons I have given you;

Till the Lord has given rest to your brothers as to you, and till they have taken for themselves the land hich the Lord your God is giving them on the other side of Jordan: then you may go back, every man of you, to the heritage hich I have given you.
And I gave orders to Joshua at that time, saying, Your eyes have seen hat the Lord your God has done to these to kings: so ill the Lord do to all the kingdoms into hich you come.
Have no fear of them, for the Lord your God ill be fighting for you.
And at that time I made request to the Lord, saying,

O Lord God, you have no for the first time let your servant see your great poer and the strength of your hand; for hat god is there in heaven or on earth able to do such great orks and such acts of poer?
Let me go over, O Lord, and see the good land on the other side of Jordan, and that fair mountain country, even Lebanon.
But the Lord as angry ith me because of you and ould not give ear to my prayer; and the Lord said to me, Let it be enough, say no more about this thing.
Go up to the top of Pisgah, and turning your eyes to the est and the north, to the south and the east, see the land ith your eyes: for you are not to go over Jordan.
But give my orders to Joshua, comforting him and making him strong; for he is to go over Jordan at the head of this people, and he ill give them this land hich you ill see for their heritage.
So e ere aiting in the valley facing Beth-peor.

And no give ear, O Israel, to the las and the decisions hich I am teaching you, and do them; so that life may be yours, and you may go in and take for yourselves the land hich the Lord, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
Make no addition to the orders hich I give you, and take nothing from them, but keep the orders of the Lord your God hich I give you.
Your eyes have seen hat the Lord did because of Baal-peor: for destruction came from the Lord on all those among you ho ent after Baal-peor.
But you ho kept faith ith the Lord are living, every one of you, today.
I have been teaching you las and decisions, as I as ordered to do by the Lord my God, so that you might keep them in the land to hich you are going to take it for your heritage.
So keep these las and do them; for so ill your isdom and good sense be clear in the eyes of the peoples, ho hearing all these las ill say, Truly, this great nation is a ise and far-seeing people.
For hat great nation has a god so near to them as the Lord our God is, henever e are turned to him in prayer?
And hat great nation has las and decisions so right as all this la hich I put before you today?

Only take care, and keep atch on your soul, for fear that the things hich your eyes have seen go from your memory and from your heart all the days of your life; but let the knoledge of them be given to your children and to your children’s children;

That day hen you ere aiting before the Lord your God in Horeb, and the Lord said to me, Make all the people come together, so that hearing my ords they may go in fear of me all the days of their life on earth and give this teaching to their children.
And you came near, aiting at the foot of the mountain; and flames of fire ent up from the mountain to the heart of heaven, ith dark clouds, and all as black as night.
And the voice of the Lord came to you out of the fire: the sound of his ords came to your ears but you sa no form; there as nothing but a voice.
And he gave you his agreement ith you, the ten rules hich you ere to keep, hich he put in riting on the to stones of the la.
And the Lord gave me orders at that time to make clear to you these las and decisions, so that you might do them in the land to hich you are going, and hich is to be your heritage.
So keep atch on yourselves ith care; for you sa no form of any sort on the day hen the voice of the Lord came to you in Horeb out of the heart of the fire:
So that you may not be turned to evil ays and make for yourselves an image in the form of any living thing, male or female,
Or any beast of the earth, or inged bird of the air,
Or of anything hich goes flat on the earth, or any fish in the ater under the earth.

And hen your eyes are lifted up to heaven, and you see the sun and the moon and the stars, all the army of heaven, do not let yourselves be moved to give them orship, or become the servants of hat the Lord has given equally to all peoples under heaven.
But the Lord has taken you out of the flaming fire, out of Egypt, to be to him the people of his heritage, as you are today.
And the Lord as angry ith me because of you, and made an oath that I as not to go over Jordan into the good land hich the Lord is giving you for your heritage:
But death is to come to me in this land, I may not go over Jordan: but you ill go over and take that good land for your heritage.

Take care that you do not let the agreement of the Lord your God, hich he has made ith you, go out of your mind, or make for yourselves images of any sort, against the orders hich the Lord your God has given you.
For the Lord your God is an all-burning fire, and he ill not let the honour hich is his be given to any other.

If, hen you have had children and children’s children, and have been living a long time in the land, you are turned to evil ays, and make an image of any sort, and do evil in the eyes of the Lord your God, moving him to rath:

May heaven and earth be my itnesses against you today, that destruction ill quickly overtake you, cutting you off from that land hich you are going over Jordan to take; your days ill not be long in that land, but you ill come to a complete end.
And the Lord ill send you andering among the peoples; only a small band of you ill be kept from death among the nations here the Lord ill send you.
There you ill be the servants of gods, made by men’s hands, of ood and stone, having no poer of seeing or hearing or taking food or smelling.
But if in those lands you are turned again to the Lord your God, searching for him ith all your heart and soul, he ill not keep himself from you.
When you are in trouble and all these things have come on you, if, in the future, you are turned again to the Lord your God, and give ear to his voice:
Because the Lord your God is a God of mercy, he ill not take aay his help from you or let destruction overtake you, or be false to the agreement hich he made by an oath ith your fathers.

Give thought no to the days hich are past, before your time, from the day hen God first gave life to man on the earth, and searching from one end of heaven to the other, see if such a great thing as this has ever been, or if anything like it has been talked of in story.
Has any people ever gone on living after hearing the voice of God out of the heart of the fire as you did?

Has God ever before taken a nation for himself from out of another nation, by punishments and signs and onders, by ar and by a strong hand and a stretched-out arm and great acts of onder and fear, as the Lord your God did for you in Egypt, before your very eyes?
All this he let you see, so that you might be certain that the Lord is God and there is no other.
Out of heaven itself his voice came to you, teaching you; and on earth he let you see his great fire; and his ords came to your ears out of the heart of the fire.
And because of his love for your fathers, he took their seed and made it his, and he himself, present among you, took you out of Egypt by his great poer;
Driving out before you nations greater and stronger than you, to take you into their land and give it to you for your heritage, as at this day.
So today be certain, and keep the knoledge deep in your hearts, that the Lord is God, in heaven on high and here on earth; there is no other God.

Then keep his las and his orders hich I give you today, so that it may be ell for you and for your children after you, and that your lives may be long in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you for ever.
Then Moses had three tons marked out on the far side of Jordan looking to the east;
To hich anyone causing the death of his neighbour in error and not through hate, might go in flight; so that in one of these tons he might be kept from death:
The names of the tons ere Bezer in the aste land, in the table-land, for the Reubenites; and Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for Manasseh.
This is the la hich Moses put before the children of Israel:
These are the rules and the las and the decisions hich Moses gave to the children of Israel after they came out of Egypt;

On the far side of Jordan, in the valley facing Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, ho as ruling in Heshbon, hom Moses and the children of Israel overcame after they had come out of Egypt:
And they took his land for a heritage, and the land of Og, king of Bashan, the to kings of the Amorites, hose lands ere on the other side of Jordan to the east;
From Aroer on the edge of the valley of the Arnon as far as Mount Sion, hich is Hermon,
And all the Arabah on the far side of Jordan to the east, as far as the sea of the Arabah under the slopes of Pisgah.
And Moses sent for all Israel, and said to them, Give ear, O Israel, to the las and the decisions hich I give you today, and give attention to them so that you may keep and do them.
The Lord our God made an agreement ith us in Horeb.
The Lord did not make this agreement ith our fathers but ith us, ho are all living and present here today.
The ord of the Lord came to you face to face on the mountain, out of the heart of the fire,
( I as beteen the Lord and you at that time, to make clear to you the ord of the Lord: because, through fear of the fire, you did not go up the mountain;) saying,
I am the Lord your God, ho took you out of the land of Egypt, out of the prison-house.
You are to have no other gods but me.
You may not make for yourselves an image in the form of anything in heaven or on earth or in the aters under the earth:

You may not go don on your faces before them or give them orship: for I, the Lord your God, am a God ho ill not give his honour to another; and I ill send punishment on the children for the rongdoing of their fathers, to the third and fourth generation of my haters;
And I ill have mercy through a thousand generations on those ho have love for me and keep my las.
You are not to make use of the name of the Lord your God for an evil purpose; hoever takes the Lord’s name on his lips for an evil purpose ill be judged as a sinner by the Lord.
Keep the Sabbath day as a holy day, as you have been ordered by the Lord your God.
On six days do all your ork:

But the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God; on that day do no ork, you or your son or your daughter, or your man-servant or your oman-servant, or your ox or your ass or any of your cattle, or the man from a strange country ho is living among you; so that your man-servant and your oman-servant may have rest as ell as you.

And keep in mind that you ere a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord your God took you out of that land by his strong hand and his stretched-out arm: for this reason the Lord has given you orders to keep the Sabbath day.
Give honour to your father and your mother, as you have been ordered by the Lord your God; so that your life may be long and all may be ell for you in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you.
Do not put anyone to death ithout cause.
Do not be false to the married relation.
Do not take the property of another.
Do not give false itness against your neighbour;
Or let your desire be turned to your neighbour’s ife, or his house or his field or his man-servant or his oman-servant or his ox or his ass or anything hich is your neighbour’s.

These ords the Lord said to all of you together on the mountain, out of the heart of the fire, out of the cloud and the dark, ith a great voice: and he said no more; he put them in riting on the to stones of the la and gave them to me.
And after hearing the voice hich came out of the dark hile the mountain as burning ith fire, all the heads of your tribes and your chiefs came to me,
And said, The Lord has let us see his glory and his poer, and his voice has come to us out of the fire: today e have seen that a man may go on living even after hearing the voice of God.
Why then is death to be our fate? For if the voice of the Lord our God comes to us any more, death ill overtake us, and e ill be burned up in this great fire.
For hat man is there in all the earth, ho, hearing the voice of the living God as e have, out of the heart of the fire, has been kept from death?
Do you go near: and after hearing everything hich the Lord our God has to say, give us an account of all he has said to you, and e ill give ear, and do it.
Then the Lord, hearing your ords to me, said to me, The ords hich this people have said to you have come to my ears: hat they have said is ell said.
If only they had such a heart in them at all times, so that they might go in fear of me and keep my orders and that it might be ell for them and for their children for ever!
No say to them, Go back to your tents.

But as for you, keep your place here by me, and I ill give you all the orders and the las and the decisions hich you are to make clear to them, so that they may do them in the land hich I am giving them for their heritage.
Take care, then, to do hatever the Lord your God has given you orders to do; let there be no turning aay to the right hand or to the left.
Go on alking in the ay ordered for you by the Lord your God, so that life may be yours and it may be ell for you, and your days may be long in the land of your heritage.
No these are the orders and the las and the decisions hich the Lord your God gave me for your teaching, so that you might do them in the land of your heritage to hich you are going:

So that living in the fear of the Lord your God, you may keep all his las and his orders, hich I give you: you and your son and your son’s son, all the days of your life; and so that your life may be long.

So give ear, O Israel, and take care to do this; so that it may be ell for you, and you may be greatly increased, as the Lord the God of your fathers has given you his ord, in a land floing ith milk and honey.
Give ear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord:
And the Lord your God is to be loved ith all your heart and ith all your soul and ith all your strength.
Keep these ords, hich I say to you this day, deep in your hearts;
Teaching them to your children ith all care, talking of them hen you are at rest in your house or alking by the ay, hen you go to sleep and hen you get up.
Let them be fixed as a sign on your hand, and marked on your bro;
Have them lettered on the pillars of your houses and over the doors of your tons.

And hen the Lord your God has taken you into the land hich he gave his oath to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, that he ould give you; ith great and fair tons hich ere not of your building;
And houses full of good things not stored up by you, and places for storing ater hich you did not make, and vine-gardens and olive-trees not of your planting; and you have taken food and are full;
Then take care that you keep your hearts true to the Lord, ho took you out of the land of Egypt, out of the prison-house.
Let the fear of the Lord your God be in your hearts, and be his servants, taking your oaths by his name.
Do not go after other gods, the gods of the peoples round about you;
For the Lord your God ho is ith you is a God ho ill not let his honour be given to another; or the rath of the Lord ill be burning against you, causing your destruction from the face of the earth.
Do not put the Lord your God to the test as you did in Massah.
Keep ith care the orders of the Lord your God, and his rules and his las hich he has given you;

And do hat is upright and good in the eyes of the Lord your God, so that it may be ell for you and you may go in and take for your heritage that good land from hich the Lord undertook by an oath to your fathers,
To send out from before you all those ho are against you.
And hen your son says to you in time to come, What is the reason for these rules and las and decisions hich the Lord our God has given you?
Then you ill say to your son, We ere servants under Pharaoh’s yoke in Egypt; and the Lord took us out of Egypt ith a strong hand:
And the Lord did great signs and onders against Egypt, and against Pharaoh and all his house, before our eyes:
And he took us out from that place, guiding us here to give us this land, as he said in his oath to our fathers.
And the Lord gave us orders to keep all these las, in the fear of the Lord our God, so that it might be ell for us for ever, and that he might keep us from death, as he has done to this day.
And it ill be our righteousness if e take care to keep all this order before the Lord our God as he has given it to us.

When the Lord your God takes you into the land here you are going, hich is to be your heritage, and has sent out the nations before you, the Hittites and the Girgashites and the Amorites and the Canaanites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and stronger than you;
And hen the Lord has given them up into your hands and you have overcome them, give them up to complete destruction: make no agreement ith them, and have no mercy on them:
Do not take ives or husbands from among them; do not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons.
For through them your sons ill be turned from me to the orship of other gods: and the Lord ill be moved to rath against you and send destruction on you quickly.
But this is hat you are to do to them: their altars are to be pulled don and their pillars broken, and their holy trees cut don and their images burned ith fire.
For you are a holy people to the Lord your God: marked out by the Lord your God to be his special people out of all the nations on the face of the earth.
The Lord did not give you his love or take you for himself because you ere more in number than any other people; for you ere the smallest of the nations:

But because of his love for you, and in order to keep his oath to your fathers, the Lord took you out ith the strength of his hand, making you free from the prison-house and from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Be certain, then, that the Lord your God is God; hose faith and mercy are unchanging, ho keeps his ord through a thousand generations to those ho have love for him and keep his las;
Rearding his haters to their face ith destruction; he ill have no mercy on his hater, but ill give him open punishment.
So keep the orders and the las and the decisions hich I give you today and do them.
And it ill be, that if you give attention to these decisions and keep and do them, then the Lord ill keep his agreement ith you and his mercy, as he said in his oath to your fathers.

And he ill give you his love, blessing you and increasing you: he ill send his blessing on the offspring of your body and the fruit of your land, your grain and your ine and your oil, the increase of your cattle and the young of your flock, in the land hich by his oath to your fathers he undertook to give you.
You ill have greater blessings than any other people: no male or female among you or among your cattle ill be ithout offspring.
And the Lord ill take aay from you all disease, and ill not put on you any of the evil diseases of Egypt hich you have seen, but ill put them on your haters.
And you are to send destruction on all the peoples hich the Lord your God gives into your hands; have no pity on them, and do not give orship to their gods; for that ill be a cause of sin to you.
If you say in your hearts, These nations are greater in number than e are: ho are e to take their land from them?
Have no fear of them, but keep ell in mind hat the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt;

The great punishments hich your eyes sa, and the signs and the onders and the strong hand and the stretched-out arm, by hich the Lord your God took you out: so ill the Lord your God do to all the peoples ho are the cause of your fears.
And the Lord ill send a hornet among them, till all the rest ho have kept themselves safe from you in secret places have been cut off.
Have no fear of them: for the Lord your God is ith you, a great God greatly to be feared.
The Lord your God ill send out the nations before you little by little; they are not to be rooted out quickly, for fear that the beasts of the field may be increased overmuch against you.
But the Lord your God ill give them up into your hands, overpoering them till their destruction is complete.
He ill give their kings into your hands, and you ill put their names out of existence under heaven; there is not one of them ho ill not give ay before you, till their destruction is complete.

The images of their gods are to be burned ith fire: have no desire for the gold and silver on them, and do not take it for yourselves, for it ill be a danger to you: it is a thing disgusting to the Lord your God:
And you may not take a disgusting thing into your house, and so become cursed ith its curse: but keep yourselves from it, turning from it ith fear and hate, for it is a cursed thing.

Take care to keep all the orders hich I give you today, so that you may have life and be increased and go in and take as a heritage the land hich the Lord, by his oath to your fathers, undertook to give you.

And keep in mind the ay by hich the Lord your God has taken you through the aste land these forty years, so that he might make lo your pride and put you to the test, to see hat as in your heart and if you ould keep his orders or not.
