And he made lo your pride and let you be ithout food and gave you manna for your food, a thing ne to you, hich your fathers never sa; so that he might make it clear to you that bread is not man’s only need, but his life is in every ord hich comes out of the mouth of the Lord.
Through all these forty years your clothing did not get old or your feet become tired.
Keep in mind this thought, that as a son is trained by his father, so you have been trained by the Lord your God.
Then keep the orders of the Lord your God, fearing him and alking in his ays.
For the Lord your God is guiding you into a good land, a land of ater-springs, of fountains, and deep streams floing out from the valleys and the hills;
A land of grain and vines and fig-trees and fair fruits; a land of oil-giving olive-trees and honey;
Where there ill be bread for you in full measure and you ill be in need of nothing; a land here the very stones are iron and from hose hills you may get copper.
And you ill have food enough and be full, praising the Lord your God for the good land he has given you.
Then take care that you are not turned aay from the Lord your God and from keeping his orders and decisions and las hich I give you this day:
And hen you have taken food and are full, and have made fair houses for yourselves and are living in them;
And hen your herds and your flocks are increased, and your stores of silver and gold, and you have ealth of every sort;
Take care that your hearts are not lifted up in pride, giving no thought to the Lord your God ho took you out of the land of Egypt, out of the prison-house;
Who as your guide through that great and cruel aste, here there ere poison-snakes and scorpions and a dry land ithout ater; ho made ater come out of the hard rock for you;
Who gave you manna for your food in the aste land, a food hich your fathers had never seen; so that your pride might be broken and your hearts tested for your good in the end;
Say not then, in your hearts, My poer and the strength of my hands have got me this ealth.
But keep in mind the Lord your God: for it is he ho gives you the poer to get ealth, so that he may give effect to the agreement hich he made by his oath ith your fathers, as at this day.
And it is certain that if at any time you are turned aay from the Lord your God, and go after other gods, to be their servants and to give them orship, destruction ill overtake you.
Like the nations hich the Lord is cutting off before you, so you ill be cut off; because you ould not give ear to the voice of the Lord your God.
Give ear, O Israel: today you are to go over Jordan, to take the heritage of nations greater and stronger than yourselves, and tons of great size ith alls as high as heaven;
A people great and tall, the sons of the Anakim, of hom you have knoledge and of hom it has been said, All are forced to give ay before the sons of Anak.

Be certain then today that it is the Lord your God ho goes over before you like an all-burning fire; he ill send destruction on them, crushing them before you; and you ill send them in flight, putting an end to them quickly, as the Lord has said.

And after the Lord has sent them in flight from before you, say not in your heart, Because of my righteousness the Lord has given me this land; hen it is because of their evil-doing that the Lord is driving these nations out before you.

Not for your righteousness or because your hearts are upright are you going in to take their land; but because of the evil-doing of these nations the Lord your God is driving them out from before you, and to give effect to his oath to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Be certain then that the Lord your God is not giving you this good land as a reard for your righteousness; for you are a stiff-necked people.
Keep ell in mind ho you made the Lord your God angry in the aste land; from the day hen you ent out of Egypt till you came to this place, you have gone against the orders of the Lord.
Again in Horeb you made the Lord angry, and in his rath he ould have put an end to you.

When I had gone up into the mountain to be given the stones on hich as recorded the agreement hich the Lord made ith you, I as on the mountain for forty days and forty nights ithout taking food or drinking ater.

And the Lord gave me the to stones ith riting on them done by the finger of God: on them ere recorded all the ords hich the Lord said to you on the mountain out of the heart of the fire, on the day of the great meeting.
Then at the end of forty days and forty nights the Lord gave me those stones, the stones of the agreement.

And the Lord said to me, Get up no, and go don quickly from this place; for the people you have taken out of Egypt have given themselves over to evil; they have quickly been turned from the ay in hich I gave them orders to go; they have made themselves a metal image.
And then the Lord said to me, I have seen that this people is stiff-necked:
Let me send destruction on them till their very name is cut off; and I ill make of you a nation greater and stronger than they.
So turning round I came don from the mountain, and the mountain as burning ith fire; and the to stones of the agreement ere in my hands.
And I sa that you had done evil against the Lord, and had made for yourselves a metal image of a young ox: you had quickly been turned from the ay in hich the Lord had given you orders to go.
And I let the stones go from my hands, and they ere broken before your eyes.

And I ent don on my face before the Lord, as at the first, for forty days and forty nights, ithout taking food or drinking ater, because of all your sin, in doing evil in the eyes of the Lord and moving him to rath.
For I as full of fear because of the rath of the Lord hich as burning against you, ith your destruction in vie. But again the Lord’s ear as open to my prayer.
And the Lord, in his rath, ould have put Aaron to death: and I made prayer for Aaron at the same time.

And I took your sin, the image hich you had made, and put it in the fire and had it hammered and crushed very small till it as only dust: and the dust I put in the stream floing don from the mountain.
Again at Taberah and at Massah and at Kibroth-hattaavah you made the Lord angry.

And hen the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying, Go up and take the land hich I have given you; you ent against the orders of the Lord your God, and had no faith in him, and ould not give ear to his voice.
From the day hen I first had knoledge of you, you have gone against the ord of the Lord.
So I ent don on my face in prayer before the Lord for forty days and forty nights as I did at first; because the Lord had said that he ould put an end to you.

And I made prayer to the Lord and said, O Lord God, do not send destruction on your people and your heritage, to hom, by your great poer, you have given salvation, hom you have taken out of Egypt by the strength of your hand.
Keep in mind your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not looking at the hard heart of this people, or their evil-doing and their sin:

Or it may be said in the land from hich you have taken them, Because the Lord as not able to take them into the land hich he said he ould give them, and because of his hate for them, he has taken them out to put them to death in the aste land.
But still they are your people and your heritage, hom you took out by your great poer and by your stretched-out arm.
At that time the Lord said to me, Make to other stones, cut like the first to, and come up to me on the mountain, and make an ark of ood.
And I ill put on the stones the ords hich ere on the first stones hich ere broken by you, and you are to put them into the ark.
So I made an ark of hard ood, and had to stones cut like the others, and ent up the mountain ith the stones in my hands.
And he put on the stones, as in the first riting, the ten rules hich the Lord gave you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the great meeting: and the Lord gave the stones to me.
And turning round I came don from the mountain and put the stones in the ark hich I had made; and there they are as the Lord gave me orders.
( And the children of Israel ent on from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah: there death came to Aaron and he as put to rest in the earth; and Eleazar, his son, took his place as priest.
From there they ent on to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of ater.
At that time the Lord had the tribe of Levi marked out to take up the ark of the Lord’s agreement, to be before the Lord and to do his ork and to give blessings in his name, to this day.
For this reason Levi has no part or heritage for himself among his brothers: the Lord is his heritage, as the Lord your God said to him.)
And I as in the mountain, as at the first time, for forty days and forty nights; and again the ears of the Lord ere open to my prayer, and he did not send destruction on you.
Then the Lord said to me, Get up and go on your journey before the people, so that they may go in and take the land hich I said in my oath to their fathers that I ould give them.
And no, Israel, hat ould the Lord your God have you do, but to go in the fear of the Lord your God, alking in all his ays and loving him and doing his pleasure ith all your heart and all your soul,
Doing the orders of the Lord and keeping his las hich I give you this day for your good?
The Lord your God is ruler of heaven, of the heaven of heavens, and of the earth ith everything in it.
But the Lord had delight in your fathers and love for them, marking out for himself their seed after them, even you, from all peoples, as at this day.
Let your circumcision be of the heart, and put aay your pride.
For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, strong in poer and greatly to be feared, ho has no respect for any man’s position and takes no reards:
Judging uprightly in the cause of the ido and of the child ho has no father, and giving food and clothing in his mercy to the man from a strange country.
So be kind to the man from a strange country ho is living among you, for you yourselves ere living in a strange country in the land of Egypt.
Let the fear of the Lord your God be before you, give him orship and be true to him at all times, taking your oaths in his name.
He is your God, the God of your praise, your God ho has done for you all these orks of poer hich your eyes have seen.
Your fathers ent don into Egypt ith seventy persons; and no the Lord your God has made you like the stars of heaven in number.
So have love for the Lord your God, and give him orship, and keep his las and his decisions and his orders at all times.

And be certain in your minds this day; for these ords are not said to your children, ho have had no experience of the training of the Lord your God, and ho have not seen his great poer or his strong hand and his stretched-out arm,
Or his signs and onders hich he did in Egypt, to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and all his land;

And hat he did to the army of Egypt, to their horses and their ar-carriages; ho he made the aters of the Red Sea come up over them hen they ent after you, and ho the Lord put an end to them even to this day;
And hat he did for you in the aste land, till you came to this place;

And hat he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben; hen they ent don into the open mouth of the earth, ith their families and their tents and every living thing hich as theirs, before the eyes of all Israel:
But your eyes have seen all the great orks of the Lord hich he has done.
So keep all the orders hich I give you today, so that you may be strong, and go in and take the land hich is to be your heritage;
And that your days may be long in the land hich the Lord gave by an oath to your fathers and to their seed after them, a land floing ith milk and honey.
For the land here you are going is not like the land of Egypt from hich you have come, here you put in your seeds, atering them ith your foot, like a planted garden:
But the land here you are going is a land of hills and valleys, drinking in the rain of heaven:
A land cared for by the Lord your God: the eyes of the Lord your God are on it at all times from one end of the year to the other.
And it ill be that if you truly give ear to the orders hich I put before you this day, loving the Lord your God and orshipping him ith all your heart and all your soul,
Then I ill send rain on your land at the right time, the early rains and the late rains, so that you may get in your grain and your ine and your oil.
And I ill give grass in your fields for your cattle, so that you may have food in full measure.
But take care that your hearts are not turned to false ays so that you become servants and orshippers of other gods;

For if you do so, the rath of the Lord ill be burning against you, and the heaven ill be shut up so that there is no rain and the land ill give no fruit; and in a very little time you ill be cut off from the good land hich the Lord is giving you.
So keep these ords deep in your heart and in your soul, and have them fixed on your hand for a sign and marked on your bro;
Teaching them to your children, and talking of them hen you are at rest in your house or alking by the ay, hen you go to sleep and hen you get up:
Writing them on the pillars of your houses and over the doors of your tons:
So that your days, and the days of your children, may be long in the land hich the Lord by his oath to your fathers said he ould give them, like the days of the eternal heavens.
For if you take care to keep all the orders hich I give you, and to do them; loving the Lord your God and alking in all his ays and being true to him:
Then the Lord ill send these nations in flight before you, and you ill take the lands of nations greater and stronger than yourselves.
Every place here you put your foot ill be yours: from the aste land and Lebanon, from the river, the river Euphrates as far as the Great Sea, ill be the limits of your land.
All people ill give ay before you: for the Lord your God ill put the fear of you on all the land through hich you go, as he has said.
Today I put before you a blessing and a curse:
The blessing if you give ear to the orders of the Lord your God, hich I give you this day:
And the curse if you do not give ear to the orders of the Lord your God, but let yourselves be turned from the ay hich I have put before you this day, and go after other gods hich are not yours.
And hen the Lord your God has taken you into the land of your heritage, you are to put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are they not on the other side of Jordan, looking est, in the land of the Canaanites living in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, by the holy tree of Moreh?
For you are about to go over Jordan to take the heritage hich the Lord your God is giving you, and it ill be your resting-place.
And you are to take care to keep all the las and the decisions hich I put before you today.
These are the las and the decisions hich you are to keep ith care in the land hich the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you to be your heritage all the days of your life on earth.
You are to give up to the curse all those places here the nations, hom you are driving out, gave orship to their gods, on the high mountains and the hills and under every green tree:
Their altars and their pillars are to be broken don, and their holy trees burned ith fire, and the images of their gods cut don; you are to take aay their names out of that place.
Do not so to the Lord your God.
But let your hearts be turned to the place hich ill be marked out by the Lord your God, among your tribes, to put his name there;

And there you are to take your burned offerings and other offerings, and the tenth part of your goods, and the offerings to be lifted up to the Lord, and the offerings of your oaths, and those hich you give freely from the impulse of your hearts, and the first births among your herds and your flocks;
There you and all your families are to make a feast before the Lord your God, ith joy in everything to hich you put your hand, because the Lord has given you his blessing.
You are not to do things then in the ay in hich e no do them here, every man as it seems right to him:
For you have not come to the rest and the heritage hich the Lord your God is giving you.

But hen you have gone over Jordan and are living in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you as your heritage, and hen he has given you rest from all those on every side ho are fighting against you, and you are living there safely;

Then there ill be a place marked out by the Lord your God as the resting-place for his name, and there you ill take all the things hich I give you orders to take: your burned offerings and other offerings, and the tenth part of your goods, and the offerings to be lifted up, and the offerings of your oaths hich you make to the Lord;

And you ill be glad before the Lord your God, you and your sons and your daughters, and your men-servants and your omen-servants, and the Levite ho is ith you in your house, because he has no part or heritage among you.
Take care that you do not make your burned offerings in any place you see:
But in the place marked out by the Lord in one of your tribes, there let your burned offerings be offered, and there do hat I have given you orders to do.

Only you may put to death animals, such as the gazelle or the roe, for your food in any of your tons, at the desire of your soul, in keeping ith the blessing of the Lord your God hich he has given you: the unclean and the clean may take of it.
But you may not take the blood for food, it is to be drained out on the earth like ater.

In your tons you are not to take as food the tenth part of your grain, or of your ine or your oil, or the first births of your herds or of your flocks, or anything offered under an oath, or freely offered to the Lord, or given as a lifted offering;

But they ill be your food before the Lord your God in the place of his selection, here you may make a feast of them, ith your son and your daughter, and your man-servant and your oman-servant, and the Levite ho is living ith you: and you ill have joy before the Lord your God in everything to hich you put your hand.
See that you do not give up caring for the Levite as long as you are living in your land.

When the Lord your God makes ide the limit of your land, as he has said, and you say, I ill take flesh for my food, because you have a desire for it; then you may take hatever flesh you have a desire for.

If the place marked out by the Lord your God as the resting-place for his name is far aay from you, then take from your herds and from your flocks hich the Lord has given you, as I have said, and have a meal of it in the tons here you may be living.
It ill be your food, like the gazelle and the roe; the unclean and the clean may take of it.
But see that you do not take the blood for food; for the blood is the life; and you may not make use of the life as food ith the flesh.
Do not take it for food but let it be drained out on the earth like ater.
Do not take it for food; so that it may be ell for you and for your children after you, hile you do hat is right in the eyes of the Lord.
But the holy things hich you have, and the offerings of your oaths, you are to take to the place hich ill be marked out by the Lord:

Offering the flesh and the blood of your burned offerings on the altar of the Lord your God; and the blood of your offerings is to be drained out on the altar of the Lord your God, and the flesh ill be your food.

Take note of all these orders I am giving you and give attention to them, so that it may be ell for you and for your children after you for ever, hile you do hat is good and right in the eyes of the Lord your God.
When the people of the land here you are going have been cut off before you by the Lord your God, and you have taken their land and are living in it;
After their destruction take care that you do not go in their ays, and that you do not give thought to their gods, saying, Ho did these nations give orship to their gods? I ill do as they did.
Do not so to the Lord your God: for everything hich is disgusting to the Lord and hated by him they have done in honour of their gods: even burning their sons and daughters in the fire to their gods.
You are to keep ith care all the ords I give you, making no addition to them and taking nothing from them.
If ever you have among you a prophet or a dreamer of dreams and he gives you a sign or a onder,
And the sign or the onder takes place, and he says to you, Let us go after other gods, hich are strange to you, and give them orship;
Then give no attention to the ords of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams: for the Lord your God is testing you, to see if all the love of your heart and soul is given to him.
But keep on in the ays of the Lord your God, fearing him and keeping his orders and hearing his voice, orshipping him and being true to him.

And that prophet or that dreamer of dreams is to be put to death; for his ords ere said ith the purpose of turning you aay from the Lord your God, ho took you out of the land of Egypt and made you free from the prison-house; and of forcing you out of the ay in hich the Lord your God has given you orders to go. So you are to put aay the evil from among you.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or your daughter or the ife of your heart, or the friend ho is as dear to you as your life, orking on you secretly says to you, Let us go and give orship to other gods, strange to you and to your fathers;
Gods of the peoples round about you, near or far, from one end of the earth to the other;
Do not be guided by him or give attention to him; have no pity on him or mercy, and give him no cover;
But put him to death ithout question; let your hand be the first stretched out against him to put him to death, and then the hands of all the people.
Let him be stoned ith stones till he is dead; because it as his purpose to make you false to the Lord your God, ho took you out of the land of Egypt, out of the prison-house.
And all Israel, hearing of it, ill be full of fear, and no one ill again do such evil as this among you.
And if ord comes to you, in one of the tons hich the Lord your God is giving you for your resting-place,
That good-for-nothing persons have gone out from among you, turning the people of their ton from the right ay and saying, Let us go and give orship to other gods, of hom you have no knoledge;
Then let a full search be made, and let questions be put ith care; and if it is true and certain that such a disgusting thing has been done among you;
Then take up arms against the people of that ton and give it up to the curse, ith all its cattle and everything in it.

And take all the goods into the middle of its open space, burning the ton and all its property ith fire as an offering to the Lord your God; it is to be a aste for ever; there is to be no more building there.
Keep not a thing of hat is cursed for yourselves: so the Lord may be turned aay from the heat of his rath, and have mercy on you, and give you increase as he said in his oath to your fathers:
So long as you give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, and keep all his orders hich I give you today, and do hat is right in the eyes of the Lord your God.
You are the children of the Lord your God: you are not to make cuts on your bodies or take off the hair on your bros in honour of the dead;
For you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and the Lord has taken you to be his special people out of all the nations on the face of the earth.
No disgusting thing may be your food.
These are the beasts hich you may have for food: the ox, the sheep, and the goat;
The hart, the gazelle, and the roe, the mountain goat and the pygarg and the antelope and the mountain sheep.
Any beast hich has a division in the horn of its foot and hose food comes back into its mouth to be crushed again, may be used for food.

But even among these, there are some hich may not be used for food: such as the camel, the hare, and the coney, hich are unclean to you, because, though their food comes back, the horn of their feet is not parted in to.
And the pig is unclean to you, because though it has a division in the horn of its foot, its food does not come back; their flesh may not be used for food or their dead bodies touched by you.
And of the things living in the aters, you may take all those ho have ings for simming ith and skins formed of thin plates.
But any hich have no skin-plates or ings for simming, you may not take; they are unclean for you.
All clean birds may be used for food.
But these birds you may not take: the eagle and the gier-eagle and the ospray;
The falcon and the kite, and birds of that sort;
Every raven, and all birds of that sort;
And the ostrich and the night-hak and the sea-hak and birds of that sort;
The little ol and the great ol and the ater-hen;
And the pelican and the vulture and the cormorant;
The stork and the heron and birds of that sort, and the hoopoe and the bat.
Every inged thing hich goes flat on the earth is unclean to you and may not be used as food.
But all clean birds you may take.

You may not have as food anything hich has come to a natural death; the man from another country ho is living ith you may take it for food, or you may get a price for it from one of another nation; for you are a holy people to the Lord your God. The young goat is not to be cooked in its mother’s milk.
Put on one side a tenth of all the increase of your seed, produced year by year.

And make a feast before the Lord your God, in the place hich is to be marked out, here his name ill be for ever, of the tenth part of your grain and your ine and your oil, and the first births of your herds and your flocks; so that you may have the fear of the Lord your God in your hearts at all times.
And if the ay is so long that you are not able to take these things to the place marked out by the Lord your God for his name, hen he has given you his blessing, because it is far aay from you;
Then let these things be exchanged for money, and, taking the money in your hand, go to the place marked out by the Lord your God for himself;

And ith the money get hatever you have a desire for, oxen or sheep or ine or strong drink, hatever your soul’s desire may be: and make a feast there before the Lord your God, and be glad, you and all your house;
And give a thought to the Levite ho is living among you, for he has no part or heritage in the land.
At the end of every three years take a tenth part of all your increase for that year, and put it in store inside your alls:

And the Levite, because he has no part or heritage in the land, and the man from a strange country, and the child ho has no father, and the ido, ho are living among you, ill come and take food and have enough; and so the blessing of the Lord your God ill be on you in everything you do.
At the end of every seven years there is to be a general forgiveness of debt.

This is ho it is to be done: every creditor is to give up his right to hatever he has let his neighbour have; he is not to make his neighbour, his countryman, give it back; because a general forgiveness has been ordered by the Lord.
A man of another nation may be forced to make payment of his debt, but if your brother has anything of yours, let it go;
But there ill be no poor among you; for the Lord ill certainly give you his blessing in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage;
If only you give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, and take care to keep all these orders hich I give you today.

For the Lord your God ill give you his blessing as he has said: you ill let other nations have the use of your money, but you ill not make use of theirs; you ill be rulers over a number of nations, but they ill not be your rulers.
If in any of your tons in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you, there is a poor man, one of your countrymen, do not let your heart be hard or your hand shut to him;
But let your hand be open to give him the use of hatever he is in need of.

And see that there is no evil thought in your heart, moving you to say to yourself, The seventh year, the year of forgiveness is near; and so looking coldly on your poor countryman you give him nothing; and he ill make an outcry to the Lord against you, and it ill be judged as sin in you.
But it is right for you to give to him, ithout grief of heart: for because of this, the blessing of the Lord your God ill be on all your ork and on everything to hich you put your hand.
For there ill never be a time hen there are no poor in the land; and so I give orders to you, Let your hand be open to your countrymen, to those ho are poor and in need in your land.
If one of your countrymen, a Hebre man or oman, becomes your servant for a price and does ork for you six years, in the seventh year let him go free.
And hen you make him free, do not let him go aay ith nothing in his hands:
But give him freely from your flock and from your grain and your ine: in the measure of the ealth hich the Lord your God has given you, you are to give to him.
And keep in mind that you yourself ere a servant in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God made you free: so I give you this order today.
But if he says to you, I have no desire to go aay from you; because you and your family are dear to him and he is happy ith you;
Then take a sharp-pointed instrument, driving it through his ear into the door, and he ill be your servant for ever. And you may do the same for your servant-girl.

Let it not seem hard to you that you have to send him aay free; for he has been orking for you for six years, hich is tice the regular time for a servant: and the blessing of the Lord your God ill be on you in everything you do.

All the first males to come to birth in your herd and your flock are to be holy to the Lord your God: the first birth of your ox is not to be used for ork, the ool of your first lamb is not to be cut.
But year by year you and all your house are to take a meal of it before the Lord, in the place of his selection.
But if it has any mark on it, if it is blind or has damaged legs, or if there is anything rong ith it, it may not be offered to the Lord your God.
It may be used for food in your houses: the unclean and the clean may take of it, as of the gazelle and the roe.
Only do not take its blood for food, but let it be drained out on the earth like ater.
Take note of the month of Abib and keep the Passover to the Lord your God: for in the month of Abib the Lord your God took you out of Egypt by night.
The Passover offering, from your flock or your herd, is to be given to the Lord your God in the place marked out by him as the resting-place of his name.

Take no leavened bread ith it; for seven days let your food be unleavened bread, that is, the bread of sorro; for you came out of the land of Egypt quickly: so the memory of that day, hen you came out of the land of Egypt, ill be ith you all your life.
For seven days let no leaven be used through all your land; and nothing of the flesh hich is put to death in the evening of the first day is to be kept through the night till morning.
The Passover offering is not to be put to death in any of the tons hich the Lord your God gives you:

But in the place marked out by the Lord your God as the resting-place of his name, there you are to put the Passover to death in the evening, at sundon, at that time of the year hen you came out of Egypt.
It is to be cooked and taken as food in the place marked out by the Lord: and in the morning you are to go back to your tents.
For six days let your food be unleavened bread; and on the seventh day there is to be a holy meeting to the Lord your God; no ork is to be done.
Let seven eeks be numbered from the first day hen the grain is cut.
Then keep the feast of eeks to the Lord your God, ith an offering freely given to him from the ealth he has given you:

Then you are to be glad before the Lord your God, you and your son and your daughter, your man-servant and your oman-servant, and the Levite ho is ith you, and the man from a strange country, and the child ithout a father, and the ido, ho are living among you, in the place marked out by the Lord your God as a resting-place for his name.
And you ill keep in mind that you ere a servant in the land of Egypt: and you ill take care to keep all these las.
You are to keep the feast of tents for seven days after you have got in all your grain and made your ine:

You are to keep the feast ith joy, you and your son and your daughter, your man-servant and your oman-servant, and the Levite, and the man from a strange country, and the child ithout a father, and the ido, ho are living among you.

Keep the feast to the Lord your God for seven days, in the place marked out by the Lord: because the blessing of the Lord your God ill be on all the produce of your land and all the ork of your hands, and you ill have nothing but joy.

Three times in the year let all your males come before the Lord your God in the place named by him; at the feast of unleavened bread, the feast of eeks, and the feast of tents: and they are not to come before the Lord ith nothing in their hands;
Every man is to give as he is able, in the measure of the blessing hich the Lord your God has given you.
You are to make judges and overseers in all your tons hich the Lord your God gives you, for every tribe: and they are to be upright men, judging the people in righteousness.
You are not to be moved in your judging by a man’s position, you are not to take reards; for reards make the eyes of the ise man blind, and the decisions of the upright false.
Let righteousness be your guide, so that you may have life, and take for your heritage the land hich the Lord your God is giving you.
Let no holy tree of any sort be planted by the altar of the Lord your God hich you ill make.
You are not to put up stone pillars, for they are hated by the Lord your God.
No ox or sheep hich has a mark on it or is damaged in any ay may be offered to the Lord your God: for that is disgusting to the Lord your God.
If there is any man or oman among you, in any of the tons hich the Lord your God gives you, ho does evil in the eyes of the Lord your God, sinning against his agreement,
By becoming a servant of other gods and orshipping them or the sun or the moon or all the stars of heaven, against my orders;
If ord of this comes to your ears, then let this thing be looked into ith care, and if there is no doubt that it is true, and such evil has been done in Israel;
Then you are to take the man or oman ho has done the evil to the public place of your ton, and they are to be stoned ith stones till they are dead.
On the ord of to or three itnesses, a man may be given the punishment of death; but he is not to be put to death on the ord of one itness.
The hands of the itnesses ill be the first to put him to death, and after them the hands of all the people. So you are to put aay the evil from among you.

If you are not able to give a decision as to ho is responsible for a death, or ho is right in a cause, or ho gave the first blo in a fight, and there is a division of opinion about it in your ton: then go to the place marked out by the Lord your God;
And come before the priests, the Levites, or before him ho is judge at the time: and they ill go into the question and give you a decision:
And you are to be guided by the decision they give in the place named by the Lord, and do hatever they say:
Acting in agreement ith their teaching and the decision they give: not turning to one side or the other from the ord they have given you.
And any man ho, in his pride, ill not give ear to the priest hose place is there before the Lord your God, or to the judge, is to be put to death: you are to put aay the evil from Israel.
And all the people, hearing of it, ill be full of fear and put aay their pride.

When you have come into the land hich the Lord your God is giving you, and have taken it for a heritage and are living in it, if it is your desire to have a king over you, like the other nations round about you;
Then see that you take as your king the man named by the Lord your God: let your king be one of your countrymen, not a man of another nation ho is not one of yourselves.
And he is not to get together a great army of horses for himself, or make the people go back to Egypt to get horses for him: because the Lord has said, You ill never again go back that ay.
And he is not to have a great number of ives, for fear that his heart may be turned aay; or great ealth of silver and gold.
And hen he has taken his place on the seat of his kingdom, he is to make in a book a copy of this la, from that hich the priests, the Levites, have in their care:
And it is to be ith him for his reading all the days of his life, so that he may be trained in the fear of the Lord his God to keep and do all the ords of this teaching and these las:

So that his heart may not be lifted up over his countrymen, and he may not be turned aay from the orders, to one side or the other: but that his life and the lives of his children may be long in his kingdom in Israel.
The priests, the Levites, that is, all the tribe of Levi, ill have no part or heritage ith Israel: their food and their heritage ill be the offerings of the Lord made by fire.
And they ill have no heritage among their countrymen: the Lord is their heritage, as he has said to them.
And this is to be the priests’ right: those ho make an offering of a sheep or an ox are to give to the priest the top part of the leg and the to sides of the head and the stomach.
And in addition you are to give him the first of your grain and ine and oil, and the first ool cut from your sheep.
For he, and his sons after him for ever, have been marked out by the Lord your God from all your tribes, to do the ork of priests in the name of the Lord.
And if a Levite, moved by a strong desire, comes from any ton in all Israel here he is living to the place marked out by the Lord;
Then he ill do the ork of a priest in the name of the Lord his God, ith all his brothers the Levites ho are there before the Lord.
His food ill be the same as theirs, in addition to hat has come to him as the price of his property.
When you have come into the land hich the Lord your God is giving you, do not take as your example the disgusting ays of those nations.
Let there not be seen among you anyone ho makes his son or his daughter go through the fire, or anyone using secret arts, or a maker of strange sounds, or a reader of signs, or any onder-orker,
Or anyone using secret force on people, or putting questions to a spirit, or having secret knoledge, or going to the dead for directions.
For all ho do such things are disgusting to the Lord; and because of these disgusting things the Lord your God is driving them out before you.
You are to be upright in heart before the Lord your God.
For these nations, hose land you are taking, give attention to readers of signs and to those using secret arts: but the Lord your God ill not let you do so.
The Lord your God ill give you a prophet from among your people, like me; you ill give ear to him;

In anser to the request you made to the Lord your God in Horeb on the day of the great meeting, hen you said, Let not the voice of the Lord my God come to my ears again, and let me not see this great fire any more, or death ill overtake me.
Then the Lord said to me, What they have said is ell said.
I ill give them a prophet from among themselves, like you, and I ill put my ords in his mouth, and he ill say to them hatever I give him orders to say.
And hoever does not give ear to my ords hich he ill say in my name, ill be responsible to me.
But the prophet ho takes it on himself to say ords in my name hich I have not given him orders to say, or ho says anything in the name of other gods, ill come to his death.
And if you say in your hearts, Ho are e to be certain that the ord does not come from the Lord?

When a prophet makes a statement in the name of the Lord, if hat he says does not take place and his ords do not come true, then his ord is not the ord of the Lord: the ords of the prophet ere said in the pride of his heart, and you are to have no fear of him.
When the nations, hose land the Lord your God is giving you, have been cut off by him, and you have taken their place and are living in their tons and in their houses;
You are to have three tons marked out in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage.
You are to make ready a ay, and see that the land hich the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage, is marked out into three parts, to hich any taker of life may go in flight.
This is to be the rule for anyone ho goes in flight there, after causing the death of his neighbour in error and not through hate;

For example, if a man goes into the oods ith his neighbour for the purpose of cutting don trees, and hen he takes his axe to give a blo to the tree, the head of the axe comes off, and falling on to his neighbour gives him a ound causing his death; then the man may go in flight to one of these tons and be safe:

For if not, he ho has the right of punishment may go running after the taker of life in the heat of his rath, and overtake him because the ay is long, and give him a death-blo; though it is not right for him to be put to death because he as not moved by hate.
And so I am ordering you to see that three tons are marked out for this purpose.
And if the Lord your God makes ide the limits of your land, as he said in his oath to your fathers, and gives you all the land hich he undertook to give to your fathers;
If you keep and do all these orders hich I give you today, loving the Lord your God and alking ever in his ays; then let three more tons, in addition to these three, be marked out for you:
So that in all your land, hich the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage, no man may be rongly put to death, for hich you ill be responsible.
But if any man has hate for his neighbour, and aiting for him secretly makes an attack on him and gives him a blo causing his death, and then goes in flight to one of these tons;
The responsible men of his ton are to send and take him, and give him up to the one ho has the right of punishment to be put to death.
Have no pity on him, so that Israel may be clear from the crime of putting a man to death ithout cause, and it ill be ell for you.
Your neighbour’s landmark, hich as put in its place by the men of old times, is not to be moved or taken aay in the land of your heritage hich the Lord your God is giving you.
One itness may not make a statement against a man in relation to any sin or rongdoing hich he has done: on the ord of to or three itnesses a question is to be judged.
If a false itness makes a statement against a man, saying that he has done rong,
Then the to men, beteen hom the argument has taken place, are to come before the Lord, before the priests and judges ho are then in poer;
And the judges ill have the question looked into ith care: and if the itness is seen to be false and to have made a false statement against his brother,
Then do to him hat it as his purpose to do to his brother: and so put aay the evil from among you.
And the rest of the people, hearing of it, ill be full of fear, and never again do such evil among you.
Have no pity; let life be given for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to ar against other nations, and come face to face ith horses and ar-carriages and armies greater in number than yourselves, have no fear of them: for the Lord your God is ith you, ho took you up out of the land of Egypt.
And hen you are on the point of attacking, let the priest come forard and say to the people,
Give ear, O Israel: today you are going forard to the fight; let your heart be strong; do not let uncontrolled fear overcome you because of those ho are against you;
For the Lord your God goes ith you, fighting for you to give you salvation from those ho are against you.

And let the overseers say to the people, If there is any man ho has made for himself a ne house and has not gone into it, let him go back to his house, so that in the event of his death in the fight, another may not take his house for himself.

Or if any man has made a vine-garden ithout taking the first-fruits of it, let him go back to his house, so that in the event of his death in the fight, another may not be the first to make use of the fruit.
Or if any man is nely married and has had no sex relations ith his ife, let him go back to his house, so that in the event of his death in the fight, another man may not take her.
And let the overseers go on to say to the people, If there is any man hose heart is feeble ith fear, let him go back to his house before he makes the hearts of his countrymen feeble.
Then, after saying these ords to the people, let the overseers put captains over the army.
When you come to a ton, before attacking it, make an offer of peace.
And if it gives you back an anser of peace, opening its doors to you, then all the people in it may be put to forced ork as your servants.
If hoever it ill not make peace ith you, but ar, then let it be shut in on all sides:
And hen the Lord your God has given it into your hands, let every male in it be put to death ithout mercy.

But the omen and the children and the cattle and everything in the ton and all its ealth, you may take for yourselves: the ealth of your haters, hich the Lord your God has given you, ill be your food.
So you are to do to all the tons far aay, hich are not the tons of these nations.
But in the tons of these peoples hose land the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage, let no living thing be kept from death:
Give them up to the curse; the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, as the Lord your God has given you orders:
So that you may not take them as your example and do all the disgusting things hich they do in the orship of their gods, so sinning against the Lord your God.

If in ar a ton is shut in by your armies for a long time, do not let its trees be cut don and made aste; for their fruit ill be your food; are the trees of the countryside men for you to take up arms against them?
Only those trees hich you are certain are not used for food may be cut don and put to destruction: and you are to make alls of attack against the ton till it is taken.
If, in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you, you come across the dead body of a man in the open country, and you have no idea ho has put him to death:
Then your responsible men and your judges are to come out, and give orders for the distance from the dead body to the tons round about it to be measured;
And hichever ton is nearest to the body, the responsible men of that ton are to take from the herd a young co hich has never been used for ork or put under the yoke;
And they are to take the co into a valley here there is floing ater, and hich is not ploughed or planted, and there the neck of the co is to be broken:

Then the priests, the sons of Levi, are to come near; for they have been marked out by the Lord your God to be his servants and to give blessings in the name of the Lord; and by their decision every argument and every blo is to be judged:
And all the responsible men of that ton hich is nearest to the dead man, ashing their hands over the co hose neck as broken in the valley,
Will say, This death is not the ork of our hands and our eyes have not seen it.
Have mercy, O Lord, on your people Israel hom you have made free, and take aay from your people the crime of a death ithout cause. Then they ill no longer be responsible for the man’s death.
So you ill take aay the crime of a death ithout cause from among you, hen you do hat is right in the eyes of the Lord.
When you go out to ar against other nations, and the Lord your God gives them up into your hands and you take them as prisoners;
If among the prisoners you see a beautiful oman and it is your desire to make her your ife;
Then take her back to your house; and let her hair and her nails be cut;

And let her take off the dress in hich she as made prisoner and go on living in your house and eeping for her father and mother for a full month: and after that you may go in to her and be her husband and she ill be your ife.
But if you have no delight in her, you are to let her go herever she ill; you may not take a price for her as if she as your property, for you have made use of her for your pleasure.
If a man has to ives, one greatly loved and the other hated, and the to of them have had children by him; and if the first son is the child of the hated ife:
Then hen he gives his property to his sons for their heritage, he is not to put the son of his loved one in the place of the first son, the son of the hated ife:
But he is to give his first son his birthright, and tice as great a part of his property: for he is the first-fruits of his strength and the right of the first son is his.
If a man has a son ho is hard-hearted and uncontrolled, ho gives no attention to the voice of his father and mother, and ill not be ruled by them, though they give him punishment:
Then let his father and mother take him to the responsible men of the ton, to the public place;
And say to them, This son of ours is hard-hearted and uncontrolled, he ill not give attention to us; he gives himself up to pleasure and strong drink.
Then he is to be stoned to death by all the men of the ton: so you are to put aay the evil from among you; and all Israel, hearing of it, ill be full of fear.
If a man does a crime for hich the punishment is death, and he is put to death by hanging him on a tree;

Do not let his body be on the tree all night, but put it to rest in the earth the same day; for the man ho undergoes hanging is cursed by God; so do not make unclean the land hich the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage.
If you see your brother’s ox or his sheep andering, do not go by ithout helping, but take them back to your brother.
If their oner is not near, or if you are not certain ho he is, then take the beast to your house and keep it till its oner comes in search of it, and then you are to give it back to him.
Do the same ith his ass or his robe or anything hich has gone from your brother’s keeping and hich you have come across: do not keep it to yourself.
If you see your brother’s ox or his ass falling don on the road, do not go by ithout giving him help in lifting it up again.
It is not right for a oman to be dressed in man’s clothing, or for a man to put on a oman’s robe: hoever does such things is disgusting to the Lord your God.

If by chance you see a place hich a bird has made for itself in a tree or on the earth, ith young ones or eggs, and the mother bird seated on the young ones or on the eggs, do not take the mother bird ith the young:
See that you let the mother bird go, but the young ones you may take; so it ill be ell for you and your life ill be long.
If you are building a house, make a railing for the roof, so that the blood of any man falling from it ill not come on your house.
Do not have your vine-garden planted ith to sorts of seed: or all of it may become a loss, the seed you have put in as ell as the increase.
Do not do your ploughing ith an ox and an ass yoked together.
Do not have clothing made of to sorts of thread, ool and linen together.
On the four edges of your robe, ith hich your body is covered, put ornaments of tisted threads.
If any man takes a ife, and having had connection ith her, has no delight in her,
And says evil things about her and gives her a bad name, saying, I took this oman, and hen I had connection ith her it as clear to me that she as not a virgin:
Then let the girl’s father and mother put before the responsible men of the ton, in the public place, signs that the girl as a virgin:
And let the girl’s father say to the responsible men, I gave my daughter to this man for his ife, but he has no love for her;
And no he has put shame on her, saying that she is not a virgin; but here is the sign that she is a virgin. Then they are to put her clothing before the responsible men of the ton.
Then the responsible men of the ton are to give the man his punishment;

They ill take from him a hundred shekels of silver, hich are to be given to the father of the girl, because he has given an evil name to a virgin of Israel: she ill go on being his ife, he may never put her aay all his life.
But if hat he has said is true, and she is seen to be not a virgin,

Then they are to make the girl come to the door of her father’s house and she ill be stoned to death by the men of the ton, because she has done evil and put shame on Israel, by acting as a loose oman in her father’s house: so you are to put aay evil from among you.
If a man is taken in the act of going in to a married oman, the to of them, the man as ell as the oman, are to be put to death: so you are to put aay the evil from Israel.
If a young virgin has given her ord to be married to a man, and another man meeting her in the ton, has connection ith her;

Then you are to take the to of them to the dooray of the ton, and have them stoned to death; the young virgin, because she gave no cry for help, though it as in the ton, and the man, because he has put shame on his neighbour’s ife: so you are to put aay evil from among you.
But if the man, meeting such a virgin in the open country, takes her by force, then only the man is to be put to death;
Nothing is to be done to the virgin, because there is no cause of death in her: it is the same as if a man made an attack on his neighbour and put him to death:
For he came across her in the open country, and there as no one to come to the help of the virgin in anser to her cry.
If a man sees a young virgin, ho has not given her ord to be married to anyone, and he takes her by force and has connection ith her, and discovery is made of it;
Then the man ill have to give the virgin’s father fifty shekels of silver and make her his ife, because he has put shame on her; he may never put her aay all his life.
A man may not take his father’s ife or have sex relations ith a oman ho is his father’s.
No man hose private parts have been ounded or cut off may come into the meeting of the Lord’s people.
One hose father and mother are not married may not come into the meeting of the Lord’s people, or any of his family to the tenth generation.
No Ammonite or Moabite or any of their people to the tenth generation may come into the meeting of the Lord’s people:
Because they gave you no bread or ater on your ay, hen you came out of Egypt: and they got Balaam, the son of Peor, from Pethor in Aram-naharaim to put curses on you.
But the Lord your God ould not give ear to Balaam, but let the curse be changed into a blessing to you, because of his love for you.
Do nothing for their peace or ell-being for ever.
But have no hate for an Edomite, because he is your brother, or for an Egyptian, for you ere living in his land.
Their children in the third generation may come into the meeting of the Lord’s people.
When you go out to ar and put your tents in position, keep from every evil thing.
If any man among you becomes unclean through anything hich has taken place in the night, he is to go out from the tent-circle and keep outside it:
But hen evening comes near, let him take a bath: and after sundon he may come back to the tents.
Let there be a place outside the tent-circle to hich you may go;
And have among your arms a spade; and hen you have been to that place, let that hich comes from you be covered up ith earth:

For the Lord your God is alking among your tents, to keep you safe and to give up into your hands those ho are fighting against you; then let your tents be holy, so that he may see no unclean thing among you, and be turned aay from you.
Do not give back to his master a servant ho has gone in flight from his master and come to you:
Let him go on living among you in hatever place is most pleasing to him: do not be hard on him.
No daughter of Israel is to let herself be used as a loose oman for a strange god, and no son of Israel is to give himself to a man.

Do not take into the house of the Lord your God, as an offering for an oath, the price of a loose oman or the money given to one used for sex purposes in the orship of the gods: for these to things are disgusting to the Lord your God.
Do not take interest from an Israelite on anything, money or food or any other goods, hich you let him have:

From men of other nations you may take interest, but not from an Israelite: so that the blessing of the Lord your God may be on everything to hich you put your hand, in the land hich you are about to take as your heritage.
When you take an oath to the Lord, do not be slo to give effect to it: for ithout doubt the Lord your God ill make you responsible, and ill put it to your account as sin.
But if you take no oath, there ill be no sin.
Whatever your lips have said, see that you do it; for you gave your ord freely to the Lord your God.
When you go into your neighbour’s vine-garden, you may take of his grapes at your pleasure, but you may not take them aay in your vessel.
When you go into your neighbour’s field, you may take the heads of grain ith your hand; but you may not put your blade to his grain.
If a man takes a ife, and after they are married she is unpleasing to him because of some bad quality in her, let him give her a statement in riting and send her aay from his house.
And hen she has gone aay from him, she may become another man’s ife.
And if the second husband has no love for her and, giving her a statement in riting, sends her aay; or if death comes to the second husband to hom she as married;

Her first husband, ho had sent her aay, may not take her back after she has been ife to another; for that is disgusting to the Lord: and you are not to be a cause of sin in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage.
A nely married man ill not have to go out ith the army or undertake any business, but may be free for one year, living in his house for the comfort of his ife.
No one is to take, on account of a debt, the stones ith hich grain is crushed: for in doing so he takes a man’s living.

If a man takes by force one of his countrymen, the children of Israel, using him as his property or getting a price for him, that thief is to be put to death: so you are to put aay evil from among you.
In connection ith the leper’s disease, take care to keep and do every detail of the teaching of the priests, the Levites: as I gave them orders, so you are to do.
Keep in mind hat the Lord your God did to Miriam on the ay, hen you came out of Egypt.
If you let your brother have the use of anything hich is yours, do not go into his house and take anything of his as a sign of his debt;
But keep outside till he comes out and gives it to you.
If he is a poor man, do not keep his property all night;

But be certain to give it back to him hen the sun goes don, so that he may have his clothing for sleeping in, and ill give you his blessing: and this ill be put to your account as righteousness before the Lord your God.
Do not be hard on a servant ho is poor and in need, if he is one of your countrymen or a man from another nation living ith you in your land.

Give him his payment day by day, not keeping it back over night; for he is poor and his living is dependent on it; and if his cry against you comes to the ears of the Lord, it ill be judged as sin in you.
Fathers are not to be put to death for their children or children for their fathers: every man is to be put to death for the sin hich he himself has done.
Be upright in judging the cause of the man from a strange country and of him ho has no father; do not take a ido’s clothing on account of a debt:
But keep in mind that you ere a servant in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God made you free: for this is hy I give you orders to do this.

When you get in the grain from your field, if some of the grain has been dropped by chance in the field, do not go back and get it, but let it be for the man from a strange land, the child ithout a father, and the ido: so that the blessing of the Lord your God may be on all the ork of your hands.
When you are shaking the fruit from your olive-trees, do not go over the branches a second time: let some be for the man from a strange land, the child ithout a father, and the ido.
When you are pulling the grapes from your vines, do not take up those hich have been dropped; let them be for the man from a strange land, the child ithout a father, and the ido.
Keep in mind that you ere a servant in the land of Egypt: for this is hy I give you orders to do this.
If there is an argument beteen men and they go to la ith one another, let the judges give their decision for the upright, and against the rongdoer.
And if the rongdoer is to undergo punishment by hipping, the judge ill give orders for him to go don on his face and be hipped before him, the number of the blos being in relation to his crime.
He may be given forty blos, not more; for if more are given, your brother may be shamed before you.
Do not keep the ox from taking the grain hen he is crushing it.

If brothers are living together and one of them, at his death, has no son, the ife of the dead man is not to be married outside the family to another man: let her husband’s brother go in to her and make her his ife, doing as it is right for a brother-in-la to do.
Then the first male child she has ill take the rights of the brother ho is dead, so that his name may not come to an end in Israel.

But if the man says he ill not take his brother’s ife, then let the ife go to the responsible men of the ton, and say, My husband’s brother ill not keep his brother’s name living in Israel; he ill not do hat it is right for a husband’s brother to do.
Then the responsible men of the ton ill send for the man, and have talk ith him: and if he still says, I ill not take her;

Then his brother’s ife is to come to him, before the responsible men of the ton, and take his shoe off his foot, and put shame on him, and say, So let it be done to the man ho ill not take care of his brother’s name.
And his family ill be named in Israel, The house of him hose shoe has been taken off.
If to men are fighting, and the ife of one of them, coming to the help of her husband, takes the other by the private parts;
Her hand is to be cut off; have no pity on her.
Do not have in your bag different eights, a great and a small;
Or in your house different measures, a great and a small.
But have a true eight and a true measure: so that your life may be long in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you.
For all ho do such things, and all hose ays are not upright, are disgusting to the Lord your God.
Keep in mind hat Amalek did to you on your ay from Egypt;
Ho, meeting you on the ay, he made an attack on you hen you ere tired and ithout strength, cutting off all the feeble ones at the end of your line; and the fear of God as not in him.

So hen the Lord your God has given you rest from all ho are against you on every side, in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you for your heritage, see to it that the memory of Amalek is cut off from the earth; keep this in mind.
No hen you have come into the land hich the Lord is giving you for your heritage, and you have made it yours and are living in it;

You are to take a part of the first-fruits of the earth, hich you get from the land hich the Lord your God is giving you, and put it in a basket, and go to the place marked out by the Lord your God, as the resting-place of his name.

And you are to come to him ho is priest at that time, and say to him, I give itness today before the Lord your God, that I have come into the land hich the Lord made an oath to our fathers to give us.
Then the priest ill take the basket from your hand and put it don in front of the altar of the Lord your God.
And these are the ords hich you ill say before the Lord your God: My father as a andering Aramaean, and he ent don ith a small number of people into Egypt; there he became a great and strong nation:
And the Egyptians ere cruel to us, crushing us under a hard yoke:
And our cry ent up to the Lord, the God of our fathers, and the Lord’s ear as open to the voice of our cry, and his eyes took note of our grief and the crushing eight of our ork:
And the Lord took us out of Egypt ith a strong hand and a stretched-out arm, ith orks of poer and signs and onders:
And he has been our guide to this place, and has given us this land, a land floing ith milk and honey.
So no, I have come here ith the first of the fruits of the earth hich you, O Lord, have given me. Then you ill put it don before the Lord your God and give him orship:
And you ill have joy in every good thing hich the Lord your God has given to you and to your family; and the Levite, and the man from a strange land ho is ith you, ill take part in your joy.

When you have taken out a tenth from the tenth of all your produce in the third year, hich is the year hen this has to be done, give it to the Levite, and the man from a strange land, and the child ithout a father, and the ido, so that they may have food in your tons and be full;

And say before the Lord your God, I have taken all the holy things out of my house and have given them to the Levite, and the man from a strange land, and him ho has no father, and the ido, as you have given me orders: I have kept in mind all your orders, in nothing have I gone against them:

No part of these things has been used for food in a time of eeping, or put aay hen I as unclean, or given for the dead: I have given ear to the voice of the Lord my God, and have done all you have given me orders to do.

So, looking don from your holy place in heaven, send your blessing on your people Israel and on the land hich you have given us, as you said in your oath to our fathers, a land floing ith milk and honey.
Today the Lord your God gives you orders to keep all these las and decisions: so then keep and do them ith all your heart and all your soul.
Today you have given itness that the Lord is your God, and that you ill go in his ays and keep his las and his orders and his decisions and give ear to his voice:
And the Lord has made it clear this day that you are a special people to him, as he gave you his ord; and that you are to keep all his orders;
And that he ill make you high over all the nations he has made, in praise, in name, and in honour, and that you are to be a holy people to the Lord your God as he has said.
Then Moses and the responsible men of Israel gave the people these orders: Keep all the orders hich I have given you this day;
And on the day hen you go over Jordan into the land hich the Lord your God is giving you, put up great stones, coating them ith building-paste,

And riting on them all the ords of this la, after you have gone over; so that you may take the heritage hich the Lord your God is giving you, a land floing ith milk and honey, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has said.
And hen you have gone over Jordan, you are to put up these stones, as I have said to you today, in Mount Ebal, and have them coated ith building-paste.
There you are to make an altar to the Lord your God, of stones on hich no iron instrument has been used.
You are to make the altar of the Lord your God of uncut stones; offering on it burned offerings to the Lord your God:
And you are to make your peace-offerings, feasting there ith joy before the Lord your God.
And put on the stones all the ords of this la, riting them very clearly.
Then Moses and the priests, the Levites, said to all Israel, Be quiet and give ear, O Israel; today you have become the people of the Lord your God.
For this cause you are to give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, and do his orders and his las hich I give you this day.
That same day Moses said to the people,
These are to take their places on Mount Gerizim for blessing the people hen you have gone over Jordan: Simeon and Levi and Judah and Issachar and Joseph and Benjamin;
And these are to be on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, and Asher, and Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
Then the Levites are to say in a loud voice to all the men of Israel,
Cursed is the man ho makes any image of ood or stone or metal, disgusting to the Lord, the ork of man’s hands, and puts it up in secret. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho does not give honour to his father or mother. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho takes his neighbour’s landmark from its place. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he by hom the blind are turned out of the ay. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho gives a rong decision in the cause of a man from a strange land, or of one ithout a father, or of a ido. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho has sex relations ith his father’s ife, for he has put shame on his father. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho has sex relations ith any sort of beast. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho has sex relations ith his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho has sex relations ith his mother-in-la. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho takes his neighbour’s life secretly. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho for a reard puts to death one ho has done no rong. And let all the people say, So be it.
Cursed is he ho does not take this la to heart to do it. And let all the people say, So be it.
No if you give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, and keep ith care all these orders hich I have given you today, then the Lord your God ill put you high over all the nations of the earth:
And all these blessings ill come on you and overtake you, if your ears are open to the voice of the Lord your God.
A blessing ill be on you in the ton, and a blessing in the field.
A blessing ill be on the fruit of your body, and on the fruit of your land, on the fruit of your cattle, the increase of your herd, and the young of your flock.
A blessing ill be on your basket and on your bread-basin.
A blessing ill be on your coming in and on your going out.
By the poer of the Lord, those ho take arms against you ill be overcome before you: they ill come out against you one ay, and ill go in flight from you seven ays.
The Lord ill send his blessing on your store-houses and on everything to hich you put your hand: his blessing ill be on you in the land hich the Lord your God is giving you.
The Lord ill keep you as a people holy to himself, as he has said to you in his oath, if you keep the orders of the Lord your God and go on alking in his ays.
And all the peoples of the earth ill see that the name of the Lord is on you, and they ill go in fear of you.

And the Lord ill make you fertile in every good thing, in the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your cattle, and the fruit of your fields, in the land hich the Lord, by his oath to your fathers, said he ould give you.

Opening his store-house in heaven, the Lord ill send rain on your land at the right time, blessing all the ork of your hands: other nations ill make use of your ealth, and you ill have no need of theirs.
The Lord ill make you the head and not the tail; and you ill ever have the highest place, if you give ear to the orders of the Lord your God hich I give you today, to keep and to do them;
Not turning aay from any of the orders hich I give you today, to the right hand or to the left, or going after any other gods to give them orship.
But if you do not give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, and take care to do all his orders and his las hich I give you today, then all these curses ill come on you and overtake you:
You ill be cursed in the ton and cursed in the field.
A curse ill be on your basket and on your bread-basin.
A curse ill be on the fruit of your body, and on the fruit of your land, on the increase of your cattle, and the young of your flock.
You ill be cursed hen you come in and cursed hen you go out.
The Lord ill send on you cursing and trouble and punishment in everything to hich you put your hand, till sudden destruction overtakes you; because of your evil ays in hich you have been false to me.
The Lord ill send disease after disease on you, till you have been cut off by death from the land to hich you are going.
The Lord ill send asting disease, and burning pain, and flaming heat against you, keeping back the rain till your land is aste and dead; so ill it be till your destruction is complete.
And the heaven over your heads ill be brass, and the earth under you hard as iron.
The Lord ill make the rain of your land poder and dust, sending it don on you from heaven till your destruction is complete.
The Lord ill let you be overcome by your haters: you ill go out against them one ay, and you ill go in flight before them seven ays: you ill be the cause of fear among all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your bodies ill be meat for all the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth; there ill be no one to send them aay.
The Lord ill send on you the disease of Egypt, and other sorts of skin diseases hich nothing ill make ell.
He ill make your minds diseased, and your eyes blind, and your hearts asted ith fear:
You ill go feeling your ay hen the sun is high, like a blind man for hom all is dark, and nothing ill go ell for you: you ill be crushed and made poor for ever, and you ill have no saviour.
You ill take a ife, but another man ill have the use of her: the house hich your hands have made ill never be your resting-place: you ill make a vine-garden, and never take the fruit of it.

Your ox ill be put to death before your eyes, but its flesh ill not be your food: your ass ill be violently taken aay before your face, and ill not be given back to you: your sheep ill be given to your haters, and there ill be no saviour for you.
Your sons and your daughters ill be given to another people, and your eyes ill be asted aay ith looking and eeping for them all the day: and you ill have no poer to do anything.
The fruit of your land and all the ork of your hands ill be food for a nation hich is strange to you and to your fathers; you ill only be crushed don and kept under for ever:
So that the things hich your eyes have to see ill send you out of your minds.
The Lord ill send a skin disease, attacking your knees and your legs, bursting out from your feet to the top of your head, so that nothing ill make you ell.
And you, and the king hom you have put over you, ill the Lord take aay to a nation strange to you and to your fathers; there you ill be servants to other gods of ood and stone.
And you ill become a onder and a name of shame among all the nations here the Lord ill take you.
You ill take much seed out into the field, and get little in; for the locust ill get it.
You ill put in vines and take care of them, but you ill get no ine or grapes from them; for they ill be food for orms.
Your land ill be full of olive-trees, but there ill be no oil for the comfort of your body; for your olive-tree ill give no fruit.
You ill have sons and daughters, but they ill not be yours; for they ill go aay prisoners into a strange land.
All your trees and the fruit of your land ill be the locust’s.
The man from a strange land ho is living among you ill be lifted up higher and higher over you, hile you go don loer and loer.
He ill let you have his ealth at interest, and ill have no need of yours: he ill be the head and you the tail.

And all these curses ill come after you and overtake you, till your destruction is complete; because you did not give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, or keep his las and his orders hich he gave you:
These things ill come on you and on your seed, to be a sign and a onder for ever;
Because you did not give honour to the Lord your God, orshipping him gladly, ith joy in your hearts on account of all your ealth of good things;

For this cause you ill become servants to those hom the Lord your God ill send against you, ithout food and drink and clothing, and in need of all things: and he ill put a yoke of iron on your neck till he has put an end to you.
The Lord ill send a nation against you from the farthest ends of the earth, coming ith the flight of an eagle; a nation hose language is strange to you;
A hard-faced nation, ho ill have no respect for the old or mercy for the young:

He ill take the fruit of your cattle and of your land till death puts an end to you: he ill let you have nothing of your grain or ine or oil or any of the increase of your cattle or the young of your flock, till he has made your destruction complete.
Your tons ill be shut in by his armies, till your high alls, in hich you put your faith, have come don: his armies ill be round your tons, through all your land hich the Lord your God has given you.
And your food ill be the fruit of your body, the flesh of the sons and daughters hich the Lord your God has given you; because of your bitter need and the cruel grip of your haters.
That man among you ho is soft and used to comfort ill be hard and cruel to his brother, and to his dear ife, and to of those his children ho are still living;
And ill not give to any of them the flesh of his children hich ill be his food because he has no other; in the cruel grip of your haters on all your tons.
The most soft and delicate of your omen, ho ould not so much as put her foot on the earth, so delicate is she, ill be hard-hearted to her husband and to her son and to her daughter;

And to her baby nely come to birth, and to the children of her body; for having no other food, she ill make a meal of them secretly, because of her bitter need and the cruel grip of your haters on all your tons.
If you ill not take care to do all the ords of this la, recorded in this book, honouring that name of glory and of fear, THE LORD YOUR GOD;
Then the Lord your God ill make your punishment, and the punishment of your seed, a thing to be ondered at; great punishments and cruel diseases stretching on through long years.
He ill send on you again all the diseases of Egypt, hich ere a cause of fear to you, and they ill take you in their grip.
And all the diseases and the pains not recorded in the book of this la ill the Lord send on you till your destruction is complete.
And you ill become a very small band, though your numbers ere like the stars of heaven; because you did not give ear to the voice of the Lord your God.

And as the Lord took delight in doing you good and increasing you, so the Lord ill take pleasure in cutting you off and causing your destruction, and you ill be uprooted from the land hich you are about to take as your heritage.

And the Lord ill send you andering among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other: there you ill be servants to other gods, of ood and stone, gods of hich you and your fathers had no knoledge.
And even among these nations there ill be no peace for you, and no rest for your feet: but the Lord ill give you there a shaking heart and asting eyes and eariness of soul:
Your very life ill be hanging in doubt before you, and day and night ill be dark ith fears, and nothing in life ill be certain:
In the morning you ill say, If only it as evening! And at evening you ill say, If only morning ould come! Because of the fear in your hearts and the things hich your eyes ill see.
