And the Lord ill take you back to Egypt again in ships, by the ay of hich I said to you, You ill never see it again: there you ill be offering yourselves as men-servants and omen-servants to your haters for a price, and no man ill take you.
These are the ords of the agreement hich Moses as ordered by the Lord to make ith the children of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the agreement hich he made ith them in Horeb.
And Moses said in the hearing of all Israel, You have seen all the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and to all his servants and all his land;
The great tests hich your eyes sa, and the signs and onders:
But even to this day the Lord has not given you a mind open to knoledge, or seeing eyes or hearing ears.
For forty years I have been your guide through the aste land: your clothing has not become old on your backs, or your shoes on your feet.
You have had no bread, or ine, or strong drink: so that you might see that I am the Lord your God.
When you came to this place, Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, came out to make ar against us and e overcame them:
And e took their land and gave it to the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for their heritage.
So keep the ords of this agreement and do them, so that it may be ell for you in everything you do.
You have come here today, all of you, before the Lord your God; the heads of your tribes, the overseers, and those ho are in authority over you, ith all the men of Israel,
And your little ones, your ives, and the men of other lands ho are ith you in your tents, don to the ood-cutter and the servant ho gets ater for you:
With the purpose of taking part in the agreement of the Lord your God, and his oath hich he makes ith you today:
And so that he may make you his people today, and be your God, as he has said to you, and as he made an oath to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And not ith you only do I make this agreement and this oath;
But ith everyone ho is here ith us today before the Lord our God, as ell as ith those ho are not here:
( For you have in mind ho e ere living in the land of Egypt; and ho e came through all the nations hich ere on your ay;
And you have seen their disgusting doings, and the images of ood and stone and silver and gold hich ere among them:)

So that there may not be among you any man or oman or family or tribe hose heart is turned aay from the Lord our God today, to go after other gods and give them orship; or any root among you hose fruit is poison and bitter sorro;
If such a man, hearing the ords of this oath, takes comfort in the thought that he ill have peace even if he goes on in the pride of his heart, taking hatever chance may give him:

The Lord ill have no mercy on him, but the rath of the Lord ill be burning against that man, and all the curses recorded in this book ill be aiting for him, and the Lord ill take aay his name completely from the earth.
He ill be marked out by the Lord, from all the tribes of Israel, for an evil fate, in keeping ith all the curses of the agreement recorded in this book of the la.
And future generations, your children coming after you, and travellers from far countries, ill say, hen they see the punishments of that land and the diseases hich the Lord has sent on it;

And that all the land is a salt and smoking aste, not planted or giving fruit or clothed ith grass, but asted like Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, on hich the Lord sent destruction in the heat of his rath:
Truly all the nations ill say, Why has the Lord done so to this land? hat is the reason for this great and burning rath?
Then men ill say, Because they gave up the agreement of the Lord, the God of their fathers, hich he made ith them hen he took them out of the land of Egypt:
And they ent after other gods and gave them orship, gods ho ere strange to them, and hom he had not given them:
And so the rath of the Lord as moved against this land, to send on it all the curse recorded in this book:
Rooting them out of their land, in the heat of his rath and passion, and driving them out into another land, as at this day.
The secret things are the Lord our God’s: but the things hich have been made clear are ours and our children’s for ever, so that e may do all the ords of this la.

No hen all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse hich I have put before you, if the thought of them comes back to your minds, hen you are living among the nations here the Lord your God has sent you,
And your hearts are turned again to the Lord your God, and you give ear to his ord hich I give you today, you and your children, ith all your heart and ith all your soul:
Then the Lord ill have pity on you, changing your fate, and taking you back again from among all the nations here you have been forced to go.
Even if those ho have been forced out are living in the farthest part of heaven, the Lord your God ill go in search of you, and take you back;
Placing you again in the land of your fathers as your heritage; and he ill do you good, increasing you till you are more in number than your fathers ere.
And the Lord your God ill give to you and to your seed a circumcision of the heart, so that, loving him ith all your heart and all your soul, you may have life.
And the Lord your God ill put all these curses on those ho are against you, and on your haters ho put a cruel yoke on you.
And you ill again give ear to the voice of the Lord, and do all his orders hich I have given you today.

And the Lord your God ill make you fertile in all good things, blessing the ork of your hands, and the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your cattle, and the fruit of your land: for the Lord ill have joy in you, as he had in your fathers:
If you give ear to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping his orders and his las hich are recorded in this book of the la, and turning to the Lord your God ith all your heart and ith all your soul.
For these orders hich I have given you today are not strange and secret, and are not far aay.
They are not in heaven, for you to say, Who ill go up to heaven for us and give us knoledge of them so that e may do them?
And they are not across the sea, for you to say, Who ill go over the sea for us and give us nes of them so that e may do them?
But the ord is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may do it.
See, I have put before you today, life and good, and death and evil;

In giving you orders today to have love for the Lord your God, to go in his ays and keep his las and his orders and his decisions, so that you may have life and be increased, and that the blessing of the Lord your God may be ith you in the land here you are going, the land of your heritage.
But if your heart is turned aay and your ear is shut, and you go after those ho ould make you servants and orshippers of other gods:
I give itness against you this day that destruction ill certainly be your fate, and your days ill be cut short in the land here you are going, the land of your heritage on the other side of Jordan.
Let heaven and earth be my itnesses against you this day that I have put before you life and death, a blessing and a curse: so take life for yourselves and for your seed:

In loving the Lord your God, hearing his voice and being true to him: for he is your life and by him ill your days be long: so that you may go on living in the land hich the Lord gave by an oath to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
So Moses said all these things to Israel.
Then he said to them, I am no a hundred and tenty years old; I am no longer able to go out and come in: and the Lord has said to me, You are not to go over Jordan.
The Lord your God, he ill go over before you; he ill send destruction on all those nations, and you ill take their land as your heritage: and Joshua ill go over at your head as the Lord has said.
The Lord ill do to them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, hom he put to destruction.
The Lord ill give them up into your hands, and you are to do to them as I have given you orders.
Be strong and take heart, and have no fear of them: for it is the Lord your God ho is going ith you; he ill not take aay his help from you.

Then Moses sent for Joshua, and before the eyes of all Israel said to him, Be strong and take heart: for you are to go ith this people into the land hich the Lord, by his oath to their fathers, has given them; by your help they ill take it for their heritage.
It is the Lord ho goes before you; he ill be ith you, he ill not take aay his help from you or give you up: so have no fear.
Then Moses put all this la in riting, and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, ho take up the ark of the Lord’s agreement, and to all the responsible men of Israel.
And Moses said to them, At the end of every seven years, at the time fixed for the ending of debts, at the feast of tents,
When all Israel has come before the Lord your God in the place named by him, let a reading be given of this la in the hearing of all Israel.

Make all the people come together, men and omen and children, and anyone from another country ho is ith you, so that hearing they may become ise in the fear of the Lord your God, and take care to do all the ords of this la;
And so that your children, to hom it is ne, may give ear and be trained in the fear of the Lord your God, hile you are living in the land hich you are going over Jordan to take for your heritage.
At that time the Lord said to Moses, The day of your death is near: send for Joshua, and come to the Tent of meeting so that I may give him his orders. So Moses and Joshua ent to the Tent of meeting.
And the Lord as seen in the Tent in a pillar of cloud resting by the door of the Tent.

And the Lord said to Moses, No you are going to rest ith your fathers; and this people ill be false to me, uniting themselves to the strange gods of the land here they are going; they ill be turned aay from me and ill not keep the agreement I have made ith them.

In that day my rath ill be moved against them, and I ill be turned aay from them, veiling my face from them, and destruction ill overtake them, and unnumbered evils and troubles ill come on them; so that in that day they ill say, Have not these evils come on us because our God is not ith us?
Truly, my face ill be turned aay from them in that day, because of all the evil they have done in going after other gods.
Make then this song for yourselves, teaching it to the children of Israel: put it in their mouths, so that this song may be a itness for me against the children of Israel.

For hen I have taken them into the land named in my oath to their fathers, a land floing ith milk and honey, and they have made themselves full of food and are fat, then they ill be turned to other gods and ill give them orship, no longer honouring me or keeping my agreement.

Then hen evils and troubles ithout number have overtaken them, this song ill be a itness to them, for the ords of it ill be clear in the memories of their children: for I see the thoughts hich are moving in their hearts even no, before I have taken them into the land of my oath.
So that same day Moses made this song, teaching it to the children of Israel.

Then he gave orders to Joshua, the son of Nun, saying to him, Be strong and take heart: for you are to go at the head of the children of Israel into the land hich I made an oath to give them; and I ill be ith you.
No after riting all the ords of this la in a book till the record of them as complete,
Moses said to the Levites ho ere responsible for taking up the ark of the Lord’s agreement,
Take this book of the la and put it by the ark of the Lord’s agreement, so that it may be a itness against you.
For I have knoledge of your hard and uncontrolled hearts: even no, hile I am still living, you ill not be ruled by the Lord; ho much less after my death?
Get together before me all those ho are in authority in your tribes, and your overseers, so that I may say these things in their hearing, and make heaven and earth my itnesses against them.

For I am certain that after my death you ill give yourselves up to sin, andering from the ay hich I have given you; and evil ill overtake you in the end, because you ill do evil in the eyes of the Lord, moving him to rath by the ork of your hands.
Then in the hearing of all the meeting of Israel, Moses said the ords of this song, to the end.
Give ear, O heavens, to my voice; let the earth take note of the ords of my mouth:
My teaching is dropping like rain, coming don like de on the fields; like rain on the young grass and shoers on the garden plants:
For I ill give honour to the name of the Lord: let our God be named great.
He is the Rock, complete is his ork; for all his ays are righteousness: a God ithout evil ho keeps faith, true and upright is he.
They have become false, they are not his children, the mark of sin is on them; they are an evil and hard-hearted generation.
Is this your anser to the Lord, O foolish people and unise? Is he not your father ho has given you life? He has made you and given you your place.
Keep in mind the days of the past, give thought to the years of generations gone by: go to your father and he ill make it clear to you, to the old men and they ill give you the story.
When the Most High gave the nations their heritage, separating into groups the children of men, he had the limits of the peoples marked out, keeping in mind the number of the children of Israel.
For the Lord’s ealth is his people; Jacob is the land of his heritage.
He came to him in the aste land, in the unpeopled aste of sand: putting his arms round him and caring for him, he kept him as the light of his eye.
As an eagle, teaching her young to make their flight, ith her ings outstretched over them, takes them up on her strong feathers:
So the Lord only as his guide, no other god as ith him.
He put him on the high places of the earth, his food as the increase of the field; honey he gave him out of the rock and oil out of the hard rock;
Butter from his cos and milk from his sheep, ith fat of lambs and sheep of Bashan, and goats, and the heart of the grain; and for your drink, ine from the blood of the grape.
But Jeshurun became fat and ould not be controlled: you have become fat, you are thick and full of food: then he as untrue to the God ho made him, giving no honour to the Rock of his salvation.
The honour hich as his they gave to strange gods; by their disgusting ays he as moved to rath.
They made offerings to evil spirits hich ere not God, to gods ho ere strange to them, hich had nely come up, not feared by your fathers.
You have no thought for the Rock, your father, you have no memory of the God ho gave you birth.
And the Lord sa ith disgust the evil-doing of his sons and daughters.
And he said, My face ill be veiled from them, I ill see hat their end ill be: for they are an uncontrolled generation, children in hom is no faith.
They have given my honour to that hich is not God, moving me to rath ith their false orship: I ill give their honour to those ho are not a people, moving them to rath by a foolish nation,
For my rath is a flaming fire, burning to the deep parts of the underorld, burning up the earth ith her increase, and firing the deep roots of the mountains.
I ill send a rain of troubles on them, my arros ill be shoered on them.
They ill be asted from need of food, and overcome by burning heat and bitter destruction; and the teeth of beasts I ill send on them, ith the poison of the orms of the dust.

I said I ould send them andering far aay, I ould make all memory of them go from the minds of men:
But for the fear that their haters, uplifted in their pride, might say, Our hand is strong, the Lord has not done all this.
For they are a nation ithout isdom; there is no sense in them.
If only they ere ise, if only this as clear to them, and they ould give thought to their future!
Ho ould it be possible for one to overcome a thousand, and to to send ten thousand in flight, if their rock had not let them go, if the Lord had not given them up?
For their rock is not like our Rock, even our haters themselves being judges.
For their vine is the vine of Sodom, from the fields of Gomorrah: their grapes are the grapes of evil, and the berries are bitter:
Their ine is the poison of dragons, the cruel poison of snakes.
Is not this among my secrets, kept safe in my store-house?
Punishment is mine and reard, at the time of the slipping of their feet: for the day of their donfall is near, sudden ill be their fate.
For the Lord ill be judge of his people, he ill have pity for his servants; hen he sees that their poer is gone, there is no one, shut up or free.

For lifting up my hand to heaven I say, By my unending life,
If I make sharp my shining sord, and my hand is outstretched for judging, I ill give punishment to those ho are against me, and their right reard to my haters.
I ill make my arros red ith blood, my sord ill be feasting on flesh, ith the blood of the dead and the prisoners, of the long-haired heads of my haters.
Be glad, O you his people, over the nations; for he ill take payment for the blood of his servants, and ill give punishment to his haters, and take aay the sin of his land, for his people.
So Moses said all the ords of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Hoshea, the son of Nun.
And after saying all this to the people,
Moses said to them, Let the ords hich I have said to you today go deep into your hearts, and give orders to your children to do every ord of this la.
And this is no small thing for you, but it is your life, and through this you may make your days long in the land hich you are going over Jordan to take for your heritage.
That same day the Lord said to Moses,
Go up into this mountain of Abarim, to Mount Nebo in the land of Moab opposite Jericho; there you may see the land of Canaan, hich I am giving to the children of Israel for their heritage:
And let death come to you on the mountain here you are going, and be put to rest ith your people; as death came to Aaron, your brother, on Mount Hor, here he as put to rest ith his people:
Because of your sin against me before the children of Israel at the aters of Meribath Kadesh in the aste land of Zin; because you did not keep my name holy among the children of Israel.
So you ill see the land before you, but you ill not go into the land hich I am giving to the children of Israel.
No this is the blessing hich Moses, the man of God, gave to the children of Israel before his death.
He said, The Lord came from Sinai, daning on them from Seir; shining out from Mount Paran, coming from Meribath Kadesh: from his right hand ent flames of fire: his rath made aste the peoples.
All his holy ones are at his hand; they go at his feet; they are lifted up on his ings.
Moses gave us a la, a heritage for the people of Jacob.
And there as a king in Jeshurun, hen the heads of the people and the tribes of Israel came together.
Let life not death be Reuben’s, let not the number of his men be small.
And this is the blessing of Judah: he said, Give ear, O Lord, to the voice of Judah and make him one ith his people: let your hands take up his cause, and be his help against his attackers.
And of Levi he said, Give your Thummim to Levi and let the Urim be ith your loved one, hom you put to the test at Massah, ith hom you ere angry at the aters of Meribah;

Who said of his father, Who is he? and of his mother, I have not seen her; he kept himself separate from his brothers and had no knoledge of his children: for they have given ear to your ord and kept your agreement.
They ill be the teachers of your decisions to Jacob and of your la to Israel: the burning of perfumes before you ill be their right, and the ordering of burned offerings on your altar.

Let your blessing, O Lord, be on his substance, may the ork of his hands be pleasing to you: may those ho take up arms against him and all ho have hate for him, be ounded through the heart, never to be lifted up again.
And of Benjamin he said, Benjamin is the loved one of the Lord, he ill be kept safe at all times; he ill be covered by the Most High, resting beteen his arms.
And of Joseph he said, Let the blessing of the Lord be on his land; for the good things of heaven on high, and the deep aters floing under the earth,
And the good things of the fruits of the sun, and the good things of the groth of the moons,
And the chief things of the oldest mountains, and the good things of the eternal hills,
The good things of the earth and all its ealth, the good pleasure of him ho as seen in the burning tree: may they come on the head of Joseph, on the head of him ho as prince among his brothers.

He is a young ox, glory is his; his horns are the horns of the mountain ox, ith hich all peoples ill be ounded, even to the ends of the earth: they are the ten thousands of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh.
And of Zebulun he said, Be glad, Zebulun, in your going out; and, Issachar, in your tents.
They ill send out the ord for the people to come to the mountain, taking there the offerings of righteousness: for the store of the seas ill be theirs, and the secret ealth of the sand.

And of Naphtali he said, O Naphtali, made glad ith grace and full of the blessing of the Lord: the sea and its fishes ill be his.
And of Asher he said, Let Asher have the blessing of children; may he be pleasing to his brothers, and let his foot be et ith oil.
Your shoes ill be iron and brass; and as your days, so may your ork be.
No other is like the God of Jeshurun, coming on the heavens to your help, and letting his glory be seen in the skies.
The God of your fathers is your safe resting-place, and under you are his eternal arms: driving out the forces of your haters from before you, he said, Let destruction overtake them.
And Israel is living in peace, the fountain of Jacob by himself, in a land of grain and ine, ith de dropping from the heavens.

Happy are you, O Israel: ho is like you, a people hose saviour is the Lord, hose help is your cover, hose sord is your strength! All those ho are against you ill put themselves under your rule, and your feet ill be planted on their high places.
And Moses ent up from the table-lands of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah hich is facing Jericho. And the Lord let him see all the land, the land of Gilead as far as Dan;
And all Naphtali and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, as far as the Great Sea of the est;
And the South, and the circle of the valley of Jericho, the ton of palm-trees, as far as Zoar.

And the Lord said to him, This is the land about hich I made an oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, I ill give it to your seed: no I have let you see it ith your eyes, but you ill not go in there.

And Moses at his death as a hundred and tenty years old: his eye had not become clouded, or his natural force become feeble.

And Joshua, the son of Nun, as full of the spirit of isdom; for Moses had put his hands on him: and the children of Israel gave ear to him, and did as the Lord had given orders to Moses.
There has never been another prophet in Israel like Moses, hom the Lord had knoledge of face to face;
In all the signs and onders hich the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and all his land;
And in all the acts of poer and fear hich Moses did before the eyes of all Israel.
No after the death of Moses, the servant of the Lord, the ord of the Lord came to Joshua, the son of Nun, Moses’ helper, saying,

From the aste land and this mountain Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, and all the land of the Hittites to the Great Sea, in the est, ill be your country.
While you are living, all ill give ay before you: as I as ith Moses, so I ill be ith you; I ill not take aay my help from you or give you up.
Take heart and be strong; for you ill give to this people for their heritage the land hich I gave by an oath to their fathers.
Only take heart and be very strong; take care to do all the la hich Moses my servant gave you, not turning from it to the right hand or to the left, so that you may do ell in all your undertakings.
Let this book of the la be ever on your lips and in your thoughts day and night, so that you may keep ith care everything in it; then a blessing ill be on all your ay, and you ill do ell.
Have I not given you your orders? Take heart and be strong; have no fear and do not be troubled; for the Lord your God is ith you herever you go,
Then Joshua gave their orders to those ho ere in authority over the people, saying,

Go through the tents and give orders to the people, saying, Get ready a store of food; for in three days you are to go over this river Jordan and take for your heritage the land hich the Lord your God is giving you.
And to the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joshua said,

Your ives, your little ones, and your cattle ill be kept here in the land hich Moses gave you on this side of Jordan; but you, the fighting-men, are to go over before your brothers, armed, to give them help;

Then Joshua, the son of Nun, sent to men from Shittim secretly, ith the purpose of searching out the land, and Jericho. So they ent and came to the house of a loose oman of the ton, named Rahab, here they took their rest for the night.

And the oman took the to men and put them in a secret place; then she said, Yes, the men came to me, but I had no idea here they came from;
And hen it as the time for shutting the doors at dark, they ent out; I have no idea here the men ent: but if you go after them quickly, you ill overtake them.
But she had taken them up to the roof, covering them ith the stems of flax hich she had put out in order there.
So the men ent after them on the road to Jordan as far as the river-crossing: and hen they had gone out after them, the door into the ton as shut.

And the seven priests ith their seven horns ent on before the ark of the Lord, bloing their horns: the armed men ent before them, and the mass of the people ent after the ark of the Lord, bloing their horns.

And the ton ill be put to the curse, and everything in it ill be given to the Lord: only Rahab, the loose oman, and all ho are in the house ith her, ill be kept safe, because she kept secret the men e sent.

And as for you, keep yourselves from the cursed thing, for fear that you may get a desire for it and take some of it for yourselves, and so be the cause of a curse and great trouble on the tents of Israel.
But all the silver and gold and the vessels of brass and iron are holy to the Lord: they are to come into the store-house of the Lord.

So the people gave a loud cry, and the horns ere sounded; and on hearing the horns the people gave a loud cry, and the all came don flat, so that the people ent up into the ton, every man going straight before him, and they took the ton.
And they put everything in the ton to the curse; men and omen, young and old, ox and sheep and ass, they put to death ithout mercy.
Then Joshua said to the to men ho had been sent to make a search through the land, Go into the house of the loose oman, and get her out, and all ho are ith her, as you gave her your oath.

But Joshua kept Rahab, the loose oman, and her father’s family and all she had, from death, and so she got a living-place among the children of Israel to this day; because she kept safe the men hom Joshua had sent to make a search through the land.

Then Joshua gave the people orders ith an oath, saying, Let that man be cursed before the Lord ho puts his hand to the building up of this ton: ith the loss of his first son ill he put the first stone of it in place, and ith the loss of his youngest son he ill put up its doors.

No Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, hich is by the side of Beth-aven, on the east side of Beth-el, and said to them, Go up and make a search through the land. And the men ent up and sa ho Ai as placed.

And Moses gave their heritage to the tribe of Gad by their families.
And their limit as Jazer, and all the tons of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, to Aroer before Rabbah;
And from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim to the edge of Debir;

And in the valley, Beth-haram, and Beth-nimrah, and Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon, having Jordan for its limit, to the end of the sea of Chinnereth on the east side of Jordan.
This is the heritage of the children of Gad by their families, ith its tons and its unalled places
And Moses gave their heritage to the half-tribe of Manasseh by their families.
And their limit as from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og, king of Bashan, and all Havvoth-Jair, in Bashan, sixty tons;
And half Gilead, and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, tons of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, ere for the children of Machir, the son of Manasseh, for half of the children of Machir by their families.
These are the heritages of hich Moses made distribution in the lolands of Moab, on the other side of Jordan in Jericho, to the east.
But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no heritage: the Lord, the God of Israel, is their heritage, as he said to them.

And these are the heritages hich the children of Israel took in the land of Canaan, hich Eleazar, the priest, and Joshua, the son of Nun, and the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, gave out to them;
Their heritage by the Lord’s decision, as he gave orders by Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For Moses had given their heritage to the to tribes and the half-tribe on the other side of Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no heritage among them.

Because the children of Joseph ere to tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim; and they gave the Levites no part in the land, only tons for their living-places, ith the grass-lands for their cattle and for their property.
As the Lord had given orders to Moses, so the people of Israel did, and they made division of the land.

Then the children of Judah ent to Joshua in Gilgal; and Caleb, the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, said to him, You have knoledge of hat the Lord said to Moses, the man of God, about me and about you in Kadesh-barnea.
I as forty years old hen Moses, the servant of the Lord, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to make a search through the land; and the account hich I gave him as in keeping ith his desire.
My brothers, hoever, ho ent up ith me, made the heart of the people like ater: but I as true to the Lord ith all my heart.

And on that day Moses took an oath, saying, Truly the land here your feet have been placed ill become a heritage for you and your children for ever, because you have been true to the Lord your God ith all your heart.
And no, as you see, the Lord has kept me safe these forty-five years, from the time hen the Lord said this to Moses, hile Israel as andering in the aste land: and no I am eighty-five years old.
And still, I am as strong today as I as hen Moses sent me out: as my strength as then, so is it no, for ar and for all the business of life.

So no, give me this hill-country named by the Lord at that time; for you had an account of it then, ho the Anakim ere there, and great alled tons: it may be that the Lord ill be ith me, and I ill be able to take their land, as the Lord said.
And Joshua gave him his blessing; and he gave Hebron to Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, for his heritage.
So Hebron became the heritage of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, to this day, because ith all his heart he as true to the Lord, the God of Israel.
In earlier times the name of Hebron had been Kiriath-arba, named after Arba, the greatest of the Anakim. And the land had rest from ar.
No the part of the land marked out for the children of Judah by families, ent up to the edge of Edom, as far as the aste land of Zin to the south, to the farthest point of it on the south.
Their south limit as from the farthest part of the Salt Sea, from the inlet looking to the south:
From there it goes south of the slope up to Akrabbim, and on to Zin, then south past Kadesh-barnea, and on by Hezron and up to Addar, turning in the direction of Karka:
Then on to Azmon, ending at the stream of Egypt: and the end of the limit is at the sea; this ill be your limit on the south.
And the east limit is the Salt Sea as far as the end of Jordan. And the limit of the north part of the land is from the inlet of the sea at the end of Jordan:
Then the line goes up to Beth-hoglah, past the north of Beth-arabah, and up to the stone of Bohan, the son of Reuben;

Then the line goes up to Debir from the valley of Achor, and so to the north, in the direction of Gilgal, hich is opposite the slope up to Adummim, on the south side of the river: and the line goes on to the aters of En-shemesh, ending at En-rogel:

Then the line goes up by the valley of the son of Hinnom to the south side of the Jebusite ( hich is Jerusalem): then up to the top of the mountain in front of the valley of Hinnom to the est, hich is at the farthest point of the valley of Rephaim on the north:
And the limit is marked out from the top of the mountain to the fountain of the aters of Nephtoah, and out to the tons of Mount Ephron, as far as Baalah ( hich is Kiriath-jearim):
Then turning est, the line goes from Baalah to Mount Seir, and on to the side of Mount Jearim ( hich is Chesalon) on the north, then don to Beth-shemesh, and on past Timnah:
And out to the side of Ekron to the north: then it is marked out to Shikkeron and on to Mount Baalah, ending at Jabneel; the end of the line is at the sea.
And the limit on the est is the edge of the Great Sea. This is the line going round the land marked out for the children of Judah, by their families.
And to Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, he gave a part among the children of Judah, as the Lord had given orders to Joshua, that is, Kiriath-arba, named after Arba, the father of Anak hich is Hebron.
And the three sons of Anak, Sheshai and Ahiman and Talmai, the children of Anak, ere forced out from there by Caleb.
From there he ent up against the people of Debir: (no the name of Debir before that as Kiriath-sepher.)
And Caleb said, I ill give Achsah, my daughter, as ife to the man ho overcomes Kiriath-sepher and takes it.
And Othniel, the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s brother, took it: so he gave him his daughter Achsah for his ife.
No hen she came to him, he put into her mind the idea of requesting a field from her father: and she got don from her ass; and Caleb said to her, What is it?
And she said, Give me a blessing; because you have put me in dry south-land, no give me springs of ater. So he gave her the higher spring and the loer spring.
This is the heritage of the tribe of Judah, by their families.
The farthest tons of the tribe of Judah in the direction of the limits of Edom to the south, ere Kabzeel, and Eder, and Jagur;
And Kinah, and Dimonah, and Adadah;
And Kedesh, and Hazor, and Ithnan;
Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth;
And Hazor-hadattah, and Kerioth-hezron ( hich is Hazor);
Amam, and Shema, and Moladah;
And Hazar-gaddah, and Heshmon, and Beth-pelet;
And Hazar-shual, and Beer-sheba, and Biziothiah;
Baalah, and Iim, and Ezem;
And Eltolad, and Chesil, and Hormah;
And Ziklag, and Madmannah, and Sansannah;
And Lebaoth, and Shilhim, and Ain, and Rimmon; all the tons are tenty-nine, ith their unalled places.
In the loland, Eshtaol, and Zorah, and Ashnah;
And Zanoah, and En-gannim, Tappuah, and Enam;
Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah;
And Shaaraim, and Adithaim, and Gederah, and Gederothaim; fourteen tons ith their unalled places.
Zenan, and Hadashah, and Migdal-gad;
And Dilan, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel;
Lachish, and Bozkath, and Eglon;
And Cabbon, and Lahmas, and Chithlish;
And Gederoth, Beth-dagon, and Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen tons ith their unalled places.
Libnah, and Ether, and Ashan;
And Iphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib;
And Keilah, and Achzib, and Mareshah; nine tons ith their unalled places.
Ekron, ith her daughter-tons and her unalled places;
From Ekron to the sea, all the tons by the side of Ashdod, ith their unalled places.
Ashdod, ith her daughter-tons and her unalled places; Gaza, ith her daughter-tons and her unalled places, to the stream of Egypt, ith the Great Sea as a limit.
And in the hill-country, Shamir, and Jattir, and Socoh;
And Dannah, and Kiriath-sannah ( hich is Debir);
And Anab, and Eshtemoh, and Anim;
And Goshen, and Holon, and Giloh; eleven tons ith their unalled places.
Arab, and Dumah, and Eshan;
And Janim, and Beth-tappuah, and Aphekah;
And Humtah, and Kiriath-arba ( hich is Hebron), and Zior; nine tons ith their unalled places.
Maon, Carmel, and Ziph, and Jutah;
And Jezreel, and Jokdeam, and Zanoah;
Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten tons ith their unalled places.
Halhul, Beth-zur, and Gedor;
And Maarath, and Beth-anoth, and Eltekon; six tons ith their unalled places.
Kiriath-baal ( hich is Kiriath-jearim), and Rabbah; to tons ith their unalled places.
In the aste land, Beth-arabah, Middin, and Secacah;
And Nibshan, and the Ton of Salt, and En-gedi; six tons ith their unalled places.
And as for the Jebusites living in Jerusalem, the children of Judah ere unable to make them go out; but the Jebusites are living ith the children of Judah at Jerusalem, to this day.

And the limit of the land marked out for the children of Joseph ent out from Jordan at Jericho, at the aters of Jericho on the east, in the aste land, going up from Jericho through the hill-country to Beth-el;
And it goes out from Beth-el to Luz, and on as far as the limit of the Archites to Ataroth;
And it goes don to the est to the limit of the Japhletites, to the limit of Beth-horon the loer, as far as Gezer; ending at the sea.
And the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their heritage.
And the limit of the land of the children of Ephraim by their families as marked out in this ay: the limit of their heritage to the east as Ataroth-addar, to Beth-horon the higher;
The line goes out to the est at Michmethath on the north; then turning to the east to Taanath-shiloh, going past it on the east of Janoah;
And from Janoah don to Ataroth, and to Naarah, and touching Jericho, it goes on to Jordan.
From Tappuah the line goes on to the est to the river of Kanah; ending at the sea. This is the heritage of the children of Ephraim by their families;
Together ith the tons marked out for the children of Ephraim in the heritage of Manasseh, all the tons ith their unalled places.
And the Canaanites ho ere living in Gezer ere not forced out; but the Canaanites have been living among Ephraim, to this day, as servants, doing forced ork.

And this as the part marked out for the tribe of Manasseh, because he as the oldest son of Joseph. As for Machir, the oldest son of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he as a man of ar he had Gilead and Bashan.

And as for the rest of the children of Manasseh, their heritage as given to them by families; for the children of Abiezer, and for the children of Helek, and for the children of Asriel, and for the children of Shechem, and for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida: these ere the male children of Manasseh, the son of Joseph, by their families.

But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but only daughters; and these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

And they came before Eleazar the priest, and Joshua, the son of Nun, and before the chiefs, saying, The Lord gave orders to Moses to give us a heritage among our brothers: so in agreement ith the orders of the Lord he gave them a heritage among their father’s brothers.
And ten parts ere given to Manasseh, in addition to the land of Gilead and Bashan, hich is on the other side of Jordan;
Because the daughters of Manasseh had a heritage among his sons, and the land of Gilead as the property of the other sons of Manasseh.
And the limit of Manasseh’s land as from Asher to Michmethath, hich is before Shechem; the line goes on to the right hand, to the people of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah as the property of Manasseh; but Tappuah on the edge of Manasseh as the property of the children of Ephraim.
And the limit goes don to the stream Kanah, to the south of the stream: these tons ere Ephraim’s among the tons of Manasseh; Manasseh’s limit as on the north side of the stream, ending at the sea:
To the south it is Ephraim’s, and to the north it is Manasseh’s, and the sea is his limit; and they are touching Asher on the north, and Issachar on the east.

In Issachar and Asher, Manasseh had Beth-shean and its daughter-tons, and Ibleam and its daughter-tons, and the people of Dor and its daughter-tons, and the people of En-dor and its daughter-tons, and the people of Taanach and its daughter-tons, and the people of Megiddo and its daughter-tons, that is, the three hills.
But the children of Manasseh ere not able to make the people of those tons go out; but the Canaanites ould go on living in that land.
And hen the children of Israel had become strong, they put the Canaanites to forced ork, in place of driving them out.

Then the children of Joseph said to Joshua, Why have you given me only one part and one stretch of land for my heritage? For through the blessing given to me by the Lord up to no, I am a great people.

Then Joshua said to them, If you are such a great people, go up into the oodlands, clearing a place there for yourselves in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, if the hill-country of Ephraim is not ide enough for you.

And the children of Joseph said, The hill-country is not enough for us: and all the Canaanites living in the valley have iron ar-carriages, those in Beth-shean and its tons as ell as those in the valley of Jezreel.
Then Joshua said to the children of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, You are a great people, and have great poer: you are not to have one property only,
For the hill-country of Gilead ill be yours ... the oodland and cut don ... its outskirts ill be yours ... get the Canaanites out, for they have iron ar-carriages ... strong.
And all the meeting of the children of Israel came together at Shiloh and put up the Tent of meeting there: and the land as crushed before them.
But there ere still seven tribes among the children of Israel ho had not taken up their heritage.
Then Joshua said to the children of Israel, Why are you so slo to go in and take up your heritage in the land hich the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you?
Take from among you three men from every tribe; and I ill send them to go through the land and make a record of it for distribution as their heritage; then let them come back to me.
And let them make division of it into seven parts: let Judah keep inside his limit on the south, and let the children of Joseph keep inside their limit on the north.
And you are to have the land marked out in seven parts, and come back to me ith the record; and I ill make the distribution for you here by the decision of the Lord our God.

For the Levites have no part among you; to be the Lord’s priests is their heritage; and Gad and Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have had their heritage on the east side of Jordan, given to them by Moses, the servant of the Lord.

So the men got up and ent; and Joshua gave orders to those ho ent, to make a record of the land, saying, Go up and don through the land, and make a record of it and come back here to me, and I ill make the distribution for you here by the decision of the Lord in Shiloh.
So the men ent, travelling through the land, and made a record of it by tons in seven parts in a book, and came back to Joshua to the tent-circle at Shiloh.
And Joshua made the distribution for them in Shiloh by the decision of the Lord, marking out the land for the children of Israel by their divisions.
And the first heritage came out for the tribe of Benjamin by their families: and the limit of their heritage ent beteen the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.
And their limit on the north as from the Jordan, and the line goes up to the side of Jericho on the north and through the hill-country to the est, ending at the aste land of Beth-aven.
And from there the line goes south to Luz, to the side of Luz ( hich is Beth-el), then don to Ataroth-addar, by the mountain to the south of Beth-horon the loer.

And the limit is marked as coming round to the south on the est side from the mountain hich is south of Beth-horon, and ending at Kiriath-baal ( hich is Kiriath-jearim), a ton of the children of Judah: this is the est part.
And the south part is from the farthest point of Kiriath-jearim, and the line goes out to the est to the fountain of the aters of Nephtoah:

And the line goes don to the farthest part of the mountain facing the valley of the son of Hinnom, hich is on the north of the valley of Rephaim: from there it goes don to the valley of Hinnom, to the side of the Jebusite on the south as far as En-rogel;
And it goes to En-shemesh and on to Geliloth, opposite the ay up to Adummim, and it goes don to the stone of Bohan, the son of Reuben;
And it goes on to the side facing the Arabah to the north, and don to the Arabah;
And on to the north side of Beth-hoglah, ending at the north inlet of the Salt Sea at the south end of Jordan; this is their limit on the south.
And the limit of the east part is the Jordan. This is the heritage of the children of Benjamin, marked out for their families by these limits on all sides.
And the tons of the children of Benjamin, given to them in the order of their families, are Jericho and Beth-hoglah and Emek-kezziz
And Beth-arabah and Zemaraim and Beth-el
And Avvim and Parah and Ophrah
And Chephar-Ammoni and Ophni and Geba; telve tons ith their unalled places;
Gibeon and Ramah and Beeroth
And Mizpeh and Chephirah and Mozah
And Rekem and Irpeel and Taralah
And Zela, Eleph and the Jebusite ( hich is Jerusalem), Gibeath and Kiriath; fourteen tons ith their unalled places. This is the heritage of the children of Benjamin by their families.
And the second heritage came out for the tribe of Simeon by their families; and their heritage as in the middle of the heritage of the children of Judah.
And they had for their heritage Beer-sheba and Shema and Moladah
And Hazar-shual and Balah and Ezem
And Eltolad and Bethul and Hormah
And Ziklag and Beth-marcaboth and Hazar-susah
And Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen; thirteen tons ith their unalled places;
Ain, Rimmon, and Ether and Ashan; four tons ith their unalled places;
And all the unalled places round about these tons as far as Baalath-beer-ramah to the south. This is the heritage of the tribe of Simeon by their families.
The heritage of Simeon as taken out of Judah’s stretch of land, for Judah’s part as more than they had need of, so the heritage of the children of Simeon as inside their heritage.
And the third heritage came out for Zebulun by their families; the limit of their heritage as as far as Sarid;
And their limit goes up to the est to Maralah, stretching to Dabbesheth, and to the stream in front of Jokneam;
Then turning east from Sarid to the limit of Chisloth-tabor, it goes out to Daberath, and up to Japhia;
And from there it goes on east to Gath-hepher, to Eth-kazin; ending at Rimmon hich goes as far as Neah;
And the line goes round it on the north to Hannathon, ending at the valley of Iphtah-el;
And Kattath and Nahalal and Shimron and Idalah and Beth-lehem; telve tons ith their unalled places.
This is the heritage of the children of Zebulun by their families, these tons ith their unalled places.
For Issachar the fourth heritage came out, for the children of Issachar by their families;
And their limit as to Jezreel and Chesulloth and Shunem
And Hapharaim and Shion and Anaharath
And Rabbith and Kishion and Ebez
And Remeth and En-gannim and En-haddah and Beth-pazzez;
And their limit goes as far as Tabor and Shahazimah and Beth-shemesh, ending at Jordan; sixteen tons ith their unalled places.
This is the heritage of the tribe of the children of Issachar by their families, these tons ith their unalled places.
And the fifth heritage came out for the tribe of Asher by their families.
And their limit as Helkath and Hali and Beten and Achshaph
And Alammelech and Amad and Mishal, stretching to Carmel on the est and Shihor-libnath;
Turning to the east to Beth-dagon and stretching to Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el as far as Beth-emek and Neiel to the north; on the left it goes as far as Cabul
And Ebron and Rehob and Hammon and Kanah, to great Zidon;
And the limit goes round to Ramah and the alled ton of Tyre and Hosah, ending at the sea by Heleb and Achzib;
And Ummah and Aphek and Rehob; tenty-to tons ith their unalled places.
This is the heritage of the tribe of the children of Asher by their families, these tons ith their unalled places.
For the children of Naphtali the sixth heritage came out, for the children of Naphtali by their families;
And their limit as from Heleph, from the oak-tree in Zaanannim, and Adami-hannekeb and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, ending at Jordan;
And turning est to Aznoth-tabor, the limit goes out from there to Hukkok, stretching to Zebulun on the south, and Asher on the est, and Judah at Jordan on the east.
And the alled tons are Ziddim, Zer, and Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth
And Adamah and Ramah and Hazor
And Kedesh and Edrei and En-Hazor
And Iron and Migdal-el, Horem and Beth-anath and Beth-shemesh; nineteen tons ith their unalled places.
This is the heritage of the tribe of the children of Naphtali by their families, these tons ith their unalled places.
For the tribe of Dan by their families the seventh heritage came out;
And the limit of their heritage as Zorah and Eshtaol and Ir-shemesh
And Shaalabbin and Aijalon and Ithlah
And Elon and Timnah and Ekron
And Eltekeh and Gibbethon and Baalath
And Jehud and Bene-berak and Gath-rimmon;
And on the est as ... opposite Joppa.

( But the limit of the children of Dan as not ide enough for them; so the children of Dan ent up and made ar on Leshem and took it, putting it to the sord ithout mercy, and they took it for their heritage and made a place for themselves there, giving it the name of Leshem-dan, after the name of their father, Dan.)
This is the heritage of the tribe of the children of Dan by their families, these tons ith their unalled places.
So the distribution of the land and its limits as complete; and the children of Israel gave Joshua, the son of Nun, a heritage among them;
By the orders of the Lord they gave him the ton for hich he made request, Timnath-serah in the hill-country of Ephraim: there, after building the ton, he made his living-place.

These are the heritages hich Eleazar the priest and Joshua, the son of Nun, and the heads of families of the tribes of the children of Israel gave out at Shiloh, by the decision of the Lord, at the door of the Tent of meeting. So the distribution of the land as complete.
And the Lord said to Joshua,
Say to the children of Israel, Let certain tons be marked out as safe places, as I said to you by the mouth of Moses,
So that any man ho in error and ithout design has taken the life of another, may go in flight to them: and they ill be safe places for you from him ho has the right of punishment for blood.

And if anyone goes in flight to one of those tons, and comes into the public place of the ton, and puts his cause before the responsible men of the ton, they ill take him into the ton and give him a place among them here he may be safe.
And if the one ho has the right of punishment comes after him, they are not to give the taker of life up to him; because he as the cause of his neighbour’s death ithout designing it and not in hate.

And he is to go on living in that ton till he has to come before the meeting of the people to be judged; ( till the death of him ho is high priest at that time:) then the taker of life may come back to his ton and to his house, to the ton from hich he had gone in flight.
So they made selection of Kedesh in Galilee in the hill-country of Naphtali, and Shechem in the hill-country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba ( hich is Hebron) in the hill-country of Judah.

And on the east side of Jordan at Jericho, they made selection of Bezer in the aste land, in the table-land, out of the tribe of Reuben, and Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh.

These ere the tons marked out for all the children of Israel and for the man from a strange country living among them, so that anyone causing the death of another in error, might go in flight there, and not be put to death by him ho has the right of punishment for blood till he had come before the meeting of the people.
Then the heads of the families of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest and Joshua, the son of Nun, and to the heads of families of the tribes of the children of Israel;
And said to them in Shiloh in the land of Canaan, The Lord gave orders by Moses that e ere to have tons for living in, ith their grass-lands for our cattle.
And the children of Israel out of their heritage gave to the Levites these tons ith their grass-lands, by the order of the Lord.
And the heritage came out for the families of the Kohathites: the children of Aaron the priest, ho ere of the Levites, ere given thirteen tons from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
The rest of the children of Kohath by their families ere given ten tons from the tribes of Ephraim and Dan and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The children of Gershon by their families ere given thirteen tons from the tribes of Issachar and Asher and Naphtali and the half-tribe of Manasseh hich as in Bashan.
The children of Merari by their families ere given telve tons from the tribes of Reuben and Gad and Zebulun.
All these tons ith their grass-lands the children of Israel gave by the decision of the Lord to the Levites, as the Lord had given orders by Moses.
From the tribes of the children of Judah and the children of Simeon they gave these tons, listed here by name:
These ere for the children of Aaron among the families of the Kohathites, of the children of Levi: for they came first in the distribution.
They gave them Kiriath-arba, the ton of Arba, the father of Anak, ( hich is Hebron) in the hill-country of Judah, ith its grass-lands.
But the open country round the ton, and its unalled places, they gave to Caleb, the son of Jephunneh, as his property.
And to the children of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron ith its grass-lands, the ton here the taker of life might be safe, and Libnah ith its grass-lands;
And Jattir ith its grass-lands, and Eshtemoa ith its grass-lands;
And Holon ith its grass-lands, and Debir ith its grass-lands;
And Ain, and Juttah, and Beth-shemesh, ith their grass-lands; nine tons from those to tribes.
And from the tribe of Benjamin they gave Gibeon and Geba ith their grass-lands;
Anathoth and Almon ith their grass-lands, four tons.
Thirteen tons ith their grass-lands ere given to the children of Aaron, the priests.
The rest of the families of the children of Kohath, the Levites, ere given tons from the tribe of Ephraim.
And they gave them Shechem ith its grass-lands in the hill-country of Ephraim, the ton here the taker of life might be safe, and Gezer ith its grass-lands;
And Kibzaim and Beth-horon ith their grass-lands, four tons.
And from the tribe of Dan, Elteke and Gibbethon ith their grass-lands;
Aijalon and Gath-rimmon ith their grass-lands, four tons.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach and Gath-rimmon ith their grass-lands, to tons.
All the tons of the rest of the families of the children of Kohath ere ten ith their grass-lands.

And she sent for Barak, the son of Abinoam, from Kedesh-naphtali, and said to him, Has not the Lord, the God of Israel, given orders saying, Go and get your force into line in Mount Tabor, and take ith you ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?
And I ill make Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, ith his ar-carriages and his forces, come against you at the river Kishon, here I ill give him into your hands.
And Barak said to her, If you ill go ith me then I ill go; but if you ill not go ith me I ill not go.
And she said, I ill certainly go ith you: though you ill get no honour in your undertaking, for the Lord ill give Sisera into the hands of a oman. So Deborah got up and ent ith Barak to Kedesh.
Then Barak sent for Zebulun and Naphtali to come to Kedesh; and ten thousand men ent up after him, and Deborah ent up ith him.
No Heber the Kenite, separating himself from the rest of the Kenites, from the children of Hobab, the brother-in-la of Moses, had put up his tent as far aay as the oak-tree in Zaanannim, by Kedesh.
And ord as given to Sisera that Barak, the son of Abinoam, had gone up to Mount Tabor.

Then Deborah said to Barak, Up! for today the Lord has given Sisera into your hands: has not the Lord gone out before you? So Barak ent don from Mount Tabor and ten thousand men after him.
And the Lord sent fear on Sisera and all his ar-carriages and all his army before Barak; and Sisera got don from his ar-carriage and ent in flight on foot.
But Barak ent after the ar-carriages and the army as far as Harosheth of the Gentiles; and all Sisera’s army as put to the sord; not a man got aay.
But Sisera ent in flight on foot to the tent of Jael, the ife of Heber the Kenite; for there as peace beteen Jabin, king of Hazor, and the family of Heber the Kenite.
And Jael ent out to Sisera, and said to him, Come in, my lord, come in to me ithout fear. So he ent into her tent, and she put a cover over him.
Then he said to her, Give me no a little ater, for I have need of a drink. And opening a skin of milk, she gave him drink, and put the cover over him again.
And he said to her, Take your place at the door of the tent, and if anyone comes and says to you, Is there any man here, say, No.

Then Jael, Heber’s ife, took a tent-pin and a hammer and ent up to him quietly, driving the pin into his head, and it ent through his head into the earth, for he as in a deep sleep from eariness; and so he came to his end.

Then Jael ent out, and meeting Barak going after Sisera, said to him, Come, and I ill let you see the man you are searching for. So he came into her tent and sa, and there as Sisera stretched out dead ith the tent-pin in his head.

And the poer of the children of Israel ent on increasing against Jabin, king of Canaan, till he as cut off.
At that time Deborah and Barak, the son of Abinoam, made this song, saying:
Because of the floing hair of the fighters in Israel, because the people gave themselves freely, give praise to the Lord.
Give attention, O kings; give ear, O rulers; I, even I, ill make a song to the Lord; I ill make melody to the Lord, the God of Israel.
Lord, hen you ent out from Seir, moving like an army from the field of Edom, the earth as shaking and the heavens ere troubled, and the clouds ere dropping ater.
The mountains ere shaking before the Lord, before the Lord, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar, the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highays ere not used, and travellers ent by side roads.
Country tons ere no more in Israel, *** ere no more, till you, Deborah, came up, till you came up as a mother in Israel.
They had no one to make arms, there ere no more armed men in the tons; as there a body-cover or a spear to be seen among forty thousand in Israel?
Come, you rulers of Israel, you ho gave yourselves freely among the people: give praise to the Lord.
Let them give thought to it, ho go on hite asses, and those ho are alking on the road.
Give ear to the omen laughing by the ater-springs; there they ill give again the story of the upright acts of the Lord, all the upright acts of his arm in Israel.
Aake! aake! Deborah: aake! aake! give a song: Up! Barak, and take prisoner those ho took you prisoner, O son of Abinoam.
Then the chiefs ent don to the doors; the Lord’s people ent don among the strong ones.
Out of Ephraim they came don into the valley; after you, Benjamin, among your tribesmen; from Machir came don the captains, and from Zebulun those in hose hand is the ruler’s rod.
Your chiefs, Issachar, ere ith Deborah; and Naphtali as true to Barak; into the valley they ent rushing out at his feet. In Reuben there ere divisions, and great searchings of heart.
Why did you keep quiet among the sheep, hearing nothing but the atchers piping to the flocks?
Gilead as living over Jordan; and Dan as aiting in his ships; Asher kept in his place by the sea’s edge, living by his inlets.
It as the people of Zebulun ho put their lives in danger, even to death, ith Naphtali on the high places of the field.
The kings came on to the fight, the kings of Canaan ere arring; in Taanach by the aters of Megiddo: they took no profit in money.
The stars from heaven ere fighting; from their highays they ere fighting against Sisera.
The river Kishon took them violently aay, stopping their flight, the river Kishon. Give praise, O my soul, to the strength of the Lord!
Then loudly the feet of the horses ere sounding ith the stamping, the stamping of their ar-horses.
A curse, a curse on Meroz! said the angel of the Lord. A bitter curse on her tonspeople! Because they came not to the help of the Lord, to the help of the Lord among the strong ones.
Blessings be on Jael, more than on all omen! Blessings greater than on any in the tents!
His request as for ater, she gave him milk; she put butter before him on a fair plate.
She put out her hand to the tent-pin, and her right hand to the orkman’s hammer; and she gave Sisera a blo, crushing his head, ounding and driving through his bro.
Bent at her feet he ent don, he as stretched out; bent at her feet he ent don; here he as bent don, there he ent don in death.
Looking out from the indo she gave a cry, the mother of Sisera as crying out through the indo, Why is his carriage so long in coming? When ill the noise of his heels be sounding?
Her ise omen gave anser to her, yes, she made anser again to herself,

Are they not getting, are they not parting the goods among them: a young girl or to to every man; and to Sisera robes of coloured needleork, orked in fair colours on this side and on that, for the neck of the queen?
So may destruction come on all your haters, O Lord; but let your lovers be like the sun going out in his strength. And for forty years the land had peace.
And the children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the Lord; and the Lord gave them up into the hand of Midian for seven years.
And Midian as stronger than Israel; and because of the Midianites, the children of Israel made holes for themselves in the mountains, and hollos in the rocks, and strong places.
And henever Israel’s grain as planted, the Midianites and the Amalekites and the people of the east came up against them;
And put their army in position against them; and they took all the produce of the earth as far as Gaza, till there as no food in Israel, or any sheep or oxen or asses.
For they came up regularly ith their oxen and their tents; they came like the locusts in number; they and their camels ere ithout number; and they came into the land for its destruction.
And Israel as in great need because of Midian; and the cry of the children of Israel ent up to the Lord.
And hen the cry of the children of Israel, because of Midian, came before the Lord,

And I took you out of the hands of the Egyptians and out of the hands of all ho ere cruel to you, and I sent them out by force from before you and gave you their land;
And I said to you, I am the Lord your God; you are not to give orship to the gods of the Amorites in hose land you are living, but you did not give ear to my voice.

No the angel of the Lord came and took his seat under the oak-tree in Ophrah, in the field of Joash the Abiezrite; and his son Gideon as crushing grain in the place here the grapes ere crushed, so that the Midianites might not see it.

And the Lord, turning to him, said, Go in the strength you have and be Israel’s saviour from Midian: have I not sent you?
And he said to him, O Lord, ho may I be the saviour of Israel? See, my family is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.
Then the Lord said to him, Truly, I ill be ith you, and you ill overcome the Midianites as if they ere one man.

Then Gideon ent in and made ready a young goat, and ith an ephah of meal he made unleavened cakes: he put the meat in a basket and the soup in hich it had been cooked he put in a pot, and he took it out to him under the oak-tree and gave it to him there.
And the angel of God said to him, Take the meat and the unleavened cakes and put them don on the rock over there, draining out the soup over them. And he did so.

Then the angel of the Lord put out the stick hich as in his hand, touching the meat and the cakes ith the end of it; and a flame came up out of the rock, burning up the meat and the cakes: and the angel of the Lord as seen no longer.

The same night the Lord said to him, Take ten men of your servants and an ox seven years old, and after pulling don the altar of Baal hich is your father’s, and cutting don the holy tree by its side,
Make an altar to the Lord your God on the top of this rock, in the ordered ay and take the ox and make a burned offering ith the ood of the holy tree hich has been cut don.

And the men of the ton got up early in the morning, and they sa the altar of Baal broken don, and the holy tree hich as by it cut don, and the ox offered on the altar hich had been put up there.

Then all the Midianites and the Amalekites and the people of the east, banding themselves together, ent over and put up their tents in the valley of Jezreel.

Then Gideon said to God, If you are going to give Israel salvation by my hand, as you have said,

No Abimelech, the son of Jerubbaal, ent to Shechem to his mother’s family, and said to them and to all the family of his mother’s father,

Then he ent to his father’s house at Ophrah, and put his brothers, the seventy sons of Jerubbaal, to death on the same stone; hoever, Jotham, the youngest, kept himself safe by going aay to a secret place.

Then the trees said to the fig-tree, You come and be king over us.
But the fig-tree said to them, Am I to give up my seet taste and my good fruit and go aving over the trees?
Then the trees said to the vine, You come and be king over us.
But the vine said to them, Am I to give up my ine, hich makes glad God and men, to go aving over the trees?

And the thorn said to the trees, If it is truly your desire to make me your king, then come and put your faith in my shade; and if not, may fire come out of the thorn, burning up the cedars of Lebanon.

If then you have done hat is true and upright to Jerubbaal and his family this day, may you have joy in Abimelech, and may he have joy in you;
But if not, may fire come out from Abimelech, burning up the tonsmen of Shechem and Beth-millo; and may fire come out from the tonsmen of Shechem and Beth-millo, for the destruction of Abimelech.

And the tonsmen of Shechem put secret atchers on the tops of the mountains, and they made attacks on all ho ent by on the road and took their goods; and ord of this came to Abimelech.
