And they ent out into their fields and got in the fruit of their vines, and hen the grapes had been crushed, they made a holy feast and ent into the house of their god, and over their food and drink they ere cursing Abimelech.

And Gaal, the son of Ebed, said, Who is Abimelech and ho is Shechem, that e are to be his servants? Is it not right for the son of Jerubbaal and Zebul his captain to be servants to the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem? But hy are e to be his servants?
If only I had authority over this people! I ould put Abimelech out of the ay, and I ould say to Abimelech, Make your army strong, and come out.
No Zebul, the ruler of the ton, hearing hat Gaal, the son of Ebed, had said, as moved to rath.
And he sent to Abimelech at Arumah, saying, See, Gaal, the son of Ebed, and his brothers have come to Shechem, and they are orking up the ton against you.
So no, get up by night, you and your people, and keep atch in the field secretly;
And in the morning, hen the sun is up, get up early and make a rush on the ton; and hen he and his people come out against you, do to them hatever you have a chance to do.
So Abimelech and the people ith him got up by night, in four bands, to make a surprise attack on Shechem.
And Gaal, the son of Ebed, ent out, and took his place at the dooray into the ton; then Abimelech and his people got up from the place here they had been aiting.
And hen Gaal sa the people, he said to Zebul, See! people are coming don from the tops of the mountains. And Zebul said to him, You see the shade of the mountains like men.
And Gaal said again, See! people are coming don from the middle of the land, and one band is coming by ay of the oak-tree of the Seers.
Then Zebul said to him, No here is your loud talk hen you said, Who is Abimelech that e are to be his servants? Is this not the people hom you ere rating so lo? Go out no, and make ar on them.
So Gaal ent out at the head of the tonsmen of Shechem and made ar on Abimelech.
And Abimelech ent after him and he ent in flight before him; and a great number ere falling by the sord all the ay up to the ton.
Then Abimelech ent back to Arumah; and Zebul sent Gaal and his brothers aay and ould not let them go on living in Shechem.
No the day after, the people ent out into the fields; and nes of it came to Abimelech.
And he took his people, separating them into three bands, and as aiting secretly in the field; and hen he sa the people coming out of the ton, he ent up and made an attack on them.
And Abimelech ith his band made a rush, and took up their position at the dooray into the ton; and the other to bands made a rush on all those ho ere in the fields, and overcame them.
And all that day Abimelech as fighting against the ton; and he took it, and put to death the people ho ere in it, and had the ton pulled don and covered ith salt.
Then all the tonsmen of the toer of Shechem, hearing of it, ent into the inner room of the house of El-berith.
And ord as given to Abimelech that all the men of the toer of Shechem ere there together.

Then Abimelech ent up to Mount Zalmon, ith all his people; and Abimelech took an axe in his hand and, cutting don branches of trees, took them and put them on his back. And he said to the people ho ere ith him, Be quick and do as you have seen me do.

So all the people got branches, every man cutting don a branch, and they ent ith Abimelech at their head and, massing the branches against the inner room, put fire to the room over them; so all those ho ere in the toer of Shechem, about a thousand men and omen, ere burned to death ith it.
Then Abimelech ent to Thebez, and put his army in position against Thebez and took it.
But in the middle of the ton there as a strong toer, to hich all the men and omen of the ton ent in flight and, shutting themselves in, ent up to the roof of the toer.
And Abimelech came to the toer and made an attack on it, and got near to the door of the toer for the purpose of firing it.
But a certain oman sent a great stone, such as is used for crushing grain, on to the head of Abimelech, cracking the bone.

Then quickly crying out to his body-servant, he said to him, Take out your sord and put an end to me straight aay, so that men may not say of me, His death as the ork of a oman. So the young man put his sord through him, causing his death.
And hen the men of Israel sa that Abimelech as dead, they ent aay, every man to his place.
In this ay Abimelech as rearded by God for the evil he had done to his father in putting his seventy brothers to death;
And God sent back on to the heads of the men of Shechem all the evil they had done, and the curse of Jotham, the son of Jerubbaal, came on them.
No after Abimelech, Tola, the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, became the saviour of Israel; he as living in Shamir in the hill-country of Ephraim.
He as judge over Israel for tenty-three years; and at his death his body as put to rest in the earth in Shamir.
And after him came Jair the Gileadite, ho as judge over Israel for tenty-to years.
And he had thirty sons, ho ent on thirty young asses; and they had thirty tons in the land of Gilead, hich are named Havvoth-Jair to this day.
And at the death of Jair his body as put to rest in the earth in Kamon.

And again the children of Israel did evil in the eyes of the Lord, orshipping the Baals and Astartes, and the gods of Aram and the gods of Zidon and the gods of Moab and the gods of the children of Ammon and the gods of the Philistines; they gave up the Lord and ere servants to him no longer.
And the rath of the Lord as burning against Israel, and he gave them up into the hands of the Philistines and into the hands of the children of Ammon.

And that year the children of Israel ere crushed under their yoke; for eighteen years all the children of Israel on the other side of Jordan, in the land of the Amorites hich is in Gilead, ere cruelly crushed don.
And the children of Ammon ent over Jordan, to make ar against Judah and Benjamin and the house of Ephraim; and Israel as in great trouble.
Then the children of Israel, crying out to the Lord, said, Great is our sin against you, for e have given up our God and have been servants to the Baals.
And the Lord said to the children of Israel, Were not the Egyptians and the Amorites and the children of Ammon and the Philistines
And the Zidonians and Amalek and Midian crushing you don, and in anser to your cry did I not give you salvation from their hands?
But, for all this, you have given me up and have been servants to other gods: so I ill be your saviour no longer.
Go, send up your cry for help to the gods of your selection; let them be your saviours in the time of your trouble.
And the children of Israel said to the Lord, We are sinners; do to us hatever seems good to you: only give us salvation this day.
So they put aay the strange gods from among them, and became the Lord’s servants; and his soul as angry because of the sorros of Israel.
Then the children of Ammon came together and put their army in position in Gilead. And the children of Israel came together and put their army in position in Mizpah.
And the people of Israel said to one another, Who ill be the first to make an attack on the children of Ammon? We ill make him head over all Gilead.
No Jephthah the Gileadite as a great man of ar; he as the son of a loose oman, and Gilead as his father.
And Gilead’s ife gave birth to sons, and hen her sons became men, they sent Jephthah aay, saying, You have no part in the heritage of our father’s house, for you are the son of another oman.
So Jephthah ent in flight from his brothers and as living in the land of Tob, here a number of good-for-nothing men, joining Jephthah, ent out ith him on his undertakings.
No after a time the children of Ammon made ar against Israel.
And hen the children of Ammon made ar against Israel, the responsible men of Gilead ent to get Jephthah back from the land of Tob;
And they said to Jephthah, Come and be our chief so that e may make ar against the children of Ammon.
But Jephthah said to the responsible men of Gilead, Did you not, in your hate for me, send me aay from my father’s house? Why do you come to me no hen you are in trouble?

And the responsible men of Gilead said to Jephthah, That is the reason e have come back to you; so go ith us and make ar against the children of Ammon, and e ill make you our head over all the people of Gilead.
Then Jephthah said to the responsible men of Gilead, If you take me back to make ar against the children of Ammon, and if ith the help of the Lord I overcome them, ill you make me your head?
And the responsible men of Gilead said to Jephthah, May the Lord be our itness: e ill certainly do as you say.
So Jephthah ent ith the responsible men of Gilead, and the people made him head and chief over them; and Jephthah said all these things before the Lord in Mizpah.
Then Jephthah sent men to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What have you against me that you have come to make ar against my land?

And the king of the children of Ammon said to the men sent by Jephthah, Because Israel, hen he came up out of Egypt, took aay my land, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and as far as Jordan: so no, give me back those lands quietly.
And Jephthah sent again to the king of the children of Ammon,
And said to him, This is the ord of Jephthah: Israel did not take aay the land of Moab or the land of the children of Ammon;
But hen they came up from Egypt, Israel ent through the aste land to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh;

Then Israel sent men to the king of Edom saying, Let me no go through your land; but the king of Edom did not give ear to them. And in the same ay he sent to the king of Moab, but he ould not; so Israel ent on living in Kadesh.

Then he ent on through the aste land and round the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and put up their tents on the other side of the Arnon; they did not come inside the limit of Moab, for the Arnon as the limit of Moab.
And Israel sent men to Sihon, king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, Let me no go through your land to my place.
But Sihon ould not give ay and let Israel go through his land; and Sihon got together all his people, and put his army in position in Jahaz, and made ar on Israel.
And the Lord, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into the hands of Israel, and they overcame them; so all the land of the Amorites, the people of that land, became Israel’s.
All the limit of the Amorites as theirs, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and from the aste land even to Jordan.
So no the Lord, the God of Israel, has taken aay their land from the Amorites and given it to his people Israel; are you then to have it?
Do you not keep the lands of those hom Chemosh your god sends out from before you? So e ill keep all the lands of those hom the Lord our God sends out from before us.
What! are you any better than Balak, the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever take up a cause against Israel or make ar against them?

While Israel as living in Heshbon and its daughter-tons and in Aroer and its daughter-tons and in all the tons hich are by the side of the Arnon, for three hundred years, hy did you not get them back at that time?
So I have done no rong against you, but you are doing rong to me in fighting against me: may the Lord, ho is Judge this day, be judge beteen the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.
The king of the children of Ammon, hoever, did not give ear to the ords hich Jephthah sent to him.
Then the spirit of the Lord came on Jephthah, and he ent through Gilead and Manasseh, and came to Mizpeh of Gilead; and from Mizpeh of Gilead he ent over to the children of Ammon.
And Jephthah took an oath to the Lord, and said, If you ill give the children of Ammon into my hands,
Then hoever comes out from the door of my house, meeting me hen I come back in peace from the children of Ammon, ill be the Lord’s and I ill give him as a burned offering.
So Jephthah ent over to the children of Ammon to make ar on them; and the Lord gave them into his hands.

And he made an attack on them from Aroer all the ay to Minnith, overrunning tenty tons, as far as Abel-cheramim, and put great numbers to the sord. So the children of Ammon ere crushed before the children of Israel.
Then Jephthah came back to his house in Mizpah, and his daughter came out, meeting him on his ay ith music and ith dances; she as his only child; he had no other sons or daughters.

And hen he sa her he as overcome ith grief, and said, Ah! my daughter! I am crushed ith sorro, and it is you ho are the chief cause of my trouble; for I have made an oath to the Lord and I may not take it back.
And she said to him, My father, you have made an oath to the Lord; do then to me hatever you have said; for the Lord has sent a full reard on your haters, on the children of Ammon.
Then she said to her father, Only do this for me: let me have to months to go aay into the mountains ith my friends, eeping for my sad fate.
And he said, Go then. So he sent her aay for to months; and she ent ith her friends to the mountains, eeping for her sad fate.
And at the end of to months she ent back to her father, ho did ith her as he had said in his oath: and she had never been touched by a man. So it became a rule in Israel,
For the omen to go year by year sorroing for the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in every year.

No the men of Ephraim came together and took up arms and ent over to Zaphon; and they said to Jephthah, Why did you go over to make ar against the children of Ammon ithout sending for us to go ith you? No e ill put your house on fire over you.
And Jephthah said to them, I and my people ere in danger, and the children of Ammon ere very cruel to us, and hen I sent for you, you gave me no help against them.

So hen I sa that there as no help to be had from you, I put my life in my hand and ent over against the children of Ammon, and the Lord gave them into my hands: hy then have you come up to me this day to make ar on me?
Then Jephthah got together all the men of Gilead and made ar on Ephraim; and the men of Gilead overcame Ephraim.

And the Gileadites took the crossing-places of Jordan against the Ephraimites; and hen any of the men of Ephraim ho had gone in flight said, let me go over; the men of Gilead said to him, Are you an Ephraimite? And if he said, No;

Then they said to him, No say Shibboleth; and he said Sibboleth, and as not able to say it in the right ay; then they took him and put him to death at the crossing-places of Jordan; and at that time forty-to thousand Ephraimites ere put to death.
No Jephthah as judge of Israel for six years. And Jephthah the Gileadite came to his death, and his body as put to rest in his ton, Mizpeh of Gilead.
And after him, Ibzan of Beth-lehem as judge of Israel.
He had thirty sons, and thirty daughters hom he sent to other places, and he got thirty ives from other places for his sons. And he as judge of Israel for seven years.
And Ibzan came to his death and his body as put to rest at Beth-lehem.
And after him, Elon the Zebulonite as judge of Israel; and he as judge of Israel for ten years.
And Elon the Zebulonite came to his death, and his body as put to rest in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
And after him, Abdon, the son of Hillel, the Pirathonite, as judge of Israel.
He had forty sons and thirty sons’ sons ho ent on seventy young asses; and he as judge of Israel for eight years.
And Abdon, the son of Hillel, came to his death, and his body as put to rest in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill-country of the Amalekites.
And the children of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the Lord; and the Lord gave them into the hands of the Philistines for forty years.
No there as a certain man of Zorah of the family of the Danites, and his name as Manoah; and his ife had never given birth to a child.
And the angel of the Lord came to the oman, and said to her, See no! though you have never given birth to children, you ill be ith child and give birth to a son.
No then take care to have no ine or strong drink and to take no unclean thing for food;

For you are ith child and ill give birth to a son; his hair is never to be cut, for the child is to be separate to God from his birth; and he ill take up the ork of freeing Israel from the hands of the Philistines.

Then the oman came in, and said to her husband, A man came to me, and his form as like the form of a god, causing great fear; I put no question to him about here he came from, and he did not give me his name;

But he said to me, You are ith child and ill give birth to a son; and no do not take any ine or strong drink or let anything unclean be your food; for the child ill be separate to God from his birth to the day of his death.
Then Manoah made prayer to the Lord, and said, O Lord, let the man of God hom you sent come to us again and make clear to us hat e are to do for the child ho is to come.
And God gave ear to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came to the oman again hen she as seated in the field; but her husband Manoah as not ith her.
So the oman, running quickly, gave her husband the nes, saying, I have seen the man ho came to me the other day.
And Manoah got up and ent after his ife, and came up to the man and said to him, Are you the man ho as talking to this oman? And he said, I am.
And Manoah said, No hen your ords come true, hat is to be the rule for the child and hat ill be his ork?
And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah, Let the oman take note of hat I have said to her.
She is to have nothing hich comes from the vine for her food, and let her take no ine or strong drink or anything hich is unclean; let her take care to do all I have given her orders to do.
And Manoah said to the angel of the Lord, No let us keep you hile e make ready a young goat for you.

And the angel of the Lord said to Manoah, Though you keep me I ill not take of your food; but if you ill make a burned offering, let it be offered to the Lord. For it had not come into Manoah’s mind that he as the angel of the Lord.
Then Manoah said to the angel of the Lord, What is your name, so that hen your ords come true e may give you honour?
But the angel of the Lord said to him, Why are you questioning me about my name, seeing that it is a onder?
So Manoah took the young goat ith its meal offering, offering it on the rock to the Lord, ho did strange things.
And hen the flame ent up to heaven from the altar, the angel of the Lord ent up in the flame of the altar, hile Manoah and his ife ere looking on; and they ent don on their faces to the earth.
But the angel of the Lord as seen no more by Manoah and his ife. Then it as clear to Manoah that he as the angel of the Lord.
And Manoah said to his ife, Death ill certainly be our fate, for it is a god hom e have seen.
But his ife said to him, If the Lord as purposing our death, he ould not have taken our burned offering and our meal offering, or have given us such orders about the child.
So the oman gave birth to a son, and gave him the name Samson; and he became a man and the blessing of the Lord as on him.
And the spirit of the Lord first came on him in Mahaneh-dan, beteen Zorah and Eshtaol.
No Samson ent don to Timnah, and sa a oman in Timnah, of the daughters of the Philistines;
And hen he came back he said to his father and mother, I have seen a oman in Timnah, of the daughters of the Philistines: get her no for me for my ife.

Then his father and mother said to him, Is there no oman among the daughters of your relations or among all my people, that you have to go for your ife to the Philistines, ho are ithout circumcision? But Samson said to his father, Get her for me, for she is pleasing to me.
No his father and mother had no knoledge that this as the purpose of the Lord, ho had the destruction of the Philistines in mind. No the Philistines at that time ere ruling over Israel.
Then Samson ent don to Timnah ( and his father and his mother,) and came to the vine-gardens of Timnah; and a young lion came rushing out at him.

And the spirit of the Lord came on him ith poer, and, unarmed as he as, pulling the lion in to as one might do to a young goat, he put him to death; ( but he said nothing to his father and mother of hat he had done.)
So he ent don and had talk ith the oman; and she as pleasing to Samson.
Then after a time he ent back to take her; and turning from the road to see the dead body of the lion, he sa a mass of bees in the body of the lion, and honey there.

And he took the honey in his hand, and ent on, tasting it on the ay; and hen he came to his father and mother he gave some to them; but did not say that he had taken the honey from the body of the lion.
Then Samson ent don to the oman, and made a feast there, as as the ay among young men.
And he took thirty friends, and they ere ith him.
And Samson said, No I have a hard question for you: if you are able to give me the anser before the seven days of the feast are over, I ill give you thirty linen robes and thirty changes of clothing;
But if you are not able to give me the anser, then you ill have to give me thirty linen robes and thirty changes of clothing. And they said to him, Put your hard question and let us see hat it is.
And he said, Out of the taker of food came food, and out of the strong came the seet. And at the end of three days they ere still not able to give the anser.

So on the fourth day they said to Samson’s ife, Get from your husband the anser to his question by some trick or other, or e ill have you and your father’s house burned ith fire; did you get us here to take all e have?

Then Samson’s ife, eeping over him, said, Truly you have no love for me but only hate; you have put a hard question to the children of my people and have not given me the anser. And he said to her, See, I have not given the anser even to my father or my mother; am I to give it to you?
And all the seven days of the feast she ent on eeping over him; and on the seventh day he gave her the anser, because she gave him no peace; and she sent ord of it to the children of her people.

Then on the seventh day, before he ent into the bride’s room, the men of the ton said to him, What is seeter than honey? and hat is stronger than a lion? And he said to them, If you had not been ploughing ith my co you ould not have got the anser to my question.

And the spirit of the Lord came rushing on him, and he ent don to Ashkelon and, attacking thirty men there, took their clothing from them, and gave it to the men ho had given the anser to his hard question. Then, full of rath, he ent back to his father’s house.
But Samson’s ife as given to the friend ho had been his best man.

No a short time after, at the time of the grain-cutting, Samson, taking ith him a young goat, ent to see his ife; and he said, I ill go in to my ife into the bride’s room. But her father ould not let him go in.
And her father said, It seemed to me that you had only hate for her; so I gave her to your friend: but is not her younger sister fairer than she? so please take her in place of the other.
Then Samson said to them, This time I ill give payment in full to the Philistines, for I am going to do them great evil.
So Samson ent and got three hundred foxes and some sticks of fire-ood; and he put the foxes tail to tail ith a stick beteen every to tails;
Then firing the sticks, he let the foxes loose among the uncut grain of the Philistines, and all the corded stems as ell as the living grain and the vine-gardens and the olives ent up in flames.

Then the Philistines said, Who has done this? And they said, Samson, the son-in-la of the Timnite, because he took his ife and gave her to his friend. So the Philistines came up and had her and her father’s house burned.
And Samson said to them, If you go on like this, truly I ill take my full payment from you; and that ill be the end of it.
And he made an attack on them, driving them in uncontrolled flight, and causing great destruction; then he ent aay to his safe place in the crack of the rock at Etam.
Then the Philistines ent and put up their tents in Judah, all round Lehi.
And the men of Judah said, Why have you come up against us? And they said, We have come up to take Samson, and to do to him as he has done to us.

Then three thousand of the men of Judah ent don to the crack of the rock of Etam, and said to Samson, Is it not clear to you that the Philistines are our rulers? What is this you have done to us? And he said to them, I only did to them as they did to me.
Then they said to him, We have come don to take you and give you up into the hands of the Philistines. And Samson said to them, Give me your oath that you ill not make an attack on me yourselves.
And they said, No; e ill take you and give you up into their hands, but truly e ill not put you to death. So knotting to ne cords round him they took him up from the rock.

And hen he came to Lehi, the Philistines came out, meeting him ith loud cries; then the spirit of the Lord came rushing on him, and the cords on his arms became like grass hich has been burned ith fire, and the bands came falling off his hands.
And taking up the mouth-bone of an ass nely dead, hich he sa by chance on the earth, he put to death a thousand men ith it.
And Samson said, With a red ass’s mouth-bone I have made them red ith blood, ith a red ass’s mouth-bone I have sent destruction on a thousand men.
And having said these ords, he let the mouth-bone go out of his hand; so that place as named Ramath-lehi.

After this, he as in great need of ater, and crying out to the Lord, he said, You have given this great salvation by the hand of your servant, and no need of ater ill be my death; and I ill be given into the hands of this people ho are ithout circumcision.

Then God made a crack in the hollo rock in Lehi and ater came out of it; and after drinking, his spirit came back to him and he as strong again; so that place as named En-hakkore; it is in Lehi to this day.
And he as judge of Israel in the days of the Philistines for tenty years.
No Samson ent to Gaza, and there he sa a loose oman and ent in to her.
And it as said to the Gazites, Samson is here. So they ent round, atching for him all day at the dooray of the ton, but at night they kept quiet, saying, When daylight comes e ill put him to death.

And Samson as there till the middle of the night; then he got up, and took a grip on the doors of the ton, pulling them up, together ith their to supports and their locks, and put them on his back and took them up to the top of the hill in front of Hebron.
No after this, he as in love ith a oman in the valley of Sorek, named Delilah.

And the chiefs of the Philistines came up to her, and said to her, Make use of your poer over him and see hat is the secret of his great strength, and ho e may get the better of him, and put bands on him, so that e may make him feeble; and every one of us ill give you eleven hundred shekels of silver.
So Delilah said to Samson, Make clear to me no hat is the secret of your great strength, and ho you may be put in bands and made feeble.
And Samson said to her, If seven ne bo-cords hich have never been made dry are knotted round me, I ill become feeble and ill be like any other man.
So the chiefs of the Philistines gave her seven ne bo-cords hich had never been made dry, and she had them tightly knotted round him.

No she had men aiting secretly in the inner room; and she said to him, The Philistines are on you, Samson. And the cords ere broken by him as a tist of thread is broken hen touched by a flame. So the secret of his strength did not come to light.
Then Delilah said to Samson, See, you have been making sport of me ith false ords; no, say truly ho may you be put in bands?
And he said to her, If they only put round me ne thick cords hich have never been used, then I ill become feeble and ill be like any other man.

So Delilah took ne thick cords, knotting them tightly round him, and said to him, The Philistines are on you, Samson. And men ere aiting secretly in the inner room. And the cords ere broken off his arms like threads.

Then Delilah said to Samson, Up to no you have made sport of me ith false ords; no say truly, ho may you be put in bands? And he said to her, If you get the seven tists of my hair orked into the cloth you are making and fixed ith the pin, I ill become feeble and ill be like any other man.

So hile he as sleeping she got the seven tists of his hair orked into her cloth and fixed ith the pin, and said to him, The Philistines are on you, Samson. Then aaking from his sleep, he got up quickly, pulling up cloth and machine together.
And she said to him, Why do you say you are my lover hen your heart is not mine? Three times you have made sport of me, and have not made clear to me the secret of your great strength.
So day after day she gave him no peace, for ever questioning him till his soul as troubled to death.

And opening all his heart to her, he said to her, My head has never been touched by a blade, for I have been separate to God from the day of my birth: if my hair is cut off, then my strength ill go from me and I ill become feeble, and ill be like any other man.

And hen Delilah sa that he had let her see into his heart, she sent ord to the chiefs of the Philistines saying, Come up this time, for he has let out all his heart to me. Then the chiefs of the Philistines came to her, ith the money in their hands.
And she made him go to sleep on her knees; and she sent for a man and had his seven tists of hair cut off; and hile it as being done he became feeble and his strength ent from him.
Then she said, The Philistines are on you, Samson. And aaking from his sleep, he said, I ill go out as at other times, shaking myself free. But he as not conscious that the Lord had gone from him.
So the Philistines took him and put out his eyes; then they took him don to Gaza, and, chaining him ith bands of brass, put him to ork crushing grain in the prison-house.
But the groth of his hair as starting again after it had been cut off.
And the chiefs of the Philistines came together to make a great offering to Dagon their god, and to be glad; for they said, Our god has given into our hands Samson our hater.

And hen the people sa him, they gave praise to their god; for they said, Our god has given into our hands the one ho as fighting against us, ho made our country aste, and ho put great numbers of us to death.

No hen their hearts ere full of joy, they said, Send for Samson to make sport for us. And they sent for Samson out of the prison-house, and he made sport before them; and they put him beteen the pillars.
And Samson said to the boy ho took him by the hand, Let me put my hand on the pillars supporting the house, so that I may put my back against them.
No the house as full of men and omen; and all the lords of the Philistines ere there; and about three thousand men and omen ere on the roof, looking on hile Samson made sport.
And Samson, crying out to the Lord, said, O Lord God, do have me no in mind, and do make me strong only this once, O God, so that I may take one last payment from the Philistines for my to eyes.
Then Samson put his arms round the to middle pillars supporting the house, putting his eight on them, on one ith his right hand and on the other ith his left.

And Samson said, Let death overtake me ith the Philistines. And he put out all his strength, and the house came don on the chiefs and on all the people ho ere in it. So the dead hom he sent to destruction by his death ere more than all those on hom he had sent destruction in his life.

Then his brothers and his father’s people came don and took him up and put his body to rest in the earth beteen Zorah and Eshtaol in the resting-place of Manoah his father. And he had been judge of Israel for tenty years.
No there as a man of the hill-country of Ephraim named Micah.

And he said to his mother, The eleven hundred shekels of silver hich ere taken from you, about hich you took an oath and said in my hearing, I have given this silver to the Lord from my hand for myself, to make a pictured image and a metal image: see, I have the silver, for I took it: so no I ill give it back to you. And his mother said, May the blessing of the Lord be on my son.
And he gave back the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, and his mother said, I have made the silver holy to the Lord from me for my son, to make a pictured image and a metal image.

So he gave the silver back to his mother. Then his mother took to hundred shekels of silver and gave them to a metal-orker ho made a pictured image and a metal image from them: and it as in the house of Micah.
And the man Micah had a house of gods; and he made an ephod and family gods and put one of his sons in the position of priest.
In those days there as no king in Israel: every man did as seemed right to him.
No there as a young man living in Beth-lehem-judah, of the family of Judah and a Levite, ho as not a tonsman of the place.
And he ent aay from the ton of Beth-lehem-judah, looking for somehere to make his living-place; and on his journey he came to the hill-country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah.
And Micah said to him, Where do you come from? And he said to him, I am a Levite from Beth-lehem-judah, and I am looking for a living-place.
Then Micah said to him, Make your living-place ith me, and be a father and a priest to me, and I ill give you ten shekels of silver a year and your clothing and food.
And the Levite said he ould make his living-place ith the man, and he became to him as one of his sons.
And Micah gave the position to the Levite, and the young man became his priest, and as in the house of Micah.
Then Micah said, No I am certain that the Lord ill do me good, seeing that the Levite has become my priest.

In those days there as no king in Israel, and in those days the Danites ere looking for a heritage for themselves, to be their living-place; for up to that time no distribution of land had been made to them among the tribes of Israel.

So the children of Dan sent five men from among their number, strong men, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to take a look at the land and make a search through it; and they said to them, Go and make a search through the land; and they came to the hill-country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, here they made a stop for the night.

When they ere near the house of Micah, hearing a voice hich as not strange to them, that of the young Levite, they ent out of their road to his place, and said to him, Ho did you come here? and hat are you doing in this place? and hy are you here?
And he said to them, This is hat Micah did for me, and he gave me payment and I became his priest.
Then they said, Do get directions from God for us, to see if the journey on hich e are going ill have a good outcome.
And the priest said to them, Go in peace: your ay is guided by the Lord.

Then the five men ent on their ay and came to Laish and sa the people ho ere there, living ithout thought of danger, like the Zidonians, quiet and safe; for they had everything on earth for their needs, and they ere far from the Zidonians and had no business ith Aram.
So they came back to their brothers in Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them, What nes have you?
And they said, Up! and let us go against Laish; for e have seen the land, and it is very good: hy are you doing nothing? Do not be slo to go in and take the land for your heritage.
When you come there you ill come to a people living ithout thought of danger; and the land is ide, and God has given it into your hands: a place here there is everything on earth for man’s needs.
So six hundred men of the Danites from Zorah and Eshtaol ent out armed ith instruments of ar.
And they ent up and put up their tents in Kiriath-jearim in Judah: so that place is named Mahaneh-dan to this day. It is to the est of Kiriath-jearim.
From there they ent on to the hill-country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.

Then the five men ho had gone to make a search through the country of Laish, said to their brothers, Have you knoledge that in these houses there is an ephod and family gods and a pictured image and a metal image? So no you see hat to do.
And turning from their road they came to the house of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and said to him, Is it ell ith you?
And the six hundred armed men of the Danites took their places by the dooray.

Then the five men ho had gone to make a search through the land, ent in and took the pictured image and the ephod and the family gods and the metal image; and the priest as by the dooray ith the six hundred armed men.
And hen they ent into Micah’s house and took out the pictured image and the ephod and the family gods and the metal image, the priest said to them, What are you doing?
And they said to him, Be quiet; say nothing, and come ith us and be our father and priest; is it better for you to be priest to one man’s house or to be priest to a tribe and a family in Israel?
Then the priest’s heart as glad, and he took the ephod and the family gods and the pictured image and ent ith the people.
So they ent on their ay again, putting the little ones and the oxen and the goods in front of them.
When they had gone some ay from the house of Micah, the men from the houses near Micah’s house came together and overtook the children of Dan,
Crying out to them. And the Danites, turning round, said to Micah, What is your trouble, that you have taken up arms?
And he said, You have taken my gods hich I made, and my priest, and have gone aay; hat is there for me no? Why then do you say to me, What is your trouble?
And the children of Dan said to him, Say no more, or men of bitter spirit may make an attack on you, causing loss of your life and the lives of your people.
Then the children of Dan ent on their ay; and hen Micah sa that they ere stronger than he, he ent back to his house.
And they took that hich Micah had made, and his priest, and came to Laish, to a people living quietly and ithout thought of danger, and they put them to the sord ithout mercy, burning don their ton.

And they had no saviour, because it as far from Zidon, and they had no business ith Aram; and it as in the valley hich is the property of Beth-rehob. And building up the ton again they took it for their living-place.
And they gave the ton the name of Dan, after Dan their father, ho as the son of Israel: though the ton had been named Laish at first.

( And the children of Dan put up the pictured image for themselves; and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons ere priests for the tribe of the Danites till the day hen the ark as taken prisoner.)
And they put up for themselves the image hich Micah had made, and it as there all the time that the house of God as in Shiloh.
No in those days, hen there as no king in Israel, a certain Levite as living in the inmost parts of the hill-country of Ephraim, and he got for himself a servant-ife from Beth-lehem-judah.
And his servant-ife as angry ith him, and ent aay from him to her father’s house at Beth-lehem-judah, and as there for four months.

Then her husband got up and ent after her, ith the purpose of talking kindly to her, and taking her back ith him; he had ith him his young man and to asses: and she took him into her father’s house, and her father, hen he sa him, came forard to him ith joy.
And his father-in-la, the girl’s father, kept him there for three days; and they had food and drink and took their rest there.
No on the fourth day they got up early in the morning and he made ready to go aay; but the girl’s father said to his son-in-la, Take a little food to keep up your strength, and then go on your ay.
So seating themselves they had food and drink, the to of them together; and the girl’s father said to the man, If it is your pleasure, take your rest here tonight, and let your heart be glad.
And the man got up to go aay, but his father-in-la ould not let him go, so he took his rest there again for the night.

Then early on the morning of the fifth day he got up to go aay; but the girl’s father said, Keep up your strength; so the to of them had a meal, and the man and his oman and his servant did not go till after the middle of the day.

And hen they got up to go aay, his father-in-la, the girl’s father, said to him, No evening is coming on, so do not go tonight; see, the day is almost gone; take your rest here and let your heart be glad, and tomorro early, go on your ay back to your house.
But the man ould not be kept there that night, and he got up and ent aay and came opposite to Jebus ( hich is Jerusalem); and he had ith him the to asses, ready for travelling, and his oman.
When they got near Jebus the day as far gone; and the servant said to his master, No let us go from our road into this ton of the Jebusites and take our night’s rest there.
But his master said to him, We ill not go out of our ay into a strange ton, hose people are not of the children of Israel; but e ill go on to Gibeah.
And he said to his servant, Come, let us go on to one of these places, stopping for the night in Gibeah or Ramah.
So they ent on their ay; and the sun ent don hen they ere near Gibeah in the land of Benjamin.
And they ent off the road there ith the purpose of stopping for the night in Gibeah: and he ent in, seating himself in the street of the ton, for no one took them into his house for the night.
No hen it as evening they sa an old man coming back from his ork in the fields; he as from the hill-country of Ephraim and as living in Gibeah: but the men of the place ere Benjamites.
And hen he sa the traveller in the street of the ton, the old man said, Where are you going? and here do you come from?

And he said to him, We are on our ay from Beth-lehem-judah to the inmost parts of the hill-country of Ephraim: I came from there and ent to Beth-lehem-judah: no I am on my ay back to my house, but no man ill take me into his house.
But e have dry grass and food for our asses, as ell as bread and ine for me, and for the oman, and for the young man ith us: e have no need of anything.
And the old man said, Peace be ith you; let all your needs be my care; only do not take your rest in the street.
So he took them into his house and gave the asses food; and after ashing their feet they took food and drink.

While they ere taking their pleasure at the meal, the good-for-nothing men of the ton came round the house, giving blos on the door; and they said to the old man, the master of the house, Send out that man ho came to your house, so that e may take our pleasure ith him.
So the man, the master of the house, ent out to them, and said, No, my brothers, do not this evil thing; this man has come into my house, and you are not to do him this rong.
See, here is my daughter, a virgin, and his servant-ife: I ill send them out for you to take them and do ith them hatever you ill. But do no such thing of shame to this man.

But the men ould not give ear to him: so the man took his oman and sent her out to them; and they took her by force, using her for their pleasure all night till the morning; and hen dan came they let her go.
Then at the dan of day the oman came, and, falling don at the door of the man’s house here her master as, as stretched there till it as light.
In the morning her master got up, and opening the door of the house ent out to go on his ay; and he sa his servant-ife stretched on the earth at the door of the house ith her hands on the step.
And he said to her, Get up and let us be going; but there as no anser; so he took her up and put her on the ass, and ent on his ay and came to his house.
And hen he had come to his house, he got his knife, and took the oman, cutting her up bone by bone into telve parts, hich he sent through all Israel.

And he gave orders to the men hom he sent, saying, This is hat you are to say to all the men of Israel, Has ever an act like this been done from the day hen the children of Israel came out of Egypt to this day? Give thought to it, turning it over in your minds, and give your opinion of it.
Then all the children of Israel took up arms, and the people came together like one man, from Dan to Beer-sheba, and the land of Gilead, before the Lord at Mizpah.
And the chiefs of the people, out of all the tribes of Israel, took their places in the meeting of the people of God, four hundred thousand footmen armed ith sords.
( No the children of Benjamin had ord that the children of Israel had gone up to Mizpah.) And the children of Israel said, Make clear ho this evil thing took place.
Then the Levite, the husband of the dead oman, said in anser, I came to Gibeah in the land of Benjamin, I and my servant-ife, for the purpose of stopping there for the night.
And the tonsmen of Gibeah came together against me, going round the house on all sides by night; it as their purpose to put me to death, and my servant-ife as violently used by them and is dead.
So I took her, cutting her into parts hich I sent through all the country of the heritage of Israel: for they have done an act of shame in Israel.
Here you all are, you children of Israel; give no your suggestions about hat is to be done.
Then all the people got up as one man and said, Not one of us ill go to his tent or go back to his house:
But this is hat e ill do to Gibeah: e ill go up against it by the decision of the Lord;

And e ill take ten men out of every hundred, through all the tribes of Israel, a hundred out of every thousand, a thousand out of every ten thousand, to get food for the people, so that they may give to Gibeah of Benjamin the right punishment for the act of shame they have done in Israel.
So all the men of Israel ere banded together against the ton, united like one man.
And the tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin saying, What is this evil hich has been done among you?

No give up those good-for-nothing persons in Gibeah so that e may put them to death, clearing aay the evil from Israel. But the children of Benjamin ould not give ear to the voice of their brothers, the children of Israel.
And the children of Benjamin came together from all their tons to Gibeah, to go to ar ith the children of Israel.
And the children of Benjamin ho came that day from the tons ere tenty-six thousand men armed ith sords, in addition to the people of Gibeah, numbering seven hundred of the best fighting-men,
Who ere left-handed, able to send a stone at a hair ithout error.
And the men of Israel, other than Benjamin, ere four hundred thousand in number, all armed ith sords; they ere all men of ar.

And they got up and ent up to Beth-el to get directions from God, and the children of Israel said, Who is to be the first to go up to the fight against the children of Benjamin? And the Lord said, Judah is to go up first.
So the children of Israel got up in the morning and put themselves in position against Gibeah.
And the men of Israel ent out to ar against Benjamin ( and the men of Israel put their forces in fighting order against them at Gibeah).
Then the children of Benjamin came out from Gibeah, cutting don tenty-to thousand of the Israelites that day.
But the people, the men of Israel, taking heart again, put their forces in order and took up the same position as on the first day.

No the children of Israel ent up, eeping before the Lord till evening, requesting the Lord and saying, Am I to go forard again to the fight against the children of Benjamin my brother? And the Lord said, Go up against him.
So the children of Israel ent forard against the children of Benjamin the second day.
And the second day Benjamin ent out against them from Gibeah, cutting don eighteen thousand men of the children of Israel, all sordsmen.

Then all the children of Israel, and all the people, ent up to Beth-el, eeping and aiting there before the Lord, going ithout food all day till evening, and offering burned offerings and peace-offerings before the Lord.
And the children of Israel made request to the Lord, ( for the ark of the agreement of the Lord as there in those days,

And Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, as in his place before it,) and said, Am I still to go on ith the fight against the children of Benjamin my brother, or am I to give it up? And the Lord said, Go on; for tomorro I ill give him into your hands.
So Israel put men secretly all round Gibeah to make a surprise attack on it.
And the children of Israel ent up against the children of Benjamin on the third day, and put themselves in fighting order against Gibeah as before.

And the children of Benjamin ent out against the people, moving aay from the ton; and as before, at their first attack, they put to death about thirty men of Israel on the highays, of hich one goes up to Beth-el and the other to Gibeah, and in the open country.
And the children of Benjamin said, They are giving ay before us as at first. But the children of Israel said, Let us go in flight and get them aay from the ton, into the highays.
So all the men of Israel got up and put themselves in fighting order at Baal-tamar: and those ho had been aiting secretly to make a surprise attack came rushing out of their place on the est of Geba.
And they came in front of Gibeah, ten thousand of the best men in all Israel, and the fighting became more violent; but the children of Benjamin ere not conscious that evil as coming on them.
Then the Lord sent sudden fear on Benjamin before Israel; and that day the children of Israel put to death tenty-five thousand, one hundred men of Benjamin, all of them sordsmen.
So the children of Benjamin sa that they ere overcome: and the men of Israel had given ay before Benjamin, putting their faith in the atchers ho ere to make the surprise attack on Gibeah.
And the atchers, rushing on Gibeah and overrunning it, put all the ton to the sord ithout mercy.
No the sign fixed beteen the men of Israel and those making the surprise attack as that hen they made a pillar of smoke go up from the ton,

The men of Israel ere to make a turn about in the fight. And Benjamin had overcome and put to death about thirty of the men of Israel, and ere saying, Certainly they are falling back before us as in the first fight.
Then the sign ent up out of the ton in the pillar of smoke, and the Benjamites, turning back, sa all the ton going up in smoke to heaven.
And the men of Israel had made a turn about, and the men of Benjamin ere overcome ith fear, for they sa that evil had overtaken them.

So turning their backs on the men of Israel, they ent in the direction of the aste land; but the fight overtook them; and those ho came out of the ton ere heading them off and putting them to the sord.
And crushing Benjamin don, they ent after them, driving them from Nohah as far as the east side of Gibeah.
Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin came to their death, all strong men of ar.

And turning, they ent in flight to the rock of Rimmon in the aste land: and on the highays five thousand of them ere cut off by the men of Israel, ho, pushing on hard after them to Geba, put to death to thousand more.
So tenty-five thousand of the sordsmen of Benjamin came to their end that day, all strong men of ar.
But six hundred men, turning back, ent in flight to the rock of Rimmon in the aste land, and ere living on the rock of Rimmon for four months.
And the men of Israel, turning again against the children of Benjamin, put to the sord ithout mercy all the tons and the cattle and everything there as, burning every ton hich came into their hands.
No the men of Israel had taken an oath in Mizpah, saying, Not one of us ill give his daughter as a ife to Benjamin.
And the people came to Beth-el, aiting there till evening before God, and gave themselves up to bitter eeping.
And they said, O Lord, the God of Israel, hy has this fate come on Israel, that today one tribe has been cut off from Israel?
Then on the day after, the people got up early and made an altar there, offering burned offerings and peace-offerings.

And the children of Israel said, Who is there among all the tribes of Israel, ho did not come up to the Lord at the meeting of all Israel? For they had taken a great oath that hoever did not come up to Mizpah to the Lord as to be put to death.
And the children of Israel ere moved ith pity for Benjamin their brother, saying, Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.
What are e to do about ives for those ho are still living? For e have taken an oath by the Lord that e ill not give them our daughters for ives.
And they said, Which one of the tribes of Israel did not come up to Mizpah to the Lord? And it as seen that no one had come from Jabesh-gilead to the meeting.
For hen the people ere numbered, not one man of the people of Jabesh-gilead as present.

So they ( the meeting) sent telve thousand of the best fighting-men, and gave them orders, saying, Go and put the people of Jabesh-gilead to the sord ithout mercy, ith their omen and their little ones.
And this is hat you are to do: every male, and every oman ho has had sex relations ith a man, you are to put to the curse, but you are to keep safe the virgins. And they did so.
No there ere among the people of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young virgins ho had never had sex relations ith a man; these they took to their tents in Shiloh in the land of Canaan.
And all the meeting sent to the men of Benjamin ho ere in the rock of Rimmon, offering them peace.
Then Benjamin came back; and they gave them the omen hom they had kept from death among the omen of Jabesh-gilead: but still there ere not enough for them.
And the people ere moved ith pity for Benjamin, because the Lord had let his rath loose on the tribes of Israel.
Then the responsible men of the meeting said, What are e to do about ives for the rest of them, seeing that the omen of Benjamin are dead?
And they said, Ho is the rest of Benjamin to be given offspring so that one tribe of Israel may not be put out of existence,
Seeing that e may not give them our daughters as ives? For the children of Israel had taken an oath, saying, Cursed is he ho gives a ife to Benjamin.

And they said, See, every year there is a feast of the Lord in Shiloh, hich is to the north of Beth-el, on the east side of the highay hich goes up from Beth-el to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah.
And they said to the men of Benjamin, Go into the vine-gardens, aiting there secretly,

And atching; and if the daughters of Shiloh come out to take part in the dances, then come from the vine-gardens and take a ife for every one of you from among the daughters of Shiloh, and go back to the land of Benjamin.

And hen their fathers or their brothers come and make trouble, you are to say to them, Give them to us as an act of grace; for e did not take them as ives for ourselves in ar; and if you yourselves had given them to us you ould have been responsible for the broken oath.

So the men of Benjamin did this, and got ives for themselves for every one of their number, taking them aay by force from the dance; then they ent back to their heritage, building up their tons and living in them.
Then the children of Israel ent aay from there, every man to his tribe and his family, every man ent back to his heritage.
In those days there as no king in Israel: every man did hat seemed right to him.

No there came a time, in the days of the judges, hen there as no food in the land. And a certain man ent from Beth-lehem-judah, he and his ife and his to sons, to make a living-place in the country of Moab.

And the name of the man as Elimelech, and the name of his ife Naomi, and the name of his to sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Beth-lehem-judah. And they came into the country of Moab, and ere there for some time.
And Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, came to his end; and only her to sons ere ith her.
And they took to omen of Moab as their ives: the name of the one as Orpah, and the name of the other Ruth; and they ent on living there for about ten years.
And Mahlon and Chilion came to their end; and the oman as ithout her to sons and her husband.
So she and her daughters-in-la got ready to go back from the country of Moab, for nes had come to her in the country of Moab that the Lord, in mercy for his people, had given them food.
And she ent out of the place here she as, and her to daughters-in-la ith her; and they ent on their ay to go back to the land of Judah.
And Naomi said to her to daughters-in-la, Go back to your mothers’ houses: may the Lord be good to you as you have been good to the dead and to me:
May the Lord give you rest in the houses of your husbands. Then she gave them a kiss; and they ere eeping bitterly.
And they said to her, No, but e ill go back ith you to your people.
But Naomi said, Go back, my daughters; hy ill you come ith me? Have I more sons in my body, to become your husbands?
Go back, my daughters, and go on your ay; I am so old no that I may not have another husband. If I said, I have hopes, if I had a husband tonight, and might have sons,
Would you keep yourselves till they ere old enough? ould you keep from having husbands for them? No, my daughters; but I am very sad for you that the hand of the Lord is against me.
Then again they ere eeping; and Orpah gave her mother-in-la a kiss, but Ruth ould not be parted from her.
And Naomi said, See, your sister-in-la has gone back to her people and to her gods: go back after your sister-in-la.

But Ruth said, Give up requesting me to go aay from you, or to go back ithout you: for here you go I ill go; and here you take your rest I ill take my rest; your people ill be my people, and your God my God.
Wherever death comes to you, death ill come to me, and there ill be my last resting-place; the Lord do so to me and more if e are parted by anything but death.
And hen she sa that Ruth as strong in her purpose to go ith her she said no more.
So the to of them ent on till they came to Beth-lehem. And hen they came to Beth-lehem all the ton as moved about them, and they said, Is this Naomi?
And she said to them, Do not let my name be Naomi, but Mara, for the Ruler of all has given me a bitter fate.
I ent out full, and the Lord has sent me back again ith nothing; hy do you give me the name Naomi, seeing that the Lord has given itness against me, and the Ruler of all has sent sorro on me?
So Naomi came back out of the country of Moab, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-la, ith her; and they came to Beth-lehem in the first days of the grain-cutting.
And Naomi had a relation of her husband, a man of ealth, of the family of Elimelech; and his name as Boaz.
And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, No let me go into the field and take up the heads of grain after him in hose eyes I may have grace. And she said to her, Go, my daughter.
And she ent, and came and took up the heads of grain in the field after the cutters; and by chance she ent into that part of the field hich as the property of Boaz, ho as of the family of Elimelech.
And Boaz came from Beth-lehem, and said to the grain-cutters, The Lord be ith you. And they made anser, The Lord give you his blessing.
Then Boaz said to his servant ho as in authority over the cutters, Whose girl is this?
And the servant ho as in authority over the cutters said, It is a Moabite girl ho came back ith Naomi out of the country of Moab;
And she said to me, Let me come into the grain-field and take up the grain after the cutters. So she came, and has been here from morning till no, ithout resting even for a minute.
Then said Boaz to Ruth, Give ear to me, my daughter: do not go to take up the grain in another field, or go aay from here, but keep here by my young omen:

Keep your eyes on the field they are cutting, and go after them; have I not given orders to the young men not to put a hand on you? And hen you are in need of drink go to the vessels and take of hat the young men have put there.
Then she ent don on her face to the earth, and said to him, Why have I grace in your eyes, that you give attention to me, seeing I am from a strange people?

And Boaz ansering said to her, I have had nes of everything you have done for your mother-in-la after the death of your husband; ho you ent aay from your father and mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people ho are strange to you.
The Lord give you a reard for hat you have done, and may a full reard be given to you by the Lord, the God of Israel, under hose ings you have come to take cover.
Then she said, May I have grace in your eyes, my lord, for you have given me comfort, and you have said kind ords to your servant, though I am not like one of your servants.

And at meal-time Boaz said to her, Come here, and take some of the bread, and put your bit into the ine. And she took her seat among the grain-cutters: and he gave her dry grain, and she took it, and there as more than enough for her meal.
And hen she got ready to take up the grain, Boaz gave his young men orders, saying, Let her take it even from among the cut grain, and say nothing to her.
And let some heads of grain be pulled out of hat has been corded up, and dropped for her to take, and let no sharp ord be said to her.
So she ent on getting together the heads of grain till evening; and after crushing out the seed it came to about an ephah of grain.

And Naomi said to her daughter-in-la, May the blessing of the Lord, ho has at all times been kind to the living and to the dead, be on him. And Naomi said to her, The man is of our family, one of our near relations.
And Ruth the Moabitess said, Truly, he said to me, Keep near my young men till all my grain is cut.
And Naomi said to Ruth, her daughter-in-la, It is better, my daughter, for you to go out ith his servant-girls, so that no danger may come to you in another field.

And Naomi, her mother-in-la, said to her, My daughter, am I not to get you a resting-place here you may be in comfort?

So take a bath, and, after rubbing your body ith seet oil, put on your best robe, and go don to the grain-floor; but do not let him see you till he has come to the end of his meal.
But see to it, hen he goes to rest, that you take note of the place here he is sleeping, and go in there, and, uncovering his feet, take your place by him; and he ill say hat you are to do.
And she said, I ill do all you say.
So she ent don to the grain-floor and did all her mother-in-la had said to her.
No hen Boaz had taken meat and drink, and his heart as glad, he ent to take his rest at the end of the mass of grain; then she came softly and, uncovering his feet, ent to rest.
No in the middle of the night, the man aaking from his sleep in fear, and lifting himself up, sa a oman stretched at his feet.

And she took her rest at his feet till the morning: and she got up before it as light enough for one to see another. And he said, Let it not come to anyone’s knoledge that the oman came to the grain-floor.

And hen she came back her mother-in-la said to her, Ho did it go ith you, my daughter? And she gave her an account of all the man had done to her.
And she said, He gave me these six measures of grain, saying, Do not go back to your mother-in-la ith nothing in your hands.
Then she said, Do nothing no, my daughter, till you see hat ill come of this; for the man ill take no rest till he has put this thing through.

And Boaz ent up to the public place of the ton, and took his seat there: and the near relation of hom he had been talking came by; and Boaz, crying out to him by name, said, Come and be seated here. And he came and as seated.
Then he got ten of the responsible men of the ton, and said, Be seated here. And they took their seats.
Then he said to the near relation, Naomi, ho has come back from the country of Moab, is offering for a price that bit of land hich as our brother Elimelech’s:

And it as in my mind to give you the chance of taking it, ith the approval of those seated here and of the responsible men of my people. If you are ready to do hat it is right for a relation to do, then do it: but if you ill not do it, say so to me no; for there is no one ho has the right to do it but you, and after you myself. And he said, I ill do it.
Then Boaz said, On the day hen you take this field, you ill have to take ith it Ruth, the Moabitess, the ife of the dead, so that you may keep the name of the dead living in his heritage.
And the near relation said, I am not able to do the relation’s part, for fear of damaging the heritage I have: you may do it in my place, for I am not able to do it myself.

No, in earlier times this as the ay in Israel hen property as taken over by a near relation, or hen there as a change of oner. To make the exchange certain one man took off his shoe and gave it to the other; and this as a itness in Israel.

Then Boaz said to the responsible men and to all the people, You are itnesses today that I have taken at a price from Naomi all the property hich as Elimelech’s, and everything hich as Chilion’s and Mahlon’s.

And all the people ho ere in the public place, and the responsible men, said, We are itnesses. May the Lord make this oman, ho is about to come into your house, like Rachel and Leah, hich to ere the builders of the house of Israel: and may you have ealth in Ephrathah, and be great in Beth-lehem;
May your family be like the family of Perez, the son hom Tamar gave to Judah, from the offspring hich the Lord may give you by this young oman.
So Boaz took Ruth and she became his ife; and he ent in to her, and the Lord made her ith child and she gave birth to a son.
And the omen said to Naomi, A blessing on the Lord, ho has not let you be this day ithout a near relation, and may his name be great in Israel.

And Naomi took the child and put her arms round it, and she took care of it.
And the omen ho ere her neighbours gave it a name, saying, Naomi has a child; and they gave him the name of Obed: he is the father of Jesse, the father of David.
No these are the generations of Perez: Perez became the father of Hezron;

And Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon became the father of Salmon;
And Salmon became the father of Boaz, and Boaz became the father of Obed;
And Obed became the father of Jesse, and Jesse became the father of David.
No there as a certain man of Ramathaim, a Zuphite of the hill-country of Ephraim, named Elkanah; he as the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite:
And he had to ives, one named Hannah and the other Peninnah: and Peninnah as the mother of children, but Hannah had no children.

And hen the day came for Elkanah to make his offering, he gave to Peninnah his ife, and to all her sons and daughters, their part of the feast:
But to Hannah he gave one part, though Hannah as very dear to him, but the Lord had not let her have children.
And the other ife did everything possible to make her unhappy, because the Lord had not let her have children;
And year by year, henever she ent up to the house of the Lord, she kept on attacking her, so that Hannah gave herself up to eeping and ould take no food.
Then her husband Elkanah said to her, Hannah, hy are you eeping? and hy are you taking no food? hy is your heart troubled? am I not more to you than ten sons?
So after they had taken food and ine in the guest room, Hannah got up. No Eli the priest as seated by the pillars of the dooray of the Temple of the Lord.
And ith grief in her soul, eeping bitterly, she made her prayer to the Lord.

And she made an oath, and said, O Lord of armies, if you ill truly take note of the sorro of your servant, not turning aay from me but keeping me in mind, and ill give me a man-child, then I ill give him to the Lord all the days of his life, and his hair ill never be cut.
No hile she as a long time in prayer before the Lord, Eli as atching her mouth.

And Eli said to her, Ho long are you going to be the orse for drink? Put aay the effects of your ine from you.
And Hannah, ansering him, said, No, my lord, I am a oman hose spirit is broken ith sorro: I have not taken ine or strong drink, but I have been opening my heart before the Lord.
Do not take your servant to be a good-for-nothing oman: for my ords have come from my stored-up sorro and pain.
Then Eli said to her, Go in peace: and may the God of Israel give you an anser to the prayer you have made to him.
And she said, May your servant have grace in your eyes. So the oman ent aay, and took part in the feast, and her face as no longer sad.
And early in the morning they got up, and after orshipping before the Lord they ent back to Ramah, to their house: and Elkanah had connection ith his ife; and the Lord kept her in mind.

And the man Elkanah ith all his family ent up to make the year’s offering to the Lord, and to give effect to his oath.
But Hannah did not go, for she said to her husband, I ill not go till the child has been taken from the breast, and then I ill take him ith me and put him before the Lord, here he may be for ever.

And her husband Elkanah said to her, Do hatever seems right to you, but not till you have taken him from the breast; only may the Lord do as he has said. So the oman, aiting there, gave her son milk till he as old enough to be taken from the breast.
Then hen she had done so, she took him ith her, ith a three-year old ox and an ephah of meal and a skin full of ine, and took him to the house of the Lord at Shiloh: no the child as still very young.
And hen they had made an offering of the ox, they took the child to Eli.
And she said, O my lord, as your soul is living, my lord, I am that oman ho as making a prayer to the Lord here by your side:
My prayer as for this child; and the Lord has given him to me in anser to my request:
So I have given him to the Lord; for all his life he is the Lord’s. Then he gave the Lord orship there.
And Hannah, in prayer before the Lord, said, My heart is glad in the Lord, my horn is lifted up in the Lord: my mouth is open ide over my haters; because my joy is in your salvation.
No other is holy as the Lord, for there is no other God but you: there is no Rock like our God.
Say no more ords of pride; let not uncontrolled sayings come out of your mouths: for the Lord is a God of knoledge, by him acts are judged.
The bos of the men of ar are broken, and the feeble are clothed ith strength.

Those ho ere full are offering themselves as servants for bread; those ho ere in need are at rest; truly, she ho had no children has become the mother of seven; and she ho had a family is asted ith sorro.
The Lord is the giver of death and life: sending men don to the underorld and lifting them up.
The Lord gives ealth and takes a man’s goods from him: crushing men don and again lifting them up;

Lifting the poor out of the dust, and him ho is in need out of the loest place, to give them their place among rulers, and for their heritage the seat of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s and he has made them the base of the orld.
He ill keep the feet of his holy ones, but the evil-doers ill come to their end in the dark night, for by strength no man ill overcome.

Those ho make ar against the Lord ill be broken; against them he ill send his thunder from heaven: the Lord ill be judge of the ends of the earth, he ill give strength to his king, lifting up the horn of him on hom the holy oil has been put.
Then Elkanah ent to Ramah to his house. And the child became the servant of the Lord under the direction of Eli the priest.
No the sons of Eli ere evil and good-for-nothing men, having no knoledge of the Lord.
And the priests’ ay ith the people as this: hen any man made an offering, the priest’s servant came hile the flesh as being cooked, having in his hand a meat-hook ith three teeth;
This he put into the pot, and everything hich came up on the hook the priest took for himself. This they did in Shiloh to all the Israelites ho came there.

And more than this, before the fat as burned, the priest’s servant ould come and say to the man ho as making the offering, Give me some of the flesh to be cooked for the priest; he has no taste for meat cooked in ater, but ould have you give it uncooked.
And if the man said to him, First let the fat be burned, then take as much as you ill; then the servant ould say, No, you are to give it to me no, or I ill take it by force.
And the sin of these young men as very great before the Lord; for they gave no honour to the Lord’s offerings.
But Samuel did the ork of the Lord’s house, hile he as a child, dressed in a linen ephod.
And his mother made him a little robe and took it to him every year hen she came ith her husband for the year’s offering.
And every year Eli gave Elkanah and his ife a blessing, saying, May the Lord give you offspring by this oman in exchange for the child you have given to the Lord. And they ent back to their house.
And the Lord had mercy on Hannah and she gave birth to three sons and to daughters. And the young Samuel became older before the Lord.
No Eli as very old; and he had nes from time to time of hat his sons ere doing to all Israel.
And he said to them, Why are you doing such things? for from all this people I get accounts of your evil ays.
No, my sons, the account hich is given me, hich the Lord’s people are sending about, is not good.

If one man does rong to another, God ill be his judge: but if a man’s sin is against the Lord, ho ill take up his cause? But they gave no attention to the voice of their father, for it as the Lord’s purpose to send destruction on them.
And the young Samuel, becoming older, had the approval of the Lord and of men.
And a man of God came to Eli and said to him, The Lord says, Did I let myself be seen by your father’s people hen they ere in Egypt, servants in Pharaoh’s house?

Did I take him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest and to go up to my altar to make the smoke of the offerings go up and to take up the ephod? Did I give to your father’s family all the offerings made by fire by the children of Israel?

Why then are you looking ith envy on my offerings of meat and of meal hich ere ordered by my ord, honouring your sons before me, and making yourselves fat ith all the best of the offerings of Israel, my people?

For this reason the Lord God of Israel has said, Truly I did say that your family and your father’s people ould have their place before me for ever: but no the Lord says, Let it not be so; I ill give honour to those by hom I am honoured, and those ho have no respect for me ill be of small value in my eyes.
See, the days are coming hen your arm and the arm of your father’s people ill be cut off;
And never again ill there be an old man in your family.
But one man of your family ill not be cut off by my hand, and his eyes ill be made dark, and grief ill be in his heart: and all the offspring of your family ill come to their end by the sord of men.
And this ill be the sign to you, hich ill come on Hophni and Phinehas, your sons; death ill overtake them on the same day.

And I ill make a true priest for myself, one ho ill do hat is in my heart and in my mind: and I ill make for him a family hich ill not come to an end; and his place ill be before my holy one for ever.

Then it ill be that the rest of your family, anyone ho has not been cut off, ill go don on his knees to him for a bit of silver or a bit of bread, and say, Be pleased to put me into one of the priest’s places so that I may have a little food.
No the young Samuel as the servant of the Lord before Eli. In those days the Lord kept his ord secret from men; there as no open vision.
And at that time, hen Eli as resting in his place, ( no his eyes ere becoming clouded so that he as not able to see,)
And the light of God as still burning, hile Samuel as sleeping in the Temple of the Lord here the ark of God as,
The voice of the Lord said Samuel’s name; and he said, Here am I.
And running to Eli he said, Here am I, for you said my name. And Eli said, I did not say your name; go to your rest again. So he ent back to his bed.
And again the Lord said, Samuel. And Samuel got up and ent to Eli and said, Here am I; for you certainly said my name. But he said in anser, I said nothing, my son; go to your rest again.

And for the third time the Lord said Samuel’s name. And he got up and ent to Eli and said, Here am I; for you certainly said my name. Then it as clear to Eli that the voice hich had said the child’s name as the Lord’s.
