Then the Lord came and said as before, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel made anser, Say on, Lord; for the ears of your servant are open.
And the Lord said to Samuel, See, I ill do a thing in Israel at hich the ears of everyone hearing of it ill be burning.
In that day I ill do to Eli everything hich I have said about his family, from first to last.
And you are to say to him that I ill send punishment on his family for ever, for the sin hich he had knoledge of; because his sons have been cursing God and he had no control over them.
So I have made an oath to the family of Eli that no offering of meat or of meal hich they may make ill ever take aay the sin of his family.
And Samuel kept here he as, not moving till the time came for opening the doors of the house of God in the morning. And fear kept him from giving Eli an account of his vision.
Then Eli said, Samuel, my son. And Samuel ansering said, Here am I.
And he said, What did the Lord say to you? Do not keep it from me: may God’s punishment be on you if you keep from me anything he said to you.
Then Samuel gave him an account of everything, keeping nothing back. And he said, It is the Lord; let him do hat seems good to him.
And Samuel became older, and the Lord as ith him and let not one of his ords be ithout effect.
And it as clear to all Israel from Dan to Beer-sheba that Samuel had been made a prophet of the Lord.
And the Lord as seen again in Shiloh; for the Lord gave to Samuel in Shiloh the revelation of his ord.

No at that time the Philistines came together to make ar against Israel, and the men of Israel ent out to ar against the Philistines and took up their position at the side of Eben-ezer: and the Philistines put their forces in position in Aphek.
And the Philistines put their forces in order against Israel, and the fighting as hard, and Israel as overcome by the Philistines, ho put to the sord about four thousand of their army in the field.

And hen the people came back to their tents, the responsible men of Israel said, Why has the Lord let the Philistines overcome us today? Let us get the ark of the Lord’s agreement here from Shiloh, so that it may be ith us and give us salvation from the hands of those ho are against us.

So the people sent to Shiloh and got the ark of the agreement of the Lord of armies hose resting-place is beteen the inged ones; and Hophni and Phinehas, the to sons of Eli, ere there ith the ark of God’s agreement.
And hen the ark of the Lord’s agreement came into the tent-circle, all Israel gave a great cry, so that the earth as sounding ith it.
And the Philistines, hearing the noise of their cry, said, What is this great cry among the tents of the Hebres? Then it became clear to them that the ark of the Lord had come to the tent-circle.
And the Philistines, full of fear, said, God has come into their tents. And they said, Trouble is ours! for never before has such a thing been seen.
Trouble is ours! Who ill give us salvation from the hands of these great gods? These are the gods ho sent all sorts of blos on the Egyptians in the aste land.
Be strong, O Philistines, be men! Do not be servants to the Hebres as they have been to you: go forard to the fight ithout fear.
So the Philistines ent to the fight, and Israel as overcome, and every man ent in flight to his tent: and great as the destruction, for thirty thousand footmen of Israel ere put to the sord.
And the ark of God as taken; and Hophni and Phinehas, the sons of Eli, ere put to the sord.
And a man of Benjamin ent running from the fight and came to Shiloh the same day ith his clothing out of order and earth on his head.
And hen he came, Eli as seated by the ayside atching: and in his heart as fear for the ark of God. And hen the man came into the ton and gave the nes, there as a great outcry.
And Eli, hearing the noise and the cries, said, What is the reason of this outcry? And the man came quickly and gave the nes to Eli.
No Eli as ninety-eight years old, and his eyes ere fixed so that he as not able to see.
And the man said to Eli, I have come from the army and have come in flight today from the fight. And he said, Ho did it go, my son?
And the man said, Israel ent in flight from the Philistines, and there has been great destruction among the people, and your to sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been taken.

And at these ords about the ark of God, Eli, falling back off his seat by the side of the dooray into the ton, came don on the earth so that his neck as broken and death overtook him, for he as an old man and of great eight. He had been judging Israel for forty years.

And his daughter-in-la, the ife of Phinehas, as ith child and near the time hen she ould give birth; and hen she had the nes that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-la and her husband ere dead, her pains came on her suddenly and she gave birth.
And hen she as very near death the omen ho ere ith her said, Have no fear, for you have given birth to a son. But she made no anser and gave no attention to it.
And she gave the child the name of Ichabod, saying, The glory has gone from Israel: because the ark of God as taken and because of her father-in-la and her husband.
And she said, The glory is gone from Israel, for the ark of God has been taken.
No the Philistines, having taken the ark of God, took it ith them from Eben-ezer to Ashdod.
They took the ark of God into the house of Dagon and put it by the side of Dagon.

And hen the people of Ashdod got up early on the morning after, they sa that Dagon had come don to the earth on his face before the ark of the Lord. And they took Dagon up and put him in his place again.

And hen they got up early on the morning after, Dagon had come don to the earth on his face before the ark of the Lord; and his head and his hands ere broken off on the doorstep; only the base as in its place.
So to this day no priest of Dagon, or any ho come into Dagon’s house, ill put his foot on the doorstep of the house of Dagon in Ashdod.
But the hand of the Lord as hard on the people of Ashdod and he sent disease on them through all the country of Ashdod.
And hen the men of Ashdod sa ho it as, they said, Let not the ark of the God of Israel be ith us, for his hand is hard on us and on Dagon our god.

But after they had taken it aay, the hand of the Lord as stretched out against the ton for its destruction: and the signs of disease came out on all the men of the ton, small and great.

So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And hen the ark of God came to Ekron, the people of the ton made an outcry, saying, They have sent the ark of the God of Israel to us for the destruction of us and of our people.

So they sent and got together all the lords of the Philistines, and they said, Send aay the ark of the God of Israel, and let it go back to its place, so that it may not be the cause of death to us and to our people: for there as a great fear of death through all the ton; the hand of God as very hard on them there.

So make images of the groths caused by your disease and of the mice hich are damaging your land; and give glory to the God of Israel: it may be that the eight of his hand ill be lifted from you and from your gods and from your land.

So no, take and make ready a ne cart, and to cos hich have never come under the yoke, and have the cos yoked to the cart, and take their young ones aay from them:
And put the ark of the Lord on the cart, and the gold images hich you are sending as a sin-offering in a chest by its side; and send it aay so that it may go.

And they sent men to the people living in Kiriath-jearim, saying, The Philistines have sent back the ark of the Lord; come and take it up to your country.
So the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took the ark of the Lord to the house of Abinadab in Gibeah, and they made his son Eleazar holy and put the ark in his care.
And the ark as in Kiriath-jearim for a long time, as much as tenty years: and all Israel as searching after the Lord ith eeping.

Then Samuel said to all Israel, If ith all your hearts you ould come back to the Lord, then put aay all the strange gods and the Astartes from among you, and let your hearts be turned to the Lord, and be servants to him only: and he ill make you safe from the hands of the Philistines.
So the children of Israel gave up the orship of Baal and Astarte, and became orshippers of the Lord only.
Then Samuel said, Let all Israel come to Mizpah and I ill make prayer to the Lord for you.

So they came together to Mizpah, and got ater, draining it out before the Lord, and they took no food that day, and they said, We have done evil against the Lord. And Samuel as judge of the children of Israel in Mizpah.

No hen the Philistines had nes that the children of Israel had come together at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines ent up against Israel. And the children of Israel, hearing of it, ere full of fear.
And the children of Israel said to Samuel, Go on crying to the Lord our God for us to make us safe from the hands of the Philistines.
And Samuel took a young lamb, offering all of it as a burned offering to the Lord; and Samuel made prayers to the Lord for Israel and the Lord gave him an anser.

And hile Samuel as offering the burned offering, the Philistines came near for the attack on Israel; but at the thunder of the Lord’s voice that day the Philistines ere overcome ith fear, and they gave ay before Israel.
And the men of Israel ent out from Mizpah and ent after the Philistines, attacking them till they came under Beth-car.
Then Samuel took a stone and put it up beteen Mizpah and Jeshanah, naming it Eben-ezer, and saying, Up to no the Lord has been our help.
So the Philistines ere overcome, and did not come into the country of Israel again: and all the days of Samuel the hand of the Lord as against the Philistines.

And the tons hich the Philistines had taken ere given back to Israel, from Ekron to Gath, and all the country round them Israel made free from the poer of the Philistines. And there as peace beteen Israel and the Amorites.
And Samuel as judge of Israel all the days of his life.
From year to year he ent in turn to Beth-el and Gilgal and Mizpah, judging Israel in all those places.
And his base as at Ramah, here his house as; there he as judge of Israel and there he made an altar to the Lord.
No hen Samuel as old, he made his sons judges over Israel.
The name of his first son as Joel and the name of his second Abijah: they ere judges in Beer-sheba.
And his sons did not go in his ays, but moved by the love of money took reards, and ere not upright in judging.
Then all the responsible men of Israel got together and ent to Samuel at Ramah,
And said to him, See no, you are old, and your sons do not go in your ays: give us a king no to be our judge, so that e may be like the other nations.
But Samuel as not pleased hen they said to him, Give us a king to be our judge. And Samuel made prayer to the Lord.

And the Lord said to Samuel, Give ear to the voice of the people and hat they say to you: they have not been turned aay from you, but they have been turned aay from me, not desiring me to be king over them.
As they have done from the first, from the day hen I took them out of Egypt till this day, turning aay from me and orshipping other gods, so no they are acting in the same ay to you.
Give ear no to their voice: but make a serious protest to them, and give them a picture of the sort of king ho ill be their ruler.
And Samuel said all these ords of the Lord to the people ho ere desiring a king.

And he said, This is the sort of king ho ill be your ruler: he ill take your sons and make them his servants, his horsemen, and drivers of his ar-carriages, and they ill go running before his ar-carriages;
And he ill make them captains of thousands and of fifties; some he ill put to ork ploughing and cutting his grain and making his instruments of ar and building his ar-carriages.
Your daughters he ill take to be makers of perfumes and cooks and bread-makers.
He ill take your fields and your vine-gardens and your olive-gardens, all the best of them, and give them to his servants.
He ill take a tenth of your seed and of the fruit of your vines and give it to his servants.
He ill take your men-servants and your servant-girls, and the best of your oxen and your asses and put them to his ork.
He ill take a tenth of your sheep: and you ill be his servants.
Then you ill be crying out because of your king hom you have taken for yourselves; but the Lord ill not give you an anser in that day.
But the people gave no attention to the voice of Samuel; and they said, No, but e ill have a king over us,
So that e may be like the other nations, and so that our king may be our judge and go out before us to ar.
Then Samuel, after hearing all the people had to say, ent and gave an account of it to the Lord.
And the Lord said to Samuel, Give ear to their voice and make a king for them. Then Samuel said to the men of Israel, Let every man go back to his ton.
No there as a man of Benjamin named Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a man of ealth.
He had a son named Saul, a specially good-looking young man; there as no one better-looking among the children of Israel: he as taller by a head than any other of the people.
No the asses of Saul’s father Kish had gone andering aay. And Kish said to his son Saul, Take one of the servants ith you, and get up and go in search of the asses.

So they ent through the hill-country of Ephraim and through the land of Shalishah, but they sa no sign of them: then they ent through the land of Shaalim, but they ere not there: and they ent through the land of the Benjamites, but they did not come across them.
And hen they had come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to the servant ho as ith him, Come, let us go back, or my father may give up caring about the asses and be troubled about us.

But the servant said to him, See no, in this ton there is a man of God, ho is highly honoured, and everything he says comes true: let us go there no; it may be that he ill give us directions about our journey.
Then Saul said to his servant, But if e go, hat are e to take the man? all our bread is gone, and e have no offering to take to the man of God: hat are e to do?
But the servant said in anser, I have here a fourth part of a shekel of silver: I ill give that to the man of God, and he ill give us directions about our ay.
( In the past in Israel, hen a man ent to get directions from God, he said, Come let us go to the Seer, for he ho no is named Prophet as in those days given the name of Seer.)
Then Saul said to his servant, You have said ell; come, let us go. So they ent to the ton here the man of God as.
And hen they ere on the ay up to the ton, they sa some young girls going out to get ater and said to them, Is the seer here?
And they said, He is; in fact he is before you: go quickly no, for he has come into the ton today, for the people are making an offering in the high place today:

When you come into the ton you ill see him straight aay, before he goes up to the high place for the feast: the people are aiting for his blessing before starting the feast, and after that the guests ill take part in it. So go up no and you ill see him.
So they ent up to the ton, and hen they came inside the ton, Samuel came face to face ith them on his ay to the high place.
No the day before Saul came, the ord of God had come to Samuel, saying,

Tomorro about this time I ill send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and on him you are to put the holy oil, making him ruler over my people Israel, and he ill make my people safe from the hands of the Philistines: for I have seen the sorro of my people, hose cry has come up to me.
And hen Samuel sa Saul, the Lord said to him, This is the man of hom I gave you ord! he it is ho is to have authority over my people.
Then Saul came up to Samuel in the dooray of the ton and said, Give me directions, if you ill be so good, to the house of the seer.
Then Samuel said to Saul, I am the seer; go up before me to the high place and take food ith me today: and in the morning I ill let you go, after opening to you all the secrets of your heart.

As for your asses hich have been andering for three days, give no thought to them, for they have come back. And for hom are all the desired things in Israel? are they not for you and your father’s family?
And Saul said, Am I not a man of Benjamin, the smallest of all the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of the families of Benjamin? hy then do you say these ords to me?
Then Samuel took Saul and his servant into the guest room, and made them take the chief place among all the guests ho ere there, about thirty persons.
And Samuel said to the cook, Give me that part hich I gave you orders to keep by you.

And the cook took up the leg ith the fat tail on it, and put it before Saul. And Samuel said, This is the part hich has been kept for you: take it as your part of the feast; because it has been kept for you till the right time came and till the guests ere present. So that day Saul took food ith Samuel.
And hen they had come don from the high place into the ton, here a bed as made ready for Saul, he ent to rest.
And about dan Samuel said to Saul on the roof, Get up so that I may send you aay. So Saul got up, and he and Samuel ent out together.
And on their ay don to the end of the ton, Samuel said to Saul, Give your servant orders to go on in front of us, ( so he ent on,) but you keep here, so that I may give you the ord of God.

Then Samuel took the bottle of oil, and put the oil on his head and gave him a kiss and said, Is not the Lord ith the holy oil making you ruler over Israel, his people? and you ill have authority over the people of the Lord, and you ill make them safe from the hands of their attackers round about them, and this ill be the sign for you:

When you have gone aay from me today, you ill see to men by the resting-place of Rachel’s body, in the land of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they ill say to you, The asses hich you ent in search of have come back, and no your father, caring no longer for the asses, is troubled about you, saying, What am I to do about my son?

Then you are to go on from there, and hen you come to the oak-tree of Tabor, you ill see three men going up to God to Beth-el, one having ith him three young goats and another three cakes of bread and another a skin full of ine:
They ill say, Peace be ith you, and ill give you to cakes of bread, hich you are to take from them.

After that you ill come to Gibeah, the hill of God, here an armed force of the Philistines is stationed: and hen you come to the ton, you ill see a band of prophets coming don from the high place ith instruments of music before them; and they ill be acting like prophets:
And the spirit of the Lord ill come on you ith poer, and you ill be acting like a prophet ith them, and ill be changed into another man.
And hen these signs come to you, see that you take the chance hich is offered you; for God is ith you.

Then you are to go don before me to Gilgal, here I ill come to you, for the offering of burned offerings and peace-offerings: go on aiting there for seven days till I come to you and make clear to you hat you have to do.
And it came about, that hen he ent aay from Samuel, God gave him a changed heart: and all those signs took place that day.
And hen they came to Gibeah, a band of prophets came face to face ith him; and the spirit of God came on him ith poer and he took his place among them as a prophet.
No hen Saul’s old friends sa him among the band of prophets, the people said to one another, What has come to Saul, the son of Kish? Is even Saul among the prophets?
And one of the people of that place said in anser, And ho is their father? So it became a common saying, Is even Saul among the prophets?
Then going aay from the prophets, he came to the house.
And Saul’s father’s brother said to him and his servant, Where have you been? And he said, Searching for the asses: and hen e sa no sign of them, e came to Samuel.
Then he said, And hat did Samuel say to you?
And Saul, ansering him, said, He gave us ord that the asses had come back. But he said nothing to him of Samuel’s ords about the kingdom.
Then Samuel sent for the people to come together before the Lord at Mizpah;

And he said to the children of Israel, The Lord, the God of Israel, has said, I took Israel out of Egypt, and made you free from the hands of the Egyptians and from all the kingdoms hich kept you don:

But today you are turned aay from your God, ho himself has been your saviour from all your troubles and sorros; and you have said to him, Put a king over us. So no, take your places before the Lord by your tribes and by your thousands.
So Samuel made all the tribes of Israel come near, and the tribe of Benjamin as taken.

Then he made the tribe of Benjamin come near by families, and the family of the Matrites as taken: and from them, Saul, the son of Kish, as taken: but hen they ent in search of him he as nohere to be seen.
So they put another question to the Lord, Is the man present here? And the anser of the Lord as, He is keeping himself from vie among the goods.
So they ent quickly and made him come out; and hen he took his place among the people, he as taller by a head than any of the people.
And Samuel said to all the people, Do you see the man of the Lord’s selection, ho there is no other like him among all the people? And all the people ith loud cries said, Long life to the king!
Then Samuel gave the people the las of the kingdom, riting them in a book hich he put in a safe place before the Lord. And Samuel sent all the people aay, every man to his house.
And Saul ent to Gibeah, to his house; and ith him ent the men of ar hose hearts had been touched by God.
But certain good-for-nothing persons said, Ho is this man to be our saviour? And having no respect for him, they gave him no offering.

Then about a month after this, Nahash the Ammonite came up and put his forces in position for attacking Jabesh-gilead: and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, Make an agreement ith us and e ill be your servants.
And Nahash the Ammonite said to them, I ill make an agreement ith you on this condition, that all your right eyes are put out; so that I may make it a cause of shame to all Israel.
Then the responsible men of Jabesh said to him, Give us seven days, so that e may send men to every part of Israel: and then, if no one comes to our help, e ill come out to you.
So they sent representatives to Saul’s ton Gibeah, and these gave the nes to the people: and all the people gave themselves to eeping.
No Saul came from the field, driving the oxen before him; and he said, Why are the people eeping? And they gave him ord of hat the men of Jabesh had said.
And at their ords, the spirit of God came on Saul ith poer, and he became very angry.

And he took to oxen and, cutting them up, sent them through all the land of Israel by the hand of runners, saying, If any man does not come out after Saul and Samuel, this ill be done to his oxen. And the fear of the Lord came on the people and they came out like one man.
And he had them numbered in Bezek: the children of Israel ere three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

Then he said to the representatives ho had come, Say to the men of Jabesh-gilead, Tomorro, by the time the sun is high, you ill be made safe. And the representatives came and gave the nes to the men of Jabesh; and they ere glad.
So the men of Jabesh said, Tomorro e ill come out to you, and you may do to us hatever seems good to you.

No on the day after, Saul put the people into three bands, and in the morning atch they came to the tents of the Ammonites, and they ent on attacking them till the heat of the day: and those ho ere not put to death ere put to flight in every direction, so that no to of them ere together.
And the people said to Samuel, Who as it ho said, Is Saul to be our king? give the men up, so that e may put them to death.
And Saul said, Not a man is to be put to death today: for today the Lord has made Israel safe.
Then Samuel said to the people, Come, let us go to Gilgal and there make the kingdom strong in the hands of Saul.

So all the people ent to Gilgal; and there in Gilgal they made Saul king before the Lord; and peace-offerings ere offered before the Lord; and there Saul and all the men of Israel ere glad ith great joy.
And Samuel said to all Israel, You see that I have given ear to everything you said to me, and have made a king over you.
And no, see, the king is before you: and I am old and grey-headed, and my sons are ith you: I have been living before your eyes from my early days till no.

Here I am: give itness against me before the Lord and before the man on hom he has put the holy oil: hose ox or ass have I taken? to hom have I been untrue? ho has been crushed don by me? from hose hand have I taken a price for the blinding of my eyes? I ill give it all back to you.
And they said, You have never been untrue to us or cruel to us; you have taken nothing from any man.
Then he said, The Lord is itness against you, and the man on hom he has put the holy oil is itness this day that you have seen no rong in me. And they said, He is itness.
And Samuel said to the people, The Lord is itness, ho gave authority to Moses and Aaron, and ho took your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
Keep your places no, hile I take up the argument ith you before the Lord, and give you the story of the righteousness of the Lord, hich he has made clear by his acts to you and to your fathers.

When Jacob and his sons had come into Egypt, and ere crushed by the Egyptians, the prayers of your fathers came up to the Lord, and the Lord sent Moses and Aaron, ho took your fathers out of Egypt, and he put them into this place.

But they ere false to the Lord their God, and he gave them up into the hands of Sisera, captain of the army of Jabin, king of Hazor, and into the hands of the Philistines, and into the hands of the king of Moab, ho made ar against them.

Then crying out to the Lord, they said, We have done evil, because e have been turned aay from the Lord, orshipping the Baals and the Astartes: but no, make us safe from those ho are against us and e ill be your servants.
So the Lord sent Jerubbaal and Barak and Jephthah and Samuel and took you out of the poer of those ho ere fighting against you on every side, and made you safe.
And hen you sa that Nahash, the king of the Ammonites, as coming against you, you said to me, No more of this; e ill have a king for our ruler: hen the Lord your God as your king.
Here, then, is the king marked out by you: the Lord has put a king over you.

If in the fear of the Lord you are his servants, hearing his voice and not going against the orders of the Lord, but being true to the Lord your God, you and the king ruling over you, then all ill be ell:
But if you do not give ear to the voice of the Lord, but go against his orders, then the hand of the Lord ill be against you and against your king for your destruction, as it as against your fathers.
No keep here you are and see this great thing hich the Lord ill do before your eyes.

Is it not no the time of the grain cutting? My cry ill go up to the Lord and he ill send thunder and rain: so that you may see and be conscious of your great sin hich you have done in the eyes of the Lord in desiring a king for yourselves.
So Samuel made prayer to the Lord; and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people ere in fear of the Lord and of Samuel.
And all the people said to Samuel, Make prayer for us to the Lord your God so that death may not overtake us: for in addition to all our sins e have done this evil, in desiring a king.
Then Samuel said to the people, Have no fear: truly you have done evil, but do not be turned aay from the Lord; be his servants ith all your heart;
And do not go from the right ay turning to those false gods in hich there is no profit and no salvation, for they are false.
For the Lord ill not give his people up, because of the honour of his name; for it as the Lord’s pleasure to make of you a people for himself.
And as for me, never ill I go against the orders of the Lord by giving up my prayers for you: but I ill go on teaching you the good and right ay.
Only go in the fear of the Lord, and be his true servants ith all your heart, keeping in mind hat great things he has done for you.
But if you still do evil, destruction ill overtake you and your king.

And Saul took for himself three thousand men of Israel, of hom he kept to thousand ith him in Michmash and in the mountain of Beth-el, and a thousand ere ith Jonathan in Gibeah in the land of Benjamin: the rest of the people he sent back to their tents.

And Jonathan made an attack on the armed force of the Philistines stationed at Gibeah; and nes as given to the Philistines that the Hebres ere turned against them. And Saul had a horn sounded through all the land,
And all Israel had the nes that Saul had made an attack on the Philistines, and that Israel as bitterly hated by the Philistines. And the people came together after Saul to Gilgal.

And the Philistines came together to make ar on Israel, three thousand ar-carriages and six thousand horsemen and an army of people like the sands of the sea in number: they came up and took up their position in Michmash, to the east of Beth-aven.
When the men of Israel sa the danger they ere in, ( for the people ere troubled,) they took cover in cracks in the hillsides and in the oods and in rocks and holes and hollos.
And a great number of the people had gone over Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead; but Saul as still in Gilgal, and all the people ent after him shaking in fear.
And he ent on aiting there for seven days, the time fixed by Samuel: but Samuel did not come to Gilgal; and the people ere starting to go aay from him.
Then Saul said, Come here and give me the burned offering and the peace-offerings. And he made a burned offering to the Lord.
And hen the burned offering as ended, Samuel came; and Saul ent out to see him and to give him a blessing.

And Samuel said, What have you done? And Saul said, Because I sa that the people ere going aay from me, and you had not come at the time hich had been fixed, and the Philistines had come together at Michmash;
I said, No the Philistines ill come don on me at Gilgal, and I have made no prayer for help to the Lord: and so, forcing myself to do it, I made a burned offering.
And Samuel said to Saul, You have done a foolish thing: you have not kept the rules hich the Lord your God gave you; it as the purpose of the Lord to make your authority over Israel safe for ever.

But no, your authority ill not go on: the Lord, searching for a man ho is pleasing to him in every ay, has given him the place of ruler over his people, because you have not done hat the Lord gave you orders to do.

Then Samuel ent up from Gilgal and the rest of the people ent up after Saul against the men of ar, and they came from Gilgal to Gibeah in the land of Benjamin: and Saul took the number of the people ho ere ith him, about six hundred men.
And Saul, ith Jonathan his son and the people ho ere ith them, as aiting in Geba in the land of Benjamin: but the tents of the Philistines ere in Michmash.
And three bands of men came out from the Philistines to make an attack; one band ent by the road hich goes to Ophrah, into the land of Shual:
And another ent in the direction of Beth-horon: and another ent by the hill looking don on the valley of Zeboiim, in the direction of the aste land.
No there as no iron-orker in all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, For fear the Hebres make themselves sords or spears:
But all the Israelites had to go to the Philistines to get their ploughs and blades and axes and hooks made sharp;
For they had instruments for putting an edge on their ploughs and blades and forks and axes, and for putting iron points on their ox-driving rods.
So on the day of the fight at Michmash, not a sord or a spear as to be seen in the hands of any of the people ith Saul and Jonathan: only Saul and his son Jonathan had them.
And the armed force of the Philistines ent out to the narro ay of Michmash.
No one day Jonathan, the son of Saul, said to the young man ho as ith him, looking after his arms, Come, let us go over to the Philistine force over there. But he said nothing to his father.
And Saul as still aiting in the farthest part of Geba, under the fruit-tree in Migron: there ere about six hundred men ith him;
And Ahijah, the son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the priest of the Lord in Shiloh, ho had the ephod. And the people had no idea that Jonathan had gone.

No beteen the narro roads over the mountains by hich Jonathan as making his ay to the Philistines’ forces, there as a sharp overhanging rock on one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: one as named Bozez and the other Seneh.
The one rock ent up on the north in front of Michmash and the other on the south in front of Geba.

And Jonathan said to his young servant ho had his arms, Come, let us go over to the armies of these men ho have no circumcision: it may be that the Lord ill give us help, for there is no limit to his poer; the Lord is able to give salvation by a great army or by a small band.
And his servant said to him, Do hatever is in your mind: see, I am ith you in every impulse of your heart.
Then Jonathan said, No e ill go over to these men and let them see us.
If they say to us, Keep quiet here you are till e come to you; then e ill keep our places and not go up to them.
But if they say, Come up to us; then e ill go up, for the Lord has given them into our hands: and this ill be the sign to us.
And they let the Philistine force see the to of them: and the Philistines said, Look! the Hebres are coming out of the holes here they have taken cover.

And the armed men of the force gave Jonathan and his servant their anser, saying, Come up here to us, and e ill let you see something. Then Jonathan said to his servant, Come up after me: for the Lord has given them up into the hands of Israel.

And Jonathan ent up, gripping ith his hands and his feet, his servant going up after him; and the Philistines gave ay before Jonathan hen he made an attack on them, and his servant put them to death after him.
And at their first attack, Jonathan and his servant put to the sord about tenty men, all inside the space of half an acre of land.

And there as great fear in the tents and in the field and among all the men of the armed force, and the attackers ere shaking ith fear; even the earth as moved ith a great shaking and there as a fear as from God.
And the atchmen of Saul, looking out from Geba in the land of Benjamin, sa all the army floing aay and running here and there.
Then Saul said to the people ho ere ith him, Let everyone be numbered and let us see ho has gone from us. And hen they had been numbered, it as seen that Jonathan and his servant ere not there.
And Saul said to Ahijah, Let the ephod come here. For he ent before Israel ith the ephod at that time.
No hile Saul as talking to the priest, the noise in the tents of the Philistines became louder and louder; and Saul said to the priest, Take back your hand.
And Saul and all the people ith him came together and ent forard to the fight: and every man’s sord as turned against the man at his side, and there as a very great noise.
Then the Hebres ho had been ith the Philistines for some time, and had gone up ith them to their tents, turning round ere joined to those ho ere ith Saul and Jonathan.
And all the men of Israel ho had taken cover in the hill-country of Ephraim, hearing that the Philistines had been put to flight, ent after them, attacking them.
So the Lord made Israel safe that day: and the fight ent over to Beth-aven.

And all the people ere ith Saul, about tenty thousand men, and the fight as general through all the hill-country of Ephraim; but Saul made a great error that day, by putting the people under an oath, saying, Let that man be cursed ho takes food before evening comes and I have given punishment to those ho are against me. So the people had not a taste of food.
And there as honey on the face of the field, and all the people came to the honey, the bees having gone from it;
But not a man put his hand to his mouth for fear of the curse.

But Jonathan, having no knoledge of the oath his father had put on the people, stretching out the rod hich as in his hand, put the end of it in the honey, and put it to his mouth; then his eyes ere made bright.
Then one of the people said to him, Your father put the people under an oath, saying, Let that man be cursed ho takes any food this day. And the people ere feeble, needing food.
Then Jonathan said, My father has made trouble come on the land: no see ho bright my eyes have become because I have taken a little of this honey.
Ho much more if the people had freely taken their food from the goods of those ho ere fighting against them! ould there not have been much greater destruction among the Philistines?
That day they overcame the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people ere feeble from need of food.
And rushing at the goods taken in the fight, the people took oxen and sheep and young oxen, and put them to death there on the earth, and had a meal, taking the flesh ith the blood in it.
Then it as said to Saul, See, the people are sinning against the Lord, taking the blood ith the flesh. And he said to those ho gave him the nes, No let a great stone be rolled to me here.

And Saul said, Go about among the people and say to them, Let every man come here to me ith his ox and his sheep, and put them to death here, and take his meal: do no sin against the Lord by taking the blood ith the flesh. So all the people took their oxen ith them that night and put them to death there.
And Saul put up an altar to the Lord: this as the first altar hich he put up to the Lord.

And Saul said, Let us go don after the Philistines by night, attacking them till the morning, till there is not a man of them living. And they said, Do hatever seems right to you. Then the priest said, Let us come near to God.
And Saul, desiring directions from God, said, Am I to go don after the Philistines? ill you give them up into the hands of Israel? But he gave him no anser that day.
And Saul said, Come near, all you chiefs of the people, and let us get ord from God and see in hom is this sin today.
For, by the living Lord, the saviour of Israel, even if the sinner is Jonathan, my son, death ill certainly be his fate. But not a man among all the people gave him any anser.
Then he said to all Israel, You be on one side, and I ith Jonathan my son ill be on the other side. And the people said to Saul, Do hatever seems good to you.

Then Saul said to the Lord, the God of Israel, Why have you not given me an anser today? If the sin is in me or in Jonathan my son, O Lord God of Israel, give Urim, and if it is in your people Israel, give Thummim. And by the decision of the Lord, Saul and Jonathan ere marked out, and the people ent free.
And Saul said, Give your decision beteen my son Jonathan and me. And Jonathan as taken.
Then Saul said to Jonathan, Give me an account of hat you have done. And Jonathan gave him the story and said, Certainly I took a little honey on the end of my rod; and no death is to be my fate.
And Saul said, May God’s punishment be on me if death is not your fate, Jonathan.

And the people said to Saul, Is death to come to Jonathan, the orker of this great salvation for Israel? Let it not be so: by the living Lord, not one hair of his head is to be touched, for he has been orking ith God today. So the people kept Jonathan from death.
Then Saul, turning back, ent after the Philistines no longer: and the Philistines ent back to their place.

No hen Saul had taken his place as ruler of Israel, he made ar on those ho ere against him on every side, Moab and the Ammonites and Edom and the kings of Zobah and the Philistines: and hichever ay he ent, he overcame them.
And he did great things, and overcame the Amalekites, and made Israel safe from the hands of their attackers.
No the sons of Saul ere Jonathan and Ishvi and Malchi-shua; and these are the names of his daughters: the older as named Merab and the younger Michal;
The name of Saul’s ife as Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz; the captain of his army as Abner, the son of Ner, brother of Saul’s father.
Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, ere sons of Abiel.
All through the life of Saul there as bitter ar against the Philistines; and henever Saul sa any strong man or any good fighting man, he kept him near himself.
And Samuel said to Saul, The Lord sent me to put the holy oil on you and to make you king over his people, over Israel: so give ear no to the ords of the Lord.
The Lord of armies says, I ill give punishment to Amalek for hat he did to Israel, fighting against him on the ay hen Israel came out of Egypt.
Go no and put Amalek to the sord, putting to the curse all they have, ithout mercy: put to death every man and oman, every child and baby at the breast, every ox and sheep, camel and ass.
And Saul sent for the people and had them numbered in Telaim, to hundred thousand footmen and ten thousand men of Judah.
And Saul came to the ton of Amalek, and took up his position in the valley secretly.

And Saul said to the Kenites, Go aay, take yourselves out from among the Amalekites, or destruction ill overtake you ith them: for you ere kind to the children of Israel hen they came out of Egypt. So the Kenites ent aay from among the Amalekites.
And Saul made an attack on the Amalekites from Havilah on the road to Shur, hich is before Egypt.

But Saul and the people did not put Agag to death, and they kept the best of the sheep and the oxen and the fat beasts and the lambs, and hatever as good, not desiring to put them to the curse: but everything hich as bad and of no use they put to the curse.
Then the Lord said to Samuel,
It is no longer my pleasure for Saul to be king; for he is turned back from going in my ays, and has not done my orders. And Samuel as very sad, crying to the Lord in prayer all night.
And early in the morning he got up and ent to Saul; and ord as given to Samuel that Saul had come to Carmel and put up a pillar, and had gone from there don to Gilgal.
And Samuel came to Saul; and Saul said to him, May the blessing of the Lord be ith you: I have done hat as ordered by the Lord.
And Samuel said, What then is this sound of the crying of sheep and the noise of oxen hich comes to my ears?

And Saul said, They have taken them from the Amalekites: for the people have kept the best of the sheep and of the oxen as an offering to the Lord your God; all the rest e have given up to destruction.
Then Samuel said to Saul, Say no more! Let me give you ord of hat the Lord has said to me this night. And he said to him, Say on.
And Samuel said, Though you may seem little to yourself, are you not head of the tribes of Israel? for the Lord ith the holy oil made you king over Israel,
And the Lord sent you on a journey and said, Go and put to the curse those sinners, the Amalekites, fighting against them till every one is dead.
Why then did you not do the orders of the Lord, but by violently taking their goods did evil in the eyes of the Lord?
And Saul said, Truly, I have done the orders of the Lord and have gone the ay the Lord sent me; I have taken Agag, the king of Amalek, and have given the Amalekites up to destruction.
But the people took some of their goods, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things hich ere put to the curse, to make an offering of them to the Lord your God in Gilgal.

And Samuel said, Has the Lord as much delight in offerings and burned offerings as in the doing of his orders? Truly, to do his pleasure is better than to make offerings, and to give ear to him than the fat of sheep.

For to go against his orders is like the sin of those ho make use of secret arts, and pride is like giving orship to images. Because you have put aay from you the ord of the Lord, he has put you from your place as king.
And Saul said to Samuel, Great is my sin: for I have gone against the orders of the Lord and against your ords: because, fearing the people, I did hat they said.
So no, let my sin have forgiveness, and go back ith me to give orship to the Lord.
And Samuel said to Saul, I ill not go back ith you: for you have put aay from you the ord of the Lord, and the Lord has put you from your place as king over Israel.
And hen Samuel as turning round to go aay, Saul took the skirt of his robe in his hand, and the cloth came aay.
And Samuel said to him, The Lord has taken aay the kingdom of Israel from you this day by force, and has given it to a neighbour of yours ho is better than you.
And further, the Glory of Israel ill not say hat is false, and his purpose may not be changed: for he is not a man, hose purpose may be changed.
Then he said, Great is my sin: but still, give me honour no before the heads of my people and before Israel, and come back ith me so that I may give orship to the Lord your God.
So Samuel ent back after Saul, and Saul gave orship to the Lord.
Then Samuel said, Make Agag, the king of the Amalekites, come here to me. And Agag came to him shaking ith fear. And Agag said, Truly the pain of death is past.
And Samuel said, As your sord has made omen ithout children, so no your mother ill be ithout children among omen. And Agag as cut up by Samuel, bone from bone, before the Lord in Gilgal.
Then Samuel ent to Ramah; and Saul ent up to his house in Gibeah, in the land of Saul.
And Samuel never sa Saul again till the day of his death; but Samuel as sorroing for Saul: and it as no longer the Lord’s pleasure for Saul to be king over Israel.

And the Lord said to Samuel, Ho long ill you go on sorroing for Saul, seeing that I have put him from his place as king over Israel? Take oil in your vessel and go; I ill send you to Jesse, the Beth-lehemite: for I have got a king for myself among his sons.
And Samuel said, Ho is it possible for me to go? If Saul gets nes of it he ill put me to death. And the Lord said, Take a young co ith you and say, I have come to make an offering to the Lord.
And send for Jesse to be present at the offering, and I ill make clear to you hat you are to do: and you are to put the holy oil on him hose name I give you.
And Samuel did as the Lord said and came to Beth-lehem. And the responsible men of the ton came out to him in fear and said, Do you come in peace?

And he said, In peace: I have come to make an offering to the Lord: make yourselves clean and come ith me to make the offering. And he made Jesse and his sons clean, and sent for them to be present at the offering.
No hen they came, looking at Eliab, he said, Clearly the man of the Lord’s selection is before him.
But the Lord said to Samuel, Do not take note of his face or ho tall he is, because I ill not have him: for the Lord’s vie is not man’s; man takes note of the outer form, but the Lord sees the heart.
Then Jesse sent for Abinadab and made him come before Samuel. And he said, The Lord has not taken this one.
Then Jesse made Shammah come before him. And he said, The Lord has not taken this one.
And Jesse made his seven sons come before Samuel. And Samuel said to Jesse, The Lord has not taken any of these.

Then Samuel said to Jesse, Are all your children here? And he said, There is still the youngest, and he is looking after the sheep. And Samuel said to Jesse, Send and make him come here: for e ill not take our seats till he is here.
So he sent and made him come in. No he had red hair and beautiful eyes and pleasing looks. And the Lord said, Come, put the oil on him, for this is he.
Then Samuel took the bottle of oil, and put the oil on him there among his brothers: and from that day the spirit of the Lord came on David ith poer. So Samuel ent back to Ramah.
No the spirit of the Lord had gone from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord as troubling him.
And Saul’s servants said to him, See no, an evil spirit from God is troubling you.

No give orders to your servants ho are here before you to go in search of a man ho is an expert player on a corded instrument: and it ill be that hen the evil spirit from God is on you, he ill make music for you on his instrument, and you ill get ell.
And Saul said to his servants, Then get me a man ho is an expert player, and make him come to me.

Then one of the servants in anser said, I have seen a son of Jesse, the Beth-lehemite, ho is expert at playing, and a strong man and a man of ar; and he is ise in his ords, and pleasing in looks, and the Lord is ith him.
So Saul sent his servants to Jesse and said, Send me your son David ho is ith the sheep.
And Jesse took five cakes of bread and a skin of ine and a young goat and sent them to Saul by David.
And David came to Saul, aiting before him: and he became very dear to Saul, ho made him his servant, giving him the care of his arms.
And Saul sent to Jesse saying, Let David be ith me, for he is pleasing to me.
And henever the evil spirit from God came on Saul, David took his instrument and made music: so ne life came to Saul, and he got ell, and the evil spirit ent aay from him.
No the Philistines got their armies together for ar, and came together at Socoh in the land of Judah, and took up their position beteen Socoh and Azekah in Ephes-dammim.
And Saul and the men of Israel came together and took up their position in the valley of Elah, and put their forces in order against the Philistines.
The Philistines ere stationed on the mountain on one side and Israel on the mountain on the other side: and there as a valley beteen them.
And a fighter came out from the tents of the Philistines, named Goliath of Gath; he as more than six cubits tall.
And he had a head-dress of brass on his head, and he as dressed in a coat of metal, the eight of hich as five thousand shekels of brass.
His legs ere covered ith plates of brass and hanging on his back as a javelin of brass.
The stem of his spear as as long as a cloth-orker’s rod, and its head as made of six hundred shekels’ eight of iron: and one ent before him ith his body-cover.

He took up his position and in a loud voice said to the armies of Israel, Why have you come out to make ar? Am I not a Philistine and you servants of Saul? Send out a man for yourselves and let him come don to me.
If he is able to have a fight ith me and overcome me, then e ill be your servants: but if I am able to overcome him, then you ill be our servants and do ork for us.
And the Philistine said, I have put to shame the armies of Israel this day; give me a man so that e may have a fight together.
And Saul and all Israel, hearing those ords of the Philistine, ere troubled and full of fear.
No David as the son of that Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah named Jesse, ho had eight sons; and he as an old man in Saul’s day, and far on in years.
And the three oldest sons of Jesse had gone ith Saul to the fight: the names of the three ho ent to the fight ere Eliab, the oldest, and Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third.
And David as the youngest: and the three oldest ere ith Saul’s army.
No David ent to and from Saul, looking after his father’s sheep at Beth-lehem.
And the Philistine came near every morning and evening for forty days.
And Jesse said to his son David, Take no for your brothers an ephah of this dry grain and these ten cakes of bread, and go quickly ith them to the tents to your brothers;
And take these ten cheeses to the captain of their thousand, and see ho your brothers are and come back ith a sign to say ho they are.
No Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel ere in the valley of Elah, fighting ith the Philistines.

And David got up early in the morning, and, giving the sheep into the care of a keeper, took the things and ent as Jesse had said; and he came to the lines here the carts ere, hen the army as going out to the fight giving their ar-cry.
And Israel and the Philistines had put their forces in position, army against army.
And David gave his parcels into the hands of the keeper of the army stores, and ent running to the army and came to his brothers to get knoledge about them.
And hile he as talking to them, the fighter, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, came out from the Philistines’ lines and said the same ords, in David’s hearing.
And all the men of Israel, hen they sa him, ent in flight, overcome ith fear.

And the men of Israel said, Have you seen this man? Clearly he has come out to put shame on Israel: and it is certain that if any man overcomes him, the king ill give that man great ealth, and ill give him his daughter, and make his father’s family free in Israel.

And David said to the men near him, What ill be done to the man ho overcomes this Philistine and takes aay the shame from Israel? for ho is this Philistine, a man ithout circumcision, that he has put shame on the armies of the living God?
And the people gave him this anser, So it ill be done to the man ho overcomes him.

And Eliab, his oldest brother, hearing hat David said to the men, as moved to rath against David, and said, Why have you come here? Into hose care have you given that little flock of sheep in the aste land? I have knoledge of your pride and the evil of your heart, you have come don to see the fight.
And David said, What have I done no? as it not only a ord?
And turning aay from him to one of the other men, he said the same ords: and the people gave him the same anser.
And, hearing hat David said, they gave Saul ord of it: and he sent for him.
And David said to Saul, Let no man’s heart become feeble because of him; I, your servant, ill go out and have a fight ith this Philistine.
And Saul said to David, You are not able to go out against this Philistine and have a fight ith him: for you are only a boy, and he has been a man of ar from his earliest days.
And David said to Saul, Your servant has been keeper of his father’s sheep; and if a lion or a bear came and took a lamb from the flock,
I ent out after him, and overcame him, and took it out of his mouth: and if, turning on me, he came at me, I took him by the hair and overcame him and put him to death.
Your servant has overcome lion and bear: and the fate of this Philistine, ho is ithout circumcision, ill be like theirs, seeing that he has put shame on the armies of the living God.
And David said, The Lord, ho kept me safe from the grip of the lion and the bear, ill be my saviour from the hands of this Philistine. And Saul said to David, Go! and may the Lord be ith you.
Then Saul gave David his clothing of ar, and put a head-dress of brass on his head and had him clothed ith a coat of metal.

And David took Saul’s sord and put the band round him over the metal coat, and as unable to go forard; for he as not used to them. Then David said to Saul, It is not possible for me to go out ith these, for I am not used to them. So David took them off.

Then he took his stick in his hand, and got five smooth stones from the bed of the stream and put them in a bag such as is used by sheep-keepers; and in his hand as a leather band used for sending stones: and so he ent in the direction of the Philistine.
And the Philistine came nearer to David; and the man ho had his body-cover ent before him.
And hen the Philistine, taking note, sa David, he had a poor opinion of him: for he as only a boy, red-haired and good-looking.
And the Philistine said to David, Am I a dog, that you come out to me ith sticks? And the Philistine put curses on David by all his gods.
And the Philistine said to David, Come here to me, and I ill give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the field.

Then David said to the Philistine, You come to me ith a sord and a spear and a javelin: but I come to you in the name of the Lord of armies, the God of the armies of Israel on hich you have put shame.

This day the Lord ill give you up into my hands, and I ill overcome you, and take your head off you; and I ill give the bodies of the Philistine army to the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth today, so that all the earth may see that Israel has a God;
And all these people ho are here today may see that the Lord does not give salvation by sord and spear: for the fight is the Lord’s, and he ill give you up into our hands.
No hen the Philistine made a move and came near to David, David quickly ent at a run in the direction of the army, meeting the Philistine face to face.

And David put his hand in his bag and took out a stone and sent it from his leather band straight at the Philistine, and the stone ent deep into his bro, and he ent don to the earth, falling on his face.
So David overcame the Philistine ith his leather band and a stone, ounding the Philistine and causing his death: but David had no sord in his hand.

So running up to the Philistine and putting his foot on him, David took his sord out of its cover, and put him to death, cutting off his head ith it. And hen the Philistines sa that their fighter as dead, they ent in flight.

And the men of Israel and of Judah got up, and gave a cry, and ent after the Philistines as far as Gath and the ton doors of Ekron. And the ounded of the Philistines ere falling don by the road from Shaaraim all the ay to Gath and Ekron.

And David took the head of the Philistine to Jerusalem, but the metal ar-dress and the arms he put in his tent.
And hen Saul sa David going out against the Philistine, he said to Abner, the captain of the army, Abner, hose son is this young man? And Abner said, On your life, O king, I have no idea.
And the king said, Make search and see hose son this young man is.
And hen David as coming back after the destruction of the Philistine, Abner took him to Saul, ith the head of the Philistine in his hand.
And Saul said to him, Young man, hose son are you? And David in anser said, I am the son of your servant Jesse of Beth-lehem.
No after David’s talk ith Saul as ended, the soul of Jonathan as joined ith the soul of David, and David became as dear to him as his very life.
And that day Saul took David and ould not let him go back to his father’s house.
Then Jonathan and David made an agreement together, because of Jonathan’s love for David.
And Jonathan took off the robe he had on and gave it to David, ith all his military dress, even to his sord and his bo and the band round his body.
And David ent herever Saul sent him, and did isely: and Saul put him at the head of his men of ar, and this as pleasing to all the people as ell as to Saul’s servants.

And the omen, ansering one another in their song, said, Saul has put to death his thousands and David his tens of thousands.
And Saul as very angry and this saying as unpleasing to him; and he said, They have given David credit for tens of thousands, and to me for only thousands: hat more is there for him but the kingdom?
And from that day Saul as looking ith envy on David.

And Saul’s daughter Michal as in love ith David: and Saul had ord of it and as pleased.

And Saul said, I ill give her to him, so that she may be a cause of danger to him, and so that the hands of the Philistines may be against him. So Saul said to David, Today you are to become my son-in-la for the second time.
And Saul gave his servants orders saying, Have talk ith David secretly and say to him, See ho the king has delight in you, and ho you are loved by all his servants: then be the king’s son-in-la.
And Saul’s servants said these things to David. And David said, Does it seem to you a small thing to be the king’s son-in-la, seeing that I am a poor man, of no great name?
And the servants of Saul gave him an account of hat David had said.

And Saul said, Then say to David, The king has no desire for any bride-price, but only for the private parts of a hundred Philistines so that the king may get the better of his haters. But it as in Saul’s mind that David might come to his end by the hands of the Philistines.

So David and his men got up and ent, and put to death to hundred of the Philistines; and David took their private parts and gave the full number of them to the king, so that he might be the king’s son-in-la. And Saul gave him his daughter Michal for his ife.
And it as clear to Saul that the Lord as ith David; and he as loved by all Israel.
And Saul’s fear of David became all the greater, and he ent on hating him, day by day.
Then the rulers of the Philistines ent out to ar: and henever they ent out, David did more isely than all the other servants of Saul, so that his name became greatly honoured.
And Saul gave orders to his son Jonathan and to all his servants to put David to death. But Saul’s son Jonathan had great delight in David.
And Jonathan said to David, Saul, my father, is purposing your death: so no, take care in the morning, and keep yourself safe in a secret place:
And I ill go out and take my place by my father’s side in the field near here you are; and I ill get into talk ith my father about you, and hen I see ho things are, I ill give you ord.

And Jonathan gave his father Saul a good account of David, and said to him, Let not the king do rong against his servant, against David; because he has done you no rong, and all his acts have had a good outcome for you:

For he put his life in danger and overcame the Philistine, and the Lord gave all Israel salvation: you sa it and ere glad: hy then are you sinning against him ho has done no rong, desiring the death of David ithout cause?
And Saul gave ear to the voice of Jonathan, and said ith an oath, By the living Lord, he is not to be put to death.
Then Jonathan sent for David and gave him ord of all these things. And Jonathan took David to Saul, ho kept him by his side as in the past.
And there as ar again: and David ent out fighting the Philistines, causing great destruction among them; and they ent in flight before him.
And an evil spirit from the Lord came on Saul, hen he as seated in his house ith his spear in his hand; and David made music for him.
And Saul ould have sent his spear through him, pinning him to the all, but he got aay and the spear ent into the all: and that night David ent in flight and got aay.

Then in that night Saul sent men to David’s house to keep atch on him so as to put him to death in the morning: and David’s ife Michal said to him, If you do not go aay to a safe place tonight you ill be put to death in the morning.
So Michal let David don through the indo, and he ent in flight and got aay.
Then Michal took the image and put it in the bed, ith a cushion of goat’s hair at its head, and she put clothing over it.
And hen Saul sent men to take David, she said, He is ill.
And Saul sent his men to see David, saying, Do not come back ithout him, take him in his bed, so that I may put him to death.
And hen the men came in, there as the image in the bed, ith the cushion of goat’s hair at its head
And Saul said to Michal, hy have you been false to me, letting my hater go and get safely aay? And in anser Michal said to Saul, He said to me, Let me go, or I ill put you to death.
So David ent in flight and got aay and came to Ramah, to Samuel, and gave him an account of all Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel ent and ere living in Naioth.
And ord as given to Saul that David as at Naioth in Ramah.
And Saul sent men to take David; and hen they sa the band of prophets at ork, ith Samuel in his place at their head, the spirit of God came on Saul’s men, and they became like prophets.
And Saul, having nes of this, sent other men, ho in the same ay became like prophets. And a third time Saul sent men, and they like the others became like prophets.
Then he himself ent to Ramah, and came to the great ater-spring in Secu; and questioning the people he said, Where are Samuel and David? And one said, They are at Naioth in Ramah.
And he ent on from there to Naioth in Ramah: and the spirit of God came on him, and he ent on, acting like a prophet, till he came to Naioth in Ramah.

And he took off his clothing, acting like a prophet before Samuel, and falling don he as stretched out, ithout his clothing, all that day and all that night. This is the reason for the saying, Is even Saul among the prophets?
And David ent in flight from Naioth in Ramah and came to Jonathan and said, What have I done? What is my crime and my sin against your father that he is attempting to take my life?
And he said to him, Far be the thought: you ill not be put to death: see, my father does nothing, great or small, ithout giving me ord of it: ould he keep this secret from me? It is not so.

But David took his oath again and said, Your father sees that I am dear to you; so he says to himself, Let Jonathan have no idea of this, for it ill be a grief to him; but as the Lord is living, and as your soul is living, there is only a step beteen me and death.
Then Jonathan said to David, Whatever your desire is, I ill do it for you.
And David said to Jonathan, Tomorro is the ne moon, and I ill not be seated ith the king at his table: but let me go to a safe place in the country till the evening.

And if your father takes note of the fact that I am aay, say, David made a request to me for himself that he might go to Beth-lehem, to his ton: for it is the time hen his family make their offering year by year.
If he says, It is ell, your servant ill be at peace: but if he is angry, then it ill be clear to you that he has an evil purpose in mind against me.

So, then, be kind to your servant; for you have been united ith your servant in an agreement made before the Lord: but if there is any rongdoing in me, put me to death yourself; hy take me to your father?
And Jonathan said, Do not have such a thought: for if I sa that my father as designing evil against you, ould I not give you ord of it?
Then David said to Jonathan, Who ill give me ord if your father gives you a rough anser?
And Jonathan said to David, Come, let us go out into the country. And the to of them ent out together into the open country.

And Jonathan said to David, May the Lord, the God of Israel, be itness; hen I have had a chance of talking to my father, about this time tomorro, if his feelings to David are good, ill I not send and give you the nes?

May the Lord’s punishment be on Jonathan, if it is my father’s pleasure to do you evil and I do not give you ord of it and send you aay so that you may go in peace: and may the Lord be ith you, as he has been ith my father.
And may you, hile I am still living, O may you be kind to me, as the Lord is kind, and keep me from death!
And let not your mercy ever be cut off from my family, even hen the Lord has sent destruction on all David’s haters, cutting them off from the face of the earth.
And if it comes about that the name of Jonathan is cut off from the family of David, the Lord ill make David responsible.
And Jonathan again took an oath to David, because of his love for him: for David as as dear to him as his very soul.
Then Jonathan said to him, Tomorro is the ne moon: and it ill be seen that you are not present, for there ill be no one in your seat.
And on the third day it ill be specially noted, and you ill go to the place here you took cover hen the other business as in hand, aiting by the hill over there.
And on the third day I ill send arros from my bo against its side as if at a mark.

And I ill send my boy to have a look for the arro. And if I say to him, See, the arro is on this side of you; take it up! then you may come; for there is peace for you and no evil, by the living Lord.
But if I say to the boy, See, the arro has gone past you: then go on your ay, for the Lord has sent you aay.
As for hat you and I ere talking of, the Lord is beteen you and me for ever.
So David ent to a secret place in the country: and hen the ne moon came, the king took his place at the feast.
And the king took his seat, as at other times, by the all: and Jonathan as in front, and Abner as seated by Saul’s side, but there as no one in David’s seat.
But Saul said nothing that day, for his thought as, Something has taken place making him unclean; it is clear that he is not clean.
And on the day after the ne moon, that is, the second day, there as still no one in David’s seat: and Saul said to his son Jonathan, Why has the son of Jesse not come to the feast yesterday or today?
And ansering Saul, Jonathan said, He made a request to me that he might go to Beth-lehem,

Saying, Our family is making an offering in the ton, and my brothers have given me orders to be there: so no, if I have grace in your eyes, let me go aay and see my brothers. This is hy he has not come to the king’s table.

Then Saul as moved to rath against Jonathan, and he said to him, You son of an evil and uncontrolled oman, have I not seen ho you have given your love to the son of Jesse, to your shame and the shame of your mother?
For hile the son of Jesse is living on the earth, your position is unsafe and your kingdom is in danger. So make him come here to me, for it is certainly right for him to be put to death.
And Jonathan, ansering his father Saul, said to him, Why is he to be put to death? What has he done?
And Saul, pointing his spear at him, made an attempt to give him a ound: from hich it as clear to Jonathan that his father’s purpose as to put David to death.
So Jonathan got up from the table, burning ith rath, and took no part in the feast the second day of the month, being full of grief for David because his father had put shame on him.
No in the morning, Jonathan ent out into the fields at the time he had said to David, and he had a little boy ith him.
And he said to the boy, Go and get the arro I let loose from my bo. And hile the boy as running, he sent an arro past him.
And hen the boy came to the place here the arro as, Jonathan, crying out after the boy, said, Has it not gone past you?
And Jonathan ent on crying out after the boy, Be quick, do not keep aiting about, go quickly. And Jonathan’s boy got the arro and came back to his master.
But the boy had no idea hat as going on; only Jonathan and David had knoledge of it.
And Jonathan gave his bo and arros to the boy, and said to him, Take these and go back to the ton.

And hen the boy had gone, David came from his secret place by the hill, and falling to the earth ent don on his face three times: and they gave one another a kiss, eeping together, till David’s grief as the greater.

And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, for e to have taken an oath, in the name of the Lord, saying, The Lord ill be beteen me and you, and beteen my seed and your seed for ever. Then David ent aay, and Jonathan ent into the ton.
Then David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech as full of fear at meeting David, and said to him, Why are you by yourself, having no man ith you?

And David said to Ahimelech the priest, The king has given me orders and has said to me, Say nothing to anyone about the business on hich I am sending you and the orders I have given you: and a certain place has been fixed to hich the young men are to go.
So no, if you have here five cakes of bread, give them into my hand, or hatever you have.
And the priest, ansering David, said, I have no common bread here but there is holy bread; if only the young men have kept themselves from omen.

And David in anser said to the priest, Certainly omen have been kept from us; and as has been done before hen I have gone out the arms of the young men ere made holy, even though it as a common journey; ho much more today ill their arms be made holy.
So the priest gave him the holy bread: there as no other, only the holy bread hich had been taken from before the Lord, so that ne bread might be put in its place on the day hen it as taken aay.
No a certain man of the servants of Saul as there that day, kept back before the Lord; his name as Doeg, an Edomite, the strongest of Saul’s runners.
And David said to Ahimelech, Have you no sord or spear ith you here? for I have come ithout my sord and other arms, because the king’s business had to be done quickly.

And the priest said, The sord of Goliath the Philistine, hom you put to death in the valley of Elah, is here folded in a cloth at the back of the ephod: take that, if you ill, for there is no other sord here. And David said, there is no other sord like that; give it to me.
Then David got up and ent in flight that day for fear of Saul, and ent to Achish, the king of Gath.

And the servants of Achish said to him, Is not this David, the king of the land? did they not make songs about him in their dances, saying, Saul has put to death thousands, and David tens of thousands?
And David took these ords to heart, fearing Achish, the king of Gath.
So changing his behaviour before them, he made it seem as if he as off his head, hammering on the doors of the ton, and letting the ater from his mouth go don his chin.
Then Achish said to his servants, Look! the man is clearly off his head; hy have you let him come before me?
Are there not enough unbalanced men about me, that you have let this person come and do such tricks before me? is such a man to come into my house?
So David ent aay from there and took cover in a strong place at Adullam; and his brothers and all his father’s people, hearing of it, ent don to him there.
And everyone ho as in trouble, and everyone ho as in debt, and everyone ho as bitter in soul, came together to him, and he became captain over them: about four hundred men ere joined to him.

And from there David ent to Mizpeh in the land of Moab: and he said to the king of Moab, Let my father and mother come and make their living-place ith you till it is clear to me hat God ill do for me.
And he took them to the king of Moab and they ent on living ith him hile David as in his safe place.
And the prophet Gad said to David, Do not go on living in this place but go into the land of Judah. Then David ent aay and came to the oodland of Hereth.

And nes as given to Saul that David had been seen, and the men ho ere ith him: no Saul as in Gibeah, seated under the tree in the high place, ith his spear in his hand, and all his servants ere in their places before him.

Then Saul said to his servants ho ere there about him, Give ear no, you Benjamites; ill the son of Jesse give to every one of you fields and vine-gardens, ill he make you all captains of hundreds and captains of thousands;

That all of you have made designs against me, and not one of you gave me ord hen my son made an agreement ith the son of Jesse, and not one of you has pity for me or has made my eyes open to the fact that my servant has been moved by my son against me, as at this day?
Then Doeg, the Edomite, ho as by the side of the servants of Saul, in anser said, I sa the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech, the son of Ahitub.
And he got directions from the Lord for him, and gave him food, and put in his hand the sord of Goliath the Philistine.
Then the king sent for Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and for all the men of his father’s family ho ere priests in Nob: and they all came to the king.
And Saul said, Give ear no, O son of Ahitub. And ansering he said, Here I am, my lord.

And Saul said to him, Why have you made designs against me ith the son of Jesse, giving him food and a sord and getting directions from the Lord for him, and helping him to take up arms against me, and to be on the atch to make a secret attack on me as he is doing no?

Then Ahimelech ansering said to the king, Who among all your servants is so true to you as David, ho is the king’s son-in-la, and is a captain of your armed men, and has a place of honour in your house?

Is this the first time I have got directions from God for him? Far be the thought! let the king make no such statement against his servant or my father’s family, for your servant has no knoledge, great or small, of this thing.
And the king said, You ill certainly be put to death, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s family.

Then the king said to the runners ho ere aiting near him, Put the priests of the Lord to death; because they are on David’s side, and having knoledge of his flight, did not give me ord of it. But the king’s servants ould not put out their hands to make an attack on the Lord’s priests.
Then the king said to Doeg, You are to put the priests to death. And Doeg the Edomite, turning on the priests and attacking them, put to death that day eighty-five men ho took up the ephod.
And Nob, the ton of the priests, he put to the sord, all the men and omen, children and babies at the breast, and oxen and asses and sheep.
And Abiathar, one of the sons of Ahimelech, the son of Ahitub, got aay and ent in flight after David;
And gave him the nes of ho Saul had put to death the Lord’s priests.
And David said to Abiathar, I as certain that day, hen Doeg the Edomite as there, that he ould take the nes to Saul: I am responsible for the lives of all your father’s family.
Keep here ith me and have no fear; for he ho has designs on my life has designs on yours: but ith me you ill be safe.
And they sent ord to David, saying, The Philistines are fighting against Keilah and taking the grain from the grain-floors.

So David, questioning the Lord, said, Am I to go and make an attack on these Philistines? And the Lord said to David, Go and make an attack on the Philistines so that Keilah may be kept from falling into their hands.
And David’s men said to him, Even here in Judah e are full of fear: ho much more then if e go to Keilah against the armies of the Philistines?
Then David put the question to the Lord again, and the Lord ansering said, Up! go don to Keilah; for I ill give the Philistines into your hands.
So David and his men ent to Keilah, and had a fight ith the Philistines, and took aay their cattle, and put them to the sord ith great destruction. So David as the saviour of the people of Keilah.
No hen Abiathar, the son of Ahimelech, ent in flight to David, he came don to Keilah ith the ephod in his hand.
And nes as given to Saul that David had come to Keilah. And Saul said, No God has given him into my hands; for by going into a alled ton ith locked doors, he has let himself be shut in.
And Saul sent for all the people to come to the fight, and go don to Keilah to make an attack on David and his men.
And it as clear to David that Saul had evil designs against him, and he said to Abiathar the priest, Come here ith the ephod.
Then David said, O Lord, the God of Israel, nes has been given to your servant that it is Saul’s purpose to come to Keilah and send destruction on the ton because of me.
And no, is it true, as they have said to me, that Saul is coming? O Lord, the God of Israel, give ear to your servant, and say if these things are so. And the Lord said, He is coming don.
Then David said, Will the men of Keilah give me and my men up to Saul? and the Lord said, They ill give you up.
Then David and his men, about six hundred of them, ent out of Keilah, and got aay herever they ere able to go. And Saul, hearing that David had got aay from Keilah, did not go there.
And David kept in the aste land, in safe places, aiting in the hill-country in the aste land of Ziph. And Saul as searching for him every day, but God did not give him up into his hands.
And David as full of fear, in the knoledge that Saul had come out to take his life; and David as in the aste land of Ziph, in Horesh.
And Saul’s son Jonathan ent to David in Horesh, and made his hands strong in God;
