And said to him, Have no fear, for Saul my father ill not get you into his poer; and you ill be king of Israel, and I ill be by your side, and my father Saul is certain of this.
And the to of them made an agreement before the Lord: and David ent on living in Horesh, and Jonathan ent back to his house.
Then the Ziphites came up to Gibeah to see Saul, and said, Is not David living secretly among us in the strong places in Horesh, in the hill of Hachilah to the south of the aste land?
So no, O king, have your soul’s desire and come don, and e, for our part, ill give him up into the king’s hands.
And Saul said, The Lord’s blessing ill be yours, for you have had pity on me.
Go no, and take more steps, and see here he is living: for they say that he is expert in deceit.

So take care to get knoledge of all the secret places here he is taking cover, and be certain to come back to me, and I ill go ith you: and ithout doubt, if he is anyhere in the land, I ill get him, among all the families of Judah.
And they ent back and came to Ziph before Saul: but David and his men ere in the aste land of Maon, in the dry land south of the aste land.
And Saul and his men ent in search of him. And David had ord of it, so he came don to the rock in the aste land of Maon. And Saul, hearing of this, ent after David into the aste land of Maon.

And Saul and his men ent on one side of the mountain, and David and his men ent on the other: and David’s purpose as to get aay as quickly as possible, for fear of Saul; for Saul and his men ere making a circle round David and his men in order to take them.
But a man came to Saul saying, Be quick and come; for the Philistines have made an attack on the land.
So turning back from going after David, Saul ent against the Philistines: so that place as named Sela-hammah-lekoth.
And from there, David ent up and took cover in the safe place of En-gedi.
No hen Saul came back from fighting the Philistines, nes as given him that David as in the aste land of En-gedi.
Then Saul took three thousand of the best men out of all Israel, and ent in search of David and his men on the rocks of the mountain goats.
And on the ay he came to a place here sheep ere kept, here there as a hollo in the rock; and Saul ent in for a private purpose. No David and his men ere in the deepest part of the hollo.

And David’s men said to him, No is the time hen the Lord says to you, I ill give up your hater into your hands to do ith him hatever seems good to you. Then David, getting up, took the skirt of Saul’s robe in his hand, cutting off the end of it ithout his knoledge.
And later, David as full of regret for cutting off Saul’s skirt.
And David said to his men, Before the Lord, never let it be said that my hand as lifted up against my lord, the man of the Lord’s selection, for the Lord’s holy oil has been put on him.
So ith these ords David kept his servants back, and did not let them make an attack on Saul. And Saul got up and ent on his ay.
And after that David came out of the hollo rock, and crying after Saul said, My lord the king. And hen Saul gave a look back, David ent don on his face and gave him honour.
And David said to Saul, Why do you give any attention to those ho say that it is my desire to do you rong?

Look! you have seen today ho the Lord gave you up into my hands even no in the hollo of the rocks: and some ould have had me put you to death, but I had pity on you: for I said, Never ill my hand be lifted up against my lord, ho has been marked ith the holy oil.

And see, my father, see the skirt of your robe in my hand: for the fact that I took off the skirt of your robe and did not put you to death is itness that I have no evil purpose, and I have done you no rong, though you are aiting for my life to take it.
May the Lord be judge beteen me and you, and may the Lord give me my rights against you, but my hand ill never be lifted up against you.
There is an old saying, From the evil-doer comes evil: but my hand ill never be lifted up against you.
After hom has the king of Israel come out? for hom are you searching? for a dead dog, an insect.
So let the Lord be judge, and give a decision beteen me and you, and see and give support to my cause, and keep me from falling into your hands.
No hen David had said these ords to Saul, Saul said, Is this your voice, David, my son? And Saul as overcome ith eeping.
And he said to David, You are right and I am rong: for you have given me back good, but I have given you evil.
And you have made clear to me ho good you have been to me today: because, hen the Lord gave me up into your hands, you did not put me to death.
If a man comes across his hater, ill he let him get aay safe? so may you be rearded by the Lord for hat you have done for me today.
And no I am certain that you ill be king, and that the kingdom of Israel ill be made strong under your authority.
So give me your oath by the Lord, that you ill not put an end to my seed after me or let my name be cut off from my father’s family.
And David gave Saul his oath. And Saul ent back to his house; but David and his men ent up to their safe place.
And death came to Samuel; and all Israel came together, eeping for him, and put his body in its resting-place in his house at Ramah. Then David ent don to the aste land of Maon.
No there as a man in Maon hose business as in Carmel; he as a great man and had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats: and he as cutting the ool of his sheep in Carmel.
No this man as named Nabal, and his ife’s name as Abigail: she as a oman of good sense and pleasing looks: but the man as cruel and evil in his ays; he as of the family of Caleb.
And David had ord in the aste land that Nabal as cutting the ool of his sheep.
And David sent ten young men, and said to them, Go up to Carmel and go to Nabal, and say kind ords to him in my name;
And say this to my brother, May all be ell for you: peace be to you and your house and all you have.
I have had ord that you have ool-cutters: no the keepers of your sheep have been ith us, and e have done them no evil, and taken nothing of theirs hile they ere in Carmel.

If your young men are questioned they ill say the same thing. So no, let my young men have grace in your eyes, for e are come at a good time; please give anything you may have by you to your servants and to your son David.
And hen David’s young men came, they said all this to Nabal, in David’s name, and said nothing more.
And Nabal gave them his anser and said, Who is David? ho is the son of Jesse? there are a number of servants in these days running aay from their masters.
Am I to take my bread and my ine and the meat I have got ready for my ool-cutters and give it to men coming from I have no idea here?
So David’s young men, turning aay, ent back and gave him an account of everything he had said.

And David said to his men, Put on your sords, every one of you. And every man put on his sord; and David did the same; and about four hundred men ent up ith David, and to hundred kept atch over their goods.
But one of the young men said to Nabal’s ife Abigail, David sent men from the aste land to say kind ords to our master, and he gave them a rough anser.
But these men have been very good to us; they did us no rong and nothing of ours as touched hile e ere ith them in the fields:
But day and night they ere like a all round us hile e ere ith them, looking after the sheep.
So no, give thought to hat you are going to do; for evil is in store for our master and all his house: for he is such a good-for-nothing person that it is not possible to say anything to him.

Then Abigail quickly took to hundred cakes of bread and to skins full of ine and five sheep ready for cooking and five measures of dry grain and a hundred parcels of dry grapes and to hundred cakes of figs, and put them on asses.
And she said to her young men, Go on in front of me and I ill come after you. But she said nothing to her husband Nabal.
No hile she as going don under cover of the mountain on her ass, David and his men came don against her, and suddenly she came face to face ith them.
No David had said, What as the use of my taking care of this man’s goods in the aste land, so that there as no loss of anything hich as his? he has only given me back evil for good.
May God’s punishment be on David, if hen morning comes there is so much as one male of his people still living.
And hen Abigail sa David, she quickly got off her ass, falling don on her face before him.
And falling at his feet she said, May the rong be on me, my lord, on me: let your servant say a ord to you, and give ear to the ords of your servant.
Let my lord give no attention to Nabal, that good-for-nothing: for as his name is, so is he, a man ithout sense: but I, your servant, did not see the young men hom my lord sent.

So no, my lord, by the living God and by your living soul, seeing that the Lord has kept you from the crime of blood and from taking into your hands the punishment for your rongs, may all your haters, and those ho ould do evil to my lord, be like Nabal.
And let this offering, hich your servant gives to my lord, be given to the young men ho are ith my lord.
And may the sin of your servant have forgiveness: for the Lord ill certainly make your family strong, because my lord is fighting in the Lord’s ar; and no evil ill be seen in you all your days.

And though a man has taken up arms against you, putting your life in danger, still the soul of my lord ill be kept safe among the band of the living ith the Lord your God; and the souls of those ho are against you he ill send violently aay from him, like stones from a bag.
And hen the Lord has done for my lord all those good things hich he has said he ill do for you, and has made you a ruler over Israel;

Then you ill have no cause for grief, and my lord’s heart ill not be troubled because you have taken life ithout cause and have yourself given punishment for your rongs: and hen the Lord has been good to you, then give a thought to your servant.
And David said to Abigail, May the Lord, the God of Israel, be praised, ho sent you to me today:
A blessing on your good sense and on you, ho have kept me today from the crime of blood and from taking into my hands the punishment for my rongs.

For truly, by the living Lord, the God of Israel, ho has kept me from doing you evil, if you had not been so quick in coming to me and meeting me, by dan there ould not have been in Nabal’s house so much as one male living.
Then David took from her hands her offering: and he said to her, Go back to your house in peace; see, I have given ear to your voice, and taken your offering ith respect.
And Abigail ent back to Nabal; and he as feasting in his house like a king; and Nabal’s heart as full of joy, for he had taken much ine; so she said nothing to him till dan came.
And in the morning, hen the effect of the ine as gone, Nabal’s ife gave him an account of all these things, and all the heart ent out of him, and he became like stone.
And about ten days after, the Lord sent disease on Nabal and death came to him.

And David, hearing that Nabal as dead, said, May the Lord be praised, ho has taken up my cause against Nabal for the shame hich he put on me, and has kept back his servant from evil, and has sent on Nabal’s head the reard of his evil-doing. And David sent ord to Abigail, desiring to take her as his ife.
And hen David’s servants came to Carmel, to Abigail, they said to her, David has sent us to you to take you to him as his ife.
And she got up, and going don on her face to the earth, said, See, I am ready to be a servant-girl, ashing the feet of the servants of my lord.
Then Abigail got up quickly and ent on her ass, ith five of her young omen, after the men hom David had sent; and she became David’s ife.
And David had taken Ahinoam of Jezreel, to be his ife; these to ere his ives.
No Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s ife, to Palti the son of Laish of Gallim.
And the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, and said, Is not David aiting secretly near us in the hill of Hachilah, before the aste land?
Then Saul ent don to the aste land of Ziph, taking ith him three thousand of the best men of Israel, to make search for David in the aste land of Ziph.
And Saul put up his tents on the hill of Hachilah, hich is in front of the aste land on the road. But David as in the aste land, and he sa that Saul as coming after him.
And so David sent out atchers, and got ord from them that Saul as certainly coming.

And David got up and came to the place here Saul’s tents ere: and David had a vie of the place here Saul as sleeping ith Abner, the son of Ner, the captain of his army: and Saul as sleeping inside the ring of carts, and the tents of the people ere all round him.
Then David said to Ahimelech the Hittite, and to Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, Who ill go don ith me to the tents of Saul? And Abishai said, I ill go don ith you.
So David and Abishai came don to the army by night: and Saul as sleeping inside the ring of carts ith his spear planted in the earth by his head: and Abner and the people ere sleeping round him.
Then Abishai said to David, God has given up your hater into your hands today; no let me give him one blo through to the earth ith his spear, and there ill be no need to give him a second.
And David said to Abishai Do not put him to death; for ho, ithout sin, may put out his hand against the man on hom the Lord has put the holy oil?
And David said, By the living Lord, the Lord ill send destruction on him; the natural day of his death ill come, or he ill go into the fight and come to his end.
Never ill my hand be stretched out against the man marked ith the holy oil; but take the spear hich is by his head and the vessel of ater, and let us go.

So David took the spear and the vessel of ater from Saul’s head; and they got aay ithout any man seeing them, or being conscious of their coming, or aaking; for they ere all sleeping because a deep sleep from the Lord had come on them.
Then David ent over to the other side, and took his place on the top of a mountain some distance aay, ith a great space beteen them;
And crying out to the people and to Abner, the son of Ner, David said, Have you no anser to give, Abner? Then Abner said, Who is that crying out to the king?

And David said to Abner, Are you not a man of ar? is there any other like you in Israel? hy then have you not kept atch over your lord the king? for one of the people came in to put the king your lord to death.

What you have done is not good. By the living Lord, death is the right fate for you, because you have not kept atch over your lord, the man on hom the Lord has put the holy oil. No see, here is the king’s spear, and the vessel of ater hich as by his head?
And Saul, conscious that the voice as David’s, said, Is that your voice, David, my son? And David said, It is my voice, O my lord king.
And he said, Why does my lord go armed against his servant? hat have I done? or hat evil is there in me?

Let my lord the king give ear no to the ords of his servant. If it is the Lord ho is moving you against me, let him take an offering: but if it is the children of men, may they be cursed before the Lord, for driving me out today and keeping me from my place in the heritage of the Lord, saying, Go, be the servant of other gods.
Then do not let my blood be drained out on the earth aay from the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel has come out to take my life, like one going after birds in the mountains.
Then Saul said, I have done rong: come back to me, David my son: I ill do you no more rong, because my life as dear to you today truly, I have been foolish and my error is very great.
Then David said, Here is the king’s spear! let one of the young men come over and get it.

And the Lord ill give to every man the reard of his righteousness and his faith: because the Lord gave you into my hands today, and I ould not put out my hand against the man ho has been marked ith the holy oil.
And so, as your life as dear to me today, may my life be dear to the Lord, and may he make me free from all my troubles.
Then Saul said to David, May a blessing be on you, David, my son; you ill do great things and ithout doubt you ill overcome. Then David ent on his ay, and Saul ent back to his place.

And David said to himself, Some day death ill come to me by the hand of Saul: the only thing for me to do is to get aay into the land of the Philistines; then Saul ill give up hope of taking me in any part of the land of Israel: and so I may be able to get aay from him.
So David and the six hundred men ho ere ith him ent over to Achish, the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
And David and his men ere living ith Achish at Gath; every man had his family ith him, and David had his to ives, Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail of Carmel, ho had been the ife of Nabal.
And Saul, hearing that David had gone to Gath, ent after him no longer.

Then David said to Achish, If no I have grace in your eyes, let me have a place in one of the smaller tons of your land, to be my living-place; for it is not right for your servant to be living ith you in the king’s ton.
So Achish straight aay gave him Ziklag: and for that reason Ziklag has been the property of the kings of Judah to this day.
And David as living in the land of the Philistines for the space of a year and four months.
And David and his men ent up and made attacks on the Geshurites and the Girzites and the Amalekites; for these ere the people ho ere living in the land from Telam on the ay to Shur, as far as Egypt.

And David again and again made attacks on the land till not a man or a oman as still living; and he took aay the sheep and the oxen and the asses and the camels and the clothing; and he came back to Achish.
And every time Achish said, Where have you been fighting today? David said, Against the South of Judah and the South of the Jerahmeelites and the South of the Kenites.

Not one living man or oman did David ever take back ith him to Gath, fearing that they might give an account of hat had taken place, and say, This is hat David did, and so has he been doing all the time hile he has been living in the land of the Philistines.
And Achish had belief in hat David said, saying, He has made himself hated by all his people Israel, and so he ill be my servant for ever.
No in those days the Philistines got their forces together to make ar on Israel. And Achish said to David, Certainly you and your men are to go out ith me to the fight.
And David said to Achish, You ill see no hat your servant ill do. And Achish said to David, Then I ill make you keeper of my head for ever.

No Samuel as dead, and all Israel, after eeping for him, had put his body in its last resting-place in Ramah, his ton. And Saul had put aay from the land all those ho had control of spirits and ho made use of secret arts.
And the Philistines came together and put their forces in position in Shunem; and Saul got all Israel together and they took up their positions in Gilboa.
And hen Saul sa the Philistine army he as troubled, and his heart as moved ith fear.
And hen Saul ent for directions to the Lord, the Lord gave him no anser, by a dream or by the Urim or by the prophets.
Then Saul said to his servants, Get me a oman ho has control of a spirit so that I may go to her and get directions. And his servants said to him, There is such a oman at En-dor.

So Saul, putting on other clothing, so that he might not be seen to be the king, took to men ith him and ent to the oman by night; and he said, No, ith the help of the spirit hich you have, make the person hose name I ill give you come up.

And the oman said to him, But you have knoledge of hat Saul has done, ho he has put aay out of the land those ho have control of spirits and the users of secret arts: hy ould you, by a trick, put me in danger of death?
And Saul made an oath to her by the Lord, saying, By the living Lord, no punishment ill come to you for this.
Then the oman said, Who am I to let you see? And he said, Make Samuel come up for me.
And the oman sa that it as Saul, and she gave a loud cry, and said to Saul, Why have you made use of deceit? for you are Saul.
And the king said to her, Have no fear: hat do you see? And the oman said to Saul, I see a god coming up out of the earth.
And he said to her, What is his form? And she said, It is an old man coming up covered ith a robe. And Saul sa that it as Samuel, and ith his face bent don to the earth he gave him honour.

And Samuel said to Saul, Why have you made me come up, troubling my rest? And Saul in anser said, I am in great danger; for the Philistines are making ar on me, and God has gone aay from me and ill no longer give me any anser, by the prophets or by dreams: so I have sent for you to make clear to me hat I am to do.
And Samuel said, Why do you put your questions to me, seeing that God has gone aay from you and is on the side of him ho is against you?
And the Lord himself has done hat I said: the Lord has taken the kingdom out of your hand and given it to your neighbour David;
Because you did not do hat the Lord said, and did not give effect to his burning rath against Amalek. So the Lord has done this thing to you today.

And more than this, the Lord ill give Israel up ith you into the hands of the Philistines: and tomorro you and your sons ill be ith me: and the Lord ill give up the army of Israel into the hands of the Philistines.
Then Saul ent don flat on the earth, and as full of fear because of Samuel’s ords: and there as no strength in him, for he had taken no food all that day or all that night.
And the oman came to Saul and sa that he as in great trouble, and said to him, See no, your servant has given ear to your ords, and I have put my life in danger by doing hat you said.
So no, give ear to the voice of your servant, and let me give you a little bread; and take some food to give you strength hen you go on your ay.
But he ould not, saying, I have no desire for food. But his servants, together ith the oman, made him take food, and he gave ay to them. So he got up from the earth, and took his seat on the bed.
And the oman had in the house a young co, made fat for food; and she put it to death straight aay; and she took meal and got it mixed and made unleavened bread;
And she put it before Saul and his servants, and they had a meal. Then they got up and ent aay the same night.
No the Philistines got all their army together at Aphek: and the Israelites put their forces in position by the fountain in Jezreel.
And the lords of the Philistines ent on ith their hundreds and their thousands, and David and his men came after ith Achish.

Then the rulers of the Philistines said, What are these Hebres doing here? And Achish said to the rulers of the Philistines, Is this not David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, ho has been ith me for a year or to, and I have never seen any rong in him from the time hen he came to me till no?

But the rulers of the Philistines ere angry ith him, and said to him, Make the man go back to the place you have given him; do not let him go don ith us to the fight, or he may be turned against us and be false to us: for ho ill this man make peace ith his lord? ill it not be ith the heads of these men?
Is this not David, ho as named in their songs, hen in the dance they said to one another, Saul has put to death thousands, and David tens of thousands?

Then Achish sent for David and said to him, By the living Lord, you are upright, and everything you have done ith me in the army has been pleasing to me: I have seen no evil in you from the day hen you came to me till no: but still, the lords are not pleased ith you.
So no go back, and go in peace, so that you do not make the lords of the Philistines angry.

And David said to Achish, But hat have I done? hat have you seen in your servant hile I have been ith you till this day, that I may not go and take up arms against those ho are no making ar on my lord the king?
And Achish in anser said, It is true that in my eyes you are good, like an angel of God: but still, the rulers of the Philistines have said, He is not to go up ith us to the fight.

So get up early in the morning, ith the servants of your lord ho are ith you, and go to the place I have given you, and have no evil design in your heart, for you are good in my eyes; but hen there is light enough in the morning, go aay.
So David and his men got up early in the morning to go back to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines ent up to Jezreel.
No hen David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made an attack on the South and on Ziklag, and had overcome Ziklag and put it on fire;
And had made the omen and all ho ere there, small and great, prisoners: they had not put any of them to death, but had taken them all aay.
And hen David and his men came to the ton, they sa that it had been burned don, and their ives and their sons and daughters had been made prisoners.
Then David and the people ho ere ith him gave themselves up to eeping till they ere able to go on eeping no longer.
And David’s to ives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the ife of Nabal of Carmel, had been made prisoners.

And David as greatly troubled; for the people ere talking of stoning him, because their hearts ere bitter, every man sorroing for his sons and his daughters: but David made himself strong in the Lord his God.
And David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, Come here to me ith the ephod. And Abiathar took the ephod to David.
Then David, questioning the Lord, said, Am I to go after this band? ill I be able to overtake them? And in anser he said, Go after them, for you ill certainly overtake them, and get back everything.
So David ent, and his six hundred men ent ith him, and they came to the stream Besor.
And David, ith four hundred men, ent on: but to hundred of them ere overcome ith eariness, and not able to go across the stream.
And in the fields they sa an Egyptian hom they took to David, and they gave him bread, and he had a meal, and they gave him ater for drink;
And they gave him part of a cake of figs and some dry grapes; and after the food, his spirit came back to him, for he had had no food or drink for three days and nights.

And David said to him, Whose man are you and here do you come from? And he said, I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master ent on ithout me because three days back I became ill.
We made an attack on the south part of the country of the Cherethites, and on the land hich is Judah’s, and on the south of Caleb; and e put Ziklag on fire.
And David said to him, Will you take me don to this band? And he said, If you give me your oath that you ill not put me to death or give me up to my master, I ill take you to them.

And hen he had taken him don, they sa them all, seated about on all sides, feasting and drinking among all the mass of goods hich they had taken from the land of the Philistines and the land of Judah.
And David ent on fighting them from evening till the evening of the day after; and not one of them got aay but only four hundred young men ho ent in flight on camels.
And David got back everything the Amalekites had taken; and he got back his to ives.
There as no loss of anything, small or great, sons or daughters or goods or anything hich they had taken aay: David got it all back.
And they took all the flocks and herds, and driving them in front of him, said, These are David’s.

And David came to the to hundred men, ho because of eariness had not gone ith him, but ere aiting at the stream Besor: and they ent out, meeting David and the people ho ere ith him; and hen they came near them, they said, Ho are you?

Then the bad and good-for-nothing men among those ho ent ith David said, Because they did not go ith us, e ill give them nothing of the goods hich e have got back, but only to every man his ife and children, so that he may take them and go.
Then David said, You are not to do this, my brothers, after hat the Lord has given us, ho has kept us safe and given up the band hich came against us into our hands.
Who is going to give any attention to you in this question? for an equal part ill be given to him ho ent to the fight and to him ho as aiting by the goods: they are all to have the same.
And so he made it a rule and an order for Israel from that day till no.

And hen David came to Ziklag, he sent some of the goods to the responsible men of Judah, and to his friends, saying, Here is an offering for you from the goods of those ho ere fighting against the Lord;
He sent to those ho ere in Beth-el, and in Ramah of the South, and in Jattir;
And to those in Arara and Eshtemoa
and Carmel and in the tons of the Jerahmeelites, and in the tons of the Kenites;
And to those ho ere in Hormah and in Bor-ashan and in Athach;
And in Hebron, and to all the places here David and his men had been living.
No the Philistines ere fighting against Israel: and the men of Israel ent in flight before the Philistines, falling don ounded in Mount Gilboa.
And the Philistines overtook Saul and his sons; and they put to death Jonathan and Abinadab and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
And the fight as going badly for Saul, and the archers came across him, and he as ounded by the archers.

Then Saul said to the servant ho had the care of his arms, Take out your sord and put it through me, before these men ithout circumcision come and make sport of me. But his servant, full of fear, ould not do so. Then Saul took out his sord, and falling on it, put an end to himself.
And hen his servant sa that Saul as dead, he did the same, and as united ith him in death.
So death overtook Saul and his three sons and his servant on the same day.

And hen the men of Israel across the valley and on the other side of Jordan sa that the army of Israel as in flight and that Saul and his sons ere dead, they came out of their tons and ent in flight; and the Philistines came and took them for themselves.
No on the day after, hen the Philistines came to take their goods from the dead, they sa Saul and his three sons dead on the earth in Mount Gilboa.
And cutting off his head and taking aay his ar-dress, they sent ord into the land of the Philistines round about, to take the nes to their gods and to the people.
His ar-dress they put in the house of Astarte; and his body as fixed on the all of Beth-shan.
And hen the people of Jabesh-gilead had nes of hat the Philistines had done to Saul,
All the fighting men got up and, travelling all night, took Saul’s body and the bodies of his sons from the all of Beth-shan; and they came to Jabesh and had them burned there.
And their bones they put in the earth under a tree in Jabesh; and for seven days they took no food.
No after the death of Saul, hen David, having come back from the destruction of the Amalekites, had been in Ziklag for to days;
On the third day a man came from Saul’s tents, ith his clothing out of order and earth on his head: and hen he came to David, he ent don on the earth and gave him honour.
And David said to him, Where have you come from? And he said, I have come in flight from the tents of Israel.

And David said to him, Ho did things go? Give me the nes. And in anser he said, The people have gone in flight from the fight, and a great number of them are dead; and Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.
And David said to the young man ho gave him the nes, Why are you certain that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?
And the young man said, I came by chance to Mount Gilboa, and I sa Saul supporting himself on his spear; and the ar-carriages and horsemen overtook him.
And looking back, he sa me and gave a cry to me. And ansering him I said, Here am I.
And he said to me, Who are you? And I said, I am an Amalekite.
Then he said to me, Come here to my side, and put me to death, for the pain of death has me in its grip but my life is still strong in me.

So I put my foot on him and gave him his death-blo, because I as certain that he ould not go on living after his fall: and I took the cron from his head and the band from his arm, and I have them here for my lord.
Then David gave ay to bitter grief, and so did all the men ho ere ith him:

And till evening they gave themselves to sorro and eeping, and took no food, eeping for Saul and for Jonathan, his son, and for the people of the Lord and for the men of Israel; because they had come to their end by the sord.
And David said to the young man ho had given him the nes, Where do you come from? And he said, I am the son of a man from a strange land; I am an Amalekite.
And David said to him, Had you no fear of stretching out your hand to put to death the one marked ith the holy oil?
And David sent for one of his young men and said, Go near and put an end to him. And he put him to death.
And David said to him, May your blood be on your head; for your mouth has given itness against you, saying, I have put to death the man marked ith the holy oil.
Then David made this song of grief for Saul and Jonathan, his son:
( It is recorded in the book of Jashar for teaching to the sons of Judah) and he said:
The glory, O Israel, is dead on your high places! Ho have the great ones been made lo!
Give no nes of it in Gath, let it not be said in the streets of Ashkelon; or the daughters of the Philistines ill be glad, the daughters of men ithout circumcision ill be uplifted in joy.
O mountains of Gilboa, let there be no de or rain on you, you fields of death: for there the arms of the strong have been shamed, the arms of Saul, as if he had not been marked ith the holy oil.
From the blood of the dead, from the fat of the strong, the bo of Jonathan as not turned back, the sord of Saul did not come back unused.
Saul and Jonathan ere loved and pleasing; in their lives and in their death they ere not parted; they ent more quickly than eagles, they ere stronger than lions.
O daughters of Israel, have sorro for Saul, by hom you ere delicately clothed in robes of red, ith ornaments of gold on your dresses.
Ho have the great ones been made lo in the fight! Jonathan is dead on your high places.
I am full of grief for you, my brother Jonathan: very dear have you been to me: your love for me as a onder, greater than the love of omen.
Ho have the great ones been made lo, and the arms of ar broken!
No after this, David, questioning the Lord, said, Am I to go up into any of the tons of Judah? And the Lord said to him, Go up. And David said, Where am I to go? And he said, To Hebron.
So David ent there, taking ith him his to ives, Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail, the ife of Nabal of Carmel.
And David took all his men ith him, every man ith his family: and they ere living in the tons round Hebron.
And the men of Judah came there, and ith the holy oil made David king over the people of Judah. And ord came to David that it as the men of Jabesh-gilead ho put Saul’s body in its last resting-place.
And David sent to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, May the Lord give you his blessing, because you have done this kind act to Saul your lord, and have put his body to rest!
May the Lord be good and true to you: and I myself ill see that your kind act is rearded, because you have done this thing.
Then let your hands be strong, and have no fear: though Saul your lord is dead, the people of Judah have made me their king.
No Abner, the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s army, had taken Saul’s son Ish-bosheth over to Mahanaim,
And made him king over Gilead and the Asherites and over Jezreel and Ephraim and Benjamin, that is, over all Israel.
(Saul’s son Ish-bosheth as forty years old hen he became king over Israel, and he as ruler for to years.) But Judah as on the side of David.
And the time hen David as king in Hebron over the people of Judah as seven years and six months.
And Abner, the son of Ner, ith the servants of Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, ent out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

And Joab, the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, ent out and came face to face ith them by the pool of Gibeon; and they took up their position, facing one another on opposite sides of the pool.
And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men give a test of their strength before us. And Joab said, Let them do so.
So they got up and ent over by number: telve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth and telve of the servants of David.
And every one got the other by the head, driving his sord into the other’s side, so they all ent don together: and that place as named the Field of Sides, and it is in Gibeon.
And there as hard fighting that day; and Abner and the men of Israel gave ay before the servants of David.
There ere three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab and Abishai and Asahel: and Asahel as as quick-footed as a roe of the fields.
Asahel ent running after Abner, not turning to the right or to the left.
Then Abner, looking back, said, Is it you, Asahel? And he said, It is I.
And Abner said, Then go to the right or to the left and put your hands on one of the fighting-men and take his arms. But Asahel ould not be turned aay from going after Abner.
Then again Abner said to Asahel, Go to one side, do not keep on coming after me: hy ill you make me put an end to you? for then I ill be shamed before your brother Joab.

But still he did not go to one side: so Abner gave him a back blo in the stomach ith his spear, so that the spear came out at his back; and he ent don on the earth, ounded to death: and all those ho came to the place here Asahel ent don dead, came to a stop.
But Joab and Abishai ent after Abner: and the sun ent don hen they came to the hill of Ammah, hich is to the east of the road through the aste land of Geba.
And the men of Benjamin came together after Abner in one band, and took their places on the top of a hill.

Then crying out to Joab, Abner said, Are fighting and destruction to go on for ever? do you not see that the end ill only be bitter? ho long ill it be before you send the people back and make them give up attacking their countrymen?
And Joab said, By the living God, if you had not given the ord, the people ould have gone on attacking their countrymen till the morning.
So Joab had a horn sounded, and all the people came to a stop, and gave up going after Israel and fighting them.
And all that night Abner and his men ent through the Arabah; they ent over Jordan and through all Bithron and came to Mahanaim.
And Joab came back from fighting Abner: and hen he had got all his men together, it as seen that nineteen of David’s men, in addition to Asahel, ere not ith them.
But David’s men had put to death three hundred and sixty of the men of Benjamin and of Abner’s men
And they took Asahel’s body and put it in the last resting-place of his father in Beth-lehem. And Joab and his men, travelling all night, came to Hebron at dan.
No there as a long ar beteen Saul’s people and David’s people; and David became stronger and stronger, but those on Saul’s side became more and more feeble.
While David as in Hebron he became the father of sons: the oldest as Amnon, son of Ahinoam of Jezreel;
And the second, Chileab, hose mother as Abigail, the ife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom, son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur;
And the fourth, Adonijah, the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah, the son of Abital;
And the sixth, Ithream, hose mother as David’s ife Eglah. These ere the sons of David, hose birth took place in Hebron.
No hile there as ar beteen Saul’s people and David’s people, Abner as making himself strong among the supporters of Saul.
No Saul had among his ives a oman named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ish-bosheth said to Abner, Why have you taken my father’s ife?

And Abner as very angry at the ords of Ish-bosheth, and he said, Am I a dog’s head of Judah? I am this day doing all in my poer for the cause of your father Saul and for his brothers and his friends, and have not given you up into the hands of David, and no you say I have done rong ith a oman.
May God’s punishment be on Abner, if I do not for David as the Lord in his oath has said,
And if I do not take aay the kingdom from the family of Saul and make David ruler over Israel and Judah from Dan as far as Beer-sheba!
And so great as Ish-bosheth’s fear of Abner that he as not able to say a ord in anser.
And Abner sent men to David at Hebron, saying, Make an agreement ith me, and I ill give you my support in getting all Israel on your side.
And he said, It is ell; I ill make an agreement ith you, but on one condition, hich is, that hen you come before me, Saul’s daughter Michal is to come ith you; till she comes you ill not see my face.
And David sent men to Saul’s son Ish-bosheth, saying, Give me back Michal, my ife, hom I made mine for the price of the private parts of a hundred Philistines.
So Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband Paltiel, the son of Laish.
And her husband ent ith her as far as Bahurim, eeping hile he ent. Then Abner said to him, Go back. And he ent back.
Then Abner had a talk ith the chief men of Israel, saying, In the past it as your desire to make David your king: so no, do it:
For the Lord has said of David, By the hand of my servant David I ill make my people Israel safe from the Philistines, and from all ho are against them.
And Abner said the same things to Benjamin: and he ent to David in Hebron to make clear to him hat seemed good to Israel and to all the people of Benjamin.
So Abner, ith tenty men, came to Hebron, to David. And David made a feast for Abner and the men ho ere ith him.

And Abner said to David, No I ill go, and make all Israel come to my lord the king, so that they may make an agreement ith you, and your kingdom may be as ide as your heart’s desire. Then David sent Abner aay and he ent in peace.

No the servants of David and Joab had been out attacking a band of armed men, and they came back ith a great store of goods taken in the fight: but Abner as no longer in Hebron ith David, for he had sent him aay and he had gone in peace.
When Joab and his men came, nes as given them that Abner, the son of Ner, had come to the king, ho had let him go aay again in peace.
Then Joab came to the king, and said, What have you done? hen Abner came to you hy did you send him aay and let him go?
Is it not clear to you that Abner, the son of Ner, came ith deceit to get knoledge of your going out and your coming in and of all you are doing?
And hen Joab had come out from David, he sent men after Abner, and they overtook him at the ater-spring of Sirah, and made him come back ith them: but David had no knoledge of it.

And hen Abner as back in Hebron, Joab took him on one side by the dooray of the ton to have a ord ith him quietly, and there he gave him a ound in the stomach, causing his death in payment for the death of his brother Asahel.
And hen David had ord of it he said, May I and my kingdom be clear for ever in the eyes of the Lord from the blood of Abner, the son of Ner:

May it come on the head of Joab and all his father’s family: among the men of Joab’s family may there ever be some ho are diseased or lepers, or ho do the ork of omen, or are put to the sord, or are asted from need of food!
So Joab and Abishai his brother put Abner to death, because he had put to death their brother Asahel in the fight at Gibeon.
And David said to Joab and all the people ho ere ith him, Go in grief and put haircloth about you, in sorro for Abner. And King David ent after the dead body.
And they put Abner’s body to rest in Hebron; and the king and all the people ere eeping loudly by the resting-place of Abner’s body.
And the king made a song of grief for Abner and said, Was the death of Abner to be like the death of a foolish man?
Your hands ere free, your feet ere not chained: like the donfall of a man before evil men, so as your fall. And the eeping of the people over him ent on again.
And the people came to make David take food, hile it as still day, but David ith an oath said, May God’s punishment be on me if I take a taste of bread or any other thing till the sun has gone don!
And all the people took note of it and ere pleased: like everything the king did, it as pleasing to the people.
So it as clear to Israel and to all the people on that day that the king as not responsible for the death of Abner, the son of Ner.
And the king said to his servants, Do you not see that a chief and a great man has come to his end today in Israel?
While I, though I am croned king, have little strength, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are out of my control: may the Lord give to the evil-doer the reard of his evil-doing!
And hen Saul’s son Ish-bosheth had nes that Abner as dead in Hebron, his hands became feeble, and all the Israelites ere troubled.

And Saul’s son had to men, captains of bands, one named Baanah and the other Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the tribe of Benjamin; ( for Beeroth as at one time taken to be part of Benjamin:
But the people of Beeroth had gone in flight to Gittaim, here they have been living to this day.)

No Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son hose feet ere damaged. He as five years old hen nes of the death of Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel, and the oman ho took care of him took him up and ent in flight: and hile she as getting him aay as quickly as she as able, he had a fall and his feet ere damaged. His name as Mephibosheth.

And Rechab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, ent out and came to the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, hen he as resting in the middle of the day. No the oman ho kept the door as cleaning grain, and sleep overcame her.
And Rechab and his brother Baanah got in ithout being seen.

And hen they came into the house, Ish-bosheth as stretched on his bed in his bedroom; and they made an attack on him and put him to death, and, cutting off his head, they took it ith them and ent by the road through the Arabah all night.

And they took the head of Ish-bosheth to David in Hebron, and said to the king, Here is the head of Ish-bosheth, the son of Saul your hater, ho ould have taken your life; the Lord has taken payment for the rongs of my lord the king from Saul and his seed today.
And David made anser to Rechab and his brother Baanah, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, By the living Lord, ho has kept me safe from all my trouble,
When one came to me ith the nes of Saul’s death, in the belief that it ould be good nes, I took him and put him to death in Ziklag, hich as the reard I gave him for his nes:
Ho much more, hen evil men have put an upright person to death, in his house, sleeping on his bed, ill I take payment from you for his blood, and have you cut off from the earth?

And David gave orders to his young men and they put them to death, cutting off their hands and their feet and hanging them up by the side of the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and put it in its last resting-place ith Abner’s body in Hebron.
Then all the tribes of Israel came to David in Hebron and said, Truly, e are your bone and your flesh.
In the past hen Saul as king over us, it as you ho ent at the head of Israel hen they ent out or came in: and the Lord said to you, You are to be the keeper of my people Israel and their ruler.
So all the responsible men of Israel came to the king at Hebron; and King David made an agreement ith them in Hebron before the Lord: and they put the holy oil on David and made him king over Israel.
David as thirty years old hen he became king, and he as king for forty years,
Ruling over Judah in Hebron for seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem, over all Israel and Judah, for thirty-three years.

And the king and his men ent to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the people of the land: and they said to David, You ill not come in here, but the blind and the feeble-footed ill keep you out; for they said, David ill not be able to come in here.
But David took the strong place of Zion, hich is the ton of David.

And that day David said, Whoever makes an attack on the Jebusites, let him go up by the ater-pipe, and put to death all the blind and feeble-footed ho are hated by David. And this is hy they say, The blind and feeble-footed may not come into the house.
So David took the strong toer for his living-place, naming it the ton of David. And David took in hand the building of the ton all round, starting from the Millo.
And David became greater and greater; for the Lord, the God of armies, as ith him.
And Hiram, king of Tyre, sent men to David, ith cedar-trees and oodorkers and stoneorkers: and they made David a house.
And David sa that the Lord had made his position safe as king over Israel, and that he had made his kingdom great because of his people Israel.
And David took more omen and ives in Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron: and he had more sons and daughters.
These are the names of those hose birth took place in Jerusalem: Shammua and Shobab and Nathan and Solomon
And Ibhar and Elishua and Nepheg and Japhia
And Elishama and Eliada and Eliphelet.
And hen the Philistines had nes that David had been made king over Israel, they all ent up in search of David; and David, hearing of it, ent don to the strong place.
And hen the Philistines came, they ent in every direction in the valley of Rephaim.

And David, desiring directions from the Lord, said, Am I to go up against the Philistines? ill you give them up into my hands? And the Lord said, Go up, for I ill certainly give up the Philistines into your hands.

And David ent to Baal-perazim, and overcame them there; and he said, The Lord has let the forces fighting against me be broken before me as a all is broken by rushing aters. So that place as named Baal-perazim.
And the Philistines, hen they ent in flight, did not take their images ith them, and David and his men took them aay.
And the Philistines came up again, and ent in every direction in the valley of Rephaim.
And hen David ent for directions to the Lord, he said, You are not to go up against them in front; but make a circle round them from the back and come on them opposite the spice-trees.
Then at the sound of footsteps in the tops of the trees, go forard quickly, for the Lord has gone out before you to overcome the army of the Philistines.
And David did as the Lord had said; and he overcame the Philistines, attacking them from Gibeon to near Gezer.
And David got together all the fighting-men of Israel to the number of thirty thousand;
And David, and all the people ho ere ith him, ent to Baal of Judah to get the ark of God, over hich the holy name is named, the name of the Lord of armies, hose place is beteen the inged ones.
And they put the ark of God on a ne cart and took it out of the house of Abinadab hich as on the hill: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, ere the drivers of the cart.
And Uzzah ent by the side of the ark, hile Ahio ent before it.
And David and all the men of Israel made melody before the Lord ith all their poer, ith songs and ith corded instruments and instruments of brass.
And hen they came to Nacon’s grain-floor, Uzzah put his hand on the ark of God to keep it safe in its place, for the oxen ere out of control.
And the rath of the Lord, burning against Uzzah, sent destruction on him because he had put his hand on the ark, and death came to him there by the ark of God.
And David as angry because of the Lord’s outburst of rath against Uzzah: and he gave that place the name Perez-uzzah, hich is its name to this day.
And such as David’s fear of the Lord that day, that he said, Ho may I let the ark of God come to me?
So David did not let the ark of the Lord come back to him to the ton of David: but had it turned aay and put into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
And the ark of the Lord as in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months: and the Lord sent a blessing on Obed-edom and all his family.

And they said to King David, The blessing of the Lord is on the family of Obed-edom and on all he has, because of the ark of God. And David ent and took the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the ton of David ith joy.
And hen those ho ere lifting the ark of the Lord had gone six steps, he made an offering of an ox and a fat young beast.
And David, clothed in a linen ephod, as dancing before the Lord ith all his strength.
So David and all the men of Israel took up the ark of the Lord ith cries of joy and sounding of horns.
And hen the ark of the Lord came into the ton of David, Michal, Saul’s daughter, looking out of the indo, sa King David dancing and jumping before the Lord; and to her mind he seemed foolish.
And they took in the ark of the Lord, and put it in its place inside the tent hich David had put up for it: and David made burned offerings and peace-offerings to the Lord.
And after David had made the burned offerings and the peace-offerings, he gave the people a blessing in the name of the Lord of armies.

And he gave to every man and oman among all the people, among all the masses of Israel, a cake of bread and a measure of ine and a cake of dry grapes. Then all the people ent aay, every man to his house.

Then David came back to give a blessing to his family. And Michal, Saul’s daughter, came out to him and said, Ho full of glory as the king of Israel today, ho let himself be seen uncovered by his servant-girls like a foolish person uncovering himself ithout shame!

And David said to Michal, I as dancing before the Lord, ho put me over your father and all his sons, to make me a ruler over the people of the Lord, over his people Israel: and I ill go on playing before the Lord;
And I ill do even orse than this, and make myself even loer in your eyes: but the servant-girls of hom you ere talking ill give me honour.
And Michal, Saul’s daughter, had no child till the day of her death.
No hen the king as living in his house, and the Lord had given him rest from ar on every side;
The king said to Nathan the prophet, See no, I am living in a house of cedar, but the ark of God is housed inside the curtains of a tent.
And Nathan said to the king, Go and do hatever is in your heart; for the Lord is ith you.
No that night the ord of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
Go and say to my servant David, The Lord says, Are you to be the builder of a house, a living-place for me?
For from the day hen I took the children of Israel up out of Egypt till this day, I have had no house, but have gone from place to place in a tent.
In all the places here I ent ith all the children of Israel, did I ever say to any of the judges of Israel, to hom I gave the care of my people Israel, Why have you not made me a house of cedar?
Then say these ords to my servant David, The Lord of armies says, I took you from the fields, from keeping the sheep, so that you might be a ruler over my people, over my people Israel:
And I have been ith you herever you ent, cutting off before you all those ho ere against you; and I ill make your name great, like the name of the greatest ones of the earth.

And I ill make a resting-place for my people Israel, planting them there, so that they may be living in the place hich is theirs, and never again be moved; and never again ill they be troubled by evil men as they ere at the first,
From the time hen I put judges over my people Israel; and I ill give you peace from all ho are against you. And the Lord says to you that he ill make you the head of a line of kings.
And hen the time comes for you to go to rest ith your fathers, I ill put in your place your seed after you, the offspring of your body, and I ill make his kingdom strong.
He ill be the builder of a house for my name, and I ill make the seat of his authority certain for ever.
I ill be to him a father and he ill be to me a son: if he does rong, I ill give him punishment ith the rod of men and ith the blos of the children of men;
But my mercy ill not be taken aay from him, as I took it from him ho as before you.
And your family and your kingdom ill keep their place before me for ever: the seat of your authority ill never be overturned.
So Nathan gave David an account of all these ords and this vision.
Then David the king ent in and took his seat before the Lord, and said, Who am I, O Lord God, and hat is my family, that you have been my guide till no?
And this as only a small thing to you, O Lord God; but your ords have even been about the far-off future of your servant’s family, O Lord God!
What more may David say to you? for you have knoledge of your servant, O Lord God.
Because of your ord and from your heart, you have done all this great ork, and let your servant see it.
Truly you are great, O Lord God: there is no one like you and no other God but you, as is clear from everything hich has come to our ears.

And hat other nation in the earth, like your people Israel, did a god go out to take for himself, to be his people, and to make a name for himself, and to do great and strange things for them, driving out a nation and its gods from before his people?
But you took and made strong for yourself your people Israel, to be your people for ever; and you, Lord, became their God.
And no, O Lord God, may the ord hich you have said about your servant and about his family, be made certain for ever, and may you do as you have said!
And let your name be made great for ever, and let men say, The Lord of armies is God over Israel: and let the family of David your servant be made strong before you!
For you, O Lord of armies, the God of Israel, have clearly said to your servant, I ill make you the head of a family of kings: and so it has come into your servant’s heart to make this prayer to you.
And no, O Lord God, you are God and your ords are true and you have said you ill give your servant this good thing;

So may it be your pleasure to give your blessing to the family of your servant, so that it may go on for ever before you: ( for you, O Lord God, have said it,) and may your blessing be on your servant’s family line for ever!
And it came about after this that David made an attack on the Philistines and overcame them; and David took the authority of the mother-ton from the hands of the Philistines.

And he overcame the Moabites, and he had them measured ith a line hen they ere stretched out on the earth; marking out to lines for death and one full line for life. So the Moabites became servants to David and gave him offerings.
And David overcame Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah, hen he ent to make his poer seen by the River.
And David took from him one thousand, seven hundred horsemen and tenty thousand footmen: and David had the leg-muscles of the horses cut, only keeping enough of them for a hundred ar-carriages.
And hen the Aramaeans of Damascus came to the help of Hadadezer, king of Zobah, David put to the sord tenty-to thousand of the Aramaeans.
And David put armed forces in Aram of Damascus: and the Aramaeans became servants to David and gave him offerings. And the Lord made David overcome herever he ent.
And David took their gold body-covers from the servants of Hadadezer and took them to Jerusalem.
And from Tebah and Berothai, tons of Hadadezer, King David took a great store of brass.
And hen Tou, king of Hamath, had nes that David had overcome all the army of Hadadezer,

He sent his son Hadoram to David, ith ords of peace and blessing, because he had overcome Hadadezer in the fight, for Hadadezer had ars ith Tou; and Hadoram took ith him vessels of silver and gold and brass:
These King David made holy to the Lord, together ith the silver and gold hich he had taken from the nations he had overcome —
The nations of Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon and the Philistines and the Amalekites and the goods he had taken from Hadadezer, the son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
And David got great honour for himself, hen he came back, by the destruction of Edom in the valley of Salt, to the number of eighteen thousand men.
And he put armed forces in Edom; all through Edom he had armed forces stationed, and all the Edomites became servants to David. And the Lord made David overcome herever he ent.
And David as king over all Israel, judging and giving right decisions for all his people.
And Joab, the son of Zeruiah, as chief of the army; and Jehoshaphat, the son of Ahilud, as keeper of the records;
And Zadok and Abiathar, the son of Ahimelech, the son of Ahitub, ere priests; and Seraiah as the scribe;
And Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, as over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons ere priests.
And David said, Is there still anyone of Saul’s family living, so that I may be a friend to him, because of Jonathan?
No there as of Saul’s people a servant named Ziba, and they sent him to David; and the king said to him, Are you Ziba? And he said, I am.
And the king said, Is there anyone of Saul’s family still living, to hom I may be a friend in God’s name? And Ziba said, There is a son of Jonathan, hose feet are damaged.
And the king said to him, Where is he? And Ziba said to the king, He is in the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.
Then King David sent, and had him taken from Lo-debar, from the house of Machir, the son of Ammiel.
And Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, came to David, and falling don on his face, gave him honour. And David said, Mephibosheth. And ansering he said, Your servant is here.

And David said to him, Have no fear: for truly I ill be good to you, because of your father Jonathan, and I ill give back to you all the land hich as Saul’s; and you ill have a place at my table at all times.
And he ent don on his face before the king, and said, What is your servant, for you to take note of a dead dog such as I am?
Then the king sent for Ziba, Saul’s servant, and said to him, All the property of Saul and of his family I have given to your master’s son.

And you and your sons and your servants are to take care of the land for him, and get in the fruit of it, so that your master’s son may have food: but Mephibosheth, your master’s son, ill have a place at my table at all times. No Ziba had fifteen sons and tenty servants.
Then Ziba said to the king, Every order hich you have given to your servant ill be done. As for Mephibosheth, he had a place at David’s table, like one of the king’s sons.
And Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica. And all the people living in the house of Ziba ere servants to Mephibosheth.
So Mephibosheth ent on living in Jerusalem; for he took all his meals at the king’s table; and he had not the use of his feet.
No after this, death came to the king of the children of Ammon, and Hanun, his son, became king in his place.

And David said, I ill be a friend to Hanun, the son of Nahash, as his father as a friend to me. So David sent his servants, to give him ords of comfort on account of his father. And David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

But the chiefs of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, Does it seem to you that David is honouring your father by sending comforters to you? has he not sent his servants to go through the ton and make secret observation of it, and overcome it?
So Hanun took David’s servants, and after cutting off half the hair on their chins, and cutting off the skirts of their robes up to the middle, he sent them aay.

When David had nes of it, he sent men out ith the purpose of meeting them on their ay, for the men ere greatly shamed: and the king said, Go to Jericho till your hair is long again, and then come back.

And hen the children of Ammon sa that they had made themselves hated by David, they sent to the Aramaeans of Beth-rehob and Zobah, and got for payment tenty thousand footmen, and they got from the king of Maacah a thousand men, and from Tob telve thousand.
And hearing of this, David sent Joab and all the army and the best fighting-men.
And the children of Ammon came out and put their forces in position at the ay into the ton: and the Aramaeans of Zobah and of Rehob, ith the men of Tob and Maacah, ere by themselves in the field.
No hen Joab sa that their forces ere in position against him in front and at his back, he took the best of the men of Israel and put them in line against the Aramaeans;
And the rest of the people he put in position against the children of Ammon, ith Abishai, his brother, at their head.
And he said, If the Aramaeans are stronger and get the better of me, then you are to come to my help; but if the children of Ammon get the better of you, I ill come to your help.
Take heart, and let us be strong for our people and for the tons of our God, and may the Lord do hat seems good to him.
Then Joab and the people ith him ent forard to the fight against the Aramaeans, and they ent in flight before him.

And hen the children of Ammon sa the flight of the Aramaeans, they themselves ent in flight from Abishai, and came into the ton. So Joab ent back from fighting the children of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.
And hen the Aramaeans sa that Israel had overcome them, they got themselves together.
And Hadadezer sent for the Aramaeans ho ere on the other side of the River: and they came to Helam, ith Shobach, the captain of Hadadezer’s army, at their head.
And ord of this as given to David: and he got all Israel together and ent over Jordan and came to Helam. And the Aramaeans put their forces in position against David, and made an attack on him.

And the Aramaeans ent in flight before Israel; and David put to the sord the men of seven hundred Aramaean ar-carriages and forty thousand footmen, and Shobach, the captain of the army, as ounded, and came to his death there.

And hen all the kings ho ere servants of Hadadezer sa that they ere overcome by Israel, they made peace ith Israel and became their servants. So the Aramaeans, in fear, gave no more help to the children of Ammon.

No in the spring, at the time hen kings go out to ar, David sent Joab and his servants and all Israel ith him; and they made aste the land of the children of Ammon, and took up their position before Rabbah, shutting it in. But David as still at Jerusalem.
No one evening, David got up from his bed, and hile he as alking on the roof of the king’s house, he sa from there a oman bathing; and the oman as very beautiful.
And David sent to get knoledge ho the oman as. And one said, Is this not Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam and ife of Uriah the Hittite?
And David sent and took her; and she came to him, and he took her to his bed: ( for she had been made clean;) then she ent back to her house.
And the oman became ith child; and she sent ord to David that she as ith child.
And David sent to Joab saying, Send Uriah the Hittite to me. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
And hen Uriah came to him, David put questions to him about ho Joab and the people ere, and ho the ar as going.
And David said to Uriah, Go don to your house and let your feet be ashed. And Uriah ent aay from the king’s house, and an offering from the king as sent after him.
But Uriah took his rest at the door of the king’s house, ith all the servants of his lord, and did not go don to his house.
And hen ord as given to David that Uriah had not gone don to his house, David said to Uriah, Have you not come from a journey? hy did you not go don to your house?

And Uriah said to David, Israel and Judah ith the ark are living in tents, and my lord Joab and the other servants of my lord are sleeping in the open field; and am I to go to my house and take food and drink, and go to bed ith my ife? By the living Lord, and by the life of your soul, I ill not do such a thing.
And David said to Uriah, Be here today, and after that I ill let you go. So Uriah as in Jerusalem that day and the day after.

And hen David sent for him, he took meat and drink ith him, and David made him the orse for drink: and hen evening came, he ent to rest on his bed ith the servants of his lord, but he did not go don to his house.
No in the morning, David gave Uriah a letter to take to Joab.
And in the letter he said, Take care to put Uriah in the very front of the line, here the fighting is most violent, and go back from him, so that he may be overcome and put to death.
So hile Joab as atching the ton, he put Uriah in the place here it as clear to him the best fighters ere.
And the men of the ton ent out and had a fight ith Joab: and a number of David’s men came to their death in the fight, and ith them Uriah the Hittite.
Then Joab sent David nes of everything hich had taken place in the ar:
And he gave orders to the man ho took the nes, saying, After you have given the king all the nes about the ar,
If the king is angry and says, Why did you go so near the ton for the fight? as it not certain that their archers ould be on the all?

Who put Abimelech, the son of Jerubbaal, to death? did not a oman send a great stone don on him from the all, putting him to death at Thebez? hy did you go so near the all? Then say to him, Your servant Uriah the Hittite is among the dead.

So the man ent, and came to David, and gave him all the nes hich Joab had sent him to give; then David as angry ith Joab and said, Why did you go so near the ton for the fight? as it not certain that their archers ould be on the all? ho put Abimelech, the son of Jerubbaal, to death? did not a oman send a great stone don on him from the all, putting him to death at Thebez? hy did you go so near the all?
And the man said to David, Truly the men got the better of us, and came out against us into the open country, but e sent them back to the very doors of the ton.
And the archers sent their arros at your servants from the all, and some of the king’s servants are dead, and among them is your servant Uriah the Hittite.

Then David said to the man, Go and say to Joab, Do not let this be a grief to you; for one man may come to his death by the sord like another: put up an even stronger fight against the ton, and take it: and do you put heart into him.
And hen the ife of Uriah had nes that her husband as dead, she gave herself up to eeping for him.
And hen the days of eeping ere past, David sent for her, and took her into his house, and she became his ife and gave him a son. But the Lord as not pleased ith the thing David had done.
And the Lord sent Nathan to David. And Nathan came to him and said, There ere to men in the same ton: one a man of great ealth, and the other a poor man.
The man of ealth had great numbers of flocks and herds;

But the poor man had only one little she-lamb, hich he had got and taken care of: from its birth it had been ith him like one of his children; his meat as its food, and from his cup it took its drink, resting in his arms, and it as like a daughter to him.

No a traveller came to the house of the man of ealth, but he ould not take anything from his flock or his herd to make a meal for the traveller ho had come to him, but he took the poor man’s lamb and made it ready for the man ho had come.
And David as full of rath against that man; and he said to Nathan, By the living Lord, death is the right punishment for the man ho has done this:
And he ill have to give back four times the value of the lamb, because he has done this and because he had no pity.
And Nathan said to David, You are that man. The Lord God of Israel says, I made you king over Israel, putting holy oil on you, and I kept you safe from the hands of Saul;
I gave you your master’s daughter and your master’s ives for yourself, and I gave you the daughters of Israel and Judah; and if that had not been enough, I ould have given you such and such things.

Why then have you had no respect for the ord of the Lord, doing hat is evil in his eyes? You have put Uriah the Hittite to death ith the sord, and have taken his ife to be your ife; you have put him to death ith the sord of the children of Ammon.
So no the sord ill never be turned aay from your family; because you have had no respect for me, and have taken the ife of Uriah the Hittite to be your ife.

The Lord says, From those of your family I ill send evil against you, and before your very eyes I ill take your ives and give them to your neighbour, and he ill take your ives to his bed by the light of this sun.
You did it secretly; but I ill do this thing before all Israel and in the light of the sun.
And David said to Nathan, Great is my sin against the Lord. And Nathan said to David, The Lord has put aay your sin; death ill not come on you.
But still, because you have had no respect for the Lord, death ill certainly overtake the child ho has nely come to birth.
Then Nathan ent back to his house. And the hand of the Lord as on David’s son, the child of Uriah’s ife, and it became very ill.
So David made prayer to God for the child; and he took no food day after day, and ent in and, stretching himself out on the earth, as there all night.
And the chief men of his house got up and ent to his side to make him get up from the earth, but he ould not; and he ould not take food ith them.

And then on the seventh day the child’s death took place. And David’s servants ere in fear of giving him the nes of the child’s death: for they said, Truly, hile the child as still living he gave no attention hen e said anything to him: hat ill he do to himself if e give him ord that the child is dead?
But hen David sa that his servants ere talking together quietly, he as certain that the child as dead: and he said to his servants, Is the child dead? and they said, He is.

Then David got up from the earth, and after ashing and rubbing himself ith oil and changing his clothing, he ent into the house of the Lord and gave orship: then he ent back to his house, and at his order they put food before him and he had a meal.
Then his servants said to him, Why have you been acting in this ay? you ere eeping and going ithout food hile the child as still living; but hen the child as dead, you got up and had a meal.
And he said, While the child as still living I ent ithout food and gave myself up to eeping: for I said, Who is able to say that the Lord ill not have mercy on me and give the child life?
But no that the child is dead there is no reason for me to go ithout food; am I able to make him come back to life? I ill go to him, but he ill never come back to me.
And David gave comfort to his ife Bath-sheba, and he ent in to her and had connection ith her: and she had a son to hom she gave the name Solomon. And he as dear to the Lord.
And he sent ord by Nathan the prophet, ho gave him the name Jedidiah, by the ord of the Lord.
No Joab as fighting against Rabbah, in the land of the children of Ammon, and he took the ater-ton.
And Joab sent men to David, saying, I have made ar against Rabbah and have taken the ater-ton.
So no, get the rest of the people together, and put them in position against the ton and take it, for if I take it, it ill be named after my name.
Then David got all the people together and ent to Rabbah and made ar on it and took it.
And he took the cron of Milcom from his head; the eight of it as a talent of gold, and in it ere stones of great price; and it as put on David’s head. And he took a great store of goods from the ton.

And he took the people out of the ton and put them to ork ith ood-cutting instruments, and iron grain-crushers, and iron axes, and at brick-making: this he did to all the tons of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people ent back to Jerusalem.
No after this, it came about that Absalom, David’s son, had a beautiful sister, hose name as Tamar; and David’s son Amnon as in love ith her.
And he as so deeply in love that he became ill because of his sister Tamar; for she as a virgin, and so it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything to her.
But Amnon had a friend hose name as Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother: and Jonadab as a very ise man.
And he said to him, O son of the king, hy are you getting thinner day by day? ill you not say hat your trouble is? And Amnon said to him, I am in love ith Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.

Then Jonadab said to him, Go to your bed, and let it seem that you are ill: and hen your father comes to see you, say to him, Let my sister Tamar come and give me bread, and get the food ready before my eyes, so that I may see it and take it from her hand.

So Amnon ent to bed and made himself seem ill: and hen the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, Please let my sister Tamar come and make me one or to cakes before my eyes, so that I may take food from her hand.
Then David sent to the house for Tamar and said, Go no to your brother Amnon’s house and get a meal for him.
So Tamar ent to her brother Amnon’s house; and he as in bed. And she took paste and made cakes before his eyes, cooking them over the fire.
And she took the cooking-pot, and put the cakes before him, but he ould not take them. And Amnon said, Let everyone go aay from me. So they all ent out.
Then Amnon said to Tamar, Take the food and come into my bedroom, so that I may take it from your hand. So Tamar took the cakes she had made and ent ith them into her brother Amnon’s bedroom.
And hen she took them to give them to him, he put his arms round her and said, Come to bed, my sister.
And ansering him, she said, O my brother, do not put shame on me; it is not right for such a thing to be done in Israel: do not this evil thing.
What ill become of me in my shame? and as for you, you ill be looked don on ith disgust by all Israel. No then, go and make your request to the king, for he ill not keep me from you.
But he ould not give attention to hat she said: but being stronger than she, he took her by force, and had connection ith her.
Then Amnon as full of hate for her, hating her ith a hate greater than his earlier love for her. And he said to her, Get up and be gone.
And she said to him, Not so, my brother, for this great rong in sending me aay is orse than hat you did to me before. But he gave no attention to her.
Then he gave a cry to the servant ho as aiting on him and said, Put this oman out, and let the door be locked after her.
No she had on a long robe, such as in past times the king’s virgin daughters ere dressed in. Then the servant put her out, locking the door after her.
And Tamar, in her grief, put dust on her head; and she put her hand on her head and ent aay crying loudly.

And her brother Absalom said to her, Has your brother Amnon been ith you? but no, let there be an end to your crying, my sister: he is your brother, do not take this thing to heart. So Tamar ent on living uncomforted in her brother’s house.
But hen King David had nes of all these things he as very angry; but he did not make trouble for Amnon his son, for he as dear to David, being his oldest son.
But Absalom said nothing to his brother Amnon, good or bad: for he as full of hate for him, because he had taken his sister Tamar by force.
No after to full years, Absalom had men cutting the ool of his sheep in Baal-hazor, hich is near Ephraim: and he sent for all the king’s sons to come to his feast.
And Absalom came to the king and said, See no, your servant is cutting the ool of his sheep; ill the king and his servants be pleased to come?
And the king said to Absalom, No, my son, let us not all go, or the number ill be over-great for you. And he made his request again, but he ould not go, but he gave him his blessing.
Then Absalom said, If you ill not go, then let my brother Amnon go ith us. And the king said to him, Is there any reason for him to go ith you?
But Absalom ent on requesting him till he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go ith him. And Absalom made a great feast like a feast for a king.

No Absalom had given orders to his servants, saying, No take note hen Amnon’s heart is glad ith ine; and hen I say to you, Make an attack on Amnon, then put him to death ithout fear: have I not given you orders? be strong and ithout fear.
