So Absalom’s servants did to Amnon as Absalom had given them orders. Then all the king’s sons got up, and every man got on his beast and ent in flight.
No hile they ere on their ay, nes as given to David that Absalom had put to death all the sons of the king and that not one of them as still living.
Then the king got up in great grief, stretching himself out on the earth: and all his servants ere by his side, ith their clothing parted.

And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, said, Let not my lord have the idea that all the sons of the king have been put to death; for only Amnon is dead: this has been purposed by Absalom from the day hen he took his sister Tamar by force.
So no, let not my lord the king take this thing to heart, ith the idea that all the king’s sons are dead: for only Amnon is dead.

But Absalom ent in flight. And the young man ho kept the atch, lifting up his eyes, sa that a great band of people as coming don the slope by the ay of the Horons; and the atchman came and gave ord to the king, saying, I sa men coming don by the ay of the Horons, from the hillside.
And Jonadab said to the king, See, the king’s sons are coming; as your servant said, so it is.
And hile he as talking, the king’s sons came, ith eeping and loud cries: and the king and all his servants ere eeping bitterly.
So Absalom ent in flight and came to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur, here he as for three years.
And the king as sorroing for his son all the time.
And the heart of David as asted ith desire for Absalom: for he as comforted for the death of Amnon.
No it as clear to Joab, the son of Zeruiah, that the king’s heart as turning to Absalom.

And Joab sent to Tekoa and got from there a ise oman, and said to her, No make yourself seem like one given up to grief, and put on the clothing of sorro, not using any seet oil for your body, but looking like one ho for a long time has been eeping for the dead:
And come to the king and say these ords to him. So Joab gave her ords to say.
And the oman of Tekoa came to the king, and falling on her face, gave him honour and said, Give me help, O king.
And the king said to her, What is your trouble? And her anser as, Truly I am a ido, and my husband is dead.
And I had to sons, and the to of them had a fight in the field, and there as no one to come beteen them, and one ith a blo put the other to death.

And no all the family is turned against me, your servant, saying, Give up him ho as the cause of his brother’s death, so that e may put him to death in payment for the life of his brother, hose life he took; and e ill put an end to the one ho ill get the heritage: so they ill put out my last burning coal, and my husband ill have no name or offspring on the face of the earth.
And the king said to the oman, Go to your house and I ill give orders about this.
And the oman of Tekoa said to the king, My lord, O king, may the sin be on me and on my family, and may the king and the seat of his kingdom be clear of sin!
And the king said, If anyone says anything to you, make him come to me, and he ill do you no more damage.

Then she said, Let the king keep in mind the Lord your God, so that he ho gives punishment for blood may be kept back from further destruction and that no one may send death on my son. And he said, By the living Lord, not a hair of your son’s head ill come to the earth.
Then the oman said, Will the king let his servant say one ord more? And he said, Say on.

And the oman said, Why have you had such a thought about the people of God? ( for in saying these very ords the king has put himself in the rong because he has not taken back the one hom he sent far aay.)

For death comes to us all, and e are like ater drained out on the earth, hich it is not possible to take up again; and God ill not take aay the life of the man hose purpose is that he ho has been sent aay may not be completely cut off from him.

And no it is my fear of the people hich has made me come to say these ords to my lord the king: and your servant said, I ill put my cause before the king, and it may be that he ill give effect to my request.
For the king ill give ear, and take his servant out of the poer of the man hose purpose is the destruction of me and my son together from the heritage of God.
Then your servant said, May the ord of my lord the king give me peace! for my lord the king is as the angel of God in his hearing of good and bad: and may the Lord your God be ith you!
Then the king said to the oman, No give me an anser to the question I am going to put to you; keep nothing back. And the oman said, Let my lord the king say on.

And the king said, Is not the hand of Joab ith you in all this? And the oman in anser said, By the life of your soul, my lord the king, it is not possible for anyone to go to the right hand or to the left from anything said by the king: your servant Joab gave me orders, and put all these ords in my mouth:
This he did, hoping that the face of this business might be changed: and my lord is ise, ith the isdom of the angel of God, having knoledge of everything on earth.
And the king said to Joab, See no, I ill do this thing: go then and Come back ith the young man Absalom.

Then Joab, falling don on his face on the earth, gave the king honour and blessing; and Joab said, Today it is clear to your servant that I have grace in your eyes, my lord king, because the king has given effect to the request of his servant.
So Joab got up and ent to Geshur and came back again to Jerusalem ith Absalom.
And the king said, Let him go to his house, but let him not see my face. So Absalom ent back to his house and did not see the face of the king.
No in all Israel there as no one so greatly to be praised for his beautiful form as Absalom: from his feet to the cron of his head he as completely beautiful.
And hen he had his hair cut, ( hich he did at the end of every year, because of the eight of his hair;) the eight of the hair as to hundred shekels by the king’s eight.
And Absalom as the father of three sons and of one daughter named Tamar, ho as very beautiful.
For to full years Absalom as living in Jerusalem ithout ever seeing the face of the king.
Then Absalom sent for Joab to send him to the king, but he ould not come to him: and he sent again a second time, but he ould not come.
So he said to his servants, See, Joab’s field is near mine, and he has barley in it; go and put it on fire. And Absalom’s servants put the field on fire.
Then Joab came to Absalom in his house and said to him, Why have your servants put my field on fire?

And Absalom’s anser as, See, I sent to you saying, Come here, so that I may send you to the king to say, Why have I come back from Geshur? it ould be better for me to be there still: let me no see the king’s face, and if there is any sin in me, let him put me to death.
So Joab ent to the king and said these ords to him: and hen the king had sent for him, Absalom came, and ent don on his face on the earth before the king: and the king gave him a kiss.
No after this, Absalom got for himself a carriage and horses, and fifty runners to go before him.

And Absalom got up early, morning after morning, and took his place at the side of the public meeting-place: and hen any man had a cause hich had to come to the king to be judged, then Absalom, crying out to him, said, What is your ton? and he ould say, Your servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.
And Absalom ould say to him, See, your cause is true and right; but no man has been named by the king to give you a hearing.
And more than this, Absalom said, If only I as made judge in the land, so that every man ho has any cause or question might come to me, and I ould give a right decision for him!
And if any man came near to give him honour, he took him by the hand and gave him a kiss.
And this Absalom did to everyone in Israel ho came to the king to have his cause judged: so Absalom, like a thief, took aay the hearts of the men of Israel.
No at the end of four years, Absalom said to the king, Let me go to Hebron and give effect to the oath hich I made to the Lord:
For hile I as living in Geshur in Aram, your servant made an oath, saying, If ever the Lord lets me come back to Jerusalem, I ill give him orship in Hebron.
And the king said to him, Go in peace. So he got up and ent to Hebron.
But Absalom at the same time sent atchers through all the tribes of Israel to say, At the sound of the horn you are to say, Absalom is king in Hebron.
And ith Absalom, at his request, ent to hundred men from Jerusalem, ho ere completely unconscious of his designs.

And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, one of David’s helpers, from Giloh his ton, hile he as making the offerings. And the design against David became strong, for more and more people ere joined to Absalom.
And one came to David and said, The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom.

And David said to all his servants ho ere ith him at Jerusalem, Come, let us go in flight, or not one of us ill be safe from Absalom: let us go ithout loss of time, or he ill overtake us quickly and send evil on us, and put the ton to the sord.
And the king’s servants said to the king, See, your servants are ready to do hatever the king says is to be done.
So the king ent out, taking ith him all the people of his house, but for ten of his omen, ho ere to take care of the house.
And the king ent out, and all his servants ent after him, and made a stop at the Far House.
And all the people ent on by his side; and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites and all the men of Ittai of Gath, six hundred men ho came after him from Gath, ent on before the king.
Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, Why are you coming ith us? go back and keep ith the king: for you are a man of another country, you are far from the land of your birth.

It as only yesterday you came to us; hy then am I to make you go up and don ith us? for I have to go here I may; go back then, and take your countrymen ith you, and may the Lord’s mercy and good faith be ith you.
And Ittai the Gittite in anser said, By the living Lord, and by the life of my lord the king, in hatever place my lord the king may be, for life or death, there ill your servant be.
And David said to Ittai, Go forard, then. And Ittai the Gittite ent on, ith all his men and all the little ones he had ith him.

And there as great eeping in all the country hen all the people ent through; and the king himself as aiting in the Kidron valley and all the people ent by him in the direction of the olive-tree on the edge of the aste land.
Then Zadok came, and Abiathar, and ith them the ark of God’s agreement: and they put don the ark of God, till all the people from the ton had gone by.
And the king said to Zadok, Take the ark of God back into the ton: if I have grace in the eyes of the Lord, he ill let me come back and see it and his House again:
But if he says, I have no delight in you: then, here I am; let him do to me hat seems good to him.
The king said further to Zadok the priest, See, you and Abiathar are to go back to the ton in peace, ith your to sons, Ahimaaz, your son, and Jonathan, the son of Abiathar.
See, I ill be aiting at the ay across the river, in the aste land, till I get nes from you.
So Zadok and Abiathar took the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and did not go aay from there.
And David ent up the slopes of the Mount of Olives eeping all the ay, ith his head covered and no shoes on his feet: and all the people ho ere ith him, covering their heads, ent up eeping.
And ord came to David, saying, Ahithophel is among those ho are joined to Absalom. And David said, O Lord, let the isdom of Ahithophel be made foolish.
No hen David had come to the top of the slope, here they gave orship to God, Hushai the Archite came to him in great grief ith dust on his head:
David said to him, If you go on ith me, you ill be a trouble to me:

But if you go back to the ton and say to Absalom, I ill be your servant, O king; as in the past I have been your father’s servant, so no I ill be yours: then you ill be able to keep Ahithophel’s designs against me from being put into effect.
And have you not there Zadok and Abiathar the priests? so hatever comes to your ears from the king’s house, give ord of it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
See, they have ith them their to sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, the son of Abiathar; by them you may send ord to me of everything hich comes to your ears.
So Hushai, David’s friend, ent into the ton, and Absalom came to Jerusalem.

And hen David had gone a little ay past the top of the slope, Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, came to him, ith to asses on hich ere to hundred cakes of bread and a hundred stems of dry grapes and a hundred summer fruits and a skin of ine.

And David said to Ziba, What is your reason for this? And Ziba said, The asses are for the use of the king’s people, and the bread and the fruit are food for the young men; and the ine is for drink for those ho are overcome by eariness in the aste land.
And the king said, And here is your master’s son? And Ziba said, He is still at Jerusalem: for he said, Today Israel ill give back to me the kingdom of my father.
Then the king said to Ziba, Truly everything hich as Mephibosheth’s is yours. And Ziba said, I give honour to my lord, may I have grace in your eyes, my lord, O king!
And hen King David came to Bahurim, a man of Saul’s family named Shimei, the son of Gera, came out from there, calling curses after him.
And he sent stones at David and at all the king’s servants and at all the people and at all the men of ar by his side, on the right hand and on the left.
And Shimei said, ith curses, Be gone, be gone, you man of blood, you good-for-nothing:

The Lord has sent punishment on you for all the blood of the family of Saul, hose kingdom you have taken; and the Lord has given the kingdom to Absalom, your son: no you yourself are taken in your evil, because you are a man of blood.
Then Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, said to the king, Is this dead dog to go on cursing my lord the king? let me go over and take off his head.
And the king said, What have I to do ith you, you sons of Zeruiah? Let him go on cursing, for the Lord has said, Put a curse on David, and ho then may say, Why have you done so?

And David said to Abishai and to all his servants, You see ho my son, the offspring of my body, has made designs against my life: ho much more then may this Benjamite do so? Let him be, and let him go on cursing; for the Lord has given him orders.
It may be that the Lord ill take note of my rongs, and give me back good in anser to his cursing of me today.
So David and his men ent on their ay: and Shimei ent by the hillside parallel ith them, cursing and sending stones and dust at him.
And the king and his people came tired to Jordan, and took their rest there.
And Absalom and the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel as ith him.
Then Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, came to Absalom and said, Long life to the king, long life to the king!
And Absalom said, Is this your love for your friend? hy did you not go ith your friend?
And Hushai said to Absalom, Not so; I am for that man hom the Lord and this people and all the men of Israel have taken as king, and I ill take my place ith him.
And more than this! here is my place as a servant? is it not before his son? as I have been your father’s servant, so ill I be yours.
Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, Give your opinion no, hat are e to do?

And Ahithophel said to Absalom, Go in to your father’s omen ho are here looking after his house; then all Israel ill have the nes that you are hated by your father, and the hands of your supporters ill be strong.
So they put up the tent for Absalom on the top of the house, and Absalom ent in to his father’s omen before the eyes of all Israel.
In those days the opinions of Ahithophel ere valued as highly as if through him a man might get direction from God; so ere they valued by David as much as by Absalom.
Then Ahithophel said to Absalom, Let me take out telve thousand men and this very night I ill go after David:
And I ill come up ith him hen he is tired and feeble, and make him full of fear: and all the people ith him ill go in flight; and I ill make an attack on the king only:
And I ill make all the people come back to you as a bride comes back to her husband: it is the life of only one man you are going after; so all the people ill be at peace.
And the saying as pleasing to Absalom and to the responsible men of Israel.
Then Absalom said, No send for Hushai the Archite, and let us give ear to hat he has to say.
And hen Hushai came, Absalom said to him, This is hat Ahithophel has said: are e to do as he says? if not, hat is your suggestion?
And Hushai said to Absalom, Ahithophel’s idea is not a good one at this time.

Hushai said further, You have knoledge of your father and his men, that they are men of ar, and that their feelings are bitter, like those of a bear in the field hose young ones have been taken from her: and your father is a man of ar, and ill not take his night’s rest ith the people;

But he ill certainly have taken cover no in some hole or secret place; and if some of our people, at the first attack, are overcome, then any hearing of it ill say, There is destruction among the people ho are on Absalom’s side.

Then even the strongest, hose heart is like the heart of a lion, ill become like ater; for all Israel is conscious that your father is a man of ar, and those ho are ith him are strong and ithout fear.
But my suggestion is that all Israel, from Dan as far as Beer-sheba, comes together to you, a great army like the sands of the sea in number; and that you yourself go out among them.
Then e ill come on him in some place, herever he may be, falling on him as the de comes on the earth: and of him and all the men ho are ith him not one ill get aay ith his life.
And if he has gone into some ton, then let all Israel take strong cords to that ton, and e ill have it pulled into the valley, till not one small stone is to be seen there.

Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, Hushai’s suggestion is better than that of Ahithophel. For it as the purpose of the Lord to make the ise designs of Ahithophel ithout effect, so that the Lord might send evil on Absalom.
Then Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, This is the suggestion made by Ahithophel to Absalom and the responsible men of Israel, and this is hat I said to them.

So no send the nes quickly to David, and say, Do not take your night’s rest by the ay across the river to the aste land, but be certain to go over; or the king and all the people ith him ill come to destruction.

No Jonathan and Ahimaaz ere aiting by En-rogel; and a servant-girl ent from time to time and gave them nes and they ent ith the nes to King David, for it as not ise for them to let themselves be seen coming into the ton.
But a boy sa them, and gave ord of it to Absalom: so the to of them ent aay quickly, and came to the house of a man in Bahurim ho had a ater-hole in his garden, and they ent don into it.
And a oman put a cover over the hole, and put crushed grain on top of it, and no one had any knoledge of it.

And Absalom’s servants came to the oman at the house and said, Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the oman said to them, They have gone from here to the stream. And after searching for them, and seeing nothing of them, they ent back to Jerusalem.

Then after the servants had gone aay, they came up out of the ater-hole and ent to give King David the nes; and they said, Get up and go quickly over the ater, for such and such are Ahithophel’s designs against you.
So David and all the people ho ere ith him ent up over Jordan: hen dan came, every one of them had gone over Jordan.

No hen Ahithophel sa that his suggestion as not acted on, he got his ass ready, and ent back to his house, to the ton here he came from, and having put his house in order, he put himself to death by hanging; so he came to his end and as put in the resting-place of his father.
And David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom, ith all the men of Israel, ent over Jordan.

And Absalom put Amasa at the head of the army in place of Joab. No Amasa as the son of a man named Ithra the Ishmaelite, ho had been the lover of Abigail, the daughter of Jesse, sister of Zeruiah, Joab’s mother.
And Israel and Absalom put up their tents in the land of Gilead.
No hen David had come to Mahanaim, Shobi, the son of Nahash of Rabbah, the Ammonite, and Machir, the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
Came ith beds and basins and pots, and grain and meal, and all sorts of dry foods,
And honey and butter and sheep and milk-cheeses, for David and his people: for they said, This people is in the aste land, needing food and drink and rest.
And David had the people ho ere ith him numbered, and he put over them captains of thousands and captains of hundreds.

And David sent the people out, a third of them under the orders of Joab, and a third under the orders of Abishai, son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, And I myself ill certainly go out ith you.

But the people said, It is better for you not to go out: for if e are put to flight, they ill not give a thought to us, and if death overtakes half of us, it ill be nothing to them: but you are of more value than ten thousand of us: so it is better for you to be ready to come to our help from this ton.
And the king said to them, I ill do hatever seems best to you. So the king took his place by the door of the ton, and all the people ent out by hundreds and by thousands.
And the king gave orders to Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Because of me, be gentle to the young man Absalom. And this order about Absalom as given in the hearing of all the people.
So the people ent out into the field against Israel, and the fight took place in the oods of Ephraim.
And the people of Israel ere overcome there by the servants of David, and there as a great destruction that day, and tenty thousand men ere put to the sord.
And the fighting ent on over all the face of the country: and the oods ere responsible for more deaths than the sord.

And Absalom came across some of David’s men. And Absalom as seated on his mule, and the mule ent under the thick branches of a great tree, and his head became fixed in the tree and he as lifted up beteen earth and heaven, and the beast under him ent on.
And a certain man sa it and said to Joab, I sa Absalom hanging in a tree.
And Joab said to the man ho had given him the nes, If you sa this, hy did you not put your sord through him, and I ould have given you ten bits of silver and a band for your robe?

And the man said to Joab, Even if you gave me a thousand bits of silver, I ould not put out my hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king gave orders to you and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Take care that the young man Absalom is not touched.
And if I had falsely put him to death ( and nothing may be kept secret from the king), you ould have had nothing to do ith me.
Then Joab said, I ould have made it safe for you. And he took three spears in his hand, and put them through Absalom’s heart, hile he as still living, in the branches of the tree.
And ten young men, servants of Joab, came round Absalom and put an end to him.
And Joab had the horn sounded, and the people came back from going after Israel, for Joab kept them back.
And they took Absalom’s body and put it into a great hole in the ood, and put a great mass of stones over it: and every man of Israel ent in flight to his tent.

No Absalom, before his death, had put up for himself a pillar in the king’s valley, naming it after himself; for he said, I have no son to keep my name in memory: and to this day it is named Absalom’s pillar.
Then Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok, said, Let me go and give the king nes of ho the Lord has done right in his cause against those ho took up arms against him.
And Joab said, You ill take no nes today; another day you may give him the nes, but you ill take no nes today, because the king’s son is dead.
Then Joab said to the Cushite, Go and give the king ord of hat you have seen. And the Cushite, making a sign of respect to Joab, ent off running.

Then Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok, said to Joab again, Whatever may come of it, let me go after the Cushite. And Joab said, Why have you a desire to go, my son, seeing that you ill get no reard for your nes?
Whatever may come of it, he said, I ill go. Then he said to him, Go. So Ahimaaz ent running by the loland road and overtook the Cushite.
No David as seated beteen the to ton doors; and the atchman ent up to the roof of the doorays, on the all, and, lifting up his eyes, sa a man running by himself.
And the atchman gave nes of it to the king. And the king said, If he is coming by himself, then he has nes. And the man as travelling quickly, and came near.
Then the atchman sa another man running: and crying out in the direction of the door he said, Here is another man running by himself. And the king said, He, like the other, comes ith nes.
And the atchman said, It seems to me that the running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz, the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and his nes ill be good.

And Ahimaaz, crying out to the king, said, It is ell. And falling don before the king, ith his face to the earth, he said, May the Lord your God be praised, ho has given up the men ho took up arms against my lord the king!
And the king said, Is it ell ith the young man Absalom? And Ahimaaz said in anser, When Joab sent me, your servant, I sa a great outcry going on, but I had no knoledge of hat it as.
And the king said, Get back and take your place here. So turning to one side, he took his place there.
And then the Cushite came and said, I have nes for my lord the king: today the Lord has done right in your cause against all those ho took up arms against you.
And the king said to the Cushite, Is the young man Absalom safe? And the Cushite said in anser, May all the king’s haters and those ho do evil against the king, be as that young man is!

Then the king as much moved, and ent up into the room over the door, eeping, and saying, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! if only my life might have been given for yours, O Absalom, my son, my son!
And ord as given to Joab that the king as eeping and sorroing for Absalom.
And the salvation of that day as changed to sorro for all the people: for it as said to the people, The king is in bitter grief for his son.
And the people made their ay back to the ton quietly and secretly, as those ho are shamed go secretly hen they go in flight from the ar.
But the king, covering his face, gave a great cry, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!

And Joab came into the house to the king and said, Today you have put to shame the faces of all your servants ho even no have kept you and your sons and your daughters and your ives and all your omen safe from death;

For your haters, it seems, are dear to you, and your friends are hated. For you have made it clear that captains and servants are nothing to you: and no I see that if Absalom as living and e had all been dead today, it ould have been right in your eyes.

So get up no, and go out and say some kind ords to your servants; for, by the Lord, I give you my oath, that if you do not go out, not one of them ill keep ith you tonight; and that ill be orse for you than all the evil hich has overtaken you from your earliest years.

Then the king got up and took his seat near the ton-door. And ord as given to all the people that the king as in the public place: and all the people came before the king. No all the men of Israel had gone back in flight to their tents.

And through all the tribes of Israel the people ere having arguments, saying, The king made us safe from the hands of those ho ere against us and made us free from the hands of the Philistines; and no he has gone in flight from the land, because of Absalom.
And Absalom, hom e made a ruler over us, is dead in the fight. So no hy do you say nothing about getting the king back? And ord of hat all Israel as saying came to the king.
And King David sent ord to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, Say to the responsible men of Judah, Why are you the last to take steps to get the king back to his house?
You are my brothers, my bone and my flesh; hy are you the last to get the king back again?
And say to Amasa, Are you not my bone and my flesh? May God’s punishment be on me, if I do not make you chief of the army before me at all times in place of Joab!
And the hearts of the men of Judah ere moved like one man; so that they sent to the king, saying, Come back, ith all your servants.
So the king came back, and came as far as Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, meeting the king there, to take him back ith them over Jordan.
And Shimei, the son of Gera, the Benjamite from Bahurim, got up quickly and ent don ith the men of Judah for the purpose of meeting King David;
And ith him a thousand men of Benjamin, and Ziba, the servant of Saul, ith his fifteen sons and tenty servants, came rushing to Jordan before the king,

And kept going across the river to take the people of the king’s house over, and to do hatever as desired by the king. And Shimei, the son of Gera, ent don on his face in the dust before the king, hen he as about to go over Jordan,
And said to him, Let me not be judged as a sinner in your eyes, O my lord, and do not keep in mind the rong I did on the day hen my lord the king ent out of Jerusalem, or take it to heart.
For your servant is conscious of his sin: and so, as you see, I have come today, the first of all the sons of Joseph, for the purpose of meeting my lord the king.
But Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, said, Is not death the right fate for Shimei, because he has been cursing the one marked by the holy oil?

And David said, What have I to do ith you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you put yourselves against me today? is it right for any man in Israel to be put to death today? for I am certain today that I am king in Israel.
So the king said to Shimei, You ill not be put to death. And the king gave him his oath.

And Mephibosheth, the son of Saul’s son, came don for the purpose of meeting the king; his feet had not been cared for or his hair cut or his clothing ashed from the day hen the king ent aay till the day hen he came back in peace.
No hen he had come from Jerusalem to see the king, the king said to him, Why did you not come ith me, Mephibosheth?

And he said in anser, Because of the deceit of my servant, my lord king: for I, your servant, said to him, You are to make ready an ass and on it I ill go ith the king, for your servant has not the use of his feet.
He has given you a false account of me: but my lord the king is like the angel of God: do then hatever seems good to you.

For all my father’s family ere only dead men before my lord the king: and still you put your servant among those hose place is at the king’s table. What right then have I to say anything more to the king?
And the king said, Say nothing more about these things. I say, Let there be a division of the land beteen Ziba and you.
And Mephibosheth said, Let him take it all, no that my lord the king has come back to his house in peace!
And Barzillai the Gileadite came don from Rogelim; and he ent on as far as Jordan ith the king to take him across Jordan.
No Barzillai as a very old man, as much as eighty years old: and he had given the king everything he had need of, hile he as at Mahanaim, for he as a very great man.
And the king said to Barzillai, Come over ith me, and I ill take care of you in Jerusalem.
And Barzillai said to the king, Ho much of my life is still before me, for me to go up to Jerusalem ith the king?

I am no eighty years old: good and bad are the same to me; have meat and drink any taste for me no? am I able to take pleasure in the voices of men or omen in song? hy then am I to be a trouble to my lord the king?
Your servant’s desire as only to take the king over Jordan; hy is the king to give me such a reard?

Let your servant no go back again, so that hen death comes to me, it may be in my ton and by the resting-place of my father and mother. But here is your servant Chimham: let him go ith my lord the king, and do for him hat seems good to you.
And the king said in anser, Let Chimham go over ith me, and I ill do for him hatever seems good to you: and hatever your desire is, I ill do it for you.
Then all the people ent over Jordan, and the king ent over: and the king gave Barzillai a kiss, ith his blessing; and he ent back to his place.
So the king ent over to Gilgal, and Chimham ent ith him: and all the people of Judah, as ell as half the people of Israel, took the king on his ay.

Then the men of Israel came to the king and said, Why have our countrymen of Judah taken you aay in secret and come over Jordan ith the king and all his family, because all his people are David’s men?

And all the men of Judah gave this anser to the men of Israel, Because the king is our near relation: hy then are you angry about this? have e taken any of the king’s food, or has he given us any offering?

And in anser to the men of Judah, the men of Israel said, We have ten parts in the king, and e are the first in order of birth: hy did you make nothing of us? and ere e not the first to make suggestions for getting the king back? And the ords of the men of Judah ere more violent than the ords of the men of Israel.

No by chance there as present a good-for-nothing person named Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he, sounding the horn, said, We have no part in David, or any interest in the son of Jesse: let every man go to his tent, O Israel.
So all the men of Israel, turning aay from David, ent after Sheba, the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah ere true to their king, going ith him from Jordan as far as Jerusalem.

And David came to his house at Jerusalem: and the king took the ten omen to hom he had given the care of the house, and had them shut up, and gave them the necessaries of life, but did not go near them. So they ere shut up till the day of their death, living as idos.
Then the king said to Amasa, Get all the men of Judah together, and in three days be here yourself.
So Amasa ent to get all the men of Judah together, but he took longer than the time David had given him.

And David said to Abishai, Sheba, the son of Bichri, ill do us more damage than Absalom did; so take some of your lord’s servants and go after him, before he makes himself safe in the alled tons, and gets aay before our eyes.
So there ent after Abishai, Joab and the Cherethites and the Pelethites and all the fighting-men; they ent out of Jerusalem to overtake Sheba, the son of Bichri.

When they ere at the great stone hich is in Gibeon, Amasa came face to face ith them. No Joab had on his ar-dress, and round him a band from hich his sord as hanging in its cover; and hile he as alking, it came out, falling to the earth.
And Joab said to Amasa, Is it ell, my brother? And ith his right hand he took him by the hair of his chin to give him a kiss.

But Amasa did not see danger from the sord hich as no in Joab’s left hand, and Joab put it through his stomach so that his inside came out on to the earth, and he did not give him another blo. So Joab and his brother Abishai ent on after Sheba, the son of Bichri.
And one of Joab’s young men, taking his place at Amasa’s side, said, Whoever is for Joab and for David, let him go after Joab!

And Amasa as stretched out in a pool of blood in the middle of the highay. And hen the man sa that all the people ere stopping, he took Amasa out of the highay and put him in a field, ith a cloth over him, hen he sa that everyone ho ent by came to a stop.
When he had been taken off the road, all the people ent on after Joab in search of Sheba, the son of Bichri.
And Sheba ent through all the tribes of Israel, to Abel of Beth-maacah; and all the Bichrites came together and ent in after him.
And Joab and his men got him shut up in Abel of Beth-maacah, and put up an earthork against the ton: and all Joab’s men did their best to get the all broken don.
Then a ise oman got up on the all, and crying out from the ton, said, Give ear, give ear; say no to Joab, Come near, so that I may have talk ith you.
And he came near, and the oman said, Are you Joab? And he said in anser, I am. Then she said, Give ear to your servant’s ords. And he said, I am giving ear.
Then she said, In the old days, there as a saying, Let them put the question in Abel and in Dan, saying, Has hat as ordered by men of good faith in Israel ever come to an end?
Your purpose is the destruction of a mother-ton in Israel: hy ould you put an end to the heritage of the Lord?
And Joab, ansering her, said, Far, far be it from me to be a cause of death or destruction;

Not so: but a man of the hill-country of Ephraim, Sheba, son of Bichri, by name, has taken up arms against the king, against David: give up this man only, and I ill go aay from the ton. And the oman said to Joab, His head ill be dropped over the all to you.

Then the oman in her isdom had talk ith all the ton. And they had Sheba’s head cut off and sent out to Joab. And he had the horn sounded, and sent them all aay from the ton, every man to his tent. And Joab ent back to Jerusalem to the king.
No Joab as over all the army; and Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, as at the head of the Cherethites and the Pelethites;
And Adoram as overseer of the forced ork; and Jehoshaphat, the son of Ahilud, as the recorder;
And Sheva as the scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar ere priests;
And in addition, Ira the Jairite as a priest to David.

In the days of David they ere short of food for three years, year after year; and David ent before the Lord for directions. And the Lord said, On Saul and on his family there is blood, because he put the Gibeonites to death.

Then the king sent for the Gibeonites; ( no the Gibeonites ere not of the children of Israel, but ere the last of the Amorites, to hom the children of Israel had given an oath; but Saul, in his passion for the children of Israel and Judah, had made an attempt on their lives:)
So David said to the Gibeonites, What may I do for you? ho am I to make up to you for your rongs, so that you may give a blessing to the heritage of the Lord?

And the Gibeonites said to him, It is not a question of silver and gold beteen us and Saul or his family; and it is not in our poer to put to death any man in Israel. And he said, Say, then, hat am I to do for you?
And they said to the king, As for the man by hom e ere asted, and ho made designs against us to have us completely cut off from the land of Israel,
Let seven men of his family be given up to us and e ill put an end to them by hanging them before the Lord in Gibeon, on the hill of the Lord. And the king said, I ill give them.
But the king did not give up Mephibosheth, the son of Saul’s son Jonathan, because of the Lord’s oath made beteen David and Jonathan, the son of Saul.

But the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the to sons of Saul to hom Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, had given birth; and the five sons of Saul’s daughter Merab, hose father as Adriel, the son of Barzillai the Meholathite:

And he gave them up to the Gibeonites, and they put them to death, hanging them on the mountain before the Lord; all seven came to their end together in the first days of the grain-cutting, at the start of the cutting of the barley.

And Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, took haircloth, placing it on the rock as a bed for herself, from the start of the grain-cutting till rain came don on them from heaven; and she did not let the birds of the air come near them by day, or the beasts of the field by night.
And nes as given to David of hat Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, one of Saul’s ives, had done.

And David ent and took the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead, ho had taken them aay secretly from the public place of Beth-shan, here the Philistines had put them, hanging up the bodies there on the day hen they put Saul to death in Gilboa:

And they put them ith the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the resting-place of Kish, his father, in Zela in the country of Benjamin; they did all the king had given them orders to do. And after that, God gave ear to their prayers for the land.
And the Philistines ent to ar again ith Israel; and David ent don ith his people, and hile they ere at Gob they had a fight ith the Philistines:
And there came against David one of the offspring of the Rephaim, hose spear as three hundred shekels of brass in eight, and having a ne sord, he made an attempt to put David to death.

But Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, came to his help, and, turning on the Philistine, gave him his death-blo. Then David’s men took an oath, and said, Never again are you to go out ith us to the fight, so that you may not put out the light of Israel.
No after this there as ar ith the Philistines again at Gob, and Sibbecai the Hushathite put to death Saph, one of the offspring of the Rephaim.
And again there as ar ith the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan, the son of Jair the Beth-lehemite, put to death Goliath the Gittite, the stem of hose spear as like a cloth-orker’s rod.
And again there as ar at Gath, here there as a very tall man, ho had tenty-four fingers and toes, six fingers on his hands and six toes on his feet; he as one of the offspring of the Rephaim.
And hen he as purposing to put shame on Israel, Jonathan, the son of Shimei, David’s brother, put him to death.
These four ere of the offspring of the Rephaim in Gath; and they came to their end by the hands of David and his servants.
And David made a song to the Lord in these ords, on the day hen the Lord made him free from the hands of all his haters, and from the hand of Saul:
And he said, The Lord is my Rock, my alled ton, and my saviour, even mine;
My God, my Rock, in him ill I put my faith; my breastplate, and the horn of my salvation, my high toer, and my safe place; my saviour, ho keeps me safe from the violent man.
I ill send up my cry to the Lord, ho is to be praised; so ill I be made safe from those ho are against me.
For the aves of death came round me, and the seas of evil put me in fear;
The cords of hell ere round me: the nets of death came on me.
In my trouble my voice ent up to the Lord, and my cry to my God: my voice came to his hearing in his holy Temple, and my prayer came to his ears.
Then the earth as moved ith a violent shock; the bases of heaven ere moved and shaking, because he as angry.
There ent up a smoke from his nose, and a fire of destruction from his mouth: coals ere lighted by it.
The heavens ere bent, so that he might come don; and it as dark under his feet.
And he ent through the air, seated on a storm-cloud: going quickly on the ings of the ind.
And he made the dark his tent round him, a mass of aters, thick clouds of the skies.
Before his shining light his dark clouds ent past, raining ice and coals of fire.
The Lord made thunder in the heavens, and the voice of the Highest as sounding out.
And he sent out his arros, driving them in all directions; by his flames of fire they ere troubled.
Then the deep beds of the sea ere seen, and the bases of the orld ere uncovered, because of the Lord’s rath, because of the breath of his mouth.
He sent from on high, he took me, pulling me out of great aters.
He made me free from my strong hater, from those ho ere against me, because they ere stronger than I.
They came on me in the day of my trouble: but the Lord as my support.
He took me out into a ide place; he as my saviour because he had delight in me.
The Lord gives me the reard of my righteousness, because my hands are clean before him.
For I have kept the ays of the Lord; I have not been turned aay in sin from my God.
For all his decisions ere before me, and I did not put aay his las from me.
And I as upright before him, and I kept myself from sin.
Because of this the Lord has given me the reard of my righteousness, because my hands are clean in his eyes.
On him ho has mercy you ill have mercy; to the upright you ill be upright;
He ho is holy ill see that you are holy; but to the man hose ay is not straight you ill be a hard judge.
For you are the saviour of those ho are in trouble; but your eyes are on men of pride, to make them lo.
For you are my light, O Lord; and the Lord ill make the dark bright for me.
By your help I have made a ay through the all hich as shutting me in: by the help of my God I have gone over a all.
As for God, his ay is all good: the ord of the Lord is tested; he is a safe cover for all those ho put their faith in him.
For ho is God but the Lord? and ho is a Rock but our God?
God puts a strong band about me, guiding me in a straight ay.
He makes my feet like roes’ feet, and puts me on high places.
He makes my hands expert in ar, so that a bo of brass is bent by my arms.
You have given me the breastplate of your salvation, and your mercy has made me great.
You have made my steps ide under me, so that my feet make no slip.
I go after my haters and overtake them; not turning back till they are all overcome.
I have sent destruction on them and given them ounds, so that they are not able to get up: they are stretched under my feet.
For I have been armed by you ith strength for the fight: you have made lo under me those ho came out against me.
By you their backs are turned in flight, so that my haters are cut off.
They ere crying out, but there as no one to come to their help: even to the Lord, but he gave them no anser.
Then they ere crushed as small as the dust of the earth, stamped don under my feet like the aste of the streets.
You have made me free from the fightings of my people; you have made me the head of the nations: a people of hom I had no knoledge ill be my servants.
Men of other countries ill, ith false hearts, put themselves under my authority: from the time hen my name comes to their ears, they ill be ruled by me.
They ill be asted aay, they ill come out of their secret places shaking ith fear.
The Lord is living; praise be to my Rock, and let the God of my salvation be honoured:
It is God ho sends punishment on my haters, and puts peoples under my rule.
He makes me free from my haters: I am lifted up over those ho come up against me: you have made me free from the violent man.
Because of this I ill give you praise, O Lord, among the nations, and ill make a song of praise to your name.
Great salvation does he give to his king; he has mercy on the king of his selection, David, and on his seed for ever.
No these are the last ords of David. David, the son of Jesse, says, the man ho as lifted up on high, the man on hom the God of Jacob put the holy oil, the loved one of Israel’s songs, says:
The spirit of the Lord had voice through me, his ord as on my tongue.
The God of Israel said, the ord of the Rock of Israel came to me: When an upright king is ruling over men, hen he is ruling in the fear of God,
It is as the light of the morning, hen the sun comes up, a morning ithout clouds; making young grass come to life from the earth.
For is not my house so ith God? For he has made ith me an eternal agreement, ordered in all things and certain: as for all my salvation and all my desire, ill he not give it increase?
But the evil-doers, all of them, ill be like thorns to be pushed aay, because they may not be gripped in the hand:
But anyone touching them has to be armed ith iron and the rod of a spear; and they ill be burned ith fire, every one of them.
These are the names of David’s men of ar: Ishbaal the Hachmonite, chief of the three; his axe as lifted up against eight hundred put to death at one time.

After him as Eleazar, the son of Dodai the Ahohite, one of the three great fighters, ho as ith David in Pas-dammim hen the Philistines came together there for the fight; and hen the men of Israel had gone in flight,

He as ith David and ent on fighting the Philistines till his hand became tired and stiff from gripping his sord: and that day the Lord gave a great salvation, and the people came back after him only to take the goods of the Philistines.
After him as Shammah, the son of Ela the Hararite. And the Philistines came together in Lehi, here there as a bit of land full of seed; and the people ent in flight from the Philistines.
But he kept his place in the middle of the bit of land, and kept back their attack and overcame the Philistines: and the Lord gave a great salvation.

And three of the thirty ent don at the start of the grain-cutting, and they came to David at the strong place of Adullam; and the band of Philistines had taken up their position in the valley of Rephaim.
And at that time David had taken cover in the strong place, and an armed force of the Philistines as in Beth-lehem.
And David, moved by a strong desire, said, If only someone ould give me a drink of ater from the ater-hole of Beth-lehem, by the dooray into the ton!

And the three men, forcing their ay through the Philistine army, got ater from the ater-hole of Beth-lehem, by the dooray into the ton, and took it back to David: but he ould not take it, but, draining it out, made an offering of it to the Lord.

And he said, Far be it from me, O Lord, to do this; ho may I take as my drink the life-blood of men ho have put their lives in danger? So he ould not take it. These things did the three great men of ar.
And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, as chief of the thirty. He put to death three hundred ith his spear, and he got for himself a name among the thirty.
Was he not the noblest of the thirty? so he as made their captain: but he as not equal to the first three.
And Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, a fighting man of Kabzeel, had done great acts; he put to death the to sons of Ariel of Moab: he ent don into a hole and put a lion to death in time of sno:

And he made an attack on an Egyptian, a tall man: and the Egyptian had a spear in his hand; but he ent don to him ith a stick, and pulling the spear out of the hands of the Egyptian, put him to death ith that same spear.
These ere the acts of Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, ho had a great name among the thirty men of ar.
He as honoured over the rest of the thirty, but he as not equal to the first three. And David put him over the fighting men ho kept him safe.
Asahel, the brother of Joab, as one of the thirty; and Elhanan, the son of Dodai, of Beth-lehem,
Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite,
Helez the Paltite, Ira, the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite,
Abiezer the Anathothite, Sibbecai the Hushathite,
Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite,
Heldai, the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai, the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin,
Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai of the valleys of Gaash,
Abiel the Arbathite, Azmaveth of Bahurim,
Eliahba the Shaalbonite, Jashen the Gunite,
Jonathan, the son of Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam, the son of Sharar the Hararite,
Eliphelet, the son of Ahasbai the Maacathite, Eliam, the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite,
Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Archite,
Igal, the son of Nathan of Zobah, Bani the Gadite,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, ho had the care of the arms of Joab, son of Zeruiah,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in number.
Again the rath of the Lord as burning against Israel, and moving David against them, he said, Go, take the number of Israel and Judah.

And the king said to Joab and the captains of the army, ho ere ith him, Go no through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan as far as Beer-sheba, and have all the people numbered, so that I may be certain of the number of the people.

And Joab said to the king, Whatever the number of the people, may the Lord make it a hundred times as much, and may the eyes of my lord the king see it: but hy does my lord the king take pleasure in doing this thing?
But the king’s order as stronger than Joab and the captains of the army. And Joab and the captains of the army ent out from the king, to take the number of the children of Israel.
And they ent over Jordan, and starting from Aroer, from the ton hich is in the middle of the valley, they ent in the direction of the Gadites, and on to Jazer;
Then they came to Gilead, and to the land of the Hittites under Hermon; and they came to Dan, and from Dan they came round to Zidon,
And to the alled ton of Tyre, and to all the tons of the Hivites and the Canaanites: and they ent out to the South of Judah at Beer-sheba.
So after going through all the land in every direction, they came to Jerusalem at the end of nine months and tenty days.
And Joab gave the king the number of all the people: there ere in Israel eight hundred thousand fighting men able to take up arms; and the men of Judah ere five hundred thousand.

And after the people had been numbered, David’s heart as troubled. And David said to the Lord, Great has been my sin in doing this; but no, O Lord, be pleased to take aay the sin of your servant, for I have done very foolishly
And David got up in the morning; no the ord of the Lord had come to the prophet Gad, David’s seer, saying,
Go and say to David, The Lord says, Three things are offered to you: say hich of them you ill have, and I ill do it to you.

So Gad came to David, and gave him ord of this and said to him, Are there to be three years hen there is not enough food in your land? or ill you go in flight from your haters for three months, hile they go after you? or ill you have three days of violent disease in your land? take thought and say hat anser I am to give to him ho sent me.
And David said to Gad, This is a hard decision for me to make: let us come into the hands of the Lord, for great are his mercies: let me not come into the hands of men.
So David made selection of the disease; and the time as the days of the grain-cutting, hen the disease came among the people, causing the death of seventy thousand men from Dan as far as Beer-sheba.

And hen the hand of the angel as stretched out in the direction of Jerusalem, for its destruction, the Lord had regret for the evil, and said to the angel ho as sending destruction on the people, It is enough; do no more. And the angel of the Lord as by the grain-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

And hen David sa the angel ho as causing the destruction of the people, he said to the Lord, Truly, the sin is mine; I have done rong: but these are only sheep; hat have they done? let your hand be against me and against my family.
And that day Gad came to David and said to him, Go up, and put up an altar to the Lord on the grain-floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
So David ent up, as Gad had said and as the Lord had given orders.
And Araunah, looking out, sa the king and his servants coming to him: and Araunah ent out, and ent don on his face to the earth before the king.

And Araunah said, Why has my lord the king come to his servant? And David said, To give you a price for your grain-floor, so that I may put up an altar to the Lord, and the disease may be stopped among the people.

And Araunah said to David, Let my lord the king take hatever seems right to him, and make an offering of it: see, here are the oxen for the burned offering, and the grain-cleaning instruments and the ox-yokes for ood:
All this does the servant of my lord the king give to the king. And Araunah said, May the Lord your God be pleased ith your offering!

And the king said to Araunah, No, but I ill give you a price for it; I ill not give to the Lord my God burned offerings for hich I have given nothing. So David got the grain-floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
And there David put up an altar to the Lord, making burned offerings and peace-offerings. So the Lord gave ear to his prayer for the land, and the disease came to an end in Israel.
No King David as old and far on in years; and though they put covers over him, his body as cold.

So his servants said to him, Let search be made for a young virgin for my lord the king, to take care of him and be aiting on him; and you may take her in your arms, and so my lord the king ill be arm.
So after searching through all the land of Israel for a fair young girl, they sa Abishag the Shunammite, and took her to the king.
No she as very beautiful; and she took care of the king, aiting on him at all times; but the king had no connection ith her.
Then Adonijah, the son of Haggith, lifting himself up in pride, said, I ill become king; and he made ready his carriages of ar and his horsemen, ith fifty runners to go before him.
No all his life his father had never gone against him or said to him, Why have you done so? and he as a very good-looking man, and younger than Absalom.
And he had talk ith Joab, the son of Zeruiah, and ith Abiathar the priest; and they ere on his side and gave him their support.
But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet and Shimei and Rei, and David’s men of ar did not take the side of Adonijah.

Then Adonijah put to death sheep and oxen and fat beasts by the stone of Zoheleth, by En-rogel; and he sent for all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah, the king’s servants, to come to him:
But he did not send for Nathan the prophet and Benaiah and the other men of ar and Solomon his brother.
Then Nathan said to Bath-sheba, the mother of Solomon, Has it not come to your ears that Adonijah, the son of Haggith, has made himself king ithout the knoledge of David our lord?
So no, let me make a suggestion, so that you may keep your life safe and the life of your son Solomon.

Come no, go to King David and say to him, Did you not, O my lord, take an oath to me, your servant, saying, Truly Solomon your son ill be king after me, seated on the seat of my kingdom? hy then is Adonijah acting as king?
And hile you are still talking there ith the king, see, I ill come in after you and say that your story is true.
Then Bath-sheba ent into the king’s room; no the king as very old, and Abishag the Shunammite as aiting on him.
And Bath-sheba ent don on her face on the earth before the king giving him honour. And he said, What is your desire?
And she said to him, My lord, you took an oath by the Lord your God and gave your ord to your servant, saying, Truly, Solomon your son ill be king after me, seated on the seat of my kingdom.
And no, see, Adonijah has made himself king ithout my lord’s knoledge;

And has put to death oxen and fat beasts and sheep in great numbers, and has sent for all the sons of the king, and Abiathar the priest, and Joab, the captain of the army; but he has not sent for Solomon your servant.
And no, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, aiting for you to say ho is to take the place of my lord the king after him.
For as things are, it ill come about, hen my lord the king is sleeping ith his fathers, that I and Solomon my son ill be made outlas.
And hile she as still talking ith the king, Nathan the prophet came in.
And they said to the king, Here is Nathan the prophet. And hen he came in before the king, he ent don on his face on the earth.
And Nathan said, O my lord king, have you said, Adonijah is to be king after me, seated on the seat of my kingdom?

Because today he has gone don and has put to death oxen and fat beasts and sheep in great numbers, and has sent for all the king’s sons to come to him, ith the captains of the army and Abiathar the priest; and they are feasting before him and crying, Long life to King Adonijah!
But me, your servant, and Zadok the priest, and Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, and your servant Solomon, he has not sent for.
Has this thing been done by my lord the king, ithout giving ord to your servants ho as to be placed on my lord the king’s seat after him?
Then King David in anser said, Send for Bath-sheba to come to me. And she came in and took her place before the king.
And the king took an oath, and said, By the living Lord, ho has been my saviour from all my troubles,
As I took an oath to you by the Lord, the God of Israel, saying, Certainly Solomon your son ill become king after me, seated on my seat in my place; so ill I do this day.
Then Bath-sheba ent don on her face on the earth before the king giving him honour, and said, May my lord King David go on living for ever.
And King David said, Send for Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada. And they came before the king.
And the king said to them, Take ith you the servants of your lord, and put Solomon my son on my beast, yes, mine, and take him don to Gihon;
And there let Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet put the holy oil on him to make him king over Israel; and sounding the horn say, Long life to King Solomon!
Then come up after him and he ill come in and take his place on the seat of my kingdom; for he is to be king in my place, and I have given orders that he is to be ruler over Israel and over Judah.
And Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, ansering the king, said, So be it: and may the Lord, the God of my lord the king, say so.
As the Lord has been ith my lord the king, even so may he be ith Solomon and make the seat of his authority greater than that of my lord King David.
So Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, ent don and put Solomon on King David’s beast and took him to Gihon.
And Zadok the priest took the vessel of oil out of the Tent, and put the holy oil on Solomon. And hen the horn as sounded, all the people said, Long life to King Solomon!
And all the people came up after him, piping ith pipes, and they ere glad ith great joy, so that the earth as shaking ith the sound.

And it came to the ears of Adonijah and all the guests ho ere ith him, hen their meal as ended. And Joab, hearing the sound of the horn, said, What is the reason of this noise as if the ton as orked up?
And hile the ords ere on his lips, Jonathan, the son of Abiathar the priest, came; and Adonijah said, Come in; for you are a man of good faith and the nes hich you have for us ill be good.
And Jonathan, ansering, said to Adonijah, Not so, but our lord King David has made Solomon king:
And he sent ith him Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and they put him on the king’s beast:

And Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet put the holy oil on him and made him king in Gihon; and they came back from there ith joy, and the ton as all orked up. This is the noise hich has come to your ears.
And no Solomon is seated on the seat of the kingdom.

And the king’s servants came to our lord King David, blessing him and saying, May God make the name of Solomon better than your name, and the seat of his authority greater than your seat; and the king as bent lo in orship on his bed.
Then the king said, May the God of Israel be praised, ho has given one of my seed to be king in my place this day and has let my eyes see it.
And all the guests of Adonijah got up in fear and ent aay, every man to his place.
And Adonijah himself as full of fear because of Solomon; and he got up and ent to the altar, and put his hands on its horns.

And they gave Solomon ord of it, saying, See, Adonijah goes in such fear of King Solomon, that he has put his hands on the horns of the altar, saying, Let King Solomon first give me his oath that he ill not put his servant to death ith the sord.
And Solomon said, If he is seen to be a man of good faith, not a hair of him ill be touched; but if any rongdoing is seen in him, he is to be put to death.
So King Solomon sent, and they took him don from the altar. And he came and gave honour to King Solomon; and Solomon said to him, Go to your house.
No the time of David’s death came near; and he gave orders to Solomon his son, saying,
I am going the ay of all the earth: so be strong and be a man;

And keep the orders of the Lord your God, alking in his ays, keeping his las and his orders and his rules and his ords, as they are recorded in the la of Moses; so that you may do ell in all you do and herever you go,

So that the Lord may give effect to hat he said of me, If your children give attention to their ays, living uprightly before me ith all their heart and their soul, you ill never be ithout a man to be king in Israel.

No you have knoledge of hat Joab, the son of Zeruiah, did to me, and to the to captains of the army of Israel, Abner, the son of Ner, and Amasa, the son of Jether, hom he put to death, taking payment for the blood of ar in time of peace, and making the band of my clothing and the shoes on my feet red ith the blood of one put to death ithout cause.
So be guided by your isdom, and let not his hite head go don to the underorld in peace.
But be good to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be guests at your table; for so they came to me hen I ent in flight from Absalom your brother.

No you have ith you Shimei, the son of Gera the Benjamite of Bahurim, ho put a bitter curse on me on the day hen I ent to Mahanaim; but he came don to see me at Jordan, and I gave him my oath by the Lord, saying, I ill not put you to death by the sord.
But do not let him be free from punishment, for you are a ise man; and it ill be clear to you hat you have to do ith him; see that his hite head goes don to the underorld in blood.
Then David ent to rest ith his fathers, and his body as put into the earth in the ton of David.
David as king over Israel for forty years: for seven years he as king in Hebron and for thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
And Solomon took his place on the seat of David his father, and his kingdom as made safe and strong.
Then Adonijah, the son of Haggith, came to Bath-sheba, the mother of Solomon. And she said, Come you in peace? And he said, Yes, in peace.
Then he said, I have something to say to you. And she said, Say on.
And he said, You sa ho the kingdom as mine, and all Israel had the idea that I ould be their king; but no the kingdom is turned about, and has become my brother’s, for it as given to him by the Lord.
No I have one request to make to you, and do not say, No, to me. And she said to him, Say on.
Then he said, Will you go to Solomon the king ( for he ill not say, No, to you) and put before him my request that he ill give me Abishag the Shunammite for a ife?
And Bath-sheba said, Good! I ill make your request to the king.

So Bath-sheba ent to King Solomon to have talk ith him on Adonijah’s account. And the king got up to come to her, and ent don lo to the earth before her; then he took his place on the king’s seat and had a seat made ready for the king’s mother and she took her place at his right hand.
Then she said, I have one small request to make to you; do not say, No, to me. And the king said, Say on, my mother, for I ill not say, No, to you.
And she said, Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother for a ife.

Then King Solomon made anser and said to his mother, Why are you requesting me to give Abishag the Shunammite to Adonijah? Take the kingdom for him in addition, for he is my older brother, and Abiathar the priest and Joab, the son of Zeruiah, are on his side.
Then King Solomon took an oath by the Lord, saying, May God’s punishment be on me if Adonijah does not give payment for these ords ith his life.
No by the living Lord, ho has given me my place on the seat of David my father, and made me one of a line of kings, as he gave me his ord, truly Adonijah ill be put to death this day.
And King Solomon sent Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, and he made an attack on him and put him to death.

And to Abiathar the priest the king said, Go to Anathoth, to your fields; for death ould be your right reard; but I ill not put you to death no, because you took up the ark of the Lord God before David my father, and you ere ith him in all his troubles.
So Solomon let Abiathar be priest no longer, so that he might make the ord of the Lord come true hich he said about the sons of Eli in Shiloh.

And nes of this came to Joab; for Joab had been one of Adonijah’s supporters, though he had not been on Absalom’s side. Then Joab ent in flight to the Tent of the Lord, and put his hands on the horns of the altar.
And they said to King Solomon, Joab has gone in flight to the Tent of the Lord and is by the altar. Then Solomon sent Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, saying, Go, make an attack on him.

And Benaiah came to the Tent of the Lord and said to him, The king says, Come out. And he said, No; but let death come to me here. And Benaiah ent back to the king and gave him ord of the anser hich Joab had given.

And the king said, Do as he has said and make an attack on him there, and put his body into the earth; so that you may take aay from me and from my family the blood of one put to death by Joab ithout cause.

And the Lord ill send back his blood on his head, because of the attack he made on to men more upright and better than himself, putting them to the sord ithout my father’s knoledge; even Abner, the son of Ner, captain of the army of Israel, and Amasa, the son of Jether, captain of the army of Judah.
So their blood ill be on the head of Joab, and on the head of his seed for ever; but for David and his seed and his family and the seat of his kingdom, there ill be peace for ever from the Lord.
So Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, ent up, and falling on him, put him to death; and his body as put to rest in his house in the aste land.
And the king put Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, in his place over the army; and Zadok the priest he put in the place of Abiathar.
Then the king sent for Shimei, and said to him, Make a house for yourself in Jerusalem and keep there and go to no other place.
For be certain that on the day hen you go out and go over the stream Kidron, death ill overtake you: and your blood ill be on your head.
And Shimei said to the king, Very ell! as my lord the king has said, so ill your servant do. And for a long time Shimei ent on living in Jerusalem.
But after three years, to of the servants of Shimei ent in flight to Achish, son of Maacah, king of Gath. And ord as given to Shimei that his servants had gone to Gath.
Then Shimei got up, and making ready his ass, he ent to Gath, to Achish, in search of his servants; and he sent and got them from Gath.
And nes as given to Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had come back again.

Then the king sent for Shimei, and said to him, Did I not make you take an oath by the Lord, protesting to you and saying, Be certain that on the day hen you go out from here, herever you go, death ill overtake you? and you said to me, Very ell!
Why then have you not kept the oath of the Lord and the order hich I gave you?
And the king said to Shimei, You have knoledge of all the evil hich you did to David my father; and no the Lord has sent back your evil on yourself.
But a blessing ill be on King Solomon, and the kingdom of David ill keep its place before the Lord for ever.
So the king gave orders to Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada; and he ent out and, falling on him, put him to death. And Solomon’s authority over the kingdom as complete.

Solomon became the son-in-la of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh’s daughter as his ife, keeping her in the ton of David, till the house he as building for himself, and the house of the Lord and the all round Jerusalem, ere complete.
But all this time the people ere making their offerings in the high places, because no house had been put up to the name of the Lord till those days.
And Solomon, in his love for the Lord, kept the las of David his father; but he made offerings and let them go up in smoke on the high places.
And the king ent to Gibeon to make an offering there, because that as the chief high place: it as Solomon’s ay to make a thousand burned offerings on that altar.
In Gibeon, Solomon had a vision of the Lord in a dream by night; and God said to him, Say hat I am to give you.

And Solomon said, Great as your mercy to David my father, as his life before you as true and upright and his heart as true to you; and you have kept for him this greatest mercy, a son to take his place this day.
And no, O Lord my God, you have made your servant king in the place of David my father; and I am only a young boy, ith no knoledge of ho to go out or come in.
And your servant has round him the people of your selection, a people so great that they may not be numbered, and no account of them may be given.
Give your servant, then, a ise heart for judging your people, able to see hat is good and hat evil; for ho is able to be the judge of this great people?
No these ords and Solomon’s request ere pleasing to the Lord.
And God said to him, Because your request is for this thing, and not for long life for yourself or for ealth or for the destruction of your haters, but for isdom to be a judge of causes;
I have done as you said: I have given you a ise and far-seeing heart, so that there has never been your equal in the past, and never ill there be any like you in the future.
And ith this I have given you hat you made no request for: ealth and honour, so that no king as ever your equal.
And if you go on in my ays, keeping my las and my orders as your father David did, I ill give you a long life.

And Solomon, aakening, sa that it as a dream; then he came to Jerusalem, here he ent before the ark of the agreement of the Lord, offering burned offerings and peace-offerings; and he made a feast for all his servants.
Then to loose omen of the ton came and took their places before the king;
And one of them said, O my lord, I and this oman are living in the same house; and I gave birth to a child by her side in the house.
And three days after the birth of my child, this oman had a child: e ere together, no other-person as ith us in the house but e to only.
In the night, this oman, sleeping on her child, as the cause of its death.
And she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side hile your servant as sleeping; and she took it in her arms and put her dead child in my arms.
And hen I got up to give my child the breast, I sa that it as dead; but in the morning, looking at it ith care, I sa that it as not my son.

And the other oman said, No; but the living child is my son and the dead one yours. But the first said, No; the dead child is your son and the living one mine. So they kept on talking before the king.
Then the king said, One says, The living child is my son, and yours is the dead: and the other says, Not so; but your son is the dead one and mine is the living.
Then he said, Get me a sord. So they ent and put a sord before the king.
And the king said, Let the living child be cut in to and one half given to one oman and one to the other.

Then the mother of the living child came forard, for her heart ent out to her son, and she said, O my lord, give her the child; do not on any account put it to death. But the other oman said, It ill not be mine or yours; let it be cut in to.
Then the king made anser and said, Give her the child, and do not put it to death; she is the mother of it.
And nes of this decision hich the king had made ent through all Israel; and they had fear of the king, for they sa that the isdom of God as in him to give decisions.
No Solomon as king over all Israel.
And these ere his chief men: Azariah, the son of Zadok, as the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, ere scribes; Jehoshaphat, the son of Ahilud, as the recorder;
Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, as head of the army; Zadok and Abiathar ere priests;
Azariah, the son of Nathan, as over those in authority in the different divisions of the country; Zabud, the son of Nathan, as priest and the king’s friend;
Ahishar as controller of the king’s house; Adoniram, the son of Abda, as overseer of the forced ork.
And Solomon put telve overseers over all Israel, to be responsible for the stores needed for the king and those of his house; every man as responsible for one month in the year.
And these are their names: ... the son of Hur in the hill country of Ephraim;
... the son of Deker in Makaz and Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh and Elonbeth-hanan;
... the son of Hesed in Arubboth; Socoh and all the land of Hepher ere under his control;
... the son of Abinadab in all Naphath-dor; his ife as Taphath, the daughter of Solomon.
Baana, the son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo, and all Beth-shean hich is by the side of Zarethan, under Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as the far side of Jokmeam;
... the son of Geber in Ramoth-gilead; he had the tons of Jair, the son of Manasseh, hich are in Gilead, and the country of Argob, hich is in Bashan, sixty great tons ith alls and locks of brass.
Ahinadab, the son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz in Naphtali; he took Basemath, the daughter of Solomon, as his ife;
Baana, the son of Hushai, in Asher and Aloth;
Jehoshaphat, the son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei, the son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber, the son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the country of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan; and one overseer had authority over all the overseers ho ere in the land.
Judah and Israel ere as great in number as the sand by the seaside, and they took their food and drink ith joy in their hearts.
And Solomon as ruler over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines, and as far as the edge of Egypt; men gave him offerings and ere his servants all the days of his life.
And the amount of Solomon’s food for one day as thirty measures of crushed grain and sixty measures of meal;
Ten fat oxen and tenty oxen from the fields, and a hundred sheep, in addition to harts and gazelles and roes and fat fols.
For he had authority over all the country on this side of the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings on this side of the River; and he had peace round him on every side.
So Judah and Israel ere living safely, every man under his vine and his fig-tree, from Dan as far as Beer-sheba, all the days of Solomon.
And Solomon had four thousand boxed-off spaces for horses for his carriages, and telve thousand horsemen.
And those overseers, every man in his month, sa that food as produced for Solomon and all his guests, they took care that nothing as overlooked.
And they took grain and dry grass for the horses and the carriage-horses, to the right place, every man as he as ordered.
And God gave Solomon a great store of isdom and good sense, and a mind of ide range, as ide as the sand by the seaside.
And Solomon’s isdom as greater than the isdom of all the people of the East and all the isdom of Egypt.
For he as iser than all men, even than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman and Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol; and he had a great name among all the nations round about.
He as the maker of three thousand ise sayings, and of songs to the number of a thousand and five.
He made sayings about all plants, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop hanging on the all; and about all beasts and birds and fishes and the small things of the earth.
People came from every nation to give ear to the isdom of Solomon, from all the kings of the earth ho had ord of his isdom.
No Hiram, king of Tyre, hearing that Solomon had been made king in place of his father, sent his servants to him; for Hiram had ever been a friend to David.
And Solomon sent back ord to Hiram, saying,

You have knoledge that David my father as not able to make a house for the name of the Lord his God, because of the ars hich ere round him on every side, till the Lord put all those ho ere against him under his feet.
