But no the Lord my God has given me rest on every side; no one is making trouble, and no evil is taking place.
And so it is my purpose to make a house for the name of the Lord my God, as he said to David my father, Your son, hom I ill make king in your place, ill be the builder of a house for my name.

So no, ill you have cedar-trees from Lebanon cut don for me, and my servants ill be ith your servants; and I ill give you payment for your servants at hatever rate you say; for it is common knoledge that e have no such ood-cutters among us as the men of Zidon.
And these ords of Solomon made Hiram glad, and he said, No may the Lord be praised ho has given to David a ise son to be king over this great people.
Then Hiram sent to Solomon, saying; The ords you sent have been given to me: I ill do all your desire in the question of cedar-ood and cypress-ood.

My men ill take them don from Lebanon to the sea, here I ill have them corded together to go by sea to hatever place you say, and I ill have them cut up there so that you may take them aay; as for payment, it ill be enough if you give me food for my people.
So Hiram gave Solomon all the cedar-ood and cypress-ood he had need of;
And Solomon gave Hiram tenty thousand measures of grain, as food for his people, and tenty measures of clear oil; this he did every year.
No the Lord had given Solomon isdom, as he had said to him; and there as peace beteen Hiram and Solomon, and they made an agreement together.
Then King Solomon got together men for the forced ork through all Israel, thirty thousand men in number;
And sent them to Lebanon in bands of ten thousand every month: for a month they ere orking in Lebanon and for to months in their country, and Adoniram as in control of them.
Then he had seventy thousand for the ork of transport, and eighty thousand stone-cutters in the mountains;
In addition to the chiefs of the responsible men put by Solomon to oversee the ork, three thousand and three hundred in authority over the orkmen.
By the king’s orders great stones, stones of high price, ere cut out, so that the base of the house might be made of squared stone.
Solomon’s builders and Hiram’s builders did the ork of cutting them, and put edges on them, and got the ood and the stone ready for the building of the house.

In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year that Solomon as king of Israel, in the month Ziv, hich is the second month, the building of the Lord’s house as started.
The house hich Solomon made for the Lord as sixty cubits long, tenty cubits ide and thirty cubits high.
The covered ay before the Temple of the house as tenty cubits long, as ide as the house, and ten cubits ide in front of the house.
And for the house he made indos, ith netork across.
And against the alls all round, and against the alls of the Temple and of the inmost room, he put up ings, ith side rooms all round:

The loest line of them being five cubits ide, the middle six cubits ide and the third seven cubits; for there as a space all round the outside alls of the house so that the boards supporting the rooms did not have to be fixed in the alls of the house.
( And the stones used in the building of the house ere squared at the place here they ere cut out; there as no sound of hammer or axe or any iron instrument hile they ere building the house.)
The door to the loest side rooms as in the right side of the house; and they ent up by tisting steps into the middle rooms, and from the middle into the third.
So he put up the house and made it complete, roofing it ith boards of cedar-ood.
And he put up the line of side rooms against the alls of the house, fifteen cubits high, resting against the house on boards of cedar-ood.
( And the ord of the Lord came to Solomon, saying,
About this house hich you are building: if you ill keep my las and give effect to my decisions and be guided by my rules, I ill give effect to my ord hich I gave to David your father.
And I ill be ever among the children of Israel, and ill not go aay from my people.
So Solomon made the building of the house complete.)
The alls of the house ere covered inside ith cedar-ood boards; from the floor to the roof of the house they ere covered inside ith ood; and the floor as covered ith boards of cypress-ood.
And at the back of the house a further space of tenty cubits as shut in ith boards of cedar-ood, for the inmost room.
And the house, that is, the Temple, in front of the holy place as forty cubits long.
( All the inside of the house as cedar-ood, ornamented ith designs of buds and floers; no stoneork as to be seen inside.)
And he made ready an inmost room in the middle of the house, in hich to put the ark of the agreement of the Lord.
And the inmost room as tenty cubits square and tenty cubits high, plated over ith clear gold, and he made an altar of cedar-ood, plating it ith gold.
Solomon had all the inside of the house covered ith gold, and he put chains of gold across in front of the inmost room, hich itself as covered ith gold.
Plates of gold ere put all through the house till it as covered completely ( and the altar in the inmost room as all covered ith gold).
In the inmost room he made to inged beings of olive-ood, ten cubits high;
With outstretched ings five cubits ide; the distance from the edge of one ing to the edge of the other as ten cubits.
The to inged ones ere ten cubits high, of the same size and form.
The to of them ere ten cubits high.
These ere placed inside the inner house, their outstretched ings touching the alls of the house, one touching one all and one the other, hile their other ings ere touching in the middle.
These inged ones ere plated over ith gold.
And all the alls of the house inside and out ere ornamented ith forms of inged ones and palm-trees and open floers.
And the floor of the house as covered ith gold, inside and out.
For the ay into the inmost room he made doors of olive-ood, the arch and the door supports forming a five-sided opening.
On the olive-ood doors ere cut designs of inged ones and palm-trees and open floers, all of them, ith the doors, plated ith gold.
Then he made pillars of olive-ood for the ay into the Temple; the pillars ere square:
And to folding doors of cypress-ood, ith to leaves.
These ere ornamented ith designs of inged ones and palm-trees and open floers, plated over ith gold.
And the inner space as alled ith three lines of squared stones and a line of cedar-ood boards.
In the fourth year the base of the house as put in its place, in the month Ziv.
And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, hich is the eighth month, the building of the house as complete in every detail, as it had been designed. So he as seven years building it.
Solomon as thirteen years building a house for himself till it as complete.

And he made the house of the Woods of Lebanon, hich as a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits ide and thirty cubits high, resting on four lines of cedar-ood pillars ith cedar-ood supports on the pillars.
And it as covered ith cedar over the forty-five supports hich ere on the pillars, fifteen in a line.
There ere three lines of indo-frames, indo facing indo in every line.
And all the doors and indos had square frames, ith the indos facing one another in three lines.
And he made a covered room of pillars, fifty cubits long and thirty cubits ide, and ... ith steps before it.
Then he made a covered room for his high seat hen he gave decisions; this as the covered room of judging; it as covered ith cedar-ood from floor to roof.
And the house for his living-place, the other open square in the covered room, as made in the same ay. And then he made a house like it for Pharaoh’s daughter, hom Solomon had taken as his ife.
All these buildings ere made, inside and out, from base to croning stone, and outside to the great alled square, of highly priced stone, cut to different sizes ith cutting-instruments.
And the base as of great masses of highly priced stone, some ten cubits and some eight cubits square.
Overhead ere highly priced stones cut to measure, and cedar-ood.

The great outer square all round as alled ith three lines of squared stones and a line of cedar-ood boards, round about the open square inside the house of the Lord and the covered room of the king’s house.
Then King Solomon sent and got Hiram from Tyre.

He as the son of a ido of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father as a man of Tyre, a orker in brass; he as full of isdom and knoledge and an expert orker in brass. He came to King Solomon and did all his ork for him.
He it as ho made the to brass pillars; the first pillar as eighteen cubits high, and a line of telve cubits ent round it; and the second as the same.
And he made the to crons to be put on the tops of the pillars, of brass made soft in the fire; the crons ere five cubits high.
There ere nets of open-ork for the crons on the tops of the pillars, a net of open-ork for one and a net of open-ork for the other.
And he made ornaments of apples; and to lines of apples all round over the netork, covering the crons of the pillars, the to crons in the same ay.
The crons on the tops of the pillars ere ornamented ith a design of floers, and ere four cubits across.
And there ere crons on the to pillars near the round part by the netork, and there ere to hundred apples in lines round every cron.
He put up the pillars at the dooray of the Temple, naming the one on the right Jachin, and that on the left Boaz.
The tops of the pillars had a design of floers; and the ork of making the pillars as complete.
And he made a great metal ater-vessel ten cubits across from edge to edge, five cubits high and thirty cubits round.
And under the edge of it, circling it all round for ten cubits, ere to lines of floer buds, made together ith it from liquid metal.

It as supported on telve oxen, ith their back parts turned to the middle of it, three of them facing to the north, three to the est, three to the south, and three to the east; the vessel as resting on top of them.
It as as thick as a man’s open hand, and as curved like the edge of a cup, like the floer of a lily: it ould take to thousand baths.
And he made ten heeled bases of brass; every one four cubits long, four cubits ide, and three cubits high.
And the bases ere made in this ay; their sides ere square, fixed in a frameork;
And on the square sides beteen the frames ere lions, oxen, and inged ones; and the same on the frame; and over and under the lions and the oxen and the inged ones ere steps.

Every base had four heels of brass, turning on brass rods, and their four angles had angle-plates under them; the angle-plates under the base ere of metal, and there ere ornaments at the side of every one.
The mouth of it inside the angle-plate as one cubit across; it as round like a pillar, a cubit and a half across; it had designs cut on it; the sides ere square, not round.
The four heels ere under the frames, and the rods on hich the heels ere fixed ere in the base; the heels ere a cubit and a half high.
The heels ere made like carriage-heels, the rods on hich they ere fixed, the parts forming their edges, their rods and the middle points of them, ere all formed out of liquid metal.
And there ere four angle-plates at the four angles of every base, forming part of the structure of the base.
And at the top of the base there as a round vessel, half a cubit high;
In the spaces of the flat sides and on the frames of them, he made designs of inged ones, lions, and palm-trees, ith ornamented edges all round.
All the ten bases ere made in this ay, after the same design, of the same size and form.
And he made ten brass ashing-vessels, everyone taking forty baths, and measuring four cubits; one vessel as placed on every one of the ten bases.
And he put the bases by the house, five on the right side and five on the left; and he put the great ater-vessel on the right side of the house, to the east, facing south.
And Hiram made the pots and spades and the basins. So Hiram came to the end of all the ork he did for King Solomon in the house of the Lord:
The to pillars and the to cups of the crons hich ere on the tops of the to pillars; and the netork covering the to cups of the crons on the tops of the pillars,
And the four hundred apples for the netork, to lines of apples for every netork, covering the to cups of the crons on the pillars;
And the ten bases, ith the ten ashing-vessels on them;
And the great ater-vessel, ith the telve oxen under it;
And the pots and the spades and the basins; all the vessels hich Hiram made for King Solomon, for the house of the Lord, ere of polished brass.
He made them of liquid metal in the loland of Jordan, at the ay across the river, at Adama, beteen Succoth and Zarethan.
The eight of all these vessels as not measured, because there as such a number of them; it as not possible to get the eight of the brass.
And Solomon had all the vessels made for use in the house of the Lord: the altar of gold and the gold table on hich the holy bread as placed;
And the supports for the lights, five on the right side and five on the left before the inmost room, of clear gold; and the floers and the lights and all the instruments of gold;

And the cups and the scissors and the basins and the spoons and the fire-trays, all of gold; and the pins on hich the doors ere turned, the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and the doors of the Temple, all of gold.

So all the ork King Solomon had done in the house of the Lord as complete. Then Solomon took the holy things hich David his father had given, the silver and the gold and all the vessels, and put them in the store-houses of the house of the Lord.

Then Solomon sent for all the responsible men of Israel, and all the chiefs of the tribes, and the heads of families of the children of Israel, to come to him in Jerusalem to take the ark of the Lord’s agreement up out of the ton of David, hich is Zion.
And all the men of Israel came together to King Solomon at the feast, in the month Ethanim, the seventh month.
And all the responsible men of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.
They took up the ark of the Lord, and the Tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels hich ere in the Tent; all these the priests and the Levites took up.
And King Solomon and all the men of Israel ho had come together there, ere ith him before the ark, making offerings of sheep and oxen more than might be numbered.
And the priests took the ark of the agreement of the Lord and put it in its place in the inner room of the house, in the most holy place, under the ings of the inged ones.
For their ings ere outstretched over the place here the ark as, covering the ark and its rods.
The rods ere so long that their ends ere seen from the holy place, in front of the inmost room; but they ere not seen from outside: and there they are to this day.
There as nothing in the ark but the to flat stones hich Moses put there at Horeb, here the Lord made an agreement ith the children of Israel hen they came out of the land of Egypt.
No hen the priests had come out of the holy place, the house of the Lord as full of the cloud,
So that the priests ere not able to keep their places to do their ork because of the cloud, for the house of the Lord as full of the glory of the Lord.
Then Solomon said, O Lord, to the sun you have given the heaven for a living-place, but your living-place as not seen by men;
So I have made for you a living-place, a house in hich you may be for ever present.
Then, turning his face about, the king gave a blessing to all the men of Israel; and they ere all on their feet together.
And he said, Praise be to the Lord, the God of Israel, ho himself gave his ord to David my father, and ith his strong hand has made his ord come true, saying,

From the day hen I took my people Israel out of Egypt, no ton in all the tribes of Israel has been marked out by me for the building of a house for the resting-place of my name; but I made selection of David to be king over my people Israel.
No it as in the heart of David my father to put up a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
But the Lord said to David my father, You did ell to have in your heart the desire to make a house for my name;
But you yourself ill not be the builder of my house; but your son, the offspring of your body, he it is ho ill put up a house for my name.

And the Lord has made his ord come true; for I have taken my father David’s place on the seat of the kingdom of Israel, as the Lord gave his ord; and I have made a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
In it I have made a place for the ark, in hich is the agreement hich the Lord made ith our fathers, hen he took them out of the land of Egypt.
Then Solomon took his place before the altar of the Lord, all the men of Israel being present, and stretching out his hands to heaven,
Said, O Lord, the God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on the earth; keeping faith and mercy unchanging for your servants, hile they go in your ays ith all their hearts.
And you have kept the ord hich you gave to your servant David, my father; ith your mouth you said it and ith your hand you have made it come true this day.

So no, O Lord, the God of Israel, let your ord to your servant David, my father, come true, hen you said, You ill never be ithout a man to take his place on the seat of the kingdom of Israel before me, if only your children give attention to their ays, alking before me as you have done.
So no, O God of Israel, it is my prayer that you ill make your ord come true hich you said to your servant David, my father.
But is it truly possible that God may be housed on earth? see, heaven and the heaven of heavens are not ide enough to be your resting-place; ho much less this house hich I have made!
Still, let your heart be turned to the prayer of your servant, O Lord God, and to his prayer for grace; give ear to the cry and the prayer hich your servant sends up to you this day;
That your eyes may be open to this house night and day, to this place of hich you have said, My name ill be there; hearing the prayer hich your servant may make, turning to this place.
Give ear to the prayers of your servant, and the prayers of your people Israel, hen they make their prayers, turning to this place; give ear in heaven your living-place, and hearing, have mercy.
If a man does rong to his neighbour, and has to take an oath, and comes before your altar to take his oath in this house:

Then let your ear be open in heaven, and be the judge of your servants, giving your decision against the rongdoer, so that punishment for his sins may come on his head; and, by your decision, keeping from evil him ho has done no rong.
When your people Israel are overcome in ar, because of their sin against you; if they are turned to you again, honouring your name, making prayers to you and requesting your grace in this house:
Then give ear in heaven, and let the sin of your people Israel have forgiveness, and take them back again into the land hich you gave to their fathers.

When heaven is shut up and there is no rain, because of their sin against you; if they make prayers ith their faces turned to this place, honouring your name and turning aay from their sin hen you send trouble on them:

Then give ear in heaven, so that the sin of your servants, and of your people Israel, may have forgiveness, hen you make clear to them the good ay in hich they are to go; and send rain on your land hich you have given to your people for their heritage.

If there is no food in the land, or if there is disease, or if the fruits of the earth are damaged through heat or ater, locust or orm; if their tons are shut in by their attackers; hatever trouble, hatever disease there may be:
Whatever prayer or request for your grace is made by any man, or by all your people Israel, hatever his trouble may be, hose hands are stretched out to this house:

Give ear in heaven your living-place, acting in mercy; and give to every man hose secret heart is open to you, the reard of all his ays; for you, and you only, have knoledge of the hearts of all the children of men:
So that they may give you orship all the days of their life in the land hich you gave to our fathers.
And as for the man from a strange land, ho is not of your people Israel; hen he comes from a far country because of the glory of your name:
( For they ill have nes of your great name and your strong hand and your out-stretched arm;) hen he comes to make his prayer, turning to this house:

Give ear in heaven your living-place, and give him his desire, hatever it may be; so that all the peoples of the earth may have knoledge of your name, orshipping you as do your people Israel, and that they may see that this house hich I have put up is truly named by your name.

If your people go out to ar against their attackers, by hatever ay you may send them, if they make their prayer to the Lord, turning their faces to this ton of yours and to this house hich I have made for your name:
Give ear in heaven to their prayer and their cry for grace, and see right done to them.

If they do rong against you, ( for no man is ithout sin,) and you are angry ith them and give them up into the poer of those ho are fighting against them, so that they take them aay as prisoners into a strange land, far off or near;
And if they take thought, in the land here they are prisoners, and are turned again to you, crying out in prayer to you in that land, and saying, We are sinners, e have done rong, e have done evil;

And ith all their heart and soul are turned again to you, in the land of those ho took them prisoners, and make their prayer to you, turning their eyes to this land hich you gave to their fathers, and to the ton hich you took for yourself, and the house hich I made for your name:
Then give ear to their prayer and to their cry in heaven your living-place, and see right done to them;

Ansering ith forgiveness the people ho have done rong against you, and overlooking the evil hich they have done against you; let those ho made them prisoners be moved ith pity for them, and have pity on them;
For they are your people and your heritage, hich you took out of Egypt, out of the iron fireplace;
Let your eyes be open to your servant’s prayer for grace and to the prayer of your people Israel, hearing them hen their cry comes to you.
For you made them separate from all the peoples of the earth, to be your heritage, as you said by Moses your servant, hen you took our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord God.
Then Solomon, after making all these prayers and requests for grace to the Lord, got up from his knees before the altar of the Lord, here his hands had been stretched out in prayer to heaven;
And, getting on his feet, he gave a blessing to all the men of Israel, saying ith a loud voice,
Praise be to the Lord ho has given rest to his people Israel, as he gave them his ord to do; every ord of all his oath, hich he gave by the hand of Moses his servant, has come true.
No may the Lord our God be ith us as he as ith our fathers; let him never go aay from us or give us up;
Turning our hearts to himself, guiding us to go in all his ays, to keep his orders and his las and his decisions, hich he gave to our fathers.
And may these my ords, the ords of my prayer to the Lord, be before the Lord our God day and night, so that he may see right done to his servant and to his people Israel, day by day as e have need.
So that all the peoples of the earth may see that the Lord is God, and there is no other.
Then let your hearts be ithout sin before the Lord our God, alking in his las and keeping his orders as at this day.
No the king, and all Israel ith him, ere making offerings before the Lord.

And Solomon gave to the Lord for peace-offerings, tenty-to thousand oxen and a hundred and tenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel kept the feast of the opening of the Lord’s house.

The same day the king made holy the middle of the open square in front of the house of the Lord, offering there the burned offering and the meal offering and the fat of the peace-offerings; for there as not room on the brass altar of the Lord for the burned offerings and the meal offerings and the fat of the peace-offerings.

So Solomon and all Israel ith him, a very great meeting, ( for the people had come together from the ay into Hamath to the river of Egypt,) kept the feast at that time before the Lord our God, for to eeks, even fourteen days.

And on the eighth day he sent the people aay, and, blessing the king, they ent to their tents full of joy and glad in their hearts, because of all the good hich the Lord had done to David his servant and to Israel his people.
No hen Solomon came to the end of building the house of the Lord and the king’s house, and all Solomon’s desires, hich he had in mind ere effected;
The Lord came to him again in a vision, as he had done at Gibeon;

And the Lord said to him, Your prayers and your requests for grace have come to my ears: I have made holy this house hich you have made, and I have put my name there for ever; my eyes and my heart ill be there at all times.
As for you, if you ill go on your ay before me, as David your father did, uprightly and ith a true heart, doing hat I have given you orders to do, keeping my las and my decisions;
Then I ill make the seat of your rule over Israel certain for ever, as I gave my ord to David your father, saying, You ill never be ithout a man to be king in Israel.
But if you are turned from my ays, you or your children, and do not keep my orders and my las hich I have put before you, but go and make yourselves servants to other gods and give them orship:

Then I ill have Israel cut off from the land hich I have given them; and this house, hich I have made holy for myself, I ill put aay from before my eyes; and Israel ill be a public example, and a ord of shame among all peoples.

And this house ill become a mass of broken alls, and everyone ho goes by ill be overcome ith onder at it and make histling sounds; and they ill say, Why has the Lord done so to this land and to this house?

And their anser ill be, Because they ere turned aay from the Lord their God, ho took their fathers out of the land of Egypt; they took for themselves other gods and gave them orship and became their servants: that is hy the Lord has sent all this evil on them.
No at the end of tenty years, in hich time Solomon had put up the to houses, the house of the Lord and the king’s house,
( Hiram, king of Tyre, had given Solomon cedar-trees and cypress-trees and gold, as much as he had need of,) King Solomon gave Hiram tenty tons in the land of Galilee.
But hen Hiram came from Tyre to see the tons hich Solomon had given him, he as not pleased ith them.
And he said, What sort of tons are these hich you have given me, my brother? So they ere named the land of Cabul, to this day.
And Hiram sent the king a hundred and tenty talents of gold.
No, this as the ay of Solomon’s system of forced ork for the building of the Lord’s house and of the king’s house, and the Millo and the all of Jerusalem and Megiddo and Gezer. ...
Pharaoh, king of Egypt, came and took Gezer, burning it don and putting to death the Canaanites living in the ton, and he gave it for a bride-offering to his daughter, Solomon’s ife. ...
... and Solomon as the builder of Gezer and Beth-horon the loer,
And Baalath and Tamar in the aste land, in that land;

And all the store-tons and the tons hich Solomon had for his ar-carriages and for his horsemen, and everything hich it as his pleasure to put up in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land under his rule.
As for the rest of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, ho ere not children of Israel;
Their children ho ere still in the land, and hom the children of Israel had not been able to put to complete destruction, them did Solomon put to forced ork, to this day.
But Solomon did not put the children of Israel to forced ork; they ere the men of ar, his servants, his captains, and his chiefs, captains of his ar-carriages and of his horsemen.
These ere the chiefs of the overseers of Solomon’s ork, five hundred and fifty, in authority over the people ho did the ork.
At that time Solomon made Pharaoh’s daughter come up from the ton of David to the house hich he had made for her: then he made the Millo.
Three times in the year it as Solomon’s ay to give burned offerings and peace-offerings on the altar he had made to the Lord, causing his fire-offering to go up on the altar before the Lord.
And King Solomon made a sea-force of ships in Ezion-geber, by Eloth, on the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent his servants, ho ere experienced seamen, in the sea-force ith Solomon’s men.
And they came to Ophir, here they got four hundred and tenty talents of gold, and took it back to King Solomon.
No the queen of Sheba, hearing great things of Solomon, came to put his isdom to the test ith hard questions.
And she came to Jerusalem ith a very great train, ith camels eighted don ith spices, and stores of gold and jeels: and hen she came to Solomon she had talk ith him of everything in her mind.
And Solomon gave her ansers to all her questions; there as no secret hich the king did not make clear to her.
And hen the queen of Sheba had seen all the isdom of Solomon, and the house hich he had made,

And the food at his table, and all his servants seated there, and those ho ere aiting on him in their places, and their robes, and his ine-servants, and the burned offerings hich he made in the house of the Lord, there as no more spirit in her.
And she said to the king, The account hich as given to me in my country of your acts and your isdom as true.
But I had no faith in hat as said about you, till I came and sa for myself; and no I see that it as not half the story; your isdom and your ealth are much greater than they said.
Happy are your ives, happy are these your servants hose place is ever before you, hearing your ords of isdom.

May the Lord your God be praised, hose pleasure it as to put you on the seat of the kingdom of Israel; because the Lord’s love for Israel is eternal, he has made you king, to be their judge in righteousness.
And she gave the king a hundred and tenty talents of gold, and a great store of spices and jeels: never again as such a ealth of spices seen as that hich the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
And the sea-force of Hiram, in addition to gold from Ophir, came back ith much sandal-ood and jeels.
And from the sandal-ood the king made pillars for the house of the Lord, and for the king’s house, and instruments of music for the makers of melody: never has such sandal-ood been seen to this day.

And King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all her desire, hatever she made request for, in addition to hat he gave her freely from the impulse of his heart. So she ent back to her country, she and her servants.
No the eight of gold hich came to Solomon in one year as six hundred and sixty-six talents;
In addition to hat came to him from the business of the traders, and from all the kings of the Arabians, and from the rulers of the country.
And Solomon made to hundred body-covers of hammered gold, every one having six hundred shekels of gold in it.
And he made three hundred smaller body-covers of hammered gold, ith three pounds of gold in every cover: and the king put them in the house of the Woods of Lebanon.
Then the king made a great ivory seat, plated ith the best gold.
There ere six steps going up to it, and the top of it as round at the back, there ere arms on the to sides of the seat, and to lions by the side of the arms;
And telve lions ere placed on the one side and on the other side on the six steps: there as nothing like it in any kingdom.

And all King Solomon’s drinking-vessels ere of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the Woods of Lebanon ere of the best gold; not one as of silver, for no one gave a thought to silver in the days of King Solomon.
For the king had Tarshish-ships at sea ith the ships of Hiram; once every three years the Tarshish-ships came ith gold and silver and ivory and monkeys and peacocks.
And King Solomon as greater than all the kings of the earth in ealth and in isdom.
And from all over the earth they came to see Solomon and to give ear to his isdom, hich God had put in his heart.
And everyone took ith him an offering, vessels of silver and vessels of gold, and robes, and coats of metal, and spices, and horses, and beasts of transport, regularly year by year.
And Solomon got together ar-carriages and horsemen; he had one thousand, four hundred carriages and telve thousand horsemen, hom he kept, some in the carriage-tons and some ith the king at Jerusalem.
And the king made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem and cedars like the sycamore-trees of the lolands in number.
And Solomon’s horses came from Egypt and from Kue; the king’s traders got them at a price from Kue.
A ar-carriage might be got from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty; they got them at the same rate for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
No a number of strange omen ere loved by Solomon, omen of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites:

The nations of hich the Lord had said to the children of Israel, You are not to take ives from them and they are not to take ives from you; or they ill certainly make you go after their gods: to these Solomon as united in love.
He had seven hundred ives, daughters of kings, and three hundred other ives; and through his ives his heart as turned aay.
For it came about that hen Solomon as old, his heart as turned aay to other gods by his ives; and his heart as no longer true to the Lord his God as the heart of his father David had been.
For Solomon ent after Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Zidonians, and Milcom, the disgusting god of the Ammonites.
And Solomon did evil in the eyes of the Lord, not alking in the Lord’s ays ith all his heart as David his father did.
Then Solomon put up a high place for Chemosh, the disgusting god of Moab, in the mountain before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the disgusting god orshipped by the children of Ammon.
And so he did for all his strange ives, ho made offerings ith burning of perfumes to their gods.
And the Lord as angry ith Solomon, because his heart as turned aay from the Lord, the God of Israel, ho had tice come to him in a vision;
And had given him orders about this very thing, that he as not to go after other gods; but he did not keep the orders of the Lord.
So the Lord said to Solomon, Because you have done this, and have not kept my agreement and my las, hich I gave you, I ill take the kingdom aay from you by force and ill give it to your servant.
I ill not do it in your life-time, because of your father David, but I ill take it from your son.
Still I ill not take all the kingdom from him; but I ill give one tribe to your son, because of my servant David, and because of Jerusalem, the ton of my selection.
So the Lord sent Hadad the Edomite to make trouble for Solomon: he as of the king’s seed in Edom.
And hen David had sent destruction on Edom, and Joab, the captain of the army, had gone to put the dead into the earth, and had put to death every male in Edom;
( For Joab and all Israel ere there six months till every male in Edom had been cut off;)
Hadad, being still a young boy, ent in flight to Egypt, ith certain Edomites, servants of his father;
And they ent on from Midian and came to Paran; and, taking men from Paran ith them, they came to Egypt, to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, ho gave him a house and gave orders for his food and gave him land.
No Hadad as very pleasing to Pharaoh, so that he gave him the sister of his ife, Tahpenes the queen, for his ife.
And the sister of Tahpenes had a son by him, Genubath, hom Tahpenes took care of in Pharaoh’s house; and Genubath as living in Pharaoh’s house among Pharaoh’s sons.
No hen Hadad had nes in Egypt that David had been put to rest ith his fathers, and that Joab, the captain of the army, as dead, he said to Pharaoh, Send me back to my country.
But Pharaoh said to him, What have you been short of hile you have been ith me, that you are desiring to go back to your country? And he said, Nothing; but even so, send me back.
And God sent another trouble-maker, Rezon, the son of Eliada, ho had gone in flight from his lord, Hadadezer, king of Zobah:
He got some men together and made himself captain of a band of outlas; and ent to Damascus and became king there.
He as a trouble to Israel all through the days of Solomon. And this is the damage Hadad did: he as cruel to Israel hile he as ruler over Edom.
And there as Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, hose mother as Zeruah, a ido; and his hand as lifted up against the king.
The ay in hich his hand came to be lifted up against the king as this: Solomon as building the Millo and making good the damaged parts of the ton of his father David;
And Jeroboam as an able and responsible man; and Solomon sa that he as a good orker and made him overseer of all the ork given to the sons of Joseph.

No at that time, hen Jeroboam as going out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite came across him on the road; no Ahijah had put on a ne robe; and the to of them ere by themselves in the open country.
And Ahijah took his ne robe in his hands, parting it violently into telve.
And he said to Jeroboam, Take ten of the parts, for this is hat the Lord has said: See, I ill take the kingdom aay from Solomon by force, and ill give ten tribes to you;
( But one tribe ill be his, because of my servant David, and because of Jerusalem, the ton hich, out of all the tribes of Israel, I have made mine,)

Because they are turned aay from me to the orship of Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Zidonians, and Chemosh, the god of Moab, and Milcom, the god of the Ammonites; they have not been alking in my ays or doing hat is right in my eyes or keeping my las and my decisions as his father David did.
But I ill not take the kingdom from him; I ill let him be king all the days of his life, because of David my servant, in hom I took delight because he kept my orders and my las.
But I ill take the kingdom from his son, and give it to you.
And one tribe I ill give to his son, so that David my servant may have a light for ever burning before me in Jerusalem, the ton hich I have made mine to put my name there.
And you I ill take, and you ill be king over Israel, ruling over hatever is the desire of your soul.

And if you give attention to the orders I give you, alking in my ays and doing hat is right in my eyes and keeping my las and my orders as David my servant did; then I ill be ith you, building up for you a safe house, as I did for David, and I ill give Israel to you.
( So that I may send trouble for this on the seed of David, but not for ever.)
And Solomon as looking for a chance to put Jeroboam to death; but he ent in flight to Egypt, to Shishak, king of Egypt, and as in Egypt till the death of Solomon.
No the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all he did, and his isdom, are they not recorded in the book of the acts of Solomon?
And the time Solomon as king in Jerusalem over all Israel as forty years.
And Solomon ent to rest ith his fathers, and as put into the earth in the ton of David his father: and Solomon ent to rest ith his fathers and Rehoboam his son became king in his place.
And Rehoboam ent to Shechem, here all Israel had come together to make him king,
And, hearing of it, Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, ho as still in Egypt, here he had gone in flight from Solomon, and as living there, came back to his ton Zeredah, in the hill-country of Ephraim;
And all the men of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
Your father put a hard yoke on us: if you ill make the conditions under hich your father kept us don less cruel, and the eight of the yoke he put on us less hard, then e ill be your servants.
And he said to them, Go aay for three days and then come back to me again. So the people ent aay.
Then King Rehoboam took the opinion of the old men ho had been ith Solomon his father hen he as living, and said, In your opinion, hat anser am I to give to this people?
And they said to him, If you ill be a servant to this people today, caring for them and giving them a gentle anser, then they ill be your servants for ever.
But he gave no attention to the opinion of the old men, and ent to the young men of his generation ho ere aiting before him:
And said to them, What is your opinion? What anser are e to give to this people ho have said to me, Make less the eight of the yoke hich your father put on us?

And the young men of his generation said to him, This is the anser to give to the people ho came to you saying, Your father put a hard yoke on us; ill you make it less? say to them, My little finger is thicker than my father’s body;
If my father put a hard yoke on you, I ill make it harder: my father gave you punishment ith hips, but I ill give you blos ith snakes.
So all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had given orders, saying, Come back to me the third day.
And the king gave them a rough anser, giving no attention to the suggestion of the old men;
But giving them the anser put forard by the young men, saying, My father made your yoke hard, but I ill make it harder; my father gave you punishment ith hips, but I ill give it ith snakes.
So the king did not give ear to the people; and this came about by the purpose of the Lord, so that hat he had said by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam, son of Nebat, might be effected.

And hen all Israel sa that the king ould give no attention to them, the people in anser said to the king, What part have e in David? hat is our heritage in the son of Jesse? to your tents, O Israel; no see to your people, David. So Israel ent aay to their tents.
( But Rehoboam as still king over those of the children of Israel ho ere living in the tons of Judah.)
Then King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, the overseer of the forced ork; and he as stoned to death by all Israel. And King Rehoboam ent quickly and got into his carriage to go in flight to Jerusalem.
So Israel as turned aay from the family of David to this day.

No hen all Israel had nes that Jeroboam had come back, they sent for him to come before the meeting of the people, and made him king over Israel: not one of them as joined to the family of David but only the tribe of Judah.

When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he got together all the men of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand of his best fighting-men, to make ar against Israel and get the kingdom back for Rehoboam, the son of Solomon.
But the ord of God came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying,
Say to Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the men of Judah and Benjamin and the rest of the people:

The Lord has said, You are not to go to ar against your brothers, the children of Israel; go back, every man to his house, because this thing is my purpose. So they gave ear to the ord of the Lord, and ent back, as the Lord had said.
Then Jeroboam made the ton of Shechem in the hill-country of Ephraim a strong place, and as living there; and from there he ent out and did the same to Penuel.
And Jeroboam said in his heart, No the kingdom ill go back to the family of David:

If the people go up to make offerings in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, their heart ill be turned again to their lord, to Rehoboam, king of Judah; and they ill put me to death and go back to Rehoboam, king of Judah.

So after taking thought the king made to oxen of gold; and he said to the people, You have been going up to Jerusalem long enough; see! these are your gods, O Israel, ho took you out of the land of Egypt.
And he put one in Beth-el and the other in Dan.
And this became a sin in Israel; for the people ent to give orship to the one at Beth-el, and to the other at Dan.
And he made places for orship at the high places, and made priests, ho ere not Levites, from among all the people.

And Jeroboam gave orders for a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast hich is kept in Judah, and he ent up to the altar. And in the same ay, in Beth-el, he gave offerings to the oxen hich he had made, placing in Beth-el the priests of the high places he had made.

He ent up to the altar he had made in Beth-el on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, the month fixed by him at his pleasure; and he gave orders for a feast for the people of Israel, and ent up to the altar, and there he made the smoke of his offerings go up.
Then a man of God came from Judah by the order of the Lord to Beth-el, here Jeroboam as by the altar, burning offerings.

And by the order of the Lord he made an outcry against the altar, saying, O altar, altar, the Lord has said, From the seed of David ill come a child, named Josiah, and on you he ill put to death the priests of the high places, ho are burning offerings on you, and men’s bones ill be burned on you.
The same day he gave them a sign, saying, This is the sign hich the Lord has given: See, the altar ill be broken and the burned aste on it overturned.

Then the king, hearing the man of God crying out against the altar at Beth-el, put out his hand from the altar, saying, Take him prisoner. And his hand, stretched out against him, became dead, and he had no poer of pulling it back.
And the altar as broken and the burned aste on it overturned; this as the sign hich the man of God had given by the ord of the Lord.

Then the king made anser and said to the man of God, Make a prayer no for the grace of the Lord your God, and for me, that my hand may be made ell. And in anser to the prayer of the man of God, the king’s hand as made ell again, as it as before.
And the king said to the man of God, Come ith me to my house for food and rest, and I ill give you a reard.
But the man of God said to the king, Even if you gave me half of all you have, I ould not go in ith you, and I ould not take food or a drink of ater in this place;
For so I as ordered by the ord of the Lord, ho said, You are not to take food or a drink of ater, and you are not to go back the ay you came.
So he ent another ay, and not by the ay he came to Beth-el.

No there as an old prophet living in Beth-el; and one of his sons came and gave him ord of all the man of God had done that day in Beth-el, and they gave their father an account of the ords he had said to the king.
Then their father said to them, Which ay did he go? No his sons had seen hich ay the man of God ho came from Judah had gone.
So the prophet said to his sons, Make ready an ass for me. So they made an ass ready, and he got on it,
And ent after the man of God, and came up ith him hile he as seated under an oak-tree. And he said to him, Are you the man of God ho came from Judah? And he said, I am.
Then he said to him, Come back to the house ith me and have a meal.
But he said, I may not go back ith you or go into your house; and I ill not take food or a drink of ater ith you in this place;
For the Lord said to me, You are not to take food or ater there, or go back again by the ay you came.
Then he said to him, I am a prophet like you; and an angel said to me by the ord of the Lord, Take him back ith you and give him food and ater. But he said false ords to him.
So he ent back ith him, and had a meal in his house and a drink of ater.
But hile they ere seated at the table, the ord of the Lord came to the prophet ho had taken him back;
And crying out to the man of God ho came from Judah, he said, The Lord says, Because you have gone against the voice of the Lord, and have not done as you ere ordered by the Lord,
But have come back, and have taken food and ater in this place here he said you ere to take no food or ater; your dead body ill not be put to rest ith your fathers.
No after the meal he made ready the ass for him, for the prophet hom he had taken back.
And he ent on his ay; but on the road a lion came rushing at him and put him to death; and his dead body as stretched in the road ith the ass by its side, and the lion as there by the body.
And some men, going by, sa the body stretched out in the road ith the lion by its side; and they came and gave nes of it in the ton here the old prophet as living.

Then the prophet ho had made him come back, hearing it, said, It is the man of God, ho ent against the ord of the Lord; that is hy the Lord has given him to the lion to be ounded to death, as the Lord said.
And he said to his sons, Make ready the ass for me. And they did so.
And he ent and sa the dead body stretched out in the road ith the ass and the lion by its side: the lion had not taken the body for its food or done any damage to the ass.
Then the prophet took up the body of the man of God and put it on the ass and took it back; and he came to the ton to put the body to rest ith eeping.
And he put the body in the resting-place made ready for himself, eeping and sorroing over it, saying, O my brother!

And hen he had put it to rest, he said to his sons, When I am dead, then you are to put my body into the earth ith the body of this man of God, and put me by his bones so that my bones may be kept safe ith his bones.
For the outcry he made by the ord of the Lord against the altar in Beth-el and against all the houses of the high places in the tons of Samaria, ill certainly come about.

After this Jeroboam, not turning back from his evil ays, still made priests for his altars from among all the people; he made a priest of anyone desiring it, so that there might be priests of the high places.
And this became a sin in the family of Jeroboam, causing it to be cut off and sent to destruction from the face of the earth.
At that time Abijah, the son of Jeroboam, became ill.

And Jeroboam said to his ife, No come, put on different clothing so that you may not seem to be the ife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh; see, Ahijah is there, the prophet ho said I ould be king over this people.
And take ith you ten cakes of bread and dry cakes and a pot of honey, and go to him: he ill give you ord of hat is to become of the child.
So Jeroboam’s ife did so, and got up and ent to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. No Ahijah as unable to see, because he as very old.
And the Lord had said to Ahijah, The ife of Jeroboam is coming to get nes from you about her son, ho is ill; give her such and such an anser; for she ill make herself seem to be another oman.
Then Ahijah, hearing the sound of her footsteps coming in at the door, said, Come in, O ife of Jeroboam; hy do you make yourself seem like another? for I am sent to you ith bitter nes.
Go, say to Jeroboam, These are the ords of the Lord, the God of Israel: Though I took you from among the people, lifting you up to be a ruler over my people Israel,

And took the kingdom aay by force from the seed of David and gave it to you, you have not been like my servant David, ho kept my orders, and as true to me ith all his heart, doing only hat as right in my eyes.
But you have done evil more than any before you, and have made for yourself other gods, and images of metal, moving me to rath, and turning your back on me.

So I ill send evil on the line of Jeroboam, cutting off from his family every male child, those ho are shut up and those ho go free in Israel; the family of Jeroboam ill be brushed aay like a man brushing aay aste till it is all gone.

Those of the family of Jeroboam ho come to death in the ton, ill become food for the dogs; and those on hom death comes in the open country, ill be food for the birds of the air; for the Lord has said it.
Up, then! go back to your house; and in the hour hen your feet go into the ton, the death of the child ill take place.

And all Israel ill put his body to rest, eeping over him, because he only of the family of Jeroboam ill be put into his resting-place in the earth; for of all the family of Jeroboam, in him only has the Lord, the God of Israel, seen some good.
And the Lord ill put up a king over Israel ho ill send destruction on the family of Jeroboam in that day;

And even no the hand of the Lord has come don on Israel, shaking it like a river-grass in the ater; and, uprooting Israel from this good land, hich he gave to their fathers, he ill send them this ay and that on the other side of the River; because they have made for themselves images, moving the Lord to rath.
And he ill give Israel up because of the sins hich Jeroboam has done and made Israel do.
Then Jeroboam’s ife got up and ent aay and came to Tirzah; and hen she came to the dooray of the house, death came to the child.
And all Israel put his body to rest, eeping over him, as the Lord had said by his servant Ahijah the prophet.
No the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, ho he made ar and ho he became king, are recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Israel.
And Jeroboam as king for tenty-to years, and as put to rest ith his fathers, and Nadab his son became king in his place.

And Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, as king in Judah. Rehoboam as forty-one years old hen he became king, and he as king for seventeen years in Jerusalem, the ton hich the Lord had made his out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there; his mother’s name as Naamah, an Ammonite oman.
And Judah did evil in the eyes of the Lord, and made him more angry than their fathers had done by their sins.
For they made high places and upright stones and ood pillars on every high hill and under every green tree;

And more than this, there ere those in the land ho ere used for sex purposes in the orship of the gods, doing the same disgusting crimes as the nations hich the Lord had sent out before the children of Israel.
No in the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak, king of Egypt, came up against Jerusalem;
And took aay all the stored ealth from the house of the Lord, and from the king’s house, and all the gold body-covers hich Solomon had made.
So in their place King Rehoboam had other body-covers made of brass, and gave them into the care of the captains of the armed men ho ere stationed at the door of the king’s house.
And henever the king ent into the house of the Lord, the armed men ent ith him taking the body-covers, and then took them back to their room.
No the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all he did, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah?
And there as ar beteen Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
And Rehoboam ent to rest ith his fathers, and as put into the earth ith his fathers in the ton of David; his mother’s name as Naamah, an Ammonite oman. And Abijam his son became king in his place.
No in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, Abijam became king over Judah.
For three years he as king in Jerusalem: and his mother’s name as Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.
And he did the same sins hich his father had done before him: his heart as not completely true to the Lord his God, like the heart of David his father.
But because of David, the Lord gave him a light in Jerusalem, making his sons king after him, so that Jerusalem might be safe;
Because David did hat as right in the eyes of the Lord, and never in all his life ent against his orders, but only in the question of Uriah the Hittite.
No the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all he did, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah? And there as ar beteen Abijam and Jeroboam.
Then Abijam ent to rest ith his fathers, and they put him into the earth in the ton of David: and Asa his son became king in his place.
In the tentieth year that Jeroboam as king of Israel, Asa became king over Judah.
And he as king for forty-one years in Jerusalem; his mother’s name as Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.
Asa did hat as right in the eyes of the Lord, as David his father did.
Those used for sex purposes in the orship of the gods he sent out of the country, and he took aay all the images hich his fathers had made.
And he ould not let Maacah his mother be queen, because she had made a disgusting image for Asherah; and Asa had the image cut don and burned by the stream Kidron.
The high places, hoever, ere not taken aay: but still the heart of Asa as true to the Lord all his life.
He took into the house of the Lord all the things hich his father had made holy, and those hich he himself had made holy, silver and gold and vessels.
No there as ar beteen Asa and Baasha, king of Israel, all their days.
And Baasha, king of Israel, ent up against Judah, building Ramah, so that no one as able to go out or in to Asa, king of Judah.

Then Asa took all the silver and gold hich as still stored in the Lord’s house, and in the king’s house, and sent them, in the care of his servants, to Ben-hadad, son of Tabrimmon, son of Rezon, king of Aram, at Damascus, saying,

Let there be an agreement beteen me and you as there as beteen my father and your father: see, I have sent you an offering of silver and gold; go and put an end to your agreement ith Baasha, king of Israel, so that he may give up attacking me.
So Ben-hadad did as King Asa said, and sent the captains of his armies against the tons of Israel, attacking Ijon and Dan and Abel-beth-maacah, and all Chinneroth as far as all the land of Naphtali.
And Baasha, hearing of it, put a stop to the building of Ramah, and as living in Tirzah.

Then King Asa got all Judah together, making every man come; and they took aay the stones and the ood ith hich Baasha as building Ramah, and King Asa made use of them for building Geba in the land of Benjamin, and Mizpah.

No the rest of the acts of Asa, and his poer, and all he did, and the tons of hich he as the builder, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah? But hen he as old he had a disease of the feet.
So Asa ent to rest ith his fathers and as put into the earth in the ton of David his father: and Jehoshaphat his son became king in his place.
Nadab, the son of Jeroboam, became king over Israel in the second year that Asa as king of Judah; and he as king of Israel for to years.
He did evil in the eyes of the Lord, copying the evil ays of his father, and the sin hich he did and made Israel do.

And Baasha, the son of Ahijah, of the family of Issachar, made a secret design against him, attacking him at Gibbethon, a ton of the Philistines; for Nadab and the armies of Israel ere making ar on Gibbethon.
In the third year of the rule of Asa, king of Judah, Baasha put him to death, and became king in his place.

And straight aay hen he became king, he sent destruction on all the offspring of Jeroboam; there as not one living person of all the family of Jeroboam hom he did not put to death, so the ord of the Lord, hich he said by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite, came about;
Because of the sins hich Jeroboam did and made Israel do, moving the Lord, the God of Israel, to rath.
No the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all he did, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Israel?
And there as ar beteen Asa and Baasha, king of Israel, all their days.
In the third year of the rule of Asa, king of Judah, Baasha, the son of Ahijah, became king over all Israel in Tirzah, and as king for tenty-four years.
He did evil in the eyes of the Lord, copying the evil ays of Jeroboam and the sin hich he made Israel do.
And the ord of the Lord came to Jehu, son of Hanani, protesting against Baasha and saying,
Because I took you up out of the dust, and made you ruler over my people Israel; and you have gone in the ays of Jeroboam, and made my people Israel do evil, moving me to rath by their sins;
Truly, I ill see that Baasha and all his family are completely brushed aay; I ill make your family like the family of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat.
Anyone of the family of Baasha ho comes to death in the ton, ill become food for the dogs; and he to hom death comes in the open country, ill be food for the birds of the air.
No the rest of the acts of Baasha, and hat he did, and his poer, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Israel?
And Baasha ent to rest ith his fathers, and as put into the earth at Tirzah; and Elah his son became king in his place.

And the Lord sent his ord against Baasha and his family by the mouth of the prophet Jehu, the son of Hanani, because of all the evil he did in the eyes of the Lord, moving him to rath by the ork of his hands, because he as like the family of Jeroboam, and because he put it to death.
In the tenty-sixth year that Asa as king of Judah, Elah, the son of Baasha, became king of Israel in Tirzah, and he as king for to years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half his ar-carriages, made secret designs against him: no he as in Tirzah, drinking hard in the house of Arza, controller of the king’s house in Tirzah.
And Zimri ent in and made an attack on him and put him to death, in the tenty-seventh year that Asa as king of Judah, and made himself king in his place.
And straight aay hen he became king and took his place on the seat of the kingdom, he put to death all the family of Baasha: not one male child of his relations or his friends kept his life.
So Zimri put to death all the family of Baasha, so that the ord hich the Lord said against him by the mouth of Jehu the prophet came about;
Because of all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, hich they did and made Israel do, moving the Lord, the God of Israel, to rath by their foolish acts.
No the rest of the acts of Elah, and all he did, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Israel?
In the tenty-seventh year of Asa, king of Judah, Zimri as king for seven days in Tirzah. No the people ere attacking Gibbethon in the land of the Philistines.
And nes came to the people in the tents that Zimri had made a secret design and had put the king to death: so all Israel made Omri, the captain of the army, king that day in the tents.
Then Omri ent up from Gibbethon, ith all the army of Israel, and they made an attack on Tirzah, shutting in the ton on every side.
And hen Zimri sa that the ton as taken, he ent into the inner room of the king’s house, and burning the house over his head, came to his end,
Because of his sin in doing evil in the eyes of the Lord, in going in the ay of Jeroboam and in his sin hich he made Israel do.
No the rest of the acts of Zimri, and the secret design he made, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Israel?
Then there as a division among the people of Israel; half the people ere for making Tibni, son of Ginath, king, and half ere supporting Omri.
But the supporters of Omri overcame those ho ere on the side of Tibni, the son of Ginath; and death came to Tibni and to his brother Joram at that time: and Omri became king in the place of Tibni.
In the thirty-first year of Asa, king of Judah, Omri became king over Israel, and he as king for telve years; for six years he as ruling in Tirzah.
He got the hill Samaria from Shemer for the price of to talents of silver, and he made a ton there, building it on the hill and naming it Samaria, after Shemer the oner of the hill.
And Omri did evil in the eyes of the Lord, even orse than all those before him,
Copying all the evil ays of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, and all the sins he did and made Israel do, moving the Lord, the God of Israel, to rath by their foolish ays.
No the rest of the acts hich Omri did, and his great poer, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Israel?
So Omri ent to rest ith his fathers, and as put into the earth in Samaria; and Ahab his son became king in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year that Asa as king of Judah, Ahab, the son of Omri, became king over Israel; and Ahab as king in Samaria for tenty-to years.
And Ahab, the son of Omri, did evil in the eyes of the Lord, even orse than all ho ent before him.
And as if copying the evil ays of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, as a small thing for him, he took as his ife Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, king of Zidon, and became a servant and orshipper of Baal.
And he put up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal hich he had made in Samaria.
And Ahab made an image of Asherah and did more than all the kings of Israel before him to make the Lord, the God of Israel, angry.

In his days Hiel made Jericho; he put its base in position at the price of Abiram, his oldest son, and he put its doors in place at the price of his youngest son Segub; even as the Lord had said by Joshua, the son of Nun.
And Elijah the Tishbite, of Tishbe in Gilead, said to Ahab, By the living Lord, the God of Israel, hose servant I am, there ill be no de or rain in these years, but only at my ord.
Then the ord of the Lord came to him, saying,
Go from here in the direction of the east, and keep yourself in a secret place by the stream Cherith, east of Jordan.
The ater of the stream ill be your drink, and by my orders the ravens ill give you food there.
So he ent and did as the Lord said, living by the stream Cherith, east of Jordan.
And the ravens took him bread in the morning and meat in the evening; and the ater of the stream as his drink.
No after a time the stream became dry, because there as no rain in the land.
Then the ord of the Lord came to him, saying,
Up! go no to Zarephath, in Zidon, and make your living-place there; I have given orders to a ido oman there to see that you have food.

So he got up and ent to Zarephath; and hen he came to the door of the ton, he sa a ido oman getting sticks together; and crying out to her he said, Will you give me a little ater in a vessel for my drink?
And hen she as going to get it, he said to her, And get me ith it a small bit of bread.

Then she said, By the life of the Lord your God, I have nothing but a little meal in my store, and a drop of oil in the bottle; and no I am getting to sticks together so that I may go in and make it ready for me and my son, so that e may have a meal before our death.
And Elijah said to her, Have no fear; go and do as you have said, but first make me a little cake of it and come and give it to me, and then make something for yourself and your son.
For this is the ord of the Lord, the God of Israel: The store of meal ill not come to an end, and the bottle ill never be ithout oil, till the day hen the Lord sends rain on the earth.
So she ent and did as Elijah said; and she and he and her family had food for a long time.
The store of meal did not come to an end, and the bottle as never ithout oil, as the Lord had said by the mouth of Elijah.
No after this, the son of the oman of the house became ill, so ill that there as no breath in him.
And she said to Elijah, What have I to do ith you, O man of God? have you come to put God in mind of my sin, and to put my son to death?
And he said to her, Give your son to me. And lifting him out of her arms, he took him up to his room and put him don on his bed.
And crying to the Lord he said, O Lord my God, have you sent evil even on the ido hose guest I am, by causing her son’s death?
And stretching herself out on the child three times, he made his prayer to the Lord, saying, O Lord my God, be pleased to let this child’s life come back to him again.
And the Lord gave ear to the voice of Elijah, and the child’s spirit came into him again, and he came back to life.
And Elijah took the child don from his room into the house and gave him to his mother and said to her, See, your son is living.
Then the oman said to Elijah, No I am certain that you are a man of God, and that the ord of the Lord in your mouth is true.
No after a long time, the ord of the Lord came to Elijah, in the third year, saying, Go and let Ahab see you, so that I may send rain on the earth.
So Elijah ent to let Ahab see him. No there as no food to be had in Samaria.
And Ahab sent for Obadiah, the controller of the king’s house. ( No Obadiah had the fear of the Lord before him greatly;
For hen Jezebel as cutting off the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah took a hundred of them, and kept them secretly in a hole in the rock, fifty at a time, and gave them bread and ater.)

And Ahab said to Obadiah, Come, let us go through all the country, to all the fountains of ater and all the rivers, and see if there is any grass to be had for the horses and the transport beasts, so that e may be able to keep some of the beasts from destruction.
So they ent through all the country, covering it beteen them; Ahab ent in one direction by himself, and Obadiah ent in another by himself.
And hile Obadiah as on his ay, he came face to face ith Elijah; and seeing ho it as, he ent don on his face and said, Is it you, my lord Elijah?
And Elijah in anser said, It is I; no go and say to your lord, Elijah is here.
And he said, What sin have I done, that you ould give up your servant into the hand of Ahab, and be the cause of my death?
By the life of the Lord your God, there is not a nation or kingdom here my lord has not sent in search of you; and hen they said, He is not here; he made them take an oath that they had not seen you.
And no you say, Go, say to your lord, Elijah is here.

And straight aay, hen I have gone from you, the spirit of the Lord ill take you aay, I have no idea here, so that hen I come and give ord to Ahab, and he sees you not, he ill put me to death: though I, your servant, have been a orshipper of the Lord from my earliest years.
Has my lord not had ord of hat I did hen Jezebel as putting the Lord’s prophets to death? ho I kept a hundred of them in a secret hole in the rock, fifty at a time, and gave them bread and ater?
And no you say, Go and say to your Lord, Elijah is here; and he ill put me to death.
And Elijah said, By the life of the Lord of armies, hose servant I am, I ill certainly let him see me today.
So Obadiah ent to Ahab and gave him the nes; and Ahab ent to see Elijah.
And hen he sa Elijah, Ahab said to him, Is it you, you troubler of Israel?
Then he said in anser, I have not been troubling Israel, but you and your family; because, turning aay from the orders of the Lord, you have gone after the Baals.
No send, and get Israel together before me at Mount Carmel, ith the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal ho get their food at Jezebel’s table.
So Ahab sent for all the children of Israel, and got the prophets together at Mount Carmel.

And Elijah came near to all the people and said, Ho long ill you go on balancing beteen to opinions? if the Lord is God, then give orship to him; but if Baal, give orship to him. And the people said not a ord in anser.
Then Elijah said to the people, I, even I, am the only living prophet of the Lord; but Baal’s prophets are four hundred and fifty men.

No, let them give us to oxen; and let them take one for themselves, and have it cut up, and put it on the ood, but put no fire under it; I ill get the other ox ready, and put it on the ood, and put no fire under it.
And do you make prayers to your god, and I ill make a prayer to the Lord: and it ill be clear that the one ho gives an anser by fire is God. And all the people in anser said, It is ell said.
Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, Take one ox for yourselves and get it ready first, for there are more of you; and make your prayers to your god, but put no fire under.

So they took the ox hich as given them, and made it ready, crying out to Baal from morning till the middle of the day, and saying, O Baal, give ear to us. But there as no voice and no anser. And they ere jumping up and don before the altar they had made.

And in the middle of the day, Elijah made sport of them, saying, Give louder cries, for he is a god; he may be deep in thought, or he may have gone aay for some purpose, or he may be on a journey, or by chance he is sleeping and has to be made aake.
So they gave loud cries, cutting themselves ith knives and sords, as as their ay, till the blood came streaming out all over them.
And from the middle of the day they ent on ith their prayers till the time of the offering; but there as no voice, or any anser, or any ho gave attention to them.
Then Elijah said to all the people, Come near to me; and all the people came near. And he put up again the altar of the Lord hich had been broken don.
And Elijah took telve stones, the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to hom the Lord had said, Israel ill be your name:
And ith the stones he made an altar to the name of the Lord; and he made a deep drain all round the altar, great enough to take to measures of seed.

And he put the ood in order, and, cutting up the ox, put it on the ood. Then he said, Get four vessels full of ater and put it on the burned offering and on the ood. And he said, Do it a second time, and they did it a second time;
And he said, Do it a third time, and they did it a third time.
And the ater ent all round the altar, till the drain as full.

Then at the time of the offering, Elijah the prophet came near and said, O Lord, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, let it be seen this day that you are God in Israel, and that I am your servant, and that I have done all these things by your order.
Give me an anser, O Lord, give me an anser, so that this people may see that you are God, and that you have made their hearts come back again.
Then the fire of the Lord came don, burning up the offering and the ood and the stones and the dust, and drinking up the ater in the drain.
And hen the people sa it, they all ent don on their faces, and said, The Lord, he is God, the Lord, he is God.
And Elijah said to them, Take the prophets of Baal, let not one of them get aay. So they took them, and Elijah made them go don to the stream Kishon, and put them to death there.
Then Elijah said to Ahab, Up! take food and drink, for there is a sound of much rain.
So Ahab ent up to have food and drink, hile Elijah ent up to the top of Carmel; and he ent don on the earth, putting his face beteen his knees.
And he said to his servant, Go no, and take a look in the direction of the sea. And he ent up, and after looking said, There is nothing. And he said, Go again seven times; and he ent seven times.
And the seventh time he said, I see a cloud coming up out of the sea, as small as a man’s hand. Then he said, Go up and say to Ahab, Get your carriage ready and go don or the rain ill keep you back.
And after a very little time, the heaven became black ith clouds and ind, and there as a great rain. And Ahab ent in his carriage to Jezreel.
And the hand of the Lord as on Elijah; and he made himself strong, and ent running before Ahab till they came to Jezreel.
Ahab gave Jezebel nes of all Elijah had done, and ho he had put all the prophets to death ith the sord.
Then Jezebel sent a servant to Elijah, saying, May the gods’ punishment be on me if I do not make your life like the life of one of them by tomorro about this time.
And he got up, fearing for his life, and ent in flight, and came to Beer-sheba in Judah, parting there from his servant;

While he himself ent a day’s journey into the aste land, and took a seat under a broom-plant, desiring for himself only death; for he said, It is enough: no, O Lord, take aay my life, for I am no better than my fathers.
And stretching himself on the earth, he ent to sleep under the broom-plant; but an angel, touching him, said to him, Get up and have some food.
And looking up, he sa by his head a cake cooked on the stones and a bottle of ater. So he took food and drink and ent to sleep again.
And the angel of the Lord came again a second time, and touching him said, Get up and have some food, or the journey ill be overmuch for your strength.
So he got up and took food and drink, and in the strength of that food he ent on for forty days and nights, to Horeb, the mountain of God.
And there he ent into a hole in the rock for the night; then the ord of the Lord came to him, saying, What are you doing here, Elijah?

And he said, I have been burning for the honour of the Lord, the God of armies; for the children of Israel have not kept your agreement; they have made destruction of your altars, and have put your prophets to death ith the sord: till I, even I, am the only one living; and no they are attempting to take aay my life.

Then he said, Go out and take your place on the mountain before the Lord. Then the Lord ent by, and mountains ere parted by the force of a great ind, and rocks ere broken before the Lord; but the Lord as not in the ind. And after the ind there as an earth-shock, but the Lord as not in the earth-shock.
And after the earth-shock a fire, but the Lord as not in the fire. And after the fire, the sound of a soft breath.
And Elijah, hearing it, ent out, covering his face ith his robe, and took his place in the opening of the hole. And there a voice came to him saying, What are you doing here, Elijah?

And he said, I have been burning for the honour of the Lord, the God of armies; for the children of Israel have not kept your agreement; they have had your altars broken don, and have put your prophets to death ith the sord: till I, even I, am the only one living; and no they are attempting to take aay my life.
And the Lord said to him, Go back on your ay through the aste land to Damascus; and hen you come there, put the holy oil on Hazael to make him king over Aram;
And on Jehu, son of Nimshi, making him king over Israel; and on Elisha, the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah, to be prophet in your place.
And it ill come about that the man ho gets aay safe from the sord of Hazael, Jehu ill put to death; and hoever gets aay safe from the sord of Jehu, Elisha ill put to death.

So he ent aay from there and came across Elisha, the son of Shaphat, ploughing ith telve yoke of oxen, he himself alking ith the telfth; and Elijah ent up to him and put his robe on him.

And letting the oxen be here they ere, he came running after Elijah, and said, Only let me give a kiss to my father and mother, and then I ill come after you. But he said to him, Go back again; for hat have I done to you?
And he ent back, and took the oxen and put them to death, and cooking their flesh ith the yokes of the oxen, he gave the people a feast. Then he got up and ent after Elijah and became his servant.
No Ben-hadad, king of Aram, got all his army together, and thirty-to kings ith him, and horses and carriages of ar; he ent up and made ar on Samaria, shutting it in.
And he sent representatives into the ton to Ahab, king of Israel;
And they said to him, Ben-hadad says, Your silver and your gold are mine; and your ives and children are mine.
And the king of Israel sent him an anser saying, As you say, my lord king, I am yours ith all I have.
Then the representatives came back again, and said, These are the ords of Ben-hadad: I sent to you saying, Give up to me your silver and your gold, your ives and your children;

And all the responsible men and the people said to him, Do not give attention to him or do hat he says.
So he said to the representatives of Ben-hadad, Say to my lord the king, All the orders you sent the first time I ill do; but this thing I may not do. And the representatives ent back ith this anser.
Then Ben-hadad sent to him, saying, May the gods’ punishment be on me if there is enough of the dust of Samaria for all the people at my feet to take some in their hands.

And Ahab said, By hom? And he said, The Lord says, By the servants of the chiefs ho are over the divisions of the land. Then he said, By hom is the fighting to be started? And he made anser, By you.
