And get together another army like the one hich came to destruction, horse for horse, and carriage for carriage; and let us make ar on them in the lolands, and certainly e ill be stronger than they. And he gave ear to hat they said, and did so.

Then his servants said to him, It is said that the kings of Israel are full of mercy: let us then put on haircloth, and cords on our heads, and go to the king of Israel; it may be that he ill give you your life.
So they put on haircloth, and cords on their heads, and came to the king of Israel and said, Your servant Ben-hadad says, Let me no keep my life. And he said, Is he still living? he is my brother.

And Ben-hadad said to him, The tons my father took from your father I ill give back; and you may make streets for yourself in Damascus as my father did in Samaria. And as for me, at the price of this agreement you ill let me go. So he made an agreement ith him and let him go.
And a certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his neighbour by the ord of the Lord, Give me a ound. But the man ould not.

Then he said to him, Because you have not given ear to the voice of the Lord, straight aay hen you have gone from me a lion ill put you to death. And hen he had gone, straight aay a lion came rushing at him and put him to death.

And hen the king ent by, crying out to him he said, Your servant ent out into the fight; and a man came out to me ith another man and said, Keep this man: if by any chance he gets aay, your life ill be the price of his life, or you ill have to give a talent of silver in payment.
But hile your servant as turning this ay and that, he as gone. Then the king of Israel said to him, You are responsible; you have given the decision against yourself.
Then he quickly took the head-band from his eyes; and the king of Israel sa that he as one of the prophets.
And he said to him, These are the ords of the Lord: Because you have let go from your hands the man hom I had put to the curse, your life ill be taken for his life, and your people for his people.
Then the king of Israel ent back to his house, bitter and angry, and came to Samaria.
No Naboth the Jezreelite had a vine-garden in Jezreel, near the house of Ahab, king of Samaria.

And Ahab said to Naboth, Give me your vine-garden so that I may have it for a garden of seet plants, for it is near my house; and let me give you a better vine-garden in exchange, or, if it seems good to you, let me give you its value in money.

So Ahab came into his house bitter and angry because Naboth the Jezreelite had said to him, I ill not give you the heritage of my fathers. And stretching himself on the bed ith his face turned aay, he ould take no food.

Then Jezebel, his ife, said, Are you no the ruler of Israel? Get up, take food, and let your heart be glad; I ill give you the vine-garden of Naboth the Jezreelite.
So she sent a letter in Ahab’s name, stamped ith his stamp, to the responsible men and the chiefs ho ere in authority ith Naboth.
And in the letter she said, Let a time of public sorro be fixed, and put Naboth at the head of the people;
And get to good-for-nothing persons to come before him and give itness that he has been cursing God and the king. Then take him out and have him stoned to death.
So the responsible men and the chiefs ho ere in authority in his ton, did as Jezebel had said in the letter she sent them.

And the to good-for-nothing persons came in and took their seats before him and gave itness against Naboth, in front of the people, saying, Naboth has been cursing God and the king. Then they took him outside the ton and had him stoned to death.
And they sent ord to Jezebel, saying, Naboth has been stoned and is dead.

Then Jezebel, hearing that Naboth had been stoned and as dead, said to Ahab, Get up and take as your heritage the vine-garden of Naboth the Jezreelite, hich he ould not give you for money, for Naboth is no longer living but is dead.
So Ahab, hearing that Naboth as dead, ent don to the vine-garden of Naboth the Jezreelite to take it as his heritage.
And the ord of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Go don to Ahab, king of Israel, in Samaria; see, he is in the vine-garden of Naboth the Jezreelite, here he has gone to take it as his heritage.

Say to him, The Lord says, Have you put a man to death and taken his heritage? Then say to him, The Lord says, In the place here dogs have been drinking the blood of Naboth, there ill your blood become the drink of dogs.
And Ahab said to Elijah, Have you come face to face ith me, O my hater? And he said, I have come to you because you have given yourself up to do evil in the eyes of the Lord.
See, I ill send evil on you and put an end to you completely, cutting off from Ahab every male child, him ho is shut up and him ho goes free in Israel;
And I ill make your family like the family of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, and like the family of Baasha, the son of Ahijah, because you have made me angry, and have made Israel do evil.
And of Jezebel the Lord said, Jezebel ill become food for dogs in the heritage of Jezreel.
Any man of the family of Ahab ho comes to his death in the ton ill become food for the dogs; and he ho comes to his death in the open country ill be food for the birds of the air.
( There as no one like Ahab, ho gave himself up to do evil in the eyes of the Lord, moved to it by Jezebel his ife.
He did a very disgusting thing in going after false gods, doing all the things the Amorites did, hom the Lord sent out before the children of Israel.)
Hearing these ords, Ahab, in great grief, put haircloth on his flesh and ent ithout food, sleeping in haircloth, and going about quietly.
Then the ord of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,
Do you see ho Ahab has made himself lo before me? because he has made himself lo before me, I ill not send the evil in his life-time, but in his son’s time I ill send the evil on his family.
No for three years there as no ar beteen Aram and Israel.
And it came about in the third year, that Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, came don to the king of Israel.
And the king of Israel said to his servants, Do you not see that Ramoth-gilead is ours? and e are doing nothing to get it back from the hands of the king of Aram.
And he said to Jehoshaphat, Will you go ith me to Ramoth-gilead to make ar? And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, I am as you are: my people as your people, my horses as your horses.
Then Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, Let us no get directions from the Lord.

So the king of Israel got all the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said to them, Am I to go to Ramoth-gilead to make ar or not? And they said, Go up: for the Lord ill give it into the hands of the king.
But Jehoshaphat said, Is there no other prophet of the Lord here from hom e may get directions?

When he came to the hill, he took them from their hands, and put them aay in the house; and he sent the men aay, and they ent.

And he said to him, Did not my heart go ith you, hen the man got don from his carriage and ent back to you? Is this a time for getting money, and clothing, and olive-gardens and vine-gardens, and sheep and oxen, and men-servants and omen-servants?
Because of hat you have done, the disease of Naaman the leper ill take you in its grip, and your seed after you, for ever. And he ent out from before him a leper as hite as sno.
No the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, There is not room enough for us in the place here e are living under your care;
So let us go to Jordan, and let everyone get to ork cutting boards, and e ill make a living-place for ourselves there. And he said to them, Go, then.
And one of them said, Be pleased to go ith your servants. And he said, I ill go.
So he ent ith them. And hen they came to Jordan, they got to ork cutting don trees.
But one of them, hile cutting a board, let the head of his axe go into the ater; and he gave a cry, and said, This is a bad business, my master, for it is another’s.
And the man of God said, Where did it go in? and hen he sa the place here it had gone into the ater, cutting a stick, he put it into the ater, and the iron came up to the top of the ater.
Then he said, Take it up. So he put out his hand and took it.
At that time the king of Aram as making ar against Israel; and he had a meeting ith the chiefs of his army and said, I ill be aiting in secret in some named place.
And the man of God sent to the king of Israel, saying, Take care to keep aay from that place, for the Aramaeans are aiting there in secret.
So the king of Israel sent to the place here the man of God had said there as danger, and kept clear of it more than once.
And at this, the mind of the king of Aram as greatly troubled, and he sent for his servants and said to them, Will you not make clear to me hich of us is helping the king of Israel?
And one of them said, Not one of us, my lord king; but Elisha, the prophet in Israel, gives the king of Israel nes of the ords you say even in your bedroom.
Then he said, Go and see here he is, so that I may send and get him. And nes came to him that he as in Dothan.
So he sent there horses and carriages and a great army; and they came by night, circling the ton.
No the servant of the man of God, having got up early and gone out, sa an army ith horses and carriages of ar all round the ton. And the servant said to him, O my master, hat are e to do?
And he said in anser, Have no fear; those ho are ith us are more than those ho are ith them.

Then Elisha made a prayer to the Lord, saying, Lord, let his eyes be open so that he may see. And the Lord made the young man’s eyes open; and he sa that all the mountain as full of horses and carriages of fire round Elisha.
No hen the Aramaeans came don to Elisha, he made a prayer to the Lord saying, Lord, make this people blind. And he made them blind at Elisha’s request.
And Elisha said to them, This is not the ay, and this is not the ton: come after me so that I may take you to the man you are searching for. And he took them to Samaria.
And hen they had come into Samaria, Elisha said, Lord, let the eyes of these men be open so that they may see. And the Lord made their eyes open, and they sa that they ere in the middle of Samaria.
And the king of Israel, hen he sa them, said to Elisha, My father, am I to put them to the sord?

But he said in anser, You are not to put them to death; have you any right to put to death those hom you have not taken prisoner ith your sord and your bo? put bread and ater before them, so that they may have food and drink and go to their master.
So he made ready a great feast for them, and hen they had had food and drink, he sent them aay and they ent back to their master. And no more bands of Aramaeans came into the land of Israel.
No after this, Ben-hadad, king of Aram, got together all his army and ent up to make an attack on Samaria, shutting the ton in on all sides ith his forces.
And they became very short of food in Samaria; for they kept it shut in till the price of an ass’s head as eighty shekels of silver, and a small measure of doves’ droppings as five shekels of silver.
And hen the king of Israel as going by on the all, a oman came crying out to him, and said, Help! my lord king.
And he said, If the Lord does not give you help, here am I to get help for you? from the grain-floor or the grape-crusher?
And the king said to her, What is troubling you? And she said in anser, This oman said to me, Give your son to be our food today, and e ill have my son tomorro.
So, boiling my son, e had a meal of him; and on the day after I said to her, No give your son for our food; but she has put her son in a secret place.

Then the king, hearing hat the oman said, took his robes in his hands, violently parting them; and, hile he as alking on the all, the people, looking, sa that under his robe he had haircloth on his flesh.
Then he said, May God’s punishment come on me if Elisha, the son of Shaphat, keeps his head on his body after this day.

But Elisha as in his house, and the responsible men ere seated there ith him; and before the king got there, Elisha said to those ho ere ith him, Do you see ho this cruel and violent man has sent to take aay my life?
While he as still talking to them, the king came don and said, This evil is from the Lord; hy am I to go on aiting any longer for the Lord?

Then Elisha said, Give ear to the ord of the Lord: the Lord says, Tomorro, about this time, a measure of good meal ill be offered for the price of a shekel and to measures of barley for a shekel, in the market-place of Samaria.

Then the captain hose arm as supporting the king said to the man of God, Even if the Lord made indos in heaven, ould such a thing be possible? And he said, Your eyes ill see it, but you ill not have a taste of the food.
No there ere four lepers seated at the dooray into the ton: and they said to one another, Why are e aiting here for death?

If e say, We ill go into the ton, there is no food in the ton, and e ill come to our end there; and if e go on aiting here, death ill come to us. Come then, let us give ourselves up to the army of Aram: if they let us go on living, then life ill be ours; and if they put us to death, then death ill be ours.
So in the half light they got up to go to the tents of Aram; but hen they came to the outer line of tents, there as no one there.

For the Lord had made the sound of carriages and horses, and the noise of a great army, come to the ears of the Aramaeans, so that they said to one another, Truly, the king of Israel has got the kings of the Hittites and of the Egyptians for a price to make an attack on us.
So they got up and ent in flight, in the half light, ithout their tents or their horses or their asses or any of their goods; they ent in flight, fearing for their lives.

And hen those lepers came to the outer line of tents, they ent into one tent, and had food and drink, and took from it silver and gold and clothing, hich they put in a secret place; then they came back and ent into another tent from hich they took more goods, hich they put aay in a secret place.

Then they said to one another, We are not doing right. Today is a day of good nes, and e say nothing: if e go on aiting here till the morning, punishment ill come to us. So let us go and give the nes to those of the king’s house.

So they came in, and, crying out to the door-keepers of the ton, they gave them the nes, saying, We came to the tents of the Aramaeans, and there as no one there and no voice of man, only the horses and the asses in their places, and the tents as they ere.
Then the door-keepers, crying out, gave the nes to those inside the king’s house.

Then the king got up in the night and said to his servants, This is my idea of hat the Aramaeans have done to us. They have knoledge that e are ithout food; and so they have gone out of their tents, and are aiting secretly in the open country, saying, When they come out of the ton, e ill take them living and get into the ton.

And one of his servants said in anser, Send men and let them take five of the horses hich e still have in the ton; if they keep their lives they ill be the same as those of Israel ho are still living here; if they come to their death they ill be the same as all those of Israel ho have gone to destruction: let us send and see.
So they took to horsemen; and the king sent them after the army of the Aramaeans, saying, Go and see.
And they ent after them as far as Jordan; and all the road as covered ith clothing and vessels dropped by the Aramaeans in their flight. So those ho ere sent ent back and gave the nes to the king.

Then the people ent out and took the goods from the tents of the Aramaeans. So a measure of good meal as to be had for the price of a shekel, and to measures of barley for a shekel, as the Lord had said.

And the king gave authority to that captain, on hose arm he as supported, to have control over the dooray into the ton; but he as crushed to death there under the feet of the people, as the man of God had said hen the king ent don to him.

So the ords of the man of God came true, hich he said to the king: To measures of barley ill be offered for the price of a shekel and a measure of good meal for a shekel, tomorro about this time in the market-place of Samaria.
And that captain said to the man of God, Even if the Lord made indos in heaven, ould such a thing be possible? And he said to him, Your eyes ill see it, but you ill not have a taste of the food.
And such as his fate; for he as crushed to death under the feet of the people, in the dooray into the ton.

No Elisha had said to the oman hose son he had given back to life, Go no, ith all the people of your house, and get a living-place for yourselves herever you are able; for by the ord of the Lord, there ill be great need of food in the land; and this ill go on for seven years.
So the oman got up and did as the man of God said; and she and the people of her house ere living in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
And hen the seven years ere ended, the oman came back from the land of the Philistines and ent to the king ith a request for her house and her land.
No the king as talking ith Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying, No, give me an account of all the great things Elisha has done.

And hile he as giving the king the story of ho Elisha had given life to the dead, the oman hose son had come back to life came to the king ith a request for her house and her land. And Gehazi said, My lord king, this is the oman and this is her son, hose life Elisha gave back to him.

And in anser to the king’s questions, the oman gave him all the story. So the king gave orders to one of his unsexed servants, saying, Give her back all her property, and all the produce of her fields from the day hen she ent aay from the land up till no.
And Elisha came to Damascus; and Ben-hadad, king of Aram, as ill; and they said to him, The man of God has come.
Then the king said to Hazael, Take an offering ith you, and go to see the man of God and get directions from the Lord by him, saying, Am I going to get better from my disease?

So Hazael ent to see him, taking ith him forty camels ith offerings on their backs of every sort of good thing from Damascus; and hen he came before him, he said, Your son Ben-hadad, king of Aram, has sent me to you, saying, Will I get better from this disease?
And Elisha said to him, Go, say to him, You ill certainly get better; but the Lord has made it clear to me that only death is before him.
And he kept his eyes fixed on him till he as shamed, and the man of God as overcome ith eeping.

And Hazael said, Why is my lord eeping? Then he said in anser, Because I see the evil hich you ill do to the children of Israel: burning don their strong tons, putting their young men to death ith the sord, smashing their little ones against the stones, and cutting open the omen ho are ith child.
And Hazael said, Ho is it possible that your servant, ho is only a dog, ill do this great thing? And Elisha said, The Lord has made it clear to me that you ill be king over Aram.
Then he ent aay from Elisha and came in to his master, ho said to him, What did Elisha say to you? And his anser as, He said that you ould certainly get ell.
No on the day after, Hazael took the bed-cover, and making it et ith ater, put it over Ben-hadad’s face, causing his death: and Hazael became king in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram, the son of Ahab, king of Israel, Jehoram, the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, became king.
He as thirty-to years old hen he became king; and he as ruling in Jerusalem for eight years.
He ent in the ays of the kings of Israel, as the family of Ahab did: for the daughter of Ahab as his ife; and he did evil in the eyes of the Lord.
But it as not the Lord’s purpose to send destruction on Judah, because of David his servant, to hom he had given his ord that he ould have a light for ever.
In his time, Edom made themselves free from the rule of Judah, and took a king for themselves.

Then Joram ent over to Zair, ith all his ar-carriages; ... made an attack by night on the Edomites, hose forces ere all round him, ... the captains of the ar-carriages; and the people ent in flight to their tents.
So Edom made themselves free from the rule of Judah to this day. And at the same time, Libnah made itself free.
No the rest of the acts of Joram, and all he did, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah?
And Joram ent to rest ith his fathers and as put into the earth ith his fathers in the ton of David: and Ahaziah his son became king in his place.
In the telfth year that Joram, the son of Ahab, as king of Israel, Ahaziah, the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, became king;
Ahaziah as tenty-to years old hen he became king, and he as ruling in Jerusalem for one year. His mother’s name as Athaliah, the daughter of Omri, king of Israel.
He ent in the ays of the family of Ahab, and did evil in the eyes of the Lord as the family of Ahab did, for he as a son-in-la of the family of Ahab.
He ent ith Joram, the son of Ahab, to make ar on Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramoth-gilead: and Joram as ounded by the Aramaeans.

So King Joram ent back to Jezreel to get ell from the ounds hich the bomen had given him at Ramah, hen he as fighting against Hazael, king of Aram. And Ahaziah, the son of Jehoram, king of Judah, ent don to see Joram, the son of Ahab, in Jezreel, because he as ill.
And Elisha the prophet sent for one of the sons of the prophets, and said to him, Make yourself ready for a journey, and take this bottle of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
And hen you get there, go in search of Jehu, the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi; and go in and make him get up from among his brothers, and take him to an inner room.
Then take the bottle and put the oil on his head, and say, The Lord says, I have put the holy oil on you to make you king over Israel. Then, opening the door, go in flight, ithout aiting.
So the young prophet ent to Ramoth-gilead.
And hen he came, he sa the captains of the army seated together; and he said, I have something to say to you, O captain. And Jehu said, To hich of us? And he said, To you, O captain.
And he got up and ent into the house; then he put the holy oil on his head and said to him, The Lord, the God of Israel, says, I have made you king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.
You are to see that the family of Ahab your master is cut off, so that I may take from Jezebel payment for the blood of my servants the prophets, and for the blood of all the servants of the Lord.
For the family of Ahab ill come to an end; every male of Ahab’s family ill be cut off, he ho is shut up and he ho goes free in Israel.
I ill make the family of Ahab like that of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, and Baasha, the son of Ahijah.
And Jezebel ill become food for the dogs in the heritage of Jezreel, and there ill be no one to put her body into the earth. Then, opening the door, he ent in flight.

Then Jehu came out again to the servants of his lord, and one said to him, Is all ell? hy did this man, ho is off his head, come to you? And he said to them, You have knoledge of the man and of his talk.
And they said, That is not true; no give us his story. Then he said, This is hat he said to me: The Lord says, I have made you king over Israel.
Then straight aay everyone took his robe and put it under him on the top of the steps, and, sounding the horn, they said, Jehu is king.
So Jehu, the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi, made designs against Joram. ( No Joram and all the army of Israel ere keeping atch on Ramoth-gilead because of Hazael, king of Aram:

But King Joram had gone back to Jezreel to get ell from the ounds hich the Aramaeans had given him hen he as fighting against Hazael, king of Aram.) And Jehu said, If this is your purpose, then let no one get aay and go out of the ton to give nes of it in Jezreel.
So Jehu got into his carriage and ent to Jezreel, for Joram as ill in bed there; and Ahaziah, king of Judah, had come don to see Joram.
And the atchman on the toer in Jezreel sa Jehu and his band coming, and said, I see a band of people. And Joram said, Send out a horseman to them, and let him say, Is it peace?

So a horseman ent out to them and said, The king says, Is it peace? And Jehu said, What have you to do ith peace? come after me. And the atchman gave them ord, saying, The horseman ent up to them, but has not come back.
Then he sent out a second horseman, ho came up to them and said, The king says, Is it peace? And Jehu said in anser, What have you to do ith peace? come after me.
And the atchman gave them ord, saying, He ent up to them and has not come back again; and the driving is like the driving of Jehu, son of Nimshi, for he is driving violently.

Then Joram said, Make ready. So they made his carriage ready; and Joram, king of Israel, ith Ahaziah, king of Judah, ent out in their carriages for the purpose of meeting Jehu; and they came face to face ith him at the field of Naboth the Jezreelite.
No hen Joram sa Jehu he said, Is it peace, Jehu? And he said in anser, What peace is possible hile all the land is full of the disgusting sins of your mother Jezebel, and her secret arts?
Then Joram, turning his horses in flight, said to Ahaziah, Broken faith, O Ahaziah!
Then Jehu took his bo in his hand, and ith all his strength sent an arro, ounding Joram beteen the arms; and the arro came out at his heart, and he ent don on his face in his carriage.

Then Jehu said to Bidkar, his captain, Take him up, and put him in the field of Naboth the Jezreelite: for is not that day in your memory hen you and I together on our horses ere going after Ahab, his father, and the Lord put this fate on him, saying:
I sa the blood of Naboth and of his sons yesterday; and I ill give you full payment in this field, says the Lord? So no, take him and put him in this field, as the Lord said.

No hen Ahaziah, king of Judah, sa this, he ent in flight by the ay of the garden house. And Jehu came after him and said, Put him to death in the same ay; and they gave him a death-ound in his carriage, on the slope up to Gur, by Ibleam; and he ent in flight to Megiddo, here death came to him.
And his servants took him in a carriage to Jerusalem, and put him into the earth ith his fathers in the ton of David.
( In the eleventh year of the rule of Joram, the son of Ahab, Ahaziah became king over Judah.)
And hen Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel had nes of it; and, painting her eyes and dressing her hair ith ornaments, she put her head out of the indo.
And hen Jehu as coming into the ton, she said, Is all ell, O Zimri, taker of your master’s life?
Then, looking up to the indo, he said, Who is on my side, ho? and to or three unsexed servants put out their heads.
And he said, Take her and put her out of the indo. So they sent her don ith force, and her blood ent in a shoer on the all and on the horses; and she as crushed under their feet.
And he came in, and took food and drink; then he said, No see to this cursed oman, and put her body into the earth, for she is a king’s daughter.
And they ent out to put her body into the earth, but nothing of her as to be seen, only the bones of her head, and her feet, and parts of her hands.
So they came back and gave him ord of it. And he said, This is hat the Lord said by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, In the heritage of Jezreel the flesh of Jezebel ill become food for dogs;
And the dead body of Jezebel ill be like aste dropped on the face of the earth in the heritage of Jezreel; so that they ill not be able to say, This is Jezebel.
No there ere in Samaria seventy of Ahab’s sons. And Jehu sent letters to Samaria, to the rulers of the ton, and to the responsible men, and to those ho had the care of the sons of Ahab, saying,
Straight aay, hen you get this letter, seeing that your master’s sons are ith you, and that you have carriages and horses and a alled ton and arms;
Take the best and most upright of your master’s sons, and make him king in his father’s place, and put up a fight for your master’s family.
But they ere full of fear, and said, The to kings have gone don before him: ho may e keep our place?

So the controller of the king’s house, ith the ruler of the ton, and the responsible men, and those ho had the care of Ahab’s sons, sent to Jehu, saying, We are your servants and ill do all your orders; e ill not make any man king; do hatever seems best to you.

Then he sent them a second letter, saying, If you are on my side, and if you ill do my orders, come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorro, ith the heads of your master’s sons. No the king’s seventy sons ere ith the great men of the ton, ho had the care of them.
And hen the letter came to them, they took the king’s sons and put them to death, all the seventy, and put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
And a man came and said to him, They have come ith the heads of the king’s sons. And he said, Put them don in to masses at the dooray of the ton till the morning.

And in the morning he ent out and, stopping, said to all the people there, You are upright men: it is true that I made designs against my master, and put him to death; but ho is responsible for the death of all these?
You may be certain that nothing hich the Lord has said about the family of Ahab ill be ithout effect; for the Lord has done hat he said by his servant Elijah.
So Jehu put to death all the rest of the seed of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his relations and his near friends and his priests, till there ere no more of them.
Then he got up and came to Samaria. And he as at the meeting-place of the keepers of sheep, by the ay,

When he came across the brothers of Ahaziah, king of Judah, and said, Who are you? And they said, We are the brothers of Ahaziah, king of Judah; e are going don to see the children of the king and of the queen.
And he said, Take them living. So they took them living, and put them to death in the ater-hole of Beth-eked; of the forty-to men he put every one to death;

And hen he had gone aay from there, he came across Jehonadab, the son of Rechab: and he said good-day to him, and said to him, Is your heart true to mine, as mine is to yours? And Jehonadab in anser said, It is; and Jehu said, If it is, give me your hand. And he gave him his hand, and he made him come up into his carriage.
And he said, Come ith me and see ho I am on fire for the Lord’s cause. So he made him go ith him in his carriage.
And hen he came to Samaria, he put to death all those of Ahab’s family ho ere still in Samaria, till there ere no more of them, as the Lord had said to Elijah.
Then Jehu got all the people together and said to them, Ahab as Baal’s servant in a small ay, but Jehu ill be his servant on a great scale.

No send for all the prophets of Baal and all his servants and all his priests, to come to me; let no one keep aay: for I have a great offering to make to Baal; anyone ho is not present, ill be put to death. This Jehu did ith deceit, his purpose being the destruction of the servants of Baal.
And Jehu said, Let there be a special holy meeting for the orship of Baal. So a public statement as made.
And Jehu sent out through all Israel; and all the servants of Baal came, not one kept aay. And they came into the house of Baal, so that it as full from end to end.
And Jehu said to him ho kept the robes, Get out robes for all the servants of Baal. So he got out robes for them.

And Jehu, ith Jehonadab, the son of Rechab, ent into the house of Baal; and he said to the servants of Baal, Make a search ith care, to see that no servant of the Lord is ith you, but only servants of Baal.

Then they ent in to make offerings and burned offerings. No Jehu had put eighty men outside, and said to them, If any man hom I give into your hands gets aay, the life of him ho lets him go ill be the price of his life.

Then hen the burned offering as ended, straight aay Jehu said to the armed men and the captains, Go in and put them to death; let not one come out. So they put them to the sord; and, pulling the images to the earth, they ent into the holy place of the house of Baal.
And they took out the image of Asherah from the house of Baal, and had it burned.
The altar of Baal as pulled don and the house of Baal as broken up and made an unclean place, as it is to this day.
So Jehu put an end to the orship of Baal in Israel.
But Jehu did not keep himself from all the sins of Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, and the evil he made Israel do; the gold oxen ere still in Beth-el and in Dan.
And the Lord said to Jehu, Because you have done ell in doing hat is right in my eyes and effecting all my purpose for the family of Ahab, your sons ill be kings of Israel to the fourth generation.
But Jehu did not take care to keep the la of the Lord ith all his heart: he did not keep himself from the sin hich Jeroboam did and made Israel do.
In those days the Lord as angry first ith Israel; and Hazael made attacks on all the land of Israel,
East of Jordan, in all the land of Gilead, the Gadites and the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer by the valley of the Arnon, all Gilead and Bashan.
No the rest of the acts of Jehu, and all he did, and his great poer, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Israel?
And Jehu ent to rest ith his fathers, and as put into the earth in Samaria. And Jehoahaz his son became king in his place.
And the time of Jehu’s rule over Israel in Samaria as tenty-eight years.
No hen Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, sa that her son as dead, she had all the rest of the seed of the kingdom put to death.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, secretly took Joash, the son of Ahaziah, ith the oman ho took care of him, aay from among the king’s sons ho ere put to death, and put him in the bedroom; and they kept him safe from Athaliah, so that he as not put to death.
And for six years she kept him safe in the house of the Lord, hile Athaliah as ruling over the land.

Then in the seventh year, Jehoiada sent for the captains of hundreds of the Carians, and the armed men, and taking them into the house of the Lord, made an agreement ith them, and made them take an oath in the house of the Lord, and let them see the king’s son.
And he gave them orders, saying, This is hat you are to do: the third part of you, ho come in on the Sabbath and keep the atch of the king’s house,
And the to divisions of you, ho go out on the Sabbath and keep the atch of the house of the Lord,
Will make a circle round the king, every man being armed; and hoever comes inside your lines is to be put to death; keep ith the king, hen he goes out and hen he comes in.

And the captains of hundreds did as Jehoiada the priest gave them orders; every one took ith him his men, those ho came in and those ho ent out on the Sabbath, and they came in to Jehoiada the priest.
And the priest gave to the captains of hundreds the spears and body-covers hich had been King David’s, and hich ere kept in the house of the Lord.
Then the armed men took up their positions, every man ith his instruments of ar in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left, round about the altar and the house.

No in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, hich as the seventh year of Hoshea, son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, came up against Samaria, shutting it in ith his armies.
And at the end of three years they took it; in the sixth year of Hezekiah’s rule, hich as the ninth year of Hoshea, king of Israel, Samaria as taken.
And the king of Assyria took Israel aay as prisoners into Assyria, placing them in Halah and in Habor on the river Gozan, and in the tons of the Medes;

Because they did not give ear to the voice of the Lord their God, but ent against his agreement, even against everything ordered by Moses, the servant of the Lord, and they did not give ear to it or do it.
No in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, came up against all the alled tons of Judah and took them.

And Hezekiah, king of Judah, sent to Lachish, to the king of Assyria, saying, I have done rong; give up attacking me, and hatever you put on me I ill undergo. And the payment he as to make as fixed by the king of Assyria at three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
So Hezekiah gave him all the silver in the house of the Lord, and in the king’s store-house.
And at that time Hezekiah had the gold from the doors of the Lord’s house, and from the door-pillars plated by him, cut off and gave it to the king of Assyria.

Then the king of Assyria sent the Tartan and the Rab-saris and the Rab-shakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, ith a strong force. And they ent up and came to Jerusalem, and took up their position by the stream of the higher pool, by the highay of the asherman’s field.
And they sent for the king, and Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, ho as over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, came out to them.
And the Rab-shakeh said to them, Say no to Hezekiah, These are the ords of the great king, the king of Assyria: In hat are you placing your hope?
You say you have a design, and strength for ar, but these are only ords. No to hom are you looking for support, that you have gone against my authority?

See, no, you are basing your hope on that broken rod of Egypt, hich ill go through a man’s hand if he makes use of it for a support; for so is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all ho put their faith in him.

And if you say to me, Our hope is in the Lord our God: is it not he, hose high places and altars Hezekiah has taken aay, saying to Judah and Jerusalem that orship may only be given before this altar in Jerusalem?
And no, take a chance ith my master, the king of Assyria, and I ill give you to thousand horses, if you are able to put horsemen on them.
Ho then may you put to shame the least of my master’s servants? and you have put your hope in Egypt for ar-carriages and horsemen:
And have I no come up to send destruction on this place ithout the Lord’s authority? It as the Lord himself ho said to me, Go up against this land and make it aste.

Then Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, and Shebna and Joah said to the Rab-shakeh, Will you kindly make use of the Aramaean language in talking to your servants, for e are used to it, and do not make use of the Jes’ language in the hearing of the people on the all.

But the Rab-shakeh said to them, Is it to your master or to you that my master has sent me to say these ords? has he not sent me to the men seated on the all? for they are the people ho ill be short of food ith you hen the ton is shut in.
Then the Rab-shakeh got up and said ith a loud voice in the Jes’ language, Give ear to the ords of the great king, the king of Assyria;
This is hat the king says: Do not be tricked by Hezekiah, for there is no salvation for you in him.
And do not let Hezekiah make you put your faith in the Lord, saying, The Lord ill certainly keep us safe, and this ton ill not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.

Do not give ear to Hezekiah, for this is hat the king of Assyria says: Make peace ith me and come out to me; and everyone ill be free to take the fruit of his vine and of his fig-tree, and the ater of his spring;

Till I come and take you aay to a land like yours, a land of grain and ine, a land of bread and vine-gardens, a land of oil-giving olives and of honey, so that life and not death may be your fate. Give no attention to Hezekiah hen he says to you, The Lord ill keep us safe.
Has any one of the gods of the nations kept his land from falling into the hands of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and of Arpad? here are the gods of Sepharvaim, of Hena and Ivvah? have they kept Samaria out of my hands?
Who among all the gods of these countries have kept their country from falling into my hands, to give cause for the thought that the Lord ill keep Jerusalem from falling into my hands?
But the people kept quiet and gave him no anser: for the king’s order as, Give him no anser.

Then Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, ho as over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah, ith their clothing parted as a sign of grief, and gave him an account of hat the Rab-shakeh had said.
And on hearing it, King Hezekiah took off his robe, and put on haircloth, and ent into the house of the Lord.
And he sent Eliakim, ho as over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the chief priests, dressed in haircloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
And they said to him, Hezekiah says, This day is a day of trouble and punishment and shame; for the children are ready to come to birth, but there is no strength to give birth to them.

It may be that the Lord your God ill give ear to the ords of the Rab-shakeh, hom the king of Assyria, his master, sent to say evil things against the living God, and ill make his ords come to nothing: so then make your prayer for the rest of the people.
So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
And Isaiah said to them, This is hat you are to say to your master: The Lord says, Be not troubled by the ords hich the servants of the king of Assyria have said against me in your hearing.
See, I ill put a spirit into him, and bad nes ill come to his ears, and he ill go back to his land; and there I ill have him put to death by the sord.
So the Rab-shakeh ent back, and hen he got there the king of Assyria as making ar against Libnah, for it had come to his ears that he had gone aay from Lachish.
And hen nes came to him that Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, had made an attack on him, he sent representatives to Hezekiah again, saying,
This is hat you are to say to Hezekiah, king of Judah: Let not your God, in hom is your faith, give you a false hope, saying, Jerusalem ill not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.
No doubt the story has come to your ears of hat the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, putting them to the curse; and ill you be kept safe?
Did the gods of the nations keep safe those on hom my fathers sent destruction, Gozan and Haran and Rezeph and the children of Eden ho ere in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the ton of Sepharvaim, of Hena and of Ivvah?
And Hezekiah took the letter from the hands of those ho had come ith it; and after reading it, Hezekiah ent up to the house of the Lord, opening the letter there before the Lord.
And Hezekiah made his prayer to the Lord, saying, O Lord, the God of Israel, seated beteen the inged ones, you only are the God of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth.
Let your ear be turned to us, O Lord, and let your eyes be open, O Lord, and see; take note of all the ords of Sennacherib ho has sent men to say evil against the living God.
Truly, O Lord, the kings of Assyria have made aste the nations and their lands,
And have given their gods to the fire; for they ere no gods, but ood and stone, the ork of men’s hands; so they have given them to destruction.
But no, O Lord our God, give us salvation from his hands, so that it may be clear to all the kingdoms of the earth that you and only you, O Lord, are God.
Then Isaiah, the son of Amoz, sent to Hezekiah, saying, The Lord, the God of Israel, says, The prayer hich you have made to me against Sennacherib, king of Assyria, has come to my ears.
This is the ord hich the Lord has said about him: In the eyes of the virgin daughter of Zion you are shamed and laughed at; the daughter of Jerusalem has made sport of you.
Against hom have you said evil and bitter things? against hom has your voice been loud and your eyes lifted up? even against the Holy One of Israel.

You have sent your servants ith evil ords against the Lord, and have said, With all my ar-carriages I have come up to the top of the mountains, to the inmost parts of Lebanon; its tall cedars ill be cut don, and the best trees of its oods; I ill come up into his highest places, into his thick oods.
I have made ater-holes and taken their aters, and ith my foot I have made all the rivers of Egypt dry.
Has it not come to your ears ho I did it long before, purposing it in times long past? No I have given effect to my design, so that by you strong tons might be turned into masses of broken alls.
This is hy their tonsmen had no poer, they ere broken and put to shame; they ere like the grass of the field and the green plant, like grass on the house-tops.
But I have knoledge of your getting up and your resting, of your going out and your coming in.
Because your rath against me and your ords of pride have come up to my ears, I ill put my hook in your nose and my cord in your lips, and I ill make you go back by the ay you came.

And this ill be the sign to you: you ill get your food this year from hat comes up of itself; and in the second year from the produce of the same; and in the third year you ill put in your seed and get in the grain and make vine-gardens and take of their fruit.
And those of Judah ho are still living ill again take root in the earth and give fruit.
For from Jerusalem those ho have been kept safe ill go out, and those ho are still living ill go out of Mount Zion: by the fixed purpose of the Lord of armies this ill be done.
For this cause the Lord says about the king of Assyria, He ill not come into this ton, or send an arro against it; he ill not come before it ith arms, or put up an earthork against it;
By the ay he came he ill go back, and he ill not get into this ton, says the Lord.
For I ill keep this ton safe, for my honour, and for the honour of my servant David.

And that night the angel of the Lord ent out and put to death in the army of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand men; and hen the people got up early in the morning, there as nothing to be seen but dead bodies.
So Sennacherib, king of Assyria, ent back to his place at Nineveh.

And it came about, hen he as orshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to death ith the sord; and they ent in flight into the land of Ararat. And Esar-haddon his son became king in his place.
In those days Hezekiah as ill and near death. And Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, The Lord says, Put your house in order, for your death is near.
Then, turning his face to the all, he made his prayer to the Lord, saying,
O Lord, keep in mind ho I have been true to you ith all my heart, and have done hat is good in your eyes. And Hezekiah gave ay to bitter eeping.
No before Isaiah had gone out of the middle of the ton, the ord of the Lord came to him, saying,

Go back and say to Hezekiah, the ruler of my people, The Lord, the God of David your father, says, Your prayer has come to my ears, and I have seen your eeping; see, I ill make you ell: on the third day you ill go up to the house of the Lord.
I ill give you fifteen more years of life; and I ill keep you and this ton safe from the hands of the king of Assyria; I ill keep this ton safe, for my honour, and for the honour of my servant David.
Then Isaiah said, Take a cake of figs. So they took it and put it on his ound, and he got better.
And Hezekiah said to Isaiah, What is to be the sign that the Lord ill make me ell, and that I ill go up to the house of the Lord on the third day?
And Isaiah said, This is the sign the Lord ill give you, that he ill do hat he has said; ill the shade go forard ten degrees or back?
And Hezekiah said in anser, It is a simple thing for the shade to go forard; but let it go back ten degrees.
Then Isaiah the prophet made prayer to the Lord, and he made the shade go back ten degrees from its position on the steps of Ahaz.
At that time, Merodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters ith an offering to Hezekiah, because he had nes that Hezekiah had been ill.

And Hezekiah as glad at their coming and let them see all his store of ealth, the silver and the gold and the spices and the oil of great price, and the house of his arms, and everything there as in his stores; there as nothing in all his house or his kingdom hich Hezekiah did not let them see.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, What did these men say and here did they come from? And Hezekiah said, They came from a far country, even from Babylon.
And he said, What have they seen in your house? And Hezekiah said in anser, They sa everything in my house: there is nothing among my stores hich I did not let them see.
And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, Give ear to the ord of the Lord.
Truly, days are coming hen everything in your house, and hatever your fathers have put in store till this day, ill be taken aay to Babylon: all ill be gone, says the Lord.
And your sons, the offspring of your body, they ill take aay to be unsexed servants in the house of the king of Babylon.
Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, Good is the ord of the Lord hich you have said. Then he said, ... if in my time there is peace and righteousness?
No the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his poer, and ho he made the pool and the stream, to take ater into the ton, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah?
And Hezekiah ent to rest ith his fathers; and Manasseh his son became king in his place.
Manasseh as telve years old hen he became king; for fifty-five years he as ruling in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name as Hephzi-bah.
He did evil in the eyes of the Lord, copying the disgusting ays of those nations hom the Lord had sent out before the children of Israel.

He put up again the high places hich had been pulled don by Hezekiah his father; he made altars for Baal, and an Asherah, as Ahab, king of Israel, had done; he as a orshipper and servant of all the stars of heaven.
And he put up altars in the house of the Lord, of hich the Lord had said, In Jerusalem ill I put my name.
And he put up altars for all the stars of heaven in the to outer squares of the house of the Lord.

And he made his son go through the fire, and made use of secret arts and signs for reading the future; he gave positions to those ho had control of spirits and to onder-orkers; he did much evil in the eyes of the Lord, moving him to rath.

He put the image of Asherah hich he had made in the house of hich the Lord had said to David and to Solomon his son, In this house, and in Jerusalem, the ton hich I have made mine out of all the tribes of Israel, I ill put my name for ever.
And never again ill I send the feet of Israel andering from the land hich I gave to their fathers; if only they ill take care to do all my orders, and keep all the la hich my servant Moses gave them.
But they did not give ear; and Manasseh made them do more evil than those nations did, hom the Lord gave up to destruction before the children of Israel.
And the Lord said, by his servants the prophets,
Because Manasseh, king of Judah, has done these disgusting things, doing more evil than all the Amorites before him, and making Judah do evil ith his false gods,
For this cause, says the Lord, the God of Israel, I ill send such evil on Jerusalem and Judah that the ears of all to hom the nes comes ill be burning.
And over Jerusalem ill be stretched the line of Samaria and the eight of Ahab; Jerusalem ill be ashed clean as a plate is ashed, and turned over on its face.
And I ill put aay from me the rest of my heritage, and give them up into the hands of their haters, ho ill take their property and their goods for themselves;
Because they have done evil in my eyes, moving me to rath, from the day hen their fathers came out of Egypt till this day.
More than this, Manasseh took the lives of upright men, till Jerusalem from one end to the other as full of blood; in addition to his sin in making Judah do evil in the eyes of the Lord.
No the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and all he did, and his sins, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah?
So Manasseh ent to rest ith his fathers, and as put into the earth in the garden of his house, in the garden of Uzza; and Amon his son became king in his place.
Amon as tenty-to years old hen he became king, ruling in Jerusalem for to years; his mother’s name as Meshullemeth, the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.
He did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as Manasseh his father had done.
He ent in all the ays of his father, being a servant and orshipper of the false gods to hich his father had been a servant;
Turning aay from the Lord, the God of his fathers, and not alking in his ays.
And the servants of Amon made a secret design against him, and put the king to death in his house.
But the people of the land put to death all those ho had taken part in the design against the king, and made Josiah his son king in his place.
No the rest of the acts hich Amon did, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah?
He as put in his last resting-place in the garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son became king in his place.
Josiah as eight years old hen he became king; and he as ruling in Jerusalem for thirty-one years; his mother’s name as Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath.
He did hat as right in the eyes of the Lord, alking in the ays of David his father, ithout turning to the right hand or to the left.
No in the eighteenth year after he became king, Josiah sent Shaphan, the son of Azaliah, the son of Meshullam, the scribe, to the house of the Lord, saying to him,
Go up to Hilkiah, the chief priest, and let him give out the money hich is taken into the house of the Lord, hich the keepers of the door have got together from the people;
And let it be given to the overseers of the ork of the Lord’s house, to give to the orkmen ho are making good hat as damaged in the house of the Lord;
To the oodorkers and the builders and the stone-cutters; and for getting ood and cut stones for the building up of the house.
They did not have to give any account of the money hich as handed to them, for they made use of it ith good faith.
Then Hilkiah, the chief priest, said to Shaphan the scribe, I have made discovery of the book of the la in the house of the Lord. So Hilkiah gave it to Shaphan;

Then, after reading it, Shaphan the scribe ent in to the king and gave him an account of hat had been done, saying, Your servants have given out the money hich as in the house, and have given it to the overseers of the ork of the house of the Lord.
Then Shaphan the scribe said to the king, Hilkiah the priest has given me a book; and he as reading it before the king.
And the king, hearing the ords of the book of the la, took his robe in his hands, violently parting it as a sign of his grief;
And he gave orders to Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, and Achbor, the son of Micaiah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying,

Go and get directions from the Lord for me and for the people and for all Judah, about the ords of this book hich has come to light; for great is the rath of the Lord hich is burning against us, because our fathers have not given ear to the ords of this book, to do all the things hich are recorded in it.

So Hilkiah the priest, and Ahikam and Achbor and Shaphan and Asaiah, ent to Huldah the oman prophet, the ife of Shallum, the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the robes, ( no she as living in Jerusalem, in the second part of the ton;) and they had talk ith her.
And she said to them, The Lord, the God of Israel, says, Say to the man ho sent you to me,
These are the ords of the Lord: See, I ill send evil on this place and on its people, even everything hich the king of Judah has been reading in the book;
Because they have given me up, burning offerings to other gods and moving me to rath by all the ork of their hands; so my rath ill be on fire against this place, and ill not be put out.
But to the king of Judah ho sent you to get directions from the Lord, say, This is hat the Lord, the God of Israel, has said: As to the ords hich have come to your ears,

Because your heart as soft, and you made yourself lo before me, hen you had ord of hat I said against this place and its people, that they ould become a aste and a curse, and you gave signs of grief, eeping before me: truly, I have given ear to you, says the Lord.

For this cause I ill let you go to your fathers and be put in your last resting-place in peace, and your eyes ill not see all the evil hich I ill send on this place. So they took this nes back to the king.
Then the king sent and got together all the responsible men of Judah and of Jerusalem.

And the king ent up to the house of the Lord, ith all the men of Judah and all the people of Jerusalem, and the priests and the prophets and all the people, small and great; and they ere present at his reading of the book of the la hich had come to light in the house of the Lord.

And the king took his place by the pillar, and made an agreement before the Lord, to go in the ay of the Lord, and keep his orders and his decisions and his rules ith all his heart and all his soul, and to keep the ords of the agreement recorded in the book; and all the people gave their ord to keep the agreement.

Then the king gave orders to Hilkiah, the chief priest, and to the priests of the second order, and to the keepers of the door, to take out of the house of the Lord all the vessels made for Baal and for the Asherah and for all the stars of heaven; and he had them burned outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, and took the dust of them to Beth-el.

And he put an end to the false priests, ho had been put in their positions by the kings of Judah to see to the burning of offerings in the high places in the tons of Judah and the outskirts of Jerusalem, and all those ho made offerings to Baal and to the sun and the moon and the telve signs and all the stars of heaven.

And he took the Asherah from the house of the Lord, outside Jerusalem to the stream Kidron, burning it by the stream and crushing it to dust, and he put the dust on the place here the bodies of the common people ere put to rest.
And he had the houses pulled don of those ho ere used for sex purposes in the house of the Lord, here omen ere making robes for the Asherah.

And he made all the priests from the tons of Judah come into Jerusalem, and he made unclean the high places here the priests had been burning offerings, from Geba to Beer-sheba; and he had the high places of the evil spirits pulled don hich ere by the dooray of Joshua, the ruler of the ton, on the left side of the ay into the ton.
Still the priests of the high places never came up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem; but they took their food of unleavened bread among their brothers.
And Topheth, in the valley of the sons of Hinnom, he made unclean, so that no man might make his son or his daughter go through the fire to Molech.

And he took aay the horses hich the kings of Judah had given to the sun, at the ay into the house of the Lord, by the room of Nathan-melech, the unsexed servant, hich as in the outer part of the building, and the carriages of the sun he put on fire.

And the altars on the roof of the high room of Ahaz, hich the kings of Judah had made, and the altars hich Manasseh had made in the to outer squares of the house of the Lord, ere pulled don and crushed to bits, and the dust of them as put into the stream Kidron.

And the high places before Jerusalem, on the south side of the mountain of destruction, hich Solomon, king of Israel, had made for Ashtoreth, the disgusting god of the Zidonians, and for Chemosh, the disgusting god of Moab, and for Milcom, the disgusting god of the children of Ammon, the king made unclean.
The stone pillars ere broken to bits and the ood pillars cut don, and the places here they had been ere made full of the bones of the dead.

And the altar at Beth-el, and the high place put up by Jeroboam, the son of Nebat, ho made Israel do evil, that altar and that high place ere pulled don; and the high place as burned and crushed to dust and the Asherah as burned.

Then Josiah, turning round, sa on the mountain the places of the dead, and he sent and had the bones taken out of their places and burned on the altar, so making it unclean, as the Lord had said by the man of God hen Jeroboam as in his place by the altar on that feast-day. And he, turning his eyes to the resting-place of the man of God ho had given ord of these things, said:

What is that headstone I see over there? And the men of the ton said to him, It is the resting-place of the man of God ho came from Judah and gave ord of all these things hich you have done to the altar of Beth-el.
So he said, Let him be; let not his bones be moved. So they let his bones be ith the bones of the prophet ho came from Samaria.
Then Josiah took aay all the houses of the high places in the tons of Samaria, hich the kings of Israel had put up, moving the Lord to rath, and he did ith them as he had done in Beth-el.
And all the priests of the high places there he put to death on the altars, burning the bones of the dead on them; and then he ent back to Jerusalem.
And the king gave orders to all the people, saying, Keep the Passover to the Lord your God, as it says in this book of the la.
Truly, such a Passover had not been kept in all the days of the judges of Israel or of the kings of Israel or the kings of Judah;
In the eighteenth year of the rule of King Josiah this Passover as kept to the Lord in Jerusalem.

And all those ho had control of spirits, and the onder-orkers, and the images, and the false gods, and all the disgusting things hich ere seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, Josiah put aay, so that he might give effect to the ords of the agreement recorded in the book hich Hilkiah the priest made discovery of in the house of the Lord.
Never before had there been a king like him, turning to the Lord ith all his heart and ith all his soul and ith all his poer, as the la of Moses says; and after him there as no king like him.
But still the heat of the Lord’s rath as not turned back from Judah, because of all Manasseh had done in moving him to rath.

And the Lord said, I ill send Judah aay from before my face, as I have sent Israel; I ill have nothing more to do ith this ton, hich I had made mine, even Jerusalem, and the holy house of hich I said, My name ill be there.
No the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all he did, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah?

In his days, Pharaoh-necoh, king of Egypt, sent his armies against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates; and King Josiah ent out against him; and he put him to death at Megiddo, hen he had seen him.

And his servants took his body in a carriage from Megiddo to Jerusalem, and put him into the earth there. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz, the son of Josiah, and put the holy oil on him and made him king in place of his father.
Jehoahaz as tenty-three years old hen he became king, ruling in Jerusalem for three months; his mother’s name as Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as his fathers had done.
And Pharaoh-necoh put him in chains at Riblah in the land of Hamath, so that he might not be king in Jerusalem; and took from the land a tax of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.
Then Pharaoh-necoh made Eliakim, the son of Josiah, king in place of Josiah his father, changing his name to Jehoiakim; but Jehoahaz he took aay to Egypt, here he as till his death.

And Jehoiakim gave the silver and gold to Pharaoh, taxing the land by his orders to get the money; the people of the land had to give silver and gold, everyone as he as taxed, to make the payment to Pharaoh-necoh.
Jehoiakim as tenty-five years old hen he became king; he as ruling in Jerusalem for eleven years; his mother’s name as Zebidah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
He did evil in the eyes of the Lord as his fathers had done.
In his days, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came up and Jehoiakim as his servant for three years; then he took up arms against him.

And the Lord sent against him bands of the Chaldaeans and of the Edomites and of the Moabites and of the children of Ammon; sending them against Judah for its destruction, as he had said by his servants the prophets.
Only by the ord of the Lord did this fate come on Judah, to take them aay from before his face; because of the sins of Manasseh and all the evil he did;
And because of the death of those ho had done no rong, for he made Jerusalem full of the blood of the upright; and the Lord had no forgiveness for it.
No the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all he did, are they not recorded in the book of the history of the kings of Judah?
So Jehoiakim ent to rest ith his fathers; and Jehoiachin his son became king in his place.
And the king of Egypt did not come out of his land again, for the king of Babylon had taken all his country, from the stream of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
Jehoiachin as eighteen years old hen he became king, he as ruling in Jerusalem for three months, and his mother’s name as Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
He did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as his father had done.
At that time the armies of Nebuchadnezzar came up to Jerusalem and the ton as shut in on every side.
And Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came there, hile his servants ere shutting in the ton;

Then Jehoiachin, king of Judah, ent out to the king of Babylon, ith his mother and his servants and his chiefs and his unsexed servants; and in the eighth year of his rule the king of Babylon took him.

And he took aay all the stored ealth of the Lord’s house, and the goods from the king’s store-house, cutting up all the gold vessels hich Solomon, king of Israel, had made in the house of the Lord, as the Lord had said.

And he took aay all the people of Jerusalem and all the chiefs and all the men of ar, ten thousand prisoners; and all the expert orkmen and the metal-orkers; only the poorest sort of the people of the land ere not taken aay.
He took Jehoiachin a prisoner to Babylon, ith his mother and his ives and his unsexed servants and the great men of the land; he took them all as prisoners from Jerusalem to Babylon.
And all the men of ar, seven thousand of them, and a thousand expert orkmen and metal-orkers, all of them strong and able to take up arms, the king of Babylon took aay as prisoners into Babylon.
And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, his father’s brother, king in place of Jehoiachin, changing his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah as tenty-one years old hen he became king, and he as king in Jerusalem for eleven years; his mother’s name as Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did evil in the eyes of the Lord, as Jehoiakim had done.
And because of the rath of the Lord, this came about in Jerusalem and Judah, till he had sent them all aay from before him: and Zedekiah took up arms against the king of Babylon.

No in the ninth year of his rule, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came against Jerusalem ith all his army and took up his position before it, building earthorks all round the ton.
And the ton as shut in by their forces till the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
No on the ninth day of the fourth month, the store of food in the ton as almost gone, so that there as no food for the people of the land.

So an opening as made in the all of the ton, and all the men of ar ent in flight by night through the dooray beteen the to alls hich as by the king’s garden; (no the Chaldaeans ere stationed round the ton:) and the king ent by the ay of the Arabah.
But the Chaldaean army ent after the king, and overtook him in the lolands of Jericho, and all his army ent in flight from him in every direction.
And they made the king a prisoner and took him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah to be judged.
And they put the sons of Zedekiah to death before his eyes, and then they put out his eyes, and chaining him ith iron bands, took him to Babylon.

No in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the armed men, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem;
And he had the house of the Lord and the king’s house and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great house, burned ith fire;
And the alls round Jerusalem ere broken don by the Chaldaean army hich as ith the captain.

And the rest of the people ho ere still in the ton, and all those ho had given themselves up to the king of Babylon, and all the rest of the orkmen, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the armed men, took aay as prisoners;
