All these had taken strange ives; and some of them had ives by hom they had offspring.
The history of Nehemiah, the son of Hacaliah. No it came about, in the month Chislev, in the tentieth year, hen I as in Shushan, the king’s ton,
That Hanani, one of my brothers, came ith certain men from Judah; and in anser to my request for nes of the Jes ho had been prisoners and had got aay, and of Jerusalem,
They said to me, The small band of Jes no living there in the land are in great trouble and shame: the all of Jerusalem has been broken don, and its doorays burned ith fire.
Then, after hearing these ords, for some days I gave myself up to eeping and sorro, seated on the earth; and taking no food I made prayer to the God of heaven,
And said, O Lord, the God of heaven, the great God, greatly to be feared, keeping faith and mercy ith those ho have love for him and are true to his las:

Let your ear no take note and let your eyes be open, so that you may give ear to the prayer of your servant, hich I make before you at this time, day and night, for the children of Israel, your servants, hile I put before you the sins of the children of Israel, hich e have done against you: truly, I and my father’s people are sinners.
We have done great rong against you, and have not kept the orders, the rules, and the decisions, hich you gave to your servant Moses.
Keep in mind, O Lord, the order you gave your servant Moses, saying, If you do rong I ill send you andering among the peoples:

But if you come back to me and keep my orders and do them, even if those of you ho have been forced out are living in the farthest parts of heaven, I ill get them from there, and take them back to the place marked out by me for the resting-place of my name.
No these are your servants and your people, hom you have made yours by your great poer and by your strong hand.

O Lord, let your ear take note of the prayer of your servant, and of the prayers of your servants, ho take delight in orshipping your name: give help, O Lord, to your servant this day, and let him have mercy in the eyes of this man. ( No I as the king’s ine-servant.)

And it came about in the month Nisan, in the tentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, hen ine as before him, that I took up the ine and gave it to the king. No I had never before been sad hen the king as present.
And the king said to me, Why is your face sad, seeing that you are not ill? this is nothing but sorro of heart. Then I as full of fear;

And said to the king, May the king be living for ever: is it not natural for my face to be sad, hen the ton, the place here the bodies of my fathers are at rest, has been made aste and its doorays burned ith fire?
Then the king said to me, What is your desire? So I made prayer to the God of heaven.

And I said to the king, If it is the king’s pleasure, and if your servant has your approval, send me to Judah, to the ton here the bodies of my fathers are at rest, so that I may take in hand the building of it.
And the king said to me ( the queen being seated by his side), Ho long ill your journey take, and hen ill you come back? So the king as pleased to send me, and I gave him a fixed time.
Further, I said to the king, If it is the king’s pleasure, let letters be given to me for the rulers across the river, so that they may let me go through till I come to Judah;

And a letter to Asaph, the keeper of the king’s park, so that he may give me ood to make boards for the doors of the toer of the house, and for the all of the ton, and for the house hich is to be mine. And the king gave me this, for the hand of my God as on me.
Then I came to the rulers of the lands across the river and gave them the king’s letters. No the king had sent ith me captains of the army and horsemen.
And Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, hearing of it, ere greatly troubled because a man had come to the help of the children of Israel.
So I came to Jerusalem and as there three days.

And in the night I got up, taking ith me a small band of men; I said nothing to any man of hat God had put into my heart to do for Jerusalem: and I had no beast ith me but the one on hich I as seated.

And I ent out by night, through the dooray of the valley, and past the dragon’s ater-spring as far as the place here aste material as put, vieing the alls of Jerusalem hich ere broken don, and the doorays hich had been burned ith fire.
Then I ent on to the door of the fountain and to the king’s pool: but there as no room for my beast to get through.
Then in the night, I ent up by the stream, vieing the all; then turning back, I ent in by the door in the valley, and so came back.

And the chiefs had no knoledge of here I had been or hat I as doing; and I had not then said anything to the Jes or to the priests or the great ones or the chiefs or the rest of those ho ere doing the ork.

Then I said to them, You see hat a bad condition e are in; ho Jerusalem is a aste, and its doorays burned ith fire: come, let us get to ork, building up the all of Jerusalem, so that e may no longer be put to shame.

Then I gave them an account of ho the hand of my God as on me, helping me; and of the king’s ords hich he had said to me. And they said, Let us get to ork on the building. So they made their hands strong for the good ork.
But Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the servant, the Ammonite, and Geshem the Arabian, hearing of it, made sport of us, laughing at us and saying, What are you doing? ill you go against the king?
Then ansering them I said, The God of heaven, he ill be our help; so e his servants ill go on ith our building: but you have no part or right or any name in Jerusalem.

Then Eliashib, the chief priest, got up ith his brothers the priests, and took in hand the building of the sheep dooray; they made it holy and put its doors in position; as far as the toer of Hammeah they made it holy, even to the toer of Hananel.
And by his side the men of Jericho ere building. And after them, Zaccur, the son of Imri.
The sons of Hassenaah ere the builders of the fish dooray; they put its boards in place and put up its doors, ith their locks and rods.
By their side Meremoth, the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, as making good the alls. Then Meshullam, the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel; and by him, Zadok, the son of Baana.
Near them, the Tekoites ere at ork; but their chiefs did not put their necks to the ork of their Lord.
Joiada, the son of Paseah, and Meshullam, the son of Besodeiah, made good the old dooray; they put its boards in place and put up its doors, ith their locks and rods.
By their side ere orking Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite, the men of Gibeon and of Mizpah from the seat of the ruler across the river.
Near them as orking Uzziel, the son of Harhaiah, the gold-orker. And by him as Hananiah, one of the perfume-makers, building up Jerusalem as far as the ide all.
Near them as orking Rephaiah, the son of Hur, the ruler of half Jerusalem.
By his side as Jedaiah, the son of Harumaph, opposite his house. And by him as Hattush, the son of Hashabneiah.
Malchijah, the son of Harim, and Hasshub, the son of Pahath-moab, ere orking on another part, and the toer of the ovens.
Near them as Shallum, the son of Hallohesh, the ruler of half Jerusalem, ith his daughters.

Hanun and the people of Zanoah ere orking on the dooray of the valley; they put it up and put up its doors, ith their locks and rods, and a thousand cubits of all as far as the dooray here the aste material as placed.
And Malchijah, the son of Rechab, the ruler of the division of Beth-haccherem, made good the dooray of the aste, building it up and putting up its doors, ith their locks and rods.

And Shallun, the son of Col-hozeh, the ruler of the division of Mizpah, made good the dooray of the fountain, building it up and covering it and putting up its doors, ith their locks and rods, ith the all of the pool of Shelah by the king’s garden, as far as the steps hich go don from the ton of David.

By his side as orking Nehemiah, the son of Azbuk, ruler of half the division of Beth-zur, as far as the place opposite the last resting-places of David’s family, and the pool hich as made and the house of the men of ar.
Then came the Levites, Rehum, the son of Bani. By his side as orking Hashabiah, ruler of half the division of Keilah, for his division.
After him ere orking their brothers, Bavvai, the son of Henadad, ruler of half the division of Keilah.
And by his side as orking Ezer, the son of Jeshua, the ruler of Mizpah, making good another part opposite the ay up to the store of arms at the turning of the all.
After him Baruch, the son of Zabbai, as hard at ork on another part, from the turning of the all to the door of the house of Eliashib, the chief priest.
After him Meremoth, the son of Uriah, the son of Hakkoz, as orking on another part, from the door of the house of Eliashib as far as the end of his house.
After him ere orking the priests, the men of the loland.
After them came Benjamin and Hasshub, opposite their house. After them Azariah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ananiah, made good the all by the house here he himself as living.
After him Binnui, the son of Henadad, as orking on another part, from the house of Azariah as far as the turning of the all and the angle.

Palal, the son of Uzai, made good the all opposite the angle and the toer hich comes out from the higher part of the king’s house, by the open space of the atch. After him as Pedaiah, the son of Parosh.
( No the Nethinim ere living in the Ophel, as far as the place facing the ater dooray to the east, and the toer hich comes out.)
After him the Tekoites ere making good another part, opposite the great toer hich comes out, and up to the all of the Ophel.
Further on, past the horse dooray, the priests ere at ork, every one opposite his house.
After them Zadok, the son of Immer, as orking opposite his house. And after him Shemaiah, the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the east door.
After him Hananiah, the son of Shelemiah, and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, ere making good another part. After him Meshullam, the son of Berechiah, made good the all opposite his room.
After him Malchijah, one of the gold-orkers to the Nethinim and the traders, made good the all opposite the dooray of Hammiphkad and as far as the ay up to the angle.
And beteen the ay up to the angle and the sheep door, the gold-orkers and the traders made good the all.
No, Sanballat, hearing that e ere building the all, as very angry, and in his rath made sport of the Jes.

And in the hearing of his countrymen and the army of Samaria he said, What are these feeble Jes doing? ill they make themselves strong? ill they make offerings? ill they get the ork done in a day? ill they make the stones hich have been burned come again out of the dust?
No Tobiah the Ammonite as by him, and he said, Such is their building that if a fox goes up it, their stone all ill be broken don.
Give ear, O our God, for e are looked don on: let their ords of shame be turned back on themselves, and let them be given up to asting in a land here they are prisoners:
Let not their rongdoing be covered or their sin ashed aay from before you: for they have made you angry before the builders.
So e ent on building the all; and all the all as joined together half-ay up: for the people ere orking hard.

But hen it came to the ears of Sanballat and Tobiah and the Arabians and the Ammonites and the Ashdodites, that the building of the alls of Jerusalem as going forard and the broken places ere being made good, they ere full of rath;
And they made designs, all of them together, to come and make an attack on Jerusalem, causing trouble there.
But e made our prayer to God, and had men on atch against them day and night because of them.
And Judah said, The strength of the orkmen is giving ay, and there is much aste material; it is impossible for us to put up the all.
And those ho ere against us said, Without their knoledge and ithout their seeing us, e ill come among them and put them to death, causing the ork to come to a stop.
And it came about that hen the Jes ho ere living near them came, they said to us ten times, From all directions they are coming against us.
So in the loest part of the space at the back of the alls, in the open places, I put the people by families, ith their sords, their spears, and their bos.

And after looking, I got up and said to the great ones and to the chiefs and to the rest of the people, Have no fear of them: keep in mind the Lord ho is great and greatly to be feared, and take up arms for your brothers, your sons, and your daughters, your ives and your houses.
And hen it came to the ears of those ho ere against us, that e had knoledge of their designs and that God had made their purpose come to nothing, e all ent back to the all, everyone to his ork

And from that time, half of my servants ere doing their part of the ork, and half kept the spears and body-covers and the bos and the metal ar-dresses; and the chiefs ere at the back of the men of Judah.
Those ho ere building the all and those ho ere moving material did their part, everyone orking ith one hand, ith his spear in the other;
Every builder as orking ith his sord at his side. And by my side as a man for sounding the horn.
And I said to the great ones and the chiefs and the rest of the people, The ork is great and idely spaced and e are far aay from one another on the all:
Wherever you may be hen the horn is sounded, come here to us; our God ill be fighting for us.
So e ent on ith the ork: and half of them had spears in their hands from the dan of the morning till the stars ere seen.
And at the same time I said to the people, Let everyone ith his servant come inside Jerusalem for the night, so that at night they may keep atch for us, and go on orking by day.
So not one of us, I or my brothers or my servants or the atchmen ho ere ith me, took off his clothing, everyone ent armed to the ater.
Then there as a great outcry from the people and their ives against their countrymen the Jes.
For there ere some ho said, We, our sons and our daughters, are a great number: let us get grain, so that e may have food for our needs.
And there ere some ho said, We are giving our fields and our vine-gardens and our houses for debt: let us get grain because e are in need.
And there ere others ho said, We have given up our fields and our vine-gardens to get money for the king’s taxes.

But our flesh is the same as the flesh of our countrymen, and our children as their children: and no e are giving our sons and daughters into the hands of others, to be their servants, and some of our daughters are servants even no: and e have no poer to put a stop to it; for other men have our fields and our vine-gardens.
And on hearing their outcry and hat they said I as very angry.

And after turning it over in my mind, I made a protest to the chiefs and the rulers, and said to them, Every one of you is taking interest from his countryman. And I got together a great meeting of protest.

And I said to them, We have given hatever e ere able to give, to make our brothers the Jes free, ho ere servants and prisoners of the nations: and ould you no give up your brothers for a price, and are they to become our property? Then they said nothing, ansering not a ord.
And I said, What you are doing is not good: is it not the more necessary for you to go in the fear of our God, because of the shame hich the nations may put on us?
Even I and my servants have been taking interest for the money and the grain e have let them have. So no, let us give up this thing.

Give back to them this very day their fields, their vine-gardens, their olive-gardens, and their houses, as ell as a hundredth part of the money and the grain and the ine and the oil hich you have taken from them.
Then they said, We ill give them back, and take nothing for them; e ill do as you say. Then I sent for the priests and made them take an oath that they ould keep this agreement.

And shaking out the folds of my robe, I said, So may God send out from his house and his ork every man ho does not keep this agreement; even so let him be sent out and made as nothing. And all the meeting of the people said, So be it, and gave praise to the Lord. And the people did as they had said.

No from the time hen I as made ruler of the people in the land of Judah, from the tentieth year till the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes the king, for telve years, I and my servants have never taken the food hich as the right of the ruler.

But earlier rulers ho ere before me made the people responsible for their upkeep, and took from them bread and ine at the rate of forty shekels of silver; and even their servants ere lords over the people: but I did not do so, because of the fear of God.
And I kept on ith the ork of this all, and e got no land for ourselves: and all my servants ere helping ith the ork.
And more than this, a hundred and fifty of the Jes and the rulers ere guests at my table, in addition to those ho came to us from the nations round about us.

No the food made ready for one day as one ox and six fat sheep, as ell as fols; and once in ten days a store of all sorts of ine: but all the same, I did not take the food to hich the ruler had a right, because the people ere crushed under a hard yoke.
Keep in mind, O my God, for my good, all I have done for this people.

No hen ord as given to Sanballat and Tobiah and to Geshem the Arabian and to the rest of our haters, that I had done the building of the all and that there ere no more broken places in it ( though even then I had not put up the doors in the doorays);
Sanballat and Geshem sent to me saying, Come, let us have a meeting in one of the little tons in the loland of Ono. But their purpose as to do me evil.
And I sent men to them saying, I am doing a great ork, so that it is not possible for me to come don: is the ork to be stopped hile I go aay from it and come don to you?
And four times they sent to me in this ay, and I sent them the same anser.
Then Sanballat sent his servant to me a fifth time ith an open letter in his hand;

And in it these ords ere recorded: It is said among the nations, and Geshem says so, that you and the Jes are hoping to make yourselves free from the king’s authority; and that this is hy you are building the all: and they say that it is your purpose to be their king;
And that you have prophets preaching about you in Jerusalem, and saying, There is a king in Judah: no an account of these things ill be sent to the king. So come no, and let us have a discussion.
Then I sent to him, saying, No such things as you say are being done, they are only a fiction you have made up yourself.
For they ere hoping to put fear in us, saying, Their hands ill become feeble and give up the ork so that it may not get done. But no, O God, make my hands strong.

And I ent to the house of Shemaiah, the son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, ho as shut up; and he said, Let us have a meeting in the house of God, inside the Temple, and let the doors be shut: for they ill come to put you to death; truly, in the night they ill come to put you to death.
And I said, Am I the sort of man to go in flight? hat man, in my position, ould go into the Temple to keep himself safe? I ill not go in.
Then it became clear to me that God had not sent him: he had given this ord of a prophet against me himself: and Tobiah and Sanballat had given him money to do so.
For this reason they had given him money, in order that I might be overcome by fear and do hat he said and do rong, and so they ould have reason to say evil about me and put shame on me.
Keep in mind, O my God, Tobiah and Sanballat and hat they did, and Noadiah, the oman prophet, and the rest of the prophets hose purpose as to put fear into me.
So the all as complete on the tenty-fifth day of the month Elul, in fifty-to days.
And hen our haters had nes of this, all the nations round about us ere full of fear and ere greatly shamed, for they sa that this ork had been done by our God.
And further, in those days the chiefs of Judah sent a number of letters to Tobiah, and his letters came to them.

For in Judah there ere a number of people ho had made an agreement by oath ith him, because he as the son-in-la of Shecaniah, the son of Arah; and his son Jehohanan had taken as his ife the daughter of Meshullam, the son of Berechiah.
And they said much before me of the good he had done, and gave him accounts of my ords. And Tobiah sent letters ith the purpose of causing me fear.
No hen the building of the all as complete and I had put up the doors, and the door-keepers and the music-makers and the Levites had been given their places,
I made my brother Hanani, and Hananiah, the ruler of the toer, responsible for the government of Jerusalem: for he as a man of good faith, fearing God more than most.

And I said to them, Do not let the doors of Jerusalem be open till the sun is high; and hile the atchmen are in their places, let the doors be shut and locked: and let the people of Jerusalem be put on atch, every one in his atch, opposite his house.
No the ton as ide and great: but the people in it ere only a small number, and the houses had not been put up.

And my God put it into my heart to get together the rulers and the chiefs and the people so that they might be listed by families. And I came across a record of the names of those ho came up at the first, and in it I sa these ords:

These are the people of the divisions of the kingdom, among those ho had been made prisoners by Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, and taken aay by him, ho ent back to Jerusalem and Judah, every one to his ton;
Who came ith Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, Baanah. The number of the men of the people of Israel:
The children of Parosh, to thousand, one hundred and seventy-to.
The children of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-to.
The children of Arah, six hundred and fifty-to.
The children of Pahath-moab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab, to thousand, eight hundred and eighteen.
The children of Elam, a thousand, to hundred and fifty-four.

The children of Bebai, six hundred and tenty-eight.
The children of Azgad, to thousand, three hundred and tenty-to.
The children of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-seven.
The children of Bigvai, to thousand and sixty-seven.
The children of Adin, six hundred and fifty-five.
The children of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight.
The children of Hashum, three hundred and tenty-eight.
The children of Bezai, three hundred and tenty-four.
The children of Hariph, a hundred and telve.
The children of Gibeon, ninety-five.
The men of Beth-lehem and Netophah, a hundred and eighty-eight.
The men of Anathoth, a hundred and tenty-eight.
The men of Beth-azmaveth, forty-to.
The men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three.
The men of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and tenty-one.
The men of Michmas, a hundred and tenty-to.
The men of Beth-el and Ai, a hundred and tenty-three.
The men of the other Nebo, fifty-to.
The children of the other Elam, a thousand, to hundred and fifty-four.
The children of Harim, three hundred and tenty.
The children of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five.
The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred and tenty-one.
The children of Senaah, three thousand, nine hundred and thirty.
The priests: the children of Jedaiah, of the family of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three.
The children of Immer, a thousand and fifty-to.
The children of Pashhur, a thousand, to hundred and forty-seven.
The children of Harim, a thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the children of Jeshua, of Kadmiel, of the children of Hodevah, seventy-four.
The music-makers: the children of Asaph, a hundred and forty-eight.
The door-keepers: the children of Shallum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub, the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai, a hundred and thirty-eight.
The Nethinim: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth,
The children of Keros, the children of Sia, the children of Padon,
The children of Lebana, the children of Hagaba, the children of Salmai,
The children of Hanan, the children of Giddel, the children of Gahar,
The children of Reaiah, the children of Rezin, the children of Nekoda,
The children of Gazzam, the children of Uzza, the children of Paseah,
The children of Besai, the children of Meunim, the children of Nephushesim,
The children of Bakbuk, the children of Hakupha, the children of Harhur,
The children of Bazlith, the children of Mehida, the children of Harsha,
The children of Barkos, the children of Sisera, the children of Temah,
The children of Neziah, the children of Hatipha.
The children of Solomon’s servants: the children of Sotai, the children of Sophereth, the children of Perida,
The children of Jaala, the children of Darkon, the children of Giddel,
The children of Shephatiah, the children of Hattil, the children of Pochereth-hazzebaim, the children of Amon.
All the Nethinim and the children of Solomon’s servants ere three hundred and ninety-to.

All these ere the people ho ent up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer; but because they had no knoledge of their fathers’ families or offspring, it as not certain if they ere Israelites:
The children of Delaiah, the children of Tobiah, the children of Nekoda, six hundred and forty-to.
And of the priests: the children of Hobaiah, the children of Hakkoz, the children of Barzillai, ho as married to one of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and took their name.
They made search for their record among the lists of families, but their names ere nohere to be seen, so they ere looked on as unclean and no longer priests.
And the Tirshatha said that they ere not to have the most holy things for their food, till a priest came to give decision by the Urim and Thummim.
The number of all the people together as forty-to thousand, three hundred and sixty;
As ell as their men-servants and their omen-servants, of hom there ere seven thousand, three hundred and thirty-seven; and they had to hundred and forty-five men and omen to make music.
They had seven hundred and thirty-six horses, to hundred and forty-five transport beasts;
Four hundred and thirty-five camels, six thousand, seven hundred and tenty asses.
And some of the heads of families gave money for the ork. The Tirshatha gave into the store a thousand darics of gold, fifty basins, five hundred and thirty priests’ robes.
And some of the heads of families gave into the store for the ork tenty thousand darics of gold, and to thousand, to hundred pounds of silver.
And that hich the rest of the people gave as tenty thousand darics of gold, and to thousand pounds of silver, and sixty-seven priests’ robes.

And their children ere talking half in the language of Ashdod; they had no knoledge of the Jes’ language, but made use of the language of the to peoples.

And I took up the cause against them, cursing them and giving blos to some of them and pulling out their hair; and I made them take an oath by God, saying, You are not to give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.

Was it not in these things that Solomon, king of Israel, did rong? among a number of nations there as no king like him, and he as dear to his God, and God made him king over all Israel: but even he as made to do evil by strange omen.
Are e then ithout protest to let you do all this great evil, sinning against our God by taking strange omen for your ives?
And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib, the chief priest, as son-in-la to Sanballat the Horonite: so I sent him aay from me.
Keep them in mind, O my God, because they have put shame on the priests’ name and on the agreement of the priests and the Levites.
So I made them clean from all strange people, and had regular atches fixed for the priests and for the Levites, everyone in his ork;
And for the ood offering, at fixed times, and for the first fruits. Keep me in mind, O my God, for good.
No it came about in the days of Ahasuerus, ( that Ahasuerus ho as ruler of a hundred and tenty-seven divisions of the kingdom, from India as far as Ethiopia:)
That in those days, hen King Ahasuerus as ruling in Shushan, his strong ton,

In the third year of his rule he gave a feast to all his captains and his servants; and the captains of the army of Persia and Media, the great men and the rulers of the divisions of his kingdom, ere present before him;
And for a long time, even a hundred and eighty days, he let them see all the ealth and the glory of his kingdom and the great poer and honour hich ere his.

And at the end of that time, the king gave a feast for all the people ho ere present in Shushan, the king’s ton, small as ell as great, for seven days, in the outer square of the garden of the king’s house.

There ere fair hangings of hite and green and blue, fixed ith cords of purple and the best linen to silver rings and pillars of polished stone: the seats ere of gold and silver on a floor of red and hite and yello and black stone.
And they gave them drink in gold vessels, every vessel being different, and ine of the kingdom, freely given by the king.
And the drinking as in keeping ith the la; no one as forced: for the king had given orders to all the chief servants of his house to do as as pleasing to every man.
And Vashti the queen gave a feast for the omen in the house of King Ahasuerus.

On the seventh day, hen the heart of the king as glad ith ine, he gave orders to Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven unsexed servants ho ere aiting before Ahasuerus the king,
That Vashti the queen as to come before him, croned ith her cron, and let the people and the captains see her: for she as very beautiful.
But hen the servants gave her the king’s order, Vashti the queen said she ould not come: then the king as very angry, and his heart as burning ith rath.
And the king said to the ise men, ho had knoledge of the times, ( for this as the king’s ay ith all ho ere expert in la and in the giving of decisions:

And second only to him ere Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven rulers of Persia and Media, ho ere friends of the king, and had the first places in the kingdom:)
What is to be done by la to Vashti the queen, because she has not done hat King Ahasuerus, by his servants, gave her orders to do?

And before the king and the captains, Memucan gave his anser: Vashti the queen has done rong, not only to the king, but to all the captains and to all the peoples in all the divisions of the kingdom of King Ahasuerus;

For nes of hat the queen has done ill come to the ears of all omen, and they ill no longer give respect to their husbands hen it is said to them, King Ahasuerus gave orders for Vashti the queen to come before him and she came not.
And the ives of the captains of Persia and Media, hearing hat the queen has done, ill say the same to all the king’s captains. So there ill be much shame and rath.

If it is pleasing to the king, let an order go out from him, and let it be recorded among the las of the Persians and the Medes, so that it may never be changed, that Vashti is never again to come before King Ahasuerus; and let the king give her place to another ho is better than she.
And hen this order, given by the king, is made public through all his kingdom ( for it is great), all the ives ill give honour to their husbands, great as ell as small.
And this suggestion seemed good to the king and the captains; and the king did as Memucan said;

And sent letters to all the divisions of the kingdom, to every division in the riting commonly used there, and to every people in the language hich as theirs, saying that every man as to be the ruler in his house, and that this order as to be given out in the language of his people.
After these things, hen the king’s feelings ere calmer, the thought of Vashti and hat she had done and the order he had made against her, came back to his mind.
Then the servants ho ere aiting on the king said to him, Let search be made for some fair young virgins for the king:

Let the king give authority to certain men in all the divisions of his kingdom, to get together all the fair young virgins and send them to Shushan, the king’s ton, to the omen’s house, under the care of Hegai, the king’s servant, the keeper of the omen: and let the things needed for making them clean be given to them;
And let the girl ho is pleasing to the king be queen in place of Vashti. And the king as pleased ith this suggestion; and he did so.
No there as a certain Je in Shushan named Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite;
Who had been taken aay from Jerusalem among those ho had been made prisoner ith Jeconiah, king of Judah, hen Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had taken him aay.

And he had been a father to Hadassah, that is Esther, the daughter of his father’s brother: for she had no father or mother, and she as very beautiful; and hen her father and mother ere dead, Mordecai took her for his daughter.

So hen the order made by the king as publicly given out, and a number of girls had been placed in the care of Hegai in the king’s house in Shushan, Esther as taken into the king’s house and put in the care of Hegai, the keeper of the omen.

And he as pleased ith the girl and as kind to her; and he quickly gave her hat as needed for making her clean, and the things hich ere hers by right, and seven servant-girls ho ere to be hers from the king’s house: and he had her and her servant-girls moved to the best place in the omen’s part of the house.
Esther had not said hat family or people she came from, for Mordecai had given her orders not to do so.
And every day Mordecai took his alk before the square of the omen’s house, to see ho Esther as and hat ould be done to her.

No every girl, hen her turn came, had to go in to King Ahasuerus, after undergoing, for a space of telve months, hat as ordered by the la for the omen ( for this as the time necessary for making them clean, that is, six months ith oil of myrrh and six months ith seet perfumes and such things as are needed for making omen clean):
And in this ay the girl ent in to the king; hatever she had a desire for as given to her to take ith her from the omen’s house into the house of the king.

In the evening she ent, and on the day after she came back to the second house of the omen, into the keeping of Shaashgaz, one of the king’s unsexed servants ho had the care of the king’s ives: only if the king had delight in her and sent for her by name did she go in to him again.

No hen the time came for Esther, the daughter of Abihail, his father’s brother, hom Mordecai had taken as his daughter, to go in to the king, she made request for nothing but hat Hegai, the king’s servant and keeper of the omen, had given her. And Esther as looked on kindly by all ho sa her.
So Esther as taken in to King Ahasuerus in his house in the tenth month, hich is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his rule.

And Esther as more pleasing to the king than all the omen, and to his eyes she as fairer and more full of grace than all the other virgins: so he put his cron on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.

Then the king gave a great feast for all his captains and his servants, even Esther’s feast; and he gave orders through all the divisions of his kingdom for a day of rest from ork, and gave ealth from his store.
And hen the virgins came together in the second house of the omen, Mordecai took his seat in the dooray of the king’s house.
Esther had still said nothing of her family or her people, as Mordecai had given her orders; for Esther did hat Mordecai said, as hen she as living ith him.

In those days, hile Mordecai as seated at the king’s dooray, to of the king’s servants, Bigthan and Teresh, keepers of the door, being angry, ere looking for a chance to make an attack on King Ahasuerus.
And Mordecai, having knoledge of their purpose, sent ord of it to Esther the queen; and Esther gave the nes to the king in Mordecai’s name.
And hen the thing had been looked into, it as seen to be true, and the to of them ere put to death by hanging on a tree: and it as put don in the records before the king.
After these things, by the order of the king, Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, as lifted up and given a position of honour and a higher place than all the other captains ho ere ith him.

And all the king’s servants ho ere in the king’s house ent don to the earth before Haman and gave him honour: for so the king had given orders. But Mordecai did not go don before him or give him honour.
Then the king’s servants ho ere in the king’s house said to Mordecai, Why do you go against the king’s order?
No hen they had said this to him day after day and he gave no attention, they let Haman have nes of it, to see if Mordecai’s behaviour ould be overlooked: for he had said to them that he as a Je.
And hen Haman sa that Mordecai did not go don before him and give him honour, Haman as full of rath.

But it as not enough for him to make an attack on Mordecai only; for they had made clear to him ho Mordecai’s people ere; so Haman made it his purpose to put an end to all the Jes, even Mordecai’s people, through all the kingdom of Ahasuerus.

In the first month, the month Nisan, in the telfth year of King Ahasuerus, from day to day and from month to month they ent on looking for a sign given by Pur ( that is chance) before Haman, till the sign came out for the thirteenth day of the telfth month, the month Adar.

And Haman said to King Ahasuerus, There is a certain nation living here and there in small groups among the people in all the divisions of your kingdom; their las are different from those of any other nation, and they do not keep the king’s las: for this reason it is not right for the king to let them be.

If it is the king’s pleasure, let a statement ordering their destruction be put in riting: and I ill give to those responsible for the king’s business, ten thousand talents of silver for the king’s store-house.
And the king took his ring from his hand and gave it to Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the hater of the Jes.
And the king said to Haman, The money is yours, and the people, to do ith them hatever seems right to you.

Then on the thirteenth day of the first month, the king’s scribes ere sent for, and they put in riting Haman’s orders to all the king’s captains and the rulers of every division of his kingdom and the chiefs of every people: for every division of the kingdom in the riting commonly used there, and to every people in the language hich as theirs; it as signed in the name of King Ahasuerus and stamped ith the king’s ring.

And letters ere sent by the runners into every division of the kingdom ordering the death and destruction of all Jes, young and old, little children and omen, on the same day, even the thirteenth day of the telfth month, the month Adar, and the taking of all their goods by force.
A copy of the riting, to be made public in every part of the kingdom, as sent out to all the peoples, so that they might be ready hen that day came.
The runners ent out quickly by the king’s order, and a public statement as made in Shushan: and the king and Haman took ine together: but the ton of Shushan as troubled.
No hen Mordecai sa hat as done, pulling off his robe, he put on haircloth, ith dust on his head, and ent out into the middle of the ton, crying out ith a loud and bitter cry.
And he came even before the king’s dooray; for no one might come inside the king’s door clothed in haircloth.

And in every part of the kingdom, herever the king’s ord and his order came, there as great sorro among the Jes, and eeping and crying and going ithout food; and numbers of them ere stretched on the earth covered ith dust and haircloth.

And Esther’s omen and her servants came and gave her ord of it. Then great as the grief of the queen: and she sent robes for Mordecai, so that his clothing of haircloth might be taken off; but he ould not have them.
Then Esther sent for Hathach, one of the king’s unsexed servants hom he had given her for aiting on her, and she gave him orders to go to Mordecai and see hat this as and hy it as.
So Hathach ent out and sa Mordecai in the open square of the ton before the king’s dooray.
And Mordecai gave him an account of hat had taken place, and of the amount of money hich Haman had said he ould put into the king’s store for the destruction of the Jes.

And he gave him the copy of the order hich had been given out in Shushan for their destruction, ordering him to let Esther see it, and to make it clear to her; and to say to her that she as to go in to the king, requesting his mercy, and making prayer for her people.
And Hathach came back and gave Esther an account of hat Mordecai had said.
Then Esther sent Hathach to say to Mordecai:

It is common knoledge among all the king’s servants and the people of every part of the kingdom, that if anyone, man or oman, comes to the king in his inner room ithout being sent for, there is only one la for him, that he is to be put to death; only those to hom the king’s rod of gold is stretched out may keep their lives: but I have not been sent for to come before the king these thirty days.
And they said these ords to Mordecai.
Then Mordecai sent this anser back to Esther: Do not have the idea that you in the king’s house ill be safe from the fate of all the Jes.

If at this time you say nothing, then help and salvation ill come to the Jes from some other place, but you and your father’s family ill come to destruction: and ho is to say that you have not come to the kingdom even for such a time as this?
Then Esther sent them back to Mordecai ith this anser:

Go, get together all the Jes ho are present in Shushan, and go ithout food for me, taking no food or drink night or day for three days: and I and my omen ill do the same; and so I ill go in to the king, hich is against the la: and if death is to be my fate, then let it come.
So Mordecai ent aay and did everything as Esther had said.

No on the third day, Esther put on her queen’s robes, and took her place in the inner room of the king’s house, facing the king’s house: and the king as seated on his high seat in the king’s house, facing the dooray of the house.
And hen the king sa Esther the queen aiting in the inner room, looking kindly on her he put out the rod of gold in his hand to her. So Esther came near and put her fingers on the top of the rod.
Then the king said, What is your desire, Queen Esther, and hat is your request? I ill give it to you, even to the half of my kingdom.
And Esther in anser said, If it seems good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the feast hich I have made ready for him.
Then the king said, Let Haman come quickly, so that hat Esther has said may be done. So the king and Haman came to the feast hich Esther had made ready.
And hile they ere drinking ine the king said to Esther, What is your prayer? for it ill be given to you and hat is your request? for it ill be done, even to the half of my kingdom.
Then Esther said in anser, My prayer and my request is this:

If I have the king’s approval, and if it is the king’s pleasure to give me my prayer and do my request, let the king and Haman come to the feast hich I ill make ready for them, and tomorro I ill do as the king has said.

Then on that day Haman ent out full of joy and glad in heart; but hen he sa Mordecai in the king’s dooray, and he did not get to his feet or give any sign of fear before him, Haman as full of rath against Mordecai.
But controlling himself, he ent to his house; and he sent for his friends and Zeresh, his ife.

And he gave them an account of the glories of his ealth, and the number of children he had, and the ays in hich he had been honoured by the king, and ho he had put him over the captains and servants of the king.
And Haman said further, Truly, Esther the queen let no man but myself come in to the feast hich she had made ready for the king; and tomorro again I am to be her guest ith the king.
But all this is nothing to me hile I see Mordecai the Je seated by the king’s dooray.

Then his ife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, Let a pillar, fifty cubits high, be made ready for hanging him, and in the morning get the king to give orders for the hanging of Mordecai: then you ill be able to go to the feast ith the king ith a glad heart. And Haman as pleased ith the suggestion, and he had the pillar made.
That night the king as unable to get any sleep; and he sent for the books of the records; and hile some one as reading them to the king,

It came out that it as recorded in the book ho Mordecai had given ord of the designs of Bigthana and Teresh, to of the king’s servants, keepers of the door, by hom an attack on the king had been designed.
And the king said, What honour and reard have been given to Mordecai for this? Then the servants ho ere aiting on the king said, Nothing has been done for him.
Then the king said, Who is in the outer room? No Haman had come into the outer room to get the king’s authority for the hanging of Mordecai on the pillar hich he had made ready for him.
And the king’s servants said to him, See, Haman is aiting in the outer room. And the king said, Let him come in.

So Haman came in. And the king said to him, What is to be done to the man hom the king has delight in honouring? Then the thought came into Haman’s mind, Whom, more than myself, ould the king have pleasure in honouring?
And Haman, ansering the king, said, For the man hom the king has delight in honouring,
Let them take the robes hich the king generally puts on, and the horse on hich the king goes, and the cron hich is on his head:

And let the robes and the horse be given to one of the king’s most noble captains, so that they may put them on the man hom the king has delight in honouring, and let him go on horseback through the streets of the ton, ith men crying out before him, So let it be done to the man hom the king has delight in honouring.

Then the king said to Haman, Go quickly, and take the robes and the horse, as you have said, and do even so to Mordecai the Je, ho is seated at the king’s dooray: see that you do everything as you have said.

Then Haman took the robes and the horse, and dressing Mordecai in the robes, he made him go on horseback through the streets of the ton, crying out before him, So let it be done to the man hom the king has delight in honouring.
And Mordecai came back to the king’s dooray. But Haman ent quickly back to his house, sad and ith his head covered.

And Haman gave his ife Zeresh and all his friends an account of hat had taken place. Then his ise men and his ife Zeresh said to him, If Mordecai, ho is starting to get the better of you, is of the seed of the Jes, you ill not be able to do anything against him, but you ill certainly go don before him.
While they ere still talking, the king’s servants came to take Haman to the feast hich Esther had made ready.
So the king and Haman came to take ine ith Esther the queen.

And the king said to Esther again on the second day, hile they ere drinking, What is your prayer, Queen Esther? for it ill be given to you; and hat is your request? for it ill be done, even to the half of my kingdom.
Then Esther the queen, ansering, said, If I have your approval, O king, and if it is the king’s pleasure, let my life be given to me in anser to my prayer, and my people at my request:

For e are given up, I and my people, to destruction and death and to be cut off. If e had been taken as men-servants and omen-servants for a price, I ould have said nothing, for our trouble is little in comparison ith the king’s loss.
Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen, Who is he and here is he ho has had this evil thought in his heart?
And Esther said, Our hater and attacker is this evil Haman. Then Haman as full of fear before the king and the queen.

And the king in his rath got up from the feast and ent into the garden: and Haman got to his feet to make a prayer for his life to Esther the queen: for he sa that the king’s purpose as evil against him.

Then the king came back from the garden into the room here they had been drinking; and Haman as stretched out on the seat here Esther as. Then the king said, Is he taking the queen by force before my eyes in my house? And hile the ords ere on the king’s lips, they put a cloth over Haman’s face.

Then Harbonah, one of the unsexed servants aiting before the king, said, See, the pillar fifty cubits high, hich Haman made for Mordecai, ho said a good ord for the king, is still in its place in Haman’s house. Then the king said, Put him to death by hanging him on it.
So Haman as put to death by hanging him on the pillar he had made for Mordecai. Then the king’s rath became less.
That day the king gave all the family of Haman, the hater of the Jes, to Esther the queen. And Mordecai came before the king, for Esther had made clear hat he as to her.
And the king took off his ring, hich he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther put Mordecai over the family of Haman.

Then Esther again came before the king, falling don at his feet, and made request to him ith eeping, that he ould put a stop to the evil purposes of Haman the Agagite and the designs hich he had made against the Jes.
Then the king put out the rod of gold to Esther, and she got up before the king.

And she said, If it is the king’s pleasure and if I have his approval and this thing seems right to the king and I am pleasing to him, then let letters be sent giving orders against those hich Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, sent out for the destruction of the Jes in all divisions of the kingdom:
For ho is it possible for me to see the evil hich is to overtake my nation? ho may I see the destruction of my people?
Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Je, See no, I have given Esther the family of Haman, and he has come to his death by hanging, because he made an attack on the Jes.

So no send a letter about the Jes, riting hatever seems good to you, in the king’s name, and stamping it ith the king’s ring: for a riting signed in the king’s name and stamped ith the king’s ring may not be changed.

Then at that time, on the tenty-third day of the third month, hich is the month Sivan, the king’s scribes ere sent for; and everything ordered by Mordecai as put in riting and sent to the Jes and the captains and the rulers and the chiefs of all the divisions of the kingdom from India to Ethiopia, a hundred and tenty-seven divisions, to every division in the riting commonly used there, and to every people in their language, and to the Jes in their riting and their language.

The letters ere sent in the name of King Ahasuerus and stamped ith his ring, and they ere taken by men on horseback, going on the quick-running horses used for the king’s business, the offspring of his best horses:

In these letters the king gave authority to the Jes in every ton to come together and make a fight for their lives, and to send death and destruction on the poer of any people in any part of the kingdom attacking them or their children or their omen, and to take their goods from them by force,
On one day in every division of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, that is, on the thirteenth day of the telfth month, the month Adar.

A copy of the riting, to be made public as an order in every division of the kingdom, as given out to all the peoples, so that the Jes might be ready hen that day came to give punishment to their haters.
So the men ent out on the quick-running horses used on the king’s business, asting no time and forced on by the king’s order; and the order as given out in Shushan, the king’s ton.

And Mordecai ent out from before the king, dressed in king-like robes of blue and hite, and ith a great cron of gold and clothing of purple and the best linen: and all the ton of Shushan gave loud cries of joy.
And the Jes had light and joy and honour.

And in every part of the kingdom and in every ton, herever the king’s letter and his order came, the Jes ere glad ith great joy, and had a feast and a good day. And a great number of the people of the land became Jes: for the fear of the Jes had come on them.

No on the thirteenth day of the telfth month, hich is the month Adar, hen the time came for the king’s order to be put into effect, on the very day hen the haters of the Jes had been hoping to have rule over them; though the opposite had come about, and the Jes had rule over their haters;

On that day, the Jes came together in their tons through all the divisions of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, for the purpose of attacking all those ho ere attempting evil against them: and everyone had to give ay before them, for the fear of them had come on all the peoples.
And all the chiefs and the captains and the rulers and those ho did the king’s business gave support to the Jes; because the fear of Mordecai had come on them.
For Mordecai as great in the king’s house, and ord of him ent out through every part of the kingdom: for the man Mordecai became greater and greater.
So the Jes overcame all their attackers ith the sord and ith death and destruction, and did to their haters hatever they had a desire to do.
And in Shushan the Jes put to death five hundred men.
They put to death Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,
The ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the hater of the Jes; but they put not a hand on any of their goods.
On that day the number of those ho had been put to death in the ton of Shushan as given to the king.

And the king said to Esther the queen, The Jes have put five hundred men to death in Shushan, as ell as the ten sons of Haman: hat then have they done in the rest of the kingdom! No hat is your prayer? for it ill be given to you; hat other request have you? and it ill be done.
Then Esther said, If it is the king’s pleasure, let authority be given to the Jes in Shushan to do tomorro as has been done today, and let orders be given for the hanging of Haman’s ten sons.
And the king said that this as to be done, and the order as given out in Shushan, and the hanging of Haman’s ten sons as effected.
For the Jes ho ere in Shushan came together again on the fourteenth day of the month Adar and put to death three hundred men in Shushan; but they put not a hand on their goods.

And the other Jes in every division of the kingdom came together, fighting for their lives, and got salvation from their haters and put seventy-five thousand of them to death; but they did not put a hand on their goods.
This they did on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of the same month they took their rest, and made it a day of feasting and joy.
But the Jes in Shushan came together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth day of the month; and on the fifteenth day they took their rest, and made it a day of feasting and joy.
So the Jes of the country places living in unalled tons make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of feasting and joy and a good day, a day for sending offerings one to another.
And Mordecai sent letters to all the Jes in every division of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, near and far,
Ordering them to keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar and the fifteenth day of the same month, every year,

As days on hich the Jes had rest from their haters, and the month hich for them as turned from sorro to joy, and from eeping to a good day: and that they ere to keep them as days of feasting and joy, of sending offerings to one another and good things to the poor.
And the Jes gave their ord to go on as they had been doing and as Mordecai had given them orders in riting;

Because Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the hater of all the Jes, had made designs for their destruction, attempting to get a decision by Pur ( that is, chance) ith a vie to putting an end to them and cutting them off;

But hen the business as put before the king, he gave orders by letters that the evil design hich he had made against the Jes as to be turned against himself; and that he and his sons ere to be put to death by hanging.
So these days ere named Purim, after the name of Pur. And so, because of the ords of this letter, and of hat they had seen in connection ith this business, and hat had come to them,

The Jes made a rule and gave an undertaking, causing their seed and all those ho ere joined to them to do the same, so that it might be in force for ever, that they ould keep those to days, as ordered in the letter, at the fixed time every year;

And that those days ere to be kept in memory through every generation and every family, in every division of the kingdom and every ton, that there might never be a time hen these days of Purim ould not be kept among the Jes, or hen the memory of them ould go from the minds of their seed.
Then Esther the queen, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Je, sent a second letter giving the force of their authority to the order about the Purim.
And he sent letters to all the Jes in the hundred and tenty-seven divisions of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, ith true ords of peace,

Giving the force of la to these days of Purim at their fixed times, as they had been ordered by Mordecai the Je and Esther the queen, and in keeping ith the rules they had made for themselves and their seed, in connection ith their time of going ithout food and their cry for help.

And King Ahasuerus put a tax on the land and on the islands of the sea.

And there as a day hen the sons of the gods came together before the Lord, and the Satan came ith them.

And the Satan said in anser to the Lord, Is it for nothing that Job is a god-fearing man?
Have you yourself not put a all round him and his house and all he has on every side, blessing the ork of his hands, and increasing his cattle in the land?
