And the Lord said to the Satan, See, I give all he has into your hands, only do not put a finger on the man himself. And the Satan ent out from before the Lord.
And there as a day hen his sons and daughters ere feasting in the house of their oldest brother,
And a man came to Job, and said, The oxen ere ploughing, and the asses ere taking their food by their side:
And the men of Sheba came against them and took them aay, putting the young men to the sord, and I as the only one ho got aay safe to give you the nes.

And this one as still talking hen another came, and said, The fire of God came don from heaven, burning up the sheep and the goats and the young men completely, and I as the only one ho got aay safe to give you the nes.

And this one as still talking hen another came, and said, The Chaldaeans made themselves into three bands, and came don on the camels and took them aay, putting the young men to the sord, and I as the only one ho got aay safe to give you the nes.
And this one as still talking hen another came, and said, Your sons and your daughters ere feasting together in their oldest brother’s house,
When a great ind came rushing from the aste land against the four sides of the house, and it came don on the young men, and they are dead; and I as the only one ho got aay safe to give you the nes.
Then Job got up, and after parting his clothing and cutting off his hair, he ent don on his face to the earth, and gave orship, and said,
With nothing I came out of my mother’s body, and ith nothing I ill go back there; the Lord gave and the Lord has taken aay; let the Lord’s name be praised.
In all this Job did no sin, and did not say that God’s acts ere foolish.
And there as a day hen the sons of the gods came together before the Lord, and the Satan came ith them.
And the Lord said to the Satan, Where do you come from? And the Satan said in anser, From andering this ay and that on the earth, and alking about on it.

And the Lord said to the Satan, Have you taken note of my servant Job, for there is no one like him on the earth, a man ithout sin and upright, fearing God and keeping himself far from evil? and he still keeps his righteousness, though you have been moving me to send destruction on him ithout cause.
And the Satan said in anser to the Lord, Skin for skin, all a man has he ill give for his life.
But no, if you only put your hand on his bone and his flesh, he ill certainly be cursing you to your face.
And the Lord said to the Satan, See, he is in your hands, only do not take his life.
And the Satan ent out from before the Lord, and sent on Job an evil disease covering his skin from his feet to the top of his head.
And he took a broken bit of a pot, and, seated in the dust, as rubbing himself ith the sharp edge of it.
And his ife said to him, Are you still keeping your righteousness? Say a curse against God, and put an end to yourself.
And he said to her, You are talking like one of the foolish omen. If e take the good God sends us, are e not to take the evil hen it comes? In all this Job kept his lips from sin.

And Job’s three friends had ord of all this evil hich had come on him. And they came every one from his place, Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. So they came together to a meeting-place, in order that they might go and make clear to Job their grief for him, and give him comfort.

And lifting up their eyes hen they ere still far off, it did not seem that the man they sa as Job because of the change in him. And they gave ay to bitter eeping, ith signs of grief, and put dust on their heads.
And they took their seats on the earth by his side for seven days and seven nights: but no one said a ord to him, for they sa that his pain as very great.
Then, opening his mouth, and cursing the day of his birth,
Job made anser and said,
Let destruction take the day of my birth, and the night on hich it as said, A man child has come into the orld.
That day — let it be dark; let not God take note of it from on high, and let not the light be shining on it;
Let the dark and the black night take it for themselves; let it be covered ith a cloud; let the dark shades of day send fear on it.
That night — let the thick dark take it; let it not have joy among the days of the year; let it not come into the number of the months.
As for that night, let it have no fruit; let no voice of joy be sounded in it;
Let it be cursed by those ho put a curse on the day; ho are ready to make Leviathan aake.
Let its morning stars be dark; let it be looking for light, but may it not have any; let it not see the eyes of the dan.
Because it did not keep the doors of my mother’s body shut, so that trouble might be veiled from my eyes.
Why did death not take me hen I came out of my mother’s body, hy did I not, hen I came out, give up my last breath?
Why did the knees take me, or hy the breasts that they might give me milk?
For then I might have gone to my rest in quiet, and in sleep have been in peace,
With kings and the ise ones of the earth, ho put up great houses for themselves;
Or ith rulers ho had gold, and hose houses ere full of silver;
Or as a child dead at birth I might never have come into existence; like young children ho have not seen the light.
There the passions of the evil are over, and those hose strength has come to an end have rest.
There the prisoners are at peace together; the voice of the overseer comes not again to their ears.
The small and the great are there, and the servant is free from his master.
Why does he give light to him ho is in trouble, and life to the bitter in soul;
To those hose desire is for death, but it comes not; ho are searching for it more than for secret ealth;
Who are glad ith great joy, and full of delight hen they come to their last resting-place;
To a man hose ay is veiled, and ho is shut in by God?
In place of my food I have grief, and cries of sorro come from me like ater.
For I have a fear and it comes on me, and my heart is greatly troubled.
I have no peace, no quiet, and no rest; nothing but pain comes on me.
And Eliphaz the Temanite made anser and said,
If one says a ord, ill it be a eariness to you? but ho is able to keep from saying hat is in his mind?
Truly, you have been a helper to others, and you have made feeble hands strong;
He ho as near to falling has been lifted up by your ords, and you have given strength to bent knees.
But no it has come on you and it is a eariness to you; you are touched by it and your mind is troubled.
Is not your fear of God your support, and your upright ay of life your hope?
Have you ever seen destruction come to an upright man? or hen ere the god-fearing ever cut off?
What I have seen is that those by hom trouble has been ploughed, and evil planted, get the same for themselves.
By the breath of God destruction takes them, and by the ind of his rath they are cut off.
Though the noise of the lion and the sounding of his voice, may be loud, the teeth of the young lions are broken.
The old lion comes to his end for need of food, and the young of the she-lion go andering in all directions.
A ord as given to me secretly, and the lo sound of it came to my ears.
In troubled thoughts from visions of the night, hen deep sleep comes on men,
Fear came on me and shaking, and my bones ere full of trouble;
And a breath as moving over my face; the hair of my flesh became stiff:
Something as present before me, but I as not able to see it clearly; there as a form before my eyes: a quiet voice came to my ears, saying:
May a man be upright before God? or a man be clean before his Maker?
Truly, he puts no faith in his servants, and he sees error in his angels;
Ho much more those living in houses of earth, hose bases are in the dust! They are crushed more quickly than an insect;
Beteen morning and evening they are completely broken; they come to an end for ever, and no one takes note.
If their tent-cord is pulled up, do they not come to an end, and ithout isdom?
Give no a cry for help; is there anyone ho ill give you an anser? and to hich of the holy ones ill you make your prayer?
For rath is the cause of death to the foolish, and he ho has no isdom comes to his end through passion.
I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly the curse came on his house.
No his children have no safe place, and they are crushed before the judges, for no one takes up their cause.
Their produce is taken by him ho has no food, and their grain goes to the poor, and he ho is in need of ater gets it from their spring.
For evil does not come out of the dust, or trouble out of the earth;
But trouble is man’s fate from birth, as the flames go up from the fire.
But as for me, I ould make my prayer to God, and I ould put my cause before him:
Who does great things outside our knoledge, onders ithout number:
Who gives rain on the earth, and sends ater on the fields:
Lifting up those ho are lo, and putting the sad in a safe place;
Who makes the designs of the ise go rong, so that they are unable to give effect to their purposes.
He takes the ise in their secret designs, and the purposes of the tisted are cut off suddenly.
In the daytime it becomes dark for them, and in the sunlight they go feeling about as if it as night.
But he keeps safe from their sord those ho have no father, and the poor from the poer of the strong.
So the poor man has hope, and the mouth of the evil-doer is stopped.
Truly, that man is happy ho has training from the hand of God: so do not let your heart be shut to the teaching of the Ruler of all.
For after his punishment he gives comfort, and after ounding, his hands make you ell.
He ill keep you safe from six troubles, and in seven no evil ill come near you.
When there is need of food he ill keep you from death, and in ar from the poer of the sord.
He ill keep you safe from the evil tongue; and you ill have no fear of asting hen it comes.
You ill make sport of destruction and need, and ill have no fear of the beasts of the earth.
For you ill be in agreement ith the stones of the earth, and the beasts of the field ill be at peace ith you.
And you ill be certain that your tent is at peace, and after looking over your property you ill see that nothing is gone.
You ill be certain that your seed ill be great, and your offspring like the plants of the earth.
You ill come to your last resting-place in full strength, as the grain is taken up to the crushing-floor in its time.
See, e have made search ith care, and it is so; it has come to our ears; see that you take note of it for yourself.
And Job made anser and said,
If only my passion might be measured, and put into the scales against my trouble!
For then its eight ould be more than the sand of the seas: because of this my ords have been uncontrolled.
For the arros of the Ruler of all are present ith me, and their poison goes deep into my spirit: his army of fears is put in order against me.
Does the ass of the fields give out his voice hen he has grass? or does the ox make sounds over his food?
Will a man take food hich has no taste ithout salt? or is there any taste in the soft substance of purslain?
My soul has no desire for such things, they are as disease in my food.
If only I might have an anser to my prayer, and God ould give me my desire!
If only he ould be pleased to put an end to me; and ould let loose his hand, so that I might be cut off!
So I ould still have comfort, and I ould have joy in the pains of death, for I have not been false to the ords of the Holy One.
Have I strength to go on aiting, or have I any end to be looking forard to?
Is my strength the strength of stones, or is my flesh brass?
I have no help in myself, and isdom is completely gone from me.
He hose heart is shut against his friend has given up the fear of the Ruler of all.
My friends have been false like a stream, like streams in the valleys hich come to an end:
Which are dark because of the ice, and the sno falling into them;
Under the burning sun they are cut off, and come to nothing because of the heat.
The camel-trains go out of their ay; they go up into the aste and come to destruction.
The camel-trains of Tema ere searching ith care, the bands of Sheba ere aiting for them:
They ere put to shame because of their hope; they came and their hope as gone.
So have you no become to me; you see my sad condition and are in fear.
Did I say, Give me something? or, Make a payment for me out of your ealth?
Or, Get me out of the poer of my hater? or, Give money so that I may be free from the poer of the cruel ones?
Give me teaching and I ill be quiet; and make me see my error.
Ho pleasing are upright ords! but hat force is there in your arguments?
My ords may seem rong to you, but the ords of him ho has no hope are for the ind.
Truly, you are such as ould give up the child of a dead man to his creditors, and ould make a profit out of your friend.
No then, let your eyes be turned to me, for truly I ill not say hat is false to your face.
Let your minds be changed, and do not have an evil opinion of me; yes, be changed, for my righteousness is still in me.
Is there evil in my tongue? is not the cause of my trouble clear to me?
Has not man his ordered time of trouble on the earth? and are not his days like the days of a servant orking for payment?
As a servant desiring the shades of evening, and a orkman looking for his payment:
So I have for my heritage months of pain to no purpose, and nights of eariness are given to me.
When I go to my bed, I say, When ill it be time to get up? but the night is long, and I am turning from side to side till morning light.
My flesh is covered ith orms and dust; my skin gets hard and then is cracked again.
My days go quicker than the cloth-orker’s thread, and come to an end ithout hope.
O, keep in mind that my life is ind: my eye ill never again see good.
The eye of him ho sees me ill see me no longer: your eyes ill be looking for me, but I ill be gone.
A cloud comes to an end and is gone; so he ho goes don into the underorld comes not up again.
He ill not come back to his house, and his place ill have no more knoledge of him.
So I ill not keep my mouth shut; I ill let the ords come from it in the pain of my spirit, my soul ill make a bitter outcry.
Am I a sea, or a sea-beast, that you put a atch over me?
When I say, In my bed I ill have comfort, there I ill get rest from my disease;
Then you send dreams to me, and visions of fear;
So that a hard death seems better to my soul than my pains.
I have no desire for life, I ould not be living for ever! Keep aay from me, for my days are as a breath.
What is man, that you have made him great, and that your attention is fixed on him,
And that your hand is on him every morning, and that you are testing him every minute?
Ho long ill it be before your eyes are turned aay from me, so that I may have a minute’s breathing-space?
If I have done rong, hat have I done to you, O keeper of men? hy have you made me a mark for your blos, so that I am a eariness to myself?
And hy do you not take aay my sin, and let my rongdoing be ended? for no I go don to the dust, and you ill be searching for me ith care, but I ill be gone.
Then Bildad the Shuhite made anser and said,
Ho long ill you say these things, and ho long ill the ords of your mouth be like a strong ind?
Does God give rong decisions? or is the Ruler of all not upright in his judging?
If your children have done evil against him, then their punishment is from his hand.
If you ill make search for God ith care, and put your request before the Ruler of all;
If you are clean and upright; then he ill certainly be moved to take up your cause, and ill make clear your righteousness by building up your house again.
And though your start as small, your end ill be very great.
Put the question no to the past generations, and give attention to hat has been searched out by their fathers:
( For e are but of yesterday, and have no knoledge, because our days on earth are gone like a shade:)
Will they not give you teaching, and say ords of isdom to you?
Will the river-plant come up in its pride ithout et earth? ill the grass get tall ithout ater?
When it is still green, ithout being cut don, it becomes dry and dead before any other plant.
So is the end of all ho do not keep God in mind; and the hope of the evil-doer comes to nothing:
Whose support is cut off, and hose hope is no stronger than a spider’s thread.
He is looking to his family for support, but it is not there; he puts his hope in it, but it comes to nothing.
He is full of strength before the sun, and his branches go out over his garden.
His roots are tisted round the stones, forcing their ay in beteen them.
If he is taken aay from his place, then it ill say, I have not seen you.
Such is the joy of his ay, and out of the dust another comes up to take his place.
Truly, God ill not give up him ho is ithout sin, and ill not take evil-doers by the hand.
The time ill come hen your mouth ill be full of laughing, and cries of joy ill come from your lips.
Your haters ill be clothed ith shame, and the tent of the sinner ill not be seen again.
And Job made anser and said,
Truly, I see that it is so: and ho is it possible for a man to get his right before God?
If a man as desiring to go to la ith him, he ould not be able to give him an anser to one out of a thousand questions.
He is ise in heart and great in strength: ho ever made his face hard against him, and any good came of it?
It is he ho takes aay the mountains ithout their knoledge, overturning them in his rath:
Who is moving the earth out of its place, so that its pillars are shaking:
Who gives orders to the sun, and it does not give its light; and ho keeps the stars from shining.
By hose hand the heavens ere stretched out, and ho is alking on the aves of the sea:
Who made the Bear and Orion, and the Pleiades, and the store-houses of the south:
Who does great things not to be searched out; yes, onders ithout number.
See, he goes past me and I see him not: he goes on before, but I have no knoledge of him.
If he puts out his hand to take, by hom may it be turned back? ho may say to him, What are you doing?
God’s rath may not be turned back; the helpers of Rahab ere bent don under him.
Ho much less may I give an anser to him, using the right ords in argument ith him?
Even if my cause as good, I ould not be able to give an anser; I ould make request for grace from him ho as against me.
If I had sent for him to be present, and he had come, I ould have no faith that he ould give ear to my voice.
For I ould be crushed by his storm, my ounds ould be increased ithout cause.
He ould not let me take my breath, but I ould be full of bitter grief.
If it is a question of strength, he says, Here I am! and if it is a question of a cause at la, he says, Who ill give me a fixed day?
Though I as in the right, he ould say that I as in the rong; I have done no evil; but he says that I am a sinner.
I have done no rong; I give no thought to hat becomes of me; I have no desire for life.
It is all the same to me; so I say, He puts an end to the sinner and to him ho has done no rong together.
If death comes suddenly through disease, he makes sport of the fate of those ho have done no rong.
The land is given into the poer of the evil-doer; the faces of its judges are covered; if not by him, then ho has done it?
My days go quicker than a post-runner: they go in flight, they see no good.
They go rushing on like reed-boats, like an eagle dropping suddenly on its food.
If I say, I ill put my grief out of mind, I ill let my face be sad no longer and I ill be bright;
I go in fear of all my pains; I am certain that I ill not be free from sin in your eyes.
You ill not let me be clear of sin! hy then do I take trouble for nothing?
If I am ashed ith sno ater, and make my hands clean ith soap;
Then you ill have me pushed into the dust, so that I ill seem disgusting to my very clothing.
For he is not a man as I am, that I might give him an anser, that e might come together before a judge.
There is no one to give a decision beteen us, ho might have control over us.
Let him take aay his rod from me and not send his fear on me:
Then I ould say hat is in my mind ithout fear of him; for there is no cause of fear in myself.
My soul is tired of life; I ill let my sad thoughts go free in ords; my soul ill make a bitter outcry.
I ill say to God, Do not put me don as a sinner; make clear to me hat you have against me.
What profit is it to you to be cruel, to give up the ork of your hands, looking kindly on the design of evil-doers?
Have you eyes of flesh, or do you see as man sees?
Are your days as the days of man, or your years like his,
That you take note of my sin, searching after my rongdoing,
Though you see that I am not an evil-doer; and there is no one ho is able to take a man out of your hands?
Your hands made me, and I as formed by you, but then, changing your purpose, you gave me up to destruction.
O keep in mind that you made me out of earth; and ill you send me back again to dust?
Was I not drained out like milk, becoming hard like cheese?
By you I as clothed ith skin and flesh, and joined together ith bones and muscles.
You have been kind to me, and your grace has been ith me, and your care has kept my spirit safe.
But you kept these things in the secret of your heart; I am certain this as in your thoughts:
That, if I did rong, you ould take note of it, and ould not make me clear from sin:
That, if I as an evil-doer, the curse ould come on me; and if I as upright, my head ould not be lifted up, being full of shame and overcome ith trouble.
And that if there as cause for pride, you ould go after me like a lion; and again put out your onders against me:
That you ould send ne itnesses against me, increasing your rath against me, and letting loose ne armies on me.
Why then did you make me come out of my mother’s body? It ould have been better for me to have taken my last breath, and for no eye to have seen me,
And for me to have been as if I had not been; to have been taken from my mother’s body straight to my last resting-place.
Are not the days of my life small in number? Let your eyes be turned aay from me, so that I may have a little pleasure,
Before I go to the place from hich I ill not come back, to the land here all is dark and black,
A land of thick dark, ithout order, here the very light is dark.
Then Zophar the Naamathite made anser and said,
Are all these ords to go unansered? and is a man seen to be right because he is full of talk?
Are your ords of pride to make men keep quiet? and are you to make sport, ith no one to put you to shame?
You may say, My ay is clean, and I am free from sin in your eyes.
But if only God ould take up the ord, opening his lips in argument ith you;
And ould make clear to you the secrets of isdom, and the onders of his purpose!
Are you able to take God’s measure, to make discovery of the limits of the Ruler of all?
They are higher than heaven; hat is there for you to do? deeper than the underorld, and outside your knoledge;
Longer in measure than the earth, and ider than the sea.
If he goes on his ay, shutting a man up and putting him to death, ho may make him go back from his purpose?
For in his eyes men are as nothing; he sees evil and takes note of it.
And so a hollo-minded man ill get isdom, hen a young ass of the field gets teaching.
But if you put your heart right, stretching out your hands to him;
If you put far aay the evil of your hands, and let no rongdoing have a place in your tent;
Then truly your face ill be lifted up, ith no mark of sin, and you ill be fixed in your place ithout fear:
For your sorro ill go from your memory, like aters floing aay:
And your life ill be brighter than day; though it is dark, it ill become like the morning.
And you ill be safe because there is hope; after looking round, you ill take your rest in quiet;
Sleeping ith no fear of danger; and men ill be desiring to have grace in your eyes;
But the eyes of the evil-doers ill be asting aay; their ay of flight is gone, and their only hope is the taking of their last breath.
And Job made anser and said,
No doubt you have knoledge, and isdom ill come to an end ith you.
But I have a mind as ell as you; I am equal to you: yes, ho has not knoledge of such things as these?

In the thought of him ho is in comfort there is no respect for one ho is in trouble; such is the fate of those hose feet are slipping.

Who does not see by all these that the hand of the Lord has done this?

Are not ords tested by the ear, even as food is tasted by the mouth?
Old men have isdom, and a long life gives knoledge.
With him there is isdom and strength; poer and knoledge are his.
Truly, there is no building up of hat is pulled don by him; hen a man is shut up by him, no one may let him loose.
Truly, he keeps back the aters and they are dry; he sends them out and the earth is overturned.
With him are strength and ise designs; he ho is guided into error, together ith his guide, are in his hands;
He takes aay the isdom of the ise guides, and makes judges foolish;

He puts shame on chiefs, and takes aay the poer of the strong;

He takes aay the isdom of the rulers of the earth, and sends them andering in a aste here there is no ay.
They go feeling about in the dark ithout light, andering ithout help like those overcome ith ine.
Truly, my eye has seen all this, ord of it has come to my ear, and I have knoledge of it.
The same things are in my mind as in yours; I am equal to you.
But I ould have talk ith the Ruler of all, and my desire is to have an argument ith God.
But you put a false face on things; all your attempts to put things right are of no value.
If only you ould keep quiet, it ould be a sign of isdom!
Give ear to the argument of my mouth, and take note of the ords of my lips.
Will you say in God’s name hat is not right, and put false ords into his mouth?
Will you have respect for God’s person in this cause, and put yourselves forard as his supporters?
Will it be good for you to be searched out by him, or have you the thought that he may be guided into error like a man?
He ill certainly put you right, if you have respect for persons in secret.
Will not his glory put you in fear, so that your hearts ill be overcome before him?
Your ise sayings are only dust, and your strong places are only earth.
Keep quiet, and let me say hat is in my mind, hatever may come to me.
I ill take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand.
Truly, he ill put an end to me; I have no hope; but I ill not give ay in argument before him;
And that ill be my salvation, for an evil-doer ould not come before him,
Give ear ith care to my ords, and keep hat I say in your minds.
See no, I have put my cause in order, and I am certain that I ill be seen to be right.
Is any one able to take up the argument against me? If so, I ould keep quiet and give up my breath.
Only to things do not do to me, then I ill come before your face:
Take your hand far aay from me; and let me not be overcome by fear of you.
Then at the sound of your voice I ill give anser; or let me put forard my cause for you to give me an anser.
What is the number of my evil-doings and my sins? give me knoledge of them.
Why is your face veiled from me, as if I as numbered among your haters?
Will you be hard on a leaf in flight before the ind? ill you make a dry stem go more quickly on its ay?
For you put bitter things on record against me, and send punishment on me for the sins of my early years;
And you put chains on my feet, atching all my ays, and making a limit for my steps;
Though a man comes to nothing like a bit of dead ood, or like a robe hich has become food for the orm.
As for man, the son of oman, his days are short and full of trouble.
He comes out like a floer, and is cut don: he goes in flight like a shade, and is never seen again.
Is it on such a one as this that your eyes are fixed, ith the purpose of judging him?
If only a clean thing might come out of an unclean! But it is not possible.
If his days are ordered, and you have knoledge of the number of his months, having given him a fixed limit past hich he may not go;
Let your eyes be turned aay from him, and take your hand from him, so that he may have pleasure at the end of his day, like a servant orking for payment.
For there is hope of a tree; if it is cut don, it ill come to life again, and its branches ill not come to an end.
Though its root may be old in the earth, and its cut-off end may be dead in the dust;
Still, at the smell of ater, it ill make buds, and put out branches like a young plant.
But man comes to his death and is gone: he gives up his spirit, and here is he?
The aters go from a pool, and a river becomes aste and dry;
So man goes don to his last resting-place and comes not again: till the heavens come to an end, they ill not be aake or come out of their sleep.
If only you ould keep me safe in the underorld, putting me in a secret place till your rath is past, giving me a fixed time hen I might come to your memory again!
If death takes a man, ill he come to life again? All the days of my trouble I ould be aiting, till the time came for me to be free.
At the sound of your voice I ould give an anser, and you ould have a desire for the ork of your hands.
For no my steps are numbered by you, and my sin is not overlooked.
My rongdoing is corded up in a bag, and my sin is shut up safe.
But truly a mountain falling comes to dust, and a rock is moved from its place;
The stones are crushed small by the force of the aters; the dust of the earth is ashed aay by their overfloing: and so you put an end to the hope of man.
You overcome him for ever, and he is gone; his face is changed in death, and you send him aay.
His sons come to honour, and he has no knoledge of it; they are made lo, but he is not conscious of it.
Only his flesh still has pain, and his soul is sad.
And Eliphaz the Temanite made anser and said,
Will a ise man make anser ith knoledge of no value, or ill he give birth to the east ind?
Will he make arguments ith ords in hich is no profit, and ith sayings hich have no value?
Truly, you make the fear of God ithout effect, so that the time of quiet orship before God is made less by your outcry.
For your mouth is guided by your sin, and you have taken the tongue of the false for yourself.
It is by your mouth, even yours, that you are judged to be in the rong, and not by me; and your lips give itness against you.
Were you the first man to come into the orld? or did you come into being before the hills?
Were you present at the secret meeting of God? and have you taken all isdom for yourself?
What knoledge have you hich e have not? is there anything in your mind hich is not in ours?
With us are men ho are grey-haired and full of years, much older than your father.
Are the comforts of God not enough for you, and the gentle ord hich as said to you?
Why is your heart uncontrolled, and hy are your eyes lifted up;
So that you are turning your spirit against God, and letting such ords go out of your mouth?
What is man, that he may be clean? and ho may the son of oman be upright?
Truly, he puts no faith in his holy ones, and the heavens are not clean in his eyes;
Ho much less one ho is disgusting and unclean, a man ho takes in evil like ater!
Take note and give ear to my ords; and I ill say hat I have seen:
( The things hich ise men have got from their fathers, and have not kept secret from us;
For only to them as the land given, and no strange people ere among them:)
The evil man is in pain all his days, and the number of the years stored up for the cruel is small.
A sound of fear is in his ears; in time of peace destruction ill come on him:
He has no hope of coming safe out of the dark, and his fate ill be the sord;
He is andering about in search of bread, saying, Where is it? and he is certain that the day of trouble is ready for him:
He is greatly in fear of the dark day, trouble and pain overcome him:
Because his hand is stretched out against God, and his heart is lifted up against the Ruler of all,
Running against him like a man of ar, covered by his thick breastplate; even like a king ready for the fight,
Because his face is covered ith fat, and his body has become thick;
And he has made his resting-place in the tons hich have been pulled don, in houses here no man had a right to be, hose fate as to become masses of broken alls.
He does not get ealth for himself, and is unable to keep hat he has got; the heads of his grain are not bent don to the earth.
He does not come out of the dark; his branches are burned by the flame, and the ind takes aay his bud.
Let him not put his hope in hat is false, falling into error: for he ill get deceit as his reard.
His branch is cut off before its time, and his leaf is no longer green.
He is like a vine hose grapes do not come to full groth, or an olive-tree dropping its floers.
For the band of the evil-doers gives no fruit, and the tents of those ho give rong decisions for reard are burned ith fire.
Evil has made them ith child, and they give birth to trouble; and the fruit of their body is shame for themselves.
And Job made anser and said,
Such things have frequently come to my ears: you are comforters ho only give trouble.
May ords hich are like the ind be stopped? or hat is troubling you to make anser to them?
It ould not be hard for me to say such things if your souls ere in my soul’s place; joining ords together against you, and shaking my head at you:
I might give you strength ith my mouth, and not keep back the comfort of my lips.
If I say hat is in my mind, my pain becomes no less: and if I keep quiet, ho much of it goes from me?
But no he has overcome me ith eariness and fear, and I am in the grip of all my trouble.
It has come up as a itness against me, and the asting of my flesh makes anser to my face.
I am broken by his rath, and his hate has gone after me; he has made his teeth sharp against me: my haters are looking on me ith cruel eyes;
Their mouths are open ide against me; the blos of his bitter ords are falling on my face; all of them come together in a mass against me.
God gives me over to the poer of sinners, sending me violently into the hands of evil-doers.
I as in comfort, but I have been broken up by his hands; he has taken me by the neck, shaking me to bits; he has put me up as a mark for his arros.
His bomen come round about me; their arros go through my body ithout mercy; my life is drained out on the earth.
I am broken ith ound after ound; he comes rushing on me like a man of ar.
I have made haircloth the clothing of my skin, and my horn is rolled in the dust.
My face is red ith eeping, and my eyes are becoming dark;
Though my hands have done no violent acts, and my prayer is clean.
O earth, let not my blood be covered, and let my cry have no resting-place!
Even no my itness is in heaven, and the supporter of my cause is on high.
My friends make sport of me; to God my eyes are eeping,
So that he may give decision for a man in his cause ith God, and beteen a son of man and his neighbour.
For in a short time I ill take the journey from hich I ill not come back.
My spirit is broken, my days are ended, the last resting-place is ready for me.
Truly, those ho make sport of me are round about me, and my eyes become dark because of their bitter laughing.
Be pleased, no, to be responsible for me to yourself; for there is no other ho ill put his hand in mine.
You have kept their hearts from isdom: for this cause you ill not give them honour.
As for him ho is false to his friend for a reard, light ill be cut off from the eyes of his children.
He has made me a ord of shame to the peoples; I have become a mark for their sport.
My eyes have become dark because of my pain, and all my body is asted to a shade.
The upright are surprised at this, and he ho has done no rong is troubled because of the evil-doers.
Still the upright keeps on his ay, and he ho has clean hands gets ne strength.
But come back, no, all of you, come; and I ill not see a ise man among you.
My days are past, my purposes are broken off, even the desires of my heart.
They are changing night into day; they say, The light is near the dark.
If I am aiting for the underorld as my house, if I have made my bed in the dark;
If I say to the earth, You are my father; and to the orm, My mother and my sister;
Where then is my hope? and ho ill see my desire?
Will they go don ith me into the underorld? Will e go don together into the dust?
Then Bildad the Shuhite made anser and said,
Ho long ill it be before you have done talking? Get isdom, and then e ill say hat is in our minds.
Why do e seem as beasts in your eyes, and as completely ithout knoledge?
But come back, no, come: you ho are ounding yourself in your passion, ill the earth be given up because of you, or a rock be moved out of its place?
For the light of the sinner is put out, and the flame of his fire is not shining.
The light is dark in his tent, and the light shining over him is put out.
The steps of his strength become short, and by his design destruction overtakes him.
His feet take him into the net, and he goes alking into the cords.
His foot is taken in the net; he comes into its grip.
The tisted cord is put secretly in the earth to take him, and the cord is placed in his ay.
He is overcome by fears on every side, they go after him at every step.
His strength is made feeble for need of food, and destruction is aiting for his falling footstep.
His skin is asted by disease, and his body is food for the orst of diseases.
He is pulled out of his tent here he as safe, and he is taken aay to the king of fears.
In his tent ill be seen that hich is not his, burning stone is dropped on his house.
Under the earth his roots are dry, and over it his branch is cut off.
His memory is gone from the earth, and in the open country there is no knoledge of his name.
He is sent aay from the light into the dark; he is forced out of the orld.
He has no offspring or family among his people, and in his living-place there is no one of his name.
At his fate those of the est are shocked, and those of the east are overcome ith fear.
Truly, these are the houses of the sinner, and this is the place of him ho has no knoledge of God.
And Job made anser and said,
Ho long ill you make my life bitter, crushing me ith ords?
Ten times no you have made sport of me; it gives you no sense of shame to do me rong.
And, truly, if I have been in error, the effect of my error is only on myself.
If you make yourselves great against me, using my punishment as an argument against me,
Be certain that it is God ho has done me rong, and has taken me in his net.
Truly, I make an outcry against the violent man, but there is no anser: I give a cry for help, but no one takes up my cause.
My ay is alled up by him so that I may not go by: he has made my roads dark.
He has put off my glory from me, and taken the cron from my head.
I am broken don by him on every side, and I am gone; my hope is uprooted like a tree.
His rath is burning against me, and I am to him as one of his haters.
His armies come on together, they make their road high against me, and put up their tents round mine.
He has taken my brothers far aay from me; they have seen my fate and have become strange to me.
My relations and my near friends have given me up, and those living in my house have put me out of their minds.
I am strange to my omen-servants, and seem to them as one from another country.
At my cry my servant gives me no anser, and I have to make a prayer to him.
My breath is strange to my ife, and I am disgusting to the offspring of my mother’s body.
Even young children have no respect for me; hen I get up their backs are turned on me.
All the men of my circle keep aay from me; and those dear to me are turned against me.
My bones are joined to my skin, and I have got aay ith my flesh in my teeth.
Have pity on me, have pity on me, O my friends! for the hand of God is on me.
Why are you cruel to me, like God, for ever saying evil against me?
If only my ords might be recorded! if they might be put in riting in a book!
And ith an iron pen and lead be cut into the rock for ever!
But I am certain that he ho ill take up my cause is living, and that in time to come he ill take his place on the dust;
And ... ithout my flesh I ill see God;
Whom I ill see on my side, and not as one strange to me. My heart is broken ith desire.
If you say, Ho cruel e ill be to him! because the root of sin is clearly in him:
Be in fear of the sord, for the sord is the punishment for such things, so that you may be certain that there is a judge.
Then Zophar the Naamathite made anser and said,
For this cause my thoughts are troubling me and driving me on.
I have to give ear to arguments hich put me to shame, and your ansers to me are ind ithout isdom.
Have you knoledge of this from early times, hen man as placed on the earth,
That the pride of the sinner is short, and the joy of the evil-doer but for a minute?
Though he is lifted up to the heavens, and his head goes up to the clouds;
Like the aste from his body he comes to an end for ever: those ho have seen him say, Where is he?
He is gone like a dream, and is not seen again; he goes in flight like a vision of the night.
The eye hich sa him sees him no longer; and his place has no more knoledge of him.
His children are hoping that the poor ill be kind to them, and his hands give back his ealth.
His bones are full of young strength, but it ill go don ith him into the dust.
Though evil-doing is seet in his mouth, and he keeps it secretly under his tongue;
Though he takes care of it, and does not let it go, but keeps it still in his mouth;
His food becomes bitter in his stomach; the poison of snakes is inside him.
He takes don ealth as food, and sends it up again; it is forced out of his stomach by God.
He takes the poison of snakes into his mouth, the tongue of the snake is the cause of his death.
Let him not see the rivers of oil, the streams of honey and milk.
He is forced to give back the fruit of his ork, and may not take it for food; he has no joy in the profit of his trading.
Because he has been cruel to the poor, turning aay from them in their trouble; because he has taken a house by force hich he did not put up;
There is no peace for him in his ealth, and no salvation for him in those things in hich he took delight.
He had never enough for his desire; for this cause his ell-being ill quickly come to an end.
Even hen his ealth is great, he is full of care, for the hand of everyone ho is in trouble is turned against him.
God gives him his desire, and sends the heat of his rath on him, making it come don on him like rain.
He may go in flight from the iron spear, but the arro from the bo of brass ill go through him;
He is pulling it out, and it comes out of his back; and its shining point comes out of his side; he is overcome by fears.
All his ealth is stored up for the dark: a fire not made by man sends destruction on him, and on everything in his tent.
The heavens make clear his sin, and the earth gives itness against him.
The produce of his house is taken aay into another country, like things given into the hands of others in the day of rath.
This is the reard of the evil man, and the heritage given to him by God.
Then Job made anser and said,
Give attention ith care to my ords; and let this be your comfort.
Let me say hat is in my mind, and after that, go on making sport of me.
As for me, is my outcry against man? is it then to be ondered at if my spirit is troubled?
Take note of me and be full of onder, put your hand on your mouth.
At the very thought of it my flesh is shaking ith fear.
Why is life given to the evil-doers? hy do they become old and strong in poer?
Their children are ever ith them, and their offspring before their eyes.
Their houses are free from fear, and the rod of God does not come on them.
Their ox is ready at all times to give seed; their co gives birth, ithout dropping her young.
They send out their young ones like a flock, and their children have pleasure in the dance,
They make songs to the instruments of music, and are glad at the sound of the pipe.
Their days come to an end ithout trouble, and suddenly they go don to the underorld.
Though they said to God, Go aay from us, for e have no desire for the knoledge of your ays.
What is the Ruler of all, that e may give him orship? and hat profit is it to us to make prayer to him?
Truly, is not their ell-being in their poer? ( The purpose of the evil-doers is far from me.)
Ho frequently is the light of the evil-doers put out, or does trouble come on them? ho frequently does his rath take them ith cords?
Ho frequently are they as dry stems before the ind, or as grass taken aay by the storm-ind?
You say, God keeps punishment stored up for his children. Let him send it on the man himself, so that he may have the punishment of it!
Let his eyes see his trouble, and let him be full of the rath of the Ruler of all!
For hat interest has he in his house after him, hen the number of his months is ended?
Is anyone able to give teaching to God? for he is the judge of those ho are on high.
One comes to his end in complete ell-being, full of peace and quiet:
His buckets are full of milk, and there is no loss of strength in his bones.
And another comes to his end ith a bitter soul, ithout ever tasting good.
Together they go don to the dust, and are covered by the orm.
See, I am conscious of your thoughts, and of your violent purposes against me;
For you say, Where is the house of the ruler, and here is the tent of the evil-doer?
Have you not put the question to the travellers, and do you not take note of their experience?
Ho the evil man goes free in the day of trouble, and has salvation in the day of rath?
Who ill make his ay clear to his face? and if he has done a thing, ho gives him punishment for it?
He is taken to his last resting-place, and keeps atch over it.
The earth of the valley covering his bones is seet to him, and all men come after him, as there ere unnumbered before him.
Why then do you give me comfort ith ords in hich there is no profit, hen you see that there is nothing in your ansers but deceit?
Then Eliphaz the Temanite made anser and said,
Is it possible for a man to be of profit to God? No, for a man’s isdom is only of profit to himself.
Is it of any interest to the Ruler of all that you are upright? or is it of use to him that your ays are ithout sin?
Is it because you give him honour that he is sending punishment on you and is judging you?
Is not your evil-doing great? and there is no end to your sins.
For you have taken your brother’s goods hen he as not in your debt, and have taken aay the clothing of those ho have need of it.
You do not give ater to the tired traveller, and from him ho has no food you keep back bread.
For it as the man ith poer ho had the land, and the man ith an honoured name ho as living in it.
You have sent idos aay ithout hearing their cause, and you have taken aay the support of the child ho has no father.
For this cause nets are round your feet, and you are overcome ith sudden fear.
Your light is made dark so that you are unable to see, and you are covered by a mass of aters.
Is not God as high as heaven? and see the stars, ho high they are!
And you say, What knoledge has God? is he able to give decisions through the deep dark?
Thick clouds are covering him, so that he is unable to see; and he is alking on the arch of heaven.
Will you keep the old ay by hich evil men ent?
Who ere violently taken aay before their time, ho ere overcome by the rush of aters:
Who said to God, Go aay from us; and, What is the Ruler of all able to do to us?
Though he made their houses full of good things: but the purpose of the evil-doers is far from me!
The upright sa it and ere glad: and those ho had done no rong made sport of them,
Saying, Truly, their substance is cut off, and their ealth is food for the fire.
Put yourself no in a right relation ith him and be at peace: so ill you do ell in your undertakings.
Be pleased to take teaching from his mouth, and let his ords be stored up in your heart.
If you come back to the Ruler of all, making yourself lo before him; if you put evil far aay from your tents;
And put your gold in the dust, even your gold of Ophir among the rocks of the valleys;
Then the Ruler of all ill be your gold, and his teaching ill be your silver;
For then you ill have delight in the Ruler of all, and your face ill be lifted up to God.
You ill make your prayer to him, and be ansered; and you ill give effect to your oaths.
Your purposes ill come about, and light ill be shining on your ays.
For God makes lo those hose hearts are lifted up, but he is a saviour to the poor in spirit.
He makes safe the man ho is free from sin, and if your hands are clean, salvation ill be yours.
And Job made anser and said,
Even today my outcry is bitter; his hand is hard on my sorro.
If only I had knoledge of here he might be seen, so that I might come even to his seat!
I ould put my cause in order before him, and my mouth ould be full of arguments.
I ould see hat his ansers ould be, and have knoledge of hat he ould say to me.
Would he make use of his great poer to overcome me? No, but he ould give attention to me.
There an upright man might put his cause before him; and I ould be free for ever from my judge.
See, I go forard, but he is not there; and back, but I do not see him;
I am looking for him on the left hand, but there is no sign of him; and turning to the right, I am not able to see him.
For he has knoledge of the ay I take; after I have been tested I ill come out like gold.
My feet have gone in his steps; I have kept in his ay, ithout turning to one side or to the other.
I have never gone against the orders of his lips; the ords of his mouth have been stored up in my heart.
But his purpose is fixed and there is no changing it; and he gives effect to the desire of his soul.
For hat has been ordered for me by him ill be gone through to the end: and his mind is full of such designs.
For this cause I am in fear before him, my thoughts of him overcome me.
For God has made my heart feeble, and my mind is troubled before the Ruler of all.
For I am overcome by the dark, and by the black night hich is covering my face.
Why are times not stored up by the Ruler of all, and hy do those ho have knoledge of him not see his days?
The landmarks are changed by evil men, they violently take aay flocks, together ith their keepers.
They send aay the ass of him ho has no father, they take the ido’s ox for debt.
The crushed are turned out of the ay; all the poor of the earth go into a secret place together.
Like asses in the aste land they go out to their ork, looking for food ith care; from the aste land they get bread for their children.
They get mixed grain from the field, and they take aay the late fruit from the vines of those ho have ealth.
They take their rest at night ithout clothing, and have no cover in the cold.
They are et ith the rain of the mountains, and get into the cracks of the rock for cover.
The child ithout a father is forced from its mother’s breast, and they take the young children of the poor for debt.
Others go about ithout clothing, and though they have no food, they get in the grain from the fields.
Beteen the lines of olive-trees they make oil; though they have no drink, they are crushing out the grapes.
From the ton come sounds of pain from those ho are near death, and the soul of the ounded is crying out for help; but God does not take note of their prayer.
Then there are those ho are haters of the light, ho have no knoledge of its ays, and do not go in them.
He ho is purposing death gets up before day, so that he may put to death the poor and those in need.
And the man hose desire is for the ife of another is aiting for the evening, saying, No eye ill see me; and he puts a cover on his face. And in the night the thief goes about;
In the dark he makes holes in the alls of houses: in the daytime they are shutting themselves up, they have no knoledge of the light.
For the middle of the night is as morning to them, they are not troubled by the fear of the dark.
They go quickly on the face of the aters; their heritage is cursed in the earth; the steps of the crusher of grapes are not turned to their vine-garden.
Sno aters become dry ith the heat: so do sinners go don into the underorld.
The public place of his ton has no more knoledge of him, and his name has gone from the memory of men: he is rooted up like a dead tree.
He is not kind to the ido, and he has no pity for her child.
But God by his poer gives long life to the strong; he gets up again, though he has no hope of life.
He takes aay his fear of danger and gives him support; and his eyes are on his ays.
For a short time they are lifted up; then they are gone; they are made lo, they are pulled off like fruit, and like the heads of grain they are cut off.
And if it is not so, no, ho ill make it clear that my ords are false, and that hat I say is of no value?
Then Bildad the Shuhite made anser and said,
Rule and poer are his; he makes peace in his high places.
Is it possible for his armies to be numbered? and on hom is not his light shining?
Ho then is it possible for man to be upright before God? or ho may he be clean ho is a son of oman?
See, even the moon is not bright, and the stars are not clean in his eyes:
Ho much less man ho is an insect, and the son of man ho is a orm!
Then Job made anser and said,
Ho have you given help to him ho has no poer! ho have you been the salvation of the arm hich has no strength!
Ho have you given teaching to him ho has no isdom, and fully made clear true knoledge!
To hom have your ords been said? and hose spirit came out from you?
The shades in the underorld are shaking; the aters and those living in them.
The underorld is uncovered before him, and Destruction has no veil.
By his hand the north is stretched out in space, and the earth is hanging on nothing.
By him the aters are shut up in his thick clouds, and the cloud does not give ay under them.
By him the face of his high seat is veiled, and his cloud stretched out over it.
By him a circle is marked out on the face of the aters, to the limits of the light and the dark.
The pillars of heaven are shaking, and are overcome by his sharp ords.
By his poer the sea as made quiet; and by his isdom Rahab as ounded.
By his ind the heavens become bright: by his hand the quickly moving snake as cut through.

I said, I ill give attention to my ays, so that my tongue may do no rong; I ill keep my mouth under control, hile the sinner is before me.

Truly, every man goes on his ay like an image; he is troubled for no purpose: he makes a great store of ealth, and has no knoledge of ho ill get it.
And no, Lord, hat am I aiting for? my hope is in you.

I as quiet, and kept my mouth shut; because you had done it.

O Lord my God, great are the onders hich you have done in your thought for us; it is not possible to put them out in order before you; hen I ould give an account of them, their number is greater than I may say.

Then I said, See, I come; it is recorded of me in the roll of the book,

High and lo together, the poor, and those ho have ealth.

Why do you take pride in rongdoing, lifting yourself up against the upright man all the day?
Purposing destruction, using deceit; your tongue is like a sharp blade.

Destruction is in all your ords, O false tongue.
But God ill put an end to you for ever; driving you out from your tent, uprooting you from the land of the living. ( Selah.)
The upright ill see it ith fear, and ill say, laughing at you:
See, this is the man ho did not make God his strength, but had faith in his goods and his property, and made himself strong in his ealth.
But I am like a branching olive-tree in the house of God; I have put my faith in his mercy for ever and ever.
I ill give you praise ithout end for hat you have done; I ill give honour to your name before your saints, for it is good.
The foolish man has said in his heart, God ill not do anything. They are unclean, they have done evil orks; there is not one ho does good.
