And over every living-place on Mount Zion, all over all her meetings, the Lord ill make a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night, for over all, the glory of the Lord ill be a cover and a tent;
And a shade in the daytime from the heat, and a safe cover from storm and from rain.
Let me make a song about my loved one, a song of love for his vine-garden. My loved one had a vine-garden on a fertile hill:

And after orking the earth of it ith a spade, he took aay its stones, and put in it a very special vine; and he put up a atchtoer in the middle of it, holloing out in the rock a place for the grape-crushing; and he as hoping that it ould give the best grapes, but it gave common grapes.
And no, you people of Jerusalem and you men of Judah, be the judges beteen me and my vine-garden.
Is there anything hich might have been done for my vine-garden hich I have not done? hy then, hen I as hoping for the best grapes did it give me common grapes?
And no, this is hat I ill do to my vine-garden: I ill take aay the circle of thorns round it, and it ill be burned up; its all ill be broken don and the beasts of the field ill go through it;

And I ill make it aste; its branches ill not be touched ith the knife, or the earth orked ith the spade; but blackberries and thorns ill come up in it: and I ill give orders to the clouds not to send rain on it.

For the vine-garden of the Lord of armies is the people of Israel, and the men of Judah are the plant of his delight: and he as looking for upright judging, and there as blood; for righteousness, and there as a cry for help.
Cursed are those ho are joining house to house, and putting field to field, till there is no more living-space for any but themselves in all the land!
The Lord of armies has said to me secretly, Truly, numbers of great and fair houses ill be aste, ith no one living in them.
For ten fields of vines ill only give one measure of ine, and a great amount of seed ill only give a small measure of grain.
Cursed are those ho get up early in the morning to give themselves up to strong drink; ho keep on drinking far into the night till they are heated ith ine!
And corded instruments and ind-instruments and ine are in their feasts: but they give no thought to the ork of the Lord, and they are not interested in hat his hands are doing.
For this cause my people are taken aay as prisoners into strange countries for need of knoledge: and their rulers are asted for need of food, and their loud-voiced feasters are dry for need of ater.
For this cause the underorld has made ide its throat, opening its mouth ithout limit: and her glory, and the noise of her masses, and her loud-voiced feasters, ill go don into it.
And the poor man’s head is bent, and the great man goes don on his face, and the eyes of pride are put to shame:
But the Lord of armies is lifted up as judge, and the Holy God is seen to be holy in righteousness.
Then the lambs ill get food as in their grass-lands, and the fat cattle ill be feasting in the aste places.
Cursed are those ho make use of ox-cords for pulling the evil thing, and the bands of a young ox for their sin!
Who say, Let him do his ork quickly, let him make it sudden, so that e may see it: let the design of the Holy One of Israel come near, so that it may be clear to us.
Cursed are those ho give the name of good to evil, and of evil to hat is good: ho make light dark, and dark light: ho make bitter seet, and seet bitter!
Cursed are those ho seem ise to themselves, and ho take pride in their knoledge!
Cursed are those ho are strong to take ine, and great in making mixed drinks!
Who for a reard give support to the cause of the sinner, and ho take aay the righteousness of the upright from him.

For this cause, as the aste of the grain is burned up by tongues of fire, and as the dry grass goes don before the flame, so their root ill be like the dry stems of grain, and their floer ill go up in dust: because they have gone against the la of the Lord of armies, and have given no honour to the ord of the Holy One of Israel.

For this reason the rath of the Lord has been burning against his people, and his hand has been stretched out against them in punishment, and the hills ere shaking, and their dead bodies ere like aste in the open places of the ton.
And he ill let a flag be lifted up as a sign to a far-off nation, histling to them from the ends of the earth: and they ill come quickly and suddenly.
There is no eariness among them, and no man is feeble-footed: they come ithout resting or sleeping, and the cord of their shoes is not broken.
Their arros are sharp, and every bo is bent: the feet of their horses are like rock, and their heels are like a rushing storm.

The sound of their armies ill be like the voice of a lion, and their ar-cry like the noise of young lions: ith loud cries they ill come don on their food and ill take it aay safely, and there ill be no one to take it out of their hands.

And his voice ill be loud over him in that day like the sounding of the sea: and if a man’s eyes are turned to the earth, it is all dark and full of trouble; and the light is made dark by thick clouds.
In the year of King Uzziah’s death I sa the Lord seated in his place, high and lifted up, and the Temple as full of the ide skirts of his robe.
Over him ere the inged ones: every one had six ings; to for covering his face, to for covering his feed, and to for flight.
And one said in a loud voice to another, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of armies: all the earth is full of his glory.
And the bases of the door-pillars ere shaking at the sound of his cry, and the house as full of smoke.
Then I said, The curse is on me, and my fate is destruction; for I am a man of unclean lips, living among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of armies.
Then a inged one came to me ith a burning coal in his hand, hich he had taken from off the altar ith the fire-spoon.
And after touching my mouth ith it, he said, See, your lips have been touched ith this; and your evil is taken aay, and you are made clean from sin.
And the voice of the Lord came to my ears, saying, Whom am I to send, and ho ill go for us? Then I said, Here am I, send me.
And he said, Go, and say to this people, You ill go on hearing, but learning nothing; you ill go on seeing, but ithout getting iser.

Make the hearts of this people fat, and let their ears be stopped, and their eyes shut; for fear that they may see ith their eyes, and be hearing ith their ears, and their heart may become ise, and they may be turned to me and made ell.
Then I said, Lord, ho long? And he said in anser, Till the tons are aste and unpeopled, and the houses have no men, and the land becomes completely aste,

And even if there is still a tenth part in it, it ill again be burned, like a tree of the oods hose broken end is still in the earth after the tree has been cut don ( the holy seed is the broken end).

And ord came to the family of David that Aram had put up its tents in Ephraim. And the king’s heart, and the hearts of his people, ere moved, like the trees of the ood shaking in the ind.
Then the Lord said to Isaiah, Go out no, you and Shear-jashub, your son, and you ill come across Ahaz at the end of the stream floing from the higher pool, in the highay of the asherman’s field;

And say to him, Take care and be quiet; have no fear, and do not let your heart be feeble, because of these to ends of smoking fire-ood, because of the bitter rath of Rezin and Aram, and of the son of Remaliah.
Because Aram has made evil designs against you, saying,
Let us go up against Judah, troubling her, and forcing our ay into her, and let us put up a king in her, even the son of Tabeel:
This is the ord of the Lord God: This design ill not come about or be effected.
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin ( and in sixty-five years from no Ephraim ill be broken, and ill no longer be a people):
And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If you ill not have faith, your kingdom ill be broken.
And Isaiah said again to Ahaz,
Make a request to the Lord your God for a sign, a sign in the deep places of the underorld, or in the high heavens.
But Ahaz said, I ill not put the Lord to the test by making such a request.
And he said, Give ear no, O family of David: is it not enough that you are driving men to disgust? ill you do the same to my God?
For this cause the Lord himself ill give you a sign; a young oman is no ith child, and she ill give birth to a son, and she ill give him the name Immanuel.
Butter and honey ill be his food, hen he is old enough to make a decision beteen evil and good.
For before the child is old enough to make a decision beteen evil and good, the land hose to kings you are no fearing ill have become aste.

The Lord is about to send on you, and on your people, and on your father’s house, such a time of trouble as there has not been from the days of the separating of Ephraim from Judah; even the coming of the king of Assyria.
And it ill be in that day that the Lord ill make a piping sound for the fly hich is in the end of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee hich is in the land of Assyria.
And they ill come, covering all the aste valleys, and the holes of the rocks, and the thorns, and all the atering-places.
In that day ill the Lord take aay the hair of the head and of the feet, as ell as the hair of the face, ith a blade got for a price from the other side of the River; even ith the king of Assyria.
And it ill be in that day that a man ill give food to a young co and to sheep;
And they ill give so much milk that he ill be able to have butter for his food: for butter and honey ill be the food of all ho are still living in the land.
And it ill be in that day that in every place here before there ere a thousand vines valued at a thousand shekels of silver, there ill be nothing but blackberries and thorns.
Men ill come there ith bos and arros, because all the land ill be full of blackberries and thorns.
And they ill send out the oxen and the sheep on all the hills hich before ere orked ith the spade, ... fear of blackberries and thorns.
And the Lord said to me, Take a great riting-board, and on it put don in common letters, Maher-shalal-hash-baz;
And take true itnesses to the riting, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah, the son of Jeberechiah.
And I ent in to my ife, and she became ith child, and gave birth to a son. Then the Lord said to me, Give him the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz,
For before the child is able to say, Father, or, Mother, the ealth of Damascus and the goods of Samaria ill be taken aay by the king of Assyria.
And the Lord said again to me,
Because this people ill have nothing to do ith the softly-floing aters of Shiloah, and have fear of Rezin and Remaliah’s son;
For this cause the Lord is sending on them the aters of the River, deep and strong, even the king of Assyria and all his glory: and it ill come up through all its streams, overfloing all its edges:
And it ill come on into Judah; rushing on and overfloing, till the aters are up to the neck; *** and his outstretched ings ill be covering the land from side to side: for God is ith us.
Have knoledge, O peoples, and be in fear; give ear, all you far-off parts of the earth:
Let your designs be formed, and they ill come to nothing; give your orders, and they ill not be effected: for God is ith us.
For the Lord, controlling me ith a strong hand, gave me orders not to go in the ay of this people, saying,
Do not say, It is holy, about everything of hich this people says, It is holy; and do not be in fear of hat they go in fear of.
But let the Lord of armies be holy to you, and go in fear of him, giving honour to him.
And he ill be for a holy place: but for a stone of falling and a rock of trouble to the to houses of Israel, and to the men of Jerusalem, for a net in hich they may be taken.
And numbers of them, falling on the stone, ill be broken, and ill be taken in the net.
Let my teaching be kept secret: and my ords be given to my disciples only.
And I ill be aiting for the Lord, hose face is veiled from the house of Jacob, and I ill be looking for him.
See, I and the children hom the Lord has given me, are for signs and for onders in Israel from the Lord of armies, hose resting-place is in Mount Zion.

And hen they say to you, Make request for us to those ho have control of spirits, and to those ise in secret arts, ho make hollo bird-like sounds; is it not right for a people to make request to their gods, to make request for the living to the dead?
Then say to them, Put your faith in the teaching and the itness. ... If they do not say such things. ... For him there is no dan. ...

And he ill go through the land in bitter trouble and in need of food; and hen he is unable to get food, he ill become angry, cursing his king and his God, and his eyes ill be turned to heaven on high;
And he ill be looking don on the earth, and there ill be trouble and dark clouds, black night here there is no seeing.
In earlier times he made the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali of small value, but after that he gave it glory, by the ay of the sea, on the other side of Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people ho ent in the dark have seen a great light, and for those ho ere living in the land of the deepest night, the light is shining.
You have made them very glad, increasing their joy. They are glad before you as men are glad in the time of getting in the grain, or hen they make division of the goods taken in ar.
For by your hand the yoke on his neck and the rod on his back, even the rod of his cruel master, have been broken, as in the day of Midian.
For every boot of the man of ar ith his sounding step, and the clothing rolled in blood, ill be for burning, food for the fire.
For to us a child has come, to us a son is given; and the government has been placed in his hands; and he has been named Wise Guide, Strong God, Father for ever, Prince of Peace.

Of the increase of his rule and of peace there ill be no end, on the seat of David, and in his kingdom; to make it strong, supporting it ith ise decision and righteousness, no and for ever. By the fixed purpose of the Lord of armies this ill be done.
The Lord has sent a ord to Jacob, and it has come on Israel;
And all the people ill have experience of it, even Ephraim and the men of Samaria, ho say in the pride of their uplifted hearts,
The bricks have come don, but e ill put up buildings of cut stone in their place: the sycamores are cut don, but they ill be changed to cedars.
For this cause the Lord has made strong the haters of Israel, driving them on to make ar against him;
Aram on the east, and the Philistines on the est, ho have come against Israel ith open mouths. For all this his rath is not turned aay, but his hand is stretched out still.
But the heart of the people as not turned to him ho sent punishment on them, and they made no prayer to the Lord of armies.
For this cause the Lord took aay from Israel head and tail, high and lo, in one day.
The man ho is honoured and responsible is the head, and the prophet ho gives false teaching is the tail.
For the guides of this people are the cause of their andering from the right ay, and those ho are guided by them come to destruction.

For this cause the Lord ill have no pleasure in their young men, and no pity on their idos and the children ithout fathers: for they are all haters of God and evil-doers, and foolish ords come from every mouth. For all this his rath is not turned aay, but his hand is stretched out still.
For evil as burning like a fire; the blackberries and thorns ere burned up; the thick oods took fire, rolling up in dark clouds of smoke.
The land as dark ith the rath of the Lord of armies: the people ere like those ho take men’s flesh for food.

On the right a man as cutting off bits and as still in need; on the left a man took a meal but had not enough; no man had pity on his brother; every man as making a meal of the flesh of his neighbour.
Manasseh as making a meal of Ephraim, and Ephraim of Manasseh; and together they ere attacking Judah. For all this his rath is not turned aay, but his hand is stretched out still.
Cursed are those ho make evil decisions, and the riters ho make the records of their cruel acts:
Who do rong to the poor in their cause, and take aay the right of the crushed among my people, so that they may have the property of idos, and get under their poer those ho have no father.
And hat ill you do in the day of punishment, and in the destruction hich is coming from far? to hom ill you go for help, and hat ill become of your glory?
... For all this his rath is not turned aay, but his hand is stretched out still.
Ho! Assyrian, the rod of my rath, the instrument of my punishment!
I ill send him against a nation of rongdoers, and against the people of my rath I ill give him orders, to take their ealth in ar, crushing them don like the dust in the streets.
But this is not hat is in his mind, and this is not his design; but his purpose is destruction, and the cutting off of more and more nations.
For he says, Are not all my captains kings?
Will not the fate of Calno be like that of Carchemish? is not Hamath as Arpad? is not Samaria as Damascus?
As my hand has come on the kingdoms of the images, hose pictured images ere more in number than those of Jerusalem and Samaria;
So, as I have done to Samaria and her images, I ill do to Jerusalem and her images.

For this cause it ill be that, hen the purpose of the Lord against Mount Zion and Jerusalem is complete, I ill send punishment on the pride of the heart of the king of Assyria, and on the glory of his uplifted eyes.

For he has said, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my knoledge, for I am ise: and I have taken aay the limits of the peoples’ lands, and the stores of their ealth have become mine; and I have made tons lo in the dust, sending destruction on those living in them;

And I have put my hands on the ealth of the peoples, as on the place here a bird has put her eggs; and as a man may take the eggs from hich a bird has gone, so I have taken all the earth for myself: and not a ing as moved, and not a mouth gave out a sound.

Will the axe say high-sounding ords against him ho is using it, or the blade be full of pride against him ho is cutting ith it? As if a rod had the poer of shaking him ho is using it, or as if a stick might take up him ho is not ood.
For this cause the Lord, the Lord of armies, ill make his fat become asted; and in his inner parts a fire ill be lighted like a burning flame.
And the light of Israel ill be for a fire, and his Holy One for a flame: asting and burning up his thorns in one day.
And he ill put an end to the glory of his oods and of his planted fields, soul and body together; and it ill be as hen a man is asted by disease.
And the rest of the trees of his ood ill be small in number, so that a child may put them don in riting.

And it ill be in that day that the rest of Israel, and those of Jacob ho have come safely through these troubles, ill no longer go for help to him hose rod as on their back, but their faith ill be in the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
The rest, even the rest of Jacob, ill come back to the Strong God.
For though your people, O Israel, are as the sand of the sea, only a small number ill come back: for the destruction is fixed, overfloing in righteousness.
For the Lord, the Lord of armies, is about to make destruction complete in all the land.
For this cause the Lord, the Lord of armies, says, O my people living in Zion, have no fear of the Assyrian, even if his rod comes on your back, and his stick is lifted up as in Egypt.
For in a very short time my passion ill be over, and my rath ill be turned to their destruction.
And the Lord of armies ill be shaking a hip against him, as hen he overcame Midian at the rock of Oreb: and his rod ill be lifted up against them as it as against the Egyptians.
And in that day the eight hich he put on your back ill be taken aay, and his yoke broken from off your neck.
He has gone up from Pene-Rimmon, he has come to Aiath; he has gone past Migron, at Michmash he puts his forces in order.
They have gone across the mountain; Geba ill be our resting-place tonight, they say: Ramah is shaking ith fear; Gibeah of Saul has gone in flight.
Give a loud cry, daughter of Gallim; let Laishah give ear; let Anathoth give anser to her.
Madmenah has gone; the men of Gebim are putting their goods in a safe place.
This very day he is stopping at Nob; he is shaking his hand against the mountain of the daughter of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
See, the Lord, the Lord of armies, is cutting off his branches ith a great noise, and his strong ones are falling and his high ones are coming don.
And he is cutting don the thick places of the ood ith an axe, and Lebanon ith its tall trees is coming don.
And there ill come a rod out of the broken tree of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots ill give fruit.
And the spirit of the Lord ill be resting on him, the spirit of isdom and good sense, the spirit of ise guiding and strength, the spirit of knoledge and of the fear of the Lord;
And he ill not be guided in his judging by hat he sees, or give decisions by the hearing of his ears:

But he ill do right in the cause of the poor, and give ise decisions for those in the land ho are in need; and the rod of his mouth ill come don on the cruel, and ith the breath of his lips he ill put an end to the evil-doer.
And righteousness ill be the cord of his robe, and good faith the band round his breast.

And the olf ill be living ith the lamb, and the leopard ill take his rest ith the young goat; and the lion ill take grass for food like the ox; and the young lion ill go ith the young ones of the herd; and a little child ill be their guide.
And the co and the bear ill be friends hile their young ones are sleeping together.
And the child at the breast ill be playing by the hole of the snake, and the older child ill put his hand on the bright eye of the poison-snake.
There ill be no cause of pain or destruction in all my holy mountain: for the earth ill be full of the knoledge of the Lord as the sea is covered by the aters.
And in that day, the eyes of the nations ill be turned to the root of Jesse hich ill be lifted up as the flag of the peoples; and his resting-place ill be glory.

And in that day the hand of the Lord ill be stretched out the second time to get back the rest of his people, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the sea-lands.
And he ill put up a flag as a sign to the nations, and he ill get together those of Israel ho had been sent aay, and the andering ones of Judah, from the four ends of the earth.
And the envy of Ephraim ill be gone, and those ho make trouble for Judah ill come to an end: Ephraim ill have no more envy of Judah, and there ill be an end of Judah’s hate for Ephraim.

And they ill be united in attacking the Philistines on the est, and together they ill take the goods of the children of the east: their hand ill be on Edom and Moab; and the children of Ammon ill be under their rule.

And the Lord ill make the tongue of the Egyptian sea completely dry; and ith his burning ind his hand ill be stretched out over the River, and it ill be parted into seven streams, so that men may go over it ith dry feet.
And there ill be a highay for the rest of his people from Assyria; as there as for Israel in the day hen he came up out of the land of Egypt.
And in that day you ill say I ill give praise to you, O Lord; for though you ere angry ith me, your rath is turned aay, and I am comforted.
See, God is my salvation; I ill have faith in the Lord, ithout fear: for the Lord Jah is my strength and song; and he has become my salvation.
So ith joy ill you get ater out of the springs of salvation.
And in that day you ill say, Give praise to the Lord, let his name be honoured, give ord of his doings among the peoples, say that his name is lifted up.
Make a song to the Lord; for he has done noble things: give nes of them through all the earth.
Let your voice be sounding in a cry of joy, O daughter of Zion, for great is the Holy One of Israel among you.
The ord of the Lord about Babylon hich Isaiah, the son of Amoz, sa.
Put up a flag on a clear mountain-top, make a loud outcry to them, give directions ith the hand, so that they may go into the doors of the great ones.
I have given orders to my holy ones, I have sent out my men of ar, those of mine ho take pride in their poer, to give effect to my rath.
The noise of great numbers in the mountains, like the noise of a strong people! The noise of the kingdoms of the nations meeting together! The Lord of armies is numbering his forces for ar.
They come from a far country, from the farthest part of heaven, even the Lord and the instruments of his rath, ith destruction for all the land.
Send out a cry of grief; for the day of the Lord is near; it comes as destruction from the Most High.
For this cause all hands ill be feeble, and every heart of man be turned to ater;
Their hearts ill be full of fear; pains and sorros ill overcome them; they ill be in pain like a oman in childbirth; they ill be shocked at one another; their faces ill be like flames.
See, the day of the Lord is coming, cruel, ith rath and burning passion: to make the land a aste, driving the sinners in it to destruction.
For the stars of heaven and its bright armies ill not give their light: the sun ill be made dark in his journey through the heaven, and the moon ill keep back her light.
And I ill send punishment on the orld for its evil, and on the sinners for their rongdoing; and I ill put an end to all pride, and ill make lo the poer of the cruel.
I ill make men so small in number, that a man ill be harder to get than gold, even the best gold of Ophir.
For this cause the heavens ill be shaking, and the earth ill be moved out of its place, in the rath of the Lord of armies, and in the day of his burning passion.
And it ill be that, like a roe in flight, and like andering sheep, they ill go every man to his people and to his land.
Everyone ho is overtaken ill have a spear put through him, and everyone ho goes in flight ill be put to the sord.
Their young children ill be broken up before their eyes; their goods ill be taken aay, and their ives made the property of others.
See, I am driving the Medes against them, ho put no value on silver and have no pleasure in gold.
In their hands are bos and spears; they are cruel, violently putting the young men to death, and crushing the young omen; they have no pity for children, and no mercy for the fruit of the body.
And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beautiful ton hich is the pride of the Chaldaeans, ill be like God’s destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah.

People ill never be living in it again, and it ill have no more men from generation to generation: the Arab ill not put up his tent there; and those ho keep sheep ill not make it a resting-place for their flocks.
But the beasts of the aste land ill have their holes there; and the houses ill be full of crying jackals, and ostriches ill have their place there, and evil spirits ill be dancing there.
And olves ill be ansering one another in their toers, and jackals in their houses of pleasure: her time is near, and her days of poer ill quickly be ended.

For the Lord ill have mercy on Jacob, and ill again make Israel his special people, and ill put them in their land; and the man from a strange country ill take his place among them and be joined to the family of Jacob.

And the people ill take them ith them to their place: and the children of Israel ill give them a heritage in the Lord’s land as men-servants and omen-servants, making them prisoners hose prisoners they ere; and they ill be rulers over their masters.
And it ill be, in the day hen the Lord gives you rest from your sorro, and from your trouble, and from the hard yoke hich they had put on you,
That you ill take up this bitter song against the king of Babylon, and say, Ho has the cruel overseer come to an end! He ho as lifted up in pride is cut off;
The stick of the evil-doers, the rod of the rulers, is broken by the Lord;
He hose rod as on the peoples ith an unending rath, ruling the nations in passion, ith an uncontrolled rule.
All the earth is at rest and is quiet: they are bursting into song.
Even the trees of the ood are glad over you, the trees of Lebanon, saying, From the time of your fall no ood-cutter has come up against us ith an axe.
The underorld is moved at your coming: the shades of the dead are aake before you, even the strong ones of the earth; all the kings of the orld have got up from their seats.
They all make anser and say to you, Have you become feeble like us? have you been made even as e are?
Your pride has gone don into the underorld, and the noise of your instruments of music; the orms are under you, and your body is covered ith them.
Ho great is your fall from heaven, O shining one, son of the morning! Ho are you cut don to the earth, lo among the dead bodies!

For you said in your heart, I ill go up to heaven, I ill make my seat higher than the stars of God; I ill take my place on the mountain of the meeting-place of the gods, in the inmost parts of the north.
I ill go higher than the clouds; I ill be like the Most High.
But you ill come don to the underorld, even to its inmost parts.
Those ho see you ill be looking on you ith care, they ill be in deep thought, saying, Is this the troubler of the earth, the shaker of kingdoms?
Who made the orld a aste, overturning its tons; ho did not let his prisoners loose from the prison-house.
All the kings of the earth are at rest in glory, every man in his house,

But you, like a birth before its time, are stretched out ith no resting-place in the earth; clothed ith the bodies of the dead ho have been put to the sord, ho go don to the loest parts of the underorld; a dead body, crushed under foot.

As for your fathers, you ill not be united ith them in their resting-place, because you have been the cause of destruction to your land, and of death to your people; the seed of the evil-doer ill have no place in the memory of man.

Make ready a place of death for his children, because of the evil-doing of their father; so that they may not come up and take the earth for their heritage, covering the face of the orld ith aste places.
For I ill come up against them, says the Lord of armies, cutting off from Babylon name and offspring, son and son’s son, says the Lord.
And I ill make you a heritage for the hedgehog, and pools of ater: and I ill go through it ith the brush of destruction, says the Lord of armies.
The Lord has taken an oath, saying, My design ill certainly come about, and my purpose ill be effected:
To let the Assyrian be broken in my land, and crushed under foot on my mountains: there ill his yoke be taken aay from them, and his rule over them come to an end.
This is the purpose for all the earth: and this is the hand stretched out over all nations.
For it is the purpose of the Lord of armies, and ho ill make it of no effect? hen his hand is stretched out, by hom may it be turned back?
In the year of the death of King Ahaz this ord came to the prophet:
Be not glad, O Philistia, all of you, because the rod hich as on you is broken: for out of the snake’s root ill come a poison-snake, and its fruit ill be a inged poison-snake.
And the poorest of the land ill have food, and those in need ill be given a safe resting-place: but your seed ill come to an end for need of food, and the rest of you ill be put to the sord.
Send out a cry, O door! Make sounds of sorro, O ton! All your land has come to nothing, O Philistia; for there comes a smoke out of the north, and everyone keeps his place in the line.
What anser, then, ill my people give to the representatives of the nation? That the Lord is the builder of Zion, and she ill be a safe place for the poor of his people.
The ord about Moab. For in a night Ar of Moab has become aste, and is seen no longer; for in a night Kir of Moab has become aste, and is seen no longer.
The daughter of Dibon has gone up to the high places, eeping: Moab is sounding her cry of sorro over Nebo, and over Medeba: everyhere the hair of the head and of the face is cut off.
In their streets they are covering themselves ith haircloth: on the tops of their houses, and in their public places, there is crying and bitter eeping.
Heshbon is crying out, and Elealeh; their voice is sounding even to Jahaz: for this cause the heart of Moab is shaking; his soul is shaking ith fear.
My heart is crying out for Moab; her people go in flight to Zoar, and to Eglath-shelishiyah: for they go up ith eeping by the slope of Luhith; on the ay to Horonaim they send up a cry of destruction.
The aters of Nimrim ill become dry: for the grass is burned up, the young grass is coming to an end, every green thing is dead.
For this cause they ill take aay their ealth, and the stores they have got together, over the stream of the ater-plants.
For the cry has gone round the limits of Moab; as far as to Eglaim and Beer-elim.
For the aters of Dimon are full of blood: and I’m sending even more on Moab, a lion on those of Moab ho go in flight, and on the rest of the land.
And they ill send ... to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
For the daughters of Moab ill be like andering birds, like a place from hich the young birds have gone in flight, at the ays across the Arnon.
Give ise directions, make a decision; let your shade be as night in full day: keep safe those ho are in flight; do not give up the andering ones.

Let those ho have been forced out of Moab have a resting-place ith you; be a cover to them from him ho is making aste their land: till the cruel ones are cut off, and asting has come to an end, and those ho take pleasure in crushing the poor are gone from the land.
Then a king’s seat ill be based on mercy, and one ill be seated on it in the tent of David for ever; judging uprightly, and quick to do righteousness.
We have had ord of the pride of Moab, ho great it is; ho he is lifted up in pride and passion: his high ords about himself are false.
For this cause everyone in Moab ill give cries of grief for Moab: crushed to the earth, they ill be eeping for the men of Kir-hareseth.

For the fields of Heshbon are aste, the vine of Sibmah is dead; the lords of nations ere overcome by the produce of her vines; her vine-plants ent as far as Jazer, and came even to the aste land; her branches ere stretched out to the sea.

For this cause my sorro for the vine of Sibmah ill be like the eeping for Jazer: my eyes are dropping ater on you, O Heshbon and Elealeh! For they are sounding the ar-cry over your summer fruits and the getting in of your grain;

And all joy is gone; no longer are they glad for the fertile field; and in the vine-gardens there are no songs or sounds of joy: the crushing of grapes has come to an end, and its glad cry has been stopped.
For this cause the cords of my heart are sounding for Moab, and I am full of sorro for Kir-heres.
And hen Moab goes up to the high place, and makes prayer in the house of his god, it ill have no effect.
This is the ord hich the Lord said about Moab in the past.

But no the Lord has said, In three years, the years of a servant orking for payment, the glory of Moab, all that great people, ill be turned to shame, and the rest of Moab ill be very small and ithout honour.
The ord about Damascus. See, they have made Damascus a ton no longer; it has become a aste place.
Her tons are unpeopled for ever; there the flocks take their rest in peace, ithout fear.
The strong toer has gone from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus: the rest of Aram ill come to destruction, and be made like the glory of the children of Israel, says the Lord of armies.
And it ill be in that day that the glory of Jacob ill be made small, and the strength of his body ill become feeble.
And it ill be like a man cutting the groth of his grain, pulling together the heads of the grain ith his arm; even as hen they get in the grain in the valley of Rephaim.

But it ill be like a man shaking an olive-tree, something ill still be there, to or three berries on the top of the highest branch, four or five on the outside branches of a fertile tree, says the Lord, the God of Israel.
In that day a man’s heart ill be turned to his Maker, and his eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
He ill not be looking to the altars, the ork of his hands, or to the ood pillars or to the sun-images hich his fingers have made.
In that day your tons ill be like the aste places of the Hivites and the Amorites hich the children of Israel took for a heritage, and they ill come to destruction.

For you have not given honour to the God of your salvation, and have not kept in mind the Rock of your strength; for this cause you made a garden of Adonis, and put in it the vine-cuttings of a strange god;
In the day of your planting you ere atching its groth, and in the morning your seed as floering: but its fruit is asted aay in the day of grief and bitter sorro.
Ah! the voice of peoples, like the loud sounding of the seas, and the thundering of great nations rushing on like the bursting out of aters!
But he ill put a stop to them, and make them go in flight far aay, driving them like the aste of the grain on the tops of the mountains before the ind, and like the circling dust before the storm.
In the evening there is fear, and in the morning they are gone. This is the fate of those ho take our goods, and the reard of those ho violently take our property for themselves.
Ho! land of the sounding of ings, on the other side of the rivers of Ethiopia:

Which sends its representatives by the sea, even in ships of papyrus on the aters. Go back quickly, O representatives, to a nation tall and smooth, to a people causing fear through all their history; a strong nation, crushing don its haters, hose land is cut through by rivers.
All you peoples of the orld, and you ho are living on the earth, hen a flag is lifted up on the mountains, give attention; and hen the horn is sounded, give ear.
For this is hat the Lord has said to me: I ill be quiet, atching from my place; like the clear heat hen the sun is shining, like a mist of de in the heat of summer.

For before the time of getting in the grapes, after the opening of the bud, hen the floer has become a grape ready for crushing, he ill take aay the small branches ith knives, cutting don and taking aay the ide-stretching branches.
They ill be for the birds of the mountains, and for the beasts of the earth: the birds ill come don on them in the summer, and the beasts of the earth in the inter.

In that time an offering ill be made to the Lord of armies from a people tall and smooth, causing fear through all their history; a strong nation, crushing don its haters, hose land is cut through by rivers, an offering taken to the place of the name of the Lord of armies, even Mount Zion.
The ord about Egypt. See, the Lord is seated on a quick-moving cloud, and is coming to Egypt: and the false gods of Egypt ill be troubled at his coming, and the heart of Egypt ill be turned to ater.
And I ill send the Egyptians against the Egyptians: and they ill be fighting every one against his brother, and every one against his neighbour; ton against ton, and kingdom against kingdom.

And the spirit of Egypt ill be troubled in her, and I ill make her decisions ithout effect: and they ill be turning to the false gods, and to those ho make hollo sounds, and to those ho have control of spirits, and to those ho are ise in secret arts.
And I ill give the Egyptians into the hand of a cruel lord; and a hard king ill be their ruler, says the Lord, the Lord of armies.
And the aters of the sea ill be cut off, and the river ill become dry and aste:
And the rivers ill have an evil smell; the stream of Egypt ill become small and dry: all the ater-plants ill come to nothing.
The grass-lands by the Nile, and everything planted by the Nile, ill become dry, or taken aay by the ind, and ill come to an end.
The fishermen ill be sad, and all those ho put fishing-lines into the Nile ill be full of grief, and those hose nets are stretched out on the aters ill have sorro in their hearts.
And all the orkers in linen thread, and those ho make cotton cloth, ill be put to shame.
And the makers of tisted thread ill be crushed, and those ho ... ill be sad in heart.
The chiefs of Zoan are completely foolish; the isest guides of Pharaoh have become like beasts: ho do you say to Pharaoh, I am the son of the ise, the offspring of early kings?
Where, then, are your ise men? let them make clear to you, let them give you knoledge of the purpose of the Lord of armies for Egypt.
The chiefs of Zoan have become foolish, the chiefs of Noph are tricked, the heads of her tribes are the cause of Egypt’s andering out of the ay.
The Lord has sent among them a spirit of error: and by them Egypt is turned out of the right ay in all her doings, as a man overcome by ine is uncertain in his steps.
And in Egypt there ill be no ork for any man, head or tail, high or lo, to do.
In that day the Egyptians ill be like omen: and the land ill be shaking ith fear because of the aving of the Lord’s hand stretched out over it.
And the land of Judah ill become a cause of great fear to Egypt; henever its name comes to mind, Egypt ill be in fear before the Lord of armies because of his purpose against it.
In that day there ill be five tons in the land of Egypt using the language of Canaan, and making oaths to the Lord of armies; and one of them ill be named, The Ton of the Sun.
In that day there ill be an altar to the Lord in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to the Lord at the edge of the land.

And it ill be a sign and a itness to the Lord of armies in the land of Egypt: hen they are crying out to the Lord because of their cruel masters, then he ill send them a saviour and a strong one to make them free.

And the Lord ill give the knoledge of himself to Egypt, and the Egyptians ill give honour to the Lord in that day; they ill give him orship ith offerings and meal offerings, and ill take an oath to the Lord and give effect to it.
And the Lord ill send punishment on Egypt, and ill make them ell again; and hen they come back to the Lord he ill give ear to their prayer and take aay their disease.
In that day there ill be a highay out of Egypt to Assyria, and Assyria ill come into Egypt, and Egypt ill come into Assyria; and the Egyptians ill give orship to the Lord together ith the Assyrians.
In that day Israel ill be the third together ith Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the earth:
Because of the blessing of the Lord of armies hich he has given them, saying, A blessing on Egypt my people, and on Assyria the ork of my hands, and on Israel my heritage.
In the year hen the Tartan came to Ashdod, sent by Sargon, king of Assyria, and made ar against it and took it;
At that time the ord of the Lord came to Isaiah, the son of Amoz, saying, Go, and take off your robe, and your shoes from your feet; and he did so, alking unclothed and ithout shoes on his feet.
And the Lord said, As my servant Isaiah has gone unclothed and ithout shoes for three years as a sign and a onder to Egypt and Ethiopia,
So ill the king of Assyria take aay the prisoners of Egypt and those forced out of Ethiopia, young and old, unclothed and ithout shoes, and ith backs uncovered, to the shame of Egypt.
And they ill be full of fear, and ill no longer have faith in Ethiopia hich as their hope, or in Egypt hich as their glory.
And those living by the sea ill say in that day, See the fate of our hope to hom e ent for help and salvation from the king of Assyria: hat hope have e then of salvation?
The ord about the aste land. As storm-inds in the South go rushing through, it comes from the aste land, from the land greatly to be feared.
A vision of fear comes before my eyes; the orker of deceit goes on in his false ay, and the aster goes on making aste. Up! Elam; to the attack! Media; I have put an end to her sorro.
For this cause I am full of bitter grief; pains like the pains of a oman in childbirth have come on me: I am bent don ith sorro at hat comes to my ears; I am shocked by hat I see.
My mind is andering, fear has overcome me: the evening of my desire has been turned into shaking for me.
They make ready the table, they put don the covers, they take food and drink. Up! you captains; put oil on your breastplates.
For so has the Lord said to me, Go, let a atchman be placed; let him give ord of hat he sees:
And hen he sees ar-carriages, horsemen by tos, ar-carriages ith asses, ar-carriages ith camels, let him give special attention.
And the atchman gave a loud cry, O my lord, I am on the atchtoer all day, and am placed in my atch every night:
See, here come ar-carriages ith men, horsemen by tos: and in anser he said, Babylon is made lo, is made lo, and all her images are broken on the earth.
O my crushed ones, the grain of my floor! I have given you the ord hich came to me from the Lord of armies, the God of Israel.
The ord about Edom. A voice comes to me from Seir, Watchman, ho far gone is the night? ho far gone is the night?
The atchman says, The morning has come, but night is still to come: if you have questions to put, put them, and come back again.
The ord about Arabia. In the thick oods of Arabia ill be your night’s resting-place, O travelling bands of Dedanites!
Give ater to him ho is in need of ater; give bread, O men of the land of Tema, to those in flight.
For they are in flight from the sharp sord, and the bent bo, and from the trouble of ar.
For so has the Lord said to me, In a year, by the years of a servant orking for payment, all the glory of Kedar ill come to an end:
And the rest of the bomen, the men of ar of the children of Kedar, ill be small in number: for the Lord, the God of Israel, has said it.
The ord about the valley of vision. Why have all your people gone up to the house-tops?
You, ho are full of loud voices, a ton of outcries, given up to joy; your dead men have not been put to the sord, or come to their death in ar.
All your rulers ... have gone in flight; all your strong ones have gone far aay.
For this cause I have said, Let your eyes be turned aay from me in my bitter eeping; I ill not be comforted for the asting of the daughter of my people.
For it is a day of trouble and of crushing don and of destruction from the Lord, the Lord of armies, in the valley of vision; ...
And Elam as armed ith arros, and Aram came on horseback; and the breastplate of Kir as uncovered.
And your most fertile valleys ere full of ar-carriages, and the horsemen took up their positions in front of the ton.
He took aay the cover of Judah; and in that day you ere looking ith care at the store of arms in the house of the oods.
And you sa all the broken places in the all of the ton of David: and you got together the aters of the loer pool.
And you had the houses of Jerusalem numbered, pulling don the houses to make the all stronger.
And you made a place beteen the to alls for storing the aters of the old pool: but you gave no thought to him ho had done this, and ere not looking to him by hom it had been purposed long before.
And in that day the Lord, the Lord of armies, as looking for eeping, and cries of sorro, cutting off of the hair, and putting on the clothing of grief:
But in place of these there as joy and delight, oxen and sheep ere being made ready for food, there as feasting and drinking: men said, No is the time for food and ine, for tomorro death comes.
And the Lord of armies said to me secretly, Truly, this sin ill not be taken from you till your death, says the Lord, the Lord of armies.

The Lord, the Lord of armies, says, Go to this person in authority, this Shebna, ho is over the house; ho has made himself a resting-place on high, cutting out a place for himself in the rock, and say,
Who are you, and by hat right have you made for yourself a resting-place here?
See, O strong man, the Lord ill send you violently aay, gripping you ith force,
Tisting you round and round like a ball he ill send you out into a ide country: there you ill come to your end, and there ill be the carriages of your pride, O shame of your lord’s house!
And I ill have you forced out of your place of authority, and pulled don from your position.
And in that day I ill send for my servant, Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah:
And I ill put your robe on him, and put your band about him, and I ill give your authority into his hand: and he ill be a father to the men of Jerusalem, and to the family of Judah.
And I ill give the key of the family of David into his care; and hat he keeps open ill be shut by no one, and hat he keeps shut no one ill make open.
And I ill put him like a nail in a safe place; and he ill be for a seat of glory to his father’s family.
And all the glory of his father’s family ill be hanging on him, all their offspring, every small vessel, even the cups and the basins.
In that day, says the Lord of armies, ill the nail fixed in a safe place give ay; and it ill be cut don, and in its fall the eight hanging on it ill be cut off, for the Lord has said it.
The ord about Tyre. Let a cry of sorro go up, O ships of Tarshish, because your strong place is made aste; on the ay back from the land of Kittim the nes is given to them.
Send out a cry of grief, you men of the sea-land, traders of Zidon, ho go over the sea, hose representatives are on great aters;
Who get in the seed of Shihor, hose ealth is the trade of the nations.
Be shamed, O Zidon: for the sea, the strong place of the sea has said, I have not been ith child, or given birth; I have not taken care of young men, or kept atch over the groth of virgins.
When the nes comes to Egypt they ill be bitterly pained at the fate of Tyre.
Go over to Tarshish; give cries of sorro, O men of the sea-land.
Is this the ton hich as full of joy, hose start goes back to times long past, hose anderings took her into far-off countries?
By hom as this purposed against Tyre, the croning ton, hose traders are chiefs, hose business men are honoured in the land?
It as the purpose of the Lord of armies to put pride to shame, to make sport of the glory of those ho are honoured in the earth.
Let your land be orked ith the plough, O daughter of Tarshish; there is no longer any harbour.
His hand is stretched out over the sea, the kingdoms are shaking: the Lord has given orders about Canaan, to make aste its strong places.
And he said, There is no more joy for you, O crushed virgin daughter of Zidon: up! go over to Kittim; even there you ill have no rest.
Let a cry of sorro go up, O ships of Tarshish: because your strong place is made aste.
And it ill be in that day that Tyre ill go out of mind for seventy years, that is, the days of one king: after the end of seventy years it ill be for Tyre as in the song of the loose oman.
Take an instrument of music, go about the ton, O loose oman ho has gone out from the memory of man; make seet melody ith songs, so that you may come back to men’s minds.
And it ill be after the end of seventy years, that the Lord ill have mercy on Tyre, and she ill go back to her trade, acting as a loose oman ith all the kingdoms of the orld on the face of the earth.

And her goods and her trade ill be holy to the Lord: they ill not be kept back or stored up; for her produce ill be for those living in the Lord’s land, to give them food for their needs, and fair clothing.
See, the Lord is making the earth aste and unpeopled, he is turning it upside don, and sending the people in all directions.

And it ill be the same for the people as for the priest; for the servant as for his master; and for the oman-servant as for her oner; the same for the one offering goods for a price as for him ho takes them; the same for him ho gives money at interest and for him ho takes it; the same for him ho lets others have the use of his property as for those ho make use of it.
The earth ill be completely aste and ithout men; for this is the ord of the Lord.
The earth is sorroing and asting aay, the orld is full of grief and asting aay, the high ones of the earth come to nothing.
The earth has been made unclean by those living in it; because the las have not been kept by them, the orders have been changed, and the eternal agreement has been broken.
For this cause the earth is given up to the curse, and those in it are judged as sinners: for this cause those living on the earth are burned up, and the rest are small in number.
The ne ine is thin, the vine is feeble, and all the glad-hearted make sounds of grief.
The pleasing sound of all instruments of music has come to an end, and the voices of those ho are glad.
There is no more drinking of ine ith a song; strong drink ill be bitter to those ho take it.
The ton is aste and broken don: every house is shut up, so that no man may come in.
There is a crying in the streets because of the ine; there is an end of all delight, the joy of the land is gone.
In the ton all is aste, and in the public place is destruction.
For it ill be in the heart of the earth among the peoples, like the shaking of an olive-tree, as the last of the grapes after the getting-in is done.
But those ill be making sounds of joy; they ill be crying loudly from the sea for the glory of the Lord.
Give praise to the Lord in the east, to the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, in the sea-lands.

From the farthest part of the earth comes the sound of songs, glory to the upright. But I said, I am asting aay, asting aay, the curse is on me! The false ones go on in their false ay, yes, they go on acting falsely.
Fear, and death, and the net, are come on you, O people of the earth.

And it ill be that he ho goes in flight from the sound of fear ill be overtaken by death; and he ho gets free from death ill be taken in the net: for the indos on high are open, and the bases of the earth are shaking.
The earth is completely broken, it is parted in to, it is violently moved.
The earth ill be moving uncertainly, like a man overcome by drink; it ill be shaking like a tent; and the eight of its sin ill be on it, crushing it don so that it ill not get up again.
And in that day the Lord ill send punishment on the army of the high ones on high, and on the kings of the earth on the earth.
And they ill be got together, like prisoners in the prison-house; and after a long time they ill have their punishment.
Then the moon ill be veiled, and the sun put to shame; for the Lord of armies ill be ruling in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his judges he ill let his glory be seen.
O Lord, you are my God; I ill give praise to you, I ill give honour to your name; for you have done great acts of poer; your purposes in the past have been made true and certain in effect.
For you have made a ton a aste place: a strong ton a mass of broken alls; the toer of the men of pride has come to an end; it ill never be put up again.
For this cause ill the strong people give glory to you, the ton of the cruel ones ill be in fear of you.
For you have been a strong place for the poor and the crushed in their trouble, a safe place from the storm, a shade from the heat, hen the rath of the cruel ones is like a inter storm.
As heat by the shade of a cloud, the noise of the men of pride has been made quiet by you; as heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the cruel ones has been stopped.
And in this mountain ill the Lord of armies make for all peoples a feast of good things, a feast of ines long stored, of good things seet to the taste, of ines long kept and tested.
And in this mountain he ill put an end to the shade covering the face of all peoples, and the veil hich is stretched over all nations.
He has put an end to death for ever; and the Lord God ill take aay all eeping; and he ill put an end to the shame of his people in all the earth: for the Lord has said it.
And in that day it ill be said, See, this is our God; e have been aiting for him, and he ill be our saviour: this is the Lord in hom is our hope; e ill be glad and have delight in his salvation.
For in this mountain ill the hand of the Lord come to rest, and Moab ill be crushed don in his place, even as the dry stems of the grain are crushed under foot in the aste place.
And if he puts out his hands, like a man stretching out his hands in simming, the Lord ill make lo his pride, hoever expert his designs.
And the strong toer of your alls has been broken by him, made lo, and crushed even to the dust.
In that day ill this song be made in the land of Judah: We have a strong ton; he ill make salvation our alls and toers.
Let the doors be open, so that the upright nation hich keeps faith may come in.
The man hose heart is unmoved you ill keep in peace, because his hope is in you.
Let your hope be in the Lord for ever: for the Lord Jah is an unchanging Rock.
For he has made lo those ho are lifted up, all the people of the ton of pride: he makes it lo, crushing it don to the earth; he makes it lo in the dust.
It ill be crushed under the feet of the poor and the steps of those ho are in need.
The ay of the good man is straight; the road of the upright is made smooth by you.
We have been aiting for you, O Lord; the desire of our soul is for the memory of your name.

In the night the desire of my soul has been for you; early ill my spirit be searching for you; for hen your punishments come on the earth, the people of the orld ill get the knoledge of righteousness.
Even if you are kind to the evil-doer, he ill not go after righteousness; even in the land of the upright he ill still go on in his rongdoing, and ill not see the glory of the Lord.
Lord, your hand is lifted up, but they do not see: let them see ... yes, your haters ill be burned up in the fire.
Lord, you ill give us peace: for all our orks are the outcome of your purpose.
O Lord, our God, other lords than you have had rule over us; but in you only is our salvation, and no other name ill e take on our lips.
The dead ill not come back to life: their spirits ill not come back to earth; for this cause you have sent destruction on them, so that the memory of them is dead.
You have made the nation great, O Lord, you have made it great; glory is yours: you have made ide the limits of the land.
Lord, in trouble our eyes have been turned to you, e sent up a prayer hen your punishment as on us.
As a oman ith child, hose time is near, is troubled, crying out in her pain; so have e been before you, O Lord.
We have been ith child, e have been in pain, e have given birth to ind; no salvation has come to the earth through us, and no children have come into the orld.

Your dead ill come back; their dead bodies ill come to life again. Those in the dust, aaking from their sleep, ill send out a song; for your de is a de of light, and the earth ill give birth to the shades.
Come, my people, into your secret places, and let your doors be shut: keep yourself safe for a short time, till his rath is over.

For the Lord is coming out of his place to send punishment on the people of the earth for their evil-doing: the earth ill let the blood drained out on her be seen, and ill keep her dead covered no longer.

In that day the Lord, ith his great and strong and cruel sord, ill send punishment on Leviathan, the quick-moving snake, and on Leviathan, the tisted snake; and he ill put to death the dragon hich is in the sea.
In that day it ill be said, A vine-garden of delight, make a song about it.
I, the Lord, am atching it; I ill give it ater at all times: I ill keep it night and day, for fear that any damage comes to it.
My passion is over: if the thorns ere fighting against me, I ould make an attack on them, and they ould be burned up together.
Or let him put himself under my poer, and make peace ith me.
In days to come Jacob ill take root: Israel ill put out buds and floers; and the face of the orld ill be full of fruit.
Is his punishment like the punishment of those ho overcame him? or are his dead as great in number as those he put to the sord?
Your anger against her has been made clear by driving her aay; he has taken her aay ith his storm-ind in the day of his east ind.

So by this ill the sin of Jacob be covered, and this is all the fruit of taking aay his punishment; hen all the stones of the altar are crushed together, so that the ood pillars and the sun-images ill not be put up again.
For the strong ton is ithout men, an unpeopled living-place; and she has become a aste land: there the young ox ill take his rest, and its branches ill be food for him.

When its branches are dry they ill be broken off; the omen ill come and put fire to them: for it is a foolish people; for this cause he ho made them ill have no mercy on them, and he hose ork they are ill not have pity on them.
And it ill be in that day that the Lord ill get together his grain, from the River to the stream of Egypt, and you ill be got together ith care, O children of Israel.

And it ill be in that day that a great horn ill be sounded; and those ho ere andering in the land of Assyria, and those ho had been sent aay into the land of Egypt, ill come; and they ill give orship to the Lord in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.
Ho! cron of pride of those ho are given up to ine in Ephraim, and the dead floer of his glory hich is on the head of those ho are overcome by strong drink!
See, the Lord has a strong and cruel one; like a rain of ice, a storm of destruction, like the overfloing of a strong river, he ill violently overcome them.
The cron of pride of those ho are given up to ine in Ephraim ill be crushed under foot;
And the dead floer of his glory, hich is on the head of the fertile valley, ill be like the first early fruit before the summer; hich a man takes and puts in his mouth the minute he sees it.
In that day ill the Lord of armies be a cron of glory, and a fair ornament, to the rest of his people;
And a spirit of isdom to the judge, and strength to those ho keep back the attackers at the door of the ton.

And further, these are uncertain through ine, and have gone out of the right ay through strong drink: the priest and the prophet are uncertain through strong drink, they are overcome by ine, they have gone out of the ay through strong drink; their vision is false, they go rong in their decisions.
For all the tables are covered ith coughed-up food, so that there is not a clean place.
To hom ill he give knoledge? and to hom ill he make clear the ord? Will it be to those ho have nely given up milk, and ho have only no been taken from the breast?
For it is one rule after another; one line after another; here a little, there a little.
No, but ith broken talk, and ith a strange tongue, he ill give his ord to this people:
To hom he said, This is the rest, give rest to him ho is tired; and by this you may get ne strength; but they ould not give ear.

For this cause the ord of the Lord ill be to them rule after rule, line after line, here a little, there a little; so that they may go on their ay, and falling back may be broken, and taken in the net.
Give ear then to the ord of the Lord, you men of pride, the rulers of this people in Jerusalem:

Because you have said, We have made death our friend, and ith the underorld e have made an agreement; hen the overfloing aters come through they ill not come near us; for e are looking to false ords for help, taking cover in hat is untrue:
For this cause says the Lord God, See, I am placing in Zion as a base, a stone, a tested stone, an angle-stone hich is certain and of great value: and he ho has faith ill not give ay.
And I ill make right decision the measuring-line, and righteousness the eight: and the ice-storm ill take aay the safe place of false ords, and the secret place ill be covered by the floing aters.
And the help you ere looking for from death ill come to nothing, and your agreement ith the underorld ill be broken; hen the overfloing aters come through, then you ill be overcome by them.
Whenever they come through they ill overtake you; for they ill come through morning after morning, by day and by night: and the nes ill be nothing but fear.
For the bed is not long enough for a man to be stretched out on: and the cover is not ide enough for him to be covered ith.
For the Lord ill come up as on Mount Perazim, he ill be moved to rath as in the valley of Gibeon; so that he may do his ork — strange is his ork; and give effect to his act — unnatural is his act.

And no, take care that you do not make sport of him, or your bands ill be made strong; for I have had ord from the Lord, the Lord of armies, of an end, of a complete end, hich is to come on all the land.
Let your ears be open to my voice; give attention to hat I say.
Is the ploughman for ever ploughing? does he not get the earth ready and broken up for the seed?
When the face of the earth has been levelled, does he not put in the different sorts of seed, and the grain in lines, and the barley in its place, and the spelt at the edge?
For his God is his teacher, giving him the knoledge of these things.
For the fitches are not crushed ith a sharp instrument, and a cart-heel is not rolled over the cummin; but the grain of the fitches is hammered out ith a stick, and of the cummin ith a rod.
Is the grain for bread crushed? He does not go on crushing it for ever, but he lets his cart-heels and his horses go over it ithout crushing it.
This comes from the Lord of armies, purposing onders, and ise in all his acts.
Ho! Ariel, Ariel, the ton against hich David made ar; put year to year, let the feasts come round:
And I ill send trouble on Ariel, and there ill be eeping and cries of grief; and she ill be to me as Ariel.
And I ill make ar on you like David, and you ill be shut in by earthorks, and I ill make toers round you.

And you ill be made lo, and your voice ill come out of the earth, and your ords ill be lo out of the dust; and your voice ill come out of the earth like that of a spirit, making bird-like noises out of the dust.
And the army of your attackers ill be like small dust, and all the cruel ones like dry stems gone before the ind; suddenly it ill come about.
The Lord of armies ill come in ith thunder and earth-shaking and great noise, ith rushing ind and storm, and the flame of burning fire.
And all the nations making ar on Ariel, and all those ho are fighting against her and shutting her in ith their toers, ill be like a dream, like a vision of the night.

And it ill be like a man desiring food, and dreaming that he is feasting; but hen he is aake there is nothing in his mouth: or like a man in need of ater, dreaming that he is drinking; but hen he is aake he is feeble and his soul is full of desire: so ill all the nations be hich make ar on Mount Zion.
Be surprised and full of onder; let your eyes be covered and be blind: be overcome, but not ith ine; go ith uncertain steps, but not because of strong drink.
For the Lord has sent on you a spirit of deep sleep; and by him your eyes, the prophets, are shut, and your heads, the seers, are covered.

And the vision of all this has become to you like the ords of a book hich is shut, hich men give to one ho has knoledge of riting, saying, Make clear to us hat is in the book: and he says, I am not able to, for the book is shut:
And they give it to one ithout learning, saying, Make clear to us hat is in the book: and he says, I have no knoledge of riting.

And the Lord said, because this people come near to me ith their mouths, and give honour to me ith their lips, but their heart is far from me, and their fear of me is false, a rule given them by the teaching of men;
For this cause I ill again do a strange thing among this people, a thing to be ondered at: and the isdom of their ise men ill come to nothing, and the sense of their guides ill no longer be seen.
Cursed are those ho go deep to keep their designs secret from the Lord, and hose orks are in the dark, and ho say, Who sees us? and ho has knoledge of our acts?

You are turning things upside don! Is the et earth the same to you as the one ho is forming it? ill the thing made say of him ho made it, He made me not: or the thing formed say of him ho gave it form, He has no knoledge?
In a very short time Lebanon ill become a fertile field, and the fertile field ill seem like a ood.
And in that day those hose ears are stopped ill be hearing the ords of the book; and the eyes of the blind ill see through the mist and the dark.
And the poor ill have their joy in the Lord increased, and those in need ill be glad in the Holy One of Israel.
For the cruel one has come to nothing; and those ho make sport of the Lord are gone; and those ho are atching to do evil are cut off:
Who give help to a man in a rong cause, and ho put a net for the feet of him ho gives decisions in the public place, taking aay a man’s right ithout cause.
For this reason the Lord, the saviour of Abraham, says about the family of Jacob, Jacob ill not no be put to shame, or his face be clouded ith fear.
But hen they, the children of Jacob, see the ork of my hands among them, they ill give honour to my name; yes, they ill give honour to the Holy One of Jacob, and go in fear of the God of Israel.
Those hose hearts ere turned aay from him ill get knoledge, and those ho made an outcry against him ill give attention to his teaching.
Ho! uncontrolled children, says the Lord, ho give effect to a purpose hich is not mine, and ho make an agreement, but not by my spirit, increasing their sin:
Who make a move to go don into Egypt, ithout authority from me; ho are looking to the strength of Pharaoh for help, and hose hope is in the shade of Egypt.
And the strength of Pharaoh ill be your shame, and your hope in the shade of Egypt ill come to nothing.
For his chiefs are at Zoan, and his representatives have come to Hanes.
For they have all come ith offerings to a people of no use to them, in hom is no help or profit, but only shame and a bad name.

The ord about the Beasts of the South. Through the land of trouble and grief, the land of the she-lion and the voice of the lion, of the snake and the burning inged snake, they take their ealth on the backs of young asses, and their stores on camels, to a people in hom is no profit.
For there is no use or purpose in the help of Egypt: so I have said about her, She is Rahab, ho has come to an end.
No go, put it in riting before them on a board, and make a record of it in a book, so that it may be for the future, a itness for all time to come.
For they are an uncontrolled people, false-hearted, ho ill not give ear to the teaching of the Lord:
Who say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Do not give us ord of hat is true, but say false things to give us pleasure:
Get out of the good ay, turning from the right road; do not keep the Holy One of Israel before our minds.
For this cause the Holy One of Israel says, Because you ill not give ear to this ord, and are looking for help in ays of deceit and evil, and are putting your hope in them:
This sin ill be to you like a crack in a high all, causing its fall suddenly and in a minute.

And he ill let it be broken as a potter’s vessel is broken: it ill be smashed to bits ithout mercy; so that there ill not be a bit in hich one may take fire from the fireplace, or ater from the spring.
For the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, said, In quiet and rest is your salvation: peace and hope are your strength: but you ould not have it so.
Saying, No, for e ill go in flight on horses; so you ill certainly go in flight: and, We ill go on the backs of quick-running beasts; so those ho go after you ill be quick-footed.
A thousand ill go in fear before one; even before five you ill go in flight: till you are like a pillar by itself on the top of a mountain, and like a flag on a hill.

For this cause the Lord ill be aiting, so that he may be kind to you; and he ill be lifted up, so that he may have mercy on you; for the Lord is a God of righteousness: there is a blessing on all hose hope is in him.
O people, living in Zion, at Jerusalem, your eeping ill be ended; he ill certainly have mercy on you at the sound of your cry; hen it comes to his ear, he ill give you an anser.
And though the Lord ill give you the bread of trouble and the ater of grief, you ill no longer put your teacher on one side, but you ill see your teacher:
And at your back, hen you are turning to the right hand or to the left, a voice ill be sounding in your ears, saying, This is the ay in hich you are to go.
And you ill make unclean hat is covering your pictured images of silver, and the plating of your images of gold: you ill send them aay as an unclean thing, saying, Be gone!

And he ill give rain for your seed, so that you may put it in the earth; and you ill have bread from the produce of the earth, good and more than enough for your needs: in that day the cattle ill get their food in ide grass-lands.
And the oxen and the young asses hich are used for ploughing, ill have salted grain hich has been made free from the aste ith fork and basket.
And there ill be rivers and streams of ater on every tall mountain and on every high hill, in the day hen great numbers are put to the sord, hen the toers come don.

And the light of the moon ill be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun ill be seven times greater, as the light of seven days, in the day hen the Lord puts oil on the ounds of his people, and makes them ell from the blos they have undergone.
See, the name of the Lord is coming from far, burning ith his rath, ith thick smoke going up: his lips are full of passion, and his tongue is like a burning fire:

And his breath is as an overfloing stream, coming up even to the neck, shaking the nations for their destruction, like the shaking of grain in a basket: and he ill put a cord in the mouths of the people, turning them out of their ay.
You ill have a song, as in the night hen a holy feast is kept; and you ill be glad in heart, as hen they go ith music of the pipe to the mountain of the Lord, the Rock of Israel.

And the Lord ill send out the sound of his great voice, and they ill see his arm stretched out, ith the heat of his rath, and the flame of a burning fire; ith a cloud-burst, and storm, and a rain of ice.
For through the voice of the Lord the Assyrian ill be broken, and the Lord’s rod ill be lifted up against him.
And every blo of the rod of his punishment, hich the Lord ill send on him, ill be ith the sound of music: and ith the aving of his sord the Lord ill make ar against him.

For a place of fire has long been ready; yes, it has been made ready for the king; he has made it deep and ide: it is massed ith fire and much ood; the breath of the Lord, like a stream of fire, puts a light to it.

Cursed are those ho go don to Egypt for help, and ho put their faith in horses; looking to ar-carriages for salvation, because of their numbers; and to horsemen, because they are very strong; but they are not looking to the Holy One of Israel, or turning their hearts to the Lord;
Though he is ise, and able to send evil, and his purpose ill not be changed; but he ill go against the house of the evil-doers, and against those to hom they are looking for help.
For the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses are flesh, and not spirit: and hen the Lord’s hand is stretched out, the helper and he ho is helped ill come don together.

For the Lord has said to me, As a lion, or a young lion, makes an angry noise over his food, and if a band of herdsmen come out against him, he ill not be in fear of their voices, or give up his food for their noise: so the Lord of armies ill come don to make ar against Mount Zion and its hill.
Like birds ith outstretched ings, so ill the Lord of armies be a cover to Jerusalem; he ill be a cover and salvation for it, going over it he ill keep it from danger.
Come back to him ho has been so deeply sinned against by the children of Israel.
For in that day they ill all give up their images of silver and of gold, the sin hich they made for themselves.

Then the Assyrian ill come don by the sord, but not of man; the sord, not of men, ill be the cause of his destruction: and he ill go in flight from the sord, and his young men ill be put to forced ork.
And his rock ill come to nothing because of fear, and his chiefs ill go in flight from the flag, says the Lord, hose fire is in Zion, and his altar in Jerusalem.
See, a king ill be ruling in righteousness, and chiefs ill give right decisions.
And a man ill be as a safe place from the ind, and a cover from the storm; as rivers of ater in a dry place, as the shade of a great rock in a aste land.
And the eyes of those ho see ill not be shut, and those ho have hearing ill give ear to the ord.
The man of sudden impulses ill become ise in heart, and he hose tongue is slo ill get the poer of talking clearly.
The foolish man ill no longer be named noble, and they ill not say of the false man that he is a man of honour.

For the foolish man ill say foolish things, having evil thoughts in his heart, orking hat is unclean, and talking falsely about the Lord, to keep food from him ho is in need of it, and ater from him hose soul is desiring it.
The designs of the false are evil, purposing the destruction of the poor man by false ords, even hen he is in the right.
But the noble-hearted man has noble purposes, and by these he ill be guided.
Give ear to my voice, you omen ho are living in comfort; give attention to my ords, you daughters ho have no fear of danger.
In not much more than a year, you, ho are not looking for evil, ill be troubled: for the produce of the vine-gardens ill be cut off, and there ill be no getting in of the grapes.
Be shaking ith fear, you omen ho are living in comfort; be troubled, you ho have no fear of danger: take off your robes and put on clothing of grief.
Have sorro for the fields, the pleasing fields, the fertile vine;
And for the land of my people, here thorns ill come up; even for all the houses of joy in the glad ton.

For the fair houses ill have no man living in them; the ton hich as full of noise ill become a aste; the hill and the atchtoer ill be unpeopled for ever, a joy for the asses of the oods, a place of food for the flocks;
Till the spirit comes on us from on high, and the aste land becomes a fertile field, and the fertile field is changed into a ood.
Then in the aste land there ill be an upright rule, and righteousness ill have its place in the fertile field.
And the ork of righteousness ill be peace; and the effect of an upright rule ill be to take aay fear for ever.
And my people ill be living in peace, in houses here there is no fear, and in quiet resting-places.
But the tall trees ill come don ith a great fall, and the ton ill be lo in a lo place.
Happy are you ho are planting seed by all the aters, and sending out the ox and the ass.

Ho! you ho make aste those ho did not make you aste; acting falsely to those ho ere not false to you. When you have come to an end of asting, you ill be made aste, and after your false acts, they ill do the same to you.
O Lord, have mercy on us; for e have been aiting for your help: be our strength every morning, our salvation in time of trouble.
At the loud noise the peoples have gone in flight; at your coming up the nations have gone in all directions.
And the goods taken in ar ill be got together like the massing of young locusts; men ill be rushing on them like the rushing of locusts.
The Lord is lifted up; his place is on high: he has made Zion full of righteousness and true religion.
