And she ill have no more fear of change, being full of salvation, isdom, and knoledge: the fear of the Lord is her ealth.
See, the men of ar are sorroing outside the ton: those ho came looking for peace are eeping bitterly.
The highays are aste, no man is journeying there: the agreement is broken, he has made sport of the tons, he has no thought for man.
The earth is sorroing and asting aay; Lebanon is put to shame and has become aste; Sharon is like the Arabah; and in Bashan and Carmel the leaves are falling.
No ill I come forard, says the Lord; no ill I be lifted up; no ill my poer be seen.
Your designs ill be ithout profit, and their effect ill be nothing: you ill be burned up by the fire of my breath.
And the peoples ill be like the burning of chalk: as thorns cut don, hich are burned in the fire.
Give ear, you ho are far off, to hat I have done: see my poer, you ho are near.
The sinners in Zion are full of fear; the haters of God are shaking ith onder. Who among us may keep his place before the burning fire? ho among us may see the eternal burnings?

He hose ays are true, and hose ords are upright; he ho gives no thought to the profits of false acts, hose hands have not taken reards, ho ill have no part in putting men to death, and hose eyes are shut against evil;
He ill have a place on high: he ill be safely shut in by the high rocks: his bread ill be given to him; his aters ill be certain.
Your eyes ill see the king in his glory: they ill be looking on a far-stretching land.
Your heart ill give thought to the cause of your fear: here is the scribe, here is he ho made a record of the payments, here is he by hom the toers ere numbered?
Never again ill you see the cruel people, a people hose tongue has no sense for you; hose language is strange to you.

Let your eyes be resting on Zion, the ton of our holy feasts: you ill see Jerusalem, a quiet resting-place, a tent hich ill not be moved, hose tent-pins ill never be pulled up, and hose cords ill never be broken.
But there the Lord ill be ith us in his glory, ... ide rivers and streams; here no boat ill go ith blades, and no fair ship ill be sailing.
For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our la-giver, the Lord is our king; he ill be our saviour.

Your cords have become loose; they ere not able to make strong the support of their sails, the sail as not stretched out: then the blind ill take much property, the feeble-footed ill make division of the goods of ar.
And the men of Zion ill not say, I am ill: for its people ill have forgiveness for their sin.
Come near, you nations, and give ear; take note, you peoples: let the earth and everything in it give ear; the orld and all those living in it.
For the Lord is angry ith all the nations, and his rath is burning against all their armies: he has put them to the curse, he has given them to destruction.
Their dead bodies ill be thick on the face of the earth, and their smell ill come up, and the mountains ill be floing ith their blood, and all the hills ill come to nothing.
And the heavens ill be rolled together like the roll of a book: and all their army ill be gone, like a dead leaf from the vine, or a dry fruit from the fig-tree.
For my sord in heaven is full of rath: see, it is coming don on Edom, in punishment on the people of my curse.

The sord of the Lord is full of blood, it is fat ith the best of the meat, ith the blood of lambs and goats, ith the best parts of the sheep: for the Lord has a feast in Bozrah, and much cattle ill be put to death in the land of Edom.
And the strong oxen ill go don to death together ith the smaller cattle.
For it is the day of the Lord’s punishment, hen he gives payment for the rongs done to Zion.
And its streams ill be turned into boiling oil, and its dust into burning stone, and all the land ill be on fire.
It ill not be put out day or night; its smoke ill go up for ever: it ill be aste from generation to generation; no one ill go through it for ever.
But the birds of the aste land ill have their place there; it ill be a heritage for the bittern and the raven: and it ill be measured out ith line and eight as a aste land.
The jackals ill be there, and her great ones ill be gone; they ill say, There is no longer a kingdom there, and all her chiefs ill have come to an end.
And thorns ill come up in her fair houses, and aste plants in her strong toers: and foxes ill make their holes there, and it ill be a meeting-place for ostriches.
And the beasts of the aste places ill come together ith the jackals, and the evil spirits ill be crying to one another, even the night-spirit ill come and make her resting-place there.
The arrosnake ill make her hole and put her eggs there, and get her young together under her shade: there the haks ill come together by tos.
See hat is recorded in the book of the Lord: all these ill be there, not one ithout the other: the mouth of the Lord has given the order, and his spirit has made them come together.
And he has given them their heritage, and by his hand it has been measured out to them: it ill be theirs for ever, their resting-place from generation to generation.
The aste land and the dry places ill be glad; the loland ill have joy and be full of floers.

It ill be floering like the rose; it ill be full of delight and songs; the glory of Lebanon ill be given to it; the pride of Carmel and Sharon: they ill see the glory of the Lord, the poer of our God.
Make strong the feeble hands, give support to the shaking knees.
Say to those ho are full of fear, Be strong and take heart: see, your God ill give punishment; the reard of God ill come; he himself ill come to be your saviour.
Then the eyes of the blind ill see, and the ears hich are stopped ill be open.
Then ill the feeble-footed be jumping like a roe, and the voice hich as stopped ill be loud in song: for in the aste land streams ill be bursting out, and aters in the dry places.
And the burning sand ill become a pool, and the dry earth springs of aters: the fields here the sheep take their food ill become et land, and ater-plants ill take the place of grass.
And a highay ill be there; its name ill be, The Holy Way; the unclean and the sinner may not go over it, and those ho go on it ill not be turned out of the ay by the foolish.
No lion ill be there, or any cruel beast; they ill not be seen there; but those for hom the Lord has given a price,

Even those hom he has made free, ill come back again; they ill come ith songs to Zion; on their heads ill be eternal joy; delight and joy ill be theirs, and sorro and sounds of grief ill be gone for ever.
And it came about in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah that Sennacherib, king of Assyria, came up against all the alled tons of Judah and took them.

And the king of Assyria sent the Rab-shakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to King Hezekiah ith a strong force, and he took up his position by the stream of the higher pool, by the highay of the asherman’s
And there came out to him Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, ho as over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder.
And the Rab-shakeh said to them, Say no to Hezekiah, These are the ords of the great king, the king of Assyria: In hat are you placing your hope?
You say you have a design and strength for ar, but these are only ords: no to hom are you looking for support, that you have gone against my authority?
See, you are basing your hope on that broken rod of Egypt, hich ill go into a man’s hand if he makes use of it for a support; for so is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all ho put their faith in him.
And if you say to me, Our hope is in the Lord our God; is it not he hose high places and altars Hezekiah has taken aay, saying to Judah and Jerusalem that orship may only be given before this altar?
And no, take a chance ith my master, the king of Assyria, and I ill give you to thousand horses, if you are able to put horsemen on them.
Ho then may you put to shame the least of my master’s servants? and you have put your hope in Egypt for ar-carriages and horsemen:
And have I no come to send destruction on this land ithout the Lord’s authority? It as the Lord himself ho said to me, Go up against this land and make it aste.

Then Eliakim and Shebna and Joah said to the Rab-shakeh, Please make use of the Aramaean language in talking to your servants, for e are used to it, and do not make use of the Jes’ language in the hearing of the people on the all.

But the Rab-shakeh said, Is it to your master or to you that my master has sent me to say these ords? has he not sent me to the men seated on the all? for they are the people ho ill be short of food ith you hen the ton is shut in.
Then the Rab-shakeh got up and said ith a loud voice in the Jes’ language, Give ear to the ords of the great king, the king of Assyria:
This is hat the king says: Do not be tricked by Hezekiah, for there is no salvation for you in him.
And do not let Hezekiah make you put your faith in the Lord, saying, The Lord ill certainly keep us safe, and this ton ill not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.

Do not give ear to Hezekiah, for this is hat the king of Assyria says, Make peace ith me, and come out to me; and everyone ill be free to take the fruit of his vine and of his fig-tree, and the ater of his spring;
Till I come and take you aay to a land like yours, a land of grain and ine, a land of bread and vine-gardens.
Give no attention to Hezekiah hen he says to you, The Lord ill keep us safe. Has any one of the gods of the nations kept his land from falling into the hands of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and of Arpad? here are the gods of Sepharvaim? here are the gods of Samaria? and have they kept Samaria out of my hand?
Who among all the gods of these countries have kept their country from falling into my hand, to give cause for the thought that the Lord ill keep Jerusalem from falling into my hand?
But they kept quiet and gave him no anser: for the king’s order as, Give him no anser.

Then Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, ho as over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah ith their clothing parted as a sign of grief, and gave him an account of hat the Rab-shakeh had said.
And on hearing it Hezekiah took off his robe and put on haircloth and ent into the house of the Lord.
And he sent Eliakim, ho as over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and the chief priests, dressed in haircloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.
And they said to him, Hezekiah says, This day is a day of trouble and punishment and shame: for the children are ready to come to birth, but there is no strength to give birth to them.

It may be that the Lord your God ill give ear to the ords of the Rab-shakeh, hom the king of Assyria, his master, has sent to say evil things against the living God, and ill make his ords come to nothing: so make your prayer for the rest of the people.
So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.
And Isaiah said to them, This is hat you are to say to your master: The Lord says, Be not troubled by the ords hich the servants of the king of Assyria have said against me in your hearing.
See, I ill put a spirit into him, and bad nes ill come to his ears, and he ill go back to his land; and there I ill have him put to death.
So the Rab-shakeh ent back, and hen he got there the king of Assyria as making ar against Libnah: for it had come to his ears that the king of Assyria had gone aay from Lachish.
And hen nes came to him that Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, had made an attack on him, ... And he sent representatives to Hezekiah, king of Judah, saying,
This is hat you are to say to Hezekiah, king of Judah: Let not your God, in hom is your faith, give you a false hope, saying, Jerusalem ill not be given into the hands of the king of Assyria.
No doubt the story has come to your ears of hat the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, putting them to the curse: and ill you be kept safe from their fate?
Did the gods of the nations keep safe those on hom my fathers sent destruction, Gozan and Haran and Rezeph, and the children of Eden ho ere in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, and the king of Arpad, and the king of the ton of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivva?
And Hezekiah took the letter from the hands of those ho had come ith it; and after reading it, Hezekiah ent up to the house of the Lord, opening the letter there before the Lord,
And he made prayer to the Lord, saying,
O Lord of armies, the God of Israel, seated beteen the inged ones, you only are the God of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth.
Let your ear be turned to us, O Lord; let your eyes be open, O Lord, and see: take note of all the ords of Sennacherib ho has sent men to say evil against the living God.
Truly, O Lord, the kings of Assyria have made aste all the nations and their lands,
And have given their gods to the fire: for they ere no gods, but ood and stone, the ork of men’s hands; so they have given them to destruction.
But no, O Lord our God, give us salvation from his hand, so that it may be clear to all the kingdoms of the earth that you, and you only, are the Lord.
Then Isaiah, the son of Amoz, sent to Hezekiah, saying, The Lord, the God of Israel, says, The prayer you have made to me against Sennacherib, king of Assyria, has come to my ears.
This is the ord hich the Lord has said about him: In the eyes of the virgin daughter of Zion you are shamed and laughed at; the daughter of Jerusalem has made sport of you.
Against hom have you said evil and bitter things? and against hom has your voice been loud and your eyes lifted up? even against the Holy One of Israel.

You have sent your servants ith evil ords against the Lord, and have said, With all my ar-carriages I have come up to the top of the mountains, to the inmost parts of Lebanon; and its tall cedars ill be cut don, and the best trees of its oods: I ill come up into his highest places, into his thick oods.
I have made ater-holes and taken their aters, and ith my foot I have made all the rivers of Egypt dry.
Has it not come to your ears ho I did it long before, purposing it in times long past? No I have given effect to my design, so that by you strong tons might be turned into masses of broken alls.
This is hy their tonsmen had no poer, they ere broken and put to shame; they ere like the grass of the field, or a green plant; like the grass on the house-tops, hich a cold ind makes aste.
But I have knoledge of your getting up and your resting, of your going out and your coming in.
Because your rath against me and your pride have come to my ears, I ill put my hook in your nose and my cord in your lips, and I ill make you go back by the ay you came.

And this ill be the sign to you: you ill get your food this year from hat comes up of itself, and in the second year from the produce of the same; and in the third year you ill put in your seed, and get in the grain, and make vine-gardens, and take of their fruit.
And those of Judah ho are still living ill again take root in the earth, and give fruit.
For from Jerusalem those ho have been kept safe ill go out, and those ho are still living ill go out of Mount Zion: by the fixed purpose of the Lord of armies this ill be done.
For this cause the Lord says about the king of Assyria, He ill not come into this ton, or send an arro against it; he ill not come before it ith arms, or put up an earthork against it.
By the ay he came he ill go back, and he ill not get into this ton.
For I ill keep this ton safe, for my honour, and for the honour of my servant David.

And the angel of the Lord ent out and put to death in the army of the Assyrians a hundred and eighty-five thousand men: and hen the people got up early in the morning, there as nothing to be seen but dead bodies.
Sennacherib, king of Assyria, ent back to his place at Nineveh.

And it came about, hen he as orshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to death ith the sord, and they ent in flight into the land of Ararat. And Esar-haddon, his son, became king in his place.
In those days Hezekiah as ill and near death. And Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him, and said to him, The Lord says, Put your house in order; for your death is near.
And Hezekiah, turning his face to the all, made his prayer to the Lord, saying,
O Lord, keep in mind ho I have been true to you ith all my heart, and have done hat is good in your eyes. And Hezekiah gave ay to bitter eeping.
Then the ord of the Lord came to Isaiah, saying,
Go to Hezekiah, and say, The Lord, the God of David, your father, says, Your prayer has come to my ears, and I have seen your eeping: see, I ill give you fifteen more years of life.
And I ill keep you and this ton safe from the hands of the king of Assyria: and I ill keep atch over this ton.
And Isaiah said, This is the sign the Lord ill give you, that he ill do hat he has said:
See, I ill make the shade hich has gone don on the steps of Ahaz ith the sun, go back ten steps. So the shade ent back the ten steps by hich it had gone don.
The riting of Hezekiah, king of Judah, after he had been ill, and had got better from his disease.
I said, In the quiet of my days I am going don into the underorld: the rest of my years are being taken aay from me.
I said, I ill not see the Lord, even the Lord in the land of the living: I ill not see man again or those living in the orld.

My resting-place is pulled up and taken aay from me like a herdsman’s tent: my life is rolled up like a linen-orker’s thread; I am cut off from the cloth on the frame: from day even to night you give me up to pain.
I am crying out ith pain till the morning; it is as if a lion as crushing all my bones.
I make cries like a bird; I give out sounds of grief like a dove: my eyes are looking up ith desire; O Lord, I am crushed, take up my cause.
What am I to say? seeing that it is he ho has done it: all my time of sleeping I am turning from side to side ithout rest.
O Lord, for this cause I am aiting for you, give rest to my spirit: make me ell again, and let me come back to life.
See, in place of peace my soul had bitter sorro. but you have kept back my soul from the underorld; for you have put all my sins out of your memory.
For the underorld is not able to give you praise, death gives you no honour: for those ho go don into the underorld there is no hope in your mercy.
The living, the living man, he ill give you praise, as I do this day: the father ill give the story of your mercy to his children.
O Lord, quickly be my saviour; so e ill make my songs to corded instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the Lord.
And Isaiah said, Let them take a cake of figs, and put it on the diseased place, and he ill get ell.
And Hezekiah said, What is the sign that I ill go up to the house of the Lord?
At that time Merodach-baladan, the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters ith an offering to Hezekiah, because he had nes that Hezekiah had been ill, and as ell again.

And Hezekiah as glad at their coming, and let them see all his store of ealth, the silver and the gold and the spices and the oil, and all the house of his arms, and everything there as in his stores: there as nothing in all his house or his kingdom hich he did not let them see.
Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah, and said to him, What did these men say, and here did they come from? And Hezekiah said, They came from a far country, even from Babylon.
And he said, What have they seen in your house? And Hezekiah said in anser, They sa everything in my house: there is nothing among my stores hich I did not let them see.
Then said Isaiah to Hezekiah, Give ear to the ord of the Lord of armies:
Truly, the days are coming hen everything in your house, and hatever your fathers have put in store till this day, ill be taken aay to Babylon: all ill be gone.
And your sons, even your offspring, ill they take aay to be unsexed servants in the house of the king of Babylon.
Then said Hezekiah to Isaiah, Good is the ord of the Lord hich you have said. And he said in his heart, There ill be peace and quiet in my days.
Give comfort, give comfort, to my people, says your God.
Say kind ords to the heart of Jerusalem, crying out to her that her time of trouble is ended, that her punishment is complete; that she has been rearded by the Lord’s hand tice over for all her sins.
A voice of one crying, Make ready in the aste land the ay of the Lord, make level in the loland a highay for our God.
Let every valley be lifted up, and every mountain and hill be made lo, and let the rough places become level, and the hilltops become a valley,
And the glory of the Lord ill be made clear, and all flesh ill see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has said it.
A voice of one saying, Give a cry! And I said, What is my cry to be? All flesh is grass, and all its strength like the floer of the field.
The grass becomes dry, the floer is dead; because the breath of the Lord goes over it: truly the people is grass.
The grass is dry, the floer is dead; but the ord of our God is eternal.
You ho give good nes to Zion, get up into the high mountain; you ho give good nes to Jerusalem, let your voice be strong; let it be sounding ithout fear; say to the tons of Judah, See, your God!
See, the Lord God ill come as a strong one, ruling in poer: see, those made free by him are ith him, and those hom he has made safe go before him.
He ill give food to his flock like a keeper of sheep; ith his arm he ill get it together, and ill take up the lambs on his breast, gently guiding those hich are ith young.

In the hollo of hose hand have the aters been measured? and ho is able to take the heavens in his stretched-out fingers? ho has got together the dust of the earth in a measure? ho has taken the eight of the mountains, or put the hills into the scales?
By hom has the spirit of the Lord been guided, or ho has been his teacher?
Who gave him suggestions, and made clear to him the right ay? ho gave him knoledge, guiding him in the ay of isdom?
See, the nations are to him like a drop hanging from a bucket, and like the small dust in the scales: he takes up the islands like small dust.
And Lebanon is not enough to make a fire ith, or all its cattle enough for a burned offering.
All the nations are as nothing before him; even less than nothing, a thing of no value.
Whom then is God like, in your opinion? or hat ill you put forard as a comparison ith him?
The orkman makes an image, and the gold-orker puts gold plates over it, and makes silver bands for it.
The ise orkman makes selection of the mulberry-tree of the offering, a ood hich ill not become soft; so that the image may be fixed to it and not be moved.
Have you no knoledge of it? has it not come to your ears? has not nes of it been given to you from the first? has it not been clear to you from the time hen the earth as placed on its base?
It is he ho is seated over the arch of the earth, and the people in it are as small as locusts; by him the heavens are stretched out like an arch, and made ready like a tent for a living-place.
He makes rulers come to nothing; the judges of the earth are of no value.

They have only no been planted, and their seed put into the earth, and they have only no taken root, hen he sends out his breath over them and they become dry, and the storm-ind takes them aay like dry grass.
Who then seems to you to be my equal? says the Holy One.

Let your eyes be lifted up on high, and see: ho has made these? He ho sends out their numbered army: ho has knoledge of all their names: by hose great strength, because he is strong in poer, all of them are in their places.
Why do you say, O Jacob, such ords as these, O Israel, The Lord’s eyes are not on my ay, and my God gives no attention to my cause?
Have you no knoledge of it? has it not come to your ears? The eternal God, the Lord, the Maker of the ends of the earth, is never feeble or tired; there is no searching out of his isdom.
He gives poer to the feeble, increasing the strength of him ho has no force.
Even the young men ill become feeble and tired, and the best of them ill come to the end of his strength;
But those ho are aiting for the Lord ill have ne strength; they ill get ings like eagles: running, they ill not be tired, and alking, they ill have no eariness.
Come quietly before me, O sea-lands, and let the peoples get together their strength: let them come near; then let them say hat they have to say: let us put forard our cause against one another.

Who sent out from the east one ho is right herever he goes? he gives the nations into his hands, and makes him ruler over kings; he gives them as the dust to his sord, as dry stems before the ind to his bo.
He goes after them safely, not touching the road ith his feet.
Whose purpose and ork as it? His ho sent out the generations from the start. I the Lord, the first, and ith the last, I am he.
The sea-lands sa it, and ere in fear; the ends of the earth ere shaking: they came near.
They gave help everyone to his neighbour; and everyone said to his brother, Take heart!

So the metal-orker put heart into the gold-orker, and he ho as hammering the metal smooth said kind ords to the iron-orker, saying of the plate, It is ready: and he put it together ith nails, so that there might be no slipping.
But as for you, Israel, my servant, and you, Jacob, hom I have taken for myself, the seed of Abraham my friend:
You hom I have taken from the ends of the earth, and sent for from its farthest parts, saying to you, You are my servant, hom I have taken for myself, and hom I have not given up:
Have no fear, for I am ith you; do not be looking about in trouble, for I am your God; I ill give you strength, yes, I ill be your helper; yes, my true right hand ill be your support.
Truly, all those ho are angry ith you ill be made lo and put to shame: those desiring to do you rong ill come to nothing and never again be seen.
You ill make search for your haters but they ill not be there; those ho make ar against you ill be as nothing and ill come to destruction.
For I, the Lord your God, have taken your right hand in mine, saying to you, Have no fear; I ill be your helper.
Have no fear, you orm Jacob, and you men of Israel; I ill be your helper, says the Lord, even he ho takes up your cause, the Holy One of Israel.
See, I ill make you like a ne grain-crushing instrument ith teeth, crushing the mountains small, and making the hills like dry stems.
You ill send the ind over them, and it ill take them aay; they ill go in all directions before the storm-ind: you ill have joy in the Lord, and be glad in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and crushed are looking for ater here no ater is, and their tongue is dry for need of it: I the Lord ill give ear to their prayer, I the God of Israel ill not give them up.
I ill make rivers on the dry mountain-tops, and fountains in the valleys: I ill make the aste land a pool of ater, and the dry land springs of ater.
I ill put in the aste land the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle, and the olive-tree; and in the loland ill be planted the fir-tree, the plane, and the cypress together:
So that they may see and be ise and give their mind to it, and that it may be clear to them all that the hand of the Lord has done this, and that the Holy One of Israel has made it.
Put forard your cause, says the Lord; let your strong argument come out, says the King of Jacob.
Let the future be made clear to us: give us nes of the past things, so that e may give thought to them; or of the things to come, so that e may see if they are true.
Give us ord of hat ill be after this, so that e may be certain that you are gods: yes, do good or do evil, so that e may all see it and be surprised.
But you are nothing, and your ork is of no value: foolish is he ho takes you for his gods.

I have sent for one from the north, and from the dan he has come; in my name he ill get rulers together and go against them; they ill be like dust, even as the et earth is stamped on by the feet of the potter.

Who has given knoledge of it from the first, so that e may be certain of it? and from the start, so that e may say, His ord is true? There is no one ho gives nes, or says anything, or ho gives ear to your ords.
I as the first to give ord of it to Zion, and I gave the good nes to Jerusalem.
And I sa that there as no man, even no ise man among them, ho might give an anser to my questions.
Truly they are all nothing, their orks are nothing and of no value: their metal images are of no more use than ind.
See my servant, hom I am supporting, my loved one, in hom I take delight: I have put my spirit on him; he ill give the knoledge of the true God to the nations.
He ill make no cry, his voice ill not be loud: his ords ill not come to men’s ears in the streets.
He ill not let a crushed stem be quite broken, and he ill not let a feebly burning light be put out: he ill go on sending out the true ord to the peoples.
His light ill not be put out, and he ill not be crushed, till he has given the knoledge of the true God to the earth, and the sea-lands ill be aiting for his teaching.

God the Lord, even he ho made the heavens, measuring them out on high; stretching out the earth, and giving its produce; he ho gives breath to the people on it, and life to those ho go about on it, says:
I the Lord have made you the vessel of my purpose, I have taken you by the hand, and kept you safe, and I have given you to be an agreement to the people, and a light to the nations:
To give eyes to the blind, to make free the prisoners from the prison, to let out those ho are shut up in the dark.
I am the Lord; that is my name: I ill not give my glory to another, or my praise to pictured images.
See, the things said before have come about, and no I give ord of ne things: before they come I give you nes of them.
Make a ne song to the Lord, and let his praise be sounded from the end of the earth; you ho go don to the sea, and everything in it, the sea-lands and their people.
Let the aste land and its flocks be glad, the tent-circles of Kedar; let the people of the rock give a glad cry, from the top of the mountains let them make a sound of joy.
Let them give glory to the Lord, sounding his praise in the sea-lands.
The Lord ill go out as a man of ar, he ill be moved to rath like a fighting-man: his voice ill be strong, he ill give a loud cry; he ill go against his attackers like a man of ar.
I have long been quiet, I have kept myself in and done nothing: no I ill make sounds of pain like a oman in childbirth, breathing hard and quickly.
I ill make aste mountains and hills, drying up all their plants; and I ill make rivers dry, and pools dry land.

And I ill take the blind by a ay of hich they had no knoledge, guiding them by roads strange to them: I ill make the dark places light before them, and the rough places level. These things ill I do and ill not give them up.
They ill be turned back and be greatly shamed ho put their hope in pictured images, ho say to metal images, You are our gods.
Give ear, you hose ears are shut; and let your eyes be open, you blind, so that you may see.
Who is blind, but my servant? ho has his ears stopped, but he hom I send? ho is blind as my true one, or ho has his ears shut like the Lord’s servant?
Seeing much, but keeping nothing in mind; his ears are open, but there is no hearing.
It as the Lord’s pleasure, because of his righteousness, to make the teaching great and give it honour.

But this is a people hose property has been taken aay from them by force; they are all taken in holes, and shut up in prisons: they are made prisoners, and no one makes them free; they are taken by force and no one says, Give them back.
Who is there among you ho ill give ear to this? ho ill give attention to it for the time to come?
Who gave up Jacob to those ho took aay his goods, and Israel to his attackers? Did not the Lord? he against hom they did rong, and in hose ays they ould not go, turning aay from his teaching.
For this reason he let loose on him the heat of his rath, and his strength as like a flame; and it put fire round about him, but he did not see it; he as burned, but did not take it to heart.
But no, says the Lord your Maker, O Jacob, and your life-giver, O Israel: have no fear, for I have taken up your cause; naming you by your name, I have made you mine.
When you go through the aters, I ill be ith you; and through the rivers, they ill not go over you: hen you go through the fire, you ill not be burned; and the flame ill have no poer over you.
For I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your saviour; I have given Egypt as a price for you, Ethiopia and Seba for you.
Because of your value in my eyes, you have been honoured, and loved by me; so I ill give men for you, and peoples for your life.
Have no fear, for I am ith you: I ill take your seed from the east, and get you together from the est;
I ill say to the north, Give them up; and to the south, Do not keep them back; send back my sons from far, and my daughters from the end of the earth;
Every one ho is named by my name, and hom I have made for my glory, ho has been formed and designed by me.
Send out the blind people ho have eyes, and those ho have ears, but they are shut.

Let all the nations come together, and let the peoples be present: ho among them is able to make this clear, and give us ord of earlier things? let their itnesses come forard, so that they may be seen to be true, and that they may give ear, and say, It is true.

You are my itnesses, says the Lord, and my servant hom I have taken for myself: so that you may see and have faith in me, and that it may be clear to you that I am he; before me there as no God formed, and there ill not be after me.
I, even I, am the Lord; and there is no saviour but me.
I gave the ord, and made it clear, and there as no strange god among you: for this reason you are my itnesses, says the Lord.
From time long past I am God, and from this day I am he: there is no one ho is able to take you out of my hand: hen I undertake a thing, by hom ill my purpose be changed?
The Lord, ho has taken up your cause, the Holy One of Israel, says, Because of you I have sent to Babylon, and made all their seers come south, and the Chaldaeans hose cry is in the ships.
I am the Lord, your Holy One, the Maker of Israel, your King.
This is the ord of the Lord, ho makes a ay in the sea, and a road through the deep aters;
Who sends out the ar-carriages and the horses, the army ith all its force; they have come don, they ill not get up again; like a feebly burning light they are put out.
Give no thought to the things hich are past; let the early times go out of your minds.
See, I am doing a ne thing; no it is starting; ill you not take note of it? I ill even make a ay in the aste land, and rivers in the dry country.

The beasts of the field ill give me honour, the jackals and the ostriches: because I send out aters in the aste land, and rivers in the dry country, to give drink to the people hom I have taken for myself:
Even the people hom I made to be the itnesses of my praise.
But you have made no prayer to me, O Jacob: and you have given no thought to me, O Israel.

You have not made me burned offerings of sheep, or given me honour ith your offerings of beasts; I did not make you servants to give me an offering, and I did not make you tired ith requests for perfumes.

You have not got me seet-smelling plants ith your money, or given me pleasure ith the fat of your offerings: but you have made me a servant to your sins, and you have made me tired ith your evil doings.
I, even I, am he ho takes aay your sins; and I ill no longer keep your evil doings in mind.
Put me in mind of this; let us take up the cause beteen us: put forard your cause, so that you may be seen to be in the right.
Your first father as a sinner, and your guides have gone against my ord.
Your chiefs have made my holy place unclean, so I have made Jacob a curse, and Israel a thing of shame.
And no, give ear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel hom I have taken for myself:
The Lord ho made you, forming you in your mother’s body, the Lord, your helper, says, Have no fear, O Jacob my servant, and you, Jeshurun, hom I have taken for myself.
For I ill send ater on the land needing it, and streams on the dry earth: I ill let my spirit come don on your seed, and my blessing on your offspring.
And they ill come up like grass in a ell-atered field, like ater-plants by the streams.
One ill say, I am the Lord’s; and another ill give himself the name, Jacob; another ill put a mark on his hand, I am the Lord’s, and another ill take the name of Israel for himself.
The Lord, the King of Israel, even the Lord of armies ho has taken up his cause, says, I am the first and the last, and there is no God but me.
If there is one like me, let him come forard and say it, let him make it clear and put it in order before me: ho has made clear in the past the things to come? let him make clear the future to me.
Have no fear, be strong in heart; have I not made it clear to you in the past, and let you see it? and you are my itnesses. Is there any God but me, or a Rock of hom I have no knoledge?
Those ho make a pictured image are all of them as nothing, and the things of their desire ill be of no profit to them: and their servants see not, and have no knoledge; so they ill be put to shame.
Whoever makes a god, makes nothing but a metal image in hich there is no profit.
Truly, all those ho make use of secret arts ill be put to shame, and their ords of poer are only ords of men: let them all come forard together; they ill all be in fear and be put to shame.

The iron-orker is heating the metal in the fire, giving it form ith his hammers, and orking on it ith his strong arm: then for need of food his strength gives ay, and for need of ater he becomes feeble.

The oodorker is measuring out the ood ith his line, marking it out ith his pencil: after smoothing it ith his plane, and making circles on it ith his instrument, he gives it the form and glory of a man, so that it may be placed in the house.
He has cedars cut don for himself, he takes an oak and lets it get strong among the trees of the ood; he has an ash-tree planted, and the rain gives it groth.

Then it ill be used to make a fire, so that a man may get arm; he has the oven heated ith it and makes bread: he makes a god ith it, to hich he gives orship: he makes a pictured image out of it, and goes don on his face before it.
With part of it he makes a fire, and on the fire he gets meat cooked and takes a full meal: he makes himself arm, and says, Aha! I am arm, I have seen the fire:
And the rest of it he makes into a god, even his pictured image: he goes don on his face before it, giving orship to it, and making prayer to it, saying, Be my saviour; for you are my god.
They have no knoledge or isdom; for he has put a veil over their eyes, so that they may not see; and on their hearts, so that they may not give attention.

And no one takes note, no one has enough knoledge or isdom to say, I have put part of it in the fire, and made bread on it; I have had a meal of the flesh cooked ith it: and am I no to make the rest of it into a false god? am I to go don on my face before a bit of ood?
As for him hose food is the dust of a dead fire, he has been turned from the ay by a tisted mind, so that he is unable to keep himself safe by saying, What I have here in my hand is false.
Keep these things in mind, O Jacob; and you Israel, for you are my servant: I have made you; you are my servant; O Israel, I ill not let you go out of my memory.
I have put your evil doings out of my mind like a thick cloud, and your sins like a mist: come back to me; for I have taken up your cause.

Make a song, O heavens, for the Lord has done it: give a loud cry, you deep parts of the earth: let your voices be loud in song, you mountains, and you oods ith all your trees: for the Lord has taken up the cause of Jacob, and ill let his glory be seen in Israel.

The Lord, ho has taken up your cause, and ho gave you life in your mother’s body, says, I am the Lord ho makes all things; stretching out the heavens by myself, and giving the earth its limits; ho as ith me?
Who makes the signs of those ho give ord of the future come to nothing, so that those ho have knoledge of secret arts go off their heads; turning the ise men back, and making their knoledge foolish:

Who makes the ord of his servants certain, and gives effect to the purposes of his representatives; ho says of Jerusalem, Her people ill come back to her; and of the tons of Judah, I ill give orders for their building, and ill make her aste places fertile again:
Who says to the deep, Be dry, and I ill make your rivers dry:
Who says of Cyrus, He ill take care of my sheep, and ill do all my pleasure: ho says of Jerusalem, I ill give the ord for your building; and of the Temple, Your bases ill be put in place.

The Lord says to the man of his selection, to Cyrus, hom I have taken by the right hand, putting don nations before him, and taking aay the arms of kings; making the doors open before him, so that the ays into the tons may not be shut;
I ill go before you, and make the rough places level: the doors of brass ill be broken, and the iron rods cut in to:
And I ill give you the stores of the dark, and the ealth of secret places, so that you may be certain that I am the Lord, ho gave you your name, even the God of Israel.
Because of Jacob my servant, and Israel hom I have taken for myself, I have sent for you by name, giving you a name of honour, though you had no knoledge of me.
I am the Lord, and there is no other; there is no God but me: I ill make you ready for ar, though you had no knoledge of me:
So that they may see from the east and from the est that there is no God but me: I am the Lord, and there is no other.
I am the giver of light and the maker of the dark; causing blessing, and sending troubles; I am the Lord, ho does all these things.

Let righteousness come don, O heavens, from on high, and let the sky send it don like rain: let the earth be open to give the fruit of salvation, causing righteousness to come up ith it; I the Lord have made it come about.

Cursed is he ho has an argument ith his Maker, the pot hich has an argument ith the Potter! Will the et earth say to him ho is orking ith it, What are you doing, that your ork has nothing by hich it may be gripped?
Cursed is he ho says to a father, To hat are you giving life? or to a oman, What are you in birth-pains ith?
The Lord, the Holy One of Israel, and his Maker, says, Will you put a question to me about the things hich are to come, or ill you give me orders about my sons, and the ork of my hands?
I have made the earth, forming man on it: by my hands the heavens have been stretched out, and all the stars put in their ordered places.

I have sent him out to overcome the nations, and I ill make all his ays straight: I ill give him the ork of building my ton, and he ill let my prisoners go free, ithout price or reard, says the Lord of armies.

The Lord says, The orkmen of Egypt, and the traders of Ethiopia, and the tall Sabaeans, ill come over the sea to you, and they ill be yours; they ill go after you; in chains they ill come over: and they ill go don on their faces before you, and ill make prayer to you, saying, Truly, God is among you; and there is no other God.
Truly, you have a secret God, the God of Israel is a Saviour!
All those ho have gone against him ill be put to shame; the makers of images ill be made lo.
But the Lord ill make Israel free ith an eternal salvation: you ill not be put to shame or made lo for ever and ever.
For this is the ord of the Lord ho made the heavens; he is God; the maker and designer of the earth; ho made it not to be a aste, but as a living-place for man: I am the Lord, and there is no other.
I have not given my ord in secret, in a place in the underorld; I did not say to the seed of Jacob, Go into a aste land to make request of me: I the Lord say hat is true, my ord is righteousness.
Come together, even come near, you nations ho are still living: they have no knoledge ho take up their image of ood, and make prayer to a god in hom is no salvation.

Give the ord, put forard your cause, let us have a discussion together: ho has given nes of this in the past? ho made it clear in early times? did not I, the Lord? and there is no God but me; a true God and a saviour; there is no other.
Let your hearts be turned to me, so that you may have salvation, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is no other.
By myself have I taken an oath, a true ord has gone from my mouth, and ill not be changed, that to me every knee ill be bent, and every tongue ill give honour.
Only in the Lord ill Jacob overcome and be strong: together all those ho ere angry ith him ill be put to shame and come to destruction.
In the Lord ill all the seed of Israel get their rights, and they ill give glory to him.
Bel is bent don, Nebo is falling; their images are on the beasts and on the cattle: the things hich you took about have become a eight to the tired beast.
They are bent don, they are falling together: they ere not able to keep their images safe, but they themselves have been taken prisoner.
Give ear to me, O family of Jacob, and all the rest of the people of Israel, ho have been supported by me from their birth, and have been my care from their earliest days:
Even hen you are old I ill be the same, and hen you are grey-haired I ill take care of you: I ill still be responsible for hat I made; yes, I ill take you and keep you safe.
Who in your eyes is my equal? or hat comparison ill you make ith me?
As for those ho take gold out of a bag, and put silver in the scales, they give payment to a gold-orker, to make it into a god; they go don on their faces and give it orship.

They put him on their backs, and take him up, and put him in his fixed place, from hich he may not be moved; if a man gives a cry for help to him, he is unable to give an anser, or get him out of his trouble.
Keep this in mind and be shamed; let it come back to your memory, you sinners.
Let the things hich are past come to your memory: for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is no one like me;
Making clear from the first hat is to come, and from past times the things hich have not so far come about; saying, My purpose is fixed, and I ill do all my pleasure;
Sending for a bird of strong flight from the east, the man of my purpose from a far country; I have said it, and I ill give effect to it; the thing designed by me ill certainly be done.
Give ear to me, you feeble-hearted, ho have no faith in my righteousness:
My righteousness is near, it is not far off; salvation ill come quickly; and I ill make Zion free, and give Israel my glory.

Come and take your seat in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon; come don from your seat of poer, and take your place on the earth, O daughter of the Chaldaeans: for you ill never again seem soft and delicate.
Take the crushing-stones and get the meal crushed: take off your veil, put aay your robe, let your legs be uncovered, go through the rivers.
The shame of your unclothed condition ill be seen by all: I ill give punishment ithout mercy,
Says the Lord ho takes up our cause; the Lord of armies is his name, the Holy One of Israel.
Be seated in the dark ithout a ord, O daughter of the Chaldaeans: for you ill no longer be named, The Queen of Kingdoms.
I as angry ith my people, I put shame on my heritage, and gave them into your hands: you had no mercy on them; you put a cruel yoke on those ho ere old;
And you said, I ill be a queen for ever: you did not give attention to these things, and did not keep in mind hat ould come after.
So no take note of this, you ho are given up to pleasure, living ithout fear of evil, saying in your heart, I am, and there is no one like me; I ill never be a ido, or have my children taken from me.
But these to things ill come on you suddenly in one day, the loss of children and of husband: in full measure they ill come on you, for all your secret arts, and all your onders.
For you had faith in your evil-doing; you said, No one sees me; by your isdom and knoledge you have been turned out of the ay: and you have said in your heart, I am, and there is no other.

Because of this evil ill come on you, hich may not be turned aay for any price: and trouble ill overtake you, from hich no money ill give salvation: destruction ill come on you suddenly, ithout your knoledge.

Go on no ith your secret arts, and all your onder-orking, to hich you have given yourself up from your earliest days; it may be that they ill be of profit to you, or by them you may put fear into your attackers.

But your mind is troubled by the number of your guides: let them no come forard for your salvation: the measurers of the heavens, the atchers of the stars, and those ho are able to say from month to month hat things are coming on you.

Truly, they have become like dry stems, they have been burned in the fire; they are not able to keep themselves safe from the poer of the flame: it is not a coal for arming them, or a fire by hich a man may be seated.
Small profit have you had from those ho, from your earliest days, got great profit out of you; they have gone in flight, every one straight before him, and you have no saviour.

Give ear to this, O family of Jacob, you ho are named by the name of Israel, and have come out of the body of Judah; ho take oaths by the name of the Lord, and make use of the name of the God of Israel, but not truly and not in good faith.
For they say that they are of the holy ton, and put their faith in the God of Israel: the Lord of armies is his name.
I gave ord in the past of the things hich came about; they came from my mouth, and I made them clear: suddenly I did them, and they came about.
Because I sa that your heart as hard, and that your neck as an iron cord, and your bro brass;
For this reason I made it clear to you in the past, before it came I gave you ord of it: for fear that you might say, My god did these things, and my pictured and metal images made them come about.
All this has come to your ears and you have seen it; ill you not give itness to it? I am no making clear ne things, even secret things, of hich you had no knoledge.
They have only no been effected, and not in the past: and before this day they had not come to your ears; for fear that you might say, I had knoledge of them.

Truly you had no ord of them, no knoledge of them; no nes of them in the past had come to your ears; because I sa ho false as your behaviour, and that your heart as turned against me from your earliest days.
Because of my name I ill put aay my rath, and for my praise I ill keep myself from cutting you off.
See, I have been testing you for myself like silver; I have put you through the fire of trouble.
For myself, even because of my name, I ill do it; for I ill not let my name be shamed; and my glory I ill not give to another.
Give ear to me, Jacob, and Israel, my loved one; I am he, I am the first and I am the last.
Yes, by my hand as the earth placed on its base, and by my right hand the heavens ere stretched out; at my ord they take up their places.
Come together, all of you, and give ear; ho among you has given nes of these things? the Lord’s loved one ill do his pleasure ith Babylon, and ith the seed of the Chaldaeans.
I, even I, have given the ord; I have sent for him: I have made him come, and have given effect to his undertakings.
Come near to me, and give ear to this; from the start I did not keep it secret; from the time of its coming into existence I as there: and no the Lord God has sent me, and given me his spirit.
The Lord ho takes up your cause, the Holy One of Israel, says, I am the Lord your God, ho is teaching you for your profit, guiding you by the ay in hich you are to go.
If only you had given ear to my orders, then your peace ould have been like a river, and your righteousness as the aves of the sea:
Your seed ould have been like the sand, and your offspring like the dust: your name ould not be cut off or come to an end before me.

Go out of Babylon, go in flight from the Chaldaeans; ith the sound of song make it clear, give the nes, let the ord go out even to the end of the earth: say, The Lord has taken up the cause of his servant Jacob.
They had no need of ater hen he as guiding them through the aste lands: he made ater come out of the rock for them: the rock as parted and the aters came floing out.
There is no peace, says the Lord, for the evil-doers.
Give ear, O sea-lands, to me; and take note, you peoples from far: I have been marked out by the Lord from the first; hen I as still in my mother’s body, he had my name in mind:
And he has made my mouth like a sharp sord, in the shade of his hand he has kept me; and he has made me like a polished arro, keeping me in his secret place;
And he said to me, You are my servant, Israel, in hom my glory ill be seen;
And I said, I have undergone eariness for nothing, I have given my strength for no purpose or profit: but still the Lord ill take up my cause, and my God ill give me my reard.

And no, says the Lord, ho made me his servant hen I as still in my mother’s body, so that I might make Jacob come back to him, and so that Israel might come together to him: and I as honoured in the eyes of the Lord, and my God became my strength.

It is not enough for one ho is my servant to put the tribes of Jacob again in their place, and to get back those of Israel ho have been sent aay: my purpose is to give you as a light to the nations, so that you may be my salvation to the end of the earth.

The Lord ho takes up Israel’s cause, even his Holy One, says to him hom men make sport of, ho is hated by the nations, a servant of rulers: Kings ill see and get up from their places, and chiefs ill give orship: because of the Lord ho keeps faith; even the Holy One of Israel ho has taken you for himself.

This is the ord of the Lord: I have given ear to you at a good time, and I have been your helper in a day of salvation: and I ill keep you safe, and ill make you a glory for the people, putting the land in order, and giving them the heritages hich no are aste;
Saying to those ho are in chains, Go free; to those ho are in the dark, Come out into the light. They ill get food by the ay herever they go, and have grass-lands on all the dry mountain-tops.
They ill not be in need of food or drink, or be troubled by the heat or the sun: for he ho has mercy on them ill be their guide, taking them by the springs of ater.
And I ill make all my mountains a ay, and my highays ill be lifted up.
See, these are coming from far; and these from the north and the est; and these from the land of Sinim.
Let your voice be loud in song, O heavens; and be glad, O earth; make sounds of joy, O mountains, for the Lord has given comfort to his people, and ill have mercy on his crushed ones.
But Zion said, The Lord has given me up, I have gone from his memory.
Will a oman give up the child at her breast, ill she be ithout pity for the fruit of her body? yes, these may, but I ill not let you go out of my memory.
See, your name is marked on my hands; your alls are ever before me.
Your builders are coming quickly; your haters and those ho made you aste ill go out of you.

Let your eyes be lifted up round about, and see: they are all coming together to you. By my life, says the Lord, truly you ill put them all on you as an ornament, and be clothed ith them like a bride.
For though the aste places of your land have been given to destruction, no you ill not be ide enough for your people, and those ho made you aste ill be far aay.
The children to hom you gave birth in other lands ill say in your ears, The place is not ide enough for me: make room for me to have a resting-place.

Then you ill say in your heart, Who has given me all these children? hen my children had been taken from me, and I as no longer able to have others, ho took care of these? hen I as by myself, here then ere these?

This is the ord of the Lord God: See, I ill make a sign ith my hand to the nations, and put up my flag for the peoples; and they ill take up your sons on their beasts, and your daughters on their backs.

And kings ill take care of you, and queens ill give you their milk: they ill go don on their faces before you, kissing the dust of your feet; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord, and that those ho put their hope in me ill not be shamed.
Will the goods of ar be taken from the strong man, or the prisoners of the cruel one be let go?
But the Lord says, Even the prisoners of the strong ill be taken from him, and the cruel made to let go his goods: for I ill take up your cause against your haters, and I ill keep your children safe.

And the flesh of your attackers ill be taken by themselves for food; and they ill take their blood for drink, as if it as seet ine: and all men ill see that I the Lord am your saviour, even he ho takes up your cause, the Strong One of Jacob.

This is the ord of the Lord: Where is the statement hich I gave your mother hen I put her aay? or to hich of my creditors have I given you for money? It as for your sins that you ere given into the hands of others, and for your evil-doing as your mother put aay.

Why, then, hen I came, as there no man? and no one to give anser to my voice? has my hand become feeble, so that it is unable to take up your cause? or have I no poer to make you free? See, at my ord the sea becomes dry, I make the rivers a aste land: their fish are dead for need of ater, and make an evil smell.
By me the heavens are clothed ith black, and I make haircloth their robe.

The Lord God has given me the tongue of those ho are experienced, so that I may be able to give the ord a special sense for the feeble: every morning my ear is open to his teaching, like those ho are experienced:
And I have not put myself against him, or let my heart be turned back from him.
I as offering my back to those ho gave me blos, and my face to those ho ere pulling out my hair: I did not keep my face covered from marks of shame.
For the Lord God is my helper; I ill not be put to shame: so I have made my face like a rock, and I am certain that he ill give me my right.
He ho takes up my cause is near; ho ill go to la ith me? let us come together before the judge: ho is against me? let him come near to me.
See, the Lord God is my helper; ho ill give a decision against me? truly, all of them ill become old like a robe; they ill be food for the orm.

Who among you has the fear of the Lord, giving ear to the voice of his servant ho has been alking in the dark and has no light? Let him put his faith in the name of the Lord, looking to his God for support.

See, all you ho make a fire, arming yourselves ith burning branches: go in the flame of your fire, and among the branches you have put a light to. This ill you have from my hand, you ill make your bed in sorro.
Give ear to me, you ho are searching for righteousness, ho are looking for the Lord: see the rock from hich you ere cut out, and the hole out of hich you ere taken.
Let your thoughts be turned to Abraham, your father, and to Sarah, ho gave you birth: for hen he as but one, my voice came to him, and I gave him my blessing, and made him a great people.

For the Lord has given comfort to Zion: he has made glad all her broken alls; making her aste places like Eden, and changing her dry land into the garden of the Lord; joy and delight ill be there, praise and the sound of melody.
Give attention to me, O my people; and give ear to me, O my nation; for teaching ill go out from me, and the knoledge of the true God ill be a light to the peoples.
Suddenly ill my righteousness come near, and my salvation ill be shining out like the light; the sea-lands ill be aiting for me, and they ill put their hope in my strong arm.

Let your eyes be lifted up to the heavens, and turned to the earth hich is under them: for the heavens ill go in flight like smoke, and the earth ill become old like a coat, and its people ill come to destruction like insects: but my salvation ill be for ever, and my righteousness ill not come to an end.
Give ear to me, you ho have knoledge of righteousness, in hose heart is my la; have no fear of the evil ords of men, and give no thought to their curses.
For like a coat they ill be food for the insect, the orm ill make a meal of them like ool: but my righteousness ill be for ever, and my salvation to all generations.
Aake! aake! put on strength, O arm of the Lord, aake! as in the old days, in the generations long past. Was it not by you that Rahab as cut in to, and the dragon Wounded?
Did you not make the sea dry, the aters of the great deep? did you not make the deep aters of the sea a ay for the Lord’s people to go through?
Those hom the Lord has made free ill come back ith songs to Zion; and on their heads ill be eternal joy: delight and joy ill be theirs, and sorro and sounds of grief ill be gone for ever.
I, even I, am your comforter: are you so poor in heart as to be in fear of man ho ill come to an end, and of the son of man ho ill be like grass?

And you have given no thought to the Lord your Maker, by hom the heavens ere stretched out, and the earth placed on its base; and you ent all day in fear of the rath of the cruel one, hen he as making ready for your destruction. And here is the rath of the cruel one?
The prisoner, bent under his chain, ill quickly be made free, and ill not go don into the underorld, and his bread ill not come to an end.
For I am the Lord your God, ho makes the sea calm hen its aves are thundering: the Lord of armies is his name.
And I have put my ords in your mouth, covering you ith the shade of my hand, stretching out the heavens, and placing the earth on its base, and saying to Zion, You are my people.
Aake! aake! up! O Jerusalem, you ho have taken from the Lord’s hand the cup of his rath; tasting in full measure the ine hich overcomes.
She has no one among all her children to be her guide; not one of the sons she has taken care of takes her by the hand.
These to things have come on you; ho ill be eeping for you? asting and destruction; death from need of food, and from the sord; ho may you be comforted?
Your sons are overcome, like a roe in a net; they are full of the rath of the Lord, the punishment of your God.
So no give ear to this, you ho are troubled and overcome, but not ith ine:

This is the ord of the Lord your master, even your God ho takes up the cause of his people: See, I have taken out of your hand the cup hich overcomes, even the cup of my rath; it ill not again be given to you:

And I ill put it into the hand of your cruel masters, and of those hose yoke has been hard on you; ho have said to your soul, Don on your face! so that e may go over you: and you have given your backs like the earth, even like the street, for them to go over.
Aake! aake! put on your strength, O Zion; put on your beautiful robes, O Jerusalem, the holy ton: for from no there ill never again come into you the unclean and those ithout circumcision.
Make yourself clean from the dust; up! and take the seat of your poer, O Jerusalem: the bands of your neck are loose, O prisoned daughter of Zion.
For the Lord says, You ere given for nothing, and you ill be made free ithout price.
For the Lord God says, My people ent don at first into Egypt, to get a place for themselves there: and the Assyrian put a cruel yoke on them ithout cause.
No then, hat have I here? says the Lord, for my people are taken aay ithout cause; they are made aste and give cries of sorro, says the Lord, and all the day the nations put shame on my name.
For this cause I ill make my name clear to my people; in that day they ill be certain that it is my ord hich comes to them; see, here am I.
Ho beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him ho comes ith good nes, ho gives ord of peace, saying that salvation is near; ho says to Zion, Your God is ruling!
The voice of your atchmen! their voices are loud in song together; for they ill see him, eye to eye, hen the Lord comes back to Zion.
Give sounds of joy, make melody together, aste places of Jerusalem: for the Lord has given comfort to his people, he has taken up the cause of Jerusalem.
The Lord has let his holy arm be seen by the eyes of all nations; and all the ends of the earth ill see the salvation of our God.
Aay! aay! go out from there, touching no unclean thing; go out from among her; be clean, you ho take up the vessels of the Lord.
For you ill not go out suddenly, and you ill not go in flight: for the Lord ill go before you, and the God of Israel ill come after you to keep you.
See, my servant ill do ell in his undertakings, he ill be honoured, and lifted up, and be very high.

As peoples ere surprised at him, And his face as not beautiful, so as to be desired: his face as so changed by disease as to be unlike that of a man, and his form as no longer that of the sons of men.
So ill nations give him honour; kings ill keep quiet because of him: for hat had not been made clear to them they ill see; and they ill give their minds to hat had not come to their ears.
Who ould have had faith in the ord hich has come to our ears, and to hom had the arm of the Lord been unveiled?
For his groth as like that of a delicate plant before him, and like a root out of a dry place: he had no grace of form, to give us pleasure;
Men made sport of him, turning aay from him; he as a man of sorros, marked by disease; and like one from hom men’s faces are turned aay, he as looked don on, and e put no value on him.
But it as our pain he took, and our diseases ere put on him: hile to us he seemed as one diseased, on hom God’s punishment had come.
But it as for our sins he as ounded, and for our evil doings he as crushed: he took the punishment by hich e have peace, and by his ounds e are made ell.
We all ent andering like sheep; going every one of us after his desire; and the Lord put on him the punishment of us all.
Men ere cruel to him, but he as gentle and quiet; as a lamb taken to its death, and as a sheep before those ho take her ool makes no sound, so he said not a ord.
They took aay from him help and right, and ho gave a thought to his fate? for he as cut off from the land of the living: he came to his death for the sin of my people.
And they put his body into the earth ith sinners, and his last resting-place as ith the evil-doers, though he had done no rong, and no deceit as in his mouth.
And the Lord as pleased ... see a seed, long life, ... ill do ell in his hand. ...
... made clear his righteousness before men ... had taken their sins on himself.

For this cause he ill have a heritage ith the great, and he ill have a part in the goods of ar ith the strong, because he gave up his life, and as numbered ith the evil-doers; taking on himself the sins of the people, and making prayer for the rongdoers.

Let your voice be loud in song, O oman ithout children; make melody and sounds of joy, you ho did not give birth: for the children of her ho had no husband are more than those of the married ife, says the Lord.
Make ide the place of your tent, and let the curtains of your house be stretched out ithout limit: make your cords long, and your tent-pins strong.
For I ill make ide your limits on the right hand and on the left; and your seed ill take the nations for a heritage, and make the aste tons full of people.

Have no fear; for you ill not be shamed or ithout hope: you ill not be put to shame, for the shame of your earlier days ill go out of your memory, and you ill no longer keep in mind the sorros of your idoed years.
For your Maker is your husband; the Lord of armies is his name: and the Holy One of Israel is he ho takes up your cause; he ill be named the God of all the earth.
For the Lord has made you come back to him, like a ife ho has been sent aay in grief of spirit; for one may not give up the ife of one’s early days.
For a short time I gave you up; but ith great mercies I ill take you back again.
In overfloing rath my face as veiled from you for a minute, but I ill have pity on you for ever, says the Lord ho takes up your cause.

For this is like the days of Noah to me: for as I took an oath that the aters of Noah ould never again go over the earth, so have I taken an oath that I ill not again be angry ith you, or say bitter ords to you.
For the mountains may be taken aay, and the hills be moved out of their places, but my love ill not be taken from you, or my agreement of peace broken, says the Lord, ho has had mercy on you.
O troubled one, storm-crushed, uncomforted! see, your stones ill be framed in fair colours, and your bases ill be sapphires.
I ill make your toers of rubies, and your doors of carbuncles, and the all round you ill be of all sorts of beautiful stones.
And all your builders ill be made ise by the Lord; and great ill be the peace of your children.
All your rights ill be made certain to you: have no fear of evil, and destruction ill not come near you.
See, they may be moved to ar, but not by my authority: all those ho come together to make an attack on you, ill be broken against you.
See, I have made the iron-orker, bloing on the burning coals, and making the instrument of ar by his ork; and I have made the aster for destruction.

No instrument of ar hich is formed against you ill be of any use; and every tongue hich says evil against you ill be judged false. This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, and their righteousness comes from me, says the Lord.
Ho! everyone in need, come to the aters, and he ho has no strength, let him get food: come, get bread ithout money; ine and milk ithout price.
Why do you give your money for hat is not bread, and the fruit of your ork for hat ill not give you pleasure? Give ear to me, so that your food may be good, and you may have the best in full measure.
Give ear, and come to me, take note ith care, so that your souls may have life: and I ill make an eternal agreement ith you, even the certain mercies of David.
See, I have given him as a itness to the peoples, a ruler and a guide to the nations.

See, you ill send for a nation of hich you had no knoledge, and those ho had no knoledge of you ill come running to you, because of the Lord your God, and because of the Holy One of Israel, for he has given you glory.
Make search for the Lord hile he is there, make prayer to him hile he is near:
Let the sinner give up his ay, and the evil-doer his purpose: and let him come back to the Lord, and he ill have mercy on him; and to our God, for there is full forgiveness ith him.
For my thoughts are not your thoughts, or your ays my ays, says the Lord.
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ays higher than your ays, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain comes don, and the sno from heaven, and does not go back again, but gives ater to the earth, and makes it fertile, giving seed to the planter, and bread for food;
So ill my ord be hich goes out of my mouth: it ill not come back to me ith nothing done, but it ill give effect to my purpose, and do that for hich I have sent it.
For you ill go out ith joy, and be guided in peace: the mountains and the hills ill make melody before you, and all the trees of the fields ill make sounds of joy.
In place of the thorn ill come up the fir-tree, and in place of the blackberry the myrtle: and it ill be to the Lord for a name, for an eternal sign hich ill not be cut off.
The Lord says, Let your ay of life be upright, and let your behaviour be rightly ordered: for my salvation is near, and my righteousness ill quickly be seen.
Happy is the man ho does this, and the son of man hose behaviour is so ordered; ho keeps the Sabbath holy, and his hand from doing any evil.
And let not the man from a strange country, ho has been joined to the Lord, say, The Lord ill certainly put a division beteen me and his people: and let not the unsexed man say, See, I am a dry tree.
For the Lord says, As for the unsexed ho keep my Sabbaths, and give their hearts to pleasing me, and keep their agreement ith me:
I ill give to them in my house, and inside my alls, a place and a name better than that of sons and daughters; I ill give them an eternal name hich ill not be cut off.

And as for those from a strange country, ho are joined to the Lord, to give orship to him and honour to his name, to be his servants, even everyone ho keeps the Sabbath holy, and keeps his agreement ith me:

I ill make them come to my holy mountain, and ill give them joy in my house of prayer; I ill take pleasure in the burned offerings hich they make on my altar: for my house ill be named a house of prayer for all peoples.
The Lord God, ho gets together the andering ones of Israel, says, I ill get together others in addition to those of Israel ho have come back.
All you beasts of the field, come together for your meat, even all you beasts of the ood.
His atchmen are blind, they are all ithout knoledge; they are all dogs ithout tongues, unable to make a sound; stretched out dreaming, loving sleep.
Yes, the dogs are for ever looking for food; hile these, the keepers of the sheep, are ithout isdom: they have all gone after their pleasure, every one looking for profit; they are all the same.
Come, they say, I ill get ine, and e ill take strong drink in full measure; and tomorro ill be like today, full of pleasure.

The upright man goes to his death, and no one gives a thought to it; and god-fearing men are taken aay, and no one is troubled by it; for the upright man is taken aay because of evil-doing, and goes into peace.
They are at rest in their last resting-places, every one going straight before him.
But come near, you sons of her ho is ise in secret arts, the seed of her ho is false to her husband, and of the loose oman.
Of hom do you make sport? against hom is your mouth open ide and your tongue put out? are you not uncontrolled children, a false seed,
You ho are burning ith evil desire among the oaks, under every green tree; putting children to death in the valleys, under the cracks of the rocks?

Among the smooth stones of the valley is your heritage; they, even they, are your part: even to them have you made a drink offering and a meal offering. Is it possible for such things to be overlooked by me?
You have put your bed on a high mountain: there you ent up to make your offering.

And on the back of the doors and on the pillars you have put your sign: for you have been false to me ith another; you have made your bed ide, and made an agreement ith them; you had a desire for their bed here you sa it
And you ent to Melech ith oil and much perfume, and you sent your representatives far off, and ent as lo as the underorld.
You ere tired ith your long journeys; but you did not say, There is no hope: you got ne strength, and so you ere not feeble.
And of hom ere you in fear, so that you ere false, and did not keep me in mind, or give thought to it? Have I not been quiet, keeping myself secret, and so you ere not in fear of me?
I ill make clear hat your righteousness is like and your orks; you ill have no profit in them.

Your false gods ill not keep you safe in anser to your cry; but the ind ill take them, they ill be gone like a breath: but he ho puts his hope in me ill take the land, and ill have my holy mountain as his heritage.
And I ill say, Make it high, make it high, get ready the ay, take the stones out of the ay of my people.

For this is the ord of him ho is high and lifted up, hose resting-place is eternal, hose name is Holy: my resting-place is in the high and holy place, and ith him ho is crushed and poor in spirit, to give life to the spirit of the poor, and to make strong the heart of the crushed.
For I ill not give punishment for ever, or be angry ithout end: for from me breath goes out; and I it as ho made the souls.
I as quickly angry ith his evil ays, and sent punishment on him, veiling my face in rath: and he ent on, turning his heart from me.
I have seen his ays, and I ill make him ell: I ill give him rest, comforting him and his people ho are sad.
I ill give the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to him ho is near and to him ho is far off, says the Lord; and I ill make him ell.
But the evil-doers are like the troubled sea, for hich there is no rest, and its aters send up earth and aste.
There is no peace, says my God, for the evil-doers.
Make a loud cry, do not be quiet, let your voice be sounding like a horn, and make clear to my people their evil doings, and to the family of Jacob their sins.

Though they make prayer to me every day, and take pleasure in the knoledge of my ays: like a nation hich has done righteousness, and has not given up the rules of their God, they make requests to me for the right orders, it is their delight to come near to God.

They say, Why have e kept ourselves from food, and you do not see it? hy have e kept ourselves from pleasure, and you take no note of it? If, in the days hen you keep from food, you take the chance to do your business, and get in your debts;
If keeping from food makes you quickly angry, ready for fighting and giving blos ith evil hands; your holy days are not such as to make your voice come to my ears on high.

Have I given orders for such a day as this? a day for keeping yourselves from pleasure? is it only a question of the bent head, of putting on haircloth, and being seated in the dust? is this hat seems to you a holy day, ell-pleasing to the Lord?
Is not this the holy day for hich I have given orders: to let loose those ho have rongly been made prisoners, to undo the bands of the yoke, and to let the crushed go free, and every yoke be broken?

Is it not to give your bread to those in need, and to let the poor ho have no resting-place come into your house? to put a robe on the unclothed one hen you see him, and not to keep your eyes shut for fear of seeing his flesh?
Then ill light be shining on you like the morning, and your ounds ill quickly be ell: and your righteousness ill go before you, and the glory of the Lord ill come after you.
Then at the sound of your voice, the Lord ill give an anser; at your cry he ill say, Here am I. If you take aay from among you the yoke, the putting out of the finger of shame, and the evil ord;
And if you give your bread to those in need of it, so that the troubled one may have his desire; then you ill have light in the dark, and your night ill be as the full light of the sun:
And the Lord ill be your guide at all times; in dry places he ill give you ater in full measure, and ill make strong your bones; and you ill be like a atered garden, and like an ever-floing spring.
And your sons ill be building again the old aste places: you ill make strong the bases of old generations: and you ill be named, He ho puts up the broken alls, and, He ho makes ready the ays for use.

If you keep the Sabbath ith care, not doing your business on my holy day; and if the Sabbath seems to you a delight, and the ne moon of the Lord a thing to be honoured; and if you give respect to him by not doing your business, or going after your pleasure, or saying unholy ords;
Then the Lord ill be your delight; and I ill put you on the high places of the earth; and I ill give you the heritage of Jacob your father: for the mouth of the Lord has said it.
Truly, the Lord’s hand has not become short, so that he is unable to give salvation; and his ear is not shut from hearing:
But your sins have come beteen you and your God, and by your evil doings his face has been veiled from you, so that he ill give you no anser.
