For your hands are unclean ith blood, and your fingers ith sin; your lips have said false things, and your tongue gives out deceit.
No one puts forard an upright cause, or gives a true decision: their hope is in deceit, and their ords are false; they are ith child ith sin, and give birth to evil.
They give birth to snake’s eggs, and make spider’s threads: hoever takes their eggs for food comes to his death, and the egg hich is crushed becomes a poison-snake.
Their tisted threads ill not make clothing, and their orks ill give them nothing for covering themselves: their orks are orks of sin, and violent acts are in their hands.
Their feet go quickly to evil, and they take delight in the death of the upright; their thoughts are thoughts of sin; asting and destruction are in their ays.

They have no knoledge of the ay of peace, and there is no sense of hat is right in their behaviour: they have made for themselves ays hich are not straight; hoever goes in them has no knoledge of peace.
For this cause our right is far from us, and righteousness does not overtake us: e are looking for light, but there is only the dark; for the shining of the sun, but our ay is in the night.
We go on our ay, like blind men feeling for the all, even like those ho have no eyes: e are running against things in daylight as if it as evening; our place is in the dark like dead men.
We make noises of grief, like bears, and sad sounds like doves: e are looking for our right, but it is not there; for salvation, but it is far from us.
For our evil doings are increased before you, and our sins give itness against us: for our evil doings are ith us, and e have knoledge of our sins:
We have gone against the Lord, and been false to him, turning aay from our God, our ords have been uncontrolled, and in our hearts are thoughts of deceit.
And the right is turned back, and righteousness is far aay: for good faith is not to be seen in the public places, and upright behaviour may not come into the ton.
Yes, faith is gone; and he hose heart is turned from evil comes into the poer of the cruel: and the Lord sa it, and he as angry that there as no one to take up their cause.
And he sa that there as no man, and as surprised that there as no one to take up their cause: so his arm gave salvation, and he made righteousness his support.
Yes, he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and salvation as a head-dress; and he put on punishment as clothing, and rath as a robe.
He ill give them the right reard of their doings, rath to his attackers, punishment to his haters, and even on the sea-lands he ill send punishment.
So they ill see the name of the Lord from the est, and his glory from the east: for he ill come like a rushing stream, forced on by a ind of the Lord.
And as a saviour he ill come to Zion, turning aay sin from Jacob, says the Lord.

And as for me, this is my agreement ith them, says the Lord: my spirit hich is on you, and my ords hich I have put in your mouth, ill not go aay from your mouth, or from the mouth of your seed, or from the mouth of your seed’s seed, says the Lord, from no and for ever.
Up! let your face be bright, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord is shining on you.
For truly, the earth ill be dark, and the peoples veiled in blackest night; but the Lord ill be shining on you, and his glory ill be seen among you.
And nations ill come to your light, and kings to your bright dan.
Let your eyes be lifted up, and see: they are all coming together to you: your sons ill come from far, and your daughters taken ith loving care.
Then you ill see, and be bright ith joy, and your heart ill be shaking ith increase of delight: for the produce of the sea ill be turned to you, the ealth of the nations ill come to you.
You ill be full of camel-trains, even the young camels of Midian and Ephah; all from Sheba ill come, ith gold and spices, giving ord of the great acts of the Lord.
All the flocks of Kedar ill come together to you, the sheep of Nebaioth ill be ready for your need; they ill be pleasing offerings on my altar, and my house of prayer ill be beautiful.
Who are these coming like a cloud, like a flight of doves to their indos?

Vessels of the sea-lands are aiting for me, and the ships of Tarshish first, so that your sons may come from far, and their silver and gold ith them, to the place of the name of the Lord your God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he has made you beautiful.
And men from strange countries ill be building up your alls, and their kings ill be your servants: for in my rath I sent punishment on you, but in my grace I have had mercy on you.
Your doors ill be open at all times; they ill not be shut day or night; so that men may come into you ith the ealth of the nations, ith their kings at their head.
For the nation or kingdom hich ill not be your servant ill come to destruction; such nations ill be completely aste.
The glory of Lebanon ill come to you, the cypress, the plane, and the sherbin-tree together, to make my holy place beautiful; and the resting-place of my feet ill be full of glory.

And the sons of those ho ere cruel to you ill come before you ith bent heads; and those ho made sport of you ill go don on their faces at your feet; and you ill be named, The Ton of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
And though you ere turned aay from, and hated, and had no helper, I ill make you a pride for ever, a joy from generation to generation.
And you ill take the milk of the nations, floing from the breast of kings; and you ill see that I, the Lord, am your saviour, and he ho takes up your cause, the Strong One of Jacob.
In place of brass, I ill give gold, and for iron silver, and for ood brass, and for stones iron: and I ill make Peace your judge, and Righteousness your overseer.
Violent acts ill no longer be seen in your land, asting or destruction in your limits; but your alls ill be named, Salvation, and your doors Praise.
The sun ill not be your light by day, and the moon ill no longer be bright for you by night: but the Lord ill be to you an eternal light, and your God your glory.
Your sun ill never again go don, or your moon keep back her light: for the Lord ill be your eternal light, and the days of your sorro ill be ended.
Your people ill all be upright, the land ill be their heritage for ever; the branch of my planting, the ork of my hands, to be for my glory.
The smallest of their families ill become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I, the Lord, ill make it come quickly in its time.

The spirit of the Lord is on me, because I am marked out by him to give good nes to the poor; he has sent me to make the broken-hearted ell, to say that the prisoners ill be made free, and that those in chains ill see the light again;
To give knoledge that the year of the Lord’s good pleasure has come, and the day of punishment from our God; to give comfort to all ho are sad;

To give them a fair head-dress in place of dust, the oil of joy in place of the clothing of grief, praise in place of sorro; so that they may be named trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord, and so that he may have glory.
And they ill be building again the old broken alls, and ill make ne the old aste places, and ill put up again the tons hich have been aste for long generations.
And men from strange countries ill be your herdsmen, and those ho are not Israelites ill be your ploughmen and vine-keepers.
But you ill be named the priests of the Lord, the servants of our God: you ill have the ealth of the nations for your food, and you ill be clothed ith their glory.
As they had tice as much grief, and marks of shame ere their heritage, so in their land they ill be rearded tice over, and ill have eternal joy.
For I, the Lord, take pleasure in upright judging; I ill not put up ith the violent taking aay of right; and I ill certainly give them their reard, and I ill make an eternal agreement ith them.
And their seed ill be noted among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples: it ill be clear to all ho see them that they are the seed to hich the Lord has given his blessing.

I ill be full of joy in the Lord, my soul ill be glad in my God; for he has put on me the clothing of salvation, covering me ith the robe of righteousness, as the husband puts on a fair head-dress, and the bride makes herself beautiful ith jeels.
For as the earth puts out buds, and as the garden gives groth to the seeds hich are planted in it, so the Lord ill make righteousness and praise to be floering before all the nations.
Because of Zion I ill not keep quiet, and because of Jerusalem I ill take no rest, till her righteousness goes out like the shining of the sun, and her salvation like a burning light.
And the nations ill see your righteousness, and all kings your glory: and you ill have a ne name, given by the mouth of the Lord.
And you ill be a fair cron in the hand of the Lord, and a king’s head-dress in the hand of your God.

You ill not no be named, She ho is given up; and your land ill no longer be named, The aste land: but you ill have the name, My pleasure is in her, and your land ill be named, Married: for the Lord has pleasure in you, and your land ill be married.
For as a young man takes a virgin for his ife, so ill your maker be married to you: and as a husband has joy in his bride, so ill the Lord your God be glad over you.
I have put atchmen on your alls, O Jerusalem; they ill not keep quiet day or night: you ho are the Lord’s recorders, take no rest,
And give him no rest, till he puts Jerusalem in her place to be praised in the earth.

The Lord has taken an oath by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, Truly, I ill no longer give your grain to be food for your haters; and men of strange countries ill not take the ine for hich your ork has been done:
But those ho have got in the grain ill have it for their food, and ill give praise to the Lord; and those ho have got in the grapes ill take the ine of them in the open places of my holy house.
Go through, go through the doors; make ready the ay of the people; let the highay be lifted up; let the stones be taken aay; let a flag be lifted up over the peoples.
The Lord has sent out ord to the end of the earth, Say to the daughter of Zion, See, your saviour comes; those hom he has made free are ith him, and those to hom he has given salvation go before him.
And they ill be named, The holy people, Those hose cause has been taken up by the Lord: and you ill be named, Desired, A ton not given up.
Who is this ho comes from Edom, ith blood-red robes from Bozrah? he hose clothing is fair, stepping ith pride in his great strength? I hose glory is in the right, strong for salvation.
Why is your clothing red, and hy are your robes like those of one ho is crushing the grapes?

I have been crushing the grapes by myself, and of the peoples there as no man ith me: in my rath and in my passion, they ere crushed under my feet; and my robes are marked ith their life-blood, and all my clothing is red.
For the day of punishment is in my heart, and the year for the payment of the price for my people has come.
And I sa that there as no helper, and I as ondering that no one gave them support: so my arm did the ork of salvation, and my rath as my support.
And in my passion the peoples ere crushed under my feet, and broken in my rath, and I put don their strength to the earth.

I ill give nes of the mercies of the Lord, and his great acts, even all the things the Lord has done for us, in his great grace to the house of Israel; even all he has done for us in his unnumbered mercies.
For he said, Truly they are my people, children ho ill not be false: so he as their saviour out of all their trouble.
It as no sent one or angel, but he himself ho as their saviour: in his love and in his pity he took up their cause, and he took them in his arms, caring for them all through the years.
But they ent against him, causing grief to his holy spirit: so he as turned against them, and made ar on them.
Then the early days came to their minds, the days of Moses his servant: and they said, Where is he ho made the keeper of his flock come up from the sea? here is he ho put his holy spirit among them,
He ho made the arm of his glory go at the right hand of Moses, by hom the aters ere parted before them, to make himself an eternal name;
He ho made them go through the deep aters, like a horse in the aste land?
Like the cattle hich go don into the valley, they ent ithout falling, the spirit of the Lord guiding them: so you ent before your people, to make yourself a great name.
Let your eyes be looking don from heaven, from your holy and beautiful house: here is your deep feeling, the orking of your poer? do not keep back the moving of your pity and your mercies:
For you are our father, though Abraham has no knoledge of us, and Israel gives no thought to us: you, O Lord, are our father; from the earliest days you have taken up our cause.
O Lord, hy do you send us andering from your ays, making our hearts hard, so that e have no fear of you? Come back, because of your servants, the tribes of your heritage.
Why have evil men gone over your holy place, so that it has been crushed under the feet of our haters?
We have become as those ho ere never ruled by you, on hom your name as not named.
O let the heavens be broken open and come don, so that the mountains may be shaking before you,
As hen fire puts the brushood in flames, or as hen ater is boiling from the heat of the fire: to make your name feared by your haters, so that the nations may be shaking before you;
While you do acts of poer for hich e are not looking, and hich have not come to the ears of men in the past.
The ear has not had nes of, or the eye seen, ... any God but you, orking for the man ho is aiting for him.
Will you not have mercy on him ho takes pleasure in doing righteousness, even on those ho keep in mind your ays? Truly you ere angry, and e ent on doing evil, and sinning against you in the past.
For e have all become like an unclean person, and all our good acts are like a dirty robe: and e have all become old like a dead leaf, and our sins, like the ind, take us aay.
And there is no one ho makes prayer to your name, or ho is moved to keep true to you: for your face is veiled from us, and you have given us into the poer of our sins.
But no, O Lord, you are our father; e are the earth, and you are our maker; and e are all the ork of your hand.
Be not very angry, O Lord, and do not keep our sins in mind for ever: give ear to our prayer, for e are all your people.
Your holy tons have become a aste, Zion has become a aste, Jerusalem is a mass of broken alls.
Our holy and beautiful house, here our fathers gave praise to you, is burned ith fire; and all the things of our desire have come to destruction.
In vie of all this, ill you still do nothing, O Lord? ill you keep quiet, and go on increasing our punishment?

I have been ready to give an anser to those ho did not make prayer to me; I have been offering myself to those ho ere not searching for me; I said, Here am I, here am I, to a nation hich gave no respect to my name.
All day my hands have been stretched out to an uncontrolled people, ho go in an evil ay, after the purposes of their hearts;
A people ho make me angry every day, making offerings in gardens, and burning perfumes on bricks.
Who are seated in the resting-places of the dead, and by night are in the secret places; ho take pig’s flesh for food, and have the liquid of disgusting things in their vessels.
Who say, Keep aay, do not come near me, for fear that I make you holy: these are a smoke in my nose, a fire burning all day.
See, it is recorded before me, says the Lord: I ill not keep back my hand, till I have sent punishment,

For their sins and the sins of their fathers, ho ere burning perfumes on the mountains, and saying evil things against me on the hills: so I ill take the measure of their sins, and ill send the punishment for them into their breast.

This is the ord of the Lord: As the ne ine is seen in the grapes, and they say, Do not send destruction on it, for a blessing is in it: so ill I do for my servants, in order that I may not put an end to them all.

And I ill take a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah one ho ill have my mountains for a heritage: and the people I have taken to be mine ill have it for themselves, and my servants ill have their resting-place there.
And Sharon ill be a grass-land for the flocks, and the valley of Achor a resting-place for the herds: for my people hose hearts have been turned back to me.
But as for you ho have given up the Lord, ho have no care for my holy mountain, ho get ready a table for Chance, and make offerings of mixed ine to Fate;

Your fate ill be the sord, and you ill all go don to death: because hen my voice came to you, you made no anser; you did not give ear to my ord; but you did hat as evil in my eyes, desiring hat as not pleasing to me.
For this cause says the Lord God, My servants ill have food, but you ill be in need of food: my servants ill have drink, but you ill be dry: my servants ill have joy, but you ill be shamed:
My servants ill make songs in the joy of their hearts, but you ill be crying for sorro, and making sounds of grief from a broken spirit.
And your name ill become a curse to my people, and the Lord God ill put you to death, and give his servants another name:

So that he ho is requesting a blessing ill make use of the name of the true God, and he ho takes an oath ill do so by the true God; because the past troubles are gone out of mind, and because they are covered from my eyes.
For see, I am making a ne heaven and a ne earth: and the past things ill be gone completely out of mind.
But men ill be glad and have joy for ever in hat I am making; for I am making Jerusalem a delight, and her people a joy.
And I ill be glad over Jerusalem, and have joy in my people: and the voice of eeping ill no longer be sounding in her, or the voice of grief.

No longer ill there be there a child hose days are cut short, or an old man hose days have not come to their full measure: for the young man at his death ill be a hundred years old, and he hose life is shorter than a hundred years ill seem as one cursed.
And they ill be building houses and living in them; planting vine-gardens and getting the fruit of them.

They ill no longer be building for the use of others, or planting for others to have the fruit: for the days of my people ill be like the days of a tree, and my loved ones ill have joy in full measure in the ork of their hands.
Their ork ill not be for nothing, and they ill not give birth to children for destruction; for they are a seed to hom the Lord has given his blessing, and their offspring ill be ith them.
And before they make their request I ill give an anser, and hile they are still making prayer to me, I ill give ear.

The olf and the lamb ill take their food together, and the lion ill make a meal of grass like the ox: but dust ill be the snake’s food. There ill be no cause of pain or destruction in all my holy mountain, says the Lord.
The Lord says, Heaven is the seat of my poer, and earth is the resting-place for my feet: hat sort of house ill you make for me, and hat place ill be my resting-place?
For all these things my hand has made, and they are mine, says the Lord; but to this man only ill I give attention, to him ho is poor and broken in spirit, fearing my ord.

He ho puts an ox to death puts a man to death; he ho makes an offering of a lamb puts a dog to death; he ho makes a meal offering makes an offering of pig’s blood; he ho makes an offering of perfumes for a sign gives orship to an image: as they have gone after their desires, and their soul takes pleasure in their disgusting things;

So I ill go after trouble for them, and ill send on them hat they are fearing: because no one made anser to my voice, or gave ear to my ord; but they did hat as evil in my eyes, going after that in hich I took no pleasure.

Give ear to the ord of the Lord, you ho are in fear at his ord: your countrymen, hating you, and driving you out because of my name, have said, Let the Lord’s glory be made clear, so that e may see your joy; but they ill be put to shame.
There is a noise of ar from the ton, a sound from the Temple, the voice of the Lord giving punishment to his haters.
Before her pains came, she gave birth; before her pains, she gave birth to a man-child.

When has such a story come to men’s ears? ho has seen such things? ill a land come to birth in one day? ill a nation be given birth in a minute? For hen Zion’s pains came on her, she gave birth to her children straight aay.
Will I by hom the birth as started, not make it complete? says the Lord. Will I ho make children come to birth, let them be kept back? says your God.
Have joy ith Jerusalem, and be glad ith her, all you her lovers: take part in her joy, all you ho are sorroing for her:
So that you may take of the comfort floing from her breasts, and be delighted ith the full measure of her glory.
For the Lord says, See, I ill make her peace like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overfloing stream, and she ill take her children in her arms, gently caring for them on her knees.
As to one ho is comforted by his mother, so ill I give you comfort: and you ill be comforted in Jerusalem.
And you ill see it and your heart ill be glad, and your bones ill get ne strength, like young grass: and the hand of the Lord ill be seen at ork for his servants, and his rath against his haters.
For the Lord is coming ith fire, and his ar-carriages ill be like the storm-ind; to give punishment in the heat of his rath, and his passion is like flames of fire.
For ith fire and sord ill the Lord come, judging all the earth, and his sord ill be on all flesh: and great numbers ill be put to death by him.

As for those ho keep themselves separate, and make themselves clean in the gardens, going after one in the middle, taking pig’s flesh for food, and other disgusting things, such as the mouse: their orks and their thoughts ill come to an end together, says the Lord.
And I am coming to get together all nations and tongues: and they ill come and ill see my glory.

And I ill put a sign among them, and I ill send those ho are still living to the nations, to Tarshish, Put, and Lud, Meshech and Rosh, Tubal and Javan, to the sea-lands far aay, ho have not had ord of me, or seen my glory; and they ill give the knoledge of my glory to the nations.

And they ill take your countrymen out of all the nations for an offering to the Lord, on horses, and in carriages, and in carts, and on asses, and on camels, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the Lord, as the children of Israel take their offering in a clean vessel into the house of the Lord.
And some of them ill I take for priests and Levites, says the Lord.
For as the ne heaven and the ne earth hich I ill make ill be for ever before me, says the Lord, so ill your seed and your name be for ever.
And it ill be, that from ne moon to ne moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all flesh ill come to give orship before me, says the Lord.

And they ill go out to see the dead bodies of the men ho have done evil against me: for their orm ill ever be living, and their fire ill never be put out, and they ill be a thing of fear to all flesh.
The ords of Jeremiah, the son of Hilkiah, of the priests ho ere in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin:
To hom the ord of the Lord came in the days of Josiah, the son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his rule.
And it came again in the days of Jehoiakim, the son of Josiah, king of Judah, up to the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the son of Josiah, king of Judah; till Jerusalem as taken aay in the fifth month.
No the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Before you ere formed in the body of your mother I had knoledge of you, and before your birth I made you holy; I have given you the ork of being a prophet to the nations.
Then said I, O Lord God! see, I have no poer of ords, for I am a child.
But the Lord said to me, Do not say, I am a child: for herever I send you, you are to go, and hatever I give you orders to say, you are to say.
Have no fear because of them: for I am ith you, to keep you safe, says the Lord.
Then the Lord put out his hand, touching my mouth; and the Lord said to me, See, I have put my ords in your mouth:
See, this day I have put you over the nations and over the kingdoms, for uprooting and smashing don, for destruction and overturning, for building up and planting.
Again the ord of the Lord came to me, saying, Jeremiah, hat do you see? And I said, I see a branch of an almond-tree.
Then the Lord said to me, You have seen ell: for I keep atch over my ord to give effect to it.
And the ord of the Lord came to me a second time, saying, What do you see? And I said, I see a boiling pot, and its face is from the north.
Then the Lord said to me, Out of the north evil ill come, bursting out on all the people of the land.

For see, I ill send for all the families of the kingdoms of the north, says the Lord; and they ill come, everyone placing his high seat at the ay into Jerusalem, and against its alls on every side, and against all the tons of Judah.
And I ill give my decision against them on account of all their evil-doing; because they have given me up, burning perfumes to other gods and orshipping the orks of their hands.
So make yourself ready, and go and say to them everything I give you orders to say: do not be overcome by fear of them, or I ill send fear on you before them.

For see, this day have I made you a alled ton, and an iron pillar, and alls of brass, against all the land, against the kings of Judah, against its captains, against its priests, and against the people of the land.
They ill be fighting against you, but they ill not overcome you: for I am ith you, says the Lord, to give you salvation.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

Go and say in the ears of Jerusalem, The Lord says, I still keep the memory of your kind heart hen you ere young, and your love hen you became my bride; ho you ent after me in the aste of sand, in an unplanted land.
Israel as holy to the Lord, the first-fruits of his increase: all ho made attacks on him ere judged as rongdoers, evil came on them, says the Lord.
Give ear to the ords of the Lord, O sons of Jacob and all the families of Israel:
These are the ords of the Lord: What evil have your fathers seen in me that they have gone far from me, and, alking after hat is false, have become false?

And they never said, Where is the Lord, ho took us up out of the land of Egypt; ho as our guide through the aste of sand, through an unplanted land full of deep holes, through a dry land of deep shade, hich no one ent through and here no man as living?
And I took you into a fertile land, here you ere living on its fruit and its ealth; but hen you came in, you made my land unclean, and made my heritage a disgusting thing.

The priests did not say, Where is the Lord? and those ho ere expert in the la had no knoledge of me: and the rulers did evil against me, and the prophets became prophets of the Baal, going after things ithout value.
For this reason, I ill again put forard my cause against you, says the Lord, even against you and against your children’s children.
For go over to the sea-lands of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and give deep thought to it; and see if there has ever been such a thing.
Has any nation ever made a change in their gods, though they are no gods? but my people have given up their glory in exchange for hat is of no profit.
Be full of onder, O heavens, at this; be overcome ith fear, be completely aste, says the Lord.
For my people have done to evils; they have given up me, the fountain of living aters, and have made for themselves ater-holes, cut out from the rock, broken ater-holes, of no use for storing ater.
Is Israel a servant? has he been a house-servant from birth? hy has he been made aste?
The young lions have made an outcry against him ith a loud voice: they have made his land aste; his tons are burned up, ith no one living in them.
Even the children of Noph and Tahpanhes have put shame on you.
Has not this come on you because you have given up the Lord your God, ho as your guide by the ay?
And no, hat have you to do on the ay to Egypt, to get your drink from the aters of the Nile? or hat have you to do on the ay to Assyria, to get your drink from the aters of the River?

The evil you yourselves have done ill be your punishment, your errors ill be your judge: be certain then, and see that it is an evil and a bitter thing to give up the Lord your God, and no longer to be moved by fear of me, says the Lord, the Lord of armies.

For in the past, your yoke as broken by your hands and your cords parted; and you said, I ill not be your servant; for on every high hill and under every branching tree, your behaviour as like that of a loose oman
But hen you ere planted by me, you ere a noble vine, in every ay a true seed: ho then have you been changed into the branching plant of a strange vine?
For even if you are ashed ith soda and take much soap, still your evil-doing is marked before me, says the Lord God.
Ho are you able to say, I am not unclean, I have not gone after the Baals? see your ay in the valley, be clear about hat you have done: you are a quick-footed camel tisting her ay in and out;

An untrained ass, used to the aste land, breathing up the ind in her desire; at her time, ho is able to send her aay? all those ho are looking for her ill have no need to make themselves tired; in her month they ill get her.
Do not let your foot be ithout shoes, or your throat dry from need of ater: but you said, There is no hope: no, for I have been a lover of strange gods, and after them I ill go.
As the thief is shamed hen he is taken, so is Israel shamed; they, their kings and their rulers, their priests and their prophets;

Who say to a tree, You are my father; and to a stone, You have given me life: for their backs have been turned to me, not their faces: but in the time of their trouble they ill say, Up! and be our saviour.

But here are the gods you have made for yourselves? let them come, if they are able to give you salvation in the time of your trouble: for the number of your gods is as the number of your tons, O Judah.
Why ill you put forard your cause against me? You have all done evil against me, says the Lord.
I gave your children blos to no purpose; they got no good from training: your sord has been the destruction of your prophets, like a death-giving lion.
O generation, see the ord of the Lord. Have I been a aste land to Israel? or a land of dark night? hy do my people say, We have got loose, e ill not come to you again?
Is it possible for a virgin to put out of her memory her ornaments, or a bride her robes? but my people have put me out of their memories for unnumbered days.
With hat care are your ays ordered hen you are looking for love! so ... your ays.
And in the skirts of your robe may be seen the life-blood of those ho have done no rong: ...
And still you said, I have done no rong; truly, his rath is turned aay from me. See, I ill take up the cause against you, because you say, I have done no rong.
Why do you go about so much for the purpose of changing your ay? you ill be shamed on account of Egypt, as you ere shamed on account of Assyria.
Truly, you ill go out from him ith your hands on your head: for the Lord has given up those in hom you have put your faith, and they ill be of no help to you.

They say, If a man puts aay his ife and she goes from him and becomes another man’s, ill he go back to her again? ill not that land have been made unclean? but though you have been acting like a loose oman ith a number of lovers, ill you no come back to me? says the Lord.

Let your eyes be lifted up to the open hilltops, and see; here have you not been taken by your lovers? You have been seated aiting for them by the ayside like an Arabian in the aste land; you have made the land unclean ith your loose ays and your evil-doing.
So the shoers have been kept back, and there has been no spring rain; still your bro is the bro of a loose oman, you ill not let yourself be shamed.
Will you not, from this time, make your prayer to me, crying, My father, you are the friend of my early years?
Will he be angry for ever? ill he keep his rath to the end? These things you have said, and have done evil and have had your ay.

And the Lord said to me in the days of Josiah the king, Have you seen hat Israel, turning aay from me, has done? She has gone up on every high mountain and under every branching tree, acting like a loose oman there.
And I said, After she has done all these things she ill come back to me; but she did not. And her false sister Judah sa it.

And though she sa that, because Israel, turning aay from me, had been untrue to me, I had put her aay and given her a statement in riting ending the relation beteen us, still Judah, her false sister, had no fear, but ent and did the same.
So that through all her loose behaviour the land became unclean, and she as untrue, giving herself to stones and trees.
But for all this, her false sister Judah has not come back to me ith all her heart, but ith deceit, says the Lord.
And the Lord said to me, Israel in her turning aay is seen to be more upright than false Judah.

Go, and give out these ords to the north, and say, Come back, O Israel, though you have been turned aay from me, says the Lord; my face ill not be against you in rath: for I am full of mercy, says the Lord, I ill not be angry for ever.
Only be conscious of your sin, the evil you have done against the Lord your God; you have gone ith strange men under every branching tree, giving no attention to my voice, says the Lord.
Come back, O children ho are turned aay, says the Lord; for I am a husband to you, and I ill take you, one from a ton and to from a family, and ill make you come to Zion;
And I ill give you keepers, pleasing to my heart, ho ill give you your food ith knoledge and isdom.

And it ill come about, hen your numbers are increased in the land, in those days, says the Lord, that they ill no longer say, The ark of the agreement of the Lord: it ill not come into their minds, they ill not have any memory of it, or be conscious of the loss of it, and it ill not be made again.

At that time Jerusalem ill be named the seat of the Lord’s kingdom; and all the nations ill come together to it, to the name of the Lord, to Jerusalem: and no longer ill their steps be guided by the purposes of their evil hearts.
In those days the family of Judah ill go ith the family of Israel, and they ill come together out of the land of the north into the land hich I gave for a heritage to your fathers.

But I said, Ho am I to put you among the children, and give you a desired land, a heritage of glory among the armies of the nations? and I said, You are to say to me, My father; and not be turned aay from me.
Truly, as a ife is false to her husband, so have you been false to me, O Israel, says the Lord.
A voice is sounding on the open hilltops, the eeping and the prayers of the children of Israel; because their ay is tisted, they have not kept the Lord their God in mind.
Come back, you children ho have been turned aay, and I ill take aay your desire for andering. See, e have come to you, for you are the Lord our God.
Truly, the hills, and the noise of an army on the mountains, are a false hope: truly, in the Lord our God is the salvation of Israel.
But the Baal has taken all the ork of our fathers from our earliest days; their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

Let us be stretched on the earth in our donfall, covering ourselves ith our shame: for e have been sinners against the Lord our God, e and our fathers, from our earliest years even till this day: and e have not given ear to the voice of the Lord our God.
If you ill come back, O Israel, says the Lord, you ill come back to me: and if you ill put aay your disgusting ays, you ill not be sent aay from before me.
And you ill take your oath, By the living Lord, in good faith and isdom and righteousness; and the nations ill make use of you as a blessing, and in you ill they take a pride.
For this is hat the Lord says to the men of Judah and to Jerusalem: Get your unorked land ploughed up, do not put in your seeds among thorns.
Undergo a circumcision of the heart, you men of Judah and people of Jerusalem: or my rath may come out like fire, burning so that no one is able to put it out, because of the evil of your doings.
Say openly in Judah, give it out in Jerusalem, and say, Let the horn be sounded in the land: crying out in a loud voice, Come together, and let us go into the alled tons.
Put up a flag for a sign to Zion: go in flight so that you may be safe, aiting no longer: for I ill send evil from the north, and a great destruction.

A lion has gone up from his secret place in the oods, and one ho makes aste the nations is on his ay; he has gone out from his place, to make your land unpeopled, so that your tons ill be made aste, ith no man living in them.
For this put on haircloth, ith eeping and loud crying: for the burning rath of the Lord is not turned back from us.
And it ill come about in that day, says the Lord, that the heart of the king ill be dead in him, and the hearts of the rulers; and the priests ill be overcome ith fear, and the prophets ith onder.
Then said I, Ah, Lord God! your ords ere not true hen you said to this people and to Jerusalem, You ill have peace; hen the sord has come even to the soul.
At that time it ill be said to this people and to Jerusalem, A burning ind from the open hilltops in the aste land is bloing on the daughter of my people, not for separating or cleaning the grain;
A full ind ill come for me: and no I ill give my decision against them.
See, he ill come up like the clouds, and his ar-carriages like the storm-ind: his horses are quicker than eagles. Sorro is ours, for destruction has come on us.
O Jerusalem, make your heart clean from evil, so that you may have salvation. Ho long are evil purposes to have a resting-place in you?
For a voice is sounding from Dan, giving out evil from the hills of Ephraim:
Make this come to the minds of the nations, make a statement openly against Jerusalem, that attackers are coming from a far country and their voices ill be loud against the tons of Judah.
Like keepers of a field they are against her on every side; because she has been fighting against me, says the Lord.
Your ays and your doings have made these things come on you; this is your sin; truly it is bitter, going deep into your heart.
My soul, my soul! I am pained to my inmost heart; my heart is troubled in me; I am not able to be quiet, because the sound of the horn, the note of ar, has come to my ears.
Nes is given of destruction on destruction; all the land is made aste: suddenly my tents, straight aay my curtains, are made aste.
Ho long ill I go on seeing the flag and hearing the sound of the ar-horn?
For my people are foolish, they have no knoledge of me; they are evil-minded children, ithout sense, all of them: they are ise in evil-doing, but have no knoledge of doing good.
Looking at the earth, I sa that it as aste and ithout form; and to the heavens, that they had no light.
Looking at the mountains, I sa them shaking, and all the hills ere moved about.
Looking, I sa that there as no man, and all the birds of heaven had gone in flight.
Looking, I sa that the fertile field as a aste, and all its tons ere broken don before the Lord and before his burning rath.
For this is hat the Lord has said: All the land ill become a aste; I ill make destruction complete.
The earth ill be eeping for this, and the heavens on high ill be black: because I have said it, and I ill not go back from it; it is my purpose, and it ill not be changed.
All the land is in flight because of the noise of the horsemen and the bomen; they have taken cover in the oodland and up on the rocks: every ton has been given up, not a man is living in them.

And you, hen you are made aste, hat ill you do? Though you are clothed in red, though you make yourself beautiful ith ornaments of gold, though you make your eyes ide ith paint, it is for nothing that you make yourself fair; your lovers have no more desire for you, they have designs on your life.

A voice has come to my ears like the voice of a oman in birth-pains, the pain of one giving birth to her first child, the voice of the daughter of Zion, fighting for breath, stretching out her hands, saying, No sorro is mine! for my strength is gone from me before the takers of life.

Go quickly through the streets of Jerusalem, and see no, and get knoledge, and make a search in her ide places if there is a man, if there is one in her ho is upright, ho keeps faith; and she ill have my forgiveness.
And though they say, By the living Lord; truly their oaths are false.

O Lord, do not your eyes see good faith? you have given them punishment, but they ere not troubled; you have sent destruction on them, but they did not take your teaching to heart: they have made their faces harder than a rock; they ould not come back.
Then I said, But these are the poor: they are foolish, for they have no knoledge of the ay of the Lord or of the behaviour desired by their God.

I ill go to the great men and have talk ith them; for they have knoledge of the ay of the Lord and of the behaviour desired by their God. But as for these, their one purpose is a broken yoke and burst bands.

And so a lion from the oods ill put them to death, a olf of the aste land ill make them aste, a leopard ill keep atch on their tons, and everyone ho goes out from them ill be food for the beasts; because of the great number of their sins and the increase of their rongdoing.

Ho is it possible for you to have my forgiveness for this? your children have given me up, taking their oaths by those ho are no gods: hen I had given them food in full measure, they ere false to their ives, taking their pleasure in the houses of loose omen.
They ere full of desire, like horses after a meal of grain: everyone ent after his neighbour’s ife.
Am I not to give punishment for these things? says the Lord: ill not my soul take payment from such a nation as this?
Go up against her vines and make aste; let the destruction be complete: take aay her branches, for they are not the Lord’s.
For the people of Israel and the people of Judah have been very false to me, says the Lord.
They ould have nothing to do ith the Lord, saying, He ill do nothing, and no evil ill come to us; e ill not see the sord or be short of food:
And the prophets ill become ind, and the ord is not in them; so it ill be done to them.
For this reason the Lord, the God of armies, has said: Because you have said this, I ill make my ords in your mouth a fire, and this people ood, and they ill be burned up by it.

See, I ill send you a nation from far aay, O people of Israel, says the Lord; a strong nation and an old nation, a nation hose language is strange to you, so that you may not get the sense of their ords.
Their arros give certain death, they are all men of ar.

They ill take all the produce of your fields, hich ould have been food for your sons and your daughters: they ill take your flocks and your herds: they ill take all your vines and your fig-trees: and ith the sord they ill make aste your alled tons in hich you put your faith.
But even in those days, says the Lord, I ill not let your destruction be complete.

And it ill come about, hen you say, Why has the Lord our God done all these things to us? that you ill say to them, As you gave me up, making yourselves servants to strange gods in your land, so ill you be servants to strange men in a land hich is not yours.
Say this openly in Jacob and give it out in Judah, saying,
Give ear no to this, O foolish people ithout sense; ho have eyes but see nothing, and ears ithout the poer of hearing:

Have you no fear of me? says the Lord; ill you not be shaking ith fear before me, ho have put the sand as a limit for the sea, by an eternal order, so that it may not go past it? and though it is ever in motion, it is not able to have its ay; though the sound of its aves is loud, they are not able to go past it.
But the heart of this people is uncontrolled and turned aay from me; they are broken loose and gone.
And they do not say in their hearts, No let us give orship to our God, ho gives the rain, the inter and the spring rain, at the right time; ho keeps for us the ordered eeks of the grain-cutting.
Through your evil-doing these things have been turned aay, and your sins have kept back good from you.
For there are sinners among my people: they keep atch, like men atching for birds; they put a net and take men in it.
As the fol-house is full of birds, so are their houses full of deceit: for this reason they have become great and have got ealth.

They have become fat and strong: they have gone far in orks of evil: they give no support to the cause of the child ithout a father, so that they may do ell; they do not see that the poor man gets his rights.
Am I not to give punishment for these things? says the Lord: ill not my soul take payment from such a nation as this?
A thing of onder and fear has come about in the land;
The prophets give false ords and the priests give decisions by their direction; and my people are glad to have it so: and hat ill you do in the end?

Go in flight out of Jerusalem, so that you may be safe, you children of Benjamin, and let the horn be sounded in Tekoa, and the flag be lifted up on Beth-haccherem: for evil is looking out from the north, and a great destruction.
The fair and delicate one, the daughter of Zion, ill be cut off by my hand.
Keepers of sheep ith their flocks ill come to her; they ill put up their tents round her; everyone ill get food in his place.
Make ar ready against her; up! let us go up hen the sun is high. Sorro is ours! for the day is turned and the shades of evening are stretched out.
Up! let us go up by night, and send destruction on her great houses.
For this is hat the Lord of armies has said: Let trees be cut don and an earthork be placed against Jerusalem: sorro on the false ton! inside her there is nothing but cruel ays.
As the spring keeps its aters cold, so she keeps her evil in her: the sound of cruel and violent behaviour is in her; before me at all times are disease and ounds.
Undergo teaching, O Jerusalem, or my soul ill be turned aay from you, and I ill make you a aste, an unpeopled land.

This is hat the Lord of armies has said: Everything ill be taken from the rest of Israel as the last grapes are taken from the vine; let your hand be turned to the small branches, like one pulling off grapes.

To hom am I to give ord, itnessing so that they may take note? see, their ears are stopped, and they are not able to give attention: see, the ord of the Lord has been a cause of shame to them, they have no delight in it.

For this reason I am full of the rath of the Lord, I am tired of keeping it in: may it be let loose on the children in the street, and on the band of the young men together: for even the husband ith his ife ill be taken, the old man ith him ho is full of days.
And their houses ill be handed over to others, their fields and their ives together: for my hand ill be stretched out against the people of the land, says the Lord.
For from the least of them even to the greatest, everyone is given up to getting money; from the prophet even to the priest, everyone is orking deceit.
And they have made little of the ounds of my people, saying, Peace, peace; hen there is no peace.

Let them be put to shame because they have done disgusting things. They had no shame, they ere not able to become red ith shame: so they ill come don ith those ho are falling: hen my punishment comes on them, they ill be made lo, says the Lord.

This is hat the Lord has said: Take your place looking out on the ays; make search for the old roads, saying, Where is the good ay? and go in it that you may have rest for your souls. But they said, We ill not go in it.
And I put atchmen over you, saying, Give attention to the sound of the horn; but they said, We ill not give attention.
So then, give ear, you nations, and ...
Give ear, O earth: see, I ill make evil come on this people, even the fruit of their thoughts, because they have not given attention to my ords, and they ould have nothing to do ith my la.
To hat purpose does seet perfume come to me from Sheba, and spices from a far country? your burned offerings give me no pleasure, your offerings of beasts are not pleasing to me.

For this reason the Lord has said, See, I ill put stones in the ay of this people: and the fathers and the sons together ill go falling over them; the neighbour and his friend ill come to destruction.
The Lord has said, See, a people is coming from the north country, a great nation ill be put in motion from the inmost parts of the earth.

Bos and spears are in their hands; they are cruel and have no mercy; their voice is like the thunder of the sea, and they go on horses; everyone in his place like men going to the fight, against you, O daughter of Zion.
The nes of it has come to our ears; our hands have become feeble: trouble has come on us and pain, like the pain of a oman in childbirth.
Go not out into the field or by the ay; for there is the sord of the attacker, and fear on every side.
O daughter of my people, put on haircloth, rolling yourself in the dust: give yourself to sorro, as for an only son, ith most bitter cries of grief; for he ho makes aste ill come on us suddenly.
I have made you a tester among my people, so that you may have knoledge of their ay and put it to the test.
All of them are turned aay, going about ith false stories; they are brass and iron: they are all orkers of deceit.
The bloer is bloing strongly, the lead is burned aay in the fire: they go on heating the metal to no purpose, for the evil-doers are not taken aay.
They ill be named aste silver, because the Lord has given them up.
The ord hich came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
Take your place in the dooray of the Lord’s house, and give out this ord there, and say, Give ear to the ord of the Lord, all you of Judah ho come inside these doors to give orship to the Lord.
The Lord of armies, the God of Israel, says, Let your ays and your doings be changed for the better and I ill let you go on living in this place.
Put no faith in false ords, saying, The Temple of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord, the Temple of the Lord, are these.
For if your ays and your doings are truly changed for the better; if you truly give right decisions beteen a man and his neighbour;

If you are not cruel to the man from a strange country, and to the child ithout a father, and to the ido, and do not put the upright to death in this place, or go after other gods, causing damage to yourselves:
Then I ill let you go on living in this place, in the land hich I gave to your fathers in the past and for ever.
See, you put your faith in false ords hich are of no profit.
Will you take the goods of others, put men to death, and be untrue to your ives, and take false oaths, and have perfumes burned to the Baal, and go after other gods hich are strange to you;
And come and take your place before me in this house, hich is named by my name, and say, We have been made safe; so that you may do all these disgusting things?
Has this house, hich is named by my name, become a hole of thieves to you? Truly I, even I, have seen it, says the Lord.
But go no to my place hich as in Shiloh, here I put my name at first, and see hat I did to it because of the evil-doing of my people Israel.
And no, because you have done all these orks, says the Lord, and I sent my ord to you, getting up early and sending, but you did not give ear; and my voice came to you, but you gave no anser:
For this reason I ill do to the house hich is named by my name, and in hich you have put your faith, and to the place hich I gave to you and to your fathers, as I have done to Shiloh.
And I ill send you aay from before my face, as I have sent aay all your brothers, even all the seed of Ephraim.
And as for you (Jeremiah), make no prayers for this people, send up no cry or prayer for them, make no request for them to me: for I ill not give ear.
Do you not see hat they are doing in the tons of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
The children go for ood, the fathers get the fire burning, the omen are orking the paste to make cakes for the queen of heaven, and drink offerings are drained out to other gods, moving me to rath.
Are they moving me to rath? says the Lord; are they not moving themselves to their shame?

So this is hat the Lord God has said: See, my rath and my passion ill be let loose on this place, on man and beast, and on the trees of the field, and on the produce of the earth; it ill be burning and ill not be put out.
These are the ords of the Lord of armies, the God of Israel: Put your burned offerings ith your offerings of beasts, and take flesh for your food.
For I said nothing to your fathers, and gave them no orders, on the day hen I took them out of Egypt, about burned offerings or offerings of beasts:
But this as the order I gave them, saying, Give ear to my voice, and I ill be your God, and you ill be my people: go in all the ay ordered by me, so that all may be ell for you.
But they took no note and did not give ear, but ere guided by the thoughts and the pride of their evil hearts, going back and not forard.
From the day hen your fathers came out of Egypt till this day, I have sent my servants the prophets to you, getting up early every day and sending them:
But still they took no note and ould not give ear, but they made their necks stiff, doing orse than their fathers.
And you are to say all these ords to them, but they ill not give ear to you: you ill send out your voice to them, but they ill give no anser.
And you are to say to them, This is the nation hich has not given ear to the voice of their God, or taken his teaching to heart: good faith is dead and is cut off from their mouths.
Let your hair be cut off, O Jerusalem, and let it go, and let a song of grief go up on the open hilltops; for the Lord is turned aay from the generation of his rath and has given them up.
For the children of Judah have done hat is evil in my eyes, says the Lord: they have put their disgusting images in the house hich is named by my name, making it unclean.

And they have put up the high place of Topheth in the valley of the son of Hinnom, burning their sons and their daughters there in the fire; a thing hich as not ordered by me and never came into my mind.

For this cause, the days are coming, says the Lord, hen it ill no longer be named Topheth, or, The valley of the son of Hinnom, but, The valley of Death: for they ill put the dead into the earth in Topheth till there is no more room.
And the bodies of this people ill be food for the birds of heaven and for the beasts of the earth; and there ill be no one to send them aay.

And in the tons of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, I ill put an end to the laughing voices, the voice of joy and the voice of the nely-married man and the voice of the bride: for the land ill become a aste.

At that time, says the Lord, they ill take the bones of the kings of Judah, and the bones of his rulers, and the bones of the priests, and the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the people of Jerusalem out of their resting-places:

And they ill put them out before the sun and the moon and all the stars of heaven, hose lovers and servants they have been, after hom they have gone, to hom they have made prayers, and to hom they have given orship: they ill not be put together or placed in the earth; they ill be aste on the face of the earth.
And death ill be desired more than life by the rest of this evil family ho are still living in all the places here I have sent them aay, says the Lord of armies.
Further, you are to say to them, This is hat the Lord has said: Will those ho are falling not be lifted up again? ill he ho has gone aay not come back?
Why do these people of Jerusalem go back, for ever turning aay? they ill not give up their deceit, they ill not come back.
I took note and gave ear, but no one said hat is right: no man had regret for his evil-doing, saying, What have I done? everyone goes off on his ay like a horse rushing to the fight.
Truly, the stork in the heavens is conscious of her fixed times; the dove and the sallo and the crane keep to the times of their coming; but my people have no knoledge of the la of the Lord.
Ho is it that you say, We are ise and the la of the Lord is ith us? But see, the false pen of the scribes has made it false.
The ise men are shamed, they are overcome ith fear and taken: see, they have given up the ord of the Lord; and hat use is their isdom to them?

So I ill give their ives to others, and their fields to those ho ill take them for themselves: for everyone, from the least to the greatest, is given up to getting money; from the priest even to the prophet, everyone is false.
And they have made little of the ounds of the daughter of Zion, saying, Peace, peace; hen there is no peace.

Let them be put to shame because they have done disgusting things. They had no shame, they ere not able to become red ith shame: so they ill come don ith those ho are falling: in the time of their punishment they ill be made lo, says the Lord.
I ill put an end to them completely, says the Lord: there are no grapes on the vine and no figs on the fig-tree, and the leaf is dry.

Why are e seated doing nothing? come together, and let us go to the alled tons, and let destruction overtake us there, for the Lord our God has sent destruction on us, and given us bitter ater for our drink, because e have done evil against the Lord.
We ere looking for peace, but no good came; and for a time of ell-being, but there is only a great fear.

The loud breathing of the horses comes to our ears from Dan: at the sound of the outcry of his ar-horses, all the land is shaking ith fear; for they have come, and have made a meal of the land and everything in it; the ton and the people living in it.
See, I ill send snakes and poison-snakes among you, against hich the onder-orker has no poer; and they ill give you ounds hich may not be made ell, says the Lord.
Sorro has come on me! my heart in me is feeble.

The voice of the cry of the daughter of my people comes from a far land: Is the Lord not in Zion? is not her King in her? Why have they made me angry ith their images and their strange gods hich are no gods?
The grain-cutting is past, the summer is ended, and no salvation has come to us.
For the destruction of the daughter of my people I am broken: I am dressed in the clothing of grief; fear has taken me in its grip.
Is there no life-giving oil in Gilead? is there no expert in medical arts? hy then have my people not been made ell?
If only my head as a stream of aters and my eyes fountains of eeping, so that I might go on eeping day and night for the dead of the daughter of my people!
If only I had in the aste land a night’s resting-place for travellers, so that I might go aay, far from my people! for they are all untrue, a band of false men.
Their tongues are bent like a bo to send out false ords: they have become strong in the land, but not for good faith: they go on from evil to evil, and they have no knoledge of me, says the Lord.
Let everyone keep atch on his neighbour, and put no faith in any brother: for every brother ill certainly be tricking his brother, and every neighbour ill go about saying evil.
Everyone ill make sport of his neighbour ith deceit, not saying hat is true: their tongues have been trained to say false ords; they are tisted, hating to come back.
There is rong on rong, deceit on deceit; they have given up the knoledge of me, says the Lord.
So the Lord of armies has said, See, I ill make them soft in the fire and put them to the test; this I ill do because of their evil-doing.
His tongue is an arro causing death; the ords of his mouth are deceit: he says ords of peace to his neighbour, but in his heart he is aiting secretly for him.
Am I not to send punishment for these things? says the Lord: ill not my soul take payment from such a nation as this?

Give yourselves to eeping, crying out in sorro for the mountains; and for the fields of the aste land send up a song of grief, because they are burned up, so that no one goes through; there is no sound of cattle; the bird of the heavens and the beast are in flight and are gone.
And I ill make Jerusalem a mass of broken stones, the living-place of jackals; and I ill make the tons of Judah a aste, ith no man living there.

Who is the ise man able to see this? ho is he to hom the ord of the Lord has come, so that he may make it clear? hy is the land given to destruction and burned up like a aste place, so that no one goes through?
And the Lord said, Because they have given up my la hich I put before them, giving no attention to my voice and not being guided by it;
But they have been alking in the pride of their hearts, going after the Baals, as their fathers gave them teaching.
So the Lord of armies, the God of Israel, has said, I ill give them, even this people, bitter plants for food and bitter ater for drink.
And I ill send them andering among the nations, among people strange to them and to their fathers: and I ill send the sord after them till I have put an end to them.
This is hat the Lord of armies has said: Take thought and send for the eeping omen, so that they may come; and send for the ise omen, so that they may come:
Let them quickly make cries of sorro for us, so that drops may be floing from our eyes till they are streaming ith ater.
For a sound of eeping goes up from Zion, a cry, Ho has destruction come on us? e are overcome ith shame because e have gone aay from our land; he has sent us out from our house.

But even no, give ear to the ord of the Lord, O you omen; let your ears be open to the ord of his mouth, training your daughters to give cries of sorro, everyone teaching her neighbour a song of grief.
For death has come up into our indos, forcing its ay into our great houses; cutting off the children in the streets and the young men in the ide places.
The bodies of men ill be falling like aste on the open fields, and like grain dropped by the grain-cutter, and no one ill take them up.
This is the ord of the Lord: Let not the ise man take pride in his isdom, or the strong man in his strength, or the man of ealth in his ealth:

But if any man has pride, let it be in this, that he has the isdom to have knoledge of me, that I am the Lord, orking mercy, giving true decisions, and doing righteousness in the earth: for in these things I have delight, says the Lord.
See, the day is coming, says the Lord, hen I ill send punishment on all those ho have circumcision in the flesh;

On Egypt and on Judah and on Edom and on the children of Ammon and on Moab and on all ho have the ends of their hair cut, ho are living in the aste land: for all these nations and all the people of Israel are ithout circumcision in their hearts.
Give ear to the ord hich the Lord says to you, O people of Israel:
This is hat the Lord has said: Do not go in the ay of the nations; have no fear of the signs of heaven, for the nations go in fear of them.
For that hich is feared by the people is foolish: it is the ork of the hands of the orkman; for a tree is cut don by him out of the oods ith his axe.
They make it beautiful ith silver and gold; they make it strong ith nails and hammers, so that it may not be moved.
It is like a pillar in a garden of plants, and has no voice: it has to be lifted, for it has no poer of alking. Have no fear of it; for it has no poer of doing evil and it is not able to do any good.
There is no one like you, O Lord; you are great and your name is great in poer.
Who ould not have fear of you, O King of the nations? for it is your right: for among all the ise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is no one like you.
But they are together like beasts and foolish: the teaching of false gods is ood.
Silver hammered into plates is sent from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the ork of the expert orkman and of the hands of the gold-orker; blue and purple is their clothing, all the ork of expert men.
But the Lord is the true God; he is the living God and an eternal king: hen he is angry, the earth is shaking ith fear, and the nations give ay before his rath.
This is hat you are to say to them: The gods ho have not made the heavens and the earth ill be cut off from the earth and from under the heavens.
He has made the earth by his poer, he has made the orld strong in its place by his isdom, and by his ise design the heavens have been stretched out.

At the sound of his voice there is a massing of aters in the heavens, and he makes the mists go up from the ends of the earth; he makes the thunder-flames for the rain, and sends out the ind from his store-houses.
Then every man becomes like a beast ithout knoledge; every gold-orker is put to shame by the image he has made: for his metal image is deceit, and there is no breath in them.
They are nothing, a ork of error: in the time of their punishment, destruction ill overtake them.
The heritage of Jacob is not like these; for the maker of all things is his heritage: the Lord of armies is his name.
Get your goods together and go out of the land, O you ho are shut up in the alled ton.
For the Lord has said, I ill send the people in flight like a stone from the land at this time, troubling them so that they ill be conscious of it.
Sorro is mine for I am ounded! my ound may not be made ell; and I said, Cruel is my disease, I may not be free from it.
My tent is pulled don and all my cords are broken: my children have gone from me, and they are not: no longer is there anyone to give help in stretching out my tent and hanging up my curtains.
For the keepers of the sheep have become like beasts, not looking to the Lord for directions: so they have not done isely and all their flocks have been put to flight.
Nes is going about, see, it is coming, a great shaking is coming from the north country, so that the tons of Judah may be made aste and become the living-place of jackals.
O Lord, I am conscious that a man’s ay is not in himself: man has no poer of guiding his steps.
O Lord, put me right, but ith ise purpose; not in your rath, or you ill make me small.

Let your rath be let loose on the nations hich have no knoledge of you, and on the families ho give no orship to your name: for they have made a meal of Jacob, truly they have made a meal of him and put an end to him and made his fields a aste.
The ord hich came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying,
Give ear to the ords of this agreement, and say to the men of Judah and to the people of Jerusalem,
The Lord, the God of Israel, has said, Let that man be cursed ho does not give ear to the ords of this agreement,

To the order hich I gave your fathers on the day hen I took them out of the land of Egypt, out of the oven of iron, saying, Give ear to my voice, and do all the orders I have given you: so you ill be my people, and I ill be your God:
So that I may give effect to the oath hich I made to your fathers, to give them a land floing ith milk and honey as at this day. And I said in anser, So be it, O Lord.
And the Lord said to me, Give out these ords in the tons of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, saying, Give ear to the ords of this agreement and do them.
For I gave certain itness to your fathers on the day hen I took them up out of the land of Egypt, and even to this day, getting up early and itnessing and saying, Give ear to my voice.

But they gave no attention and did not give ear, but they ent on, every man in the pride of his evil heart: so I sent on them all the curses in this agreement, hich I gave them orders to keep, but they did not.
And the Lord said to me, There is an evil design at ork among the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem.

They are turned back to the sins of their fathers, ho ould not give ear to my ords; they have gone after other gods and become their servants: the people of Israel and the people of Judah have not kept the agreement hich I made ith their fathers.
So the Lord has said, I ill send evil on them, hich they ill not be able to get aay from; and they ill send up a cry for help to me, but I ill not give ear to them.
Then the tons of Judah and the people of Jerusalem ill go crying for help to the gods to hom they have been burning perfumes: but they ill give them no salvation in the time of their trouble.
For the number of your gods is as the number of your tons, O Judah; and for every street in Jerusalem you have put up altars to the Baal for burning perfumes to the Baal.
And as for you, make no prayers for this people, send up no cry or prayer for them: for I ill not give ear to their cry in the time of their trouble.
About Judah. What have you to do in my house? is it your thought that oaths and holy flesh ill get you out of your trouble? ill you make yourself safe in this ay?
You had been named by the Lord, A branching olive-tree, fair ith beautiful fruit: ith the noise of a great rushing he has put it on fire and its branches are broken.

For the Lord of armies, by hom you ere planted, has given his decision for evil against you, because of the evil hich the people of Israel and the people of Judah have done, In moving me to rath by offering perfumes to the Baal.
And the Lord gave me knoledge of it and I sa it: then you made clear to me their doings.

But I as like a gentle lamb taken to be put to death; I had no thought that they ere designing evil against me, saying, Come and let us make trouble his food, cutting him off from the land of the living, so that there may be no more memory of his name.
But, O Lord of armies, judging in righteousness, testing the thoughts and the heart, let me see your punishment come on them: for I have put my cause before you.

So this is hat the Lord of armies has said about the men of Anathoth ho have made designs against your life, saying, You are not to be a prophet in the name of the Lord, or death ill overtake you by our hands:
So the Lord of armies has said, See, I ill send punishment on them: the young men ill be put to the sord; their sons and their daughters ill come to death through need of food:
Not one of them ill keep his life, for I ill send evil on the men of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.
You are in the right, O Lord, hen I put my cause before you: still let me take up ith you the question of your decisions: hy does the evil-doer do ell? hy are the orkers of deceit living in comfort?
They have been planted by you, they have taken root; they go on and give fruit: you are near in their mouths but far from their thoughts.
But you, O Lord, have knoledge of me; you see me, searching and testing ho my heart is ith you: let them be pulled out like sheep to be put to death, make them ready for the day of death.

Ho long ill the land have grief, and the plants of all the land be dry? because of the sins of the people living in it, destruction has overtaken the beasts and the birds; because they said, God does not see our ays.
If running ith the fighting-men has made you tired, ho ill you be able to keep up ith horses? and if in a land of peace you go in flight, hat ill become of you in the thick groth of Jordan?
For even your brothers, your father’s family, even they have been untrue to you, crying loudly after you: have no faith in them, though they say fair ords to you.
I have given up my house, I have let my heritage go; I have given the loved one of my soul into the hands of her haters.
My heritage has become like a lion in the oodland to me; her voice has been loud against me; so I have hate for her.
My heritage is like a brightly coloured bird to me; the cruel birds are attacking her on every side: go, get together all the beasts of the field, make them come for destruction.
The keepers of sheep have been the destruction of my vine-garden, crushing my heritage under their feet; they have made my fair heritage an unplanted aste;
They have made it aste; it is eeping to me, being asted; all the land is made aste, because no man takes it to heart.
Those ho make aste have come on all the open hilltops in the aste land; for the sord of the Lord sends destruction from one end of the land to the other end of the land: no flesh has peace.
Though good grain as planted, they have got in thorns: they have given themselves pain ithout profit: they ill be shamed on account of their produce, because of the burning rath of the Lord.

This is hat the Lord has said against all my evil neighbours, ho put their hands on the heritage hich I gave my people Israel: See, I ill have them uprooted from their land, uprooting the people of Judah from among them.
And it ill come about that, after they have been uprooted, I ill again have pity on them; and I ill take them back, every man to his heritage and every man to his land.

And it ill be that, if they give their minds to learning the ays of my people, using my name in their oaths, By the living Lord; as they have been teaching my people to take oaths by the Baal; then their place ill be made certain among my people.
But if they ill not give ear, then I ill have that nation uprooted, and given to destruction, says the Lord.
This is hat the Lord said to me: Go and get yourself a linen band and put it round you and do not put it in ater.
So, as the Lord said, I got a band for a price and put it round my body.
And the ord of the Lord came to me a second time, saying,
Take the band hich you got for a price, hich is round your body, and go to Parah and put it in a secret place there in a hole of the rock.
So I ent and put it in a secret place by Parah, as the Lord had said to me.
Then after a long time, the Lord said to me, Up! go to Parah and get the band hich I gave you orders to put there.
So I ent to Parah and, uncovering the hole, took the band from the place here I had put it aay: and the band as damaged and of no use for anything.
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
The Lord has said, In this ay I ill do damage to the pride of Judah and to the great pride of Jerusalem.

These evil people ho say they ill not give ear to my ords, ho go on in the pride of their hearts and have become servants and orshippers of other gods, ill become like this band hich is of no use for anything.

For as a band goes tightly round a man’s body, so I made all the people of Israel and all the people of Judah tightly united to me; so that they might be a people for me and a name and a praise and a glory: but they ould not give ear.

So you are to say this ord to them: This is the ord of the Lord, the God of Israel: Every skin bottle ill be full of ine; and they ill say to you, Is it not quite clear to us that every skin bottle ill be full of ine?

Then you are to say to them, The Lord has said, I ill make all the people of this land, even the kings seated on David’s seat, and the priests and the prophets and all the people of Jerusalem, overcome ith strong drink.
I ill have them smashed against one another, fathers and sons together, says the Lord: I ill have no pity or mercy, I ill have no feeling for them to keep me from giving them to destruction.
Give ear and let your ears be open; be not lifted up: for these are the ords of the Lord.
Give glory to the Lord your God, before he makes it dark, and before your feet are slipping on the dark mountains, and, hile you are looking for a light, he makes it into deep dark, into black night.
But if you do not give ear to it, my soul ill be eeping in secret for your pride; my eye ill be eeping bitterly, streaming ith ater, because the Lord’s flock has been taken aay as prisoners.
Say to the king and to the queen-mother, Make yourselves lo, be seated on the earth: for the cron of your glory has come don from your heads.
The tons of the south are shut up, and there is no one to make them open: Judah is taken aay as prisoners; all Judah is taken aay as prisoners.
Let your eyes be lifted up (O Jerusalem), and see those ho are coming from the north. Where is the flock hich as given to you, your beautiful flock?
What ill you say hen he puts over you those hom you yourself have made your friends? ill not pains take you like a oman in childbirth?
And if you say in your heart, Why have these things come on me? because of the number of your sins, your skirts have been uncovered and violent punishment overtakes you.
Is it possible for the skin of the Ethiopian to be changed, or the markings on the leopard? Then it might be possible for you to do good, ho have been trained to do evil.
So I ill send them in all directions, as dry grass is taken aay by the ind of the aste land.
This is your fate, the part measured out to you by me, says the Lord, because you have put me out of your memory and put your faith in hat is false.
So I ill have your skirts uncovered before your face, in order that your shame may be seen.

I have seen your disgusting acts, even your false behaviour and your cries of desire and your loose ays on the hills in the field. Unhappy are you, O Jerusalem, you have no desire to be made clean; ho long ill you be in turning back to me?
The ord of the Lord came to Jeremiah hen there as no ater.
Judah is eeping and its doors are dark ith sorro, and people are seated on the earth clothed in black; and the cry of Jerusalem has gone up.

Their great men have sent their servants for ater: they come to the holes and there is no ater to be seen; they come back ith nothing in their vessels; they are overcome ith shame and fear, covering their heads.
Those ho do ork on the land are in fear, for there has been no rain on the land, and the farmers are shamed, covering their heads.
And the roe, giving birth in the field, lets her young one be uncared for, because there is no grass.
And the asses of the field on the open hilltops are opening their mouths ide like jackals to get air; their eyes are hollo because there is no grass.
Though our sins give itness against us, do something, O Lord, for the honour of your name: for again and again e have been turned aay from you, e have done evil against you.
O you hope of Israel, its saviour in time of trouble, hy are you like one ho is strange in the land, and like a traveller putting up his tent for a night?
Why are you like a man surprised, like a man of ar ho is not able to give help? but you, O Lord, are ith us, and e are named by your name; do not go aay from us.

This is hat the Lord has said about this people: Even so they have been glad to go from the right ay; they have not kept their feet from andering, so the Lord has no pleasure in them; no he ill keep their rongdoing in mind and send punishment for their sins.
And the Lord said to me, Make no prayer for this people for their good.

When they go ithout food, I ill not give ear to their cry; hen they give burned offerings and meal offerings, I ill not take pleasure in them: but I ill put an end to them by the sord and by need of food and by disease.
Then I said, Ah, Lord God! see, the prophets say to them, You ill not see the sord or be short of food; but I ill give you certain peace in this place.

Then the Lord said to me, The prophets say false ords in my name, and I gave them no orders, and I said nothing to them: hat they say to you is a false vision and onder-orking ords ithout substance, the deceit of their hearts.
