The daughter of Egypt ill be put to shame; she ill be given up into the hands of the people of the north.
The Lord of armies, the God of Israel, has said: See, I ill send punishment on Amon of No and on Pharaoh and on those ho put their faith in him;

And I ill give them up into the hands of those ho ill take their lives, and into the hands of Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, and into the hands of his servants: and later, it ill be peopled as in the past, says the Lord.

But have no fear, O Jacob, my servant, and do not be troubled, O Israel: for see, I ill make you come back from far aay, and your seed from the land here they are prisoners; and Jacob ill come back, and ill be quiet and in peace, and no one ill give him cause for fear.

Have no fear, O Jacob, my servant, says the Lord; for I am ith you: for I ill put an end to all the nations here I have sent you, but I ill not put an end to you completely: though ith ise purpose I ill put right your errors, and ill not let you go quite ithout punishment.
The ord of the Lord hich came to Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines, before Pharaoh’s attack on Gaza.

This is hat the Lord has said: See, aters are coming up out of the north, and ill become an overfloing stream, overfloing the land and everything in it, the ton and those ho are living in it; and men ill give a cry, and all the people of the land ill be crying out in pain.
At the noise of the stamping of the feet of his ar-horses, at the rushing of his carriages and the thunder of his heels, fathers ill give no thought to their children, because their hands are feeble;

Because of the day hich is coming ith destruction on all the Philistines, cutting off from Tyre and Zidon the last of their helpers: for the Lord ill send destruction on the Philistines, the rest of the sea-land of Caphtor.
The hair is cut off from the head of Gaza; Ashkelon has come to nothing; the last of the Anakim are deeply ounding themselves.
O sord of the Lord, ho long ill you have no rest? put yourself back into your cover; be at peace, be quiet.
Ho is it possible for it to be quiet, seeing that the Lord has given it orders? against Ashkelon and against the sea-land he has given it directions.
Of Moab. The Lord of armies, the God of Israel, has said: Sorro on Nebo, for it has been made aste; Kiriathaim has been put to shame and is taken: the strong place is put to shame and broken don.
The praise of Moab has come to an end; as for Heshbon, evil has been designed against her; come, let us put an end to her as a nation. But your mouth ill be shut, O Madmen; the sord ill go after you.
There is the sound of crying from Horonaim, asting and great destruction;
Moab is broken; her cry has gone out to Zoar.
For by the slope of Luhith they ill go up, eeping all the ay; for on the ay don to Horonaim the cry of destruction has come to their ears.
Go in flight, get aay ith your lives, and let your faces be turned to Aroer in the Arabah.
For because you have put your faith in your strong places, you, even you, ill be taken: and Chemosh ill go out as a prisoner, his priests and his rulers together.
And the attacker ill come against every ton, not one ill be safe; and the valley ill be made aste, and destruction ill come to the loland, as the Lord has said.
Put up a pillar for Moab, for she ill come to a complete end: and her tons ill become a aste, ithout anyone living in them.
Let him be cursed ho does the Lord’s ork half-heartedly; let him be cursed ho keeps back his sord from blood.

From his earliest days, Moab has been living in comfort; like ine long stored he has not been drained from vessel to vessel, he has never gone aay as a prisoner: so his taste is still in him, his smell is unchanged.
So truly, the days are coming, says the Lord, hen I ill send to him men ho ill have him turned over till there is no more ine in his vessels, and his ine-skins ill be completely broken.
And Moab ill be shamed on account of Chemosh, as the children of Israel ere shamed on account of Beth-el their hope.
Ho say you, We are men of ar and strong fighters?
He ho makes Moab aste has gone up against her; and the best of her young men have gone don to their death, says the King, hose name is the Lord of armies.
The fate of Moab is near, and trouble is coming on him very quickly.
All you ho are round about him, give signs of grief for him, and all you ho have knoledge of his name, say, Ho is the strong rod broken, even the beautiful branch!
Come don from your glory, O people of Dibon, and take your seat in the place of the aste; for the attacker of Moab has gone up against you, sending destruction on your strong places.
O daughter of Aroer, take your station by the ay, on the atch: questioning him ho is in flight, and her ho has got aay safe, say, What has been done?
Moab has been put to shame, she is broken: make loud sounds of grief, crying out for help; give the nes in Arnon, that Moab has been made aste.
And punishment has come on the lolands; on Holon and Jahzah, and on Mephaath,
And on Dibon, and on Nebo, and on Beth-diblathaim,
And on Kiriathaim, and on Beth-gamul, and on Beth-meon,
And on Kerioth, and on Bozrah, and on all the tons of the land of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, says the Lord.
Make him full of ine, for his heart has been lifted up against the Lord: and Moab ill be rolling in the food he as not able to keep don, and everyone ill be making sport of him.
For did you not make sport of Israel? as he taken among thieves? for henever you ere talking about him, you ere shaking your head over him.
O people of Moab, go aay from the tons and take cover in the rock; be like the dove of the Arabah, hich makes her living-place in holes.
We have had ord of the pride of Moab, ho great it is; ho he is lifted up in pride; and his great opinion of himself, and that his heart is lifted up.
I have knoledge of his rath, says the Lord, that it is nothing; his high-sounding ords have done nothing.
For this cause I ill give cries of grief for Moab, crying out for Moab, even for all of it; I ill be sorroing for the men of Kir-heres.

My eeping for you, O vine of Sibmah, ill be more than the eeping of Jazer: your branches have gone over the sea, stretching even to Jazer: destruction has come don on your summer fruits and your cut grapes.

All joy is gone; no longer are they glad for the fertile field and for the land of Moab; I have made the ine come to an end from the crushing vessels: no longer ill the grapes be crushed ith the sound of glad voices.
The cry of Heshbon comes even to Elealeh; to Jahaz their voice is sounding; from Zoar even to Horonaim and to Eglath-shelishiyah: for the aters of Nimrim ill become dry.
And I ill put an end in Moab, says the Lord, to him ho is making offerings in the high place and burning perfumes to his gods.
So my heart is sounding for Moab like the sound of pipes, and my heart is sounding like pipes for the men of Kir-heres: for the ealth he has got for himself has come to an end.
For everyhere the hair of the head and the hair of the face is cut off: on every hand there are ounds, and haircloth on every body.
On all the house-tops of Moab and in its streets there is eeping everyhere; for Moab has been broken like a vessel in hich there is no pleasure, says the Lord.
Ho is it broken don! ho is Moab’s back turned in shame! so Moab ill be a cause of sport and of fear to everyone round about him.
For the Lord has said, See, he ill come like an eagle in flight, stretching out his ings against Moab.
Kerioth is taken, and the strong places have been forced, and the hearts of Moab’s men of ar in that day ill be like the heart of a oman in birth-pains.
And Moab ill come to an end as a people, because he has been lifting himself up against the Lord.
Fear and death and the net have come on you, O people of Moab, says the Lord.

He ho goes in flight from the fear ill be overtaken by death; and he ho gets free from death ill be taken in the net: for I ill make this come on Moab, even the year of their punishment, says the Lord.

Those ho ent in flight from the fear are aiting under the shade of Heshbon: for a fire has gone out from Heshbon and a flame from the house of Sihon, burning up the pride of Moab and the cron of the head of the violent ones.
Sorro is yours, O Moab! the people of Chemosh are overcome: for your sons have been taken aay as prisoners, and your daughters made servants.
But still, I ill let the fate of Moab be changed in the last days, says the Lord.
About the children of Ammon. These are the ords of the Lord: Has Israel no sons? has he no one to take the heritage? hy then has Milcom taken Gad for himself, putting his people in its tons?

Because of this, see, the days are coming hen I ill have a cry of ar sounded against Rabbah, the ton of the children of Ammon; it ill become a aste of broken alls, and her daughter-tons ill be burned ith fire: then Israel ill take the heritage of those ho took his heritage, says the Lord.

Make sounds of grief, O Heshbon, for Ai is asted; give loud cries, O daughters of Rabbah, and put haircloth round you: give yourselves to eeping, running here and there and ounding yourselves; for Milcom ill be taken prisoner together ith his rulers and his priests.
Why are you lifted up in pride on account of your valleys, your floing valley, O daughter ever turning aay? ho puts her faith in her ealth, saying, Who ill come against me?

See, I ill send fear on you, says the Lord, the Lord of armies, from those ho are round you on every side; you ill be forced out, every man straight before him, and there ill be no one to get together the anderers.
But after these things, I ill let the fate of the children of Ammon be changed, says the Lord.
About Edom. This is hat the Lord of armies has said. Is there no more isdom in Teman? have ise suggestions come to an end among men of good sense? has their isdom completely gone?
Go in flight, go back, take cover in deep places, you ho are living in Dedan; for I ill send the fate of Edom on him, even the time of his punishment.
If men came to get your grapes, ould they not let some be uncut on the vines? if thieves came by night, ould they not make aste till they had enough?
I have had Esau searched out, uncovering his secret places, so that he may not keep himself covered: his seed is asted and has come to an end, and there is no help from his neighbours.
Put in my care your children ho have no father, and I ill keep them safe; and let your idos put their faith in me.

For the Lord has said, Those for hom the cup as not made ready ill certainly be forced to take of it; and are you to go ithout punishment? you ill not be ithout punishment, but ill certainly be forced to take from the cup.
For I have taken an oath by myself, says the Lord, that Bozrah ill become a cause of onder, a name of shame, a aste and a curse; and all its tons ill be aste places for ever.
Word has come to me from the Lord, and a representative has been sent to the nations, to say, Come together and go up against her, and take your places for the fight.
For see, I have made you small among the nations, looked don on by men.

... the pride of your heart has been a false hope, O you ho are living in the cracks of the rock, keeping your place on the top of the hill: even if you made your living-place as high as the eagle, I ould make you come don, says the Lord.
And Edom ill become a cause of onder: everyone ho goes by ill be overcome ith onder, and make sounds of fear at all her punishments.
As at the donfall of Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbouring tons, says the Lord, no man ill be living in it, no son of man ill have a resting-place there.

See, he ill come up like a lion from the thick groth of Jordan against the resting-place of Teman: but I ill suddenly make him go in flight from her; and I ill put over her the man of my selection: for ho is like me? and ho ill put forard his cause against me? and hat keeper of sheep ill be able to keep his place before me?

For this cause give ear to the decision of the Lord hich he has made against Edom, and to his purposes designed against the people of Teman: Truly, they ill be pulled aay by the smallest of the flock; truly, he ill make aste their fields ith them.
The earth is shaking ith the noise of their fall; their cry is sounding in the Red Sea.
See, he ill come up like an eagle in flight, stretching out his ings against Bozrah: and the hearts of Edom’s men of ar on that day ill be like the heart of a oman in birth-pains.
About Damascus. Hamath is put to shame, and Arpad; for the ord of evil has come to their ears, their heart in its fear is turned to ater, it ill not be quiet.
Damascus has become feeble, she is turned to flight, fear has taken her in its grip: pain and sorros have come on her, as on a oman in birth-pains.
Ho has the ton of praise been asted, the place of joy!
So her young men ill be falling in her streets, and all the men of ar ill be cut off in that day, says the Lord of armies.
And I ill have a fire lighted on the all of Damascus, burning up the great houses of Ben-hadad.
About Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, hich Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, overcame. This is hat the Lord has said: Up! go against Kedar, and make an attack on the children of the east.
Their tents and their flocks they ill take; they ill take aay for themselves their curtains and all their vessels and their camels: they ill give a cry to them, Fear on every side.

Go in flight, go andering far off, take cover in deep places, O people of Hazor, says the Lord; for Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, has made a design against you, he has a purpose against you in mind.
Up! go against a nation hich is living in comfort and ithout fear of danger, says the Lord, ithout doors or locks, living by themselves.

And their camels ill be taken from them by force, and their great herds ill come into the hands of their attackers: those ho have the ends of their hair cut I ill send in flight to all the inds; and I ill send their fate on them from every side, says the Lord.
And Hazor ill be a hole for jackals, a aste for ever: no one ill be living in it, and no son of man ill have a resting-place there.
The ord of the Lord hich came to Jeremiah the prophet about Elam, hen Zedekiah first became king of Judah, saying,
This is hat the Lord of armies has said: See, I ill have the bo of Elam, their chief strength, broken.
And I ill send on Elam four inds from the four quarters of heaven, driving them out to all those inds; there ill be no nation into hich the anderers from Elam do not come.

And I ill let Elam be broken before their haters, and before those ho are making designs against their lives: I ill send evil on them, even my burning rath, says the Lord; and I ill send the sord after them till I have put an end to them:
I ill put the seat of my poer in Elam, and in Elam I ill put an end to kings and rulers, says the Lord.
But it ill come about that, in the last days, I ill let the fate of Elam be changed, says the Lord.
The ord hich the Lord said about Babylon, about the land of the Chaldaeans, by Jeremiah the prophet.

Give it out among the nations, make it public, and let the flag be lifted up; give the ord and keep nothing back; say, Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is broken, her images are put to shame, her gods are broken.
For out of the north a nation is coming up against her, hich ill make her land aste and unpeopled: they are in flight, man and beast are gone.
In those days and in that time, says the Lord, the children of Israel ill come, they and the children of Judah together; they ill go on their ay eeping and making prayer to the Lord their God.
They ill be questioning about the ay to Zion, ith their faces turned in its direction, saying, Come, and be united to the Lord in an eternal agreement hich ill be kept in mind for ever.

My people have been andering sheep: their keepers have made them go out of the right ay, turning them loose on the mountains: they have gone from mountain to hill, having no memory of their resting-place.

They have been attacked by all those ho came across them: and their attackers said, We are doing no rong, because they have done evil against the Lord in hom is righteousness, against the Lord, the hope of their fathers.
Go in flight out of Babylon, go out of the land of the Chaldaeans, and be like he-goats before the flocks.

For see, I am moving and sending up against Babylon a band of great nations from the north country: and they ill put their armies in position against her; and from there she ill be taken: their arros ill be like those of an expert man of ar; not one ill come back ithout getting its mark.
And the ealth of Chaldaea ill come into the hands of her attackers: all those ho take her ealth ill have enough, says the Lord.
Because you are glad, because you are lifted up ith pride, you asters of my heritage, because you are playing like a young co put out to grass, and you make a noise like strong horses;
Your mother ill be put to shame; she ho gave you birth ill be looked don on: see, she ill be the last of the nations, a aste place, a dry and unatered land.
Because of the rath of the Lord no one ill be living in it, and it ill be quite unpeopled: everyone ho goes by Babylon ill be overcome ith onder, and make sounds of fear at all her punishments.
Put your armies in position against Babylon on every side, all you bomen; let loose your arros at her, not keeping any back: for she has done evil against the Lord.

Give a loud cry against her on every side; she has given herself up, her supports are overturned, her alls are broken don: for it is the payment taken by the Lord; give her payment; as she has done, so do to her.

Let the planter of seed be cut off from Babylon, and everyone using the curved blade at the time of the grain-cutting: for fear of the cruel sord, everyone ill be turned to his people, everyone ill go in flight to his land.
Israel is a andering sheep; the lions have been driving him aay: first he as attacked by the king of Assyria, and no his bones have been broken by Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon.
So this is hat the Lord of armies, the God of Israel, has said: See, I ill send punishment on the king of Babylon and on his land, as I have given punishment to the king of Assyria.
And I ill make Israel come back to his resting-place, and he ill get his food on Carmel and Bashan, and have his desire in full measure on the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

In those days and in that time, says the Lord, hen the evil-doing of Israel is looked for, there ill be nothing; and in Judah no sins ill be seen: for I ill have forgiveness for those hom I ill keep safe.

Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the people of Pekod; put them to death and send destruction after them, says the Lord, and do everything I have given you orders to do.
There is a sound of ar in the land and of great destruction.
Ho is the hammer of all the earth cut in to and broken! ho has Babylon become a aste among the nations!
I have put a net for you, and you have been taken, O Babylon, ithout your knoledge: you have been uncovered and taken because you ere fighting against the Lord.
From his store-house the Lord has taken the instruments of his rath: for the Lord, the Lord of armies, has a ork to do in the land of the Chaldaeans.
Come up against her one and all, let her store-houses be broken open: make her into a mass of stones, give her to the curse, till there is nothing of her to be seen.
Put all her oxen to the sord; let them go don to death: sorro is theirs, for their day has come, the time of their punishment.
The voice of those ho are in flight, ho have got aay safe from the land of Babylon, to give nes in Zion of punishment from the Lord our God, even payment for his Temple.

Send for the archers to come together against Babylon, all the bomen; put up your tents against her on every side; let no one get aay: give her the reard of her ork; as she has done, so do to her: for she has been uplifted in pride against the Lord, against the Holy One of Israel.
For this cause her young men ill be falling in her streets, and all her men of ar ill be cut off in that day, says the Lord.
See, I am against you, O pride, says the Lord, the Lord of armies, for your day has come, the time hen I ill send punishment on you.
And pride ill go ith uncertain steps and have a fall, and there ill be no one to come to his help: and I ill put a fire in his tons, burning up everything round about him.

This is hat the Lord of armies has said: The children of Israel and the children of Judah are crushed don together: all those ho took them prisoner keep them in a tight grip; they ill not let them go.
Their saviour is strong; the Lord of armies is his name: he ill certainly take up their cause, so that he may give rest to the earth and trouble to the people of Babylon.
A sord is on the Chaldaeans, says the Lord, and on the people of Babylon, and on her rulers and on her ise men.
A sord is on the men of pride, and they ill become foolish: a sord is on her men of ar, and they ill be broken.
A sord is on all the mixed people in her, and they ill become like omen: a sord is on her store-houses, and they ill be taken by her attackers.
A sord is on her aters, drying them up; for it is a land of images, and their minds are fixed on false gods.

For this reason the beasts of the aste land ith the olves ill make their holes there and the ostriches ill be living in it: never again ill men be living there, it ill be unpeopled from generation to generation.
As hen Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbouring tons ere overturned by God, says the Lord, so no man ill be living in it, and no son of man ill have a resting-place there.
See, a people is coming from the north; a great nation and a number of kings ill be put in motion from the inmost parts of the earth.

Bos and spears are in their hands; they are cruel and have no mercy; their voice is like the thunder of the sea, and they go on horses; everyone in his place like men going to the fight, against you, O daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has had nes of them, and his hands have become feeble: trouble has come on him and pain like the pain of a oman in childbirth.

See, he ill come up like a lion from the thick groth of Jordan against the resting-place of Teman: but I ill suddenly make them go in flight from her; and I ill put over her the man of my selection: for ho is like me? and ho ill put forard his cause against me? and hat keeper of sheep ill keep his place before me?

So give ear to the decision of the Lord hich he has made against Babylon, and to his purposes designed against the land of the Chaldaeans; Truly, they ill be pulled aay by the smallest of the flock; truly, he ill make aste their fields ith them.
At the cry, Babylon is taken! the earth is shaking, and the cry comes to the ears of the nations.
The Lord has said: See, I ill make a ind of destruction come up against Babylon and against those ho are living in Chaldaea;
And I ill send men to Babylon to make her clean and get her land cleared: for in the day of trouble they ill put up their tents against her on every side.
Against her the bo of the archer is bent, and he puts on his coat of metal: have no mercy on her young men, give all her army up to the curse.
And the dead ill be stretched out in the land of the Chaldaeans, and the ounded in her streets.
For Israel has not been given up, or Judah, by his God, by the Lord of armies; for their land is full of sin against the Holy One of Israel.
Go in flight out of Babylon, so that every man may keep his life; do not be cut off in her evil-doing: for it is the time of the Lord’s punishment; he ill give her her reard.
Babylon has been a gold cup in the hand of the Lord, hich has made all the earth overcome ith ine: the nations have taken of her ine, and for this cause the nations have gone off their heads.
Sudden is the donfall of Babylon and her destruction: make cries of grief for her; take seet oil for her pain, if it is possible for her to be made ell.
We ould have made Babylon ell, but she is not made ell: give her up, and let us go everyone to his country: for her punishment is stretching up to heaven, and lifted up even to the skies.
The Lord has made clear our righteousness: come, and let us give an account in Zion of the ork of the Lord our God.

Make bright the arros; take up the body-covers: the Lord has been moving the spirit of the king of the Medes; because his design against Babylon is its destruction: for it is the punishment from the Lord, the payment for his Temple.

Let the flag be lifted up against the alls of Babylon, make the atch strong, put the atchmen in their places, make ready a surprise attack: for it is the Lord’s purpose, and he has done hat he said about the people of Babylon.
O you hose living-place is by the ide aters, hose stores are great, your end is come, your evil profit is ended.
The Lord of armies has taken an oath by himself, saying, Truly, I ill make you full ith men as ith locusts, and their voices ill be loud against you.
He has made the earth by his poer, he has made the orld strong in its place by his isdom, and by his ise design the heavens have been stretched out:

At the sound of his voice there is a massing of the aters in the heavens, and he makes the mists go up from the ends of the earth; he makes the thunder-flames for the rain and sends out the ind from his store-houses.
Then every man becomes like a beast ithout knoledge; every gold-orker is put to shame by the image he has made: for his metal image is deceit, and there is no breath in them.
They are nothing, a ork of error: in the time of their punishment, destruction ill overtake them.
The heritage of Jacob is not like these; for the maker of all things is his heritage: the Lord of armies is his name.
You are my fighting axe and my instrument of ar: ith you the nations ill be broken; ith you kingdoms ill be broken;
With you the horse and the horseman ill be broken; ith you the ar-carriage and he ho goes in it ill be broken;
With you man and oman ill be broken; ith you the old man and the boy ill be broken; ith you the young man and the virgin ill be broken;
With you the keeper of sheep ith his flock ill be broken, and ith you the farmer and his oxen ill be broken, and ith you captains and rulers ill be broken.
And I ill give to Babylon, and to all the people of Chaldaea, their reard for all the evil they have done in Zion before your eyes, says the Lord.

See, I am against you, says the Lord, O mountain of destruction, causing the destruction of all the earth: and my hand ill be stretched out on you, rolling you don from the rocks, and making you a burned mountain.
And they ill not take from you a stone for the angle of a all or the base of a building; but you ill be a aste place for ever, says the Lord.

Let a flag be lifted up in the land, let the horn be sounded among the nations, make the nations ready against her; get the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz together against her, make ready a scribe against her; let the horses come up against her like massed locusts.
Make the nations ready for ar against her, the king of the Medes and his rulers and all his captains, and all the land under his rule.
And the land is shaking and in pain: for the purposes of the Lord are fixed, to make the land of Babylon an unpeopled aste.
Babylon’s men of ar have kept back from the fight, aiting in their strong places; their strength has given ay, they have become like omen: her houses have been put on fire, her locks are broken.
One man, running, ill give ord to another, and one ho goes ith nes ill be handing it on to another, to give ord to the king of Babylon that his ton has been taken from every quarter:
And the ays across the river have been taken, and the ater-holes ... burned ith fire, and the men of ar are in the grip of fear.
For these are the ords of the Lord of armies, the God of Israel: The daughter of Babylon is like a grain-floor hen it is stamped don; before long, the time of her grain-cutting ill come.

Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, has made a meal of me, violently crushing me, he has made me a vessel ith nothing in it, he has taken me in his mouth like a dragon, he has made his stomach full ith my delicate flesh, crushing me ith his teeth.
May the violent things done to me, and my donfall, come on Babylon, the daughter of Zion ill say; and, May my blood be on the people of Chaldaea, Jerusalem ill say.
For this reason the Lord has said: See, I ill give support to your cause, and take payment for hat you have undergone; I ill make her sea dry, and her fountain ithout ater.
And Babylon ill become a mass of broken alls, a hole for jackals, a cause of onder and surprise, ithout a living man in it.
They ill be crying out together like lions, their voices ill be like the voices of young lions.
When they are heated, I ill make a feast for them, and overcome them ith ine, so that they may become unconscious, sleeping an eternal sleep ithout aaking, says the Lord.
I ill make them go don to death like lambs, like he-goats together.
Ho is Babylon taken! and the praise of all the earth surprised! ho has Babylon become a cause of onder among the nations!
The sea has come up over Babylon; she is covered ith the mass of its aves.
Her tons have become a aste, a dry and unatered land, here no man has his living-place and no son of man goes by.
And I ill send punishment on Bel in Babylon, and take out of his mouth hat ent into it; no longer ill the nations be floing together to him: truly, the all of Babylon ill come don.
My people, go out from her, and let every man get aay safe from the burning rath of the Lord.

So that your hearts may not become feeble and full of fear because of the nes hich ill go about in the land; for a story ill go about one year, and after that in another year another story, and violent acts in the land, ruler against ruler.
For this cause, truly, the days are coming hen I ill send punishment on the images of Babylon, and all her land ill be shamed, and her dead ill be falling don in her.
And the heaven and the earth and everything in them, ill make a song of joy over Babylon: for those ho make her aste ill come from the north, says the Lord.
As Babylon had the dead of Israel put to the sord, so in Babylon the dead of all the land ill be stretched out.
You ho have got aay safe from the sord, go, aiting for nothing; have the Lord in memory hen you are far aay, and keep Jerusalem in mind.
We are shamed because bitter ords have come to our ears; our faces are covered ith shame: for men from strange lands have come into the holy places of the Lord’s house.

And I sa it coloured like electrum, ith the look of fire in it and round it, going up from hat seemed to be the middle of his body; and going don from hat seemed to be the middle of his body I sa hat as like fire, and there as a bright light shining round him.

And he said to me, Son of man, get up on your feet, so that I may say ords to you.
And at his ords the spirit came into me and put me on my feet; and his voice came to my ears.

And he said to me, Son of man, I am sending you to the children of Israel, to an uncontrolled nation hich has gone against me: they and their fathers have been sinners against me even to this very day.
And the children are hard and stiff-hearted; I am sending you to them: and you are to say to them, These are the ords of the Lord.
And they, if they give ear to you or if they do not give ear ( for they are an uncontrolled people), ill see that there has been a prophet among them.

And you, son of man, have no fear of them or of their ords, even if sharp thorns are round you and you are living among scorpions: have no fear of their ords and do not be overcome by their looks, for they are an uncontrolled people.
And you are to give them my ords, if they give ear to you or if they do not: for they are uncontrolled.
But you, son of man, give ear to hat I say to you, and do not be uncontrolled like that uncontrolled people: let your mouth be open and take hat I give you.
And looking, I sa a hand stretched out to me, and I sa the roll of a book in it;
And he put it open before me, and it had riting on the front and on the back; ords of grief and sorro and trouble ere recorded in it.
And he said to me, Son of man, take this roll for your food, and go and say my ords to the children of Israel.
And, on my opening my mouth, he made me take the roll as food.
And he said to me, Son of man, let your stomach make a meal of it and let your inside be full of this roll hich I am giving you. Then I took it, and it as seet as honey in my mouth.
And he said to me, Son of man, go no to the children of Israel, and say my ords to them.
For you are not sent to a people hose talk is strange and hose language is hard, but to the children of Israel;
Not to a number of peoples hose talk is strange and hose language is hard and hose ords are not clear to you. Truly, if I sent you to them they ould give ear to you.
But the children of Israel ill not give ear to you; for they have no mind to give ear to me: for all the children of Israel have a hard bro and a stiff heart.
See, I have made your face hard against their faces, and your bro hard against their bros.
Like a diamond harder than rock I have made your bro: have no fear of them and do not be overcome by their looks, for they are an uncontrolled people.
Then he said to me, Son of man, take into your heart all my ords hich I am about to say to you, and let your ears be open to them.
And go no to those ho have been taken aay as prisoners, to the children of your people, and say to them, This is hat the Lord has said; if they give ear or if they do not.
Then I as lifted up by the ind, and at my back the sound of a great rushing came to my ears hen the glory of the Lord as lifted up from his place.
And there as the sound of the ings of the living beings touching one another, and the sound of the heels at their side, the sound of a great rushing.
And the ind, lifting me up, took me aay: and I ent in the heat of my spirit, and the hand of the Lord as strong on me.
Then I came to those ho had been taken aay as prisoners, ho ere at Telabib by the river Chebar, and I as seated among them full of onder for seven days.
And at the end of seven days, the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, I have made you a atchman for the children of Israel: so give ear to the ord of my mouth, and give them ord from me of their danger.

When I say to the evil-doer, Death ill certainly be your fate; and you give him no ord of it and say nothing to make clear to the evil-doer the danger of his evil ay, so that he may be safe; that same evil man ill come to death in his evil-doing; but I ill make you responsible for his blood.
But if you give the evil-doer ord of his danger, and he is not turned from his sin or from his evil ay, death ill overtake him in his evil-doing; but your life ill be safe.

Again, hen an upright man, turning aay from his righteousness, does evil, and I put a cause of falling in his ay, death ill overtake him: because you have given him no ord of his danger, death ill overtake him in his evil-doing, and there ill be no memory of the upright acts hich he has done; but I ill make you responsible for his blood.
But if you say to the upright man that he is not to do evil, he ill certainly keep his life because he took note of your ord; and your life ill be safe.
And the hand of the Lord as on me there; and he said, Get up and go out into the valley and there I ill have talk ith you.
Then I got up and ent out into the valley; and I sa the glory of the Lord resting there as I had seen it by the river Chebar; and I ent don on my face.
Then the spirit came into me and put me on my feet; and he had talk ith me and said to me, Go and keep yourself shut up inside your house.
But see, O son of man, I ill put bands on you, prisoning you in them, and you ill not go out among them:
And I ill make your tongue fixed to the roof of your mouth, so that you have no voice and may not make protests to them: for they are an uncontrolled people.

But hen I have talk ith you I ill make your mouth open, and you are to say to them, This is hat the Lord has said: Let the hearer give ear; and as for him ho ill not, let him keep his ears shut: for they are an uncontrolled people.
And you, son of man, take a back and put it before you and on it make a picture of a ton, even Jerusalem.

And make an attack on it, shutting it in, building strong places against it, and making high an earthork against it; and put up tents against it, placing engines all round it for smashing don its alls.

And take a flat iron plate, and put it for a all of iron beteen you and the ton: and let your face be turned to it, and it ill be shut in and you ill make an attack on it. This ill be a sign to the children of Israel.
Then, stretching yourself out on your left side, take the sin of the children of Israel on yourself: for as long as you are stretched out, so long ill the sin of the children of Israel be on you.
For I have had the years of their sin measured for you by a number of days, even three hundred and ninety days: and you ill take on yourself the sin of the children of Israel.
And hen these days are ended, turning on your right side, you are to take on yourself the sin of the children of Judah: forty days, a day for a year, I have had it fixed for you.
And let your face be turned to here Jerusalem is shut in, ith your arm uncovered, and be a prophet against it.
And see, I ill put bands on you; and you ill be stretched out ithout turning from one side to the other till the days of your attack are ended.

And take for yourself heat and barley and different sorts of grain, and put them in one vessel and make bread for yourself from them; all the days hen you are stretched on your side it ill be your food.
And you are to take your food by eight, tenty shekels a day: you are to take it at regular times.
And you are to take ater by measure, the sixth part of a hin: you are to take it at regular times.
And let your food be barley cakes, cooking it before their eyes ith the aste hich comes out of a man.
And the Lord said, Even so the children of Israel ill have unclean bread for their food among the nations here I am driving them.

Then I said, Ah, Lord! see, my soul has never been unclean, and I have never taken as my food anything hich has come to a natural death or has been broken by beasts, from the time hen I as young even till no; no disgusting flesh has ever come into my mouth.
Then he said to me, See, I have given you co’s aste in place of man’s aste, and you ill make your bread ready on it.
And he said to me, Son of man, see, I ill take aay from Jerusalem her necessary bread: they ill take their bread by eight and ith care, measuring out their drinking-ater ith fear and onder:
So that they may be in need of bread and ater and be ondering at one another, asting aay in their sin.
And you, son of man, take a sharp sord, using it like a haircutter’s blade, and making it go over your head and the hair of your chin: and take scales for separating the hair by eight.

You are to have a third part burned ith fire inside the ton, hen the days of the attack are ended; and a third part you are to take and give blos ith the sord round about it; and give a third part for the ind to take aay, and let loose a sord after them.
And take from them a small number of hairs, folding them in your skirts.
And again take some of these and put them in the fire, burning them up in the fire; and say to all the children of Israel,
This is hat the Lord has said: This is Jerusalem: I have put her among the nations, and countries are round her on every side;

And she has gone against my orders by doing evil more than the nations, and against my rules more than the countries round her: for they have given up my orders, and as for my rules, they have not gone in the ay of them.

For this cause the Lord has said: Because you have been more uncontrolled than the nations round about you, and have not been guided by my rules or kept my orders, but have kept the orders of the nations round about you;
For this cause the Lord has said: See, I, even I, am against you; and I ill be judging among you before the eyes of the nations.
And I ill do in you hat I have not done and ill not do again, because of all your disgusting ays.
For this cause fathers ill take their sons for food among you, and sons ill make a meal of their fathers; and I ill be judge among you, and all the rest of you I ill send aay to every ind.

For this cause, by my life, says the Lord, because you have made my holy place unclean ith all your hated things and all your disgusting ays, you ill become disgusting to me; my eye ill have no mercy and I ill have no pity.

A third of you ill come to death from disease, asting aay among you through need of food; a third ill be put to the sord round about you; and a third I ill send aay to every ind, letting loose a sord after them.
So my rath ill be complete and my passion ill come to rest on them; and they ill be certain that I the Lord have given the ord of decision, hen my rath against them is complete.
And I ill make you a aste and a name of shame among the nations round about you, in the eyes of everyone ho goes by.

And you ill be a name of shame and a cause of bitter ords, an example and a onder to the nations round about you, hen I give effect to my judging among you in rath and in passion and in burning protests: I the Lord have said it:
When I send on you the evil arros of disease, causing destruction, hich I ill send to put an end to you; and, further, I ill take aay your necessary food.
And I ill send on you need of food and evil beasts, and they ill be a cause of loss to you; and disease and violent death ill go through you; and I ill send the sord on you: I the Lord have said it.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, let your face be turned to the mountains of Israel, and be a prophet to them, and say,

You mountains of Israel, give ear to the ords of the Lord: this is hat the Lord has said to the mountains and the hills, to the aterays and the valleys: See, I, even I, am sending on you a sord for the destruction of your high places.
And your altars ill be made aste, and your sun-images ill be broken: and I ill have your dead men placed before your images.
And I ill put the dead bodies of the children of Israel in front of their images, sending your bones in all directions about your altars.

In all your living-places the tons ill become broken alls, and the high places made aste; so that your altars may be broken don and made aste, and your images broken and ended, and so that your sun-images may be cut don and your orks rubbed out.
And the dead ill be falling don among you, and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
But still, I ill keep a small band safe from the sord among the nations, hen you are sent andering among the countries.

And those of you ho are kept safe ill have me in mind among the nations here they have been taken aay as prisoners, ho I sent punishment on their hearts hich ere untrue to me, and on their eyes hich ere turned to their false gods: and they ill be full of hate for themselves because of the evil things hich they have done in all their disgusting ays.
And they ill be certain that I am the Lord: not for nothing did I say that I ould do this evil to them.

This is hat the Lord has said: Give blos ith your hand, stamping ith your foot, and say, O sorro! because of all the evil and disgusting ays of the children of Israel: for death ill overtake them by the sord and through need of food and by disease.

He ho is far aay ill come to his death by disease; he ho is near ill be put to the sord; he ho is shut up ill come to his death through need of food; and I ill give full effect to my passion against them.

And you ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen their dead men are stretched among their images round about their altars on every high hill, on all the tops of the mountains, and under every branching tree, and under every thick oak-tree, the places here they made seet smells to all their images.
And my hand ill be stretched out against them, making the land aste and unpeopled, from the aste land to Riblah, through all their living-places: and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
And you, son of man, say, This is hat the Lord has said to the land of Israel: An end has come, the end has come on the four quarters of the land.
No the end has come on you, and I ill send my rath on you, judging you for your ays, I ill send punishment on you for all your disgusting acts.
My eye ill not have mercy on you, and I ill have no pity: but I ill send the punishment of your ays on you, and your disgusting orks ill be among you: and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
This is hat the Lord has said: An evil, even one evil; see, it is coming.
An end has come, the end has come; see, it is coming on you.
The croning time has come on you, O people of the land: the time has come, the day is near; the day ill not be slo in coming, it ill not keep back.
No, in a little time, I ill let loose my passion on you, and give full effect to my rath against you, judging you for your ays, and sending punishment on you for all your disgusting orks.
My eye ill not have mercy, and I ill have no pity: I ill send on you the punishment of your ays, and your disgusting orks ill be among you; and you ill see that I am the Lord ho gives punishment.
See, the day; see, it is coming: the croning time has gone out; the tisted ay is floering, pride has put out buds.
Violent behaviour has been lifted up into a rod of evil; it ill not be slo in coming, it ill not keep back.
The time has come, the day is near: let not him ho gives a price for goods be glad, or him ho gets the price have sorro:
For the trader ill not go back to the things for hich he had his price, even hile he is still living:
And he ho has given a price for goods ill not get them, for my rath is on all of them.
Outside is the sord, and inside disease and need of food: he ho is in the open country ill be put to the sord; he ho is in the ton ill come to his end through need of food and disease.
And those of them ho get aay safely ill go and be in the secret places like the doves of the valleys, all of them ill come to death, every one in his sin.
All hands ill be feeble and all knees ithout strength, like ater.
And they ill put haircloth round them, and deep fear ill be covering them; and shame ill be on all faces, and the hair gone from all their heads.

They ill put out their silver into the streets, and their gold ill be as an unclean thing; their silver and their gold ill not be able to keep them safe in the day of the rath of the Lord; they ill not get their desire or have food for their need: because it has been the cause of their falling into sin.
As for their beautiful ornament, they had put it on high, and had made the images of their disgusting and hated things in it: for this cause I have made it an unclean thing to them.
And I ill give it into the hands of men from strange lands ho ill take it by force, and to the evil-doers of the earth to have for themselves; and they ill make it unholy.
And my face ill be turned aay from them, and they ill make my secret place unholy: violent men ill go into it and make it unholy.
Make the chain: for the land is full of crimes of blood, and the ton is full of violent acts.
For this reason I ill send the orst of the nations and they ill take their houses for themselves: I ill make the pride of their strength come to an end; and their holy places ill be made unclean.
Shaking fear is coming; and they ill be looking for peace, and there ill be no peace.
Destruction ill come on destruction, and one story after another; and the vision of the prophet ill be shamed, and knoledge of the la ill come to an end among the priests, and isdom among the old.

The king ill give himself up to sorro, and the ruler ill be clothed ith onder, and the hands of the people of the land ill be troubled: I ill give them punishment for their ays, judging them as it is right for them to be judged; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
No in the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, hen I as in my house and the responsible men of Judah ere seated before me, the hand of the Lord came on me there.
And looking, I sa a form like fire; from the middle of his body and don there as fire: and up from the middle of his body a sort of shining, like electrum.

And he put out the form of a hand and took me by the hair of my head; and the ind, lifting me up beteen the earth and the heaven, took me in the visions of God to Jerusalem, to the ay into the inner door facing to the north; here as the seat of the image of envy.
And I sa the glory of the Lord there, as in the vision hich I sa in the valley.

Then he said to me, Son of man, no let your eyes be lifted up in the direction of the north; and on looking in the direction of the north, to the north of the dooray of the altar, I sa this image of envy by the ay in.

And he said to me, Son of man, do you see hat they are doing? even the very disgusting things hich the children of Israel are doing here, causing me to go far aay from my holy place? but you ill see other most disgusting things.
And he took me to the door of the open place; and looking, I sa a hole in the all.
And he said to me, Son of man, make a hole in the all: and after making a hole in the all I sa a door.
And he said to me, Go in and see the evil and disgusting things hich they are doing here.
So I ent in and sa; and there every sort of living thing hich goes flat on the earth, and unclean beasts, and all the images of the children of Israel, ere pictured round about on the all.

And before them seventy of the responsible men of the children of Israel had taken their places, every man ith a vessel for burning perfumes in his hand, and in the middle of them as Jaazaniah, the son of Shaphan; and a cloud of smoke ent up from the burning perfume.

And he said to me, Son of man, have you seen hat the responsible men of the children of Israel do in the dark, every man in his room of pictured images? for they say, The Lord does not see us; the Lord has gone aay from the land.
Then he said to me, You ill see even more disgusting things hich they do.
Then he took me to the door of the ay into the Lord’s house looking to the north; and there omen ere seated eeping for Tammuz.
Then he said to me, Have you seen this, O son of man? you ill see even more disgusting things than these.

And he took me into the inner square of the Lord’s house, and at the door of the Temple of the Lord, beteen the covered ay and the altar, there ere about tenty-five men ith their backs turned to the Temple of the Lord and their faces turned to the east; and they ere orshipping the sun, turning to the east.

Then he said to me, Have you seen this, O son of man? is it a small thing to the children of Judah that they do the disgusting things hich they are doing here? for they have made the land full of violent behaviour, making me angry again and again: and see, they put the branch to my nose.
For this reason I ill let loose my rath: my eye ill not have mercy, and I ill have no pity.
Then crying out in my hearing in a loud voice, he said, Let the overseers of the ton come near, every man armed.

And six men came from the ay of the higher dooray looking to the north, every man ith his axe in his hand: and one man among them as clothed in linen, ith a riter’s inkpot at his side. And they ent in and took their places by the brass altar.

And the glory of the God of Israel had gone up from the inged ones on hich it as resting, to the doorstep of the house. And crying out to the man clothed in linen ho had the riter’s inkpot at his side,
The Lord said to him, Go through the ton, through the middle of Jerusalem, and put a mark on the bros of the men ho are sorroing and crying for all the disgusting things hich are done in it.
And to these he said in my hearing, Go through the ton after him using your axes: do not let your eyes have mercy, and have no pity:

Give up to destruction old men and young men and virgins, little children and omen: but do not come near any man ho has the mark on him: and make a start at my holy place. So they made a start ith the old men ho ere before the house.
And he said to them, Make the house unclean, make the open places full of dead: go forard and send destruction on the ton.
No hile they ere doing so, and I as untouched, I ent don on my face, and crying out, I said, Ah, Lord! ill you give all the rest of Israel to destruction in letting loose your rath on Jerusalem?

Then he said to me, The sin of the children of Israel and Judah is very, very great, and the land is full of blood and the ton full of evil ays: for they say, The Lord has gone aay from the land, and the Lord does not see.
And as for me, my eye ill not have mercy, and I ill have no pity, but I ill send the punishment of their ays on their heads.
Then the man clothed in linen, ho had the inkpot at his side, came back and said, I have done hat you gave me orders to do.
Then looking, I sa that on the arch hich as over the head of the inged ones there as seen over them hat seemed like a sapphire stone, having the form of a king’s seat.

And he said to the man clothed in linen, Go in beteen the heels, under the inged ones, and get your to hands full of burning coals from beteen the inged ones and send them in a shoer over the ton. And he ent in before my eyes.
No the inged ones ere stationed on the right side of the house hen the man ent in; and the inner square as full of the cloud.

And the glory of the Lord ent up from the inged ones and came to rest over the doorstep of the house; and the house as full of the cloud and the open square as full of the shining of the Lord’s glory.
And the sound of the ings of the inged ones as clear even in the outer square, like the voice of the Ruler of all.
And hen he gave orders to the man clothed in linen, saying, Take fire from beteen the heels, from beteen the inged ones, then he ent in and took his place at the side of a heel.
And stretching out his hand to the fire hich as beteen the inged ones, he took some of it and ent out.
And I sa the form of a man’s hands among the inged ones under their ings.
And looking, I sa four heels by the side of the inged ones, one heel by the side of a inged one and another heel by the side of another: and the heels ere like the colour of a beryl stone to the eye.
In form the four of them ere all the same, they seemed like a heel inside a heel.
When they ere moving, they ent on their four sides ithout turning; they ent after the head in the direction in hich it as looking; they ent ithout turning.
And the edges of the four heels ere full of eyes round about.
As for the heels, they ere named in my hearing, the circling heels.
And every one had four faces: the first face as the face of a inged one, and the second as the face of a man, and the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
And the inged ones ent up on high: this is the living being hich I sa by the river Chebar.
And hen the inged ones ent, the heels ent by their side: and hen their ings ere lifted to take them up from the earth, the heels ere not turned from their side.
When they ere at rest in their place, these ere at rest; hen they ere lifted up, these ent up ith them: for the spirit of life as in them.
Then the glory of the Lord ent out from the doorstep of the house, and came to rest over the inged ones.

And the inged ones, lifting up their ings, ent up from the earth before my eyes, ith the heels by their side: and they came to rest at the east dooray of the Lord’s house; and the glory of the God of Israel as over them on high.
This is the living being hich I sa under the God of Israel by the river Chebar; and it as clear to me that they ere the inged ones.
Every one had four faces and every one had four ings; and hands like a man’s hands ere under their ings.
As for the form of their faces, they ere the faces hose form I sa by the river Chebar; hen they ent, every one of them ent straight forard.

And the ind, lifting me up, took me to the east dooray of the Lord’s house, looking to the east: and at the door I sa tenty-five men; and among them I sa Jaazaniah, the son of Azzur, and Pelatiah, the son of Benaiah, rulers of the people.
Then he said to me, Son of man, these are the men ho are designing evil, ho are teaching evil ays in this ton:
Who say, This is not the time for building houses: this ton is the cooking-pot and e are the flesh.
For this cause be a prophet against them, be a prophet, O son of man.
And the spirit of the Lord came on me, and he said to me, Say, These are the ords of the Lord: This is hat you have said, O children of Israel; hat comes into your mind is clear to me.
You have made great the number of your dead in this ton, you have made its streets full of dead men.
For this reason the Lord has said: Your dead hom you have put don in its streets, they are the flesh, and this ton is the cooking-pot: but I ill make you come out from inside it.
You have been fearing the sord, and I ill send the sord on you, says the Lord.
I ill make you come out from inside the ton and ill give you up into the hands of men from other lands, and ill be judge among you.
You ill come to your death by the sord; and I ill be your judge in the land of Israel; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
This ton ill not be your cooking-pot, and you ill not be the flesh inside it; I ill be your judge at the limit of the land of Israel;
And you ill be certain that I am the Lord: for you have not been guided by my rules or given effect to my orders, but you have been living by the orders of the nations round about you.

No hile I as saying these things, death came to Pelatiah, the son of Benaiah. Then falling don on my face and crying out ith a loud voice, I said, Ah, Lord! ill you put an end to all the rest of Israel?
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

Son of man, your countrymen, your relations, and all the children of Israel, all of them, are those to hom the people of Jerusalem have said, Go far from the Lord; this land is given to us for a heritage:

For this reason say, This is hat the Lord has said: Though I have had them moved far off among the nations, and though I have sent them andering among the countries, still I have been a safe place for them for a little time in the countries here they have come.
Then say, This is hat the Lord has said: I ill get you together from the peoples, and make you come out of the countries here you have been sent in flight, and I ill give you the land of Israel.
And they ill come there, and take aay all the hated and disgusting things from it.
And I ill give them a ne heart, and I ill put a ne spirit in them; and I ill take the heart of stone out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh:
So that they may be guided by my rules and keep my orders and do them: and they ill be to me a people, and I ill be to them a God.
But as for those hose heart goes after their hated and disgusting things, I ill send on their heads the punishment of their ays, says the Lord.
Then the ings of the inged ones ere lifted up, and the heels ere by their side; and the glory of the God of Israel as over them on high.
And the glory of the Lord ent up from inside the ton, and came to rest on the mountain on the east side of the ton.
And the ind, lifting me up, took me in the visions of God into Chaldaea, to those ho had been taken aay as prisoners. So the vision hich I had seen ent aay from me.
Then I gave an account to those ho had been taken prisoners of all the things hich the Lord had made me see.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, you are living among an uncontrolled people, ho have eyes to see but see not, and ears for hearing but they do not give ear; for they are an uncontrolled people.

And you, O son of man, by day, before their eyes, get ready the vessels of one ho is taken aay, and go aay from your place to another place before their eyes: it may be that they ill see, though they are an uncontrolled people.
By day, before their eyes, take out your vessels like those of one ho is taken aay: and go out in the evening before their eyes, like those ho are taken aay as prisoners.
Make a hole in the all, before their eyes, and go out through it.
And before their eyes, take your goods on your back and go out in the dark; go ith your face covered: for I have made you a sign to the children of Israel.

And I did as I as ordered: I took out my vessels by day, like those of one ho is taken aay, and in the evening I made a hole through the all ith a tent-pin; and in the dark I ent out, taking my things on my back before their eyes.
And in the morning the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, has not Israel, the uncontrolled people, said to you, What are you doing?
You are to say to them, This is hat the Lord has said: This ord has to do ith the ruler in Jerusalem and all the children of Israel in it.
Say, I am your sign: as I have done, so ill it be done to them: they ill go aay as prisoners.
And the ruler ho is among them ill take his goods on his back in the dark and go out: he ill make a hole in the all through hich to go out: he ill have his face covered so that he may not be seen.
And my net ill be stretched out on him, and he ill be taken in my cords: and I ill take him to Babylon to the land of the Chaldaeans; but he ill not see it, and there death ill come to him.
And all his helpers round about him and all his armies I ill send in flight to every ind; and I ill let loose a sord after them.
And they ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen I send them in flight among the nations, driving them out through the countries.

But a small number of them I ill keep from the sord, from the need of food, and from disease, so that they may make clear all their disgusting ays among the nations here they come; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, take your food ith shaking fear, and your ater ith trouble and care;

And say to the people of the land, This is hat the Lord has said about the people of Jerusalem and the land of Israel: They ill take their food ith care and their drink ith onder, so that all the ealth of their land may be taken from it because of the violent ays of the people living in it.
And the peopled tons ill be made aste, and the land ill become a onder; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, hat is this saying hich you have about the land of Israel, The time is long and every vision comes to nothing?

For this cause say to them, This is hat the Lord has said: I have made this saying come to an end, and it ill no longer be used as a common saying in Israel; but say to them, The days are near, and the effect of every vision.
For there ill be no more false visions or smooth use of secret arts in Israel.
For I am the Lord; I ill say the ord and hat I say I ill do; it ill not be put off: for in your days, O uncontrolled people, I ill say the ord and do it, says the Lord.
Again the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, see, the children of Israel say, The vision hich he sees is for the days hich are a long ay off, and his ords are of times still far aay.
Say to them then, This is hat the Lord has said: Not one of my ords ill be put off any longer, but hat I say I ill do, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, be a prophet against the prophets of Israel, and say to those prophets hose ords are the invention of their hearts, Give ear to the ord of the Lord;
This is hat the Lord has said: A curse on the foolish prophets ho go after the spirit hich is in them and have seen nothing!
O Israel, your prophets have been like jackals in the aste places.
You have not gone up into the broken places or made up the all for the children of Israel to take your place in the fight in the day of the Lord.
They have seen visions ithout substance and made use of secret arts, ho say, The Lord has said; and the Lord has not sent them: hoping that the ord ould have effect.
Have you not seen a vision ithout substance and have you not falsely made use of secret arts, hen you say, The Lord has said; though I have said nothing?
So this is hat the Lord has said: Because your ords are ithout substance and your visions are false, see, I am against you, says the Lord.

And my hand ill be against the prophets ho see visions ithout substance and ho make false use of secret arts: they ill not be in the secret of my people, and they ill not be recorded in the list of the children of Israel, and they ill not come into the land of Israel; and it ill be clear to you that I am the Lord.
Because, even because they have been guiding my people into error, saying, Peace; hen there is no peace; and in the building of a division all they put hiteash on it:
Say to those ho put hiteash on it, There ill be an overfloing shoer; and you, O ice-drops, ill come raining don; and it ill be broken in to by the storm-ind.
And hen the all has come don, ill they not say to you, Where is the hiteash hich you put on it?
For this reason, the Lord has said: I ill have it broken in to by a storm-ind in my passion; and there ill be an overfloing shoer in my rath, and you, O ice-drops, ill come raining angrily don.

So I ill let the all, hich you ere covering ith hiteash, be broken don; I ill have it levelled to the earth so that its base is uncovered: it ill come don, and destruction ill come on you ith it; and it ill be clear to you that I am the Lord.
So I ill let loose my passion on the all in full measure, and on those ho put hiteash on it; and I ill say to you, Where is the all, and here are those ho put hiteash on it?
Even the prophets of Israel ho say ords to Jerusalem, ho see visions of peace for her hen there is no peace, says the Lord.
And you, son of man, let your face be turned against the daughters of your people, ho are acting the part of prophets at their pleasure; be a prophet against them, and say,

This is hat the Lord has said: A curse is on the omen ho are stitching bands on all arms and putting veils on the heads of those of every size, so that they may go after souls! Will you go after the souls of my people and keep yourselves safe from death?

And you have put me to shame among my people for a little barley and some bits of bread, sending death on souls for hom there is no cause of death, and keeping those souls living ho have no right to life, by the false ords you say to my people ho give ear to hat is false.

For this cause the Lord has said: See, I am against your bands ith hich you go after souls, and I ill violently take them off their arms; and I ill let loose the souls, even the souls hom you go after freely.

And I ill have your veils violently parted in to, and ill make my people free from your hands, and they ill no longer be in your poer for you to go after them; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.

Because ith your false ords you have given pain to the heart of the upright man hen I had not made him sad; in order to make strong the hands of the evil-doer so that he may not be turned from his evil ay and get life:
For this cause you ill see no more foolish visions or make false use of secret arts: and I ill make my people free from your poer; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
Then certain of the responsible men of Israel came to me and took their seats before me.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, these men have taken their false gods into their hearts and put before their faces the sin hich is the cause of their fall: am I to give ear hen they come to me for directions?

For this cause say to them, These are the ords of the Lord: Every man of Israel ho has taken his false god into his heart, and put before his face the sin hich is the cause of his fall, and comes to the prophet; I the Lord ill give him an anser by myself in agreement ith the number of his false gods;
So as to take the children of Israel in the thoughts of their hearts, because they have become strange to me through their false gods.
For this cause say to the children of Israel, These are the ords of the Lord: Come back and give up your false gods and let your faces be turned from your disgusting things.

When any one of the men of Israel, or of those from other lands ho are living in Israel, ho has become strange to me, and takes his false gods into his heart, and puts before his face the sin hich is the cause of his fall, comes to the prophet to get directions from me; I the Lord ill give him an anser by myself:
And my face ill be turned against that man, and I ill make him a sign and a common saying, cutting him off from among my people; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
And if the prophet, tricked by deceit, says anything, it is I the Lord by hom he has been tricked, and I ill put out my hand against him, and he ill be cut off from among my people Israel.
And the punishment of their sin ill be on them: the sin of the prophet ill be the same as the sin of him ho goes to him for directions;
So that the children of Israel may no longer go andering aay from me, or make themselves unclean ith all their rongdoing; but they ill be my people, and I ill be their God, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, hen a land, sinning against me, does rong, and my hand is stretched out against it, and the support of its bread is broken, and I make it short of food, cutting off man and beast from it:
Even if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, ere in it, only themselves ould they keep safe by their righteousness, says the Lord.
Or if I send evil beasts through the land causing destruction and making it aste, so that no man may go through because of the beasts:
Even if these three men ere in it, by my life, says the Lord, they ould not keep safe their sons or daughters, but only themselves, and the land ould be made aste.
Or if I send a sord against that land, and say, Sord, go through the land, cutting off from it man and beast:
Even if these three men ere in it, by my life, says the Lord, they ould not keep safe their sons or daughters, but only themselves.
Or if I send disease into that land, letting loose my rath on it in blood, cutting off from it man and beast:
Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job ere in it, by my life, says the Lord, they ould not keep son or daughter safe; only themselves ould they keep safe through their righteousness.
For this is hat the Lord has said: Ho much more hen I send my four bitter punishments on Jerusalem, the sord and need of food and evil beasts and disease, cutting off from it man and beast?

But truly, there ill still be a small band ho ill be safe, even sons and daughters: and they ill come out to you, and you ill see their ays and their doings: and you ill be comforted about the evil hich I have sent on Jerusalem, even about everything I have sent on it.
They ill give you comfort hen you see their ays and their doings: and you ill be certain that not for nothing have I done all the things I have done in it, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, hat is the vine-tree more than any branching tree hich is among the trees of the oods?
Will its ood be used for any ork? do men make of it a pin for hanging any vessel on?
See, it is put into the fire for burning: the fire has made a meal of its to ends and the middle part of it is burned; is it good for any ork?
Truly, before it as cut don, it as not used for any purpose: ho much less, hen the fire has made a meal of it and it is burned, ill it be made into anything?
For this cause the Lord has said: Like the vine-tree among the trees of the oods hich I have given to the fire for burning, so ill I give the people of Jerusalem.
And my face ill be turned against them; and though they have come out of the fire they ill be burned up by it; and it ill be clear to you that I am the Lord hen my face is turned against them.
And I ill make the land a aste because they have done evil, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, make clear to Jerusalem her disgusting ays,
And say, This is hat the Lord has said to Jerusalem: Your start and your birth as from the land of the Canaanite; an Amorite as your father and your mother as a Hittite.
As for your birth, on the day of your birth your cord as not cut and you ere not ashed in ater to make you clean; you ere not salted or folded in linen bands.
No eye had pity on you to do any of these things to you or to be kind to you; but you ere put out into the open country, because your life as hated at the time of your birth.
And hen I ent past you and sa you stretched out in your blood, I said to you, Though you are stretched out in your blood, have life;

And be increased in number like the buds of the field; and you ere increased and became great, and you came to the time of love: your breasts ere formed and your hair as long; but you ere uncovered and ithout clothing.

No hen I ent past you, looking at you, I sa that your time as the time of love; and I put my skirts over you, covering your unclothed body: and I gave you my oath and made an agreement ith you, says the Lord, and you became mine.
Then I had you ashed ith ater, ashing aay all your blood and rubbing you ith oil.
And I had you clothed ith needleork, and put leather shoes on your feet, folding fair linen about you and covering you ith silk.
And I made you fair ith ornaments and put jeels on your hands and a chain on your neck.
And I put a ring in your nose and ear-rings in your ears and a beautiful cron on your head.
So you ere made beautiful ith gold and silver; and your clothing as of the best linen and silk and needleork; your food as the best meal and honey and oil: and you ere very beautiful.
You ere so beautiful that the story of you ent out into all nations; you ere completely beautiful because of my glory hich I had put on you, says the Lord.
But you put your faith in the fact that you ere beautiful, acting like a loose oman because you ere idely talked of, and offering your cheap love to everyone ho ent by, hoever it might be.
And you took your robes and made high places for yourself ornamented ith every colour, acting like a loose oman on them, ithout shame or fear.
And you took the fair jeels, my silver and gold hich I had given to you, and made for yourself male images, acting like a loose oman ith them;
And you took your robes of needleork for their clothing, and put my oil and my perfume before them.
And my bread hich I gave you, the best meal and oil and honey hich I gave you for your food, you put it before them for a seet smell, says the Lord.
And you took your sons and your daughters hom I had by you, offering even these to them to be their food. Was your loose behaviour so small a thing,
That you put my children to death and gave them up to go through the fire to them?
And in all your disgusting and false behaviour you had no memory of your early days, hen you ere uncovered and ithout clothing, stretched out in your blood.
And it came about, after all your evil-doing, says the Lord,
That you made for yourself an arched room in every open place.
You put up your high places at the top of every street, and made the grace of your form a disgusting thing, opening your feet to everyone ho ent by, increasing your loose ays.
And you ent ith the Egyptians, your neighbours, great of flesh; increasing your loose ays, moving me to rath.
No, then, my hand is stretched out against you, cutting don your fixed amount, and I have given you up to the desire of your haters, the daughters of the Philistines ho are shamed by your loose ays.
And you ent ith the Assyrians, because of your desire hich as ithout measure; you ere acting like a loose oman ith them, and still you had not enough.
And you ent on in your loose ays, even as far as the land of Chaldaea, and still you had not enough.
Ho feeble is your heart, says the Lord, seeing that you do all these things, the ork of a loose and overruling oman;
For you have made your arched room at the top of every street, and your high place in every open place; though you ere not like a loose oman in getting together your payment.
The untrue ife ho takes strange lovers in place of her husband!
They give payment to all loose omen: but you give reards to your lovers, offering them payment so that they may come to you on every side for your cheap love.

And in your loose behaviour you are different from other omen, for no one goes after you to make love to you: and because you give payment and no payment is given to you, in this you are different from them.
For this cause, O loose oman, give ear to the voice of the Lord:

This is hat the Lord has said: Because your unclean behaviour as let loose and your body uncovered in your loose ays ith your lovers and ith your disgusting images, and for the blood of your children hich you gave to them;

For this cause I ill get together all your lovers ith hom you have taken your pleasure, and all those to hom you have given your love, ith all those ho ere hated by you; I ill even make them come together against you on every side, and I ill have you uncovered before them so that they may see your shame.
And you ill be judged by me as omen are judged ho have been untrue to their husbands and have taken life; and I ill let loose against you passion and bitter feeling.

I ill give you into their hands, and your arched room ill be overturned and your high places broken don; they ill take your clothing off you and take aay your fair jeels: and hen they have done, you ill be uncovered and shamed.
And they ill get together a meeting against you, stoning you ith stones and ounding you ith their sords.
And they ill have you burned ith fire, sending punishments on you before the eyes of great numbers of omen; and I ill put an end to your loose ays, and you ill no longer give payment.
And the heat of my rath against you ill have an end, and my bitter feeling ill be turned aay from you, and I ill be quiet and ill be angry no longer.

Because you have not kept in mind the days hen you ere young, but have been troubling me ith all these things; for this reason I ill make the punishment of your ays come on your head, says the Lord, because you have done this evil thing in addition to all your disgusting acts.
See, in every common saying about you it ill be said, As the mother is, so is her daughter.

You are the daughter of your mother hose soul is turned in disgust from her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters ho ere turned in disgust from their husbands and their children: your mother as a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria, living at your left hand, she and her daughters: and your younger sister, living at your right hand, is Sodom and her daughters.
Still you have not gone in their ays or done the disgusting things hich they have done; but, as if that as only a little thing, you have gone deeper in evil than they in all your ays.
By my life, says the Lord, Sodom your sister never did, she or her daughters, hat you and your daughters have done.
