Truly, this as the sin of your sister Sodom: pride, a full measure of food, and the comforts of ealth in peace, ere seen in her and her daughters, and she gave no help to the poor or to those in need.
They ere full of pride and did hat as disgusting to me: and so I took them aay as you have seen.

And Samaria has not done half your sins; but you have made the number of your disgusting acts greater than theirs, making your sisters seem more upright than you by all the disgusting things hich you have done.

And you yourself ill be put to shame, in that you have given the decision for your sisters; through your sins, hich are more disgusting than theirs, they are more upright than you: truly, you ill be shamed and made lo, for you have made your sisters seem upright.
And I ill let their fate be changed, the fate of Sodom and her daughters, and the fate of Samaria and her daughters, and your fate ith theirs.
So that you ill be shamed and made lo because of all you have done, hen I have mercy on you.

And your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, ill go back to their first condition, and Samaria and her daughters ill go back to their first condition, and you and your daughters ill go back to your first condition.
Was not your sister Sodom an oath in your mouth in the day of your pride,
Before your shame as uncovered? No you have become like her a ord of shame to the daughters of Edom and all ho are round about you, the daughters of the Philistines ho put shame on you round about.
The reard of your evil designs and your disgusting ays has come on you, says the Lord.
For this is hat the Lord has said: I ill do to you as you have done, you ho, putting the oath on one side, have let the agreement be broken.
But still I ill keep in mind the agreement made ith you in the days hen you ere young, and I ill make ith you an eternal agreement.
Then at the memory of your ays you ill be overcome ith shame, hen I take your sisters, the older and the younger, and give them to you for daughters, but not by your agreement.
And I ill make my agreement ith you; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord:
So that, at the memory of these things, you may be at a loss, never opening your mouth because of your shame; hen you have my forgiveness for all you have done, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, give out a dark saying, and make a comparison for the children of Israel,
And say, This is hat the Lord has said: A great eagle ith great ings, full of long feathers of different colours, came to Lebanon, and took the top of the cedar:
Biting off the highest of its young branches, he took it to the land of Canaan, and put it in a ton of traders.
And he took some of the seed of the land, planting it in fertile earth, placing it by great aters; he put it in like a illo-tree.
And its groth ent on and it became a vine, lo and idely stretching, hose branches ere turned to him and its roots ere under him: so it became a vine, putting out branches and young leaves.

And there as another eagle ith great ings and thick feathers: and no this vine, pushing out its roots to him, sent out its branches in his direction from the bed here it as planted, so that he might give it ater.
He had it planted in a good field by great aters so that it might put out branches and have fruit and be a strong vine.
Say, This is hat the Lord has said: Will it do ell? ill he not have its roots pulled up and its branches cut off, so that all its young leaves may become dry and it may be pulled up by its roots?
And if it is planted ill it do ell? ill it not become quite dry at the touch of the east ind, drying up in the bed here it as planted?
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Say no to this uncontrolled people, Are these things not clear to you? Say to them, See, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and its rulers aay ith him to Babylon;
And he took one of the sons of the king and made an agreement ith him; and he put him under an oath, and took aay the great men of the land:
So that the kingdom might be made lo ith no poer of lifting itself up, but might keep his agreement to be his servants.

But he ent against his authority in sending representatives to Egypt to get from them horses and a great army. Will he do ell? ill he be safe ho does such things? if the agreement is broken ill he be safe?
By my life, says the Lord, truly in the place of the king ho made him king, hose oath he put on one side and let his agreement ith him be broken, even in Babylon he ill come to his death.
And Pharaoh ith his strong army and great forces ill be no help to him in the ar, hen they put up earthorks and make strong alls for the cutting off of lives:
For he put his oath on one side in letting the agreement be broken; and though he had given his hand to it, he did all these things; he ill not get aay safe.
And so the Lord has said, By my life, truly, for my oath hich he put on one side, and my agreement hich has been broken, I ill send punishment on his head.
My net ill be stretched out over him, and he ill be taken in my cords, and I ill send him to Babylon, and there I ill be his judge for the rong hich he has done against me.
All his best fighting-men ill be put to the sord, and the rest ill be sent aay to every ind: and you ill be certain that I the Lord have said it.

This is hat the Lord has said: Further, I ill take the highest top of the cedar and put it in the earth; cutting off from the highest of his young branches a soft one, I ill have it planted on a high and great mountain;

It ill be planted on the high mountain of Israel: it ill put out branches and have fruit and be a fair cedar: under it all birds of every sort ill make their living-place, resting in the shade of its branches.

And it ill be clear to all the trees of the field that I the Lord have made lo the high tree and made high the lo tree, drying up the green tree and making the dry tree full of groth; I the Lord have said it and have done it.
The ord of the Lord came to me again, saying,
Why do you make use of this saying about the land of Israel, The fathers have been tasting bitter grapes and the children’s teeth are on edge?
By my life, says the Lord, you ill no longer have this saying in Israel.
See, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so the soul of the son is mine: death ill be the fate of the sinner’s soul.
But if a man is upright, living rightly and doing righteousness,

And has not taken flesh ith the blood for food, or given orship to the images of the children of Israel; if he has not had connection ith his neighbour’s ife, or come near to a oman at the time hen she is unclean;
And has done no rong to any, but has given back to the debtor hat is his, and has taken no one’s goods by force, and has given food to him ho as in need of it, and clothing to him ho as ithout it;
And has not given his money out at interest or taken great profits, and, turning his hand from evil-doing, has kept faith beteen man and man,
And has been guided by my rules and has kept my las and done them: he is upright, life ill certainly be his, says the Lord.
If he has a son ho is a thief, a taker of life, ho does any of these things,
Who has taken flesh ith the blood as food, and has had connection ith his neighbour’s ife,
Has done rong to the poor and to him ho is in need, and taken property by force, and has not given back to one in his debt hat is his, and has given orship to images and has done disgusting things,
And has given out his money at interest and taken great profits: he ill certainly not go on living: he has done all these disgusting things: death ill certainly be his fate; his blood ill be on him.
No if he has a son ho sees all his father’s sins hich he has done, and in fear does not do the same:
Who has not taken the flesh ith the blood for food, or given orship to the images of the children of Israel, and has not had connection ith his neighbour’s ife,
Or done rong to any, or taken anything from one in his debt, or taken goods by force, but has given food to him ho as in need of it, and clothing to him ho as ithout it;

Who has kept his hand from evil-doing and has not taken interest or great profits, ho has done my orders and been guided by my rules: he ill certainly not be put to death for the evil-doing of his father; life ill certainly be his.
As for his father, because he as cruel, took goods by force, and did hat is not good among his people, truly, death ill overtake him in his evil-doing.
But you say, Why does not the son undergo punishment for the evil-doing of the father? When the son has done hat is ordered and right, and has kept my rules and done them, life ill certainly be his.

The soul hich does sin ill be put to death: the son ill not be made responsible for the evil-doing of the father, or the father for the evil-doing of the son; the righteousness of the upright ill be on himself, and the evil-doing of the evil-doer on himself.
But if the evil-doer, turning aay from all the sins hich he has done, keeps my rules and does hat is ordered and right, life ill certainly be his; death ill not be his fate.
Not one of the sins hich he has done ill be kept in memory against him: in the righteousness hich he has done he ill have life.
Have I any pleasure in the death of the evil-doer? says the Lord: am I not pleased if he is turned from his ay so that he may have life?

But hen the upright man, turning aay from his righteousness, does evil, like all the disgusting things hich the evil man does, ill he have life? Not one of his upright acts ill be kept in memory: in the rong hich he has done and in his sin death ill overtake him.
But you say, The ay of the Lord is not equal. Give ear, no, O children of Israel; is my ay not equal? are not your ays unequal?
When the upright man, turning aay from his righteousness, does evil, death ill overtake him; in the evil hich he has done death ill overtake him.
Again, hen the evil-doer, turning aay from the evil he has done, does hat is ordered and right, he ill have life for his soul.
Because he had fear and as turned aay from all the rong hich he had done, life ill certainly be his, death ill not be his fate.
But still the children of Israel say, The ay of the Lord is not equal. O children of Israel, are my ays not equal? are not your ays unequal?

For this cause I ill be your judge, O children of Israel, judging every man by his ays, says the Lord. Come back and be turned from all your sins; so that they may not be the cause of your falling into evil.
Put aay all your evil-doing in hich you have done sin; and make for yourselves a ne heart and a ne spirit: hy are you desiring death, O children of Israel?
For I have no pleasure in the death of him on hom death comes, says the Lord: be turned back then, and have life.
Take up no a song of grief for the ruler of Israel, and say,
What as your mother? Like a she-lion among lions, stretched out among the young lions she gave food to her little ones.
And one of her little ones came to groth under her care, and became a young lion, learning to go after beasts for his food; and he took men for his meat.
And the nations had nes of him; he as taken in the hole they had made: and, pulling him ith hooks, they took him into the land of Egypt.
No hen she sa that her hope as made foolish and gone, she took another of her little ones and made him into a young lion.
And he ent up and don among the lions and became a young lion, learning to go after beasts for his food; and he took men for his meat.
And he sent destruction on their idos and made aste their tons; and the land and everything in it became aste because of the loud sound of his voice.
Then the nations came against him from the kingdoms round about: their net as stretched over him and he as taken in the hole they had made.
They made him a prisoner ith hooks, and took him to the king of Babylon; they put him in the strong place so that his voice might be sounding no longer on the mountains of Israel.
Your mother as in comparison like a vine, planted by the aters: she as fertile and full of branches because of the great aters.
And she had a strong rod for a rod of authority for the rulers, and it became tall among the clouds and it as seen lifted up among the number of its branches.
But she as uprooted in burning rath, and made lo on the earth; the east ind came, drying her up, and her branches ere broken off; her strong rod became dry, the fire made a meal of it.
And no she is planted in the aste land, in a dry and unatered country.

And fire has gone out from her rod, causing the destruction of her branches, so that there is no strong rod in her to be the ruler’s rod of authority. This is a song of grief, and it as for a song of grief.
No it came about in the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, that certain of the responsible men of Israel came to get directions from the Lord and ere seated before me.
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, say to the responsible men of Israel, This is hat the Lord has said: Have you come to get directions from me? By my life, says the Lord, you ill get no directions from me.
Will you be their judge, O son of man, ill you be their judge? make clear to them the disgusting ays of their fathers,

And say to them, This is hat the Lord has said: In the day hen I took Israel for myself, hen I made an oath to the seed of the family of Jacob, and I gave them knoledge of myself in the land of Egypt, saying to them ith an oath, I am the Lord your God;
In that day I gave my oath to take them out of the land of Egypt into a land hich I had been searching out for them, a land floing ith milk and honey, the glory of all lands:
And I said to them, Let every man among you put aay the disgusting things to hich his eyes are turned, and do not make yourselves unclean ith the images of Egypt; I am the Lord your God.

But they ould not be controlled by me, and did not give ear to me; they did not put aay the disgusting things to hich their eyes ere turned, or give up the images of Egypt: then I said I ould let loose my passion on them to give full effect to my rath against them in the land of Egypt.

And I as acting for the honour of my name, so that it might not be made unclean before the eyes of the nations among hom they ere, and before hose eyes I gave them knoledge of myself, by taking them out of the land of Egypt.
So I made them go out of the land of Egypt and took them into the aste land.
And I gave them my rules and made clear to them my orders, hich, if a man keeps them, ill be life to him.
And further, I gave them my Sabbaths, to be a sign beteen me and them, so that it might be clear that I, ho make them holy, am the Lord.

But the children of Israel ould not be controlled by me in the aste land: they ere not guided by my rules, and they ere turned aay from my orders, hich, if a man does them, ill be life to him; and they had no respect for my Sabbaths: then I said that I ould let loose my passion on them in the aste land, and put an end to them.
And I as acting for the honour of my name, so that it might not be made unclean in the eyes of the nations, before hose eyes I had taken them out.
And further, I gave my oath to them in the aste land, that I ould not take them into the land hich I had given them, a land floing ith milk and honey, the glory of all lands;
Because they ere turned aay from my orders, and ere not guided by my rules, and had no respect for my Sabbaths: for their hearts ent after their images.
But still my eye had pity on them and I kept them from destruction and did not put an end to them completely in the aste land.
And I said to their children in the aste land, Do not be guided by the rules of your fathers or keep their orders or make yourselves unclean ith their images:
I am the Lord your God; be guided by my rules and keep my orders and do them:
And keep my Sabbaths holy; and they ill be a sign beteen me and you so that it may be clear to you that I am the Lord your God.

But the children ould not be controlled by me; they ere not guided by my rules, and they did not keep and do my orders, hich, if a man does them, ill be life to him; and they had no respect for my Sabbaths: then I said I ould let loose my passion on them to give full effect to my rath against them in the aste land.
And I as acting for the honour of my name, so that it might not be made unclean in the eyes of the nations, before hose eyes I had taken them out.
Further, I gave my oath to them in the aste land that I ould send them andering among the nations, driving them out among the countries;
Because they had not done my orders, but had been turned aay from my rules, and had not given respect to my Sabbaths, and their eyes ere turned to the images of their fathers.
And further, I gave them rules hich ere not good and orders in hich there as no life for them;
I made them unclean in the offerings they gave, causing them to make every first child go through the fire, so that I might put an end to them.
For this cause, son of man, say to the children of Israel, This is hat the Lord has said: In this your fathers have further put shame on my name by doing rong against me.

For hen I had taken them into the land hich I made an oath to give to them, then they sa every high hill and every branching tree and made their offerings there, moving me to rath by their offerings; and there the seet smell of their offerings ent up and their drink offerings ere drained out.
Then I said to them, What is this high place here you go to no purpose? And it is named Bamah to this day.
For this cause say to the children of Israel, This is hat the Lord has said: Are you making yourselves unclean as your fathers did? are you being untrue to me by going after their disgusting orks?

And hen you give your offerings, causing your sons to go through the fire, you make yourselves unclean ith all your images to this day; and ill you come to me for directions, O children of Israel? By my life, says the Lord, you ill get no direction from me.
And that hich comes into your minds ill never take place; hen you say, We ill be like the nations, like the families of the countries, servants of ood and stone;
By my life, says the Lord, truly, ith a strong hand and ith an outstretched arm and ith burning rath let loose, I ill be King over you:
And I ill take you out from the peoples and get you together out of the countries here you are andering, ith a strong hand and ith an outstretched arm and ith burning rath let loose:
And I ill take you into the aste land of the peoples, and there I ill take up the cause ith you face to face.
As I took up the cause ith your fathers in the aste land of the land of Egypt, so ill I take up the cause ith you says the Lord.
And I ill make you go under the rod and ill make you small in number:

Clearing out from among you all those ho are uncontrolled and ho are sinning against me; I ill take them out of the land here they are living, but they ill not come into the land of Israel: and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
As for you, O children of Israel, the Lord has said: Let every man completely put aay his images and give ear to me: and let my holy name no longer be shamed by your offerings and your images.

For in my holy mountain, in the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord, there all the children of Israel, all of them, ill be my servants in the land; there I ill take pleasure in them, and there I ill be orshipped ith your offerings and the first-fruits of the things you give, and ith all your holy things.

I ill take pleasure in you as in a seet smell, hen I take you out from the peoples and get you together from the countries here you have been sent in flight; and I ill make myself holy in you before the eyes of the nations.
And you ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen I take you into the land of Israel, into the country hich I made an oath to give to your fathers.
And there, at the memory of your ays and of all the things you did to make yourselves unclean, you ill have bitter hate for yourselves because of all the evil things you have done.
And you ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen I take you in hand for the honour of my name, and not for your evil ays or your unclean doings, O children of Israel, says the Lord.
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, let your face be turned to the south, let your ords be dropped to the south, and be a prophet against the oodland of the South;

And say to the oodland of the South, Give ear to the ords of the Lord: this is hat the Lord has said: See, I ill have a fire lighted in you, for the destruction of every green tree in you and every dry tree: the flaming flame ill not be put out, and all faces from the south to the north ill be burned by it.
And all flesh ill see that I the Lord have had it lighted: it ill not be put out.
Then I said, Ah, Lord! they say of me, Is he not a maker of stories?
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, let your face be turned to Jerusalem, let your ords be dropped in the direction of her holy place, and be a prophet against the land of Israel;
And say to the land of Israel, These are the ords of the Lord: See, I am against you, and I ill take my sord out of its cover, cutting off from you the upright and the evil.
Because I am going to have the upright and the evil cut off from you, for this cause my sord ill go out from its cover against all flesh from the south to the north:
And all flesh ill see that I the Lord have taken my sord out of its cover: and it ill never go back.
Make sounds of grief, son of man; ith body bent and a bitter heart make sounds of grief before their eyes.

And hen they say to you, Why are you making sounds of grief? then say, Because of the nes, for it is coming: and every heart ill become soft, and all hands ill be feeble, and every spirit ill be burning lo, and all knees ill be turned to ater: see, it is coming and it ill be done, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, say as a prophet, These are the ords of the Lord: Say, A sord, a sord hich has been made sharp and polished:
It has been made sharp to give death; it is polished so that it may be like a thunder-flame: ...
And I have given it to the polisher so that it may be taken in the hand: he has made the sord sharp, he has had it polished, to put it into the hand of him ho gives death.

Give loud cries and make sounds of grief, O son of man: for it has come on my people, it has come on all the rulers of Israel: fear of the sord has come on my people: for this cause give signs of grief.

So then, son of man, be a prophet, and put your hands together ith a loud sound, and give to blos ith the sord, and even three; it is the sord of those ho are ounded, even the sord of the ounded; the great sord hich goes round about them.

In order that hearts may become soft, and the number of those ho are falling may be increased, I have sent death by the sord against all their doors: you are made like a flame, you are polished for death.
Be pointed to the right, to the left, herever your edge is ordered.
And I ill put my hands together ith a loud sound, and I ill let my rath have rest: I the Lord have said it.
And the ord of the Lord came to me again, saying,
And you, son of man, have to ays marked out, so that the sord of the king of Babylon may come; let the to of them come out of one land: and let there be a pillar at the top of the road:
Put a pillar at the top of the road for the sord to come to Rabbah in the land of the children of Ammon, and to Judah and to Jerusalem in the middle of her.

For the king of Babylon took his place at the parting of the ays, at the top of the to roads, to make use of secret arts: shaking the arros this ay and that, he put questions to the images of his gods, he took note of the inner parts of dead beasts.
At his right hand as the fate of Jerusalem, to give orders for destruction, to send up the ar-cry, to put engines of ar against the doors, lifting up earthorks, building alls.
And this anser given by secret arts ill seem false to those ho have given their oaths and have let them be broken: but he ill keep the memory of evil-doing so that they may be taken.

For this cause the Lord has said: Because you have made your evil-doing come to mind by the uncovering of your rongdoing, causing your sins to be seen in all your evil-doings; because you have come to mind, you ill be taken in them.
And you, O evil one, ounded to death, O ruler of Israel, hose day has come in the time of the last punishment;
This is hat the Lord has said: Take aay the holy head-dress, take off the cron: this ill not be again: let that hich is lo be lifted up, and that hich is high be made lo.
I ill let it be overturned, overturned, overturned: this ill not be again till he comes hose right it is; and I ill give it to him.

And you, son of man, say as a prophet, This is hat the Lord has said about the children of Ammon and about their shame: Say, A sord, even a sord let loose, polished for death, to make it shining so that it may be like a flame:
Your vision is to no purpose, your use of secret arts gives a false anser, to put it on the necks of evil-doers ho are ounded to death, hose day has come, in the time of the last punishment.
Go back into your cover. In the place here you ere made, in the land from hich you ere taken, I ill be your judge.
And I ill let loose my burning passion on you, breathing out on you the fire of my rath: and I ill give you up into the hands of men like beasts, trained to destruction.
You ill be food for the fire; your blood ill be drained out in the land; there ill be no more memory of you: for I the Lord have said it.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
And you, son of man, ill you be a judge, ill you be a judge of the ton of blood? then make clear to her all her disgusting ays.
And you are to say, This is hat the Lord has said: A ton causing blood to be drained out in her streets so that her time may come, and making images in her to make her unclean!

You are responsible for the blood drained out by you, and you are unclean through the images hich you have made; and you have made your day come near, and the time of your judging has come; for this cause I have made you a name of shame to the nations and a cause of laughing to all countries.
Those ho are near and those ho are far from you ill make sport of you; your name is unclean, you are full of sounds of fear.
See, the rulers of Israel, every one in his family, have been causing death in you.
In you they have had no respect for father and mother; in you they have been cruel to the man from a strange land; in you they have done rong to the child ithout a father and to the ido.
You have made little of my holy things, and have made my Sabbaths unclean.
In you there are men ho say evil of others, causing death; in you they have taken the flesh ith the blood for food; in your streets they have put evil designs into effect.
In you they have let the shame of their fathers be seen; in you they have done rong to a oman at the time hen she as unclean.
And in you one man has done hat as disgusting ith his neighbour’s ife; and another has made his daughter-in-la unclean; and another has done rong to his sister, his father’s daughter.
In you they have taken reards as the price of blood; you have taken interest and great profits, and you have taken aay your neighbours’ goods by force, and have not kept me in mind, says the Lord.
See, then, I have made my hands come together in rath against your taking of goods by force and against the blood hich has been floing in you.
Will your heart be high or your hands strong in the days hen I take you in hand? I the Lord have said it and ill do it.
And I ill send you in flight among the nations and andering among the countries; and I ill completely take aay out of you everything hich is unclean.
And you ill be made lo before the eyes of the nations; and it ill be clear to you that I am the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, the children of Israel have become like the poorest sort of aste metal to me: they are all silver and brass and tin and iron and lead mixed ith aste.
For this cause the Lord has said: Because you have all become aste metal, see, I ill get you together inside Jerusalem.

As they put silver and brass and iron and lead and tin together inside the oven, heating up the fire on it to make it soft; so ill I get you together in my rath and in my passion, and, heating the fire ith my breath, ill make you soft.
Yes, I ill take you, breathing on you the fire of my rath, and you ill become soft in it.
As silver becomes soft in the oven, so you ill become soft in it; and you ill be certain that I the Lord have let loose my passion on you.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, say to her, You are a land on hich no rain or thunderstorm has come in the day of rath.
Her rulers in her are like a loud-voiced lion violently taking his food; they have made a meal of souls; they have taken ealth and valued property; they have made great the number of idos in her.

Her priests have been acting violently against my la; they have made my holy things unclean: they have made no division beteen hat is holy and hat is common, and they have not made it clear that the unclean is different from the clean, and their eyes have been shut to my Sabbaths, and I am not honoured among them.
Her rulers in her are like olves violently taking their food; putting men to death and causing the destruction of souls, so that they may get their profit.
And her prophets have been using hiteash, seeing foolish visions and making false use of secret arts, saying, This is hat the Lord has said, hen the Lord has said nothing.
The people of the land have been acting cruelly, taking men’s goods by force; they have been hard on the poor and those in need, and have done rong to the man from a strange land.
And I as looking for a man among them ho ould make up the all and take his station in the broken place before me for the land, so that I might not send destruction on it: but there as no one.
And I let loose my passion on them, and have put an end to them in the fire of my rath: I have made the punishment of their ays come on their heads, says the Lord.
The ord of the Lord came to me again, saying,
Son of man, there ere to omen, daughters of one mother:
They ere acting like loose omen in Egypt; hen they ere young their behaviour as loose: there their breasts ere crushed, even the points of their young breasts ere crushed.
Their names ere Oholah, the older, and Oholibah, her sister: and they became mine, and gave birth to sons and daughters. As for their names, Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem, Oholibah.
And Oholah as untrue to me hen she as mine; she as full of desire for her lovers, even for the Assyrians, her neighbours,
Who ere clothed in blue, captains and rulers, all of them young men to be desired, horsemen seated on horses.
And she gave her unclean love to them, all of them the noblest men of Assyria: and she made herself unclean ith the images of all ho ere desired by her.

And she has not given up her loose ays from the time hen she as in Egypt; for hen she as young they ere her lovers, and by them her young breasts ere crushed, and they let loose on her their unclean desire.
For this cause I gave her up into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the Assyrians on hom her desire as fixed.
By these her shame as uncovered: they took her sons and daughters and put her to death ith the sord: and she became a cause of onder to omen; for they gave her the punishment hich as right.
And her sister Oholibah sa this, but her desire as even more unmeasured, and her loose behaviour as orse than that of her sister.
She as full of desire for the Assyrians, captains and rulers, her neighbours, clothed in blue, horsemen going on horses, all of them young men to be desired.
And I sa that she had become unclean; the to of them ent the same ay.
And her loose behaviour became orse; for she sa men pictured on a all, pictures of the Chaldaeans painted in bright red,
With bands round their bodies and ith head-dresses hanging round their heads, all of them looking like rulers, like the Babylonians, the land of hose birth is Chaldaea.
And hen she sa them she as full of desire for them, and sent servants to them in Chaldaea.
And the Babylonians came to her, into the bed of love, and made her unclean ith their loose desire, and she became unclean ith them, and her soul as turned from them.
So her loose behaviour as clearly seen and her shame uncovered: then my soul as turned from her as it had been turned from her sister.
But still she ent on the more ith her loose behaviour, keeping in mind the early days hen she had been a loose oman in the land of Egypt.
And she as full of desire for her lovers, hose flesh is like the flesh of asses and hose seed is like the seed of horses.
And she made the memory of the loose ays of her early years come back to mind, hen her young breasts ere crushed by the Egyptians.

For this cause, O Oholibah, this is hat the Lord has said: See, I ill make your lovers come up against you, even those from hom your soul is turned aay in disgust; and I ill make them come up against you on every side;

The Babylonians and all the Chaldaeans, Pekod and Shoa and Koa, and all the Assyrians ith them: young men to be desired, captains and rulers all of them, and chiefs, her neighbours, all of them on horseback.

And they ill come against you from the north on horseback, ith ar-carriages and a great band of peoples; they ill put themselves in order against you ith breastplate and body-cover and metal head-dress round about you: and I ill make them your judges, and they ill give their decision against you as seems right to them.

And my bitter feeling ill be orking against you, and they ill take you in hand ith passion; they ill take aay your nose and your ears, and the rest of you ill be put to the sord: they ill take your sons and daughters, and the rest of you ill be burned up in the fire.
And they ill take all your clothing off you and take aay your ornaments.
So I ill put an end to your evil ays and your loose behaviour hich came from the land of Egypt: and your eyes ill never be lifted up to them again, and you ill have no more memory of Egypt.
For this is hat the Lord has said: See, I ill give you up into the hands of those ho are hated by you, into the hands of those from hom your soul is turned aay in disgust:

And they ill take you in hand ith hate, and take aay all the fruit of your ork, and let you be unveiled and ithout clothing: and the shame of your loose behaviour ill be uncovered, your evil designs and your loose ays.
They ill do these things to you because you have been untrue to me, and have gone after the nations, and have become unclean ith their images.
You have gone in the ay of your sister; and I ill give her cup into your hand.
This is hat the Lord has said: You ill take a drink from your sister’s cup, hich is deep and ide: you ill be laughed at and looked don on, more than you are able to undergo.
You ill be broken and full of sorro, ith the cup of onder and destruction, ith the cup of your sister Samaria.
And after drinking it and draining it out, you ill take the last drops of it to the end, pulling off your breasts: for I have said it, says the Lord.

So this is hat the Lord has said: Because you have not kept me in your memory, and because your back has been turned to me, you ill even undergo the punishment of your evil designs and your loose ays.
Then the Lord said to me: Son of man, ill you be the judge of Oholibah? then make clear to her the disgusting things she has done.
For she has been false to me, and blood is on her hands, and ith her images she has been untrue; and more than this, she made her sons, hom she had by me, go through the fire to them to be burned up.
Further, this is hat she has done to me: she has made my holy place unclean and has made my Sabbaths unclean.
For hen she had made an offering of her children to her images, she came into my holy place to make it unclean; see, this is hat she has done inside my house.
And she even sent for men to come from far aay, to hom a servant as sent, and they came: for hom she as ashing her body and painting her eyes and making herself fair ith ornaments.
And she took her seat on a great bed, ith a table put ready before it on hich she put my perfume and my oil.
... and they put jeels on her hands and beautiful crons on her head.
Then I said ... no she ill go on ith her loose ays.
And they ent in to her, as men go to a loose oman: so they ent in to Oholibah, the loose oman.
And upright men ill be her judges, judging her as false ives and omen ho take lives are judged; because she has been untrue to me and blood is on her hands.
For this is hat the Lord has said: I ill make a great meeting of the people come together against her, and ill send on her shaking fear and take everything from her.
And the meeting, after stoning her ith stones, ill put an end to her ith their sords; they ill put her sons and daughters to death and have her house burned up ith fire.
And I ill put an end to evil in all the land, teaching all omen not to do as you have done.
And I ill send on you the punishment of your evil ays, and you ill be rearded for your sins ith your images: and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, saying,
Son of man, put don in riting this very day: The king of Babylon let loose the eight of his attack against Jerusalem on this very day.
And make a comparison for this uncontrolled people, and say to them, This is hat the Lord has said: Put on the cooking-pot, put it on the fire and put ater in it:
And get the bits together, the fat tail, every good part, the leg and the top part of it: make it full of the best bones.
Take the best of the flock, put much ood under it: see that its bits are boiling ell; let the bones be cooked inside it.
For this is hat the Lord has said: A curse is on the ton of blood, the cooking-pot hich is unclean inside, hich has never been made clean! take out its bits; its fate is still to come on it.
For her blood is in her; she has put it on the open rock not draining it on to the earth so that it might be covered ith dust;
In order that it might make rath come up to give punishment, she has put her blood on the open rock, so that it may not be covered.
For this cause the Lord has said: A curse is on the ton of blood! and I ill make great the burning mass.
Put on much ood, heating up the fire, boiling the flesh ell, and making the soup thick, and let the bones be burned.
And I ill put her on the coals so that she may be heated and her brass burned, so that hat is unclean in her may become soft and her aste be completely taken aay.
I have made myself tired to no purpose: still all the aste hich is in her has not come out, it has an evil smell.

As for your unclean purpose: because I have been attempting to make you clean, but you have not been made clean from it, you ill not be made clean till I have let loose my passion on you in full measure.
I the Lord have said the ord and I ill do it; I ill not go back or have mercy, and my purpose ill not be changed; in the measure of your ays and of your evil doings you ill be judged, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, see, I am taking aay the desire of your eyes by disease: but let there be no sorro or eeping or drops running from your eyes.
Let there be no sound of sorro; make no eeping for your dead, put on your head-dress and your shoes on your feet, let not your lips be covered, and do not take the food of those in grief.
So in the morning I as teaching the people and in the evening death took my ife; and in the morning I did hat I had been ordered to do.
And the people said to me, Will you not make clear to us the sense of these things; is it for us you do them?
Then I said to them, The ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

Say to the people of Israel, The Lord has said, See, I ill make my holy place unclean, the pride of your strength, the pleasure of your eyes, and the desire of your soul; and your sons and daughters, ho did not come ith you here, ill be put to the sord.
And you ill do as I have done, not covering your lips or taking the food of those in grief.

And your head-dresses ill be on your heads and your shoes on your feet: there ill be no sorro or eeping; but you ill be asting aay in the punishment of your evil-doing, and you ill be looking at one another in onder.
And Ezekiel ill be a sign to you; everything he has done you ill do: hen this takes place, you ill be certain that I am the Lord.

And as for you, son of man, your mouth ill be shut in the day hen I take from them their strength, the joy of their glory, the desire of their eyes, and that on hich their hearts are fixed, and their sons and daughters.
In that day, one ho has got aay safe ill come to you to give you nes of it.

In that day your mouth ill be open to him ho has got aay safe, and you ill say ords to him and your lips ill no longer be shut: so you ill be a sign to them and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, let your face be turned to the children of Ammon, and be a prophet against them:

And say to the children of Ammon, Give ear to the ord of the Lord; this is hat the Lord has said: Because you said, Aha! against my holy place hen it as made unclean, and against the land of Israel hen it as made aste, and against the people of Judah hen they ere taken aay as prisoners;

For this cause I ill give you up to the children of the east for their heritage, and they ill put their tent-circles in you and make their houses in you; they ill take your fruit for their food and your milk for their drink.
And I ill make Rabbah a place for housing camels, and the children of Ammon a resting-place for flocks: and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
For the Lord has said, Because you have made sounds of joy ith your hands, stamping your feet, and have been glad, putting shame ith all your soul on the land of Israel;

For this cause my hand has been stretched out against you, and I ill give up your goods to be taken by the nations; I ill have you cut off from the peoples and ill put an end to you among the countries: I ill give you up to destruction; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
This is hat the Lord has said: Because Moab and Seir are saying, See, the people of Judah are like all the nations;
For this cause, I ill let the side of Moab be uncovered, and his tons on every side, the glory of the land, Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon and as far as Kiriathaim.
To the children of the east I have given her for a heritage, as ell as the children of Ammon, so that there may be no memory of her among the nations:
And I ill be the judge of Moab; and they ill see that I am the Lord.
This is hat the Lord has said: Because Edom has taken his payment from the people of Judah, and has done great rong in taking payment from them;
The Lord has said, My hand ill be stretched out against Edom, cutting off from it man and beast: and I ill make it aste, from Teman even as far as Dedan they ill be put to the sord.
I ill take payment from Edom because of my people Israel; and I ill take Edom in hand in my rath and in my passion: and they ill have experience of my reard, says the Lord.
This is hat the Lord has said: Because the Philistines have taken payment, ith the purpose of causing shame and destruction ith unending hate;
The Lord has said, See, my hand ill be stretched out against the Philistines, cutting off the Cherethites and sending destruction on the rest of the sea-land.
And I ill take great payment from them ith acts of rath; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord hen I send my punishment on them.
No in the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, because Tyre has said against Jerusalem, Aha, she ho as the dooray of the peoples is broken; she is turned over to them; she ho as full is made aste;
For this cause the Lord has said, See, I am against you, O Tyre, and ill send up a number of nations against you as the sea sends up its aves.
And they ill give the alls of Tyre to destruction and have its toers broken: and I ill take even her dust aay from her, and make her an uncovered rock
She ill be a place for the stretching out of nets in the middle of the sea; for I have said it, says the Lord: and her goods ill be given over to the nations.
And her daughters in the open country ill be put to the sord: and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.

For this is hat the Lord has said: See, I ill send up from the north Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, king of kings, against Tyre, ith horses and ar-carriages and ith an army and great numbers of people.
He ill put to the sord your daughters in the open country: he ill make strong alls against you and put up an earthork against you, arming himself for ar against you.
He ill put up his engines of ar against your alls, and your toers ill be broken don by his axes.

Because of the number of his horses you ill be covered ith their dust: your alls ill be shaking at the noise of the horsemen and of the heels and of the ar-carriages, hen he comes through your doorays, as into a ton hich has been broken open.
Your streets ill be stamped don by the feet of his horses: he ill put your people to the sord, and ill send don the pillars of your strength to the earth.

They ill take by force all your ealth and go off ith the goods ith hich you do trade: they ill have your alls broken don and all the houses of your desire given up to destruction: they ill put your stones and your ood and your dust deep in the ater.
I ill put an end to the noise of your songs, and the sound of your instruments of music ill be gone for ever.
I ill make you an uncovered rock: you ill be a place for the stretching out of nets; there ill be no building you up again: for I the Lord have said it, says the Lord.
This is hat the Lord has said to Tyre: Will not the sea-lands be shaking at the sound of your fall, hen the ounded give cries of pain, hen men are put to the sord in you?

Then all the rulers of the sea ill come don from their high seats, and put aay their robes and take off their clothing of needleork: they ill put on the clothing of grief, they ill take their seats on the earth, shaking ith fear every minute and overcome ith onder at you.

And they ill send up a song of grief for you, and say to you, What destruction has come on you, ho are you cut off from the sea, the noted ton, hich as strong in the sea, she and her people, causing the fear of them to come on all the dry land!
No the sea-lands ill be shaking in the day of your fall; and all the ships on the sea ill be overcome ith fear at your going.
For this is hat the Lord has said: I ill make you a aste ton, like the tons hich are unpeopled; hen I make the deep come upon you, covering you ith great aters.

Then I ill make you go don ith those ho go don into the underorld, to the people of the past, causing your living-place to be in the deepest parts of the earth, in places long unpeopled, ith those ho go don into the deep, so that there ill be no one living in you; and you ill have no glory in the land of the living.
I ill make you a thing of fear, and you ill come to an end: even if you are looked for, you ill not be seen again for ever, says the Lord.
The ord of the Lord came to me again, saying,
And you, son of man, make a song of grief for Tyre;

And say to Tyre, O you ho are seated at the dooray of the sea, trading for the peoples ith the great sea-lands, these are the ords of the Lord: You, O Tyre, have said, I am a ship completely beautiful.
Your builders have made your outlines in the heart of the seas, they have made you completely beautiful.
They have made all your boards of fir-trees from Senir: they have taken cedars from Lebanon to make the supports for your sails.
Of oak-trees from Bashan they have made your driving blades; they have made your floors of ivory and boxood from the sea-lands of Kittim.
The best linen ith needleork from Egypt as your sail, stretched out to be a flag for you; blue and purple from the sea-lands of Elishah gave you shade.
The people of Zidon and Arvad ere your boatmen; the ise men of Zemer ere in you; they ere guiding your ships;
The responsible men of Gebal and its ise men ere in you, making your boards atertight: all the ships of the sea ith their seamen ere in you trading in your goods.
Cush and Lud and Put ere in your army, your men of ar, hanging up their body-covers and head-dresses of ar in you: they gave you your glory.
The men of Arvad in your army ere on your alls, and ere atchmen in your toers, hanging up their arms on your alls round about; they made you completely beautiful.
Tarshish did business ith you because of the great amount of your ealth; they gave silver, iron, tin, and lead for your goods.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech ere your traders; they gave living men and brass vessels for your goods.
The people of Togarmah gave horses and ar-horses and transport beasts for your goods.
The men of Rodan ere your traders: a great number of sea-lands did business ith you: they gave you horns of ivory and ebony as an offering.
Edom did business ith you because of the great number of things hich you made; they gave emeralds, purple, and needleork, and the best linen and coral and rubies for your goods.
Judah and the land of Israel ere your traders; they gave grain of Minnith and seet cakes and honey and oil and perfume for your goods.
Damascus did business ith you because of the great amount of your ealth, ith ine of Helbon and hite ool.
... for your goods: they gave polished iron and spices for your goods.
Dedan did trade ith you in cloths for the backs of horses.
Arabia and all the rulers of Kedar did business ith you; in lambs and sheep and goats, in these they did business ith you.
The traders of Sheba and Raamah did trade ith you; they gave the best of all sorts of spices and all sorts of stones of great price and gold for your goods.
Haran and Canneh and Eden, the traders of Asshur and all the Medes:
These ere your traders in beautiful robes, in rolls of blue and needleork, and in chests of coloured cloth, corded ith cords and made of cedar-ood, in them they did trade ith you.
Tarshish ships did business for you in your goods: and you ere made full, and great as your glory in the heart of the seas.
Your boatmen have taken you into great aters: you have been broken by the east ind in the heart of the seas.

Your ealth and your goods, the things in hich you do trade, your seamen and those guiding your ships, those ho make your boards atertight, and those ho do business ith your goods, and all your men of ar ho are in you, ith all ho have come together in you, ill go don into the heart of the seas in the day of your donfall.
At the sound of the cry of your ships’ guides, the boards of the ship ill be shaking.
And all the boatmen, the seamen and those ho are expert at guiding a ship through the sea, ill come don from their ships and take their places on the land;
And their voices ill be sounding over you, and crying bitterly they ill put dust on their heads, rolling themselves in the dust:
And they ill have the hair of their heads cut off because of you, and ill put haircloth on their bodies, eeping for you ith bitter grief in their souls, even ith bitter sorro.
And in their eeping they ill make a song of grief for you, sorroing over you and saying, Who is like Tyre, ho has come to an end in the deep sea?
When your goods ent out over the seas, you made numbers of peoples full; the ealth of the kings of the earth as increased ith your great ealth and all your goods.
No that you are broken by the seas in the deep aters, your goods and all your people ill go don ith you.
All the people of the sea-lands are overcome ith onder at you, and their kings are full of fear, their faces are troubled.
Those ho do business among the peoples make sounds of surprise at you; you have become a thing of fear, you have come to an end for ever.
The ord of the Lord came to me again, saying,

Son of man, say to the ruler of Tyre, This is hat the Lord has said: Because your heart has been lifted up, and you have said, I am a god, I am seated on the seat of God in the heart of the seas; but you are man and not God, though you have made your heart as the heart of God:
See, you are iser than Daniel; there is no secret hich is deeper than your knoledge:
By your isdom and deep knoledge you have got poer for yourself, and put silver and gold in your store-houses:
By your great isdom and by your trade your poer is increased, and your heart is lifted up because of your poer:
For this cause the Lord has said: Because you have made your heart as the heart of God,
See, I am sending against you strange men, feared among the nations: they ill let loose their sords against your bright isdom, they ill make your glory a common thing.
They ill send you don to the underorld, and your death ill be the death of those ho are put to the sord in the heart of the seas.
Will you say, in the face of those ho are taking your life, I am God? but you are man and not God in the hands of those ho are ounding you.
Your death ill be the death of those ho are ithout circumcision, by the hands of men from strange lands: for I have said it, says the Lord.
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, make a song of grief for the king of Tyre, and say to him, This is hat the Lord has said: You are all-ise and completely beautiful;

You ere in Eden, the garden of God; every stone of great price as your clothing, the sardius, the topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper, the emerald and the carbuncle: your store-houses ere full of gold, and things of great price ere in you; in the day hen you ere made they ere got ready.
I gave you your place ith the inged one; I put you on the mountain of God; you ent up and don among the stones of fire.
There has been no evil in your ays from the day hen you ere made, till sin as seen in you.
Through all your trading you have become full of violent ays, and have done evil: so I sent you out shamed from the mountain of God; the inged one put an end to you from among the stones of fire.
Your heart as lifted up because you ere beautiful, you made your isdom evil through your sin: I have sent you don, even to the earth; I have made you lo before kings, so that they may see you.

By all your sin, even by your evil trading, you have made your holy places unclean; so I ill make a fire come out from you, it ill make a meal of you, and I ill make you as dust on the earth before the eyes of all ho see you.
All ho have knoledge of you among the peoples ill be overcome ith onder at you: you have become a thing of fear, and you ill never be seen again.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, let your face be turned to Zidon, and be a prophet against it, and say,

These are the ords of the Lord: See, I am against you, O Zidon; and I ill get glory for myself in you: and they ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen I send my punishments on her, and I ill be seen to be holy in her.
And I ill send on her disease and blood in her streets; and the ounded ill be falling in the middle of her, and the sord ill be against her on every side; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.

And there ill no longer be a plant ith sharp points ounding the children of Israel, or a thorn troubling them among any ho are round about them, ho put shame on them; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.

This is hat the Lord has said: When I have got together the children of Israel from the peoples among hom they are andering, and have been made holy among them before the eyes of the nations, then they ill have rest in the land hich is theirs, hich I gave to my servant Jacob

And they ill be safe there, building houses and planting vine-gardens and living ithout fear; hen I have sent my punishments on all those ho put shame on them round about them; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord their God.
In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the telfth day of the month, the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, let your face be turned against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and be a prophet against him and against all Egypt:

Say to them, These are the ords of the Lord: See, I am against you, Pharaoh, king of Egypt, the great river-beast stretched out among his Nile streams, ho has said, The Nile is mine, and I have made it for myself.
And I ill put hooks in your mouth, and the fish of your streams ill be hanging from your skin; and I ill make you come up out of your streams, ith all the fish of your streams hanging from your skin.

And I ill let you be in the aste land, you and all the fish of your streams: you ill go don on the face of the land; you ill not be taken up or put to rest in the earth; I have given you for food to the beasts of the field and the birds of the heaven.
And it ill be clear to all the people of Egypt that I am the Lord, because you have been a false support to the children of Israel.
When they took a grip of you in their hands, you ere crushed so that their arms ere broken: and hen they put their eight on you for support, you ere broken and all their muscles gave ay.
For this cause the Lord has said: See, I am sending a sord on you, cutting off from you man and beast.
And the land of Egypt ill be an unpeopled aste; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord: because he has said, The Nile is mine, and I made it.
See, then, I am against you and against your streams, and I ill make the land of Egypt an unpeopled aste, from Migdol to Syene, even as far as the edge of Ethiopia.
No foot of man ill go through it and no foot of beast, and it ill be unpeopled for forty years.

I ill make the land of Egypt a aste among the countries hich are made aste, and her tons ill be unpeopled among the tons hich have been made aste, for forty years: and I ill send the Egyptians in flight among the nations and andering through the countries.
For this is hat the Lord has said: At the end of forty years I ill get the Egyptians together from the peoples here they have gone in flight:
I ill let the fate of Egypt be changed, and ill make them come back into the land of Pathros, into the land from hich they came; and there they ill be an unimportant kingdom.
It ill be the loest of the kingdoms, and never again ill it be lifted up over the nations: I ill make them small, so that they may not have rule over the nations.
And Egypt ill no longer be the hope of the children of Israel, causing sin to come to mind hen their eyes are turned to them: and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
No in the tenty-seventh year, in the first month, on the first day of the month, the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon, made his army do hard ork against Tyre, and the hair came off every head and every arm as rubbed smooth: but he and his army got no payment out of Tyre for the hard ork hich he had done against it.

For this cause the Lord has said: See, I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon: he ill take aay her ealth, and take her goods by force and everything hich is there; and this ill be the payment for his army.
I have given him the land of Egypt as the reard for his hard ork, because they ere orking for me, says the Lord.
In that day I ill make a horn put out buds for the children of Israel, and I ill let your ords come freely among them, and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
The ord of the Lord came to me again, saying,
Son of man, be a prophet, and say, These are the ords of the Lord: Give a cry, Aha, for the day!
For the day is near, the day of the Lord is near, a day of cloud; it ill be the time of the nations.
And a sord ill come on Egypt, and cruel pain ill be in Ethiopia, hen they are falling by the sord in Egypt; and they ill take aay her ealth and her bases ill be broken don.
Ethiopia and Put and Lud and all the mixed people and Libya and the children of the land of the Cherethites ill all be put to death ith them by the sord.
This is hat the Lord has said: The supporters of Egypt ill have a fall, and the pride of her poer ill come don: from Migdol to Syene they ill be put to the sord in it, says the Lord.
And she ill be made aste among the countries hich have been made aste, and her tons ill be among the tons hich are unpeopled.
And they ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen I have put a fire in Egypt and all her helpers are broken.
In that day men ill go out quickly to take the nes, causing fear in untroubled Ethiopia; and bitter pain ill come on them as in the day of Egypt; for see, it is coming.
This is hat the Lord has said: I ill put an end to great numbers of the people of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon.
He and the people ith him, causing fear among the nations, ill be sent for the destruction of the land; their sords ill be let loose against Egypt and the land ill be full of dead.

And I ill make the Nile streams dry, and ill give the land into the hands of evil men, causing the land and everything in it to be asted by the hands of men from a strange country: I the Lord have said it.

This is hat the Lord has said: In addition to this, I ill give up the images to destruction and put an end to the false gods in Noph; never again ill there be a ruler in the land of Egypt: and I ill put a fear in the land of Egypt.
And I ill make Pathros a aste, and put a fire in Zoan, and send my punishments on No.
I ill let loose my rath on Sin, the strong place of Egypt, cutting off the mass of the people of No.
And I ill put a fire in Egypt; Syene ill be tisting in pain, and No ill be broken into, as by the onrush of aters.
The young men of On and Pi-beseth ill be put to the sord: and these tons ill be taken aay prisoners.

And at Tehaphnehes the day ill become dark, hen the yoke of Egypt is broken there, and the pride of her poer comes to an end: as for her, she ill be covered ith a cloud, and her daughters ill be taken aay prisoners.
And I ill send my punishments on Egypt: and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
No in the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh day of the month, the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, the arm of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, has been broken by me, and no band has been put round it to make it ell, no band has been tisted round it to make it strong for gripping the sord.
For this cause the Lord has said: See, I am against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and by me his strong arm ill be broken; and I ill make the sord go out of his hand.
And I ill send the Egyptians in flight among the nations and andering through the countries.

And I ill make the arms of the king of Babylon strong, and ill put my sord in his hand: but Pharaoh’s arms ill be broken, and he ill give cries of pain before him like the cries of a man ounded to death.

And I ill make the arms of the king of Babylon strong, and the arms of Pharaoh ill be hanging don; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen I put my sord into the hand of the king of Babylon and it is stretched out against the land of Egypt.
And I ill send the Egyptians in flight among the nations and andering through the countries; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
No in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first day of the month, the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, say to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and to his people; Whom are you like in your great poer?
See, a pine-tree ith beautiful branches and thick groth, giving shade and very tall; and its top as among the clouds.
It got strength from the aters and the deep made it tall: its streams ent round about its planted land and it sent out its aterays to all the trees of the field.
In this ay it became taller than all the trees of the field; and its branches ere increased and its arms became long because of the great aters.
In its branches all the birds of heaven came to rest, and under its arms all the beasts of the field gave birth to their young, and great nations ere living in its shade.
So it as beautiful, being so tall and its branches so long, for its root as by great aters.
No cedars ere equal to it in the garden of God; the fir-trees ere not like its branches, and plane-trees ere as nothing in comparison ith its arms; no tree in the garden of God as so beautiful.
I made it beautiful ith its mass of branches: so that all the trees in the garden of God ere full of envy of it.
For this cause the Lord has said: Because he is tall, and has put his top among the clouds, and his heart is full of pride because he is so high,
I have given him up into the hands of a strong one of the nations; he ill certainly give him the reard of his sin, driving him out.

And men from strange lands, ho are to be feared among the nations, after cutting him off, have let him be: on the mountains and in all the valleys his branches have come don; his arms are broken by all the aterays of the land; all the peoples of the earth have gone from his shade, and have let him be.
All the birds of heaven have come to rest on his broken stem here it is stretched on the earth, and all the beasts of the field ill be on his branches:

In order that no trees by the aters may be lifted up in their groth, putting their tops among the clouds; and that no trees hich are atered may take their place on high: for they are all given up to death, to the loest parts of the earth among the children of men, ith those ho go don to the underorld.

This is hat the Lord has said: The day hen he goes don to the underorld, I ill make the deep full of grief for him; I ill keep back her streams and the great aters ill be stopped: I ill make Lebanon dark for him, and all the trees of the field ill be feeble because of him.

I ill send shaking on the nations at the sound of his fall, hen I send him don to the underorld ith those ho go don into the deep: and on earth they ill be comforting themselves, all the trees of Eden, the best of Lebanon, even all the atered ones.
And they ill go don ith him to the underorld, to those ho have been put to the sord; even those ho ere his helpers, living under his shade among the nations

Whom then are you like? for you ill be sent don ith the trees of Eden into the loest parts of the earth: there you ill be stretched out among those ithout circumcision, ith those ho ere put to the sord. This is Pharaoh and all his people, says the Lord.
And it came about in the telfth year, in the telfth month, on the first day of the month, that the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

Son of man, make a song of grief for Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and say to him, Young lion of the nations, destruction has come on you; and you ere like a sea-beast in the seas, sending out bursts of ater, troubling the aters ith your feet, making their streams dirty.
This is hat the Lord has said: My net ill be stretched out over you, and I ill take you up in my fishing-net.

And I ill let you be stretched on the land; I ill send you out violently into the open field; I ill let all the birds of heaven come to rest on you and ill make the beasts of all the earth full of you.
And I ill put your flesh on the mountains, and make the valleys full of your blood.
And the land ill be atered ith your blood, and the aterays ill be full of you.
And hen I put out your life, the heaven ill be covered and its stars made dark; I ill let the sun be covered ith a cloud and the moon ill not give her light.
All the bright lights of heaven I ill make dark over you, and put dark night on your land, says the Lord.
And the hearts of numbers of peoples ill be troubled, hen I send your prisoners among the nations, into a country hich is strange to you.

And I ill make a number of peoples overcome ith onder at you, and their kings ill be full of fear because of you, hen my sord is aved before them: they ill be shaking every minute, every man fearing for his life, in the day of your fall.
For this is hat the Lord has said: The sord of the king of Babylon ill come on you.

I ill let the sords of the strong be the cause of the fall of your people; all of them men to be feared among the nations: and they ill make aste the pride of Egypt, and all its people ill come to destruction.
And I ill put an end to all her beasts hich are by the great aters, and they ill never again be troubled by the foot of man or by the feet of beasts.
Then I ill make their aters clear and their rivers ill be floing like oil, says the Lord.
When I make Egypt an unpeopled aste, cutting off from the land all the things in it; hen I send punishment on all those living in it, then it ill be clear to them that I am the Lord.
It is a song of grief, and people ill give voice to it, the daughters of the nations ill give voice to it, even for Egypt and all her people, says the Lord.
And in the telfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

Son of man, let your voice be loud in sorro for the people of Egypt and send them don, even you and the daughters of the nations; I ill send them don into the loest parts of the earth, ith those ho go don into the underorld.
Are you more beautiful than any? go don, and take your rest among those ithout circumcision,
Among those ho have been put to the sord: they ill give a resting-place ith them to all their people.

The strong among the great ones ill say to him from the underorld, Are you more beautiful than any? go don, you and your helpers, and take your rest among those ithout circumcision, and those ho have been put to the sord.
There is Asshur and all her army, round about her last resting-place: all of them put to death by the sord:
Whose resting-places are in the inmost parts of the underorld, ho ere a cause of fear in the land of the living.

There is Elam and all her people, round about her last resting-place: all of them put to death by the sord, ho have gone don ithout circumcision into the loest parts of the earth, ho ere a cause of fear in the land of the living, and are put to shame ith those ho go don to the underorld:

They have made a bed for her among the dead, and all her people are round about her resting-place: all of them ithout circumcision, put to death ith the sord; for they ere a cause of fear in the land of the living, and are put to shame ith those ho go don to the underorld: they have been given a place among those ho have been put to the sord.
There is Meshech, Tubal, and all her people, round about her last resting-place: all of them ithout circumcision, put to death by the sord; for they ere a cause of fear in the land of the living.

And they have been put to rest ith the fighting men ho came to their end in days long past, ho ent don to the underorld ith their instruments of ar, placing their sords under their heads, and their body-covers are over their bones; for their strength as a cause of fear in the land of the living.
But you ill have your bed among those ithout circumcision, and ill be put to rest ith those ho have been put to death ith the sord.

There is Edom, her kings and all her princes, ho have been given a resting-place ith those ho ere put to the sord: they ill be resting among those ithout circumcision, even ith those ho go don to the underorld.

There are the chiefs of the north, all of them, and all the Zidonians, ho have gone don ith those ho have been put to the sord: they are shamed on account of all the fear caused by their strength; they are resting there ithout circumcision, among those ho have been put to the sord, and are put to shame ith those ho go don to the underorld.
Pharaoh ill see them and be comforted on account of all his people: even Pharaoh and all his army, put to death by the sord, says the Lord.

For he put his fear in the land of the living: and he ill be put to rest among those ithout circumcision, ith those ho have been put to death ith the sord, even Pharaoh and all his people, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, give a ord to the children of your people, and say to them, When I make the sord come on a land, if the people of the land take a man from among their number and make him their atchman:
If, hen he sees the sord coming on the land, by sounding the horn he gives the people nes of their danger;
Then anyone ho, hearing the sound of the horn, does not take note of it, ill himself be responsible for his death, if the sord comes and takes him aay.
On hearing the sound of the horn, he did not take note; his blood ill be on him; for if he had taken note his life ould have been safe.

But if the atchman sees the sord coming, and does not give a note on the horn, and the people have no ord of the danger, and the sord comes and takes any person from among them; he ill be taken aay in his sin, but I ill make the atchman responsible for his blood.
So you, son of man, I have made you a atchman for the children of Israel; and you are to give ear to the ord of my mouth and give them nes from me of their danger.

When I say to the evil-doer, Death ill certainly overtake you; and you say nothing to make clear to the evil-doer the danger of his ay; death ill overtake that evil man in his evil-doing, but I ill make you responsible for his blood.

But if you make clear to the evil-doer the danger of his ay for the purpose of turning him from it, and he is not turned from his ay, death ill overtake him in his evil-doing, but your life ill be safe.
And you, son of man, say to the children of Israel, You say, Our rongdoing and our sins are on us and e are asting aay in them; ho then may e have life?

Say to them, By my life, says the Lord, I have no pleasure in the death of the evil-doer; it is more pleasing to me if he is turned from his ay and has life: be turned, be turned from your evil ays; hy are you looking for death, O children of Israel?

And you, son of man, say to the children of your people, The righteousness of the upright man ill not make him safe in the day hen he does rong; and the evil-doing of the evil man ill not be the cause of his fall in the day hen he is turned from his evil-doing; and the upright man ill not have life because of his righteousness in the day hen he does evil.

When I say to the upright that life ill certainly be his; if he puts his faith in his righteousness and does evil, not one of his upright acts ill be kept in memory; but in the evil he has done, death ill overtake him.
And hen I say to the evil-doer, Death ill certainly be your fate; if he is turned from his sin and does hat is ordered and right;

If the evil-doer lets one ho is in his debt have back hat is his, and gives back hat he had taken by force, and is guided by the rules of life, doing no evil; life ill certainly be his, death ill not overtake him.
Not one of the sins hich he has done ill be kept in mind against him: he has done hat is ordered and right, life ill certainly be his.
But the children of your people say, The ay of the Lord is not equal: hen it is they hose ay is not equal.
When the upright man, turning aay from his righteousness, does evil, death ill overtake him in it.
And hen the evil man, turning aay from his evil-doing, does hat is ordered and right, he ill get life by it.
And still you say, The ay of the Lord is not equal. O children of Israel, I ill be your judge, giving to everyone the reard of his ays.
No in the telfth year after e had been taken aay prisoners, in the tenth month, on the fifth day of the month, one ho had got aay in flight from Jerusalem came to me, saying, The ton has been taken.

No the hand of the Lord had been on me in the evening, before the man ho had got aay came to me; and he made my mouth open, ready for his coming to me in the morning; and my mouth as open and I as no longer ithout voice.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

Son of man, those ho are living in these aste places in the land of Israel say, Abraham as but one, and he had land for his heritage: but e are a great number; the land is given to us for our heritage.

For this cause say to them, This is hat the Lord has said: You take your meat ith the blood, your eyes are lifted up to your images, and you are takers of life: are you to have the land for your heritage?
You put your faith in your sords, you do disgusting things, everyone takes his neighbour’s ife: are you to have the land for your heritage?

This is hat you are to say to them: The Lord has said, By my life, truly, those ho are in the aste places ill be put to the sord, and him ho is in the open field I ill give to the beasts for their food, and those ho are in the strong places and in holes in the rocks ill come to their death by disease.
And I ill make the land a aste and a cause of onder, and the pride of her strength ill come to an end; and the mountains of Israel ill be made aste so that no one ill go through.
Then they ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen I have made the land a aste and a cause of onder, because of all the disgusting things hich they have done,

And as for you, son of man, the children of your people are talking together about you by the alls and in the doorays of the houses, saying to one another, Come no, give ear to the ord hich comes from the Lord.
And they come to you as my people come, and are seated before you as my people, hearing your ords but doing them not: for deceit is in their mouth and their heart goes after profit for themselves.
And truly you are to them like a love song by one ho has a very pleasing voice and is an expert player on an instrument: for they give ear to your ords but do them not.
And hen this comes about ( see, it is coming), then it ill be clear to them that a prophet has been among them.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

Son of man, be a prophet against the keepers of the flock of Israel, and say to them, O keepers of the sheep! this is the ord of the Lord: A curse is on the keepers of the flock of Israel ho take the food for themselves! is it not right for the keepers to give the food to the sheep?
You take the milk and are clothed ith the ool, you put the fat beasts to death, but you give the sheep no food.

You have not made the diseased ones strong or made ell that hich as ill; you have not put bands on the broken or got back that hich had been sent aay or made search for the andering ones; and the strong you have been ruling cruelly.
And they ere andering in every direction because there as no keeper: and they became food for all the beasts of the field.

And my sheep ent out of the ay, andering through all the mountains and on every high hill: my sheep ent here and there over all the face of the earth; and no one as troubled about them or ent in search of them.
For this cause, O keepers of the flock, give ear to the ord of the Lord:

By my life, says the Lord, truly, because my sheep have been taken aay, and my sheep became food for all the beasts of the field, because there as no keeper, and my keepers did not go in search of the sheep, but the keepers took food for themselves and gave my sheep no food;
For this reason, O you keepers of the flock, give ear to the ord of the Lord;
