This is hat the Lord has said: See I am against the keepers of the flock, and I ill make search and see hat they have done ith my sheep, and ill let them be keepers of my sheep no longer; and the keepers ill no longer get food for themselves; I ill take my sheep out of their mouths so that they may not be food for them.
For this is hat the Lord has said: Truly, I, even I, ill go searching and looking for my sheep.

As the keeper goes looking for his flock hen he is among his andering sheep, so I ill go looking for my sheep, and ill get them safely out of all the places here they have been sent andering in the day of clouds and black night.

And I ill take them out from among the peoples, and get them together from the countries, and ill take them into their land; and I ill give them food on the mountains of Israel by the ater-streams and herever men are living in the country.

I ill give them good grass-land for their food, and their safe place ill be the mountains of the high place of Israel: there they ill take their rest in a good place, and on fat grass-land they ill take their food on the mountains of Israel.
I myself ill give food to my flock, and I ill give them rest, says the Lord.

I ill go in search of that hich had gone andering from the ay, and ill get back that hich had been sent in flight, and ill put bands on that hich as broken, and give strength to that hich as ill: but the fat and the strong I ill give up to destruction; I ill give them for their food the punishment hich is theirs by right.
And as for you, O my flock, says the Lord, truly, I ill be judge beteen sheep and sheep, the he-sheep and the he-goats.

Does it seem a small thing to you to have taken your food on good grass-land hile the rest of your grass-land is stamped don under your feet? and that after drinking from clear aters you make the rest of the aters dirty ith your feet?
And as for my sheep, their food is the grass hich has been stamped on by your feet, and their drink the ater hich has been made dirty by your feet.
For this reason the Lord has said to them, Truly, I, even I, ill be judge beteen the fat sheep and the thin sheep.
Because you have been pushing ith side and leg, pushing the diseased ith your horns till they ere sent aay in every direction;
I ill make my flock safe, and they ill no longer be taken aay, and I ill be judge beteen sheep and sheep.
And I ill put over them one keeper, and he ill give them food, even my servant David; he ill give them food and be their keeper.
And I the Lord ill be their God and my servant David their ruler; I the Lord have said it.
And I ill make ith them an agreement of peace, and ill put an end to evil beasts through all the land: and they ill be living safely in the aste land, sleeping in the oods.
And I ill give the rain at the right time, and I ill make the shoer come don at the right time; there ill be shoers of blessing.

And the tree of the field ill give its fruit and the earth ill give its increase, and they ill be safe in their land; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord, hen I have had their yoke broken and have given them salvation from the hands of those ho made them servants.
And their goods ill no longer be taken by the nations, and they ill not again be food for the beasts of the earth; but they ill be living safely and no one ill be a cause of fear to them.
And I ill give them planting-places of peace, and they ill no longer be asted from need of food or put to shame by the nations.
And they ill be certain that I the Lord their God am ith them, and that they, the children of Israel, are my people, says the Lord.
And you are my sheep, the sheep of my grass-lands, and I am your God, says the Lord.
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, let your face be turned to Mount Seir, and be a prophet against it,
And say to it, This is hat the Lord has said: See, I am against you, O Mount Seir, and my hand ill be stretched out against you, and I ill make you a aste and a cause for onder.
I ill make your tons unpeopled and you ill be a aste; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
Because yours has been a hate ithout end, and you have given up the children of Israel to the poer of the sord in the time of their trouble, in the time of the punishment of the end:
For this cause, by my life, says the Lord, because you have been sinning through blood, blood ill come after you.
And I ill make Mount Seir a cause for onder and a aste, cutting off from it all comings and goings.
I ill make his mountains full of those ho have been put to death; in your valleys and in all your ater-streams men ill be falling by the sord.
I ill make you aste for ever, and your tons ill be unpeopled: and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
Because you have said, The to nations and the to countries are to be mine, and e ill take them for our heritage; though the Lord as there:

For this cause, by my life, says the Lord, I ill do to you as you have done in your rath and in your envy, hich you have made clear in your hate for them; and I ill make clear to you ho I am hen you are judged by me.

And you ill see that I the Lord have had knoledge of all the bitter things hich you have said against the mountains of Israel, saying, They have been made aste, they are given to us to take for our heritage.
And you have made yourselves great against me ith your mouths, increasing your ords against me; and it has come to my ears.
This is hat the Lord has said: Because you ere glad over my land hen it as a aste, so ill I do to you:
You ill become a aste, O Mount Seir, and all Edom, even all of it: and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
And you, son of man, be a prophet about the mountains of Israel, and say, You mountains of Israel, give ear to the ord of the Lord:
This is hat the Lord has said: Because your hater has said against you, Aha! and, The old aste places are our heritage, e have taken them:

For this cause be a prophet, and say, This is hat the Lord has said: Because, even because they have been glad over you and put you to shame on every side, because you have become a heritage for the rest of the nations, and you are taken up on the lips of talkers and in the evil talk of the people:

For this reason, you mountains of Israel, give ear to the ord of the Lord; this is hat the Lord has said to the mountains and to the hills, to the streams and to the valleys, to the unpeopled astes and to the tons here no one is living, from hich the goods have been taken and hich have been put to shame by the rest of the nations ho are round about:

For this cause the Lord has said: Truly, in the heat of my bitter feeling I have said things against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, ho have taken my land as a heritage for themselves ith the joy of all their heart, and ith bitter envy of soul have made attacks on it:

For this cause be a prophet about the land of Israel, and say to the mountains and to the hills, to the streams and to the valleys, This is hat the Lord has said: Truly, in my bitter feeling and in my rath I have said these things, because you have undergone the shame of the nations:
For this cause the Lord has said, See, I have taken an oath that the nations hich are round about you are themselves to undergo the shame hich they have put on you.
But you, O mountains of Israel, ill put out your branches and give your fruit to my people Israel; for they are ready to come.
For truly I am for you, and I ill be turned to you, and you ill be ploughed and planted:
And I ill let your numbers be increased, all the children of Israel, even all of them: and the tons ill be peopled and the aste places ill have buildings;

Man and beast ill be increased in you, and they ill have offspring and be fertile: I ill make you thickly peopled as you ere before, and ill do more for you than at the first: and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
Yes, I ill have you alked on by the feet of men, even my people Israel; they ill have you for a heritage and you ill be theirs, and never again ill you take their children from them.
This is hat the Lord has said: Because they say to you, You, O land, are the destruction of men, causing loss of children to your nation;
For this reason you ill no longer take the lives of men and ill never again be the cause of loss of children to your nation, says the Lord.
And I ill not let the shaming of the nations come to your ears, and no longer ill you be looked don on by the peoples, says the Lord.
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, hen the children of Israel ere living in their land, they made it unclean by their ay and their acts: their ay before me as as hen a oman is unclean at the time hen she is kept separate.
So I let loose my rath on them because of those hom they had violently put to death in the land, and because they had made it unclean ith their images:
And I sent them in flight among the nations and andering through the countries: I as their judge, rearding them for their ay and their acts.
And hen they came among the nations, herever they ent, they made my holy name unclean, hen it as said of them, These are the people of the Lord ho have gone out from his land.
But I had pity for my holy name hich the children of Israel had made unclean herever they ent.

For this cause say to the children of Israel, This is hat the Lord has said: I am doing this, not because of you, O children of Israel, but because of my holy name, hich you have made unclean among the nations herever you ent.

And I ill make holy my great name hich has been made unclean among the nations, hich you have made unclean among them; and it ill be clear to the nations that I am the Lord, says the Lord, hen I make myself holy in you before their eyes.
For I ill take you out from among the nations, and get you together from all the countries, and take you into your land.
And I ill put clean ater on you so that you may be clean: from all your unclean ays and from all your images I ill make you clean.
And I ill give you a ne heart and put a ne spirit in you: I ill take aay the heart of stone from your flesh, and give you a heart of flesh.
And I ill put my spirit in you, causing you to be guided by my rules, and you ill keep my orders and do them.
So that you may go on living in the land hich I gave to your fathers; and you ill be to me a people, and I ill be to you a God.
And I ill make you free from all your unclean ays: and at my voice the grain ill come up and be increased, and I ill not let you be short of food.
And I ill make the tree give more fruit and the field fuller produce, and no longer ill you be shamed among the nations for need of food.
And at the memory of your evil ays and your rongdoings, you ill have bitter hate for yourselves because of your evil-doings and your disgusting ays, O children of Israel.
Not because of you am I doing it, says the Lord; let it be clear to you, and be shamed and made lo because of your ays, O children of Israel.
This is hat the Lord has said: In the day hen I make you clean from all your evil-doings I ill let the tons be peopled and there ill be building on the aste places.
And the land hich as aste ill be farmed, in place of being a aste in the eyes of everyone ho ent by.
And they ill say, This land hich as aste has become like the garden of Eden; and the tons hich ere unpeopled and asted and pulled don are alled and peopled.

Then the rest of the nations round about you ill be certain that I the Lord am the builder of the places hich ere pulled don and the planter of that hich as aste: I the Lord have said it, and I ill do it.
This is hat the Lord has said: The children of Israel ill again make prayer to me for this, that I may do it for them; I ill make them increased ith men like a flock.
Like sheep for the offerings, like the sheep of Jerusalem at her fixed feasts, so the unpeopled tons ill be made full of men: and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
The hand of the Lord had been on me, and he took me out in the spirit of the Lord and put me don in the middle of the valley; and it as full of bones;
And he made me go past them round about: and I sa that there as a very great number of them on the face of the ide valley, and they ere very dry.
And he said to me, Son of man, is it possible for these bones to come to life? And I made anser, and said, It is for you to say, O Lord.
And again he said to me, Be a prophet to these bones, and say to them, O you dry bones, give ear to the ord of the Lord.
This is hat the Lord has said to these bones: See, I ill make breath come into you so that you may come to life;
And I ill put muscles on you and make flesh come on you, and put skin over you, and breath into you, so that you may have life; and you ill be certain that I am the Lord.
So I gave the ord as I as ordered: and at my ords there as a shaking of the earth, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
And looking I sa that there ere muscles on them and flesh came up, and they ere covered ith skin: but there as no breath in them.
And he said to me, Be a prophet to the ind, be a prophet, son of man, and say to the ind, The Lord has said: Come from the four inds, O ind, breathing on these dead so that they may come to life.
And I gave the ord at his orders, and breath came into them, and they came to life and got up on their feet, a very great army.
Then he said to me, Son of man, these bones are all the children of Israel: and see, they are saying, Our bones have become dry our hope is gone, e are cut off completely.

For this cause be a prophet to them, and say, This is hat the Lord has said: See, I am opening the resting-places of your dead, and I ill make you come up out of your resting-places, O my people; and I ill take you into the land of Israel.
And you ill be certain that I am the Lord by my opening the resting-places of your dead and making you come up out of your resting-places, O my people.
And I ill put my spirit in you, so that you may come to life, and I ill give you a rest in your land: and you ill be certain that I the Lord have said it and have done it, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,

And you, son of man, take one stick, riting on it, For Judah and for the children of Israel ho are in his company: then take another stick, riting on it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all the children of Israel ho are in his company:
Then, joining them one to another, make them one stick, so that they may be one in your hand.
And hen the children of your people say to you, Will you not make clear to us hat these things have to do ith us?

Then say to them, This is hat the Lord has said: See, I am taking the stick of Joseph, hich is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel ho are in his company; and I ill put it on the stick of Judah and make them one stick, and they ill be one in my hand.
And the sticks ith your riting on them ill be in your hand before their eyes.

And say to them, These are the ords of the Lord: See, I am taking the children of Israel from among the nations here they have gone, and ill get them together on every side, and take them into their land:
And I ill make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel; and one king ill be king over them all: and they ill no longer be to nations, and ill no longer be parted into to kingdoms:

And they ill no longer make themselves unclean ith their images or ith their hated things or ith any of their sins: but I ill give them salvation from all their turning aay in hich they have done evil, and ill make them clean; and they ill be to me a people, and I ill be to them a God.
And my servant David ill be king over them; and they ill all have one keeper: and they ill be guided by my orders and ill keep my rules and do them.

And they ill be living in the land hich I gave to Jacob, my servant, in hich your fathers ere living; and they ill go on living there, they and their children and their children’s children, for ever: and David, my servant, ill be their ruler for ever.
And I ill make an agreement of peace ith them: it ill be an eternal agreement ith them: and I ill have mercy on them and make their numbers great, and ill put my holy place among them for ever.
And my House ill be over them; and I ill be to them a God, and they ill be to me a people.
And the nations ill be certain that I ho make Israel holy am the Lord, hen my holy place is among them for ever.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Son of man, let your face be turned against Gog, of the land of Magog, the ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal, and be a prophet against him,
And say, This is hat the Lord has said: See, I am against you, O Gog, ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal:

And turning you round, I ill put hooks in your mouth and make you come out ith all your army, horses and horsemen, all of them in full ar-dress, a great force ith breastplate and body-cover, all of them armed ith sords:
Persia, Cush, and Put ith them; all of them ith body-cover and metal head-dress:
Gomer and all her forces; the people of Togarmah in the inmost parts of the north, ith all his forces: a great number of peoples ith you.
Be ready, make yourself ready, you and all the forces ho are ith you, and be ready for my orders.

After a long time you ill get your orders: in the last years you ill come into the land hich has been given back from the sord, hich has been got together out of a great number of peoples, on the mountains of Israel hich have ever been a aste: but it has been taken out from the peoples and they ill be living, all of them, ithout fear of danger.
And you ill go up, you ill come like a storm, you ill be like a cloud covering the land, you and all your forces, and a great number of peoples ith you.
This is hat the Lord has said: In that day it ill come about that things ill come into your mind, and you ill have thoughts of an evil design:
And you ill say, I ill go up to the land of small unalled tons; I ill go to those ho are quiet, living, all of them, ithout fear of danger, ithout alls or locks or doors:

To take their property by force and go off ith their goods; turning your hand against the aste places hich no are peopled, and against the people ho have been got together out of the nations, ho have got cattle and goods for themselves, ho are living in the middle of the earth.

Sheba, and Dedan and her traders, Tarshish ith all her traders, ill say to you, Have you come to take our goods? have you got your armies together to take aay our property by force? to take aay silver and gold, cattle and goods, to go off ith great ealth?
For this cause, son of man, be a prophet and say to Gog, These are the ords of the Lord: In that day, hen my people Israel are living ithout fear of danger, ill you not be moved against them?
And you ill come from your place in the inmost parts of the north, you and a great number of peoples ith you, all of them on horseback, a great force and a strong army:

And you ill come up against my people Israel, like a cloud covering the land; and it ill come about, in the last days, that I ill make you come against my land, so that the nations may have knoledge of me hen I make myself holy in you, O Gog, before their eyes.

This is hat the Lord has said: You are he of hom I gave them ord in earlier times by my servants, the prophets of Israel, ho in those days ent on saying, year after year, that I ould make you come up against them.
And it ill come about in that day, hen Gog comes up against the land of Israel, says the Lord, that my rath ill come up, and my passion and my bitter feeling.
For in the fire of my rath I have said, Truly, in that day there ill be a great shaking in the land of Israel;

So that the fish of the sea and the birds of heaven and the beasts of the field and everything moving on the earth, and all the men ho are on the face of the earth, ill be shaking before me, and the mountains ill be overturned and the high places ill come don, and every all ill come falling don to the earth.
And I ill send to all my mountains for a sord against him, says the Lord: every man’s sord ill be against his brother.

And I ill take up my cause against him ith disease and ith blood; and I ill send don on him and on his forces and on the peoples ho are ith him, an overfloing shoer and great ice-drops, fire, and burning.
And I ill make my name great and make myself holy, and I ill make myself clear to a number of nations; and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
And you, son of man, be a prophet against Gog, and say, These are the ords of the Lord: See, I am against you, O Gog, ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal:
And turning you round, I ill be your guide, and make you come up from the inmost parts of the north; I ill make you come on to the mountains of Israel:
And ith a blo I ill send your bo out of your left hand and your arros falling from your right hand.
On the mountains of Israel you ill come don, you and all your forces and the peoples ho are ith you: I ill give you to cruel birds of every sort and to the beasts of the field to be their food.
You ill come don in the open field: for I have said it, says the Lord.
And I ill send a fire on Magog, and on those ho are living in the sea-lands ithout fear: and they ill be certain that I am the Lord.
And I ill make clear my holy name among my people Israel; I ill no longer let my holy name be made unclean: and the nations ill be certain that I am the Lord, the Holy One in Israel.
See, it is coming and it ill be done, says the Lord; this is the day of hich I have given ord.

And those ho are living in the tons of Israel ill go out and make fires of the instruments of ar, burning the body-covers and the breastplates, the bos and the arros and the sticks and the spears, and for seven years they ill make fires of them:

And they ill take no ood out of the field or have any cut don in the oods; for they ill make their fires of the instruments of ar: and they ill take by force the property of those ho took their property, and go off ith the goods of those ho took their goods, says the Lord.

And it ill come about in those days, that I ill give to Gog a last resting-place there in Israel, in the valley of Abarim on the east of the sea: and those ho go through ill be stopped: and there Gog and all his people ill be put to rest, and the place ill be named, The valley of Hamon-gog.
And the children of Israel ill be seven months putting them in the earth, so as to make the land clean.
And all the people of the land ill put them in the earth; and it ill be to their honour in the day hen I let my glory be seen, says the Lord.

And they ill put on one side men to do no other ork but to go through the land and put in the earth the rest of those ho are still on the face of the land, to make it clean: after seven months are ended they are to make a search.
And hile they go through the land, if anyone sees a man’s bone, he is to put up a sign by the place till those ho are doing the ork have put it in the earth in the valley of Hamon-gog.
And there they ill put all the army of Gog in the earth. So they ill make the land clean.

And you, son of man, this is hat the Lord has said: Say to the birds of every sort and to all the beasts of the field, Get together and come; come together on every side to the offering hich I am putting to death for you, a great offering on the mountains of Israel, so that you may have flesh for your food and blood for your drink.
The flesh of the men of ar ill be your food, and your drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of sheep and lambs, of he-goats, of oxen, all of them fat beasts of Bashan.
You ill go on feasting on the fat till you are full, and drinking the blood till you are overcome ith it, of my offering hich I have put to death for you.
At my table you ill have food in full measure, horses and ar-carriages, great men and all the men of ar, says the Lord.
And I ill put my glory among the nations, and all the nations ill see my punishments hich I have put into effect, and my hand hich I have put on them.
So the children of Israel ill be certain that I am the Lord their God, from that day and for the future.

And it ill be clear to the nations that the children of Israel ere taken aay prisoners for their evil-doing; because they did rong against me, and my face as covered from them: so I gave them up into the hands of their attackers, and they all came to their end by the sord.
In the measure of their unclean ays and their sins, so I did to them; and I kept my face covered from them.
For this cause the Lord has said, No I ill let the fate of Jacob be changed, and I ill have mercy on all the children of Israel, and ill take care of the honour of my holy name.
And they ill be conscious of their shame and of all the rong hich they have done against me, hen they are living in their land ith no sense of danger and ith no one to be a cause of fear to them;
When I have taken them back from among the peoples and got them together out of the lands of their haters, and have made myself holy in them before the eyes of a great number of nations.

And they ill be certain that I am the Lord their God, because I sent them aay as prisoners among the nations, and have taken them together back to their land; and I have not let one of them be there any longer.
And my face ill no longer be covered from them: for I have sent the out-floing of my spirit on the children of Israel, says the Lord.

In the tenty-fifth year after e had been taken aay prisoners, in the first month of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the ton as taken, on the very same day, the hand of the Lord as on me, and he took me there.
In the visions of God he took me into the land of Israel, and put me don on a very high mountain, on hich there as, as it seemed, a building like a ton opposite me.
He took me there, and I sa a man, looking like brass, ith a linen cord in his hand and a measuring rod: and he as stationed in the dooray.

And the man said to me, Son of man, see ith your eyes and give hearing ith your ears, and take to heart everything I am going to let you see; for in order that I might let you see them, you have come here: and give an account of all you see to the children of Israel.

And there as a all on the outside of the house all round, and in the man’s hand there as a measuring rod six cubits long by a cubit and a hand’s measure: so he took the measure of the building from side to side, one rod; and from base to top, one rod.
Then he came to the dooray looking to the east, and ent up by its steps; and he took the measure of the doorstep, one rod ide.
And the atchmen’s rooms ere one rod long and one rod ide; and the space beteen the rooms as five cubits; the doorstep of the dooray, by the covered ay of the dooray inside, as one rod.
And he took the measure of the covered ay of the dooray inside,
Eight cubits; and its uprights, to cubits; the covered ay of the dooray as inside.
And the rooms of the dooray on the east ere three on this side and three on that; all three ere of the same size; and the uprights on this side and on that ere of the same size.
And he took the measure of the opening of the dooray, ten cubits ide; and the ay don the dooray as thirteen cubits;
And the space in front of the rooms, a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side; and the rooms six cubits on this side and six cubits on that.
And he took the measure of the dooray from the back of one room to the back of the other, tenty-five cubits across, from door to door.
And he took the measure of the covered ay, tenty cubits; and opening from the covered ay of the dooray as the open square round about.
And from before the opening of the dooray to before the inner covered ay of the dooray as fifty cubits.
And the rooms and their uprights had sloping indos inside the dooray all round, and in the same ay the covered ay had indos all round on the inside: and on every upright there ere palm-trees.
Then he took me into the outer square, and there ere rooms and a stone floor made for the open square all round: there ere thirty rooms on the stone floor.
And the stone floor as by the side of the doorays, and as as ide as the doorays ere long, even the loer floor.
Then he took the measure of the square across, from before the loer dooray inside to before the inner dooray outside, one hundred cubits. And he took me in the direction of the north,
And there as a dooray to the outer square, looking to the north; and he took the measure of it to see ho ide and ho long it as.
And it had three rooms on this side of it and three on that; its uprights and its covered ays ere the same size as those of the first dooray: it as fifty cubits long and tenty-five cubits ide.
And its indos, and the indos of its covered ays, and its palm-trees, ere the same as those of the dooray looking to the east; and there ere seven steps up to it; and the covered ay ent inside.
And there as a dooray to the inner square opposite the dooray on the north, like the dooray on the east; and he took the measure from dooray to dooray, a hundred cubits.
And he took me to the south, and I sa a dooray looking to the south: and he took the measure of its rooms and its uprights and its covered ays by these measures.
And there ere indos in it and in the covered ay all round, like the other indos: it as fifty cubits long and tenty-five cubits ide.
And there ere seven steps up to it, and its covered ay ent inside: and it had palm-trees, one on this side and one on that, on its uprights.
And there as a dooray to the inner square looking to the south: he took the measure from dooray to dooray to the south, a hundred cubits.
Then he took me to the inner square by the south dooray: and he took the measure of the south dooray by these measures;
And the rooms in it and the uprights and the covered ays, by these measures:
And there ere indos in it and in the covered ay all round: it as fifty cubits long and tenty-five cubits ide.
The covered ay as on the side nearest the outer square; and there ere palm-trees on the uprights: and there ere eight steps going up to it.
And he took me into the inner square facing the east: and he took the measure of the dooray by these measures;
And of the rooms in it and its uprights and its covered ays, by these measures: and there ere indos in it and in the covered ay round about: it as fifty cubits long and tenty-five cubits ide.
And the covered ay as on the side nearest the outer square; there ere palm-trees on the uprights, on this side and on that: and there ere eight steps going up to it.
And he took me to the north dooray: and he took the measure of it by these measures;
Its rooms, its uprights, and its covered ay had the same measures, and its covered ay had indos all round: it as fifty cubits long and tenty-five cubits ide.
Its uprights ere on the side nearest to the outer square; there ere palm-trees on the uprights, on this side and on that: and there ere eight steps going up to it.
And there as a room ith a door in the covered ay of the dooray, here the burned offering as ashed.
And in the covered ay of the dooray there ere to tables on this side and to tables on that side, on hich the burned offering and the sin-offering and the offering for error ere put to death:
On the outer side, to the north, as one goes up to the opening of the dooray, ere to tables.
There ere four tables on one side and four tables on the other, by the side of the dooray; eight tables, on hich they put to death the beasts for the offerings.

And there ere four tables for the burned offering, made of cut stone, one and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits ide and a cubit high, here the instruments ere placed hich ere used for putting to death the burned offering and the beasts for the offerings.
And they had edges all round as ide as a man’s hand: and on the tables as the flesh of the offerings.
And he took me into the inner square, and there ere to rooms in the inner square, one at the side of the north dooray, facing south; and one at the side of the south dooray, facing north.
And he said to me, This room, facing south, is for the priests ho have the care of the house.
And the room facing north is for the priests ho have the care of the altar: these are the sons of Zadok, ho, from among the sons of Levi, come near to the Lord to do the ork of his house.
And he took the measure of the open square, a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits ide, being square; and the altar as in front of the house.

Then he took me to the covered ay before the house, and took the measure of its uprights, five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other: and the dooray as fourteen cubits ide; and the side-alls of the dooray ere three cubits on one side and three cubits on the other.
The covered ay as tenty cubits long and telve cubits ide, and they ent up to it by ten steps; and there ere pillars by the uprights, one on one side and one on the other.
And he took me to the Temple, and took the measure of the uprights, six cubits ide on one side and six cubits ide on the other.
And the door-opening as ten cubits ide; and the side alls of the door-opening ere five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other: and it as forty cubits long and tenty cubits ide.

And he ent inside and took the measure of the uprights of the door-opening, to cubits: and the door-opening, six cubits; and the side-alls of the door-opening ere seven cubits on one side and seven cubits on the other.
And by his measure it as tenty cubits long and tenty cubits ide in front of the Temple: and he said to me, This is the most holy place.
Then he took the measure of the all of the house, hich as six cubits; and of the side-rooms round the house, hich ere four cubits ide.
And the side-rooms, room over room, ere three times thirty; there ere inlets in the all of the house for the side-rooms round about, for supports in the all of the house.

The side-rooms became ider as they ent higher up the house, by the amount of the space let into the all up round about the house, because of the inlets in the house; and one ent up from the loest floor by steps to the middle, and from the middle to the upper floor.
And I sa that the house had a stone floor all round; the bases of the side-rooms ere a full rod of six great cubits high.
The all supporting the side-rooms on the outside as five cubits thick: and there as a free space of five cubits beteen the side-rooms of the house.
And beteen the rooms as a space tenty cubits ide all round the house.
And the free space had doors opening from the side-rooms, one door on the north and one door on the south: and the free space as five cubits ide all round.
And the building hich as in front of the separate place at the side to the est as seventy cubits ide; the all of the building as five cubits thick all round and ninety cubits long.
And he took the measure of the house; it as a hundred cubits long; and the separate place and the building ith its alls as a hundred cubits long;
And the east front of the house and of the separate place as a hundred cubits ide.

And he took the measure of the building in front of the separate place hich as at the back of it, and the pillared alks on one side and on the other side; they ere a hundred cubits long; and the Temple and the inner part and its outer covered ay ere covered in;
And the sloping indos and the covered ays round all three of them ere of shakiph-ood all round from the level of the earth up to the indos;
And there as a roof over the dooray and as far as the inner house, and to the outside and on the all all round, inside and outside.
And it had pictured forms of inged beings and palm-trees; a palm-tree beteen to inged ones, and every inged one had to faces;
So that there as the face of a man turned to the palm-tree on one side, and the face of a young lion on the other side: so it as made all round the house.
From earth level up to the indos there ere inged ones and palm-trees pictured on the all.
The altar as made of ood, and as three cubits high and to cubits long; it had angles, and its base and sides ere of ood; and he said to me, This is the table hich is before the Lord.
The Temple had to doors.
And the holy place had to doors, and the doors had to turning leaves, to for one and to for the other.
And on them ere pictured inged ones and palm-trees, as on the alls; and a ... of ood as on the front of the covered ay outside.
And there ere sloping indos and palm-trees on one side and on the other, on the sides of the covered ay: and the side-rooms of the house and the ...
And he took me out into the inner square in the direction of the north: and he took me into the rooms hich ere opposite the separate place and opposite the building to the north.
On the north side it as a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits ide,
Opposite the space of tenty cubits hich as part of the inner square, and opposite the stone floor of the outer square. There ere covered ays facing one another on the third floor.
And in front of the rooms as a alk, ten cubits ide and a hundred cubits long; and their doors ere facing north.
And the higher rooms ere shorter: for the covered ays took up more space from these than from the loer and middle rooms.
For they ere on three floors, and they had no pillars like the pillars of the outer square; so the highest as narroer than the loest and middle floors from the earth level.
And the all hich ent outside by the side of the rooms, in the direction of the outer square in front of the rooms, as fifty cubits long.
For the rooms in the outer square ere fifty cubits long: and in front of the Temple as a space of a hundred cubits.
And under these rooms as the ay in from the east side, as one goes into them from the outer square at the head of the outer all.
( And he took me) to the south, and in front of the separate place and in front of the building there ere rooms.
And there as a alk in front of them like that by the rooms on the north; they ere equally long and ide; and the ays out of them ere the same in design and had the same sort of doors.
And under the rooms on the south as a door at the head of the outer all in the direction of the east as one goes in.

And he said to me, The north rooms and the south rooms in front of the separate place are the holy rooms, here the priests ho come near the Lord take the most holy things for their food: there the most holy things are placed, ith the meal offering and the sin-offering and the offering for error; for the place is holy.

When the priests go in, they may not go out of the holy place into the outer square, and there they are to put the robes in hich they do the ork of the Lord’s house, for they are holy: and they have to put on other clothing before they come near that hich has to do ith the people.
And hen he had come to the end of measuring the inner house, he took me out to the dooray looking to the east, and took its measure all round.
He ent round and took the measure of it on the east side ith the measuring rod, five hundred, measured ith the rod all round.
And he ent round and took the measure of it on the north side ith the measuring rod, five hundred, measured ith the rod all round.
And he ent round and took the measure of it on the south side ith the measuring rod, five hundred, measured ith the rod all round.
And he ent round and took the measure of it on the est side ith the measuring rod, five hundred, measured ith the rod all round.
He took its measure on the four sides: and it had a all all round, five hundred long and five hundred ide, separating hat as holy from hat as common.
And he took me to the dooray looking to the east:
And there as the glory of the God of Israel coming from the ay of the east: and his voice as like the sound of great aters, and the earth as shining ith his glory.
And the vision hich I sa as like the vision I had seen hen he came for the destruction of the ton: and like the vision hich I sa by the river Chebar; and I ent don on my face.
And the glory of the Lord came into the house by the ay of the dooray looking to the east.
And the spirit, lifting me up, took me into the inner square; and I sa that the house as full of the glory of the Lord.
And the voice of one talking to me came to my ears from inside the house; and the man as by my side.

And he said to me, Son of man, this is the place here the seat of my poer is and the resting-place of my feet, here I ill be among the children of Israel for ever: and no longer ill the people of Israel make my holy name unclean, they or their kings, by their loose ays and by the dead bodies of their kings;

By putting their doorstep by my doorstep, and the pillar of their door by the pillar of my door, ith only a all beteen me and them; and they have made my holy name unclean by the disgusting things hich they have done: so in my rath I sent destruction on them.
No let them put their loose ays and the dead bodies of their kings far from me, and I ill be among them for ever.
You, son of man, give the children of Israel an account of this house, so that they may be shamed because of their evil-doing: and let them see the vision of it and its image.

And they ill be shamed by hat they have done; so give them the knoledge of the form of the house and its structure, and the ays out of it and into it, and all its las and its rules, riting it don for them: so that they may keep all its las and do them.
This is the la of the house: On the top of the mountain all the space round it on every side ill be most holy. See, this is the la of the house.

And these are the measures of the altar in cubits: ( the cubit being a cubit and a hand’s measure;) its hollo base is a cubit high and a cubit ide, and it has an overhanging edge as ide as a hand-stretch all round it:
And from the base on the earth level to the loer shelf, the altar is to cubits high and a cubit ide; and from the smaller shelf to the greater shelf it is four cubits high and a cubit ide.
And the fireplace is four cubits high: and coming up from the fireplace are the horns, a cubit high.
And the fireplace is telve cubits long and telve cubits ide, square on its four sides.
And the shelf is fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits ide, on its four sides; the edge round it is half a cubit; the base of it is a cubit all round, and its steps are facing the east.
And he said to me, Son of man, the Lord God has said, These are the rules for the altar, hen they make it, for the offering of burned offerings on it and the draining out of the blood.
You are to give to the priests, the Levites of the seed of Zadok, ho come near to me, says the Lord God, to do my ork, a young ox for a sin-offering.
You are to take some of its blood and put it on the four horns and on the four angles of the shelf and on the edge all round: and you are to make it clean and free from sin.
And you are to take the ox of the sin-offering, and have it burned in the special place ordered for it in the house, outside the holy place.
And on the second day you are to have a he-goat ithout any mark on it offered for a sin-offering; and they are to make the altar clean as they did ith the young ox.
And after you have made it clean, let a young ox ithout a mark be offered, and a male sheep from the flock ithout a mark.
And you are to take them before the Lord, and the priests ill put salt on them, offering them up for a burned offering to the Lord.
Every day for seven days you are to give a goat for a sin-offering: and let them give in addition a young ox and a male sheep from the flock ithout any mark on them.
For seven days they are to make offerings to take aay sin from the altar and to make it clean; so they are to make it holy.

And hen these days have come to an end, then on the eighth day and after, the priests ill make your burned offerings on the altar and your peace-offerings; and I ill take pleasure in you, says the Lord.
And he took me back to the outer dooray of the holy place, looking to the east; and it as shut.
And the Lord said to me, This dooray is to be shut, it is not to be open, and no man is to go in by it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, has gone in by it; and it is to be shut.
But the ruler ill be seated there to take his food before the Lord; he ill go in by the covered ay to the door, and ill come out by the same ay.
And he took me to the north dooray in front of the house; and, looking, I sa that the house of the Lord as full of the glory of the Lord; and I ent don on my face.

And the Lord said to me, Son of man, take to heart, and let your eyes see and your ears be open to everything I say to you about all the rules of the house of the Lord and all its las; and take note of the ays into the house and all the ays out of the holy place.
And say to the uncontrolled children of Israel, This is hat the Lord has said: O you children of Israel, let it be enough for you, among the disgusting things hich you have done,

To have let men from strange lands, ithout circumcision of heart or flesh, come into my holy place, making my house unclean; and to have made the offering of my food, even the fat and the blood; and in addition to all your disgusting ays, you have let my agreement be broken.
And you have not taken care of my holy things; but you have put them as keepers to take care of my ork in my holy place.
For this cause the Lord has said, No man from a strange land, ithout circumcision of heart and flesh, of all those ho are living among the children of Israel, is to come into my holy place.
But as for the Levites, ho ent far from me, hen Israel ent out of the right ay, turning aay from me to go after their images; their punishment ill come on them.

But they may be caretakers in my holy place, and overseers at the doors of the house, doing the ork of the house: they ill put to death the burned offering and the beasts offered for the people, and they ill take their place before them as their servants.

Because they did this ork for them before their images, and became a cause of sin to the children of Israel; for this cause my hand has been lifted up against them, says the Lord, and their punishment ill be on them.

And they ill not come near me to do the ork of priests to me, or come near any of my holy things, or the things hich are most holy: but their shame ill be on them, and the punishment for the disgusting things hich they have done.
But I ill make them responsible for the care of the house and all its ork and everything hich is done in it.

But as for the priests, the sons of Zadok, ho took care of my holy place hen the children of Israel ere turned aay from me, they are to come near me to do my ork, they ill take their places before me, offering to me the fat and the blood, says the Lord;
They are to come into my holy place and they are to come near to my table, to do my ork and have the care of my house.

And hen they come in by the doorays of the inner square, they are to be clothed in linen robes; there is to be no ool on them hile they are doing my ork in the dooray of the inner square and inside the house.
They are to have linen head-dresses on their heads and linen trousers on their legs, and they are to have nothing round them to make their skin et ith heat.

And hen they go out into the outer square to the people, they are to take off the robes in hich they do the ork of priests, and put them aay in the holy rooms, and put on other clothing, so that the people may not be made holy by their robes.
They are not to have all the hair cut off their heads, and they are not to let their hair get long, but they are to have the ends of their hair cut.
The priests are not to take ine hen they go into the inner square.
And they are not to take as ives any ido or oman hose husband has put her aay: but they may take virgins of the seed of Israel, or a ido ho is the ido of a priest.
And they are to make clear to my people the division beteen hat is holy and hat is common, and to give them the knoledge of hat is clean and hat is unclean.
In any cause, they are to be in the position of judges, judging in harmony ith my decisions: they are to keep my las and my rules in all my fixed feasts; and they are to keep my Sabbaths holy.
They are not to come near any dead person so as to become unclean: but for a father or mother or son or daughter or brother or for a sister ho has no husband, they may make themselves unclean.
And after he has been made clean, seven days are to be numbered for him.
And on the day hen he goes into the inner square, to do the ork of the holy place, he is to make his sin-offering, says the Lord.
And they are to have no heritage; I am their heritage: you are to give them no property in Israel; I am their property.
Their food is to be the meal offering and the sin-offering and the offering for error; and everything given specially to the Lord in Israel ill be theirs.

And the best of all the first-fruits of everything, and every offering hich is lifted up of all your offerings, ill be for the priests: and you are to give the priest the first of your bread-making, so causing a blessing to come on your house.
The priests may not take for food any bird or beast hich has come to a natural death or hose death has been caused by another animal.

And hen you are making a distribution of the land, by the decision of the Lord, for your heritage, you are to make an offering to the Lord of a part of the land as holy: it is to be tenty-five thousand long and tenty thousand ide: all the land inside these limits is to be holy.
Of this, a square five hundred long and five hundred ide is to be for the holy place, ith a space of fifty cubits all round it.
And of this measure, let a space be measured, tenty-five thousand long and ten thousand ide: in it there ill be the holy place, even the most holy.
This holy part of the land is to be for the priests, the servants of the holy place, ho come near to the Lord to do his ork; it is to be a place for their houses and for grass-land and for cattle.
A space of land tenty-five thousand long and ten thousand ide is to be for the Levites, the servants of the house, a property for themselves, for tons for their living-places.

And as the property for the ton you are to have a part five thousand ide and tenty-five thousand long, by the side of the offering of the holy part of the land: this is to be for all the children of Israel.

And for the ruler there is to be a part on one side and on the other side of the holy offering and of the property of the ton, in front of the holy offering and in front of the property of the ton on the est of it and on the east: measured in the same line as one of the parts of the land, from its limit on the est to its limit on the east of the land.
And this ill be his heritage in Israel: and my rulers ill no longer be cruel masters to my people; but they ill give the land as a heritage to the children of Israel by their tribes.

This is hat the Lord has said: Let this be enough for you, O rulers of Israel: let there be an end of violent behaviour and asting; do hat is right, judging uprightly; let there be no more driving out of my people, says the Lord.
Have true scales and a true ephah and a true bath.
The ephah and the bath are to be of the same measure, so that the bath is equal to a tenth of a homer, and the ephah to a tenth of a homer: the unit of measure is to be a homer.
And the shekel is to be tenty gerahs: five shekels are five, and ten shekels are ten, and your maneh is to be fifty shekels
This is the offering you are to give: a sixth of an ephah out of a homer of heat, and a sixth of an ephah out of a homer of barley;
And the fixed measure of oil is to be a tenth of a bath from the cor, for ten baths make up the cor;
And one lamb from the flock out of every to hundred, from all the families of Israel, for a meal offering and for a burned offering and for peace-offerings, to take aay their sin, says the Lord.
All the people are to give this offering to the ruler.

And the ruler ill be responsible for the burned offering and the meal offering and the drink offering, at the feasts and the ne moons and the Sabbaths, at all the fixed feasts of the children of Israel: he ill give the sin-offering and meal offering and burned offering and the peace-offerings, to take aay the sin of the children of Israel.
This is hat the Lord has said: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you are to take a young ox ithout any mark on him, and you are to make the holy place clean.

And the priest is to take some of the blood of the sin-offering and put it on the uprights at the sides of the doors of the house, and on the four angles of the shelf of the altar, and on the sides of the dooray of the inner square.
And this you are to do on the seventh day of the month for everyone ho is in error and for the feeble-minded: you are to make the house free from sin.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you are to have the Passover, a feast of seven days; unleavened bread is to be your food.
And on that day the ruler is to give for himself and for all the people of the land an ox for a sin-offering.

And on the seven days of the feast he is to give a burned offering to the Lord, seven oxen and seven sheep ithout any mark on them, every day for seven days; and a he-goat every day for a sin-offering.
And he is to give a meal offering, an ephah for every ox and an ephah for every sheep and a hin of oil to every ephah.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the feast, he is to give the same for seven days; the sin-offering, the burned offering, the meal offering, and the oil as before.

This is hat the Lord has said: The dooray of the inner square looking to the east is to be shut on the six orking days; but on the Sabbath it is to be open, and at the time of the ne moon it is to be open.

And the ruler is to go in through the covered ay of the outer dooray outside, and take his place by the pillar of the dooray, and the priests ill make his burned offering and his peace-offerings and he ill give orship at the doorstep of the dooray; then he ill go out, and the door ill not be shut till the evening.
And the people of the land are to give orship at the door of that dooray before the Lord on the Sabbaths and at the ne moons.
And the burned offering offered to the Lord by the ruler on the Sabbath day is to be six lambs ithout a mark on them and a male sheep ithout a mark;
And the meal offering is to be an ephah for the sheep, and for the lambs hatever he is able to give, and a hin of oil to an ephah.
And at the time of the ne moon it is to be a young ox of the herd ithout a mark on him, and six lambs and a male sheep, all ithout a mark:
And he is to give a meal offering, an ephah for the ox and an ephah for the sheep, and for the lambs hatever he is able to give, and a hin of oil to an ephah.
And hen the ruler comes in, he is to go in through the covered ay of the dooray, and he is to go out by the same ay.

But hen the people of the land come before the Lord at the fixed feasts, he ho comes in by the north dooray to give orship is to go out by the south dooray; and he ho comes in by the south dooray is to go out by the north dooray: he is not to come back by the dooray through hich he ent in, but is to go straight before him.
And the ruler, hen they come in, is to come among them, and is to go out hen they go out.
At the feasts and the fixed meetings the meal offerings are to be an ephah for an ox, and an ephah for a male sheep, and for the lambs hatever he is able to give, and a hin of oil to an ephah.

And hen the ruler makes a free offering, a burned offering or a peace-offering freely given to the Lord, the dooray looking to the east is to be made open for him, and he is to make his burned offering and his peace-offerings as he does on the Sabbath day: and he ill go out; and the door ill be shut after he has gone out.
And you are to give a lamb a year old ithout any mark on it for a burned offering to the Lord every day: morning by morning you are to give it.

And you are to give, morning by morning, a meal offering ith it, a sixth of an ephah and a third of a hin of oil dropped on the best meal; a meal offering offered to the Lord at all times by an eternal order.
And they are to give the lamb and the meal offering and the oil, morning by morning, for a burned offering at all times.
This is hat the Lord has said: If the ruler gives a property to any of his sons, it is his heritage and ill be the property of his sons; it is theirs for their heritage.
And if he gives a part of his heritage to one of his servants, it ill be his till the year of making free, and then it ill go back to the ruler; for it is his sons’ heritage, and is to be theirs.

And the ruler is not to take the heritage of any of the people, driving them out of their property; he is to give a heritage to his sons out of the property hich is his: so that my people may not be sent aay from their property.
And he took me through by the ay in at the side of the dooray into the holy rooms hich are the priests’, looking to the north: and I sa a place at the side of them to the est.

And he said to me, This is the place here the offering for error and the sin-offering are to be cooked in ater by the priests, and here the meal offering is to be cooked in the oven; so that they may not be taken out into the outer square to make the people holy.
And he took me out into the outer square and made me go by the four angles of the square; and I sa that in every angle of the open square there as a space shut in.
In the four angles there ere spaces alled in, forty cubits long and thirty ide; the four ere of the same size.
And there as a line of all all round inside them, round all four, and boiling-places ere made under it all round about.
And he said to me, These are the boiling-rooms, here the offering of the people is cooked by the servants of the house.

And he took me back to the door of the house; and I sa that aters ere floing out from under the doorstep of the house on the east, for the house as facing east: and the aters came don from under, from the right side of the house, on the south side of the altar.
And he took me out by the north dooray, and made me go round to the outside of the dooray looking to the east; and I sa aters running sloly out on the south side.
And the man ent out to the east ith the line in his hand, and after measuring a thousand cubits, he made me go through the aters, hich came over my feet.
And again, measuring a thousand cubits, he made me go through the aters hich came up to my knees. Again, measuring a thousand, he made me go through the aters up to the middle of my body.
Again, after his measuring a thousand, it became a river hich it as not possible to go through: for the aters had become deep enough for simming, a river it as not possible to go through.
And he said to me, Son of man, have you seen this? Then he took me to the river’s edge.
And he took me back, and I sa at the edge of the river a very great number of trees on this side and on that.
And he said to me, These aters are floing out to the east part of the land and don into the Arabah; and they ill go to the sea, and the aters ill be made seet.

And it ill come about that every living and moving thing, herever their streams come, ill have life; and there ill be very much fish because these aters have come there and have been made seet: and everything herever the river comes ill have life.

And fishermen ill take up their places by it: from En-gedi as far as En-eglaim ill be a place for the stretching out of nets; the fish ill be of every sort, like the fish of the Great Sea, a very great number.
The et places and the pools ill not be made seet; they ill be given up to salt.

And by the edge of the river, on this side and on that, ill come up every tree used for food, hose leaves ill ever be green and its fruit ill not come to an end: it ill have ne fruit every month, because its aters come out from the holy place: the fruit ill be for food and the leaf ill make ell those ho are ill.
This is hat the Lord has said: These are the limits by hich you ill take up your heritage in the land among the telve tribes of Israel: Joseph is to have to parts.
And you are to make an equal division of it; as I gave my oath to your fathers to give it to you: for this land is to be your heritage.
And this is to be the limit of the land: on the north side, from the Great Sea, in the direction of Hethlon, as far as the ay into Hamath;
To Zedad, Berothah, Sibraim, hich is beteen the limit of Damascus and the limit of Hazar-hatticon, hich is on the limit of Hauran.
And this is the limit from the sea in the direction of Hazar-enon; and the limit of Damascus is to the north, and on the north is the limit of Hamath. This is the north side.
And the east side ill be from Hazar-enon, hich is beteen Hauran and Damascus; and beteen Gilead and the land of Israel the Jordan ill be the limit, to the east sea, to Tamar. This is the east side.
And the south side to the south ill be from Tamar as far as the aters of Meribath-kadesh, to the stream of Egypt, to the Great Sea. This is the south side, on the south.
And the est side ill be the Great Sea, from the limit on the south to a point opposite the ay into Hamath. This is the est side.
You ill make a division of the land among you, tribe by tribe.

And you are to make a distribution of it, by the decision of the Lord, for a heritage to you and to the men from other lands ho are living among you and ho have children in your land: they ill be the same to you as if they ere Israelites by birth, they ill have their heritage ith you among the tribes of Israel.
In hatever tribe the man from a strange land is living, there you are to give him his heritage, says the Lord.

No these are the names of the tribes: from the north end, from the est on the ay of Hethlon to the ay into Hamath, in the direction of Hazar-enon, ith the limit of Damascus to the north, by Hamath; and on the limit from the east side to the est side: Dan, one part.
And on the limit of Dan, from the east side to the est side: Asher, one part.
And on the limit of Asher, from the east side to the est side: Naphtali, one part.
And on the limit of Naphtali, from the east side to the est side: Manasseh, one part.
And on the limit of Manasseh, from the east side to the est side: Ephraim, one part.
And on the limit of Ephraim, from the east side to the est side: Reuben, one part.
And on the limit of Reuben, from the east side to the est side: Judah, one part.

And on the limit of Judah, from the east side to the est side, ill be the offering hich you are to make, tenty-five thousand ide, and as long as one of the parts, from the east side to the est side: and the holy place ill be in the middle of it.
The offering you ill give to the Lord is to be tenty-five thousand long and tenty-five thousand ide.

And for these, that is the priests, the holy offering is to be tenty-five thousand long to the north, ten thousand ide to the est, ten thousand ide to the east and tenty-five thousand long to the south; and the holy place of the Lord ill be in the middle of it.
For the priests ho have been made holy, those of the sons of Zadok ho kept the orders I gave them, ho did not go out of the right ay hen the children of Israel ent from the ay, as the Levites did,
Even for them ill be the offering from the offering of the land, a thing most holy, on the limit of the land given to the Levites.

And the Levites are to have a part of the land equal to the limit of the priests’, tenty-five thousand long and ten thousand ide, all of it together to be tenty-five thousand long and tenty thousand ide.
And they are not to let any of it go for a price, or give it in exchange; and the part of the land given to the Lord is not to go into other hands: for it is holy to the Lord.

And the other five thousand, measured from side to side, in front of the tenty-five thousand, is to be for common use, for the ton, for living in and for a free space: and the ton ill be in the middle of it.

And these ill be its measures: the north side, four thousand five hundred, and the south side, four thousand five hundred, and on the east side, four thousand five hundred, and on the est side, four thousand five hundred.
And the ton ill have a free space on the north of to hundred and fifty, on the south of to hundred and fifty, on the east of to hundred and fifty, and on the est of to hundred and fifty.
And the rest, in measure as long as the holy offering, ill be ten thousand to the east and ten thousand to the est: and its produce ill be for food for the orkers of the ton.
It ill be farmed by orkers of the ton from all the tribes of Israel.
The size of the offering all together is to be tenty-five thousand by tenty-five thousand: you are to make the holy offering a square, together ith the property of the ton.

And the rest is to be for the prince, on this side and on that side of the holy offering and of the property of the ton, in front of the tenty-five thousand to the east, as far as the east limit, and to the est, in front of the tenty-five thousand, as far as the est limit, and of the same measure as those parts; it ill be the property of the prince: and the holy offering and holy place of the house ill be in the middle of it.
And the property of the Levites and the property of the ton ill be in the middle of the prince’s property; beteen the limit of Judah’s part and the limit of Benjamin’s part ill be for the prince.
And as for the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the est side: Benjamin, one part.
And on the limit of Benjamin, from the east side to the est side: Simeon, one part.
And on the limit of Simeon, from the east side to the est side: Issachar, one part.
And on the limit of Issachar, from the east side to the est side: Zebulun, one part.
And on the limit of Zebulun, from the east side to the est side: Gad one part.
And on the limit of Gad, on the south side and to the south of it, the limit ill be from Tamar to the aters of Meribath-kadesh, to the stream, to the Great Sea.
This is the land of hich distribution is to be made by the decision of the Lord, among the tribes of Israel for their heritage, and these are their heritages, says the Lord.
And these are the outskirts of the ton: on the north side, four thousand five hundred by measure;
And the doors of the ton are to be named by the names of the tribes of Israel; three doors on the north, one for Reuben, one for Judah, one for Levi;
And at the east side, four thousand five hundred by measure, and three doors, one for Joseph, one for Benjamin, one for Dan;
And at the south side, four thousand five hundred by measure, and three doors, one for Simeon, one for Issachar, one for Zebulun;
At the est side, four thousand five hundred by measure, ith their three doors, one for Gad, one for Asher, one for Naphtali.
It is to be eighteen thousand all round: and the name of the ton from that day ill be, The Lord is there.
In the third year of the rule of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem, shutting it in ith his forces.

And the Lord gave into his hands Jehoiakim, king of Judah, ith some of the vessels of the house of God; and he took them aay into the land of Shinar to the house of his god; and he put the vessels into the store-house of his god.
And the king gave orders to Ashpenaz, the captain of his unsexed servants, to take in some of the children of Israel, certain of the king’s family, and those of high birth;

Young men ho ere strong and healthy, good-looking, and trained in all isdom, having a good education and much knoledge, and able to take positions in the king’s house; and to have them trained in the riting and language of the Chaldaeans.

And a regular amount of food and ine every day from the king’s table as ordered for them by the king; and they ere to be cared for for three years so that at the end of that time they might take their places before the king.
And among these there ere, of the children of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

And the captain of the unsexed servants gave them names; to Daniel he gave the name of Belteshazzar, to Hananiah the name of Shadrach, to Mishael the name of Meshach, and to Azariah the name of Abed-nego.

And Daniel had come to the decision that he ould not make himself unclean ith the king’s food or ine; so he made a request to the captain of the unsexed servants that he might not make himself unclean.
And God put into the heart of the captain of the unsexed servants kind feelings and pity for Daniel.

And the captain of the unsexed servants said to Daniel, I am in fear of my lord the king, ho has given orders about your food and your drink; hat if he sees you looking less happy than the other young men of your generation? then you ould have put my head in danger from the king.
Then Daniel said to the keeper in hose care the captain of the unsexed servants had put Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
Put your servants to the test for ten days; let them give us grain for our food and ater for our drink.
Then take a look at our faces and the faces of the young men ho have food from the king’s table; and, having seen them, do to your servants as it seems right to you.
So he gave ear to them in this thing and put them to the test for ten days.
And at the end of ten days their faces seemed fairer and they ere fatter in flesh than all the young men ho had their food from the king’s table.
So the keeper regularly took aay their meat and the ine hich as to have been their drink, and gave them grain.
No as for these four young men, God gave them knoledge and made them expert in all book-learning and isdom: and Daniel as ise in all visions and dreams.
No at the end of the time fixed by the king for them to go in, the captain of the unsexed servants took them in to Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king had talk ith them; and among them all there as no one like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; so they ere given places before the king.

And in any business needing isdom and good sense, about hich the king put questions to them, he sa that they ere ten times better than all the onder-orkers and users of secret arts in all his kingdom.
And Daniel ent on till the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of the rule of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams; and his spirit as troubled and his sleep ent from him.

Then the king gave orders that the onder-orkers, and the users of secret arts, and those ho made use of evil poers, and the Chaldaeans, ere to be sent for to make clear to the king his dreams. So they came and took their places before the king.
And the king said to them, I have had a dream, and my spirit is troubled by the desire to have the dream made clear to me.
Then the Chaldaeans said to the king in the Aramaean language, O King, have life for ever: give your servants an account of your dream, and e ill make clear to you the sense of it.
The king made anser and said to the Chaldaeans, This is my decision: if you do not make clear to me the dream and the sense of it, you ill be cut in bits and your houses made aste.
But if you make clear the dream and the sense of it, you ill have from me offerings and reards and great honour: so make clear to me the dream and the sense of it.
A second time they said in anser, Let the king give his servants an account of his dream, and e ill make clear the sense.
The king made anser and said, I am certain that you are attempting to get more time, because you see that my decision is fixed;

That if you do not make my dream clear to me there is only one fate for you: for you have made ready false and evil ords to say before me till the times are changed: so give me an account of the dream, and I ill be certain that you are able to make the sense of it clear.

Then the Chaldaeans said to the king in anser, There is not a man on earth able to make clear the king’s business; for no king, hoever great his poer, has ever made such a request to any onder-orker or user of secret arts or Chaldaean.
The king’s request is a very hard one, and there is no other ho is able to make it clear to the king, but the gods, hose living-place is not ith flesh.
Because of this the king as angry and full of rath, and gave orders for the destruction of all the ise men of Babylon.
So the order ent out that the ise men ere to be put to death; and they ere looking for Daniel and his friends to put them to death.
Then Daniel gave an anser ith isdom and good sense to Arioch, the captain of the king’s armed men, ho had gone out to put to death the ise men of Babylon;
He made anser and said to Arioch, O captain of the king, hy is the king’s order so cruel? Then Arioch gave Daniel an account of the business.
And Daniel ent in and made a request to the king to give him time and he ould make clear the sense of his dream to the king.
And Daniel ent to his house and gave his friends Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah the nes:

So that they might make a request for the mercy of the God of heaven in the question of this secret; so that Daniel and his friends might not come to destruction ith the rest of the ise men of Babylon.
Then the secret as made clear to Daniel in a vision of the night. And Daniel gave blessing to the God of heaven.
And Daniel said in anser, May the name of God be praised for ever and ever: for isdom and strength are his:
By him times and years are changed: by him kings are taken aay and kings are lifted up: he gives isdom to the ise, and knoledge to those hose minds are aake:
He is the unveiler of deep and secret things: he has knoledge of hat is in the dark, and the light has its living-place ith him.

I give you praise and orship, O God of my fathers, ho have given me isdom and strength, and have no made clear to me hat e ere requesting from you: for you have given us knoledge of the king’s business.

For this reason Daniel ent to Arioch, to hom the king had given orders for the destruction of the ise men of Babylon, and said to him, Do not put to death the ise men of Babylon: take me in before the king and I ill make clear to him the sense of the dream.
Then Arioch quickly took Daniel in before the king, and said to him, Here is a man from among the prisoners of Judah, ho ill make clear to the king the sense of the dream.
The king made anser and said to Daniel, hose name as Belteshazzar, Are you able to make clear to me the dream hich I sa and its sense?
Then Daniel said in anser to the king, No ise men, or users of secret arts, or onder-orkers, or readers of signs, are able to make clear to the king the secret he is searching for;

But there is a God in heaven, the unveiler of secrets, and he has given to King Nebuchadnezzar knoledge of hat ill take place in the last days. Your dreams and the visions of your head on your bed are these:
As for you, O King, the thoughts hich came to you on your bed ere of hat ill come about after this: and the unveiler of secrets has made clear to you hat is to come.

As for me, this secret is not made clear to me because of any isdom hich I have more than any living man, but in order that the sense of the dream may be made clear to the king, and that you may have knoledge of the thoughts of your heart.
You, O King, ere looking, and a great image as there. This image, hich as very great, and hose glory as very bright, as placed before you: its form sent fear into the heart.
As for this image, its head as made of the best gold, its breast and its arms ere of silver, its middle and its sides ere of brass,
Its legs of iron, its feet ere in part of iron and in part of potter’s earth.
While you ere looking at it, a stone as cut out, but not by hands, and it gave the image a blo on its feet, hich ere of iron and earth, and they ere broken in bits.

Then the iron and the earth, the brass and the silver and the gold, ere smashed together, and became like the dust on the floors here grain is crushed in summer; and the ind took them aay so that no sign of them as to be seen: and the stone hich gave the image a blo became a great mountain, covering all the earth.
This is the dream; and e ill make clear to the king the sense of it.
You, O King, king of kings, to hom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the poer, and the strength, and the glory,
Wherever the children of men are living; into hose hands he has given the beasts of the field and the birds of heaven, and has made you ruler over them all, you are the head of gold.
And after you another kingdom, loer than you, ill come to poer; and a third kingdom, of brass, ruling over all the earth.
And the fourth kingdom ill be strong as iron: because, as all things are broken and overcome by iron, so it ill have the poer of crushing and smashing don all the earth.

And as you sa the feet and toes, part of potter’s ork and part of iron, there ill be a division in the kingdom; but there ill be some of the strength of iron in it, because you sa the iron mixed ith the potter’s earth.
And as the toes of the feet ere in part of iron and in part of earth, so part of the kingdom ill be strong and part of it ill readily be broken.
And as you sa the iron mixed ith earth, they ill give their daughters to one another as ives: but they ill not be united one ith another, even as iron is not mixed ith earth.

And in the days of those kings, the God of heaven ill put up a kingdom hich ill never come to destruction, and its poer ill never be given into the hands of another people, and all these kingdoms ill be broken and overcome by it, but it ill keep its place for ever.

Because you sa that a stone as cut out of the mountain ithout hands, and that by it the iron and the brass and the earth and the silver and the gold ere broken to bits, a great God has given the king knoledge of hat is to take place in the future: the dream is fixed, and its sense is certain.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar, falling don on his face, gave orship to Daniel, and gave orders for an offering and spices to be given to him;
And the king made anser to Daniel and said, Truly, your God is a God of gods and a Lord of kings, and an unveiler of secrets, for you have been able to make this secret clear.
Then the king made Daniel great, and gave him offerings in great number, and made him ruler over all the land of Babylon, and chief over all the ise men of Babylon.
And at Daniel’s request, the king gave Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego authority over the business of the land of Babylon: but Daniel as kept near the king’s person.
Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits ide: he put it up in the valley of Dura, in the land of Babylon.

And Nebuchadnezzar the king sent to get together all the captains, the chiefs, the rulers, the ise men, the keepers of public money, the judges, the overseers, and all the rulers of the divisions of the country, to come to see the unveiling of the image hich Nebuchadnezzar the king had put up.

Then the captains, the chiefs, the rulers, the ise men, the keepers of public money, the judges, the overseers, and all the rulers of the divisions of the country, came together to see the unveiling of the image hich Nebuchadnezzar the king had put up; and they took their places before the image hich Nebuchadnezzar had put up.
Then one of the king’s criers said in a loud voice, To you the order is given, O peoples, nations, and languages,

That hen the sound of the horn, pipe, harp, trigon, psaltery, bagpipe, and all sorts of instruments, comes to your ears, you are to go don on your faces in orship before the image of gold hich Nebuchadnezzar the king has put up:
