And anyone not falling don and orshipping ill that same hour be put into a burning and flaming fire.

So at that time, all the people, hen the sound of the horn, pipe, harp, trigon, psaltery, and all sorts of instruments, came to their ears, ent don on their faces in orship before the image of gold hich Nebuchadnezzar the king had put up.
At that time certain Chaldaeans came near and made a statement against the Jes.
They made anser and said to Nebuchadnezzar the king, O King, have life for ever.

You, O King, have given an order that every man, hen the sound of the horn, pipe, harp, trigon, psaltery, bagpipe, and all sorts of instruments, comes to his ears, is to go don on his face in orship before the image of gold:
And anyone not falling don and orshipping is to be put into a burning and flaming fire.

There are certain Jes hom you have put over the business of the land of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; these men have not given attention to you, O King: they are not servants of your gods or orshippers of the gold image hich you have put up.
Then Nebuchadnezzar in his rath and passion gave orders for Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego to be sent for. Then they made these men come in before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar made anser and said to them, Is it true, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, that you ill not be servants of my god or give orship to the image of gold hich I have put up?

No if you are ready, on hearing the sound of the horn, pipe, harp, trigon, psaltery, bagpipe, and all sorts of instruments, to go don on your faces in orship before the image hich I have made, it is ell: but if you ill not give orship, that same hour you ill be put into a burning and flaming fire; and hat god is there ho ill be able to take you out of my hands?
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, ansering Nebuchadnezzar the king, said, There is no need for us to give you an anser to this question.
If our God, hose servants e are, is able to keep us safe from the burning and flaming fire, and from your hands, O King, he ill keep us safe.
But if not, be certain, O King, that e ill not be the servants of your gods, or give orship to the image of gold hich you have put up.

Then Nebuchadnezzar as full of rath, and the form of his face as changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego: and he gave orders that the fire as to be heated up seven times more than it as generally heated.
And he gave orders to certain strong men in his army to put cords on Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego and put them into the burning and flaming fire.
Then these men had cords put round them as they ere, in their coats, their trousers, their hats, and their clothing, and ere dropped into the burning and flaming fire.
And because the king’s order as not to be put on one side, and the heat of the fire as so great, the men ho took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego ere burned to death by the flame of the fire.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, ith the cords about them, ent don into the burning and flaming fire.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar, full of fear and onder, got up quickly, and said to his ise men, Did e not put three men in cords into the fire? and they made anser and said to the king, True, O King.
He made anser and said, Look! I see four men loose, alking in the middle of the fire, and they are not damaged; and the form of the fourth is like a son of the gods.

Then Nebuchadnezzar came near the door of the burning and flaming fire: he made anser and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, you servants of the Most High God, come out and come here. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego came out of the fire.

And the captains, the chiefs, and the rulers, and the king’s ise men ho had come together, sa these men, over hose bodies the fire had no poer, and not a hair of their heads as burned, and their coats ere not changed, and there as no smell of fire about them.

Nebuchadnezzar made anser and said, Praise be to the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, ho has sent his angel and kept his servants safe ho had faith in him, and ho put the king’s ord on one side and gave up their bodies to the fire, so that they might not be servants or orshippers of any other god but their God.

And it is my decision that any people, nation, or language saying evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, ill be cut to bits and their houses made aste: because there is no other god ho is able to give salvation such as this.
Then the king gave Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego even greater authority in the land of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar the king, to all the peoples, nations, and languages living in all the earth: May your peace be increased.
It has seemed good to me to make clear the signs and onders hich the Most High God has done ith me.
Ho great are his signs! and ho full of poer are his onders! his kingdom is an eternal kingdom and his rule goes on from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, as at rest in my place, and all things ere going ell for me in my great house:
I sa a dream hich as a cause of great fear to me; I as troubled by the images of my mind on my bed, and by the visions of my head.
And I gave orders for all the ise men of Babylon to come in before me so that they might make clear to me the sense of my dream.
Then the onder-orkers, the users of secret arts, the Chaldaeans, and the readers of signs came in to me: and I put the dream before them but they did not make clear the sense of it to me.
But at last Daniel came in before me, he hose name as Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and in hom is the spirit of the holy gods: and I put the dream before him, saying,

O Belteshazzar, master of the onder-orkers, because I am certain that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and you are troubled by no secret; this is the dream hich I sa: make clear to me its sense.
On my bed I sa a vision: there as a tree in the middle of the earth, and it as very high.
And the tree became tall and strong, stretching up to heaven, and to be seen from the ends of the earth:

Its leaves ere fair and it had much fruit, and in it as food enough for all: the beasts of the field had shade under it, and the birds of heaven ere resting in its branches, and it gave food to all living things.
In the visions of my head on my bed I sa a atcher, a holy one, coming don from heaven,

Crying out ith a loud voice; and this is hat he said: Let the tree be cut don and its branches broken off; let its leaves be taken off and its fruit sent in every direction: let the beasts get aay from under it and the birds from its branches:

But keep its broken end and its roots still in the earth, even ith a band of iron and brass; let him have the young grass of the field for food, and let him be et ith the de of heaven, and let his part be ith the beasts.
Let his heart be changed from that of a man, and the heart of a beast be given to him; and let seven times go by him.

This order is fixed by the atchers, and the decision is by the ord of the holy ones: so that the living may be certain that the Most High is ruler over the kingdom of men, and gives it to any man at his pleasure, lifting up over it the loest of men.

This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, sa; and do you, O Belteshazzar, make clear the sense of it, for all the ise men of my kingdom are unable to make the sense of it clear to me; but you are able, for the spirit of the holy gods is in you.

Then Daniel, hose name as Belteshazzar, as at a loss for a time, his thoughts troubling him. The king made anser and said, Belteshazzar, do not be troubled by the dream or by the sense of it. Belteshazzar, ansering, said, My lord, may the dream be about your haters, and its sense about those ho are against you.
The tree hich you sa, hich became tall and strong, stretching up to heaven and seen from the ends of the earth;
Which had fair leaves and much fruit, and had in it food for all; under hich the beasts of the field ere living, and in the branches of hich the birds of heaven had their resting-places:
It is you, O King, ho have become great and strong: for your poer is increased and stretching up to heaven, and your rule to the end of the earth.
And as for the vision hich the king sa of a atcher, a holy one, coming don from heaven, saying, Let the tree be cut don and given to destruction;
This is the sense of it, O King, and it is the decision of the Most High hich has come on my lord the king:

That they ill send you out from among men, to be ith the beasts of the field; they ill give you grass for your food like the oxen, and you ill be et ith the de of heaven, and seven times ill go by you, till you are certain that the Most High is ruler in the kingdom of men, and gives it to any man at his pleasure.
And as they gave orders to let the broken end and the roots of the tree be, so your kingdom ill be safe for you after it is clear to you that the heavens are ruling.
For this cause, O King, let my suggestion be pleasing to you, and let your sins be covered by righteousness and your evil-doing by mercy to the poor, so that the time of your ell-being may be longer.
All this came to King Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of telve months he as alking on the roof of his great house in Babylon.
The king made anser and said, Is this not great Babylon, hich I have made for the living-place of kings, by the strength of my poer and for the glory of my honour?
While the ord as still in the king’s mouth, a voice came don from heaven, saying, O King Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is said: The kingdom has gone from you:

And they ill send you out from among men, to be ith the beasts of the field; they ill give you grass for your food like the oxen, and seven times ill go by you, till you are certain that the Most High is ruler in the kingdom of men, and gives it to any man at his pleasure.

That very hour the order about Nebuchadnezzar as put into effect: and he as sent out from among men, and had grass for his food like the oxen, and his body as et ith the de of heaven, till his hair became long as eagles’ feathers and his nails like those of birds.

And at the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifting up my eyes to heaven, got back my reason, and, blessing the Most High, I gave praise and honour to him ho is living for ever, hose rule is an eternal rule and hose kingdom goes on from generation to generation.

And all the people of the earth are as nothing: he does his pleasure in the army of heaven and among the people of the earth: and no one is able to keep back his hand, or say to him, What are you doing?

At the same time my reason came back to me; and for the glory of my kingdom, my honour and my great name came back to me; and my ise men and my lords ere turned to me again; and I as made safe in my kingdom and had more poer than before.
No I, Nebuchadnezzar, give orship and praise and honour to the King of heaven; for all his orks are true and his ays are right: and those ho go in pride he is able to make lo.
Belshazzar the king made a great feast for a thousand of his lords, drinking ine before the thousand.

Belshazzar, hile he as overcome ith ine, gave orders for them to put before him the gold and silver vessels hich Nebuchadnezzar, his father, had taken from the Temple in Jerusalem; so that the king and his lords, his ives and his other omen, might take their drink from them.
Then they took in the gold and silver vessels hich had been in the Temple of the house of God at Jerusalem; and the king and his lords, his ives and his other omen, took ine from them.
They took their ine and gave praise to the gods of gold and silver, of brass and iron and ood and stone.
In that very hour the fingers of a man’s hand ere seen, riting opposite the support for the light on the hite all of the king’s house, and the king sa the part of the hand hich as riting.
Then the colour ent from the king’s face, and he as troubled by his thoughts; strength ent from his body, and his knees ere shaking.

The king, crying out ith a loud voice, said that the users of secret arts, the Chaldaeans, and the readers of signs, ere to be sent for. The king made anser and said to the ise men of Babylon, Whoever is able to make out this riting, and make clear to me the sense of it, ill be clothed in purple and have a chain of gold round his neck, and ill be a ruler of high authority in the kingdom.
Then all the king’s ise men came in: but they ere not able to make out the riting or give the sense of it to the king.
Then King Belshazzar as greatly troubled and the colour ent from his face, and his lords ere at a loss.

The queen, because of the ords of the king and his lords, came into the house of the feast: the queen made anser and said, O King, have life for ever; do not be troubled by your thoughts or let the colour go from your face:

There is a man in your kingdom in hom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of your father, light and reason like the isdom of the gods ere seen in him: and King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, made him master of the onder-orkers, and the users of secret arts, and the Chaldaeans, and the readers of signs;

Because a most special spirit, and knoledge and reason and the poer of reading dreams and unfolding dark sayings and ansering hard questions, ere seen to be in him, even in Daniel ( named Belteshazzar by the king): no let Daniel be sent for, and he ill make clear the sense of the riting.
Then they took Daniel in before the king; the king made anser and said to Daniel, So you are that Daniel, of the prisoners of Judah, hom my father took out of Judah.
And I have had nes of you, that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that light and reason and special isdom have been seen in you.

And no the ise men, the users of secret arts, have been sent in before me for the purpose of reading this riting and making clear to me the sense of it: but they are not able to make clear the sense of the thing:

And I have had nes of you, that you have the poer of making things clear, and of ansering hard questions: no if you are able to make out the riting and give me the sense of it, you ill be clothed in purple and have a gold chain round your neck and be a ruler of high authority in the kingdom.
Then Daniel made anser and said to the king, Keep your offerings for yourself, and give your reards to another; but I, after reading the riting to the king, ill give him the sense of it.
As for you, O King, the Most High God gave to Nebuchadnezzar, your father, the kingdom and great poer and glory and honour:

And because of the great poer he gave him, all peoples and nations and languages ere shaking in fear before him: some he put to death and others he kept living, at his pleasure, lifting up some and putting others don as it pleased him.
But hen his heart as lifted up and his spirit became hard ith pride, he as put don from his place as king, and they took his glory from him:

And he as sent out from among the sons of men; and his heart as made like the beasts’, and he as living ith the asses of the fields; he had grass for his food like the oxen, and his body as et ith the de of heaven, till he as certain that the Most High is ruler in the kingdom of men, and gives poer over it to anyone at his pleasure.
And you, his son, O Belshazzar, have not kept your heart free from pride, though you had knoledge of all this;

But you have been lifting yourself up against the Lord of heaven, and they have put the vessels of his house before you, and you and your lords, your ives and your omen, have taken ine in them; and you have given praise to gods of silver and gold, of brass and iron and ood and stone, ho are ithout the poer of seeing or hearing, and ithout knoledge: and to the God in hose hand your breath is, and hose are all your ays, you have not given glory;
Then the part of the hand as sent out from before him, and this riting as recorded.
And this is the riting hich as recorded, Mene, tekel, peres.
This is the sense of the ords: Mene; your kingdom has been numbered by God and ended.
Tekel; you have been put in the scales and seen to be under eight.
Peres; your kingdom has been cut up and given to the Medes and Persians.
Then, by the order of Belshazzar, they put a purple robe on Daniel, and a gold chain round his neck, and a public statement as made that he as to be a ruler of high authority in the kingdom.
That very night Belshazzar, the king of the Chaldaeans, as put to death.
And Darius the Mede took the kingdom, being then about sixty-to years old.
Darius as pleased to put over the kingdom a hundred and tenty captains, ho ere to be all through the kingdom;
And over them ere three chief rulers, of hom Daniel as one; and the captains ere to be responsible to the chief rulers, so that the king might undergo no loss.
Then this Daniel did his ork better than the chief rulers and the captains, because there as a special spirit in him; and it as the king’s purpose to put him over all the kingdom.

Then the chief rulers and the captains ere looking for some cause for putting Daniel in the rong in connection ith the kingdom, but they ere unable to put forard any rongdoing or error against him; because he as true, and no error or rong as to be seen in him.
Then these men said, We ill only get a reason for attacking Daniel in connection ith the la of his God.
Then these chief rulers and the captains came to the king and said to him, O King Darius, have life for ever.

All the chief rulers of the kingdom, the chiefs and the captains, the ise men and the rulers, have made a common decision to put in force a la having the king’s authority, and to give a strong order, that hoever makes any request to any god or man but you, O King, for thirty days, is to be put into the lions’ hole.
No, O King, put the order in force, signing the riting so that it may not be changed, like the la of the Medes and Persians hich may not come to an end.
For this reason King Darius put his name on the riting and the order.

And Daniel, on hearing that the riting had been signed, ent into his house; ( no he had indos in his room on the roof opening in the direction of Jerusalem;) and three times a day he ent don on his knees in prayer and praise before his God, as he had done before.
Then these men ere atching and sa Daniel making prayers and requesting grace before his God.

Then they came near before the king and said, O King, have you not put your name to an order that any man ho makes a request to any god or man but you, O King, for thirty days, is to be put into the lions’ hole? The king made anser and said, The thing is fixed by the la of the Medes and Persians hich may not come to an end.
Then they made anser and said before the king, Daniel, one of the prisoners of Judah, has no respect for you, O King, or for the order signed by you, but three times a day he makes his prayer to God.
When this thing came to the king’s ears, it as very evil to him, and his heart as fixed on keeping Daniel safe, and till the going don of the sun he as doing everything in his poer to get him free.
Then these men said to the king, Be certain, O King, that by the la of the Medes and Persians no order or la hich the king has put into force may be changed.
Then the king gave the order, and they took Daniel and put him into the lions’ hole. The king made anser and said to Daniel, Your God, hose servant you are at all times, ill keep you safe.
Then they got a stone and put it over the mouth of the hole, and it as stamped ith the king’s stamp and ith the stamp of the lords, so that the decision about Daniel might not be changed.
Then the king ent to his great house, and took no food that night, and no ... ere placed before him, and his sleep ent from him.
Then very early in the morning the king got up and ent quickly to the lions’ hole.

And hen he came near the hole here Daniel as, he gave a loud cry of grief; the king made anser and said to Daniel, O Daniel, servant of the living God, is your God, hose servant you are at all times, able to keep you safe from the lions?
Then Daniel said to the king, O King, have life for ever.
My God has sent his angel to keep the lions’ mouths shut, and they have done me no damage: because I as seen to be ithout sin before him; and further, before you, O King, I have done no rong.
Then the king as very glad, and gave orders for them to take Daniel up out of the hole. So Daniel as taken up out of the hole and he as seen to be untouched, because he had faith in his God.

And at the king’s order, they took those men ho had said evil against Daniel, and put them in the lions’ hole, ith their ives and their children; and they had not got to the floor of the hole before the lions overcame them and all their bones ere broken.
Then King Darius sent a letter to all the peoples, nations, and languages, living in all the earth: May your peace be increased.

It is my order that in all the kingdom of hich I am ruler, men are to be shaking ith fear before the God of Daniel: for he is the living God, unchanging for ever, and his kingdom is one hich ill never come to destruction, his rule ill go on to the end.
He gives salvation and makes men free from danger, and does signs and onders in heaven and earth, ho has kept Daniel safe from the poer of the lions.
So this Daniel did ell in the kingdom of Darius and in the kingdom of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar, king of Babylon, Daniel sa a dream, and visions came into his head on his bed: then he put the dream in riting.
I had a vision by night, and sa the four inds of heaven violently moving the great sea.
And four great beasts came up from the sea, different one from another.
The first as like a lion and had eagle’s ings; hile I as atching its ings ere pulled off, and it as lifted up from the earth and placed on to feet like a man, and a man’s heart as given to it.
And I sa another beast, like a bear, and it as lifted up on one side, and three side-bones ere in its mouth, beteen its teeth: and they said to it, Up! take much flesh.
After this I sa another beast, like a leopard, hich had on its back four ings like those of a bird; and the beast had four heads, and the poer of a ruler as given to it.

After this, in my vision of the night, I sa a fourth beast, a thing causing fear and very troubling, full of poer and very strong; and it had great iron teeth: it took its food, crushing some of it to bits and stamping don the rest ith its feet: it as different from all the beasts before it; and it had ten horns.

I as atching the horns ith care, and I sa another coming up among them, a little one, before hich three of the first horns ere pulled up by the roots: and there ere eyes like a man’s eyes in this horn, and a mouth saying great things.

I ent on looking till the seats of kings ere placed, and one like a very old man took his seat: his clothing as hite as sno, and the hair of his head as like clean ool; his seat as flames of fire and its heels burning fire.

A stream of fire as floing and coming out from before him: a thousand thousands ere his servants, and ten thousand times ten thousand ere in their places before him: the judge as seated and the books ere open.
Then I sa — because of the voice of the great ords hich the horn said — I sa till the beast as put to death, and its body as given to destruction, and the beast as given to the burning of fire.

I sa in visions of the night, and there as coming ith the clouds of heaven one like a man, and he came to the one ho as very old, and they took him near before him.

And to him as given authority and glory and a kingdom; and all peoples, nations, and languages ere his servants: his authority is an eternal authority hich ill not come to an end, and his kingdom is one hich ill not come to destruction.
As for me, Daniel, my spirit as pained because of this, and the visions of my head ere troubling me.
I came near to one of those ho ere aiting there, questioning him about hat all this as. And he said to me that he ould make clear to me the sense of these things.

Then it as my desire to have certain knoledge about the fourth beast, hich as different from all the others, a cause of great fear, hose teeth ere of iron and his nails of brass; ho took his food, crushing some of it to bits and stamping on the rest ith his feet;
And about the ten horns on his head and the other hich came up, causing the fall of three; that horn hich had eyes, and a mouth saying great things, hich seemed to be greater than the other horns.
And I sa ho that horn made ar on the saints and overcame them,
Till he came, ho as very old, and the decision as made and the authority as given to the saints of the Most High; and the time came hen the saints took the kingdom.
This is hat he said: The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom hich ill come on earth, different from all the kingdoms, and it ill overcome all the earth, crushing it don and smashing it.
And as for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings ill come to poer; and after them another ill come up: he ill be different from the first ones and ill put don three kings.

And the kingdom and the authority and the poer of the kingdoms under all the heaven ill be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: his kingdom is an eternal kingdom, and all poers ill be his servants and do his pleasure.
Here is the end of the account. As for me, Daniel, I as greatly troubled by my thoughts, and the colour ent from my face: but I kept the thing in my heart.
In the third year of the rule of Belshazzar the king, a vision as seen by me, Daniel, after the one I sa at first.
And I sa in the vision; and hen I sa it, I as in the strong ton Shushan, hich is in the country of Elam; and in the vision I as by the ater-door of the Ulai.

And the he-goat became very great: and hen he as strong, the great horn as broken, and in its place came up four other horns turned to the four inds of heaven.
And out of one of them came another horn, a little one, hich became very great, stretching to the south and to the east and to the beautiful land.
And it became great, even as high as the army of heaven, pulling don some of the army, even of the stars, to the earth and crushing them under its feet.

... against the regular burned offering; and ... crushed don to the earth, and it did its pleasure and things ent ell for it.

Then there came to my ears the voice of a holy one talking; and another holy one said to that certain one ho as talking, Ho long ill the vision be hile the regular burned offering is taken aay, and the unclean thing causing fear is put up, and the holy place crushed under foot?

And it came about that hen I, Daniel, had seen this vision, I had a desire for the sense of it to be unfolded; and I sa one before me in the form of a man.

So he came and took his place near here I as; and hen he came, I as full of fear and ent don on my face: but he said to me, Let it be clear to you, O son of man; for the vision has to do ith the time of the end.

And he said, See, I ill make clear to you hat is to come in the later time of the rath: for it has to do ith the fixed time of the end.

And as for that hich as broken, in place of hich four came up, four kingdoms ill come up from his nation, but not ith his poer.

And I, Daniel, as ill for some days; then I got up and did the king’s business: and I as full of onder at the vision, but no one as able to give the sense of it.
In the first year of Darius, the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, ho as made king over the kingdom of the Chaldaeans;

In the first year of his rule, I, Daniel, sa clearly from the books the number of years given by the ord of the Lord to the prophet Jeremiah, in hich the making aste of Jerusalem as to be complete, that is, seventy years.
And turning my face to the Lord God, I gave myself up to prayer, requesting his grace, going ithout food, in haircloth and dust.

And I made prayer to the Lord my God, putting our sins before him, and said, O Lord, the great God, greatly to be feared. keeping your agreement and mercy ith those ho have love for you and do your orders;
We are sinners, acting rongly and doing evil; e have gone against you, turning aay from your orders and from your las:
We have not given ear to your servants the prophets, ho said ords in your name to our kings and our rulers and our fathers and all the people of the land.

O Lord, righteousness is yours, but shame is on us, even to this day; and on the men of Judah and the people of Jerusalem, and on all Israel, those ho are near and those ho are far off, in all the countries here you have sent them because of the sin hich they have done against you.
O Lord, shame is on us, on our kings and our rulers and our fathers, because of our sin against you.
With the Lord our God are mercies and forgiveness, for e have gone against him;
And have not given ear to the voice of the Lord our God to go in the ay of his las hich he put before us by the mouth of his servants the prophets.

And all Israel have been sinners against your la, turning aay so as not to give ear to your voice: and the curse has been let loose on us, and the oath recorded in the la of Moses, the servant of God, for e have done evil against him.

And he has given effect to his ords hich he said against us and against those ho ere our judges, by sending a great evil on us: for under all heaven there has not been done hat has been done to Jerusalem.
As it as recorded in the la of Moses, all this evil has come on us: but e have made no prayer for grace from the Lord our God that e might be turned from our evil doings and come to true isdom.
So the Lord has been atching over this evil and has made it come on us: for the Lord our God is upright in all his acts hich he has done, and e have not given ear to his voice.
And no, O Lord our God, ho took your people out of the land of Egypt ith a strong hand and made a great name for yourself even to this day; e are sinners, e have done evil.

O Lord, because of your righteousness, let your rath and your passion be turned aay from your ton Jerusalem, your holy mountain: because, through our sins and the evil-doing of our fathers, Jerusalem and your people have become a cause of shame to all ho are round about us.
And no, give ear, O our God, to the prayer of your servant and to his request for grace, and let your face be shining on your holy place hich is made aste, because of your servants, O Lord.

O my God, let your ear be turned and give hearing; let your eyes be open and see ho e have been made aste and the ton hich is named by your name: for e are not offering our prayers before you because of our righteousness, but because of your great mercies.
O Lord, give ear; O Lord, have forgiveness; O Lord, take note and do; let there be no more aiting; for the honour of your name, O my God, because your ton and your people are named by your name.
And hile I as still saying these ords in prayer, and putting my sins and the sins of my people Israel before the Lord, and requesting grace from the Lord my God for the holy mountain of my God;
Even hile I as still in prayer, the man Gabriel, hom I had seen in the vision at first hen my eariness as great, put his hand on me about the time of the evening offering.
And teaching me and talking to me he said, O Daniel, I have come no to give you isdom.
At the first ord of your prayer a ord ent out, and I have come to give you knoledge; for you are a man dearly loved: so give thought to the ord and let the vision be clear to you.

Seventy eeks have been fixed for your people and your holy ton, to let rongdoing be complete and sin come to its full limit, and for the clearing aay of evil-doing and the coming in of eternal righteousness: so that the vision and the ord of the prophet may be stamped as true, and to put the holy oil on a most holy place.

Have then the certain knoledge that from the going out of the ord for the building again of Jerusalem till the coming of a prince, on hom the holy oil has been put, ill be seven eeks: in sixty-to eeks its building ill be complete, ith square and earthork.

And at the end of the times, even after the sixty-to eeks, one on hom the holy oil has been put ill be cut off and have no...; and the ton and the holy place ill be made aste together ith a prince; and the end ill come ith an overfloing of aters, and even to the end there ill be ar; the making aste hich has been fixed.

And a strong order ill be sent out against the great number for one eek; and so for half of the eek the offering and the meal offering ill come to an end; and in its place ill be an unclean thing causing fear; till the destruction hich has been fixed is let loose on him ho has made aste.

In the third year of Cyrus, king of Persia, a secret as unfolded to Daniel, hose name as Belteshazzar; and the thing as true, even a hard ork: and he had knoledge of it, and the vision as clear to him.
In those days I, Daniel, gave myself up to grief for three full eeks.
I had no pleasing food, no meat or ine came into my mouth, and I put no oil on my body till three full eeks ere ended.
And on the tenty-fourth day of the first month I as by the side of the great river;
And lifting up my eyes I sa the form of a man clothed in a linen robe, and round him there as a band of gold, of the best gold:

And his body as like the beryl, and his face had the look of a thunder-flame, and his eyes ere like burning lights, and his arms and feet like the colour of polished brass, and the sound of his voice as like the sound of an army.
And I, Daniel, as the only one ho sa the vision, for the men ho ere ith me did not see it; but a great shaking came on them and they ent in flight to take cover.
So I as by myself, and I sa this great vision, and all my strength ent from me; and the colour ent from my face.
But the sound of his ords came to my ears, and on hearing his voice I ent into a deep sleep ith my face to the earth.
Then a hand gave me a touch, aaking me, and putting me on my knees and my hands.

And he said to me, O Daniel, you man dearly loved, take in the sense of the ords I say to you and get up on to your feet: for to you I am no sent; and hen he had said this to me I got on to my feet, shaking ith fear.

Then he said to me, Have no fear, Daniel; for from the first day hen you gave your heart to getting isdom and making yourself poor in spirit before your God, your ords have come to his ears: and I have come because of your ords.

But the angel of the kingdom of Persia put himself against me for tenty-one days; but Michael, one of the chief angels, came to my help; and hen I came he as still there ith the angel of the kings of Persia.
No I have come to give you knoledge of the fate of your people in the later days; for there is still a vision for the days.
And after he had said these ords to me, I kept my face turned to the earth and as unable to say anything.

Then one hose form as like the sons of men put his finger on my lips; and opening my mouth, I said to him ho as before me, O my lord, because of the vision my pains have come on me, and I have no more strength.
For ho may this servant of my lord have talk ith my lord? for, as for me, straight aay my strength ent from me and there as no breath in my body.
Then again one having the form of a man put his hand on me and gave me strength.

And he said to me, O man greatly loved, have no fear: peace be ith you, be strong and let your heart be lifted up. And at his ords I became strong, and said, Let my lord say on, for you have given me strength.
Then he said, It is clear to you hy I have come to you. And no I ill give you an account of hat is recorded in the true ritings:
But I am going back to make ar ith the angel of Persia, and hen I am gone, the angel of Greece ill come. And there is no one on my side against these, but Michael, your angel.
And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede I as on his side to make his position safe and make him strong.

And no I ill make clear to you hat is true. There are still three kings to come in Persia, and the fourth ill have much greater ealth than all of them: and hen he has become strong through his ealth, he ill put his forces in motion against all the kingdoms of Greece.
And a strong king ill come to poer, ruling ith great authority and doing hatever is his pleasure.

And hen he has become strong, his kingdom ill be broken and parted to the four inds of heaven; but not to his offspring, for it ill be uprooted; and his kingdom ill be for the others and not for these: but not ith the same authority as his.
And the king of the south ill be strong, but one of his captains ill be stronger than he and ill be ruler; and his rule ill be a great rule.

And at the end of years they ill be joined together; and the daughter of the king of the south ill come to the king of the north to make an agreement: but she ill not keep the strength of her arm; and his offspring ill not keep their place; but she ill be uprooted, ith those ho ere the cause of her coming, and her son, and he ho took her in those times.

But out of a branch from her roots one ill come up to take his place, ho ill come against the army, forcing his ay into the strong place of the king of the north, and he ill take them in hand and overcome them:
And their gods and their metal images and their fair vessels of silver and gold he ill take aay into the south; and for some years he ill keep aay from the king of the north.
And he ill come into the kingdom of the king of the south, but he ill go back to his land.
And his son ill make ar, and ill get together an army of great forces, and he ill make an attack on him, overfloing and going past: and he ill again take the ar even to his strong place.
And the king of the south ill be moved ith rath, and ill come out and make ar on him, on this same king of the north: and he ill get together a great army, but the army ill be given into his hand.
And the army ill be taken aay, and his heart ill be uplifted: he ill be the cause of the donfall of tens of thousands, but he ill not be strong.
And again the king of the north ill get together an army greater than the first; and he ill make an attack on him at the end of years, ith a great army and much ealth.

In those times, a number ill take up arms against the king of the south: and the children of the violent among your people ill be lifting themselves up to make the vision come true; but it ill be their donfall.

So the king of the north ill come, and put up earthorks and take a ell-armed ton: and the forces of the king of the south ill make an attempt to keep their position, even the best of his army, but they ill not have strength to do so.
And he ho comes against him ill do his pleasure, and no one ill be able to keep his place before him: he ill take up his position in the beautiful land and in his hand there ill be destruction.

And it ill be his purpose to come ith the strength of all his kingdom, but in place of this he ill make an agreement ith him; and he ill give him the daughter of omen to send destruction on it; but this ill not take place or come about.

After this, his face ill be turned to the islands, and he ill take a number of them: but a chief, by his destruction, ill put an end to the shame offered by him; and more than this, he ill make his shame come back on him.
Then his face ill be turned to the strong places of his land: but his ay ill be stopped, causing his donfall, and he ill not be seen again.
Then his place ill be taken by one ho ill send out a man ith the glory of a king to get ealth together; but after a short time destruction ill overtake him, but not in rath or in the fight.
And his place ill be taken by a lo person, to hom the honour of the kingdom had not been given: but he ill come in time of peace and ill get the kingdom by fair ords.
And his forces ill be completely taken aay from before him and broken; and even the ruler of the agreement ill have the same fate.
And from the time hen they make an agreement ith him, he ill be orking falsely: for he ill take up arms suddenly ith a small force,

Against fertile places, and ill make aste a part of the country; and he ill do hat his fathers have not done, or his fathers’ fathers; he ill make distribution among them of goods taken in ar and by force, and of property: he ill even make designs against the strong places for a time.

And he ill put in motion his poer and his strength against the king of the south ith a great army; and the king of the south ill go to ar ith a very great and strong army: but he ill be forced to give ay, because of their designs against him;
And his fears ill overcome him and be the cause of his donfall, and his army ill come to complete destruction, and a great number ill be put to the sord.
And as for these to kings, their hearts ill be fixed on doing evil and they ill say false ords at one table; but it ill come to nothing: for the end ill be at the time fixed.
And he ill go back to his land ith great ealth; and his heart ill be against the holy agreement; and he ill do his pleasure and go back to his land.
At the time fixed he ill come back and come into the south; but in the later time it ill not be as it as before.

For those ho go out from the est ill come against him, and he ill be in fear and ill go back, full of rath against the holy agreement; and he ill do his pleasure: and he ill go back and be united ith those ho have given up the holy agreement.

And armies sent by him ill take up their position and they ill make unclean the holy place, even the strong place, and take aay the regular burned offering and put in its place an unclean thing causing fear.
And those ho do evil against the agreement ill be turned to sin by his fair ords: but the people ho have knoledge of their God ill be strong and do ell.

And those ho are ise among the people ill be the teachers of the mass of the people: but they ill come to their donfall by the sord and by the flame, being made prisoners and undergoing loss for a long time.
No at the time of their donfall they ill have a little help, but numbers ill be joined to them in the ton, and in their separate heritages.
And some of those ho are ise ill have isdom in testing themselves and making themselves clean, till the time of the end: for it is still for the fixed time.

And the king ill do his pleasure; he ill put himself on high, lifting himself over every god, and saying things to be ondered at against the God of gods; and all ill be ell for him till the rath is complete; for hat has been purposed ill be done.
He ill have no respect for the gods of his fathers or for the god desired by omen; he ill have no respect for any god: for he ill put himself on high over all.
But in place of this he ill give honour to the god of armed places, and to a god of hom his fathers had no knoledge he ill give honour ith gold and silver and jeels and things to be desired.

And he ill make use of the people of a strange god to keep his strongest places; to those hom he takes note of he ill give high honour: and he ill make them rulers over the mass of the people, and ill make division of the land for a price.

And at the time of the end, the king of the south ill make an attack on him: and the king of the north ill come against him like a storm-ind, ith ar-carriages and horsemen and numbers of ships; and he ill go through many lands like overfloing aters.
And he ill come into the beautiful land, and tens of thousands ill be overcome: but these ill be kept from falling into his hands: Edom and Moab and the chief of the children of Ammon.
And his hand ill be stretched out on the countries: and the land of the south ill not be safe from him.
But he ill have poer over the stores of gold and silver, and over all the valued things of the south: and the Libyans and the Ethiopians ill be at his steps.
But he ill be troubled by nes from the east and from the north; and he ill go out in great rath, to send destruction on, and put an end to, great numbers.
He ill put the tents of his great house beteen the sea and the beautiful holy mountain: but he ill come to his end ith no helper.

And at that time Michael ill take up his place, the great angel, ho is the supporter of the children of your people: and there ill be a time of trouble, such as there never as from the time there as a nation even till that same time: and at that time your people ill be kept safe, everyone ho is recorded in the book.
And a number of those ho are sleeping in the dust of the earth ill come out of their sleep, some to eternal life and some to eternal shame.
And those ho are ise ill be shining like the light of the outstretched sky; and those by hom numbers have been turned to righteousness ill be like the stars for ever and ever.
But as for you, O Daniel, let the ords be kept secret and the book rolled up and kept shut till the time of the end: numbers ill be going out of the ay and troubles ill be increased.
Then I, Daniel, looking, sa to others, one at the edge of the river on this side and one at the edge of the river on that side.
And I said to the man clothed in linen, ho as over the aters of the river, Ho long ill it be to the end of these onders?

Then in my hearing the man clothed in linen, ho as over the river, lifting up his right hand and his left hand to heaven, took an oath by him ho is living for ever that it ould be a time, times, and a half; and hen the poer of the crusher of the holy people comes to an end, all these things ill be ended.
And the ords came to my ears, but the sense of them as not clear to me: then I said, O my lord, hat is the sense of these things?
And he said, Go on your ay, Daniel: for the ords are secret and shut up till the time of the end;
Till a number are tested and make themselves clean; and the evil-doers ill do evil; for not one of the evil-doers ill have knoledge; but all ill be made clear to those ho are ise.
And from the time hen the regular burned offering is taken aay, and an unclean thing causing fear is put up, there ill be a thousand, to hundred and ninety days.
A blessing ill be on the man ho goes on aiting, and comes to the thousand, three hundred and thirty-five days.
But you, go on your ay and take your rest: for you ill be in your place at the end of the days.
The ord of the Lord hich came to Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam, the son of Joash, king of Israel.
The start of the ord of the Lord by Hosea: And the Lord said to Hosea, Go, take for yourself a ife of loose ays, and children of the same, for the land has been untrue to the Lord.
So he took as his ife Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, and she gave birth to a son.
And the Lord said to him, Give him the name of Jezreel, for after a little time I ill send punishment for the blood of Jezreel on the line of Jehu, and put an end to the kingdom of Israel.
And in that day I ill let the bo of Israel be broken in the valley of Jezreel.
And after that she gave birth to a daughter. And the Lord said, Give her the name Lo-ruhamah; for I ill not again have mercy on Israel, to give them forgiveness.
But I ill have mercy on Judah and ill give them salvation by the Lord their God, but not by the bo or the sord or by fighting or by horses or horsemen.
No hen Lo-ruhamah had been taken from the breast, the oman gave birth to a son.
And the Lord said, Give him the name Lo-ammi; for you are not my people, and I ill not be your God.

But still the number of the children of Israel ill be like the sand of the sea, hich may not be measured or numbered; and in place of its being said to them, You are not my people, it ill be said to them, You are the sons of the living God
And the children of Israel and the children of Judah ill come together and take for themselves one head, and ill go up from the land, for great ill be the day of Jezreel.
Say to your brothers, Ammi; and to your sisters, Ruhamah.
Take up the cause against your mother, take it up, for she is not my ife, and I am not her husband; let her put aay her loose ays from her face, and her false ays from beteen her breasts;
For fear that I may take aay her robe from her, making her uncovered as in the day of her birth; making her like a aste place and a dry land, causing her death through need of ater.
And I ill have no mercy on her children, for they are the children of her loose ays.
For their mother has been untrue; she ho gave them birth has done things of shame, for she said, I ill go after my lovers, ho give me my bread and my ater, my ool and my linen, my oil and my ine.
For this cause I ill put thorns in her road, building up a all round her so that she may not go on her ay.

And if she goes after her lovers she ill not overtake them; if she makes search for them she ill not see them; then ill she say, I ill go back to my first husband, for then it as better for me than no.
For she had no knoledge that it as I ho gave her the grain and the ine and the oil, increasing her silver and gold hich they gave to the Baal.
So I ill take aay again my grain in its time and my ine, and I ill take aay my ool and my linen ith hich her body might have been covered.
And no I ill make her shame clear before the eyes of her lovers, and no one ill take her out of my hand.
And I ill put an end to all her joy, her feasts, her ne moons, and her Sabbaths, and all her regular meetings.

And I ill make aste her vines and her fig-trees, of hich she has said, These are the payments hich my lovers have made to me; and I ill make them a aste of trees, and the beasts of the field ill take them for food.

And I ill give her punishment for the days of the Baals, to hom she has been burning perfumes, hen she made herself fair ith her nose-rings and her jeels, and ent after her lovers, giving no thought to me, says the Lord.
For this cause I ill make her come into the aste land and ill say ords of comfort to her.

And I ill give her vine-gardens from there, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope; and she ill give her anser there as in the days hen she as young, and as in the time hen she came up out of the land of Egypt.
And in that day, says the Lord, you ill say to me, Ishi; and you ill never again give me the name of Baali;
For I ill take aay the names of the Baals out of her mouth, and never again ill she say their names.

And in that day I ill make an agreement for them ith the beasts of the field and the birds of heaven and the things hich go lo on the earth; I ill put an end to the bo and the sord and ar in all the land, and ill make them take their rest in peace.
And I ill take you as my bride for ever; truly, I ill take you as my bride in righteousness and in right judging, in love and in mercies.
I ill take you as my bride in good faith, and you ill have knoledge of the Lord.
And it ill be, in that day, says the Lord, that I ill give an anser to the heavens, and the heavens to the earth;
And the earth ill give its anser to the grain and the ine and the oil, and they ill give an anser to Jezreel;
And I ill put her as seed in the earth, and I ill have mercy on her to hom no mercy as given; and I ill say to those ho ere not my people, You are my people, and they ill say, My God.

And the Lord said to me, Give your love again to a oman ho has a lover and is false to her husband, even as the Lord has love for the children of Israel, though they are turned to other gods and are lovers of grape-cakes.
So I got her for myself for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a half of barley;
And I said to her, You are to be mine for a long space of time; you are not to be false to me, and no other man is to have you for his ife; and so ill I be to you.
For the children of Israel ill for a long time be ithout king and ithout ruler, ithout offerings and ithout pillars, and ithout ephod or images.
And after that, the children of Israel ill come back and go in search of the Lord their God and David their king; and they ill come in fear to the Lord and to his mercies in the days to come.
Give ear to the ord of the Lord, O children of Israel; for the Lord has a cause against the people of this land, because there is no good faith in it, and no mercy and no knoledge of God in the land.
There is cursing and broken faith, violent death and attacks on property, men are untrue in married life, houses are broken into, and there is blood touching blood.
Because of this the land ill be dry, and everyone living in it ill be asted aay, ith the beasts of the field and the birds of heaven; even the fishes of the sea ill be taken aay.
Let no man go to la or make protests, for your people are like those ho go to la ith a priest.
You ill not be able to keep on your feet by day, and by night the prophet ill be falling don ith you, and I ill give your mother to destruction.

Destruction has overtaken my people because they have no knoledge; because you have given up knoledge, I ill give you up, so that you ill be no priest to me, because you have not kept in mind the la of your God, I ill not keep your children in my memory.
Even hile they ere increasing in number they ere sinning against me; I ill let their glory be changed into shame.
The sin of my people is like food to them; and their desire is for their rongdoing.
And the priest ill be like the people; I ill give them punishment for their evil ays, and the reard of their acts.
They ill have food, but they ill not be full; they ill be false to me, but they ill not be increased, because they no longer give thought to the Lord.
Loose ays and ne ine take aay isdom.
My people get knoledge from their tree, and their rod gives them nes; for a false spirit is the cause of their andering, and they have been false to their God.

They make offerings on the tops of mountains, burning perfumes in high places, under trees of every sort, because their shade is good: and so your daughters are given up to loose ays and your brides are false to their husbands.

I ill not give punishment to your daughters or your brides for their evil behaviour; for they make themselves separate ith loose omen, and make offerings ith those ho are used for sex purposes in the orship of the gods: the people ho have no isdom ill be sent aay.
Do not you, O Israel, come into error; do not you, O Judah, come to Gilgal, or go up to Beth-aven, or take an oath, By the living Lord.
For Israel is uncontrolled, like a co hich may not be controlled; no ill the Lord give them food like a lamb in a ide place.
Ephraim is joined to false gods; let him be.
Their drink has become bitter; they are completely false; her rulers take pleasure in shame.
They are folded in the skirts of the ind; they ill be shamed because of their offerings.
Give ear to this, O priests; give attention, O Israel, and you, family of the king; for you are to be judged; you have been a deceit at Mizpah and a net stretched out on Tabor.
They have gone deep in the evil ays of Shittim, but I am the judge of all.
I have knoledge of Ephraim, and Israel is not secret from me; for no, O Ephraim, you have been false to me, Israel has become unclean.
Their orks ill not let them come back to their God, for a false spirit is in them and they have no knoledge of the Lord.
And the pride of Israel gives an anser to his face; and Ephraim ill have a fall through his sins, and the fall of Judah ill be the same as theirs.
They ill go, ith their flocks and their herds, in search of the Lord, but they ill not see him; he has taken himself out of their vie.
They have been false to the Lord; they have given birth to strange children; no the ne moon ill make them aste ith their fields.
Let the horn be sounded in Gibeah and in Ramah; give a loud cry in Beth-aven, They are after you, O Benjamin.
Ephraim ill become a aste in the day of punishment; I have given knoledge among the tribes of Israel of hat is certain.
The rulers of Judah are like those ho take aay a landmark; I ill let loose my rath on them like floing ater.
Ephraim is troubled; he is crushed by his judges, because he took pleasure in alking after deceit.
And so to Ephraim I am like a asting insect, and a destruction to the children of Judah.
When Ephraim sa his disease and Judah his ound, then Ephraim ent to Assyria and sent to the great king; but he is not able to make you ell or give you help for your ound.
For I ill be to Ephraim as a lion, and as a young lion to the children of Judah; I, even I, ill give him ounds and go aay; I ill take him aay, and there ill be no helper.
I ill go back to my place till they are made aste; in their trouble they ill go after me early and ill make search for me.
Come, let us go back to the Lord; for he has given us ounds and he ill make us ell; he has given blos and he ill give help.
After to days he ill give us life, and on the third day he ill make us get up, and e ill be living before him.

And let us have knoledge, let us go after the knoledge of the Lord; his going out is certain as the dan, his decisions go out like the light; he ill come to us like the rain, like the spring rain atering the earth.
O Ephraim, hat am I to do to you? O Judah, hat am I to do to you? For your love is like a morning cloud, and like the de hich goes early aay.
So I have had it cut in stones; I gave them teaching by the ords of my mouth;
Because my desire is for mercy and not offerings; for the knoledge of God more than for burned offerings.
But like a man, they have gone against the agreement; there they ere false to me.
Gilead is a ton of evil-doers, marked ith blood.
And like a band of thieves aiting for a man, so are the priests atching secretly the ay of those going quickly to Shechem, for they are orking ith an evil design.
In Israel I have seen a very evil thing; there false ays are seen in Ephraim, Israel is unclean;
And Judah has put up disgusting images for himself.

When my desire as for the fate of my people to be changed and to make Israel ell, then the sin of Ephraim as made clear, and the evil-doing of Samaria; for their ays are false, and the thief comes into the house, hile the band of outlas takes property by force in the streets.
And they do not say to themselves that I keep in mind all their sin; no their evil acts come round them on every side; they are before my face.
In their sin they make a king for themselves, and rulers in their deceit.
They are all untrue; they are like a burning oven; the bread-maker does not make up the fire from the time hen the paste is mixed till it is leavened.
On the day of our king, the rulers made him ill ith the heat of ine; his hand as stretched out ith the men of pride.
For they have made their hearts ready like an oven, hile they are aiting secretly; their rath is sleeping all night; in the morning it is burning like a flaming fire.
They are all heated like an oven, and they put an end to their judges; all their kings have been made lo; not one among them makes prayer to me.
Ephraim is mixed ith the peoples; Ephraim is a cake not turned.
Men from other lands have made aste his strength, and he is not conscious of it; grey hairs have come on him here and there, and he has no knoledge of it.
And the pride of Israel gives an anser to his face; but for all this, they have not gone back to the Lord their God, or made search for him.
And Ephraim is like a foolish dove, ithout isdom; they send out their cry to Egypt, they go to Assyria.
When they go, my net ill be stretched out over them; I ill take them like the birds of heaven, I ill give them punishment, I ill take them aay in the net for their sin.
May trouble be theirs! for they have gone far aay from me; and destruction, for they have been sinning against me; I as ready to be their saviour, but they said false ords against me.
And they have not made prayer to me in their hearts, but they make loud cries on their beds; they are cutting themselves for food and ine, they are turned against me.
Though I have given training and strength to their arms, they have evil designs against me.
They have gone to hat is of no value; they are like a false bo; their captains ill come to destruction by the sord, and their ruler by my rath; for this, the land of Egypt ill make sport of them.
Put the horn to your mouth. He comes like an eagle against the house of the Lord; because they have gone against my agreement, they have not kept my la.
They ill send up to me a cry for help: We, Israel, have knoledge of you, O God of Israel.
Israel has given up hat is good; his haters ill go after him.
They have put up kings, but not by me; they have made princes, but I had no knoledge of it; they have made images of silver and gold, so that they may be cut off.
I ill have nothing to do ith your young ox, O Samaria; my rath is burning against them; ho long ill it be before the children of Israel make themselves clean?
The orkman made it, it is no god; the ox of Samaria ill be broken into bits.
For they have been planting the ind, and their fruit ill be the storm; his grain has no stem, it ill give no meal, and if it does, a strange nation ill take it.
Israel has come to destruction; no they are among the nations like a cup in hich there is no pleasure.
For they have gone up to Assyria like an ass going by himself; Ephraim has given money to get lovers.
But though they give money to the nations for help, still I ill send them in all directions; and in a short time they ill be ithout a king and rulers.
Because Ephraim has been increasing altars for sin, altars have become a cause of sin to him.
Though I put my la in riting for him in ten thousand rules, they are to him as a strange thing.

He gives the offerings of his lovers, and takes the flesh for food; but the Lord has no pleasure in them; no he ill keep in mind their evil-doing and give them the punishment of their sins; they ill go back to Egypt.
For Israel has no memory of his Maker, and has put up the houses of kings; and Judah has made great the number of his alled tons. But I ill send a fire on his tons and put an end to his great houses.
Have no joy, O Israel, and do not be glad like the nations; for you have been untrue to your God; your desire has been for the loose oman’s reard on every grain-floor.
The grain-floor and the place here the grapes are crushed ill not give them food; there ill be no ne ine for them.
They ill have no resting-place in the Lord’s land, but Ephraim ill go back to Egypt, and they ill take unclean food in Assyria.

They ill give no ine offering to the Lord, they ill not make offerings ready for him; their bread ill be like the bread of those in sorro; all ho take it ill be unclean, because their bread ill be only for their desire, it ill not come into the house of the Lord.
What ill you do on the day of orship, and on the day of the feast of the Lord?

For see, they are going aay into Assyria; Egypt ill get them together, Memphis ill be their last resting-place; their fair silver vessels ill be covered over ith field plants, and thorns ill come up in their tents.
The days of punishment, the days of reard are come; Israel ill be put to shame; the prophet is foolish, the man ho has the spirit is off his head, because of your great sin.
There is great hate against the atchman of Ephraim, the people of my God; as for the prophet, there is a net in all his ays, and hate in the house of his God.
They have gone deep in evil as in the days of Gibeah; he ill keep in mind their rongdoing, he ill give them punishment for their sins.

I made discovery of Israel as of grapes in the aste land; I sa your fathers as the first-fruits of the fig-tree in her early fruit time; but they came to Baal-peor, and made themselves holy to the thing of shame, and became disgusting like that to hich they gave their love.
As for Ephraim, their glory ill go in flight like a bird: there ill be no birth and no one ith child and no giving of life.
Even though their children have come to groth I ill take them aay, so that not a man ill be there; for their evil-doing ill be complete and they ill be put to shame because of it.
As I have seen a beast hose young have been taken from her, so Ephraim ill give birth to children only for them to be put to death.
O Lord, hat ill you give them? Give them bodies hich may not give birth and breasts ithout milk.
All their evil-doing is in Gilgal; there I had hate for them; because of their evil-doing I ill send them out of my house; they ill no longer be dear to me; all their rulers are uncontrolled.
The rod has come on Ephraim, their root is dry, let them have no fruit; even though they give birth, I ill put to death the dearest fruit of their bodies.
My God ill give them up because they did not give ear to him; they ill be andering among the nations.
Israel is a branching vine, full of fruit; as his fruit is increased, so the number of his altars is increased; as the land is fair, so they have made fair pillars.
Their mind is taken aay; no they ill be made aste: he ill have their altars broken don, he ill give their pillars to destruction.
No, truly, they ill say, We have no king, e have no fear of the Lord; and the king, hat is he able to do for us?
Their ords are foolish; they make agreements ith false oaths, so punishment ill come up like a poison-plant in a ploughed field.
The people of Samaria ill be full of fear because of the ox of Beth-aven; its people ill have sorro for it, and its priests ill give cries of grief for its glory, for the glory has gone in flight.
And they ill take it to Assyria and give it to the great king; shame ill come on Ephraim, and Israel ill be shamed because of its image.
As for Samaria, her king is cut off, like mist on the ater.

And the high places of Aven, the sin of Israel, ill come to destruction; thorns and aste plants ill come up on their altars; they ill say to the mountains, Be a cover over us; and to the hills, Come don on us.
O Israel, you have done evil from the days of Gibeah; there they took up their position, so that the fighting against the children of evil might not overtake them in Gibeah.
I ill come and give them punishment; and the peoples ill come together against them hen I give them the reard of their to sins.

And Ephraim is a trained co, taking pleasure in crushing the grain; but I have put a yoke on her fair neck; I ill put a horseman on the back of Ephraim; Judah ill be orking the plough, Jacob ill be turning up the earth.

Put in the seed of righteousness, get in your grain in mercy, let your unploughed earth be turned up: for it is time to make search for the Lord, till he comes and sends righteousness on you like rain.
You have been ploughing sin, you have got in a store of evil, the fruit of deceit has been your food: for you put faith in your ay, in the number of your men of ar.

So a great outcry ill go up from among your people, and all your strong places ill be broken, as Beth-arbel as broken by Shalman in the day of ar, as the mother as broken on the rocks ith her children.
So ill Beth-el do to you because of your evil-doing; at dan ill the king of Israel be cut off completely.
When Israel as a child he as dear to me; and I took my son out of Egypt.
When I sent for them, then they ent aay from me; they made offerings to the Baals, burning perfumes to images.
But I as guiding Ephraim’s footsteps; I took them up in my arms, but they ere not conscious that I as ready to make them ell.
I made them come after me ith the cords of a man, ith the bands of love; I as to them as one ho took the yoke from off their mouths, putting meat before them.
He ill go back to the land of Egypt and the Assyrian ill be his king, because they ould not come back to me.
And the sord ill go through his tons, asting his children and causing destruction because of their evil designs.
My people are given up to sinning against me; though their voice goes up on high, no one ill be lifting them up.
Ho may I give you up, O Ephraim? ho may I be your saviour, O Israel? ho may I make you like Admah? ho may I do to you as I did to Zeboim? My heart is turned in me, it is soft ith pity.
I ill not put into effect the heat of my rath; I ill not again send destruction on Ephraim; for I am God and not man, the Holy One among you; I ill not put an end to you.
They ill go after the Lord; his cry ill be like that of a lion; his cry ill be loud, and the children ill come from the est, shaking ith fear;
Shaking ith fear like a bird, they ill come out of Egypt, like a dove out of the land of Assyria: and I ill give them rest in their houses, says the Lord.
The deceit of Ephraim and the false ords of Israel are about me on every side. ...
Ephraim’s food is the ind, and he goes after the east ind: deceit and destruction are increasing day by day; they make an agreement ith Assyria, and take oil into Egypt.
The Lord has a cause against Judah, and ill give punishment to Jacob for his ays; he ill give him the reard of his acts.
In the body of his mother he took his brother by the foot, and in his strength he as fighting ith God;
He had a fight ith the angel and overcame him; he made request for grace to him ith eeping; he came face to face ith him in Beth-el and there his ords came to him;
Even the Lord, the God of armies; the Lord is his name.
So then, come back to your God; keep mercy and right, and be aiting at all times on your God.
As for Canaan, the scales of deceit are in his hands; he takes pleasure in tisted ays.
And Ephraim said, No I have got ealth and much property; in all my orks no sin may be seen in me.
But I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt; I ill give you tents for your living-places again as in the days of the holy meeting.
My ord came to the ears of the prophets and I gave them visions in great number, and by the mouths of the prophets I made use of comparisons.
In Gilead there is evil. They are quite ithout value; in Gilgal they make offerings of oxen; truly their altars are like masses of stones in the hollos of a ploughed field.
And Jacob ent in flight into the field of Aram, and Israel became a servant for a ife, and for a ife he kept sheep.
And by a prophet the Lord made Israel come up out of Egypt, and by a prophet he as kept safe.
I have been bitterly moved to rath by Ephraim; so that his blood ill be on him, and the Lord ill make his shame come back on him.
When the ords of my la came from Ephraim, he as lifted up in Israel; but hen he did evil through the Baal, death overtook him.

And no their sins are increased; they have made themselves a metal image, false gods from their silver, after their designs, all of them the ork of the metal-orkers; they say of them, Let them give offerings, let men give kisses to the oxen.
So they ill be like the morning cloud, like the de hich goes early aay, like the dust of the grain hich the ind is driving out of the crushing-floor, like smoke going up from the fireplace.
But I am the Lord your God, from the land of Egypt; you have knoledge of no other God and there is no saviour but me.
I had knoledge of you in the aste land here no ater as.
When I gave them food they ere full, and their hearts ere full of pride, and they did not keep me in mind.
So I ill be like a lion to them; as a cruel beast I ill keep atch by the road;

I ill come face to face ith them like a bear hose young ones have been taken from her, and their inmost hearts ill be broken; there the dogs ill make a meal of them; they ill be ounded by the beasts of the field.
I have sent destruction on you, O Israel; ho ill be your helper?
Where is your king, that he may be your saviour? and all your rulers, that they may take up your cause? of hom you said, Give me a king and rulers.
I have given you a king, because I as angry, and have taken him aay in my rath.
The rongdoing of Ephraim is shut up; his sin is put aay in secret.
The pains of a oman in childbirth ill come on him: he is an unise son, for at this time it is not right for him to keep his place hen children come to birth.

I ill give the price to make them free from the poer of the underorld, I ill be their saviour from death: O death! here are your pains? O underorld! here is your destruction? my eyes ill have no pity.

Though he gives fruit among his brothers, an east ind ill come, the ind of the Lord coming up from the aste land, and his spring ill become dry, his fountain ill be ithout ater: it ill make aste the store of all the vessels of his desire.
Samaria ill be made aste, for she has gone against her God: they ill be cut don by the sord, their little children ill be broken on the rocks, their omen ho are ith child ill be cut open.
O Israel, come back to the Lord your God; for your evil-doing has been the cause of your fall.
Take ith you ords, and come back to the Lord; say to him, Let there be forgiveness for all rongdoing, so that e may take hat is good, and give in payment the fruit of our lips.
Assyria ill not be our salvation; e ill not go on horses; e ill not again say to the ork of our hands, You are our gods; for in you there is mercy for the child ho has no father.
I ill put right their errors; freely ill my love be given to them, for my rath is turned aay from him.
I ill be as the de to Israel; he ill put out floers like a lily, and send out his roots like Lebanon.
His branches ill be stretched out, he ill be beautiful as the olive-tree and seet-smelling as Lebanon.
They ill come back and have rest in his shade; their life ill be made ne like the grain, and they ill put out floers like the vine; his name ill be like the ine of Lebanon.
As for Ephraim, hat has he to do ith false gods any longer? I have given an anser and I ill keep atch over him; I am like a branching fir-tree, from me comes your fruit.
He ho is ise ill see these things; he ho has good sense ill have knoledge of them. For the ays of the Lord are straight, and the upright ill go in them, but sinners ill be falling in them.
The ord of the Lord hich came to Joel, the son of Pethuel.
Give ear to this, you old men, and take note, you people of the land. Has this ever been in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
Give the story of it to your children, and let them give it to their children, and their children to another generation.

What the orm did not make a meal of, has been taken by the locust; and hat the locust did not take, has been food for the plant-orm; and hat the plant-orm did not take, has been food for the field-fly.
Come out of your sleep, you ho are overcome ith ine, and give yourselves to eeping; give cries of sorro, all you drinkers of ine, because of the seet ine; for it has been cut off from your mouths.
For a nation has come up over my land, strong and ithout number; his teeth are the teeth of a lion, and he has the back teeth of a great lion.
By him my vine is made aste and my fig-tree broken: he has taken all its fruit and sent it don to the earth; its branches are made hite.
Make sounds of grief like a virgin dressed in haircloth for the husband of her early years.
The meal offering and the drink offering have been cut off from the house of the Lord; the priests, the Lord’s servants, are sorroing.
The fields are asted, the land has become dry; for the grain is asted, the ne ine is kept back, the oil is poor.
The farmers are shamed, the orkers in the vine-gardens give cries of grief, for the heat and the barley; for the produce of the fields has come to destruction.
The vine has become dry and the fig-tree is feeble; the pomegranate and the palm-tree and the apple-tree, even all the trees of the field, are dry: because joy has gone from the sons of men.

Put haircloth round you and give yourselves to sorro, you priests; give cries of grief, you servants of the altar: come in, and, clothed in haircloth, let the night go past, you servants of my God: for the meal offering and the drink offering have been kept back from the house of your God.
Let a time be fixed for going ithout food, have a holy meeting, let the old men, even all the people of the land, come together to the house of the Lord your God, crying out to the Lord.
Sorro for the day! for the day of the Lord is near, and as destruction from the Ruler of all it ill come.
Is not food cut off before our eyes? joy and delight from the house of our God?
The grains have become small and dry under the spade; the store-houses are made aste, the grain-stores are broken don; for the grain is dry and dead.
What sounds of pain come from the beasts! the herds of cattle are at a loss because there is no grass for them; even the flocks of sheep are no longer to be seen.
O Lord, my cry goes up to you: for fire has put an end to the grass-lands of the aste, and all the trees of the field are burned ith its flame.
The beasts of the field are turning to you ith desire: for the ater-streams are dry and fire has put an end to the grass-lands of the aste.
Let the horn be sounded in Zion, and a ar-cry in my holy mountain; let all the people of the land be troubled: for the day of the Lord is coming;

For a day of dark and deep shade is near, a day of cloud and black night: like a black cloud a great and strong people is covering the mountains; there has never been any like them and ill not be after them again, from generation to generation.
Before them fire sends destruction, and after them flame is burning: the land is like the garden of Eden before them, and after them an unpeopled aste; truly, nothing has been kept safe from them.
Their form is like the form of horses, and they are running like ar-horses.
Like the sound of ar-carriages they go jumping on the tops of the mountains; like the noise of a flame of fire burning up the grain-stems, like a strong people lined up for the fight.
At their coming the people are bent ith pain: all faces become red together.
They are running like strong men, they go over the all like men of ar; every man goes straight on his ay, their lines are not broken.
No one is pushing against another; everyone goes straight on his ay: bursting through the sord points, their order is not broken.
They make a rush on the ton, running on the all; they go up into the houses and in through the indos like a thief.
The earth is troubled before them and the heavens are shaking: the sun and the moon have become dark, and the stars keep back their shining:

And the Lord is thundering before his forces; for very great is his army; for he is strong ho gives effect to his ord: for the day of the Lord is great and greatly to be feared, and ho has strength against it?
But even no, says the Lord, come back to me ith all your heart, keeping from food, ith eeping and ith sorro:

Let your hearts be broken, and not your clothing, and come back to the Lord your God: for he is full of grace and pity, slo to be angry and great in mercy, ready to be turned from his purpose of punishment.
May it not be that he ill again let his purpose be changed and let a blessing come after him, even a meal offering and a drink offering for the Lord your God?
Let a horn be sounded in Zion, let a time be fixed for going ithout food, have a holy meeting:

Get the people together, make the mass of the people holy, send for the old men, get together the children and babies at the breast: let the nely married man come out of his room and the bride from her tent.

Let the priests, the servants of the Lord, be eeping beteen the covered ay and the altar, and let them say, Have mercy on your people, O Lord, do not give up your heritage to shame, so that the nations become their rulers: hy let them say among the peoples, Where is their God?
Then the Lord had a care for the honour of his land and had pity on his people.
And the Lord made anser and said to his people, See, I ill send you grain and ine and oil in full measure: and I ill no longer let you be shamed among the nations:
