I ill send the one from the north far aay from you, driving him into a dry and aste land, ith his front to the sea of the east and his back to the sea of the est, and the smell of him ill go up, even his evil smell ill go up.
Have no fear, O land; be glad ith great joy; for the Lord has done great things.
Have no fear, you beasts of the field, for the grass-lands of the aste are becoming green, for the trees are producing fruit, the fig-tree and the vine give out their strength.
Be glad, then, you children of Zion, and have joy in the Lord your God: for he gives you food in full measure, making the rain come don for you, the early and the late rain as at the first.
And the floors ill be full of grain, and the crushing-places overfloing ith ine and oil.
I ill give back to you the years hich ere food for the locust, the plant-orm, the field-fly, and the orm, my great army hich I sent among you.
You ill have food in full measure, and give praise to the name of the Lord your God, ho has done onders for you:
And you ill be certain that I am in Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and there is no other: and my people ill never be shamed.

And after that, it ill come about, says the Lord, that I ill send my spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters ill be prophets, your old men ill have dreams, your young men ill see visions:
And on the servants and the servant-girls in those days I ill send my spirit.
And I ill let onders be seen in the heavens and on the earth, blood and fire and pillars of smoke.
The sun ill be made dark and the moon turned to blood, before the great day of the Lord comes, a day to be feared.

And it ill be that hoever makes his prayer to the name of the Lord ill be kept safe: for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem some ill be kept safe, as the Lord has said, and ill be among the small band marked out by the Lord.
For in those days and in that time, hen I let the fate of Judah and Jerusalem be changed,

I ill get together all the nations, and make them come don into the valley of Jehoshaphat; and there I ill take up ith them the cause of my people and of my heritage Israel, hom they have sent andering among the nations, and of my land hich has been parted by them.
And they have put the fate of my people to the decision of chance: giving a boy for the price of a loose oman and a girl for a drink of ine.
And further, hat are you to me, O Tyre and Zidon and all the circle of Philistia? ill you give me back any payment? and if you do, quickly and suddenly I ill send it back on your head,
For you have taken my silver and my gold, putting in the houses of your gods my beautiful and pleasing things.
And the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem you have given for a price to the sons of the Greeks, to send them far aay from their land:
See, I ill have them moved from the place here you have sent them, and ill let hat you have done come back on your head;
I ill give your sons and your daughters into the hands of the children of Judah for a price, and they ill give them for a price to the men of Sheba, a nation far off: for the Lord has said it.
Give this out among the nations; make ready for ar: get the strong men aake; let all the men of ar come near, let them come up.
Get your plough-blades hammered into sords, and your vine-knives into spears: let the feeble say, I am strong.
Come quickly, all you nations round about, and get yourselves together there: make your strong ones come don, O Lord.
Let the nations be aake, and come to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there I ill be seated as judge of all the nations round about.
Put in the blade, for the grain is ready: come, get you don, for the ine-crusher is full, the vessels are overfloing; for great is their evil-doing.
Masses on masses in the valley of decision! for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.
The sun and the moon have become dark, and the stars keep back their shining.

And the Lord ill be thundering from Zion, and his voice ill be sounding from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth ill be shaking: but the Lord ill be a breastplate for his people and a strong place for the children of Israel.
And you ill be certain that I am the Lord your God, living in Zion, my holy mountain: and Jerusalem ill be holy, and no strange person ill ever again go through her.

And it ill come about in that day that the mountains ill be dropping seet ine, and the hills ill be floing ith milk, and all the streams of Judah ill be floing ith ater; and a fountain ill come out from the house of the Lord, atering the valley of acacia-trees.
Egypt ill be a aste and Edom a land of destruction, because of the evil done to the children of Judah, because they have let blood be drained out in their land ithout cause.
But Judah ill be peopled for ever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
And I ill send punishment for their blood, for hich punishment has not been sent, for the Lord is living in Zion.

The ords of Amos, ho as among the herdsmen of Tekoa; hat he sa about Israel in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam, the son of Joash, king of Israel, to years before the earth-shock.
And he said, The Lord ill give a lion’s cry from Zion, his voice ill be sounding from Jerusalem; and the fields of the keepers of sheep ill become dry, and the top of Carmel ill be asted aay.
These are the ords of the Lord: For three crimes of Damascus, and for four, I ill not let its fate be changed; because they have been crushing Gilead ith iron grain-crushing instruments.
And I ill send a fire into the house of Hazael, burning up the great houses of Ben-hadad.

And I ill have the locks of the door of Damascus broken, and him ho is seated in poer cut off from the valley of Aven, and him in hose hand is the rod from the house of Eden; and the people of Aram ill go aay as prisoners into Kir, says the Lord.
These are the ords of the Lord: For three crimes of Gaza, and for four, I ill not let its fate be changed; because they took all the people aay prisoners, to give them up to Edom.
And I ill send a fire on the all of Gaza, burning up its great houses:

Him ho is seated in poer I ill have cut off from Ashdod, and him in hose hand is the rod from Ashkelon; and my hand ill be turned against Ekron, and the rest of the Philistines ill come to destruction, says the Lord God.

These are the ords of the Lord: For three crimes of Tyre, and for four, I ill not let its fate be changed; because they gave up all the people prisoners to Edom, ithout giving a thought to the brothers’ agreement beteen them.
And I ill send a fire on the all of Tyre, burning up its great houses.

These are the ords of the Lord: For three crimes of Edom, and for four, I ill not let its fate be changed; because his sord as turned against his brother, ithout pity, and his rath as burning at all times, and he as angry for ever.
And I ill send a fire on Teman, burning up the great houses of Bozrah.

These are the ords of the Lord: For three crimes of the children of Ammon, and for four, I ill not let its fate be changed; because in Gilead they had omen ith child cut open, so that they might make ider the limits of their land.
And I ill make a fire in the all of Rabbah, burning up its great houses, ith loud cries in the days of ar, ith a storm in the day of the great ind:
And their king ill be made prisoner, he and his captains together, says the Lord.
These are the ords of the Lord: For three crimes of Moab, and for four, I ill not let its fate be changed; because he had the bones of the king of Edom burned to dust.
And I ill send a fire on Moab, burning up the great houses of Kerioth: and death ill come on Moab ith noise and outcries and the sound of the horn:
And I ill have the judge cut off from among them, and all their captains I ill put to death ith him, says the Lord.

These are the ords of the Lord: For three crimes of Judah, and for four, I ill not let its fate be changed; because they have given up the la of the Lord, and have not kept his rules; and their false ays, in hich their fathers ent, have made them go out of the right ay.
And I ill send a fire on Judah, burning up the great houses of Jerusalem.

These are the ords of the Lord: For three crimes of Israel, and for four, I ill not let its fate be changed; because they have given the upright man for silver, and the poor for the price of to shoes;
Crushing the head of the poor, and turning the steps of the gentle out of the ay: and a man and his father go in to the same young oman, putting shame on my holy name:
By every altar they are stretched on clothing taken from those ho are in their debt, drinking in the house of their god the ine of those ho have made payment for rongdoing.
Though I sent destruction on the Amorite before them, ho as tall as the cedar and strong as the oak-tree, cutting off his fruit from on high and his roots from under the earth.
And I took you up out of the land of Egypt, guiding you for forty years in the aste land, so that you might take for your heritage the land of the Amorite.
And some of your sons I made prophets, and some of your young men I made separate for myself. Is it not even so, O children of Israel? says the Lord.
But to those ho ere separate you gave ine for drink; and to the prophets you said, Be prophets no longer.
See, I am crushing you don, as one is crushed under a cart full of grain.
And flight ill be impossible for the quick-footed, and the force of the strong ill become feeble, and the man of ar ill not get aay safely:
And the boman ill not keep his place; he ho is quick-footed ill not get aay safely: and the horseman ill not keep his life.
And he ho is ithout fear among the fighting men ill go in flight ithout his clothing in that day, says the Lord.
Give ear to this ord hich the Lord has said against you, O children of Israel, against all the family hich I took up out of the land of Egypt, saying,
You only of all the families of the earth have I taken care of: for this reason I ill send punishment on you for all your sins.
Is it possible for to to go alking together, if not by agreement?
Will a lion give his loud cry in the oodland hen no food is there? ill the voice of the young lion be sounding from his hole if he has taken nothing?
Is it possible for a bird to be taken in a net on the earth here no net has been put for him? ill the net come up from the earth if it has taken nothing at all?
If the horn is sounded in the ton ill the people not be full of fear? ill evil come on a ton if the Lord has not done it?
Certainly the Lord ill do nothing ithout making clear his secret to his servants, the prophets.
The cry of the lion is sounding; ho ill not have fear? The Lord God has said the ord; is it possible for the prophet to keep quiet?
Give out the nes in the great houses of Assyria and in the land of Egypt, and say, Come together on the mountains of Samaria, and see hat great outcries are there, and hat cruel acts are done in it.
For they have no knoledge of ho to do hat is right, says the Lord, ho are storing up violent acts and destruction in their great houses.
For this reason, says the Lord, an attacker ill come, shutting in the land on every side; and your strength ill come don and your great houses ill be made aste.

These are the ords of the Lord: As the keeper of sheep takes out of the mouth of the lion to legs or part of an ear; so ill the children of Israel be made safe, ho are resting in Samaria on seats of honour or on the silk cushions of a bed.
Give ear no, and give itness against the family of Jacob, says the Lord God, the God of armies;
For in the day hen I give Israel punishment for his sins, I ill send punishment on the altars of Beth-el, and the horns of the altar ill be cut off and come don to the earth.
And I ill send destruction on the inter house ith the summer house; the ivory houses ill be falling don and the great houses ill come to an end, says the Lord.
Give ear to this ord, you cos of Bashan, ho are in the hill of Samaria, by hom the poor are kept don, and those in need are crushed; ho say to their lords, Get out the ine and give us drink.
The Lord God has taken an oath by his holy name, that the days are coming hen they ill take you aay ith hooks, and the rest of you ith fish-hooks.
And you ill go out through the broken places, every one going straight before her, and you ill be sent into Harmon, says the Lord.
Come to Beth-el and do evil; to Gilgal, increasing the number of your sins; come ith your offerings every morning and your tenths every three days:
Let that hich is leavened be burned as a praise-offering, let the nes of your free offerings be given out publicly; for this is pleasing to you, O children of Israel, says the Lord.
But in all your tons I have kept food from your teeth, and in all your places there has been need of bread: and still you have not come back to me, says the Lord.

And I have kept back the rain from you, hen it as still three months before the grain-cutting: I sent rain on one ton and kept it back from another: one part as rained on, and the part here there as no rain became a aste.
So to or three tons ent andering to one ton looking for ater, and did not get enough: and still you have not come back to me, says the Lord.

I have sent destruction on your fields by burning and disease: the increase of your gardens and your vine-gardens, your fig-trees and your olive-trees, has been food for orms: and still you have not come back to me, says the Lord.

I have sent disease among you, as it as in Egypt: I have put your young men to the sord, and have taken aay your horses; I have made the evil smell from your tents come up to your noses: and still you have not come back to me, says the Lord.

And I have sent destruction among you, as hen God sent destruction on Sodom and Gomorrah, and you ere like a burning stick pulled out of the fire: and still you have not come back to me, says the Lord.
So this is hat I ill do to you, O Israel: and because I ill do this to you, be ready for a meeting ith your God, O Israel.

For see, he ho gave form to the mountains and made the ind, giving knoledge of his purpose to man, ho makes the morning dark, and is alking on the high places of the earth: the Lord, the God of armies, is his name.
Give ear to this ord, my song of sorro over you, O children of Israel.
The virgin of Israel has been made lo, never again to be lifted up: she is stretched out by herself on her land; there is no one to put her on her feet again.
For these are the ords of the Lord God: The ton hich as able to send out a thousand, ill have only a hundred; and that hich sent out a hundred, ill have only ten, in Israel.
For these are the ords of the Lord to the children of Israel: Let your hearts be turned to me, so that you may have life:
Do not be looking for help to Beth-el, and do not go to Gilgal, or make your ay to Beer-sheba: for Gilgal ill certainly be taken prisoner, and Beth-el ill come to nothing.
Go to the Lord for help so that you may have life; for fear that he may come like fire bursting out in the family of Joseph, causing destruction, and there ill be no one to put it out in Beth-el.
You ho make the ork of judging a bitter thing, crushing don righteousness to the earth;

Go for help to him ho makes Orion and the Pleiades, by hom the deep dark is turned into morning, ho makes the day black ith night; hose voice goes out to the aters of the sea, sending them out over the face of the earth: the Lord is his name;
Who sends sudden destruction on the strong, so that destruction comes on the alled ton.
They have hate for him ho makes protest against evil in the public place, and he hose ords are upright is disgusting to them.

So because the poor man is crushed under your feet, and you take taxes from him of grain: you have made for yourselves houses of cut stone, but you ill not take your rest in them; the fair vine-gardens planted by your hands ill not give you ine.
For I have seen ho your evil-doing is increased and ho strong are your sins, you troublers of the upright, ho take reards and do rong to the cause of the poor in the public place.
So the ise ill say nothing in that time; for it is an evil time.
Go after good and not evil, so that life may be yours: and so the Lord, the God of armies, ill be ith you, as you say.
Be haters of evil and lovers of good, and let right be done in the public place: it may be that the Lord, the God of armies, ill have mercy on the rest of Joseph.

So these are the ords of the Lord, the God of armies, the Lord: There ill be eeping in all the open spaces; and in all the streets they ill say, Sorro! sorro! and they ill get in the farmer to the eeping, and the makers of sad songs to give cries of grief.
In all the vine-gardens there ill be cries of grief: for I ill go through among you, says the Lord.
Sorro to you ho are looking for the day of the Lord! hat is the day of the Lord to you? it is dark and not light.
As if a man, running aay from a lion, came face to face ith a bear; or ent into the house and put his hand on the all and got a bite from a snake.
Will not the day of the Lord be dark and not light? even very dark, ith no light shining in it?
Your feasts are disgusting to me, I ill have nothing to do ith them; I ill take no delight in your holy meetings.
Even if you give me your burned offerings and your meal offerings, I ill not take pleasure in them: I ill have nothing to do ith the peace-offerings of your fat beasts.
Take aay from me the noise of your songs; my ears are shut to the melody of your instruments.
But let the right go rolling on like aters, and righteousness like an ever-floing stream.
Did you come to me ith offerings of beasts and meal offerings in the aste land for forty years, O Israel?
Truly, you ill take up Saccuth your king and Kaian your images, the star of your god, hich you made for yourselves.
And I ill send you aay as prisoners farther than Damascus, says the Lord, hose name is the God of armies.
Sorro to those ho are resting in comfort in Zion, and to those ho have no fear of danger in the mountain of Samaria, the noted men of the chief of the nations, to hom the people of Israel come!
Go on to Calneh and see; and from there go to Hamath the great; then go don to Gath of the Philistines: are you better than these kingdoms? or is your land ider than theirs?
You ho put far aay the evil day, causing the rule of the violent to come near;
Who are resting on beds of ivory, stretched out on soft seats, feasting on lambs from the flock and young oxen from the cattle-house;
Making foolish songs to the sound of corded instruments, and designing for themselves instruments of music, like David;
Drinking ine in basins, rubbing themselves ith the best oils; but they have no grief for the destruction of Joseph.
So no they ill go aay prisoners ith the first of those ho are made prisoners, and the loud cry of those ho ere stretched out ill come to an end.

The Lord God has taken an oath by himself, says the Lord, the God of armies: the pride of Jacob is disgusting to me, and I have hate for his great houses: so I ill give up the ton ith everything in it.
Then it ill come about that if there are still ten men in a house, death ill overtake them.

And hen a man’s relation, even the one ho is responsible for burning his body, lifting him up to take his bones out of the house, says to him ho is in the inmost part of the house, Is there still anyone ith you? and he says, No; then he ill say, Keep quiet, for the name of the Lord may not be named.
For see, at the order of the Lord the great house ill be full of cracks and the little house ill be broken.
Is it possible for horses to go running on the rock? may the sea be ploughed ith oxen? for the right to be turned by you into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into a bitter plant?
You hose joy is in a thing of no value, ho say, Have e not taken for ourselves horns by the strength hich is ours?
For see, I ill send against you a nation, O Israel, says the Lord, the God of armies, ruling you cruelly from the ay into Hamath as far as the stream of the Arabah.
This is hat the Lord God let me see: and I sa that, hen the groth of the late grass as starting, he made locusts; it as the late groth after the king’s cutting as done.
And it came about that after they had taken all the grass of the land, I said, O Lord God, have mercy: ho ill Jacob be able to keep his place? for he is small.
The Lord, changing his purpose about this, said, It ill not be.

This is hat the Lord let me see: and I sa that the Lord God sent for a great fire to be the instrument of his punishment; and, after burning up the great deep, it as about to put an end to the Lord’s heritage.
Then said I, O Lord God, let there be an end: ho ill Jacob be able to keep his place? for he is small.
The Lord, changing his purpose about this, said, And this ill not be.
This is hat he let me see: and I sa the Lord stationed by a all made straight by a eighted line, and he had a eighted line in his hand.
And the Lord said to me, Amos, hat do you see? And I said, A eighted line. Then the Lord said, See, I ill let don a eighted line among my people Israel; never again ill my eyes be shut to their sin:
And the high places of Isaac ill be unpeopled, and the holy places of Israel ill be made aste; and I ill come up against the family of Jeroboam ith the sord.
Then Amaziah, the priest of Beth-el, sent to Jeroboam, king of Israel, saying, Amos has made designs against you among the people of Israel: the land is troubled by his ords.
For Amos has said, Jeroboam ill be put to the sord, and Israel ill certainly be taken aay as a prisoner out of his land.
And Amaziah said to Amos, O seer, go in flight into the land of Judah, and there get your living by orking as a prophet:
But be a prophet no longer at Beth-el: for it is the holy place of the king, and the king’s house.
Then Amos in anser said to Amaziah, I am no prophet, or one of the sons of the prophets; I am a herdman and one ho takes care of sycamore-trees:
And the Lord took me from the flock, and the Lord said to me, Go, be a prophet to my people Israel.
No then, give ear to the ord of the Lord: You say, Be no prophet to Israel, and say not a ord against the people of Isaac.

So this is hat the Lord has said: Your ife ill be a loose oman in the ton, and your sons and your daughters ill be put to the sord, and your land ill be cut up into parts by a line; and you yourself ill come to your end in an unclean land, and Israel ill certainly be taken aay a prisoner out of his land.
This is hat the Lord God let me see: and I sa a basket of summer fruit.
And he said, Amos, hat do you see? And I said, A basket of summer fruit. Then the Lord said to me, The end has come to my people Israel; never again ill my eyes be shut to their sin.
And the songs of the king’s house ill be cries of pain in that day, says the Lord God: great ill be the number of the dead bodies, and everyhere they ill put them out ithout a ord.
Give ear to this, you ho are crushing the poor, and hose purpose is to put an end to those ho are in need in the land,

Saying, When ill the ne moon be gone, so that e may do trade in grain? and the Sabbath, so that e may put out in the market the produce of our fields? making the measure small and the price great, and trading falsely ith scales of deceit;
Getting the poor for silver, and him ho is in need for the price of to shoes, and taking a price for the aste parts of the grain.
The Lord has taken an oath by the pride of Jacob, Truly I ill ever keep in mind all their orks.
Will not the land be shaking ith fear because of this, and everyone in it have sorro? and all of it ill be overfloing like the River; and it ill be troubled and go don again like the River of Egypt.
And it ill come about in that day, says the Lord God, that I ill make the sun go don in the middle of the day, and I ill make the earth dark in daylight:

Your feasts ill be turned into sorro and all your melody into songs of grief; everyone ill be clothed ith haircloth, and the hair of every head ill be cut; I ill make the eeping like that for an only son, and the end of it like a bitter day.
See, the days are coming, says the Lord God, hen I ill send times of great need on the land, not need of food or desire for ater, but for hearing the ords of the Lord.
And they ill go andering from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east, running here and there in search of the ord of the Lord, and they ill not get it.
In that day the fair virgins and the young men ill be feeble from need of ater.
Those ho make their oaths by the sin of Samaria and say, By the life of your God, O Dan; and, By the living ay of Beer-sheba; even they ill go don, never again to be lifted up.

I sa the Lord stationed by the side of the altar, giving blos to the tops of the pillars so that the doorsteps ere shaking: and he said, I ill let all of them be broken ith earth-shocks; I ill put the last of them to the sord: if any one of them goes in flight he ill not get aay, not one of them ill be safe.
Even if they go deep into the underorld, my hand ill take them up from there; if they go up to heaven, I ill get them don:

Though they take cover on the top of Carmel, I ill go in search of them and get them out; though they keep themselves from my eyes in the bed of the sea, I ill give orders to the great snake there and he ill give them a bite:
And though they are taken aay as prisoners by their attackers, even there ill I give orders to the sord to put them to death: my eyes ill be fixed on them for evil and not for good.

For the Lord, the God of armies, is he at hose touch the land is turned to ater, and everyone in it ill be given up to sorro; all of it ill be overfloing like the River, and ill go don again like the River of Egypt;
It is he ho makes his rooms in the heaven, basing his arch on the earth; hose voice goes out to the aters of the sea, and sends them floing over the face of the earth; the Lord is his name.

Are you not as the children of the Ethiopians to me, O children of Israel? says the Lord. Have I not taken Israel up out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Aramaeans from Kir?
See, the eyes of the Lord are on the evil kingdom, and I ill put an end to it in all the earth; but I ill not send complete destruction on Jacob, says the Lord.
For see, I ill give orders, and I ill have Israel moved about among all the nations, as grain is moved about by the shaking of the tray, but not the smallest seed ill be dropped on the earth.
All those sinners among my people ill be put to the sord ho say, Evil ill not overtake us or come face to face ith us.
In that day I ill put up the tent of David hich has come don, and make good its broken places; and I ill put up again his damaged alls, building it up as in the past;
So that the rest of Edom may be their heritage, and all the nations ho have been named by my name, says the Lord, ho is doing this.

See, the days ill come, says the Lord, hen the ploughman ill overtake him ho is cutting the grain, and the crusher of the grapes him ho is planting seed; and seet ine ill be dropping from the mountains, and the hills ill be turned into streams of ine.

And I ill let the fate of my people Israel be changed, and they ill be building up again the aste tons and living in them; they ill again be planting vine-gardens and taking the ine for their drink; and they ill make gardens and get the fruit of them.
And I ill have them planted in their land, and never again ill they be uprooted from their land hich I have given them, says the Lord your God.
The vision of Obadiah. This is hat the Lord has said about Edom: We have had ord from the Lord, and a representative has been sent among the nations, saying, Up! and let us make ar against her.
See, I have made you small among the nations: you are much looked don on.
You have been tricked by the pride of your heart, O you hose living-place is in the cracks of the rock, hose house is high up; ho has said in his heart, Who ill make me come don to earth?
Though you go up on high like an eagle, though your house is placed among the stars, I ill make you come don from there, says the Lord.
If thieves came, attacking you by night, ( ho are you cut off!) ould they not go on taking till they had enough? if men came cutting your grapes ould they take them all?
Ho are the things of Esau searched out! ho are his secret stores looked for!
All the men ho ere united ith you have been false to you, driving you out to the edge of the land: the men ho ere at peace ith you have overcome you; they have taken their heritage in your place.
Will I not, in that day, says the Lord, take aay the ise men out of Edom, and isdom out of the mountain of Esau?
And your men of ar, O Teman, ill be overcome ith fear, so that every one of them may be cut off from the mountain of Esau.
Because you ere the cause of violent death and because of your cruel behaviour to your brother Jacob, you ill be covered ith shame and ill be cut off for ever.
Because you ere there atching hen men from other lands took aay his goods, and strange men came into his doors, and put the fate of Jerusalem to the decision of chance; you ere like one of them.
Do not see ith pleasure your brother’s evil day, the day of his fate, and do not be glad over the children of Judah on the day of their destruction, or make ide your mouth on the day of trouble.

Do not go into the doors of my people on the day of their donfall; do not be looking on their trouble ith pleasure on the day of their donfall, or put your hands on their goods on the day of their donfall.
And do not take your place at the cross-roads, cutting off those of his people ho get aay; and do not give up to their haters those ho are still there in the day of trouble.
For the day of the Lord is coming quickly on all nations: as you have done it ill be done to you; the reard of your acts ill come on your head.

For as you have been drinking on my holy mountain, so ill all the nations go on drinking ithout end; they ill go on drinking and the ine ill go don their throats, and they ill be as if they had never been.
But in Mount Zion some ill be kept safe, and it ill be holy; and the children of Jacob ill take their heritage.

And the children of Jacob ill be a fire and those of Joseph a flame, and the children of Esau dry stems of grass, burned up by them till all is gone: and there ill be no people living in Esau; for the Lord has said it.
And they ill take the South, and the loland, and the country of Ephraim, and Gilead, as their heritage.

And those of the children of Israel ho ere the first to be taken aay as prisoners, ill have their heritage among the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and those ho ere taken aay from Jerusalem, ho are in Sepharad, ill have the tons of the South.
And those ho have been kept safe ill come up from Mount Zion to be judges of the mountain of Esau; and the kingdom ill be the Lord’s.
And the ord of the Lord came to Jonah, the son of Amittai, saying,
Up! go to Nineveh, that great ton, and let your voice come to it; for their evil-doing has come up before me.

And Jonah got up to go in flight to Tarshish, aay from the Lord; and he ent don to Joppa, and sa there a ship going to Tarshish: so he gave them the price of the journey and ent don into it to go ith them to Tarshish, aay from the Lord.
And the Lord sent out a great ind on to the sea and there as a violent storm in the sea, so that the ship seemed in danger of being broken.

Then the sailors ere full of fear, every man crying to his god; and the goods in the ship ere dropped out into the sea to make the eight less. But Jonah had gone don into the inmost part of the ship here he as stretched out in a deep sleep.
And the ship’s captain came to him and said to him, What are you doing sleeping? Up! say a prayer to your God, if by chance God ill give a thought to us, so that e may not come to destruction.
And they said to one another, Come, let us put this to the decision of chance and see on hose account this evil has come on us. So they did so, and Jonah as seen to be the man.
Then they said to him, No make clear to us hat is your ork, and here you come from? hat is your country, and ho are your people?
And he said to them, I am a Hebre, a orshipper of the Lord, the God of heaven, ho made the sea and the dry land.
And the men ere in great fear, and they said to him, What is this you have done? For the men had knoledge of his flight from the Lord because he had not kept it from them.
And they said to him, What are e to do to you so that the sea may become calm for us? For the sea as getting rougher and rougher.
And he said to them, Take me up and put me into the sea, and the sea ill become calm for you: for I am certain that because of me this great storm has come on you.
And the men ere orking hard to get back to the land, but they ere not able to do so: for the sea got rougher and rougher against them.

So, crying to the Lord, they said, Give ear to our prayer, O Lord, give ear, and do not let destruction overtake us because of this man’s life; do not put on us the sin of taking life ithout cause: for you, O Lord, have done hat seemed good to you.
So they took Jonah up and put him into the sea: and the sea as no longer angry.
Then great as the men’s fear of the Lord; and they made an offering to the Lord and took oaths to him.
And the Lord made ready a great fish to take Jonah into its mouth; and Jonah as inside the fish for three days and three nights.
Then Jonah made prayer to the Lord his God from the inside of the fish, and said,
In my trouble I as crying to the Lord, and he gave me an anser; out of the deepest underorld I sent up a cry, and you gave ear to my voice.
For you have put me don into the deep, into the heart of the sea; and the river as round about me; all your aves and your rolling aters ent over me.
And I said, I have been sent aay from before your eyes; ho may I ever again see your holy Temple?
The aters ere circling round me, even to the neck; the deep as about me; the sea-grass as tisted round my head.
I ent don to the bases of the mountains; as for the earth, her alls ere about me for ever: but you have taken up my life from the underorld, O Lord my God.
When my soul in me as overcome, I kept the memory of the Lord: and my prayer came in to you, into your holy Temple.
The orshippers of false gods have given up their only hope.
But I ill make an offering to you ith the voice of praise; I ill give effect to my oaths. Salvation is the Lord’s.
And at the Lord’s order, the fish sent Jonah out of its mouth on to the dry land.
And the ord of the Lord came to Jonah a second time, saying,
Up! go to Nineveh, that great ton, and give it the ord hich I have given you.
So Jonah got up and ent to Nineveh as the Lord had said. No Nineveh as a very great ton, three days’ journey from end to end.
And Jonah first of all ent a day’s journey into the ton, and crying out said, In forty days destruction ill overtake Nineveh.
And the people of Nineveh had belief in God; and a time as fixed for going ithout food, and they put on haircloth, from the greatest to the least.
And the ord came to the king of Nineveh, and he got up from his seat of authority, and took off his robe, and covering himself ith haircloth, took his seat in the dust.
And he had it given out in Nineveh, By the order of the king and his great men, no man or beast, herd or flock, is to have a taste of anything; let them have no food or ater:
And let man and beast be covered ith haircloth, and let them make strong prayers to God: and let everyone be turned from his evil ay and the violent acts of their hands.
Who may say that God ill not be turned, changing his purpose and turning aay from his burning rath, so that destruction may not overtake us?
And God sa hat they did, ho they ere turned from their evil ay; and God’s purpose as changed as to the evil hich he said he ould do to them, and he did it not.
But this seemed very rong to Jonah, and he as angry.

And he made prayer to the Lord and said, O Lord, is this not hat I said hen I as still in my country? This is hy I took care to go in flight to Tarshish: for I as certain that you ere a loving God, full of pity, slo to be angry and great in mercy, and ready to be turned from your purpose of evil.
So no, O Lord, give ear to my prayer and take my life from me; for death is better for me than life.
And the Lord said, Have you any right to be angry?
Then Jonah ent out of the ton, and took his seat on the east side of the ton and made himself a roof of branches and took his seat under its shade till he sa hat ould become of the ton.
And the Lord God made a vine come up over Jonah to give him shade over his head. And Jonah as very glad because of the vine.
But early on the morning after, God made ready a orm for the destruction of the vine, and it became dry and dead.

Then hen the sun came up, God sent a burning east ind: and so great as the heat of the sun on his head that Jonah as overcome, and, requesting death for himself, said, Death is better for me than life.
And the Lord said to Jonah, Have you any right to be angry about the vine? And he said, I have a right to be truly angry.
And the Lord said, You had pity on the vine, for hich you did no ork and for the groth of hich you ere not responsible; hich came up in a night and came to an end in a night;
And am I not to have mercy on Nineveh, that great ton, in hich there are more than a hundred and tenty thousand persons ithout the poer of judging beteen right and left, as ell as much cattle?
The ord of the Lord hich came to Micah the Morashtite, in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah: his vision about Samaria and Jerusalem.
Give ear, you peoples, all of you; give attention, O earth and everything in it: let the Lord God be itness against you, the Lord from his holy Temple.
For see, the Lord is coming out from his place, and ill come don, stepping on the high places of the earth.
And the mountains ill be turned to ater under him, and the deep valleys ill be broken open, like ax before the fire, like aters floing don a slope.
All this is because of the rongdoing of Jacob and the sins of the children of Israel. What is the rongdoing of Jacob? is it not Samaria? and hat are the high places of Judah? are they not Jerusalem?
So I ill make Samaria into a field and the plantings of a vine-garden: I ill send its stones falling don into the valley, uncovering its bases.

And all her pictured images ill be hammered into bits, and all the payments for her loose ays ill be burned ith fire, and all the images of her gods I ill make aste: for ith the price of a loose oman she got them together, and as the price of a loose oman ill they be given back.
For this I ill be full of sorro and give cries of grief; I ill go uncovered and unclothed: I ill give cries of grief like the jackals and ill be in sorro like the ostriches.
For her ounds may not be made ell: for it has come even to Judah, stretching up to the dooray of my people, even to Jerusalem.
Give no ord of it in Gath, let there be no eeping at all: at Beth-le-aphrah be rolling in the dust.
Be uncovered and go aay, you ho are living in Shaphir: the one living in Zaanan has not come out of her ton; Beth-ezel is taken aay from its base, even from its resting-place.
For the one living in Maroth is aiting for good: for evil has come don from the Lord to the doorays of Jerusalem.
Let the ar-carriage be yoked to the quick-running horse, you ho are living in Lachish: she as the first cause of sin to the daughter of Zion; for the rongdoings of Israel ere seen in you.
For this cause give a parting offering to Moresheth-gath: the daughter of Achzib ill be a deceit to the king of Israel.
Even no ill the taker of your heritage come to you, you ho are living in Mareshah: the glory of Israel ill come to destruction for ever.
Let your head be uncovered and your hair cut off in sorro for the children of your delight: let the hair be pulled from your head like an eagle’s; for they have been taken aay from you as prisoners.
A curse on the designers of evil, orking on their beds! in the morning light they do it, because it is in their poer.
They have a desire for fields and take them by force; and for houses and take them aay: they are cruel to a man and his family, even to a man and his heritage.
For this cause the Lord has said, See, against this family I am purposing an evil from hich you ill not be able to take your necks aay, and you ill be eighted don by it; for it is an evil time.

In that day this saying ill be said about you, and this song of grief ill be made: The heritage of my people is measured out, and there is no one to give it back; those ho have made us prisoners have taken our fields from us, and complete destruction has come to us.
For this cause you ill have no one to make the decision by the measuring line in the meeting of the Lord.
Let not ords like these be dropped, they say: Shame and the curse ill not come to the family of Jacob!
Is the Lord quickly made angry? are these his doings? do not his ords do good to his people Israel?
As for you, you have become haters of those ho ere at peace ith you: you take the clothing of those ho go by ithout fear, and make them prisoners of ar.
The omen of my people you have been driving aay from their dearly loved children; from their young ones you are taking my glory for ever.
Up! and go; for this is not your rest: because it has been made unclean, the destruction ordered ill come on you.
If a man came ith a false spirit of deceit, saying, I ill be a prophet to you of ine and strong drink: he ould be the sort of prophet for this people.

I ill certainly make all of you, O Jacob, come together; I ill get together the rest of Israel; I ill put them together like the sheep in their circle: like a flock in their green field; they ill be full of the noise of men.
The opener of the ay ill go up before them: forcing their ay out they ill go on to the dooray and out through it: their king ill go on before them, and the Lord at their head.
And I said, Give ear, no, you heads of Jacob and rulers of the people of Israel: is it not for you to have knoledge of hat is right?
You ho are haters of good and lovers of evil, pulling off their skin from them and their flesh from their bones;
Like meat they take the flesh of my people for their food, skinning them and crushing their bones, yes, cutting them up as if for the pot, like flesh inside the cooking-pot.
Then they ill be crying to the Lord for help, but he ill not give them an anser: yes, he ill keep his face veiled from them at that time, because their acts have been evil.

This is hat the Lord has said about the prophets by hom my people have been turned from the right ay; ho, biting ith their teeth, say, Peace; and if anyone puts nothing in their mouths they make ready for ar against him.
For this cause it ill be night for you, ithout a vision; and it ill be dark for you, ithout knoledge of the future; the sun ill go don over the prophets, and the day ill be black over them.
And the seers ill be shamed, and the readers of the future ill be at a loss, all of them covering their lips; for there is no anser from God.
But I truly am full of the spirit of the Lord, ith poer of judging and ith strength to make clear to Jacob his rongdoing and to Israel his sin.
Then give ear to this, you heads of the children of Jacob, you rulers of the children of Israel, hating hat is right, tisting hat is straight.
They are building up Zion ith blood, and Jerusalem ith evil-doing.

Its heads take reards for judging, and the priests take payment for teaching, and the prophets get silver for reading the future: but still, supporting themselves on the Lord, they say, Is not the Lord among us? no evil ill overtake us.
For this reason, Zion ill be ploughed like a field because of you, and Jerusalem ill become a mass of broken alls, and the mountain of the house like a high place in the oods.
But in the last days it ill come about that the mountain of the Lord’s house ill be placed on the top of the mountains, and be lifted up over the hills; and peoples ill be floing to it.

And a number of nations ill go and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he ill give us knoledge of his ays and e ill be guided by his ord: for from Zion the la ill go out, and the ord of the Lord from Jerusalem.

And he ill be judge beteen great peoples, and strong nations far aay ill be ruled by his decisions; their sords ill be hammered into plough-blades and their spears into vine-knives: nations ill no longer be lifting up their sords against one another, and knoledge of ar ill have gone for ever.
But every man ill be seated under his vine and under his fig-tree, and no one ill be a cause of fear to them: for the mouth of the Lord of armies has said it.
For all the peoples ill be alking, every one in the name of his god, and e ill be alking in the name of the Lord our God for ever and ever.
In that day, says the Lord, I ill get together her ho goes ith uncertain steps, I ill get together her ho has been sent aay, and her on hom I have sent evil;
And I ill make her hose steps ere uncertain a small band, and her ho as feeble a strong nation: and the Lord ill be their King in Mount Zion from no and for ever.
And you, O toer of the flock, Ophel of the daughter of Zion, to you it ill come, even the earlier authority, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
No hy are you crying so loudly? is there no king in you? has destruction come on your ise helper? so that pains have taken you like the pains of a oman in childbirth:

Be in pain, make sounds of grief, O daughter of Zion, like a oman in childbirth: for no you ill go out of the ton, living in the open country, and ill come even to Babylon; there you ill have salvation; there the Lord ill make you free from the hands of your haters.
And no a number of nations have come together against you, and they say, Let her be made unclean and let our eyes see the fate of Zion.
But they have no knoledge of the thoughts of the Lord, their minds are not able to see his purpose: for he has got them together like stems of grain to the crushing-floor.

Up! and let the grain be crushed, O daughter of Zion, for I ill make your horn iron and your feet brass, and a number of peoples ill be broken by you, and you ill give up their increase to the Lord and their ealth to the Lord of all the earth.
No you ill give yourselves deep ounds for grief; they ill put up a all round us: they ill give the judge of Israel a blo on the face ith a rod.

And you, Beth-lehem Ephrathah, the least among the families of Judah, out of you one ill come to me ho is to be ruler in Israel; hose going out has been purposed from time past, from the eternal days.
For this cause he ill give them up till the time hen she ho is ith child has given birth: then the rest of his brothers ill come back to the children of Israel.

And he ill take his place and give food to his flock in the strength of the Lord, in the glory of the name of the Lord his God; and their resting-place ill be safe: for no he ill be great to the ends of the earth.
And this ill be our peace: hen the Assyrian comes into our country and his feet are in our land, then e ill put up against him seven keepers of the flocks and eight chiefs among men.

And they ill make aste the land of Assyria ith the sord, and the land of Nimrod ith the edge of the sord: he ill give us salvation from the Assyrian hen he comes into our country, hen his feet come inside the limit of our land.
And the rest of Jacob ill be among the mass of peoples like de from the Lord, like shoers on the grass, hich may not be kept back by man, or be aiting for the sons of men.

And the rest of Jacob ill be among the nations, in the middle of the mass of peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the oods, like a young lion among the flocks of sheep: if he goes through, they ill be crushed under foot and pulled to bits, and there ill be no saviour.
Your hand is lifted up against those ho are against you, and all your haters ill be cut off.
And it ill come about in that day, says the Lord, that I ill take aay your horses from you, and ill give your ar-carriages to destruction:
I ill have the tons of your land cut off and all your strong places pulled don:
I ill put an end to your use of secret arts, and you ill have no more readers of signs:
And I ill have your images and your pillars cut off from you; and you ill no longer give orship to the ork of your hands.
I ill have your Asherahs pulled up from among you: and I ill send destruction on your images.
And my punishment ill be effected on the nations ith such burning rath as they have not had ord of.
Give ear no to the ords of the Lord: Up! put forard your cause before the mountains, let your voice be sounding among the hills.
Give ear, O you mountains, to the Lord’s cause, and take note, you bases of the earth: for the Lord has a cause against his people, and he ill take it up ith Israel.
O my people, hat have I done to you? ho have I been a eariness to you? give anser against me.
For I took you up out of the land of Egypt and made you free from the prison-house; I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

O my people, keep in mind no hat as designed by Balak, king of Moab, and the anser hich Balaam, son of Beor, gave him; the events, from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may be certain of the upright acts of the Lord.
With hat am I to come before the Lord and go ith bent head before the high God? am I to come before him ith burned offerings, ith young oxen a year old?
Will the Lord be pleased ith thousands of sheep or ith ten thousand rivers of oil? am I to give my first child for my rongdoing, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
He has made clear to you, O man, hat is good; and hat is desired from you by the Lord; only doing hat is right, and loving mercy, and alking ithout pride before your God.
The voice of the Lord is crying out to the ton: Give ear, you tribes and the meeting of the ton.
Am I to let the stores of the evil-doer go out of my memory, and the short measure, hich is cursed?
Is it possible for me to let rong scales and the bag of false eights go ithout punishment?
For its men of ealth are cruel, and its people have said hat is not true, and their tongue is false in their mouth.
So I have made a start ith your punishment; I have made you aste because of your sins.
You ill have food, but not enough; your shame ill be ever ith you: you ill get your goods moved, but you ill not take them aay safely; and hat you do take aay I ill give to the sord.
You ill put in seed, but you ill not get in the grain; you ill be crushing olives, but your bodies ill not be rubbed ith the oil; and you ill get in the grapes, but you ill have no ine.

For you have kept the las of Omri and all the orks of the family of Ahab, and you have been guided by their designs: so that I might make you a cause of onder and your people a cause of hisses; and the shame of my people ill be on you.
Sorro is mine! for I am as hen they have got in the summer fruits, like the last of the grapes: there is nothing for food, not even an early fig for my desire.
The good man is gone from the earth, there is no one upright among men: they are all aiting secretly for blood, every man is going after his brother ith a net.
Their hands are made ready to do evil; the ruler makes requests for money, and the judge is looking for a reard; and the great man gives decisions at his pleasure, and the right is tisted.
The best of them is like a aste plant, and their upright ones are like a all of thorns. Sorro! the day of their fate has come; no ill trouble come on them.
Put no faith in a friend, do not let your hope be placed in a relation: keep atch on the doors of your mouth against her ho is resting on your breast.
For the son puts shame on his father, the daughter goes against her mother and the daughter-in-la against her mother-in-la; and a man’s haters are those of his family.
But as for me, I am looking to the Lord; I am aiting for the God of my salvation: the ears of my God ill be open to me.
Do not be glad because of my sorro, O my hater: after my fall I ill be lifted up; hen I am seated in the dark, the Lord ill be a light to me.
I ill undergo the rath of the Lord, because of my sin against him; till he takes up my cause and does hat is right for me: hen he makes me come out into the light, I ill see his righteousness;

And my hater ill see it and be covered ith shame; she ho said to me, Where is the Lord your God? my eyes ill see their desire effected on her, no she ill be crushed under foot like the dust of the streets.
A day for building your alls! in that day ill your limits be stretched far and ide.
In that day they ill come to you from Assyria and the tons of Egypt, and from Egypt even to the River, and from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
But the land ill become a aste because of its people, as the fruit of their orks.
Keep your people safe ith your rod, the flock of your heritage, living by themselves in the oods in the middle of Carmel: let them get their food in Bashan and Gilead as in the past.
As in the days hen you came out from the land of Egypt, let us see things of onder.
The nations ill see and be shamed because of all their strength; they ill put their hands on their mouths, their ears ill be stopped.

They ill take dust as their food like a snake, like the things hich go flat on the earth; they ill come shaking ith fear out of their secret places: they ill come ith fear to the Lord our God, full of fear because of you.
Who is a God like you, offering forgiveness for evil-doing and overlooking the sins of the rest of his heritage? he does not keep his rath for ever, because his delight is in mercy.
He ill again have pity on us; he ill put our sins under his feet: and you ill send all our sins don into the heart of the sea.
You ill make clear your good faith to Jacob and your mercy to Abraham, as you gave your oath to our fathers from times long past.
The ord about Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
The Lord is a God ho takes care of his honour and gives punishment for rong; the Lord gives punishment and is angry; the Lord sends punishment on those ho are against him, being angry ith his haters.
The Lord is slo to get angry and great in poer, and ill not let the sinner go ithout punishment: the ay of the Lord is in the ind and the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
He says sharp ords to the sea and makes it dry, drying up all the rivers: Bashan is feeble, and Carmel, and the floer of Lebanon is ithout strength.
The mountains are shaking because of him, and the hills floing aay; the earth is falling to bits before him, the orld and all ho are in it.
Who may keep his place before his rath? and ho may undergo the heat of his passion? his rath is let loose like fire and the rocks are broken open by him.
The Lord is good, a strong place in the day of trouble; and he has knoledge of those ho take him for their safe cover.
But like ater overfloing he ill take them aay; he ill put an end to those ho come up against him, driving his haters into the dark.
What are you designing against the Lord? he ill put an end to it: his haters ill not come up again a second time.
For though they are like tisted thorns, and are overcome as ith drink, they ill come to destruction like stems of grass fully dry.
One has gone out from you ho is designing evil against the Lord, hose purposes are of no value.
This is hat the Lord has said: The days of my cause against you are ended; they are cut off and past. Though I have sent trouble on you, you ill no longer be troubled.
And no I ill let his yoke be broken off you, and your chains be parted.

The Lord has given an order about you, that no more of your name are to be planted: from the house of your gods I ill have the pictured and metal images cut off; I ill make your last resting-place a place of shame; for you are completely evil.

See on the mountains the feet of him ho comes ith good nes, giving ord of peace! Keep your feasts, O Judah, give effect to your oaths: for the good-for-nothing man ill never again go through you; he is completely cut off.
A crusher has come up before your face: keep a good look-out, let the ay be atched, make yourself strong, let your poer be greatly increased.
For the Lord ill make good the vine of Jacob, as ell as the vine of Israel: for the asters have made them aste and sent destruction on the branches of their vine.
The body-covers of his fighting men have been made red, the men of ar are clothed in bright red: the ar-carriages are like flames of fire in the day hen he gets ready, the horses are shaking.
The ar-carriages are rushing through the streets, pushing against one another in the ide ays, looking like burning lights, running like thunder-flames.
He takes the record of his great men: they go falling on their ay; they go quickly to the all, the cover is made ready.
The river doorays are forced open, and the king’s house is floing aay.
And the queen is uncovered, she is taken aay and her servant-girls are eeping like the sound of doves, hammering on their breasts.
But Nineveh is like a pool of ater hose aters are floing aay; Keep your place, they say; but no one is turning back.
Take silver, take gold; for there is no end to the store; take for yourselves a eight of things to be desired.
Everything has been taken from her, all is gone, she has nothing more: the heart is turned to ater, the knees are shaking, all are tisted in pain, and colour has gone from all faces.
Where is the lions’ hole, the place here the young lions got their food, here the lion and the she-lion ere alking ith their young, ithout cause for fear?
Food enough for his young and for his she-lions as pulled don by the lion; his hole as full of flesh and his resting-place stored ith meat.

See, I am against you, says the Lord of armies, and I ill have your ar-carriages burned in the smoke, and your young lions ill be food for the sord: you ill no longer get your food by force on the earth, and the voice of your she-lions ill be stopped for ever.
A curse is on the ton of blood; it is full of deceit and violent acts; and there is no end to the taking of life.
The noise of the hip, and the noise of thundering heels; horses rushing and ar-carriages jumping,
Horsemen driving forard, and the shining sord and the bright spear: and a great number of ounded, and masses of dead bodies; they are falling over the bodies of the dead:
Because of all the false ays of the loose oman, expert in attraction and ise in secret arts, ho takes nations in the net of her false ays, and families through her secret arts.
See, I am against you, says the Lord of armies, and I ill have your skirts pulled over your face, and let the nations see you unclothed, and the kingdoms your shame.
I ill make you completely disgusting and full of shame, and ill put you up to be looked at by all.
And it ill come about that all ho see you ill go in flight from you and say, Nineveh is made aste: ho ill be eeping for her? here am I to get comforters for her?
Are you better than No-amon, seated on the Nile streams, ith aters all round her; hose all as the sea and her earthork the aters?
Ethiopia as her strength and Egyptians ithout number; Put and Lubim ere her helpers.

But even she has been taken aay, she has gone aay as a prisoner: even her young children are smashed to bits at the top of all the streets: the fate of her honoured men is put to the decision of chance, and all her great men are put in chains.
And you ill be overcome ith ine, you ill become feeble; you ill be looking for a safe place from those ho are fighting against you.
All your alled places ill be like fig-trees and your people like the first figs, falling at a shake into the mouth hich is open for them.
See, the people ho are in you are omen; the doorays of your land are ide open to your attackers: the locks of your doors have been burned aay in the fire.
Get ater for the time hen you are shut in, make strong your tons: go into the potter’s earth, stamping it don ith your feet, make strong the brickorks.
There the fire ill make you aste; you ill be cut off by the sord: make yourself as great in number as the orms, as great in number as the locusts.
Let your traders be increased more than the stars of heaven:

Your croned ones are like the locusts, and your scribes like the clouds of insects hich take cover in the alls on a cold day, but hen the sun comes up they go in flight, and are seen no longer in their place.
Sorro! ho are the keepers of your flock sleeping, O king of Assyria! your strong men are at rest; your people are andering on the mountains, and there is no one to get them together.

Your pain may not be made better; you are ounded to death: all those hearing the nes about you ill be aving their hands in joy over you: for ho has not undergone the eight of your evil-doing again and again?
The ord hich Habakkuk the prophet sa.
Ho long, O Lord, ill your ears be shut to my voice? I make an outcry to you about violent behaviour, but you do not send salvation.
Why do you make me see evil-doing, and hy are my eyes fixed on rong? for asting and violent acts are before me: and there is fighting and bitter argument.
For this reason the la is feeble and decisions are not effected: for the upright man is circled round by evil-doers; because of hich right is tisted.
See among the nations, and take note, and be full of onder: for in your days I am doing a ork in hich you ill have no belief, even if nes of it is given to you.
For see, I am sending the Chaldaeans, that bitter and quick-moving nation; ho go through the ide spaces of the earth to get for themselves living-places hich are not theirs.
They are greatly to be feared: their right comes from themselves.
And their horses are quicker than leopards and their horsemen more cruel than evening olves; they come from far aay, like an eagle in flight rushing on its food.
They are coming all of them ith force; the direction of their faces is forard, the number of their prisoners is like the sands of the sea.
He makes little of kings, rulers are a sport to him; all the strong places are to be laughed at; for he makes earthorks and takes them.
Then his purpose ill be changed, over-stepping the limit; he ill make his strength his god.
Are you not eternal, O Lord my God, my Holy One? for you there is no death. O Lord, he has been ordered by you for our punishment; and by you, O Rock, he has been marked out to put us right.

Before your holy eyes sin may not be seen, and you are unable to put up ith rong; hy, then, are your eyes on the false? hy do you say nothing hen the evil-doer puts an end to one ho is more upright than himself?
He has made men like the fishes of the sea, like the orms hich have no ruler over them.
He takes them all up ith his hook, he takes them in his net, getting them together in his fishing-net: for hich cause he is glad and full of joy.
For this reason he makes an offering to his net, burning perfume to his fishing-net; because by them he gets much food and his meat is fat.
For this cause his net is ever open, and there is no end to his destruction of the nations.
I ill take my position and be on atch, placing myself on my toer, looking out to see hat he ill say to me, and hat anser he ill give to my protest.
And the Lord gave me an anser, and said, Put the vision in riting and make it clear on stones, so that the reader may go quickly.

For the vision is still for the fixed time, and it is moving quickly to the end, and it ill not be false: even if it is slo in coming, go on aiting for it; because it ill certainly come, it ill not be kept back.
As for the man of pride, my soul has no pleasure in him; but the upright man ill have life through his good faith.

A curse on the cruel and false one! the man full of pride, ho never has enough; ho makes his desires ide as the underorld! he is like death; he is never full, but he makes all nations come to him, getting all peoples together to himself.
Will not all these take up a ord of shame against him and a bitter saying against him, and say, A curse on him ho goes on taking hat is not his and is eighted don ith the property of debtors!
Will not your creditors suddenly be moved against you, and your troublers get up from their sleep, and you ill be to them like goods taken in ar?

Because you have taken their goods from great nations, all the rest of the peoples ill take your goods from you; because of men’s blood and violent acts against the land and the ton and all ho are living in it.
A curse on him ho gets evil profits for his family, so that he may put his resting-place on high and be safe from the hand of the rongdoer!
You have been a cause of shame to your house by cutting off a number of peoples, and sinning against your soul.
For the stone ill give a cry out of the all, and it ill be ansered by the board out of the oodork.
A curse on him ho is building a place ith blood, and basing a ton on evil-doing!
See, is it not the pleasure of the Lord of armies that the peoples are orking for the fire and using themselves up for nothing?
For the earth ill be full of the knoledge of the glory of the Lord as the sea is covered by the aters.
A curse on him ho gives his neighbour the ine of his rath, making him overcome ith strong drink from the cup of his passion, so that you may be a itness of their shame!

You are full of shame in place of glory: take your part in the drinking, and let your shame be uncovered: the cup of the Lord’s right hand ill come round to you and your glory ill be covered ith shame.

For the violent acts against Lebanon ill come on you, and the destruction of the cattle ill be a cause of fear to you, because of men’s blood and the violent acts against the land and the ton and all ho are living in it.
What profit is the pictured image to its maker? and as for the metal image, the false teacher, hy does its maker put his faith in it, making false gods ithout a voice?
A curse on him ho says to the ood, Aake! to the unbreathing stone, Up! let it be a teacher! See, it is plated ith gold and silver, and there is no breath at all inside it.
But the Lord is in his holy Temple: let all the earth be quiet before him.
A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, put to Shigionoth.
O Lord, ord of you has come to my ears; I have seen your ork, O Lord; hen the years come near make it clear; in rath keep mercy in mind.
God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. The heavens ere covered ith his glory, and the earth as full of his praise.
He as shining like the light; he had rays coming out from his hand: there his poer as kept secret.
Before him ent disease, and flames ent out at his feet.
From his high place he sent shaking on the earth; he sa and nations ere suddenly moved: and the eternal mountains ere broken, the unchanging hills ere bent don; his ays are eternal.
The curtains of Cushan ere troubled, and the tents of Midian ere shaking.
Was your rath burning against the rivers? ere you angry ith the sea, that you ent on your horses, on your ar-carriages of salvation?
Your bo as quite uncovered. Selah. By you the earth as cut through ith rivers.
The mountains sa you and ere moved ith fear; the clouds ere streaming ith ater: the voice of the deep as sounding; the sun did not come up, and the moon kept still in her place.
At the light of your arros they ent aay, at the shining of your polished spear.
You ent stepping through the land in rath, crushing the nations in your passion.
You ent out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of the one on hom your holy oil as put; ounding the head of the family of the evil-doer, uncovering the base even to the neck. Selah.
You have put your spears through his head, his horsemen ere sent in flight like dry stems; they had joy in driving aay the poor, in making a meal of them secretly.
The feet of your horses ere on the sea, on the mass of great aters.

Hearing it, my inner parts ere moved, and my lips ere shaking at the sound; my bones became feeble, and my steps ere uncertain under me: I gave sounds of grief in the day of trouble, hen his forces came up against the people in bands.

For though the fig-tree has no floers, and there is no fruit on the vine, and ork on the olive comes to nothing, and the fields give no food; and the flock is cut off from its resting-place, and there is no herd in the cattle-house:
Still, I ill be glad in the Lord, my joy ill be in the God of my salvation.
The Lord God is my strength, and he makes my feet like roes’ feet, guiding me on my high places. For the chief music-maker on corded instruments.
The ord of the Lord hich came to Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah, the son of Amon, king of Judah.
I ill take aay everything from the face of the earth, says the Lord.
I ill take aay man and beast; I ill take aay the birds of the heaven and the fishes of the sea; causing the donfall of the evil-doers, and cutting man off from the face of the earth, says the Lord.
And my hand ill be stretched out on Judah and on all the people of Jerusalem, cutting off the name of the Baal from this place, and the name of the false priests,
And the orshippers of the army of heaven on the house-tops, and the Lord’s orshippers ho take oaths by Milcom,
And those ho are turned back from going after the Lord, and those ho have not made prayer to the Lord or got directions from him.
Let there be no sound before the Lord God: for the day of the Lord is near: for the Lord has made ready an offering, he has made his guests holy.
And it ill come about in the day of the Lord’s offering, that I ill send punishment on the rulers and the king’s sons and all ho are clothed in robes from strange lands.
And in that day I ill send punishment on all those ho come jumping over the doorstep and make their master’s house full of violent behaviour and deceit.

And in that day, says the Lord, there ill be the sound of a cry from the fish dooray, and an outcry from the ne ton, and a great thundering from the hills, and cries of grief from the people of the Hollo;
Because of the donfall of all the people of Canaan: all those ho ere eighted don ith silver have been cut off.

And it ill come about at that time, that I ill go searching through Jerusalem ith lights; and I ill send punishment on the men ho have become like ine stored over-long, ho say to themselves, The Lord ill not do good and ill not do evil.
And their ealth ill be violently taken aay, and their houses ill be made aste: they ill go on building houses and never living in them, and planting vine-gardens but not drinking the ine from them.
The great day of the Lord is near, it is near and coming very quickly; the bitter day of the Lord is near, coming on more quickly than a man of ar.
That day is a day of rath, a day of trouble and sorro, a day of asting and destruction, a day of dark night and deep shade, a day of cloud and thick dark.
A day of sounding the horn and the ar-cry against the alled tons and the high toers.
And I ill send trouble on men so that they ill go about like the blind, because they have done evil against the Lord: and their blood ill be drained out like dust, and their strength like aste.

Even their silver and their gold ill not be able to keep them safe in the day of the Lord’s rath; but all the land ill be burned up in the fire of his bitter rath: for he ill put an end, even suddenly, to all ho are living in the land.
Come together, make everyone come together, O nation ithout shame;
Before the Lord sends you violently aay in flight like the aste from the grain; before the burning rath of the Lord comes on you, before the day of the Lord’s rath comes on you.

Make search for the Lord, all you quiet ones of the earth, ho have done hat is right in his eyes; make search for righteousness and a quiet heart: it may be that you ill be safely covered in the day of the Lord’s rath.
For Gaza ill be given up and Ashkelon ill become aste: they ill send Ashdod out in the middle of the day, and Ekron ill be uprooted.

Sorro to the people living by the sea, the nation of the Cherethites! The ord of the Lord is against you, O Canaan, the land of the Philistines; I ill send destruction on you till there is no one living in you.
And the land by the sea ill be grass-land, ith houses for keepers of sheep and alled places for flocks.

The land by the sea ill be for the rest of the children of Judah; by the sea they ill give their flocks food: in the houses of Ashkelon they ill take their rest in the evening; for the Lord their God ill take them in hand and their fate ill be changed.
My ears have been open to the bitter ords of Moab and the ords of shame of the children of Ammon, hich they have said against my people, lifting themselves up against the limit of their land.

For this cause, by my life, says the Lord of armies, the God of Israel, truly Moab ill become like Sodom and the children of Ammon like Gomorrah, given up to aste plants and salt pools and unpeopled for ever: the rest of my people ill take their property, the overflo of my nation ill take their heritage.
This ill be their fate because of their pride, because they have said evil, lifting themselves up against the people of the Lord of armies.
The Lord ill let himself be seen by them: for he ill make all the gods of the earth feeble; and men ill go don before him in orship, everyone from his place, even all the sea-lands of the nations.
And you Ethiopians ill be put to death by my sord.
And his hand ill be stretched out against the north, for the destruction of Assyria; and he ill make Nineveh unpeopled and dry like the aste land.

And herds ill take their rest in the middle of her, all the beasts of the valley: the pelican and the porcupine ill make their living-places on the tops of its pillars; the ol ill be crying in the indo; the raven ill be seen on the doorstep.

This is the ton hich as full of joy, living ithout fear of danger, saying in her heart, I am, and there is no other: ho has she been made aste, a place for beasts to take their rest in! everyone ho goes by her ill make hisses, aving his hand.
Sorro to her ho is uncontrolled and unclean, the cruel ton!
She gave no attention to the voice, she had no use for teaching, she put no faith in the Lord, she did not come near to her God.
Her rulers are like loud-voiced lions in her; her judges are olves of the evening, crushing up the bones before the morning.
Her prophets are good-for-nothing persons, full of deceit: her priests have made the holy place unclean and have gone violently against the la.
The Lord in her is upright; he ill not do evil; every morning he lets his righteousness be seen, he is unchanging; but the evil-doer has no sense of shame.

I have had the nations cut off, their toers are broken don; I have made their streets a aste so that no one goes through them: destruction has overtaken their tons, so that there is no man living in them.
I said, Certainly you ill go in fear of me, and come under my training, so that hatever I may send on her may not be cut off before her eyes: but they got up early and made all their orks evil.

For this reason, go on aiting for me, says the Lord, till the day hen I come up as a itness: for my purpose is to send for the nations and to get the kingdoms together, so that I may let loose on them my passion, even all my burning rath: for all the earth ill be burned up in the fire of my bitter passion.
For then I ill give the people a clean language, so that they may all make prayer to the Lord and be his servants ith one mind.
From over the rivers of Ethiopia, and from the sides of the north, they ill come to me ith an offering.

In that day you ill have no shame on account of all the things in hich you did evil against me: for then I ill take aay from among you those ho ere lifted up in pride, and you ill no longer be lifted up ith pride in my holy mountain.
But I ill still have among you a quiet and poor people, and they ill put their faith in the name of the Lord.
The rest of Israel ill do no evil and say no false ords; the tongue of deceit ill not be seen in their mouth: for they ill take their food and their rest, and no one ill be a cause of fear to them.
Make melody, O daughter of Zion; give a loud cry, O Israel; be glad and let your heart be full of joy, O daughter of Jerusalem.
The Lord has taken aay those ho ere judging you, he has sent your haters far aay: the King of Israel, even the Lord, is among you: you ill have no more fear of evil.
In that day it ill be said to Jerusalem, Have no fear: O Zion, let not your hands be feeble.
The Lord your God is among you, as a strong saviour: he ill be glad over you ith joy, he ill make his love ne again, he ill make a song of joy over you as in the time of a holy feast.
I ill take aay your troubles, lifting up your shame from off you.

See, at that time I ill put an end to all ho have been troubling you: I ill give salvation to her hose steps are uncertain, and get together her ho has been sent in flight; and I ill make them a cause of praise and an honoured name in all the earth, hen I let their fate be changed.

At that time I ill make you come in, at that time I ill get you together: for I ill make you a name and a praise among all the peoples of the earth hen I let your fate be changed before your eyes, says the Lord.

In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, came the ord of the Lord by Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, ruler of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying,
These are the ords of the Lord of armies: These people say, The time has not come for building the Lord’s house.
Then the ord of the Lord came by Haggai the prophet, saying,
Is it a time for you to be living in roofed houses hile this house is a aste?
For this cause the Lord of armies has said, Give thought to your ays.

Much has been planted, but little got in; you take food, but have not enough; you take drink, but are not full; you are clothed, but no one is arm; and he ho gets payment for his ork, gets it to put it into a bag full of holes.
This is hat the Lord of armies has said: Give thought to your ays.
Go up to the hills and get ood and put up the house; and I ill take pleasure in it and be honoured, says the Lord.

You ere looking for much, and it came to little; and hen you got it into your house, I took it aay ith a breath. Why? says the Lord of armies. Because of my house hich is a aste, hile every man takes care of the house hich is his.
For this cause the heaven over you is kept from giving de, and the earth from giving her fruit.
And by my order no rain came on the land or on the mountains or the grain or the ine or the oil or the produce of the earth or on men or cattle or on any ork of man’s hands.

Then Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the rest of the people, gave ear to the voice of the Lord their God and to the ords of Haggai the prophet, because the Lord their God had sent him, and the people ere in fear before the Lord.
Then Haggai, hom the Lord had sent to give his ords to the people, said, I am ith you, says the Lord.
