And the spirit of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, ruler of Judah, as moved by the Lord, as as the spirit of Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people; and they came and did ork in the house of the Lord of armies, their God.
On the tenty-fourth day of the month, in the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.
In the seventh month, on the tenty-first day of the month, the ord of the Lord came by Haggai the prophet, saying,
Say no to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, ruler of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the rest of the people,
Who is there still among you ho sa this house in its first glory? and ho do you see it no? is it not in your eyes as nothing?

But no be strong, O Zerubbabel, says the Lord; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; and be strong, all you people of the land, says the Lord, and get to ork: for I am ith you, says the Lord of armies:
The agreement hich I made ith you hen you came out of Egypt, and my spirit, are ith you still; have no fear.
For this is hat the Lord of armies has said: In a short time I ill make a shaking of the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry land;
And I ill make a shaking of all the nations, and the desired things of all nations ill come: and I ill make this house full of my glory, says the Lord of armies.
The silver is mine and the gold is mine, says the Lord of armies.
The second glory of this house ill be greater than the first, says the Lord of armies: and in this place I ill give peace, says the Lord of armies.
On the tenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the ord of the Lord came by Haggai the prophet, saying,
These are the ords of the Lord of armies: Put no a point of la to the priests, saying,
If anyone has some holy flesh folded in the skirt of his robe, ill bread or soup or ine or oil or any other food be made holy if touched by his skirt? And the priests ansering said, No.
Then Haggai said, Will any of these be made unclean by the touch of one ho is unclean through touching a dead body? And the priests ansering said, It ill be made unclean.
Then Haggai said, So is this people and so is this nation before me, says the Lord; and so is every ork of their hands; and the offering they give there is unclean.
And no, give thought, looking back from this day to the time before one stone as put on another in the Temple of the Lord:
Ho, hen anyone came to a store of tenty measures, there ere only ten: hen anyone ent to the ine-store to get fifty vessels full, there ere only tenty.
And I sent burning and asting and a rain of ice-drops on all the orks of your hands; but still you ere not turned to me, says the Lord.
And no, give thought; looking on from this day, from the tenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the time hen the base of the Lord’s house as put in its place, give thought to it.
Is the seed still in the store-house? have the vine and the fig-tree, the pomegranate and the olive-tree, still not given their fruit? from this day I ill send my blessing on you.
And the ord of the Lord came a second time to Haggai, on the tenty-fourth day of the month, saying,
Say to Zerubbabel, ruler of Judah, I ill make a shaking of the heavens and the earth,

Overturning the poer of kingdoms; and I ill send destruction on the strength of the kingdoms of the nations; by me ar-carriages ill be overturned ith those ho are in them; and the horses and the horsemen ill come don, everyone by the sord of his brother.

In that day, says the Lord of armies, I ill take you, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, says the Lord, and ill make you as a jeelled ring: for I have taken you to be mine, says the Lord of armies.
In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the ord of the Lord came to Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying,
The Lord has been very angry ith your fathers:
And you are to say to them, These are the ords of the Lord of armies: Come back to me, says the Lord of armies, and I ill come back to you.

Be not like your fathers, to hom the voice of the earlier prophets came, saying, Be turned no from your evil ays and from your evil doings: but they did not give ear to me or take note, says the Lord.
Your fathers, here are they? and the prophets, do they go on living for ever?

But my ords and my orders, hich I gave to my servants the prophets, have they not overtaken your fathers? and turning back they said, As it as the purpose of the Lord of armies to do to us, in reard for our ays and our doings, so has he done.
On the tenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the ord of the Lord came to Zechariah, the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo the prophet, saying,
I sa in the night a man on a red horse, beteen the mountains in the valley, and at his back ere horses, red, black, hite, and of mixed colours.
Then I said, O my lord, hat are these? And the angel ho as talking to me said to me, I ill make clear to you hat they are.
And the man ho as beteen the mountains, ansering me, said, These are those hom the Lord has sent to go up and don through the earth.
And the man ho as beteen the mountains, ansering, said to the angel of the Lord, We have gone up and don through the earth, and all the earth is quiet and at rest.
Then the angel of the Lord, ansering, said, O Lord of armies, ho long ill it be before you have mercy on Jerusalem and on the tons of Judah against hich your rath has been burning for seventy years?
And the Lord gave an anser in good and comforting ords to the angel ho as talking to me.
And the angel ho as talking to me said to me, Let your voice be loud and say, These are the ords of the Lord of armies: I am greatly moved about the fate of Jerusalem and of Zion.
And I am very angry ith the nations ho are living untroubled: for hen I as only a little angry, they made the evil orse.
So this is hat the Lord has said: I have come back to Jerusalem ith mercies; my house is to be put up in her, says the Lord of armies, and a line is to be stretched out over Jerusalem.

And again let your voice be loud and say, This is hat the Lord of armies has said: My tons ill again be overfloing ith good things, and again the Lord ill give comfort to Zion and take Jerusalem for himself.
And lifting up my eyes I sa four horns.
And I said to the angel ho as talking to me, What are these? And he said to me, These are the horns hich have sent Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem in flight.
And the Lord gave me a vision of four metal-orkers.

Then I said, What have these come to do? And he said, These are the horns hich sent Judah in flight, and kept him from lifting up his head: but these men have come to send fear on them and to put don the nations ho are lifting up their horns against the land of Judah to send it in flight.
And lifting up my eyes, I sa a man ith a measuring-line in his hand.
And I said to him, Where are you going? And he said to me, To take the measure of Jerusalem, to see ho ide and ho long it is.
And the angel ho as talking to me ent out, and another angel ent out, and, meeting him,
Said to him, Go quickly and say to this young man, Jerusalem ill be an unalled ton, because of the great number of men and cattle in her.
For I, says the Lord, ill be a all of fire round about her, and I ill be the glory inside her.
Ho, ho! go in flight from the land of the north, says the Lord: for I have sent you far and ide to the four inds of heaven, says the Lord.
Ho! Zion, go in flight from danger, you ho are living ith the daughter of Babylon.
For this is hat the Lord of armies has said: In the ay of glory he has sent me to the nations hich have taken your goods: for anyone touching you is touching hat is most dear to him.
For at the shaking of my hand over them, their goods ill be taken by those ho ere their servants: and you ill see that the Lord of armies has sent me.
Give songs of joy, O daughter of Zion: for I come, and I ill make my resting-place among you, says the Lord.
And a number of nations ill be joined to the Lord in that day, and ill become my people; and I ill be living among you, and you ill see that the Lord of armies has sent me to you.
And Judah ill be the Lord’s heritage in the holy land, and Jerusalem ill again be his.
Let all flesh be quiet and make no sound before the Lord: for he is aake and has come from his holy resting-place.
And he let me see Joshua, the high priest, in his place before the angel of the Lord, and the Satan at his right hand ready to take up a cause against him.
And the Lord said to the Satan, May the Lord’s ord be sharp against you, O Satan, the ord of the Lord ho has taken Jerusalem for himself: is this not a burning branch pulled out of the fire?
No Joshua as clothed in unclean robes, and he as in his place before the angel.
And he made anser and said to those ho ere there before him, Take the unclean robes off him, and let him be clothed in clean robes;
And let them put a clean head-dress on his head. So they put a clean head-dress on his head, clothing him ith clean robes: and to him he said, See, I have taken your sin aay from you.
And the angel of the Lord made a statement to Joshua, and said,

These are the ords of the Lord of armies: If you ill go in my ays and keep hat I have put in your care, then you ill be judge over my Temple and have the care of my house, and I ill give you the right to come in among those ho are there.
Give ear no, O Joshua, the high priest, you and your friends ho are seated before you; for these are men ho are a sign: for see, I ill let my servant the Branch be seen.
For see, the stone hich I have put before Joshua; on one stone are seven eyes: see, the design cut on it ill be my ork, says the Lord of armies, and I ill take aay the sin of that land in one day.
In that day, says the Lord of armies, you ill be one another’s guests under the vine and under the fig-tree.
And the angel ho as talking to me came again, aaking me as a man out of his sleep.

And he said to me, What do you see? And I said, I see a light-support, made all of gold, ith its cup on the top of it and seven lights on it; and there are seven pipes to every one of the lights hich are on the top of it;
And to olive-trees by it, one on the right side of the cup and one on the left.
And I made anser and said to the angel ho as talking to me, What are these, my lord?
Then the angel ho as talking to me, ansering me, said, Have you no knoledge of hat these are? And I said, No, my lord.
This is the ord of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying, Not by force or by poer, but by my spirit, says the Lord of armies.
Who are you, O great mountain? before Zerubbabel you ill become level: and he ill let all see the headstone, ith cries of Grace, grace, to it.
Then the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
The hands of Zerubbabel have put the base of this house in place, and his hands ill make it complete; and it ill be clear to you that the Lord of armies has sent me to you.

For ho has had a poor opinion of the day of small things? for they ill be glad hen they see the eighted measuring-line in the hand of Zerubbabel. Then he said in anser to me, These seven lights are the eyes of the Lord hich go quickly up and don through all the earth.
And I made anser and said to him, What are these to olive-trees on the right side of the light-support and on the left?
And ansering a second time, I said to him, What are these to olive branches, through hose gold pipes the oil is drained out?
And he said in anser to me, Have you no knoledge hat these are? And I said, No, my lord.
And he said, These are the to sons of oil, hose place is by the Lord of all the earth.
Then again lifting up my eyes I sa a roll in flight through the air.
And he said to me, What do you see? And I said, A roll going through the air; it is tenty cubits long and ten cubits ide.

Then he said to me, This is the curse hich goes out over the face of all the land: for long enough has every thief gone ithout punishment, and long enough has every taker of false oaths gone ithout punishment.

And I ill send it out, says the Lord of armies, and it ill go into the house of the thief and into the house of him ho takes a false oath by my name: and it ill be in his house, causing its complete destruction, ith its oodork and its stones.
And the angel ho as talking to me ent out and said to me, Let your eyes be lifted up no, and see the ephah hich is going out.
And I said, What is it? And he said, This is an ephah hich is going out. And he said further, This is their evil-doing in all the land.
And I sa a round cover of lead lifted up; and a oman as seated in the middle of the ephah.
And he said, This is Sin; and pushing her don into the ephah, he put the eight of lead on the mouth of it.
And lifting up my eyes I sa to omen coming out, and the ind as in their ings; and they had ings like the ings of a stork: and they took the ephah, lifting it up beteen earth and heaven.
And I said to the angel ho as talking to me, Where are they taking the ephah?
And he said to me, To make a house for her in the land of Shinar: and they ill make a place ready, and put her there in the place hich is hers.
And again lifting up my eyes I sa four ar-carriages coming out from beteen the to mountains; and the mountains ere mountains of brass.
In the first ar-carriage ere red horses; and in the second, black horses;
And in the third, hite horses; and in the fourth, horses of mixed colour.
And I made anser and said to the angel ho as talking to me, What are these, my lord?
And the angel, ansering, said to me, These go out to the four inds of heaven from their place before the Lord of all the earth.
The carriage in hich are the black horses goes in the direction of the north country; the hite go to the est; and those of mixed colour go in the direction of the south country.
And the red ones go to the east; and they made request that they might go up and don through the earth: and he said, Go up and don through the earth. So they ent up and don through the earth.
Then crying out to me, he said, See, those ho are going to the north country have given rest to the spirit of the Lord in the north country.
And the ord of the Lord came to me, saying,
Take the offerings of those ho ent aay as prisoners, from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, and from the family of Josiah, the son of Zephaniah, ho have come from Babylon;
And take silver and gold and make a cron and put it on the head of Zerubbabel;
And say to him, These are the ords of the Lord of armies: See, the man hose name is the Branch, under hom there ill be fertile groth.

And he ill be the builder of the Temple of the Lord; and the glory ill be his, and he ill take his place as ruler on the seat of poer; and Joshua ill be a priest at his right hand, and beteen them there ill be a design of peace.
And the cron ill be for grace to Heldai and Tobijah and Jedaiah and the son of Zephaniah, to keep their memory living in the house of the Lord.
And those ho are far aay ill come and be builders in the Temple of the Lord, and it ill be clear to you that the Lord of armies has sent me to you.
And it came about in the fourth year of King Darius, that the ord of the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month Chislev.
No they of Beth-el had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech to make a request for grace from the Lord,
And to say to the priests of the house of the Lord of armies and to the prophets, Am I to go on eeping in the fifth month, separating myself as I have done in past years?
Then the ord of the Lord of armies came to me, saying

Say to all the people of the land and to the priests, When you ent ithout food and gave yourselves to grief in the fifth and the seventh months for these seventy years, did you ever do it because of me?
And hen you are feasting and drinking, are you not doing it only for yourselves?
Are not these the ords hich the Lord said to you by the earlier prophets, hen Jerusalem as full of people and ealth, and the tons round about her and the South and the Loland ere peopled?
And the ord of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying,
This is hat the Lord of armies has said: Let your judging be upright and done in good faith, let every man have mercy and pity for his brother:
Do not be hard on the ido, or the child ithout a father, on the man from a strange country, or on the poor; let there be no evil thought in your heart against your brother.
But they ould not give attention, turning their backs and stopping their ears from hearing;

And they made their hearts like the hardest stone, so that they might not give ear to the la and the ords hich the Lord of armies had said by the earlier prophets: and there came great rath from the Lord of armies.
And it came about that as they ould not give ear to his voice, so I ould not give ear to their voice, says the Lord of armies:

But ith a storm-ind I sent them in flight among all the nations of hom they had no knoledge. So the land as aste after them, so that no man ent through or came back: for they had made aste the desired land.
And the ord of the Lord of armies came to me, saying,
These are the ords of the Lord of armies: I am angry about the fate of Zion, I am angry about her ith great rath.

This is hat the Lord has said: I have come back to Zion, and ill make my living-place in Jerusalem: and Jerusalem ill be named The ton of good faith; and the mountain of the Lord of armies The holy mountain.
This is hat the Lord of armies has said: There ill again be old men and old omen seated in the open spaces of Jerusalem, every man ith his stick in his hand because he is so old.
And the open spaces of the ton ill be full of boys and girls playing in its open spaces.
This is hat the Lord of armies has said: If this is a onder to the rest of this people, is it a onder to me? says the Lord of armies.
This is hat the Lord of armies has said: See, I ill be the saviour of my people from the east country, and from the est country;
And I ill make them come and be living in Jerusalem and they ill be to me a people and I ill be to them a God, in good faith and in righteousness.

This is hat the Lord of armies has said: Let your hands be strong, you ho are no hearing these ords from the mouths of the prophets, that is to say, in the days hen the base of the house of the Lord of armies has been put in place for the building of the house, that is the Temple.

For before those days there as no payment for a man’s ork, or for the use of a beast, and there as no peace for him ho ent out or him ho came in, because of the attacker: for I had every man turned against his neighbour.
But no I ill not be to the rest of this people as I as in the past, says the Lord of armies.

For I ill let the seed of peace be planted; the vine ill give her fruit and the land ill give her increase and the heavens ill give their de; and I ill give to the rest of this people all these things for their heritage.

And it ill come about that, as you ere a curse among the nations, O children of Judah and children of Israel, so I ill give you salvation and you ill be a blessing: have no fear and let your hands be strong.
For this is hat the Lord of armies has said: As it as my purpose to do evil to you hen your fathers made me angry, says the Lord of armies, and my purpose as not changed:
So in these days it is again my purpose to do good to Jerusalem and to the children of Judah: have no fear.
These are the things hich you are to do: Let every man say hat is true to his neighbour; and let your judging give peace in your tons.
Let no one have any evil thought in his heart against his neighbour; and have no love for false oaths: for all these things are hated by me, says the Lord.
And the ord of the Lord of armies came to me, saying,

This is hat the Lord of armies has said: The times of going ithout food in the fourth month and in the fifth and the seventh and the tenth months, ill be for the people of Judah times of joy and happy meetings; so be lovers of good faith and of peace.
This is hat the Lord of armies has said: It ill again come about that hen peoples and those living in great tons come,
And the people of one ton go to another and say, Let us certainly go ith a request for grace from the Lord, and to give orship to the Lord of armies, then I ill go ith you.
And great peoples and strong nations ill come to give orship to the Lord of armies in Jerusalem and to make requests for grace from the Lord.

This is hat the Lord of armies has said: In those days, ten men from all the languages of the nations ill put out their hands and take a grip of the skirt of him ho is a Je, saying, We ill go ith you, for it has come to our ears that God is ith you.
A ord of the Lord: The Lord has come to the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is his resting-place: for the tons of Aram are the Lord’s,
As ell as Hamath, hich is by its limit, and Tyre and Zidon, because they are very ise.
And Tyre made for herself a strong place, and got together silver like dust and the best gold like the earth of the streets.
See, the Lord ill take aay her heritage, overturning her poer in the sea; and she ill be burned up ith fire.
Ashkelon ill see it ith fear, and Gaza, bent ith pain; and Ekron, for her hope ill be shamed: and the king ill be cut off from Gaza, and Ashkelon ill be unpeopled.
And a mixed people ill be living in Ashdod, and I ill have the pride of the Philistines cut off.

And I ill take aay his blood from his mouth, and his disgusting things from beteen his teeth; and some of his people ill be kept for our God: and he ill be as a family in Judah, and Ekron as one living in Jerusalem.
And I ill put my forces in position round my house, so that there may be no coming and going: and no cruel master ill again go through them: for no I have seen his trouble.
Be full of joy, O daughter of Zion; give a glad cry, O daughter of Jerusalem: see, your king comes to you: he is upright and has overcome; gentle and seated on an ass, on a young ass.

And he ill have the ar-carriage cut off from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bo of ar ill be cut off: and he ill say ords of peace to the nations: and his rule ill be from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
And as for you, because of the blood of your agreement, I have sent out your prisoners from the deep hole in hich there is no ater.
And they ill come back to you, O daughter of Zion, as prisoners of hope: today I say to you that I ill give you back tice as much;

For I have made Judah a bo bent for my use, I have made Ephraim the arros of the bo; I ill make your sons, O Zion, take up arms against your sons, O Greece, and ill make you like the sord of a man of ar.
And the Lord ill be seen over them, and his arro ill go out like the thunder-flame: and the Lord God, sounding the ar-horn, ill go in the storm-inds of the South.
The Lord of armies ill be a cover for them; and they ill overcome, crushing under foot the armed men; they ill take their blood for drink like ine: they ill be full like the sides of the altar.
And the Lord their God ill be their saviour in that day, giving them food like the flock of his people: for they ill be like the jeels of a cron shining over his land.
For ho good it is and ho beautiful! grain ill make the young men strong and ne ine the virgins.
Make your request to the Lord for rain in the time of the spring rains, even to the Lord ho makes the thunder-flames; and he ill give them shoers of rain, to every man grass in the field.

For the images have said hat is not true, and the readers of signs have seen deceit; they have given accounts of false dreams, they give comfort to no purpose: so they go out of the ay like sheep, they are troubled because they have no keeper.

My rath is burning against the keepers of the flock, and I ill send punishment on the he-goats: for the Lord of armies takes care of his flock, the people of Judah, and ill make them like the horse of his pride in the fight.
From him ill come the keystone, from him the nail, from him the bo of ar, from him ill come every ruler;
Together they ill be like men of ar, crushing don their haters into the earth of the streets in the fight; they ill make ar because the Lord is ith them: and the horsemen ill be shamed.

And I ill make the children of Judah strong, and I ill be the saviour of the children of Joseph, and I ill make them come back again, for I have had mercy on them: they ill be as if I had not given them up: for I am the Lord their God and I ill give them an anser.
And Ephraim ill be like a man of ar, and their hearts ill be glad as ith ine; and their children ill see it ith joy; their hearts ill be glad in the Lord.
With the sound of the pipe I ill get them together; for I have given the price to make them free: and they ill be increased as they ere increased.
Though I had them planted among the peoples, they ill keep me in mind in far countries: and they ill take care of their children and ill come back.
And I ill make them come back out of the land of Egypt, and ill get them together out of Assyria; and I ill take them into the land of Gilead, and it ill not be ide enough for them.
And they ill go through the sea of Egypt, and all the deep aters of the Nile ill become dry: and the pride of Assyria ill be made lo, and the poer of Egypt ill be taken aay.
And their strength ill be in the Lord; and their pride ill be in his name, says the Lord.
Let your doors be open, O Lebanon, so that fire may be burning among your cedars.
Give a cry of grief, O fir-tree, for the fall of the cedar, because the great ones have been made lo: give cries of grief, O you oaks of Bashan, for the strong trees of the ood have come don.
The sound of the crying of the keepers of the flock! for their glory is made aste: the sound of the loud crying of the young lions! for the pride of Jordan is made aste.
This is hat the Lord my God has said: Take care of the flock of death;
Whose oners put them to death and have no sense of sin; and those ho get a price for them say, May the Lord be praised for I have much ealth: and the keepers of the flock have no pity for them.

For I ill have no more pity for the people of the land, says the Lord; but I ill give up everyone into his neighbour’s hand and into the hand of his king: and they ill make the land aste, and I ill not keep them safe from their hands.
So I took care of the flock of death, for those ho made profit out of the flock; and I took for myself to rods, naming one Beautiful, and the other Bands; and I took care of the flock.
And in one month I put an end to the three keepers of the flock; for my soul as tired of them, and their souls ere disgusted ith me.
And I said, I ill not take care of you: If death comes to any, let death be its fate; if any is cut off, let it be cut off; and let the rest take one another’s flesh for food.
And I took my rod Beautiful, cutting it in to, so that the Lord’s agreement, hich he had made ith all the peoples, might be broken.
And it as broken on that day: and the sheep-traders, ho ere atching me, ere certain that it as the ord of the Lord.
And I said to them, If it seems good to you, give me my payment; and if not, do not give it. So they gave me my payment by eight, thirty shekels of silver.
And the Lord said to me, Put it into the store-house, the price at hich I as valued by them. And I took the thirty shekels of silver and put them into the store-house in the house of the Lord.
Then I took my other rod, the one named Bands, cutting it in to, so that the relation of brothers beteen Judah and Israel might be broken.
And the Lord said to me, Take again the instruments of a foolish keeper of sheep.

For see, I ill put a sheep-keeper over the land, ho ill have no care for that hich is cut off, and ill not go in search of the anderers, or make ell hat is broken, and he ill not give food to that hich is ill, but he ill take for his food the flesh of the fat, and let their feet be broken.
A curse on the foolish keeper ho goes aay from the flock! the sord ill be on his arm and on his right eye: his arm ill become quite dry and his eye ill be made completely dark.
The ord of the Lord about Israel. The Lord by hom the heavens are stretched out and the bases of the earth put in place, and the spirit of man formed inside him, has said:
See, I ill make Jerusalem a cup of shaking fear to all the peoples round about, hen Jerusalem is shut in.

And it ill come about in that day that I ill make Jerusalem a stone of great eight for all the peoples; all those ho take it up ill be badly ounded; and all the nations of the earth ill come together against it.
In that day, says the Lord, I ill put fear into every horse and make every horseman go off his head: and my eyes ill be open on the people of Judah, and I ill make every horse of the peoples blind.
And the families of Judah ill say in their hearts, The people of Jerusalem have their strength in the Lord of armies, their God.

In that day I ill make the families of Judah like a pot ith fire in it among trees, and like a flaming stick among cut grain; they ill send destruction on all the peoples round about, on the right hand and on the left: and Jerusalem ill be living again in the place hich is hers, that is, in Jerusalem.
And the Lord ill give salvation to the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the family of David and the glory of the people of Jerusalem may not be greater than that of Judah.

In that day the Lord ill be a cover over the people of Jerusalem; and he ho is feeble among them in that day ill be as strong as David, and the family of David ill be as God, as the angel of the Lord before them.
And it ill come about on that day that I ill take in hand the destruction of all the nations ho come against Jerusalem.

And I ill send don on the family of David and on the people of Jerusalem the spirit of grace and of prayer; and their eyes ill be turned to the one ho as ounded by their hands: and they ill be eeping for him as for an only son, and their grief for him ill be bitter, like the grief of one sorroing for his oldest son.
In that day there ill be a great eeping in Jerusalem, like the eeping of Hadad-rimmon in the valley of Megiddon.
And the land ill give itself to eeping, every family separately; the family of David by themselves, and their ives by themselves; the family of Nathan by themselves, and their ives by themselves;
The family of Levi by themselves, and their ives by themselves; the family of Shimei by themselves, and their ives by themselves;
And all the other families by themselves, and their ives by themselves.
In that day there ill be a fountain open to the family of David and to the people of Jerusalem, for sin and for that hich is unclean.

And it ill come about on that day, says the Lord of armies, that I ill have the names of the images cut off out of the land, and there ill be no more memory of them: and I ill send all the prophets and the unclean spirit aay from the land.

And if anyone goes on acting as a prophet, then his father and his mother ho gave him life ill say to him, You may not go on living, for you are saying hat is false in the name of the Lord; and his father and his mother ill put a sord through him hen he does so.
And it ill come about in that day that the prophets ill be shamed, every man on account of his vision, hen he is talking as a prophet; and they ill not put on a robe of hair for purposes of deceit:
But he ill say, I am no prophet, but a orker on the land; for I have been an oner of land from the time hen I as young.
And if anyone says to him, What are these ounds beteen your hands? then he ill say, Those ith hich I as ounded in the house of my friends.

Aake! O sord, against the keeper of my flock, and against him ho is ith me, says the Lord of armies: put to death the keeper of the sheep, and the sheep ill go in flight: and my hand ill be turned against the little ones.
And it ill come about that in all the land, says the Lord, to parts of it ill be cut off and come to an end; but the third ill be still living there.

And I ill make the third part go through the fire, cleaning them as silver is made clean, and testing them as gold is tested: and they ill make their prayer to me and I ill give them an anser: I ill say, It is my people; and they ill say, The Lord is my God.
See, a day of the Lord is coming hen they ill make division of your goods taken by force before your eyes.

For I ill get all the nations together to make ar against Jerusalem; and the ton ill be overcome, and the goods taken from the houses, and the omen taken by force: and half the ton ill go aay as prisoners, and the rest of the people ill not be cut off from the ton.
Then the Lord ill go out and make ar against those nations, as he did in the day of the fight.

And in that day his feet ill be on the Mount of Olives, hich is opposite Jerusalem on the east, and the Mount of Olives ill be parted in the middle to the east and to the est, forming a very great valley; and half the mountain ill be moved to the north and half of it to the south.
And the valley ill be stopped ... and you ill go in flight as you ent in flight from the earth-shock in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah: and the Lord my God ill come, and all his holy ones ith him.
And in that day there ill be no heat or cold or ice;
And it ill be unbroken day, such as the Lord has knoledge of, ithout change of day and night, and even at nightfall it ill be light.
And on that day living aters ill go out from Jerusalem; half of them floing to the sea on the east and half to the sea on the est: in summer and in inter it ill be so.
And the Lord ill be King over all the earth: in that day there ill be one Lord and his name one.

And all the land ill become like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; and she ill be lifted up and be living in her place; from the dooray of Benjamin to the place of the first dooray, to the dooray of the angle, and from the toer of Hananel to the king’s ine-crushing places, men ill be living in her.
And there ill be no more curse; but Jerusalem ill be living ithout fear of danger.

And this ill be the disease hich the Lord ill send on all the peoples hich have been arring against Jerusalem: their flesh ill be asted aay hile they are on their feet, their eyes ill be asted in their heads and their tongues in their mouths.
And it ill be on that day that a great fear ill be sent among them from the Lord; and everyone ill take his neighbour’s hand, and every man’s hand ill be lifted against his neighbour’s.
And even Judah ill be fighting against Jerusalem; and the ealth of all the nations round about ill be massed together, a great store of gold and silver and clothing.
And the horses and the transport beasts, the camels and the asses and all the beasts in those tents ill be attacked by the same disease.

And it ill come about that everyone ho is still living, of all those nations ho came against Jerusalem, ill go up from year to year to give orship to the King, the Lord of armies, and to keep the feast of tents.
And it ill be that if any one of all the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to give orship to the King, the Lord of armies, on them there ill be no rain.
And if the family of Egypt does not go up or come there, they ill be attacked by the disease hich the Lord ill send on the nations:
This ill be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all the nations ho do not go up to keep the feast of tents.
On that day all the bells of the horses ill be holy to the Lord, and the pots in the Lord’s house ill be like the basins before the altar.

And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah ill be holy to the Lord of armies: and all those ho make offerings ill come and take them for boiling their offerings: in that day there ill be no more traders in the house of the Lord of armies.
The ord of the Lord to Israel by Malachi.
You have been loved by me, says the Lord. But you say, Where as your love for us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? says the Lord: but Jacob as loved by me,
And Esau as hated, and I sent destruction on his mountains, and gave his heritage to the beasts of the aste land.

Though Edom says, We are crushed don but e ill come back, building up the aste places; this is hat the Lord of armies has said: They may put up buildings, but I ill have them pulled don; and they ill be named The land of evil-doing, and The people against hom the Lord keeps his rath for ever.
And your eyes ill see it; and you ill say, The Lord is great even outside the limits of Israel.

A son gives honour to his father, and a servant has fear of his master: if then I am a father, here is my honour? and if I am a master, here is the fear of me? says the Lord of armies to you, O priests, ho give no value to my name. And you say, Ho have e not given value to your name?
You put unclean bread on my altar. And you say, Ho have e made it unclean? By your saying, The table of the Lord is of no value.

And hen you give hat is blind for an offering, it is no evil! and hen you give hat is damaged and ill, it is no evil! Give it no to your ruler; ill he be pleased ith you, or ill you have his approval? says the Lord of armies.
And no, make request for the grace of God so that he may have mercy on us: this has been your doing: ill he give his approval to any of you? says the Lord of armies.

If only there as one among you ho ould see that the doors ere shut, so that you might not put a light to the fire on my altar for nothing! I have no pleasure in you, says the Lord of armies, and I ill not take an offering from your hands.

For, from the coming up of the sun till its going don, my name is great among the Gentiles; and in every place the smell of burning flesh is offered to my name, and a clean offering: for my name is great among the Gentiles, says the Lord of armies.
But you make it unholy by saying, The Lord’s table has become unclean, and his food is of no value.

And you say, See, hat a eariness it is! and you let out your breath at it, says the Lord of armies; and you have given hat has been cut about by beasts, and hat is damaged in its feet and ill; this is the offering you give: ill this be pleasing to me from your hands? says the Lord.

A curse on the false man ho has a male in his flock, and takes his oath, and gives to the Lord a damaged thing: for I am a great King, says the Lord of armies, and my name is to be feared among the Gentiles.
And no, O you priests, this order is for you.

If you ill not give ear and take it to heart, to give glory to my name, says the Lord of armies, then I ill send the curse on you and ill put a curse on your blessing: truly, even no I have put a curse on it, because you do not take it to heart.
See, I ill have your arm cut off, and ill put aste on your faces, even the aste from your feasts; and you ill be taken aay ith it.
And you ill be certain that I have sent this order to you, so that it might be my agreement ith Levi, says the Lord of armies.
My agreement ith him as on my side life and peace, and I gave them to him; on his side fear, and he had fear of me and gave honour to my name.
True teaching as in his mouth, and no evil as seen on his lips: he as alking ith me in peace and righteousness, turning numbers of people aay from evil-doing.
For it is right for the priest’s lips to keep knoledge, and for men to be aiting for the la from his mouth: for he is the servant sent from the Lord of armies.
But you are turned out of the ay; you have made the la hard for numbers of people; you have made the agreement of Levi of no value, says the Lord of armies.
And so I have taken aay your honour and made you lo before all the people, even as you have not kept my ays, and have given no thought to me in using the la.
Have e not all one father? has not one God made us? hy are e, every one of us, acting falsely to his brother, putting shame on the agreement of our fathers?

Judah has been acting falsely, and a disgusting thing has been done in Jerusalem; for Judah has made unclean the holy place of the Lord hich is dear to him, and has taken as his ife the daughter of a strange god.
The Lord ill have the man ho does this cut off root and branch out of the tents of Jacob, and him ho makes an offering to the Lord of armies.
And this again you do: covering the altar of the Lord ith eeping and ith grief, so that he gives no more thought to the offering, and does not take it ith pleasure from your hand.

But you say, For hat reason? Because the Lord has been a itness beteen you and the ife of your early years, to hom you have been untrue, though she is your friend and the ife to hom you have given your ord.
... So give thought to your spirit, and let no one be false to the ife of his early years.

For I am against the putting aay of a ife, says the Lord, the God of Israel, and against him ho is clothed ith violent acts, says the Lord of armies: so give thought to your spirit and do not be false in your acts.

You have made the Lord tired ith your ords. And still you say, Ho have e made him tired? By your saying, Everyone ho does evil is good in the eyes of the Lord, and he has delight in them; or, Where is God the judge?

See, I am sending my servant, and he ill make ready the ay before me; and the Lord, hom you are looking for, ill suddenly come to his Temple; and the angel of the agreement, in hom you have delight, see, he is coming, says the Lord of armies.
But by hom may the day of his coming be faced? and ho may keep his place hen he is seen? for he is like the metal-tester’s fire and the cleaner’s soap.
He ill take his seat, testing and cleaning the sons of Levi, burning aay the evil from them as from gold and silver; so that they may make offerings to the Lord in righteousness.
Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem ill be pleasing to the Lord, as in days gone by, and as in past years.

And I ill come near to you for judging; I ill quickly be a itness against the onder-orkers, against those ho have been untrue in married life, against those ho take false oaths; against those ho keep back from the servant his payment, and ho are hard on the ido and the child ithout a father, ho do not give his rights to the man from a strange country, and have no fear of me, says the Lord of armies.
For I am the Lord, I am unchanged; and so you, O sons of Jacob, have not been cut off.
From the days of your fathers you have been turned aay from my rules and have not kept them. Come back to me, and I ill come back to you, says the Lord of armies. But you say, Ho are e to come back?
Will a man keep back from God hat is right? But you have kept back hat is mine. But you say, What have e kept back from you? Tenths and offerings.
You are cursed ith a curse; for you have kept back from me hat is mine, even all this nation.

Let your tenths come into the store-house so that there may be food in my house, and put me to the test by doing so, says the Lord of armies, and see if I do not make the indos of heaven open and send don such a blessing on you that there is no room for it.
And on your account I ill keep back the locusts from asting the fruits of your land; and the fruit of your vine ill not be dropped on the field before its time, says the Lord of armies
And you ill be named happy by all nations: for you ill be a land of delight, says the Lord of armies.
Your ords have been strong against me, says the Lord. And still you say, What have e said against you?
You have said, It is no use orshipping God: hat profit have e had from keeping his orders, and going in clothing of sorro before the Lord of armies?
And no to us the men of pride seem happy; yes, the evil-doers are doing ell; they put God to the test and are safe.

Then those in hom as the fear of the Lord had talk together: and the Lord gave ear, and it as recorded in a book to be kept in mind before him, for those ho had the fear of the Lord and gave thought to his name.
And they ill be mine, says the Lord, in the day hen I make them my special property; and I ill have mercy on them as a man has mercy on his son ho is his servant.
Then you ill again see ho the upright man is different from the sinner, and the servant of God from him ho is not.

For see, the day is coming, it is burning like an oven; all the men of pride and all ho do evil ill be dry stems of grass: and in the day hich is coming they ill be burned up, says the Lord of armies, till they have not a root or a branch.
But to you ho give orship to my name, the sun of righteousness ill come up ith ne life in its ings; and you ill go out, playing like young oxen full of food.
And the evil-doers ill be crushed under you, they ill be dust under your feet, in the day hen I do my ork, says the Lord of armies.
Keep in mind the la of Moses, my servant, hich I gave him in Horeb for all Israel, even the rules and the decisions.
See, I am sending you Elijah the prophet before the day of the Lord comes, that great day, greatly to be feared.
And by him the hearts of fathers ill be turned to their children, and the hearts of children to their fathers; for fear that I may come and put the earth under a curse.
The book of the generations of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
The son of Abraham as Isaac; and the son of Isaac as Jacob; and the sons of Jacob ere Judah and his brothers;
And the sons of Judah ere Perez and Zerah by Tamar; and the son of Perez as Hezron; and the son of Hezron as Ram;
And the son of Ram as Amminadab; and the son of Amminadab as Nahshon; and the son of Nahshon as Salmon;
And the son of Salmon by Rahab as Boaz; and the son of Boaz by Ruth as Obed; and the son of Obed as Jesse;
And the son of Jesse as David the king; and the son of David as Solomon by her ho had been the ife of Uriah;
And the son of Solomon as Rehoboam; and the son of Rehoboam as Abijah; and the son of Abijah as Asa;
And the son of Asa as Jehoshaphat; and the son of Jehoshaphat as Joram; and the son of Joram as Uzziah;
And the son of Uzziah as Jotham; and the son of Jotham as Ahaz; and the son of Ahaz as Hezekiah;
And the son of Hezekiah as Manasseh; and the son of Manasseh as Amon; and the son of Amon as Josiah;
And the sons of Josiah ere Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the taking aay to Babylon.
And after the taking aay to Babylon, Jechoniah had a son Shealtiel; and Shealtiel had Zerubbabel;
And Zerubbabel had Abiud; and Abiud had Eliakim; and Eliakim had Azor;
And Azor had Zadok; and Zadok had Achim; and Achim had Eliud;
And Eliud had Eleazar; and Eleazar had Matthan; and Matthan had Jacob;
And the son of Jacob as Joseph the husband of Mary, ho gave birth to Jesus, hose name is Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; and from David to the taking aay to Babylon, fourteen generations; and from the taking aay to Babylon to the coming of Christ, fourteen generations.
No the birth of Jesus Christ as in this ay: hen his mother Mary as going to be married to Joseph, before they came together the discovery as made that she as ith child by the Holy Spirit.
And Joseph, her husband, being an upright man, and not desiring to make her a public example, had a mind to put her aay privately.

But hen he as giving thought to these things, an angel of the Lord came to him in a dream, saying, Joseph, son of David, have no fear of taking Mary as your ife; because that hich is in her body is of the Holy Spirit.
And she ill give birth to a son; and you ill give him the name Jesus; for he ill give his people salvation from their sins.
No all this took place so that the ord of the Lord by the prophet might come true,
See, the virgin ill be ith child, and ill give birth to a son, and they ill give him the name Immanuel, that is, God ith us.
And Joseph did as the angel of the Lord had said to him, and took her as his ife;
And he had no connection ith her till she had given birth to a son; and he gave him the name Jesus.
No hen the birth of Jesus took place in Beth-lehem of Judaea, in the days of Herod the king, there came ise men from the east to Jerusalem,
Saying, Where is the King of the Jes hose birth has no taken place? We have seen his star in the east and have come to give him orship.
And hen it came to the ears of Herod the king, he as troubled, and all Jerusalem ith him.
And he got together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, questioning them as to here the birth-place of the Christ ould be.
And they said to him, In Beth-lehem of Judaea; for so it is said in the ritings of the prophet,
You Beth-lehem, in the land of Judah, are not the least among the chiefs of Judah: out of you ill come a ruler, ho ill be the keeper of my people Israel.
Then Herod sent for the ise men privately, and put questions to them about hat time the star had been seen.
And he sent them to Beth-lehem and said, Go and make certain here the young child is; and hen you have seen him, let me have nes of it, so that I may come and give him orship.
And after hearing the king, they ent on their ay; and the star hich they sa in the east ent before them, till it came to rest over the place here the young child as.
And hen they sa the star they ere full of joy.

And they came into the house, and sa the young child ith Mary, his mother; and falling don on their faces they gave him orship; and from their store they gave him offerings of gold, perfume, and spices.
And it as made clear to them by God in a dream that they ere not to go back to Herod; so they ent into their country by another ay.

And hen they had gone, an angel of the Lord came to Joseph in a dream, saying, Get up and take the young child and his mother, and go into Egypt, and do not go from there till I give you ord; for Herod ill be searching for the young child to put him to death.
So he took the young child and his mother by night, and ent into Egypt;
And as there till the death of Herod; so that the ord of the Lord through the prophet might come true, Out of Egypt have I sent for my son.

Then Herod, hen he sa that he had been tricked by the ise men, as very angry; and he sent out, and put to death all the male children in Beth-lehem and in all the parts round about it, from to years old and under, acting on the knoledge hich he had got ith care from the ise men.
Then the ord of Jeremiah the prophet came true,
In Ramah there as a sound of eeping and great sorro, Rachel eeping for her children, and she ould not be comforted for their loss.
But hen Herod as dead, an angel of the Lord came in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
Saying, Get up and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel: because they ho ere attempting to take the young child’s life are dead.
And he got up, and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.

But hen it came to his ears that Archelaus as ruling over Judaea in the place of his father Herod, he as in fear of going there; and God having given him nes of the danger in a dream, he ent out of the ay into the country parts of Galilee.
And he came and as living in a ton named Nazareth: so that the ord of the prophets might come true, He ill be named a Nazarene.
And in those days John the Baptist came preaching in the aste land of Judaea,
Saying, Let your hearts be turned from sin; for the kingdom of heaven is near.
For this is he of hom Isaiah the prophet said, The voice of one crying in the aste land, Make ready the ay of the Lord, make his roads straight.
No John as clothed in camel’s hair, ith a leather band about him; and his food as locusts and honey.
Then Jerusalem and all Judaea ent out to him, and all the people from near Jordan;
And they ere given baptism by him in the river Jordan, saying openly that they had done rong.
But hen he sa a number of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, Offspring of snakes, at hose ord are you going in flight from the rath to come?
Let your change of heart be seen in your orks:
And say not to yourselves, We have Abraham for our father; because I say to you that God is able from these stones to make children for Abraham.
And even no the axe is put to the root of the trees; every tree then hich does not give good fruit is cut don, and put into the fire.

Truly, I give baptism ith ater to those of you hose hearts are changed; but he ho comes after me is greater than I, hose shoes I am not good enough to take up: he ill give you baptism ith the Holy Spirit and ith fire:
In hose hand is the instrument ith hich he ill make clean his grain; he ill put the good grain in his store, but the aste ill be burned up in the fire hich ill never be put out.
Then Jesus came from Galilee to John at the Jordan, to be given baptism by him.
But John ould have kept him back, saying, It is I ho have need of baptism from you, and do you come to me?
But Jesus made anser, saying to him, Let it be so no: because so it is right for us to make righteousness complete. Then he gave him baptism.
And Jesus, having been given baptism, straight aay ent up from the ater; and, the heavens opening, he sa the Spirit of God coming don on him as a dove;
And a voice came out of heaven, saying, This is my dearly loved Son, ith hom I am ell pleased.
Then Jesus as sent by the Spirit into the aste land to be tested by the Evil One.
And after going ithout food for forty days and forty nights, he as in need of it.
And the Evil One came and said to him, If you are the Son of God, give the ord for these stones to become bread.
But he made anser and said, It is in the Writings, Bread is not man’s only need, but every ord hich comes out of the mouth of God.
Then the Evil One took him to the holy ton; and he put him on the highest point of the Temple and said to him,

If you are the Son of God, let yourself go don; for it is in the Writings, He ill give his angels care over you; and, In their hands they ill keep you up, so that your foot may not be crushed against a stone.
Jesus said to him, Again it is in the Writings, You may not put the Lord your God to the test.
Again, the Evil One took him up to a very high mountain, and let him see all the kingdoms of the orld and the glory of them;
And he said to him, All these things ill I give you, if you ill go don on your face and give me orship.
Then said Jesus to him, Aay, Satan: for it is in the Writings, Give orship to the Lord your God and be his servant only.
Then the Evil One ent aay from him, and angels came and took care of him.
No hen it came to his ears that John had been put in prison, he ent aay to Galilee;
And going aay from Nazareth, he came and made his living-place in Capernaum, hich is by the sea, in the country of Zebulun and Naphtali:
So that the ord of the prophet Isaiah might come true,
The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, by the ay of the sea, the other side of Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,
The people ho ere in the dark sa a great light, and to those in the land of the shade of death did the dan come up.
From that time Jesus ent about preaching and saying, Let your hearts be turned from sin, for the kingdom of heaven is near.
And hen he as alking by the sea of Galilee, he sa to brothers, Simon, hose other name as Peter, and Andre, his brother, ho ere putting a net into the sea; for they ere fishermen.
And he said to them, Come after me, and I ill make you fishers of men.
And straight aay they let go the nets and ent after him.
And going on from there he sa to other brothers, James, the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, in the boat ith their father, stitching up their nets; and he said, Come.
And they ent straight from the boat and their father and came after him.
And Jesus ent about in all Galilee, teaching in their Synagogues and preaching the good nes of the kingdom, and making ell those ho ere ill ith any disease among the people.

And nes of him ent out through all Syria; and they took to him all ho ere ill ith different diseases and pains, those having evil spirits and those ho ere off their heads, and those ho had no poer of moving. And he made them ell.
And there ent after him great numbers from Galilee and Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judaea and from the other side of Jordan.
And seeing great masses of people he ent up into the mountain; and hen he as seated his disciples came to him.
And ith these ords he gave them teaching, saying,
Happy are the poor in spirit: for the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
Happy are those ho are sad: for they ill be comforted.
Happy are the gentle: for the earth ill be their heritage.
Happy are those hose heart’s desire is for righteousness: for they ill have their desire.
Happy are those ho have mercy: for they ill be given mercy.
Happy are the clean in heart: for they ill see God.
Happy are the peacemakers: for they ill be named sons of God.
Happy are those ho are attacked on account of righteousness: for the kingdom of heaven ill be theirs.
Happy are you hen men give you a bad name, and are cruel to you, and say all evil things against you falsely, because of me.
Be glad and full of joy; for great is your reard in heaven: for so ere the prophets attacked ho ere before you.
You are the salt of the earth; but if its taste goes from the salt, ho ill you make it salt again? it is then good for nothing but to be put out and crushed under foot by men.
You are the light of the orld. A ton put on a hill may be seen by all.
And a burning light is not put under a vessel, but on its table; so that its rays may be shining on all ho are in the house.
Even so let your light be shining before men, so that they may see your good orks and give glory to your Father in heaven.
Let there be no thought that I have come to put an end to the la or the prophets. I have not come for destruction, but to make complete.
Truly I say to you, Till heaven and earth come to an end, not the smallest letter or part of a letter ill in any ay be taken from the la, till all things are done.

Whoever then goes against the smallest of these las, teaching men to do the same, ill be named least in the kingdom of heaven; but he ho keeps the las, teaching others to keep them, ill be named great in the kingdom of heaven.
For I say to you, If your righteousness is not greater than the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, you ill never go into the kingdom of heaven.
You have knoledge that it as said in old times, You may not put to death; and, Whoever puts to death ill be in danger of being judged:

But I say to you that everyone ho is angry ith his brother ill be in danger of being judged; and he ho says to his brother, Raca, ill be in danger from the Sanhedrin; and hoever says, You foolish one, ill be in danger of the hell of fire.
If then you are making an offering at the altar and there it comes to your mind that your brother has something against you,
While your offering is still before the altar, first go and make peace ith your brother, then come and make your offering.

Come to an agreement quickly ith him ho has a cause against you at la, hile you are ith him on the ay, for fear that he may give you up to the judge and the judge may give you to the police and you may be put into prison.
Truly I say to you, You ill not come out from there till you have made payment of the very last farthing.
You have knoledge that it as said, You may not have connection ith another man’s ife:
But I say to you that everyone hose eyes are turned on a oman ith desire has had connection ith her in his heart.
And if your right eye is a cause of trouble to you, take it out and put it aay from you; because it is better to undergo the loss of one part, than for all your body to go into hell.
And if your right hand is a cause of trouble to you, let it be cut off and put it aay from you; because it is better to undergo the loss of one part, than for all your body to go into hell.
Again, it as said, Whoever puts aay his ife has to give her a statement in riting for this purpose:

But I say to you that everyone ho puts aay his ife for any other cause but the loss of her virtue, makes her false to her husband; and hoever takes her as his ife after she is put aay, is no true husband to her.
Again, you have knoledge that it as said in old times, Do not take false oaths, but give effect to your oaths to the Lord:
But I say to you, Take no oaths at all: not by the heaven, because it is the seat of God;
Or by the earth, because it is the resting-place for his foot; or by Jerusalem, because it is the ton of the great King.
You may not take an oath by your head, because you are not able to make one hair hite or black.
But let your ords be simply, Yes or No: and hatever is more than these is of the Evil One.
You have knoledge that it as said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth:
But I say to you, Do not make use of force against an evil man; but to him ho gives you a blo on the right side of your face let the left be turned.
And if any man goes to la ith you and takes aay your coat, do not keep back your robe from him.
And hoever makes you go one mile, go ith him to.
Give to him ho comes ith a request, and keep not your property from him ho ould for a time make use of it.
You have knoledge that it as said, Have love for your neighbour, and hate for him ho is against you:
But I say to you, Have love for those ho are against you, and make prayer for those ho are cruel to you;
So that you may be the sons of your Father in heaven; for his sun gives light to the evil and to the good, and he sends rain on the upright man and on the sinner.
For if you have love for those ho have love for you, hat credit is it to you? do not the tax-farmers the same?
And if you say, Good day, to your brothers only, hat do you do more than others? do not even the Gentiles the same?
Be then complete in righteousness, even as your Father in heaven is complete.
Take care not to do your good orks before men, to be seen by them; or you ill have no reard from your Father in heaven.

When then you give money to the poor, do not make a noise about it, as the false-hearted men do in the Synagogues and in the streets, so that they may have glory from men. Truly, I say to you, They have their reard.
But hen you give money, let not your left hand see hat your right hand does:
So that your giving may be in secret; and your Father, ho sees in secret, ill give you your reard.

And hen you make your prayers, be not like the false-hearted men, ho take pleasure in getting up and saying their prayers in the Synagogues and at the street turnings so that they may be seen by men. Truly I say to you, They have their reard.
But hen you make your prayer, go into your private room, and, shutting the door, say a prayer to your Father in secret, and your Father, ho sees in secret, ill give you your reard.
And in your prayer do not make use of the same ords again and again, as the Gentiles do: for they have the idea that God ill give attention to them because of the number of their ords.
So be not like them; because your Father has knoledge of your needs even before you make your requests to him.
Let this then be your prayer: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your kingdom come. Let your pleasure be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
Give us this day bread for our needs.
And make us free of our debts, as e have made those free ho are in debt to us.
And let us not be put to the test, but keep us safe from the Evil One.
For if you let men have forgiveness for their sins, you ill have forgiveness from your Father in heaven.
But if you do not let men have forgiveness for their sins, you ill not have forgiveness from your Father for your sins.

And hen you go ithout food, be not sad-faced as the false-hearted are. For they go about ith changed looks, so that men may see that they are going ithout food. Truly I say to you, They have their reard.
But hen you go ithout food, put oil on your head and make your face clean;
So that no one may see that you are going ithout food, but your Father in secret; and your Father, ho sees in secret, ill give you your reard.
Make no store of ealth for yourselves on earth, here it may be turned to dust by orms and eather, and here thieves may come in by force and take it aay.
But make a store for yourselves in heaven, here it ill not be turned to dust and here thieves do not come in to take it aay:
For here your ealth is, there ill your heart be.
The light of the body is the eye; if then your eye is true, all your body ill be full of light.
But if your eye is evil, all your body ill be dark. If then the light hich is in you is dark, ho dark it ill be!

No man is able to be a servant to to masters: for he ill have hate for the one and love for the other, or he ill keep to one and have no respect for the other. You may not be servants of God and of ealth.
So I say to you, Take no thought for your life, about food or drink, or about clothing for your body. Is not life more than food, and the body more than its clothing?
See the birds of heaven; they do not put seeds in the earth, they do not get in grain, or put it in store-houses; and your Father in heaven gives them food. Are you not of much more value than they?
And hich of you by taking thought is able to make himself a cubit taller?
And hy are you troubled about clothing? See the floers of the field, ho they come up; they do no ork, they make no thread:
But I say to you that even Solomon in all his glory as not clothed like one of these.
But if God gives such clothing to the grass of the field, hich is here today and tomorro is put into the oven, ill he not much more give you clothing, O you of little faith?
Then do not be full of care, saying, What are e to have for food or drink? or, With hat may e be clothed?
Because the Gentiles go in search of all these things: for your Father in heaven has knoledge that you have need of all these things:
But let your first care be for his kingdom and his righteousness; and all these other things ill be given to you in addition.
Then have no care for tomorro: tomorro ill take care of itself. Take the trouble of the day as it comes.
Be not judges of others, and you ill not be judged.
For as you have been judging, so you ill be judged, and ith your measure ill it be measured to you.
And hy do you take note of the grain of dust in your brother’s eye, but take no note of the bit of ood hich is in your eye?
Or ho ill you say to your brother, Let me take out the grain of dust from your eye, hen you yourself have a bit of ood in your eye?
You false one, first take out the bit of ood from your eye, then ill you see clearly to take out the grain of dust from your brother’s eye.
Do not give that hich is holy to the dogs, or put your jeels before pigs, for fear that they ill be crushed under foot by the pigs hose attack ill then be made against you.
Make a request, and it ill be ansered; hat you are searching for you ill get; give the sign, and the door ill be open to you:
Because to everyone ho makes a request, it ill be given; and he ho is searching ill get his desire, and to him ho gives the sign, the door ill be open.
Or hich of you, if his son makes a request for bread, ill give him a stone?
Or if he makes a request for a fish, ill give him a snake?
If you, then, being evil, are able to give good things to your children, ho much more ill your Father in heaven give good things to those ho make requests to him?
All those things, then, hich you ould have men do to you, even so do you to them: because this is the la and the prophets.
Go in by the narro door; for ide is the door and open is the ay hich goes to destruction, and great numbers go in by it.
For narro is the door and hard the road to life, and only a small number make discovery of it.
Be on the atch for false prophets, ho come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inside they are cruel olves.
By their fruits you ill get knoledge of them. Do men get grapes from thorns or figs from thistles?
Even so, every good tree gives good fruit; but the bad tree gives evil fruit.
It is not possible for a good tree to give bad fruit, and a bad tree ill not give good fruit.
Every tree hich does not give good fruit is cut don and put in the fire.
So by their fruits you ill get knoledge of them.
Not everyone ho says to me, Lord, Lord, ill go into the kingdom of heaven; but he ho does the pleasure of my Father in heaven.
A great number ill say to me on that day, Lord, Lord, ere e not prophets in your name, and did e not by your name send out evil spirits, and by your name do orks of poer?
And then ill I say to them, I never had knoledge of you: go from me, you orkers of evil.
Everyone, then, to hom my ords come and ho does them, ill be like a ise man ho made his house on a rock;
And the rain came don and there as a rush of aters and the inds ere driving against that house, but it as not moved; because it as based on the rock.
And everyone to hom my ords come and ho does them not, ill be like a foolish man ho made his house on sand;
And the rain came don and there as a rush of aters and the inds ere driving against that house; and it came don and great as its fall.
And it came about, hen Jesus had come to the end of these ords, that the people ere surprised at his teaching,
for he as teaching as one having authority, and not as their scribes.
And hen he had come don from the mountain, great numbers of people came after him.
And a leper came and gave him orship, saying, Lord, if it is your pleasure, you have poer to make me clean.
And he put his hand on him, saying, It is my pleasure; be clean. And straight aay he as made clean.
And Jesus said to him, See that you say nothing about this to anyone; but go and let the priest see you and make the offering hich as ordered by Moses, for a itness to them.
And hen Jesus as come into Capernaum, a certain captain came to him ith a request,
Saying, Lord, my servant is ill in bed at the house, ith no poer in his body, and in great pain.
And he said to him, I ill come and make him ell.
And the captain in anser said, Lord, I am not good enough for you to come under my roof; but only say the ord, and my servant ill be made ell.
Because I myself am a man under authority, having under me fighting men; and I say to this one, Go, and he goes; and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my servant, Do this, and he does it.
And hen these ords came to the ears of Jesus he as surprised, and said to those ho came after him, Truly I say to you, I have not seen such great faith, no, not in Israel.
And I say to you that numbers ill come from the east and the est, and ill take their seats ith Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven:
But the sons of the kingdom ill be put out into the dark, and there ill be eeping and cries of pain.
And Jesus said to the captain, Go in peace; as your faith is, so let it be done to you. And the servant as made ell in that hour.
And hen Jesus had come into Peter’s house, he sa his ife’s mother in bed, very ill.
And he put his hand on hers and the disease ent from her, and she got up and took care of his needs.
And in the evening, they took to him a number of people ho had evil spirits; and he sent the spirits out of them ith a ord, and made ell all ho ere ill;
So that the ord of Isaiah the prophet might come true: He himself took our pains and our diseases.
No hen Jesus sa a great mass of people about him, he gave an order to go to the other side.
And there came a scribe and said to him, Master, I ill come after you herever you go.
And Jesus said to him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of heaven have a resting-place; but the Son of man has nohere to put his head.
And another of the disciples said to him, Lord, let me first go and give the last honours to my father.
But Jesus said to him, Come after me; and let the dead take care of their dead.
And hen he had got into a boat, his disciples ent after him.
And there came up a great storm in the sea, so that the boat as covered ith the aves: but he as sleeping.
And they came to him, and, aaking him, said, Help, Lord; destruction is near.
And he said to them, Why are you full of fear, O you of little faith? Then he got up and gave orders to the inds and the sea; and there as a great calm.
And the men ere full of onder, saying, What sort of man is this, that even the inds and the sea do his orders?
And hen he had come to the other side, to the country of the Gadarenes, there came out to him from the place of the dead, to ho had evil spirits, so violent that no man as able to go that ay.
And they gave a loud cry, saying, What have e to do ith you, you Son of God? Have you come here to give us punishment before the time?
No there as, some distance aay, a great herd of pigs taking their food.
And the evil spirits made strong prayers to him, saying, If you send us out, let us go into the herd of pigs.
And he said to them, Go. And they came out, and ent into the pigs; and the herd ent rushing don a sharp slope into the sea and came to their end in the ater.
And their keepers ent in flight to the ton and gave an account of everything, and of the men ho had the evil spirits.
And all the ton came out to Jesus; and seeing him they made request that he ould go aay from their part of the country.
And he got into a boat and ent across and came to his ton.
And they took to him a man stretched on a bed ho had no poer of moving; and Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the man ho as ill, Son, take heart; you have forgiveness for your sins.
And some of the scribes said among themselves, This man has no respect for God.
And Jesus, having knoledge of hat as in their minds, said, Why are your thoughts evil?
For hich is the simpler, to say, You have forgiveness for your sins; or to say, Get up and go?
But so that you may see that on earth the Son of man has authority for the forgiveness of sins, ( then said he to the man ho as ill,) Get up, and take up your bed, and go to your house.
And he got up and ent aay to his house.
But hen the people sa it they ere full of fear, and gave glory to God ho had given such authority to men.
And hen Jesus as going from there, he sa a man hose name as Matthe, seated at the place here taxes ere taken; and he said to him, Come after me. And he got up and ent after him.
And it came about, hen he as in the house taking food, that a number of tax-farmers and sinners came and took their places ith Jesus and his disciples.
And hen the Pharisees sa it, they said to his disciples, Why does your Master take food ith tax-farmers and sinners?
But on hearing this he said, Those ho are ell have no need of a medical man, but those ho are ill.
But go and take to heart the sense of these ords, My desire is for mercy, not offerings: for I have come not to get the upright, but sinners.
Then the disciples of John came to him, saying, Why do e and the Pharisees frequently go ithout food, but your disciples do not?
And Jesus said to them, Will the friends of the nely-married man be sad as long as he is ith them? But the days ill come hen he ill be taken aay from them, and then ill they go ithout food.
And no man puts a bit of ne cloth on an old coat, for by pulling aay from the old, it makes a orse hole.
And men do not put ne ine into old ine-skins; or the skins ill be burst and the ine ill come out, and the skins are of no more use: but they put ne ine into ne ine-skins, and so the to ill be safe.
While he as saying these things to them, there came a ruler and gave him orship, saying, My daughter is even no dead; but come and put your hand on her, and she ill come back to life.
And Jesus got up and ent after him, and so did his disciples.
And a oman, ho for telve years had had a flo of blood, came after him, and put her hand on the edge of his robe:
Because, she said to herself, if I may but put my hand on his robe, I ill be made ell.
But Jesus, turning and seeing her, said, Daughter, take heart; your faith has made you ell. And the oman as made ell from that hour.
And hen Jesus came into the ruler’s house and sa the players ith their instruments and the people making a noise,
He said, Make room; for the girl is not dead, but sleeping. And they ere laughing at him.
But hen the people ere sent out, he ent in and took her by the hand; and the girl got up.
And the nes of it ent out into all that land.
And hen Jesus ent on from there, to blind men came after him, crying out, Have mercy on us, you Son of David.
And hen he had come into the house, the blind men came to him; and Jesus said to them, Have you faith that I am able to do this? They said to him, Yes, Lord.
Then he put his hand on their eyes, saying, As your faith is, let it be done to you.
And their eyes ere made open. And Jesus said to them sharply, Let no man have knoledge of it.
But they ent out and gave nes of him in all that land.
And hile they ere going aay, there came to him a man ithout the poer of talking, and ith an evil spirit.
And hen the evil spirit had been sent out, the man had the poer of talking: and they ere all surprised, saying, Such a thing has never been seen in Israel.
But the Pharisees said, By the ruler of evil spirits, he sends evil spirits out of men.
And Jesus ent about all the tons and small places, teaching in their Synagogues and preaching the good nes of the kingdom and making ell all sorts of disease and pain.
But hen he sa all the people he as moved ith pity for them, because they ere troubled and andering like sheep ithout a keeper.
Then he said to his disciples, There is much grain but not enough men to get it in.
Make prayer, then, to the Lord of the grain-fields, that he may send out orkers to get in his grain.
And he got together his telve disciples and gave them the poer of driving out unclean spirits, and of making ell all sorts of disease and pain.
No the names of the telve are these: The first, Simon, ho is named Peter, and Andre, his brother; James, the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother;
Philip and Bartholome; Thomas and Matthe, the tax-farmer; James, the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot, ho as false to him.
These telve Jesus sent out and gave them orders, saying, Do not go among the Gentiles, or into any ton of Samaria,
But go to the andering sheep of the house of Israel,
And, on your ay, say, The kingdom of heaven is near.
Make ell those ho are ill, give life to the dead, make lepers clean, send evil spirits out of men; freely it has been given to you, freely give.
Take no gold or silver or copper in your pockets;
Take no bag for your journey and do not take to coats or shoes or a stick: for the orkman has a right to his food.
And into hatever ton or small place you go, make search there for someone ho is respected, and make his house your resting-place till you go aay.
And hen you go in, say, May peace be on this house.
And if the house is good enough, let your peace come on it: but if not, let your peace come back to you.
And hoever ill not take you in, or give ear to your ords, hen you go out from that house or that ton, put off its dust from your feet.
Truly I say to you, It ill be better for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of God’s judging than for that ton.
See, I send you out as sheep among olves. Be then as ise as snakes, and as gentle as doves.
But be on the atch against men: for they ill give you up to the Sanhedrins, and in their Synagogues they ill give you blos;
And you ill come before rulers and kings because of me, for a itness to them and to the Gentiles.
But hen you are given up into their hands, do not be troubled about hat to say or ho to say it: for in that hour hat you are to say ill be given to you;
Because it is not you ho say the ords, but the Spirit of your Father in you.
