And brother ill give up brother to death, and the father his child: and children ill go against their fathers and mothers, and put them to death.
And you ill be hated by all men because of my name: but he ho is strong to the end ill have salvation.
But hen they are cruel to you in one ton, go in flight to another: for truly, I say to you, You ill not have gone through the tons of Israel before the Son of man comes.
A disciple is not greater than his master, or a servant than his lord.
It is enough for the disciple that he may be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have given the name Beelzebub to the master of the house, ho much more to those of his house!
Have, then, no fear of them: because nothing is covered hich ill not come to light, or secret hich ill not be made clear.
What I say to you in the dark, say in the light: and hat comes to your ear secretly, say publicly from the house-tops.
And have no fear of those ho put to death the body, but are not able to put to death the soul. But have fear of him ho has poer to give soul and body to destruction in hell.
Are not sparros to a farthing? and not one of them comes to an end ithout your Father:
But the hairs of your head are all numbered.
Then have no fear; you are of more value than a flock of sparros.
To everyone, then, ho gives itness to me before men, I ill give itness before my Father in heaven.
But if anyone says before men that he has no knoledge of me, I ill say that I have no knoledge of him before my Father in heaven.
Do not have the thought that I have come to send peace on the earth; I came not to send peace but a sord.
For I have come to put a man against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter-in-la against her mother-in-la:
And a man ill be hated by those of his house.
He ho has more love for his father or mother than for me is not good enough for me; he ho has more love for son or daughter than for me is not good enough for me.
And he ho does not take his cross and come after me is not good enough for me.
He ho has the desire to keep his life ill have it taken from him, and he ho gives up his life because of me ill have it given back to him.
He ho gives honour to you gives honour to me; and he ho gives honour to me gives honour to him ho sent me.

He ho gives honour to a prophet, in the name of a prophet, ill be given a prophet’s reard; and he ho gives honour to an upright man, in the name of an upright man, ill be given an upright man’s reard.
And hoever gives to one of these little ones a cup of cold ater only, in the name of a disciple, truly I say to you, he ill not go ithout his reard.
And it came about that hen Jesus had come to the end of giving these orders to his telve disciples, he ent aay from there, teaching and preaching in their tons.
No hen John had nes in prison of the orks of the Christ, he sent his disciples
To say to him, Are you he ho is to come, or are e aiting for another?
And Jesus, ansering, said to them, Go and give nes to John of the things hich you are seeing and hearing:

The blind see; those ho ere not able to, are alking; lepers are made clean; those ho ere ithout hearing, no have their ears open; the dead come to life again, and the poor have the good nes given to them.
And a blessing ill be on him ho has no doubts about me.
And hen they ere going aay, Jesus, talking of John, said to all the people, What ent you out into the aste land to see? a tall stem moving in the ind?
But hat ent you out to see? a man delicately clothed? Those ho have fair robes are in kings’ houses.
But hy did you go out? to see a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
This is he of hom it has been said, See, I send my servant before your face, ho ill make ready your ay before you.
Truly I say to you, Among the sons of omen there has not been a greater than John the Baptist: but he ho is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
And from the days of John the Baptist till no, the kingdom of heaven is forcing its ay in, and men of force take it.
For all the prophets and the la ere in force till John.
And if you are able to see it, this is Elijah ho as to come.
He ho has ears, let him give ear.
But hat comparison may I make of this generation? It is like children seated in the market-places, crying out to one another,
We made music for you and you did not take part in the dance; e gave cries of sorro and you made no signs of grief.
For John came, taking no food or drink, and they say, He has an evil spirit.
The Son of man has come feasting, and they say, See, a lover of food and ine, a friend of tax-farmers and sinners! And isdom is judged to be right by her orks.
Then he ent on to say hard things to the tons here most of his orks of poer ere done, because they had not been turned from their sins.

Unhappy are you, Chorazin! Unhappy are you, Beth-saida! For if the orks of poer hich ere done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they ould have been turned from their sins in days gone by, clothing themselves in haircloth and putting dust on their heads.
But I say to you, It ill be better for Tyre and Sidon in the day of judging, than for you.
And you, Capernaum, ere you not to be lifted up to heaven? you ill go don into hell: for if the orks of poer hich ere done in you had been done in Sodom, it ould have been here to this day.
But I say to you that it ill be better for the land of Sodom in the day of judging, than for you.

At that time Jesus made anser and said, I give praise to you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have kept these things secret from the ise and the men of learning, and have made them clear to little children.
Yes, Father, for so it as pleasing in your eyes.
All things have been given to me by my Father; and no one has knoledge of the Son, but the Father; and no one has knoledge of the Father, but the Son, and he to hom the Son ill make it clear.
Come to me, all you ho are troubled and eighted don ith care, and I ill give you rest.
Take my yoke on you and become like me, for I am gentle and ithout pride, and you ill have rest for your souls;
For my yoke is good, and the eight I take up is not hard.
At that time Jesus ent through the fields on the Sabbath day; and his disciples, being in need of food, ere taking the heads of grain.
But the Pharisees, hen they sa it, said to him, See, your disciples do that hich it is not right to do on the Sabbath.
But he said to them, Have you no knoledge of hat David did hen he had need of food, and those ho ere ith him?
Ho he ent into the house of God and took for food the holy bread hich it as not right for him or for those ho ere ith him to take, but only for the priests?
Or is it not said in the la, ho the Sabbath is broken by the priests in the Temple and they do no rong?
But I say to you that a greater thing than the Temple is here.
But if these ords had been in your minds, My desire is for mercy and not for offerings, you ould not have been judging those ho have done no rong.
For the Son of man is lord of the Sabbath.
And he ent from there into their Synagogue:
And there as a man ith a dead hand. And they put a question to him, saying, Is it right to make a man ell on the Sabbath day? so that they might have something against him.
And he said to them, Which of you, having a sheep, if it gets into a hole on the Sabbath day, ill not put out a helping hand and get it back?
Of ho much more value is a man than a sheep! For this reason it is right to do good on the Sabbath day.
Then said he to the man, Put out your hand. And he put it out, and it as made as ell as the other.
But the Pharisees ent out and made designs against him, ho they might put him to death.
And Jesus, having knoledge of this, ent aay from there, and a great number ent after him; and he made them all ell,
Ordering them not to give people ord of him:
So that hat as said by Isaiah the prophet might come true,
See my servant, the man of my selection, my loved one in hom my soul is ell pleased: I ill put my Spirit on him, and he ill make my decision clear to the Gentiles.
His coming ill not be ith fighting or loud cries; and his voice ill not be lifted up in the streets.
The crushed stem ill not be broken by him; and the feebly burning light ill he not put out, till he has made righteousness overcome all.
And in his name ill the Gentiles put their hope.
Then they took to him one ith an evil spirit, ho as blind and had no poer of talking: and he made him ell so that he had the poer of talking and seeing.
And all the people ere surprised and said, Is not this the Son of David?
But the Pharisees, hearing of it, said, This man only sends evil spirits out of men by Beelzebub, the ruler of evil spirits.
And having knoledge of their thoughts he said to them, Every kingdom having division in itself is made aste, and every ton or house having division in itself ill come to destruction.
And if Satan sends out Satan, he makes ar against himself; ho then ill he keep his kingdom?
And if I by Beelzebub send evil spirits out of men, by hom do your sons send them out? So let them be your judges.
But if I by the Spirit of God send out evil spirits, then is the kingdom of God come on you.
Or ho may one go into a strong man’s house and take his goods, if he does not first put cords round the strong man? and then he may take his goods.
Whoever is not ith me is against me; and he ho does not take part ith me in getting people together, is driving them aay.
So I say to you, Every sin and every evil ord against God ill have forgiveness; but for evil ords against the Spirit there ill be no forgiveness.
And hoever says a ord against the Son of man, ill have forgiveness; but hoever says a ord against the Holy Spirit, ill not have forgiveness in this life or in that hich is to come.
Make the tree good, and its fruit good; or make the tree bad, and its fruit bad; for by its fruit you ill get knoledge of the tree.
You offspring of snakes, ho are you, being evil, able to say good things? because out of the heart’s store come the ords of the mouth.
The good man out of his good store gives good things; and the evil man out of his evil store gives evil things.
And I say to you that in the day hen they are judged, men ill have to give an account of every foolish ord they have said.
For by your ords ill your righteousness be seen, and by your ords you ill be judged.
Then some of the scribes and Pharisees, hearing this, said to him, Master, e are looking for a sign from you.
But he, ansering, said to them, An evil and false generation is looking for a sign; and no sign ill be given to it but the sign of the prophet Jonah:
For as Jonah as three days and three nights in the stomach of the great fish, so ill the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

The men of Nineveh ill come up in the day of judging and give their decision against this generation: because they ere turned from their sins at the preaching of Jonah; and no a greater than Jonah is here.

The queen of the South ill come up in the day of judging and give her decision against this generation: for she came from the ends of the earth to give ear to the isdom of Solomon; and no a greater than Solomon is here.
But the unclean spirit, hen he is gone out of a man, goes through dry places looking for rest, and getting it not.
Then he says, I ill go back into my house from hich I came out; and hen he comes, he sees that there is no one in it, but that it has been made fair and clean.

Then he goes and takes ith him seven other spirits orse than himself, and they go in and make it their living-place: and the last condition of that man is orse than the first. Even so ill it be ith this evil generation.
While he as still talking to the people, his mother and his brothers came, desiring to have talk ith him.
And one said to him, See, your mother and your brothers are outside, desiring to have talk ith you.
But he in anser said to him ho gave the nes, Who is my mother and ho are my brothers?
And he put out his hand to his disciples and said, See, my mother and my brothers!
For hoever does the pleasure of my Father in heaven, he is my brother, and sister, and mother.
On that day Jesus ent out of the house and as seated by the seaside.
And great numbers of people came together to him, so that he got into a boat; and the people took up their position by the sea.
And he gave them teaching in the form of a story, saying, A man ent out to put seed in the earth;
And hile he did so, some seeds ere dropped by the ayside, and the birds came and took them for food:
And some of the seed ent among the stones, here it had not much earth, and straight aay it came up because the earth as not deep:
And hen the sun as high, it as burned; and because it had no root it became dry and dead.
And some seeds ent among thorns, and the thorns came up and they had no room for groth:
And some, falling on good earth, gave fruit, some a hundred, some sixty, some thirty times as much.
He ho has ears, let him give ear.
And the disciples came and said to him, Why do you say things to them in the form of stories?
And he said to them in anser, To you is given the knoledge of the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
Because hoever has, to him ill be given, and he ill have more; but from him ho has not, even hat he has ill be taken aay.
For this reason I put things into the form of stories; because they see ithout seeing, and give ear ithout hearing, and the sense is not clear to them.
And for them the ords of Isaiah have come true, Though you give ear, you ill not get knoledge; and seeing, you ill see, but the sense ill not be clear to you:

For the heart of this people has become fat and their ears are slo in hearing and their eyes are shut; for fear that they might see ith their eyes and give hearing ith their ears and become ise in their hearts and be turned again to me, so that I might make them ell.
But a blessing be on your eyes, because they see; and on your ears, because they are open.
For truly, I say to you that prophets and upright men had a desire to see the things hich you see, and sa them not; and to have knoledge of the ords hich have come to your ears, and they had it not.
Give ear, then, to the story of the man ho put the seed in the earth.

When the ord of the kingdom comes to anyone, and the sense of it is not clear to him, then the Evil One comes, and quickly takes aay that hich as put in his heart. He is the seed dropped by the ayside.
And that hich ent on the stones, this is he ho, hearing the ord, straight aay takes it ith joy;
But having no root in himself, he goes on for a time; and hen trouble comes or pain, because of the ord, he quickly becomes full of doubts.
And that hich as dropped among the thorns, this is he ho has the ord; and the cares of this life, and the deceits of ealth, put a stop to the groth of the ord and it gives no fruit.
And the seed hich as put in good earth, this is he ho gives ear to the ord, and gets the sense of it; ho gives fruit, some a hundred, some sixty, some thirty times as much.
And he gave them another story, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like a man ho put good seed in his field:
But hile men ere sleeping, one ho had hate for him came and put evil seeds among the grain, and ent aay.
But hen the green stem came up and gave fruit, the evil plants ere seen at the same time.
And the servants of the master of the house came and said to him, Sir, did you not put good seed in your field? ho then has it evil plants?
And he said, Someone has done this in hate. And the servants say to him, Is it your pleasure that e go and take them up?
But he says, No, for fear that by chance hile you take up the evil plants, you may be rooting up the grain ith them.
Let them come up together till the getting in of the grain; and then I ill say to the orkers, Take up first the evil plants, and put them together for burning: but put the grain into my store-house.
He put another story before them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of mustard seed hich a man took and put in his field:
Which is smaller than all seeds; but hen it has come up it is greater than the plants, and becomes a tree, so that the birds of heaven come and make their resting-places in its branches.
Another story he gave to them: The kingdom of heaven is like leaven, hich a oman took, and put in three measures of meal, till it as all leavened.
All these things Jesus said to the people in the form of stories; and ithout a story he said nothing to them:
That it might come true hich as said by the prophet, Opening my mouth, I ill give out stories; I ill give knoledge of things kept secret from before all time.
Then he ent aay from the people, and ent into the house; and his disciples came to him, saying, Make clear to us the story of the evil plants in the field.
And he made anser and said, He ho puts the good seed in the earth is the Son of man;
And the field is the orld; and the good seed is the sons of the kingdom; and the evil seeds are the sons of the Evil One;
And he ho put them in the earth is Satan; and the getting in of the grain is the end of the orld; and those ho get it in are the angels.
As then the evil plants are got together and burned ith fire, so ill it be in the end of the orld.
The Son of man ill send out his angels, and they ill take out of his kingdom everything hich is a cause of error, and all those ho do rong,
And ill put them into the fire; there ill be eeping and cries of sorro.
Then ill the upright be shining as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He ho has ears, let him give ear.
The kingdom of heaven is like a secret store of ealth in a field, hich a man came across and put back again; and in his joy he goes and gives all he has, to get that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a trader searching for beautiful jeels.
And having come across one jeel of great price, he ent and gave all he had in exchange for it.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net, hich as put into the sea and took in every sort of fish:
When it as full, they took it up on the sands; and seated there they put the good into vessels, but the bad they put aay.
So ill it be in the end of the orld: the angels ill come and take out the bad from the good,
And ill put them into the fire: there ill be eeping and cries of sorro.
Are all these things no clear to you? They say to him, Yes.
And he said to them, For this reason every scribe ho has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like the oner of a house, ho gives out from his store things ne and old.
And hen Jesus had come to the end of these stories he ent aay from there.
And coming into his country, he gave them teaching in their Synagogue, so that they ere greatly surprised and said, Where did this man get this isdom and these orks of poer?
Is not this the oodorker’s son? is not his mother named Mary? and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
And his sisters, are they not all ith us? from here, then, has he all these things?
And they ere bitter against him. But Jesus said to them, A prophet is nohere ithout honour but in his country and among his family.
And the orks of poer hich he did there ere small in number because they had no faith.
At that time nes of Jesus came to Herod the king;
And he said to his servants, This is John the Baptist; he has come back from the dead, and so these poers are orking in him.
For Herod had taken John and put him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s ife.
Because John had said to him, It is not right for you to have her.
And he ould have put him to death, but for his fear of the people, because in their eyes John as a prophet.
But hen Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias as dancing before them, and Herod as pleased ith her.
So he gave her his ord ith an oath to let her have hatever she might make request for.
And she, at her mother’s suggestion, said, Give me here on a plate the head of John the Baptist.
And the king as sad; but because of his oaths and because of his guests, he gave the order for it to be given to her;
And he sent and had John’s head cut off in the prison.
And his head as put on a plate and given to the girl; and she took it to her mother.
And his disciples came, and took up his body and put it in the earth; and they ent and gave Jesus nes of hat had taken place.
No hen it came to the ears of Jesus, he ent aay from there in a boat, to a aste place by himself: and the people hearing of it, ent after him on foot from the tons.
And he came out and sa a great number of people and he had pity on them, and made ell those of them ho ere ill.
And hen evening had come, the disciples came to him, saying, This place is aste land, and the time is no past; send the people aay so that they may go into the tons and get themselves food.
But Jesus said to them, There is no need for them to go aay; give them food yourselves.
And they say to him, We have here but five cakes of bread and to fishes.
And he said, Give them to me.

And he gave orders for the people to be seated on the grass; and he took the five cakes of bread and the to fishes and, looking up to heaven, he said ords of blessing, and made division of the food, and gave it to the disciples, and the disciples gave it to the people.
And they all took of the food and had enough: and they took up telve baskets full of broken bits hich ere not used.
And those ho had food ere about five thousand men, in addition to omen and children.
And straight aay he made the disciples get into the boat and go before him to the other side, till he had sent the people aay.
And after he had sent the people aay, he ent up into the mountain by himself for prayer: and hen evening as come, he as there by himself.
But the boat as no in the middle of the sea, and as troubled by the aves: for the ind as against them.
And in the fourth atch of the night he came to them, alking on the sea.
And hen they sa him alking on the sea, they ere troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they gave cries of fear.
But straight aay Jesus said to them, Take heart; it is I, have no fear.
And Peter, ansering, said to him, Lord, if it is you, give me the order to come to you on the ater.
And he said, Come. And Peter got out of the boat, and alking on the ater, ent to Jesus.
But hen he sa the ind he as in fear and, starting to go don, he gave a cry, saying, Help, Lord.
And straight aay Jesus put out his hand and took a grip of him, and said to him, O man of little faith, hy ere you in doubt?
And hen they had got into the boat, the ind ent don.
And those ho ere in the boat gave him orship, saying, Truly you are the Son of God.
And hen they had gone across, they came to land at Gennesaret.
And hen the men of that place had nes of him, they sent into all the country round about, and took to him all ho ere ill,
With the request that they might only put their hands on the edge of his robe: and all those ho did so ere made ell.
Then there came to Jesus from Jerusalem Pharisees and scribes, saying,
Why do your disciples go against the teaching of the fathers? for they take food ith unashed hands.
And in anser he said to them, Why do you, yourselves, go against the ord of God on account of the teaching hich has been handed don to you?
For God said, Give honour to your father and mother: and, He ho says evil of father or mother ill be put to death.
But you say, If a man says to his father or his mother, That by hich you might have had profit from me is given to God;
There is no need for him to give honour to his father. And you have made the ord of God ithout effect because of your teaching.
You false ones, ell did Isaiah say of you,
These people give me honour ith their lips, but their heart is far from me.
But their orship is to no purpose, hile they give as their teaching the rules of men.
And he got the people together and said to them, Give ear, and let my ords be clear to you:
Not that hich goes into the mouth makes a man unclean, but that hich comes out of the mouth.
Then the disciples came and said to him, Did you see that the Pharisees ere troubled hen these ords came to their ears?
But he said in anser, Every plant hich my Father in heaven has not put in the earth, ill be taken up by the roots.
Let them be: they are blind guides. And if a blind man is guiding a blind man, the to ill go falling into a hole together.
Then Peter said to him, Make the story clear to us.
And he said, Are you, like them, still ithout isdom?
Do you not see that hatever goes into the mouth goes on into the stomach, and is sent out as aste?
But the things hich come out of the mouth come from the heart; and they make a man unclean.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, the taking of life, broken faith beteen the married, unclean desires of the flesh, taking of property, false itness, bitter ords:
These are the things hich make a man unclean; but to take food ith unashed hands does not make a man unclean.
And Jesus ent aay from there into the country of Tyre and Sidon.
And a oman of Canaan came out from those parts, crying and saying, Have pity on me, O Lord, Son of David; my daughter is greatly troubled ith an unclean spirit.
But he gave her no anser. And his disciples came and said to him, Send her aay, for she is crying after us.
But he made anser and said, I as sent only to the andering sheep of the house of Israel.
But she came and gave him orship, saying, Help, Lord.
And he made anser and said, It is not right to take the children’s bread and give it to the dogs.
But she said, Yes, Lord: but even the dogs take the bits from under their masters’ table.
Then Jesus, ansering, said to her, O oman, great is your faith: let your desire be done. And her daughter as made ell from that hour.
And Jesus ent from there and came to the sea of Galilee; and he ent up into the mountain, and took his seat there.

And there came to him great numbers of people having ith them those ho ere broken in body, or blind, or ithout voice, or ounded, or ill in any ay, and a number of others; they put them don at his feet and he made them ell:

So that the people ere full of onder hen they sa that those ho had no voice ere talking, the feeble ere made strong, those hose bodies ere broken had the poer of alking, and the blind ere able to see: and they gave glory to the God of Israel.

And Jesus got his disciples together and said, I have pity for the people, because they have no been ith me three days and have no food: and I ill not send them aay ithout food, or they ill have no strength for the journey.
And the disciples say to him, Ho may e get enough bread in a aste place, to give food to such a number of people?
And Jesus says to them, Ho much bread have you? And they said, Seven cakes, and some small fishes.
Then he gave an order to the people to be seated on the earth,
And he took the seven cakes of bread and the fishes; and having given praise, he gave the broken bread to the disciples, and the disciples gave it to the people.
And they all took food, and had enough; and they took up of the broken bits, seven baskets full.
And there ere four thousand men ho took food, together ith omen and children.
And hen he had sent the people aay, he got into the boat, and came into the country of Magadan.
And the Pharisees and Sadducees came and, testing him, made a request to him to give them a sign from heaven.
But in anser he said to them, At nightfall you say, The eather ill be good, for the sky is red.
And in the morning, The eather ill be bad today, for the sky is red and angry. You are able to see the face of heaven, but not the signs of the times.
An evil and false generation is searching after a sign; and no sign ill be given to it but the sign of Jonah. And he ent aay from them.
And hen the disciples came to the other side they had not taken thought to get bread.
And Jesus said to them, Take care to have nothing to do ith the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
And they ere reasoning among themselves, saying, We took no bread.
And Jesus, seeing it, said, O you of little faith, hy are you reasoning among yourselves, because you have no bread?
Do you still not see, or keep in mind the five cakes of bread of the five thousand, and the number of baskets you took up?
Or the seven cakes of bread of the four thousand, and the number of baskets you took up?
Ho is it that you do not see that I as not talking to you about bread, but about keeping aay from the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees?
Then they sa that it as not the leaven of bread hich he had in mind, but the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
No hen Jesus had come into the parts of Caesarea Philippi, he said, questioning his disciples, Who do men say that the Son of man is?
And they said, Some say, John the Baptist; some, Elijah; and others, Jeremiah, or one of the prophets.
He says to them, But ho do you say that I am?
And Simon Peter made anser and said, You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
And Jesus made anser and said to him, A blessing on you, Simon Bar-jonah: because this knoledge has not come to you from flesh and blood, but from my Father in heaven.
And I say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock ill my church be based, and the doors of hell ill not overcome it.
I ill give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and hatever is fixed by you on earth ill be fixed in heaven: and hatever you make free on earth ill be made free in heaven.
Then he gave orders to the disciples to give no man ord that he as the Christ.

From that time Jesus ent on to make clear to his disciples ho he ould have to go up to Jerusalem, and undergo much at the hands of those in authority and the chief priests and scribes, and be put to death, and the third day come again from the dead.
And Peter, protesting, said to him, Be it far from you, Lord; it is impossible that this ill come about.
But he, turning to Peter, said, Get out of my ay, Satan: you are a danger to me because your mind is not on the things of God, but on the things of men.
Then Jesus said to his disciples, If any man ould come after me, let him give up all, and take up his cross, and come after me.
Because hoever has a desire to keep his life safe ill have it taken from him; but hoever gives up his life because of me, ill have it given back to him.
For hat profit has a man, if he gets all the orld ith the loss of his life? or hat ill a man give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of man ill come in the glory of his Father ith his angels; and then he ill give to every man the reard of his orks.
Truly I say to you, There are some of those here ho ill not have a taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
And after six days Jesus takes ith him Peter, and James, and John, his brother, and makes them go up ith him into a high mountain by themselves.
And he as changed in form before them; and his face as shining like the sun, and his clothing became hite as light.
And Moses and Elijah came before their eyes, talking ith him.
And Peter made anser and said to Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if you ill let me, I ill make here three tents, one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
While he as still talking, a bright cloud came over them: and a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my dearly loved Son, ith hom I am ell pleased; give ear to him.
And at these ords the disciples ent don on their faces in great fear.
And Jesus came and put his hand on them and said, Get up and have no fear.
And lifting up their eyes, they sa no one, but Jesus only.
And hen they ere coming don from the mountain, Jesus gave them orders, saying, Let no man have ord of hat you have seen, till the Son of man has come again from the dead.
And his disciples, questioning him, said, Why then do the scribes say that Elijah has to come first?
And in anser he said, Elijah truly has to come and put all things right:
But I say to you that Elijah has come, and they had no knoledge of him, but did to him hatever they ere pleased to do; the same ill the Son of man undergo at their hands.
Then the disciples sa that he as talking to them of John the Baptist.
And hen they came to the people, a man ent don on his knees to him, saying,
Lord have mercy on my son: for he is off his head, and is in great pain; and frequently he goes falling into the fire, and frequently into the ater.
And I took him to your disciples, and they ere not able to make him ell.
And Jesus, ansering, said, O false and foolish generation, ho long ill I be ith you? ho long ill I put up ith you? let him come here to me.
And Jesus gave orders to the unclean spirit, and it ent out of him: and the boy as made ell from that hour.
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately, and said, Why ere e not able to send it out?

And he says to them, Because of your little faith: for truly I say to you, If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you ill say to this mountain, Be moved from this place to that; and it ill be moved; and nothing ill be impossible to you.
And hile they ere going about in Galilee, Jesus said to them, The Son of man ill be given up into the hands of men;
And they ill put him to death, and the third day he ill come again from the dead. And they ere very sad.
And hen they had come to Capernaum, those ho took the Temple tax came to Peter and said, Does not your master make payment of the Temple tax?
He says, Yes. And hen he came into the house, Jesus said to him, What is your opinion, Simon? from hom do the kings of the earth get payment or tax? from their sons or from other people?
And hen he said, From other people, Jesus said to him, Then are the sons free.

But, so that e may not be a cause of trouble to them, go to the sea, and let don a hook, and take the first fish hich comes up; and in his mouth you ill see a bit of money: take that, and give it to them for me and you.
In that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, Who is greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
And he took a little child, and put him in the middle of them,
And said, Truly, I say to you, If you do not have a change of heart and become like little children, you ill not go into the kingdom of heaven.
Whoever, then, ill make himself as lo as this little child, the same is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And hoever gives honour to one such little child in my name, gives honour to me:
But hoever is a cause of trouble to one of these little ones ho have faith in me, it ould be better for him to have a great stone fixed to his neck, and to come to his end in the deep sea.
A curse is on the earth because of trouble! for it is necessary for trouble to come; but unhappy is that man through hom the trouble comes.

And if your hand or your foot is a cause of trouble, let it be cut off and put it aay from you: it is better for you to go into life ith the loss of a hand or a foot than, having to hands or to feet, to go into the eternal fire.
And if your eye is a cause of trouble to you, take it out, and put it aay from you: it is better for you to go into life ith one eye than, having to eyes, to go into the hell of fire.
Let it not seem to you that one of these little ones is of no value; for I say to you that in heaven their angels see at all times the face of my Father in heaven.
What ould you say no? if a man has a hundred sheep, and one of them has gone andering aay, ill he not let the ninety-nine be, and go to the mountains in search of the andering one?
And if he comes across it, truly I say to you, he has more joy over it than over the ninety-nine hich have not gone out of the ay.
Even so it is not the pleasure of your Father in heaven for one of these little ones to come to destruction.
And if your brother does rong to you, go, make clear to him his error beteen you and him in private: if he gives ear to you, you have got your brother back again.
But if he ill not give ear to you, take ith you one or to more, that by the lips of to or three itnesses every ord may be made certain.
And if he ill not give ear to them, let it come to the hearing of the church: and if he ill not give ear to the church, let him be to you as a Gentile and a tax-farmer.
Truly I say to you, Whatever things are fixed by you on earth ill be fixed in heaven: and hatever you make free on earth ill be made free in heaven.
Again, I say to you, that if to of you are in agreement on earth about anything for hich they ill make a request, it ill be done for them by my Father in heaven.
For here to or three are come together in my name, there am I among them.
Then Peter came and said to him, Lord, hat number of times may my brother do rong against me, and I give him forgiveness? till seven times?
Jesus says to him, I say not to you, Till seven times; but, Till seventy times seven.
For this reason the kingdom of heaven is like a king, ho ent over his accounts ith his servants.
And at the start, one came to him ho as in his debt for ten thousand talents.
And because he as not able to make payment, his lord gave orders for him, and his ife, and his sons and daughters, and all he had, to be given for money, and payment to be made.
So the servant ent don on his face and gave him orship, saying, Lord, give me time to make payment and I ill give you all.
And the lord of that servant, being moved ith pity, let him go, and made him free of the debt.
But that servant ent out, and meeting one of the other servants, ho as in debt to him for one hundred pence, he took him by the throat, saying, Make payment of your debt.
So that servant ent don on his face, requesting him and saying, Give me time and I ill make payment to you.
And he ould not: but ent and put him into prison till he had made payment of the debt.
So hen the other servants sa hat as done they ere very sad, and came and gave ord to their lord of hat had been done.
Then his lord sent for him and said, You evil servant; I made you free of all that debt, because of your request to me:
Was it not right for you to have mercy on the other servant, even as I had mercy on you?
And his lord as very angry, and put him in the hands of those ho ould give him punishment till he made payment of all the debt.
So ill my Father in heaven do to you, if you do not everyone, from your hearts, give forgiveness to his brother.
And it came about that after saying these ords, Jesus ent aay from Galilee, and came into the parts of Judaea on the other side of Jordan.
And a great number ent after him; and he made them ell there.
And certain Pharisees came to him, testing him, and saying, Is it right for a man to put aay his ife for every cause?
And he said in anser, Have you not seen in the Writings, that he ho made them at the first made them male and female, and said,
For this cause ill a man go aay from his father and mother, and be joined to his ife; and the to ill become one flesh?
So that they are no longer to, but one flesh. Then let not that hich has been joined by God be parted by man.
They say to him, Why then did Moses give orders that a husband might give her a statement in riting and be free from her?
He says to them, Moses, because of your hard hearts, let you put aay your ives: but it has not been so from the first.

And I say to you, Whoever puts aay his ife for any other cause than the loss of her virtue, and takes another, is a false husband: and he ho takes her as his ife hen she is put aay, is no true husband to her.
The disciples say to him, If this is the position of a man in relation to his ife, it is better not to be married.
But he said to them, Not all men are able to take in this saying, but only those to hom it is given.

For there are men ho, from birth, ere ithout sex: and there are some ho ere made so by men: and there are others ho have made themselves so for the kingdom of heaven. He ho is able to take it, let him take it.
Then some people took little children to him, so that he might put his hands on them in blessing: and the disciples said sharp ords to them.
But Jesus said, Let the little ones come to me, and do not keep them aay: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
And he put his hands on them, and ent aay.
And one came to him and said, Master, hat good thing have I to do, so that I may have eternal life?
And he said to him, Why are you questioning me about hat is good? One there is ho is good: but if you have a desire to go into life, keep the rules of the la.
He says to him, Which? And Jesus said, Do not put anyone to death, Do not be untrue in married life, Do not take hat is not yours, Do not give false itness,
Give honour to your father and your mother: and, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself.
The young man says to him, All these things have I done: hat more is there?
Jesus said to him, If you have a desire to be complete, go, get money for your property, and give it to the poor, and you ill have ealth in heaven: and come after me.
But hearing these ords the young man ent aay sorroing: for he had much property.
And Jesus said to his disciples, Truly I say to you, It is hard for a man ith much money to go into the kingdom of heaven.
And again I say to you, It is simpler for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a man ith much money to go into the kingdom of God.
And the disciples, hearing this, ere greatly surprised, saying, Who then may have salvation?
And Jesus, looking at them, said, With men this is not possible; but ith God all things are possible.
Then Peter said to him, See, e have given up everything and have come after you; hat then ill e have?

And Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you that in the time hen all things are made ne, and the Son of man is seated in his glory, you ho have come after me ill be seated on telve seats, judging the telve tribes of Israel.
And everyone ho has given up houses, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or child, or land, for my name, ill be given a hundred times as much, and have eternal life.
But a great number ho are first ill be last, and some ho are last ill be first.
For the kingdom of heaven is like the master of a house, ho ent out early in the morning to get orkers into his vine-garden.
And hen he had made an agreement ith the orkmen for a penny a day, he sent them into his vine-garden.
And he ent out about the third hour, and sa others in the market-place doing nothing;
And he said to them, Go into the vine-garden ith the others, and hatever is right I ill give you. And they ent to ork.
Again he ent out about the sixth and the ninth hour, and did the same.
And about the eleventh hour he ent out and sa others doing nothing; and he says to them, Why are you here all the day doing nothing?
They say to him, Because no man has given us ork. He says to them, Go in ith the rest, into the vine-garden.
And hen evening came, the lord of the vine-garden said to his manager, Let the orkers come, and give them their payment, from the last to the first.
And hen those men came ho had gone to ork at the eleventh hour, they ere given every man a penny.
Then those ho came first had the idea that they ould get more; and they, like the rest, ere given a penny.
And hen they got it, they made a protest against the master of the house,
Saying, These last have done only one hour’s ork, and you have made them equal to us, ho have undergone the hard ork of the day and the burning heat.
But he in anser said to one of them, Friend, I do you no rong: did you not make an agreement ith me for a penny?
Take hat is yours, and go aay; it is my pleasure to give to this last, even as to you.
Have I not the right to do as seems good to me in my house? or is your eye evil, because I am good?
So the last ill be first, and the first last.
And hen Jesus as going up to Jerusalem, he took the telve disciples on one side, and said to them,
See, e go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man ill be given into the hands of the chief priests and scribes; and they ill give orders for him to be put to death,
And ill give him up to the Gentiles to be made sport of and to be hipped and to be put to death on the cross: and the third day he ill come back again from the dead.
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him ith her sons, giving him orship and making a request of him.
And he said to her, What is your desire? She says to him, Let my to sons be seated, the one at your right hand, and the other at your left, in your kingdom.
But Jesus made anser and said, You have no idea hat you are requesting. Are you able to take of the cup hich I am about to take?

They say to him, We are able. He says to them, Truly, you ill take of my cup: but to be seated at my right hand and at my left is not for me to give, but it is for those for hom my Father has made it ready.
And hen it came to the ears of the ten, they ere angry ith the to brothers.
But Jesus said to them, You see that the rulers of the Gentiles are lords over them, and their great ones have authority over them.
Let it not be so among you: but if anyone has a desire to become great among you, let him be your servant;
And hoever has a desire to be first among you, let him take the loest place:
Even as the Son of man did not come to have servants, but to be a servant, and to give his life for the salvation of men.
And hen they ere going out from Jericho, a great number ent after him.
And to blind men seated by the ayside, hen they had the nes that Jesus as going by, gave a loud cry, saying, Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us.
And the people gave them orders to be quiet; but they ent on crying even louder, Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us.
And Jesus, stopping, sent for them, and said, What ould you have me do to you?
They say to him, Lord, that our eyes may be open.
And Jesus, being moved ith pity, put his fingers on their eyes: and straight aay they ere able to see, and ent after him.
And hen they ere near Jerusalem, and had come to Beth-phage, to the Mountain of Olives, Jesus sent to disciples,
Saying to them, Go into the little ton in front of you, and straight aay you ill see an ass ith a cord round her neck, and a young one ith her; let them loose and come ith them to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, you ill say, The Lord has need of them; and straight aay he ill send them.
No this took place so that these ords of the prophet might come true,
Say to the daughter of Zion, See, your King comes to you, gentle and seated on an ass, and on a young ass.
And the disciples ent and did as Jesus had given them orders,
And got the ass and the young one, and put their clothing on them, and he took his seat on it.
And all the people put their clothing don in the ay; and others got branches from the trees, and put them don in the ay.
And those ho ent before him, and those ho came after, gave loud cries, saying, Glory to the Son of David: A blessing on him ho comes in the name of the Lord: Glory in the highest.
And hen he came into Jerusalem, all the ton as moved, saying, Who is this?
And the people said, This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.
And Jesus ent into the Temple and sent out all ho ere trading there, overturning the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those trading in doves.
And he said to them, It is in the Writings, My house is to be named a house of prayer, but you are making it a hole of thieves.
And the blind and the broken in body came to him in the Temple, and he made them ell.
But hen the chief priests and the scribes sa the orks of poer hich he did, and the children crying out in the Temple, Glory to the son of David, they ere angry and said to him,
Have you any idea hat these are saying? And Jesus said to them, Yes: have you not seen in the Writings, From the lips of children and babies at the breast you have made your praise complete?
And he ent aay from them, and ent out of the ton to Bethany, and as there for the night.
No in the morning hen he as coming back to the ton, he had a desire for food.

And seeing a fig-tree by the ayside, he came to it, and sa nothing on it but leaves only; and he said to it, Let there be no fruit from you from this time forard for ever. And straight aay the fig-tree became dry and dead.
And hen the disciples sa it they ere surprised, saying, Ho did the fig-tree become dry in so short a time?

And Jesus in anser said to them, Truly I say to you, If you have faith, ithout doubting, not only may you do hat has been done to the fig-tree, but even if you say to this mountain, Be taken up and put into the sea, it ill be done.
And all things, hatever you make request for in prayer, having faith, you ill get.

And hen he had come into the Temple, the chief priests and those in authority over the people came to him hile he as teaching, and said, By hat authority do you do these things? and ho gave you this authority?
And Jesus said to them in anser, I ill put one question to you, and if you give me the anser, I ill say by hat authority I do these things.
The baptism of John, here did it come from? from heaven or from men? And they ere reasoning among themselves, saying, If e say, From heaven; he ill say to us, Why then did you not have faith in him?
But if e say, From men; e are in fear of the people, because all take John to be a prophet.
And they made anser and said, We have no idea. Then he said to them, And I ill not say to you by hat authority I do these things.
But ho does it seem to you? A man had to sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go and do ork today in the vine-garden.
And he said in anser, I ill not: but later, changing his decision, he ent.
And he came to the second and said the same. And he made anser and said, I go, sir: and ent not.
Which of the to did his father’s pleasure? They say, The first. Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you, that tax-farmers and loose omen are going into the kingdom of God before you.

For John came to you in the ay of righteousness, and you had no faith in him, but the tax-farmers and the loose omen had faith in him: and you, hen you sa it, did not even have regret for your sins, so as to have faith in him.

Give ear to another story. A master of a house made a vine garden, and put a all round it, and made a place for crushing out the ine, and made a toer, and let it out to field-orkers, and ent into another country.
And hen the time for the fruit came near, he sent his servants to the orkmen, to get the fruit.
And the orkmen made an attack on his servants, giving blos to one, putting another to death, and stoning another.
Again, he sent other servants more in number than the first: and they did the same to them.
But after that he sent his son to them, saying, They ill have respect for my son.
But hen the orkmen sa the son, they said among themselves, This is he ho ill one day be the oner of the property; come, let us put him to death and take his heritage.
And they took him and, driving him out of the vine-garden, put him to death.
When, then, the lord of the vine-garden comes, hat ill he do to those orkmen?
They say to him, He ill put those cruel men to a cruel death, and ill let out the vine-garden to other orkmen, ho ill give him the fruit hen it is ready.

Jesus says to them, Did you never see in the Writings, The stone hich the builders put on one side, the same has been made the chief stone of the building: this as the Lord’s doing, and it is a onder in our eyes?
For this reason I say to you, The kingdom of God ill be taken aay from you, and ill be given to a nation producing the fruits of it.
Any man falling on this stone ill be broken, but he on hom it comes don ill be crushed to dust.
And hen his stories came to the ears of the chief priests and the Pharisees, they sa that he as talking of them.
And though they had a desire to take him, they ere in fear of the people, because in their eyes he as a prophet.
And Jesus, talking to them again in stories, said:
The kingdom of heaven is like a certain king, ho made a feast hen his son as married,
And sent out his servants to get in the guests to the feast: and they ould not come.
Again he sent out other servants, ith orders to say to the guests, See, I have made ready my feast: my oxen and my fat beasts have been put to death, and all things are ready: come to the feast.
But they gave no attention, and ent about their business, one to his farm, another to his trade:
And the rest put violent hands on his servants, and did evil to them, and put them to death.
But the king as angry; and he sent his armies, and those ho had put his servants to death he gave to destruction, burning don their ton ith fire.
Then he said to his servants, The feast is ready but the guests ere not good enough.
Go then to the cross-roads, and get all those hom you see to come to the bride-feast.
And those servants ent out into the streets, and got together all those hom they came across, bad and good: and the feast as full of guests.
But hen the king came in to see the guests, he sa there a man ho had not on a guest’s robe;
And he says to him, Friend, ho came you in here not having a guest’s robe? And he had nothing to say.
Then the king said to the servants, Put cords round his hands and feet and put him out into the dark; there ill be eeping and cries of sorro.
For out of all to hom the good nes has come, only a small number ill get salvation.
Then the Pharisees ent and had a meeting to see ho they might make use of his ords to take him.

And they sent to him their disciples, ith the Herodians, saying, Master, e see that you are true, and that you are teaching the true ay of God, and have no fear of anyone, because you have no respect for a man’s position.
Give us, then, your opinion of this: Is it right to give tax to Caesar, or not?
But Jesus sa their trick and said, Oh false ones, hy are you attempting to put me in the rong?
Let me see the tax money. And they gave him a penny.
And he said to them, Whose is this image and name on it?
They say to him, Caesar’s. Then he said to them, Give to Caesar the things hich are Caesar’s, and to God the things hich are God’s.
And hearing it, they ere full of onder, and ent aay from him.
On the same day there came to him the Sadducees, ho say that there is no coming back from the dead: and they put a question to him, saying,
Master, Moses said, If a man, at the time of his death, has no children, let his brother take his ife, and get a family for his brother;
No there ere among us seven brothers; and the first as married and at his death, having no seed, gave his ife to his brother;
In the same ay the second and the third, up to the seventh.
And last of all the oman came to her end.
When they come back from the dead, then, hose ife ill she be of the seven? because they all had her.
But Jesus said to them in anser, You are in error, not having knoledge of the Writings, or of the poer of God.
For hen they come back from the dead there are no husbands and ives, but they are as the angels in heaven.
But about the dead coming back to life, have you no knoledge of hat as said to you by God in the Writings:
I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead but of the living.
And the people hearing it ere surprised at his teaching.
But the Pharisees, hearing ho the mouths of the Sadducees had been stopped, came together;
And one of them, a teacher of the la, put a question to him, testing him, and saying,
Master, hich is the chief rule in the la?
And he said to him, Have love for the Lord your God ith all your heart, and ith all your soul, and ith all your mind.
This is the first and greatest rule.
And a second like it is this, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself.
On these to rules all the la and the prophets are based.
No hile the Pharisees ere together, Jesus put a question to them, saying,
What is your opinion of the Christ? hose son is he? They say to him, The Son of David.
He says to them, Ho then does David in the Spirit give him the name of Lord, saying,
The Lord said to my Lord, Be seated at my right hand, till I put under your feet all those ho are against you?
If David then gives him the name of Lord, ho is he his son?
And no one as able to give him an anser, and so great as their fear of him, that from that day no one put any more questions to him.
Then Jesus said to the people and to his disciples:
The scribes and the Pharisees have the authority of Moses;
All things, then, hich they give you orders to do, these do and keep: but do not take their orks as your example, for they say and do not.
They make hard las and put great eights on men’s backs; but they themselves ill not put a finger to them.
But all their orks they do so as to be seen by men: for they make ide their phylacteries, and the edges of their robes,
And the things desired by them are the first places at feasts, and the chief seats in the Synagogues,
And ords of respect in the market-places, and to be named by men, Teacher.
But you may not be named Teacher: for one is your teacher, and you are all brothers.
And give no man the name of father on earth: because one is your Father, ho is in heaven.
And you may not be named guides: because one is your Guide, even Christ.
But let the greatest among you be your servant.
And hoever makes himself high ill be made lo, and hoever makes himself lo ill be made high.
But a curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! because you are shutting the kingdom of heaven against men: for you do not go in yourselves, and those ho are going in, you keep back.
A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! for you go about land and sea to get one disciple and, having him, you make him tice as much a son of hell as yourselves.
A curse is on you, blind guides, ho say, Whoever takes an oath by the Temple, it is nothing; but hoever takes an oath by the gold of the Temple, he is responsible.
You foolish ones and blind: hich is greater, the gold, or the Temple hich makes the gold holy?
And, Whoever takes an oath by the altar, it is nothing; but hoever takes an oath by the offering hich is on it, he is responsible.
You blind ones: hich is greater, the offering, or the altar hich makes the offering holy?
He, then, ho takes an oath by the altar, takes it by the altar and by all things on it.
And he ho takes an oath by the Temple, takes it by the Temple and by him hose house it is.
And he ho takes an oath by heaven, takes it by the seat of God, and by him ho is seated on it.

A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! for you make men give a tenth of all sorts of seet-smelling plants, but you give no thought to the more important things of the la, righteousness, and mercy, and faith; but it is right for you to do these, and not to let the others be undone.
You blind guides, ho take out a fly from your drink, but make no trouble over a camel.
A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! for you make clean the outside of the cup and of the plate, but inside they are full of violent behaviour and uncontrolled desire.
You blind Pharisee, first make clean the inside of the cup and of the plate, so that the outside may become equally clean.

A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! for you are like the resting-places of the dead, hich are made hite, and seem beautiful on the outside, but inside are full of dead men’s bones and of all unclean things.
Even so you seem to men to be full of righteousness, but inside you are all false and full of rongdoing.
A curse is on you, scribes and Pharisees, false ones! because you put up buildings for housing the dead bodies of the prophets, and make fair the last resting-places of good men, and say,
If e had been living in the days of our fathers, e ould not have taken part ith them in the blood of the prophets.
So that you are itnesses against yourselves that you are the sons of those ho put the prophets to death.
Make full, then, the measure of your fathers.
You snakes, offspring of snakes, ho ill you be kept from the punishment of hell?

For this reason, I send you prophets, and ise men, and scribes: some of them you ill put to death and put on the cross, and to some of them you ill give blos in your Synagogues, driving them from ton to ton;
So that on you may come all the blood of the upright on the earth, from the blood of upright Abel to the blood of Zachariah, son of Barachiah, hom you put to death beteen the Temple and the altar.
Truly I say to you, All these things ill come on this generation.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, putting to death the prophets, and stoning those ho are sent to her! Again and again ould I have taken your children to myself as a bird takes her young ones under her ings, and you ould not!
See, your house is made aste.
For I say to you, You ill not see me from this time till you say, A blessing on him ho comes in the name of the Lord.
And Jesus ent out of the Temple, and on the ay his disciples came to him, pointing out the buildings of the Temple.
But he, ansering, said to them, See you not all these things? truly I say to you that here there ill not be one stone resting on another, hich ill not be pulled don.

And hile he as seated on the Mountain of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, Make clear to us, hen ill these things be? and hat ill be the sign of your coming and of the end of the orld?
And Jesus said to them in anser, Take care that you are not tricked.
For people ill come in my name, saying, I am the Christ; and a number ill be turned from the true ay through them.
And nes ill come to you of ars and talk of ars: do not be troubled, for these things have to be; but it is still not the end.
For nation ill be moved against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and men ill be ithout food, and the earth ill be shaking in different places;
But all these things are the first of the troubles.
Then they ill be cruel to you, and ill put you to death: and you ill be hated by all nations because of my name.
And numbers of people ill be turned from the right ay, and ill give one another up and have hate for one another.
And a number of false prophets ill come, causing error.
And because rongdoing ill be increased, the love of most people ill become cold.
But he ho goes through to the end ill get salvation.
And this good nes of the kingdom ill be given through all the orld for a itness to all nations; and then the end ill come.
When, then, you see in the holy place the unclean thing hich makes destruction, of hich ord as given by Daniel the prophet ( let this be clear to the reader),
Then let those ho are in Judaea go in flight to the mountains:
Let not him ho is on the house-top go don to take anything out of his house:
And let not him ho is in the field go back to get his coat.
But it ill be hard for omen ho are ith child and for those ith babies at the breast in those days.
And say a prayer that your flight may not be in the inter, or on a Sabbath.
Because in those days there ill be great sorro, such as there has not been from the start of the orld till no, or ever ill be.
And if those days had not been made short there ould have been no salvation for any, but because of the saints those days ill be made short.
Then if any man says to you, See, here is the Christ, or, Here; do not put faith in him;
For there ill come up false Christs, and false prophets, ho ill do great signs and onders; so that if possible even the saints might be tricked.
See, I have made it clear to you before it comes about.
If, then, they say to you, See, he is in the aste land; go not out: See, he is in the inner rooms; put no faith in it.
Because as in a thunderstorm the bright light coming from the east is seen even in the est; so ill be the coming of the Son of man.
Wherever the dead body is, there ill the eagles come together.
But straight aay, after the trouble of those days, the sun ill be made dark and the moon ill not give her light and the stars ill come don from heaven and the poers of heaven ill be moved:

And then the sign of the Son of man ill be seen in heaven: and then all the nations of the earth ill have sorro, and they ill see the Son of man coming on the clouds of heaven ith poer and great glory.
And he ill send out his angels ith a great sound of a horn, and they ill get his saints together from the four inds, from one end of heaven to the other.
No take an example from the fig-tree: hen her branch has become soft and puts out its leaves, you are certain that the summer is near;
Even so, hen you see all these things, you may be certain that he is near, even at the doors.
Truly I say to you, This generation ill not come to an end till all these things are complete.
Heaven and earth ill come to an end, but my ords ill not come to an end.
But of that day and hour no one has knoledge, not even the angels in heaven, or the Son, but the Father only.
And as ere the days of Noah, so ill be the coming of the Son of man.
Because as in those days before the overfloing of the aters, they ere feasting and taking ives and getting married, till the day hen Noah ent into the ark,
And they had no care till the aters came and took them all aay; so ill be the coming of the Son of man.
Then to men ill be in the field; one is taken, and one let go;
To omen ill be crushing grain; one is taken, and one let go.
Be atching, then! for you have no knoledge on hat day your Lord ill come.
But be certain of this, that if the master of the house had had knoledge of the time hen the thief as coming, he ould have been atching, and ould not have let his house be broken into.
Be ready then; for at a time hich you have no thought of the Son of man ill come.
Who is the true and ise servant, hom his lord has put over those in his house, to give them their food at the right time?
A blessing on that servant, ho ill be doing so hen his lord comes.
Truly, I say to you, he ill put him over all he has.
But if that evil servant says in his heart, My lord is a long time in coming;
And is cruel to the other servants, taking his pleasure ith those ho are overcome ith ine;
The lord of that servant ill come in a day hen he is not looking for him, and in an hour of hich he has no knoledge,
And ill have him cut in to, and ill give him a part in the fate of the false ones: there ill be eeping and cries of sorro.
Then the kingdom of heaven ill be like ten virgins, the friends of the bride, ho took their lights, and ent out ith the purpose of meeting the husband.
And five of them ere foolish, and five ere ise.
For the foolish, hen they took their lights, took no oil ith them.
But the ise took oil in their vessels ith their lights.
No the husband as a long time in coming, and they all ent to sleep.
But in the middle of the night there is a cry, The husband comes! Go out to him.
Then all those virgins got up, and made ready their lights.
And the foolish said to the ise, Give us of your oil; for our lights are going out.
But the ise made anser, saying, There may not be enough for us and you; it ould be better for you to go to the traders and get oil for yourselves.
And hile they ent to get oil, the master came; and those ho ere ready ent in ith him to the feast: and the door as shut.
After that the other virgins came, saying, Lord, Lord, let us in.

But the days ill come hen the husband ill be taken aay from them, and then they ill go ithout food.
No man puts a bit of ne cloth on an old coat: or the ne, by pulling aay from the old, makes a orse hole.
And no man puts ne ine into old ine-skins: or the skins ill be burst by the ine, and the ine and the skins ill be asted: but ne ine has to be put into ne ine-skins.
And it came about that on the Sabbath day he as going through the grain-fields; and hile they ere alking, his disciples took the heads of grain.
And the Pharisees said to him, Why are they doing hat it is not right to do on the Sabbath?
And he said to them, Have you no knoledge of hat David did, hen he had need and as ithout food, he, and those ho ere ith him?
Ho he ent into the house of God hen Abiathar as high priest, and took for food the holy bread, hich only the priests may take, and gave it to those ho ere ith him?
And he said to them, The Sabbath as made for man, and not man for the Sabbath;
So that the Son of man is lord even of the Sabbath.
And he ent again into the Synagogue; and there as a man there hose hand as dead.
And they ere atching him to see if he ould make him ell on the Sabbath day, so that they might have something against him.
And he said to the man, Get up and come forard.
And he said to them, Is it right to do good on the Sabbath or to do evil? to give life or to put to death? But they said nothing.
And looking round on them he as angry, being sad because of their hard hearts; and he said to the man, Put out your hand. And he put it out, and his hand as made ell.
And the Pharisees ent out, and straight aay made designs ith the Herodians about ho they might put him to death.
And Jesus ent aay ith his disciples to the sea, and a great number from Galilee came after him: and from Judaea,
And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and the other side of Jordan, and the country about Tyre and Sidon, a great number, hearing hat great things he did, came to him.
And he made a request to his disciples to have a little boat ready for him, so that he might not be crushed by the people;
For he had made such a great number ell that all those ho ere diseased ere falling don before him for the purpose of touching him.
And the unclean spirits, henever they sa him, ent don before him, crying out, and saying, You are the Son of God.
And he gave them special orders not to say ho he as.
And he ent up into the mountain, and sent for those hom it as his pleasure to have ith him: and they ent to him.
And he took telve to be ith him, so that he might send them out as preachers,
And give them the poer of driving out evil spirits:
To Simon he gave the second name of Peter;
And to James, the son of Zebedee, and John, the brother of James, he gave the second name of Boanerges, hich is, Sons of thunder:
And Andre, and Philip, and Bartholome, and Matthe, and Thomas, and James, the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Zealot;
And Judas Iscariot, ho as false to him.
And he ent into a house. And the people came together again, so that they ere not even able to take bread.
And hen his friends had nes of it, they ent out to get him, saying, He is off his head.
And the scribes ho came don from Jerusalem, said, He has Beelzebub, and, By the ruler of evil spirits he sends evil spirits out of men.
And turning to them, he said to them in the form of a story, Ho is it possible for Satan to put out Satan?
If there is division in a kingdom, that kingdom ill come to destruction;
And if there is division in a house, that house ill come to destruction;
And if Satan is at ar ith himself, and there is division in him, he ill not keep his place but ill come to an end.
But no one is able to go into the house of the strong man and take his goods, ithout first putting cords round the strong man, and then he ill take his goods.
Truly, I say to you, The sons of men ill have forgiveness for all their sins and for all the evil ords they say:
But hoever says evil things against the Holy Spirit ill never have forgiveness, but the evil he has done ill be ith him for ever:
Because they said, He has an unclean spirit.
And his mother and brothers came and ere outside, and sent for him, requesting to see him.
And a great number ere seated round him; and they said to him, See, your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you.
And he said in anser, Who are my mother and my brothers?
And looking round at those ho ere seated about him, he said, See, my mother and my brothers!
Whoever does God’s pleasure, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.
And again he as teaching by the seaside. And a very great number of people had come to him, so that he got into a boat on the sea and took his seat; and all the people ere on the land by the seaside.
And he gave them teaching about a number of things in the form of stories, and said to them in his teaching, Give ear:
A man ent out to put seed in the earth:
And hile he as doing it, some as dropped by the ayside, and the birds came and took it for food.
And some ent on the stones, here it had not much earth; and it came up straight aay, because the earth as not deep:
And hen the sun as high, it as burned; and because it had no root, it became dry and dead.
And some ent among the thorns, and the thorns came up, and it had no room for groth and gave no fruit.
And some, falling on good earth, gave fruit, coming up and increasing, and giving thirty, sixty, and a hundred times as much.
And he said to them, Whoever has ears, let him give ear.
And hen he as by himself, those ho ere round him ith the telve put questions to him about the purpose of the stories.
And he said to them, To you is given the secret of the kingdom of God, but to those ho are outside, all things are given in the form of stories;
So that seeing they may see, and it ill not be clear to them; and hearing it, they ill not get the sense; for fear that they may be turned again to me and have forgiveness.
And he said to them, If you are not clear about this story, ho ill you be clear about the others?
The seed is the ord.
And these are they by the ayside, here the ord is planted; and hen they have given ear, the Evil One comes straight aay and takes aay the ord hich has been planted in them.
And in the same ay, these are they ho are planted on the stones, ho, hen the ord has come to their ears, straight aay take it ith joy;
And they have no root in themselves, but go on for a time; then, hen trouble comes or pain, because of the ord, they quickly become full of doubts.
And others are those planted among the thorns; these are they ho have given ear to the ord,
And the cares of this life, and the deceits of ealth, and the desire for other things coming in, put a stop to the groth of the ord, and it gives no fruit.
And these are they ho ere planted on the good earth; such as give ear to the ord, and take it into their hearts, and give fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundred times as much.
And he said to them, When the light comes in, do people put it under a vessel, or under the bed, and not on its table?
There is nothing covered hich ill not be seen openly, and nothing has been made secret hich ill not come to light.
If any man has ears, let him give ear.
And he said to them, Take care hat you give ear to: in the same measure as you give you ill get, and more ill be given to you.
He ho has, to him ill be given: and he ho has not, from him ill be taken even that hich he has.
And he said, Such is the kingdom of God, as if a man put seed in the earth,
And ent to sleep and got up, night and day, and the seed came to groth, though he had no idea ho.
The earth gives fruit by herself; first the leaf, then the head, then the full grain.
But hen the grain is ready, he quickly sends men to get it cut, because the time for cutting has come.
And he said, What picture may e give of the kingdom of God, or ith hat story may e make it clear?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, hich, hen it is put in the earth, is smaller than all the seeds on the earth,
But hen it is planted, it comes up, and becomes taller than all the plants, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of heaven are able to take rest in its shade.
And ith a number of such stories he gave them his teaching, as they ere able to take it:
And ithout a story he said nothing to them: but privately to his disciples he made all things clear.
And on that day, hen the evening had come, he said to them, Let us go over to the other side.
And going aay from the people, they took him ith them, as he as, in the boat. And other boats ere ith him.
And a great storm of ind came up, and the aves came into the boat, so that the boat as no becoming full.
And he himself as in the back of the boat, sleeping on the cushion: and they, aaking him, said, Master, is it nothing to you that e are in danger of destruction?
And he came out of his sleep, and gave strong orders to the ind, and said to the sea, Peace, be at rest. And the ind ent don, and there as a great calm.
And he said to them, Why are you full of fear? have you still no faith?
And their fear as great, and they said one to another, Who then is this, that even the ind and the sea do his orders?
And they came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gerasenes.
And hen he had got out of the boat, straight aay there came to him from the place of the dead a man ith an unclean spirit.
He as living in the place of the dead: and no man as able to keep him don, no, not ith a chain;
Because he had frequently been prisoned in chains and iron bands, and the chains had been parted and the bands broken by him: and no man as strong enough to make him quiet.
And all the time, by day and by night, in the place of the dead, and in the mountains, he as crying out and cutting himself ith stones.
And hen he sa Jesus from far off, he ent quickly to him and gave him orship;
And crying out ith a loud voice he said, What have I to do ith you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? In God’s name, do not be cruel to me.
For Jesus had said to him, Come out of the man, you unclean spirit.
And Jesus said, What is your name? And he made anser, My name is Legion, because there are a great number of us.
And he made strong prayers to him not to send them aay out of the country.
No on the mountain side there as a great herd of pigs getting their food.
And they said to him, Send us into the pigs, so that e may go into them.

And he let them do it. And the unclean spirits came out and ent into the pigs; and the herd ent rushing don a sharp slope into the sea, about to thousand of them; and they came to their death in the sea.
And their keepers ent running and gave an account of it in the ton and in the country. And people came to see hat had taken place.
And they came to Jesus, and sa the man in hom had been the evil spirits seated, clothed and ith full use of his senses, and they ere full of fear.
And those ho had seen it gave them an account of hat had been done to him ho had the evil spirits, and of the fate of the pigs.
And they made a request to him to go out of their country.
And hen he as getting into the boat, the man in hom had been the evil spirits had a great desire to come ith him.
And he ould not let him, but said to him, Go to your house, to your friends, and give them nes of the great things the Lord has done for you, and ho he had mercy on you.
And he ent on his ay, and made public in the country of Decapolis hat great things Jesus had done for him: and all men ere full of onder.
And hen Jesus had gone over again in the boat to the other side, a great number of people came to him: and he as by the sea.
And one of the rulers of the Synagogue, Jairus by name, came, and seeing him, ent don at his feet,
And made strong prayers to him, saying, My little daughter is near to death: it is my prayer that you ill come and put your hands on her, so that she may be made ell, and have life.
And he ent ith him; and a great number of people ent after him, and came round him.
And a oman, ho had had a flo of blood for telve years,
And had undergone much at the hands of a number of medical men, and had given all she had, and as no better, but even orse,
When she had nes of the things hich Jesus did, ent among the people coming after him, and put her hand on his robe.
For she said, If I may only put my hand on his robe, I ill be made ell.
And straight aay the fountain of her blood as stopped, and she had a feeling in her body that her disease had gone and she as ell.
And straight aay Jesus as conscious that poer had gone out of him; and, turning to the people, he said, Who as touching my robe?
And his disciples said to him, You see the people round you on every side, and you say, Who as touching me?
