And on his looking round to see her ho had done this thing,
The oman, shaking ith fear, conscious of hat had been done to her, came and, falling on her face before him, gave him a true account of everything.
And he said to her, Daughter, your faith has made you ell; go in peace, and be free from your disease.
And hile he as still talking, they came from the ruler of the Synagogue’s house, saying, Your daughter is dead: hy are you still troubling the Master?
But Jesus, giving no attention to their ords, said to the ruler of the Synagogue, Have no fear, only have faith.
And he did not let anyone come ith him, but Peter and James and John, the brother of James.
And they came to the house of the ruler of the Synagogue; and he sa people running this ay and that, and eeping and crying loudly.
And hen he had gone in, he said to them, Why are you making such a noise and eeping? The child is not dead, but sleeping.
And they ere laughing at him. But he, having sent them all out, took the father of the child and her mother and those ho ere ith him, and ent in here the child as.
And taking her by the hand, he said to her, Talitha cumi, hich is, My child, I say to you, Get up.
And the young girl got up straight aay, and as alking about; she being telve years old. And they ere overcome ith onder.
And he gave them special orders that they ere not to say anything of this; and he said that some food as to be given to her.
And he ent aay from there, and came into his country; and his disciples ent ith him.

And hen the Sabbath day had come, he as teaching in the Synagogue; and a number of people hearing him ere surprised, saying, From here did this man get these things? and, What is the isdom given to this man, and hat are these orks of poer done by his hands?
Is not this the oodorker, the son of Mary, and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? and are not his sisters here ith us? And they ere bitter against him.
And Jesus said to them, A prophet is nohere ithout honour, but in his country, and among his relations, and in his family.
And he as unable to do any ork of poer there, but only to put his hands on one or to persons ho ere ill, and make them ell.
And he as greatly surprised because they had no faith. And he ent about the country places teaching.
And he gave orders to the telve, and sent them out to by to; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits;
And he said that they ere to take nothing for their journey, but a stick only; no bread, no bag, no money in their pockets;
They ere to go ith common shoes on their feet, and not to take to coats.
And he said to them, Wherever you go into a house, make that your resting-place till you go aay.
And hatever place ill not take you in and ill not give ear to you, hen you go aay, put off the dust from your feet as a itness against them.
And they ent out, preaching the need for a change of heart in men.
And they sent out a number of evil spirits, and put oil on a great number ho ere ill, and made them ell.
And king Herod had nes of him, because his name as on the lips of all; and he said, John the Baptist has come back from the dead, and for this reason these poers are orking in him.
But others said, It is Elijah. And others said, It is a prophet, even like one of the prophets.
But Herod, hen he had nes of it, said, John, hom I put to death, has come back from the dead.
For Herod himself had sent men out to take John and put him in prison, because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s ife, hom he had taken for himself.
For John said to Herod, It is rong for you to have your brother’s ife.
And Herodias as bitter against him, desiring to put him to death; but she as not able;
For Herod as in fear of John, being conscious that he as an upright and holy man, and kept him safe. And hearing him, he as much troubled; and he gave ear to him gladly.
And the chance came hen Herod on his birthday gave a feast to his lords, and the high captains, and the chief men of Galilee;

And hen the daughter of Herodias herself came in and did a dance, Herod and those ho ere at table ith him ere pleased ith her; and the king said to the girl, Make a request for anything and I ill give it you.
And he took an oath, saying to her, Whatever is your desire I ill give it to you, even half of my kingdom.
And she ent out and said to her mother, What is my request to be? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
And she came in quickly to the king, and said, My desire is that you give me straight aay on a plate the head of John the Baptist.
And the king as very sad; but because of his oaths, and those ho ere ith him at table, he ould not say ’No’ to her.
And straight aay the king sent out one of his armed men, and gave him an order to come back ith the head: and he ent and took off John’s head in prison,
And came back ith the head on a plate, and gave it to the girl; and the girl gave it to her mother.
And hen his disciples had nes of it, they came and took up his body, and put it in its last resting-place.
And the telve came together to Jesus; and they gave him an account of all the things they had done, and all they had been teaching.
And he said to them, Come aay by yourselves to a quiet place, and take a rest for a time. Because there ere a great number coming and going, and they had no time even for food.
And they ent aay in the boat to a aste place by themselves.
And the people sa them going, and a number of them, having knoledge ho they ere, ent running there together on foot from all the tons, and got there before them.
And he got out, and sa a great mass of people, and he had pity on them, because they ere like sheep ithout a keeper: and he gave them teaching about a number of things.
And at the end of the day, his disciples came to him and said, This place is aste land, and it is late:
Send them aay, so that they may go into the country and small tons round about, and get some food for themselves.
But he said to them in anser, Give them food yourselves. And they said to him, Are e to go and get bread for to hundred pence, and give it to them?
And he said to them, Ho much bread have you? go and see. And hen they had seen, they said, Five cakes of bread and to fishes.
And he made them all be seated in groups on the green grass.
And they ere placed in groups, by hundreds and by fifties.

And he took the five cakes of bread and the to fishes and, looking up to heaven, he said ords of blessing over them; and hen the cakes ere broken, he gave them to the disciples to put before the people; and he made division of the to fishes among them all.
And they all took of the food and had enough.
And they took up telve baskets full of the broken bits and of the fishes.
And those ho took of the bread ere five thousand men.
And straight aay he made his disciples get into the boat, and go before him to the other side to Beth-saida, hile he himself sent the people aay.
And after he had sent them aay, he ent up into a mountain for prayer.
And by evening, the boat as in the middle of the sea, and he by himself on the land.

And seeing that they had trouble in getting their boat through the ater, because the ind as against them, about the fourth atch of the night he came to them, alking on the sea; and he ould have gone past them;
But they, hen they sa him alking on the sea, took him for a spirit, and gave a loud cry:
For they all sa him, and ere troubled. But straight aay he said to them, Take heart, it is I, have no fear.
And he ent to them into the boat, and the ind ent don, and they ere full of onder in themselves;
For it as not clear to them about the bread; but their hearts ere hard.
And hen they had gone across, they came to Gennesaret, and got their boat to land.
And hen they had got out of the boat, the people quickly had nes of him,
And ent running through all the country round about, and took on their beds those ho ere ill, to here it as said that he as.

And herever he ent, into small tons, or great tons, or into the country, they took those ho ere ill into the market-places, requesting him that they might put their hands even on the edge of his robe: and all those ho did so ere made ell.
And there came together to him the Pharisees and certain of the scribes ho had come from Jerusalem,
And had seen that some of his disciples took their bread ith unclean, that is, unashed, hands.
No the Pharisees, and all the Jes, do not take food ithout ashing their hands ith care, keeping the old rule hich has been handed don to them:

And hen they come from the market-place, they take no food till their hands are ashed; and a number of other orders there are, hich have been handed don to them to keep — ashings of cups and pots and brass vessels.
And the Pharisees and the scribes put the question to him, Why do your disciples not keep the rules of the fathers, but take their bread ith unashed hands?
And he said, Well did Isaiah say of you, you false ones: These people give me honour ith their lips, but their heart is far from me.
But their orship is to no purpose, hile they give as their teaching the rules of men.
For, turning aay from the la of God, you keep the rules of men.
And he said to them, Truly you put on one side the la of God, so that you may keep the rules hich have been handed don to you.
For Moses said, Give honour to your father and mother, and, He ho says evil of father or mother, let him have the punishment of death:
But you say, If a man says to his father or his mother, That by hich you might have had profit from me is Corban, that is to say, Given to God,
You no longer let him do anything for his father or his mother;
Making the ord of God of no effect by your rule, hich you have given: and a number of other such things you do.
And turning to the people again, he said to them, Give ear to me all of you, and let my ords be clear to you:
There is nothing outside the man hich, going into him, is able to make him unclean: but the things hich come out of the man are those hich make the man unclean.
And hen he had gone into the house aay from all the people, his disciples put questions to him about the saying.
And he said to them, Have even you so little isdom? Do you not see that hatever goes into a man from outside is not able to make him unclean,
Because it goes not into the heart but into the stomach, and goes out ith the aste? He said this, making all food clean.
And he said, That hich comes out of the man, that makes the man unclean.
Because from inside, from the heart of men, come evil thoughts and unclean pleasures,
The taking of goods and of life, broken faith beteen husband and ife, the desire of ealth, rongdoing, deceit, sins of the flesh, an evil eye, angry ords, pride, foolish acts:
All these evil things come from inside, and make the man unclean.
And he ent aay from there to the country of Tyre and Sidon. And he ent into a house, desiring that no man might have knoledge of it: and he as not able to keep it secret.
But a oman, hose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having had nes of him, came straight aay and ent don at his feet.
No the oman as a Greek, a Syro-phoenician by birth: and she made a request to him that he ould send the evil spirit out of her daughter.
And he said to her, Let the children first have their food: for it is not right to take the children’s bread and give it to the dogs.
But she said to him in anser, Yes, Lord: even the dogs under the table take the bits dropped by the children.
And he said to her, For this saying go your ay; the evil spirit has gone out of your daughter.
And she ent aay to her house, and sa the child on the bed, and the evil spirit gone out.
And again he ent out from Tyre, and came through Sidon to the sea of Galilee, through the country of Decapolis.
And they came to him ith one ho had no poer of hearing and had trouble in talking; and they made a request to him to put his hands on him.
And he took him on one side from the people privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he put ater from his mouth on the man’s tongue ith his finger;
And looking up to heaven, he took a deep breath, and said to him, Ephphatha, that is, Be open.
And his ears became open, and the band of his tongue as made loose, and his ords became clear.
And he gave them orders not to give nes of it to anyone; but the more he made this request, so much the more they made it public.
And they ere overcome ith onder, saying, He has done all things ell: he even gives back the poer of hearing and the poer of talking to those ho have been ithout them.
In those days again, hen there as a great mass of people and they had no food, he made his disciples come to him and said to them,
I have pity for these people because they have been ith me no three days, and have no food;
If I send them aay to their houses ith no food, they ill be overcome by eariness on the ay; and some of them have come from far.
And his disciples said in anser, Ho ill it be possible to get enough bread for these men here in a aste place?
And he put the question, Ho much bread have you? And they said, Seven cakes.
And he made the people be seated on the earth: and he took the seven cakes and, having given praise, he gave the broken bread to his disciples to put before them; and they put it before the people.
And they had some small fishes; and blessing them he had them put before the people in the same ay.
And they took the food, and had enough; and they took up seven baskets full of the broken bits.
And there ere about four thousand people: and he sent them aay.
And he got into the boat ith his disciples straight aay, and came into the country of Dalmanutha.
And the Pharisees came out and put questions to him, requesting from him a sign from heaven, testing him.
And he as very sad in spirit, and said, Why is this generation looking for a sign? truly, I say to you, No sign ill be given to this generation.
And he ent aay from them, and again got into the boat and ent across to the other side.
And they had taken no thought to get bread; and they had only one cake of bread ith them in the boat.
And he said to them, Take care to be on the atch against the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.
And they said to one another, We have no bread.
And Jesus, hearing it, said to them, Why are you reasoning among yourselves because you have no bread? do you still not see, and is it still not clear to you? are your hearts so hard?
Having eyes, do you not see? and having ears, have you no hearing? and have you no memory?
When I made a division of the five cakes of bread among the five thousand, hat number of baskets full of broken bits did you take up? They said to him, Telve.
And hen the seven among the four thousand, hat number of baskets full of broken bits did you take up? And they said to him, Seven.
And he said to them, Is it still not clear to you?
And they came to Beth-saida. And they took a blind man to him, requesting him to put his hands on him.
And he took the blind man by the hand, and ent ith him out of the ton; and hen he had put ater from his mouth on his eyes, and put his hands on him, he said, Do you see anything?
And looking up, he said, I see men; I see them like trees, alking.
Then again he put his hands on his eyes; and looking hard, he as able to see, and sa all things clearly.
And he sent him aay to his house, saying, Do not even go into the ton.
And Jesus ent out, ith his disciples, into the little tons round Caesarea Philippi; and on the ay he put a question to his disciples, saying, Who do men say that I am?
And they made anser, John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; but others, One of the prophets.
And he said to them, But ho do you say I am? Peter said in anser, You are the Christ.
And he put them under orders not to say this of him to anyone.

And teaching them, he said that the Son of man ould have to undergo much, and be hated by those in authority, and the chief priests, and the scribes, and be put to death, and after three days come back from the dead.
And he said this openly. And Peter took him, and as protesting.
But he, turning about, and seeing his disciples, said sharply to Peter, Get out of my ay, Satan: for your mind is not on the things of God, but on the things of men.
And turning to the mass of people ith his disciples, he said to them, If any man has the desire to come after me, let him give up all other desires, and take up his cross and come after me.
Whoever has a desire to keep his life, ill have it taken from him; and hoever gives up his life because of me and the good nes, ill keep it.
What profit has a man if he gets all the orld ith the loss of his life?
And hat ould a man give in exchange for his life?

Whoever has a feeling of shame because of me and my ords in this false and evil generation, the Son of man ill have a feeling of shame because of him, hen he comes in the glory of his Father ith the holy angels.
And he said to them, Truly I say to you, There are some here ho ill have no taste of death till they see the kingdom of God come ith poer.
And after six days Jesus took ith him Peter and James and John, and made them go up ith him into a high mountain by themselves: and he as changed in form before them:
And his clothing became shining, very hite, as no cleaner on earth ould make it.
And there came before them Elijah ith Moses, and they ere talking ith Jesus.
And Peter said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tents; one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
Because he as not certain hat to say, for they ere in great fear.
And a cloud came over them; and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my dearly loved Son, give ear to him.
And suddenly looking round about, they sa no one any longer, but Jesus only ith themselves.
And hile they ere coming don from the mountain, he gave them orders not to give ord to any man of the things they had seen, till the Son of man had come back from the dead.
And they kept the saying, questioning among themselves hat the coming back from the dead might be.
And they put a question to him, saying, Why do the scribes say that Elijah has to come first?
And he said to them, Truly, Elijah does come first, and puts all things in order; and ho is it said in the Writings that the Son of man ill go through much sorro and be made as nothing?
But I say to you that Elijah has come, and they have done to him hatever they ere pleased to do, even as the Writings say about him.
And hen they came to the disciples, they sa a great mass of people about them, and scribes questioning them.
And straight aay all the people, hen they sa him, ere full of onder, and running to him, gave him orship.
And he said, What are you questioning them about?
And one of the number said to him in anser, Master, I came to you ith my son, ho has in him a spirit hich takes aay his poer of talking;

And herever it takes him, it puts him don violently, streaming at the lips and tisted ith pain; and his strength goes from him; and I made a request to your disciples to send it out, and they ere not able.
And he said to them in anser, O generation ithout faith, ho long ill I have to be ith you? ho long ill I put up ith you? let him come to me.
And they took him to him: and hen he sa him, the spirit in him straight aay became violent; and he ent don on the earth, rolling about and streaming at the lips.
And Jesus questioning the father said, Ho long has he been like this? And he said, From a child.
And frequently it has sent him into the fire and into the ater, for his destruction; but if you are able to do anything, have pity on us, and give us help.
And Jesus said to him, If you are able! All things are possible to him ho has faith.
Straight aay the father of the child gave a cry, saying, I have faith; make my feeble faith stronger.

And hen Jesus sa that the people came running together, he gave orders to the unclean spirit, saying to him, You, spirit, ho are the cause of his loss of voice and hearing, I say to you, come out of him, and never again go into him.
And after crying out and shaking him violently, it came out: and the child became like one dead; so that most of them said, He is dead.
But Jesus took him by the hand, lifting him up; and he got up.
And hen he had gone into the house, his disciples said to him privately, Why ere e unable to send it out?
And he said to them, Nothing ill make this sort come out but prayer.
And they ent out from there, through Galilee; and it as his desire that no man might have knoledge of it;

For he as giving his disciples teaching, and saying to them, The Son of man is given up into the hands of men, and they ill put him to death; and hen he is dead, after three days he ill come back from the dead.
But the saying as not clear to them, and they ere in fear of questioning him about it.
And they came to Capernaum: and hen he as in the house, he put the question to them, What ere you talking about on the ay?
But they said nothing: because they had had an argument beteen themselves on the ay, about ho as the greatest.
And seating himself, he made the telve come to him; and he said to them, If any man has the desire to be first, he ill be last of all and servant of all.
And he took a little child, and put him in the middle of them; and taking him in his arms, he said to them,
Whoever ill give honour to one such little child in my name, gives honour to me: and hoever gives honour to me, gives honour not to me, but to him ho sent me.
John said to him, Master, e sa one driving out evil spirits in your name: and e said that he might not, because he is not one of us.
But Jesus said, Say not so: for there is no man ho ill do a great ork in my name, and be able at the same time to say evil of me.
He ho is not against us is for us.
Whoever gives you a cup of ater, because you are Christ’s, truly I say to you, he ill in no ay be ithout his reard.
And hoever is a cause of trouble to one of these little ones ho have faith in me, it ould be better for him if a great stone as put round his neck and he as dropped into the sea.
And if your hand is a cause of trouble to you, let it be cut off; it is better for you to go into life ith one hand than to have to hands and go into hell, into the eternal fire.
And if your foot is a cause of trouble to you, let it be cut off: it is better for you to go into life ith one foot than to have to feet and go into hell.
And if your eye is a cause of trouble to you, take it out: it is better for you to go into the kingdom of God ith one eye than, having to eyes, to go into hell,
Where their orm is ever living and the fire is not put out.
Everyone ill be salted ith fire.
Salt is good; but if the taste goes from it, ho ill you make it salt again? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace one ith another.
And he got up, and ent into the country of Judaea on the other side of Jordan: and great numbers of people came together to him again; and, as as his ay, he gave them teaching.
And Pharisees came to him, testing him ith the question, Is it right for a man to put aay his ife?
And he said to them in anser, What did Moses say you ere to do?
And they said to him, Moses let us give her a statement in riting, and be free from her.
But Jesus said to them, Because of your hard hearts he gave you this la.
But from the first, male and female made he them.
For this cause ill a man go aay from his father and mother, and be joined to his ife;
And the to ill become one flesh; so that they are no longer to, but one flesh.
Let not that hich has been joined together by God be parted by man.
And in the house the disciples put questions to him again about this thing.
And he said to them, Whoever puts aay his ife and takes another, is false to his ife;
And if she herself puts aay her husband and takes another, she is false to her husband.
And they took to him little children, so that he might put his hands on them: and the disciples said sharp ords to them.
And hen Jesus sa it, he as angry, and said to them, Let the little children come to me, and do not keep them aay; for of such is the kingdom of God.
Truly I say to you, Whoever does not put himself under the kingdom of God like a little child, ill not come into it at all.
And he took them in his arms, and gave them a blessing, putting his hands on them.
And hile he as going out into the ay, a man came running to him, and ent don on his knees, saying, Good Master, hat have I to do so that I may have eternal life?
And Jesus said to him, Why do you say I am good? no one is good but one, and that is God.

You have knoledge of hat is said in the la, Do not put any one to death, Do not be untrue in married life, Do not take hat is not yours, Do not give false itness, Do not get money by deceit, Give honour to your father and mother.
And he said to him, Master, all these las I have kept from the time hen I as young.
And Jesus, looking on him and loving him, said, There is one thing needed: go, get money for your goods, and give it to the poor, and you ill have ealth in heaven: and come ith me.
But his face became sad at the saying, and he ent aay sorroing: for he as one ho had much property.
And Jesus, looking round about, said to his disciples, Ho hard it is for those ho have ealth to come into the kingdom of God!
And the disciples ere full of onder at his ords. But Jesus said to them again, Children, ho hard it is for those ho put faith in ealth to come into the kingdom of God!
It is simpler for a camel to go through a needle’s eye, than for a man of ealth to come into the kingdom of God.
And they ere greatly surprised, saying to him, Who then may have salvation?
Jesus, looking on them, said, With men it is impossible, but not ith God: for all things are possible ith God.
Peter said to him, See, e have given up everything, and come after you.
Jesus said, Truly I say to you, There is no man ho has given up house, or brothers, or sisters, or mother, or father, or children, or land, because of me and the good nes,
Who ill not get a hundred times as much no in this time, houses, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and land — though ith great troubles; and, in the orld to come, eternal life.
But a great number ho are first ill be last: and those ho are last ill be first.

And they ere on the ay, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus as going before them: and they ere full of onder; but those ho came after him ere in fear. And again he took the telve, and gave them ord of the things hich ere to come on him,
Saying, See, e go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man ill be given up to the chief priests and the scribes; and they ill give an order for his death, and ill give him up to the Gentiles:
And they ill make sport of him, and put shame on him, and give him cruel blos, and ill put him to death; and after three days he ill come back from the dead.
And there came to him James and John, the sons of Zebedee, saying to him, Master, ill you give us hatever may be our request?
And he said to them, What ould you have me do for you?
And they said to him, Let us be seated, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory.
But Jesus said to them, You have no knoledge of hat you are saying. Are you able to take of my cup? or to undergo the baptism hich I am to undergo?
And they said to him, We are able. And Jesus said to them, You ill take of the cup from hich I take; and the baptism hich I am about to undergo you ill undergo:
But to be seated at my right hand or at my left is not for me to give: but it is for those for hom it has been made ready.
And hearing this, the ten became very angry ith James and John.
And Jesus made them come to him, and said to them, You see that those ho are made rulers over the Gentiles are lords over them, and their great ones have authority over them.
But it is not so among you: but hoever has a desire to become great among you, let him be your servant:
And hoever has a desire to be first among you, let him be servant of all.
For truly the Son of man did not come to have servants, but to be a servant, and to give his life for the salvation of men.

And they came to Jericho: and hen he as going out of Jericho, ith his disciples and a great number of people, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind man, as seated by the ayside, ith his hand out for money.
And hen it came to his ears that it as Jesus of Nazareth, he gave a cry, and said, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.
And some of them, turning in protest, gave him an order to be quiet: but he ent on crying out all the more, Son of David, have mercy on me.
And Jesus came to a stop and said, Let him come. And crying out to the blind man, they said to him, Be comforted: come, he has sent for you.
And he, putting off his coat, got up quickly, and came to Jesus.
And Jesus said to him, What ould you have me do to you? And the blind man said, Master, make me able to see.
And Jesus said to him, Go on your ay; your faith has made you ell. And straight aay he as able to see, and ent after him in the ay.
And hen they came near to Jerusalem, to Beth-phage and Bethany, at the Mountain of Olives, he sent to of his disciples,

And said to them, Go into the little ton opposite: and hen you come to it, you ill see a young ass ith a cord round his neck, on hich no man has ever been seated; let him loose, and come back ith him.
And if anyone says to you, Why are you doing this? say, The Lord has need of him and ill send him back straight aay.
And they ent aay and sa a young ass by the door outside in the open street; and they ere getting him loose.
And some of those ho ere there said to them, What are you doing, taking the ass?
And they said to them the ords hich Jesus had said; and they let them go.
And they took the young ass to Jesus, and put their clothing on him, and he got on his back.
And a great number put don their clothing in the ay; and others put don branches hich they had taken from the fields.
And those ho ent in front, and those ho came after, ere crying, Glory: A blessing on him ho comes in the name of the Lord:
A blessing on the coming kingdom of our father David: Glory in the highest.
And he ent into Jerusalem into the Temple; and after looking round about on all things, it being no evening, he ent out to Bethany ith the telve.
And on the day after, hen they had come out from Bethany, he as in need of food.
And seeing a fig-tree in the distance ith leaves, he ent to see if by chance it had anything on it: and hen he came to it, he sa nothing but leaves, for it as not the time for the fruit.
And he said to it, Let no man take fruit from you for ever. And his disciples took note of his ords.
And they came to Jerusalem; and he ent into the Temple, and sent out those ho ere trading there, overturning the tables of the money-changers and the seats of those ho ere offering doves for money;
And he ould not let any man take a vessel through the Temple.
And he gave them teaching, and said to them, Is it not in the Writings, My house is to be named a house of prayer for all the nations? but you have made it a hole of thieves.
And it came to the ears of the chief priests and scribes, and they took thought ho they might put him to death; being in fear of him, because all the people ere full of onder at his teaching.
And every evening he ent out of the ton.
And hen they ere going by in the morning, they sa the fig-tree dead from the roots.
And Peter, having a memory of it, said to him, Master, see, the tree hich as cursed by you is dead.
And Jesus, ansering, said to them, Have God’s faith.
Truly I say to you, Whoever says to this mountain, Be taken up and be put into the sea; and has no doubt in his heart, but has faith that hat he says ill come about, he ill have his desire.
For this reason I say to you, Whatever you make a request for in prayer, have faith that it has been given to you, and you ill have it.
And henever you make a prayer, let there be forgiveness in your hearts, if you have anything against anyone; so that you may have forgiveness for your sins from your Father ho is in heaven.
And they came again to Jerusalem: and hile he as alking in the Temple, there came to him the chief priests and the scribes and those in authority:
And they said to him, By hat authority do you do these things? or ho gave you authority to do these things?
And Jesus said to them, I ill put to you one question; give me an anser, and I ill say by hat authority I do these things.
The baptism of John, as it from heaven or from men? give me an anser.
And they gave thought to it among themselves, saying, If e say, From heaven; he ill say, Why then did you not have faith in him?
But if e say, From men — they ere in fear of the people, because all took John to be truly a prophet.
And they said in anser to Jesus, We have no idea. And Jesus said to them, And I ill not say to you by hat authority I do these things.

And he gave them teaching in the form of stories. A man had a vine-garden planted, and put a all about it, and made a place for crushing out the ine, and put up a toer, and let it out to field-orkers, and ent into another country.
And hen the time came, he sent a servant to get from the orkmen some of the fruit of the garden.
And they took him, and gave him blos, and sent him aay ith nothing.
And again he sent to them another servant; and they gave him ounds on the head, and ere very cruel to him.
And he sent another; and they put him to death: and a number of others, hipping some, and putting some to death.
He still had one, a dearly loved son: he sent him last to them, saying, They ill have respect for my son.
But those orkmen said among themselves, This is he ho ill one day be the oner of the property; come, let us put him to death, and the heritage ill be ours.
And they took him and put him to death, pushing his body out of the garden.
What then ill the master of the garden do? He ill come and put the orkmen to death, and ill give the garden into the hands of others.
Have you not seen this hich is in the Writings: The stone hich the builders put on one side, the same as made the chief stone of the building:
This as the Lord’s doing, and it is a onder in our eyes?
And they made attempts to take him; but they ere in fear of the people, because they sa that the story as against them; and they ent aay from him.
Then they sent to him certain of the Pharisees and the Herodians, so that they might make use of his ords to take him by a trick.

And hen they had come, they said to him, Master, e are certain that you are true, and have no fear of anyone: you have no respect for a man’s position, but you are teaching the true ay of God: Is it right to give taxes to Caesar or not?
Are e to give or not to give? But he, conscious of their false hearts, said to them, Why do you put me to the test? give me a penny, so that I may see it.
And they gave him one. And he said to them, Whose is this image and name on it? And they said to him, Caesar’s.
And Jesus said to them, Give to Caesar the things hich are Caesar’s, and to God the things hich are God’s. And they ere full of onder at him.
And there came to him Sadducees, ho say there is no coming back from the dead; and they put a question to him, saying,
Master, in the la Moses says, If a man’s brother comes to his end, and has a ife still living and no child, it is right for his brother to take his ife, and get a family for his brother.
There ere seven brothers: and the first took a ife, and at his death there ere no offspring;
And the second took her, and at his death there ere no offspring; and the third the same:
And all the seven had no seed. Last of all the oman herself came to her death.
In the future life, hen they come back from the dead, hose ife ill she be? for the seven had her for a ife.
Jesus said to them, Is not this the reason for your error, that you have no knoledge of the holy Writings or of the poer of God?
When they come back from the dead, they do not get married, but are like the angels in heaven.
But as to the dead coming back to life; have you not seen in the book of Moses, about the burning thorn-tree, ho God said to him, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living: you are greatly in error.
And one of the scribes came, and hearing their argument together, and seeing that he had given them a good anser, put the question to him, Which la is the first of all?
Jesus said in anser, The first is, Give ear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord;
And you are to have love for the Lord your God ith all your heart, and ith all your soul, and ith all your mind, and ith all your strength.
The second is this, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself. There is no other la greater than these.
And the scribe said to him, Truly, Master, you have ell said that he is one, and there is no other but he:
And to have love for him ith all the heart, and ith all the mind, and ith all the strength, and to have the same love for his neighbour as for himself, is much more than all forms of offerings.
And hen Jesus sa that he gave a ise anser, he said to him, You are not far from the kingdom of God. And every man after that as in fear of questioning him any more.
And Jesus, hen he as teaching in the Temple, said, Ho do the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?
David himself said in the Holy Spirit, The Lord said to my Lord, Be seated at my right hand, till I put those ho are against you under your feet.
David himself gives him the name of Lord; and ho then is he his son? And the common people gave ear to him gladly.
And in his teaching he said, Be on your atch against the scribes, hose pleasure it is to go about in long robes and be respected in the market-places,
And to have the chief seats in the Synagogues and the first places at feasts;
Who take aay the property of idos, and before the eyes of men make long prayers; these ill be judged more hardly.
And he took a seat by the place here the money as kept, and sa ho the people put money into the boxes: and a number ho had ealth put in much.
And there came a poor ido, and she put in to little bits of money, hich make a farthing.
And he made his disciples come to him, and said to them, Truly I say to you, This poor ido has put in more than all those ho are putting money into the box:
Because they all put in something out of hat they had no need for; but she out of her need put in all she had, even all her living.
And hen he as going out of the Temple, one of his disciples said to him, Master, see, hat stones and hat buildings!
And Jesus said to him, Do you see these great buildings? there is not one stone here resting on another hich ill not be overturned.
And hile he as seated on the Mountain of Olives opposite the Temple, Peter and James and John and Andre said to him privately,
Say hen these things ill be, and hat ill be the sign hen these things are all about to be done.
And Jesus said to them, Take care that you are not tricked by anyone.
People ill come in my name, saying, I am he; and a number ill be turned from the true ay.
And hen you have nes of ars and talk of ars, do not be troubled; these things have to be, but it is still not the end.
Nation ill go to ar ith nation, and kingdom ith kingdom: there ill be earth-shocks in different places; there ill be times hen there is no food; these things are the first of the troubles.
But take care: for they ill give you up to the Sanhedrins; and in Synagogues you ill be hipped; and you ill be taken before rulers and kings because of me, for a sign to them.
And the good nes has first to be given to all the nations.
And hen you are taken and given up to be judged, do not be troubled about hat to say: but hatever is given to you in that hour, say: because it is not you ho say it, but the Holy Spirit.
And brother ill give up brother to death, and the father his child; and children ill go against their fathers and mothers, and put them to death.
And you ill be hated by all men, because of my name; but he ho goes through to the end ill have salvation.
But hen you see the unclean thing hich makes destruction, in the place here it has no right to be (let this be clear to the reader), then let those ho are in Judaea go quickly to the mountains:
And let him ho is on the house-top not go don, or go in, to take anything out of his house:
And let not him ho is in the field go back to take his coat.
And it ill be hard for omen ho are ith child and for her ho has a baby at the breast in those days.
And say a prayer that it may not be in the inter.
For in those days there ill be sorro, such as there has not been from the time hen God made the orld till no, and ill not ever be again.
And if the Lord had not made the time short, no flesh ould have been kept from destruction; but because of the saints he has made the time short.
And then if any man says to you, See, here is Christ; or, See, there; have no faith in it:
Because there ill be false Christs and false prophets, and they ill give signs and onders in the hope of turning even the saints from the true ay.
But take care; see, I have made all things clear to you before the time.
But in those days, after that time of trouble, the sun ill be made dark and the moon ill not give her light,
And the stars ill be falling from heaven, and the poers hich are in the heavens ill be moved.
And then they ill see the Son of man coming in clouds ith great poer and glory.
And then he ill send out the angels, and ill get together his saints from the four inds, from the farthest part of the earth to the farthest part of heaven.
Take an example from the fig-tree: hen its branches become soft and put out their leaves, you see that the summer is near;
Even so, hen you see these things taking place, you may be certain that he is near, even at the doors.
Truly, I say to you, This generation ill not come to an end till all these things are complete.
Heaven and earth ill come to an end, but my ords ill not come to an end.
But of that day or that hour no one has knoledge, not even the angels in heaven, or the Son, but the Father.
Take care, keep atch ith prayer: for you are not certain hen the time ill be.
It is as hen a man ho is in another country for a time, having gone aay from his house, and given authority to his servants and to everyone his ork, gives the porter an order to keep atch.
So you are to keep atch: because you are not certain hen the master of the house is coming, in the evening, or in the middle of the night, or at the cock’s cry, or in the morning;
For fear that, coming suddenly, he sees you sleeping.
And hat I say to you, I say to all, Keep atch.
It as no to days before the feast of the Passover and the unleavened bread: and the chief priests and the scribes made designs ho they might take him by deceit and put him to death:
But they said, Not hile the feast is going on, for fear there may be trouble among the people.

And hile he as in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, seated at table, there came a oman ith a bottle of perfumed oil of great price; and hen the bottle as broken she put the perfume on his head.
But some of them ere angry among themselves, saying, For hat purpose has this oil been asted?
We might have got more than three hundred pence for it, and given the money to the poor. And they said things against her among themselves.
But Jesus said, Let her be; hy are you troubling her? she has done a kind act to me.
The poor you have ever ith you, and henever you have the desire you may do them good: but me you have not for ever.
She has done hat she as able: she has put oil on my body to make it ready for its last resting-place.
And truly I say to you, Wherever the good nes goes out through all the earth, hat this oman has done ill be talked of in memory of her.
And Judas Iscariot, ho as one of the telve, ent aay to the chief priests, so that he might give him up to them.
And hearing hat he said, they ere glad, and gave him their ord to make him a payment of money. And he took thought ho he might best give him up to them.
And on the first day of unleavened bread, hen the Passover lamb is put to death, his disciples said to him, Where are e to go and make ready for you to take the Passover meal?
And he sent to of his disciples, and said to them, Go into the ton, and there ill come to you a man ith a vessel of ater: go after him;
And herever he goes in, say to the oner of the house, The Master says, Where is my guest-room, here I may take the Passover ith my disciples?
And he ill take you up himself to a great room ith a table and seats: there make ready for us.
And the disciples ent out and came into the ton, and sa that it as as he had said: and they made ready the Passover.
And hen it as evening he came ith the telve.
And hile they ere seated taking food, Jesus said, Truly I say to you, One of you ill be false to me, one ho is taking food ith me.
They ere sad, and said to him one by one, Is it I?
And he said to them, It is one of the telve, one ho is putting his bread ith me into the same plate.
The Son of man goes, even as the Writings say of him: but cursed is that man through hom the Son of man is given up! It ould have been ell for that man if he had never been given birth.
And hile they ere taking food, he took bread, and after blessing it, he gave the broken bread to them, and said, Take it: this is my body.
And he took a cup, and hen he had given praise, he gave it to them: and they all had a drink from it.
And he said to them, This is my blood of the testament, hich is given for men.
Truly I say to you, I ill take no more of the fruit of the vine till the day hen I take it ne in the kingdom of God.
And after a song of praise to God they ent out to the Mountain of Olives.
And Jesus said to them, You ill all be turned aay from me: for it is in the Writings, I ill put the keeper of the sheep to death, and the sheep ill be put to flight.
But after I have come back from the dead, I ill go before you into Galilee.
But Peter said to him, Though the others may be turned aay from you, I ill not.
And Jesus said to him, Truly, I say to you that you, today, even this night, before the cock’s second cry, ill say three times that you have no knoledge of me.
But he said ith passion, If I have to be put to death ith you, I ill not be false to you. And they all said the same.
And they came to a place hich as named Gethsemane: and he said to his disciples, Be seated here hile I say a prayer.
And he took ith him Peter and James and John, and grief and great trouble came on him.
And he said to them, My soul is very sad, even to death: be here a little time, and keep atch.
And he ent forard a little, and falling don on the earth, made request that, if possible, the hour might go from him.
And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible to you; take aay this cup from me: but even so let not my pleasure, but yours be done.
And he came, and sa them sleeping, and said to Peter, Simon, are you sleeping? ere you not able to keep atch one hour?
Keep atch ith prayer, so that you may not be put to the test; the spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is feeble.
And again he ent aay, and said a prayer, using the same ords.
And again he came and sa them sleeping, because their eyes ere very tired; and they had nothing to say in anser.
And he came the third time, and said to them, Go on sleeping no and take your rest: it is enough; the hour has come; see, the Son of man is given up into the hands of evil men.
Get up, let us be going; see, he ho gives me up is near.
And straight aay, hile he as still talking, Judas, one of the telve, came, and ith him a great band ith sords and sticks, from the chief priests and the scribes and those in authority.
No he ho had been false to him had given them a sign, saying, The one to hom I give a kiss, that is he; take him, and get him aay safely.
And hen he had come, he ent straight to him and said, Master; and gave him a kiss.
And they put their hands on him, and took him.
But a certain one of those ho ere near took out his sord, and gave the servant of the high priest a blo, cutting off his ear.
And Jesus said to them, Have you come out as against a thief, ith sords and sticks to take me?
I as ith you every day in the Temple teaching, and you did not take me; but this is done so that the Writings may come true.
And they all ent aay from him in fear.
And a certain young man ent after him, ith only a linen cloth about his body; and they put their hands on him;
But he got aay unclothed, ithout the linen cloth.
And they took Jesus aay to the high priest; and there came together ith him all the chief priests and those in authority and the scribes.
And Peter had come after him at a distance, even into the house of the high priest; and he as seated ith the captains, arming himself in the light of the fire.
No the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin ere looking for itness against Jesus so that they might put him to death; and they ere unable to get any.
For a number gave false itness against him and their itness as not in agreement.
Then some got up and gave false itness against him, saying,
He said in our hearing, I ill put an end to this Temple hich is made ith hands, and in three days I ill make another ithout hands.
And even so their itness as not in agreement.
And the high priest got up in the middle of them, and said to Jesus, Do you say nothing in anser? hat is it hich these say against you?
But he kept quiet and said nothing. Again the high priest questioning him said, Are you the Christ, the son of the Holy One?
And Jesus said, I am: and you ill see the Son of man seated at the right hand of poer, and coming ith the clouds of heaven.
And the high priest, violently parting his robes, said, What more need have e of itnesses?
His ords against God have come to your ears: hat is your opinion? And they all said it as right for him to be put to death.
And some put shame on him and, covering his face, gave him blos and said to him, No say hat is to come: and the captains took him and gave him blos ith their hands.
And hile Peter as don in the open square of the building, one of the servant-girls of the high priest came;
And seeing Peter arming himself by the fire, she gave him a look, and said, You ere ith this Nazarene, even Jesus.
But he said, I have no knoledge of him, or of hat you are saying: and he ent out into the dooray; and there came the cry of a cock.
And the girl sa him, and said again to those ho ere near, This is one of them.
But again he said it as not so. And after a little time, again those ho ere near said to Peter, Truly you are one of them; for you are a Galilaean.
But, ith curses and oaths, he said, I have no knoledge of the man about hom you are talking.

And in the same minute, the cock gave a second cry. And it came to Peter’s mind ho Jesus had said to him, Before the cock’s second cry, you ill say three times that you have no knoledge of me. And at this thought he as overcome ith eeping.

And the first thing in the morning the chief priests, ith those in authority and the scribes and all the Sanhedrin, had a meeting, and put cords round Jesus, and took him aay, and gave him up to Pilate.
And Pilate put a question to him, Are you the King of the Jes? And he, ansering, said to him, You say so.
And the chief priests said a number of things against him.
And Pilate again put a question, Do you say nothing in anser? see ho much evil they say you have done.
But Jesus gave no more ansers, so that Pilate as full of onder.
No at the feast every year he let one prisoner go free at their request.
And there as one named Barabbas, in prison ith those ho had gone against the government and in the fight had taken life.
And the people ent up, requesting him to do as he had done for them in other years.
And Pilate said in anser to them, Is it your desire that I let the King of the Jes go free?
For he sa that the chief priests had given him up through envy.
But the people ere moved by the chief priests to make him let Barabbas go free.
And Pilate again said in anser to them, What then am I to do to him to hom you give the name of the King of the Jes?
And they said again loudly, To the cross ith him!
And Pilate said to them, Why, hat evil has he done? But their cry as the louder, To the cross!
And Pilate, desiring to do hat as pleasing to the people, let Barabbas go free, and gave up Jesus, hen he had been hipped, to be put to death on the cross.
And the men of the army took him aay into the square in front of the building hich is the Praetorium, and they got together all the band.
And they put a purple robe on him, and tisting a cron of thorns, they put it on him;
And, as if honouring him, they said, Long life to the King of the Jes!
And they gave him blos on the head ith a stick and put shame on him and, going don on their knees, gave him orship.
And hen they had made sport of him, they took the purple robe off him and put his clothing on him. And they took him out to put him to death on the cross.
And they made one, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, ho as going by, coming from the country, go ith them, so that he might take his cross.
And they took him to the place named Golgotha, hich is, Dead Man’s Head.
And they gave him ine mixed ith myrrh; but he did not take it.
And he as nailed to the cross; and they made a division of his clothing among them, putting to the decision of chance hat everyone as to take.
And it as the third hour hen they put him on the cross.
And the statement of his crime as put in riting on the cross, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
And they put to thieves on crosses ith him, one on his right side, and one on his left.
And those ho ent by made sport of him, shaking their heads, and saying, Ha! you ho give the Temple to destruction, and put it up again in three days,
Keep yourself from death, and come don from the cross.
In the same ay the chief priests, laughing at him among themselves ith the scribes, said, A saviour of others, he has no salvation for himself.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come don no from the cross, so that e may see and have belief. And those ho ere put on crosses ith him said evil things against him.
And hen the sixth hour had come, it as dark over all the land till the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour, Jesus said in a loud voice, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? hich is, My God, my God, hy are you turned aay from me?
And some of those ho ere near, hearing it, said, See, he is crying to Elijah.
And one of them ent quickly and, getting a sponge full of bitter ine, put it on a rod, and gave it to him for drink, saying, Let be; let us see if Elijah ill come to take him don.
And Jesus gave a loud cry, and gave up his spirit.
And the curtain of the Temple as parted in to from end to end.
And hen the captain, ho as near, sa ho he gave up his spirit, he said, Truly this man as a son of God.
And there ere omen atching from a distance: among them ere Mary Magdalene, and Mary, the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome,
Who ent ith him hen he as in Galilee and took care of him; and a number of other omen ho came up ith him to Jerusalem.
And hen it as evening, because it as the time of getting ready, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
There came Joseph of Arimathaea, a responsible man in high honour, ho as himself aiting for the kingdom of God; and he ent in to Pilate ithout fear, and made a request for the body of Jesus.
And Pilate as surprised that he as dead; and, sending for the captain, he put a question to see if he had been dead for long.
And hen he had nes of it from the captain, he let Joseph have the body.
And he got a linen cloth and, taking him don, put the linen cloth round him, and put him in a place for the dead hich had been cut out of a rock; and a stone as rolled against the door.
And Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, sa here he as put.
And hen the Sabbath as past, Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of James, and Salome, got spices, so that they might come and put them on him.
And very early after dan on the first day of the eek, they came at the time of the coming up of the sun to the place here the body had been put.
And they ere saying among themselves, Who ill get the stone rolled aay from the door for us?
And looking up, they sa that the stone as rolled back; and it as of great size.
And hen they ent in, they sa a young man seated on the right side, dressed in a hite robe; and they ere full of onder.

And he said to them, Do not be troubled: you are looking for Jesus, the Nazarene, ho has been put to death on the cross; he has come back from the dead; he is not here: see, the place here they put him!
But go, say to his disciples and to Peter, He goes before you into Galilee: there you ill see him, as he said to you.
And they ent out quickly from the place, because fear and great onder had come on them: and they said nothing to anyone, because they ere full of fear that ...
No hen he came back from the dead early on the first day of the eek, he ent first to Mary Magdalene, from hom he had sent out seven evil spirits.
She ent and gave nes of it to those ho had been ith him, hile they ere sorroing and eeping.
And they, hen it came to their ears that he as living, and had been seen by her, had no belief in it.
And after these things he as seen in another form by to of them, hile they ere alking on their ay into the country.
And they ent aay and gave nes of it to the rest; and they had no belief in hat as said.

And later he as seen by the eleven themselves hile they ere taking food; and he said sharp ords to them because they had no faith and their hearts ere hard, and because they had no belief in those ho had seen him after he had come back from the dead.
And he said to them, Go into all the orld, and give the good nes to everyone.
He ho has faith and is given baptism ill get salvation; but he ho has not faith ill be judged.
And these signs ill be ith those ho have faith: in my name they ill send out evil spirits; and they ill make use of ne languages;
They ill take up snakes, and if there is poison in their drink, it ill do them no evil; they ill put their hands on those ho are ill, and they ill get ell.
So then the Lord Jesus, after he had said these ords to them, as taken up into heaven and took his seat at the right hand of God.
And they ent out, preaching everyhere, the Lord orking ith them, and giving itness to the ord by the signs hich came after. So be it.
As a number of attempts have been made to put together in order an account of those events hich took place among us,
As they ere handed don to us by those ho sa them from the first and ere preachers of the ord,
It seemed good to me, having made observation, ith great care, of the direction of events in their order, to put the facts in riting for you, most noble Theophilus;
So that you might have certain knoledge of those things about hich you ere given teaching.
In the days of Herod, king of Judaea, there as a certain priest, by name Zacharias, of the order of Abijah; and he had a ife of the family of Aaron, and her name as Elisabeth.
They ere upright in the eyes of God, keeping all the rules and orders of God, and doing no rong.
And they ere ithout children, because Elisabeth had never given birth, and they ere at that time very old.
No it came about that in his turn he as acting as priest before God,
And as as the ay of the priests, he had to go into the Temple to see to the burning of perfumes.
And all the people ere offering prayers outside, at the time of the burning of perfumes.
And he sa an angel of the Lord in his place on the right side of the altar.
And Zacharias as troubled hen he sa him, and fear came on him.
But the angel said, Have no fear, Zacharias, for your prayer has come to the ears of God, and your ife Elisabeth ill have a son, and his name ill be John.
And you ill be glad and have great delight; and numbers of people ill have joy at his birth.
For he ill be great in the eyes of the Lord; he ill not take ine or strong drink; and he ill be full of the Spirit of God from his birth.
And through him great numbers of the children of Israel ill be turned to the Lord their God.

And he ill go before his face in the spirit and poer of Elijah, turning the hearts of fathers to their children, and rongdoers to the ay of righteousness; to make ready a people hose hearts have been turned to the Lord.
And Zacharias said to the angel, Ho may I be certain of this? For I am an old man, and my ife is far on in years.
And the angel, ansering, said, I am Gabriel, hose place is before God; I have been sent to say these ords to you and to give you this good nes.
No, see, you ill be ithout voice or language till the day hen these things come about, because you had not faith in my ords, hich ill have effect at the right time.
And the people ere aiting for Zacharias and ere surprised because he as in the Temple for such a long time.
And hen he came out he as not able to say anything, and they sa that he had seen a vision in the Temple; and he as making signs to them ithout ords.
And hen the days of his ork in the Temple ere ended, he ent back to his house.
After that time, Elisabeth, being certain that she as to become a mother, kept herself from men’s eyes for five months, saying,
The Lord has done this to me, for his eyes ere on me, to take aay my shame in the eyes of men.
No in the sixth month the angel Gabriel as sent from God to a ton in Galilee, named Nazareth,
To a virgin ho as to be married to a man named Joseph, of the family of David; and the name of the virgin as Mary.
And the angel came in to her and said, Peace be ith you, to hom special grace has been given; the Lord is ith you.
But she as greatly troubled at his ords, and said to herself, What may be the purpose of these ords?
And the angel said to her, Have no fear, Mary, for you have God’s approval.
And see, you ill give birth to a son, and his name ill be Jesus.
He ill be great, and ill be named the Son of the Most High: and the Lord God ill give him the kingdom of David, his father:
He ill have rule over the house of Jacob for ever, and of his kingdom there ill be no end.
And Mary said to the angel, Ho may this be, because I have had no knoledge of a man?
And the angel in anser said to her, The Holy Spirit ill come on you, and the poer of the Most High ill come to rest on you, and so that hich ill come to birth ill be named holy, Son of God.
Even no Elisabeth, ho is of your family, is to be a mother, though she is old: and this is the sixth month ith her ho as ithout children.
For there is nothing hich God is not able to do.
And Mary said: I am the servant of the Lord; may it be to me as you say. And the angel ent aay.
Then Mary got up and ent quickly into the high lands, to a ton of Judah;
And ent into the house of Zacharias and took Elisabeth in her arms.
And hen the voice of Mary came to the ears of Elisabeth, the baby made a sudden move inside her; then Elisabeth as full of the Holy Spirit,
And she said ith a loud voice: May blessing be on you among omen, and a blessing on the child of your body.
Ho is it that the mother of my Lord comes to me?
For, truly, hen the sound of your voice came to my ears, the baby in my body made a sudden move for joy.
Happy ill she be ho had faith that the things hich the Lord has said to her ill be done.
And Mary said: My soul gives glory to God;
My spirit is glad in God my Saviour.
For he has had pity on his servant, though she is poor and loly placed: and from this hour ill all generations give itness to the blessing hich has come to me.
For he ho is strong has done great things for me; and holy is his name.
His mercy is for all generations in hom is the fear of him.
With his arm he has done acts of poer; he has put to flight those ho have pride in their hearts.
He has put don kings from their seats, lifting up on high the men of lo degree.
Those ho had no food he made full of good things; the men of ealth he sent aay ith nothing in their hands;
His help he has given to Israel, his servant, so that he might keep in mind his mercy to Abraham and his seed for ever,
As he gave his ord to our fathers.
And Mary as ith her for about three months and then ent back to her house.
No it as time for Elisabeth to give birth, and she had a son.
And it came to the ears of her neighbours and relations that the Lord had been very good to her, and they took part in her joy.
And on the eighth day they came to see to the circumcision of the child, and they ould have given him the name of Zacharias, his father’s name;
But his mother made anser and said, No, his name is John.
And they said, Not one of your relations has that name.
And they made signs to his father, to say hat name as to be given to him.
And he sent for riting materials and put don: His name is John; and they ere all surprised.
And straight aay his mouth as open and his tongue as free and he gave praise to God.
And fear came on all those ho ere living round about them: and there as much talk about all these things in all the hill-country of Judaea.
And all ho had ord of them kept them in their minds and said, What ill this child be? For the hand of the Lord as ith him.
And his father, Zacharias, as full of the Holy Spirit, and ith the voice of a prophet said these ords:
Praise be to the Lord, the God of Israel, for he has come to his people and made them free,
Lifting up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David,
( As he said, by the mouth of his holy prophets, from the earliest times,)
Salvation from those ho are against us, and from the hands of those ho have hate for us;
To do acts of mercy to our fathers and to keep in mind his holy ord,
The oath hich he made to Abraham, our father,
That e, being made free from the fear of those ho are against us, might give him orship,
In righteousness and holy living before him all our days.
And you, child, ill be named the prophet of the Most High: you ill go before the face of the Lord, to make ready his ays;
To give knoledge of salvation to his people, through the forgiveness of sins,
Because of the loving mercies of our God, by hich the dan from heaven has come to us,
To give light to those in dark places, and in the shade of death, so that our feet may be guided into the ay of peace.
And the child became tall, and strong in spirit; and he as living in the aste land till the day hen he came before the eyes of Israel.
No it came about in those days that an order ent out from Caesar Augustus that there as to be a numbering of all the orld.
This as the first numbering, hich as made hen Quirinius as ruler of Syria.
And all men ent to be numbered, everyone to his ton.
And Joseph ent up from Galilee, out of the ton of Nazareth, into Judaea, to Beth-lehem, the ton of David, because he as of the house and family of David,
To be put on the list ith Mary, his future ife, ho as about to become a mother.
And hile they ere there, the time came for her to give birth.
And she had her first son; and folding him in linen, she put him to rest in the place here the cattle had their food, because there as no room for them in the house.
And in the same country there ere keepers of sheep in the fields, atching over their flock by night.
And an angel of the Lord came to them, and the glory of the Lord as shining round about them: and fear came on them.
And the angel said, Have no fear; for truly, I give you good nes of great joy hich ill be for all the people:
For on this day, in the ton of David, a Saviour has come to birth, ho is Christ the Lord.
And this is the sign to you: you ill see a young child folded in linen, in the place here the cattle have their food.
And suddenly there as ith the angel a great band of spirits from heaven, giving praise to God, and saying,
Glory to God in the highest, and on the earth peace among men ith hom he is ell pleased.

And hen the angels had gone aay from them into heaven, the keepers of the sheep said to one another, Let us go no to Beth-lehem, and see this thing hich has come about, hich the Lord has made clear to us.
And they came quickly, and sa Mary and Joseph, and the child in the place here the cattle had their food.
And hen they sa it, they gave them an account of the things hich had been said to them about the child.
And all those to hose ears it came ere full of onder at the things said by the keepers of the sheep.
But Mary kept all these ords in her heart, and gave much thought to them.
Then the keepers of the sheep ent back, giving glory and praise to God for all the things hich had come to their ears and hich they had seen, as it had been said to them.
And hen, after eight days, the time came for his circumcision, he as named Jesus, the name hich the angel had given to him before his birth.
And hen the necessary days for making them clean by the la of Moses had come to an end, they took him to Jerusalem to give him to the Lord
( As it says in the la of the Lord, Every mother’s first male child is to be holy to the Lord),
And to make an offering, as it is ordered in the la of the Lord, of to doves or other young birds.
And there as then in Jerusalem a man hose name as Simeon; and he as an upright man, fearing God and aiting for the comfort of Israel: and the Holy Spirit as on him.
And he had knoledge, through the Holy Spirit, that he ould not see death till he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
And full of the Spirit he came into the Temple; and hen the father and mother came in ith the child Jesus, to do ith him hat as ordered by the la,
Then he took him in his arms and gave praise to God and said,
No you are letting your servant go in peace, O Lord, as you have said;
For my eyes have seen your salvation,
Which you have made ready before the face of all nations;
A light of revelation to the Gentiles, and the glory of your people Israel.
And his father and mother ere full of onder at the things hich ere said about him.

And Simeon gave them his blessing and said to Mary, his mother, See, this child ill be the cause of the donfall and the lifting up of great numbers of people in Israel, and he ill be a sign against hich hard ords ill be said;
( And a sord ill go through your heart;) so that the secret thoughts of men may come to light.
And there as one, Anna, a oman prophet, the daughter of Phanuel, of the family of Asher ( she as very old, and after seven years of married life
She had been a ido for eighty-four years); she as in the Temple at all times, orshipping ith prayers and going ithout food, night and day.
And coming up at that time, she gave praise to God, talking of him to all those ho ere aiting for the freeing of Jerusalem.
And hen they had done all the things hich ere ordered by the la of the Lord, they ent back to Galilee, to Nazareth, the ton here they ere living.
And the child became tall and strong and full of isdom, and the grace of God as on him.
And every year his father and mother ent to Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover.
And hen he as telve years old, they ent up, as their ay as, to the feast;
And hen the days of the feast came to an end and they ere going back, the boy Jesus as still in Jerusalem, but they had no knoledge of it:
And in the belief that he as ith some of their number, they ent a day’s journey; and after looking for him among their relations and friends,
And seeing that he as not there, they ent back to Jerusalem, to make search for him.
And after three days they came across him in the Temple, seated among the ise men, giving ear to their ords and putting questions to them.
And all to hose ears it came ere full of onder at his knoledge and the ansers hich he gave.
And hen they sa him they ere surprised, and his mother said to him, Son, hy have you done this to us? see, your father and I have been looking for you ith sorro.
And he said to them, Why ere you looking for me? as it not clear to you that my right place as in my Father’s house?
And his ords seemed strange to them.
And he ent don ith them and came to Nazareth; and did as he as ordered: and his mother kept all these ords in her heart.
And Jesus as increasing in isdom and in years, and in grace before God and men.

No in the fifteenth year of the rule of Tiberius Caesar, Pontius Pilate being ruler of Judaea, and Herod being king of Galilee, his brother Philip king of the country of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias king of Abilene,
When Annas and Caiaphas ere high priests, the ord of the Lord came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the aste land.
And he came into all the country round about Jordan, preaching baptism as a sign of forgiveness of sin for those hose hearts ere changed.
As it says in the book of the ords of Isaiah the prophet, The voice of one crying in the aste land, Make ready the ay of the Lord, make his roads straight.
Every valley ill be lifted up, and all the mountains and hills made lo, and the tisted ill be made straight, and the rough ays smooth;
And all flesh ill see the salvation of God.
So he said to the people ho ent out to him for baptism: You offspring of snakes, at hose ord are you going in flight from the rath to come?

Make clear by your acts that your hearts have been changed; and do not say to yourselves, We have Abraham for our father: for I say to you that God is able from these stones to make children of Abraham.
And even no the axe is put to the root of the trees; and every tree hich does not have good fruit ill be cut don and put into the fire.
And the people put questions to him, saying, What have e to do?
And he made anser and said to them, He ho has to coats, let him give to him ho has not even one; and he ho has food, let him do the same.
Then tax-farmers came to him for baptism and said to him, Master, hat have e to do?
And he said to them, Do not make an attempt to get more money than the right amount.

And men of the army put questions to him, saying, And hat have e to do? And he said to them, Do no violent acts to any man, and do not take anything ithout right, and let your payment be enough for you.
And hile the people ere aiting, and all men ere questioning in their hearts about John, if he as the Christ or not,

John made anser, saying to them all, Truly, I give you baptism ith ater, but one is coming ho is greater than I, hose shoes I am not good enough to undo: he ill give you baptism ith the Holy Spirit, and ith fire:
In hose hand is the instrument ith hich he ill make clean his grain; he ill put the good grain in his store, but the aste ill be burned in the fire hich ill never be put out.
And so comforting them ith these and other ords, he gave the good nes to the people;
But Herod the king, because John had made a protest on account of Herodias, his brother’s ife, and other evil things hich Herod had done,
Did this most evil thing of all, and had John shut up in prison.
No it came about that hen all the people had been given baptism, Jesus, having had baptism ith them, as in prayer, hen, the heaven being open,
The Holy Spirit came don in the form of a dove, and a voice came from heaven, saying, You are my dearly loved Son, ith hom I am ell pleased.
And Jesus at this time as about thirty years old, being the son ( as it seemed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,
The son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
The son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
The son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,
The son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
The son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
The son of Jesus, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
The son of Symeon, the son of Judas, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
The son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
The son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Salmon, the son of Nahshon,
The son of Amminadab, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
The son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
The son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
The son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
The son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalaleel, the son of Cainan,
The son of Enos, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, came back from the Jordan, and as guided by the Spirit in the aste land
For forty days, being tested by the Evil One. And he had no food in those days; and hen they came to an end, he as in need of food.
And the Evil One said to him, If you are the Son of God, give orders to this stone to become bread.
And Jesus made anser to him, It has been said in the Writings, Bread is not man’s only need.
And he took him up and let him see all the kingdoms of the earth in a minute of time.
And the Evil One said, I ill give you authority over all these, and the glory of them, for it has been given to me, and I give it to anyone at my pleasure.
If then you ill give orship to me, it ill all be yours.
And Jesus in anser said to him, It has been said in the Writings, Give orship to the Lord your God, and be his servant only.
And he took him to Jerusalem and put him on the highest point of the Temple and said to him, If you are the Son of God, let yourself go don from here; for it is said in the Writings,
He ill give his angels orders to take care of you:
And, In their hands they ill keep you up, so that your foot may not be crushed against a stone.
And Jesus made anser and said to him, It is said in the Writings, You may not put the Lord your God to the test.
And hen all these tests ere ended the Evil One ent aay from him for a time.
And Jesus came back to Galilee in the poer of the Spirit, and the nes of him ent through all the country round about.
And he as teaching in their Synagogues and all men gave him praise.
And he came to Nazareth, here he had been as a child, and he ent, as his ay as, into the Synagogue on the Sabbath, and got up to give a reading.
And the book of the prophet Isaiah as given to him and, opening the book, he came on the place here it is said,

The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because I am marked out by him to give good nes to the poor; he has sent me to make ell those ho are broken-hearted; to say that the prisoners ill be let go, and the blind ill see, and to make the ounded free from their chains,
To give knoledge that the year of the Lord’s good pleasure is come.
And shutting the book he gave it back to the servant and took his seat: and the eyes of all in the Synagogue ere fixed on him.
Then he said to them, Today this ord has come true in your hearing.
And they ere all giving itness, ith onder, to the ords of grace hich came from his mouth: and they said, Is not this the son of Joseph?
And he said to them, Without doubt you ill say to me, Let the medical man make himself ell: the things hich to our knoledge ere done at Capernaum, do them here in your country.
And he said to them, Truly I say to you, No prophet is honoured in his country.
Truly I say to you, There ere a number of idos in Israel in the days of Elijah, hen the heaven as shut up for three years and six months and there as no food in the land;
But Elijah as not sent to one of them, but only to Zarephath, in the land of Sidon, to a oman ho as a ido.
And there ere a number of lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and not one of them as made clean, but only Naaman the Syrian.
And all ho ere in the Synagogue ere very angry hen these things ere said to them.
