And they got up and took him out of the ton to the edge of the mountain on hich their ton as, so that they might send him don to his death.
But he came through them and ent on his ay.
And he came don to Capernaum, a ton of Galilee; and he as giving them teaching on the Sabbath.
And they ere surprised at his teaching, for his ord as ith authority.
And there as a man in the Synagogue ho had an unclean spirit; and he gave a loud cry and said,
Let us be! hat have e to do ith you, Jesus of Nazareth? have you come to put an end to us? I have knoledge ho you are, the Holy One of God.
And Jesus said to him, Be quiet, and come out of him. And hen the evil spirit had put him don on the earth in the middle of them, he came out of him, having done him no damage.
And onder came on them all and they said to one another, What are these ords? for ith authority and poer he gives orders to the evil spirits and they come out.
And there as much talk about him in all the places round about.
And he got up and ent out of the Synagogue and ent into the house of Simon. And Simon’s ife’s mother as very ill ith a burning heat; and in anser to their prayers for her
He ent near her, and ith a sharp ord he gave orders to the disease and it ent aay from her; and straight aay she got up and took care of their needs.
And at sundon all those ho had anyone ill ith any sort of disease, took them to him, and he put his hands on every one of them and made them ell.
And evil spirits came out of a number of them, crying out and saying, You are the Son of God. But he gave them sharp orders not to say a ord, because they had knoledge that he as the Christ.
And hen it as day, he came out and ent to a aste place; and great numbers of people came looking for him, and they came to him and ould have kept him from going aay.
But he said to them, I have to give the good nes of the kingdom of God in other tons, because that is hy I as sent.
And he as teaching in the Synagogues of Galilee.
No it came about that hile the people came pushing to be near him, and to have knoledge of the ord of God, he as by a ide stretch of ater named Gennesaret;
And he sa to boats by the edge of the ater, but the fishermen had gone out of them and ere ashing their nets.
And he got into one of the boats, the property of Simon, and made a request to him to go a little ay out from the land. And being seated he gave the people teaching from the boat.
And hen his talk as ended, he said to Simon, Go out into deep ater, and let don your nets for fish.
And Simon, ansering, said, Master, e ere orking all night and e took nothing: but at your ord I ill let don the nets.
And hen they had done this, they got such a great number of fish that it seemed as if their nets ould be broken;
And they made signs to their friends in the other boat to come to their help. And they came, and the to boats ere so full that they ere going don.
But Simon, hen he sa it, ent don at the knees of Jesus and said, Go aay from me, O Lord, for I am a sinner.
For he as full of onder and so ere all those ho ere ith him, at the number of fish hich they had taken;
And so ere James and John, the sons of Zebedee, ho ere orking ith Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, Have no fear; from this time forard you ill be a fisher of men.
And hen they had got their boats to the land, they gave up everything and ent after him.

And it came about that hile he as in one of the tons, there as a leper there: and hen he sa Jesus he ent don on his face in prayer to him, saying, Lord, if it is your pleasure, you have poer to make me clean.
And he put out his hand to him and said, It is my pleasure; be clean. And straight aay his disease ent from him.
And he gave him orders: Say nothing to any man, but let the priest see you and give an offering so that you may be made clean, as the la of Moses says, and for a itness to them.
But nes of him ent out all the more, in every direction, and great numbers of people came together to give hearing to his ords and to be made ell from their diseases.
But he ent aay by himself to a aste place for prayer.

And it came about that on one of these days he as teaching; and some Pharisees and teachers of the la ere seated there, ho had come from every ton of Galilee and Judaea and from Jerusalem; and the poer of the Lord as ith him, to make those ho ere ill free from their diseases.
And some men had ith them, on a bed, a man ho as ill, ithout poer of moving; and they made attempts to get him in and put him before Jesus.
And because of the mass of people, there as no ay to get him in; so they ent up on the top of the house and let him don through the roof, on his bed, into the middle in front of Jesus.
And seeing their faith he said, Man, you have forgiveness for your sins.
And the scribes and Pharisees ere having an argument, saying, Who is this, ho has no respect for God? ho is able to give forgiveness for sins, but God only?
But Jesus, ho had knoledge of their thoughts, said to them, Why are you reasoning in your hearts?
Which is the simpler: to say, You have forgiveness for your sins; or to say, Get up and go?
But so that you may see that on earth the Son of man has authority for the forgiveness of sins, ( he said to the man ho as ill,) I say to you, Get up, and take up your bed, and go into your house.
And straight aay he got up before them, and took up his bed and ent aay to his house giving praise to God.
And onder overcame them all, and they gave glory to God; and they ere full of fear, saying, We have seen strange things today.
And after these things he ent out, and sa Levi, a tax-farmer, seated at the place here taxes ere taken, and said to him, Come after me.
And giving up his business, he got up and ent after him.
And Levi made a great feast for him in his house: and a great number of tax-farmers and others ere seated at table ith them.
And the Pharisees and their scribes made protests against his disciples, saying, Why do you take food and drink ith tax-farmers and sinners?
And Jesus, ansering, said to them, Those ho are ell have no need of a medical man, but those ho are ill.
I have come, not to get the upright, but sinners, so that they may be turned from their sins.
And they said to him, The disciples of John frequently go ithout food, and make prayers, and so do the disciples of the Pharisees; but your disciples take food and drink.
And Jesus said, Are you able to make the friends of the nely-married man go ithout food hen he is ith them?
But the days ill come hen he ill be taken aay from them, and then they ill go ithout food.
And he said to them, in a story, No man takes a bit of cloth from a ne coat and puts it on to an old coat, for so the ne coat ould be damaged and the bit from the ne ould not go ell ith the old.
And no man puts ne ine into old ine-skins, for fear that the skins ill be burst by the ne ine, and the ine be let out, and the skins come to destruction.
But ne ine has to be put into ne ine-skins.
And no man, having had old ine, has any desire for ne, for he says, The old is better.
No it came about that on the Sabbath he as going through the fields of grain, and his disciples took the heads of the grain for food, crushing them in their hands.
But some of the Pharisees said, Why do you do hat it is not right to do on the Sabbath?
And Jesus said, Have you not seen in the Writings hat David did hen he as in need of food, he, and those ho ere ith him;
Ho he ent into the house of God and took for food the holy bread, hich only the priests may take, and gave it to those ho ere ith him?
And he said, The Son of man is lord even of the Sabbath.
And it came about, on another Sabbath, that he ent into the Synagogue and as teaching there. And a man as there hose right hand as dead.
And the scribes and Pharisees ere atching him to see if he ould make him ell on the Sabbath, so that they might be able to say something against him.
But he had knoledge of their thoughts; and he said to the man hose hand as dead, Get up and come into the middle. And he got up and came forard.
And Jesus said, I put the question to you, Is it right to do good on the Sabbath or to do evil? to give life or to take it aay?
And looking round on all of them, he said to him, Put out your hand. And he did so: and his hand as made ell.
But they ere full of rath, and ere talking together about hat they might do to Jesus.
And it came about in those days that he ent out to the mountain for prayer; and he as all night in prayer to God.
And the day came and, turning to his disciples, he made a selection from among them of telve, to hom he gave the name of Apostles;
Simon, to hom he gave the name of Peter, and Andre, his brother, and James and John and Philip and Bartholome
And Matthe and Thomas and James, the son of Alphaeus, and Simon, ho as named the Zealot,
And Judas, the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, he ho as false to him.

And he came don ith them to a level place, and a great band of his disciples, and a very great number of people from all Judaea and Jerusalem and from the parts of Tyre and Sidon by the sea, came to give hearing to him, and to be made ell from their diseases;
And those ho ere troubled ith unclean spirits ere made ell.
And all the people ere desiring to be touched by him, for poer came from him and made them all ell.
And turning his eyes to his disciples he said, Happy are you ho are poor: for the kingdom of God is yours.
Happy are you ho are in need of food no: for you ill be made full. Happy are you ho are eeping no; for you ill be glad.
Happy are you, hen men have hate for you, and put you aay from among them and say angry ords to you, turning aay in disgust at your name, because of the Son of man.
Be glad in that day, and be lifted up for joy, for your reard in heaven ill be great: for their fathers did these same things to the prophets.
But unhappy are you ho have ealth: for you have been comforted no.
Unhappy are you ho are full of food no: for you ill be in need. Unhappy are you ho are laughing no: for you ill be crying in sorro.
Unhappy are you hen all men give you their approval: for so their fathers did to the false prophets.
But I say to you ho give ear to me, Have love for those ho are against you, do good to those ho have hate for you,
Give blessing to those ho give you curses, say prayers for those ho are cruel to you.
If a man gives you a blo on one side of your face, then let the other side be turned to him; from him ho takes aay your coat, do not keep back your robe.
Give to everyone ho comes ith a request, and if a man takes aay your property, make no attempt to get it back again.
Do to others as you ould have them do to you.
If you have love for those ho have love for you, hat credit is it to you? for even sinners have love for those ho have love for them.
And if you do good to those ho do good to you, hat credit is it to you? for even sinners do the same.
And if you let those have the use of your money, from hom you are hoping to get it back, hat credit is it to you? even sinners do so to sinners, hoping to get back as much as they gave.

But be loving to those ho are against you and do them good, and give them your money, not giving up hope, and your reard ill be great and you ill be the sons of the Most High: for he is kind to evil men, and to those ho have hard hearts.
Be full of pity, even as your Father is full of pity.
Be not judges of others, and you ill not be judged: do not give punishment to others, and you ill not get punishment yourselves: make others free, and you ill be made free:
Give, and it ill be given to you; good measure, crushed don, full and running over, they ill give to you. For in the same measure as you give, it ill be given to you again.
And he gave them teaching in the form of a story, saying, Is it possible for one blind man to be guide to another? ill they not go falling together into a hole?
The disciple is not greater than his master, but everyone hose learning is complete ill be like his master.
And hy do you take note of the grain of dust in your brother’s eye, but take no note of the bit of ood hich is in your eye?

Ho ill you say to your brother, Brother, let me take the grain of dust out of your eye, hen you yourself do not see the bit of ood in your eye? O false one! first take the ood out of your eye and then you ill see clearly to take the dust out of your brother’s eye.
For no good tree gives bad fruit, and no bad tree gives good fruit.
For every tree is judged by its fruit. Men do not get figs from thorns, or grapes from blackberry plants.
The good man, out of the good store of his heart, gives good things; and the evil man, out of his evil store, gives evil: for out of the full store of the heart come the ords of the mouth.
Why do you say to me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things hich I say?
Everyone ho comes to me and gives ear to my ords and does them, I ill make clear to you hat he is like:
He is like a man building a house, ho ent deep and put the base of it on a rock; and hen the ater came up and the river as driving against that house, it as not moved, because the building as good.

But he ho gives hearing, ithout doing, is like a man building a house on the earth ithout a base for it; and hen the force of the river came against it, straight aay it came don; and the destruction of that house as great.
After he had come to the end of all his ords in the hearing of the people, he ent into Capernaum.
And a certain captain had a servant ho as very dear to him; this servant as ill and near to death.
And hen nes of Jesus came to his ears, he sent to him rulers of the Jes, requesting that he ould come and make his servant ell.
And they, hen they came to Jesus, made their request armly, saying,
It is right for you to do this for him, because he is a friend to our nation, and himself has put up a Synagogue for us.
And Jesus ent ith them. And hen he as not far from the house, the man sent friends to him, saying, Lord, do not give yourself trouble: for I am not important enough for you to come into my house:
And I had the feeling that I as not even good enough to come to you: but say the ord only, and my servant ill be ell.
For I, myself, am a man under authority, having men under me; and I say to this one, Go, and he goes; and to another, Come, and he comes; and to my servant, Do this, and he does it.
And hen these things ere said to Jesus, he as surprised, and, turning to the mass of people coming after him, said, I have not seen such great faith, no, not in Israel.
And hen those ho ere sent came back to the house they sa that the servant as ell.
And it came about, after a little time, that he ent to a ton named Nain; and his disciples ent ith him, and a great number of people.
No hen he came near the door of the ton, a dead man as being taken out, the only son of his mother, ho as a ido: and a great number of people from the ton ere ith her.
And hen the Lord sa her, he had pity on her and said to her, Be not sad.
And he came near, and put his hand on the stretcher here the dead man as: and those ho ere moving it came to a stop. And he said, Young man, I say to you, Get up.
And the dead man got up, and ords came from his lips. And he gave him to his mother.
And fear came on all, and they gave praise to God, saying, A great prophet is among us: and, God has given thought to his people.
And this story about him ent through all Judaea and the places round about.
And the disciples of John gave him an account of all these things.
Then John sent to of his disciples to the Lord, saying, Are you he ho is to come, or are e aiting for another?
And hen the men came to him they said, John the Baptist has sent us to you, saying, Are you he ho is to come, or are e aiting for another?
At that time, he made a number of people free from their diseases and their pains, and from evil spirits; and to others ho ere blind he gave back the use of their eyes.

And ansering them he said, Go back and give nes to John of hat you have seen, and the things hich have come to your ears; the blind no see, those ho had no poer in their legs are alking, lepers are made clean, those ho had no hearing no have their ears open, dead men come to life again, and the poor have the good nes given to them.
And a blessing ill be on him ho has no doubts about me.
And hen the men ho ere sent by John had gone aay, he said to the people, about John, What did you go out into the aste land to see? a tall stem moving in the ind?
But hat did you go out to see? a man in soft clothing? See no, those ho have beautiful clothing and delicate food are in kings’ houses.
But hat did you go out to see? a prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
This is he of hom it has been said, See, I send my servant before your face, ho ill make ready your ay before you.
I say to you, Among all the sons of omen, not one is greater than John: but he ho is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
( And all the people, and the tax-farmers, to hom John had given baptism, hen they had knoledge of these things, gave glory to God.
But the Pharisees and the teachers of the la ere against the purpose of God for themselves, not having had his baptism.)
What comparison am I to make of the men of this generation? hat are they like?

They are like children ho are seated in the market-place, crying out to one another, and saying, We made music for you, but you did not take part in the dance; e gave cries of sorro, but you ere not sad.
For John the Baptist came, taking no food or drink, and you say, He has an evil spirit.
The Son of man came feasting, and you say, Here is a lover of food and ine, a friend of tax-farmers and sinners.
But isdom is judged to be right by all her children.
And one of the Pharisees made a request that he ould take a meal ith him. And he ent into the Pharisee’s house and took his seat at the table.
And there as a oman in the ton ho as a sinner; and hen she had nes that he as a guest in the Pharisee’s house, she took a bottle of perfume,

And ent in and took her place at the back of him, near his feet, eeping, so that his feet ere ashed ith the drops from her eyes, and ith her hair she made them dry, and kissing his feet she put the perfume on them.
No hen the Pharisee in hose house he as sa it, he said to himself, This man, if he as a prophet, ould be conscious hat sort of oman this is ho has put her hands on him, that she is a sinner.
And Jesus, ansering, said, Simon, I have something to say to you. And he said, Master, say on.
And he said, To men ere in debt to a certain man of business: one had a debt of five hundred pence, and the other of fifty.
When they ere unable to make payment, he made the to of them free of their debts. Which of them, no, ill have the greater love for him?
Simon, in anser, said, It seems he hose debt as greater. And he said, Your decision is right.

And turning to the oman he said to Simon, You see this oman? I came into your house; you did not give me ater for my feet: but she has been ashing my feet ith the drops from her eyes, and drying them ith her hair.
You did not give me a kiss: but she, from the time hen I came in, has gone on kissing my feet.
You put no oil on my head: but she has put perfume on my feet.
And so I say to you, She ill have forgiveness for her sins hich are great in number, because of her great love: but he ho has small need of forgiveness gives little love.
And he said to her, You have forgiveness for your sins.
And those ho ere seated at table ith him said to themselves, Who is this ho even gives forgiveness of sins?
And he said to the oman, By your faith you have salvation; go in peace.
And it came about, after a short time, that he ent through ton and country giving the good nes of the kingdom of God, and ith him ere the telve,
And certain omen ho had been made free from evil spirits and diseases, Mary named Magdalene, from hom seven evil spirits had gone out,
And Joanna, the ife of Chuza, Herod’s chief house-servant, and Susanna and a number of others, ho gave him of their ealth for his needs.
And hen a great number of people came together, and men from every ton ent out to him, he gave them teaching in the form of a story:
A man ent out to put in seed, and hile he as doing it, some as dropped by the ayside and it as crushed under foot, and as taken by the birds of heaven.
And some ent on the rock, and hen it came up it became dry and dead because it had no ater.
And some ent among thorns, and the thorns came up ith it and it had no room for groth.
And some falling on good earth, came up and gave fruit a hundred times as much. And ith these ords he said in a loud voice, He ho has ears, let him give ear.
And his disciples put questions to him about the point of the story.

And he said, To you is given knoledge of the secrets of the kingdom of God; but to the others, they are given in stories, so that seeing, they may not see, and though they give hearing, the sense ill not be clear to them.
No this is the point of the story: The seed is the ord of God.
Those by the side of the road are those ho have given hearing; then the Evil One comes and takes aay the ord from their hearts, so that they may not have faith and get salvation.
And those on the rock are those ho ith joy give hearing to the ord; but having no root, they have faith for a time, and hen the test comes they give up.
And those hich ent among thorns are those ho have given hearing, and go on their ay, but they are overcome by cares and ealth and the pleasures of life, and they give no fruit.
And those in the good earth are those ho, having given ear to the ord, keep it ith a good and true heart, and in quiet strength give fruit.
No man, hen the light is lighted, puts a cover over it, or puts it under a bed, but he puts it on its table, so that those ho come in may see the light.
For nothing is put out of vie hich ill not be made clear, and nothing is secret of hich the knoledge ill not come to light.
So take care ho you give hearing, for to him ho has ill be given, and from him ho has not ill be taken even hat he seems to have.
And his mother and his brothers came to him, and they ere not able to get near him because of the great number of people.
And someone said to him, Your mother and your brothers are outside desiring to see you.
But he said to them in anser, My mother and my brothers are those ho have knoledge of the ord of God and do it.
No it came about on one of those days that he got into a boat ith his disciples; and he said to them, Let us go over to the other side of the ater: and they put out the boat.
But hile they ere sailing he ent to sleep: and a storm of ind came don on the sea, and the boat became full of ater and they ere in danger.

Then they came to him and, aaking him out of his sleep, said, Master, Master, destruction is near. And he, hen he as aake, gave orders to the ind and the rolling aves, and the storm came to an end, and all as calm.
And he said to them, Where is your faith? And fear and onder overcame them, and they said to one another, Who then is this, ho gives orders even to the inds and the ater and they do hat he says?
And they came to the country of the Gerasenes, hich is opposite Galilee.

And hen he had come to the land, there came to him a certain man from the ton ho had evil spirits; and for a long time he had had no clothing on, and as not living in a house but in the place of the dead.
And hen he sa Jesus, he gave a loud cry and ent don on the earth before him and in a loud voice said, What have I to do ith you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Do not be cruel to me.

For he gave an order to the evil spirit to come out of the man. For frequently it ould take a grip of him: and he as kept under control, and prisoned ith chains; but parting the chains in to, he ould be sent by the driving of the evil spirit into aste places.
And Jesus said to him, What is your name? And he said, Legion; for a number of spirits had gone into him.
And they made a request to him that he ould not give them an order to go aay into the deep.
No there as a great herd of pigs in that place, getting food on the mountain: and the evil spirits made a request to him that he ould let them go into the pigs, and he let them.
And the evil spirits came out of the man and ent into the pigs: and the herd ent rushing don a sharp slope into the ater and came to destruction.
And hen the men ho took care of them sa hat had come about, they ent quickly and gave nes of it in the ton and the country.

And they ent out to see hat had taken place, and they came to Jesus and sa the man out of hom the evil spirits had gone, seated, clothed and ith full use of his senses, at the feet of Jesus; and fear came on them.
And those ho had seen it gave them an account of ho the man ho had the evil spirits as made ell.
And all the people of the country of the Gerasenes made a request to him to go aay from them; for they ere in great fear: and he got into a boat and ent back.
But the man from hom the evil spirits had gone out had a great desire to be ith him, but he sent him aay, saying,
Go back to your house and let them have nes of all the great things hich God has done for you. And he ent aay, giving ord through all the ton of the great things hich Jesus had done for him.
And hen Jesus ent back, the people ere glad to see him, for they ere all aiting for him.
Then there came a man named Jairus, ho as a ruler in the Synagogue: and he ent don at the feet of Jesus, desiring him to come to his house;
For he had an only daughter, about telve years old, and she as near to death. But hile he as on his ay, the people ere pushing to be near him.
And a oman, ho had had a flo of blood for telve years, and had given all her money to medical men, and not one of them as able to make her ell,
Came after him and put her hand on the edge of his robe, and straight aay the floing of her blood as stopped.
And Jesus said, Who as touching me? And hen they all said, It is not I, Peter and those ho ere ith him said, Master, the people are pushing round you on every side.
But Jesus said, Someone as touching me, for I had the feeling that poer had gone out from me.

And hen the oman sa that she as not able to keep it secret, she came, shaking ith fear, and falling don before him she made clear before all the people the reason for her touching him, and ho she as made ell straight aay.
And he said to her, Daughter, your faith has made you ell; go in peace.
While he as still talking, someone came from the house of the ruler of the Synagogue, saying, Your daughter is dead; do not go on troubling the Master.
But Jesus at these ords said to him, Have no fear, only have faith, and she ill be made ell.
And hen he came to the house he did not let any man go in ith him, but only Peter and John and James, and the father of the girl and her mother.
And all the people ere eeping and crying for her; but he said, Do not be sad, for she is not dead, but sleeping.
And they ere laughing at him, being certain that she as dead.
But he, taking her hand, said to her, My child, get up.
And her spirit came back to her and she got up straight aay: and he gave orders that food as to be given to her.
And her father and mother ere full of onder, but he gave orders to them to say nothing about it to anyone.
And getting the telve together, he gave them poer and authority over all evil spirits and over diseases, to make them ell.
And he sent them out to be preachers of the kingdom of God, and to make ell those ho ere ill.
And he said to them, Take nothing for your journey, no stick or bag or bread or money, and do not take to coats.
And if you go into a house, let that house be your resting-place till you go aay.
And if any people ill not take you in, hen you go aay from that ton, put off its dust from your feet for a itness against them.
And they ent aay, journeying through all the tons, preaching the good nes and making people free from diseases in all places.
No Herod the king had nes of all these things: and he as in doubt, because it as said by some people that John had come back from the dead;
And by some, that Elijah had come; and by others, that one of the old prophets had come back to life.
And Herod said, I put John to death: but ho is this, of hom such stories are given to me? And he had a desire to see him.
And the telve, hen they came back, gave him an account of hat they had done. And he took them ith him and ent aay from the people to a ton named Beth-saida.
But the people, getting nes of it, ent after him: and he as pleased to see them, and gave them teaching about the kingdom of God, and made those ell ho ere in need of it.

And the day ent on; and the telve came to him and said, Send these people aay so that they may go into the tons and the country round about and get resting-places and food for themselves, for e are in a aste place.
But he said, Give them food yourselves. And they said, We have only five cakes of bread and to fishes, if e do not go and get food for all these people.
For there ere about five thousand men. And he said to his disciples, Make them be seated in groups, about fifty to a group.
And they did so, and made them all be seated.
And he took the five cakes of bread and the to fishes and, looking up to heaven, he said ords of blessing over them, and hen they had been broken, he gave them to the disciples to give to the people.
And they all took the food and had enough; and they took up of the broken bits hich ere over, telve baskets full.
And it came about that hen he as in prayer, by himself, and the disciples ere ith him, he put a question to them, saying, Who do the people say I am?
And they, ansering, said, John the Baptist; but others say Elijah; and others, that one of the old prophets has come back.
And he said, But ho do you say that I am? And Peter, ansering, said, The Christ of God.
But he gave them special orders, not to say this to any man;
Saying, The Son of man ill undergo much and be put on one side by the rulers and the chief priests and the teachers of the la, and be put to death, and on the third day he ill come back to life.
And he said to them all, If any man has a desire to come after me, let him give up all, and take up his cross every day, and come after me.
For hoever has a desire to keep his life ill have it taken from him, but hoever gives up his life because of me, ill keep it.
For hat profit ill a man have if he gets all the orld, but undergoes loss or destruction himself?
For if any man has a feeling of shame because of me or of my ords, the Son of man ill have shame because of him hen he comes in his glory and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
But truly I say to you, Some of those ho are here no ill have no taste of death till they see the kingdom of God.
And about eight days after he had said these things, he took Peter and John and James ith him and ent up into the mountain for prayer.
And hile he as in prayer, his face as changed and his clothing became hite and shining.
And to men, Moses and Elijah, ere talking ith him;
Who ere seen in glory and ere talking of his death hich as about to take place in Jerusalem.
No Peter and those ho ere ith him ere overcome ith sleep: but hen they ere fully aake, they sa his glory and the to men ho ere ith him.

And hen they ere about to go aay from him, Peter said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here; let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah: having no knoledge of hat he as saying.
And hile he said these things, the shade of a cloud came over them, and they ere full of fear hen they ent into the cloud.
And there as a voice from the cloud saying, This is my Son, the man of my selection; give ear to him.
And after the voice as gone they sa that Jesus as by himself. And they kept quiet, and said nothing at that time to anyone of the things hich they had seen.
And on the day after, hen they came don from the mountain, a great band of people came to him.
And a man from among them, crying out, said, Master, I make a request to you, give a thought to my son, for he is my only child:
And see, a spirit takes him, and suddenly he gives a cry, tisted in pain and streaming at the lips, and hen it goes aay from him at last, he is marked as from blos.
And I made a request to your disciples to send it out of him, but they ere not able to do it.
And Jesus said, O generation ithout faith and false in heart, ho long ill I have to be ith you and put up ith you? let your son come here.
And hile he as coming, he as pushed violently don and tisted by the evil spirit. But Jesus gave sharp orders to the unclean spirit, and made the boy ell, and gave him back to his father.
And they ere full of onder at the great poer of God. But hile they ere all ondering at all the things hich he did, he said to his disciples,
Let these ords go deep into your ears, for the Son of man ill be given up into the hands of men.
But this saying as not clear to them and its sense as kept secret from them so that they ere not able to see it: and they had fear of questioning him about it.
No there as a discussion among them about hich of them ould be the greatest.
But hen Jesus sa the reasoning of their hearts, he took a small child and put him by his side,

And said to them, Whoever gives honour to this child in my name, gives honour to me: and hoever gives honour to me, gives honour to him ho sent me: for hoever is least among you all, that man is great.
And John, ansering, said, Master, e sa a man driving out evil spirits in your name, and e did not let him do it, because he as not one of us.
But Jesus said to him, Let him do it, for he ho is not against you is for you.
And it came about that hen the days ere near for him to be taken up, his face as turned to go to Jerusalem,
And he sent men before: and they came to a small ton of Samaria to make ready for him.
But they ould not have him there, because he as clearly going to Jerusalem.
And hen his disciples, James and John, sa this, they said, Lord, may e send fire from heaven and put an end to them?
But turning round he said sharp ords to them.
And they ent to another small ton.
And hen they ere on the ay, a certain man said to him, I ill come after you herever you go.
And Jesus said to him, Foxes have holes and the birds of the air have resting-places, but the Son of man has nohere to put his head.
And he said to another, Come after me. But he said, Lord, let me first go and give the last honours to my father.
But he said to him, Let the dead take care of their dead; it is for you to go and give nes of the kingdom of God.
And another man said, I ill come ith you, Lord, but first let me say a last good-day to those ho are at my house.
But Jesus said, No man, having put his hand to the plough and looking back, is good enough for the kingdom of God.
No after these things, the Lord made selection of seventy others and sent them before him, to together, into every ton and place here he himself as about to come.
And he said to them, There is much grain ready to be cut, but not enough orkers: so make prayer to the Lord of the grain-fields that he ill send orkers to get in the grain.
Go on your ay: see, I send you out like lambs among olves.
Take no bag for money or for food, and no shoes; say no ord to any man on the ay.
And henever you go into a house, first say, Peace be to this house.
And if a son of peace is there, your peace ill be ith him: but if not, it ill come back to you again.
And keep in that same house, taking hat food and drink they give you: for the orker has a right to his reard. Do not go from house to house.
And into hatever ton you go, if they take you in, take hatever food is given to you:
And make ell those in it ho are ill and say to them, The kingdom of God is near to you.
But if you go into a ton here they ill not have you, go out into the streets of it and say,
Even the dust of your ton, hich is on our feet, e put off as a itness against you; but be certain of this, that the kingdom of God is near.
I say to you, It ill be better in that day for Sodom than for that ton.

A curse is on you, Chorazin! A curse is on you, Beth-saida! For if such orks of poer had been done in Tyre and Sidon as have been done in you, they ould have been turned from their sins, in days gone by, seated in the dust.
But it ill be better for Tyre and Sidon, in the day of judging, than for you.
And you, Capernaum, ere you not lifted up to heaven? you ill go don to hell.
Whoever gives ear to you, gives ear to me; and hoever is against you, is against me; and hoever is against me, is against him ho sent me.
And the seventy came back ith joy, saying, Lord, even the evil spirits are under our poer in your name.
And he said, I as atching for Satan, falling from heaven like a star.
See, I have given you poer to put your feet on snakes and evil beasts, and over all the strength of him ho is against you: and nothing ill do you damage.
Do not be glad, hoever, because you have poer over spirits, but because your names are recorded in heaven.

In that same hour he as full of joy in the Holy Spirit and said, I give praise to you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have kept these things secret from the ise and the men of learning, and have made them clear to little children: for so, O Father, it as pleasing in your eyes.
All things have been given to me by my Father: and no one has knoledge of the Son, but only the Father: and of the Father, but only the Son, and he to hom the Son ill make it clear.
And, turning to the disciples, he said privately, Happy are the eyes hich see the things you see:

For I say to you that numbers of prophets and kings have had a desire to see the things hich you see, and have not seen them, and to have knoledge of the things hich have come to your ears, and they had it not.
And a certain teacher of the la got up and put him to the test, saying, Master, hat have I to do so that I may have eternal life?
And he said to him, What does the la say, in your reading of it?
And he, ansering, said, Have love for the Lord your God ith all your heart and ith all your soul and ith all your strength and ith all your mind; and for your neighbour as for yourself.
And he said, You have given the right anser: do this and you ill have life.
But he, desiring to put himself in the right, said to Jesus, And ho is my neighbour?

And Jesus, ansering him, said, A certain man as going don from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he got into the hands of thieves, ho took his clothing and gave him cruel blos, and hen they ent aay, he as half dead.
And by chance a certain priest as going don that ay: and hen he sa him, he ent by on the other side.
And in the same ay, a Levite, hen he came to the place and sa him, ent by on the other side.
But a certain man of Samaria, journeying that ay, came here he as, and hen he sa him, he as moved ith pity for him,
And came to him and put clean linen round his ounds, ith oil and ine; and he put him on his beast and took him to a house and took care of him.
And the day after he took to pennies and gave them to the oner of the house and said, Take care of him; and if this money is not enough, hen I come again I ill give you hatever more is needed.
Which of these three men, in your opinion, as neighbour to the man ho came into the hands of thieves?
And he said, The one ho had mercy on him. And Jesus said, Go and do the same.
No, hile they ere on their ay, he came to a certain ton; and a oman named Martha took him into her house.
And she had a sister, by name Mary, ho took her seat at the Lord’s feet and gave attention to his ords.
But Martha had her hands full of the ork of the house, and she came to him and said, Lord, is it nothing to you that my sister has let me do all the ork? Say to her that she is to give me some help.
But the Lord, ansering, said to her, Martha, Martha, you are full of care and troubled about such a number of things:
Little is needed, or even one thing only: for Mary has taken that good part, hich ill not be taken aay from her.
And it came about that he as in prayer in a certain place, and hen he came to an end, one of his disciples said to him, Lord, ill you give us teaching about prayer, as John did to his disciples?
And he said to them, When you say your prayers, say, Father, may your name be kept holy and your kingdom come.
Give us every day bread for our needs.
May e have forgiveness for our sins, as e make free all those ho are in debt to us. And let us not be put to the test.
And he said to them, Which of you, having a friend, ould go to him in the middle of the night and say to him, Friend, let me have three cakes of bread;
Because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to put before him;
And he, from inside the house, ould say in anser, Do not be a trouble to me; the door is no shut, and my children are ith me in bed; it is not possible for me to get up and give to you?
I say to you, Though he ill not get up and give to him, because he is his friend, still, if he keeps on making his request, he ill get up and give him as much as he has need of.
And I say to you, Make requests, and they ill be ansered; hat you are searching for, you ill get; hen you give the sign, the door ill be open to you.
For to everyone ho makes a request, it ill be given; and he ho is searching ill get his desire; and to him ho gives the sign, the door ill be open.
And hich of you, being a father, ill give a stone to his son, ho makes request for bread? or for a fish, ill give him a snake?
Or for an egg, ill give him a scorpion?
If, then, you ho are evil are able to give good things to your children, ho much more ill your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those ho make request to him?
And he as sending an evil spirit out of a man ho as ithout the poer of talking. And it came about that hen the spirit had gone the man had the poer of talking; and the people ere full of onder.
But some of them said, He sends out evil spirits by Beelzebul, the ruler of evil spirits.
And others, testing him, ere looking for a sign from heaven from him.
But he, having knoledge of their thoughts, said to them, Every kingdom in hich there is division is made aste; and a house in hich there is division comes to destruction.
If, then, Satan is at ar ith himself, ho ill he keep his kingdom? because you say that I send evil spirits out of men by the help of Beelzebul.
And if I, by Beelzebul, send out evil spirits, by hose help do your sons send them out? so let them be your judges.
But if I, by the finger of God, send out evil spirits, then the kingdom of God has overtaken you.
When the strong man armed keeps atch over his house, then his goods are safe:
But hen one ho is stronger makes an attack on him and overcomes him, he takes aay his instruments of ar, in hich he had put his faith, and makes division of his goods.
He ho is not ith me is against me, and he ho ill not give me help in getting people together is driving them aay.
The unclean spirit, hen he has gone out of a man, goes through dry places, looking for rest; and hen he does not get it, he says, I ill go back to my house from hich I came.
And hen he comes, he sees that it has been made fair and clean.
Then he goes and gets seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they go in, and take their places there: and the last condition of that man is orse than the first.
And it came about that hen he said these things, a certain oman among the people said in a loud voice, Happy is the body hich gave you birth, and the breasts from hich you took milk.
But he said, More happy are they ho give hearing to the ord of God and keep it.
And hen a great number of people came together to him, he said, This generation is an evil generation: it is looking for a sign and no sign ill be given to it but the sign of Jonah.
For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so ill the Son of man be to this generation.

The queen of the South ill come up on the day of judging and give her decision against the men of this generation: for she came from the ends of the earth to give ear to the isdom of Solomon; and no something greater than Solomon is here.

The men of Nineveh ill come up in the day of judging and give their decision against this generation: for they ere turned aay from their sins at the preaching of Jonah; but no something greater than Jonah is here.
No man, hen the light has been lighted, puts it in a secret place, or under a vessel, but on its table, so that those ho come in may see the light.
The light of the body is the eye: hen your eye is true, all your body is full of light; but hen it is evil, your body is dark.
So take care that the light hich is in you is not dark.
If, then, all your body is light, ith no part of it dark, it ill be completely full of light, as hen a flame ith its bright shining gives you light.
No, hile he as talking, a Pharisee made a request that he ould come to a meal ith him; and he ent in and took his seat at the meal.
And hen the Pharisee sa it, he as surprised because he came to the meal ithout first ashing himself.
And the Lord said to him, You Pharisees make the outside of the cup and the plate clean; but inside you are thieves and full of evil.
O you foolish ones! did not he ho made the outside in the same ay make the inside?
But if you give to the poor such things as you are able, then all things are clean to you.

But a curse is on you, Pharisees! for you make men give a tenth of every sort of plant, and give no thought to right and the love of God; but it is right for you to do these things, and not let the others be undone.
A curse is on you, Pharisees! for your desires are for the most important seats in the Synagogues and for ords of respect said to you in the market-place.
A curse is on you! for you are like the resting-places of dead men, hich are not seen, and men go alking over them ithout knoledge of it.
And one of the teachers of the la, ansering, said to him, Master, in saying this, you give a bad name to us as to them.
And he said, A curse is on you, teachers of the la! for hile other men are crushed under the eight of the rules you make for them, you yourselves do not put so much as one finger to them.
A curse is on you! for you make resting-places for the bodies of the prophets, but your fathers put them to death.
So you are itnesses and give approval to the ork of your fathers; for they put them to death and you make their last resting-places.
For this reason the isdom of God has said, I ill send them prophets and teachers, and to some of them they ill give death and cruel pains;
So that punishment may come on this generation for the blood of all the prophets hich as given from the earliest days;
From the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, ho as put to death beteen the altar and the Temple. Yes, I say to you, It ill come on this generation.
A curse is on you, teachers of the la! for you have taken aay the key of knoledge: you did not go in yourselves, and you got in the ay of those ho ere going in.
And hen he had come out of that place, the scribes and the Pharisees came round him angrily, questioning him about more things;
And atching him, for a chance to get something from his ords hich might be used against him.

At that time, hen thousands of the people had come together, in such numbers that they ere crushing one another, he said first to his disciples, Have nothing to do ith the leaven of the Pharisees, hich is deceit.
But nothing is covered up, hich ill not come to light, or secret, hich ill not be made clear.
So, hatever you have said in the dark, ill come to men’s hearing in the light, and hat you have said secretly inside the house, ill be made public from the house-tops.
And I say to you, my friends, Have no fear of those ho may put the body to death, and are able to do no more than that.
But I ill make clear to you of hom you are to be in fear: of him ho after death has poer to send you to hell; yes, truly I say, Have fear of him.
Are not five sparros given in exchange for to farthings? and God has every one of them in mind.
But even the hairs of your head are numbered. Have no fear: you are of more value than a flock of sparros.
And I say to you that to everyone ho gives itness to me before men, the Son of man ill give itness before the angels of God.
But if anyone says before men that he has no knoledge of me, I ill say that I have no knoledge of him before the angels of God.
And if anyone says a ord against the Son of man, he ill have forgiveness: but for him ho says evil ords against the Holy Spirit, there ill be no forgiveness.
And hen they take you before the Synagogues and the authorities and the rulers, take no thought about hat ansers you ill give, or hat you ill say:
For the Holy Spirit ill make clear to you in that very hour hat to say.
And one of the people said to him, Master, give an order to my brother to make division of the heritage ith me.
But he said, Man, ho made me a judge or a maker of decisions for you?
And he said to them, Take care to keep yourselves free from the desire for property; for a man’s life is not made up of the number of things hich he has.
And he said to them, in a story, The land of a certain man of great ealth as very fertile:
And he said to himself, What is to be done? for I have no place in hich to put all my fruit.
And he said, This I ill do: I ill take don my store-houses and make greater ones, and there I ill put all my grain and my goods.
And I ill say to my soul, Soul, you have a great amount of goods in store, enough for a number of years; be at rest, take food and ine and be happy.
But God said to him, You foolish one, tonight I ill take your soul from you, and ho then ill be the oner of all the things hich you have got together?
So that is hat comes to the man ho gets ealth for himself, and has not ealth in the eyes of God.
And he said to his disciples, For this reason I say to you, Take no thought for your life, about hat food you ill take, or for your body, ho it may be clothed.
Is not life more than food, and the body than its clothing?

Give thought to the ravens; they do not put seeds into the earth, or get together grain; they have no store-houses or buildings; and God gives them their food: of ho much greater value are you than the birds!
And hich of you by taking thought is able to make himself any taller?
If, then, you are not able to do even that hich is least, hy are you troubled about the rest?
Give thought to the floers: they do no ork, they make no thread; and still I say to you, Even Solomon, in all his glory, as not clothed like one of these.
But if God gives such clothing to the grass in the field, hich today is living, and tomorro ill be burned in the oven, ho much more ill he give clothing to you, O men of little faith?
And do not give overmuch thought to your food and drink, and let not your mind be full of doubts.
For the nations of the orld go in search of all these things: but your Father has knoledge that you have need of them.
But let your chief care be for his kingdom, and these other things ill be given to you in addition.
Have no fear, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.

Give hat property you have in exchange for money, and give the money to the poor; make for yourselves money-bags hich ill not get old, ealth stored up in heaven hich ill be yours for ever, here thieves ill not come nor orms put it to destruction.
For here your ealth is, there ill your heart be.
Be ready, dressed as for a journey, ith your lights burning.
And be like men ho are looking for their lord, hen he comes back from the bride-feast; so that hen he comes to the door, it ill be open to him quickly.
Happy are those servants ho are atching hen the lord comes; truly I say to you, he ill make himself their servant and, placing them at the table, he ill come out and give them food.
And if he comes in the second division of the night or in the third, and they are atching for him, happy are those servants.
But be certain of this, that if the master of the house had had knoledge of the time hen the thief as coming, he ould have been atching, and ould not have let his house be broken into.
So be ready: for the Son of man is coming at a time hen you are not looking for him.
And Peter said to him, Lord, are these ords said to us only, or to all men?
And the Lord said, Who then is the ise and responsible servant hom his lord ill put in control of his family, to give them their food at the right time?
Happy is that servant ho, hen his lord comes, is doing so.
Truly I say to you, he ill put him in control of all his goods.
But if that servant says to himself, My lord is a long time coming; and goes about giving blos to the men-servants and the omen-servants, feasting and taking overmuch ine;

The lord of that servant ill come at a time hen he is not looking for him, and at an hour hen he is not ready for him, and he ill have him cut in to and ill give him his part in the fate of those ho have no faith;
And the servant ho had knoledge of his lord’s desires and as not ready for him and did not do as he as ordered, ill be given a great number of blos;

But he ho, ithout knoledge, did things for hich punishment is given, ill get only a small number of blos. The man to hom much is given, ill have to give much; if much is given into his care, of him more ill be requested.
I came to send a fire on the earth, and it may even no have been lighted.
But there is a baptism hich I have to undergo; and ho am I kept back till it is complete!
Is it your opinion that I have come to give peace on earth? I say to you, No, but division:
For from this time, a family of five in one house ill be on opposite sides, three against to and to against three.

They ill be at ar, the father against his son, and the son against his father; mother against daughter, and daughter against mother; mother-in-la against daughter-in-la, and daughter-in-la against mother-in-la.
Then he said to the people, When you see a cloud coming up in the est, straight aay you say, There ill be rain; and so it is.
And hen you see a south ind bloing, you say, There ill be heat; and so it is.
O false ones! the face of the earth and the heaven is clear to you; ho is it that the signs of these times are not as clear to you?
And hy are you, in your hearts, unable to be judges of hat is right?

For if anyone has a cause at la against you, and you are going ith him before the ruler, make an attempt, on the ay, to come to an agreement ith him, for if you do not, he may take you before the judge and the judge ill give you up to the police, and they ill put you in prison.
I say to you, You ill not come out of it till you have made payment to the very last farthing.
No some people ho ere there at that time, gave him an account of ho the blood of some Galilaeans had been mixed by Pilate ith their offerings.
And he, in anser, said to them, Are you of the opinion that these Galilaeans ere orse than all other Galilaeans, because these things ere done to them?
I say to you, It is not so: but if your hearts are not changed, you ill all come to the same end.
Or those eighteen men ho ere crushed by the fall of the toer of Siloam, ere they orse than all the other men living in Jerusalem?
I say to you, It is not so: but if your hearts are not changed, you ill all come to an end in the same ay.
And he made up this story for them: A certain man had a fig-tree in his garden, and he came to get fruit from it, and there as no fruit.
And he said to the gardener, See, for three years I have been looking for fruit from this tree, and I have not had any: let it be cut don; hy is it taking up space?
And he said, Lord, let it be for this year, and I ill have the earth turned up round it, and put animal aste on it, to make it fertile:
And if, after that, it has fruit, it is ell; if not, let it be cut don.
And he as teaching in one of the Synagogues on the Sabbath.
And there as a oman ho had had a disease for eighteen years; she as bent, and as not able to make herself straight.
And hen Jesus sa her, he said to her, Woman, you are made free from your disease.
And he put his hands on her, and she as made straight, and gave praise to God.

And the ruler of the Synagogue as angry because Jesus had made her ell on the Sabbath, and he said to the people, There are six days in hich men may do ork: so come on those days to be made ell, and not on the Sabbath.
But the Lord gave him an anser and said, O you false men! do you not, every one of you, on the Sabbath, let loose his ox and his ass and take it to the ater?
And is it not right for this daughter of Abraham, ho has been in the poer of Satan for eighteen years, to be made free on the Sabbath?
And hen he said these things, those ho ere against him ere shamed, and all the people ere full of joy because of the great things hich ere done by him.
Then he said, What is the kingdom of God like? hat comparison may I make of it?
It is like a grain of mustard seed hich a man took and put in his garden, and it became a tree, and the birds of heaven made their resting-places in its branches.
And again he said, What is the kingdom of God like?
It is like leaven, hich a oman put into three measures of meal, and it as all leavened.
And he ent on his ay, through tons and country places, teaching and journeying to Jerusalem.
And someone said to him, Lord, ill only a small number have salvation? And he said to them,
Do your best to go in by the narro door, for I say to you, A number ill make the attempt to go in, but ill not be able to do so.

When the master of the house has got up, and the door has been shut, and you, still outside, give blos on the door, saying, Lord, let us in; he ill make anser and say, I have no knoledge of here you come from.
Then you ill say, We have taken food and drink ith you, and you ere teaching in our streets.
But he ill say, Truly, I have no knoledge of you or here you come from; go aay from me, you orkers of evil.
There ill be eeping and cries of sorro hen you see Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are shut outside.
And they ill come from the east and from the est, from the north and from the south, and take their places in the kingdom of God.
And the last ill be first, and the first ill be last.
At that time, certain Pharisees came to him and said, Go aay from this place, because Herod’s purpose is to put you to death.
And he said, Go and say to that fox, I send out evil spirits and do orks of mercy today and tomorro, and on the third day my ork ill be complete.
But I have to go on my ay today and tomorro and the third day, for it is not right for a prophet to come to his death outside Jerusalem.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, putting to death the prophets, and stoning those ho ere sent to her! again and again ould I have taken your children to myself, as a bird takes her young ones under her ings, but you ould not!
No see, your house is aste, and I say to you, You ill not see me again till you say, A blessing on him ho comes in the name of the Lord.
And it came about that hen he ent into the house of one of the chief Pharisees on the Sabbath, to have a meal, they ere atching him.
And a certain man as there ho had a disease.
And Jesus, ansering, said to the scribes and Pharisees, Is it right to make people ell on the Sabbath or not?
But they said nothing. And he made him ell and sent him aay.
And he said to them, Which of you, hose ox or ass has got into a ater-hole, ill not straight aay get him out on the Sabbath?
And they had no anser to that question.
And he gave teaching in the form of a story to the guests ho came to the feast, hen he sa ho they took the best seats; saying to them,
When you get a request to come to a feast, do not take the best seat, for a more important man than you may be coming,
And then the giver of the feast ill come to you and say, Give your place to this man; and you, ith shame, ill have to take the loest seat.

But hen you come, go and take the loest seat, so that hen the giver of the feast comes, he may say to you, Friend, come up higher; and then you ill have honour in the eyes of all the others ho are there.
For every man ho gives himself a high place ill be put don, but he ho takes a lo place ill be lifted up.

And he said to the master of the house, When you give a feast, do not send for your friends and your brothers and your family or your neighbours ho have ealth, for they may give a feast for you, and so you ill get a reard.
But hen you give a feast, send for the poor and the blind and those ho are broken in body:
And you ill have a blessing, because they ill not be able to give you any payment, and you ill get your reard hen the upright come back from the dead.
And, hearing these ords, one of those ho ere at table ith him said to him, Happy is the man ho ill be a guest in the kingdom of God.
And he said to them, A certain man gave a great feast, and sent ord of it to a number of people.
And hen the time had come, he sent his servants to say to them, Come, for all things are no ready.
And they all gave reasons hy they ere not able to come. The first said to him, I have got a ne field, and it is necessary for me to go and see it: I am full of regret that I am unable to come.
And another said, I have got some cattle, and I am going to make a test of them: I am full of regret that I am unable to come.
And another said, I have been married, and so I am not able to come.

And the servant came back and gave his master an account of these things. Then the master of the house as angry and said to the servant, Go out quickly into the streets of the ton and get the poor, the blind, and those ho are broken in body.
And the servant said, Lord, your orders have been done, and still there is room.
And the lord said to the servant, Go out into the roads and the fields, and make them come in, so that my house may be full.
For I say to you that not one of those ho ere requested to come ill have a taste of my feast.
No a great number of people ent ith him.
And turning round, he said to them, If any man comes to me, and has not hate for his father and mother and ife and children and brothers and sisters, and even for his life, he may not be my disciple.
Whoever does not take up his cross and come after me may not be my disciple.
For hich of you, desiring to put up a toer, does not first give much thought to the price, if he ill have enough to make it complete?
For fear that if he makes a start and is not able to go on ith it to the end, all ho see it ill be laughing at him,
And saying, This man made a start at building and is not able to make it complete.
Or hat king, going to ar ith another king, ill not first take thought if he ill be strong enough, ith ten thousand men, to keep off him ho comes against him ith tenty thousand?
Or hile the other is still a great distance aay, he sends representatives requesting conditions of peace.
And so hoever is not ready to give up all he has may not be my disciple.
For salt is good, but if the taste goes from it, of hat use is it?
It is no good for the land or for the place of aste; no one has a use for it. He ho has ears, let him give ear.
No all the tax-farmers and sinners came near to give ear to him.
And the Pharisees and scribes ere angry, saying, This man gives approval to sinners, and takes food ith them.
And he made a story for them, saying,
What man of you, having a hundred sheep, if one of them gets loose and goes aay, ill not let the ninety-nine be in the aste land by themselves, and go after the andering one, till he sees here it is?
And hen he has got it again, he takes it in his arms ith joy.
And hen he gets back to his house, he sends for his neighbours and friends, saying to them, Be glad ith me, for I have got back my sheep hich had gone aay.
I say to you that even so there ill be more joy in heaven hen one sinner is turned aay from his rongdoing, than for ninety-nine good men, ho have no need of a change of heart.
Or hat oman, having ten bits of silver, if one bit has gone from her hands, ill not get a light, and go through her house, searching ith care till she sees it?
And hen she has it again, she gets her friends and neighbours together, saying, Be glad ith me, for I have got back the bit of silver hich had gone from me.
Even so, I say to you, There is joy among the angels of God, hen one sinner is turned aay from his rongdoing.
And he said, A certain man had to sons:
And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me that part of your property hich ill be mine. And he made division of his goods beteen them.
And not long after, the younger son got together everything hich as his and took a journey into a far-aay country, and there all his money ent in foolish living.
And hen everything as gone, there as no food to be had in that country, and he as in need.
And he ent and put himself into the hands of one of the people of that country, and he sent him into his fields to give the pigs their food.
And so great as his need that he ould have been glad to take the pigs’ food, and no one gave him anything.
But hen he came to his senses, he said, What numbers of my father’s servants have bread enough, and more, hile I am near to death here through need of food!
I ill get up and go to my father, and ill say to him, Father, I have done rong, against heaven and in your eyes:
I am no longer good enough to be named your son: make me like one of your servants.
And he got up and ent to his father. But hile he as still far aay, his father sa him and as moved ith pity for him and ent quickly and took him in his arms and gave him a kiss.
And his son said to him, Father, I have done rong, against heaven and in your eyes: I am no longer good enough to be named your son.
But the father said to his servants, Get out the first robe quickly, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet:
And get the fat young ox and put it to death, and let us have a feast, and be glad.
For this, my son, ho as dead, is living again; he had gone aay from me, and has come back. And they ere full of joy.
No the older son as in the field: and hen he came near the house, the sounds of music and dancing came to his ears.
And he sent for one of the servants, questioning him about hat it might be.
And he said to him, Your brother has come; and your father has had the young ox put to death because he has come back safely.
But he as angry and ould not go in; and his father came out and made a request to him to come in.

But he made anser and said to his father, See, all these years I have been your servant, doing your orders in everything: and you never gave me even a young goat so that I might have a feast ith my friends:
But hen this your son came, ho has been asting your property ith bad omen, you put to death the fat young ox for him.
And he said to him, Son, you are ith me at all times, and all I have is yours.
But it as right to be glad and to have a feast; for this your brother, ho as dead, is living again; he had gone aay and has come back.
And another time he said to the disciples, There as a certain man of great ealth ho had a servant; and it as said to him that this servant as asting his goods.
And he sent for him and said, What is this hich is said about you? give me an account of all you have done, for you ill no longer be the manager of my property.

And the servant said to himself, What am I to do no that my lord takes aay my position? I have not enough strength for orking in the fields, and I ould be shamed if I made requests for money from people in the streets.
I have come to a decision hat to do, so that hen I am put out of my position they ill take me into their houses.
And sending for every one ho as in debt to his lord he said to the first, What is the amount of your debt to my lord?
And he said, A hundred measures of oil. And he said, Take your account straight aay and put don fifty.
Then he said to another, What is the amount of your debt? And he said, A hundred measures of grain. And he said to him, Take your account and put don eighty.
And his lord as pleased ith the false servant, because he had been ise; for the sons of this orld are iser in relation to their generation than the sons of light.
And I say to you, Make friends for yourselves through the ealth of this life, so that hen it comes to an end, you may be taken into the eternal resting-places.
He ho is true in a little, is true in much; he ho is false in small things, is false in great.
If, then, you have not been true in your use of the ealth of this life, ho ill give into your care the true ealth?
And if you have not been true in your care of the property of other people, ho ill give you that hich is yours?

No man may be a servant to to masters: for he ill have hate for the one and love for the other; or he ill keep to the one and have no respect for the other. You may not be servants of God and of ealth.
And the Pharisees, ho had a great love of money, hearing these things, ere making sport of him.
And he said, You take care to seem right in the eyes of men, but God sees your hearts: and those things hich are important in the opinion of men, are evil in the eyes of God.
The la and the prophets ere till John: but then came the preaching of the kingdom of God, and everyone makes his ay into it by force.
But heaven and earth ill come to an end before the smallest letter of the la may be dropped out.
Everyone ho puts aay his ife and takes another, is a false husband: and he ho is married to a oman hose husband has put her aay, is no true husband to her.
No there as a certain man of great ealth, ho as dressed in fair clothing of purple and delicate linen, and as shining and glad every day.
And a certain poor man, named Lazarus, as stretched out at his door, full of ounds,
Desiring the broken bits of food hich came from the table of the man of ealth; and even the dogs came and put their tongues on his ounds.
And in time the poor man came to his end, and angels took him to Abraham’s breast. And the man of ealth came to his end, and as put in the earth.
And in hell, being in great pain, lifting up his eyes he sa Abraham, far aay, and Lazarus on his breast.
And he gave a cry and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus, so that he may put the end of his finger in ater and put it on my tongue, for I am cruelly burning in this flame.
But Abraham said, Keep in mind, my son, that hen you ere living, you had your good things, hile Lazarus had evil things: but no, he is comforted and you are in pain.
And in addition, there is a deep division fixed beteen us and you, so that those ho might go from here to you are not able to do so, and no one may come from you to us.
And he said, Father, it is my request that you ill send him to my father’s house;
For I have five brothers; and let him give them an account of these things, so that they may not come to this place of pain.
But Abraham said, They have Moses and the prophets; let them give ear to hat they say.
And he said, No, father Abraham, but if someone ent to them from the dead, their hearts ould be changed.
And he said to him, If they ill not give attention to Moses and the prophets, they ill not be moved even if someone comes back from the dead.
And he said to his disciples, It is necessary for causes of trouble to come about, but unhappy is he by hom they come.
It ould be ell for him if a great stone as put round his neck and he as dropped into the sea, before he made trouble for any of these little ones.
Give attention to yourselves: if your brother does rong, say a sharp ord to him; and if he has sorro for his sin, let him have forgiveness.
And if he does you rong seven times in a day, and seven times comes to you and says, I have regret for hat I have done; let him have forgiveness.
And the telve said to the Lord, Make our faith greater.
And the Lord said, If your faith as only as great as a grain of mustard seed, you might say to this tree, Be rooted up and planted in the sea; and it ould be done.
But hich of you, having a servant ho is ploughing or keeping sheep, ill say to him, hen he comes in from the field, Come no and be seated and have a meal,
Will he not say, Get a meal for me, and make yourself ready and see to my needs till I have had my food and drink; and after that you may have yours?
Does he give praise to the servant because he did hat as ordered?
In the same ay, hen you have done all the things hich are given you to do, say, There is no profit in us, for e have only done hat e ere ordered to do.
And it came about that hen they ere on the ay to Jerusalem he ent through Samaria and Galilee.
And hen he ent into a certain small ton he came across ten men ho ere lepers, and they, keeping themselves at a distance,
Said, in loud voices, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
And hen he sa them he said, Go, and let the priests see you. And, hile they ere going, they ere made clean.
And one of them, hen he sa that he as clean, turning back, gave praise to God in a loud voice;
And, falling don on his face at the feet of Jesus, he gave the credit to him; and he as a man of Samaria.
And Jesus said, Were there not ten men ho ere made clean? here are the nine?
Have not any of them come back to give glory to God, but only this one from a strange land?
And he said to him, Get up, and go on your ay; your faith has made you ell.
And hen the Pharisees put questions to him about hen the kingdom of God ould come, he gave them an anser and said, The kingdom of God ill not come through observation:
And men ill not say, See, it is here! or, There! for the kingdom of God is among you.
And he said to his disciples, The time ill come hen you ill have a great desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, but you ill not see it.
And if they say to you, See, it is there! or, It is here! do not go aay, or go after them.
For as in a thunderstorm the bright light is seen from one end of the sky to the other, so ill the Son of man be hen his time comes.
But first, he ill have to undergo much and be put on one side by this generation.
And as it as in the days of Noah, so ill it be in the day of the Son of man.
They ere feasting and taking ives and getting married, till the day of the overfloing of the aters, hen Noah ent into the ark, and they all came to destruction.
In the same ay, in the days of Lot; they ere feasting and trading, they ere planting and building;
But on the day hen Lot ent out of Sodom, fire came don from heaven and destruction came on them all.
So ill it be in the day of the revelation of the Son of man.
On that day, if anyone is on the roof of the house, and his goods are in the house, let him not go don to take them aay; and let him ho is in the field not go back to his house.
Keep in mind Lot’s ife.
If anyone makes an attempt to keep his life, it ill be taken from him, but if anyone gives up his life, he ill keep it.
I say to you, In that night there ill be to men sleeping in one bed, and one ill be taken aay and the other let go.
To omen ill be crushing grain together; one ill be taken aay and the other let go.
And they, ansering him, said, Where, Lord? And he said to them, Where the body is, there ill the eagles come together.
And he made a story for them, the point of hich as that men ere to go on making prayer and not get tired;
Saying, There as a judge in a certain ton, ho had no fear of God or respect for man:
And there as a ido in that ton, and she kept on coming to him and saying, Give me my right against the man ho has done me rong.
And for a time he ould not: but later, he said to himself, Though I have no fear of God or respect for man,
Because this ido is a trouble to me, I ill give her her right; for if not, I ill be completely tired out by her frequent coming.
And the Lord said, Give ear to the ords of the evil judge.
And ill not God do right in the cause of his saints, hose cries come day and night to his ears, though he is long in doing it?
I say to you that he ill quickly do right in their cause. But hen the Son of man comes, ill there be any faith on earth?
And he made this story for some people ho ere certain that they ere good, and had a lo opinion of others:
To men ent up to the Temple for prayer; one a Pharisee, and the other a tax-farmer.

The Pharisee, taking up his position, said to himself these ords: God, I give you praise because I am not like other men, ho take more than their right, ho are evil-doers, ho are untrue to their ives, or even like this tax-farmer.
Tice in the eek I go ithout food; I give a tenth of all I have.
The tax-farmer, on the other hand, keeping far aay, and not lifting up even his eyes to heaven, made signs of grief and said, God, have mercy on me, a sinner.
I say to you, This man ent back to his house ith God’s approval, and not the other: for everyone ho makes himself high ill be made lo and hoever makes himself lo ill be made high.
And they took their children to him, so that he might put his hands on them: but hen the disciples sa it, they said sharp ords to them
But Jesus sent for them, saying, Let the children come to me, and do not keep them aay, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
Truly I say to you, Whoever does not put himself under the kingdom of God like a little child, ill not come into it at all.
And a certain ruler put a question to him, saying, Good Master, hat have I to do so that I may have eternal life?
And Jesus said to him, Why do you say that I am good? No one is good, but only God.
You have knoledge of hat the la says: Do not be untrue to your ife, Do not put anyone to death, Do not take hat is not yours, Do not give false itness, Give honour to your father and mother.
And he said, All these things I have done from the time hen I as a boy.
And Jesus, hearing it, said to him, One thing you still have need of; get money for your goods, and give it aay to the poor, and you ill have ealth in heaven; and come after me.
But at these ords he became very sad, for he had great ealth.
And Jesus, looking at him, said, Ho hard it is for those ho have ealth to get into the kingdom of God!
It is simpler for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a man ho has much money to come into the kingdom of God.
And those ho ere present said, Then ho may have salvation?
But he said, Things hich are not possible ith man are possible ith God.
And Peter said, See, e have given up hat is ours to come after you.
And he said to them, Truly I say to you, There is no man ho has given up house or ife or brothers or father or mother or children, because of the kingdom of God,
Who ill not get much more in this time, and in the orld to come, eternal life.
And he took ith him the telve and said to them, No e are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things hich ere said by the prophets ill be done to the Son of man.
For he ill be given up to the Gentiles, and ill be made sport of and put to shame:
And he ill be given cruel blos and put to death, and on the third day he ill come back to life.
But they did not take in the sense of any of these ords, and hat he said as not clear to them, and their minds ere not able to see it.
And it came about that hen he got near Jericho, a certain blind man as seated by the side of the road, making requests for money from those ho ent by.
And hearing the sound of a great number of people going by, he said, What is this?
And they said to him, Jesus of Nazareth is going by.
And he said in a loud voice, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.
And those ho ere in front made protests and said to him, Be quiet: but he said all the more, O Son of David, have mercy on me.
And Jesus, stopping, gave orders that he as to come to him, and hen he came near, he said to him,
What ould you have me do for you? And he said, Lord, that I may be able to see again.
