And Jesus said, See again: your faith has made you ell.
And straight aay he as able to see, and he ent after him, giving glory to God; and all the people hen they sa it gave praise to God.
And he ent into Jericho, and hen he as going through it,
A man, named Zacchaeus, ho as the chief tax-farmer, and a man of ealth,
Made an attempt to get a vie of Jesus, and as not able to do so, because of the people, for he as a small man.
And he ent quickly in front of them and got up into a tree to see him, for he as going that ay.
And hen Jesus came to the place, looking up, he said to him, Zacchaeus, be quick and come don, for I am coming to your house today.
And he came don quickly, and took him into his house ith joy.
And hen they sa it, they ere all angry, saying, He has gone into the house of a sinner.
And Zacchaeus, aiting before him, said to the Lord, See, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from anyone rongly, I give him back four times as much.
And Jesus said to him, Today salvation has come to this house, for even he is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of man came to make search for those ho are andering from the ay, and to be their Saviour.
And hile they ere giving ear to these ords, he made another story for them, because he as near Jerusalem, and because they ere of the opinion that the kingdom of God as coming straight aay.
So he said, A certain man of high birth ent into a far-aay country to get a kingdom for himself, and to come back.
And he sent for ten of his servants and gave them ten pounds and said to them, Do business ith this till I come.
But his people had no love for him, and sent representatives after him, saying, We ill not have this man for our ruler.
And hen he came back again, having got his kingdom, he gave orders for those servants to hom he had given the money to come to him, so that he might have an account of hat business they had done.
And the first came before him, saying, Lord, your pound has made ten pounds.
And he said to him, You have done ell, O good servant: because you have done ell in a small thing you ill have authority over ten tons.
And another came, saying, Your pound has made five pounds.
And he said, You ill be ruler over five tons.
And another came, saying, Lord, here is your pound, hich I put aay in a cloth;
Because I as in fear of you, for you are a hard man: you take up hat you have not put don, and get in grain here you have not put seed.
He said to him, By the ords of your mouth you ill be judged, you bad servant. You had knoledge that I am a hard man, taking up hat I have not put don and getting in grain here I have not put seed;
Why then did you not put my money in a bank, so that hen I came I ould get it back ith interest?
And he said to the others ho ere near, Take the pound aay from him, and give it to the man ho has ten.
And they say to him, Lord, he has ten pounds.
And I say to you that to everyone ho has, more ill be given, but from him ho has not, even hat he has ill be taken aay.
And as for those ho ere against me, ho ould not have me for their ruler, let them come here, and be put to death before me.
And hen he had said this, he ent on in front of them, going up to Jerusalem.
And it came about that hen he got near Beth-phage and Bethany by the mountain hich is named the Mountain of Olives, he sent to of the disciples,
Saying, Go into the little ton in front of you, and on going in you ill see a young ass fixed ith a cord, on hich no man has ever been seated; let him loose and take him.
And if anyone says to you, Why are you taking him? say, The Lord has need of him.
And those hom he sent ent aay, and it as as he said.
And hen they ere getting the young ass, the oners of it said to them, Why are you taking the young ass?
And they said, The Lord has need of him.
And they took him to Jesus, and they put their clothing on the ass, and Jesus got on to him.
And hile he ent on his ay they put their clothing don on the road in front of him.
And hen he came near the foot of the Mountain of Olives, all the disciples ith loud voices gave praise to God ith joy, because of all the great orks hich they had seen;
Saying, A blessing on the King ho comes in the name of the Lord; peace in heaven and glory in the highest.
And some of the Pharisees among the people said to him, Master, make your disciples be quiet.
And he said in anser, I say to you, if these men keep quiet, the very stones ill be crying out.
And hen he got near and sa the ton, he as overcome ith eeping for it,
Saying, If you, even you, had knoledge today, of the things hich give peace! but you are not able to see them.
For the time ill come hen your attackers ill put a all round you, and come all round you and keep you in on every side,
And ill make you level ith the earth, and your children ith you; and there ill not be one stone resting on another in you, because you did not see that it as your day of mercy.
And he ent into the Temple and put out those ho ere trading there,
Saying to them, It has been said, My house is to be a house of prayer, but you have made it a hole of thieves.
And every day he as teaching in the Temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people ere attempting to put him to death;
But they ere not able to do anything, because the people all kept near him, being greatly interested in his ords.
And it came about on one of those days, hen he as teaching the people in the Temple and preaching the good nes,
That the chief priests and the scribes and the rulers of the people came to him and said, Make clear to us by hat authority you do these things and ho gave you this authority.
And in anser he said to them, I ill put a question to you, and do you give me an anser:
The baptism of John, as it from heaven or of men?

And he gave the people this story: A man made a vine-garden and gave the use of it to some field-orkers and ent into another country for a long time.

But hen the orkmen sa him, they said to one another, This is he ho ill one day be the oner of the property: let us put him to death and the heritage ill be ours.

And the chief priests and the scribes made attempts to get their hands on him in that very hour; and they ere in fear of the people, for they sa that he had made up this story against them.

And they kept atch on him, and sent out secret representatives, ho ere acting the part of good men, in order that they might get something from his ords, on account of hich they might give him up to the government and into the poer of the ruler.

Is it right for us to make payment of taxes to Caesar or not?
But he sa through their trick and said to them,
Let me see a penny. Whose image and name are on it? And they said, Caesar’s.

And they ere not able to get anything from these ords before the people: but they ere full of onder at his anser, and said nothing.
And some of the Sadducees came to him, ho say that there is no coming back from the dead; and they said to him,

No there ere seven brothers, and the first had a ife and came to his end, having no children;
And the second;
And the third took her; and in the same ay, all the seven, ithout having any children, came to their end.
And last of all, the oman came to her end.
When they come back from the dead, hose ife ill she be? for all the seven had her.
And Jesus said to them, The sons of this orld are married and have ives;

And death has no more poer over them, for they are equal to the angels, and are sons of God, being of those ho ill come back from the dead.
But even Moses made it clear that the dead come back to life, saying, in the story of the burning thorn-tree, The Lord, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.

And some of the scribes, in anser to this, said, Master, you have said ell.

But give attention to yourselves, for fear that your hearts become over-full of the pleasures of food and ine, and the cares of this life, and that day may come on you suddenly, and take you as in a net:

But the hand of him ho is false to me is ith me at the table.

And they ere ondering among themselves hich of them it as ho ould do this thing.

And he said, The kings of the Gentiles are lords over them, and those ho have authority are given names of honour.

For hich is greater, the guest ho is seated at a meal or the servant ho is aiting on him? is it not the guest? but I am among you as a servant.
But you are those ho have kept ith me through my troubles;
And I ill give you a kingdom as my Father has given one to me,
So that you may take food and drink at my table in my kingdom, and be seated like kings, judging the telve tribes of Israel.
Simon, Simon, Satan has made a request to have you, so that he may put you to the test as grain is tested:
But I have made prayer for you, that your faith may not go from you: and hen you are turned again, make your brothers strong.
And he said to him, Lord, I am ready to go ith you to prison and to death.
And he said, I say to you, Peter, before the cock’s second cry today, you ill say three times that you have no knoledge of me.
And he said to them, When I sent you out ithout money or bag or shoes, ere you in need of anything? And they said, Nothing.
And he said to them, But no, he ho has a money-bag, or a bag for food, let him take it: and he ho has not, let him give his coat for money and get a sord.
For I say to you that these ords ill be put into effect in me, And he as numbered among the evil-doers: for hat has been said in the Writings about me has an end.
And they said, Lord, here are to sords. And he said, It is enough.
And he came out, and ent, as his ay as, to the Mountain of Olives, and the disciples ent ith him.

Father, if it is your pleasure, take this cup from me: but still, let your pleasure, not mine, be done.

And, getting up from prayer, he came to the disciples, and sa that they ere sleeping for sorro.
And he said, Why are you sleeping? Get up, and give yourselves to prayer, so that you may not be put to the test.
And hile he as saying these ords, there came a band of people, and Judas, one of the telve, as in front of them, and he came near to Jesus to give him a kiss.
But Jesus said to him, Judas, ill you be false to the Son of man ith a kiss?

And they made him a prisoner and took him aay to the house of the high priest. But Peter ent after them at a distance.

You say that this man has been teaching the people evil things: no I, after going into the question before you, see nothing rong in this man in connection ith the things hich you have said against him:

For the days are coming in hich they ill say, Happy are those ho have had no children, hose bodies have never given birth, hose breasts have never given milk.

For if they do these things hen the tree is green, hat ill they do hen it is dry?
And to others, evil-doers, ere taken ith him to be put to death.
And hen they came to the place hich is named Golgotha, they put him on the cross, and the evil-doers, one on the right side, and the other on the left.
And Jesus said, Father, let them have forgiveness, for they have no knoledge of hat they are doing. And they made division of his clothing among them by the decision of chance.
And the people ere looking on. And the rulers made sport of him, saying, He as a saviour of others; let him do something for himself, if he is the Christ, the man of God’s selection.
And the men of the army made sport of him, coming to him and giving him bitter ine,
And saying, If you are the King of the Jes, get yourself free.
And these ords ere put in riting over him, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.

And ith reason; for e have the right reard of our acts, but this man has done nothing rong.

And it as no about the sixth hour; and all the land as dark till the ninth hour;

And all the people ho had come together to see it, hen they sa the things hich ere done, ent back again making signs of grief.
And all his friends and the omen ho came ith him from Galilee, ere aiting at a distance, atching these things.
No there as a man named Joseph, a man of authority and a good and upright man
( He had not given his approval to their decision or their acts), of Arimathaea, a ton of the Jes, ho as aiting for the kingdom of God:
This man ent to Pilate and made a request for the body of Jesus.
And he took it don, and folding it in a linen cloth, he put it in a place cut in the rock for a dead body; and no one had ever been put in it.
No it as the day of making ready and the Sabbath as coming on.

And they ent back and got ready spices and perfumes; and on the Sabbath they took their rest, in agreement ith the la.

And they sa that the stone had been rolled aay.

The Son of man ill be given up into the hands of evil-doers, and be put to death on the cross, and on the third day he ill come back to life.
And his ords came back into their minds,

And he said to them, What things? And they said, The things to do ith Jesus of Nazareth, ho as a prophet, great in his acts and his ords, before God and all the people:
And ho the chief priests and our rulers gave him up to be put to death on the cross.
But e ere hoping that he ould be the Saviour of Israel. In addition to all this he has no let three days go by from the time hen these things took place;

But they kept him back, saying, Do not go, for evening is near, the day is almost gone. And he ent in ith them.

From the first he as the Word, and the Word as in relation ith God and as God.
This Word as from the first in relation ith God.
All things came into existence through him, and ithout him nothing as.
What came into existence in him as life, and the life as the light of men.

He came for itness, to give itness about the light, so that all men might have faith through him.

To all those ho did so take him, hoever, he gave the right of becoming children of God — that is, to those ho had faith in his name:
Whose birth as from God and not from blood, or from an impulse of the flesh and man’s desire.
And so the Word became flesh and took a place among us for a time; and e sa his glory — such glory as is given to an only son by his father — sa it to be true and full of grace.
John gave itness about him, crying, This is he of hom I said, He ho is coming after me is put over me because he as in existence before me.
From his full measure e have all been given grace on grace.
For the la as given through Moses; grace and the true ay of life are ours through Jesus Christ.

And this is the itness of John hen the Jes sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to him ith the question, Who are you?

So they said to him, Who are you then? We have to give some anser to those ho sent us. What have you to say about yourself?
He said, I am the voice of one crying in the aste land, Make straight the ay of the Lord, as said Isaiah the prophet.
Those ho had been sent came from the Pharisees.
And they put this question to him, saying, Why then are you giving baptism if you are not the Christ, or Elijah, or the prophet?
John’s anser as: I give baptism ith ater; but there is one among you of hom you have no knoledge;
It is he ho is coming after me; I am not good enough to undo his shoes.
These things took place at Bethany on the other side of the Jordan, here John as giving baptism.
The day after, John sees Jesus coming to him and says, See, here is the Lamb of God ho takes aay the sin of the orld!
This is he of hom I said, One is coming after me ho is put over me because he as in existence before me.
I myself had no knoledge of him, but I came giving baptism ith ater so that he might be seen openly by Israel.
And John gave this itness, saying, I sa the Spirit coming don from heaven like a dove and resting on him.
I had no knoledge ho he as, but he ho sent me to give baptism ith ater said to me, The one on hom you see the Spirit coming don and resting, it is he ho gives baptism ith the Holy Spirit.
This I sa myself and my itness is that he is the Son of God.
The day after, John as there again ith to of his disciples;
And looking at Jesus hile he as alking he said, See, there is the Lamb of God!
Hearing hat he said, the to disciples ent after Jesus.
And Jesus, turning round, sa them coming after him and said to them, What are you looking for? They said to him, Rabbi ( hich is to say, Master), here are you living?
He said to them, Come and see. They ent ith him then and sa here he as living; and they ere ith him all that day: it as then about the tenth hour of the day.
Andre, Simon Peter’s brother, as one of the to men ho, hearing hat John said, ent after Jesus.
Early in the morning he came across his brother and said to him, We have made discovery! It is the Messiah! ( hich is to say, the Christ).
And he took him to Jesus. Looking at him fixedly Jesus said, You are Simon, the son of John; your name ill be Cephas ( hich is to say, Peter).
The day after this, Jesus had a desire to go into Galilee. He came across Philip and said to him, Come and be my disciple.
No Philip’s ton as Beth-saida, here Andre and Peter came from.
Philip came across Nathanael and said to him, We have made a discovery! It is he of hom Moses, in the la, and the prophets ere riting, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.
Nazareth! said Nathanael, Is it possible for any good to come out of Nazareth? Philip said to him, Come and see.
Jesus sa Nathanael coming to him and said of him, See, here is a true son of Israel in hom there is nothing false.
Nathanael said to him, Where did you get knoledge of me? In anser Jesus said, Before Philip as talking ith you, hile you ere still under the fig-tree, I sa you.
Nathanael said to him, Rabbi, you are the Son of God, you are King of Israel!
In anser Jesus said to him, You have faith because I said to you, I sa you under the fig-tree. You ill see greater things than these.
And he said to him, Truly I say to you all, You ill see heaven opening and God’s angels going up and coming don on the Son of man.
On the third day to people ere going to be married at Cana in Galilee. The mother of Jesus as there:
And Jesus ith his disciples came as guests.
When they had not enough ine, the mother of Jesus said to him, They have no ine.
Jesus said to her, Woman, this is not your business; my time is still to come.
His mother said to the servants, Whatever he says to you, do it.
No six pots of stone, every one taking to or three firkins of ater, ere placed there for the purpose of ashing, as is the ay of the Jes.
Jesus said to the servants, Make the pots full of ater. And they made them full to the top.
Then he said to them, No take some, and give it to the master of the feast. So they took it to him.
After tasting the ater hich had no become ine, the master of the feast (having no idea here it came from, though it as clear to the servants ho took the ater out) sent for the nely-married man,
And said to him, Every man first puts out his best ine and hen all have had enough he puts out hat is not so good; but you have kept the good ine till no.
This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee and let his glory be seen openly; and his disciples put their faith in him.
After this he ent don to Capernaum, ith his mother, his brothers, and his disciples, and they ere there not more than to or three days.
The time of the Passover of the Jes as near and Jesus ent up to Jerusalem.
And there in the Temple he sa men trading in oxen and sheep and doves, and he sa the changers of money in their seats:
And he made a hip of small cords and put them all out of the Temple, ith the sheep and the oxen, sending in all directions the small money of the changers and overturning their tables;
And to those ho ere trading in doves he said, Take these things aay; do not make my Father’s house a market.
And it came to the minds of the disciples that the Writings say, I am on fire ith passion for your house.
Then the Jes put this question to him: What sign of authority have you to give us, seeing that you do these things?
And Jesus said to them, Send destruction on this Temple and I ill put it up again in three days.
The Jes said, The building of this Temple took forty-six years; and you ill put it up in three days!
But his ords ere about that holy building hich as his body.
So hen he had come back again from the dead, the memory of these ords came back to the disciples, and they had faith in the holy Writings and in the ord hich Jesus had said.
No hile he as in Jerusalem at the feast of the Passover, a great number of people came to have faith in his name, after seeing the signs hich he did.
But Jesus did not have faith in them, because he had knoledge of them all.
He had no need for any itness about man; for he himself had knoledge of hat as in man.
No there as among the Pharisees a man named Nicodemus, ho as one of the rulers of the Jes.
He came to Jesus by night and said to him, Rabbi, e are certain that you have come from God as a teacher, because no man ould be able to do these signs hich you do if God as not ith him.
Jesus said to him, Truly, I say to you, Without a ne birth no man is able to see the kingdom of God.
Nicodemus said to him, Ho is it possible for a man to be given birth hen he is old? Is he able to go into his mother’s body a second time and come to birth again?
Jesus said in anser, Truly, I say to you, If a man’s birth is not from ater and from the Spirit, it is not possible for him to go into the kingdom of God.
That hich has birth from the flesh is flesh, and that hich has birth from the Spirit is spirit.
Do not be surprised that I say to you, It is necessary for you to have a second birth.
The ind goes here its pleasure takes it, and the sound of it comes to your ears, but you are unable to say here it comes from and here it goes: so it is ith everyone hose birth is from the Spirit.
And Nicodemus said to him, Ho is it possible for these things to be?
And Jesus, ansering, said, Are you the teacher of Israel and have no knoledge of these things?
Truly, I say to you, We say that of hich e have knoledge; e give itness of hat e have seen; and you do not take our itness to be true.
If you have no belief hen my ords are about the things of earth, ho ill you have belief if my ords are about the things of heaven?
And no one has ever gone up to heaven but he ho came don from heaven, the Son of man.
As the snake as lifted up by Moses in the aste land, even so it is necessary for the Son of man to be lifted up:
So that hoever has faith may have in him eternal life.
For God had such love for the orld that he gave his only Son, so that hoever has faith in him may not come to destruction but have eternal life.
God did not send his Son into the orld to be judge of the orld; he sent him so that the orld might have salvation through him.
The man ho has faith in him does not come up to be judged; but he ho has no faith in him has been judged even no, because he has no faith in the name of the only Son of God.
And this is the test by hich men are judged: the light has come into the orld and men have more love for the dark than for the light, because their acts are evil.
The light is hated by everyone hose acts are evil and he does not come to the light for fear that his acts ill be seen.
But he hose life is true comes to the light, so that it may be clearly seen that his acts have been done by the help of God.
After these things Jesus and his disciples ent into the land of Judaea, and there he as ith them for some time, giving baptism.
No John as then giving baptism at Aenon near Salim, because there as much ater there; and people came and ere given baptism.
For at this time John had not been put into prison.
Then a question came up beteen John’s disciples and a Je about ashing.
And they ent to John and said to him, Rabbi, the man ho as ith you on the other side of the Jordan, the man to hom you gave itness, is no giving baptism, and everyone is going to him.
And this as John’s anser: A man is unable to have anything if it is not given to him from heaven.
You yourselves give itness that I said, I am not the Christ. What I said as, I am sent before the Christ.

He ho has the bride is the husband: but the husband’s friend, hose place is by his side and hose ears are open to him, is full of joy because of the husband’s voice: such is my joy, and it is complete.
He has to become greater hile I become less.
He ho comes from heaven is greater than all others: he ho comes from earth is of the earth, and of the earth are his ords: he ho comes from heaven is over all.
He gives itness of hat he has seen and of hat has come to his ears; and no man takes his itness as true.
He ho so takes his itness has made clear his faith that God is true.
For he hom God has sent says God’s ords; and God does not give him the Spirit by measure.
The Father has love for the Son and has put all things into his hands.
He ho has faith in the Son has eternal life; but he ho has not faith in the Son ill not see life; God’s rath is resting on him.
No hen it as clear to the Lord that ord had come to the ears of the Pharisees that Jesus as making more disciples than John and as giving them baptism
(Though, in fact, it as his disciples ho gave baptism, not Jesus himself),
He ent out of Judaea into Galilee again.
And it as necessary for him to go through Samaria.
So he came to a ton of Samaria hich as named Sychar, near to the bit of land hich Jacob gave to his son Joseph:
No Jacob’s fountain as there. Jesus, being tired after his journey, as resting by the fountain. It as about the sixth hour.
A oman of Samaria came to get ater, and Jesus said to her, Give me some ater.
For his disciples had gone to the ton to get food.
The oman of Samaria said to him, Why do you, a Je, make a request for ater to me, a oman of Samaria? She said this because Jes have nothing to do ith the people of Samaria.
In anser Jesus said, If you had knoledge of hat God gives freely and ho it is ho says to you, Give me ater, you ould make your prayer to him, and he ould give you living ater.
The oman said to him, Sir, you have no vessel and the fountain is deep; from here ill you get the living ater?
Are you greater than our father Jacob ho gave us the fountain and took the ater of it himself, ith his children and his cattle?
Jesus said to her, Everyone ho takes this ater ill be in need of it again:
But hoever takes the ater I give him ill never be in need of drink again; for the ater I give him ill become in him a fountain of eternal life.
The oman said to him, Sir, give me this ater, so that I may not be in need again of drink and ill not have to come all this ay for it.
Jesus said to her, Go, get your husband and come back here ith him.
In anser, the oman said, I have no husband. Jesus said to her, You have said rightly, I have no husband:
You have had five husbands, and the man you have no is not your husband: that as truly said.
The oman said to him, Sir, I see that you are a prophet.
Our fathers gave orship on this mountain, but you Jes say that the right place for orship is in Jerusalem.
Jesus said to her, Woman, take my ord for this; the time is coming hen you ill not give orship to the Father on this mountain or in Jerusalem.
You give orship, but ithout knoledge of hat you are orshipping: e give orship to hat e have knoledge of: for salvation comes from the Jes.
But the time is coming, and is even no here, hen the true orshippers ill give orship to the Father in the true ay of the spirit, for these are the orshippers desired by the Father.
God is Spirit: then let his orshippers give him orship in the true ay of the spirit.
The oman said to him, I am certain that the Messiah, ho is named Christ, is coming; hen he comes he ill make all things clear to us.
Jesus said to her, I, ho am talking to you, am he.
At that point the disciples came back, and they ere surprised to see him talking to a oman; but not one of them said to him, What is your purpose? or, Why are you talking to her?
Then the oman put don her ater-pot and ent into the ton, and said to the people,
Come and see a man ho has been talking to me of everything I ever did! Is it possible that this is the Christ?
So they ent out of the ton and came to him.
While this as taking place, the disciples ere saying to Jesus, Master, take some food.
But he said to them, I have food of hich you have no knoledge.
So the disciples said one to another, Did anyone give him food?
Jesus said, My food is to do the pleasure of him ho sent me and to make his ork complete.
You ould say, Four months from no is the time of the grain-cutting. Take a look, I say to you, at the fields; they are even no hite for cutting.
He ho does the cutting no has his reard; he is getting together fruit for eternal life, so that he ho did the planting and he ho gets in the grain may have joy together.
In this the saying is a true one, One does the planting, and another gets in the grain.
I sent you to get in grain hich you had no hand in planting: other men did that ork, and you take the reard.
No a number of the people of that ton had faith in him because of the oman’s itness: He has been talking to me of everything I ever did.
So hen the people came to him they made request to him to be among them for a time, and he as there to days.
And a great number more of them came to have faith in him because of hat he himself said.
And they said to the oman, No e have faith, but not because of your story: e ourselves have given ear to his ords, and e are certain that he is truly the Saviour of the orld.
And after the to days he ent on from there into Galilee.
For Jesus himself said that a prophet has no honour in the country of his birth.
So hen he came into Galilee, the Galilaeans took him to their hearts because of the things hich they had seen him do in Jerusalem at the feast — they themselves having been there at the feast.
So he came to Cana in Galilee, here he had made the ater ine. And there as a certain man of high position hose son as ill at Capernaum.
When it came to his ears that Jesus had come from Judaea into Galilee, he ent to him and made a request that he ould come don to his son, ho as near to death, and make him ell.
Then Jesus said to him, You ill not have faith if you do not see signs and onders.
The man said, Sir, come don before my boy is dead.
And Jesus said, Go in peace; your son is living. The man had faith in the ord hich Jesus said to him and ent aay.
And hile he as going don, his servants came to him and said, Your boy is living.
So he put a question to them as to the hour hen he became better; and they said to him, The disease ent from him yesterday at the seventh hour.
It as clear then to the father that this as the very time at hich Jesus said to him, Your son is living. And he had faith in Jesus, he and all his family.
No this is the second sign hich Jesus did after he had come out of Judaea into Galilee.
After these things there as a feast of the Jes, and Jesus ent up to Jerusalem.
No in Jerusalem near the sheep-market there is a public bath hich in Hebre is named Beth-zatha. It has five doorays.
In these doorays there ere a great number of people ith different diseases: some unable to see, some ithout the poer of alking, some ith asted bodies.
One man as there ho had been ill for thirty-eight years.
When Jesus sa him there on the floor it as clear to him that he had been no a long time in that condition, and so he said to the man, Is it your desire to get ell?
The ill man said in anser, Sir, I have nobody to put me into the bath hen the ater is moving; and hile I am on the ay don some other person gets in before me.
Jesus said to him, Get up, take your bed and go.
And the man became ell straight aay, and took up his bed and ent. No that day as the Sabbath.
So the Jes said to the man ho had been made ell, It is the Sabbath; and it is against the la for you to take up your bed.
He said to them, But he ho made me ell, said to me, Take up your bed and go.
Then they put to him the question: Who is the man ho said to you, Take it up and go?
No he ho had been made ell had no knoledge ho it as, Jesus having gone aay because of the number of people ho ere in that place.
After a time Jesus came across him in the Temple and said to him, See, you are ell and strong; do no more sin for fear a orse thing comes to you.
The man ent aay and said to the Jes that it as Jesus ho had made him ell.
And for this reason the Jes ere turned against Jesus, because he as doing these things on the Sabbath.
But his anser as: My Father is still orking even no, and so I am orking.
For this cause the Jes had an even greater desire to put Jesus to death, because not only did he not keep the Sabbath but he said God as his Father, so making himself equal ith God.

So Jesus made anser and said, Truly I say to you, The Son is not able to do anything himself; he is able to do only hat he sees the Father doing; hatever the Father does the Son does it in the same ay.
For the Father has love for the Son and lets him see everything hich he does: and he ill let him see greater orks than these so that you may be full of onder.
In the same ay, as the Father gives life to the dead, even so the Son gives life to those to hom he is pleased to give it.
The Father is not the judge of men, but he has given all decisions into the hands of the Son;
So that all men may give honour to the Son even as they give honour to the Father. He ho gives no honour to the Son gives no honour to the Father ho sent him.
Truly I say to you, The man hose ears are open to my ord and ho has faith in him ho sent me, has eternal life; he ill not be judged, but has come from death into life.
Truly I say to you, The time is coming, it has even no come, hen the voice of the Son of God ill come to the ears of the dead, and those hearing it ill have life.
For even as the Father has life in himself, so he has given to the Son to have life in himself.
And he has given him authority to be judge because he is the Son of man.
Do not be surprised at this: for the time is coming hen his voice ill come to all ho are in the place of the dead,
And they ill come out; those ho have done good, into the ne life; and those ho have done evil, to be judged.

Of myself I am unable to do anything: as the voice comes to me so I give a decision: and my decision is right because I have no desire to do hat is pleasing to myself, but only hat is pleasing to him ho sent me.
If I gave itness about myself, my itness ould not be true.
There is another ho gives itness about me and I am certain that the itness he gives about me is true.
You sent to John and he gave true itness.
But I have no need of a man’s itness: I only say these things so that you may have salvation.
He as a burning and shining light, and for a time you ere ready to be happy in his light.
But the itness hich I have is greater than that of John: the ork hich the Father has given me to do, the very ork hich I am no doing, is a itness that the Father has sent me.
And the Father himself ho sent me has given itness about me. Not one of you has ever given ear to his voice; his form you have not seen.
And you have not kept his ord in your hearts, because you have not faith in him hom he has sent.
You make search in the holy Writings, in the belief that through them you get eternal life; and it is those Writings hich give itness about me.
And still you have no desire to come to me so that you may have life.
I do not take honour from men;
But I have knoledge of you that you have no love for God in your hearts.
I have come in my Father’s name, and your hearts are not open to me. If another comes ith no other authority but himself, you ill give him your approval.
Ho is it possible for you to have faith hile you take honour one from another and have no desire for the honour hich comes from the only God?
Put out of your minds the thought that I ill say things against you to the Father: the one ho says things against you is Moses, on hom you put your hopes.
If you had belief in Moses you ould have belief in me; for his ritings are about me.
If you have no belief in his ritings, ho ill you have belief in my ords?
After these things Jesus ent aay to the other side of the sea of Galilee — that is, the sea of Tiberias.
And a great number of people ent after him because they sa the signs hich he did on those ho ere ill.
Then Jesus ent up the mountain and as seated there ith his disciples.
No the Passover, a feast of the Jes, as near.
Lifting up his eyes, Jesus sa a great number of people coming to here he as, and he said to Philip, Where may e get bread for all these people?
This he said, testing him: for he had no doubt hat he himself ould do.
Philip made anser, Bread to the value of to hundred pence ould not be enough even to give everyone a little.
One of his disciples, Andre, the brother of Simon Peter, said to Jesus,
There is a boy here ith five barley cakes and to fishes: but hat is that among such a number?
Jesus said, Let the people be seated. No there as much grass in that place. And those seated on the grass ere about five thousand.
Then Jesus took the cakes and having given praise to God, he gave them to the people ho ere seated, and the fishes in the same ay, as much as they had need of.
And hen they had had enough, Jesus said to his disciples, Take up the broken bits hich are over, so that nothing may be asted.
So they took them up: telve baskets full of broken bits of the five cakes hich ere over after the people had had enough.
And hen the people sa the sign hich he had done, they said, Truly, this is the prophet ho is to come into the orld.
No hen Jesus sa that the people ere about to come and take him by force to make him a king, he ent aay again up the mountain by himself.
When evening came the disciples ent don to the sea;
And they took a boat and ent across the sea in the direction of Capernaum. By then it as dark and still Jesus had not come to them.
The sea as getting rough because of a strong ind hich as bloing.
After they had gone three or four miles they sa Jesus alking on the sea and coming near to the boat; and they had great fear.
But he said to them, It is I, have no fear.
Then they readily took him into the boat: and straight aay the boat as at the land to hich they ere going.

The day after, the people ho ere on the other side of the sea sa that only one small boat had been there, that Jesus had not gone in that boat ith the disciples, but that the disciples had gone aay by themselves.
Some other boats, hoever, came from Tiberias near to the place here they had taken the bread after the Lord had given praise.
So hen the people sa that Jesus as not there, or his disciples, they got into those boats and ent over to Capernaum looking for Jesus.
And hen they came across him on the other side of the sea they said, Rabbi, hen did you come here?
Jesus, ansering them, said, Truly I say to you, You come after me, not because you sa signs, but because you ere given the bread and had enough.
Let your ork not be for the food hich comes to an end, but for the food hich goes on for eternal life, hich the Son of man ill give to you, for on him has God the Father put his mark.
Then they said to him, Ho may e do the orks of God?
Jesus, ansering, said to them, This is to do the ork of God: to have faith in him hom God has sent.
So they said, What sign do you give us, so that e may see and have faith in you? What do you do?
Our fathers had the manna in the aste land, as the Writings say, He gave them bread from heaven.
Jesus then said to them, Truly I say to you, What Moses gave you as not the bread from heaven; it is my Father ho gives you the true bread from heaven.
The bread of God is the bread hich comes don out of heaven and gives life to the orld.
Ah, Lord, they said, give us that bread for ever!
And this as the anser of Jesus: I am the bread of life. He ho comes to me ill never be in need of food, and he ho has faith in me ill never be in need of drink.
But it is as I said to you: you have seen me, and still you have no faith.
Whatever the Father gives to me ill come to me; and I ill not send aay anyone ho comes to me.
For I have come don from heaven, not to do my pleasure, but the pleasure of him ho sent me.
And this is the pleasure of him ho sent me, that I am not to let out of my hands anything hich he has given me, but I am to give it ne life on the last day.
This, I say, is my Father’s pleasure, that everyone ho sees the Son and has faith in him may have eternal life: and I ill take him up on the last day.
No the Jes said bitter things about Jesus because of his ords, I am the bread hich came don from heaven.
And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, hose father and mother e have seen? Ho is it then that he no says, I have come don from heaven?
Jesus made anser and said, Do not say things against me, one to another.
No man is able to come to me if the Father ho sent me does not give him the desire to come: and I ill take him up from the dead on the last day.
The ritings of the prophets say, And they ill all have teaching from God. Everyone hose ears have been open to the teaching of the Father comes to me.
Not that anyone has ever seen the Father; only he ho is from God, he has seen the Father.
Truly I say to you, He ho has faith in me has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers took the manna in the aste land — and they are dead.
The bread hich comes from heaven is such bread that a man may take it for food and never see death.

I am the living bread hich has come from heaven: if any man takes this bread for food he ill have life for ever: and more than this, the bread hich I ill give is my flesh hich I ill give for the life of the orld.
Then the Jes had an angry discussion among themselves, saying, Ho is it possible for this man to give us his flesh for food?
Then Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you, If you do not take the flesh of the Son of man for food, and if you do not take his blood for drink, you have no life in you.
He ho takes my flesh for food and my blood for drink has eternal life: and I ill take him up from the dead at the last day.
My flesh is true food and my blood is true drink.
He ho takes my flesh for food and my blood for drink is in me and I in him.
As the living Father has sent me, and I have life because of the Father, even so he ho takes me for his food ill have life because of me.
This is the bread hich has come don from heaven. It is not like the food hich your fathers had: they took of the manna, and are dead; but he ho takes this bread for food ill have life for ever.
Jesus said these things in the Synagogue hile he as teaching at Capernaum.
Then, hearing this, a number of his disciples said, This is a hard saying; ho is able to take in such teaching?
When Jesus became conscious that his disciples ere protesting about hat he said, he said to them, Does this give you trouble?
What then ill you say if you see the Son of man going up to here he as before?
The spirit is the life giver; the flesh is of no value: the ords hich I have said to you are spirit and they are life.
But still some of you have no faith. For it as clear to Jesus from the first ho they ere ho had no faith, and ho it as ho ould be false to him.
And he said, This is hy I said to you, No man is able to come to me if he is not given the poer to do so by the Father.
Because of hat he said, a number of the disciples ent back and ould no longer go ith him.
So Jesus said to the telve, Have you a desire to go aay?
Then Simon Peter gave this anser: Lord, to hom are e to go? you have the ords of eternal life;
And e have faith and are certain that you are the Holy One of God.
Then Jesus said, Did I not make a selection of you, the telve, and one of you is a son of the Evil One?
He as talking of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. It as he ho as to be false to Jesus — one of the telve.
After this, Jesus ent from place to place in Galilee. He did not go about in Judaea, because the Jes ere looking for a chance to put him to death.
But the feast of the Jes, the feast of tents, as near.
So his brothers said to him, Go aay from here into Judaea so that your disciples may see the orks hich you do.
Because no man does things secretly if he has a desire that men may have knoledge of him. If you do these things, let yourself be seen by all men.
For even his brothers had no belief in him.
Jesus said to them, My time is still to come, but any time is good for you.
It is not possible for you to be hated by the orld; but I am hated by it, because I give itness that hat it does is evil.
Go you up to the feast: I am not going up no to the feast because my time has not fully come.
Having said these things to them, he still kept in Galilee.
But after his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he ent up, not publicly, but in secret.
At the feast the Jes ere looking for him and saying, Where is he?
And there as much discussion about him among the mass of the people. Some said, He is a good man; but others said, No, he is giving people false ideas.
But no man said anything about him openly for fear of the Jes.
No in the middle of the feast Jesus ent up to the Temple and as teaching.
Then the Jes ere surprised and said, Ho has this man got knoledge of books? He has never been to school.
Jesus gave them this anser: It is not my teaching, but his ho sent me.
If any man is ready to do God’s pleasure he ill have knoledge of the teaching and of here it comes from — from God or from myself.
The man hose ords come from himself is looking for glory for himself, but he ho is looking for the glory of him ho sent him — that man is true and there is no evil in him.
Did not Moses give you the la? Even so, not one of you keeps the la. Why have you a desire to put me to death?
The people said in anser, You have an evil spirit: ho has any desire to put you to death?
This as the anser of Jesus: I have done one ork and you are all surprised at it.
Moses gave you circumcision — not that it comes from Moses, but from the fathers — and even on the Sabbath you give a child circumcision.
If a child is given circumcision on the Sabbath so that the la of Moses may not be broken, hy are you angry ith me because I made a man completely ell on the Sabbath?
Let not your decisions be based on hat you see, but on righteousness.
Then some of the people of Jerusalem said, Is not this the man hose death is desired?
And here he is talking openly and they say nothing to him! Is it possible that the rulers have knoledge that this is truly the Christ?
Hoever, it is clear to us here this man comes from: but hen the Christ comes no one ill have knoledge here he comes from.

Then, hen he as teaching in the Temple, Jesus said ith a loud voice, You have knoledge of me and you have knoledge of here I come from; and I have not come of myself; but there is One ho has sent me; he is true, but you have no knoledge of him.
I have knoledge of him because I came from him and he sent me.
Then they had a desire to take him: but no man put hands on him because his hour as still to come.
And numbers of the people had belief in him, and they said, When the Christ comes ill he do more signs than this man has done?
This discussion of the people came to the ears of the Pharisees; and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent servants to take him.
Then Jesus said, I ill be ith you a little longer and then I go to him ho sent me.
You ill be looking for me, and you ill not see me: and here I am you may not come.
So the Jes said among themselves, To hat place is he going here e ill not see him? ill he go to the Jes living among the Greeks and become the teacher of the Greeks?
What is this saying of his, You ill be looking for me and ill not see me, and here I am you may not come?
On the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus got up and said in a loud voice, If any man is in need of drink let him come to me and I ill give it to him.
He ho has faith in me, out of his body, as the Writings have said, ill come rivers of living ater.
This he said of the Spirit hich ould be given to those ho had faith in him: the Spirit had not been given then, because the glory of Jesus as still to come.
When these ords came to their ears, some of the people said, This is certainly the prophet.
Others said, This is the Christ. But others said, Not so; ill the Christ come from Galilee?
Do not the Writings say that the Christ comes of the seed of David and from Beth-lehem, the little ton here David as?
So there as a division among the people because of him.
And some of them had a desire to take him; but no man put hands on him.
Then the servants ent back to the chief priests and Pharisees, ho said to them, Why have you not got him ith you?
The servants made anser, No man ever said things like this man.
Then the Pharisees said to them, Have you, like the others, been given false ideas?
Have any of the rulers belief in him, or any one of the Pharisees?
But these people ho have no knoledge of the la are cursed.
Nicodemus — he ho had come to Jesus before, being himself one of them — said to them,
Is a man judged by our la before it has given him a hearing and has knoledge of hat he has done?
This as their anser: And do you come from Galilee? Make search and you ill see that no prophet comes out of Galilee.
[ And every man ent to his house;
But Jesus ent to the Mountain of Olives.
And early in the morning he came again into the Temple and all the people came to him and he as seated teaching them.
No the scribes and Pharisees came, ith a oman ho had been taken in the act of sinning against the married relation;
And putting her forard, they said to him, Master, this oman has been taken in the very act of sinning against the married relation.
No in the la Moses gave directions that such omen ere to be stoned; hat do you say about it?
They said this, testing him, so that they might have something against him. But Jesus, ith his head bent don, made letters on the floor ith his finger.
But hen they ent on ith their questions, he got up and said to them, Let him among you ho is ithout sin be the first to send a stone at her.
And again, ith bent head, he made letters on the floor.

And hen his ords came to their ears, they ent out one by one, starting ith the oldest even to the last, because they ere conscious of hat as in their hearts: and Jesus as there by himself ith the oman before him.
Then Jesus got up, and seeing nobody but the oman, he said to her, Where are the men ho said things against you? did no one give a decision against you?
And she said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said, And I do not give a decision against you: go, and never do rong again.]
Then again Jesus said to them, I am the light of the orld; he ho comes ith me ill not be alking in the dark but ill have the light of life.
So the Pharisees said to him, The itness you give is about yourself: your itness is not true.

Jesus said in anser, Even if I give itness about myself, my itness is true, because I have knoledge of here I came from and here I am going; but you have no knoledge of here I come from or of here I am going.
You are judging from hat you see; I am judging no man.
Even if I am judging, my decision is right, because I am not by myself — ith me is the Father ho sent me.
Even in your la it is said that the itness of to men is true.
I give itness about myself and the Father ho sent me gives itness about me.
Then they said to him, Where is your Father? Jesus said in anser, You have no knoledge of me or of my Father: if you had knoledge of me you ould have knoledge of my Father.
Jesus said these ords in the place here the offerings ere stored, hile he as teaching in the Temple: but no man took him because his time as still to come.
Then he said to them again, I am going aay and you ill be looking for me, but death ill overtake you in your sins. It is not possible for you to come here I am going.
So the Jes said, Will he take his life? Is that hy he says, Where I go it is not possible for you to come?
And he said to them, You are of the earth; I am from heaven: you are of this orld; I am not of this orld.
For this reason I said to you that death ill overtake you in your sins: for if you have not faith that I am he, death ill come to you hile you are in your sins.
Then they said to him, Who are you? Jesus said, What I said to you from the first.
I have much to say about you and against you: but he ho sent me is true and hat he has said to me I say to the orld.
They did not see that his ords ere about the Father.
So Jesus said, When the Son of man has been lifted up by you, then it ill be clear to you ho I am, and that I do nothing of myself, but say as the Father gave me teaching.
He ho sent me is ith me; he has not gone from me, because at all times I do the things hich are pleasing to him.
When he said this a number came to have faith in him.
Then Jesus said to the Jes ho had faith in him, If you keep my ord, then you are truly my disciples;
And you ill have knoledge of hat is true, and that ill make you free.
They said to him in anser, We are Abraham’s seed and have never been any man’s servant: hy do you say, You ill become free?
And this as the anser Jesus gave them: Truly I say to you, Everyone ho does evil is the servant of sin.
No the servant does not go on living in the house for ever, but the son does.
If then the son makes you free, you ill be truly free.
I am conscious that you are Abraham’s seed; but you have a desire to put me to death because my ord has no place in you.
I say the things hich I have seen in my Father’s house: and you do the things hich come to you from your father’s house.
In anser they said to him, Our father is Abraham. Jesus said to them, If you ere Abraham’s children you ould do hat Abraham did.
But no you have a desire to put me to death, a man ho has said to you hat is true, as I had it from God: Abraham did not do that.
You are doing the orks of your father. They said to him, We are true sons of Abraham; e have one Father, ho is God.
Jesus said to them, If God as your Father you ould have love for me, because it as from God I came and am here. I did not come of myself, but he sent me.
Why are my ords not clear to you? It is because your ears are shut to my teaching.

You are the children of your father the Evil One and it is your pleasure to do his desires. From the first he as a taker of life; and he did not go in the true ay because there is no true thing in him. When he says hat is false, it is natural to him, for he is false and the father of hat is false.
But because I say hat is true, you have no belief in me.
Which of you is able truly to say that I am a sinner? If I say hat is true, hy have you no belief in me?
He ho is a child of God gives ear to the ords of God: your ears are not open to them because you are not from God.
The Jes said to him in anser, Are e not right in saying that you are of Samaria and have an evil spirit?
And this as the anser of Jesus: I have not an evil spirit; but I give honour to my Father and you do not give honour to me.
I, hoever, am not in search of glory for myself: there is One ho is searching for it and he is judge.
Truly I say to you, If a man keeps my ord he ill never see death.
The Jes said to him, No e are certain that you have an evil spirit. Abraham is dead, and the prophets are dead; and you say, If a man keeps my ord he ill never see death.
Are you greater than our father Abraham, ho is dead? and the prophets are dead: ho do you say that you are?
Jesus said in anser, If I take glory for myself, my glory is nothing: it is my Father ho gives me glory, of hom you say that he is your God.
You have no knoledge of him, but I have knoledge of him; and if I said I have no knoledge of him I ould be talking falsely like you: but I have full knoledge of him, and I keep his ord.
Your father Abraham as full of joy at the hope of seeing my day: he sa it and as glad.
Then the Jes said to him, You are not fifty years old; have you seen Abraham?
Jesus said to them, Truly I say to you, Before Abraham came into being, I am.
So they took up stones to send at him: but Jesus got secretly out of their ay and ent out of the Temple.
And hen he ent on his ay, he sa a man blind from birth.
And his disciples put a question to him, saying, Master, as it because of this man’s sin, or the sin of his father and mother, that he has been blind from birth?
Jesus said in anser, It as not because of his sin, or because of his father’s or mother’s; it as so that the orks of God might be seen openly in him.
While it is day e have to do the orks of him ho sent me: the night comes hen no ork may be done.
As long as I am in the orld, I am the light of the orld.
Having said these ords, he put earth, mixed ith ater from his mouth, on the man’s eyes,
And said to him, Go and make yourself clean in the bath of Siloam ( the sense of the name is, Sent). So he ent aay and, after ashing, came back able to see.
Then the neighbours and others ho had seen him before in the street, ith his hand out for money, said, Is not this the man ho got money from people?
Some said, It is he: others said, No, but he is like him. He said, I am he.
So they said to him, Ho then ere your eyes made open?
His anser as: The man ho is named Jesus put earth mixed ith ater on my eyes, and said to me, Go and make yourself clean in Siloam: so I ent aay and, after ashing, am no able to see.
And they said to him, Where is he? His anser as: I have no knoledge.
They took him before the Pharisees — this man ho had been blind.
No the day on hich the earth as mixed by Jesus and the man’s eyes ere made open as the Sabbath.
So the Pharisees put more questions to him about ho his eyes had been made open. And he said to them, He put earth on my eyes, and I had a ash and am able to see.
Then some of the Pharisees said, That man has not come from God, for he does not keep the Sabbath. Others said, Ho is it possible for a sinner to do such signs? So there as a division among them.
Again they said to the blind man, What have you to say about him for opening your eyes? And he said, He is a prophet.
No the Jes had no belief in the statement that he had been blind and as no able to see, till they sent for the father and mother of the man hose eyes had been made open,
And put the question to them, saying, Is this your son, of hom you say that he as blind at birth? ho is it then that he is no able to see?
In anser his father and mother said, We are certain that this is our son and that he as blind at birth:
But ho it is he is no able to see, or ho made his eyes open, e are not able to say: put the question to him; he is old enough to give an anser for himself.
They said this because of their fear of the Jes: for the Jes had come to an agreement that if any man said that Jesus as the Christ he ould be put out of the Synagogue.
That as the reason hy they said, He is old enough; put the question to him.
So they sent a second time for the man ho had been blind and they said to him, Give glory to God: it is clear to us that this man is a sinner.
He said in anser, I have no knoledge if he is a sinner or not, but one thing I am certain about; I as blind, and no I see.
Then they said to him, What did he do to you? ho did he give you the use of your eyes?
His anser as: I have said it before, but your ears ere shut: hy ould you have me say it again? is it your desire to become his disciples?
And they ere angry ith him and said, You are his disciple, but e are disciples of Moses.
We are certain that God gave his ord to Moses: but as for this man, e have no knoledge here he comes from.
The man said in anser, Why, here is a strange thing! You have no knoledge here he comes from though he gave me the use of my eyes.
We have knoledge that God does not give ear to sinners, but if any man is a orshipper of God and does his pleasure, to him God’s ears are open.
In all the years nobody has ever before seen the eyes of a man blind from birth made open.
If this man did not come from God he ould be unable to do anything.
Their anser as: You came to birth through sin; do you make yourself our teacher? And they put him out of the Synagogue.
It came to the ears of Jesus that they had put him out, and meeting him he said, Have you faith in the Son of man?
He said in anser, And ho is he, Lord? Say, so that I may have faith in him.
Jesus said to him, You have seen him; it is he ho is talking to you.
And he said, Lord, I have faith. And he gave him orship.
And Jesus said, I came into this orld to be a judge, so that those ho do not see may see, and those ho see may become blind.
These ords came to the ears of the Pharisees ho ere ith him and they said to him, Are e, then, blind?
Jesus said to them, If you ere blind you ould have no sin: but no that you say, We see; your sin is there still.
Truly I say to you, He ho does not go through the door into the place here the sheep are kept, but gets in by some other ay, is a thief and an outla.
He ho goes in by the door is the keeper of the sheep.
The porter lets him in; and the sheep give ear to his voice; he says over the names of the sheep, and takes them out.
When he has got them all out, he goes before them, and the sheep go after him, for they have knoledge of his voice.
They ill not go after another ho is not their keeper, but ill go from him in flight, because his voice is strange to them.
In this Jesus as teaching them in the form of a story: but hat he said as not clear to them.
So Jesus said again, Truly I say to you, I am the door of the sheep.
All ho came before me are thieves and outlas: but the sheep did not give ear to them.
I am the door: if any man goes in through me he ill have salvation, and ill go in and go out, and ill get food.
The thief comes only to take the sheep and to put them to death: he comes for their destruction: I have come so that they may have life and have it in greater measure.
I am the good keeper of sheep: the good keeper gives his life for the sheep.
He ho is a servant, and not the keeper or the oner of the sheep, sees the olf coming and goes in flight, aay from the sheep; and the olf comes don on them and sends them in all directions:
Because he is a servant he has no interest in the sheep.
I am the good keeper; I have knoledge of my sheep, and they have knoledge of me,
Even as the Father has knoledge of me and I of the Father; and I am giving my life for the sheep.
And I have other sheep hich are not of this field: I ill be their guide in the same ay, and they ill give ear to my voice, so there ill be one flock and one keeper.
For this reason am I loved by the Father, because I give up my life so that I may take it again.
No one takes it aay from me; I give it up of myself. I have poer to give it up, and I have poer to take it again. These orders I have from my Father.
There as a division again among the Jes because of these ords.
And a number of them said, He has an evil spirit and is out of his mind; hy do you give ear to him?
Others said, These are not the ords of one ho has an evil spirit. Is it possible for an evil spirit to make blind people see?
Then came the feast of the opening of the Temple in Jerusalem: it as inter;
And Jesus as alking in the Temple, in Solomon’s covered ay.
Then the Jes came round him, saying, ho long are you going to keep us in doubt? If you are the Christ, say so clearly.
Jesus said in anser, I have said it and you have no belief: the orks hich I do in my Father’s name, these give itness about me.
But you have no belief because you are not of my sheep.
My sheep give ear to my voice, and I have knoledge of them, and they come after me:
And I give them eternal life; they ill never come to destruction, and no one ill ever take them out of my hand.
That hich my Father has given to me has more value than all; and no one is able to take anything out of the Father’s hand.
I and my Father are one.
Then the Jes took up stones again to send at him.
Jesus said to them in anser, I have let you see a number of good orks from the Father; for hich of those orks are you stoning me?
This as their anser: We are not stoning you for a good ork but for evil ords; because being a man you make yourself God.
In anser, Jesus said, Is there not a saying in your la, I said, You are gods?
If he said they ere gods, to hom the ord of God came ( and the Writings may not be broken),
Do you say of him hom the Father made holy and sent into the orld, Your ords are evil; because I said, I am God’s Son?
If I am not doing the orks of my Father, do not have belief in me;
But if I am doing them, then have belief in the orks even if you have no belief in me; so that you may see clearly and be certain that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.
Then again they made an attempt to take him; but he got aay from them.
And he ent again to the other side of the Jordan, to the place here John first gave baptism; and he as there for a time.
And a great number of people came to him, saying, John did no sign: but everything John said of this man as true.
And a number came to have faith in him there.
No a certain man named Lazarus as ill; he as of Bethany, the ton of Mary and her sister Martha.
( The Mary hose brother Lazarus as ill, as the Mary ho put perfumed oil on the Lord and made his feet dry ith her hair.)
So the sisters sent to him, saying, Lord, your dear friend is ill.
When this came to his ears, Jesus said, The end of this disease is not death, but the glory of God, so that the Son of God may have glory because of it.
No Jesus had love in his heart for Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
So hen the nes came to him that Lazarus as ill, he did not go from the place here he as for to days.
Then after that time he said to his disciples, Let us go into Judaea again.
The disciples said to him, Master, the Jes ere attempting only the other day to have you stoned, and are you going back there again?
Then Jesus said in anser, Are there not telve hours in the day? A man may go about in the day ithout falling, because he sees the light of this orld.
But if a man goes about in the night, he may have a fall because the light is not in him.
These things said he: and after that he said to them, Lazarus our friend is at rest; but I go so that I may make him come out of his sleep.
Then his disciples said to him, Lord, if he is resting he ill get ell.
Jesus, hoever, as talking of his death: but they had the idea that he as talking about taking rest in sleep.
Then Jesus said to them clearly, Lazarus is dead.
And because of you I am glad I as not there, so that you may have faith; but let us go to him.
Then Thomas, ho as named Didymus, said to the other disciples, Let us go so that e may be ith him in death.
No hen Jesus came, he made the discovery that Lazarus had been put into the earth four days before.
No Bethany as near to Jerusalem, about to miles aay;
And a number of Jes had come to Martha and Mary to give them comfort about their brother.
When Martha had the nes that Jesus as on the ay, she ent out to him, but Mary did not go from the house.
Then Martha said to Jesus, Lord, if you had been here my brother ould not be dead.
But I am certain that, even no, hatever request you make to God, God ill give it to you.
Jesus said to her, Your brother ill come to life again.
Martha said to him, I am certain that he ill come to life again hen all come back from the dead at the last day.
Jesus said to her, I am myself that day and that life; he ho has faith in me ill have life even if he is dead;
And no one ho is living and has faith in me ill ever see death. Is this your faith?
She said to him, Yes, Lord: my faith is that you are the Christ, the Son of God, ho as to come into the orld.
And having said this, she ent aay and said secretly to her sister Mary, The Master is here and has sent for you.
And Mary, hearing this, got up quickly and ent to him.
No Jesus had not at this time come into the ton, but as still in the place here Martha had seen him.
Then the Jes ho ere ith her in the house, comforting her, hen they sa Mary get up quickly and go out, ent after her in the belief that she as going to the place of the dead and ould be eeping there.
When Mary came to here Jesus as and sa him, she ent don at his feet, saying, Lord, if you had been here my brother ould not be dead.
And hen Jesus sa her eeping, and sa the Jes eeping ho came ith her, his spirit as moved and he as troubled,
And said, Where have you put him? They said, Come and see, Lord.
And Jesus himself as eeping.
So the Jes said, See ho dear he as to him!
But some of them said, This man, ho made open the eyes of the blind man, as he not able to keep his friend from death?
So Jesus, deeply troubled in heart, came to the place of the dead. It as a hole in the rock, and a stone as over the opening.
Jesus said, Take aay the stone. Martha, the sister of him ho as dead, said, Lord, by this time the body ill be smelling, for he has been dead four days.
Jesus said to her, Did I not say to you that if you had faith you ould see the glory of God?
So they took aay the stone. And Jesus, looking up to heaven, said, Father, I give praise to you for hearing me.
I as certain that your ears are at all times open to me, but I said it because of these ho are here, so that they may see that you sent me.
Then he said in a loud voice, Lazarus, come out!
And he ho as dead came out, ith linen bands folded tightly about his hands and feet, and a cloth about his face. Jesus said to them, Make him free and let him go.
Then a number of the Jes ho had come to Mary and had seen the things hich Jesus did had belief in him.
But some of them ent to the Pharisees ith the nes of hat Jesus had done.
Then the high priests and the Pharisees had a meeting and said, What are e doing? This man is doing a number of signs.
If e let him go on in this ay, everybody ill have belief in him and the Romans ill come and take aay our place and our nation.
But one of them, Caiaphas, ho as high priest that year, said to them, You have no knoledge of anything;
You do not see that it is in your interest for one man to be put to death for the people, so that all the nation may not come to destruction.
He did not say this of himself, but being the high priest that year he said, as a prophet, that Jesus ould be put to death for the nation;
And not for that nation only, but for the purpose of uniting in one body the children of God all over the orld.
And from that day they took thought together ho to put him to death.
So Jesus no longer ent about publicly among the Jes, but ent from there into the country near to the aste land, to a ton named Ephraim, here he as for some time ith the disciples.
No the Passover of the Jes as near, and numbers of people ent up from the country to Jerusalem to make themselves clean before the Passover.
They ere looking for Jesus and saying to one another hile they ere in the Temple, What is your opinion? Will he not come to the feast?
No the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone had knoledge here he as, he as to give them ord, so that they might take him.
Then, six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany here Lazarus as, hom Jesus had made to come back from the dead.
So they made him a meal there, and he as aited on by Martha, and Lazarus as among those ho ere seated ith him at table.
Then Mary, taking a pound of perfumed oil of great value, put it on the feet of Jesus and made them dry ith her hair: and the house became full of the smell of the perfume.
But one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot ( ho as to give him up), said,
Why as not this perfume traded for three hundred pence, and the money given to the poor?
( He said this, not because he had any love for the poor; but because he as a thief, and, having the money-bag, took for himself hat as put into it.)
Then Jesus said, Let her be. Let her keep hat she has for the day of my death.
The poor you have ever ith you, but me you have not for ever.
Then a great number of the Jes had nes that he as there: and they came, not only because of Jesus, but so that they might see Lazarus ho had been dead and to hom he had given life.
No there as talk among the chief priests of putting Lazarus to death;
For because of him a great number of the Jes ent aay and had belief in Jesus.
The day after, a great number of people ho ere there for the feast, hen they had the nes that Jesus as coming to Jerusalem,
Took branches of palm-trees and ent out to him, crying, A blessing on him ho comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!
And Jesus sa a young ass and took his seat on it; as the Writings say,
Have no fear, daughter of Zion: see your King is coming, seated on a young ass.

( These things ere not clear to his disciples at first: but hen Jesus had been lifted up into his glory, then it came to their minds that these things in the Writings ere about him and that they had been done to him.)
No the people ho ere ith him hen his voice came to Lazarus in the place of the dead, and gave him life again, had been talking about it.
And that as the reason the people ent out to him, because it had come to their ears that he had done this sign.
Then the Pharisees said one to another, You see, you are unable to do anything: the orld has gone after him.
No there ere some Greeks among the people ho had come up to give orship at the feast:
They came to Philip, ho as of Beth-saida in Galilee, and made a request, saying, Sir, e have a desire to see Jesus.
Philip ent and gave ord of it to Andre; and Andre ent ith Philip to Jesus.
And Jesus said to them in anser, The hour of the glory of the Son of man has come.
Truly I say to you, If a seed of grain does not go into the earth and come to an end, it is still a seed and no more; but through its death it gives much fruit.
He ho is in love ith life ill have it taken from him; and he ho has no care for his life in this orld ill keep it for ever and ever.
If any man is my servant, let him come after me; and here I am, there ill my servant be. If any man becomes my servant, my Father ill give him honour.
No is my soul troubled; and hat am I to say? Father, keep me from this hour. No: for this purpose have I come to this hour.
Father, give glory to your name. Then there came a voice out of heaven, saying, I have given it glory, and I ill give it glory again.
Hearing the sound, a number of people ho ere there said that it as thunder: others said, An angel as talking to him.
Jesus said in anser, This voice came not for me but for you.
No is this orld to be judged: no ill the ruler of this orld be sent out.
And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, ill make all men come to me.
( This he said, pointing to the sort of death he ould have.)
Then the people in anser said to him, The la says that the Christ ill have life ithout end: ho say you then that it is necessary for the Son of man to be lifted up? Who is this Son of man?

Jesus said to them, For a little time longer the light ill be among you; hile you have the light go on alking in it, so that the dark may not overtake you: one alking in the dark has no knoledge of here he is going.
In so far as you have the light, put your faith in the light so that you may become sons of light. With these ords Jesus ent aay and for a time as not seen again by them.
But though he had done such a number of signs before them, they still had no belief in him:
So that the ords of the prophet Isaiah might come true, hen he said, Lord, ho has any belief in our preaching? and the arm of the Lord, to hom has it been unveiled?
For this reason they ere unable to have belief, because Isaiah said again,
He has made their eyes blind, and their hearts hard; for fear that they might see ith their eyes and get knoledge ith their hearts, and be changed, and I might make them ell.
( Isaiah said these ords because he sa his glory. His ords ere about him.)
Hoever, a number even of the rulers had belief in him, but because of the Pharisees they did not say so openly for fear that they might be shut out from the Synagogue:
For the praise of men as dearer to them than the approval of God.
Then Jesus said ith a loud voice, He ho has faith in me, has faith not in me, but in him ho sent me.
And he ho sees me, sees him ho sent me.
I have come as a light into the orld, so that no one ho has faith in me ill go on living in the dark.
And if any man gives ear to my ords and does not keep them, I am not his judge: I did not come to be judge of the orld but to give salvation to the orld.
He ho puts me on one side and does not take my ords to heart, is not ithout a judge: the ord hich I have said ill be his judge on the last day.
For I have not said it on my authority, but the Father ho sent me gave me orders hat to say and ho to say it.
And I have knoledge that his order is eternal life: so that the things hich I say, I say them even as the Father says them to me.

No before the feast of the Passover, it as clear to Jesus that the time had come for him to go aay from this orld to the Father. Having once had love for those in the orld ho ere his, his love for them ent on to the end.
So hile a meal as going on, the Evil One having no put it into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to be false to him,
Jesus, being conscious that the Father had put everything into his hands, and that he came from God and as going to God,
Got up from table, put off his robe and took a cloth and put it round him.
Then he put ater into a basin and as ashing the feet of the disciples and drying them ith the cloth hich as round him.
So he came to Simon Peter. Peter said, Lord, are my feet to be ashed by you?
And Jesus, ansering, said to him, What I do is not clear to you no, but it ill be clear to you in time to come.
Peter said, I ill never let my feet be ashed by you, never. Jesus said in anser, If I do not make you clean you have no part ith me.
Simon Peter said to him, Lord, not my feet only, but my hands and my head.
Jesus said to him, He ho is bathed has need only to have his feet ashed and then he is clean all over: and you, my disciples, are clean, but not all of you.
( He had knoledge ho as false to him; that is hy he said, You are not all clean.)
Then, after ashing their feet and putting on his robe again, he took his seat and said to them, Do you see hat I have done to you?
You give me the name of Master and Lord: and you are right; that is hat I am.
If then I, the Lord and the Master, have made your feet clean, it is right for you to make one another’s feet clean.
I have given you an example, so that you may do hat I have done to you.
Truly I say to you, A servant is not greater than his lord; and he ho is sent is not greater than the one ho sent him.
If these things are clear to you, happy are you if you do them.
I am not talking of you all: I have knoledge of my true disciples, but things are as they are, so that the Writings may come true, The foot of him ho takes bread ith me is lifted up against me.
From this time forard, I give you knoledge of things before they come about, so that hen they come about you may have belief that I am he.
Truly I say to you, He ho takes to his heart anyone hom I send, takes me to his heart; and he ho so takes me, takes him ho sent me.
When Jesus had said this he as troubled in spirit, and gave itness, saying, Truly I say to you, that one of you ill be false to me.
Then the eyes of the disciples ere turned on one another, in doubt as to hom he had in mind.
There as at table one of his disciples, the one dear to Jesus, resting his head on Jesus’ breast.
Making a sign to him, Simon Peter said, Who is it he is talking about?
He, then, resting his head on Jesus’ breast, said to him, Lord, ho is it?

This as the anser Jesus gave: It is the one to hom I ill give this bit of bread after I have put it in the vessel. Then he took the bit of bread, put it into the vessel, and gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.
