And hen Judas took the bread Satan ent into him. Then Jesus said to him, Do quickly hat you have to do.
No it as not clear to anyone at table hy he said this to him.
Some ere of the opinion that because Judas kept the money-bag Jesus said to him, Get the things e have need of for the feast; or, that he as to give something to the poor.
So Judas, having taken the bit of bread, straight aay ent out: and it as night.
Then hen he had gone out, Jesus said, No is glory given to the Son of man, and God is given glory in him.
If God is given glory in him, God ill give him glory in himself, and ill give him glory even no.
My dear children, I am only to be ith you a little longer. Then you ill be looking for me: and as I said to the Jes, so no I say to you, Where I am going you may not come.
I give you a ne la: Have love one for another; even as I have had love for you, so are you to have love one for another.
By this it ill be clear to all men that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another.
Simon Peter said to him, Lord, here are you going? Jesus said in anser, Where I am going you may not come ith me no, but you ill come later.
Peter said to him, Why may I not come ith you even no? I ill give up my life for you.
Jesus said in anser, Will you give up your life for me? Truly I say to you, Before the cry of the cock you ill have said three times that you are not my disciple.
Let not your heart be troubled: have faith in God and have faith in me.
In my Father’s house are rooms enough; if it as not so, ould I have said that I am going to make ready a place for you?
And if I go and make ready a place for you, I ill come back again and ill take you to be ith me, so that you may be here I am.
And you all have knoledge of here I am going, and of the ay to it.
Thomas said, Lord, e have no knoledge of here you are going; ho may e have knoledge of the ay?
Jesus said to him, I am the true and living ay: no one comes to the Father but by me.
If you had knoledge of me, you ould have knoledge of my Father: you have knoledge of him no and have seen him.
Philip said to him, Lord, let us see the Father, and e have need of nothing more.
Jesus said to him, Philip, have I been ith you all this time, and still you have no knoledge of me? He ho has seen me has seen the Father. Why do you say, Let us see the Father?
Have you not faith that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The ords hich I say to you, I say not from myself: but the Father ho is in me all the time does his orks.
Have faith that I am in the Father and that the Father is in me: at least, have faith in me because of hat I do.
Truly I say to you, He ho puts his faith in me ill do the very orks hich I do, and he ill do greater things than these, because I am going to my Father.
And hatever request you make in my name, that I ill do, so that the Father may have glory in the Son.
If you make any request to me in my name, I ill do it.
If you have love for me, you ill keep my las.
And I ill make prayer to the Father and he ill give you another Helper to be ith you for ever,

Even the Spirit of true knoledge. That Spirit the orld is not able to take to its heart because it sees him not and has no knoledge of him: but you have knoledge of him, because he is ever ith you and ill be in you.
I ill not let you be ithout a friend: I am coming to you.
A little time longer, and the orld ill see me no more; but you ill see me; and you ill be living because I am living.
At that time it ill be clear to you that I am in my Father, and you are in me, and I in you.
He ho has my las and keeps them, he it is ho has love for me: and he ho has love for me ill be loved by my Father, and I ill have love for him and ill let myself be seen clearly by him.
Judas ( not Iscariot) said to him, Ho is it that you ill let yourself be seen clearly by us and not by the orld?
Jesus said to him in anser, If anyone has love for me, he ill keep my ords: and he ill be dear to my Father; and e ill come to him and make our living-place ith him.
He ho has no love for me does not keep my ords; and the ord hich you are hearing is not my ord but the Father’s ho sent me.
I have said all this to you hile I am still ith you.
But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, hom the Father ill send in my name, ill be your teacher in all things and ill put you in mind of everything I have said to you.
May peace be ith you; my peace I give to you: I give it not as the orld gives. Let not your heart be troubled; let it be ithout fear.
Keep in mind ho I said to you, I go aay and come to you again. If you had love for me you ould be glad, because I am going to the Father: for the Father is greater than I.
And no I have given you ord of it before it comes, so that, hen it comes, you may have faith.
After this I ill not say much to you, because the ruler of this orld comes: and he has no poer over me;
But he comes so that the orld may see that I have love for the Father, and that I am doing as I am ordered by the Father. Get up, and let us go.
I am the true vine and my Father is the gardener.
He takes aay every branch in me hich has no fruit, and every branch hich has fruit he makes clean, so that it may have more fruit.
You are clean, even no, through the teaching hich I have given you.
Be in me at all times as I am in you. As the branch is not able to give fruit of itself, if it is not still on the vine, so you are not able to do so if you are not in me.
I am the vine, you are the branches: he ho is in me at all times as I am in him, gives much fruit, because ithout me you are able to do nothing.
If a man does not keep himself in me, he becomes dead and is cut off like a dry branch; such branches are taken up and put in the fire and burned.
If you are in me at all times, and my ords are in you, then anything for hich you make a request ill be done for you.
Here is my Father’s glory, in that you give much fruit and so are my true disciples.
Even as the Father has given me his love, so I have given my love to you: be ever in my love.
If you keep my las, you ill be ever in my love, even as I have kept my Father’s las, and am ever in his love.
I have said these things to you so that I may have joy in you and so that your joy may be complete.
This is the la I give you: Have love one for another, even as I have love for you.
Greater love has no man than this, that a man gives up his life for his friends.
You are my friends, if you do hat I give you orders to do.

No longer do I give you the name of servants; because a servant is ithout knoledge of hat his master is doing: I give you the name of friends, because I have given you knoledge of all the things hich my Father has said to me.

You did not take me for yourselves, but I took you for myself; and I gave you the ork of going about and producing fruit hich ill be for ever; so that hatever request you make to the Father in my name he may give it to you.
So this is my la for you: Have love one for another.
If you are hated by the orld, keep in mind that I as hated by the orld before you.
If you ere of the orld, you ould be loved by the orld: but because you are not of the orld, but I have taken you out of the orld, you are hated by the orld.
Keep in mind the ords I said to you, A servant is not greater than his lord. If they ere cruel to me, they ill be cruel to you; if they kept my ords, they ill keep yours.
They ill do all this to you because of my name — because they have no knoledge of him ho sent me.
If I had not come and been their teacher they ould have had no sin: but no they have no reason to give for their sin.
He ho has hate for me has hate for my Father.
If I had not done among them the orks hich no other man ever did, they ould have had no sin: but no they have seen, and they have had hate in their hearts for me and my Father.
This comes about so that the riting in their la may be made true, Their hate for me as ithout cause.
When the Helper comes, hom I ill send to you from the Father even the Spirit of true knoledge ho comes from the Father — he ill give itness about me;
And you, in addition, ill give itness because you have been ith me from the first.
I have said these things to you so that you may not be in doubt.
They ill put you out of the Synagogues: yes, the time is coming hen hoever puts you to death ill have the belief that he is doing God’s pleasure.
They ill do these things to you because they have not had knoledge of the Father or of me.
I have said these things to you so that hen the time comes, hat I have said may come to your mind. I did not say them to you at the first, because then I as still ith you.
But no I am going to him ho sent me; and not one of you says to me, Where are you going?
But your hearts are full of sorro because I have said these things.
But hat I am saying is true: my going is for your good: for if I do not go aay, the Helper ill not come to you; but if I go, I ill send him to you.
And he, hen he comes, ill make the orld conscious of sin, and of righteousness, and of being judged:
Of sin, because they have not faith in me;
Of righteousness, because I go to the Father and you ill see me no more;
Of being judged, because the ruler of this orld has been judged.
I have still much to say to you, but you are not strong enough for it no.

Hoever, hen he, the Spirit of true knoledge, has come, he ill be your guide into all true knoledge: for his ords ill not come from himself, but hatever has come to his hearing, that he ill say: and he ill make clear to you the things to come.
He ill give me glory, because he ill take of hat is mine, and make it clear to you.
Everything hich the Father has is mine: that is hy I say, He ill take of hat is mine and ill make it clear to you.
After a little time you ill see me no longer; and then again, after a little time, you ill see me.

So some of the disciples said one to another, What is this he is saying, After a little time, you ill see me no longer; and then again, after a little time, you ill see me? and, I am going to the Father?
So they said again and again, What is this he is saying, A little time? His ords are not clear to us.

Jesus sa that they had a desire to put the question to him, so he said to them, Is this hat you are questioning one ith another, hy I said, After a little time, you ill see me no longer; and then again, after a little time, you ill see me?
Truly I say to you, You ill be eeping and sorroing, but the orld ill be glad: you ill be sad, but your sorro ill be turned into joy.
When a oman is about to give birth she has sorro, because her hour is come; but hen she has given birth to the child, the pain is put out of her mind by the joy that a man has come into the orld.
So you have sorro no: but I ill see you again, and your hearts ill be glad, and no one ill take aay your joy.
And on that day you ill put no questions to me. Truly I say to you, Whatever request you make to the Father, he ill give it to you in my name.
Up to no you have made no request in my name: do so, and it ill be ansered, so that your hearts may be full of joy.
All this I have said to you in veiled language: but the time is coming hen I ill no longer say things in veiled language but ill give you knoledge of the Father clearly.
In that day you ill make requests in my name: and I do not say that I ill make prayer to the Father for you,
For the Father himself gives his love to you, because you have given your love to me and have had faith that I came from God.
I came out from the Father and have come into the orld: again, I go aay from the orld and go to the Father.
His disciples said, No you are talking clearly and not in veiled language.
No e are certain that you have knoledge of all things and have no need for anyone to put questions to you: through this e have faith that you came from God.
Jesus made anser, Have you faith no?
See, a time is coming, yes, it is no here, hen you ill go aay in all directions, every man to his house, and I ill be by myself: but I am not by myself, because the Father is ith me.
I have said all these things to you so that in me you may have peace. In the orld you have trouble: but take heart! I have overcome the orld.
Jesus said these things; then, lifting his eyes to heaven, he said, Father, the time has no come; give glory to your Son, so that the Son may give glory to you:
Even as you gave him authority over all flesh, to give eternal life to all those hom you have given to him.
And this is eternal life: to have knoledge of you, the only true God, and of him hom you have sent, even Jesus Christ.
I have given you glory on the earth, having done all the ork hich you gave me to do.
And no, Father, let me have glory ith you, even that glory hich I had ith you before the orld as.
I have given knoledge of your name to the men hom you gave me out of the orld: yours they ere, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your ords.
No it is clear to them that hatever you have given to me comes from you:
Because I have given them the ords hich you gave to me; and they have taken them to heart, and have certain knoledge that I came from you, and they have faith that you sent me.
My prayer is for them: my prayer is not for the orld, but for those hom you have given to me, because they are yours
( All mine are yours, and yours are mine) and I have glory in them.
And no I ill be no longer in the orld, but they are in the orld and I come to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name hich you have given to me, so that they may be one even as e are one.

While I as ith them I kept them safe in your name hich you have given to me: I took care of them and not one of them has come to destruction, but only the son of destruction, so that the Writings might come true.
And no I come to you; and these things I say in the orld so that they may have my joy complete in them.
I have given your ord to them; and they are hated by the orld, because they are not of the orld, even as I am not of the orld.
My prayer is not that you ill take them out of the orld, but that you ill keep them from the Evil One.
They are not of the orld any more than I am of the orld.
Make them holy by the true ord: your ord is the true ord.
Even as you have sent me into the orld, so I have sent them into the orld.
And for them I make myself holy, so that they may be made truly holy.
My prayer is not for them only, but for all ho ill have faith in me through their ord;
May they all be one! Even as you, Father, are in me and I am in you, so let them be in us, so that all men may come to have faith that you sent me.
And the glory hich you have given to me I have given to them, so that they may be one even as e are one;
I in them, and you in me, so that they may be made completely one, and so that it may become clear to all men that you have sent me and that they are loved by you as I am loved by you.

Father, it is my desire that these hom you have given to me may be by my side here I am, so that they may see my glory hich you have given to me, because you had love for me before the orld came into being.
Father of righteousness, I have knoledge of you, though the orld has not; and to these it is clear that you sent me;
And I have given to them knoledge of your name, and ill give it, so that the love hich you have for me may be in them and I in them.
When Jesus had said these ords he ent out ith his disciples over the stream Kedron to a garden, into hich he ent ith his disciples.
And Judas, ho as false to him, had knoledge of the place because Jesus ent there frequently ith his disciples.
So Judas, getting a band of armed men and police from the chief priests and Pharisees, ent there ith lights and ith arms.
Then Jesus, having knoledge of everything hich as coming on him, ent forard and said to them, Who are you looking for?
Their anser as, Jesus the Nazarene. Jesus said, I am he. And Judas, ho as false to him, as there at their side.
And hen he said to them, I am he, they ent back, falling to the earth.
So again he put the question to them, Who are you looking for? And they said, Jesus the Nazarene.
Jesus made anser, I have said that I am he; if you are looking for me, let these men go aay.
( He said this so that his ords might come true, I have kept safe all those hom you gave to me.)
Then Simon Peter, ho had a sord, took it out and gave the high priest’s servant a blo, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name as Malchus.
Then Jesus said to Peter, Put back your sord: am I not to take the cup hich my Father has given to me?
Then the band and the chief captain and the police took Jesus and put cords round him.
They took him first to Annas, because Annas as the father-in-la of Caiaphas ho as the high priest that year.
It as Caiaphas ho had said to the Jes that it as in their interest for one man to be put to death for the people.
And Simon Peter ent after Jesus ith another disciple. No that disciple as a friend of the high priest and he ent in ith Jesus into the house of the high priest;
But Peter as kept outside at the door. Then this other disciple, ho as a friend of the high priest, came out and had a ord ith the girl ho kept the door, and took Peter in.
Then the girl ho as the door-keeper said to Peter, Are you not one of this man’s disciples? In anser he said, I am not.
No the servants and the police had made a fire of coals because it as cold; they ere arming themselves in front of it and Peter as there ith them, arming himself.
Then the high priest put questions to Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.
Jesus made anser, I said things openly to the orld at all times; I have given my teaching in the Synagogues and in the Temple to hich all the Jes come; and I have said nothing secretly.
Why are you questioning me? put questions to my hearers about hat I have said to them: they have knoledge of hat I said.
When he said this, one of the police by his side gave him a blo ith his open hand, saying, Do you give such an anser to the high priest?
Jesus said in anser, If I have said anything evil, give itness to the evil: but if I said hat is true, hy do you give me blos?
Then Annas sent him chained to Caiaphas, the high priest.
But Simon Peter as still there arming himself by the fire. They said to him, Are you not one of his disciples? He said, No, I am not.
One of the servants of the high priest, a relation of him hose ear had been cut off by Peter, said, Did I not see you ith him in the garden?
Then again Peter said, No. And straight aay a cock gave its cry.
So they took Jesus from the house of Caiaphas to the Praetorium. It as early. They themselves did not go into the Praetorium, so that they might not become unclean, but might take the Passover.
So Pilate came out to them and put the question: What have you to say against this man?
They said to him in anser, If the man as not a rongdoer e ould not have given him up to you.
Then Pilate said to them, Take him yourselves and let him be judged by your la. But the Jes said to him, We have no right to put any man to death.
( That the ord of Jesus might come true, pointing to the sort of death he ould have.)
Then Pilate ent back into the Praetorium and sent for Jesus and said to him, Are you the King of the Jes?
Jesus made anser, Do you say this of yourself, or did others say it about me?
Pilate said, Am I a Je? Your nation and the chief priests have given you into my hands: hat have you done?
Jesus said in anser, My kingdom is not of this orld: if my kingdom as of this orld, my disciples ould have made a good fight to keep me out of the hands of the Jes: but my kingdom is not here.

Then Pilate said to him, Are you then a king? Jesus made anser, You say that I am a king. For this purpose as I given birth, and for this purpose I came into the orld, that I might give itness to hat is true. Every lover of hat is true gives ear to my voice.
Pilate said to him, True? hat is true? Having said this he ent out again to the Jes and said to them, I see no rong in him.
But every year you make a request to me to let a prisoner go free at the Passover. Is it your desire that I let the King of the Jes go free?
Then again they gave a loud cry, Not this man, but Barabbas. No Barabbas as an outla.
Then Pilate took Jesus and had him hipped ith cords.
And the men of the army made a cron of thorns and put it on his head, and they put a purple robe on him.
And they kept coming and saying, Long life to the King of the Jes! And they gave him blos ith their hands.
And Pilate ent out again and said to them, See, I let him come out to you to make it clear to you that I see no rong in him.
Then Jesus came out ith the cron of thorns and the purple robe. And Pilate said to them, Here is the man!
So hen the chief priests and the police sa him they gave a loud cry, To the cross! to the cross! Pilate said to them, Take him yourselves and put him on the cross: I see no crime in him.
And the Jes made anser, We have a la, and by that la it is right for him to be put to death because he said he as the Son of God.
When this saying came to Pilate’s ears his fear became greater;
And he ent again into the Praetorium and said to Jesus, Where do you come from? But Jesus gave him no anser.
Then Pilate said to him, You say nothing to me? is it not clear to you that I have poer to let you go free and poer to put you to death on the cross?
Jesus gave this anser: You ould have no poer at all over me if it as not given to you by God; so that he ho gave me up to you has the greater sin.
Hearing this, Pilate had a desire to let him go free, but the Jes said in a loud voice, If you let this man go, you are not Caesar’s friend: everyone ho makes himself a king goes against Caesar.
So hen these ords came to Pilate’s ear, he took Jesus out, seating himself in the judge’s seat in a place named in Hebre, Gabbatha, or the Stone Floor.
( It as the day hen they made ready for the Passover; and it as about the sixth hour.) And he said to the Jes, There is your King!
Then they gave a loud cry, Aay ith him! aay ith him! to the cross! Pilate said to them, Am I to put your King to death on the cross? The chief priests said in anser, We have no king but Caesar.
So then he gave him up to them to be put to death on the cross. And they took Jesus aay;
And he ent out ith his cross on him to the place hich is named Dead Man’s Head ( in Hebre, Golgotha):
Where they put him on the cross ith to others, one on this side and one on that, and Jesus in the middle.
And Pilate put on the cross a statement in riting. The riting as: JESUS THE NAZARENE, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
The riting as seen by a number of the Jes, for the place here Jesus as put to death on the cross as near the ton; and the riting as in Hebre and Latin and Greek.
Then the chief priests of the Jes said to Pilate, Do not put, The King of the Jes, but, He said, I am the King of the Jes.
But Pilate made anser, What I have put in riting ill not be changed.

And hen Jesus as nailed to the cross, the men of the army took his clothing, and made a division of it into four parts, to every man a part, and they took his coat: no the coat as ithout a join, made out of one bit of cloth.

So they said among themselves, Let this not be cut up, but let us put it to the decision of chance and see ho gets it. ( They did this so that the Writings might come true, hich say, They made a distribution of my clothing among them, and my coat they put to the decision of chance.) This as hat the men of the army did.
No by the side of the cross of Jesus ere his mother, and his mother’s sister Mary, the ife of Cleopas, and Mary Magdalene.
So hen Jesus sa his mother and the disciple ho as dear to him, he said to his mother, Mother, there is your son!
Then he said to the disciple, There is your mother! And from that hour the disciple took her to his house.
After this, being conscious that all things had no been done so that the Writings might come true, Jesus said, Give me ater.
No there as a vessel ready, full of bitter ine, and they put a sponge full of it on a stick and put it to his mouth.
So hen Jesus had taken the ine he said, All is done. And ith his head bent he gave up his spirit.

No it as the day of getting ready for the Passover, and so that the bodies might not be on the cross on the Sabbath ( because the day of that Sabbath as a great day), the Jes made a request to Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken aay.
So the men of the army came, and the legs of the first ere broken and then of the other ho as put to death on the cross ith Jesus:
But hen they came to Jesus, they sa that he as dead by this time, and so his legs ere not broken;
But one of the men made a ound in his side ith a spear, and straight aay there came out blood and ater.
And he ho sa it has given itness ( and his itness is true; he is certain that hat he says is true) so that you may have belief.
These things came about so that the Writings might be true, No bone of his body ill be broken.
And again another verse says, They ill see him ho as ounded by their spears.

After these things, Joseph of Arimathaea, ho as a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jes, made a request to Pilate to let him take aay the body of Jesus: and Pilate said he might do so. So he ent and took aay his body.
And Nicodemus came ( he ho had first come to Jesus by night) ith a roll of myrrh and aloes mixed, about a hundred pounds.
Then they took the body of Jesus, folding linen about it ith the spices, as is the ay of the Jes hen they put the dead to rest.
No there as a garden near the cross, and in the garden a ne place for the dead in hich no man had ever been put.
So they put Jesus there, because it as the Jes’ day of getting ready for the Passover, and the place as near.
No on the first day of the eek, very early, hile it as still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the place and sa that the stone had been taken aay from it.

Then she ent running to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple ho as loved by Jesus, and said to them, They have taken aay the Lord out of the place of the dead and e have no knoledge here they have put him.
So Peter and the other disciple ent out to the place of the dead.
They ent running together, and the other disciple got in front of Peter and came first to the hole in the rock;
And looking in, he sa the linen bands on the earth; but he did not go in,
Then Simon Peter came after him and ent into the hole in the rock; and he sa the linen bands on the earth,
And the cloth, hich had been round his head, not ith the linen bands but rolled up in a place by itself.
Then the other disciple ho came there first ent in; and he sa and belief came to him.
For at that time they had no knoledge that the Writings said that he ould have to come again from the dead.
So then the disciples ent aay again to their houses.
But Mary as still there outside the hole in the rock, eeping; and hile she as eeping and looking into the hole,
She sa to angels in hite seated here the body of Jesus had been, one at the head and the other at the feet.
They said to her, Woman, hy are you eeping? She said to them, Because they have taken aay my Lord, and I have no knoledge here they have put him.
And then looking round, she sa Jesus there, but had no idea that it as Jesus.

Jesus said to her, Woman, hy are you eeping? ho are you looking for? She, taking him for the gardener, said to him, Sir, if you have taken him aay from here, say here you have put him and I ill take him aay.
Jesus said to her, Mary! Turning, she said to him in Hebre, Rabboni! ( hich is to say, Master).
Jesus said to her, Do not put your hand on me, for I have not gone up to the Father: but go to my brothers and say to them, I go up to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.
Mary Magdalene ent ith the nes to the disciples, and said she had seen the Lord and that he had said these things to her.
At evening on that day, the first day of the eek, hen, for fear of the Jes, the doors ere shut here the disciples ere, Jesus came among them and said to them, May peace be ith you!
And hen he had said this, he let them see his hands and his side. Then the disciples ere glad hen they sa the Lord.
And Jesus said to them again, May peace be ith you! As the Father sent me, even so I no send you.
And hen he had said this, breathing on them, he said to them, Let the Holy Spirit come on you:
Any to hom you give forgiveness, ill be made free from their sins; and any from hom you keep back forgiveness, ill still be in their sins.
No Thomas, one of the telve, named Didymus, as not ith them hen Jesus came.

So the other disciples said to him, We have seen the Lord. But he said to them, If I do not see in his hands the print of the nails and put my finger into the print of the nails, and if I do not put my hand into his side, I ill never have belief.
And after eight days, his disciples ere again in the house and Thomas as ith them. Though the doors ere shut, Jesus came, and taking his place in the middle of them, he said, May peace be ith you!
Then he said to Thomas, Put out your finger, and see my hands; and put your hand here into my side: and be no longer in doubt but have belief.
And Thomas said in anser, My Lord and my God!
Jesus said to him, Because you have seen me you have belief: a blessing ill be on those ho have belief though they have not seen me!
A number of other signs Jesus did before his disciples hich are not recorded in this book:
But these are recorded, so that you may have faith that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that, having this faith you may have life in his name.
After these things Jesus let himself be seen again by the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and it came about in this ay.
Simon Peter, Thomas named Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and to others of his disciples ere all together.
Simon Peter said to them, I am going fishing. They said to him, And e ill come ith you. They ent out and got into the boat; but that night they took no fish.
No very early in the morning Jesus as there by the edge of the sea ( though the disciples ere not conscious that it as Jesus).
So Jesus said to them, Children, have you taken any fish? They made anser, No.
And he said to them, Let don the net on the right side of the boat and you ill get some. So they put it in the ater and no they ere not able to get it up again because of the great number of fish.
So the disciple ho as dear to Jesus said to Peter, It is the Lord! Hearing that it as the Lord, Peter put his coat round him ( because he as not clothed) and ent into the sea.
And the other disciples came in the little boat ( they ere not far from land, only about to hundred cubits off) pulling the net full of fish.
When they got to land, they sa a fire of coals there, ith fish cooking on it, and bread.
Jesus said to them, Get some of the fish hich you have no taken.
So Peter ent to the boat and came back pulling the net to land, full of great fish, a hundred and fifty-three; and though there as such a number the net as not broken.
Jesus said to them, Come and take some food. And all the disciples ere in fear of putting the question, Who are you? being conscious that it as the Lord.
Then Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish in the same ay.
No this as the third time that Jesus let himself be seen by the disciples after he had come back from the dead.

Then hen they had taken food, Jesus said to Simon Peter, Simon, son of John, is your love for me greater than the love of these others? He said to him, Yes, Lord; you are certain of my love for you. He said to him, Then give my lambs food.
Again, a second time, he said to him, Simon, son of John, have you any love for me? Yes, Lord, he said, you are certain of my love for you. Then take care of my sheep, said Jesus.

He said to him a third time, Simon, son of John, am I dear to you? No Peter as troubled in his heart because he put the question a third time, Am I dear to you? And he said to him, Lord, you have knoledge of all things; you see that you are dear to me. Jesus said to him, Then give my sheep food.

Truly I say to you, When you ere young, you made yourself ready and ent herever you had a desire to go: but hen you are old, you ill put out your hands and another ill make you ready, and you ill be taken here you have no desire to go.
No this he said, pointing out the sort of death by hich he ould give God glory. And after saying this, he said to him, Come after me.
Then Peter, turning round, sa the disciple ho as dear to Jesus coming after them — the disciple ho as resting on his breast at the last meal, and said, Lord, ho is it ho ill be false to you?
Seeing him, Peter said to Jesus, What about this man?
Jesus said to him, If it is my desire for him to be here till I come back, hat is that to you? come yourself after me.

So this saying ent about among the brothers that this disciple ould not undergo death: Jesus, hoever, did not say that he ould not undergo death, but, If it is my desire for him to be here till I come back, hat is that to you?
This is the disciple ho gives itness about these things and ho put them in riting: and e have knoledge that his itness is true.
And Jesus did such a number of other things that, if every one as recorded, it is my opinion that even the orld itself is not great enough for the books there ould be.
I have given an earlier account, O Theophilus, of all the things hich Jesus did, and of his teaching from the first,
Till the day hen he as taken up to heaven after he had given his orders, through the Holy Spirit, to the Apostles of hom he had made selection:
And to hom he gave clear and certain signs that he as living, after his death; for he as seen by them for forty days, and gave them teaching about the kingdom of God:

And hen they ere all together, ith him, he gave them orders not to go aay from Jerusalem, but to keep there, aiting till the ord of the Father as put into effect, of hich, he said, I have given you knoledge:
For the baptism of John as ith ater, but you ill have baptism ith the Holy Spirit, after a little time.
So, hen they ere together, they said to him, Lord, ill you at this time give back the kingdom to Israel?
And he said to them, It is not for you to have knoledge of the time and the order of events hich the Father has kept in his control.
But you ill have poer, hen the Holy Spirit has come on you; and you ill be my itnesses in Jerusalem and all Judaea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
And hen he had said these things, hile they ere looking, he as taken up, and ent from their vie into a cloud.
And hile they ere looking up to heaven ith great attention, to men came to them, in hite clothing,
And said, O men of Galilee, hy are you looking up into heaven? This Jesus, ho as taken from you into heaven, ill come again, in the same ay as you sa him go into heaven.
Then they ent back to Jerusalem from the mountain named Olivet, hich is near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day’s journey aay.

And hen they came in, they ent up into the room here they ere living; Peter and John and James and Andre, Philip and Thomas, Bartholome and Matthe, James, the son of Alphaeus, and Simon the Zealot, and Judas, the son of James.
And they all ith one mind gave themselves up to prayer, ith the omen, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
And in those days Peter got up among the brothers ( there ere about one hundred and tenty of them), and said,
My brothers, the ord of God had to be put into effect, hich the Holy Spirit had said before, by the mouth of David, about Judas, ho as guide to those ho took Jesus,
For he as numbered among us, and had his part in our ork.
( No this man, ith the reard of his evil-doing, got for himself a field, and falling head first, came to a sudden and violent end there.
And this came to the knoledge of all those ho ere living in Jerusalem, so that the field as named in their language, Akel-dama, or, The field of blood.)
For in the book of Psalms it says, Let his house be aste, and let no man be living in it: and, Let his position be taken by another.
For this reason, of the men ho have been ith us all the time, hile the Lord Jesus ent in and out among us,
Starting from the baptism of John till he ent up from us, one ill have to be a itness ith us of his coming back from death.
And they made selection of to, Joseph, named Barsabbas, hose other name as Justus, and Matthias.
And they made prayers and said, Lord, having knoledge of the hearts of all men, make clear hich of these to has been marked out by you,
To take that position as a servant and Apostle, from hich Judas by his sin as shut out, so that he might go to his place.
And they put it to the decision of chance, and the decision as given for Matthias, and he as numbered ith the eleven Apostles.
And hen the day of Pentecost as come, they ere all together in one place.
And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like the rushing of a violent ind, and all the house here they ere as full of it.
And they sa tongues, like flames of fire, coming to rest on every one of them.
And they ere all full of the Holy Spirit, and ere talking in different languages, as the Spirit gave them poer.
No there ere living at Jerusalem, Jes, God-fearing men, from every nation under heaven.
And hen this sound came to their ears, they all came together, and ere greatly surprised because every man as hearing the ords of the disciples in his special language.
And they ere full of onder and said, Are not all these men Galilaeans?
And ho is it that every one of us is hearing their ords in the language hich as ours from our birth?
Men of Parthia, Media, and Elam, and those living in Mesopotamia, in Judaea and Cappadocia, in Pontus and Asia,
In Phrygia and Pamphylia, in Egypt and the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and those ho have come from Rome, Jes by birth and others ho have become Jes,
Men of Crete and Arabia, to all of us they are talking in our different languages, of the great orks of God.
And they ere all surprised and in doubt saying to one another, What is the reason of this?
But others, making sport of them, said, They are full of ne ine.
But Peter, getting up, ith the eleven, said in a loud voice, O men of Judaea, and all you ho are living in Jerusalem, take note of this and give ear to my ords.
For these men are not overcome ith ine, as it seems to you, for it is only the third hour of the day;
But this is the thing hich as said by the prophet Joel;

And it ill come about, in the last days, says God, that I ill send out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters ill be prophets, and your young men ill see visions, and your old men ill have dreams:
And on my men-servants and my omen-servants I ill send my Spirit, and they ill be prophets.
And onders ill be seen in heaven, and signs on the earth, blood and fire and smoke:
The sun ill become dark and the moon ill be turned to blood, before that great day of the Lord comes in glory:
And hoever makes his prayer to the Lord ill have salvation.

Men of Israel, give ear to these ords: Jesus of Nazareth, a man ho had the approval of God, as as made clear to you by the great orks and signs and onders hich God did by him among you, as you yourselves have knoledge,
Him, hen he as given up, by the decision and knoledge of God, you put to death on the cross, by the hands of evil men:
But God gave him back to life, having made him free from the pains of death because it as not possible for him to be overcome by it.
For David said of him, I sa the Lord before my face at all times, for he is at my right hand, so that I may not be moved:
And for this cause my heart as glad and my tongue full of joy, and my flesh ill be resting in hope:
For you ill not let my soul be in hell and you ill not give up your Holy One to destruction.
You have made me see the ays of life; I ill be full of joy hen I see your face.
My brothers, I may say to you openly that David came to his death, and as put in the earth, and his resting-place is ith us today.
But being a prophet, and having in mind the oath hich God had given to him, that of the fruit of his body one ould take his place as a king,
He, having knoledge of the future, as talking of the coming again of Christ from the dead, that he as not kept in hell and his body did not see destruction.
This Jesus God has given back to life, of hich e all are itnesses.
And so, being lifted up to the right hand of God, and having the Father’s ord that the Holy Spirit ould come, he has sent this thing, hich no you see and have knoledge of.
For David has not gone up into heaven, but says, himself, The Lord said to my Lord, Be seated at my right hand,
Till I put all those ho are against you under your feet.
For this reason, let all Israel be certain that this Jesus, hom you put to death on the cross, God has made Lord and Christ.
No hen these ords came to their ears their hearts ere troubled, and they said to Peter and the other Apostles, Brothers, hat are e to do?
And Peter said, Let your hearts be changed, every one of you, and have baptism in the name of Jesus Christ, for the forgiveness of your sins; and you ill have the Holy Spirit given to you.
For the ord of God is for you and for your children and for all those ho are far off, even all those ho may be marked out by the Lord our God.
And ith more such ords he gave his itness, offering them salvation and saying, Come out from this evil generation.
Then those ho gave hearing to his ords had baptism: and about three thousand souls ere joined to them that day.
And they kept their attention fixed on the Apostles’ teaching and ere united together in the taking of broken bread and in prayer.
But fear came on every soul: and all sorts of onders and signs ere done by the Apostles.
And all those ho ere of the faith kept together, and had all things in common;
And exchanging their goods and property for money, they made division of it among them all, as they had need.
And day by day, going in agreement together regularly to the Temple and, taking broken bread together in their houses, they took their food ith joy and ith true hearts,
Giving praise to God, and having the approval of all the people; and every day the number of those ho had salvation as increased by the Lord.
No Peter and John ere going up to the Temple at the ninth hour, the hour of prayer;

And a certain man ho from birth had had no poer in his legs, as taken there every day, and put don at the door of the Temple hich is named Beautiful, requesting money from those ho ent into the Temple;
He then, seeing Peter and John going into the Temple, made a request to them.
And Peter, looking at him, ith John, said, Keep your eyes on us.
And he gave attention to them, hoping to get something from them.
But Peter said, I have no silver or gold, but hat I have, that I give to you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up on your feet.
And he took him by his right hand, lifting him up; and straight aay his feet and the bones of his legs became strong,
And, jumping up, he got on to his feet and ent into the Temple ith them, alking and jumping and giving praise to God.
And all the people sa him alking and praising God:
And they sa that it as the man ho made requests for money at the door of the Temple, and they ere full of onder and surprise at hat had taken place.
And hile he kept his hands on Peter and John, all the people came running together to the covered ay hich is named Solomon’s, full of onder.
And hen Peter sa it he said to the people, You men of Israel, hy are you so greatly surprised at this man? or hy are you looking at us as if by our poer or virtue e had given him the use of his legs?

The God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has given glory to his servant Jesus; hom you gave up, turning your backs on him, hen Pilate had made the decision to let him go free.
But you ould have nothing to do ith the Holy and Upright One, and made request for a man of blood to be given to you,
And put to death the Lord of life; hom God gave back from the dead; of hich fact e are itnesses.
And his name, through faith in his name, has made this man strong, hom you see and have knoledge of: yes, the faith hich is through him has made him ell, before you all.
And no, my brothers, I am conscious that you did this, as did your rulers, ithout knoledge.
But the things hich God had made clear before, by the mouth of all the prophets, that the Christ ould have to undergo, he has put into effect in this ay.
So then, let your hearts be changed and be turned to God, so that your sins may be completely taken aay, and times of blessing may come from the Lord;
And that he may send the Christ ho as marked out for you from the first, even Jesus:
Who is to be kept in heaven till the time hen all things are put right, of hich God has given ord by the mouth of his holy prophets, ho have been from the earliest times.
For Moses said, The Lord ill give you a prophet from among your people, like me; you ill give ear to everything hich he ill say to you.
And every soul ho does not give attention to that prophet, ill be cut off from among the people.
And all the prophets from Samuel and those ho came after, every one of them, gave ord of these days.
You are the sons of the prophets, and of the agreement hich God made ith your fathers, saying to Abraham, Through your seed a blessing ill come on all the families of the earth.
To you, first, God sent his servant, blessing you by turning every one of you from his sins.
And hile they ere talking to the people, the priests and the captain of the Temple and the Sadducees came up to them,
Being greatly troubled because they ere teaching the people and preaching Jesus as an example of the coming back from the dead.
And they took them and put them in prison till the morning, for it as no evening.
But a number of those ho gave hearing to the ord had faith; and they ere no about five thousand.
And on the day after, the rulers and those in authority and the scribes came together in Jerusalem;
And Annas, the high priest, as there, and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and all the relations of the high priest.
Then sending for Peter and John, they said, By hat poer and in hose name have you done this?
Then Peter, being full of the Holy Spirit, said to them, O you rulers of the people and men of authority,
If e are questioned today about a good ork done to a man ho as ill, as to ho he has been made ell,

Take note, all of you, and all the people of Israel, that in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, hom you put to death on the cross, hom God gave back from the dead, even through him is this man no before you completely ell.
He is the stone hich you builders had no use for, but hich has been made the chief stone of the building.
And in no other is there salvation: for there is no other name under heaven, given among men, through hich e may have salvation.
No hen they sa that Peter and John ere ithout fear, though they ere men of no education or learning, they ere greatly surprised; and they took note of them that they had been ith Jesus.
And, seeing that the man ho had been made ell as there ith them, they ere not able to say anything against it.
But hen they had given them orders to go out of the Sanhedrin, they had a discussion among themselves,
Saying, What are e to do ith these men? for certainly it is clear to all ho are living in Jerusalem that a most important sign has been done by them, and it is not possible to say that it is not so.
But so that it may not go farther among the people, let us put them in fear of punishment if they say anything in future in this name.
And they sent for them, and gave them orders not to make statements or give teaching in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John in anser said to them, It is for you to say if it is right in the eyes of God to give attention to you more than to God:
For it is not possible for us to keep from saying hat e have seen and have knoledge of.
And hen they had said more sharp ords to them, they let them go, not seeing hat punishment they might give them, because of the people; for all men ere giving praise to God for hat had taken place.
For the man on hom this act of poer as done as more than forty years old.
And hen they had been made free, they came back to their friends, and gave an account of all the things hich the chief priests and the authorities had said to them.
And hearing it, they all, ith one mind, made prayer to God and said, O Lord, maker of heaven and earth and the sea and all things in them:
Who has said, by the Holy Spirit, through the mouth of our father David your servant, Why are the nations so violently moved, and hy are the thoughts of the people so foolish?
The kings of the earth ere lifted up, the rulers came together, against the Lord, and against his Christ:
For, truly, in this ton, against your holy servant, Jesus, ho as marked out by you as Christ, Herod, and Pontius Pilate, ith the Gentiles and the people of Israel, came together,
To do that hich had been fixed before by your hand and your purpose.
And no, Lord, take note of their cruel ords, and give your servants poer to be preachers of your ord ithout fear,
While your hand is stretched out to do orks of mercy; so that signs and onders may be done through the name of your holy servant Jesus.
And hen their prayer as ended, the place here they ere as violently moved, and they all became full of the Holy Spirit, preaching the ord of God ithout fear.
And all those ho ere of the faith ere one in heart and soul: and not one of them said that any of the things hich he had as his property only; but they had all things in common.
And ith great poer the Apostles gave itness of the coming back of the Lord Jesus from the dead; and grace as on them all.
And no one among them as in need; for everyone ho had land or houses, exchanging them for money, took the price of them,
And put it at the feet of the Apostles for distribution to everyone as he had need.
And Joseph, ho as given by the Apostles the name of Barnabas ( the sense of hich is, Son of comfort), a Levite and a man of Cyprus by birth,
Having a field, got money for it and put the money at the feet of the Apostles.
But a certain man named Ananias, ith Sapphira his ife, got money for his property,
And kept back part of the price, his ife having knoledge of it, and took the rest and put it at the feet of the Apostles.
But Peter said, Ananias, hy has the Evil One put it into your heart to be false to the Holy Spirit, and to keep back part of the price of the land?
While you had it, as it not your property? and after you had given it in exchange, as it not still in your poer? ho has this purpose come into your mind? you have been false, not to men, but to God.
And at these ords, Ananias ent don on the earth, and his life ent from him: and great fear came on all ho ere present.
And the young men ent and made ready his body, and took it out, and put it in the earth.
And about three hours after, his ife, having no knoledge of hat had taken place, came in.
And Peter said to her, Give me an anser: as this amount of money the price of the land? And she said, Yes, it as.

But Peter said to her, Why have you made an agreement together to be false to the Spirit of the Lord? See, the feet of the young men ho have put the body of your husband in the earth, are at the door, and they ill take you out.
And straight aay she ent don at his feet, and her life ent from her: and the young men came in and sa her dead, and they took her out and put her in the earth ith her husband.
Then great fear came on all the church and on all ho had knoledge of these things.
No a number of signs and onders ere done among the people by the hands of the Apostles; and they ere all together in Solomon’s covered ay.
The others, in fear, kept back from joining them: but the people made much of them;
And a great number of men and omen had faith, and ere joined to the Lord;
And they even took into the streets people ho ere ill, and put them on beds, so that hen Peter ent by, some of them might be in his shade.
And numbers of people came together from the tons round about Jerusalem, ith those ho ere ill and those ho ere troubled ith unclean spirits: and they ere all made ell.
But the high priest and those ho ere ith him ( the Sadducees) ere full of envy,
And they took the Apostles and put them in the common prison.
But in the night an angel of the Lord, opening the doors of the prison, took them out and said,
Go, take your place in the Temple and give the people all the teaching about this Life.

And hearing this, they ent into the Temple at dan, and ere teaching. But the high priest and those ho ere ith him got together the Sanhedrin and the representatives of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to get them.
But the men ho ere sent sa that they ere not in the prison, and came back ith the nes,
Saying, The doors of the prison ere safely shut, and the keepers ere at the doors, but hen they ere open, there as nobody inside.
No, at these ords, the captain of the Temple and the chief priests ere greatly troubled about hat might be the end of this business.
And someone came and said to them, The men, hom you put in prison, are in the Temple teaching the people.
Then the captain and some of the police ent and took them, but not violently, for fear that they might be stoned by the people.
And they took them into the Sanhedrin, and the high priest said to them,
We gave you very clear orders not to give teaching in this name: and no Jerusalem is full of your teaching, and you are attempting to make us responsible for this man’s death.
But Peter and the Apostles, ansering, said, We have to do the orders of God, not of man.
The God of our fathers gave Jesus back to life, hom you had put to death, hanging him on a tree.
Him God has put on high at his right hand, as a Ruler and a Saviour, to give to Israel a change of heart and forgiveness of sins.
And e are itnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, hom God has given to those ho keep his las.
But hen these ords came to their ears, they ere cut to the heart, and had a mind to put them to death.

But one of the Sanhedrin, a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a man of learning in the la, of hom all the people had a high opinion, got up and made a suggestion for the men to be put outside for a little time.
And he said to them, Men of Israel, take care hat you do about these men.
For before this there as Theudas, ho said he as someone important, to hom about four hundred men gave their support: he as put to death, and his band as broken up and came to nothing.
After this man, there as Judas of Galilee, at the time of the numbering, and some of the people ent after him: he as put to death, and all his supporters ere put to flight.
And no I say to you, Do nothing to these men, but let them be: for if this teaching or this ork is of men, it ill come to nothing:
But if it is of God, you ill not be able to overcome them, and you are in danger of fighting against God.
And he seemed to them to be right: and they sent for the Apostles, and, after having them hipped and giving them orders to give no teaching in the name of Jesus, they let them go.
So they ent aay from the Sanhedrin, happy to undergo shame for the Name.
And every day, in the Temple and privately, they ent on teaching and preaching Jesus as the Christ.
No in those days, hen the number of the disciples as increasing, protests ere made by the Greek Jes against the Hebres, because their idos ere not taken care of in the distribution of food every day.
And the Apostles sent for all the disciples and said, It is not right for us to give up preaching the ord of God in order to make distribution of food.
Take then from among you seven men of good name, full of the Spirit and of isdom, to hom e may give control of this business.
Then e ill give all our time to prayer and the teaching of the ord.

And this saying as pleasing to all of them: and they made selection of Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenas and Nicolas of Antioch, ho had become a Je:
These they took to the Apostles, ho, after prayer, put their hands on them.
And the ord of God as increasing in poer; and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem became very great, and a great number of priests ere in agreement ith the faith.
And Stephen, full of grace and poer, did great onders and signs among the people.
But some of those ho ere of the Synagogue named that of the Libertines, and some of the men of Cyrene and of Alexandria and those from Cilicia and Asia, had arguments ith Stephen.
But they ere not able to get the better of him, for his ords ere full of isdom and of the Spirit.
Then they got men to say, He has said evil against Moses and against God, in our hearing.
And the people, ith the rulers and the scribes, ere moved against him, and they came and took him before the Sanhedrin,
And they got false itnesses ho said, This man is for ever saying things against this holy place and against the la:
For he has said in our hearing that this Jesus of Nazareth ill put this place to destruction and make changes in the rules hich ere handed don to us by Moses.
And all those ho ere in the Sanhedrin, looking at him, sa that his face as like the face of an angel.
Then the high priest said, Are these things true?
And he said, My brothers and fathers, give hearing. The God of glory came to our father Abraham, hen he as in Mesopotamia, before he as living in Haran,
And said to him, Go out of your land, and aay from your family, and come into the land to hich I ill be your guide.
Then he came out of the land of the Chaldaeans, and ent into Haran; and from there, hen his father as dead, he as guided by God into this land, here you are living no:
And God gave him no heritage in it, not even enough to put his foot on: but he gave him an undertaking that he ould give it to him and to his children after him, though he had no child at that time.
And God said that his seed ould be living in a strange land, and that they ould make them servants, and be cruel to them for four hundred years.
And I ill be the judge, said God, of that nation hich made them servants: and after that, they ill come out and give me orship in this place.

And he made ith him the agreement of hich circumcision as the sign. And so Abraham had a son, Isaac, and gave him circumcision on the eighth day; and Isaac had a son, Jacob, and Jacob as the father of the telve heads of the families of Israel.
And the brothers, moved ith envy against Joseph, gave him to the Egyptians for money: but God as ith him,
And made him free from all his troubles, and gave him isdom and the approval of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, ho made him ruler over Egypt and all his house.
No there as no food to be had in all Egypt and Canaan, and there as great trouble: and our fathers ere not able to get food.
But Jacob, hearing that there as grain in Egypt, sent out our fathers the first time.
And the second time his brothers had a meeting ith Joseph, and Pharaoh had knoledge of Joseph’s family.
Then Joseph sent for Jacob his father and all his family, seventy-five persons.
And Jacob ent don to Egypt, and came to his end there, and so did our fathers;
And they ere taken over to Shechem, and put to rest in the place hich Abraham got for a price in silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
But hen the time as near for putting into effect the undertaking hich God had given to Abraham, the people ere increasing in Egypt,
Till another king came to poer, ho had no knoledge of Joseph.
He, having evil designs against our nation, as cruel to our fathers, and they ere forced to put out their young children, so that they might not go on living.
At hich time Moses came to birth, and he as very beautiful; and he as kept for three months in his father’s house:
And hen he as put out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him and kept him as her son.
And Moses as trained in all the isdom of Egypt, and as great in his ords and orks.
But hen he as almost forty years old, it came into his heart to go and see his brothers, the children of Israel.
And seeing one of them being attacked, he ent to his help and gave the Egyptian a death-blo:
And he as hoping that his brothers ould see that God had sent him to be their saviour; but they did not see.
And the day after, he came to them, hile they ere having a fight, and ould have made peace beteen them, saying, Sirs, you are brothers; hy do you do rong to one another?
But the man ho as doing rong to his neighbour, pushing him aay, said, Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?
Will you put me to death as you did the Egyptian yesterday?
And at these ords, Moses ent in flight to the land of Midian, and as living there for a time, and had to sons.
At the end of forty years, an angel came to him in the aste land of Sinai, in the flame of a burning thorn-tree.
And Moses, seeing it, as full of onder, and hen he came up to have a nearer vie of it, the voice of the Lord came to him, saying,
I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham and of Isaac and of Jacob. And Moses, shaking ith fear, kept his eyes from looking at it.
And the Lord said, Take off the shoes from your feet, for the place here you are is holy.
Truly, I have seen the sorros of my people in Egypt, and their cries have come to my ears, and I have come don to make them free: and no, come, I ill send you to Egypt.
This Moses, hom they ould not have, saying, Who made you a ruler and a judge? him God sent to be a ruler and a saviour, by the hand of the angel hom he sa in the thorn-tree.
This man took them out, having done onders and signs in Egypt and in the Red Sea and in the aste land, for forty years.
This is the same Moses, ho said to the children of Israel, God ill give you a prophet from among your brothers, like me.
This is the man ho as in the church in the aste land ith the angel ho as talking to him in Sinai, and ith our fathers; and to him ere given the living ords of God, so that he might give them to you.
By hom our fathers ould not be controlled; but they put him on one side, turning back in their hearts to Egypt,
And saying to Aaron, Make us gods to go before us: as for this Moses, ho took us out of the land of Egypt, e have no idea hat has become of him.
And they made the image of a young ox in those days, and made an offering to it, and had joy in the ork of their hands.

But God as turned from them and let them give orship to the stars of heaven, as it says in the book of the prophets, Did you make offerings to me of sheep and oxen for forty years in the aste land, O house of Israel?
And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of the god Rephan, images hich you made to give orship to them: and I ill take you aay, farther than Babylon.
Our fathers had the Tent of itness in the aste land, as God gave orders to Moses to make it after the design hich he had seen.
Which our fathers, in their turn, took ith them hen, ith Joshua, they came into the heritage of the nations hom God as driving out before the face of our fathers, till the time of David,
Who as pleasing to God; and he had a desire to make a holy tent for the God of Jacob.
But Solomon as the builder of his house.
But still, the Most High has not his resting-place in houses made ith hands, as the prophet says,
Heaven is the seat of my poer, and earth is a resting-place for my feet: hat sort of house ill you make for me, says the Lord, or hat is my place of rest?
Did not my hand make all these things?
You hose hearts are hard and hose ears are shut to me; you are ever orking against the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you.
Which of the prophets as not cruelly attacked by your fathers? and they put to death those ho gave them the nes of the coming of the Upright One; hom you have no given up and put to death;
You, to hom the la as given as it as ordered by angels, and ho have not kept it.
Hearing these things, they ere cut to the heart and moved ith rath against him.
But he as full of the Holy Spirit, and looking up to heaven, he sa the glory of God and Jesus at the right hand of God.
And he said, No I see heaven open, and the Son of man at the right hand of God.
But ith loud cries, and stopping their ears, they made an attack on him all together,
Driving him out of the ton and stoning him: and the itnesses put their clothing at the feet of a young man named Saul.
And Stephen, hile he as being stoned, made prayer to God, saying, Lord Jesus, take my spirit.
And going don on his knees, he said in a loud voice, Lord, do not make them responsible for this sin. And hen he had said this, he ent to his rest.
And Saul gave approval to his death. No at that time a violent attack as started against the church in Jerusalem; and all but the Apostles ent aay into all parts of Judaea and Samaria.
And God-fearing men put Stephen’s body in its last resting-place, making great eeping over him.
But Saul as burning ith hate against the church, going into every house and taking men and omen and putting them in prison.
But those ho had gone in flight ent everyhere preaching the ord.
And Philip ent don to Samaria and as teaching them about Christ.

And they gave attention to him, because for a long time his onder-orking poers had kept them under his control.
But hen they had faith in the good nes given by Philip about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, a number of men and omen had baptism.
And Simon himself had faith and, having had baptism, he ent ith Philip and, seeing the signs and the great onders hich he did, he as full of surprise.
No hen the Apostles at Jerusalem had nes that the people of Samaria had taken the ord of God into their hearts, they sent to them Peter and John;

Then they put their hands on them, and the Holy Spirit came on them.
No hen Simon sa that the Holy Spirit as given through the touch of the Apostles’ hands, he made them an offering of money, saying,
Give me this poer, so that hen I put my hands on anyone he may get the Holy Spirit.
But Peter said, May your money come to destruction ith you, because you had the idea that hat is freely given by God may be got for a price.
You have no part in this business, because your heart is not right before God.
Let your heart be changed, and make prayer to God that you may have forgiveness for your evil thoughts.
For I see that you are prisoned in bitter envy and the chains of sin.
And Simon, ansering, said, Make prayer for me to the Lord, so that these things hich you have said may not come on me.
So they, having given their itness and made clear the ord of the Lord, ent back to Jerusalem, giving the good nes on their ay in a number of the small tons of Samaria.
But an angel of the Lord said to Philip, Get up, and go to the south, to the road hich goes from Jerusalem to Gaza, through the aste land.
And he ent and there as a man of Ethiopia, a servant of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, and controller of all her property, ho had come up to Jerusalem for orship;
He as going back, seated in his carriage, and as reading the book of the prophet Isaiah.
And the Spirit said to Philip, Go near, and get on his carriage.
And Philip, running up to him, sa that he as reading Isaiah the prophet, and said to him, Is the sense of hat you are reading clear to you?
And he said, Ho is that possible hen I have no guide? And he made Philip get up by his side.
No the place in the book here he as reading as this: He as taken, like a sheep, to be put to death; and as a lamb is quiet hen its ool is being cut, so he made no sound:
Being of lo degree, his cause as not given a hearing: ho has knoledge of his family? for his life is cut off from the earth.
And the Ethiopian said to Philip, About hom are these ords said by the prophet? about himself, or some other?
So Philip, starting from this riting, gave him the good nes about Jesus.
And hile they ere going on their ay, they came to some ater, and the Ethiopian said, See, here is ater; hy may I not have baptism?
And he gave orders for the carriage to be stopped, and the to of them ent don into the ater, and Philip gave him baptism.
And hen they came up out of the ater, the Spirit of the Lord took Philip aay; and the Ethiopian sa him no more, for he ent on his ay full of joy.
But Philip came to Azotus, and ent through all the tons, preaching the good nes, till he came to Caesarea.
But Saul, still burning ith desire to put to death the disciples of the Lord, ent to the high priest,
And made a request for letters from him to the Synagogues of Damascus, so that if there ere any of the Way there, men or omen, he might take them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
And hile he as journeying, he came near Damascus; and suddenly he sa a light from heaven shining round him;
And he ent don on the earth, and a voice said to him, Saul, Saul, hy are you attacking me so cruelly?
And he said, Who are you, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus, hom you are attacking:
But get up, and go into the ton, and it ill be made clear to you hat you have to do.
And the men ho ere ith him ere not able to say anything; hearing the voice, but seeing no one.
And Saul got up from the earth, and hen his eyes ere open, he sa nothing; and he as guided by the hand into Damascus.
And for three days he as not able to see, and he took no food or drink.
No there as a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and the Lord said to him in a vision, Ananias! and he said, Here I am, Lord.
And the Lord said to him, Get up, and go to the street hich is named Straight, and make search at the house of Judas for one named Saul of Tarsus: for he is at prayer;
And he has seen a man named Ananias coming in and putting his hands on him, so that he may be able to see.
But Ananias said, Lord, I have had accounts of this man from a number of people, ho much evil he has done to your saints at Jerusalem:
And here he has authority from the chief priests to make prisoners all ho give orship to your name.
But the Lord said, Go ithout fear: for he is a special vessel for me, to give to the Gentiles and kings and to the children of Israel the knoledge of my name:
For I ill make clear to him hat troubles he ill have to undergo for me.

And Ananias ent out and came to the house, and putting his hands on him, said, Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, hom you sa hen you ere on your journey, has sent me, so that you may be able to see, and be full of the Holy Spirit.
And straight aay it seemed as if a veil as taken from his eyes, and he as able to see; and he got up, and had baptism;
And hen he had taken food his strength came back. And for some days he kept ith the disciples ho ere in Damascus.
And straight aay, in the Synagogues, he as preaching Jesus as the Son of God.

And all those hearing him ere full of onder and said, Is not this the man ho in Jerusalem as attacking all the orshippers of this name? and he had come here so that he might take them as prisoners before the chief priests.
But Saul ent on increasing in poer, and the Jes in Damascus ere not able to give ansers to the arguments by hich he made it clear that Jesus as the Christ.

But his disciples took him by night and let him don from the all in a basket.

But Barnabas took him to the Apostles and gave them an account of ho he had seen the Lord on the road, and had given hearing to his ords, and ho at Damascus he had been preaching in the name of Jesus ithout fear.
And he as ith them, going in and out at Jerusalem,
Preaching in the name of the Lord ithout fear; and he had discussions ith the Greek Jes; but they ere orking for his death.
And hen the brothers had knoledge of it, they took him to Caesarea and sent him to Tarsus.
And so the church through all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria had peace and as made strong; and, living in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, as increased greatly.
And it came about that hile Peter as going through all parts of the country he came to the saints ho ere living at Lydda.
And there as a certain man there, named Aeneas, ho for eight years had been in bed, ithout poer of moving.
And Peter said to him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ makes you ell: get up and make your bed. And straight aay he got up.
And all those living in Lydda and Sharon sa him, and ere turned to the Lord.
No there as at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, that is, Dorcas: this oman as given to good orks and acts of mercy at all times.
And it came about, in those days, that she got ill and came to her death: and hen she had been ashed, they put her in a room hich as high up.
And because Lydda as near Joppa, the disciples, having knoledge that Peter as there, sent to men to him, requesting him to come to them straight aay.
And Peter ent ith them. And hen he had come, they took him into the room: and all the idos ere there, eeping and putting before him the coats and clothing hich Dorcas had made hile she as ith them.
But Peter made them all go outside, and ent don on his knees in prayer; and turning to the body, he said, Tabitha, get up. And, opening her eyes, she sa Peter and got up.
And he took her hand, lifting her up; and, sending for the saints and idos, he gave her to them, living.
And nes of it ent all through Joppa, and a number of people had faith in the Lord.
And he as living in Joppa for some time ith Simon, a leather-orker.
No there as a certain man in Caesarea, named Cornelius, the captain of the Italian band of the army;
A serious-minded man, fearing God ith all his family; he gave much money to the poor, and made prayer to God at all times.
He sa in a vision, clearly, at about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of the Lord coming to him and saying to him, Cornelius!
And he, looking on him in fear, said, What is it, Lord? And he said to him, Your prayers and your offerings have come up to God, and he has kept them in mind.
No send men to Joppa, and get one Simon, named Peter,
Who is living ith Simon, a leather-orker, hose house is by the sea.
And hen the angel ho said these ords to him had gone aay, he sent for to of his house-servants, and a God-fearing man of the army, one of those ho ere aiting on him at all times;
And having given them an account of everything, he sent them to Joppa.
No the day after, hen they ere on their journey and ere near the ton, Peter ent up to the top of the house for prayer, about the sixth hour:
And he as in need of food: but hile they ere getting it ready, a deep sleep came on him;
And he sa the heavens opening, and a vessel coming don, like a great cloth let don on the earth,
In hich ere all sorts of beasts and birds.
And a voice came to him, saying, Come, Peter; take them for food.
But Peter said, No, Lord; for I have never taken food hich is common or unclean.
And the voice came to him a second time, What God has made clean, do not you make common.
And this as done three times: and then the vessel as taken back into heaven.
No hile Peter as in doubt as to the purpose of this vision, the men ho ere sent by Cornelius, having made search for Simon’s house, came to the door,
To see if Simon, named Peter, as living there.
And, hile Peter as turning the vision over in his mind, the Spirit said to him, See, three men are looking for you.
Go don, then, and go ith them, doubting nothing, for I have sent them.
And Peter ent don to the men, and said, I am the man you are looking for: hy have you come?

And they said, Cornelius, a captain, an upright and God-fearing man, respected by all the nation of the Jes, had ord from God by an angel to send for you to his house, and to give hearing to your ords.
So he took them in for the night. And the day after, he ent ith them, taking some of the brothers from Joppa ith him.
And the day after that, they came to Caesarea. And Cornelius as aiting for them, having got together his relations and his near friends.
And hen Peter came in, Cornelius came to him and, falling don at his feet, gave him orship.
But Peter, lifting him up, said, Get up, for I am a man as you are.
And saying these ords, he ent in, and sa that a great number of people had come together;

And he said to them, You yourselves have knoledge that it is against the la for a man ho is a Je to be in the company of one ho is of another nation; but God has made it clear to me that no man may be named common or unclean:
And so I came ithout question, hen I as sent for. What then is your purpose in sending for me?
And Cornelius said, Four days from no I as in my house in prayer at the ninth hour; and I sa before me a man in shining clothing,
Who said, Cornelius, your prayer has come to the ears of God, and your offerings are kept in his memory.
Send, then, to Joppa, and get Simon, named Peter, to come to you; he is living in the house of Simon, a leather-orker, by the sea.
So, straight aay, I sent for you; and you have done ell to come. And no, e are all present before God, ready to give attention to all the things hich the Lord has given you to say.
Then Peter said, Truly, I see clearly that God is no respecter of persons:
But in every nation, the man ho has fear of him and does righteousness is pleasing to him.
The ord hich he sent to the children of Israel, giving the good nes of peace through Jesus Christ ( ho is Lord of all) —
That ord you yourselves have knoledge of, hich as made public through all Judaea, starting from Galilee, after the baptism of hich John as the preacher,
About Jesus of Nazareth, ho God gave the Holy Spirit to him, ith poer: and ho he ent about doing good and making ell all ho ere troubled by evil spirits, for God as ith him.
And e are itnesses of all the things hich he did in the country of the Jes and in Jerusalem; hom they put to death, hanging him on a tree.
On the third day God gave him back to life, and let him be seen,
Not by all the people, but by itnesses marked out before by God, even by us, ho took food and drink ith him after he came back from the dead.
And he gave us orders to give nes of this to the people, and to give public itness that this is he hom God has made judge of the living and the dead.
To him all the prophets give itness, that through his name everyone ho has faith in him ill have forgiveness of sins.
While Peter as saying these ords, the Holy Spirit came on all those ho ere hearing the ord.
And the Jes of the faith, ho had come ith Peter, ere full of onder, because the Holy Spirit as given to the Gentiles,
And they ere talking in tongues, and giving glory to God. Then Peter said,
Will any man say that these may not have baptism ho have been given the Holy Spirit as e have?
And he gave orders for them to have baptism in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they kept him ith them for some days.
No the Apostles and the brothers ho ere in Judaea had nes that the ord of God had been given to the Gentiles.
And hen Peter came to Jerusalem, those ho kept the rule of circumcision had an argument ith him,
Saying, You ent to men ithout circumcision, and took food ith them.
But Peter gave them an account of it all in order, saying to them,
I as in the ton of Joppa, at prayer: and falling into a deep sleep, I sa in a vision a vessel like a great cloth let don from heaven, and it came don to me:
And looking on it ith attention I sa in it all sorts of beasts and birds.

And at that minute, three men, sent from Caesarea, came to the house here e ere.
And the Spirit gave me orders to go ith them, doubting nothing. And these six brothers came ith me; and e ent into that man’s house:
And he gave us an account of ho he had seen the angel in his house, saying, Send to Joppa, and get Simon, named Peter, to come to you;
Who ill say ords to you through hich you and all your family may get salvation.
And, hile I as talking to them, the Holy Spirit came on them, as on us at first.
