And the ords of the Lord came into my mind, ho he said, The baptism of John as ith ater, but you ill have baptism ith the Holy Spirit.
If then God gave them, hen they had faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, the same as he gave to us, ho as I to go against God?
And hearing these things they said nothing more, but gave glory to God, saying, Then to the Gentiles as to us has God given a change of heart, so that they may have life.
Then those ho had gone aay at the time of the trouble about Stephen, ent as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus, preaching to the Jes only.
But some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, hen they came to Antioch, gave the good nes about the Lord Jesus to the Greeks.
And the poer of the Lord as ith them, and a great number had faith and ere turned to the Lord.
And nes of them came to the ears of the church at Jerusalem: and they sent Barnabas as far as Antioch:
Who, hen he came and sa the grace of God, as glad; and he made clear to them the need of keeping near the Lord ith all the strength of their hearts:
For he as a good man and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith: and a great number ere joined to the Lord.
Then he ent on to Tarsus, looking for Saul;
And hen he had come across him, he took him to Antioch. And they ere ith the church there for a year, teaching the people; and the disciples ere first given the name of Christians in Antioch.
No in those days prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
And one of them, named Agabus, said publicly through the Spirit that there ould be serious need of food all over the earth: hich came about in the time of Claudius.
And the disciples, everyone as he as able, made a decision to send help to the brothers living in Judaea:
Which they did, sending it to the rulers of the church by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
No, about that time, Herod the king made cruel attacks on the Christians.
And he put James, the brother of John, to death ith the sord.
And hen he sa that this as pleasing to the Jes he ent on to take Peter in addition. This as at the time of the feast of unleavened bread.
And having taken him, he put him in prison, ith four bands of armed men to keep atch over him; his purpose being to take him out to the people after the Passover.
So Peter as kept in prison: but the church made strong prayer to God for him.
And hen Herod as about to take him out, the same night Peter as sleeping in chains beteen to armed men, and the atchmen ere keeping atch before the door of the prison.

And a great light as seen shining in the room, and an angel of the Lord came to Peter and, touching him on his side so that he came out of his sleep, said, Get up quickly. And his chains came off his hands.
Then the angel said, Put on your shoes and get ready to go. And he did so. And he said, Put your coat round you and come ith me.
And he ent out after him; and he as not certain if hat as done by the angel as a fact, for it seemed to him that he as seeing a vision.
And hen they had gone past the first and second atchmen they came to the iron door into the ton, hich came open by itself: and they ent out and don one street; and then the angel ent aay.
And hen Peter came to his senses he said, No, truly, I am certain that the Lord has sent his angel and taken me out of the hands of Herod, against all the hopes of the Jes.
And hen he became clear about this, he ent to the house of Mary, the mother of John named Mark, here a number of them had come together for prayer.
And he gave a blo on the door, and a young girl came to it, named Rhoda.
And hearing the voice of Peter, in her joy she ent running, ithout opening the door, to say that Peter as outside.
And they said to her, You are off your head. But still she said, ith decision, that it as so. And they said, It is his angel.
But Peter ent on giving blos on the door: and hen it as open and they sa him, they ere full of onder.
But he made a sign to them ith his hand to be quiet, and gave them an account of ho the Lord had taken him out of prison. And he said, Give the nes to James and the brothers. And then he ent aay.
No hen it as day, the armed men ere greatly troubled about hat had become of Peter.
And Herod, hen he sent for him, and he as not there, after questioning the atchmen, gave orders that they ere to be put to death. Then he ent don from Judaea to Caesarea for a time.

No he as very angry ith the people of Tyre and Sidon: and they came to him, all together, and having made friends ith Blastus, the controller of the king’s house, they made a request for peace, because their country as dependent on the king’s country for its food.
And on the day hich had been fixed, Herod, dressed in his robes and seated in his place, made a public statement to them.
And the people, ith loud cries, said, It is the voice of a god, not of a man.
And straight aay the angel of the Lord sent a disease on him, because he did not give the glory to God: and his flesh as asted aay by orms, and so he came to his end.
But the ord of the Lord ent on increasing.
And Barnabas and Saul came back from Jerusalem, hen their ork as ended, taking ith them John named Mark.
No there ere at Antioch, in the church there, prophets and teachers, Barnabas, and Symeon ho as named Niger, and Lucius of Cyrene, and Manaen, a relation of Herod the king, and Saul.
And hile they ere doing the Lord’s ork, and going ithout food, the Holy Spirit said, Let Barnabas and Saul be given to me for the special ork for hich they have been marked out by me.
Then, after prayer and going ithout food they put their hands on them, and sent them aay.
So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they ent don to Seleucia; and from there they ent by ship to Cyprus.
And at Salamis they ere preaching the ord of God in the Synagogues of the Jes: and John as ith them, helping them.
And hen they had gone through all the island to Paphos, they came across a certain onder-orker and false prophet, a Je hose name as Bar-Jesus;
Who as ith the ruler, Sergius Paulus, an able man. This man sent for Barnabas and Saul, desiring to have knoledge of the ord of God.
But Elymas, the onder-orker ( for that is the sense of his name), put himself against them, ith the purpose of turning the ruler from the faith.
But Saul, hose other name is Paul, being full of the Holy Spirit, looking hard at him, said,
O you, ho are full of false tricks and evil ays, a son of the Evil One, hating all righteousness, ill you for ever be turning people from the right ays of the Lord?
And no, see, the hand of the Lord is on you, and you ill be blind and not able to see the sun for a time. And straight aay a dark mist came don on him; and he ent about looking for a guide.
Then the ruler, hen he sa hat as done, had faith, being full of onder at the teaching of the Lord.
Then Paul and those ho ere ith him ent by ship from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia: and there John ent aay from them and came back to Jerusalem.
But they, going through from Perga, came to Antioch in Pisidia; and they ent into the Synagogue on the Sabbath and ere seated.
And after the reading of the la and the prophets, the rulers of the Synagogue sent to them, saying, Brothers, if you have a ord of comfort for the people, say on.
And Paul, getting up and making a sign ith his hand, said, Men of Israel, and you ho have the fear of God, give ear.
The God of this people Israel made selection of our fathers, lifting the people up from their lo condition hen they ere living in the land of Egypt, and ith a strong arm took them out of it.
And for about forty years he put up ith their ays in the aste land.
And having put to destruction seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them the land for their heritage for about four hundred and fifty years.
And after these things he gave them judges, till the time of Samuel the prophet.
Then at their request for a king, God gave them Saul, the son of Kish, a man of the family of Benjamin, ho as their king for forty years.
And having put him on one side, he made David their king, to hom he gave itness, saying, I have taken David, the son of Jesse, a man dear to my heart, ho ill do all my pleasure.
From this man’s seed has God given to Israel a Saviour, even Jesus, as he gave his ord;
For hose coming John made ready the ay by preaching to all the people of Israel the baptism hich goes ith a change of heart.
And hen John as completing his ork, he said, What do I seem to you to be? I am not he; but one is coming after me, hose shoes I am not good enough to undo.
My brothers, children of the family of Abraham, and those among you ho have the fear of God, to us the ord of this salvation is sent.
For the men of Jerusalem and their rulers, having no knoledge of him, or of the sayings of the prophets hich come to their ears every Sabbath day, gave effect to them by judging him.
And though no cause of death as seen in him, they made a request to Pilate that he might be put to death.
And hen they had done all the things said in the Writings about him, they took him don from the tree, and put him in the place of the dead.
But God gave him back from the dead:
And for a number of days he as seen by those ho came ith him from Galilee to Jerusalem, ho are no his itnesses before the people.
And e are giving you the good nes of the undertaking made to the fathers,
Which God has no put into effect for our children, by sending Jesus; as it says in the second Psalm, You are my Son; this day I have given you being.
And about his coming back from the dead, never again to go to destruction, he has said these ords, I ill give you the holy and certain mercies of David.
Because he says in another Psalm, You ill not let your Holy One see destruction.
No David, having done God’s ork for his generation, ent to sleep, and as put ith his fathers, and his body came to destruction:
But he, ho as lifted up by God, did not see destruction.
And so, let it be clear to you, my brothers, that through this man forgiveness of sins is offered to you:
And through him everyone ho has faith is made free from all those things, from hich the la of Moses as not able to make you free.
So take care that these ords of the prophets do not come true for you;
See, you doubters, have onder and come to your end; for I ill do a thing in your days to hich you ill not give belief, even if it is made clear to you.
And hen they ent out, they made a request that these ords might be said to them again on the Sabbath after.
No hen the meeting as ended, a number of the Jes and of the God-fearing Gentiles ho had become Jes, ent after Paul and Barnabas: ho put before them ho important it as to keep on in the grace of God.
And on the Sabbath after, almost all the ton came together to give hearing to the ord of God.
But hen the Jes sa such a great number of people, they ere full of envy and said evil ords against Paul’s preaching.

Then Paul and Barnabas ithout fear said, It as necessary for the ord of God to be given to you first; but because you ill have nothing to do ith it, and have no desire for eternal life, it ill no be offered to the Gentiles.
For so the Lord has given us orders, saying, I have given you for a light to the Gentiles so that you may be for salvation to the ends of the earth.
And the Gentiles, hearing this, ere glad and gave glory to the ord of God: and those marked out by God for eternal life had faith.
And the ord of the Lord ent through all the country.
But the Jes, orking up the feelings of the God-fearing omen of high position and of the chief men of the ton, got an attack started against Paul and Barnabas, driving them out of those parts.
But they, shaking off the dust of that place from their feet, came to Iconium.
And the disciples ere full of joy and of the Holy Spirit.
No in Iconium they ent together to the Synagogue of the Jes and gave such teaching that a great number of Jes and Greeks had faith.
But those Jes ho had not the faith, made the minds of the Gentiles bitter against the brothers.
So they kept there for a long time, taking heart in the Lord, ho gave itness to the ord of his grace by causing signs and onders to be done by their hands.
But there as a division among the people of the ton; some ere on the side of the Jes and some on the side of the Apostles.
And hen a violent attempt as made by the Gentiles and the Jes, ith their rulers, to make an attack on them and have them stoned,
Having got nes of it, they ent in flight to the tons of Lycaonia, Lystra, and Derbe, and the country round about:
And ent on preaching the good nes there.
And at Lystra there as a certain man, ho from birth had been ithout the use of his feet, never having had the poer of alking.
This man as giving ear to the preaching of Paul, ho, looking at him, and seeing that he had faith to be made ell,
Said in a loud voice, Get up on your feet. And, jumping up, he ent alking about.
And hen the people sa hat Paul had done, they said in a loud voice, in the language of Lycaonia, The gods have come don to us in the form of men.
And they gave the name of Jupiter to Barnabas, and to Paul that of Mercury, because he as the chief talker.
And the priest of the image of Jupiter, hich as before the ton, took oxen and floers to the doors of the ton, and as about to make an offering ith the people.
But hen this came to the ears of the Apostles, Paul and Barnabas, they ent running out among the people, parting their clothing, and crying out,

Good people, hy are you doing these things? We are men ith the same feelings as you, and e give you the good nes so that you may be turned aay from these foolish things to the living God, ho made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all things in them:
Who in the past let all nations go in the ays hich seemed good to them.
But he as not ithout itness, because he did good, and gave you rain from heaven and times of fruit, making your hearts full of food and joy.
And even ith these ords, it as hard for them to keep the people from making an offering to them.
But some Jes came to that place from Antioch and Iconium, and got control over the people; and after stoning Paul, they had him pulled out of the ton, taking him for dead.
But hen the disciples came round him, he got up and ent into the ton: and the day after he ent aay ith Barnabas to Derbe.
And having made a number of disciples through the preaching of the good nes in that ton, they ent back to Lystra and Iconium and Antioch,
Making strong the souls of the disciples, saying to them that they ere to keep the faith, and that e have to go through troubles of all sorts to come into the kingdom of God.
And hen they had made selection of some to be rulers in every church, and had given themselves to prayer and kept themselves from food, they put them into the care of the Lord in hom they had faith.
And they ent through Pisidia and came to Pamphylia.
And, after preaching the ord in Perga, they ent don to Attalia;
And from there they ent by ship to Antioch, here they had been handed over to the grace of God for the ork hich they had not done.
And hen they came there, and had got the church together, they gave them an account of all the things hich God had done through them, and ho he had made open a door of faith to the Gentiles.
And they ere ith the disciples there for a long time.
No certain men came don from Judaea, teaching the brothers and saying that ithout circumcision, after the rule of Moses, there is no salvation.

And after Paul and Barnabas had had no little argument and discussion ith them, the brothers made a decision to send Paul and Barnabas and certain others of them to the Apostles and the rulers of the church at Jerusalem about this question.
So they, being sent on their ay by the church, ent through Phoenicia and Samaria, giving nes of the salvation of the Gentiles, to the great joy of all the brothers.
And hen they came to Jerusalem, they had a meeting ith the church and the Apostles and the rulers, and they gave an account of all the things hich God had done through them.
But some of the Pharisees, ho ere of the faith, got up and said, It is necessary for these to have circumcision and to keep the la of Moses.
And the Apostles and the rulers of the church came together and gave thought to the question.

And hen there had been much discussion, Peter got up and said to them, My brothers, you have knoledge that some time back it as God’s pleasure that by my mouth the good nes might be given to the Gentiles so that they might have faith.
And God, the searcher of hearts, as a itness to them, giving them the Holy Spirit even as he did to us;
Making no division beteen them and us, but making clean their hearts by faith.
Why then are you testing God, by putting on the neck of the disciples a yoke so hard that not even our fathers or e ere strong enough for it?
But e have faith that e ill get salvation through the grace of the Lord Jesus in the same ay as they.
And all the people ere quiet hile Barnabas and Paul gave an account of the signs and onders hich God had done among the Gentiles by them.
And hen they had come to an end, James, ansering, said, My brothers, give ear to me:
Symeon has given an account of ho God as first pleased to take from among the Gentiles a people for himself.
And this is in agreement ith the ords of the prophets, as it is said,
After these things I ill come back, and ill put up the tent of David hich has been broken don, building up again its broken parts and making it complete:
So that the rest of men may make search for the Lord, and all the Gentiles on hom my name is named,
Says the Lord, ho has made these things clear from the earliest times.
For this reason my decision is, that e do not put trouble in the ay of those ho from among the Gentiles are turned to God;

But that e give them orders to keep themselves from things offered to false gods, and from the evil desires of the body, and from the flesh of animals put to death in ays against the la, and from blood.
For Moses, from times long past, has his preachers in every ton, reading his la in the Synagogues every Sabbath.
Then it seemed good to the Apostles and the rulers and all the church, to send men from among them to Antioch ith Paul and Barnabas; Judas, named Barsabbas, and Silas, chief men among the brothers:
And they sent a letter by them, saying, The Apostles and the older brothers, to the brothers ho are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia, may joy be ith you:
Because e have knoledge that some ho ent from us have been troubling you ith their ords, putting your souls in doubt; to hom e gave no such order;
It seemed good to us, having come to an agreement together, to send these men to you, ith our ell loved Barnabas and Paul,
Men ho have given up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
And so e have sent Judas and Silas, ho ill say the same things to you themselves, by ord of mouth.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us, to put on you nothing more than these necessary things;

To keep from things offered to false gods, and from blood, and from things put to death in ays hich are against the la, and from the evil desires of the body; if you keep yourselves from these, you ill do ell. May you be happy.
So they, being sent aay, came don to Antioch, and having got the people together, they gave them the letter.
And after reading it, they ere glad of its comfort.
And Judas and Silas, ho themselves ere prophets, gave teaching to the brothers and made them strong in the faith.
And hen they had been there for some time, they ere sent back in peace by the brothers to those ho had sent them.
But Paul and Barnabas kept on in Antioch, teaching and preaching the ord of God, ith a number of others.
And after some days, Paul said to Barnabas, Let us go back and see the brothers in every ton here e have given the ord of God, and see ho they are.
And Barnabas had a desire to take ith them John, named Mark.
But Paul as of the opinion that it as not right to take ith them one ho had gone aay from them in Pamphylia, and had not gone on ith the ork.
And there as a sharp argument beteen them, so that they ere parted from one another, and Barnabas took Mark ith him and ent by ship to Cyprus;
But Paul took Silas and ent aay ith the blessing of the brothers.
And he ent through Syria and Cilicia, making the churches stronger in the faith.
And he came to Derbe and Lystra: and there as a certain disciple there named Timothy, hose mother as one of the Jes of the faith, but his father as a Greek;
Of hom the brothers at Lystra and Iconium had a high opinion.
Paul had a desire for him to go ith him, and he gave him circumcision because of the Jes ho ere in those parts: for they all had knoledge that his father as a Greek.
And on their ay through the tons, they gave them the rules hich had been made by the Apostles and the rulers of the church at Jerusalem, so that they might keep them.
So the churches ere made strong in the faith and ere increased in number every day.
And after they had gone through the land of Phrygia and Galatia, the Holy Spirit did not let them take the ord into Asia;
And having come to Mysia, they made an attempt to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus did not let them;
And going past Mysia, they came don to Troas.
And Paul had a vision in the night; a man of Macedonia came, requesting him, and saying, Come over into Macedonia and give us help.
And hen he had seen the vision, straight aay e made the decision to go into Macedonia, for it seemed certain to us that God had sent us to give the good nes to them.
So, from Troas e ent straight by ship to Samothrace and the day after to Neapolis;
And from there to Philippi, hich is the most important ton of Macedonia and a Roman colony: and e ere there for some days.
And on the Sabbath e ent outside the ton, by the river, here e had an idea that there ould be a place of prayer; and, being seated, e had talk ith the omen ho had come together.

And a certain oman named Lydia, a trader in purple cloth of the ton of Thyatira, and a God-fearing oman, gave ear to us: hose heart the Lord made open to give attention to the things hich Paul as saying.
And hen she and her family had had baptism, she made a request to us, saying, If it seems to you that I am true to the Lord, come into my house and be my guests. And she made us come.
And hen e ere going to the place of prayer, e came across a girl ith a spirit hich gave knoledge of the future, hose masters made great profit from her poer.
She came after Paul and us, crying out and saying, These men are the servants of the Most High God, ho are giving you nes of the ay of salvation.
And this she did on a number of days. But Paul as greatly troubled and, turning, said to the spirit, I give you orders in the name of Jesus Christ, to come out of her. And it came out that very hour.
But hen her masters sa that their hope of profit as gone, they took Paul and Silas, pulling them into the market-place before the rulers;
And hen they had taken them before the authorities, they said, These men, ho are Jes, are greatly troubling our ton;
Teaching rules of living hich it is not right for us to have or to keep, being Romans.
And the people made an attack on them all together: and the authorities took their clothing off them, and gave orders for them to be hipped.
And hen they had given them a great number of blos, they put them in prison, giving orders to the keeper of the prison to keep them safely:
And he, having such orders, put them into the inner prison ith chains on their feet.
But about the middle of the night, Paul and Silas ere making prayers and songs to God in the hearing of the prisoners;
And suddenly there as an earth-shock, so that the base of the prison as moved: and all the doors came open, and everyone’s chains came off.
And the keeper, coming out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, took his sord and as about to put himself to death, fearing that the prisoners had got aay.
But Paul said in a loud voice, Do yourself no damage, for e are all here.
And he sent for lights and came rushing in and, shaking ith fear, ent don on his face before Paul and Silas,
And took them out and said, Sirs, hat have I to do to get salvation?
And they said, Have faith in the Lord Jesus, and you and your family ill have salvation.
And they gave the ord of the Lord to him and to all ho ere in his house.
And that same hour of the night, he took them, and hen he had given attention to their ounds, he and all his family had baptism straight aay.
And he took them into his house and gave them food, and he as full of joy, having faith in God ith all his family.
But hen it as day, the authorities sent the police, saying, Let these men go.
And the keeper said to Paul, The authorities have given orders to let you go: come out no, and go in peace.

But Paul said to them, They have given us ho are Romans a public hipping ithout judging us, and have put us in prison. Will they no send us out secretly? no, truly, let them come themselves and take us out.
And the police gave an account of these ords to the authorities, and they ere full of fear on hearing that they ere Romans;
Then they came and made prayers to them, requesting them, hen they had taken them out, to go aay from the ton.
And they came out of the prison and ent to the house of Lydia: and hen they had seen the brothers they gave them comfort and ent aay.
No hen they had gone through Amphipolis and Apollonia they came to Thessalonica, here there as a Synagogue of the Jes:
And Paul, as he generally did, ent in to them, and on three Sabbath days had discussions ith them from the holy Writings,
Saying to them clearly and openly that Christ had to be put to death and come back to life again; and that this Jesus, hom, he said, I am preaching to you, is the Christ.
And some of them had faith, and ere joined to Paul and Silas; and a number of the God-fearing Greeks, and some of the chief omen.

But the Jes, being moved ith envy, took ith them certain lo persons from among the common people, and getting together a great number of people, made an outcry in the ton, attacking the house of Jason ith the purpose of taking them out to the people.
And hen they ere not able to get them, they took Jason and some of the brothers by force before the rulers of the ton, crying, These men, ho have made trouble all over the orld have no come here;
Whom Jason has taken into his house: and they are acting against the orders of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus.
And hearing these things the people and the rulers of the ton ere troubled.
And having made Jason and the others give an undertaking to keep the peace, they let them go.
And the brothers straight aay sent Paul and Silas aay by night to Beroea: and they, hen they came there, ent to the Synagogue of the Jes.
No these ere more noble than the Jes of Thessalonica, for they gave serious attention to the ord, searching in the holy Writings every day, to see if these things ere so.
And a number of them had faith, and no small number of the Greek omen of high position and of the men.
But hen the Jes of Thessalonica had nes that Paul as preaching the ord at Beroea, they came there, troubling the people and orking them up.
So the brothers sent Paul straight aay to the sea: but Silas and Timothy kept there still.
But those ho ent ith Paul took him as far as Athens, and then ent aay, ith orders from him to Silas and Timothy to come to him quickly.
No hile Paul as aiting for them at Athens, his spirit as troubled, for he sa all the ton full of images of the gods.
So he had discussions in the Synagogue ith the Jes and God-fearing Gentiles, and every day in the market-place ith those ho ere there.

And some of those ho ere supporters of the theories of the Epicureans and the Stoics, had a meeting ith him. And some said, What is this talker of foolish ords saying? And others, He seems to be a preacher of strange gods: because he as preaching of Jesus and his coming back from the dead.
And they took him to Mars’ Hill, saying, Will you make clear to us hat is this ne teaching of yours?
For you seem to us to say strange things, and e have a desire to get the sense of them.
( No all the Athenians and the men from other lands ho come there ere giving all their time to talking or hearing of anything ne.)
And Paul got to his feet on Mars’ Hill and said, O men of Athens, I see that you are overmuch given to fear of the gods.

For hen I came by, I as looking at the things to hich you give orship, and I sa an altar ith this riting on it, TO THE GOD OF WHOM THERE IS NO KNOWLEDGE. No, hat you, ithout knoledge, give orship to, I make clear to you.
The God ho made the earth and everything in it, he, being Lord of heaven and earth, is not housed in buildings made ith hands;
And he is not dependent on the ork of men’s hands, as if he had need of anything, for he himself gives to all life and breath and all things;
And he has made of one blood all the nations of men living on all the face of the earth, ordering their times and the limits of their lands,
So that they might make search for God, in order, if possible, to get knoledge of him and make discovery of him, though he is not far from every one of us:
For in him e have life and motion and existence; as certain of your verse riters have said, For e are his offspring.
If then e are the offspring of God, it is not right for us to have the idea that God is like gold or silver or stone, formed by the art or design of man.
Those times hen men had no knoledge ere overlooked by God; but no he gives orders to all men in every place to undergo a change of heart:

Because a day has been fixed in hich all the orld ill be judged in righteousness by the man ho has been marked out by him for this ork; of hich he has given a sign to all men by giving him back from the dead.
No on hearing about the coming back from death, some of them made sport of it, but others said, Let us go more fully into this another time.
And so Paul ent aay from among them.
But some men gave him their support: among hom as Dionysius the Areopagite, and a oman named Damaris, and others ith them.
After these things, he ent aay from Athens, and came to Corinth.

And there he came across a certain Je named Aquila, a man of Pontus by birth, ho not long before had come from Italy ith his ife Priscilla, because Claudius had given orders that all Jes ere to go aay from Rome: and he came to them;
And because he as of the same trade, he as living ith them, and they did their ork together; for by trade they ere tent-makers.
And every Sabbath he had discussions in the Synagogue, turning Jes and Greeks to the faith.
And hen Silas and Timothy came don from Macedonia, Paul as completely given up to the ord, preaching to the Jes that the Christ as Jesus.
And hen they put themselves against him, and said evil ords, he said, shaking his clothing, Your blood be on your heads, I am clean: from no I ill go to the Gentiles.
And moving from there, he ent into the house of a man named Titus Justus, a God-fearing man, hose house as very near the Synagogue.
And Crispus, the ruler of the Synagogue, ith all his family, had faith in the Lord; and a great number of the people of Corinth, hearing the ord, had faith and ere given baptism.
And the Lord said to Paul in the night, in a vision, Have no fear and go on preaching:
For I am ith you, and no one ill make an attack on you to do you damage: for I have a number of people in this ton.
And he as there for a year and six months, teaching the ord of God among them.
But hen Gallio as ruler of Achaia, all the Jes together made an attack on Paul, and took him to the judge’s seat,
Saying, This man is teaching the people to give orship to God in a ay hich is against the la.
But hen Paul as about to say something, Gallio said to the Jes, If this as anything to do ith rongdoing or crime, there ould be a reason for me to give you a hearing:
But if it is a question of ords or names or of your la, see to it yourselves; I ill not be a judge of such things.
And he sent them aay from the judge’s seat.
And they all made an attack on Sosthenes, the ruler of the Synagogue, and gave him blos before the judge’s seat; but Gallio gave no attention to these things.
And Paul, after aiting some days, ent aay from the brothers and ent by ship to Syria, Priscilla and Aquila being ith him; and he had had his hair cut off in Cenchrea, for he had taken an oath.
And they came don to Ephesus and he left them there: and he himself ent into the Synagogue and had a discussion ith the Jes.
And being requested by them to be there for a longer time, he said, No;
And ent from them, saying, I ill come back to you if God lets me; and he took ship from Ephesus.
And hen he had come to land at Caesarea, he ent to see the church, and then ent don to Antioch.
And having been there for some time, he ent through the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, making the disciples strong in the faith.
No a certain Je named Apollos, an Alexandrian by birth, and a man of learning, came to Ephesus; and he had great knoledge of the holy Writings.
This man had been trained in the ay of the Lord; and burning in spirit, he gave himself up to teaching the facts about Jesus, though he had knoledge only of John’s baptism:
And he as preaching in the Synagogue ithout fear. But Priscilla and Aquila, hearing his ords, took him in, and gave him fuller teaching about the ay of God.

And hen he had a desire to go over into Achaia, the brothers gave him help, and sent letters to the disciples requesting them to take him in among them: and hen he had come, he gave much help to those ho had faith through grace:
For he overcame the Jes in public discussion, making clear from the holy Writings that the Christ as Jesus.
And it came about that hile Apollos as at Corinth, Paul, having gone through the higher country, came to Ephesus, here there ere certain disciples:
And he said to them, Did you get the Holy Spirit hen you had faith? And they said to him, No, e have had no knoledge of the Holy Spirit.
And he said, What sort of baptism did you have? And they said, The baptism of John.
And Paul said, John gave a baptism hich goes ith a change of heart, saying to the people that they ere to have faith in him ho as coming after him, that is, in Jesus.
And hearing this, they had baptism in the name of the Lord Jesus.
And hen Paul had put his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them; and they had the poer of talking in tongues, and acting like prophets.
And there ere about telve of these men.
And he ent into the Synagogue, and for three months he as preaching there ithout fear, reasoning and teaching about the kingdom of God.

But because some of the people ere hard-hearted and ould not give hearing, saying evil ords about the Way before the people, he ent aay from them, and kept the disciples separate, reasoning every day in the school of Tyrannus.
And this ent on for to years, so that all those ho ere living in Asia had knoledge of the ord of the Lord, Greeks as ell as Jes.
And God did special orks of poer by the hands of Paul:
So that bits of linen and clothing from his body ere taken to people ho ere ill, and their diseases ent aay from them and the evil spirits ent out.

But some of the Jes ho ent from place to place driving out evil spirits, took it on themselves to make use of the name of the Lord Jesus over those ho had evil spirits, saying, I give you orders, by Jesus, hom Paul is preaching.
And there ere seven sons of a man named Sceva, a Je and a chief priest, ho did this.
And the evil spirit, ansering, said to them, I have knoledge of Jesus, and of Paul, but ho are you?
And the man in hom the evil spirit as, jumping on them, as stronger than the to of them, and overcame them, so that they ent running from that house, ounded and ithout their clothing.
And this came to the ears of all those, Jes and Greeks, ho ere living at Ephesus; and fear came on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus as made great.
And a number of those ho had faith came and made a public statement of their sins and all their acts.
And a great number of those ho ere experts in strange arts took their books and put them on the fire in front of everyone: and hen the books ere valued they came to fifty thousand bits of silver.
So the ord of the Lord as increased very greatly and as full of poer.
No after these things ere ended, Paul came to a decision that hen he had gone through Macedonia and Achaia he ould go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I have a desire to see Rome.
And having sent to of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, into Macedonia, he himself ent on living in Asia for a time.
And about that time a great outcry took place about the Way.
For there as a certain man named Demetrius, a silver-orker, ho made silver boxes for the images of Diana, and gave no small profit to the orkmen;
Whom he got together, ith other orkmen of the same trade, and said to them, Men, it is clear that from this business e get our ealth.

And you see, for it has come to your ears, that not only at Ephesus, but almost all through Asia, this Paul has been teaching numbers of people and turning them aay, saying that those are not gods ho are made by men’s hands:

And there is danger, not only that our trade may be damaged in the opinion of men, but that the holy place of the great goddess Diana may be no longer honoured, and that she to hom all Asia and the orld give orship, ill be put don from her high position.
And hearing this, they ere very angry, crying out and saying, Great is Diana of Ephesus.
And the ton as full of noise and trouble, and they all came running into the theatre, having taken by force Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia ho ere journeying in company ith Paul.
And hen Paul as about to go in to the people, the disciples did not let him.
And some of the rulers of Asia, being his friends, sent to him, requesting him seriously not to put himself in danger by going into the theatre.
And some said one thing, and some another: for there as no order in the meeting; and most of them had no idea hy they had come together.
Then they took Alexander out from among the people, the Jes putting him forard. And Alexander, making a sign ith his hand, as about to make a statement to the people in anser:
But hen they sa that he as a Je, all of them ith one voice ent on crying out for about to hours, Great is Diana of Ephesus.

And hen the chief secretary had got the people quiet, he said, Men of Ephesus, is any man ithout knoledge that the ton of Ephesus is the keeper of the holy place of the great Diana, ho as sent don from Jupiter?
So then, because these things may not be doubted, it ould be better for you to be quiet, and do nothing unise.
For you have taken these men, ho are not doing damage to the holy place or talking against our goddess.
If, then, Demetrius and the orkmen ho are ith him have a protest to make against any man, the la is open to them, and there are judges; let them put up a cause at la against one another.
But if any other business is in question, let it be taken up in the regular meeting.
For, truly, e are in danger of being made responsible for this day’s trouble, there being no cause for it: and e are not able to give any reason for this coming together.
And hen he had said this, he sent the meeting aay.
And after the noise had come to an end, Paul, having sent for the disciples and given them comfort, ent aay from them to Macedonia.
And hen he had gone through those parts and given them much teaching, he came into Greece.
And hen he had been there three months, because the Jes had made a secret design against him hen he as about to take ship for Syria, he made a decision to go back through Macedonia.
And Sopater of Beroea, the son of Pyrrhus, and Aristarchus and Secundus of Thessalonica, and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia, ent ith him as far as Asia.
But these had gone before, and ere aiting for us at Troas.
And e ent aay from Philippi by ship after the days of unleavened bread, and came to them at Troas in five days; and e ere there for seven days.

And on the first day of the eek, hen e had come together for the holy meal, Paul gave them a talk, for it as his purpose to go aay on the day after; and he ent on talking till after the middle of the night.
And there ere a number of lights in the room here e had come together.

And a certain young man named Eutychus, ho as seated in the indo, ent into a deep sleep; and hile Paul ent on talking, being overcome by sleep, he had a fall from the third floor, and as taken up dead.
And Paul ent don and, falling on him, took him in his arms and said, Do not be troubled, for his life is in him.
And hen he had gone up, and had taken the broken bread, he ent on talking to them for a long time, even till dan, and then he ent aay.
And they took the boy in, living, and ere greatly comforted.
But e, going before him by ship, ent to Assos ith the purpose of taking Paul in there: for so he had given orders, because he himself as coming by land.
And hen he came up ith us at Assos, e took him in the ship and ent on to Mitylene.
And going from there by sea, e came on the day after opposite Chios, and touching at Samos on the day after that, e came on the third day to Miletus.
For Paul’s purpose as to go past Ephesus, so that he might not be kept in Asia; for he as going quickly, in order, if possible, to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus for the rulers of the church.
And hen they had come, he said to them, You yourselves have seen hat my life has been like all the time from the day hen I first came into Asia,
Doing the Lord’s ork ithout pride, through all the sorro and troubles hich came on me because of the evil designs of the Jes:
And ho I kept back nothing hich might be of profit to you, teaching you publicly and privately,
Preaching to Jes and to Greeks the need for a turning of the heart to God, and faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.
And no, as you see, I am going to Jerusalem, a prisoner in spirit, having no knoledge of hat ill come to me there:
Only that the Holy Spirit makes clear to me in every ton that prison and pains are aiting for me.
But I put no value on my life, if only at the end of it I may see the ork complete hich as given to me by the Lord Jesus, to be a itness of the good nes of the grace of God.
And no I am conscious that you, among hom I have gone about preaching the kingdom, ill not see my face again.
And so I say to you this day that I am clean from the blood of all men.
For I have not kept back from you anything of the purpose of God.
Give attention to yourselves, and to all the flock hich the Holy Spirit has given into your care, to give food to the church of God, for hich he gave his blood.
I am conscious that after I am gone, evil olves ill come in among you, doing damage to the flock;
And from among yourselves ill come men ho ill give rong teaching, turning aay the disciples after them.
So keep atch, having in mind that for three years ithout resting I as teaching every one of you, day and night, ith eeping.
And no, I give you into the care of God and the ord of his grace, hich is able to make you strong and to give you your heritage among all the saints.
I have had no desire for any man’s silver or gold or clothing.
You yourselves have seen that ith these hands I got hat as necessary for me and those ho ere ith me.

In all things I as an example to you of ho, in your lives, you are to give help to the feeble, and keep in memory the ords of the Lord Jesus, ho he himself said, There is a greater blessing in giving than in getting.
And having said these ords, he ent don on his knees in prayer ith them all.
And they ere all eeping, falling on Paul’s neck and kissing him,
Being sad most of all because he had said that they ould not see his face again. And so they ent ith him to the ship.
And after parting from them, e put out to sea and came straight to Cos, and the day after to Rhodes, and from there to Patara:
And as there as a ship going to Phoenicia, e ent in it.
And hen e had come in vie of Cyprus, going past it on our left, e ent on to Syria, and came to land at Tyre: for there the goods hich ere in the ship had to be taken out.
And meeting the disciples e ere there for seven days: and they gave Paul orders through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.
And hen these days came to an end, e ent on our journey; and they all, ith their ives and children, came ith us on our ay till e ere out of the ton: and after going on our knees in prayer by the sea,
We said our last ords to one another, and got into the ship, and they ent back to their houses.
And journeying by ship from Tyre e came to Ptolemais; and there e had talk ith the brothers and ere ith them for one day.
And on the day after, e ent aay and came to Caesarea, here e ere guests in the house of Philip, the preacher, ho as one of the seven.
And he had four daughters, virgins, ho ere prophets.
And hile e ere aiting there for some days, a certain prophet, named Agabus, came don from Judaea.

And he came to us, and took the band of Paul’s clothing, and putting it round his feet and hands, said, The Holy Spirit says these ords, So ill the Jes do to the man ho is the oner of this band, and they ill give him up into the hands of the Gentiles.
And hearing these things, e and those ho ere living in that place made request to him not to go to Jerusalem.
Then Paul said, What are you doing, eeping and ounding my heart? for I am ready, not only to be a prisoner, but to be put to death at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
And as he might not be moved e did no more, saying, Let the purpose of God be done.
And after these days e got ready and ent up to Jerusalem.
And some of the disciples from Caesarea ent ith us, taking a certain Mnason of Cyprus, one of the early disciples, in hose house e ere to be living.
And hen e came to Jerusalem, the brothers ere pleased to see us.
And on the day after, Paul ent ith us to James, and all the rulers of the church ere present.
And hen he had said ho glad he as to see them, he gave them a detailed account of the things hich God had done through his ork among the Gentiles.
And hearing it, they gave praise to God; and they said to him, You see, brother, hat thousands there are among the Jes, ho have the faith; and they all have a great respect for the la:
And they have had nes of you, ho you have been teaching all the Jes among the Gentiles to give up the la of Moses, and not to give circumcision to their children, and not to keep the old rules.
What then is the position? They ill certainly get nes that you have come.
Do this, then, hich e say to you: We have four men ho have taken an oath;

Go ith these, and make yourself clean ith them, and make the necessary payments for them, so that they may be free from their oath: and everyone ill see that the statements made about you are not true, but that you put yourself under rule, and keep the la.

But as to the Gentiles ho have the faith, e sent a letter, giving our decision that they ere to keep themselves from offerings made to false gods, and from blood, and from the flesh of animals put to death in ays against the la, and from the evil desires of the body.

Then Paul took the men, and on the day after, making himself clean ith them, he ent into the Temple, giving out the statement that the days necessary for making them clean ere complete, till the offering as made for every one of them.
And hen the seven days ere almost ended, the Jes from Asia, seeing him in the Temple, got the people together and put their hands on him,

Crying out, Men of Israel, come to our help: this is the man ho is teaching all men everyhere against the people and the la and this place: and in addition, he has taken Greeks into the Temple, and made this holy place unclean.
For they had seen him before in the ton ith Trophimus of Ephesus, and had the idea that Paul had taken him ith him into the Temple.
And all the ton as moved, and the people came running together and put their hands on Paul, pulling him out of the Temple: and then the doors ere shut.
And hile they ere attempting to put him to death, nes came to the chief captain of the band that all Jerusalem as out of control.
And straight aay he took some armed men and ent quickly don to them: and the Jes, seeing them, gave no more blos to Paul.
Then the chief captain came near and took him, and gave orders for him to be put in chains, questioning them as to ho he as and hat he had done.
And some said one thing and some another, among the people: and as he as not able to get a knoledge of the facts because of the noise, he gave orders for Paul to be taken into the army building.
And hen he came on to the steps, he as lifted up by the armed men, because of the force of the people;
For a great mass of people came after them, crying out, Aay ith him!
And hen Paul as about to be taken into the building, he said to the chief captain, May I say something to you? And he said, Have you a knoledge of Greek?
Are you by chance the Egyptian ho, before this, got the people orked up against the government and took four thousand men of the Assassins out into the aste land?
But Paul said, I am a Je of Tarsus in Cilicia, hich is not an unimportant ton: I make a request to you to let me say a ord to the people.
And hen he let him do so, Paul, from the steps, made a sign ith his hand to the people, and hen they ere all quiet, he said to them in the Hebre language,
My brothers and fathers, give ear to the story of my life hich I no put before you.
And, hearing him talking in the Hebre language, they became the more quiet, and he said,

I am a Je of Tarsus in Cilicia by birth, but I had my education in this ton at the feet of Gamaliel, being trained in the keeping of every detail of the la of our fathers; given up to the cause of God ith all my heart, as you are today.
And I made attacks on this Way, even to death, taking men and omen and putting them in prison.
Of hich the high priest ill be a itness, and all the rulers, from hom I had letters to the brothers; and I ent into Damascus, to take those ho ere there as prisoners to Jerusalem for punishment.
And it came about that hile I as on my journey, coming near to Damascus, about the middle of the day, suddenly I sa a great light from heaven shining round me.
And hen I ent don on the earth, a voice came to my ears saying to me, Saul, Saul, hy are you attacking me so cruelly?
And I, ansering, said, Who are you; Lord? And he said to me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, hom you are attacking.
And those ho ere ith me sa the light, but the voice of him ho as talking to me came not to their ears.
And I said, What have I to do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Get up, and go into Damascus; and it ill be made clear to you hat you have to do.
And because I as unable to see because of the glory of that light, those ho ere ith me took me by the hand, and so I came to Damascus.
And one Ananias, a God-fearing man, ho kept the la, and of hom all the Jes in that place had a high opinion,
Came to my side and said, Brother Saul, let your eyes be open. And in that very hour I as able to see him.
And he said, You have been marked out by the God of our fathers to have knoledge of his purpose, and to see the Upright One and to give ear to the ords of his mouth.
For you ill be a itness for him to all men of hat you have seen and of hat has come to your ears.
And no, hy are you aiting? get up, and have baptism, for the ashing aay of your sins, giving orship to his name.
And it came about that hen I had come back to Jerusalem, hile I as at prayer in the Temple, my senses became more than naturally clear,
And I sa him saying to me, Go out of Jerusalem straight aay because they ill not give hearing to your itness about me.
And I said, Lord, they themselves have knoledge that I ent through the Synagogues putting in prison and hipping all those ho had faith in you:
And hen Stephen your itness as put to death, I as there, giving approval, and looking after the clothing of those ho put him to death.
And he said to me, Go, for I ill send you far aay to the Gentiles.
And they gave him a hearing as far as this ord; then ith loud voices they said, Aay ith this man from the earth; it is not right for him to be living.
And hile they ere crying out, and pulling off their clothing, and sending dust into the air,

The chief captain gave orders for him to be taken into the army building, saying that he ould put him to the test by hipping, so that he might have knoledge of the reason hy they ere crying out so violently against him.
And hen they had put leather bands round him, Paul said to the captain ho as present, Is it the la for you to give blos to a man ho is a Roman and has not been judged?
And hearing this, the man ent to the chief captain and gave him an account of it, saying, What are you about to do? for this man is a Roman.
And the chief captain came to him and said, Give me an anser, are you a Roman? And he said, Yes.
And the chief captain said, I got Roman rights for myself at a great price. And Paul said, But I had them by birth.
Then those ho ere about to put him to the test ent aay: and the chief captain as in fear, seeing that he as a Roman, and that he had put chains on him.

But on the day after, desiring to have certain knoledge of hat the Jes had to say against him, he made him free, and gave orders for the chief priests and all the Sanhedrin to come together, and he took Paul and put him before them.
And Paul, looking fixedly at the Sanhedrin, said, My brothers, my life has been upright before God till this day.
And the high priest, Ananias, gave orders to those ho ere near him to give him a blo on the mouth.
Then Paul said to him, God ill give blos to you, you hiteashed all: are you here to be my judge by la, and by your orders am I given blos against the la?
And those ho ere near said, Do you say such ords against God’s high priest?
And Paul said, Brother, I had no idea that he as the high priest: for it has been said, You may not say evil about the ruler of your people.

But hen Paul sa that half of them ere Sadducees and the rest Pharisees, he said in the Sanhedrin, Brothers, I am a Pharisee, and the son of Pharisees: I am here to be judged on the question of the hope of the coming back from the dead.
And hen he had said this, there as an argument beteen the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and a division in the meeting.
For the Sadducees say that there is no coming back from the dead, and no angels or spirits: but the Pharisees have belief in all these.

And there as a great outcry: and some of the scribes on the side of the Pharisees got up and took part in the discussion, saying, We see no evil in this man: hat if he has had a revelation from an angel or a spirit?

And hen the argument became very violent, the chief captain, fearing that Paul ould be pulled in to by them, gave orders to the armed men to take him by force from among them, and take him into the army building.
And the night after, the Lord came to his side and said, Be of good heart, for as you have been itnessing for me in Jerusalem, so ill you be my itness in Rome.
And hen it as day, the Jes came together and put themselves under an oath that they ould take no food or drink till they had put Paul to death.
And more than forty of them took this oath.
And they came to the chief priests and the rulers and said, We have taken a great oath to take no food till e have put Paul to death

So no, ill you and the Sanhedrin make a request to the military authorities to have him sent don to you, as if you ere desiring to go into the business in greater detail; and e, before ever he gets to you, ill be aiting to put him to death.
But Paul’s sister’s son had ord of their design, and he came into the army building and gave nes of it to Paul.
And Paul sent for a captain and said, Take this young man to your chief, for he has nes for him.
So he took him to the chief captain and said, Paul, the prisoner, made a request to me to take this young man to you, for he has something to say to you.
And the chief took him by the hand and, going on one side, said to him privately, What is it you have to say to me?
And he said, The Jes are in agreement together to make a request to you for Paul to be taken, on the day after this, into the Sanhedrin, to be questioned in greater detail.

But do not give ay to them, for more than forty of them are aiting for him, having taken an oath not to take food or drink till they have put him to death: and no they are ready, aiting for your order.
So the chief captain let the young man go, saying to him, Do not say to anyone that you have given me ord of these things.
And he sent for to captains and said, Make ready to hundred men, ith seventy horsemen and to hundred spearmen, to go to Caesarea, at the third hour of the night:
And get beasts so that they may put Paul on them, and take him safely to Felix, the ruler.
And he sent a letter in these ords:
Claudius Lysias, to the most noble ruler, Felix, peace be ith you.
This man as taken by the Jes, and as about to be put to death by them, hen I came on them ith the army and took him out of danger, having knoledge that he as a Roman.
And, desiring to get at the reason for their attack on him, I took him don to their Sanhedrin:
Then it became clear to me that it as a question of their la, and that nothing as said against him hich might be a reason for prison or death.
And hen nes as given to me that a secret design as being made against the man, I sent him straight aay to you, giving orders to those ho are against him to make their statements before you.
So the armed men, as they ere ordered, took Paul and came by night to Antipatris.
But on the day after, they sent the horsemen on ith him, and ent back to their place:
And they, hen they came to Caesarea, gave the letter to the ruler, and took Paul before him.
And after reading it, he said, What part of the country do you come from? And, hearing that he as from Cilicia,
I ill give hearing to your cause, he said, hen those ho are against you have come. And he gave orders for him to be kept in Herod’s Praetorium.
And after five days, the high priest, Ananias, came ith certain of the rulers, and an expert talker, one Tertullus; and they made a statement to Felix against Paul.
And hen he had been sent for, Tertullus, starting his statement, said, Because by you e are living in peace, and through your isdom rongs are put right for this nation,
In all things and in all places e are conscious of our great debt to you, most noble Felix.
But, so that I may not make you tired, I make a request to you of your mercy, to give hearing to a short statement.
For this man, in our opinion, is a cause of trouble, a maker of attacks on the government among Jes through all the empire, and a chief mover in the society of the Nazarenes:
Who, in addition, as attempting to make the Temple unclean: hom e took,
And from hom you ill be able, by questioning him yourself, to get knoledge of all the things hich e say against him.
And the Jes ere in agreement ith his statement, saying that these things ere so.
Then hen the ruler had given him a sign to make his anser, Paul said, Because I have knoledge that you have been a judge over this nation for a number of years, I am glad to make my anser:
Seeing that you are able to make certain of the fact that it is not more than telve days from the time hen I came up to Jerusalem for orship;
And they have not seen me in argument ith any man in the Temple, or orking up the feelings of the people, in the Synagogues or in the ton:
And they are not able to give facts in support of the things hich they say against me no.

But this I ill say openly to you, that I do give orship to the God of our fathers after that Way, hich to them is not the true religion: but I have belief in all the things hich are in the la and in the books of the prophets:
Hoping in God for that hich they themselves are looking for, that there ill be a coming back from the dead for upright men and rongdoers.
And in this, I do my best at all times to have no reason for shame before God or men.
No after a number of years I came to give help and offerings to my nation:
And having been made clean, I as in the Temple, but not ith a great number of people, and not ith noise: but there ere certain Jes from Asia,
And it ould have been better if they had come here to make a statement, if they have anything against me.
Or let these men here present say hat rongdoing as seen in me hen I as before the Sanhedrin,
But only this one thing hich I said among them in a loud voice, I am this day being judged on the question of the coming back from the dead.
But Felix, ho had a more detailed knoledge of the Way, put them off, saying, When Lysias, the chief captain, comes don, I ill give attention to your business.
And he gave orders to the captain to keep Paul under his control, and to let him have everything he had need of; and not to keep his friends from coming to see him.
But after some days, Felix came ith Drusilla his ife, ho as of the Jes by birth, and sent for Paul, and gave hearing to him about faith in Christ Jesus.
And hile he as talking about righteousness and self-control and the judging hich as to come, Felix had great fear and said, Go aay for the present, and hen the right time comes I ill send for you.
For he as hoping that Paul ould give him money: so he sent for him more frequently and had talk ith him.
But after to years Porcius Festus took the place of Felix, ho, desiring to have the approval of the Jes, kept Paul in chains.
So Festus, having come into that part of the country hich as under his rule, after three days ent up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
And the chief priests and the chief men of the Jes made statements against Paul,
Requesting Festus to give effect to their design against him, and send him to Jerusalem, hen they ould be aiting to put him to death on the ay.
But Festus, in anser, said that Paul as being kept in prison at Caesarea, and that in a short time he himself as going there.
So, he said, let those ho have authority among you go ith me, and if there is any rong in the man, let them make a statement against him.
And hen he had been ith them not more than eight or ten days, he ent don to Caesarea; and on the day after, he took his place on the judge’s seat, and sent for Paul.
And hen he came, the Jes ho had come don from Jerusalem came round him, and made all sorts of serious statements against him, hich ere not supported by the facts.
Then Paul, in his anser to them, said, I have done no rong against the la of the Jes, or against the Temple, or against Caesar.
But Festus, desiring to get the approval of the Jes, said to Paul, Will you go up to Jerusalem, and be judged before me there in connection ith these things?
And Paul said, I am before the seat of Caesar’s authority here it is right for me to be judged: I have done no rong to the Jes, as you are ell able to see.
If, then, I am a rongdoer and there is a cause of death in me, I am ready for death: if it is not as they say against me, no man may give me up to them. Let my cause come before Caesar.
Then Festus, having had a discussion ith the Jes, made anser, You have said, Let my cause come before Caesar; to Caesar you ill go.
No hen some days had gone by, King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea and ent to see Festus.
And as they ere there for some days, Festus gave them Paul’s story, saying, There is a certain man here ho as put in prison by Felix:
Against hom the chief priests and the rulers of the Jes made a statement hen I as at Jerusalem, requesting me to give a decision against him.

To hom I gave anser that it is not the Roman ay to give a man up, till he has been face to face ith those ho are attacking him, and has had a chance to give an anser to the statements made against him.
So, hen they had come together here, straight aay, on the day after, I took my place on the judge’s seat and sent for the man.
But hen they got up they said nothing about such crimes as I had in mind:
But had certain questions against him in connection ith their religion, and about one Jesus, no dead, ho, Paul said, as living.
And as I had not enough knoledge for the discussion of these things, I made the suggestion to him to go to Jerusalem and be judged there.
But hen Paul made a request that he might be judged by Caesar, I gave orders for him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar.
And Agrippa said to Festus, I have a desire to give the man a hearing myself. Tomorro, he said, you may give him a hearing.

So on the day after, hen Agrippa and Bernice in great glory had come into the public place of hearing, ith the chief of the army and the chief men of the ton, at the order of Festus, Paul as sent for.

And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all those ho are present here ith us, you see this man, about hom all the Jes have made protests to me, at Jerusalem and in this place, saying that it is not right for him to be living any longer.
But, in my opinion, there is no cause of death in him, and as he himself has made a request to be judged by Caesar, I have said that I ould send him.

But I have no certain account of him to send to Caesar. So I have sent for him to come before you, and specially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the business has been gone into, I may have something to put in riting.
For it seems to me against reason to send a prisoner ithout making clear hat there is against him.
And Agrippa said to Paul, You may put your cause before us. Then Paul, stretching out his hand, made his anser, saying:
In my opinion I am happy, King Agrippa, to be able to give my anser before you today to all these things hich the Jes say against me:
The more so, because you are expert in all questions to do ith the Jes and their ays: so I make my request to you to give me a hearing to the end.
All the Jes have knoledge of my ay of life from my early years, as it as from the start among my nation, and at Jerusalem;
And they are able to say, if they ould give itness, that I as living as a Pharisee, in that division of our religion hich is most regular in the keeping of the la.
And no I am here to be judged because of the hope given by God’s ord to our fathers;
For the effecting of hich our telve tribes have been orking and aiting night and day ith all their hearts. And in connection ith this hope I am attacked by the Jes, O king!
Why, in your opinion, is it outside belief for God to make the dead come to life again?
For I, truly, as of the opinion that it as right for me to do a number of things against the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
And this I did in Jerusalem: and numbers of the saints I put in prison, having had authority given to me from the chief priests, and hen they ere put to death, I gave my decision against them.
And I gave them punishment frequently, in all the Synagogues, forcing them to say things against God; and burning ith passion against them, I ent after them even into far-aay tons.
Then, hen I as journeying to Damascus ith the authority and orders of the chief priests,
In the middle of the day, on the road I sa a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining round me and those ho ere journeying ith me.

And hen e had all gone don on the earth, a voice came to me, saying in the Hebre language, Saul, Saul, hy are you attacking me so cruelly? It is hard for you to go against the impulse hich is driving you.
And I said, Who are you, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus, hom you are attacking.
But get up on your feet: for I have come to you for this purpose, to make you a servant and a itness of the things in hich you have seen me, and of those in hich you ill see me;
And I ill keep you safe from the people, and from the Gentiles, to hom I send you,

To make their eyes open, turning them from the dark to the light, and from the poer of Satan to God, so that they may have forgiveness of sins and a heritage among those ho are made holy by faith in me.
So, then, King Agrippa, I did not go against the vision from heaven;

But I ent about, first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, and through all the country of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, preaching a change of heart, so that they, being turned to God, might give, in their orks, the fruits of a changed heart.
For this reason, the Jes took me in the Temple, and made an attempt to put me to death.
And so, by God’s help, I am here today, itnessing to small and great, saying nothing but hat the prophets and Moses said ould come about;
That the Christ ould go through pain, and being the first to come back from the dead, ould give light to the people and to the Gentiles.
And hen he made his anser in these ords, Festus said in a loud voice, Paul, you are off your head; your great learning has made you unbalanced.
Then Paul said, I am not off my head, most noble Festus, but my ords are true and ise.
For the king has knoledge of these things, to hom I am talking freely; being certain that all this is common knoledge to him; for it has not been done in secret.
King Agrippa, have you faith in the prophets? I am certain that you have.
And Agrippa said to Paul, A little more and you ill be making me a Christian.
And Paul said, It is my prayer to God that, in little or great measure, not only you, but all those hearing me today might be even as I am, but for these chains.
And the king and the ruler and Bernice and those ho ere seated ith them got up;
And hen they had gone aay they said to one another, This man has done nothing hich might give cause for death or prison.
And Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been made free, if he had not put his cause before Caesar.
And hen the decision had been made that e ere to go by sea to Italy, they gave Paul and certain other prisoners into the care of a captain named Julius, of the Augustan band.
And e ent to sea in a ship of Adramyttium hich as sailing to the sea tons of Asia, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being ith us.
And on the day after, e came to Sidon; and Julius as kind to Paul, and let him go to see his friends and take a rest.
And sailing again from there, e ent on under cover of Cyprus, because the ind as against us.
And having gone across the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia e came to Myra, in Lycia.
And there the captain came across a ship of Alexandria, sailing for Italy, and put us in it.
And hen e had gone on sloly for a long time, and had had hard ork getting across to Cnidus, for the ind as against us, e ent under cover of Crete, in the direction of Salmone;
And sailing don the side of it, as ell as e ere able, e came to a certain place named Fair Havens, near hich as the ton of Lasea.
And as a long time had gone by, and the journey as no full of danger, because it as late in the year, Paul put the position before them,
Saying, Friends, I see that this journey ill be one of great damage and loss, not only to the goods and the ship, but to ourselves.
But the captain gave more attention to the master and the oner of the ship than to hat Paul said.

And as the harbour as not a good one in hich to be for the inter, the greater number of them ere for going out to sea, in order, if possible, to put in for the inter at Phoenix, a harbour of Crete, looking to the north-east and south-east.
And hen the south ind came softly, being of the opinion that their purpose might be effected, they let the ship go and ent sailing don the side of Crete, very near to the land.
But after a little time, a very violent ind, named Euraquilo, came don from it ith great force.
And hen the ship got into the grip of it, and as not able to make headay into the ind, e gave ay, and ent before it.
And, sailing near the side of a small island named Cauda, e ere able, though it as hard ork, to make the ship’s boat safe:
And having got it up, they put cords under and round the ship; but fearing that they might be pushed on to the Syrtis, they let don the sails and so ent running before the ind.
And, still fighting the storm ith all our strength, the day after they made a start at getting the goods out of the ship;
And on the third day, they let all the sailing apparatus go over the side.
And as e had not seen the sun or stars for a long time, and a great storm as on us, all hope of salvation as gone.

And hen they had been ithout food for a long time, Paul got up among them and said, Friends, it ould have been better if you had given attention to me and not gone sailing out from Crete, to undergo this damage and loss.
But no, I say to you, be of good heart, for there ill be no loss of life, but only of the ship.
For this night there came to my side an angel of the God ho is my Master and hose servant I am,
Saying, Have no fear, Paul, for you ill come before Caesar, and God has given to you all those ho are sailing ith you.
And so, O men, be of good heart, for I have faith in God that it ill be as he said to me.
But e ill be sent on to a certain island.
But hen the fourteenth day came, hile e ere going here and there in the Adriatic sea, about the middle of the night the sailors had an idea that they ere getting near land;
And they let don the lead, and sa that the sea as a hundred and tenty feet deep; and after a little time they did it again and it as ninety feet.
Then, fearing that by chance e might come on to the rocks, they let don four hooks from the back of the ship, and made prayers for the coming of day.
Then the sailors made attempts secretly to get aay from the ship, letting don a boat as if they ere about to put don hooks from the front of the ship;
But Paul said to the captain and his men, If you do not keep these men in the ship, you ill not be safe.
Then the armed men, cutting the cords of the boat, let her go.
And hen dan as near, Paul gave them all orders to take food, saying, This is the fourteenth day you have been aiting and taking no food.
So I make request to you to take food; for this is for your salvation: not a hair from the head of any of you ill come to destruction.
And hen he had said this and had taken bread, he gave praise to God before them all, and took a meal of the broken bread.
Then they all took heart and did the same.
And e ere, in the ship, to hundred and seventy-six persons.
And hen they had had enough food, they made the eight of the ship less, turning the grain out into the sea.
And hen it as day, they had no knoledge of the land, but they sa an inlet of the sea ith a floor of sand, and they had the idea of driving the ship up on to it if possible.
So cutting aay the hooks, and letting them go into the sea, and freeing the cords of the guiding-blades, and lifting up the sail to the ind, they ent in the direction of the inlet.
And coming to a point beteen to seas, they got the ship to land; and the front part as fixed in the sand and not able to be moved, but the back part as broken by the force of the aves.
Then the armed men ere for putting the prisoners to death, so that no one ould get aay by simming.
But the captain, desiring to keep Paul safe, kept them from their purpose, and gave orders that those ho had knoledge of simming ere to go off the ship and get first to land:
And the rest, some on boards and some on things from the ship. And so it came about that they all got safe to land.
And hen e ere safe, e made the discovery that the island as named Melita.
And the simple people living there ere uncommonly kind to us, for they made a fire for us, and took us in, because it as raining and cold.
But hen Paul had got some sticks together and put them on the fire, a snake came out, because of the heat, and gave him a bite on the hand.

And hen the people sa it hanging on his hand, they said to one another, Without doubt this man has put someone to death, and though he has got safely aay from the sea, God ill not let him go on living.
But shaking off the beast into the fire, he got no damage.

But they had the idea that they ould see him becoming ill, or suddenly falling don dead; but after aiting a long time, and seeing that no damage came to him, changing their opinion, they said he as a god.
No near that place there as some land, the property of the chief man of the island, ho as named Publius; ho very kindly took us into his house as his guests for three days.
And the father of Publius as ill, ith a disease of the stomach; to hom Paul ent, and put his hands on him, ith prayer, and made him ell.
And hen this took place, all the others in the island ho had diseases came and ere made ell.
Then they gave us great honour, and, hen e ent aay, they put into the ship hatever things e ere in need of.
And after three months e ent to sea in a ship of Alexandria sailing under the sign of the Dioscuri, hich had been at the island for the inter.
And going into the harbour at Syracuse, e ere aiting there for three days.
And from there, going about in a curve, e came to Rhegium: and after one day a south ind came up and on the day after e came to Puteoli:
Where e came across some of the brothers, ho kept us ith them for seven days; and so e came to Rome.
And the brothers, hen they had nes of us, came out from ton as far as Appii Forum and the Three Taverns to have a meeting ith us: and Paul, seeing them, gave praise to God and took heart.
And hen e came into Rome, they let Paul have a house for himself and the armed man ho kept atch over him.

Then after three days he sent for the chief men of the Jes: and hen they had come together, he said to them, My brothers, though I had done nothing against the people or the ays of our fathers, I as given, a prisoner from Jerusalem, into the hands of the Romans.
Who, hen they had put questions to me, ere ready to let me go free, because there as no cause of death in me.
But hen the Jes made protest against it, I had to put my cause into Caesar’s hands; not because I have anything to say against my nation.
But for this reason I sent for you, to see and have talk ith you: for because of the hope of Israel I am in these chains.
And they said to him, We have not had letters from Judaea about you, and no one of the brothers has come to us here to give an account or say any evil about you.
But e have a desire to give hearing to your opinion: for as to this form of religion, e have knoledge that in all places it is attacked.

And hen a day had been fixed, they came to his house in great numbers; and he gave them teaching, giving itness to the kingdom of God, and having discussions ith them about Jesus, from the la of Moses and from the prophets, from morning till evening.
And some ere in agreement ith hat he said, but some had doubts.
And they ent aay, for there as a division among them after Paul had said this one thing: Well did the Holy Spirit say by the prophet Isaiah to your fathers,
Go to this people and say, Though you give ear, you ill not get knoledge; and seeing, you ill see, but the sense ill not be clear to you:

For the heart of this people has become fat and their ears are slo in hearing and their eyes are shut; for fear that they might see ith their eyes and give hearing ith their ears and become ise in their hearts and be turned again to me, so that I might make them ell.
Be certain, then, that the salvation of God is sent to the Gentiles, and they ill give hearing.
And for the space of to years, Paul as living in the house of hich he had the use, and had talk ith all those ho ent in to see him,
Preaching the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ ithout fear, and no orders ere given that he as not to do so.
Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, an Apostle by the selection of God, given authority as a preacher of the good nes,
Of hich God had given ord before by his prophets in the holy Writings,
