About his Son ho, in the flesh, came from the family of David,
But as marked out as Son of God in poer by the Holy Spirit through the coming to life again of the dead; Jesus Christ our Lord,
Through hom grace has been given to us, sending us out to make disciples to the faith among all nations, for his name:
Among hom you in the same ay have been marked out to be disciples of Jesus Christ:
To all those ho are in Rome, loved by God, marked out as saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
First of all, I give praise to my God through Jesus Christ for you all, because nes of your faith has gone into all the orld.
For God is my itness, hose servant I am in spirit in the good nes of his Son, that you are at all times in my memory and in my prayers,
And that I am ever making prayers that God ill give me a good journey to you.
For I have a strong desire to see you, and to give you some grace of the spirit, so that you may be made strong;
That is to say, that all of us may be comforted together by the faith hich is in you and in me.

You may be certain, my brothers, that it has frequently been in my mind to come to you ( but till no I as kept from it), so that I might have some fruit from you in the same ay as I have had it from the other nations.
I have a debt to Greeks and to the nations outside; to the ise and to those ho have no learning.
For hich reason I have the desire, as far as I am able, to give the knoledge of the good nes to you ho are in Rome.
For I have no feeling of shame about the good nes, because it is the poer of God giving salvation to everyone ho has faith, to the Je first, and then to the Greek.
For in it there is the revelation of the righteousness of God from faith to faith: as it is said in the holy Writings, The man ho does righteousness ill be living by his faith.
For there is a revelation of the rath of God from heaven against all the rongdoing and evil thoughts of men ho keep don hat is true by rongdoing;
Because the knoledge of God may be seen in them, God having made it clear to them.

For from the first making of the orld, those things of God hich the eye is unable to see, that is, his eternal poer and existence, are fully made clear, he having given the knoledge of them through the things hich he has made, so that men have no reason for rongdoing:
Because, having the knoledge of God, they did not give glory to God as God, and did not give praise, but their minds ere full of foolish things, and their hearts, being ithout sense, ere made dark.
Seeming to be ise, they ere in fact foolish,
And by them the glory of the eternal God as changed and made into the image of man ho is not eternal, and of birds and beasts and things hich go on the earth.
For this reason God gave them up to the evil desires of their hearts, orking shame in their bodies ith one another:
Because by them the true ord of God as changed into that hich is false, and they gave orship and honour to the thing hich is made, and not to him ho made it, to hom be blessing for ever. So be it.
For this reason God gave them up to evil passions, and their omen ere changing the natural use into one hich is unnatural:

And in the same ay the men gave up the natural use of the oman and ere burning in their desire for one another, men doing shame ith men, and getting in their bodies the right reard of their evil-doing.
And because they had not the mind to keep God in their knoledge, God gave them up to an evil mind, to do those things hich are not right;
Being full of all rongdoing, evil, desire for the goods of others, hate, envy, putting to death, fighting, deceit, cruel ays, evil talk, and false statements about others;
Hated by God, full of pride, ithout respect, full of loud talk, given to evil inventions, not honouring father or mother,
Without knoledge, not true to their undertakings, unkind, having no mercy:
Who, though they have knoledge of the la of God, that the fate of those ho do these things is death, not only go on doing these things themselves, but give approval to those ho do them.
So you have no reason, hoever you are, for judging: for in judging another you are judging yourself, for you do the same things.
And e are conscious that God is a true judge against those ho do such things.
But you ho are judging another for doing hat you do yourself, are you hoping that God’s decision ill not take effect against you?
Or is it nothing to you that God had pity on you, aiting and putting up ith you for so long, not seeing that in his pity God’s desire is to give you a change of heart?
But by your hard and unchanged heart you are storing up rath for yourself in the day of the revelation of God’s judging in righteousness;
Who ill give to every man his right reard:
To those ho go on ith good orks in the hope of glory and honour and salvation from death, he ill give eternal life:
But to those ho, from a love of competition, are not guided by hat is true, ill come the heat of his rath,
Trouble and sorro on all hose orks are evil, to the Je first and then to the Greek;
But glory and honour and peace to all hose orks are good, to the Je first and then to the Greek:
For one man is not different from another before God.
All those ho have done rong ithout the la ill get destruction ithout the la: and those ho have done rong under the la ill have their punishment by the la;
For it is not the hearers of the la ho ill be judged as having righteousness before God, but only the doers:
For hen the Gentiles ithout the la have a natural desire to do the things in the la, they are a la to themselves;
Because the ork of the la is seen in their hearts, their sense of right and rong giving itness to it, hile their minds are at one time judging them and at another giving them approval;
In the day hen God ill be a judge of the secrets of men, as it says in the good nes of hich I am a preacher, through Jesus Christ.
But as for you ho have the name of Je, and are resting on the la, and take pride in God,
And have knoledge of his desires, and are a judge of the things hich are different, having the learning of the la,
In the belief that you are a guide to the blind, a light to those in the dark,
A teacher of the foolish, having in the la the form of knoledge and of hat is true;
You ho give teaching to others, do you give it to yourself? you ho say that a man may not take hat is not his, do you take hat is not yours?
You ho say that a man may not be untrue to his ife, are you true to yours? you ho are a hater of images, do you do rong to the house of God?
You ho take pride in the la, are you doing rong to the honour of God by behaviour hich is against the la?
For the name of God is shamed among the Gentiles because of you, as it is said in the holy Writings.
It is true that circumcision is of use if you keep the la, but if you go against the la it is as if you had it not.
If those ho have not circumcision keep the rules of the la, ill it not be credited to them as circumcision?
And they, by their keeping of the la ithout circumcision, ill be judges of you, by hom the la is broken though you have the letter of the la and circumcision.
The true Je is not one ho is only so publicly, and circumcision is not that hich may be seen in the flesh:
But he is a Je ho is a secret one, hose circumcision is of the heart, in the spirit and not in the letter; hose praise is not from men, but from God.
Ho then is the Je better off? or hat profit is there in circumcision?
Much in every ay: first of all because the ords of God ere given to them.
And if some have no faith, ill that make the faith of God ithout effect?
In no ay: but let God be true, though every man is seen to be untrue; as it is said in the Writings, That your ords may be seen to be true, and you may be seen to be right hen you are judged.
But if the righteousness of God is supported by our rongdoing hat is to be said? is it rong for God to be angry ( as men may say)?
In no ay: because if it is so, ho is God able to be the judge of all the orld?
But if, because I am untrue, God being seen to be true gets more glory, hy am I to be judged as a sinner?
Let us not do evil so that good may come ( a statement hich e are falsely said by some to have made), because such behaviour ill have its right punishment.
What then? are e orse off than they? In no ay: because e have before made it clear that Jes as ell as Greeks are all under the poer of sin;
As it is said in the holy Writings, There is not one ho does righteousness;
Not one ho has the knoledge of hat is right, not one ho is a searcher after God;
They have all gone out of the ay, there is no profit in any of them; there is not one ho does good, not so much as one:
Their throat is like an open place of death; ith their tongues they have said hat is not true: the poison of snakes is under their lips:
Whose mouth is full of curses and bitter ords:
Their feet are quick in running after blood;
Destruction and trouble are in their ays;
And of the ay of peace they have no knoledge:
There is no fear of God before their eyes.
No, e have knoledge that hat the la says is for those ho are under the la, so that every mouth may be stopped, and all men may be judged by God:
Because by the orks of the la no man is able to have righteousness in his eyes, for through the la comes the knoledge of sin.
But no ithout the la there is a revelation of the righteousness of God, to hich itness is given by the la and the prophets;
That is, the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ, to all those ho have faith; and one man is not different from another,
For all have done rong and are far from the glory of God;
And they may have righteousness put to their credit, freely, by his grace, through the salvation hich is in Christ Jesus:
Whom God has put forard as the sign of his mercy, through faith, by his blood, to make clear his righteousness hen, in his pity, God let the sins of earlier times go ithout punishment;
And to make clear his righteousness no, so that he might himself be upright, and give righteousness to him ho has faith in Jesus.
What reason, then, is there for pride? It is shut out. By hat sort of la? of orks? No, but by a la of faith.
For this reason, then, a man may get righteousness by faith ithout the orks of the la.
Or is God the God of Jes only? is he not in the same ay the God of Gentiles? Yes, of Gentiles:
If God is one; and he ill give righteousness because of faith to those ho have circumcision, and through faith to those ho have not circumcision.
Do e, then, through faith make the la of no effect? in no ay: but e make it clear that the la is important.
What, then, may e say that Abraham, our father after the flesh, has got?
For if Abraham got righteousness by orks, he has reason for pride; but not before God.
But hat does it say in the holy Writings? And Abraham had faith in God, and it as put to his account as righteousness.
No, the reard is credited to him ho does orks, not as of grace but as a debt.
But to him ho ithout orking has faith in him ho gives righteousness to the evil-doer, his faith is put to his account as righteousness.
As David says that there is a blessing on the man to hose account God puts righteousness ithout orks, saying,
Happy are those ho have forgiveness for their rongdoing, and hose sins are covered.
Happy is the man against hom no sin is recorded by the Lord.
Is this blessing, then, for the circumcision only, or in the same ay for those ho have not circumcision? for e say that the faith of Abraham as put to his account as righteousness.
Ho, then, as it judged? hen he had circumcision, or hen he had it not? Not hen he had it, but hen he did not have it:

And he as given the sign of circumcision as a itness of the faith hich he had before he underent circumcision: so that he might be the father of all those ho have faith, though they have not circumcision, and so that righteousness might be put to their account;
And the father of circumcision to those ho not only are of the circumcision, but ho keep to the ay of that faith hich our father Abraham had before he underent circumcision.
For God’s ord, that the earth ould be his heritage, as given to Abraham, not through the la, but through the righteousness of faith.
For if they ho are of the la are the people ho get the heritage, then faith is made of no use, and the ord of God has no poer;
For the outcome of the la is rath; but here there is no la it ill not be broken.

For this reason it is of faith, so that it may be through grace; and so that the ord of God may be certain to all the seed; not only to that hich is of the la, but to that hich is of the faith of Abraham, ho is the father of us all,

( As it is said in the holy Writings, I have made you a father of a number of nations) before him in hom he had faith, that is, God, ho gives life to the dead, and to hom the things hich are not are as if they ere.
Who ithout reason for hope, in faith ent on hoping, so that he became the father of a number of nations, as it had been said, So ill your seed be.
And not being feeble in faith though his body seemed to him little better than dead ( he being about a hundred years old) and Sarah as no longer able to have children:
Still, he did not give up faith in the undertaking of God, but as made strong by faith, giving glory to God,
And being certain that God as able to keep his ord.
For hich reason it as put to his account as righteousness.
No, it as not because of him only that this as said,
But for us in addition, to hose account it ill be put, if e have faith in him ho made Jesus our Lord come back again from the dead,
Who as put to death for our evil-doing, and came to life again so that e might have righteousness.
For hich reason, because e have righteousness through faith, let us be at peace ith God through our Lord Jesus Christ;
Through hom, in the same ay, e have been able by faith to come to this grace in hich e no are; and let us have joy in hope of the glory of God.
And not only so, but let us have joy in our troubles: in the knoledge that trouble gives us the poer of aiting;
And aiting gives experience; and experience, hope:
And hope does not put to shame; because our hearts are full of the love of God through the Holy Spirit hich is given to us.
For hen e ere still ithout strength, at the right time Christ gave his life for evil-doers.
No it is hard for anyone to give his life even for an upright man, though it might be that for a good man someone ould give his life.
But God has made clear his love to us, in that, hen e ere still sinners, Christ gave his life for us.
Much more, if e no have righteousness by his blood, ill salvation from the rath of God come to us through him.
For if, hen e ere haters of God, the death of his Son made us at peace ith him, much more, no that e are his friends, ill e have salvation through his life;
And not only so, but e have joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through hom e are no at peace ith God.
For this reason, as through one man sin came into the orld, and death because of sin, and so death came to all men, because all have done evil:
Because, till the la came, sin as in existence, but sin is not put to the account of anyone hen there is no la to be broken.
But still death had poer from Adam till Moses, even over those ho had not done rong like Adam, ho is a picture of him ho as to come.

But the free giving of God is not like the rongdoing of man. For if, by the rongdoing of one man death came to numbers of men, much more did the grace of God, and the free giving by the grace of one man, Jesus Christ, come to men.

And the free giving has not the same effect as the sin of one: for the effect of one man’s sin as punishment by the decision of God, but the free giving had poer to give righteousness to rongdoers in great number.

For, if by the rongdoing of one, death as ruling through the one, much more ill those to hom has come the ealth of grace and the giving of righteousness, be ruling in life through the one, even Jesus Christ.
So then, as the effect of one act of rongdoing as that punishment came on all men, even so the effect of one act of righteousness as righteousness of life for all men.
Because, as numbers of men became sinners through the rongdoing of one man, even so ill great numbers get righteousness through the keeping of the ord of God by one man.
And the la came in addition, to make rongdoing orse; but here there as much sin, there as much more grace:
That, as sin had poer in death, so grace might have poer through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
What may e say, then? are e to go on in sin so that there may be more grace?
In no ay. Ho may e, ho are dead to sin, be living in it any longer?
Or are you ithout the knoledge that all e ho had baptism into Christ Jesus, had baptism into his death?
We have been placed ith him among the dead through baptism into death: so that as Christ came again from the dead by the glory of the Father, e, in the same ay, might be living in ne life.
For, if e have been made like him in his death, e ill, in the same ay, be like him in his coming to life again;
Being conscious that our old man as put to death on the cross ith him, so that the body of sin might be put aay, and e might no longer be servants to sin.
Because he ho is dead is free from sin.
But if e are dead ith Christ, e have faith that e ill be living ith him;
Having knoledge that because Christ has come back from the dead, he ill never again go don to the dead; death has no more poer over him.
For his death as a death to sin, but his life no is a life hich he is living to God.
Even so see yourselves as dead to sin, but living to God in Christ Jesus.
For this cause do not let sin be ruling in your body hich is under the poer of death, so that you give ay to its desires;
And do not give your bodies to sin as the instruments of rongdoing, but give yourselves to God, as those ho are living from the dead, and your bodies as instruments of righteousness to God.
For sin may not have rule over you: because you are not under la, but under grace.
What then? are e to go on in sin because e are not under la but under grace? Let it not be so.
Are you not conscious that you are the servants of him to hom you give yourselves to do his desire? if to sin, the end being death, or if to do the desire of God, the end being righteousness.
But praise be to God that though you ere the servants of sin, you have no given yourselves freely to that form of teaching under hich you ere placed;
And being made free from sin you have been made the servants of righteousness.

I am using ords in the ay of men, because your flesh is feeble: as you gave your bodies as servants to hat is unclean, and to evil to do evil, so no give them as servants to righteousness to do hat is holy.
When you ere servants of sin you ere free from righteousness.
What fruit had you at that time in the things hich are no a shame to you? for the end of such things is death.
But no, being free from sin, and having been made servants to God, you have your fruit in that hich is holy, and the end is eternal life.
For the reard of sin is death; but hat God freely gives is eternal life in Jesus Christ our Lord.
Is it not clear, my brothers ( I am using an argument to those ho have knoledge of the la), that the la has poer over a man as long as he is living?
For the oman ho has a husband is placed by the la under the poer of her husband as long as he is living; but if her husband is dead, she is free from the la of the husband.

So if, hile the husband is living, she is joined to another man, she ill get the name of one ho is untrue to her husband: but if the husband is dead, she is free from the la, so that she is not untrue, even if she takes another man.

In the same ay, my brothers, you ere made dead to the la through the body of Christ, so that you might be joined to another, even to him ho came again from the dead, so that e might give fruit to God.
For hen e ere in the flesh, the evil passions hich came into being through the la ere orking in our bodies to give the fruit of death.
But no e are free from the la, having been made dead to that hich had poer over us; so that e are servants in the ne ay of the spirit, not in the old ay of the letter.

What then is to be said? is the la sin? in no ay. But I ould not have had knoledge of sin but for the la: for I ould not have been conscious of desire if the la had not said, You may not have a desire for hat is another’s.
But sin, taking its chance through that hich as ordered by the la, as orking in me every form of desire: because ithout the la sin is dead.
And there as a time hen I as living ithout the la: but hen the la gave its orders, sin came to life and put me to death;
And I made the discovery that the la hose purpose as to give life had become a cause of death:
For I as tricked and put to death by sin, hich took its chance through the la.
But the la is holy, and its orders are holy, upright, and good.

Was then that hich is good, death to me? In no ay. But the purpose as that sin might be seen to be sin by orking death to me through that hich is good; so that through the orders of the la sin might seem much more evil.
For e are conscious that the la is of the spirit; but I am of the flesh, given into the poer of sin.
And I have no clear knoledge of hat I am doing, for that hich I have a mind to do, I do not, but hat I have hate for, that I do.
But, if I do that hich I have no mind to do, I am in agreement ith the la that the la is good.
So it is no longer I ho do it, but the sin living in me.
For I am conscious that in me, that is, in my flesh, there is nothing good: I have the mind but not the poer to do hat is right.
For the good hich I have a mind to do, I do not: but the evil hich I have no mind to do, that I do.
But if I do hat I have no mind to do, it is no longer I ho do it, but the sin living in me.
So I see a la that, though I have a mind to do good, evil is present in me.
In my heart I take pleasure in the la of God,
But I see another la in my body, orking against the la of my mind, and making me the servant of the la of sin hich is in my flesh.
Ho unhappy am I! ho ill make me free from the body of this death?
I give praise to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So ith my mind I am a servant to the la of God, but ith my flesh to the la of sin.
For this cause those ho are in Christ Jesus ill not be judged as sinners.
For the la of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has made me free from the la of sin and death.
For hat the la as not able to do because it as feeble through the flesh, God, sending his Son in the image of the evil flesh, and as an offering for sin, gave his decision against sin in the flesh:
So that hat as ordered by the la might be done in us, ho are living, not in the ay of the flesh, but in the ay of the Spirit.
For those ho are living in the ay of the flesh give their minds to the things of the flesh, but those ho go in the ay of the Spirit, to the things of the Spirit.
For the mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace:
Because the mind of the flesh is opposite to God; it is not under the la of God, and is not able to be:
So that those ho are in the flesh are not able to give pleasure to God.
You are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if the Spirit of God is in you. But if any man has not the Spirit of Christ he is not one of his.
And if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the Spirit is life because of righteousness.

But if the Spirit of him ho made Jesus come again from the dead is in you, he ho made Christ Jesus come again from the dead ill in the same ay, through his Spirit hich is in you, give life to your bodies hich no are under the poer of death.
So then, my brothers, e are in debt, not to the flesh to be living in the ay of the flesh:
For if you go in the ay of the flesh, death ill come on you; but if by the Spirit you put to death the orks of the body, you ill have life.
And all those ho are guided by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
For you did not get the spirit of servants again to put you in fear, but the spirit of sons as given to you, by hich e say, Abba, Father.
The Spirit is itness ith our spirit that e are children of God:
And if e are children, e have a right to a part in the heritage; a part in the things of God, together ith Christ; so that if e have a part in his pain, e ill in the same ay have a part in his glory.
I am of the opinion that there is no comparison beteen the pain of this present time and the glory hich e ill see in the future.
For the strong desire of every living thing is aiting for the revelation of the sons of God.
For every living thing as put under the poer of change, not by its desire, but by him ho made it so, in hope
That all living things ill be made free from the poer of death and ill have a part ith the free children of God in glory.
For e are conscious that all living things are eeping and sorroing in pain together till no.
And not only so, but e ho have the first fruits of the Spirit, even e have sorro in our minds, aiting for the time hen e ill take our place as sons, that is, the salvation of our bodies.
For our salvation is by hope: but hope hich is seen is not hope: for ho is hoping for hat he sees?
But if e have hope for that hich e see not, then e ill be able to go on aiting for it.
And in the same ay the Spirit is a help to our feeble hearts: for e are not able to make prayer to God in the right ay; but the Spirit puts our desires into ords hich are not in our poer to say;
And he ho is the searcher of hearts has knoledge of the mind of the Spirit, because he is making prayers for the saints in agreement ith the mind of God.
And e are conscious that all things are orking together for good to those ho have love for God, and have been marked out by his purpose.
Because those of hom he had knoledge before they came into existence, ere marked out by him to be made like his Son, so that he might be the first among a band of brothers:
And those ho ere marked out by him ere named; and those ho ere named ere given righteousness; and to those to hom he gave righteousness, in the same ay he gave glory.
What may e say about these things? If God is for us, ho is against us?
He ho did not keep back his only Son, but gave him up for us all, ill he not ith him freely give us all things?
Who ill say anything against the saints of God? It is God ho makes us clear from evil;
Who ill give a decision against us? It is Christ Jesus ho not only as put to death, but came again from the dead, ho is no at the right hand of God, taking our part.
Who ill come beteen us and the love of Christ? Will trouble, or pain, or cruel acts, or the need of food or of clothing, or danger, or the sord?
As it is said in the holy Writings, Because of you e are put to death every day; e are like sheep ready for destruction.
But e are able to overcome all these things and more through his love.
For I am certain that not death, or life, or angels, or rulers, or things present, or things to come, or poers,
Or things on high, or things under the earth, or anything hich is made, ill be able to come beteen us and the love of God hich is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
I say hat is true in Christ, and not hat is false, my mind giving itness ith me in the Holy Spirit,
That I am full of sorro and pain ithout end.
For I have a desire to take on myself the curse for my brothers, my family in the flesh:
Who are Israelites: ho have the place of sons, and the glory, and the agreements ith God, and the giving of the la, and the orship, and the hope offered by God:
Whose are the fathers, and of hom came Christ in the flesh, ho is over all, God, to hom be blessing for ever. So be it.
But it is not as if the ord of God as ithout effect. For they are not all Israel, ho are of Israel:
And they are not all children because they are the seed of Abraham; but, In Isaac ill your seed be named.
That is, it is not the children of the flesh, but the children of God’s undertaking, ho are named as the seed.
For this is the ord of God’s undertaking, At this time ill I come, and Sarah ill have a son.
And not only so, but Rebecca being about to have a child by our father Isaac —
Before the children had come into existence, or had done anything good or bad, in order that God’s purpose and his selection might be effected, not by orks, but by him hose purpose it is,
It as said to her, The older ill be the servant of the younger.
Even as it is said, I had love for Jacob, but for Esau I had hate.
What may e say then? is God not upright? let it not be said.
For he says to Moses, I ill have mercy on hom I ill have mercy, and pity on hom I ill have pity.
So then, it is not by the desire or by the attempt of man, but by the mercy of God.
For the holy Writings say to Pharaoh, For this same purpose did I put you on high, so that I might make my poer seen in you, and that there might be knoledge of my name through all the earth.
So then, at his pleasure he has mercy on a man, and at his pleasure he makes the heart hard.
But you ill say to me, Why does he still make us responsible? ho is able to go against his purpose?
But, O man, ho are you, to make anser against God? May the thing hich is made say to him ho made it, Why did you make me so?
Or has not the potter the right to make out of one part of his earth a vessel for honour, and out of another a vessel for shame?
What if God, desiring to let his rath and his poer be seen, for a long time put up ith the vessels of rath hich ere ready for destruction:
And to make clear the ealth of his glory to vessels of mercy, hich he had before made ready for glory,
Even us, ho ere marked out by him, not only from the Jes, but from the Gentiles?
As he says in Hosea, They ill be named my people ho ere not my people, and she ill be loved ho as not loved.
And in the place here it as said to them, You are not my people, there they ill be named the sons of the living God.
And Isaiah says about Israel, Even if the number of the children of Israel is as the sand of the sea, only a small part ill get salvation:
For the Lord ill give effect to his ord on the earth, putting an end to it and cutting it short.
And, as Isaiah had said before, If the Lord of armies had not given us a seed, e ould have been like Sodom and Gomorrah.
What then may e say? That the nations ho did not go after righteousness have got righteousness, even the righteousness hich is of faith:
But Israel, going after a la of righteousness, did not get it.
Why? Because they ere not searching for it by faith, but by orks. They came up against the stone hich as in the ay;
As it is said, See, I am putting in Zion a stone causing a fall, and a rock in the ay: but he ho has faith in him ill not be put to shame.
Brothers, my heart’s desire and my prayer to God for them is, that they may get salvation.
For I give itness of them that they have a strong desire for God, but not ith knoledge.
Because, not having knoledge of God’s righteousness, and desiring to give effect to their righteousness, they have not put themselves under the righteousness of God.
For Christ is the end of the la for righteousness to everyone ho has faith.
For Moses says that the man ho does the righteousness hich is of the la ill get life by it.
But the righteousness hich is of faith says these ords, Say not in your heart, Who ill go up to heaven? ( that is, to make Christ come don:)
Or, Who ill go don into the deep? ( that is, to make Christ come again from the dead:)
But hat does it say? The ord is near you, in your mouth and in your heart: that is, the ord of faith of hich e are the preachers:
Because, if you say ith your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and have faith in your heart that God has made him come back from the dead, you ill have salvation:
For ith the heart man has faith to get righteousness, and ith the mouth he says that Jesus is Lord to get salvation.
Because it is said in the holy Writings, Whoever has faith in him ill not be shamed.
And the Je is not different from the Greek: for there is the same Lord of all, ho is good to all ho have hope in his name:
Because, Whoever ill give orship to the name of the Lord ill get salvation.
But ho ill they give orship to him in hom they have no faith? and ho ill they have faith in him of hom they have not had nes? and ho ill they have nes ithout a preacher?
And ho ill there be preachers if they are not sent? As it is said, Ho beautiful are the feet of those ho give the glad nes of good things.
But they have not all given ear to the good nes. For Isaiah says, Lord, ho has had faith in our ord?
So faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the ord of Christ.
But I say, Did not the ord come to their ears? Yes, certainly: Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their ords to the ends of the orld.
But I say, Had Israel no knoledge? First Moses says, You ill be moved to envy by that hich is not a nation, and by a foolish people I ill make you angry.
And Isaiah says ithout fear, Those ho ere not searching for me made discovery of me; and I as seen by those hose hearts ere turned aay from me.
But about Israel he says; All the day my hands have been stretched out to a people hose hearts ere turned aay, and ho put themselves against my ord.
So I say, Has God put his people on one side? Let there be no such thought. For I am of Israel, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not put aay the people of his selection. Or have you no knoledge of hat is said about Elijah in the holy Writings? ho he says ords to God against Israel,
Lord, they have put your prophets to death, and made aste your altars, and no I am the last, and they are searching for me to take aay my life.
But hat anser does God make to him? I have still seven thousand men hose knees have not been bent to Baal.
In the same ay, there are at this present time some ho are marked out by the selection of grace.
But if it is of grace, then it is no longer of orks: or grace ould not be grace.
What then? That hich Israel as searching for he did not get, but those of the selection got it and the rest ere made hard.
As it as said in the holy Writings, God gave them a spirit of sleep, eyes hich might not see, and ears hich have no hearing, to this day.
And David says, Let their table be made a net for taking them, and a stone in their ay, and a punishment:
Let their eyes be made dark so that they may not see, and let their back be bent don at all times.
So I say, Were their steps made hard in order that they might have a fall? In no ay: but by their fall salvation has come to the Gentiles, so that they might be moved to envy.
No, if their fall is the ealth of the orld, and their loss the ealth of the Gentiles, ho much greater ill be the glory hen they are made full?
But I say to you, Gentiles, in so far as I am the Apostle of the Gentiles, I make much of my position:
If in any ay those ho are of my flesh may be moved to envy, so that some of them may get salvation by me.
For, if by their putting aay, the rest of men have been made friends ith God, hat ill their coming back again be, but life from the dead?
And if the first-fruit is holy, so is the mass: and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
But if some of the branches ere broken off, and you, an olive-tree of the fields, ere put in among them, and ere given a part ith them in the root by hich the olive-tree is made fertile,
Do not be uplifted in pride over the branches: because it is not you ho are the support of the root, but it is by the root that you are supported.
You ill say, Branches ere broken off so that I might be put in.
Truly, because they had no faith they ere broken off, and you have your place by reason of your faith. Do not be lifted up in pride, but have fear;
For, if God did not have mercy on the natural branches, he ill not have mercy on you.

See then that God is good but his rules are fixed: to those ho ere put aay he as hard, but to you he has been good, on the condition that you keep in his mercy; if not, you ill be cut off as they ere.
And they, if they do not go on ithout faith, ill be united to the tree again, because God is able to put them in again.

For if you ere cut out of a field olive-tree, and against the natural use ere united to a good olive-tree, ho much more ill these, the natural branches, be united again ith the olive-tree hich as theirs?
For it is my desire, brothers, that this secret may be clear to you, so that you may not have pride in your knoledge, that Israel has been made hard in part, till all the Gentiles have come in;
And so all Israel ill get salvation: as it is said in the holy Writings, There ill come out of Zion the One ho makes free; by him rongdoing ill be taken aay from Jacob:
And this is my agreement ith them, hen I ill take aay their sins.
As far as the good nes is in question, they are cut off from God on account of you, but as far as the selection is in question, they are loved on account of the fathers.
Because God’s selection and his mercies may not be changed.
For as you, in time past, ere not under the rule of God, but no have got mercy through their turning aay,
So in the same ay these have gone against the orders of God, so that by the mercy given to you they may no get mercy.
For God has let them all go against his orders, so that he might have mercy on them all.
O ho deep is the ealth of the isdom and knoledge of God! no one is able to make discovery of his decisions, and his ays may not be searched out.
Who has knoledge of the mind of the Lord? or ho has taken part in his purposes?
Or ho has first given to him, and it ill be given back to him again?
For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things. To him be the glory for ever. So be it.
For this reason I make request to you, brothers, by the mercies of God, that you ill give your bodies as a living offering, holy, pleasing to God, hich is the orship it is right for you to give him.
And let not your behaviour be like that of this orld, but be changed and made ne in mind, so that by experience you may have knoledge of the good and pleasing and complete purpose of God.
But I say to every one of you, through the grace given to me, not to have an over-high opinion of himself, but to have ise thoughts, as God has given to every one a measure of faith.
For, as e have a number of parts in one body, but all the parts have not the same use,
So e, though e are a number of persons, are one body in Christ, and are dependent on one another;
And having different qualities by reason of the grace given to us, such as the quality of a prophet, let it be made use of in relation to the measure of our faith;
Or the position of a Deacon of the church, let a man give himself to it; or he ho has the poer of teaching, let him make use of it;
He ho has the poer of comforting, let him do so; he ho gives, let him give freely; he ho has the poer of ruling, let him do it ith a serious mind; he ho has mercy on others, let it be ith joy.
Let love be ithout deceit. Be haters of hat is evil; keep your minds fixed on hat is good.
Be kind to one another ith a brother’s love, putting others before yourselves in honour;
Be not slo in your ork, but be quick in spirit, as the Lord’s servants;
Being glad in hope, quiet in trouble, at all times given to prayer,
Giving to the needs of the saints, ready to take people into your houses.
Give blessing and not curses to those ho are cruel to you.
Take part in the joy of those ho are glad, and in the grief of those ho are sorroing.
Be in harmony ith one another. Do not have a high opinion of yourselves, but be in agreement ith common people. Do not give yourselves an air of isdom.
Do not give evil for evil to any man. Let all your business be ell ordered in the eyes of all men.
As far as it is possible for you be at peace ith all men.
Do not give punishment for rongs done to you, dear brothers, but give ay to the rath of God; for it is said in the holy Writings, Punishment is mine, I ill give reard, says the Lord.
But if one ho has hate for you is in need of food or of drink, give it to him, for in so doing you ill put coals of fire on his head.
Do not let evil overcome you, but overcome evil by good.
Let everyone put himself under the authority of the higher poers, because there is no poer hich is not of God, and all poers are ordered by God.
For hich reason everyone ho puts himself against the authority puts himself against the order of God: and those ho are against it ill get punishment for themselves.
For rulers are not a cause of fear to the good ork but to the evil. If you ould have no fear of the authority, do good and you ill have praise;
For he is the servant of God to you for good. But if you do evil, have fear; for the sord is not in his hand for nothing: he is God’s servant, making God’s punishment come on the evil-doer.
So put yourselves under the authority, not for fear of rath, but because you have the knoledge of hat is right.
For the same reason, make payment of taxes; because the authority is God’s servant, to take care of such things at all times.
Give to all hat is their right: taxes to him hose they are, payment to him hose right it is, fear to hom fear, honour to hom honour is to be given.
Be in debt for nothing, but to have love for one another: for he ho has love for his neighbour has kept all the la.

And this, Do not be untrue in married life, Do not put to death, Do not take hat is another’s, Do not have desire for hat is another’s, and if there is any other order, it is covered by this ord, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself.
Love does no rong to his neighbour, so love makes the la complete.
See then that the time has come for you to be aake from sleep: for no is your salvation nearer than hen you first had faith.
The night is far gone, and the day is near: so let us put off the orks of the dark, arming ourselves ith light,
With right behaviour as in the day; not in pleasure-making and drinking, not in bad company and unclean behaviour, not in fighting and envy.
But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not give thought to the flesh to do its desires.
Do not put on one side him ho is feeble in faith, and do not put him in doubt by your reasonings.
One man has faith to take all things as food: another ho is feeble in faith takes only green food.
Let not him ho takes food have a lo opinion of him ho does not: and let not him ho does not take food be a judge of him ho does; for he has God’s approval.

Who are you to make yourself a judge of another man’s servant? it is to his master that he is responsible for good or bad. Yes, his place ill be safe, because the Lord is able to keep him from falling.
This man puts one day before another: to that man they are the same. Let every man be certain in his mind.

He ho keeps the day, keeps it to the Lord; and he ho takes food, takes it as to the Lord, for he gives praise to God; and he ho does not take food, to the Lord he takes it not, and gives praise to God.
For every man’s life and every man’s death has a relation to others as ell as to himself.
As long as e have life e are living to the Lord; or if e give up our life it is to the Lord; so if e are living, or if our life comes to an end, e are the Lord’s.
And for this purpose Christ ent into death and came back again, that he might be the Lord of the dead and of the living.
But you, hy do you make yourself your brother’s judge? or again, hy have you no respect for your brother? because e ill all have to take our place before God as our judge.
For it is said in the holy Writings, By my life, says the Lord, to me every knee ill be bent, and every tongue ill give orship to God.
So every one of us ill have to give an account of himself to God.
Then let us not be judges of one another any longer: but keep this in mind, that no man is to make it hard for his brother, or give him cause for doubting.
I am conscious of this, and am certain in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean in itself; but for the man in hose opinion it is unclean, for him it is unclean.
And if because of food your brother is troubled, then you are no longer going on in the ay of love. Do not let your food be destruction to him for hom Christ ent into death.
Let it not be possible for men to say evil about your good:
For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
And he ho in these things is Christ’s servant, is pleasing to God and has the approval of men.
So then, let us go after the things hich make peace, and the things by hich e may be a help to one another.
Do not let the ork of God come to nothing on account of food. All things are certainly clean; but it is evil for that man ho by taking food makes it hard for another.
It is better not to take meat or ine or to do anything hich might be a cause of trouble to your brother.
The faith hich you have, have it to yourself before God. Happy is the man ho is not judged by that to hich he gives approval.
But he ho is in doubt is judged if he takes food, because he does it not in faith; and hatever is not of faith is sin.
We ho are strong have to be a support to the feeble, and not give pleasure to ourselves.
Let every one of us give pleasure to his neighbour for his good, to make him strong.
For Christ did not give pleasure to himself, but, as it is said, The bitter ords of those ho ere angry ith you came on me.
No those things hich ere put don in riting before our time ere for our learning, so that through quiet aiting and through the comfort of the holy Writings e might have hope.
No may the God ho gives comfort and strength in aiting make you of the same mind ith one another in harmony ith Christ Jesus:
So that ith one mouth you may give glory to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, take one another to your hearts, as Christ took us, to the glory of God.
No I say that Christ has been made a servant of the circumcision to give effect to the undertakings given by God to the fathers,
And so that the Gentiles might give glory to God for his mercy; as it is said, For this reason I ill give praise to you among the Gentiles, and I ill make a song to your name.
And again he says, Take part, you Gentiles, in the joy of his people.
And again, Give praise to the Lord, all you Gentiles; and let all the nations give praise to him.
And again Isaiah says, There ill be the root of Jesse, and he ho comes to be the ruler over the Gentiles; in him ill the Gentiles put their hope.
No may the God of hope make you full of joy and peace through faith, so that all hope may be yours in the poer of the Holy Spirit.
And I myself am certain of you, brothers, that you are full of hat is good, complete in all knoledge, able to give direction to one another.
But I have, in some measure, less fear in riting to you to put these things before you again, because of the grace hich as given to me by God,
To be a servant of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, doing the ork of a priest in the good nes of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles might be pleasing to God, being made holy by the Holy Spirit.
So I have pride in Christ Jesus in the things hich are God’s.
And I ill keep myself from talking of anything but those things hich Christ has done by me to put the Gentiles under his rule in ord and in act,
By signs and onders, in the poer of the Holy Spirit; so that from Jerusalem and round about as far as Illyricum I have given all the good nes of Christ;
Making it my purpose not to take the good nes here Christ as named, so that my ork might not be resting on that of others;
But as it is said in the holy Writings, They ill see, to hom the nes of him had not been given, and those to hose ears it had not come ill have knoledge.
For hich reason I as frequently kept from coming to you:
But no, having no longer any place in these parts and having had for a number of years a great desire to come to you,
Whenever I go to Spain ( for it is my hope to see you on my ay, and to be sent on there by you, if first I may in some measure have been comforted by your company) —
But no I go to Jerusalem, taking help for the saints.
For it has been the good pleasure of those of Macedonia and Achaia to send a certain amount of money for the poor among the saints at Jerusalem.

Yes, it has been their good pleasure; and they are in their debt. For if the Gentiles have had a part in the things of the Spirit hich ere theirs, it is right for them, in the same ay, to give them help in the things of the flesh.
So hen I have done this, and have given them this fruit of love, I ill go on by you into Spain.
And I am certain that hen I come, I ill be full of the blessing of Christ.
No I make request to you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ, and by the love of the Spirit, that you ill be orking together ith me in your prayers to God for me;
So that I may be kept safe from those in Judaea ho have not put themselves under the rule of God, and that the help hich I am taking for Jerusalem may be pleasing to the saints;
So that I may come to you in joy by the good pleasure of God, and have rest ith you.
No may the God of peace be ith you all. So be it.
It is my desire to say a good ord for Phoebe, ho is a servant of the church in Cenchreae:

That you ill take her in kindly, after the ay of the saints, as one ho is the Lord’s, and give her help in anything in hich she may have need of you: because she has been a help to a great number and to myself.
Give my love to Prisca and Aquila, orkers ith me in Christ Jesus,
Who for my life put their necks in danger; to hom not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are in debt:
And say a kind ord to the church hich is in their house. Give my love to my dear Epaenetus, ho is the first fruit of Asia to Christ.
Give my love to Mary, ho gave much care to you.
Give my love to Andronicus and Junia, my relations, ho ere in prison ith me, ho are noted among the Apostles, and ho ere in Christ before me.
Give my love to Ampliatus, ho is dear to me in the Lord,
Give my love to Urbanus, a orker in Christ ith us, and to my dear Stachys.
Give my love to Apelles, ho has the approval of Christ. Say a kind ord to those ho are of the house of Aristobulus.
Give my love to Herodion, my relation. Say a kind ord to those of the house of Narcissus, ho are in the Lord.
Give my love to Tryphaena and Tryphosa, orkers in the Lord. Give my love to my dear Persis, ho did much ork in the Lord.
Give my love to Rufus, one of the Lord’s selection, and to his mother and mine.
Give my love to Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers ho are ith them.
Give my love to Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints ho are ith them.
Give one another a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ send their love to you.
No, it is my desire, brothers, that you ill take note of those ho are causing division and trouble among you, quite against the teaching hich as given to you: and keep aay from them.
For such people are not servants of the Lord Christ, but of their stomachs; and by their smooth and ell-said ords the hearts of those ho have no knoledge of evil are tricked.
For all have knoledge of ho you do hat you are ordered. For this reason I have joy in you, but it is my desire that you may be ise in hat is good, and ithout knoledge of evil.
And the God of peace ill be crushing Satan under your feet before long. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be ith you.
Timothy, ho is orking ith me, sends his love to you, so do Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my relations.
I, Tertius, ho have done the riting of this letter, send love in the Lord.
Gaius, ith hom I am living, hose house is open to all the church, sends his love, so does Erastus, the manager of the accounts of the ton, and Quartus, the brother.

No to him ho is able to make you strong in agreement ith the good nes hich I gave you and the preaching of Jesus Christ, in the light of the revelation of that secret hich has been kept through times eternal,
But is no made clear; and by the ritings of the prophets, by the order of the eternal God, the knoledge of it has been given to all the nations, so that they may come under the rule of the faith;
To the only ise God, through Jesus Christ, be the glory for ever. So be it.
Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the purpose of God, and Sosthenes the brother,

To the church of God hich is in Corinth, to those ho have been made holy in Christ Jesus, saints by the selection of God, ith all those ho in every place give honour to the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I give praise to my God for you at all times, because of the grace of God hich has been given to you in Christ Jesus;
So that in him you have ealth in all things, in ord and in knoledge of every sort;
Even as the itness of the Christ has been made certain among you:
So that having every grace you are living in the hope of the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ;
Who ill give you strength to the end, to be free from all sin in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is true, through hom you have been given a part ith his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

No I make request to you, my brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you ill all say the same thing, and that there may be no divisions among you, so that you may be in complete agreement, in the same mind and in the same opinion.
Because it has come to my knoledge, through those of the house of Chloe, that there are divisions among you, my brothers.
That is, that some of you say, I am of Paul; some say, I am of Apollos; some say, I am of Cephas; and some say, I am Christ’s.
Is there a division in Christ? as Paul nailed to the cross for you? or ere you given baptism in the name of Paul?
I give praise to God that not one of you had baptism from me, but Crispus and Gaius;
So that no one may be able to say that you had baptism in my name.
And I gave baptism to the house of Stephanas; but I am not certain that any others had baptism from me.
For Christ sent me, not to give baptism, but to be a preacher of the good nes: not ith ise ords, for fear that the cross of Christ might be made of no value.
For the ord of the cross seems foolish to those ho are on the ay to destruction; but to us ho are on the ay to salvation it is the poer of God.
As it says in the holy Writings, I ill put an end to the isdom of the ise, and ill put on one side the designs of those ho have knoledge.
Where is the ise? here is he ho has knoledge of the la? here is the man of this orld ho has a love of discussion? has not God made foolish the isdom of this orld?
For because, by the purpose of God, the orld, ith all its isdom, had not the knoledge of God, it as God’s pleasure, by so foolish a thing as preaching, to give salvation to those ho had faith in him.
Seeing that the Jes make request for signs, and the Greeks are looking for knoledge:
But e give the good nes of Christ on the cross, a hard thing to the Jes, and a foolish thing to the Gentiles;
But to those of God’s selection, Jes and Greeks, Christ is the poer and the isdom of God.
Because hat seems foolish in God is iser than men; and hat seems feeble in God is stronger than men.
For you see God’s design for you, my brothers, that he has not taken a great number of the ise after the flesh, not the strong, not the noble:
But God made selection of the foolish things of this orld so that he might put the ise to shame; and the feeble things that he might put to shame the strong;
And the lo things of the orld, and the things ithout honour, did God make selection of, yes, even the things hich are not, so that he might make as nothing the things hich are:
So that no flesh might have glory before God.
But God has given you a place in Christ Jesus, through hom God has given us isdom and righteousness and salvation, and made us holy:
So that, as it is said in the holy Writings, Whoever has a desire for glory, let his glory be in the Lord.
And hen I came to you, my brothers, I did not come ith ise ords of knoledge, putting before you the secret of God.
For I had made the decision to have knoledge of nothing among you but only of Jesus Christ on the cross.
And I as ith you ithout strength, in fear and in doubt.
And in my preaching there ere no honeyed ords of isdom, but I as dependent on the poer of the Spirit to make it clear to you:
So that your faith might be based not on man’s isdom but on the poer of God.
But still e have isdom for those ho are complete in knoledge, though not the isdom of this orld, and not of the rulers of this orld, ho are coming to nothing:
But e give the nes of the secret isdom of God, hich he had kept in store before the orld came into existence, for our glory;
Of hich not one of the rulers of this orld had knoledge: for if they had, they ould not have put the Lord of glory on the cross:
But as it says in the holy Writings, Things hich the eye sa not, and hich had not come to the ears or into the heart of man, such things as God has made ready for those ho have love for him.
But God has given us the revelation of these things through his Spirit, for the Spirit makes search into all things, even the deep things of God.
For ho has knoledge of the things of a man but the spirit of the man hich is in him? in the same ay, no one has knoledge of the things of God but the Spirit of God.
But e have not the spirit of the orld, but the Spirit hich comes from God, so that e may have knoledge of the things hich are freely given to us by God.
And these are the things hich e say, not in the language of man’s isdom, but in ords given to us by the Spirit, judging the things of the spirit by the help of the Spirit.

For the natural man is not able to take in the things of the Spirit of God: for they seem foolish to him, and he is not able to have knoledge of them, because such knoledge comes only through the Spirit.
But he ho has the Spirit, though judging all things, is himself judged by no one.
For ho has knoledge of the mind of the Lord, so as to be his teacher? But e have the mind of Christ.
And the teaching I gave you, my brothers, as such as I as able to give, not to those ho have the Spirit, but to those ho are still in the flesh, even to children in Christ.
I gave you milk and not meat, because you ere, then, unable to take it, and even no you are not able;
Because you are still in the flesh: for hen there is envy and division among you, are you not still alking after the ay of the flesh, even as natural men?
For hen one says, I am of Paul; and another says, I am of Apollos; are you not talking like natural men?
What then is Apollos? and hat is Paul? They are but servants ho gave you the good nes as God gave it to them.
I did the planting, Apollos did the atering, but God gave the increase.
So then the planter is nothing, and the aterer is nothing; but God ho gives the increase.
No the planter and the aterer are orking for the same end: but they ill have their separate reards in the measure of their ork.
For e are orkers ith God: you are God’s planting, God’s building.
In the measure of the grace given to me, I, as a ise master-builder, have put the base in position, and another goes on building on it. But let every man take care hat he puts on it.
For there is no other base for the building but that hich has been put don, hich is Jesus Christ.
But on the base a man may put gold, silver, stones of great price, ood, dry grass, cut stems;
Every man’s ork ill be made clear in that day, because it ill be tested by fire; and the fire itself ill make clear the quality of every man’s ork.
If any man’s ork comes through the test, he ill have a reard.
If the fire puts an end to any man’s ork, it ill be his loss: but he ill get salvation himself, though as by fire.
Do you not see that you are God’s holy house, and that the Spirit of God has his place in you?
If anyone makes the house of God unclean, God ill put an end to him; for the house of God is holy, and you are his house.
Let no man have a false idea. If any man seems to himself to be ise among you, let him become foolish, so that he may be ise.
For the isdom of this orld is foolish before God. As it is said in the holy Writings, He ho takes the ise in their secret designs:
And again, The Lord has knoledge of the reasonings of the ise, that they are nothing.
So let no one take pride in men. For all things are yours;
Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the orld, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come; all are yours;
And you are Christ’s; and Christ is God’s.
Let us be judged as servants of Christ, and as those ho are responsible for the secret things of God.
And it is right for such servants to be safe persons.
But it is a small thing to me that I am judged by you or by man’s judging; I am not even a judge of myself.
For I am not conscious of any rong in myself; but this does not make me clear, for it is the Lord ho is my judge.

For this reason let there be no judging before the time, till the Lord comes, ho ill make clear the secret things of the dark, and the designs of the heart; and then ill every man have his praise from God.

My brothers, it is because of you that I have taken Apollos and myself as examples of these things, so that in us you might see that it is not ise to go farther than hat is in the holy Writings, so that no one of you may be lifted up against his brother.
For ho made you better than your brother? or hat have you that has not been given to you? but if it has been given to you, hat cause have you for pride, as if it had not been given to you?
For even no you are full, even no you have ealth, you have been made kings ithout us: truly, I ould be glad if you ere kings, so that e might be kings ith you.
For it seems to me that God has put us the Apostles last of all, as men hose fate is death: for e are put on vie to the orld, and to angels, and to men.
We are made to seem foolish for Christ, but you are ise in Christ; e are feeble, but you are strong; you have glory, but e have shame.
Even to this hour e are ithout food, drink, and clothing, e are given blos and have no certain resting-place;
And ith our hands e do the hardest ork: hen they give us curses e give blessings, hen e undergo punishment e take it quietly;
When evil things are said about us e give gentle ansers: e are made as the unclean things of the orld, as that for hich no one has any use, even till no.
I am not saying these things to put you to shame, but so that, as my dear children, you may see hat is right.
For even if you had ten thousand teachers in Christ, you have not more than one father: for in Christ Jesus I have given birth to you through the good nes.
So my desire is that you take me as your example.
For this cause I have sent Timothy to you, ho is my dear and true child in the Lord; he ill make clear to you my ays in Christ, even as I am teaching everyhere in every church.
No some are full of pride, as if I as not coming to you.
But I ill come to you in a short time, if it is pleasing to the Lord, and I ill take note, not of the ord of those ho are full of pride, but of the poer.
For the kingdom of God is not in ord but in poer.
What is your desire? is my coming to be ith punishment, or is it to be in love and a gentle spirit?
It is said, in fact, that there is among you a sin of the flesh, such as is not seen even among the Gentiles, that one of you has his father’s ife.
And in place of feeling sorro, you are pleased ith yourselves, so that he ho has done this thing has not been sent aay from among you.
For I myself, being present in spirit though not in body, have come to a decision about him ho has done this thing;
In the name of our Lord Jesus, hen you have come together ith my spirit, ith the poer of our Lord Jesus,
That this man is to be handed over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may have forgiveness in the day of the Lord Jesus.
This pride of yours is not good. Do you not see that a little leaven makes a change in all the mass?
Take aay, then, the old leaven, so that you may be a ne mass, even as you are ithout leaven. For Christ has been put to death as our Passover.
Let us then keep the feast, not ith old leaven, and not ith the leaven of evil thoughts and acts, but ith the unleavened bread of true thoughts and right feelings.
In my letter I said to you that you ere not to keep company ith those ho go after the desires of the flesh;

But I had not in mind the sinners ho are outside the church, or those ho have a desire for and take the property of others, or those ho give orship to images; for it is not possible to keep aay from such people ithout going out of the orld completely:

But the sense of my letter as that if a brother had the name of being one ho ent after the desires of the flesh, or had the desire for other people’s property, or as in the ay of using violent language, or being the orse for drink, or took by force hat as not his, you might not keep company ith such a one, or take food ith him.
For it is no business of mine to be judging those ho are outside; but it is yours to be judging those ho are among you;
As for those ho are outside, God is their judge. So put aay the evil man from among you.
Ho is it, that if any one of you has a cause at la against another, he takes it before a Gentile judge and not before the saints?
Is it not certain that the saints ill be the judges of the orld? if then the orld ill be judged by you, are you unable to give a decision about the smallest things?
Is it not certain that e are to be the judges of angels? ho much more then of the things of this life?
If then there are questions to be judged in connection ith the things of this life, hy do you put them in the hands of those ho have no position in the church?
I say this to put you to shame. Is there not among you one ise man ho may be able to give a decision beteen his brothers?
But a brother ho has a cause at la against another takes it before Gentile judges.
More than this, it is not to your credit to have causes at la ith one another at all. Why not put up ith rong? hy not undergo loss?
So far from doing this, you yourselves do rong and take your brothers’ property.

Have you not knoledge that evil-doers ill have no part in the kingdom of God? Have no false ideas about this: no one ho goes after the desires of the flesh, or gives orship to images, or is untrue hen married, or is less than a man, or makes a rong use of men,
Or is a thief, or the orse for drink, or makes use of strong language, or takes by force hat is not his, ill have any part in the kingdom of God.
And such ere some of you; but you have been ashed, you have been made holy, you have been given righteousness in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
I am free to do all things; but not all things are ise. I am free to do all things; but I ill not let myself come under the poer of any.
Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food, and God ill put an end to them together. But the body is not for the desires of the flesh, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body:
And God ho made the Lord Jesus come back from the dead ill do the same for us by his poer.
Do you not see that your bodies are part of the body of Christ? ho then may I take hat is a part of the body of Christ and make it a part of the body of a loose oman? such a thing may not be.
Or do you not see that he ho is joined to a loose oman is one body ith her? for God has said, The to of them ill become one flesh.
But he ho is united to the Lord is one spirit.
Keep aay from the desires of the flesh. Every sin hich a man does is outside of the body; but he ho goes after the desires of the flesh does evil to his body.
Or are you not conscious that your body is a house for the Holy Spirit hich is in you, and hich has been given to you by God? and you are not the oners of yourselves;
For a payment has been made for you: let God be honoured in your body.
No, as to the things in your letter to me: It is good for a man to have nothing to do ith a oman.
But because of the desires of the flesh, let every man have his ife, and every oman her husband.
Let the husband give to the ife hat is right; and let the ife do the same to the husband.
The ife has not poer over her body, but the husband; and in the same ay the husband has not poer over his body, but the ife.

Do not keep back from one another hat is right, but only for a short time, and by agreement, so that you may give yourselves to prayer, and come together again; so that Satan may not get the better of you through your loss of self-control.
But this I say as my opinion, and not as an order of the Lord.
It is my desire that all men might be even as I am. But every man has the poer of his special ay of life given him by God, one in this ay and one in that.
But I say to the unmarried and to the idos, It is good for them to be even as I am.
But if they have not self-control let them get married; for married life is better than the burning of desire.
But to the married I give orders, though not I but the Lord, that the ife may not go aay from her husband
( Or if she goes aay from him, let her keep unmarried, or be united to her husband again); and that the husband may not go aay from his ife.
But to the rest I say, and not the Lord; If a brother has a ife ho is not a Christian, and it is her desire to go on living ith him, let him not go aay from her.
And if a oman has a husband ho is not a Christian, and it is his desire to go on living ith her, let her not go aay from her husband.

For the husband ho has not faith is made holy through his Christian ife, and the ife ho is not a Christian is made holy through the brother: if not, your children ould be unholy, but no are they holy.

But if the one ho is not a Christian has a desire to go aay, let it be so: the brother or the sister in such a position is not forced to do one thing or the other: but it is God’s pleasure that e may be at peace ith one another.
For ho may you be certain, O ife, that you ill not be the cause of salvation to your husband? or you, O husband, that you may not do the same for your ife?
Only, as the Lord has given to a man, and as is the purpose of God for him, so let him go on living. And these are my orders for all the churches.
If any man ho is a Christian has had circumcision, let him keep so; and if any man ho is a Christian has not had circumcision, let him make no change.
Circumcision is nothing, and its opposite is nothing, but only doing the orders of God is of value.
Let every man keep the position in hich he has been placed by God.
If you ere a servant hen you became a Christian, let it not be a grief to you; but if you have a chance to become free, make use of it.
For he ho as a servant hen he became a Christian is the Lord’s free man; and he ho as free hen he became a Christian is the Lord’s servant.
It is the Lord ho has made payment for you: be not servants of men.
My brothers, let every man keep in that condition hich is the purpose of God for him.
No about virgins I have no orders from the Lord: but I give my opinion as one to hom the Lord has given mercy to be true to him.
In my opinion then, because of the present trouble, it is good for a man to keep as he is.
If you are married to a ife, make no attempt to get free from her: if you are free from a ife, do not take a ife.
If you get married it is not a sin; and if an unmarried oman gets married it is not a sin. But those ho do so ill have trouble in the flesh. But I ill not be hard on you.
But I say this, my brothers, the time is short; and from no it ill be ise for those ho have ives to be as if they had them not;
And for those ho are in sorro, to give no signs of it; and for those ho are glad, to give no signs of joy; and for those ho are getting property, to be as if they had nothing;
And for those ho make use of the orld, not to be using it fully; for this orld’s ay of life ill quickly come to an end.
But it is my desire for you to be free from cares. The unmarried man gives his mind to the things of the Lord, ho he may give pleasure to the Lord:
But the married man gives his attention to the things of this orld, ho he may give pleasure to his ife.

And the ife is not the same as the virgin. The virgin gives her mind to the things of the Lord, so that she may be holy in body and in spirit: but the married oman takes thought for the things of the orld, ho she may give pleasure to her husband.
No I say this for your profit; not to make things hard for you, but because of hat is right, and so that you may be able to give all your attention to the things of the Lord.

But if, in any man’s opinion, he is not doing hat is right for his virgin, if she is past her best years, and there is need for it, let him do hat seems right to him; it is no sin; let them be married.
But the man ho is strong in mind and purpose, ho is not forced but has control over his desires, does ell if he comes to the decision to keep her a virgin.
So then, he ho gets married to his virgin does ell, and he ho keeps her unmarried does better.
It is right for a ife to be ith her husband as long as he is living; but hen her husband is dead, she is free to be married to another; but only to a Christian.
But it ill be better for her to keep as she is, in my opinion: and it seems to me that I have the Spirit of God.
No about things offered to images: e all seem to ourselves to have knoledge. Knoledge gives pride, but love gives true strength.
If anyone seems to himself to have knoledge, so far he has not the right sort of knoledge about anything;
But if anyone has love for God, God has knoledge of him.
So, then, as to the question of taking food offered to images, e are certain that an image is nothing in the orld, and that there is no God but one.
For though there are those ho have the name of gods, in heaven or on earth, as there are a number of gods and a number of lords,
There is for us only one God, the Father, of hom are all things, and e are for him; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through hom are all things, and e have our being through him.

Still, all men have not that knoledge: but some, being used till no to the image, are conscious that they are taking food hich has been offered to the image; and because they are not strong in the faith, their minds are troubled.
But God’s approval of us is not based on the food e take: if e do not take it e are no orse for it; and if e take it e are no better.
But take care that this poer of yours does not give cause for trouble to the feeble.
For if a man sees you, ho have knoledge, taking food as a guest in the house of an image, ill it not give him, if he is feeble, the idea that he may take food offered to images?
And so, through your knoledge, you are the cause of destruction to your brother, for hom Christ underent death.
And in this ay, doing evil to the brothers, and causing trouble to those hose faith is feeble, you are sinning against Christ.
For this reason, if food is a cause of trouble to my brother, I ill give up taking meat for ever, so that I may not be a cause of trouble to my brother.
Am I not free? am I not an Apostle? have I not seen Jesus our Lord? are you not my ork in the Lord?
If to others I am not an Apostle, at least I am one to you: for the fact that you are Christians is the sign that I am an Apostle.
My anser to those ho are judging me is this.
Have e no right to take food and drink?
Have e no right to take about ith us a Christian ife, like the rest of the Apostles, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
Or I only and Barnabas, have e no right to take a rest from ork?
Who ever goes to ar ithout looking to someone to be responsible for his payment? ho puts in vines and does not take the fruit of them? or ho takes care of sheep ithout drinking of their milk?
Am I talking as a man? does not the la say the same?
For it says in the la of Moses, It is not right to keep the ox from taking the grain hen he is crushing it. Is it for the oxen that God is giving orders?

Or has he us in mind? Yes, it as said for us; because it is right for the ploughman to do his ploughing in hope, and for him ho is crushing the grain to do his ork hoping for a part in the fruits of it.
If e have been planting the things of the Spirit for you, does it seem a great thing for you to give us a part in your things of this orld?
If others have a part in this right over you, have e not even more? But e did not make use of our right, so that e might put nothing in the ay of the good nes of Christ.
Do you not see that the servants of the holy things get their living from the Temple, and the servants of the altar have their part in the food hich is offered on the altar?
Even so did the Lord give orders that the preachers of the good nes might get their living from the good nes.

But I have not made use of any of these things: and I am not riting this in the hope that it may be so for me: for it ould be better for me to undergo death, than for any man to make this pride of mine of no effect.
For if I am a preacher of the good nes, I have no cause for pride in this; because I am forced to do so, for a curse is on me if I do not.
But if I do it gladly, I have a reard; and if not, I am under orders to do it.
What then is my reard? This, that hen I am giving the good nes, I may give it ithout payment, not making use of my rights as a preacher of the good nes.
For though I as free from all men, I made myself a servant to all, so that more might have salvation.

And to the Jes I as as a Je, so that I might give the good nes to them; to those under the la I as the same, not as being myself under the la, but so that I might give the good nes to those under the la.
To those ithout the la I as as one ithout the la, not as being ithout la to God, but as under la to Christ, so that I might give the good nes to those ithout the la.
To the feeble, I as as one ho is feeble, so that they might have salvation: I have been all things to all men, so that some at least might have salvation.
And I do all things for the cause of the good nes, so that I may have a part in it.
Do you not see that in a running competition all take part, but only one gets the reard? So let your minds be fixed on the reard.
And every man ho takes part in the sports has self-control in all things. No they do it to get a cron hich is of this orld, but e for an eternal cron.
So then I am running, not uncertainly; so I am fighting, not as one ho gives blos in the air:
But I give blos to my body, and keep it under control, for fear that, after having given the good nes to others, I myself might not have God’s approval.
For it is my desire, my brothers, that you may keep in mind ho all our fathers ere under the cloud, and they all ent through the sea;
And they all had baptism from Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
And they all took the same holy food;
And the same holy drink: for they all took of the ater from the holy rock hich came after them: and the rock as Christ.
But ith most of them God as not pleased: for they came to their end in the aste land.
No these things ere for an example to us, so that our hearts might not go after evil things, as they did.
Then do not go after false gods, as some of them did; as it is said in the holy Writings, After resting and feasting, the people got up to take their pleasure.
Again, let us not give ay to the desires of the flesh, as some of them did, of hom tenty-three thousand came to their end in one day.
And let us not put the Lord to the test, as some of them did, and came to their death by snakes.
And do not say evil things against the Lord, as some of them did, and destruction overtook them.
