No these things ere done as an example; and ere put don in riting for our teaching, on hom the last days have come.
So let him ho seems to himself to be safe go in fear of a fall.

You have been put to no test but such as is common to man: and God is true, ho ill not let any test come on you hich you are not able to undergo; but he ill make ith the test a ay out of it, so that you may be able to go through it.
For this cause, my dear brothers, give no orship to false gods.
What I am saying is for ise men, do you be the judges of it.
The cup of blessing hich e take, does it not give us a part in the blood of Christ? and is not the broken bread a taking part in the body of Christ?
Because e, being a number of persons, are one bread, e are one body: for e all take part in the one bread.
See Israel after the flesh: do not those ho take as food the offerings of the altar take a part in the altar?
Do I say, then, that hat is offered to images is anything, or that the image is anything?
What I say is that the things offered by the Gentiles are offered to evil spirits and not to God; and it is not my desire for you to have any part ith evil spirits.
It is not possible for you, at the same time, to take the cup of the Lord and the cup of evil spirits; you may not take part in the table of the Lord and the table of evil spirits.
Or may e be the cause of envy to the Lord? are e stronger than he?
We are free to do all things, but there are things hich it is not ise to do. We are free to do all things, but not all things are for the common good.
Let a man give attention not only to hat is good for himself, but equally to his neighbour’s good.
Whatever meat may be had at the public market, take as food ithout question of right or rong;
For the earth is the Lord’s and all things in it.
If a Gentile makes a feast for you, and you are pleased to go as a guest, take hatever is put before you, ithout question of right or rong.
But if anyone says to you, This food has been used as an offering, do not take it, on account of him ho said it, and on account of his sense of right and rong:
Right and rong, I say, not for you, but for the other man; for the fact that I am free is not dependent on another man’s sense of right or rong.
But if I give praise to God for the food hich I take, let no man say evil of me for that reason.
So then, if it is a question of food or drink, or any other thing, hatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
Give no cause of trouble to Jes, or to Greeks, or to the church of God.
Even as I give ay to all men in all things, not looking for profit for myself, but for the good of others, that they may get salvation.
So take me for your example, even as I take Christ for mine.
No I am pleased to see that you keep me in memory in all things, and that you give attention to the teaching hich as handed don from me to you.
But it is important for you to keep this fact in mind, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the oman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
Every man ho takes part in prayer, or gives teaching as a prophet, ith his head covered, puts shame on his head.
But every oman ho does so ith her head unveiled, puts shame on her head: for it is the same as if her hair as cut off.
For if a oman is not veiled, let her hair be cut off; but if it is a shame to a oman to have her hair cut off, let her be veiled.
For it is not right for a man to have his head covered, because he is the image and glory of God: but the oman is the glory of the man.
For the man did not come from the oman, but the oman from the man.
And the man as not made for the oman, but the oman for the man.
For this reason it is right for the oman to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
But the oman is not separate from the man, and the man is not separate from the oman in the Lord.
For as the oman is from the man, so the man is through the oman; but all things are from God.
Be judges yourselves of the question: does it seem right for a oman to take part in prayer unveiled?
Does it not seem natural to you that if a man has long hair, it is a cause of shame to him?
But if a oman has long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given to her for a covering.
But if any man ill not be ruled in this question, this is not our ay of doing things, and it is not done in the churches of God.
But in giving you this order, there is one thing about hich I am not pleased: it is that hen you come together it is not for the better but for the orse.
For first of all, it has come to my ears that hen you come together in the church, there are divisions among you, and I take the statement to be true in part.
For divisions are necessary among you, in order that those ho have God’s approval may be clearly seen among you.
But no, hen you come together, it is not possible to take the holy meal of the Lord:
For hen you take your food, everyone takes his meal before the other; and one has not enough food, and another is the orse for drink.
What? have you not houses to take your meals in? or have you no respect for the church of God, putting the poor to shame? What am I to say to you? am I to give you praise? certainly not.
For it as handed don to me from the Lord, as I gave it to you, that the Lord Jesus, on the night hen Judas as false to him, took bread,
And hen it had been broken ith an act of praise, he said, This is my body hich is for you: do this in memory of me.
In the same ay, ith the cup, after the meal, he said, This cup is the ne testament in my blood: do this, henever you take it, in memory of me.
For henever you take the bread and the cup you give itness to the Lord’s death till he comes.
If, then, anyone takes the bread or the cup of the Lord in the rong spirit, he ill be responsible for the body and blood of the Lord.
But let no man take of the bread and the cup ithout testing himself.
For a man puts himself in danger, if he takes part in the holy meal ithout being conscious that it is the Lord’s body.
For this cause a number of you are feeble and ill, and a number are dead.
But if e ere true judges of ourselves, punishment ould not come on us.
But if punishment does come, it is sent by the Lord, so that e may be safe hen the orld is judged.
So then, my brothers, hen you come together to the holy meal of the Lord, let there be aiting for one another.
If any man is in need of food, let him take his meal in his house; so that you may not come together to your damage. And the rest I ill put in order hen I come.
But about the things of the spirit, my brothers, it is not right for you to be ithout teaching.
You are conscious that hen you ere Gentiles, in hatever ay you ere guided, you ent after images ithout voice or poer.
So it is my desire for you to be clear about this; that no one is able to say by the Spirit of God that Jesus is cursed; and no one is able to say that Jesus is Lord, but by the Holy Spirit.
No there are different qualities given to men, but the same Spirit.
And there are different sorts of servants, but the same Lord.
And there are different operations, but the same God, ho is orking all things in all.
But to every man some form of the Spirit’s orking is given for the common good.
For to one are given ords of isdom through the Spirit; and to another ords of knoledge through the same Spirit:
To another faith in the same Spirit; and to another the poer of taking aay disease, by the one Spirit;

And to another the poer of orking onders; and to another the prophet’s ord; and to another the poer of testing spirits; to another different sorts of tongues; and to another the poer of making clear the sense of the tongues:
But all these are the operations of the one and the same Spirit, giving to every man separately as his pleasure is.
For as the body is one, and has a number of parts, and all the parts make one body, so is Christ.
For through the baptism of the one Spirit e ere all formed into one body, Jes or Greeks, servants or free men, and ere all made full of the same Spirit.
For the body is not one part, but a number of parts.
If the foot says, Because I am not the hand, I am not a part of the body; it is no less a part of the body.
And if the ear says, Because I am not the eye, I am not a part of the body; it is a part of the body all the same.
If all the body as an eye, here ould be the hearing? if all as hearing, here ould be the smelling?
But no God has put every one of the parts in the body as it as pleasing to him.
And if they ere all one part, here ould the body be?
But no they are all different parts, but one body.
And the eye may not say to the hand, I have no need of you: or again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.
No, those parts hich seem to be feeble are the more necessary;
And to those parts of the body hich seem to have less honour e give all the more honour; and to those parts of the body hich are a cause of shame to us e give the greater respect;
But those parts of the body hich are beautiful have no need of such care: and so the body has been joined together by God in such a ay as to give more honour to those parts hich had need of it;
So that there might be no division in the body; but all the parts might have the same care for one another.
And if there is pain in one part of the body, all the parts ill be feeling it; or if one part is honoured, all the parts ill be glad.
No you are the body of Christ, and every one of you the separate parts of it.

And God has put some in the church, first, Apostles; second, prophets; third, teachers; then those ith onder-orking poers, then those ith the poer of taking aay disease, helpers, ise guides, users of strange tongues.
Are all Apostles? are all prophets? are all teachers? have all the poer of orking onders?
Are all able to take aay disease? have all the poer of tongues? are all able to give their sense?
But let your desires be turned to the more important things given by the Spirit. And no I am pointing out to you an even better ay.
If I make use of the tongues of men and of angels, and have not love, I am like sounding brass, or a loud-tongued bell.
And if I have a prophet’s poer, and have knoledge of all secret things; and if I have all faith, by hich mountains may be moved from their place, but have not love, I am nothing.
And if I give all my goods to the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it is of no profit to me.
Love is never tired of aiting; love is kind; love has no envy; love has no high opinion of itself, love has no pride;
Love’s ays are ever fair, it takes no thought for itself; it is not quickly made angry, it takes no account of evil;
It takes no pleasure in rongdoing, but has joy in hat is true;
Love has the poer of undergoing all things, having faith in all things, hoping all things.
Though the prophet’s ord may come to an end, tongues come to nothing, and knoledge have no more value, love has no end.
For our knoledge is only in part, and the prophet’s ord gives only a part of hat is true:
But hen that hich is complete is come, then that hich is in part ill be no longer necessary.
When I as a child, I made use of a child’s language, I had a child’s feelings and a child’s thoughts: no that I am a man, I have put aay the things of a child.
For no e see things in a glass, darkly; but then face to face: no my knoledge is in part; then it ill be complete, even as God’s knoledge of me.
But no e still have faith, hope, love, these three; and the greatest of these is love.
Go after love; still desiring to have the things hich the Spirit gives, but most of all that you may have the prophet’s poer.
For he ho makes use of tongues is not talking to men but to God; because no one has the sense of hat he is saying; but in the Spirit he is talking of secret things.
But the ord of the prophet gives men knoledge and comfort and strength.
He ho makes use of tongues may do good to himself; but he ho gives the prophet’s ord does good to the church.

No though it is my desire for you all to have the poer of tongues, it ould give me more pleasure to be hearing the prophet’s ord from you; for this is a greater thing than using tongues, if the sense is not given at the same time, for the good of the church.
But, no, my brothers, if I come to you using tongues, hat profit ill it be to you, if I do not give you a revelation, or knoledge, or the ord of the prophet, or teaching?
Even things ithout life, having a voice, such as a music-pipe or other instrument, if they do not give out different sounds, ho may be certain hat is being played?
For if the ar-horn gives out an uncertain note, ho ill get ready for the fight?
So if you, in using a strange tongue, say ords hich have no sense, ho ill anyone take in hat you are saying? for you ill be talking to the air.
There are, it may be, a number of different voices in the orld, and no voice is ithout sense.
But if the sense of the voice is not clear to me, I am like a man from a strange country to him ho is talking, and he ill be the same to me.
So if you are desiring the things hich the Spirit gives, let your minds be turned first to the things hich are for the good of the church.
For this reason, let the man ho has the poer of using tongues make request that he may, at the same time, be able to give the sense.
For if I make use of tongues in my prayers, my spirit makes the prayer, but not my mind.
What then? let my prayer be from the spirit, and equally from the mind; let my song be from the spirit, and equally from mind.
For if you give a blessing ith the spirit, ho ill the man ho has no knoledge say, So be it, after your prayer, seeing that he has not taken in hat you are saying?
For your giving of the blessing is certainly ell done, but of no profit to the man ithout knoledge.
I give praise to God that I am able to make use of tongues more than you all:
But in the church it ould be better for me to make use of five ords of hich the sense as clear, so that others might have profit, than ten thousand ords in a strange tongue.
My brothers, do not be children in mind: in evil be as little children, but in mind be of full groth.
In the la it is said, By men of other tongues and by strange lips ill my ords come to this people; and not even so ill they give ear to me, says the Lord.
For this reason tongues are for a sign, not to those ho have faith, but to those ho have not: but the prophet’s ord is for those ho have faith, and not for the rest ho have not.
If, then, the church has come together, and all are using tongues, and there come in men ithout knoledge or faith, ill they not say that you are unbalanced?
But if all are teaching as prophets, and a man ithout faith or knoledge comes in, he is tested by all, he is judged by all;
The secrets of his heart are made clear; and he ill go don on his face and give orship to God, saying that God is truly among you.
What is it then, my brothers? hen you come together everyone has a holy song, or a revelation, or a tongue, or is giving the sense of it. Let everything be done for the common good.
If any man makes use of a tongue, let it not be more than to, or at the most three, and in turn; and let someone give the sense:
But if there is no one to give the sense, let him keep quiet in the church; and let his ords be to himself and to God.
And let the prophets give their ords, but not more than to or three, and let the others be judges of hat they say.
But if a revelation is given to another ho is seated near, let the first be quiet.
For you may all be prophets in turn so that all may get knoledge and comfort;
And the spirits of the prophets are controlled by the prophets;
For God is not a God hose ays are ithout order, but a God of peace; as in all the churches of the saints.
Let omen keep quiet in the churches: for it is not right for them to be talking; but let them be under control, as it says in the la.
And if they have a desire for knoledge about anything, let them put questions to their husbands privately: for talking in the church puts shame on a oman.
What? as it from you that the ord of God ent out? or did it only come in to you?
If any man seems to himself to be a prophet or to have the Spirit, let him take note of the things hich I am riting to you, as being the ord of the Lord.
But if any man is ithout knoledge, let him be so.
So then, my brothers, let it be your chief desire to be prophets; but let no one be stopped from using tongues.
Let all things be done in the right and ordered ay.
No I am going to make clear to you, my brothers, hat the good nes as hich I gave to you, and hich you took, and on hich your faith is based,
By hich you have salvation; that is to say, the form in hich it as given to you, if it is fixed in your minds, and if your faith in it is not ithout effect.
For I gave to you first of all hat as handed don to me, ho Christ underent death for our sins, as it says in the Writings;
And he as put in the place of the dead; and on the third day he came back from the dead, as it says in the Writings;
And he as seen by Cephas; then by the telve;
Then by more than five hundred brothers at the same time, most of hom are still living, but some are sleeping;
Then he as seen by James; then by all the Apostles.
And last of all, as by one hose birth as out of the right time, he as seen by me.
For I am the least of the Apostles, having no right to be named an Apostle, because of my cruel attacks on the church of God.
But by the grace of God, I am hat I am: and his grace hich as given to me has not been for nothing; for I did more ork than all of them; though not I, but the grace of God hich as ith me.
If then it is I ho am the preacher, or they, this is our ord, and to this you have given your faith.
No if the good nes says that Christ came back from the dead, ho do some of you say that there is no coming back from the dead?
But if there is no coming back from the dead, then Christ has not come back from the dead:
And if Christ did not come again from the dead, then our good nes and your faith in it are of no effect.
Yes, and e are seen to be false itnesses of God; because e gave itness of God that by his poer Christ came again from the dead: hich is not true if there is no coming back from the dead.
For if it is not possible for the dead to come to life again, then Christ has not come to life again:
And if that is so, your faith is of no effect; you are still in your sins.
And, in addition, the dead in Christ have gone to destruction.
If in this life only e have hope in Christ, e are of all men most unhappy.
But no Christ has truly come back from the dead, the first-fruits of those ho are sleeping.
For as by man came death, so by man there is a coming back from the dead.
For as in Adam death comes to all, so in Christ ill all come back to life.
But every man in his right order: Christ the first-fruits; then those ho are Christ’s at his coming.
Then comes the end, hen he ill give up the kingdom to God, even the Father; hen he ill have put an end to all rule and to all authority and poer.
For his rule ill go on till he has put all those ho are against him under his feet.
The last poer to come to an end is death.
For, as it says, He has put all things under his feet. But hen he says, All things are put under him, it is clear that it is not said about him ho put all things under him.
And hen all things have been put under him, then ill the Son himself be under him ho put all things under him, so that God may be all in all.
Again, hat ill they do ho are given baptism for the dead? if the dead do not come back at all, hy are people given baptism for them?
And hy are e in danger every hour?
Yes, truly, by your pride in me, my brothers in Christ Jesus our Lord, my life is one long death.
If, after the ay of men, I as fighting ith beasts at Ephesus, hat profit is it to me? If the dead do not come to life again, let us take our pleasure in feasting, for tomorro e come to an end.
Do not be tricked by false ords: evil company does damage to good behaviour.
Be aake to righteousness and keep yourselves from sin; for some have no knoledge of God: I say this to put you to shame.
But someone ill say, Ho do the dead come back? and ith hat sort of body do they come?
Foolish man, it is necessary for the seed hich you put into the earth to undergo death in order that it may come to life again:
And hen you put it into the earth, you do not put in the body hich it ill be, but only the seed, of grain or some other sort of plant;
But God gives it a body, as it is pleasing to him, and to every seed its special body.
All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one flesh of men, another of beasts, another of birds, and another of fishes.
And there are bodies of heaven and bodies of earth, but the glory of the one is different from that of the other.
There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for the glory of one star is different from that of another.
So is it ith the coming back from the dead. It is planted in death; it comes again in life:
It is planted in shame; it comes again in glory: feeble hen it is planted, it comes again in poer:
It is planted a natural body; it comes again as a body of the spirit. If there is a natural body, there is equally a body of the spirit.
And so it is said, The first man Adam as a living soul. The last Adam is a life-giving spirit.
But that hich is natural comes before that hich is of the spirit.
The first man is from the earth, and of the earth: the second man is from heaven.
Those ho are of the earth are like the man ho as from the earth: and those ho are of heaven are like the one from heaven.
And in the same ay as e have taken on us the image of the man from the earth, so e ill take on us the image of the one from heaven.
No I say this, my brothers, that it is not possible for flesh and blood to have a part in the kingdom of God; and death may not have a part in life.
See, I am giving you the revelation of a secret: e ill not all come to the sleep of death, but e ill all be changed.
In a second, in the shutting of an eye, at the sound of the last horn: for at that sound the dead ill come again, free for ever from the poer of death, and e ill be changed.
For this body hich comes to destruction ill be made free from the poer of death, and the man ho is under the poer of death ill put on eternal life.
But hen this has taken place, then that hich as said in the Writings ill come true, Death is overcome by life.
O death, here is your poer? O death, here are your pains?
The pain of death is sin; and the poer of sin is the la:
But praise be to God ho gives us strength to overcome through our Lord Jesus Christ.
For this cause, my dear brothers, be strong in purpose and unmoved, ever giving yourselves to the ork of the Lord, because you are certain that your ork is not ithout effect in the Lord.
No about the giving of money for the saints, as I gave orders to the churches of Galatia, so do you.
On the first day of the eek, let every one of you put by him in store, in measure as he has done ell in business, so that it may not be necessary to get money together hen I come.
And hen I come, I ill send the men of your selection ith letters to take the money you have got together to Jerusalem.
And if it is possible for me to go there, they ill go ith me.
But I ill come to you after I have gone through Macedonia, for that is my purpose;
But I may be ith you for a time, or even for the inter, so that you may see me on my ay, herever I go.
For it is not my desire to see you no, on my ay; because it is my hope to be ith you for some time, if that is the Lord’s pleasure.
But I ill be at Ephesus till Pentecost;
For a great and important door there is open to me, and there are a number of people against me.
No if Timothy comes, see that he is ith you ithout fear; because he is doing the Lord’s ork, even as I am:
See then that he has the honour hich is right. But send him on his ay in peace, so that he may come to me: for I am looking for him ith the brothers.
But as for Apollos, the brother, I had a great desire for him to come to you ith the brothers, but it as not his pleasure to come no; but he ill come hen he has a chance.
Be on the atch, unmoved in the faith, and be strong like men.
Let all you do be done in love.
No I make my request to you, my brothers, for you have knoledge that the house of Stephanas is the first-fruits of Achaia, and that they have made themselves the servants of the saints,
That you put yourselves under such, and under everyone ho is helping the Lord’s ork.
And I am glad of the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: for they have done hat as needed to make your ork complete.
For they gave comfort to my spirit and to yours: for hich cause give respect to such people.
The churches of Asia send their love to you. So do Aquila and Prisca, ith the church hich is in their house.
All the brothers send their love to you. Give one another a holy kiss.
I, Paul, send you these ords of love in my riting.
If any man has not love for the Lord, let him be cursed. Maran atha ( our Lord comes).
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be ith you.
My love be ith you all in Christ Jesus. So be it.
Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the purpose of God, and Timothy the brother, to the church of God hich is in Corinth, ith all the saints ho are in all Achaia:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort;
Who gives us comfort in all our troubles, so that e may be able to give comfort to others ho are in trouble, through the comfort ith hich e ourselves are comforted by God.
For as e undergo more of the pain hich Christ underent, so through Christ does our comfort become greater.
But if e are troubled, it is for your comfort and salvation; or if e are comforted, it is for your comfort, hich takes effect through your quiet undergoing of the same troubles hich e undergo:
And our hope for you is certain; in the knoledge that as you take part in the troubles, so you ill take part in the comfort.

For it is our desire that you may not be ithout knoledge of our trouble hich came on us in Asia, that the eight of it as very great, more than our poer, so that it seemed that e had no hope even of life:
Yes, e ourselves have had the anser of death in ourselves, so that our hope might not be in ourselves, but in God ho is able to give life to the dead:
Who gave us salvation from so great a death: on hom e have put our hope that he ill still go on to give us salvation;
You at the same time helping together by your prayer for us; so that for hat has been given to us through a number of persons, praise may go up to God for us from all of them.

For our glory is in this, in the knoledge hich e have that our ay of life in the orld, and most of all in relation to you, has been holy and true in the eyes of God; not in the isdom of the flesh, but in the grace of God.
For in our letters e say no other things to you, but those hich you are reading, and to hich you give agreement, and, it is my hope, ill go on doing so to the end:
Even as you have been ready, in part, to say that e are your glory, in the same ay that you are ours, in the day of the Lord Jesus.
And being certain of this, it as my purpose to come to you before, so that you might have a second grace;
And by ay of Corinth to go into Macedonia, and from there to come back again to you, so that you might send me on my ay to Judaea.
If then I had such a purpose, did I seem to be changing suddenly? or am I guided in my purposes by the flesh, saying, Yes, today, and, No, tomorro?
As God is true, our ord to you is not Yes and No.
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, hom e ere preaching among you, even I and Silvanus and Timothy, as not Yes and No, but in him is Yes.
For he is the Yes to all the undertakings of God: and by him all the ords of God are made certain and put into effect, to the glory of God through us.
No he ho makes our faith strong together ith you, in Christ, and has given us of his grace, is God;
And it is he ho has put his stamp on us, even the Spirit, as the sign in our hearts of the coming glory.
But God is my itness that it as in pity for you that I did not come to Corinth at that time.
Not that e have authority over your faith, but e are helpers of your joy: for it is faith hich is your support.
But it as my decision for myself, not to come again to you ith sorro.
For if I give you sorro, ho then ill make me glad, but he ho is made sad by me?
And I said this very thing in my letter, for fear that hen I came I might have sorro from those from hom it as right for me to have joy; being certain of this, that my joy is the joy of you all.
For out of much trouble and pain of heart and much eeping I sent my letter to you; not to give you sorro, but so that you might see ho great is the love hich I have to you.
But if anyone has been a cause of sorro, he has been so, not to me only, but in some measure to all of you ( I say this that I may not be over-hard on you).
Let it be enough for such a man to have undergone the punishment hich the church put on him;
So that no, on the other hand, it is right for him to have forgiveness and comfort from you, for fear that his sorro may be over-great.
For hich cause my desire is that you ill make your love to him clear by your acts.
And for the same reason I sent you a letter so that I might be certain of your desire to do my orders in all things.
But if you give forgiveness to anyone, I do the same: for if I have given forgiveness for anything, I have done it because of you, in the person of Christ;
So that Satan may not get the better of us: for e are not ithout knoledge of his designs.
No hen I came to Troas for the good nes of Christ, and there as an open door for me in the Lord,
I had no rest in my spirit because Titus my brother as not there: so I ent aay from them, and came into Macedonia.
But praise be to God ho makes us strong to overcome in Christ, and makes clear through us in every place the value of the knoledge of him.
For e are a seet perfume of Christ to God in those ho are getting salvation and in those ho are going to destruction;
To the one it is a perfume of death to death; to the other a perfume of life to life. And ho is enough for such things?
For e are not like the great number ho make use of the ord of God for profit: but our ords are true, as from God, being said as before God in Christ.
Do e seem to be again attempting to put ourselves in the right? or have e need, as some have, of letters of approval to you or from you?
You yourselves are our letter, hose riting is in our heart, open for every man’s reading and knoledge;
For you are clearly a letter of Christ, the fruit of our ork, recorded not ith ink, but ith the Spirit of the living God; not in stone, but in hearts of flesh.
And this is the certain faith hich e have in God through Christ:
Not as if e ere able by ourselves to do anything for hich e might take the credit; but our poer comes from God;
Who has made us able to be servants of a ne agreement; not of the letter, but of the Spirit: for the letter gives death, but the Spirit gives life.

For if the operation of the la, giving death, recorded in letters on stone, came ith glory, so that the eyes of the children of Israel had to be turned aay from the face of Moses because of its glory, a glory hich as only for a time:
Will not the operation of the Spirit have a much greater glory?
For if the operation of the la, producing punishment, had its glory, ho much greater ill be the operation of the Spirit causing righteousness?
For the glory of the first no longer seems to be glory, because of the greater glory of that hich comes after.
For if the order hich as for a time had its glory, much more ill the eternal order have its glory.
Having then such a hope, e keep nothing back,
And are not like Moses, ho put a veil on his face, so that the children of Israel might not see clearly to the end of the present order of things:
But their minds ere made hard: for to this very day at the reading of the old agreement the same veil is still unlifted; though it is taken aay in Christ.
But to this day, at the reading of the la of Moses, a veil is over their heart.
But hen it is turned to the Lord, the veil ill be taken aay.
No the Lord is the Spirit: and here the Spirit of the Lord is, there the heart is free.
But e all, ith unveiled face giving back as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord ho is the Spirit.
For this reason, because e have been made servants of this ne order, through the mercy given to us, e are strong:

And e have given up the secret things of shame, not alking in false ays, and not making use of the ord of God ith deceit; but by the revelation of hat is true, as before God, e have the approval of every man’s sense of right and rong.
But if our good nes is veiled, it is veiled from those ho are on the ay to destruction:
Because the god of this orld has made blind the minds of those ho have not faith, so that the light of the good nes of the glory of Christ, ho is the image of God, might not be shining on them.
For our preaching is not about ourselves, but about Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants through Jesus.
Seeing that it is God ho said, Let light be shining out of the dark, ho has put in our hearts the light of the knoledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
But e have this ealth in vessels of earth, so that it may be seen that the poer comes not from us but from God;
Troubles are round us on every side, but e are not shut in; things are hard for us, but e see a ay out of them;
We are cruelly attacked, but not ithout hope; e are made lo, but e are not ithout help;
In our bodies there is ever the mark of the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may be seen in our bodies.
For, hile living, e are still being given up to death because of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may be seen in our flesh, though it is under the poer of death.
So then, death is orking in us, but life in you.
But having the same spirit of faith, as it is said in the Writings, The ords of my mouth came from the faith in my heart; in the same ay, our ords are the outcome of our faith;
Because e are certain that he ho made the Lord Jesus come back from the dead, ill do the same for us, and ill give us a place in his glory ith you.
For e go through all things on account of you, because the greater the number to hom the grace is given, the greater is the praise to the glory of God.
For hich cause e do not give ay to eariness; but though our outer man is getting feebler, our inner man is made ne day by day.
For our present trouble, hich is only for a short time, is orking out for us a much greater eight of glory;
While our minds are not on the things hich are seen, but on the things hich are not seen: for the things hich are seen are for a time; but the things hich are not seen are eternal.
For e are conscious that if this our tent of flesh is taken don, e have a building from God, a house not made ith hands, eternal, in heaven.
For in this e are crying in eariness, greatly desiring to be clothed ith our house from heaven:
So that our spirits may not be unclothed.

For truly, e ho are in this tent do give out cries of eariness, for the eight of care hich is on us; not because e are desiring to be free from the body, but so that e may have our ne body, and death may be overcome by life.
No he ho has made us for this very thing is God, ho has given us the Spirit as a itness of hat is to come.
So, then, e are ever ithout fear, and though conscious that hile e are in the body e are aay from the Lord,
( For e are alking by faith, not by seeing,)
We are ithout fear, desiring to be free from the body, and to be ith the Lord.
For this reason e make it our purpose, in the body or aay from it, to be ell-pleasing to him.
For e all have to come before Christ to be judged; so that every one of us may get his reard for the things done in the body, good or bad.
Having in mind, then, the fear of the Lord, e put these things before men, but God sees our hearts; and it is my hope that e may seem right in your eyes.
We are not again requesting your approval, but e are giving you the chance of taking pride in us, so that you may be able to give an anser to those hose glory is in seeming, and not in the heart.
For if e are foolish, it is to God; or if e are serious, it is for you.
For it is the love of Christ hich is moving us; because e are of the opinion that if one as put to death for all, then all have undergone death;
And that he underent death for all, so that the living might no longer be living to themselves, but to him ho underent death for them and came back from the dead.
For this reason, from this time forard e have knoledge of no man after the flesh: even if e have had knoledge of Christ after the flesh, e have no longer any such knoledge.
So if any man is in Christ, he is in a ne orld: the old things have come to an end; they have truly become ne.
But all things are of God, ho has made us at peace ith himself through Christ, and has given to us the ork of making peace;
That is, that God as in Christ making peace beteen the orld and himself, not putting their sins to their account, and having given to us the preaching of this nes of peace.
So e are the representatives of Christ, as if God as making a request to you through us: e make our request to you, in the name of Christ, be at peace ith God.
For him ho had no knoledge of sin God made to be sin for us; so that e might become the righteousness of God in him.
We then, orking together ith God, make our request to you not to take the grace of God to no purpose.
( For he says, I have given ear to you at a good time, and I have been your helper in a day of salvation: see, no is the good time; no is the day of salvation):
Giving no cause for trouble in anything, so that no one may be able to say anything against our ork;
But in everything making it clear that e are the servants of God, in quiet strength, in troubles, in need, in sorro,
In blos, in prisons, in attacks, in hard ork, in atchings, in going ithout food;
In a clean heart, in knoledge, in long aiting, in being kind, in the Holy Spirit, in true love,
In the true ord, in the poer of God; ith the arms of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,
By glory and by shame, by an evil name and a good name; as untrue, and still true;
Unnoted, but still kept fully in mind; as near to death, but still living; as undergoing punishment, but not put to death;
As full of sorro, but ever glad; as poor, but giving ealth to others; as having nothing, but still having all things.
Our mouth is open to you, O Corinthians, our heart is ide.
It is not our feelings to you hich are narro, but yours to us.
No to give me back payment of the same sort ( I am talking as to my children), let your hearts be ide open to me.
Do not keep company ith those ho have not faith: for hat is there in common beteen righteousness and evil, or beteen light and dark?
And hat agreement is there beteen Christ and the Evil One? or hat part has one ho has faith ith one ho has not?

And hat agreement has the house of God ith images? for e are a house of the living God; even as God has said, I ill be living among them, and alking ith them; and I ill be their God, and they ill be my people.
For hich cause, Come out from among them, and be separate, says the Lord, and let no unclean thing come near you; and I ill take you for myself,
And ill be a Father to you; and you ill be my sons and daughters, says the Lord, the Ruler of all.
Because God, then, ill give us such reards, dear brothers, let us make ourselves clean from all evil of flesh and spirit, and become completely holy in the fear of God.
Let your hearts be open to us: e have done no man rong, no man has been damaged by us, e have made no profit out of any man,
It is not ith the purpose of judging you that I say this: for I have said before that you are in our hearts for life and death together.
My ords to you are ithout fear, I am full of pride on account of you: I have great comfort and joy in all our troubles.
For even hen e had come into Macedonia our flesh had no rest, but e ere troubled on every side; there ere fightings outside and fears inside.
But God ho gives comfort to the poor in spirit gave us comfort by the coming of Titus;
And not by his coming only, but by the comfort hich he had in you, hile he gave us ord of your desire, your sorro, your care for me; so that I as still more glad.
For though my letter gave you pain, I have no regret for it no, though I had before; for I see that the letter gave you pain, but only for a time.
No I am glad, not that you had sorro, but that your sorro as the cause of a change of heart; for yours as a holy sorro so that you might undergo no loss by us in anything.
For the sorro hich God gives is the cause of salvation through a change of heart, in hich there is no reason for grief: but the sorro of the orld is a cause of death.

For you see hat care as produced in you by this very sorro of yours before God, hat clearing of yourselves, hat rath against sin, hat fear, hat desire, hat serious purpose, hat punishment. In everything you have made it clear that you are free from sin in this business.
So though I sent you a letter, it as not only because of the man ho did the rong, or because of him to hom the rong as done, but so that your true care for us might be made clear in the eyes of God.
So e have been comforted: and e had the greater joy in our comfort because of the joy of Titus, for his spirit had been made glad by you all.

For I as not put to shame in anything in hich I may have made clear to him my pride in you; but as e said nothing to you but hat as true, so the good things hich I said to Titus about you ere seen by him to be true.
And his love to you is the more increased by his memory of you all, ho you gave ay to his authority, and ho you took him to your hearts ith fear and honour.
It gives me great joy to see you ansering to my good opinion of you in every ay.
And no e give you nes, brothers, about the grace of God hich has been given to the churches of Macedonia;
Ho hile they ere undergoing every sort of trouble, and ere in the greatest need, they took all the greater joy in being able to give freely to the needs of others.
For I give them itness, that as they ere able, and even more than they ere able, they gave from the impulse of their hearts,
Seriously requesting us that they might have a part in this grace of being servants to the needs of the saints:
And going even farther than our hope, they first gave themselves to the Lord and to us after the purpose of God.
So that e made a request to Titus that, as he had made a start before, so he might make this grace complete in you.
And that as you are full of every good thing, of faith, of the ord, of knoledge, of a ready mind, and of love to us, so you may be full of this grace in the same ay.
I am not giving you an order, but using the ready mind of others as a test of the quality of your love.
For you see the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, ho though he had ealth, he became poor on your account, so that through his need you might have ealth.
And in this I give my opinion: for it is to your profit, ho ere the first to make a start a year before, not only to do this, but to make clear that your minds ere more than ready to do it.
Then make the doing of it complete; so that as you had a ready mind, you may give effect to it as you are able.
For if there is a ready mind, a man ill have God’s approval in the measure of hat he has, and not of hat he has not.
And I am not saying this so that others may get off free, hile the eight comes on you:

But so that things may be equal; that from those things of hich you have more than enough at the present time their need may be helped, and that if you are in any need they may be a help to you in the same ay, making things equal.
As it says in the Writings, He ho had taken up much had nothing over and he ho had little had enough.
But praise be to God, ho puts the same care for you into the heart of Titus.
For hile he gladly gave ear to our request, he as interested enough to go to you from the impulse of his heart.
And ith him e have sent a brother hose praise in the good nes has gone through all the churches;
And not only so, but he as marked out by the churches to go ith us in the grace of this giving hich e have undertaken to the glory of the Lord and to make clear that our mind as ready:
And so that no man might be able to say anything against us in the business of this giving hich has been put into our hands:
For the business has been so ordered by us as to have the approval, not only of the Lord, but of men.
And e have sent ith them our brother, hose ready spirit has been made clear to us at times and in ays ithout number, but it is no all the more so because of the certain faith hich he has in you.
If any question comes up about Titus, he is my brother-orker, orking ith me for you; or about the others, they are the representatives of the churches to the glory of Christ.
Make clear then to them, as representatives of the churches, the quality of your love, and that the things hich e have said about you are true.
But there is no need for me to say anything in my letter about the giving to the saints:

For I have before made clear to those of Macedonia my pride in your ready mind, saying to them that Achaia has been ready for a year back; and a great number have been moved to do the same by your example.
But I have sent the brothers, so that the good things e said about you may be seen to be true, and that, as I said, you may be ready:
For fear that, if any from Macedonia come ith me, and you are not ready, e ( not to say, you) might be put to shame in this thing.

So it seemed to me ise for the brothers to go before, and see that the amount hich you had undertaken to give as ready, so that it might be a cause for praise, and not as if e ere making profit out of you.
But in the Writings it says, He ho puts in only a small number of seeds, ill get in the same; and he ho puts them in from a full hand, ill have produce in full measure from them.
Let every man do after the purpose of his heart; not giving ith grief, or by force: for God takes pleasure in a ready giver.
And God is able to give you all grace in full measure; so that ever having enough of all things, you may be full of every good ork:
As it is said in the Writings, He has sent out far and ide, he has given to the poor; his righteousness is for ever.
And he ho gives seed for putting into the field and bread for food, ill take care of the groth of your seed, at the same time increasing the fruits of your righteousness;
Your ealth being increased in everything, ith a simple mind, causing praise to God through us.
For this ork of giving not only takes care of the needs of the saints, but is the cause of much praise to God;

For hen, through this ork of giving, they see hat you are, they give glory to God for the ay in hich you have given yourselves to the good nes of Christ, and for the ealth of your giving to them and to all;
While their hearts go out to you in love and in prayer for you, because of the great grace of God hich is in you.
Praise be to God for hat he has given, hich ords have no poer to say.
No I, Paul, myself make request to you by the quiet and gentle behaviour of Christ, I ho am poor in spirit hen ith you, but ho say hat is in my mind to you ithout fear hen I am aay from you:
Yes, I make my request to you, so that hen I am ith you I may not have to make use of the authority hich may be needed against some to hom e seem to be alking after the flesh.
For though e may be living in the flesh, e are not fighting after the ay of the flesh
( For the arms ith hich e are fighting are not those of the flesh, but are strong before God for the destruction of high places);
Putting an end to reasonings, and every high thing hich is lifted up against the knoledge of God, and causing every thought to come under the authority of Christ;
Being ready to give punishment to hatever is against his authority, after you have made it clear that you are completely under his control.
Give attention to the things hich are before you. If any man seems to himself to be Christ’s, let him keep in mind that e are as much Christ’s as he is.
For though I might take pride in our authority ( hich the Lord gave for building you up, and not for your destruction), it ill not be a cause of shame to me:
That I may not seem to have the desire of causing you fear by my letters.
For his letters, they say, have eight and are strong; but in body he is feeble, and his ay of talking has little force.
Let those ho say this keep in mind that, hat e are in ord by letters hen e are aay, so ill e be in act hen e are present.

For e ill not make comparison of ourselves ith some of those ho say good things about themselves: but these, measuring themselves by themselves, and making comparison of themselves ith themselves, are not ise.
We ill not give glory to ourselves in over-great measure, but after the measure of the rule hich God has given us, a measure hich comes even to you.
For e have no need to make ourselves seem more than e are, as if our authority did not come as far as to you: for e came even as far as you ith the good nes of Christ:

Not taking credit to ourselves for hat is not our business, that is, for the ork of others; but having hope that, ith the groth of your faith, e may get the credit for an increase hich is the effect of our ork,
So that e may be able to go on and take the good nes to countries still farther aay than you are, and not take credit for another man’s ork in making things ready to our hand.
But hoever has a desire for glory, let his glory be in the Lord.
For the Lord’s approval of a man is not dependent on his opinion of himself, but on the Lord’s opinion of him.
Put up ith me if I am a little foolish: but, truly, you do put up ith me.
For I have a very great care for you: because you have been married by me to one husband, and it is my desire to give you completely holy to Christ.
But I have a fear, that in some ay, as Eve as tricked by the deceit of the snake, your minds may be turned aay from their simple and holy love for Christ.

For if anyone comes preaching another Jesus from the one hose preachers e are, or if you have got a different spirit, or a different sort of good nes from those hich came to you, ho ell you put up ith these things.
For in my opinion, I am in no ay less than the most important of the Apostles.
But though I am rough in my ay of talking, I am not so in knoledge, as e have made clear to all by our acts among you.
Or did I do rong in making myself lo so that you might be lifted up, because I gave you the good nes of God ithout reard?
I took money from other churches as payment for my ork, so that I might be your servant;

And hen I as present ith you, and as in need, I let no man be responsible for me; for the brothers, hen they came from Macedonia, gave me hatever as needed; and in everything I kept myself from being a trouble to you, and I ill go on doing so.
As the true ord of Christ is in me, I ill let no man take from me this my cause of pride in the country of Achaia.
Why? because I have no love for you? let God be judge.
But hat I do, that I ill go on doing, so that I may give no chance to those ho are looking for one; so that, in the cause of their pride, they may be seen to be the same as e are.
For such men are false Apostles, orkers of deceit, making themselves seem like Apostles of Christ.
And it is no onder; for even Satan himself is able to take the form of an angel of light.
So it is no great thing if his servants make themselves seem to be servants of righteousness; hose end ill be the reard of their orks.
I say again, Let me not seem foolish to anyone; but if I do, put up ith me as such, so that I may take a little glory to myself.
What I am no saying is not by the order of the Lord, but as a foolish person, taking credit to myself, as it seems.
Seeing that there are those ho take credit to themselves after the flesh, I ill do the same.
For you put up ith the foolish gladly, being ise yourselves.
You put up ith a man if he makes servants of you, if he makes profit out of you, if he makes you prisoners, if he puts himself in a high place, if he gives you blos on the face.
I say this by ay of shaming ourselves, as if e had been feeble. But if anyone puts himself forard ( I am talking like a foolish person), I ill do the same.
Are they Hebres? so am I. Are they of Israel? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.
Are they servants of Christ? ( I am talking foolishly) I am more so; I have had more experience of hard ork, of prisons, of blos more than measure, of death.
Five times the Jes gave me forty blos but one.
Three times I as hipped ith rods, once I as stoned, three times the ship I as in came to destruction at sea, a night and a day I have been in the ater;

In frequent travels, in dangers on rivers, in dangers from outlas, in dangers from my countrymen, in dangers from the Gentiles, in dangers in the ton, in dangers in the aste land, in dangers at sea, in dangers among false brothers;
In hard ork and eariness, in frequent atchings, going ithout food and drink, cold and in need of clothing.
In addition to all the other things, there is that hich comes on me every day, the care of all the churches.
Who is feeble and I am not feeble? ho is in danger of falling, and I am not angry?
If I have to take credit to myself, I ill do so in the things in hich I am feeble.
The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, to hom be praise for ever, is itness that the things hich I say are true.
In Damascus, the ruler under Aretas the king kept atch over the ton of the people of Damascus, in order to take me:
And being let don in a basket from the all through a indo, I got free from his hands.
As it is necessary for me to take glory to myself, though it is not a good thing, I ill come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
I have knoledge of a man in Christ, fourteen years back ( if he as in the body, or out of the body, I am not able to say, but God only), ho as taken up to the third heaven.
And I have knoledge of such a man ( if he as in the body, or out of the body, I am not able to say, but God only),
Ho he as taken up into Paradise, and ords came to his ears hich may not be said, and hich man is not able to say.
On account of such a one I ill have glory: for myself I ill take no glory, but only in my feeble body.

For if I had a desire to take credit to myself, it ould not be foolish, for I ould be saying hat is true: but I ill not, for fear that I might seem to any man more than he sees me to be, or has ord from me that I am.
And because the revelations ere so very great, in order that I might not be overmuch lifted up, there as given to me a thorn in the flesh, one sent from Satan to give me pain.
And about this thing I made request to the Lord three times that it might be taken aay from me.
And he said to me, My grace is enough for you, for my poer is made complete in hat is feeble. Most gladly, then, ill I take pride in my feeble body, so that the poer of Christ may be on me.
So I take pleasure in being feeble, in unkind ords, in needs, in cruel attacks, in troubles, on account of Christ: for hen I am feeble, then am I strong.
I have been forced by you to become foolish, though it as right for my praise to have come from you: for in no ay as I less than the chief of the Apostles, though I am nothing.
Truly the signs of an Apostle ere done among you in quiet strength, ith onders and acts of poer.
For hat is there in hich you ere made less than the other churches, but in the one thing that I as not a trouble to you? Let me have forgiveness for this rong.

This is no the third time that I am ready to come to you; and I ill not be a trouble to you: my desire is for you, not for your property: for it is not the children’s business to make store for their fathers, but the fathers for the children.
And I ill gladly give all I have for your souls. If I have the more love for you, am I to be loved the less?
But let it be so, that I as not a trouble to you myself; but (someone may say) being false, I took you ith deceit.
Did I make a profit out of you by any of those hom I sent to you?
I gave orders to Titus, and I sent the brother ith him. Did Titus make any profit out of you? ere e not guided by the same Spirit, in the same ays?
It may seem to you that all this time e have been attempting to put ourselves in the right; but e are saying these things before God in Christ. For all things, dear brothers, are for your profit.

For I have a fear that, hen I come, you may not be ansering to my desire, and that I may not be ansering to yours; that there may be fighting, hate, angry feeling, divisions, evil talk about others, secrets, thoughts of pride, outbursts against authority;

And that hen I come again, my God may put me to shame among you, and I may have grief for those ho have done rong before and have had no regret for their unclean ays, and for the evil desires of the flesh to hich they have given ay.
This is the third time that I am coming to you. From the mouth of to or three itnesses ill every ord be made certain.

I said before, and still say it before I come, as being present for the second time, though I am still aay from you, to those ho have done rong before, and to all the others, that if I come again I ill not have pity;
Seeing that you are looking for a sign of Christ giving out his ord in me; ho is not feeble in relation to you, but is strong in you:
For he as feeble in that he as put to death on the cross, but he is living by the poer of God. And e are feeble in him, but e ill be living ith him through the poer of God in relation to you.
Make a test of yourselves, if you are in the faith; make certain of yourselves. Or are you not conscious in yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you, if you are truly Christ’s?
But it is my hope that you ill have no doubt that e are truly Christ’s.
No our prayer to God is that you may do no evil; not in order that it may be put to our credit, but so that you may do hat is right, hatever e may seem.
Because e are able to do nothing against hat is true, but only for it.
For e are glad hen e are feeble and you are strong: and this is our prayer, even that you may be made complete.

For this cause I am riting these things hile I am aay, so that there may be need for me, hen I am present, to make use of sharp measures, by the authority hich the Lord has given me for building up and not for destruction.
Let this be my last ord, brothers; be glad; be complete; be comforted; be of the same mind; be at peace ith one another: and the God of love and peace ill be ith you.
Give one another a holy kiss.
All the saints send their love to you.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the harmony of the Holy Spirit, be ith you all.
Paul, an Apostle ( not from men, and not through man, but through Jesus Christ, and God the Father, ho made him come back from the dead),
And all the brothers ho are ith me, to the churches of Galatia:
Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,
Who gave himself for our sins, so that he might make us free from this present evil orld, after the purpose of our God and Father:
To hom be the glory for ever and ever. So be it.
I am surprised that you are being so quickly turned aay from him hose ord came to you in the grace of Christ, to good nes of a different sort;
Which is not another sort: only there are some ho give you trouble, desiring to make changes in the good nes of Christ.
But even if e, or an angel from heaven, ere to be a preacher to you of good nes other than that hich e have given you, let there be a curse on him.
As e have said before, so say I no again, If any man is a preacher to you of any good nes other than that hich has been given to you, let there be a curse on him.
Am I no using arguments to men, or God? or is it my desire to give men pleasure? if I as still pleasing men, I ould not be a servant of Christ.
Because I say to you, my brothers, that the good nes of hich I as the preacher is not man’s.
For I did not get it from man, and I as not given teaching in it, but it came to me through revelation of Jesus Christ.
For nes has come to you of my ay of life in the past in the Jes’ religion, ho I as cruel ithout measure to the church of God, and did great damage to it:
And I ent farther in the Jes’ religion than a number of my generation among my countrymen, having a more burning interest in the beliefs handed don from my fathers.
But hen it as the good pleasure of God, by hom I as marked out even from my mother’s body, through his grace,
To give the revelation of his Son in me, so that I might give the nes of him to the Gentiles; then I did not take the opinion of flesh and blood,
And I ent not up to Jerusalem to those ho ere Apostles before me; but I ent aay into Arabia, and again I came back to Damascus.
Then after three years I ent up to Jerusalem to see Cephas, and as there ith him fifteen days.
But of the other Apostles I sa only James, the Lord’s brother.
No God is itness that the things hich I am riting to you are true.
Then I came to the parts of Syria and Cilicia.
And the churches of Judaea hich ere in Christ still had no knoledge of my face or person:
Only it came to their ears that he ho at one time as cruel to us is no preaching the faith hich before had been attacked by him;
And they gave glory to God in me.
Then after the space of fourteen years I ent up again to Jerusalem ith Barnabas, taking Titus ith me.

And I ent up by revelation; and I put before them the good nes hich I as preaching among the Gentiles, but privately before those ho ere of good name, so that the ork hich I as or had been doing might not be ithout effect.
But not even Titus ho as ith me, being a Greek, as made to undergo circumcision:
And that because of the false brothers let in secretly, ho came searching out our free condition hich e have in Christ Jesus, so that they might make servants of us;
To hom e gave ay not even for an hour; so that the true ords of the good nes might still be ith you.
But from those ho seemed to be important ( hatever they ere has no eight ith me: God does not take man’s person into account): those ho seemed to be important gave nothing ne to me;
But, quite the opposite, hen they sa that I had been made responsible for preaching the good nes to those ithout circumcision, even as Peter had been for those of the circumcision
( Because he ho as orking in Peter as the Apostle of the circumcision as orking no less in me among the Gentiles);

When they sa the grace hich as given to me, James and Cephas and John, ho had the name of being pillars, gave to me and Barnabas their right hands as friends so that e might go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcision;
Only it as their desire that e ould give thought to the poor; hich very thing I had much in mind to do.
But hen Cephas came to Antioch, I made a protest against him to his face, because he as clearly in the rong.
For before certain men came from James, he did take food ith the Gentiles: but hen they came, he ent back and made himself separate, fearing those ho ere of the circumcision.
And the rest of the Jes ent after him, so that even Barnabas as overcome by their false ays.

But hen I sa that they ere not living uprightly in agreement ith the true ords of the good nes, I said to Cephas before them all, If you, being a Je, are living like the Gentiles, and not like the Jes, ho ill you make the Gentiles do the same as the Jes?
We being Jes by birth, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

Being conscious that a man does not get righteousness by the orks of the la, but through faith in Jesus Christ, e had faith in Christ Jesus, so that e might get righteousness by faith in Christ, and not by the orks of the la: because by the orks of the la ill no flesh get righteousness.
But if, hile e ere desiring to get righteousness through Christ, e ourselves ere seen to be sinners, is Christ a servant of sin? In no ay!
For if I put up again those things hich I gave to destruction, I am seen to be a rongdoer.
For I, through the la, have become dead to the la, so that I might be living to God.

I have been put to death on the cross ith Christ; still I am living; no longer I, but Christ is living in me; and that life hich I no am living in the flesh I am living by faith, the faith of the Son of God, ho in love for me, gave himself up for me.
I do not make the grace of God of no effect: because if righteousness is through the la, then Christ as put to death for nothing.
O foolish Galatians, by hat strange poers have you been tricked, to hom it as made clear that Jesus Christ as put to death on the cross?
Give me an anser to this one question, Did the Spirit come to you through the orks of the la, or by the hearing of faith?
Are you so foolish? having made a start in the Spirit, ill you no be made complete in the flesh?
Did you undergo such a number of things to no purpose? if it is in fact to no purpose.
He ho gives you the Spirit, and does orks of poer among you, is it by the orks of la, or by the hearing of faith?
Even as Abraham had faith in God, and it as put to his account as righteousness.
Be certain, then, that those ho are of faith, the same are sons of Abraham.
And the holy Writings, seeing before the event that God ould give the Gentiles righteousness by faith, gave the good nes before to Abraham, saying, In you ill all the nations have a blessing.
So then those ho are of faith have a part in the blessing of Abraham ho as full of faith.
For all ho are of the orks of the la are under a curse: because it is said in the Writings, A curse is on everyone ho does not keep on doing all the things hich are ordered in the book of the la.
No that no man gets righteousness by the la in the eyes of God, is clear; because, The upright ill be living by faith.
And the la is not of faith; but, He ho does them ill have life by them.
Christ has made us free from the curse of the la, having become a curse for us: because it is said in the Writings, A curse on everyone ho is put to death by hanging on a tree:
So that on the Gentiles might come the blessing of Abraham in Christ Jesus; in order that e through faith might have the Spirit hich God had undertaken to give.
Brothers, as men ould say, even a man’s agreement, hen it has been made certain, may not be put on one side, or have additions made to it.
No to Abraham ere the undertakings given, and to his seed. He says not, And to seeds, as of a great number; but as of one, he says, And to your seed, hich is Christ.
No this I say: The la, hich came four hundred and thirty years after, does not put an end to the agreement made before by God, so as to make the undertaking ithout effect.
Because if the heritage is by the la, it is no longer dependent on the ord of God; but God gave it to Abraham by his ord.
What then is the la? It as an addition made because of sin, till the coming of the seed to hom the undertaking had been given; and it as ordered through angels by the hand of a go-beteen.
No a go-beteen is not a go-beteen of one; but God is one.
Is the la then against the ords of God? in no ay; because if there had been a la hich as able to give life, truly righteousness ould have been by the la.
Hoever, the holy Writings have put all things under sin, so that that for hich God gave the undertaking, based on faith in Jesus Christ, might be given to those ho have such faith.
But before faith came, e ere kept in prison under the la, aiting for the revelation of the faith hich as to come.
So the la has been a servant to take us to Christ, so that e might have righteousness by faith.
But no that faith is come, e are no longer under a servant.
Because you are all sons of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
For all those of you ho ere given baptism into Christ did put on Christ.
There is no Je or Greek, servant or free, male or female: because you are all one in Jesus Christ.
And if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s seed, and yours is the heritage by the right of God’s undertaking given to Abraham.
But I say that as long as the son is a child, he is in no ay different from a servant, though he is lord of all;
But is under keepers and managers till the time fixed by the father.
So e, hen e ere young, ere kept under the first rules of the orld;
But hen the time had come, God sent out his Son, made of a oman, made under the la,
That he might make them free ho ere under the la, and that e might be given the place of sons.
And because you are sons, God has sent out the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, saying, Abba, Father.
So that you are no longer a servant, but a son; and if a son, then the heritage of God is yours.
But at that time, having no knoledge of God, you ere servants to those ho by right are no gods:
But no that you have come to have knoledge of God, or more truly, God has knoledge of you, ho is it that you go back again to the poor and feeble first things, desiring to be servants to them again?
You keep days, and months, and fixed times, and years.
I am in fear of you, that I may have been orking for you to no purpose.
My desire for you, brothers, is that you may be as I am, because I am as you are. You have done me no rong;
But you have knoledge that ith a feeble body I as preaching the good nes to you the first time;
And you did not have a poor opinion of me because of the trouble in my flesh, or put shame on it; but you took me to your hearts as an angel of God, even as Christ Jesus.
Where then is that happy condition of yours? because I give you itness, that, if possible, you ould have taken out your eyes and given them to me.
So then am I no longer your friend, because I give you true ords?
Their interest in you is not good; but their desire is that you may be shut out, so that you may go after them.
But it is good to have an interest in a good cause at all times, and not only hen I am present ith you.
My children, of hom I am again in birth-pains till Christ is formed in you,
Truly my desire is to be present ith you no, using a changed voice; for I am troubled about you.
Say, you hose desire it is to be under the la, do you not give ear to the la?
Because it is in the Writings, that Abraham had to sons, one by the servant-oman, and one by the free oman.
No the son by the servant-oman has his birth after the flesh; but the son by the free oman has his birth through the undertaking of God.
Which things have a secret sense; because these omen are the to agreements; one from the mountain of Sinai, giving birth to servants, hich is Hagar.
No this Hagar is the mountain Sinai in Arabia, and is the image of the Jerusalem hich no is: hich is a servant ith her children.
But the Jerusalem on high is free, hich is our mother.

For it is in the Writings, You ho have never given birth, be glad; give cries of joy, you ho have had no birth-pains; for the children of her ho has been given up by her husband are more than those of the oman ho has a husband.
No e, brothers, as Isaac as, are the children of the undertaking of God.
But as in those days he ho had birth after the flesh as cruel to him ho had birth after the Spirit, even so it is no.
What then do the Writings say? Send aay the servant-oman and her son; for the son of the servant-oman ill not have a part in the heritage ith the son of the free oman.
So, brothers, e are not children of the servant-oman, but of the free oman.
Christ has truly made us free: then keep your free condition and let no man put a yoke on you again.
See, I Paul say to you, that if you undergo circumcision, Christ ill be of no use to you.
Yes, I give itness again to every man ho undergoes circumcision, that he ill have to keep all the la.
You are cut off from Christ, you ho ould have righteousness by the la; you are turned aay from grace.
For e through the Spirit by faith are aiting for the hope of righteousness.
Because in Christ Jesus, having circumcision or not having circumcision are equally of no profit; but only faith orking through love.
You ere going on ell; ho as the cause of your not giving ear to hat is true?
This ready belief did not come from him ho had made you his.
A little leaven makes a change in all the mass.
I am certain about you in the Lord, that you ill be of no other mind; but he ho is troubling you ill have his punishment, hoever he is.
But I, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, hy am I still attacked? then has the shame of the cross been taken aay.
My desire is that they ho give you trouble might even be cut off themselves.
Because you, brothers, ere marked out to be free; only do not make use of your free condition to give the flesh its chance, but through love be servants one to another.
For all the la is made complete in one ord, even in this, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself.
But if you are given to fighting ith one another, take care that you are not the cause of destruction one to another.
But I say, Go on in the Spirit, and you ill not come under the rule of the evil desires of the flesh.
For the flesh has desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; because these are opposite the one to the other; so that you may not do the things hich you have a mind to do.
But if you are guided by the Spirit, you are not under the la.
No the orks of the flesh are clear, hich are these: evil desire, unclean things, rong use of the senses,
Worship of images, use of strange poers, hates, fighting, desire for hat another has, angry feelings, attempts to get the better of others, divisions, false teachings,
Envy, uncontrolled drinking and feasting, and such things: of hich I give you ord clearly, even as I did in the past, that they ho do such things ill have no part in the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, a quiet mind, kind acts, ell-doing, faith,
Gentle behaviour, control over desires: against such there is no la.
And those ho are Christ’s have put to death on the cross the flesh ith its passions and its evil desires.
If e are living by the Spirit, by the Spirit let us be guided.
Let us not be full of self-glory, making one another angry, having envy of one another.
Brothers, if a man is taken in any rongdoing, you ho are of the Spirit ill put such a one right in a spirit of love; keeping atch on yourself, for fear that you yourself may be tested.
Take on yourselves one another’s troubles, and so keep the la of Christ.
For if a man has an idea that he is something hen he is nothing, he is tricked by himself.
But let every man make test of his ork, and then ill his cause for glory be in himself only, and not in his neighbour.
Because every man is responsible for his part of the ork.
But let him ho gets teaching in the ord give a part in all good things to his teacher.
Be not tricked; God is not made sport of: for hatever seed a man puts in, that ill he get back as grain.
Because he ho puts in the seed of the flesh ill of the flesh get the reard of death; but he ho puts in the seed of the Spirit ill of the Spirit get the reard of eternal life.
And let us not get tired of ell-doing; for at the right time e ill get in the grain, if e do not give ay to eariness.
So then, as e have the chance, let us do good to all men, and specially to those ho are of the family of the faith.
See the size of the handriting hich I myself have made use of in riting to you.
Those ho have the desire to seem important in the flesh, put force on you to undergo circumcision; only that they may not be attacked because of the cross of Christ.
Because even those ho undergo circumcision do not themselves keep the la; but they ould have you undergo circumcision, so that they may have glory in your flesh.
But far be it from me to have glory in anything, but only in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through hich this orld has come to an end on the cross for me, and I for it.
For having circumcision is nothing, and not having circumcision is nothing, but only a ne order of existence.
And on all ho are guided by this rule be peace and mercy, and on the Israel of God.
From this time on let no man be a trouble to me; because my body is marked ith the marks of Jesus.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be ith your spirit, brothers. So be it.
Paul, an Apostle of Christ Jesus by the purpose of God, to the saints ho are at Ephesus, and those ho have faith in Christ Jesus:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, ho has given us every blessing of the Spirit in the heavens in Christ:
Even as he made selection of us in him from the first, so that e might be holy and free from all evil before him in love:
As e ere designed before by him for the position of sons to himself, through Jesus Christ, in the good pleasure of his purpose,
To the praise of the glory of his grace, hich he freely gave to us in the Loved One:
In hom e have salvation through his blood, the forgiveness of our sins, through the ealth of his grace,
Which he gave us in full measure in all isdom and care;
Having made clear to us the secret of his purpose, in agreement ith the design hich he had in mind, to put into his hands
The ordering of the times hen they are complete, so that all things might come to a head in Christ, the things in heaven and the things on the earth; in him, I say,
In hom e have a heritage, being marked out from the first in his purpose ho does all things in agreement ith his designs;
So that his glory might have praise through us ho first had hope in Christ:
In hom you, having been given the true ord, the good nes of your salvation, and through your faith in him, ere given the sign of the Holy Spirit of hope,
Which is the first-fruit of our heritage, till God gets back that hich is his, to the praise of his glory.
For this cause I, having had nes of the faith in the Lord Jesus hich is among you, and hich you make clear to all the saints,
Give praise ithout end for you, keeping you in mind in my prayers;
That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give to you a spirit of isdom and revelation in the knoledge of him;
And that having the eyes of your heart full of light, you may have knoledge of hat is the hope of his purpose, hat is the ealth of the glory of his heritage in the saints,
And ho unlimited is his poer to us ho have faith, as is seen in the orking of the strength of his poer,
By hich he made Christ come back from the dead, and gave him a place at his right hand in heaven,
Far over all rule and authority and poer and every name hich is named, not only in the present order, but in that hich is to come:
And he has put all things under his feet, and has made him to be head over all things to the church,
Which is his body, the full measure of him in hom all things are made complete.
And to you did he give life, hen you ere dead through your rongdoing and sins,
In hich you ere living in the past, after the ays of this present orld, doing the pleasure of the lord of the poer of the air, the spirit ho is no orking in those ho go against the purpose of God;
Among hom e all at one time ere living in the pleasures of our flesh, giving ay to the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and the punishment of God as aiting for us even as for the rest.
But God, being full of mercy, through the great love hich he had for us,
