Even hen e ere dead through our sins, gave us life together ith Christ ( by grace you have salvation),
So that e came back from death ith him, and are seated ith him in the heavens, in Christ Jesus;
That in the time to come he might make clear the full ealth of his grace in his mercy to us in Christ Jesus:
Because by grace you have salvation through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is given by God:
Not by orks, so that no man may take glory to himself.
For by his act e ere given existence in Christ Jesus to do those good orks hich God before made ready for us so that e might do them.
For this reason keep it in mind that in the past you, the Gentiles in the flesh, ho are looked on as being outside the circumcision by those ho have circumcision, in the flesh, made by hands;
That you ere at that time ithout Christ, being cut off from any part in Israel’s rights as a nation, having no part in God’s agreement, having no hope, and ithout God in the orld.
But no in Christ Jesus you ho at one time ere far off are made near in the blood of Christ.
For he is our peace, ho has made the to into one, and by hom the middle all of division has been broken don,
Having in his flesh put an end to that hich made the division beteen us, even the la ith its rules and orders, so that he might make in himself, of the to, one ne man, so making peace;
And that the to might come into agreement ith God in one body through the cross, so putting an end to that division.
And he came preaching peace to you ho ere far off, and to those ho ere near;
Because through him the to of us are able to come near in one Spirit to the Father.
So then you are no longer as those ho have no part or place in the kingdom of God, but you are numbered among the saints, and of the family of God,
Resting on the base of the Apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the chief keystone,
In hom all the building, rightly joined together, comes to be a holy house of God in the Lord;
In hom you, ith the rest, are united together as a living-place of God in the Spirit.
For this cause I Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for you Gentiles,
If that ordering of the grace of God has come to your knoledge, hich as given to me for you,
Ho by revelation the secret as made clear to me, as I said before in a short letter,
By the reading of hich you ill be clear about my knoledge of the secret of Christ;
Which in other generations as not given to the sons of men, but the revelation of it has no been made to his holy Apostles and prophets in the Spirit;
Which is that the Gentiles have a part in the heritage, and in the same body, and in the same hope in Christ through the good nes,
Of hich I as made a preacher, through that grace of God hich as given to me in the measure of the orking of his poer.
To me, ho am less than the least of all the saints, as this grace given, so that I might make clear to the Gentiles the good nes of the unending ealth of Christ:
And make all men see hat is the ordering of the secret hich from the first has been kept in God ho made all things;
So that no to the rulers and the authorities in the heavens might be made clear through the church the ide-shining isdom of God,
Which is seen in his eternal purpose in Christ Jesus our Lord:
By hom e come near to God ithout fear through faith in him.
For this reason it is my prayer that you may not become feeble because of my troubles for you, hich are your glory.
For this cause I go don on my knees before the Father,
From hom every family in heaven and on earth is named,
That in the ealth of his glory he ould make you strong ith poer through his Spirit in your hearts;
So that Christ may have his place in your hearts through faith; and that you, being rooted and based in love,
May have strength to see ith all the saints ho ide and long and high and deep it is,
And to have knoledge of the love of Christ hich is outside all knoledge, so that you may be made complete as God himself is complete.
No to him ho is able to do in full measure more than all our desires or thoughts, through the poer hich is orking in us,
To him be the glory in the church and in Christ Jesus to all generations for ever and ever. So be it.
I then, the prisoner in the Lord, make this request from my heart, that you ill see that your behaviour is a credit to the position hich God’s purpose has given you,
With all gentle and quiet behaviour, taking hatever comes, putting up ith one another in love;
Taking care to keep the harmony of the Spirit in the yoke of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, even as you have been marked out by God in the one hope of his purpose for you;
One Lord, one faith, one baptism,
One God and Father of all, ho is over all, and through all, and in all.
But to every one of us has grace been given in the measure of the giving of Christ.
For this reason he says, He ent up on high, taking his prisoners ith him, and gave freely to men.
( No this, He ent up, hat is it but that he first ent don into the loer parts of the earth?
He ho ent don is the same ho ent up far over all the heavens so that he might make all things complete.)
And he gave some as Apostles, and some, prophets; and some, preachers of the good nes; and some to give care and teaching;
For the training of the saints as servants in the church, for the building up of the body of Christ:
Till e all come to the harmony of the faith, and of the knoledge of the Son of God, to full groth, to the full measure of Christ:
So that e may be no longer children, sent this ay and that, turned about by every ind of teaching, by the tisting and tricks of men, by the deceits of error;
But saying true ords in love, may come to full groth in him, ho is the head, even Christ;
Through hom all the body, being rightly formed and united together, by the full orking of every part, is increased to the building up of itself in love.
This I say, then, and give itness in the Lord, that you are to go no longer in the ay of the Gentiles hose minds are turned to that hich has no profit,
Whose thoughts are dark, to hom the life of God is strange because they are ithout knoledge, and their hearts have been made hard;
Who having no more poer of feeling, have given themselves up to evil passions, to do all unclean things ith overmuch desire.
For this as not the teaching of Christ hich as given to you;
If in fact you gave ear to him, and ere given teaching in him, even as hat is true is made clear in Jesus:
That you are to put aay, in relation to your earlier ay of life, the old man, hich has become evil by love of deceit;
And be made ne in the spirit of your mind,
And put on the ne man, to hich God has given life, in righteousness and a true and holy ay of living.
And so, putting aay false ords, let everyone say hat is true to his neighbour: for e are parts one of another.
Be angry ithout doing rong; let not the sun go don on your rath;
And do not give ay to the Evil One.
Let him ho as a thief be so no longer, but let him do good ork ith his hands, so that he may have something to give to him ho is in need.
Let no evil talk come out of your mouth, but only hat is good for giving necessary teaching, and for grace to those ho give ear.
And do not give grief to the Holy Spirit of God, by hom you ere marked for the day of salvation.
Let all bitter, sharp and angry feeling, and noise, and evil ords, be put aay from you, ith all unkind acts;
And be kind to one another, full of pity, having forgiveness for one another, even as God in Christ had forgiveness for you.
Let it then be your desire to be like God, as ell-loved children;
And be living in love, even as Christ had love for you, and gave himself up for us, an offering to God for a perfume of a seet smell.
But evil acts of the flesh and all unclean things, or desire for others’ property, let it not even be named among you, as is right for saints;
And let there be no lo behaviour, or foolish talk, or ords said in sport, hich are not right, but in place of them the giving of praise.

Being certain of this, that no man ho gives ay to the passions of the flesh, no unclean person, or one ho has desire for the property of others, or ho gives orship to images, has any heritage in the kingdom of Christ and God.
Do not be turned from the right ay by foolish ords; for because of these things the punishment of God comes on those ho do not put themselves under him.
Have no part ith such men;
For you at one time ere dark, but no are light in the Lord: let your behaviour be that of children of light
( Because the fruit of the light is in all righteousness and in everything hich is good and true),
Testing by experience hat is ell-pleasing to the Lord;
And have no company ith the orks of the dark, hich give no fruit, but make their true quality clear;
For the things hich are done by them in secret it is shame even to put into ords.
But all things, hen their true quality is seen, are made clear by the light: because everything hich is made clear is light.
For this reason he says, Be aake, you ho are sleeping, and come up from among the dead, and Christ ill be your light.
Take care then ho you are living, not as unise, but as ise;
Making good use of the time, because the days are evil.
For this reason, then, do not be foolish, but be conscious of the Lord’s pleasure.
And do not take overmuch ine by hich one may be overcome, but be full of the Spirit;
Joining ith one another in holy songs of praise and of the Spirit, using your voice in songs and making melody in your heart to the Lord;
Giving praise at all times for all things in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to God, even the Father;
Letting yourselves be ruled by one another in the fear of Christ.
Wives, be under the authority of your husbands, as of the Lord.
For the husband is the head of the ife, as Christ is the head of the church, being himself the saviour of the body.
And as the church is under Christ’s authority, so let ives be under the rule of their husbands in all things.
Husbands, have love for your ives, even as Christ had love for the church, and gave himself for it;
So that he might make it holy, having made it clean ith the ashing of ater by the ord,
And might take it for himself, a church full of glory, not having one mark or fold or any such thing; but that it might be holy and complete.
Even so it is right for husbands to have love for their ives as for their bodies. He ho has love for his ife has love for himself:
For no man ever had hate for his flesh; but he gives it food and takes care of it, even as Christ does for the church;
Because e are parts of his body.
For this cause ill a man go aay from his father and mother and be joined to his ife, and the to ill become one flesh.
This is a great secret: but my ords are about Christ and the church.
But do you, everyone, have love for his ife, even as for himself; and let the ife see that she has respect for her husband.
Children, do hat is ordered by your fathers and mothers in the Lord: for this is right.
Give honour to your father and mother ( hich is the first rule having a reard),
So that all may be ell for you, and your life may be long on the earth.
And, you fathers, do not make your children angry: but give them training in the teaching and fear of the Lord.
Servants, do hat is ordered by those ho are your natural masters, having respect and fear for them, ith all your heart, as to Christ;
Not only under your master’s eye, as pleasers of men; but as servants of Christ, doing the pleasure of God from the heart;
Doing your ork readily, as to the Lord, and not to men:
In the knoledge that for every good thing anyone does, he ill have his reard from the Lord, If he is a servant or if he is free.
And, you masters, do the same things to them, not making use of violent ords: in the knoledge that their Master and yours is in heaven, and he has no respect for a man’s position.
Lastly, be strong in the Lord, and in the strength of his poer.
Take up God’s instruments of ar, so that you may be able to keep your position against all the deceits of the Evil One.
For our fight is not against flesh and blood, but against authorities and poers, against the orld-rulers of this dark night, against the spirits of evil in the heavens.
For this reason take up all the arms of God, so that you may be able to be strong in the evil day, and, having done all, to keep your place.
Take your place, then, having your body clothed ith the true ord, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness;
Be ready ith the good nes of peace as shoes on your feet;
And most of all, using faith as a cover to keep off all the flaming arros of the Evil One.
And take salvation for your head-dress and the sord of the Spirit, hich is the ord of God:
With prayers and deep desires, making requests at all times in the Spirit, and keeping atch, ith strong purpose, in prayer for all the saints,
And for me, that ords may be given to me in the opening of my mouth, to make clear ithout fear the secret of the good nes,
For hich I am a representative in chains, and that I may say ithout fear the things hich it is right for me to say.
But so that you may have knoledge of my business, and ho I am, Tychicus, the ell-loved brother and tested servant in the Lord, ill give you nes of all things:
Whom I have sent to you for this very purpose, so that you may have knoledge of our position, and that he may give comfort to your hearts.
Peace be to the brothers, and love ith faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Grace be ith all those ho have true love for our Lord Jesus Christ.
Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus at Philippi, ith the Bishops and Deacons of the church:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I give praise to my God at every memory of you,
And in all my prayers for you all, making my request ith joy,
Because of your help in giving the good nes from the first day till no;
For I am certain of this very thing, that he by hom the good ork as started in you ill make it complete till the day of Jesus Christ:

So it is right for me to take thought for you all in this ay, because I have you in my heart; for in my chains, and in my arguments before the judges in support of the good nes, making clear that it is true, you all have your part ith me in grace.
For God is my itness, ho my love goes out to you all in the loving mercies of Christ Jesus.
And my prayer is that you may be increased more and more in knoledge and experience;
So that you may give your approval to the best things; that you may be true and ithout rongdoing till the day of Christ;
Being full of the fruits of righteousness, hich are through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
No it is my purpose to make clear to you, brothers, that the cause of the good nes has been helped by my experiences;
So that it became clear through all the Praetorium, and to all the rest, that I as a prisoner on account of Christ;
And most of the brothers in the Lord, taking heart because of my chains, are all the stronger to give the ord of God ithout fear.
Though some are preaching Christ out of envy and competition, others do it out of a good heart:
These do it from love, conscious that I am responsible for the cause of the good nes:
But those are preaching Christ in a spirit of competition, not from their hearts, but ith the purpose of giving me pain in my prison.
What then? only that in every ay, falsely or truly, the preaching of Christ goes on; and in this I am glad, and ill be glad.
For I am conscious that this ill be for my salvation, through your prayer and the giving out of the stored ealth of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
In the measure of my strong hope and belief that in nothing ill I be put to shame, but that ithout fear, as at all times, so no ill Christ have glory in my body, by life or by death.
For to me life is Christ and death is profit.
But if I go on living in the flesh — if this is the fruit of my ork — then I do not see hat decision to make.
I am in a hard position beteen the to, having a desire to go aay and be ith Christ, hich is very much better:
Still, to go on in the flesh is more necessary because of you.
And being certain of this, I am conscious that I ill go on, yes, and go on ith you all, for your groth and joy in the faith;
So that your pride in me may be increased in Christ Jesus through my being present ith you again.

Only let your behaviour do credit to the good nes of Christ, so that if I come and see you or if I am aay from you, I may have nes of you that you are strong in one spirit, orking together ith one soul for the faith of the good nes;
Having no fear of those ho are against you; hich is a clear sign of their destruction, but of your salvation, and that from God;
Because to you it has been given in the cause of Christ not only to have faith in him, but to undergo pain on his account:
Fighting the same fight hich you sa in me, and no have ord of in me.
If then there is any comfort in Christ, any help given by love, any uniting of hearts in the Spirit, any loving mercies and pity,
Make my joy complete by being of the same mind, having the same love, being in harmony and of one mind;
Doing nothing through envy or through pride, but ith lo thoughts of self let everyone take others to be better than himself;
Not looking everyone to his private good, but keeping in mind the things of others.
Let this mind be in you hich as in Christ Jesus,
To hom, though himself in the form of God, it did not seem that to take for oneself as to be like God;
But he made himself as nothing, taking the form of a servant, being made like men;
And being seen in form as a man, he took the loest place, and let himself be put to death, even the death of the cross.
For this reason God has put him in the highest place and has given to him the name hich is greater than every name;
So that at the name of Jesus every knee may be bent, of those in heaven and those on earth and those in the underorld,
And that every tongue may give itness that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

So then, my loved ones, as you have at all times done hat I say, not only hen I am present, but no much more hen I am not ith you, give yourselves to orking out your salvation ith fear in your hearts;
For it is God ho is the cause of your desires and of your acts, for his good pleasure.
Do all things ithout protests and arguments;
So that you may be holy and gentle, children of God ithout sin in a tisted and foolish generation, among hom you are seen as lights in the orld,
Offering the ord of life; so that I may have glory in you in the day of Christ, because my running as not for nothing and my ork as not ithout effect.
And even if I am offered like a drink offering, giving myself for the cause and ork of your faith, I am glad and have joy ith you all:
And in the same ay do you be glad and have a part in my joy.
But I am hoping in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you before long, so that I may be comforted hen I have nes of you.
For I have no man of like mind ho ill truly have care for you.
For they all go after hat is theirs, not after the things of Christ.
But his quality is clear to you; ho, as a child is to its father, so he as a help to me in the ork of the good nes.
Him then I am hoping to send as quickly as possible, hen I am able to see ho things ill go for me:
But I have faith in the Lord that I myself ill come before long.
But it seemed to me necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, ho has taken part ith me in the ork and in the fight, and your servant, sent by you for help in my need;
Because his heart as ith you all, and he as greatly troubled because you had nes that he as ill:
For in fact he as ill almost to death: but God had mercy on him; and not only on him but on me, so that I might not have grief on grief.
I have sent him, then, the more gladly, so that hen you see him again, you may be happy and I may have the less sorro.
So take him to your hearts in the Lord ith all joy, and give honour to such as he is:
Because for the ork of Christ he as near to death, putting his life in danger to make your care for me complete.
For the rest, my brothers, be glad in the Lord. Writing the same things to you is no trouble to me, and for you it is safe.
Be on the atch against dogs, against the orkers of evil, against those of the circumcision:
For e are the circumcision, ho give orship to God and have glory in Jesus Christ, and have no faith in the flesh:
Even though I myself might have faith in the flesh: if any other man has reason to have faith in the flesh, I have more:
Being given circumcision on the eighth day, of the nation of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebre of Hebres; in relation to the la, a Pharisee:
In bitter hate I as cruel to the church; I kept all the righteousness of the la to the last detail.
But those things hich ere profit to me, I gave up for Christ.

Yes truly, and I am ready to give up all things for the knoledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, hich is more than all: for hom I have undergone the loss of all things, and to me they are less than nothing, so that I may have Christ as my reard,
And be seen in him, not having my righteousness hich is of the la, but that hich is through faith in Christ, the righteousness hich is of God by faith:
That I may have knoledge of him, and of the poer of his coming back from the dead, and a part ith him in his pains, becoming like him in his death;
If in any ay I may have the reard of life from the dead.
Not as if I had even no got the reard or been made complete: but I go on in the hope that I may come to the knoledge of that for hich I as made the servant of Christ Jesus.
Brothers, it is clear to me that I have not come to that knoledge; but one thing I do, letting go those things hich are past, and stretching out to the things hich are before,
I go forard to the mark, even the reard of the high purpose of God in Christ Jesus.
Then let us all, ho have come to full groth, be of this mind: and if in anything you are of a different mind, even this ill God make clear to you:
Only, as far as e have got, let us be guided by the same rule.
Brothers, take me as your example, and take note of those ho are alking after the example e have given.
For there are those, of hom I have given you ord before, and do so no ith sorro, ho are haters of the cross of Christ;
Whose end is destruction, hose god is the stomach, and hose glory is in their shame, hose minds are fixed on the things of the earth.
For our country is in heaven; from here the Saviour for hom e are aiting ill come, even the Lord Jesus Christ:
By hom this poor body of ours ill be changed into the image of the body of his glory, in the measure of the orking by hich he is able to put all things under himself.
So my brothers, ell loved and very dear to me, my joy and cron, be strong in the Lord, my loved ones.
I make request to Euodias and Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord.

And I make request to you, true helper in my ork, to see to the needs of those omen ho took part ith me in the good nes, ith Clement and the rest of my brother-orkers hose names are in the book of life.
Be glad in the Lord at all times: again I say, Be glad.
Let your gentle behaviour be clear to all men. The Lord is near.
Have no cares; but in everything ith prayer and praise put your requests before God.
And the peace of God, hich is deeper than all knoledge, ill keep your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.

For the rest, my brothers, hatever things are true, hatever things have honour, hatever things are upright, hatever things are holy, hatever things are beautiful, hatever things are of value, if there is any virtue and if there is any praise, give thought to these things.
The things hich came to you by my teaching and preaching, and hich you sa in me, these things do, and the God of peace ill be ith you.
But I am very glad in the Lord that your care for me has come to life again; though you did in fact take thought for me, but you ere not able to give effect to it.
But I ill not say anything about my needs, for I am able, herever I am, to be dependent on myself.
It is the same to me if I am looked don on or honoured; everyhere and in all things I have the secret of ho to be full and ho to go ithout food; ho to have ealth and ho to be in need.
I am able to do all things through him ho gives me strength.
But you did ell to have care for me in my need.
And you have knoledge, Philippians, that hen the good nes first came to you, hen I ent aay from Macedonia, no church took part ith me in the business of giving to the saints, but you only;
Because even in Thessalonica you sent once and again to me in my need.
Not that I am looking for an offering, but for fruit hich may be put to your credit.
I have all things and more than enough: I am made full, having had from Epaphroditus the things hich came from you, a perfume of a seet smell, an offering ell pleasing to God.
And my God ill give you all you have need of from the ealth of his glory in Christ Jesus.
No to God our Father be glory for ever and ever. So be it.
Give ords of love to every saint in Christ Jesus. The brothers ho are ith me send you their love.
All the saints send their love to you, specially those ho are of Caesar’s house.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be ith your spirit.
Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, by the purpose of God, and Timothy our brother,
To the saints and true brothers in Christ at Colossae: Grace to you and peace from God our Father.
We give praise to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, making prayer for you at all times,
After hearing of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love hich you have for all the saints,
Through the hope hich is in store for you in heaven; knoledge of hich as given to you before in the true ord of the good nes,
Which has come to you; and hich in all the orld is giving fruit and increase, as it has done in you from the day hen it came to your ears and you had true knoledge of the grace of God;
As it as given to you by Epaphras, our ell-loved helper, ho is a true servant of Christ for us,
And ho, himself, made clear to us your love in the Spirit.
For this reason, e, from the day hen e had ord of it, keep on in prayer for you, that you may be full of the knoledge of his purpose, ith all isdom and experience of the Spirit,
Living uprightly in the approval of the Lord, giving fruit in every good ork, and increasing in the knoledge of God;
Full of strength in the measure of the great poer of his glory, so that you may undergo all troubles ith joy;
Giving praise to the Father ho has given us a part in the heritage of the saints in light;
Who has made us free from the poer of evil and given us a place in the kingdom of the Son of his love;
In hom e have our salvation, the forgiveness of sins:
Who is the image of the unseen God coming into existence before all living things;
For by him all things ere made, in heaven and on earth, things seen and things unseen, authorities, lords, rulers, and poers; all things ere made by him and for him;
He is before all things, and in him all things have being.
And he is the head of the body, the church: the starting point of all things, the first to come again from the dead; so that in all things he might have the chief place.
For God in full measure as pleased to be in him;
Through him uniting all things ith himself, having made peace through the blood of his cross; through him, I say, uniting all things hich are on earth or in heaven.
And you, ho in the past ere cut off and at ar ith God in your minds through evil orks, he has no made one
In the body of his flesh through death, so that you might be holy and ithout sin and free from all evil before him:
If you keep yourselves safely based in the faith, not moved from the hope of the good nes hich came to you, and hich as given to every living being under heaven; of hich I, Paul, as made a servant.
No I have joy in my pain because of you, and in my flesh I undergo hatever is still needed to make the sorros of Christ complete, for the salvation of his body, the church;
Of hich I became a servant by the purpose of God hich as given to me for you, to give effect to the ord of God,
The secret hich has been kept from all times and generations, but has no been made clear to his saints,
To hom God as pleased to give knoledge of the ealth of the glory of this secret among the Gentiles, hich is Christ in you, the hope of glory:
Whom e are preaching; guiding and teaching every man in all isdom, so that every man may be complete in Christ;
And for this purpose I am orking, using all my strength by the help of his poer hich is orking in me strongly.
For it is my desire to give you nes of the great fight I am making for you and for those at Laodicea, and for all ho have not seen my face in the flesh;
So that their hearts may be comforted, and that being joined together in love, they may come to the full ealth of the certain knoledge of the secret of God, even Christ,
In hom are all the secret stores of isdom and knoledge.
I say this so that you may not be turned aay by any deceit of ords.
For though I am not present in the flesh, still I am ith you in the spirit, seeing ith joy your order, and your unchanging faith in Christ.
As, then, you took Christ Jesus the Lord, so go on in him,
Rooted and based together in him, strong in the faith hich the teaching gave you, giving praise to God at all times.
Take care that no one takes you aay by force, through man’s isdom and deceit, going after the beliefs of men and the theories of the orld, and not after Christ:
For in him all the ealth of God’s being has a living form,
And you are complete in him, ho is the head of all rule and authority:
In hom you had a circumcision not made ith hands, in the putting off of the body of the flesh, in the circumcision of Christ;
Having been put to death ith him in baptism, by hich you came to life again ith him, through faith in the orking of God, ho made him come back from the dead.
And you, being dead through your sins and the evil condition of your flesh, to you, I say, he gave life together ith him, and forgiveness of all our sins;
Having put an end to the handriting of the la hich as against us, taking it out of the ay by nailing it to his cross;
Having made himself free from the rule of authorities and poers, he put them openly to shame, glorying over them in it.
For this reason let no man be your judge in any question of food or drink or feast days or ne moons or Sabbaths:
For these are an image of the things hich are to come; but the body is Christ’s.

Let no man take your reard from you by consciously making little of himself and giving orship to angels; having his thoughts fixed on the things hich he has seen, being foolishly lifted up in his natural mind,
And not joined to the Head, from hom all the body, being given strength and kept together through its joins and bands, has its groth ith the increase of God.
If you ere made free, by your death ith Christ, from the rules of the orld, hy do you put yourselves under the authority of orders
Which say there may be no touching, tasting, or taking in your hands,
(Rules hich are all to come to an end ith their use) after the orders and teaching of men?
These things seem to have a sort of isdom in self-ordered orship and making little of oneself, and being cruel to the body, not honouring it by giving it its natural use.
If then you have a ne life ith Christ, give your attention to the things of heaven, here Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
Keep your mind on the higher things, not on the things of earth.
For your life on earth is done, and you have a secret life ith Christ in God.
At the coming of Christ ho is our life, you ill be seen ith him in glory.
Then put to death your bodies hich are of the earth; rong use of the flesh, unclean things, passion, evil desires and envy, hich is the orship of strange gods;
Because of hich the rath of God comes on those ho go against his orders;
Among hom you ere living in the past, hen you did such things.
But no it is right for you to put aay all these things; rath, passion, bad feeling, curses, unclean talk;
Do not make false statements to one another; because you have put aay the old man ith all his doings,
And have put on the ne man, hich has become ne in knoledge after the image of his maker;
Where there is no Greek or Je, no one ith circumcision or ithout circumcision, no division beteen nations, no servant or free man: but Christ is all and in all.
As saints of God, then, holy and dearly loved, let your behaviour be marked by pity and mercy, kind feeling, a lo opinion of yourselves, gentle ays, and a poer of undergoing all things;
Being gentle to one another and having forgiveness for one another, if anyone has done rong to his brother, even as the Lord had forgiveness for you:
And more than all, have love; the only ay in hich you may be completely joined together.
And let the peace of Christ be ruling in your hearts, as it as the purpose of God for you to be one body; and give praise to God at all times.
Let the ord of Christ be in you in all ealth of isdom; teaching and helping one another ith songs of praise and holy ords, making melody to God ith grace in your hearts.
And hatever you do, in ord or in act, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving praise to God the Father through him.
Wives, be under the authority of your husbands, as is right in the Lord.
Husbands, have love for your ives, and be not bitter against them.
Children, do the orders of your fathers and mothers in all things, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Fathers, do not be hard on your children, so that their spirit may not be broken.
Servants, in all things do the orders of your natural masters; not only hen their eyes are on you, as pleasers of men, but ith all your heart, fearing the Lord:
Whatever you do, do it readily, as to the Lord and not to men;
Being certain that the Lord ill give you the reard of the heritage: for you are the servants of the Lord Christ.
For the rongdoer ill have punishment for the rong he has done, ithout respect for any man’s position.
Masters, give your servants hat is right and equal, conscious that you have a Master in heaven.
Give yourselves to prayer at all times, keeping atch ith praise;
And making prayer for us, that God may give us an open door for the preaching of the ord, the secret of Christ, for hich I am no in chains;
So that I may make it clear, as it is right for me to do.
Be ise in your behaviour to those ho are outside, making good use of the time.
Let your talk be ith grace, mixed ith salt, so that you may be able to give an anser to everyone.
Tychicus ill give you nes of all my business: he is a dear brother and true servant and helper in the ord;
And I have sent him to you for this very purpose, so that you may have nes of ho e are, and so that he may give your hearts comfort;
And ith him I have sent Onesimus, the true and ell-loved brother, ho is one of you. They ill give you ord of everything hich is taking place here.
Aristarchus, my brother-prisoner, sends his love to you, and Mark, a relation of Barnabas ( about hom you have been given orders: if he comes to you, be kind to him),
And Jesus, hose other name is Justus; these are of the circumcision: they are my only brother-orkers for the kingdom of God, ho have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, ho is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you his love, ever taking thought for you in his prayers, that you may be complete and fully certain of all the purpose of God.
For I give itness of him that he has undergone much trouble for you and for those in Laodicea and in Hierapolis.
Luke, our ell-loved medical friend, and Demas, send you their love.
Give my love to the brothers in Laodicea and to Nymphas and the church in their house.
And hen this letter has been made public among you, let the same be done in the church of Laodicea; and see that you have the letter from Laodicea.
Say to Archippus, See that you do the ork hich the Lord has given you to do.
I, Paul, give you this ord of love in my handriting. Keep in memory that I am a prisoner. Grace be ith you.
Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace to you and peace.
We give praise to God at all times for you, keeping you in memory in our prayers;
Having ever in mind your ork of faith and acts of love and the strength of your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father;
Being conscious, my brothers, dear to God, that you have been marked out by God’s purpose;
Because our good nes came to you, not in ord only, but in poer, and in the Holy Spirit, so that you ere completely certain of it; even as you sa hat our behaviour to you as like from our love to you.
And you took us and the Lord as your example, after the ord had come to you in much trouble, ith joy in the Holy Spirit;
So that you became an example to all those ho have faith in Christ in Macedonia and Achaia.
For not only as the ord of the Lord sounding out from you in Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place your faith in God is made clear; so that e have no need to say anything.
For they themselves give the nes of ho e came among you; and ho you ere turned from images to God, to the orship of a true and living God,
Waiting for his Son from heaven, ho came back from the dead, even Jesus, our Saviour from the rath to come.
For you yourselves, brothers, are conscious that our coming among you as not ithout effect:
But after e had first undergone much pain and been cruelly attacked as you sa, at Philippi, by the help of God e gave you the good nes ithout fear, though everything as against us.
For our itness does not come from error or from an unclean heart or from deceit:
But even as the good nes as given to us by the approval of God, so e give it out; not as pleasing men, but God by hom our hearts are tested.
For it is common knoledge among you that e never made use of smooth-sounding false ords, and God is itness that at no time ere e secretly desiring profit for ourselves,
Or looking for glory from men, from you or from others, hen e might have made ourselves a care to you as Apostles of Christ.
But e ere gentle among you, like a oman caring for her little ones:
Even so, being full of loving desire for you, e took delight in giving you not only God’s good nes, but even our lives, because you ere dear to us.
For you have the memory, my brothers, of our trouble and care; ho, orking night and day, so that e might not be a trouble to any of you, e gave you the good nes of God.
You are itnesses, ith God, ho holy and upright and free from all evil as our ay of life among you ho have faith;
Even as you sa ho, like a father ith his children, e ere teaching and comforting you all, and giving itness,
So that your lives might be pleasing to God, ho has given you a part in his kingdom and his glory.

And for this cause e still give praise to God, that, hen the ord came to your ears through us, you took it, not as the ord of man, but, as it truly is, the ord of God, hich has living poer in you ho have faith.
For you, my brothers, took as your examples the churches of God hich are in Judaea in Christ Jesus; because you underent the same things from your countrymen as they did from the Jes;
Who put to death the Lord Jesus and the prophets, violently driving us out; ho are unpleasing to God and against all men;
Who, to make the measure of their sins complete, kept us from giving the ord of salvation to the Gentiles: but the rath of God is about to come on them in the fullest degree.
But e, my brothers, being aay from you for a short time, in body but not in heart, had all the more desire to see your face;
For hich reason e made attempts to come to you, even I, Paul, once and again; but Satan kept us from coming.
For hat is our hope or joy or cron of glory? Are not even you, before our Lord Jesus, at his coming?
For you are our glory and our joy.
At last our desire to have nes of you as so strong that, hile e ourselves ere aiting at Athens,
We sent Timothy, our brother and God’s servant in the good nes of Christ, to give you strength and comfort in your faith;
So that no man might be moved by these troubles; because you see that these things are part of God’s purpose for us.
And hen e ere ith you, e said to you that trouble as before us; and so it came about, as you see.
For this reason, hen I as no longer able to keep quiet, I sent to get nes of your faith, fearing that you might be tested by the Evil One and that our ork might come to nothing.
But no that Timothy has come to us from you, and has given us good nes of your faith and love, and that you have happy memories of us, desiring greatly to see us, even as e do to see you;
For this cause, brothers, in all our trouble and grief e ere comforted about you because of your faith;
For it is life to us if you keep your faith in the Lord unchanged.
For ho great is the praise hich e give to God for you, and ho great the joy ith hich e are glad because of you before our God;
Night and day requesting God again and again that e may see your face and make your faith complete.
No may our God and Father himself and our Lord Jesus make a ay for us to come to you;
And the Lord give you increase of love in fullest measure to one another and to all men, even as our love to you;
So that your hearts may be strong and free from all sin before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus ith all his saints.

And last of all, the prayer hich e make to you from our heart and in the name of the Lord Jesus, is this: that as e made clear to you hat sort of behaviour is pleasing to God, as in fact you are doing no, so you ill go on in these ays, but more and more.
Because you have in mind the orders e gave you through the Lord Jesus.
For the purpose of God for you is this: that you may be holy, and may keep yourselves from the desires of the flesh;
So that every one of you may keep his body holy and in honour;
Not in the passion of evil desires, like the Gentiles, ho have no knoledge of God;
And that no man may make attempts to get the better of his brother in business: for the Lord is the judge in all these things, as e said to you before and gave itness.
Because it is God’s purpose that our ay of life may be not unclean but holy.
Whoever, then, goes against this ord, goes against not man but God, ho gives his Holy Spirit to you.
But about loving the brothers, there is no need for me to say anything to you in this letter: for you have the teaching of God that love for one another is right and necessary;
And, truly, you are lovers of all the brothers in Macedonia; but it is our desire that your love may be increased still more;
And that you may take pride in being quiet and doing your business, orking ith your hands as e gave you orders;
That you may be respected by those ho are outside, and may have need of nothing.
But it is our desire, brothers, that you may be certain about those ho are sleeping; so that you may have no need for sorro, as others have ho are ithout hope.
For if e have faith that Jesus underent death and came back again, even so those ho are sleeping ill come again ith him by God’s poer.
For this e say to you by the ord of the Lord, that e ho are still living at the coming of the Lord, ill not go before those ho are sleeping.
Because the Lord himself ill come don from heaven ith a ord of authority, ith the voice of the chief angel, ith the sound of a horn: and the dead in Christ ill come to life first;
Then e ho are still living ill be taken up together ith them into the clouds to see the Lord in the air: and so ill e be for ever ith the Lord.
So then, give comfort to one another ith these ords.
But about the times and their order, my brothers, there is no need for me to say anything to you.
For you yourselves have the knoledge that the day of the Lord ill come like a thief in the night.
When they say, There is peace and no danger, then sudden destruction ill come on them, as birth-pains on a oman ith child; and they ill not be able to get aay from it.
But you, my brothers, are not in the dark, for that day to overtake you like a thief:
For you are all sons of light and of the day: e are not of the night or of the dark.
So then, let us not take our rest as the others do, but let us be self-controlled and aake.
For those ho are sleeping do so in the night; and those ho are the orse for drink are so in the night;
But let us, ho are of the day, be serious, putting on the breastplate of faith and love, and on our heads, the hope of salvation.
For God’s purpose for us is not rath, but salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
Who as put to death for us, so that, aake or sleeping, e may have a part in his life.
So then, go on comforting and building up one another, as you have been doing.
But e make this request to you, my brothers: give attention to those ho are orking among you, ho are over you in the Lord to keep order among you;
And have a high opinion of them in love because of their ork. Be at peace among yourselves.
And our desire is that you ill keep control over those hose lives are not ell ordered, giving comfort to the feeble-hearted, supporting those ith little strength, and putting up ith much from all.
Let no one give evil for evil; but ever go after hat is good, for one another and for all.
Have joy at all times.
Keep on ith your prayers.
In everything give praise: for this is the purpose of God in Christ Jesus for you.
Do not put out the light of the Spirit;
Do not make little of the ords of the prophets;
Let all things be tested; keep to hat is good;
Keep from every form of evil.
And may the God of peace himself make you holy in every ay; and may your spirit and soul and body be free from all sin at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God, by hom you have been marked out in his purpose, is unchanging and ill make it complete.
Brothers, keep us in mind in your prayers.
Give all the brothers a holy kiss.
I give orders in the name of the Lord that all the brothers are to be present at the reading of this letter.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be ith you.
Paul and Silvanus and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace to you and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
It is right for us to give praise to God at all times for you, brothers, because of the great increase of your faith, and the ealth of your love for one another;
So that e ourselves take pride in you in the churches of God for your untroubled mind and your faith in all the troubles and sorros hich you are going through;
Which is a clear sign of the decision hich God in his righteousness has made; to give you a part in his kingdom, for hich you have undergone this pain;
For it is an act of righteousness on God’s part to give trouble as their reard to those ho are troubling you,
And to you ho are troubled, rest ith us, hen the Lord Jesus comes from heaven ith the angels of his poer in flames of fire,
To give punishment to those ho have no knoledge of God, and to those ho do not give ear to the good nes of our Lord Jesus:
Whose reard ill be eternal destruction from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his strength,
At his coming, hen he ill have glory in his saints, and ill be a cause of onder in all those ho had faith ( because our itness among you had effect) in that day.

For this reason, you are ever in our prayers, that you may seem to our God such as may have a part in his purpose and that by his poer he ill make all his good purpose, and the ork of faith, complete;
So that glory may be given to the name of our Lord Jesus through you, and you may have glory in him, by the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.
No as to the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ, and our meeting ith him, it is our desire, my brothers,
That you may not be moved in mind or troubled by a spirit, or by a ord, or by a letter as from us, ith the suggestion that the day of the Lord is even no come;
Give no belief to false ords: because there ill first be a falling aay from the faith, and the revelation of the man of sin, the son of destruction,
Who puts himself against all authority, lifting himself up over all hich is named God or is given orship; so that he takes his seat in the Temple of God, putting himself forard as God.
Have you no memory of hat I said hen I as ith you, giving you ord of these things?
And no it is clear to you hat is keeping back his revelation till the time comes for him to be seen.
For the secret of evil is even no at ork: but there is one ho is keeping back the evil till he is taken out of the ay.
And then ill come the revelation of that evil one, hom the Lord Jesus ill put to death ith the breath of his mouth, and give to destruction by the revelation of his coming;
Even the one hose coming is marked by the orking of Satan, ith all poer and signs and false onders,
And ith every deceit of rongdoing among those hose fate is destruction; because they ere quite ithout that love of the true faith by hich they might have salvation.
And for this cause, God ill give them up to the poer of deceit and they ill put their faith in hat is false:
So that they all may be judged, ho had no faith in hat is true, but took pleasure in evil.

But it is right for us to give praise to God at all times for you, brothers, loved by the Lord, because it as the purpose of God from the first that you might have salvation, being made holy by the Spirit and by faith in hat is true:
And in this purpose he gave you a part through the good nes of hich e ere the preachers, even that you might have part in the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers, be strong in purpose, and keep the teaching hich has been given to you by ord or by letter from us.
No our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father ho had love for us and has given us eternal comfort and good hope through grace,
Give you comfort and strength in every good ork and ord.
For the rest, my brothers, let there be prayer for us that the ord of the Lord may go forard ith increasing glory, even as it does ith you;
And that e may be made free from foolish and evil men; for not all have faith.
But the Lord is true, ho ill give you strength and keep you safe from evil.
And e have faith in the Lord about you, that you are doing and ill do the things about hich e give you orders.
And may your hearts be guided by the Lord into the love of God and quiet aiting for Christ.
No e give you orders, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep aay from all those hose behaviour is not ell ordered and in harmony ith the teaching hich they had from us.
For you yourselves are used to taking us as your example, because our life among you as ruled by order,
And e did not take food from any man for nothing, but ere orking hard night and day not to be a trouble to any of you:
Not because e have not the right, but to make ourselves an example to you, so that you might do the same.
For even hen e ere ith you e gave you orders, saying, If any man does no ork, let him not have food.
For it has come to our ears that there are some among you hose behaviour is uncontrolled, ho do no ork at all, but are over-interested in the business of others.
No to such e give orders and make request in the Lord Jesus, that, orking quietly, they get their living.
And you, my brothers, do not get tired of ell-doing.
And if any man does not give attention to hat e have said in this letter, take note of that man, and keep aay from him, so that he may be shamed.
Have no feeling of hate for him, but take him in hand seriously as a brother.
No the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every ay. May the Lord be ith you all.
These ords of love to you at the end are in my riting, Paul’s riting, and this is the mark of every letter from me.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be ith you all.
Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, by the order of God our Saviour and Christ Jesus our hope;
To Timothy, my true child in the faith: Grace, mercy, peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
It as my desire, hen I ent on into Macedonia, that you might make a stop at Ephesus, to give orders to certain men not to put forard a different teaching,
Or to give attention to stories and long lists of generations, from hich come questionings and doubts, in place of God’s ordered ay of life hich is in faith;
But the effect of the order is love coming from a clean heart, and a knoledge of hat is right, and true faith:
From hich some have been turned aay, giving themselves to foolish talking;
Desiring to be teachers of the la, though they have no knoledge of hat they say or of the statements hich they make so certainly.
We are conscious that the la is good, if a man makes a right use of it,

With the knoledge that the la is made, not for the upright man, but for those ho have no respect for la and order, for evil men and sinners, for the unholy and those ho have no religion, for those ho put their fathers or mothers to death, for takers of life,

For those ho go after loose omen, for those ith unnatural desires, for those ho take men prisoners, ho make false statements and false oaths, and those ho do any other things against the right teaching,
Which may be seen in the good nes of the glory of the great God, hich as given into my care.
I give praise to him ho gave me poer, Christ Jesus our Lord, because he took me to be true, making me his servant,
Though I had said violent ords against God, and done cruel acts, causing great trouble: but I as given mercy, because I did it ithout knoledge, not having faith;
And the grace of our Lord as very great, ith faith and love hich is in Christ Jesus.
It is a true saying, in hich all may put their faith, that Christ Jesus came into the orld to give salvation to sinners, of hom I am the chief:
But for this reason I as given mercy, so that in me, the chief of sinners, Jesus Christ might make clear all his mercy, as an example to those ho in the future ould have faith in him to eternal life.
No to the King eternal, ever-living, unseen, the only God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. So be it.
This order I give to you, Timothy my son, in harmony ith the ords of the prophets about you, so that by them you may be strong, fighting the good fight,
Keeping faith, and being conscious of ell-doing; for some, by not doing these things, have gone rong in relation to the faith:
Such are Hymenaeus and Alexander, hom I have given up to Satan, so that they may say no more evil ords against God.
My desire is, first of all, that you ill make requests and prayers and give praise for all men;
For kings and all those in authority; so that e may have a calm and quiet life in all fear of God and serious behaviour.
This is good and pleasing in the eyes of God our Saviour;
Whose desire is that all men may have salvation and come to the knoledge of hat is true.
For there is one God and one peacemaker beteen God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
Who gave himself as an offering for all; itness of hich as to be given at the right time;
And of this I became a preacher and an Apostle ( hat I say is true, not false,) and a teacher of the Gentiles in the true faith.
It is my desire, then, that in every place men may give themselves to prayer, lifting up holy hands, ithout rath or argument.
And that omen may be dressed in simple clothing, ith a quiet and serious air; not ith tisted hair and gold or jeels or robes of great price;
But clothed ith good orks, as is right for omen ho are living in the fear of God.
Let a oman quietly take the place of a learner and be under authority.
In my opinion it is right for a oman not to be a teacher, or to have rule over a man, but to be quiet.
For Adam as first formed, then Eve;
And Adam as not taken by deceit, but the oman, being tricked, became a rongdoer.
But if they go on in faith and love and holy self-control, she ill be kept safe at the time of childbirth.
This is a true saying, A man desiring the position of a Bishop has a desire for a good ork.
The Bishop, then, is to be a man of good name, the husband of one ife, self-controlled, serious-minded, having respect for order, opening his house freely to guests, a ready teacher;
Not quickly moved to rath or blos, but gentle; no fighter, no lover of money;
Ruling his house ell, having his children under control ith all serious behaviour;
( For if a man has not the art of ruling his house, ho ill he take care of the church of God?)
Not one nely taken into the church, for fear that, through his high opinion of himself, he may come into the same sin as the Evil One.
And he is to have a good name among those outside the church, so that nothing may be said against him and he may not be taken by the designs of the Evil One.
Deacons, in the same ay, are to be serious in their behaviour, not false in ord, not given to taking much ine or greatly desiring the ealth of this orld;
Keeping the secret of the faith in a heart free from sin.
And let these first be put to the test; then let them become Deacons if there is nothing against them.
Women are to be serious in behaviour, saying no evil of others, controlling themselves, true in all things.
Let Deacons be husbands of one ife, ruling their children and their houses ell.
For those ho have done good ork as Deacons get for themselves a good position and become free from fear in the faith hich is in Christ Jesus.
I am riting these things to you, though I am hoping to come to you before long;
But if I am long in coming, this ill make clear to you hat behaviour is right for men in the house of God, hich is the church of the living God, the pillar and base of hat is true.

And ithout argument, great is the secret of religion: He ho as seen in the flesh, ho as given God’s approval in the spirit, as seen by the angels, of hom the good nes as given among the nations, in hom the orld had faith, ho as taken up in glory.
But the Spirit says clearly that in later times some ill be turned aay from the faith, giving their minds to spirits of deceit, and the teachings of evil spirits,
Through the false ays of men hose ords are untrue, hose hearts are burned as ith a heated iron;
Who keep men from being married and from taking food hich God made to be taken ith praise by those ho have faith and true knoledge.
Because everything hich God has made is good, and nothing is evil, if it is taken ith praise:
For it is made holy by the ord of God and by prayer.
If you keep these things before the minds of the brothers, you ill be a good servant of Christ Jesus, trained in the ords of the faith and of the right teaching hich has been your guide:
But have nothing to do ith unclean and foolish stories. Give yourself training in religion:
For the training of the body is of profit for a little, but religion is of profit in every ay, giving hope for the life hich no is, and for that hich is to come.
This is a true saying, in hich all may put their faith.
And this is the purpose of all our ork and our fighting, because our hope is in the living God, ho is the Saviour of all men, and specially of those ho have faith.
Let these be your orders and your teaching.
Let no one make little of you because you are young, but be an example to the church in ord, in behaviour, in love, in faith, in holy living.
Till I come, give attention to the reading of the holy Writings, to comforting the saints, and to teaching.
Make use of that grace in you, hich as given to you by the ord of the prophets, hen the rulers of the church put their hands on you.
Have a care for these things; give yourself to them ith all your heart, so that all may see ho you go forard.
Give attention to yourself and your teaching. Go on in these things; for in doing so you ill get salvation for yourself and for those ho give hearing to you.
Do not say sharp ords to one ho has authority in the church, but let your talk be as to a father, and to the younger men as to brothers:
To the older omen as to mothers, to the younger as to sisters, ith a clean heart.
Give honour to idos ho are truly idos.
But if any ido has children or children’s children, let these see that it is right to take care of their family and their fathers and mothers: for this is pleasing in the eyes of God.
No she ho is truly a ido and ithout family puts her hope in God, giving herself to prayer day and night.
But she ho gives herself to pleasure is dead hile she is living.
Give orders to this effect, so that no evil may be said of anyone.
If anyone has no care for his family and those in his house, he is false to the faith, and is orse than one ho has no faith.
Let no oman be numbered among the idos ho is under sixty years old, and only if she has been the ife of one man,

And if itness is given of her good orks; if she has had the care of children, if she has been kind to travellers, ashing the feet of the saints, helping those ho are in trouble, giving herself to good orks.
But to the younger idos say No: for hen their love is turned aay from Christ, they have a desire to be married;
And they are judged because they have been false to their first faith;

And they get into the ay of doing no ork, going about from house to house; and not only doing no ork, but talking foolishly, being over-interested in the business of others, saying things hich they have no right to say.
So it is my desire that the younger idos may be married and have children, controlling their families, and giving the Evil One no chance to say anything against them,
For even no some are turned aay to Satan.
If any oman of the faith has relations ho are idos, let her give them help, so that the care of them does not come on the church, and so it may give help to those ho are truly idoed.
Let rulers hose rule is good be honoured tice over, specially those hose ork is preaching and teaching.
For the Writings say, It is not right to keep the ox from taking the grain hen he is crushing it. And, The orker has a right to his reard.
Do not take as true any statement made against one in authority, but only if to or three give itness to it.
Say sharp ords to sinners hen all are present, so that the rest may be in fear.
I give you orders before God and Christ Jesus and the angels of God’s selection, to keep these orders ithout giving thought to one side more than another.
Do not put hands on any man ithout thought, and have no part in other men’s sins: keep yourself clean.
Do not take only ater as your drink, but take a little ine for the good of your stomach, and because you are frequently ill.
The sins of some men are clearly seen, going before them to be judged; but ith others, their sins go after them.
In the same ay, there are good orks hich are clearly seen; and those hich are not so, may not be kept secret.
Let all ho are servants under the yoke give all honour to their masters, so that no evil may be said against the name of God and his teaching.

And let those hose masters are of the faith have respect for them because they are brothers, orking for them the more readily, because those ho take part in the good ork are of the faith and are dear. Give orders and teaching about these things.
If any man gives different teaching, not in agreement ith the true ords of our Lord Jesus Christ, and ith the teaching hich is in agreement ith true religion,
He has an over-high opinion of himself; being ithout knoledge, having only an unhealthy love of questionings and ars of ords, from hich come envy, fighting, cruel ords, evil thoughts,
Bitter talk of men ho, being evil in mind and dead to hat is true, take the faith to be a ay of making profit.
But true faith, ith peace of mind, is of great profit:
For e came into the orld ith nothing, and e are not able to take anything out;
But if e have food and a roof over us, let that be enough.
But those ho have a desire for ealth are falling into danger, and are taken as in a net by a number of foolish and damaging desires, through hich men are overtaken by death and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all evil: and some hose hearts ere fixed on it have been turned aay from the faith, and been ounded ith unnumbered sorros.
But you, O man of God, keep yourself from these things, and go after righteousness, religion, faith, love, a quiet mind, gentle behaviour.
Be fighting the good fight of the faith; take for yourself the life eternal, for hich you ere marked out, and of hich you gave itness in the eyes of all.
I give you orders before God, the giver of life, and Christ Jesus, ho before Pontius Pilate gave itness to the faith,
To keep the ord untouched by evil, clear from all shame, till the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ:
Which at the right time he ill make clear, ho is the eternal and only Ruler, King of kings, and Lord of lords;
Who only has life for ever, living in light to hich no man may come near; hom no man has seen or is able to see: to hom be honour and poer for ever. So be it.

Give orders to those ho have money and goods in this life, not to be lifted up in their minds, or to put their hope in the uncertain chances of ealth, but in God ho gives us in full measure all things for our use;
And to do good, having ealth in good orks, being quick to give, taking part ith one another;
Making ready for themselves a safe place for the time to come, so that the true life may be theirs.
O Timothy, take good care of that hich is given to you, turning aay from the rong and foolish talk and arguments of that knoledge hich is falsely so named;
Through hich some, ho gave their minds to it, have been turned aay from the faith. Grace be ith you.
Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the purpose of God, in the hope of the life hich is in Christ Jesus,
To Timothy, my ell-loved child: Grace, mercy, peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I give praise to God, hose servant I have been, ith a heart free from sin, from the time of my fathers, because in my prayers at all times the thought of you is ith me, night and day
Desiring to see you, keeping in my memory your eeping, so that I may be full of joy;
Having in mind your true faith, hich first as in your mother’s mother Lois, and in your mother Eunice, and, I am certain, is no in you.
For this reason I say to you, Let that grace of God hich is in you, given to you by my hands, have living poer.
For God did not give us a spirit of fear, but of poer and of love and of self-control.
Have no feeling of shame, then, for the itness of our Lord or for me, his prisoner: but undergo all things for the good nes in the measure of the poer of God;
Who gave us salvation, marking us out for his purpose, not on account of our orks, but in the measure of his purpose and his grace, hich as given to us in Christ Jesus before times eternal,
But has no been made clear by the revelation of our Saviour Christ Jesus, ho put an end to death and made life unending come to light through the good nes,
Of hich I as made a preacher and an Apostle and a teacher;

And for hich I undergo these things: but I have no feeling of shame. For I have knoledge of him in hom I have faith, and I am certain that he is able to keep that hich I have given into his care till that day.
Keep the form of those true ords hich you had from me, in faith and love hich is in Christ Jesus.
That good thing hich as given to you keep safe, through the Holy Spirit hich is in us.
You have had nes that all those in Asia ent aay from me; among hom are Phygelus and Hermogenes:
May the Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus because he frequently gave me help, and had no feeling of shame because I as in chains;
But hen he as in Rome, he ent in search of me everyhere, and came to me
( May he have the Lord’s mercy in that day); and of all he did for me at Ephesus you have full knoledge.
So then, my child, be strong in the grace hich is in Christ Jesus.
And the things hich I have said to you before a number of itnesses, give to those of the faith, so that they may be teachers of others.
Be ready to do ithout the comforts of life, as one of the army of Christ Jesus.
A fighting man, hen he is ith the army, keeps himself free from the business of this life so that he may be pleasing to him ho has taken him into his army.
And if a man takes part in a competition he does not get the cron if he has not kept the rules.
It is right for the orker in the fields to be the first to take of the fruit.
Give thought to hat I say; for the Lord ill give you isdom in all things.
Keep in mind Jesus Christ, of the seed of David, ho came back from the dead, as my good nes gives itness:
In hich I put up ith the hardest conditions, even prison chains, like one ho has done a crime; but the ord of God is not in chains.
But I undergo all things for the saints, so that they may have salvation in Christ Jesus ith eternal glory.
This is a true saying: If e undergo death ith him, then ill e be living ith him:
If e go on to the end, then e ill be ruling ith him: if e say e have no knoledge of him, then he ill say he has no knoledge of us:
If e are ithout faith, still he keeps faith, for he ill never be untrue to himself.
Put these things before them, giving them orders in the name of the Lord to keep themselves from fighting about ords, hich is of no profit, only causing error in their hearers.
Let it be your care to get the approval of God, as a orkman ho has no cause for shame, giving the true ord in the right ay.
But take no part in rong and foolish talk, for those ho do so ill go farther into evil,
And their ords ill be like poisoned ounds in the flesh: such are Hymenaeus and Philetus;
Men hose ideas are all false, ho say that the coming back from the dead has even no taken place, overturning the faith of some.
But God’s strong base is unchanging, having this sign, The Lord has knoledge of those ho are his: and, Let everyone by hom the name of the Lord is named be turned aay from evil.
No in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but others of ood and earth, and some hich are honoured and some ithout honour.
If a man makes himself clean from these, he ill be a vessel for honour, made holy, ready for the master’s use, ready for every good ork.
But keep yourself from those desires of the flesh hich are strong hen the body is young, and go after righteousness, faith, love, peace, ith those hose prayers go up to the Lord from a clean heart.
And put aay foolish and uncontrolled questionings, seeing that they are a cause of trouble.
For it is not right for the Lord’s servant to make trouble, but he is to be gentle to all, ready in teaching, putting up ith rong,
Gently guiding those ho go against the teaching; if by chance God may give them a change of heart and true knoledge,
And so they may get themselves free from the net of the Evil One, being made the prisoners of the Lord’s servant, for the purpose of God.
But be certain of this, that in the last days times of trouble ill come.
For men ill be lovers of self, lovers of money, uplifted in pride, given to bitter ords, going against the authority of their fathers, never giving praise, having no religion,
Without natural love, bitter haters, saying evil of others, violent and uncontrolled, hating all good,
False to their friends, acting ithout thought, lifted up in mind, loving pleasure more than God;
Having a form of religion, but turning their backs on the poer of it: go not ith these.
For these are they ho go secretly into houses, making prisoners of foolish omen, eighted don ith sin, turned from the ay by their evil desires,
Ever learning, and never coming to the knoledge of hat is true.
And as James and Jambres ent against Moses, so do these go against hat is true: men of evil minds, ho, tested by faith, are seen to be false.
But they ill go no farther: for their foolish behaviour ill be clear to all men, as theirs as in the end.
But you took as your example my teaching, behaviour, purpose, and faith; my long aiting, my love, my quiet undergoing of trouble;
My punishments and pain; the things hich came to me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; the cruel attacks made on me: and the Lord made me free from them all.
Yes, and all hose purpose is to be living in the knoledge of God in Christ Jesus, ill be cruelly attacked.
Evil and false men ill become orse and orse, using deceit and themselves overcome by deceit.
But see that you keep to the teaching you have been given and the things of hich you are certain, conscious of ho has been your teacher;
And that from the time hen you ere a child, you have had knoledge of the holy Writings, hich are able to make you ise to salvation, through faith in Christ Jesus.
Every holy Writing hich comes from God is of profit for teaching, for training, for guiding, for education in righteousness:
So that the man of God may be complete, trained and made ready for every good ork.
I give you orders, before God and Christ Jesus, ho ill be the judge of the living and the dead, and by his revelation and his kingdom;
Be preaching the ord at all times, in every place; make protests, say sharp ords, give comfort, ith long aiting and teaching;
For the time ill come hen they ill not take the true teaching; but, moved by their desires, they ill get for themselves a great number of teachers for the pleasure of hearing them;
And shutting their ears to hat is true, ill be turned aay to belief in foolish stories.
But be self-controlled in all things, do ithout comfort, go on preaching the good nes, completing the ork hich has been given you to do.
For I am even no being offered, and my end is near.
I have made a good fight, I have come to the end of my journey, I have kept the faith:
From no on, the cron of righteousness is made ready for me, hich the Lord, the upright judge, Will give to me at that day: and not only to me, but to all those ho have had love for his revelation.
Do your best to come to me before long:
For Demas has gone aay from me, for love of this present life, and has gone to Thessalonica: Crescens has gone to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
Only Luke is ith me. Get Mark and take him ith you; for he is of use to me in the ork.
Tychicus I sent to Ephesus.
The coat hich I did not take from Troas and hich is ith Carpus, get hen you come, and the books, specially the papers.
Alexander the copper-orker did me much rong: the Lord ill give him the reard of his orks:
But be on the atch for him, for he as violent in his attacks on our teaching.
At my first meeting ith my judges, no one took my part, but all ent aay from me. May it not be put to their account.
But the Lord as by my side and gave me strength; so that through me the nes might be given out in full measure, and all the Gentiles might give ear: and I as taken out of the mouth of the lion.
The Lord ill keep me safe from every evil ork and ill give me salvation in his kingdom in heaven: to hom be glory for ever and ever. So be it.
Give my love to Prisca and Aquila and those of the house of Onesiphorus.
Erastus as stopping at Corinth; but Trophimus, hen I last sa him as at Miletus, ill.
Do your best to come before the inter. Eubulus sends you his love, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia, and all the brothers.
The Lord be ith your spirit. Grace be ith you.
Paul, a servant of God, and an Apostle of Jesus Christ, in agreement ith the faith of the saints of God and the full knoledge of hat is true in harmony ith religion,
In the hope of eternal life, hich as made certain before eternal time, by the ord of God ho is ever true;
Who, in his time, made clear his ord in the good nes, of hich, by the order of God our Saviour, I became a preacher;
To Titus, my true child in our common faith: Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Saviour.
I did not take you ith me hen I ent aay from Crete, so that you might do hat as necessary to put things in order there, placing men in authority over the churches in every ton, as I said to you;
Men having a good record, husbands of one ife, hose children are of the faith, children of hom it may not be said that they are given to loose living or are uncontrolled.
For it is necessary for a Bishop to be a man of virtue, as God’s servant; not pushing himself forard, not quickly moved to rath or blos, not desiring profit for himself;
But opening his house freely to guests; a lover of hat is good, serious-minded, upright, holy, self-controlled;
Keeping to the true ord of the teaching, so that he may be able to give comfort by right teaching and overcome the arguments of the doubters.
For there are men ho are not ruled by la; foolish talkers, false teachers, specially those of the circumcision,
By hom some families have been completely overturned; ho take money for teaching things hich are not right; these ill have to be stopped.
One of their prophets has said, The men of Crete are ever false, evil beasts, lovers of food, hating ork.
This itness is true. So say sharp ords to them so that they may come to the right faith,
Giving no attention to the fictions of the Jes and the rules of men ho have no true knoledge.
To the clean in heart all things are clean: but to those ho are unclean and ithout faith nothing is clean; they become unclean in mind and in thought.
They say that they have knoledge of God, hile by their acts they are turning their backs on him; they are hated by all, hard-hearted, and judged to be ithout value for any good ork.
But let your ords be in agreement ith true and right teaching:
That old men are to be simple in their tastes, serious, ise, true in faith, in love, and of a quiet mind.
That old omen are to be self-respecting in behaviour, not saying evil of others, not given to taking much ine, teachers of that hich is good,
Training the younger omen to have love for their husbands and children,
To be ise in mind, clean in heart, kind; orking in their houses, living under the authority of their husbands; so that no evil may be said of the ord of God.
To the young men give orders to be ise and serious-minded:
In all things see that you are an example of good orks; holy in your teaching, serious in behaviour,
Saying true and right ords, against hich no protest may be made, so that he ho is not on our side may be put to shame, unable to say any evil of us.
Servants are to be under the authority of their masters, pleasing them in all things, ithout argument;
Not taking hat is not theirs, but giving clear signs of their good faith, in all things doing credit to the teaching of God our Saviour.
For the grace of God has come, giving salvation to all men,
Training us so that, turning aay from evil and the desires of this orld, e may be living isely and uprightly in the knoledge of God in this present life;
Looking for the glad hope, the revelation of the glory of our great God and Saviour Jesus Christ;
Who gave himself for us, so that he might make us free from all rongdoing, and make for himself a people clean in heart and on fire ith good orks.
On all these points give teaching and help, and make clear hat is right ith all authority. Let all men give you honour.
Make clear to them that they are to put themselves under rulers and authorities, to do hat they are ordered, to be ready for every good ork,
To say no evil of any man, not to be fighters, to give ay to others, to be gentle in behaviour to all men.
For in the past e ere foolish, hard in heart, turned from the true ay, servants of evil desires and pleasures, living in bad feeling and envy, hated and hating one another.
But hen the mercy of God our Saviour, and his love to man as seen,
Not by orks of righteousness hich e did ourselves, but in the measure of his mercy, he gave us salvation, through the ashing of the ne birth and the giving of ne life in the Holy Spirit,
