Which he gave us freely through Jesus Christ our Saviour;
So that, having been given righteousness through grace, e might have a part in the heritage, the hope of eternal life.

This is a true saying; and it is my desire that you may give certain itness about these things, so that those ho have had faith in God may give attention to good orks. These things are good and of profit to men;
But have nothing to do ith foolish questionings, and lists of generations, and fights and arguments about the la; for they are of no profit and foolish.
A man hose opinions are not those of the church, after a first and second protest, is to be kept out of your society;
Clearly he is in error and a sinner, being self-judged.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis: for it is my purpose to be there for the inter.
Send Zenas, the man of la, and Apollos on their journey ith all care, so that they may be in need of nothing.
And let our people go on ith good orks for necessary purposes, so that they may not be ithout fruit.
All ho are ith me send you their love. Give our love to our friends in the faith. Grace be ith you all.
Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon, our dear helper in the faith,
And to Apphia, our sister, and to Archippus, our brother in God’s army, and to the church in your house:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I give praise to God at all times and make prayer for you,
Hearing of the love and the faith hich you have to the Lord Jesus and to all the saints;
That the faith hich you have in common ith them may be orking ith poer, in the knoledge of every good thing in you, for Christ.
For I had great joy and comfort in your love, because the hearts of the saints have been made strong again through you, brother.
And so, though I might, in the name of Christ, give you orders to do hat is right,
Still, because of love, in place of an order, I make a request to you, I, Paul, an old man and no a prisoner of Christ Jesus:
My request is for my child Onesimus, the child of my chains,
Who in the past as of no profit to you, but no is of profit to you and to me:
Whom I have sent back to you, him ho is my very heart:
Though my desire as to keep him ith me, to be my servant in the chains of the good nes, in your place:
But ithout your approval I ould do nothing; so that your good orks might not be forced, but done freely from your heart.
For it is possible that for this reason he as parted from you for a time, so that you might have him for ever;
No longer as a servant, but more than a servant, a brother, very dear to me specially, but much more to you, in the flesh as ell as in the Lord.
If then you take me to be your friend and brother, take him in as myself.
If he has done you any rong or is in debt to you for anything, put it to my account.
I, Paul, riting this myself, say, I ill make payment to you: and I do not say to you that you are in debt to me even for your life.
So brother, let me have joy of you in the Lord: give ne life to my heart in Christ.
Being certain that you ill do my desire, I am riting to you, in the knoledge that you ill do even more than I say.
And make a room ready for me; for I am hoping that through your prayers I ill be given to you.
Epaphras, my brother-prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you his love;
And so do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my brother-orkers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be ith your spirit. So be it.
In times past the ord of God came to our fathers through the prophets, in different parts and in different ays;
But no, at the end of these days, it has come to us through his Son, to hom he has given all things for a heritage, and through hom he made the order of the generations;

Who, being the outshining of his glory, the true image of his substance, supporting all things by the ord of his poer, having given himself as an offering making clean from sins, took his seat at the right hand of God in heaven;
Having become by so much better than the angels, as the name hich is his heritage is more noble than theirs.
To hich of the angels did God say at any time, You are my Son, this day I have given you being? or, I ill be his Father, and he ill be my Son?
And again, hen he is sending his only Son into the orld, he says, Let all the angels of God give him orship.
And of the angels he says, Who makes his angels inds, and his servants flames of fire:
But of the Son he says, Your seat of poer, O God, is for ever and ever; and the rod of your kingdom is a rod of righteousness.
You have been a lover of righteousness and a hater of evil; and so God, your God, has put the oil of joy on your head more than on the heads of those ho are ith you.
You, Lord, at the first did put the earth on its base, and the heavens are the orks of your hands:
They ill come to their end; but you are for ever; they ill become old as a robe;
They ill be rolled up like a cloth, even like a robe, and they ill be changed: but you are the same and your years ill have no end.
But of hich of the angels has he said at any time, Take your seat at my right hand till I put all those ho are against you under your feet?
Are they not all helping spirits, ho are sent out as servants to those hose heritage ill be salvation?
For this reason there is the more need for us to give attention to the things hich have come to our ears, for fear that by chance e might be slipping aay.
Because if the ord hich came through the angels as fixed, and in the past every evil act against God’s orders as given its full punishment;

What ill come on us, if e do not give our minds to such a great salvation? a salvation of hich our fathers first had knoledge through the ords of the Lord, and hich as made certain to us by those to hom his ords came;
And God as a itness ith them, by signs and onders, and by more than natural poers, and by his distribution of the Holy Spirit at his pleasure.
For he did not make the angels rulers over the orld to come, of hich I am riting.
But a certain riter has given his itness, saying, What is man, that you keep him in mind? hat is the son of man, that you take him into account?
You made him a little loer than the angels; you gave him a cron of glory and honour, and made him ruler over all the orks of your hands:
You put all things under his feet. For in making man the ruler over all things, God did not put anything outside his authority; though e do not see everything under him no.
But e see him ho as made a little loer than the angels, even Jesus, croned ith glory and honour, because he let himself be put to death so that by the grace of God he might undergo death for all men.
Because it as right for him, for hom and through hom all things have being, in guiding his sons to glory, to make the captain of their salvation complete through pain.
For he ho makes holy and those ho are made holy are all of one family; and for this reason it is no shame for him to give them the name of brothers,
Saying, I ill give the knoledge of your name to my brothers, I ill make a song of praise to you before the church.
And again he says, I ill put my faith in him. And again, See, I am here, and the children hich God has given to me.
And because the children are flesh and blood, he took a body himself and became like them; so that by his death he might put an end to him ho had the poer of death, that is to say, the Evil One;
And let those ho all their lives ere in chains because of their fear of death, go free.
For, truly, he does not take on the life of angels, but that of the seed of Abraham.

Because of this it as necessary for him to be made like his brothers in every ay, so that he might be a high priest full of mercy and keeping faith in everything to do ith God, making offerings for the sins of the people.
For having been put to the test himself, he is able to give help to others hen they are tested.
For this reason, holy brothers, marked out to have a part in heaven, give thought to Jesus the representative and high priest of our faith;
Who kept faith ith God ho gave him his place, even as Moses did in all his house.
And it as right for this man to have more honour than Moses, even as the builder of a house has more honour than the house.
For every house has a builder; but the builder of all things is God.
And Moses certainly kept faith as a servant, in all his house, and as a itness of those things hich ere to be said later;
But Christ as a son, over his house; hose house are e, if e keep our hearts fixed in the glad and certain hope till the end.
And so, as the Holy Spirit says, Today if you let his voice come to your ears,
Be not hard of heart, as hen you made me angry, on the day of testing in the aste land,
When your fathers put me to the test, and sa my orks for forty years.
So that I as angry ith this generation, and I said, Their hearts are in error at all times, and they have no knoledge of my ays;
And being angry I made an oath, saying, They may not come into my rest.
My brothers, take care that there is not by chance in any one of you an evil heart ithout belief, turning aay from the living God:
But give comfort to one another every day as long as it is still Today; so that no one among you may be made hard by the deceit of sin:
For if e keep the substance of the faith hich e had at the start, even till the end, e have a part ith Christ;
As it is said, Today if you ill let his voice come to your ears, be not hard of heart, as hen you made him angry.
Who made him angry hen his voice came to them? as it not all those ho came out of Egypt ith Moses?
And ith hom as he angry for forty years? as it not ith those ho did evil, ho came to their deaths in the aste land?
And to hom did he make an oath that they might not come into his rest? as it not to those ho ent against his orders?
So e see that they ere not able to go in because they had no belief.
Let us then, though e still have God’s ord that e may come into his rest, go in fear that some of you may be unable to do so.
And, truly, the good nes came to us, even as it did to them; but the hearing of the ord did them no good, because they ere not united in faith ith the true hearers.

For those of us ho have belief come into his rest; even as he has said, As I said in my oath hen I as angry, They may not come into my rest: though the orks ere done from the time of the making of the orld.
For in one place he has said of the seventh day, And God had rest from all his orks on the seventh day;
And in the same place he says again, They ill not come into my rest.
So that as it is clear that some have to go in, and that the first hearers of the good nes ere not able to go in because they ent against God’s orders,
After a long time, again naming a certain day, he says in David, Today ( as he had said before), Today if you ill let his voice come to your ears, be not hard of heart,
For if Joshua had given them rest, he ould not have said anything about another day.
So that there is still a Sabbath-keeping for the people of God.
For the man ho comes into his rest has had rest from his orks, as God did from his.
Because of this, let us have a strong desire to come into that rest, and let no one go after the example of those ho ent against God’s orders.

For the ord of God is living and full of poer, and is sharper than any to-edged sord, cutting through and making a division even of the soul and the spirit, the bones and the muscles, and quick to see the thoughts and purposes of the heart.
And there is nothing made hich is not completely clear to him; there is nothing covered, but all things are open to the eyes of him ith hom e have to do.
Having then a great high priest, ho has made his ay through the heavens, even Jesus the Son of God, let us be strong in our faith.
For e have not a high priest ho is not able to be touched by the feelings of our feeble flesh; but e have one ho has been tested in all points as e ourselves are tested, but ithout sin.
Then let us come near to the seat of grace ithout fear, so that mercy may be given to us, and e may get grace for our help in time of need.
Every high priest ho is taken from among men is given his position to take care of the interests of men in those things hich have to do ith God, so that he may make offerings for sins.
He is able to have feeling for those ho have no knoledge and for those ho are andering from the true ay, because he himself is feeble;
And being feeble, he has to make sin-offerings for himself as ell as for the people.
And no man ho is not given authority by God, as Aaron as, takes this honour for himself.
In the same ay Christ did not take for himself the glory of being made a high priest, but as given it by him ho said, You are my Son, this day I have given you being:
As he says in another place, You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.
Who in the days of his flesh, having sent up prayers and requests ith strong crying and eeping to him ho as able to give him salvation from death, had his prayer ansered because of his fear of God.
And though he as a Son, through the pain hich he underent, the knoledge came to him of hat it as to be under God’s orders;
And hen he had been made complete, he became the giver of eternal salvation to all those ho are under his orders;
Being named by God a high priest of the order of Melchizedek.
Of hom e have much to say hich it is hard to make clear, because you are slo of hearing.

And though by this time it ould be right for you to be teachers, you still have need of someone to give you teaching about the first simple rules of God’s revelation; you have become like babies ho have need of milk, and not of solid food.
For everyone ho takes milk is ithout experience of the ord of righteousness: he is a child.
But solid food is for men of full groth, even for those hose senses are trained by use to see hat is good and hat is evil.
For this reason let us go on from the first things about Christ to full groth; not building again that on hich it is based, that is, the turning of the heart from dead orks, and faith in God,
The teaching of baptisms, and of the putting on of hands, and of the future life of the dead, and of the judging on the last day.
No e ill do this, if God lets us.
As for those ho at one time sa the light, tasting the good things from heaven, and having their part in the Holy Spirit,
With knoledge of the good ord of God, and of the poers of the coming time,
And then let themselves be turned aay, it is not possible for their hearts to be made ne a second time; because they themselves put the Son of God on the cross again, openly shaming him.
For a land, drinking in the frequent rain and producing good plants for those for hom it is orked, has a blessing from God:
But if it sends up thorns and evil plants, it is of no use and is ready to be cursed; its only end is to be burned.
But, my loved ones, though e say this, e are certain that you have better things in you, things hich go ith salvation;
For God is true, and ill not put aay from him the memory of your ork and of your love for his name, in the help hich you gave and still give to the saints.
And it is our desire that you may all keep the same high purpose in certain hope to the end:
So that you may not be slo in heart, but may take as your example those to hom God has given their heritage, because of their faith and their long aiting.
For hen God made his oath to Abraham, because there as no greater oath, he made it by himself,
Saying, Be certain that I ill give you my blessing, and make your numbers very great.
And so, hen he had been aiting calmly for a long time, God’s ord to him as put into effect.
For men at all times make their oaths by hat is greater; and any argument is ended by the decision of the oath.
So that hen it as God’s desire to make it specially clear to those ho by his ord ere to have the heritage, that his purpose as fixed, he made it more certain ith an oath;
So that e, ho have gone in flight from danger to the hope hich has been put before us, may have a strong comfort in to unchanging things, in hich it is not possible for God to be false;
And this hope is like a strong band for our souls, fixed and certain, and going in to that hich is inside the veil;
Where Jesus has gone before us, as a high priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.
For this Melchizedek, the king of Salem, a priest of the Most High God, ho gave Abraham his blessing, meeting him hen he came back after putting the kings to death,
And to hom Abraham gave a tenth part of everything hich he had, being first named King of righteousness, and then in addition, King of Salem, that is to say, King of peace;
Being ithout father or mother, or family, having no birth or end to his life, being made like the Son of God, is a priest for ever.
No see ho great this man as, to hom our father Abraham gave a tenth part of hat he had got in the fight.

And it is true that by the la, those of the sons of Levi ho have the position of priests may take a tenth part of the people’s goods; that is to say, they take it from their brothers though these are the sons of Abraham.
But this man, ho as not of their family, took the tenth from Abraham, and gave a blessing to him to hom God had given his undertaking.
But there is no doubt that the less gets his blessing from the greater.
No at the present time, men over hom death has poer take the tenth; but then it as taken by one of hom it is itnessed that he is living.
And e may say that in Abraham, even Levi, ho has a right to take the tenth part, gave it;
Because he as still in his father’s body hen Melchizedek came to him.

No if it as possible for things to be made complete through the priests of the house of Levi ( for the la as given to the people in connection ith them), hat need as there for another priest ho as of the order of Melchizedek and not of the order of Aaron?
Because if the priests are changed, it is necessary to make a change in the la.
For he of hom these things are said comes of another tribe, of hich no man has ever made offerings at the altar.
Because it is clear that our Lord comes out of Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests from that tribe.
And this is even more clear if a second priest has come up ho is like Melchizedek,
That is to say, not made by a la based on the flesh, but by the poer of a life ithout end:
For it has been itnessed of him, You are a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.
So the la hich ent before is put on one side, because it as feeble and ithout profit.
( Because the la made nothing complete), and in its place there is a better hope, through hich e come near to God.
And as this is not ithout the taking of an oath
( For those ere made priests ithout an oath, but this one as made a priest ith an oath by him ho says of him, The Lord gave his oath, hich he ill not take back, that you are a priest for ever);
By so much is it a better agreement hich e have through Jesus.
And it is true that there have been a great number of those priests, because death does not let them go on for ever;
But this priest, because his life goes on for ever, is unchanging.
So that he is fully able to be the saviour of all ho come to God through him, because he is ever living to make prayer to God for them.
It as right for us to have such a high priest, one ho is holy and ithout evil, doing no rong, having no part ith sinners, and made higher than the heavens:
Who has no need to make offerings for sins every day, like those high priests, first for himself, and then for the people; because he did this once and for ever hen he made an offering of himself.
The la makes high priests of men ho are feeble; but the ord of the oath, hich as made after the la, gives that position to a Son, in hom all good is for ever complete.
No of the things e are saying this is the chief point: We have such a high priest, ho has taken his place at the right hand of God’s high seat of glory in heaven,
As a servant of the holy things and of the true Tent, hich as put up by God, not by man.
No every high priest is given authority to take to God the things hich are given and to make offerings; so that it is necessary for this man, like them, to have something for an offering.
If he had been on earth he ould not have been a priest at all, because there are other priests ho make the offerings ordered by the la;

Being servants of that hich is a copy and an image of the things in heaven, as Moses, hen he as about to make the Tent, had special orders from God: for, See, he said, that you make everything like the design hich you sa in the mountain.
But no his position as priest is higher. because through him God has made a better agreement ith man, based on the giving of better things.
For if that first agreement had been as good as possible, there ould have been no place for a second.
For, protesting against them, he says, See, the days are coming hen I ill make a ne agreement ith the house of Israel, and ith the house of Judah;

Not like the agreement hich I made ith their fathers hen I took them by the hand, to be their guide out of the land of Egypt; for they did not keep the agreement ith me, and I gave them up, says the Lord.
For this is the agreement hich I ill make ith the people of Israel after those days: I ill put my las into their minds, riting them in their hearts: and I ill be their God, and they ill be my people:
And there ill be no need for every man to be teaching his brother, or his neighbour, saying, This is the knoledge of the Lord: for they ill all have knoledge of me, great and small.
And I ill have mercy on their evil-doing, and I ill not keep their sins in mind.
When he says, A ne agreement, he has made the first agreement old. But anything hich is getting old and past use ill not be seen much longer.
No the first agreement had its rules of orship, and a holy order.
For the first Tent as made ready, having in it the vessels for the lights and the table and the ordering of the bread; and this is named the holy place.
And inside the second veil as the place hich is named the Holy of holies;

Having a vessel of gold in it for burning perfumes, and the ark of the agreement, hich as covered ith gold and hich had in it a pot made of gold for the manna, and Aaron’s rod hich put out buds, and the stones ith the riting of the agreement;
And over it ere the inged ones of glory ith their ings covering the mercy-seat; about hich it is not possible no to say anything in detail.
No hile these things ere in existence, the priests ent into the first Tent at all times, for prayer and the making of offerings.
But only the high priest ent into the second, once a year, not ithout making an offering of blood for himself and for the errors of the people:
The Holy Spirit itnessing by this that the ay into the holy place had not at that time been made open, hile the first Tent as still in being;
And this is an image of the present time; hen the offerings hich are given are not able to make the heart of the orshipper completely clean,
Because they are only rules of the flesh, of meats and drinks and ashings, hich have their place till the time comes hen things ill be put right.
But no Christ has come as the high priest of the good things of the future, through this greater and better Tent, not made ith hands, that is to say, not of this orld,
And has gone once and for ever into the holy place, having got eternal salvation, not through the blood of goats and young oxen, but through his blood.
For if the blood of goats and oxen, and the dust from the burning of a young co, being put on the unclean, make the flesh clean:
Ho much more ill the blood of Christ, ho, being ithout sin, made an offering of himself to God through the Holy Spirit, make your hearts clean from dead orks to be servants of the living God?

And for this cause it is through him that a ne agreement has come into being, so that after the errors under the first agreement had been taken aay by his death, the ord of God might have effect for those ho ere marked out for an eternal heritage.
Because here there is a testament, there has to be the death of the man ho made it.
For a testament has effect after death; for hat poer has it hile the man ho made it is living?
So that even the first agreement as not made ithout blood.
For hen Moses had given all the rules of the la to the people, he took the blood of goats and young oxen, ith ater and red ool and hyssop, and put it on the book itself and on all the people,
Saying, This blood is the sign of the agreement hich God has made ith you.
And the blood as put on the Tent and all the holy vessels in the same ay.
And by the la almost all things are made clean ith blood, and ithout blood there is no forgiveness.
For this cause it as necessary to make the copies of the things in heaven clean ith these offerings; but the things themselves are made clean ith better offerings than these.
For Christ did not go into a holy place hich had been made by men’s hands as the copy of the true one; but he ent into heaven itself, and no takes his place before the face of God for us.
And he did not have to make an offering of himself again and again, as the high priest goes into the holy place every year ith blood hich is not his;
For then he ould have undergone a number of deaths from the time of the making of the orld: but no he has come to us at the end of the old order, to put aay sin by the offering of himself.
And because by God’s la death comes to men once, and after that they are judged;
So Christ, having at his first coming taken on himself the sins of men, ill be seen a second time, ithout sin, by those ho are aiting for him, for their salvation.

For the la, being only a poor copy of the future good things, and not the true image of those things, is never able to make the people ho come to the altar every year ith the same offerings completely clean.
For if this had been possible, ould there not have been an end of those offerings, because the orshippers ould have been made completely clean and ould have been no longer conscious of sins?
But year by year there is a memory of sins in those offerings.
Because it is not possible for the blood of oxen and goats to take aay sins.
So that hen he comes into the orld, he says, You had no desire for offerings, but you made a body ready for me;
You had no joy in burned offerings or in offerings for sin.
Then I said, See, I have come to do your pleasure, O God ( as it is said of me in the roll of the book).
After saying, You had no desire for offerings, for burned offerings or offerings for sin ( hich are made by the la) and you had no pleasure in them,
Then he said, See, I have come to do your pleasure. He took aay the old order, so that he might put the ne order in its place.
By that pleasure e have been made holy, by the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once and for ever.
And every priest takes his place at the altar day by day, doing hat is necessary, and making again and again the same offerings hich are never able to take aay sins.
But hen Jesus had made one offering for sins for ever, he took his place at the right hand of God;
And has been aiting there from that time, till all ho are against him are made a foot-rest for his feet.
Because by one offering he has made complete for ever those ho are made holy.
And the Holy Spirit is a itness for us: for after he had said,
This is the agreement hich I ill make ith them after those days, says the Lord; I ill put my las in their hearts, riting them in their minds; he said,
And I ill keep no more memory of their sins and of their evil-doings.
No here there is forgiveness of these, there is no more offering for sin.
So then, my brothers, being able to go into the holy place ithout fear, because of the blood of Jesus,
By the ne and living ay hich he made open for us through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
And having a great priest over the house of God,
Let us go in ith true hearts, in certain faith, having our hearts made free from the sense of sin and our bodies ashed ith clean ater:
Let us keep the itness of our hope strong and unshaking, for he is true ho has given his ord:
And let us be moving one another at all times to love and good orks;
Not giving up our meetings, as is the ay of some, but keeping one another strong in faith; and all the more because you see the day coming near.
For if e do evil on purpose after e have had the knoledge of hat is true, there is no more offering for sins,
But only a great fear of being judged, and of the fire of rath hich ill be the destruction of the haters of God.
A man ho has gone against the la of Moses is put to death ithout pity on the ord of to or three itnesses:

But ill not the man by hom the Son of God has been crushed under foot, and the blood of the agreement ith hich he as ashed clean has been taken as an unholy thing, and ho has had no respect for the Spirit of grace, be judged bad enough for a very much orse punishment?
For e have had experience of him ho says, Punishment is mine, I ill give reard. And again, The Lord ill be judge of his people.
We may ell go in fear of falling into the hands of the living God.
But give thought to the days after you had seen the light, hen you ent through a great ar of troubles;
In part, in being attacked by angry ords and cruel acts, before the eyes of everyone, and in part, in being united ith those ho ere attacked in this ay.
For you had pity on those ho ere in prison, and had joy in the loss of your property, in the knoledge that you still had a better property and one hich you ould keep for ever.
So do not give up your hope hich ill be greatly rearded.
For, having done hat as right in God’s eyes, you have need of aiting before his ord has effect for you.
In a very little time he ho is coming ill come; he ill not be slo.
But the upright man ill be living by his faith; and if he goes back, my soul ill have no pleasure in him.
But e are not of those ho go back to destruction; but of those ho have faith even to the salvation of the soul.
No faith is the substance of things hoped for, and the sign that the things not seen are true.
For by it our fathers had God’s approval.
By faith it is clear to us that the order of events as fixed by the ord of God, so that hat is seen has not been made from things hich only seem to be.

By faith Abel made a better offering to God than Cain, and he had itness through it of his righteousness, God giving his approval of his offering: and his voice still comes to us through it though he is dead.
By faith Enoch as taken up to heaven so that he did not see death; he as seen no longer, for God took him aay: for before he as taken, itness had been given that he as ell-pleasing to God:

And ithout faith it is not possible to be ell-pleasing to him, for it is necessary for anyone ho comes to God to have the belief that God is, and that he is a rearder of all those ho make a serious search for him.

By faith Noah, being moved by the fear of God, made ready an ark for the salvation of his family, because God had given him nes of things hich ere not seen at the time; and through it the orld as judged by him, and he got for his heritage the righteousness hich is by faith.
By faith Abraham did as God said hen he as ordered to go out into a place hich as to be given to him as a heritage, and ent out ithout knoledge of here he as going.
By faith he as a anderer in the land of the agreement, as in a strange land, living in tents ith Isaac and Jacob, ho had a part ith him in the same heritage:
For he as looking for the strong ton, hose builder and maker is God.
And by faith Sarah herself had poer to give birth, hen she as very old, because she had faith in him ho gave his ord;
So that from one man, ho as near to death, came children in number as the stars in heaven, or as the sand by the seaside, hich may not be numbered.
All these came to their end in faith, not having had the heritage; but having seen it ith delight far aay, they gave itness that they ere anderers and not of the earth.
For those ho say such things make it clear that they are searching for a country for themselves.
And truly if they had kept in mind the country from hich they ent out, they ould have had chances of turning back.
But no their desire is for a better country, that is to say, for one in heaven; and so it is no shame to God to be named their God; for he has made ready a ton for them.
By faith Abraham made an offering of Isaac, hen he as tested: and he ith hom the agreement had been made gave up as an offering the only son of his body,
Of hom it had been said, From Isaac ill your seed take their name:
Judging that God as able to give life even to the dead; and because of this he did get him back as if from death.
By faith Isaac, blessing Jacob and Esau, gave nes of things to come.
By faith Jacob gave a blessing to the to sons of Joseph, hen he as near to death; and gave God orship, supported by his stick.
By faith Joseph, hen his end as near, said that the children of Israel ould go out of Egypt; and gave orders about his bones.
By faith Moses as kept secretly by his father and mother for three months after his birth, because they sa that he as a fair child; and they had no fear of the king’s orders.
By faith Moses, hen he became a man, had no desire to be named the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;
Feeling that it as better to undergo pain ith the people of God, than for a short time to have a taste of the pleasures of sin;
Judging a part in the shame of Christ to be better than all the ealth of Egypt; for he as looking forard to his reard.
By faith he ent out of Egypt, not being turned from his purpose by fear of the rath of the king; for he kept on his ay, as seeing him ho is unseen.
By faith he kept the Passover, and put the sign of the blood on the houses, so that the angel of destruction might not put their oldest sons to death.
By faith they ent through the Red Sea as if it had been dry land, though the Egyptians ere overcome by the ater hen they made an attempt to do the same.
By faith the alls of Jericho came don, after they had been circled for seven days.
By faith Rahab, the loose oman, as not put to death ith those ho had gone against God’s orders, because she had taken into her house in peace those sent to see the land.
What more am I to say? For there ould not be time to give the stories of Gideon, Barak, Samson, and Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets:
Who through faith overcame kingdoms, did righteousness, got their reard, kept the mouths of lions shut,
Put out the poer of fire, got safely aay from the edge of the sord, ere made strong hen they had been feeble, became full of poer in ar, and put to flight the armies of the nations.
Women had their dead given back to them living; others let themselves be cruelly attacked, having no desire to go free, so that they might have a better life to come;
And others ere tested by being laughed at or by blos, and even ith chains and prisons:
They ere stoned, they ere cut up ith knives, they ere tested, they ere put to death ith the sord, they ent about in sheepskins and in goatskins; being poor and in pain and cruelly attacked,
Wandering in aste places and in mountains and in holes in the rocks; for hom the orld as not good enough.
And not one of these got the good things of the agreement, though they all had a good record through faith,
Because God had kept some better thing for us, so that it as not possible for them to become complete ithout us.
For this reason, as e are circled by so great a cloud of itnesses, putting off every eight, and the sin into hich e come so readily, let us keep on running in the ay hich is marked out for us,

Having our eyes fixed on Jesus, the guide and end of our faith, ho ent through the pains of the cross, not caring for the shame, because of the joy hich as before him, and ho has no taken his place at the right hand of God’s seat of poer.
Give thought to him ho has undergone so much of the hate of sinners against himself, so that you may not be tired and feeble of purpose.
Till no you have not given your blood in your fight against sin:
And you have not kept in mind the ord hich says to you as to sons, My son, do not make little of the Lord’s punishment, and do not give up hope hen you are judged by him;
For the Lord sends punishment on his loved ones; everyone hom he takes as his son has experience of his rod.
It is for your training that you undergo these things; God is acting to you as a father does to his sons; for hat son does not have punishment from his father?
But if you have not that punishment of hich e all have our part, then you are not true sons, but children of shame.
And again, if the fathers of our flesh gave us punishment and had our respect, ho much more ill e be under the authority of the Father of spirits, and have life?
For they truly gave us punishment for a short time, as it seemed good to them; but he does it for our profit, so that e may become holy as he is.
At the time all punishment seems to be pain and not joy: but after, those ho have been trained by it get from it the peace-giving fruit of righteousness.
For this cause let the hands hich are hanging don be lifted up, and let the feeble knees be made strong,
And make straight roads for your feet, so that the feeble may not be turned out of the ay, but may be made strong.
Let your desire be for peace ith all men, and to be made holy, ithout hich no man may see the Lord;

Looking ith care to see that no man among you in his behaviour comes short of the grace of God; for fear that some bitter root may come up to be a trouble to you, and that some of you may be made unclean by it;
And that there may not be any evil liver, or any man ithout respect for God, like Esau, ho let his birthright go for a plate of food.

For you have knoledge that even long after, hen he as desiring the blessing for his heritage, he as turned aay, though he made his request frequently and ith eeping; because the past might not be changed.
You have not come to a mountain hich may be touched, and is burning ith fire, and to a black cloud, and a dark smoke, and a violent ind,
And to the sound of a horn, and the voice of ords, the hearers of hich made request that not a ord more might be said to them:
For the order hich said, If the mountain is touched even by a beast, the beast is to be stoned, seemed hard to them;
And the vision as so overpoering that even Moses said, I am shaking and full of fear.
But you have come to the mountain of Zion, to the place of the living God, to the Jerusalem hich is in heaven, and to an army of angels hich may not be numbered,
To the great meeting and church of the first of those ho are named in heaven, and to God the judge of all, and to the spirits of good men made complete,
And to Jesus by hom the ne agreement has been made beteen God and man, and to the sign of the blood hich says better things than Abel’s blood.

See that you give ear to his voice hich comes to you. For if those hose ears ere shut to the voice hich came to them on earth did not go free from punishment, hat chance have e of going free if e give no attention to him hose voice comes from heaven?
Whose voice as the cause of the shaking of the earth; but no he has made an oath, saying, There ill be still one more shaking, not only of the earth, but of heaven.

And the ords, Still one more, make it clear that there ill be a taking aay of those things hich are shaking, as of things hich are made, so that there may be only those things of hich no shaking is possible.
If then, e have a kingdom hich ill never be moved, let us have grace, so that e may give God such orship as is pleasing to him ith fear and respect:
For our God is an all-burning fire.
Go on loving your brothers in the faith.
Take care to keep open house: because in this ay some have had angels as their guests, ithout being conscious of it.
Keep in mind those ho are in chains, as if you ere chained ith them, and those ho are in trouble, as being yourselves in the body.
Let married life be honoured among all of you and not made unclean; for men untrue in married life ill be judged by God.
Be free from the love of money and pleased ith the things hich you have; for he himself has said, I ill be ith you at all times.
So that e say ith a good heart, The Lord is my helper; I ill have no fear: hat is man able to do to me?
Keep in mind those ho ere over you, and ho gave you the ord of God; seeing the outcome of their ay of life, let your faith be like theirs.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and for ever.
Do not be turned aay by different strange teachings, because it is good for your hearts to be made strong by grace, and not by meats, hich ere of no profit to those ho took so much trouble over them.
We have an altar from hich those priests ho are servants in the Tent may not take food.
For the bodies of the beasts hose blood is taken into the holy place by the high priest as an offering for sin are burned outside the circle of the tents.
For this reason Jesus as put to death outside the alls, so that he might make the people holy by his blood.
Let us then go out to him outside the circle of the tents, taking his shame on ourselves.
For here e have no fixed resting-place, but our search is for the one hich is to come.
Let us then make offerings of praise to God at all times through him, that is to say, the fruit of lips giving itness to his name.
But go on doing good and giving to others, because God is ell-pleased ith such offerings.

Give ear to those ho are rulers over you, and do as they say: for they keep atch over your souls, ready to give an account of them; let them be able to do this ith joy and not ith grief, because that ould be of no profit to you.
Make prayers for us, for e are certain that our hearts are free from the sense of sin, desiring the right ay of life in all things.
I make this request more strongly, in the hope of coming back to you more quickly.
No may the God of peace, ho made that great keeper of his flock, even our Lord Jesus, come back from the dead through the blood of the eternal agreement,
Make you full of every good ork and ready to do all his desires, orking in us hatever is pleasing in his eyes through Jesus Christ; and may the glory be given to him for ever and ever. So be it.
But, brothers, take kindly the ords hich I have said for your profit; for I have not sent you a long letter.
Our brother Timothy has been let out of prison; and if he comes here in a short time, he and I ill come to you together.
Give ords of love from me to those ho are rulers over you, and to all the saints. Those ho are in Italy send you their love.
May grace be ith you all.
James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, sends ords of love to the telve tribes of the Jes living in all parts of the earth.
Let it be all joy to you, my brothers, hen you undergo tests of every sort;
Because you have the knoledge that the testing of your faith gives you the poer of going on in hope;
But let this poer have its full effect, so that you may be made complete, needing nothing.
But if any man among you is ithout isdom, let him make his request to God, ho gives freely to all ithout an unkind ord, and it ill be given to him.
Let him make his request in faith, doubting nothing; for he ho has doubt in his heart is like the aves of the sea, hich are troubled by the driving of the ind.
Let it not seem to such a man that he ill get anything from the Lord;
For there is a division in his mind, and he is uncertain in all his ays.
But let the brother of lo position be glad that he is lifted up;
But the man of ealth, that he is made lo; because like the floer of the grass he ill come to his end.
For hen the sun comes up ith its burning heat, the grass gets dry and the grace of its form is gone ith the falling floer; so the man of ealth comes to nothing in his ays.
There is a blessing on the man ho undergoes testing; because, if he has God’s approval, he ill be given the cron of life, hich the Lord has said he ill give to those ho have love for him.
Let no man say hen he is tested, I am tested by God; for it is not possible for God to be tested by evil, and he himself puts no man to such a test:
But every man is tested hen he is turned out of the right ay by the attraction of his desire.
Then hen its time comes, desire gives birth to sin; and sin, hen it is of full groth, gives birth to death.
Do not be turned from the right ay, dear brothers.
Every good and true thing is given to us from heaven, coming from the Father of lights, ith hom there is no change or any shade made by turning.
Of his purpose he gave us being, by his true ord, so that e might be, in a sense, the first-fruits of all the things hich he had made.
You have knoledge of this, dear brothers. But let every man be quick in hearing, slo in ords, slo to get angry;
For the righteousness of God does not come about by the rath of man.
For this reason, putting aay all dirty behaviour and the overeight of evil, take into your souls ithout pride the ord hich, being planted there, is able to give you salvation.
But be doers of the ord, and not only hearers of it, blinding yourselves ith false ideas.
Because if any man is a hearer of the ord and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a glass;
For after looking at himself he goes aay, and in a short time he has no memory of hat he as like.
But he ho goes on looking into the true la hich makes him free, being not a hearer ithout memory but a doer putting it into effect, this man ill have a blessing on his acts.
If a man seems to have religion and has no control over his tongue but lets himself be tricked by hat is false, this man’s religion is of no value.

The religion hich is holy and free from evil in the eyes of our God and Father is this: to take care of children ho have no fathers and of idos ho are in trouble, and to keep oneself untouched by the orld.
My brothers, if you have the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ of glory, do not take a man’s position into account.
For if a man comes into your Synagogue in fair clothing and ith a gold ring, and a poor man comes in ith dirty clothing,
And you do honour to the man in fair clothing and say, Come here and take this good place; and you say to the poor man, Take up your position there, or be seated at my feet;
Is there not a division in your minds? have you not become judges ith evil thoughts?

Give ear, my dear brothers; are not those ho are poor in the things of this orld marked out by God to have faith as their ealth, and for their heritage the kingdom hich he has said he ill give to those ho have love for him?
But you have put the poor man to shame. Are not the men of ealth rulers over you? do they not take you by force before their judges?
Do they not say evil of the holy name hich as given to you?
But if you keep the greatest la of all, as it is given in the holy Writings, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself, you do ell:
But if you take a man’s position into account, you do evil, and are judged as evil-doers by the la.
For anyone ho keeps all the la, but makes a slip in one point, is judged to have gone against it all.
For he ho said, Do not be untrue in married life, is the same ho said, Put no man to death. No if you are not untrue in married life, but you put a man to death, the la is broken.
Let your ords and your acts be those of men ho are to be judged by the la hich makes free.
For the man ho has had no mercy ill be judged ithout mercy, but mercy takes pride in overcoming judging.
What use is it, my brothers, for a man to say that he has faith, if he does nothing? ill such a faith give him salvation?
If a brother or a sister is ithout clothing and in need of the day’s food,
And one of you says to them, Go in peace, be arm and full of food; but you do not give them the things of hich their bodies have need, hat profit is there in this?
Even so faith ithout orks is dead.
But a man may say, You have faith and I have orks; let me see your faith ithout your orks, and I ill make my faith clear to you by my orks.
You have the belief that God is one, and you do ell: the evil spirits have the same belief, shaking ith fear.
Do you not see, O foolish man, that faith ithout orks is of no use?
Was not the righteousness of Abraham our father judged by his orks, hen he made an offering of Isaac his son on the altar?
You see that his faith as helping his orks and as made complete by them;
And the holy Writings ere put into effect hich said, And Abraham had faith in God and it as put to his account as righteousness; and he as named the friend of God.
You see that a man’s righteousness is judged by his orks and not by his faith only.
And in the same ay, as not the righteousness of Rahab, the loose oman, judged by her orks, hen she took into her house those ho ere sent and let them go out by another ay?
For as the body ithout the spirit is dead even so faith ithout orks is dead.
Do not all be teachers, my brothers, because e teachers ill be judged more hardly than others.
For e all go rong in a number of things. If a man never makes a slip in his talk, then he is a complete man and able to keep all his body in control.
No if e put bits of iron into horses’ mouths so that they may be guided by us, e have complete control of their bodies.
And again ships, though they are so great and are moved by violent inds, are turned by a very small guiding-blade, at the impulse of the man ho is using it.
Even so the tongue is a small part of the body, but it takes credit for great things. Ho much ood may be lighted by a very little fire!
And the tongue is a fire; it is the poer of evil placed in our bodies, making all the body unclean, putting the heel of life on fire, and getting its fire from hell.
For every sort of beast and bird and every living thing on earth and in the sea has been controlled by man and is under his authority;
But the tongue may not be controlled by man; it is an unresting evil, it is full of the poison of death.
With it e give praise to our Lord and Father; and ith it e put a curse on men ho are made in God’s image.
Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing. My brothers, it is not right for these things to be so.
Does the fountain send from the same outlet seet and bitter ater?
Is a fig-tree able to give us olives, my brothers, or do e get figs from a vine, or seet ater from the salt sea?
Who has isdom and good sense among you? let him make his orks clear by a life of gentle isdom.
But if you have bitter envy in your heart and the desire to get the better of others, have no pride in this, talking falsely against hat is true.
This isdom is not from heaven, but is of the earth and the flesh and the Evil One.
For here envy is, and the desire to get the better of others, there is no order, but every sort of evil-doing.
But the isdom hich is from heaven is first holy, then gentle, readily giving ay in argument, full of peace and mercy and good orks, not doubting, not seeming other than it is.
And the fruit of righteousness is planted in peace for those ho make peace.
What is the cause of ars and fighting among you? is it not in your desires hich are at ar in your bodies?

You are burning ith desire, and have not your desire, so you put men to death; you are full of envy, and you are not able to get your desire, so you are fighting and making ar; you have not your desire, because you do not make request for it.
You make your request but you do not get it, because your request has been rongly made, desiring the thing only so that you may make use of it for your pleasure.
O you ho are false to God, do you not see that the friends of this orld are not God’s friends? Every man desiring to be a friend of this orld makes himself a hater of God.
Or does it seem to you that it is for nothing that the holy Writings say, The spirit hich God put into our hearts has a strong desire for us?
But he gives more grace. So that the Writings say, God is against the men of pride, but he gives grace to those ho make themselves lo before him.
For this cause be ruled by God; but make ar on the Evil One and he ill be put to flight before you.
Come near to God and he ill come near to you. Make your hands clean, you evil-doers; put aay deceit from your hearts, you false in mind.
Be troubled, ith sorro and eeping; let your laughing be turned to sorro and your joy to grief.
Make yourselves lo in the eyes of the Lord and you ill be lifted up by him.

Do not say evil against one another, my brothers. He ho says evil against his brother or makes himself his brother’s judge, says evil against the la and is judging the la: and in judging the la you become, not a doer of the la but a judge.
There is only one judge and la-giver, even he ho has the poer of salvation and of destruction; but ho are you to be your neighbour’s judge?
Ho foolish it is to say, Today or tomorro e ill go into this ton, and be there for a year and do business there and get ealth:
When you are not certain hat ill take place tomorro. What is your life? It is a mist, hich is seen for a little time and then is gone.
But the right thing to say ould be, If it is the Lord’s pleasure and if e are still living, e ill do this and that.
But no you go on glorying in your pride: and all such glorying is evil.
The man ho has knoledge of ho to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin.
Come no, you men of ealth, give yourselves to eeping and crying because of the bitter troubles hich are coming to you.
Your ealth is unclean and insects have made holes in your clothing.
Your gold and your silver are asted and their aste ill be a itness against you, burning into your flesh. You have put by your store in the last days.

See, the money hich you falsely kept back from the orkers cutting the grass in your field, is crying out against you; and the cries of those ho took in your grain have come to the ears of the Lord of armies.
You have been living delicately on earth and have taken your pleasure; you have made your hearts fat for a day of destruction.
You have given your decision against the upright man and have put him to death. He puts up no fight against you.
Go on aiting calmly, my brothers, till the coming of the Lord, like the farmer aiting for the good fruit of the earth till the early and late rains have come.
Be as calm in your aiting; let your hearts be strong: because the coming of the Lord is near.
Say no hard things against one another, brothers, so that you ill not be judged; see, the judge is aiting at the doors.
Take as an example of pain nobly undergone and of strength in trouble, the prophets ho gave to men the ords of the Lord.
We say that those men ho have gone through pain are happy: you have the story of Job and the troubles through hich he ent and have seen that the Lord as full of pity and mercy in the end.
But most of all, my brothers, do not take oaths, not by the heaven, or by the earth, or by any other thing: but let your Yes be Yes, and your No be No: so that you may not be judged.
Is anyone among you in trouble? let him say prayers. Is anyone glad? let him make a song of praise.
Is anyone among you ill? let him send for the rulers of the church; and let them say prayers over him, putting oil on him in the name of the Lord.
And by the prayer of faith the man ho is ill ill be made ell, and he ill be lifted up by the Lord, and for any sin hich he has done he ill have forgiveness.
So then, make a statement of your sins to one another, and say prayers for one another so that you may be made ell. The prayer of a good man is full of poer in its orking.
Elijah as a man of flesh and blood as e are, and he made a strong prayer that there might be no rain; and there as no rain on the earth for three years and six months.
And he made another prayer, and the heaven sent don rain and the earth gave her fruit.
My brothers, if one of you has gone out of the ay of the true faith and another has made him see his error,
Be certain that he through hom a sinner has been turned from the error of his ay, keeps a soul from death and is the cause of forgiveness for sins ithout number.
Peter, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, to the saints ho are living in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
Who, through the purpose of God, have been made holy by the Spirit, disciples of Jesus, made clean by his blood: May you have grace and peace in full measure.
Praise be to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, ho through his great mercy has given us a ne birth and a living hope by the coming again of Jesus Christ from the dead,
And a heritage fair, holy and for ever ne, aiting in heaven for you,
Who, by the poer of God are kept, through faith, for that salvation, hich ill be seen at the last day.
You have cause for great joy in this, though it may have been necessary for you to be troubled for a little time, being tested in all sorts of ays,

So that the true metal of your faith, being of much greater value than gold ( hich, though it comes to an end, is tested by fire), may come to light in praise and glory and honour, at the revelation of Jesus Christ:
To hom your love is given, though you have not seen him; and the faith hich you have in him, though you do not see him no, gives you joy greater than ords and full of glory:
For so you have the true end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.
For the prophets ho gave the nes of the grace hich ould come to you, made search ith all care for knoledge of this salvation;
Attempting to see hat sort of time the Spirit of Christ hich as in them as pointing to, hen it gave itness to the pains hich Christ ould undergo and the glories hich ould come after them.

And it as made clear to those prophets that they ere God’s servants not for themselves but for you, to give you ord of the things hich have no come to your ears from the preachers of the good nes through the Holy Spirit sent don from heaven; things hich even angels have a desire to see.
So make your minds ready, and keep on the atch, hoping ith all your poer for the grace hich is to come to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;
Like children ruled by God, do not go back to the old desires of the time hen you ere ithout knoledge:
But be holy in every detail of your lives, as he, hose servants you are, is holy;
Because it has been said in the Writings, You are to be holy, for I am holy.
And if you give the name of Father to him ho, judging every man by his acts, has no respect for a man’s position, then go in fear hile you are on this earth:
Being conscious that you have been made free from that foolish ay of life hich as your heritage from your fathers, not through a payment of things like silver or gold hich come to destruction,
But through holy blood, like that of a clean and unmarked lamb, even the blood of Christ:
Who as marked out by God before the making of the orld, but as caused to be seen in these last times for you,
Who through him have faith in God ho took him up again from the dead into glory; so that your faith and hope might be in God.
And as you have made your souls clean, being ruled by hat is true, and loving one another ithout deceit, see that your love is arm and from the heart:
Because you have had a ne birth, not from the seed of man, but from eternal seed, through the ord of a living and unchanging God.
For it is said, All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the floer of the grass. The grass becomes dry and the floer dead:
But the ord of the Lord is eternal. And this is the ord of the good nes hich as given to you.
So putting aay all rongdoing, and all tricks and deceits and envies and evil talk,
Be full of desire for the true milk of the ord, as babies at their mothers’ breasts, so that you may go on to salvation;
If you have had a taste of the grace of the Lord:
To hom you come, as to a living stone, not honoured by men, but of great and special value to God;
You, as living stones, are being made into a house of the spirit, a holy order of priests, making those offerings of the spirit hich are pleasing to God through Jesus Christ.
Because it is said in the Writings, See, I am placing a keystone in Zion, of great and special value; and the man ho has faith in him ill not be put to shame.
And the value is for you ho have faith; but it is said for those ithout faith, The very stone hich the builders put on one side, as made the chief stone of the building;
And, A stone of falling, a rock of trouble; the ord is the cause of their fall, because they go against it, and this as the purpose of God.

But you are a special people, a holy nation, priests and kings, a people given up completely to God, so that you may make clear the virtues of him ho took you out of the dark into the light of heaven.
In the past you ere not a people, but no you are the people of God; then there as no mercy for you, but no mercy has been given to you.
My loved ones, I make this request ith all my heart, that, as those for hom this orld is a strange country, you ill keep yourselves from the desires of the flesh hich make ar against the soul;
Being of good behaviour among the Gentiles; so that though they say no that you are evil-doers, they may see your good orks and give glory to God hen he comes to be their judge.
Keep all the las of men because of the Lord; those of the king, ho is over all,
And those of the rulers ho are sent by him for the punishment of evil-doers and for the praise of those ho do ell.
Because it is God’s pleasure that foolish and narro-minded men may be put to shame by your good behaviour:
As those ho are free, not using your free position as a cover for rongdoing, but living as the servants of God;
Have respect for all, loving the brothers, fearing God, honouring the king.
Servants, take orders from your masters ith all respect; not only if they are good and gentle, but even if they are bad-humoured.
For it is a sign of grace if a man, desiring to do right in the eyes of God, undergoes pain as punishment for something hich he has not done.
What credit is it if, hen you have done evil, you take your punishment quietly? but if you are given punishment for doing right, and take it quietly, this is pleasing to God.
This is God’s purpose for you: because Jesus himself underent punishment for you, giving you an example, so that you might go in his footsteps:
Who did no evil, and there as no deceit in his mouth:
To sharp ords he gave no sharp anser; hen he as undergoing pain, no angry ord came from his lips; but he put himself into the hands of the judge of righteousness:
He took our sins on himself, giving his body to be nailed on the tree, so that e, being dead to sin, might have a ne life in righteousness, and by his ounds e have been made ell.
Because, like sheep, you had gone out of the ay; but no you have come back to him ho keeps atch over your souls.
Wives, be ruled by your husbands; so that even if some of them give no attention to the ord, their hearts may be changed by the behaviour of their ives,
When they see your holy behaviour in the fear of God.
Do not let your ornaments be those of the body such as dressing of the hair, or putting on of jeels of gold or fair clothing;
But let them be those of the unseen man of the heart, the ever-shining ornament of a gentle and quiet spirit, hich is of great price in the eyes of God.
And these ere the ornaments of the holy omen of the past, hose hope as in God, being ruled by their husbands:
As Sarah as ruled by Abraham, naming him lord; hose children you are if you do ell, and are not put in fear by any danger.

And you husbands, give thought to your ay of life ith your ives, giving honour to the oman ho is the feebler vessel, but ho has an equal part in the heritage of the grace of life; so that you may not be kept from prayer.
Last of all, see that you are all in agreement; feeling for one another, loving one another like brothers, full of pity, ithout pride:
Not giving back evil for evil, or curse for curse, but in place of cursing, blessing; because this is the purpose of God for you that you may have a heritage of blessing.
For it is said, Let the man ho has a love of life, desiring to see good days, keep his tongue from evil and his lips from ords of deceit:
And let him be turned from evil and do good; searching for peace and going after it ith all his heart.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the upright, and his ears are open to their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against those ho do evil.
Who ill do you any damage if you keep your minds fixed on hat is good?
But you are happy if you undergo pain because of righteousness; have no part in their fear and do not be troubled;
But give honour to Christ in your hearts as your Lord; and be ready at any time hen you are questioned about the hope hich is in you, to give an anser in the fear of the Lord and ithout pride;
Being conscious that you have done no rong; so that those ho say evil things about your good ay of life as Christians may be put to shame.
Because if it is God’s purpose for you to undergo pain, it is better to do so for ell-doing than for evil-doing.

Because Christ once ent through pain for sins, the upright one taking the place of sinners, so that through him e might come back to God; being put to death in the flesh, but given life in the Spirit;
By hom he ent to the spirits in prison, preaching to those

Who, in the days of Noah, ent against God’s orders; but God in his mercy kept back the punishment, hile Noah got ready the ark, in hich a small number, that is to say eight persons, got salvation through ater:

And baptism, of hich this is an image, no gives you salvation, not by ashing clean the flesh, but by making you free from the sense of sin before God, through the coming again of Jesus Christ from the dead;
Who has gone into heaven, and is at the right hand of God, angels and authorities and poers having been put under his rule.
So that as Jesus as put to death in the flesh, do you yourselves be of the same mind; for the death of the flesh puts an end to sin;
So that you may give the rest of your lives in the flesh, not to the desires of men, but to the purpose of God.

Because for long enough, in times past, e have been living after the ay of the Gentiles, given up to the desires of the flesh, to drinking and feasting and loose behaviour and unclean orship of images;
And they are ondering that you no longer go ith them in this violent asting of life, and are saying evil things of you:
But they ill have to give an account of themselves to him ho is ready to be the judge of the living and the dead.
For this as the reason hy the good nes of Jesus as given even to the dead, so that they might be judged as men in the flesh, but might be living before God in the spirit.
But the end of all things is near: so be serious in your behaviour and keep on the atch ith prayer;
And most of all be arm in your love for one another; because in love there is forgiveness for sins ithout number:
Keep open house for all ith a glad heart;
Making distribution among one another of hatever has been given to you, like true servants of the unmeasured grace of God;

If anyone has anything to say, let it be as the ords of God; if anyone has the desire to be the servant of others, let him do it in the strength hich is given by God; so that in all things God may have the glory through Jesus Christ, hose are the glory and the poer for ever.
Dear brothers, do not be surprised, as if it as something strange, if your faith is tested as by fire:
But be glad that you are given a part in the pains of Christ; so that at the revelation of his glory you may have great joy.
If men say evil things of you because of the name of Christ, happy are you; for the Spirit of glory and of God is resting on you.
Let no one among you undergo punishment as a taker of life, or as a thief, or as an evil-doer, or as one ho is over-interested in other men’s business;
But if he undergoes punishment as a Christian, that is no shame to him; let him give glory to God in this name.
For the time has come for the judging, starting ith the church of God; but if it makes a start ith us, hat ill be the end of those ho are not under the rule of God?
And if it is hard for even the good man to get salvation, hat chance has the man ithout religion or the sinner?
For this reason let those ho by the purpose of God undergo punishment, keep on in ell-doing and put their souls into the safe hands of their Maker.
I ho am myself one of the rulers of the church, and a itness of the death of Christ, having my part in the coming glory, send this serious request to the chief men among you:
Keep atch over the flock of God hich is in your care, using your authority, not as forced to do so, but gladly; and not for unclean profit but ith a ready mind;
Not as lords over God’s heritage, but making yourselves examples to the flock.
And at the coming of the chief Keeper of the sheep, you ill be given the eternal cron of glory.

And in the same ay, let the younger men be ruled by the older ones. Let all of you put aay pride and make yourselves ready to be servants: for God is a hater of pride, but he gives grace to those ho make themselves lo.
For this cause make yourselves lo under the strong hand of God, so that hen the time comes you may be lifted up;
Putting all your troubles on him, for he takes care of you.
Be serious and keep atch; the Evil One, ho is against you, goes about like a lion ith open mouth in search of food;
Do not give ay to him but be strong in your faith, in the knoledge that your brothers ho are in the orld undergo the same troubles.

And after you have undergone pain for a little time, the God of all grace ho has given you a part in his eternal glory through Christ Jesus, ill himself give you strength and support, and make you complete in every good thing;
His is the poer for ever. So be it.
I have sent you this short letter by Silvanus, a true brother, in my opinion; comforting you and itnessing that this is the true grace of God; keep to it.
She ho is in Babylon, ho has a part ith you in the purpose of God, sends you her love; and so does my son Mark.
Give one another the kiss of love. Peace be to you all in Christ.
Simon Peter, a servant and Apostle of Jesus Christ, to those ho ith us have a part in the same holy faith in the righteousness of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ:
May grace and peace ever be increasing in you, in the knoledge of God and of Jesus our Lord;
Because by his poer he has given us everything necessary for life and righteousness, through the knoledge of him ho has been our guide by his glory and virtue;

And through this he has given us the hope of great reards highly to be valued; so that by them e might have our part in God’s being, and be made free from the destruction hich is in the orld through the desires of the flesh.
So, for this very cause, take every care; joining virtue to faith, and knoledge to virtue,
And self-control to knoledge, and a quiet mind to self-control, and fear of God to a quiet mind,
And love of the brothers to fear of God, and to love of the brothers, love itself.
For if you have these things in good measure, they ill make you fertile and full of fruit in the knoledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For the man ho has not these things is blind, seeing only hat is near, having no memory of ho he as made clean from his old sins.
For this reason, my brothers, take all the more care to make your selection and approval certain; for if you do these things you ill never have a fall:
For so the ay ill be open to you into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
For this reason I ill be ready at all times to keep your memory of these things aake, though you have the knoledge of them no and are ell based in your present faith.
And it seems right to me, as long as I am in this tent of flesh, to keep your minds aake by orking on your memory;
For I am conscious that in a short time I ill have to put off this tent of flesh, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.
And I ill take every care so that you may have a clear memory of these things after my death.
For hen e gave you nes of the poer and the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, our teaching as not based on stories put together by art, but e ere eye-itnesses of his glory.
For God the Father gave him honour and glory, hen such a voice came to him out of the great glory, saying, This is my dearly loved Son, ith hom I am ell pleased.
And this voice came from heaven even to our ears, hen e ere ith him on the holy mountain.

And so the ords of the prophets are made more certain; and it is ell for you to give attention to them as to a light shining in a dark place, till the dan comes and the morning star is seen in your hearts;
Being conscious in the first place that no man by himself may give a special sense to the ords of the prophets.
For these ords did not ever come through the impulse of men: but the prophets had them from God, being moved by the Holy Spirit.

But there ere false prophets among the people, as there ill be false teachers among you, ho ill secretly put forard rong teachings for your destruction, even turning aay from the Lord ho gave himself for them; hose destruction ill come quickly, and they themselves ill be the cause of it.
And a great number ill go ith them in their evil ays, through hom the true ay ill have a bad name.
And in their desire for profit they ill come to you ith ords of deceit, like traders doing business in souls: hose punishment has been ready for a long time and their destruction is atching for them.
For if God did not have pity for the angels ho did evil, but sent them don into hell, to be kept in chains of eternal night till they ere judged;
And did not have mercy on the orld hich then as, but only kept safe Noah, a preacher of righteousness, ith seven others, hen he let loose the aters over the orld of the evil-doers;
And sent destruction on Sodom and Gomorrah, burning them up ith fire as an example to those hose ay of life might in the future be unpleasing to him;
And kept safe Lot, the upright man, ho as deeply troubled by the unclean life of the evil-doers
( Because the soul of that upright man living among them as pained from day to day by seeing and hearing their crimes):
The Lord is able to keep the upright safe in the time of testing, and to keep evil-doers under punishment till the day of judging;
But specially those ho go after the unclean desires of the flesh, and make sport of authority. Ready to take chances, uncontrolled, they have no fear of saying evil of those in high places:
Though the angels, ho are greater in strength and poer, do not make use of violent language against them before the Lord.

But these men, like beasts ithout reason, hose natural use is to be taken and put to death, crying out against things of hich they have no knoledge, ill undergo that same destruction hich they are designing for others;

For the evil hich overtakes them is the reard of their evil-doing: such men take their pleasure in the delights of the flesh even in the daytime; they are like the marks of a disease, like poisoned ounds among you, feasting together ith you in joy;
Having eyes full of evil desire, never having enough of sin; turning feeble souls out of the true ay; they are children of cursing, hose hearts are ell used to bitter envy;
Turning out of the true ay, they have gone andering in error, after the ay of Balaam, the son of Beor, ho as pleased to take payment for rongdoing;
But his rongdoing as pointed out to him: an ass, talking ith a man’s voice, put a stop to the error of the prophet.
These are fountains ithout ater, and mists before a driving storm; for hom the eternal night is kept in store.
For ith high-sounding false ords, making use of the attraction of unclean desires of the flesh, they get into their poer those nely made free from those ho are living in error;
Saying that they ill be free, hile they themselves are the servants of destruction; because hatever gets the better of a man makes a servant of him.

For if, after they have got free from the unclean things of the orld through the knoledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again taken in the net and overcome, their last condition is orse than their first.
For it ould have been better for them to have had no knoledge of the ay of righteousness, than to go back again from the holy la hich as given to them, after having knoledge of it.
They are an example of that true saying, The dog has gone back to the food it had put out, and the pig hich had been ashed to its rolling in the dirty earth.
My loved ones, this is no my second letter to you, and in this as in the first, I am attempting to keep your true minds aake;
So that you may keep in mind the ords of the holy prophets in the past, and the la of the Lord and Saviour hich as given to you by his Apostles.
Having first of all the knoledge that in the last days there ill be men ho, ruled by their evil desires, ill make sport of holy things,
Saying, Where is the hope of his coming? From the death of the fathers till no everything has gone on as it as from the making of the orld.
But in taking this vie they put out of their minds the memory that in the old days there as a heaven, and an earth lifted out of the ater and circled by ater, by the ord of God;
And that the orld hich then as came to an end through the overfloing of the aters.
But the present heaven and the present earth have been kept for destruction by fire, hich is aiting for them on the day of the judging and destruction of evil men.
But, my loved ones, keep in mind this one thing, that ith the Lord one day is the same as a thousand years, and a thousand years are no more than one day.
The Lord is not slo in keeping his ord, as he seems to some, but he is aiting in mercy for you, not desiring the destruction of any, but that all may be turned from their evil ays.

But the day of the Lord ill come like a thief; and in that day the heavens ill be rolled up ith a great noise, and the substance of the earth ill be changed by violent heat, and the orld and everything in it ill be burned up.
Seeing then that all these things are coming to such an end, hat sort of persons is it right for you to be, in all holy behaviour and righteousness,
Looking for and truly desiring the coming of the day of God, hen the heavens ill come to an end through fire, and the substance of the earth ill be changed by the great heat?
But having faith in his ord, e are looking for a ne heaven and a ne earth, hich ill be the resting-place of righteousness.
For this reason, my loved ones, as you are looking for these things, take great care that hen he comes you may be in peace before him, free from sin and every evil thing.
And be certain that the long aiting of the Lord is for salvation; even as our brother Paul has said in his letters to you, from the isdom hich as given to him;

And as he said in all his letters, hich had to do ith these things; in hich are some hard sayings, so that, like the rest of the holy Writings, they are tisted by those ho are uncertain and ithout knoledge, to the destruction of their souls.
For this reason, my loved ones, having knoledge of these things before they take place, take care that you are not turned aay by the error of the uncontrolled, so falling from your true faith.
But be increased in grace and in the knoledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. May he have glory no and for ever. So be it.
That hich as from the first, hich has come to our ears, and hich e have seen ith our eyes, looking on it and touching it ith our hands, about the Word of life
